Text: Ah, the Hill Tavern. Used to be a top neighborhood hangout back when I was in school at Suffolk - I still love going back! It can get pretty crowded on weekend nights, but the atmosphere and awesome jukebox more than make up for it. The Hill is fairly laid-back, although you can also go dressed up and not feel out of place. The food I've had there has been pretty good, and there's a good drink selection. They will always have a place in my heart!

Pre- CV19 visit. I'm happy to report this is still a 4-star venue. You should be aware that TF is not large so during their busy periods they will be jammed. One thing that I don't like is their seating, but it's a small price to pay to truly wonderful tortillas 

Be aware that they have rotating taps so ask your server if they have any small batches available. We have been here a number of times and there always seems to be a local or CA-based specialty beer available. But I'm not here for the beer I'm here for quaff down some of their righteous tortillas. 

Onto the food. Homemade tortillas you bet! I went with barbacoa and a pork option. I could have gone for a third but beer, chips, and amazing sauces had filled my panza to satisfaction. 

Not sure if this is still happening but be aware of the no parking signs for the lot next door. If you park there you are booted immediately and your only recourse is to pay up there to have the boot removed.

I can only reiterate what others have said, and what I've told my friends for a long time.  Besides the Alamo Drafthouse locations, this is by far the best theater in the Austin area.  The DLP projection and digital sound is exceptional.

I've seen lots of movies here over the last two years primarily because the Galaxy hosts a large amount of free screenings for movies.  I get a chance to go to many of these screenings which I thoroughly enjoy when they are held here.  The seats are comfortable with a lot of leg room.  The arms for the seats can move up and out of the way if you need the extra room.  I haven't tried the DBOX setup yet, but I've heard that can be rather enjoyable as well (although the price can really set you back a bit).

The only problem is location. For whatever reason (and I'm sure there are many), this part of town has really started to fall apart.  There was a time that the Lincoln Village Shopping Center and Highland Mall were fine places to shop, etc.  Now, not so much.  I'm surprised there were only a couple of mentions of vehicle break-ins in earlier reviews since I've seen my fair share of people walk out of the theater to broken glass on the side of their vehicle.   As with anything else, at night, park as close to the theater as you can preferably under a light and keep any valuables hidden or take them with you.  Common sense, sure, but break-ins still continue to be a problem in the parking lot of this theater.

Oh, Kendall Square. You don't offer much in the way of culture or entertainment, but when you do restaurants you do them well. Hungry Mother. EVOO. And The Helmand.

I can't speak on the authenticity as the only other time I've had Afghan cuisine was during a food festival in my high school world issues class from an Afghani classmate. It was delicious, but it didn't make me an expert. But I'm going to assume the food is pretty authentic considering The Helmand is owned by Hamid Karzai's brother.

In any case, it's just delicious. My friend and I split the Kaddo to start. Fried pumpkin with yogurt garlic sauce and seasoned ground beef. Oh God, it was like the UN was invited to my mouth and everyone brought beer! So many diverse flavors and textures. Incredible! 

For entrees, this is the place to go if you love lamb. There are so many lamb dishes to choose from. After agonizing for an embarrassingly long time, I finally settled on the Khorma Challow. Leg of lamb sauteed with onions, tomatoes, garlic, green beans, and potatoes, with challow rice. Hello, UN party no. 2! Oh, you brought strippers this time? That's nice! My god, this dish was delicious. The lamb was so tender and flavorful and the melding of all those vegetables created the most heavenly stew to mix with rice. My friend had the Chapendaz and raved about how delicious it still was after being microwaved and eaten again the next day. 

They have a really great wine list and the waiters are good at suggesting pairings. The restaurant is beautifully decorated with rugs, blue glassware and various other almost kitschy touches that make the room colorful and lively without being too sleek or modern.

Come here so your food senses can experience the equivalent of a raging kegger with the coolest people in the world. There's nothing like The Helmand.

Aside from always having to wait for a very long time to be seated, I love this place (I have only been here for hot pot)
The meats are fresh, the broths are tasty and the combo comes with a lot of veggies that we love in out pot.
I just wish they had real hot tea (and mugs) to go with the food, instead of a bagged tea in a water glass.

Sometimes the music is too loud, and too party-like, but overall I really like Q. Been there 2 times and will definitely return.

I had a mild panic attack while strapped in. I almost flagged to get off! But my wife kept telling me I wouldn't die. This was both of ours first hypercoaster (300-399 ft drop). I kept watching it. And kept saying "omg that is going to be horrible."  Guess what? I lived! That drop, almost 90 degrees, 300 feet, and 72 mph was insane..but amazing. And the rest was total up and down air time leaving your seat on each crest. No loops. No corkscrews. Just up and down hills. Now I love inversions so I rate it 4 stars. But wow. Exhilarating.

Kiva is expensive but has some amazing treats! Almost everything is organic and they have plenty of milk alternatives and options for those with food allergies. 

The atmosphere is clean but not super homey. They did recently added cushions to the seats so it's easier to sit for longer periods of time, which is nice because sometimes it takes a while for your food to be ready. 

I absolutely love their Habibi bowl (who knew kale could taste so wonderful!) and green smoothies. The acai bowls are amazing too, but Moberi (a few blocks away) makes them twice as big for the same price. 

Overall they have a great selection and I always recommend it to friends. The biggest thing they could work on is customer service. Just asking "how's your day going?" before taking my order would be nice. I had a few months where I was at Kiva twice a week and always ordered the same thing, but none of the staff asked my name or seemed to remember me. Way different vibe than the staff at Dragonfly (a block away) who have my name and drink memorized and always greet me with a smile. Just a thought!

This place could really get give stars for the price and the food. I love the wings and the shrimp fried rice. The fish, too. My only issue with the place is the service. And not in general. Just when 1 guy is at work. Dare I say the Black guy. (I'm black so not trying to play that card.)  But only when he is at work that the calls to the restaurant go unanswered. So no call-in orders. I have called on several occasions several times for nearly an hour once, and 30-40 mins on a couple other occasions. (sometimes i really want those wings...lol... and I can pretty much walk to this place).  I figured they were busy today but when I finally just stopped by, there was only a couple eating together inside. I walked rt up and ordered.  The first time I ordered here, he stared at me blankly when I first walked in, didnt say hello, welcome, what do u want, nothing. And at first I just waited to see if he wud say anything. I can be an ass, too. But after it got weird, I broke the silence n ordered. I started to leave. He has an extremely dry n rude demeanor. He has his days where he is sufferable.   He is costing the business money. He's an idiot. #sorry. Like why be an a#s n work in customer service. Decided to send this after wanting to on too many prior occasions.

Finally got around to trying to chickpea fritter sandwich 
Don't really like red cabbage but in this combo, I wasn't toooo tempted to pick it all out. Yes, I sometimes do this in salads, even though I am probably too old to be picky about my veggies and have no allergies.
The flavor was good and I thoroughly enjoyed my rather large lunch. I probably shouldn't have tried so hard to finish it haha. 
This might be a terrible comparison but for some reason, the chickpea fritter sandwich and the falafel wrap at Amsterdam Falafelshop seem comparable in my head. While Clover's location is far more convenient for me, I prefer the Davis Square eatery more than this one.

My date decided to surprise me with a booked reservation to this restaurant. It has been on my to try list for a number of years but for some reason, I always ended up somewhere else. Good thing he placed a reservation because the place was packed soon after 6pm.

Service was fantastic. Our server was very on top of keeping the dinner flow going and our drinks were never empty.

We ordered cornbread to share. Unfortunately, I make a better version at home so it was a miss for us. The duck meatball and spaghetti was fantastic though. It should be an entree size as well. 

I ordered the smoked duck breast and my date ordered a beef chuck for our entrees. I ended up liking the beef dish more. I found the hollandaise sauce to be a bit too tangy for my liking. The duck was perfectly done, but I found the sourness of the sauce took away from the duck. Not to mention, it was drowning in a lot of sauce. Some people love sauce so this would be great for those type of people.

We ordered a s'mores to share for dessert. It was beautifully presented. The brownie was very rich that we could not finish eating it. Overall, it was a nice meal.

Bought at a great price a used Canon Mark 5D mark 2 rated at EX. FedEx made a mess out of the delivery but that's not on KEH. They responded fast and gave great attention to my needs. Not even my mom does that! When the camera arrived (thanks to a cousin who worked at FedEx cleared it up) I was surprised to see how new the camera looked. It even smelled new. (what? you don't smell your electronics) Very happy with these guys. You will be to.
Thanks KEH!

This is a semi full cafe with some eats, however, wouldn't go as far as calling this a full out cafe by any means. I have had their bubble tea a few times in the area. Unlike some of the places in Richmond, this place is okay. They stick to the original recipe to the best of their ability and although average there always seems to be something missing, especially in the berry infusion blends. Not that cheap either. Customer service was okay.

Overall, a very good experience. So yes, the wait on a Friday was about an hour, but we expected that.  We found seats at the bar & the bar staff were all very friendly & attentive. Even when one of the bartenders forgot two of our drinks, she was very apologetic & quickly made the drinks.

Once seated we had Kelsey(?). While she was clearly having a busy night, she was attentive, friendly, & helpful with the menu.  Our party of 4 included 2 guys who like to "interact" with the server, so she definitely handled their obnoxiousness well.  We also somehow received a comp'ed margarita & martini from the bar, so that was an extra perk.

The food:  Here is really the only area where I dropped one star.  Here's a breakdown of what the table ordered & their comments:

Calamari & Zuccini:  "Good, but a little cold"; "nothing special"
Queso:  "Runny", "needs to be hotter" (temperature hot), "the chips are a little odd".  Would suggest the option of adding sausage or ground beef as well.
Mushroom Pizza:  "very good, I would order this again!"
Ribeye:  "the wood firing was tasty, as were the potatoes"
Lamb Chops:  "they were pretty good, but the potatoes and asparagus were great"
Carnivore Pizza:  they forgot the requested jalapenos & egg, but.... "excellent! I would come back just for this pizza", "crispy, hot, cheesy, just the right balance of toppings."  This was what I personally ordered.  The two aforementioned guys took slices as well, so this part of the review is balanced by 3 out of 4 people at our table.
Gelato: I shared the Trio with my husband & we chose: Creamcicle, Pistachio & Stracciatella (which is basically chocolate chip).  They were all very, very good & we ate all of it.  Our friends had the cheesecake & cobbler & there were zero complaints there as well.

We live about 15/20 mins away, so we probably won't be making this a regular stop just due to the commute down 620, BUT as I told my husband in the car on the way home, if someone asked about Napa Flats, I would definitely agree to go or recommend it.

Overall, a great dinner!  I would go back & tell other friends to do so as well.

Wings done well. Atmosphere and overall location were eh.  Let me break this down simply.  If all you are looking for are good wings and could care less about the venue itself, Papa Bees is worth the stop.  The wings, which my guests and I shared fifty with five different flavors, were crispy as requested and delicious.

We had garlic parm, spicy teriyaki, honey mustard, honey garlic, and chipotle BBQ.  They were all yummy flavors, but garlic parm was my favorite.  

The venue offered some TVs for sport watchers.  It was a basic, open location.  It just didn't have much theme/decor to it so it seemed plain and un-inviting of a space.  Also not a huge fan of logo, etc.  With that said, 4 stars for the wings!  And that fifth would be added if they could find a way for me to actually be excited to be in that space.

I really enjoyed eating here. The place is cozy with a very welcoming vibe and relaxed atmosphere. They had outdoor and indoor seating and left mask wearing up to you. Also everything here is somehow made with donuts! 

My husband got Grandma's Dumplings which had donut dough used for the dumplings and oh my goodness did that make it so pillowy and soft! I had the Country Clucker which was very delicious though I didn't feel having the donut added anything to it.

Good place to visit in Austin if you want a unique tasting experience!

Right off the bat I want to note that the above hours for the RPAC are their hours while students are in classes.  The weeks between quarters and during holidays are not usually as accomodating.

But wow, this gym is awesome. I was a student during the days of Larkins, the old fitness building, then I remember when the first phase of the RPAC opened up. It was beautiful, especially when you compared it to Larkins - it was decrepit, smelly, cold and it was like a maze in there sometimes.  I always felt like I could get lost somewhere down there and no one would ever find me because my cell phone got no reception in there at all.  *shudders*  Working out at Larkins was like punishing yourself for wanting to get off your butt and work out.

Then along comes the RPAC, all bright, shiny and new, and it made you actually want to work out. People who never worked out a day in their lives were suddenly coming up with excuses to go to the gym. And there were other reasons to go there besides exercise.  There was the Courtside Cafe: right inside the door you could have a seat at this little cafe and eat snacks and sandwiches, like their peanut butter and banana with granola sandwich.  That thing was huge, yummy, and so filling that I got 3 meals out of it.

There was also the Juice Bar, where you could get smoothies, coffee, teas, etc.  There was also a little shop downstairs where you could buy Powerbars and things like that.  

If you felt like getting semi-active, you could change into your bathing suit and hit the recreational pool. Seriously, free awesome swimming pool on campus. Greatest thing ever. There was a little part of the pool that looked like a hot tub but wasn't, unfortunately.  And half the pool was roped off for those who wanted to swim laps.  But it was big enough to go and play around.  

The locker rooms were also nice, had plenty of space, but you had to pay to use the lockers.  I really liked the private bathrooms.  They have like two or three of them, close to where the pool is, and if you're lucky enough to snag one, you have a whole bathroom (that you lock) to yourself. This includes a toilet, sink, shower and sitting area.

There was also a daycare center in there so people could leave their kids in there to play and watch cartoons while they did their thing. I should also mention that there were 2 gyms where you could play basketball and volleyball and stuff like that. I remember that while I was there, and not too long after the RPAC opened, the gym on the lower floor flooded and was shut down for a while because they had to redo it. But I'm sure it's back to normal by now.

I loved the second floor cardio area and used to live on the EFX machines and the treadmills.  There was a whole canyon of them downstairs, but that was too crowded for my taste.  Plus I liked the upstairs because you could see out the glass walls to the outside and it was so bright and cheery up there from all the sunshine coming through.  They had TVs mounted from the ceiling in front of the exercise equipment so you had something to look at, but the sound wasn't very loud and you couldn't hear the TV. They usually had the TVs playing mtvU - the college MTV channel.  I always just brought my iPod and listened to that.

There was usually plenty of machines to go around, but sometimes you had to wait.  I can't really say when the busy hours were, but I remember them being something around noon and 5-6 pm during the weekdays.  I tried to go at odd times and hardly ever had a problem getting right on a machine.

There was a huge weight room downstairs, but I never went there to work out, although I would have liked to.  It was usually full of guys who looked like they were taking lifting weights too seriously, and I didn't really want to go in there and show off that lifting 50 pounds with my weak lady arms is a struggle for me. Just a bit intimidating.

There were all kinds of classrooms in the RPAC, and I had a few classes in there, like Women's Self Defense. I know that they also hosted martial arts and yoga classes.  

I almost forgot to mention the running track upstairs.  That was awesome. It was at the highest point in the buidling, and when you were up there looking over the railing you could see down through the RPAC. It is such a pretty building.

Too bad I only got to use it for part of my college career.  Back then my loans were paying for my reduced membership. But now that I'm out of school?  I don't think I'm even eligible to join, but even if I was, I can't afford it.  It's so expensive, but I think you have to be a staff member or grad student or something to purchase a membership outside of undergrad school.  That sucks, because I would love to work out here again. If you are able to get a membership, try it out. It's the best gym I've ever worked out in and I miss it!

If you are into watching the game, any game this is the place to be.  They have a gazillion televisions for your viewing pleasure.  It's a pretty decent sized place, and business seems pretty steady.  

Full liquid bar with 2 for 1 drinks.  The strawberry mojito is delish, but I could only drink one. With a stick of rock candy in each drink, the drink just became super sweet.

The menu is decent, lots of options.  I personally love their artichoke and goat cheese flat bread. My b/f loves the chicken sandwich.  They offer a hangover burger, perfect for "those" types of days. 

I was a little disappointed that there isn't an area for games to keep the kids entertained.  The service has always been good, so we can live without the video games.

I've been here a few times and am a big, big fan.  

Reasonable drink prices, (usually) awesome live music, no cover!, and a very intimate setting, if that's what you're going for.

Of course, there's a fine line between "intimate setting" and "there's no room for me or my coat and I'm tripping over everyone and crap, the trombone player is in the way so I can't go to the bathroom without bumping into him and having everyone at the bar glare at me."  And sometimes, Toad walks that line.

But it is what it is.  From the few times I've gone (Brendan Hogan, Dietrich Strause [amazing], and Greg Klyma), the bands tend to be a little more on the folksy side, but I think they'll just jam with whomever decides to show up that night.  A hole in the wall, sure, but well worth checking out.

Sitting here in a very empty restaurant. Nobody is here dining but our table of 3 wait staff and another table of 4. So glad we left the others so we could try this place recommended by another yelper who loves the Kiwi/watermelon drink. :) On this day there wasn't any souvenir glasses to take home after you ordered the kiwi lemonade drink. (Not happy about that) :(

We ordered one of the most popular menu items the chicken/waffles which was enough for my table of 3. When it came out my Mr. Didn't wanna share. (Knowing doggone well he would have leftovers) So I ordered the egg scramble with avocado, and Swiss with potatoes. ALL HUGE PORTIONS. My 6 year old thought we were on a set for cloudy with a chance of meatballs by the size of his waffle with bacon and our gigantic meals!!

 I wish we had tried this on our first night visiting. The prices for the quantity is awesome. The waitress Heather just did what she was suppose to do and that was it. I would definitely brag to the rest of our group of 18 . Maybe they will get a chance to eat here before we leave Orlando.  Just glad we beat them to it!

I came here at a busy time and we were seated immediately. The vibe was very welcoming and warming.... the drinks were ok, we ordered a few appetizers (chicken wings and pretzels - which had very good sauces). My meal was the produce bowl with added steak, I ordered a medium rare which came out rare(I had hardly a problem with). I'd have to say, I couldn't clean the plate enough, the quinoa had a spice that complicates the steak perfectly. I will come back.

I love this place. I found it on here actually and a couple months ago, I called up and booked an appointment and was given one with an advanced stylist, Nancy.  

She spent a good amount of time talking with me about what I wanted, what I didn't want, and she helped give me some new ideas. She persuaded me to do something a bit more diferent, and I did, and I was so happy with the results. I walked in there just to get basically the same thing I've had for years and she helped me realize that my color wasn't working well with my skin and that I should go for something new. She's the first stylist I've ever had that really understands what will and won't work on my hair and she won't do anything or cut it a certain way that she knows won't work. 

I had my second appointment with her just the other day and did something even more dramatic with my hair and again, I am so pleased with the results. Nancy does not make you feel like she is rushing to get your hair done like a lot of stylists tend to do and she spends a nice, long time with the styling, too. I have a ton of hair and my old hairdresser was never shy about how much she disliked blow drying it. Nancy is always relaxed and she spent a really long time with the blow dry, which is one of my favorite things about going to the salon.

All in all....great experience. I highly recommend Nancy. She is really nice and friendly, is so great with coloring and styling and  she makes sure to spend a lot of time on the consultation, making sure you are comfortable with what she's doing and she explains every step along the way. 
(The assistants there are really nice and friendly, too.)

* * * Heavenly food, but space too close for comfort * * *
On my first visit today, I took a friend for his birthday. He had the moussaka, and I had a flatbread with lamb, spinach and shiitake. We shared some hummus and an almond rose cake. The food was perfection: fresh, flavorful, delicate. I appreciated the moderate portions (no supersizing here) and the beautiful flavors.
My only issue was space. The lounge seating there is lovely, but quite small. We went at 1:30 PM on a Friday and it was packed. My friend and I had to squeeze on a bench and share a tiny round table. When the corner spot next to us (with a slightly larger table) opened up, we transferred, only to be given the evil eye and get trapped in the corner by the family of four and a half -- two grandparents, two mommies and small child -- who took our previous, minuscule spot. Clearly they had been waiting for the corner spot, but sadly we didn't realize it until it was too late and awkward to do anything about it. 
What a bummer: I wanted to savor my food slowly but had to rush because we were squished too close for comfort.
Moral of the story: Skip the lunchtime rush.  If you're a party of 1-3 and you want to savor your food without feeling rushed, come mid-morning or mid-afternoon. And if you're a large group, order TAKE OUT or consider other options -- at least until the restaurant has better seating!

3 Brothers Diner is a new restaurant in Grove City. It's much nicer than a greasy diner. The inside is clean and the food is healthier. It has a few better options than the slop at most diners. The service is pretty fast too.

I had the vegetable salad. It's about $8 which is good for how much you get. The salad had black beans, rice, and vegetables. It's much healthier than most things in a diner. The place has a Mexican theme. It has items like burritos. They have many vegetarian options. 

It could use more business. It's usually quiet. There are much worse places around there people choose to eat at but this is superior in price and taste.

I was very hesitant to try this place because of some of the Yelp reviews. However, I have to say that it was much better than I expected. My Mom had been wanting to try it, so I thought, "Why not? Let's try it". The burgers were actually quite good (we both got Classics) and they were cooked perfectly. They were seasoned well and juicy-overall a solid burger. Much better than Johnny Rockets, Five Guys, Burger King, McDonalds etc. We also got the onion rings, which were also very good. Good batter and sweet onions. All of the staff were friendly and helpful. 
I didn't like the way the restaurant was set up and the "family style" seating. It was a good thing for us that the restaurant was empty, so it wasn't an issue. But, it was a Friday night at 6pm and there were only a handful of people in the restaurant. It was odd...I wonder if it is because this place really doesn't have a niche. It is better than traditional fast food burger places, but more expensive...It may be too expensive for a family of four to go to dinner, so it might get passed over. I don't know. What I do know is I will go back again to try some of the other burgers and the shakes.

Very intimate and a cute place to meet for happy hour. Their happy hour menu is great! Cheaper prices and smaller portions, but are comparable to regular size items. I'd recommend coming here for happy hour and only happy hour. 

My friends and I dropped in after happy hour and while we were happy with what we got, it wasn't anything extraordinary. We got this massive bowl of a drink, which was actually a lot of liquor, despite having an entire bowl in there taking up space to hold up a flaming piece of bread (super cool, would recommend ordering this). 

The food itself was alright! A bit overpriced for the portions, and a tad over salted. I didn't love it but I didn't hate it either.

It was a quiet, chilly, late weekday evening when we descended the steps into Nuba. There were a few tables scattered around the classy candlelit dining room. The friendly server approached us right away and greeted us with a big smile. 

We both ordered teas to warm up, but the selection of three run of the mill black teas that were available did not include any spiced or blended teas that we had hoped for. Nonetheless, we were pleasantly surprised when our server was able to produce both the honey and soy milk condiments that we had requested.

For nibbles, we ordered what we thought would be a light snack - assorted veggie platters for two ($28). For our dipping pleasure, the pita wedges arrived first with generous pools of tzatziki, hummous, and tabouleh melting into each other on a large plate. The second mezze was a mammoth mountain of warm goodies. Lightly breaded scallop-shaped falafel, rectangular sticks of feta, flavourfully marinated mushrooms, fried cauliflower, and sweet and hearty fuul (brown bean mash), were served with a trio of savoury sauces. 

The service was attentive throughout the evening, with constant water refills (both iced and hot for our teapots) and smiles to make sure that everything was going well.

All in all, Nuba provided a truly enjoyable meal in a comfortable and stylish space. I will definitely be back for more.

Absolutely Appealing and Almost Affordable

All of their flavors are strong yet sane,
Assorted menu, seldom mundane, 
As you dine, sip some champagne,
And service is a beauty and brain (neither a pain nor plain!)
An open kitchen to witness your meat slain,
Albeit, worry not, it is all humane, 
Artery it clogs though and the vein,
After many courses it will you detain,
Appetizers over main courses reign,
Although the price makes your head spin in vain, 
A-minus grade goes to Craigie on Main.

Went to look at a used jeep just to test drive and get a feel. Talked with a salesmen named Matt Saia. He was very helpful in explaining all the different options and pricing, a true jeep guy. I told him I just wanted to look and he didnt give me any pressure to buy what so ever, he let me take a new jeep wrangler unlimited on a test drive by self for over an hour. It was nice to have him encourage my to test it on streets I know and go show my family. When I came back I dropped the keys off to him, he gave me a card and said to call if I had anymore questions and I left. It was nice to deal with someone that seemed human and gave me very little pressure!

Yummmm. I loved the atmosphere here. This is a great place to try some authentic Persian food!

The (free) appetizer they serve before you order was so interesting! Some flatbread, cheese and mint leaves. The flavors work so well together when you put all three into one bite.

We got the combination kabob plate, and a couple of their cocktails. 
The kabob plate was delicious! The meats were cooked well, and the meat also tastes great with the flatbread/cheese/mint.
The cocktails were okay. They were a bit pricy, but smooth tasting considering their strength. Service was great, of course.

Went here yesterday with a buddy of mine. I had heard great things about this place for years and had meaning meaning to try it yet never had gotten around to going until now. 

An ex girlfriend of mine, who was a strict vegan, often declared that Udipi and Vatica (in Marietta / East Cobb) were her two favorite strict / pure vegetarian restaurants in ATL (that also just happened to be Indian Restaurants).

My friend and I started off with a potato fritter appetizer that came with mint sauce and some other kind of sauce. It was awesome; especially the mint sauce.

He and I both got curry dishes, both come with rice. He got a spinach curry whereas I got a spicy tofu curry. We decided to split our entrees. Both were good but I think I liked his spinach dish a little better; however, my tofu curry was decidedly spicier. My friend, who can't take the spice heat levels that I can, was not able to eat too much of the tofu dish I ordered. Both come with a yogurt dipping sauce which is fantastic. 

We also ordered garlic nan which was soaked in melted ghee (some kind of Indian / Pakistani yogurt butter I think); again fantastic.

A little bit on the pricy side for what we got ($12-$13 dollar range each) but all in all a great dinner.

Rocking chicken is a must try. Sweet, salty, spicy, and tender. Reminds me of the Korean chickens. Better yet comes with free refill of white rice. Makes me wanna go back for more the next day.

Another must try is the green tea shake. More like slush, perfect for a hot summer day. Good quality ingredients, and you can actually taste the matcha. 

As for environment, it has a small area for sitting. It's a lucky day if you don't have to wait to be seated. It's almost always the case when you have to sit with strangers

Based on the mixed reviews I read, I wasn't sure if I'd enjoy it but I was pleasantly surprised. Like everything else, there are usually discounts available (I found a 20% off coupon online).

The first room of the tour, your tour guide, dressed in authentic garb, introduces himself and introduces you to the owner of the ship via video. The next room is the shipyard and the following is the ticket office. Then you get to experience the inside of the ship from the artifacts, a recreation of the grand staircase, even the cargo hold.

Now when you are checked in for the tour, you are given a paper ticket with the name and information of a passenger on the ship. Once you make your way through the boiler room and brave the freezing temperatures of the deck and captains bridge, you find yourself in the memorial room. There you will look up on the walls and find your characters name; my character, despite being second class and female, perished when the ship sank.

Next you get to the room with an actual iceberg! The iceberg is 31 degrees and they have you hold your hand there for 10 seconds. It was freezing and was pretty painful; I can only imagine floating in water that cold for 40 minutes (although most didn't last that long). They even had a huge portion of the ship available to see in the final room.

Although I came in with low expectations, the tour guide really brought the tour to life with colorful stories and even some cheesy jokes. If you need something to do near international drive to kill an hour, it might be worth your while.

If Yelp had half-stars, this would be a 3.5 review, but since I am hopelessly in love with Levenger's paper products, I'm rounding up. And yes, I am a no-fooling Levenger addict; I absolutely live through my Circa. (I lost the previous Circa a couple of years ago and literally could not function or collect my wits for days; not only was my life in that thing, not only were various business notes in that thing, MY REMODEL SKETCHES WERE IN THAT THING. Still not okay. Still not okay. *deep breath*) 

Where was I? Oh yeah, about to enter the temple of Levenger, after buying online for years (and reading the catalog aspirationally in college, because a certain type of person regards fancy pens as The Key To Everything, and sadly I was that person). Anyway, in I went to select my movin'-on-up fancy pen to go with my aforementioned life-encompassing Circa.

The store was okay -- you know, okay. It's possible I expected too much (whatever in the previous two paragraphs gave you that idea?). The store is tidy and easy to navigate; the paper refills I was seeking were handy, and the samples set out for examination were good samples and nice to examine in person. Lots of emphasis on the leather goods and the desk accoutrements, which aren't for me, but someone's buying those too. 

The pen section -- the goal of the visit -- was where the experience slumped just a little. Not the pens themselves; this ends with me choosing a very nice fountain pen that I use daily. The buying experience itself, though, was a little bumpy. I liked the pens I was shown and didn't necessarily feel upsell pressure, but I wish I'd gotten more information on both other pens that might be appealing (seriously, I *announce* that I'm here to spend like a drunken pen-loving sailor and you show me three pens?) and a little more data on the one I eventually chose. (When I said something about buying another nib for it down the line, that would have been a good time to mention that Levenger doesn't offer swappable nibs on this model. Just sayin'.) 

It was okay. I still like my pen. I still live in, through, and for my Circa. I still buy Levenger products...online. Glad I went in. Not frantic to go back.

It gives me great pleasure, more of which than I should probably admit, to inform others of when I have found a deal. Usually, it starts with my quoting a price and then rattling off what I believe to be the vast amount of value (in goods and/or services) that I received for this price. Sometimes, it's a lunch special, other times a sale and, at the most amazing times, it's just how things always are at a particular place.

Enter Berry Freeze. For $2.98, I was able to scarf down a generous portion of frozen yogurt with a multitude of toppings--all of which, I got to concoct myself! For just $2.98, I filled my size small cup with mostly chocolate yogurt and a dash of pomegranate and topped it off with chocolate sprinkles, an oreo, a piece of milky way, a piece of twix, vanilla syrup and a swirl of chocolate syrup, too. For $2.98, I got to feel like a kid again.

Worth noting is the ability to create your own flavors by adding as much or as little of each type of yogurt available, not to mention the vast choices in topping, from fruit pebbles and a chocolate bars, to fresh fruits and nuts.  Worth pointing out as potential downfalls are the yogurt's actual lack of tartness and it's mildly grainy texture. However, paired with a DIY service style and low, low price tag, these are smaller points you'll hardly notice. Especially if you go a little nuts on the toppings.

Four stars for the food and flavor.  Three stars for the portion size, as it was quite small.   Their entrees are inexpensive, and the portions reflect the price.  For $2 more you can get "family size."  I was unaware of the vast difference, although I did think that the overall cost was quite inexpensive.  The portion would be right for a small child.  The garlic chicken was minuscule.  I would go back because the flavor was pretty good, but for every item you need to upgrade, and it would still be very reasonable.  Even with the 2 dollar upgrade the entrees would still be 8.95-10.95.  They should just serve one size that is reasonable and charge for it as well.  If you are in this part of town it would be worth stopping in for some good thai food.

So I finally got to go and check this place out.

Surprisingly there was food you could order. Not a huge menu but enough.

I ordered three drinks and they were pretty good and strong! I wasn't expecting that. I'm used to the watered down booze that Vancouverites can fall victim to at certain places.

The ambiance was very dark...dark green in particular. Very cool vibe that goes with the 20s prohibition theme.

I ordered the "punch" which was very unique. Another cranberry drink with cinnamon and gin.  Very unique and super strong.  You could barely see the cranberry juice.  Lastly I had a mojito which was made to perfection!

The drink came with a few pretzels and some really tasty almonds.  I wI'll definetly be back to try more drinks on the menu.

Oh and my waitress was awesome!

Now that I've passed 40 reviews I notice my criterion for 5 stars has gotten much higher, in fact while I love Cityside Subaru I just don't see how I could possibly give a car dealership 5 stars. So consider this a 4 1/2 star review please.

I am a Subaru addict! Especially on a day like today with 13 inches of snow on the ground, I appreciate not even having to shovel my car out. You can't beat the All Wheel Drive and now it seems like so many other car's are following the lead. I love Cityside because the service center is run by a bunch of nice guys. They are always polite and informative and the new facility in Belmont (used to be in a cramped little spot in Arlington) is beautiful and makes waiting for my car go by quickly. If you want to buy a Subaru go here and stay for the service.

So, I guess Mu Mu's is better known for their nightlife than their culinary offerings, but as we walked by, glancing over their menu, it seemed like we should at least give it a shot.  I'm glad we did too.

It seemed pretty mellow inside, playing some Steely Dan over the stereo, put me right into a nice state of relaxation.  It was about high noon on a Sunday, and I wasn't sure if I wanted to do breakfast or lunch, lucky for me, they serve up both (I guess that's fairly customary for Sunday brunch).  

I went with their Brutus Smash sandwich.  It was delicious!  Now, I'm pretty familiar with places that serve up sandwiches with french fries on them; i.e. the Grease Trucks in New Brunswick, NJ and Pramanti Brothers in Pittsburgh.  Let me tell you, this one was the best of them all.  The fries didn't consume the flavor of the sandwich, instead added to the overall taste quite nicely.  I enjoyed every last bite.

The interior of the place is also well conceived, utilizing quite a bit of metal working.  Check out their ceiling, it's pretty cool, at least I thought so.

Just got back from a trip to Portland.  We had brunch at Jam and it was super delicious.  I'm allergic to gluten and the gluten free oatmeal-chai-blueberry pancakes were fantastic.   I loved that they are served with real maple syrup.  The applewood smoked bacon was also very tasty.  I took off one star because the service was very odd.  We were waiting for two friends to join us and no one stopped by to offer us a beverage while we were waiting.  We finally flagged the server.  Once we did so, she was super friendly and helpful, it was just strange at first.  
We also stopped in one night for just coffee as we had been stood up by  our friends.  The female bartender was extremely friendly and fun.

I'm a Florida Jew with New York parents, so we are mild bagel snobs. Not jerks, but mild snobs. Mom is in town for the holidays, so we grabbed a pre-Passover bagel and cream cheese at the Magnificent. They "import" their bagels from NYC, so they've got the magic. I got an ET bagel toasted, open-faced, thin shmear of chive cream cheese on each side, slice of tomato. Classic!

the ladies there are a perfect mix of sweet n surly, the bagel was toasted well, and was no wussy imitation.

We ate in, which was fun, low-brow and mellow.

Highly recommended

Stopped in here for a quick bite before heading to Legoland. Restaurant wasn't busy luckily but things picked up shortly after our arrival, it was clean and staff was super friendly! We were seated upon arrival and our waitress came within seconds of us getting settled to take our drink order. The had a few specials listed but my go breakfast is corned beef hash, I can't pass it up and love trying it wherever we go. This place offered typical breakfast items and had lunch offerings as well. 
Once the food order was taken it wasn't long before it was brought out to the table. My hash didn't disappoint- generous portion with 2 eggs, hash browns and a homemade biscuit. The biscuit definitely hit the spot, it was delicious!! Kids meals also were a good portion, served with 3-4 slices of bacon each. 
Nice spot for a quick, hardy bite!

My wife and I have been looking for a nice local Italian restaurant and we have found our spot.  This is a family owned restaurant that is beautifully decorated with amazing food.  Definitely give this place a shot, you will enjoy the warm greeting you get.  The fried mozzarella is seasoned and delicious.  My wife loves the caprese salad and there's plenty of freshly baked bread.  The lasagna is my favorite.  It's a huge portion and tastes amazing.  The owner goes out of her way to make you comfortable.  You won't be disappointed if you try this.

Based on a recommendation from a locally based friend we rocked up here on a beautiful, balmy Sunday evening after a fabulous football game (Atlanta won. Go Falcons!). It's a neighborhood restaurant without pretensions and inexpensive in the bargain. Absolutely no complaints. We opted to sit outside as twilight descended. It's not the most romantic of locations but they make the best of it so props there as well. The frozen margaritas came in several sizes - small, medium and goodbye 'til Tuesday! And they were excellent. My chicken fajitas were superb, possibly among the best I'd had for a while. Recommended.

Stopped here as a turn around point in a bike ride from the Hoover dam (12.6 miles each way and a gorgeous ride).

Galena is a cute little town that started as an old mill town and there is about a one block section of "downtown" and that's where the galena diner is.

I ordered the Molly's Benedict thinking I would eat one muffin and force the other in my friend who "wasn't hungry".  Think eggs Benedict minus Canadian bacon add real bacon and FRESH delicious tomato and spinach. Ohemgee...this was amazing...and I ate the whole dang thing!

My none hungry friend ate the fruit bowl which had some yummy deliciously fresh fruit including mango and some interesting melon.

The service was fast and friendly...definitely Midwest small town! There were some tables outside but they were full when I was there so we sat inside.  Nothing fancy just old school diner and clean...lots of old photos on the walls to check out.

I'm looking forward to my next visit!

Four stars are given for the service and drinks. 
We did the bottles mimosas for $13.50 the special runs till 4:00 and is definitely worth the price. The atmosphere is fun and makes for a great spot to brunch and drink. Our table also ordered a load smoked bloodymary. The taste was spot on, however the drink price is okay but if you want it loaded (with toppings) the cost goes up by $3.00 dollars. Our fries came out cold and the chicken and waffles was okay, however it could have been better. The breakfast tacos were really tasty and full of flavor. The only thing I would change about the taco is a better tortilla. Our server was upbeat knowledgeable and friendly. If you check in on yelp you get 10% off the bill. If you happen to be in the area and are looking for a brunch spot with good drinks than this is your place. Enjoy!

Great drinks. Very cool option of having the bartender "judge you" and improvise a drink they think you will love based on their impression of you. My 2 drinks were spot-on fruity with lots of hidden alcohol, haha. A friend of mine said that his drink resembled another that he had ordered from the menu, which was disconcerting due to the pricing difference. The first time we came here, the food was a little too salty for my taste. This time, everything was just right. Be forewarned that most of the apps are great, but they come with buttered bread for dipping, so if you're trying to avoid processed grains maybe go straight to charcuterie (the brie mixed with the money was heavenly) or the entrées and get a fish or meat dish.  The brownie with caramel ice cream dessert was delicious. Would go back for the cool atmosphere and drinks. Seemed to be very popular starting around 9pm or so... the place was about half full until then.

I always pass this place on my way to work and I was curious about Somnio's Cafe. I decided to hang out with my friend from work and try out the place.

It's a small place and it was really intimate. It wasn't crowded at all on a Saturday night. The menu is really small and I wish they would add more items to the menu. The food is great and healthy. I had the shittake dumplings which was really good. The service was awesome. 

I ordered Portobello Mushrooms with Yellow Curry Mash Potatoes and that took longer than my friends Sweet Potato Risotto. It was ironic because she got her food first. 

But no matter. I will come back to this place again.

Welcome to the neighborhood!  Very solid pizza, not up to par with Antico, but I can drink draft beer and walk here, so easy win.  I'd also put their pizza ahead of Vesuivus, which hasn't been as good since the remodeling.

The atmosphere in here is very cool, which makes it a great spot to meet up with friends in the neighborhood.  Although I often get confused where I'm supposed to order, as it seems to change every time I'm in.  And if it's busy, I often decide to go elsewhere.  There's a line that you have to wait in even if you're only going to the bar for drinks and don't want a table.  Pretty crazy.

Sky Lounge is one of my favorite places! My only complaint is that I wish they would figure out how to get more seating options. And maybe stay open until at least 2am on Friday and Saturday during the summer. We went there this past Saturday after a great dinner, to continue my birthday celebration. Drinks were good. They only issue is that there were no seats for our party of 4, for almost 45 minutes. Other than that, you can't beat the view or the atmosphere!

I wanted to write a review mainly because I don't think the overall rating reflects the establishment.  Clearly they have invested and put effort to create a cool atmosphere and I hope this place gets good business.  Its nice to find a place that is something a bit different and new and I think that sums up The Punk & Poet.  Enjoyed how they used old music cassettes on their menu for the drink list and to serve the check in at the table, nice touch!

You can still have a typical bar experience, with a long bar and nice casual dining/drinking table down the middle of the space.  If you are prefer traditional seating there are plenty of high tops and low tops to choose from and on a warm day the storefront opens up to the street. 

We went for brunch and and both were happy with our meals, tasty food all around.  It's priced a bit higher but you arent getting typical frozen hash browns at a standard diner.  I think they are still working out some of the kitchen/service kinks (according to other reviews, not our experience) but hopefully they will get more consistent as they are open longer. My advice to management is to stick with what you are doing but focus on consistency in food prep and emphasize a bit more on the attentiveness and welcomeness of staff.   Definitely worth a visit if you live in the area. 

We are interested to return to try some of the their cocktails, look tasty and unique. Will update the review when we try some of the entrees too.

So they don't even make the Berry Tart anymore. Why???? It was the best thing here.

But I'm bumping my review to one additional star because anything disparaging that I wrote in my original review is made up by the cool basement bar that is here and hidden away. It's a nice place to grab some pub fare (or dessert from the bakery) and have some beers while you watch the game. Trivia happens on Thursday nights so it's always packed for that.

I had the dilemma of ordering between Punjab Palace v. India Quality last night. Granted, it has been years since I ate at IQ, but all I can remember was how tasty the chicken tikka masala was at PP when I first went there back in August. They also have my favorite side condiment/dish-- onion chutney, which is amazing with rice.  I also got the baigan bhartha.  I overstuffed myself.  Ate the leftovers for lunch today and the flavors were better the night before.

I also had the garlic naan when I ate at the restaurant and remembered how delicious it was---there were visible and tasty morsels of minced garlic, the naan was somewhat flaky and light also (not too thick).


solid place for indian food.

This is by far one of the nicest hotels I've ever had the pleasure of staying at. A couple of friends and I stayed here for a convention that was happening in the hotel that weekend. I thought the decorum on the lobby areas were very pretty, and the staff was very helpful. To be honest I had expected them to be a little annoyed with having to deal with a bunch of convention goers, but they seemed rather pleasant. Even the Starbucks employees were friendly despite the huge lines, and mass amounts of people. We had 7 people staying in a two-bed suite, which I thought might cause a few problems if we were found to be crowding that many people in a room, but they didn't seem to care. The staff even brought us two roll away beds.

The only thing I can complain about is the parking situation. You have to pay to park, and can't have more than a certain amount of cars, which I think is ridiculous considering how much you are actually paying to stay here, I don't think they should require you to pay for parking.

Stopped in with a friend for a casual dinner and some drinks.

It's clear from reading the menu that the people responsible for this place are very food saavy.  From the available options on the cheese plate (Humboldt Fog!) to making a point of the heritage of their 100 y.o. sourdough starter, it seems that the quality of their ingredients is a priority.

The selection of beers on tap is excellent and all would pair well with the menu.

The pizza was very good.  Excellent crust and the perfect size to split and share.

The entire staff (our waiter, the cooks and others) were very friendly and attentive, and very tuned into food quality and customer satisfaction.  I was asked at several different points by several chefs/cooks how the food was (and you could tell they weren't just "making the rounds").

I'll definitely be coming back to try their other choices.

I've been to this cart and the one at Lloyd multiple times now.  The food is always good.  My only complaint might be that the spice can overwhelm the flavor.   Don't get me wrong.  I love spicy food and don't mind a strong habanero salsa. Here, though, a medium spice level had me reaching for something to drink. I order my food mild now and the flavor is fantastic.  

I've not ever had a bad experience - just know your heat tolerance.  :)

I had my brows waxed about 3 weeks ago here. The place was completely empty when I went, so I can't really speak much for the privacy, but yeah, the "rooms" are divided by thin curtains. If I were getting my junk waxed, I'd probably feel a bit unnerved by that.

The wax itself was fairly painless. I've had brow waxes that were in fact painful, but they seemed to get it right and give a good shape.  So uh, thumbs up?

If this review were solely on the food, Mike & Patty's would get 5 stars because the sandwiches (especially the torta) are absolutely delicious, but I have to knock it down to a 4 (I was very close to a 3, but held back my frustration) because it takes wayy tooo long to get food, and I am not looking to spend 45 precious lunch minutes getting to this not too conveniently located tiny shop and waiting for a sandwich. 

As a heads up, the shop is always full at peak hours (which isnt saying much because it only holds around 12 people, at which point it is pretty crammed) and the few times I have gotten food here its taken a while (~15-20 minutes) to actually get my sandwich after finally making it to the register. 

However, a little not-so-insider tip I... they take phone orders for customers who want to pickup their meals to-go, which I HIGHLY recommend you do if you want to come here at any peak hours.

It's been about a week since my first visit to Sister Honey's and I'm just coming down from my sugar high. 
I didn't even know this place existed until Colleen started a pie thread. After reading the reviews and craving pie for a week I decided to stop by and I'm glad I did! I got my wife the coconut cream pie and a slice of apple pie for myself....errr, AND a giant slice of hummingbird cake for both of us to share. 
My wife loved the coconut cream pie, especially the crust that had a layer of chocolate. Apple pie was wonderful too. The crust had such a nice flavor with a lingering taste of butter. mmmm. But the star was the hummingbird cake. It;s kind of like banana bread (with some pineapple) layered with cream cheese frosting. Holy moly! My head almost exploded. 
I shall return.

In location, concept, and offerings, Hills Downtown is 5 stars all the way! They have a beautiful produce sections, amazing local product offering, and the best gourmet salad bar I have ever seen. The store has a great vibe and very friendly staff.

Where the Hills Downtown fails me is the tiny super cramped isles that can't even fit two people side by side and the fact that some of their items are a $1 more than at my local co-op. During a busy time, this market is a nightmare for someone who is claustrophobic. I can say this because I am not claustrophobic and it makes me feel that way when the place is packed at weekday lunch time. 

Avoid the high prices by shopping on Mondays with your Civitas Now/Hills market bag and get 20% off all non alcoholic groceries you can fit in the bags. Do yourself a favor and buy the $25 Civitas Now bag ($32 online)!  It's made of recycled billboard vinyl and can be used as a backpack or tote. Best investment I ever made.  

Do I do all my shopping here? No. Do I enjoy stopping by once and a while for a urban shopping experience? Yes.

One of my friends I went with is paleo, and she found it a little hard to find items she could eat, buuuut that's what happens when you're on a restricting diet. I loved this place!!

I found the drinks to be a little pricey but WORTH EVERY PENNY. They do not skimp on the alcohol and the cocktails are creative and delicious with hilarious names (I think mine was the Ricky Ricardo?).

The atmosphere is playful and fun. I would call it sophisticated but sassy.  No formal frumps here.  If it were the prohibition period and you wanted to go to a sexy/classy underground joint that served alcohol on the downlow, I think Cuchi Cuchi would've been that place.

Also, they have this dessert called "banana bread extravaganza" and it is incredible. So much whipped cream, and the banana bread/cake is sooooo good. I'm salivating just typing about it.

Love this place, great neighborhood addition. 

What I loved about it was the thoughtfully designed atmosphere, the excellent variety of craft beer & bourbon, and the upbeat & attentive staff. I visited on St Pats - they'd been open only a couple of days, and was really impressed with the service. 

What's great about the layout is how open and airy it feels and how they've really designed the space to allow for gathering with your friends (and watching a game) without feeling like your going to be rundown or having to stay at the bar. 

Definitely one of my new fav spots.

I am a big WOB fan. It was my go to place once I turned 21 in college and was no longer only able to go to 18+ disgusting college bars around UCF. The facility is kept clean and the staff is very friendly and attentive. The bar does get PACKED on college night (Wednesday nights) when they have a half off list on certain drafts. I use to love college night bc of the great deals, but standing up  the entire evening and sweating like a pig is no longer very enjoyable to me. If you get there early enough you can snag a seat, but they do leave the entire place open at night so it still gets very hot. I recommend coming any other day/night  than Wednesday (unless you enjoy the overly crowded type of environment). I also recommend coming here to watch games. It will get a little crowded for game, but nothing too bad. Just get there early and you will be able to find a seat. I also recommend joing the WOB club. You get a point for every new beer you try. It is a fun way to get you to explore different types of beers and you can also win prizes for hitting certain "milestone".

I took the After Effects training and thought it was really great! It was definitely geared more toward people that are completely foreign to AE and really need to learn the basics, but all-in-all two thumbs up. You had the option to use Mac or Windows platform and the instructor walked you through every lesson. It was 3 days long and I feel that was the perfect amount of time for something this caliber. I would definitely recommend this training to someone who is interested in starting from scratch with graphics and special effects.

I love Honey Bubble. The tea is delicious-- admittedly, a bit sweet at times, so ask for VERY light honey (I get 2 pumps) unless you want a very dessert-y tea. I've never tried the gelato, because I always think it looks a bit freezer burnt, but I've had the macarons from Alon's which are delicious. The space itself is cleverly designed, and the staff is mostly friendly. I love that they're open relatively late.

I do think it's a bit pricey for bubble tea-- at $5 for a large, I can't justify going as often as I'd like. And parking can be a nightmare, depending on the time-- they have the spaces slanted, which means if you pull in on a crowded night you're going to have a hell of a time backing out, especially with crazy Ponce traffic.

A side note-- I think it's a little tacky that the owner (or at least, SOMEONE with a Honey Bubble sticker on their car) parks in the tiny front parking lot. It's already super tiny-- why not reserve those spots for customers? I also wish they were able to give out samples of the more unique teas. I'd love to try some, but since they've plastered "NO REFUNDS ONCE YOU'VE TAKEN A SIP" everywhere, I'm worried I'll be stuck with something terrible. I get the need for those signs, really, I just wish there was some way to try a few things out.

Despite all those negatives, however, they're still my favorite (and only) bubble tea spot.

I am so sick of hearing about Brian D.'s picky pizza eating experience. Who loses a star just for being cut in squares? Just ask for it in pie cut! Just sayin'. Anyways...

I love coming to Terita's. The pizza is great! Sometimes the cooking is a little inconsistent. For example, we ordered on a Monday night and had a very crispy bottom with a centimeter of crispy edges, and then the next night the pizza was more flimsy and didn't have much crisp. Many people I'm sure would complain about darker edges, but I loved it that was so I was a little disappointed that it didn't turn out that way the second time around. The dough is thin with a slight airy thickness, a good quality sauce, and thin, greasy pepperonis that curl up and have some spice to them. The cheese is a good quality, but isn't a strong flavor. We also ordered garlic bread with cheese, and that was good too. It has plenty of cheese and plenty of garlic butter. 

My only issue is that you are required to bring your coupon in. Unfortunately, my printer is out of ink, so I couldn't print out the coupon and they require you to physically bring in the coupon to get the $1.25 off, even if you mention it on the phone.  This situation makes me slightly irritated because the area I live in has at least 15 other pizza shops that are super close, but yet I am driving 20 minutes to pick up my pizza at Terita's, and the least they could do is to make it easiest on the customer so that way they are likely to order again, because I'm not sure when I'll be getting ink, since I don't print often. If I know Terita's is less likely to accommodate me for my coupon, I'm more inclined to order from someplace that I don't have to hassle with physically bringing a coupon.

Decided to order the chicken and waffles and it was so bizarre. The flavors did not seem to mesh well at all. I still like sway a lot don't get me wrong but whoa man I was confused eating this. It had too much going on. The matcha waffle and matcha butter was a no for me and I Adore matcha. The chicken was good by itself. Not sure why there was a salad in the first place but that was also good by itself...not on top of my waffle. And what was also confusing is because the waitress said this was the new and improved recipe? Maybe third times the charm. Still go! Just order something else

One of the perks of where I work is that I'm entitled to a massage once a month with a small copay through my insurance. It's odd for me because prior to living up here in Portland, I could count how many times on one hand I had ever had a professional massage. 

I've been coming to Zen Space for a number of months now on a recommendation from a woman I work with. I prefer deep tissue massage but have had a Chinese style that one of the massage therapists does. It helps because I'm pretty active between riding my bike everywhere and working out at the gym, besides the fact that my job keeps me bouncing around all the time.

The place is great on communication and readily lets you know by email if spots become available. I've gone between two of the masseuses but one recently left and hopefully someone that does deep tissue will be on staff soon. 

On one of the last times I was there, a manager mentioned that they do cupping there and it was something that I knew very little about. Well, they gave me a complimentary 10 minute demo on my back about it. It was different. Other than the marks it left on me for over a week, I'm not sure that it is something that I need currently. But I was glad to have experienced it.

The atmosphere is great and the staff is quite friendly. And I always look forward to getting my monthly massage!

Enjoy.

A lot of people will quickly crap all over this place.  "Ohhh its a chain, ohhh its in the Landmark center, ohhh I was not hugged enough as a child".  Seriously, this place is fantastic and I will guide you through the process as I have eaten at the LH S-house dozens of time. I mean really, I practically paid the electric bill for a couple of years with my patronage.
First, sit in the bar.  The atmosphere is better and the service is better, too.  The people behind the bar are quite competent.  
Second, the wine list is decent and they have plenty of beers, but I highly recommend the margarita list.  LH serves their margs in lame plastic shakers so you can "pour your own".  It seems stupid at first, until you realize that that 1 margarita really = about 2.5.  That = yay in my book.  Get the Perfect Margarita, it is all top shelf stuff, with a twist of orange.
Make sure you ask for bread.  They serve fresh, hot whole wheat loafs with some whipped butter = 2X yay.  
Third, don't order any appetizers, as they all come off of the Sysco food service truck.    
Longhorn, now owned by Darden, was part of the Rare Hospitality Group, which owns the Capital Grille, etc. Hint, hint, order steak at the Longhorn.  These guys know how to broil steak and grill fish, that's it.  Fourth. my suggestion: go right to the steaks.  I get the Flo's filet, 7oz. with blue cheese melted on top, side of either brandied apples or grilled asparagus (get the asparagus in warm weather).  Ask for a side of horseradish, too.  By now, you will be in heaven... the effect of the margarita is kicking in, the steak and blue cheese are melding together and the grilled asparagus are topping things off just right.  
Fifth, if you have the cojones, huevos, etc, order the Chocolate Stampede for desert.  It is delicious, but you need at least two people to eat it.
Longhorn is in the Landmark Center and is great for Red Sox pre-game, pre- and post-movie at the AMC, parents weekend, or just a night out to get a high quality steak at a very decent price.

okay so when KK came to Oregon I couldnt understand why everyone was all atwitter over glazed doughnuts. Then I was dragged to the store right after they finished a batch. I was first impressed that you got to see how they were made. Then I was handed a hot..... I do mean hot out of the oil doughnut.... I took a bite..... I swear... my eyes got 10 times bigger and became all pupil. My heart may have grown 3 sizes and I was hooked on the sugary crack puffed air that was in my hand. I did not know how I  HAVE LIVED BEFORE THIS DOUGHNUT. and was saddened when it was gone. I am positive it is coated in and baked with a special kind of crack. Seriously my gods this was heaven.... I ate a bit of heaven..... then I proceeded to run in circles for hours. I may have been banished from several friends houses since I couldnt stay still or anything. The sugar had hit me and I was an instantly on the ceiling. 

I now only go here once or twice a year as my body can only handle that kind of onslaught that much. 

I have tried their other treats that they have and while they are okay.... nothing to write home about or make me turn into a kitten on crack.

Got to Austin, besides a little research on the internet, did not know much about it, except it was in Central Texas. Called Apartment Experts, something my wife found on the internet. I told her I would call them, got lucky as it was a Sunday and someone picked up. Just so happened a fellow by the name of Nick was in. Told him i was looking for an apartment in the Austin area. Nick said he would be glad to help me find an apartment and there was no fee. I replied, it must  be hard to make money like that. Good news for me. Nick said he was independently wealthy (lol). Anyways after talking for a few. I knew he knew the area and thought ok if you're willing to show me around and help me find a place, why not? We agreed to meet early Monday morning. Yes Nick was there and had some layouts of available apartments. He was even connected to each complex. He knew what was available and the rental price. It really help narrow down the options. I told him when I liked something and he made a note. Nick then said let's  go. Before I knew it we were looking at apartments. I have to admit the places he took me were very nice. We went to a total of 
4 places. Nick never pushed me. He was always saying, i want you to get the place you like. When I didn't like a place (and it was only one) and just gave him a look like, no. We were promptly moving on to another place.

To make a long story short, Nick really helped me find a place I'm very happy with. He was professional, kind. and not pushy or harsh! If you are looking for an apartment in the Austin area, do yourself a favor! Call Nick first @ Apartment Experts. You won't regret it. Plus there's no fee. Really no fee.
Good luck with your new apartment!!

Oh biif I sound like a spokesmen for them (lol) i'm not. Just really appreciate it Nick! Thanks love the place you helped me find!!!

I've visited a good number of game bars in other cities and play games all the time. With that competition in mind, I still really liked this place. One of the things that you'll either love or hate here is that you play a $5 cover to enter and play as many games as you like. For me, I like that--it made me feel like I wasn't obligated to buy a drink. Usually I want a drink anyways, but I have friends who don't drink and don't know what to do at board game bars that get by on drink orders alone.

The game library here was big, probably not as big as some of the places I've seen in Seattle and Vancouver, but helpfully coded and easy to navigate. The bartenders also were helpful with starting instructions if needed.

One thing I will give them major credit for is that we started out at a large table with another group on half of it. That group left, so it was just the two of us at an 8-top. They needed the table for a big group and asked us if we could move to a 2-top. No problem at all, but on top of that--they comped us a free dessert, which ended up being a tasty bread pudding.

The only reason why I'm knocking them down from 5 stars is because my cocktail didn't really seem to be a cocktail. I ordered the elder sage. As I watched the bartender make it, he didn't seem to be doing much of anything...and then sure enough, I ended up with what seemed to be whiskey on the rocks. I like whiskey, but please don't call that a cocktail.

The alcoholic slushies are the big draw here, but I wanted something more authentic and Rose Cotes de Provence fit the bill. The price ($9) is a bit high for three ounces (if that) of inexpensive-moderately priced wine, and while I understand plastic glasses, a more conventional wine glass shape would have been ideal.

Regardless, there's a good assortment of drinks. If I was going to get a slushie, I would probably prefer the Rosé slushie at the Fleur de Lys kiosk, but it's only here during the Flower and Garden Festival.

Service is absolutely friendly. 

I have no idea why people bag on the French pavilion cast members. It's like they decided the stereotype was the truth, but my server was as friendly here as anywhere else.

I haven't been to this location since it opened up and it was so awesome to go to!

I really love how accessible everything is downtown and it isn't too far from my office. Instead of boozy brunch we decided to take the new guy here.  

The restaurant sits on the corner of some prime people watching. If anyone knows me, they know I love to people watch. The bar area is huge and this is one of the nicest Torchys locations I have been too. The chairs are comfy, the walls look clean and the staff is friendly. That's all I pretty much ask for really :) 

I ordered a Baja shrimp and friend avocado taco. I could have done without the beans on the avocado taco, but nothing I can do about that really. I opted for both on a flour tortilla since I know the corn tortillas and be quite flimsy, so they double wrap. I maybe saved a few carbs. 

Either way I will be definitely coming back to this location:)

Stopped in for a GREAT brunch when Broder had too long a line. Detour had no wait and a very nice outdoor patio. The staff was friendly and service was prompt as well.

Grab your own bottomless coffee. Everything on the menu sounded delicious, and build-your-own frittata or potato skillet make for basically unlimited combinations. My friend and I tried the frittata and an egg sandwich. The focaccia on the sandwich was very soft and fresh. The cardamom bread toast was good as well. Nice presentation and good sized portions for a very reasonable price! 

I also ordered a bloody mary...a drink I'm exceptionally leery of, and their take on it was delicious! Very spicy, good consistency. I rarely like a bloody mary, and even when I do I usually get bored after a few sips and regret the purchase as I'm forced to finish the rest of the glass. However, this one kept me interested until the last drop. I don't drink enough to claim it is the best in Portland, but it is good enough to get someone who usually doesn't even like bloody maries to consider ordering a second!

I would definitely come back to try more things on their menu.

My fiance and I just moved to the Southwest area, and we ran across this place in search of a good meal after a day of lawn work. I ordered a Jackfruit smoothie, and it was quite delicious. There were real chunks of jackfruit in the smoothie and did not taste like they added too much sugar.

We had the spring rolls to start, and they were very good. I could eat a few orders of these as a meal. The lettuce served with the rolls was a little on the older/thinner side, but this did not seem to detract from the taste at all.

I had some Pho, and I found it very good and authentic. The jalapenos given on the side were so potent that just putting 3 of them into the soup made the soup nice and spicy. The flank and meatballs in the soup were good quality meat and did not have any chunks of fat in the meat. Probably one of the best steak meats I have had in pho ever.

My fiance had some pad thai dish, and it was just as good as any other place we've been to. She orders the same exact dish at ever thai place so she's become somewhat of an expert on this dish. She liked the sauce, but there wasn't quite enough of it for the dish. Doubling the sauce put into this dish should solve the issues with this, and we will definitely ask for this next time.

All in all, I'm glad we found a good place near home, and we will definitely be visiting again. I've read some other readers reviews, and it really seems like the menu is hit and miss. There are quite a few different things on the menu, and I think it may benefit them to either cut things out of the menu or work to improve the dishes which are not up to par. I have a feeling there are more gems in their menu, and I intend to find them. We didn't try to ask the waitress for recommendations,  but this could be a good course of action for future visits.

We went here for a late lunch and had the onion soup, and shared the turkey/cranberry sandwich and the bleu cheeseburger. All of the food was delicious :) We were seated outside, underneath one of the warm heat lamps. At 3:30 in the afternoon, it was not crowded, so we got seated right away. I didn't get a good look of the place inside (but from the quick glance I got it was spacious, dark wood, dim lighting, and big bar).  The food was brought out in a timely manner. The service was good (just good). 

Overall, I think it's a nice place to grab a bite to eat, relax, and it's worth the price.

Bon appétit !!

Typically great, A+ service.  Staff is friendly, and always helpful.  Also very efficient as well - however, during my last visit, it was a bit "too" efficient.  That is, the last car shop before I brought it to VW Medford screwed up my tire installation (causing rough vibrations during the drive) so I brought it here (as I felt more at ease for them to fix things up) stating my issue, and believing one of the tires was improperly balanced.  I told them to please do what they can, until the problem was resolved.  It was a busy Saturday, so I think they wanted to get to the root of the problem ASAP - so they balanced it, and said it was fixed.  Got it back, and indeed, they did a good job balancing the one wheel under my suggestion, allowing for a smoother ride.  Unfortunately, it wasn't completely fixed.  My car still vibrates slightly once I go above 65mph or so - indicating there's still a slightly issue somewhere.  Still debating if this is something I want these folks to dig more into or to just let it ride out.  Overall, a good place to bring your car.

This little market is awesome ! 
The sandwiches are old school and awesome !
The people behind the deli were great! The fact they recognized I was from Oklahoma and engaged to make sure my experience was one To remember instilled  my believe in simple courtesy of the human spirit! I ordered Italian sub and ate only half of it on small table outside the market. It was fresh and incredible! What made it more than a sandwich was the fact the people who made it interacted verbally and made it an experience! I think I paid $10 for the Italian sub and could only eat half of it!
What's even better is the other items you can purchase . I purchased different chocolates and candies that my kids loved! I wished I would have purchased different olive oils and basalmics that I could have had shipped to Oklahoma .
I go to Boston every year and I look forward to go back here out of any other place in Boston

Great place tucked away in an ugly strip mall. We sat at the bar and were greeted right away.  We ordered kale salads with salmon. The salads were delicious but the salmon was so small my friend asked the bartender if it was a mistake . It was an $8 add on and was no bigger than two bites. She went back to the kitchen and got more but if that was the intended portion it was  embarrassingly small. I wouldn't have had the guts to ask but I hope this was a mistake . Everything else was great  I would try this place again when I'm back in Marblehead.

Went for the Weekend Buffet. The item count is a little less than some other Indian buffets, but they make up for it in Quality.
