Overall, I wish the curries had a little more spice, but perhaps they'd watered it down to make it palatable for a larger demographic. The Service was friendly, fast and helpful  : 

Let me preface everything by saying - If you want good Mango Lassi, go here, Best in Austin ! 

1. Naan (Bread) : Standard Fare. A little too crispy for my liking, but otherwise ok.
2. Papad : Not the one with the peppercorns (Which has more Zing), but these were cooked in oil ! Which is Good ! Most other places microwave it, which reduces the crispiness.
3. Idli : Below average, too soft and mushy, ideally, should be dry and airy.
4. Vada : A little Small and thin , but the taste was ok.
5. Puri : Below Average, it was just too hard, possibly from sitting too long on the little  burner, not sure.
6. Chana Masala : Good, decent amount of spice, could've used a little more.
7. Mixed Veg. Curry : Better than most Indian buffets which make this curry into a cream-fest.
8. Palak Paneer : Same comment as the Mixed Veg. Decidedly better than the average Indian buffet, could've used a touch more seasoning though.
9. Dal Curry : Average. A little too lacking in spice for my taste.
10. White Rice : Standard Far.
11. Dum Chicken Biryani : This was the highlight of the buffet. Well Seasoned, Tender chicken, really good !
12. Chicken Curry : Same issue as with the other curries - low on spice, but the chicken was well cooked and tender.
13. Fish Curry : I dont eat seafood, so this will have to go unreviewed ! :)
14. French/Green Bean Dish : Another one which was hit out of the park. You dont normally find this in Indian buffets, it's a dry dish made using french beans which have been sliced, and cooked with some spices and coconut, REALLY good.
15. Chaat : Another item you dont normally see in the weekend buffets, the Chaat table had the Papri Chaat and the Pani Puri. The little Chili+Garlic dish that went into the papri chaat was an original !
16. Sambar : Ok.
17. Desserts: The desserts consisted of Shahi Tukda (Crustless Bread, Fried and Soaked in Custard), which was different and good. The second dessert was Dudhi Halwa - like the Carrot Halwa made from Grated Bottle Gourd. It was as it should be - sinful and tasty !

The Lunch Buffet also comes with a Masala Dosa,  The Dosa suffered from the same fate of the idli - just not cooked enough, needed to be done just another minute more, and the masala was watered down as well.

Overall, I'd go again, because the Chaat, Desserts, Biryani and Lassi are not only different from the standard buffet fare, they're worth the trip.

I think Cosecha gets a bad wrap for being pricey compared to other taco places, but the bottom line is I'm willing to pay more for higher quality, more creative food, and I think Cosecha meets that bill.  The shrimp taco is my favorite dish and worth every penny.  The vegetable enchilada and octopus are also good, and the caramelized sweet potato is rich and wonderful (recommend splitting this with a friend).  I also enjoyed the vegetable enchilada (the sauce is great).  Yes you have to pay for chips and salsa, but the chips are hands down better than any of the free-chip places.  I am not normally a queso person, but I really enjoy their queso topped with pickled veg.  The service I've had sitting at the bar has been top notch, and the Monastrell red by the glass is delightful.

Yum Yum Thai will always have a special place in my heart. My first introduction to Thai food was at this place and I've been addicted ever since. No, it's  not the fanciest of places, but the great customer service and excellent food make up for any lack in the aesthetic department. The owners are warm and welcoming and they always take good care of me. They make some of the best sweet tea I've ever tasted! I usually order the spicy basil, panang curry or pad Thai when I come. You can add a variety meats to the dishes. The flavors in each dish are outstanding and everything is made from scratch. Their spring rolls are a little bite of heaven! They're light and filled with veggies. Other notables are the coconut soup and pot stickers. 

Yes, they're plenty of Thai restaurants out there, but this one is special. The prices are extremely reasonable as well.

I am super picky about nail places after having lived in Asia, where excellent, cheap manicures + pedicures are everywhere. Nu Nails is definitely solid. Very clean, very good attention to detail, did my cuticles without causing me to wince once, nail painting was impeccable.

Atmosphere is standard, a bit gloomy because of basement location.

They really prefer to be paid in cash.

Overall, good but still a bit pricey to be my staple place (I think it was $50 for regular main-pedi).

I am from Hawaii and Asian (Filipino).  When I came to this place makes me feel like home with Asian people all around me in Austin's Chinatown.

This place seems very popular.  They have the Vietnamese sandwich, regular sandwich, croissants, pastries,spring rolls, plate lunch, bun, coffee, tea and smoothies.  I got a special banh mi with pate, raw meat, and meat.  My sister got the BBQ pork. We shared the fresh summer roll with pork and shrimp.  We both got iced coffee.  

Overall this place was not bad and tasted pretty good.

So, here's a list of things that DIDN'T happen at Tamale House in all the times I have been there.

I DIDN'T order anything but breakfast tacos, as I could probably eat breakfast tacos for every single meal.

I DIDN'T pull up and think, "Man, this place looks Classy!  I hope I brought enough money to tip the Maitre 'D!"

I DIDN'T have to wait very long at all for some tasty sausage egg and cheese breakfast tacos.

I DIDN'T taste the home made salsa and think, "Yawn, these are boring."  The HOT salsa can only amount to the oral version of the chemical burn Jack gets from Tyler in Fight Club.

I DIDN'T use my debit card here, as they only take cash.  They run this joint like Rusty runs his life.  "When you're dealing in cash, you don't need a fence."  "Some people lack vision." "Probably everybody in Cell Block E."
But not the dudes at the Tamale House, no sir.

The guy who owns and runs the place, who looks a little like a short, Cuban Rod Steiger in a guybera, DIDN'T say to me, "Hey! Jefe! Good to see you neighbor! I'm so glad that you came by my shop, since you and I live right across the street from each other!  Let me get you some free grub amigo, it's wonderful that you are here!"  I do live across the street from that dude, you'd think he would know that.  I am Yelp Elite, after all ;)

I DIDN'T pay an arm and a leg for great chow.  They have $.85 breakfast tacos.  REALLY?  I can get 4 tacos for the price of a gallon of gas?  Between the eggs and the super hot salsa, I may just convert my house to run on methane like BarterTown from "Thunderdome" and be done with energy bills all together.  "Who runs BarterTown?!?!"

I DIDN'T just give y'all too much information whilst making great pop culture movie references.  

Actually, I DID do one of those things, can you figure out which one?

My fiance could talk about the duck FOR DAYS.  DAYS.  It was fall of the bone tender, obviously a labour of patience and love.  Confit, after all, takes time.

The escargots were lush with garlic and buttery flavour, that soaked deeply into the thin crisps accompanying.

I had the beef hache, which I learned is raw steak meat, minced and molded into what is essentially a patty of beef tartare.  

Overall we had an really good experience.  I had always heard about long waits and having to make reservations, so the fact that we got in without any on a Friday night (although it was about 9:30 pm already) was a huge plus!

My friend and I stopped in Biltong Bar after a day of eating and drinking and wanted something small to munch on before calling it a day. 

First of all, the ambiance is fantastic. It may be small, but it's so cosy. Shelves upon shelves of liquor bottles set against the windows, a few tables and comfy chairs. 

My friend and I split the Biltong and Cheese board, which was a perfect amount of food. I will say that the Biltong comes with a spice mix dusted on it - if you get a piece without much seasoning, it doesn't really taste like anything. The traditional seasoning tastes kind of citrusy, which was unexpected yet tasty. The cheese was soooooooo good - I love Manchego, and the locally made Brie was spot on! We also both had the Genepy Tonic to drink, which was refreshing and delicious! 

The service was on point and I can't wait to go back and try some more delicious food and libations here!

On the hottest of Boston days, when you are sweaty, your feet hurt, and you are done elbowing your way through the throngs of people on Newbury Street, find yourself a seat on the patio at Cactus Club.  Take a look at all their froofy colored and flavored margaritas on their menu, and pick the most ridiculous one.  Go ahead, it's ok, everyone else is drinking pink and blue drinks too!   Order it frozen.  I know what you're thinking, but just do it.  Then wait.  When it comes out to you and you see the outside of the glass turning white and frosty because what's inside is so cold, you will know you made the right choice by listening to me.  One sip of the funny colored and perfectly blended margarita will cool you down completely.  You'll sink back a little in your chair, and life will be good again.

I've been taking both of my Toyotas to Yost II for about a year now.  The mechanics have been friendly and honest.  Their prices have been better than what I was paying at Rising Sun.  Now, I haven't done anything particularly difficult.  It's mostly been maintenance and inspections.  I've been pleased.
Make a reservation.  You can't just show up.
Full disclosure:  Mike Yost used to be my neighbor in the early/mid 90's when he was still a shade tree mechanic.  While I picked Yost Auto because I knew if worst came to worst, I'd call Mike and give him an earful, I have not come close to being disappointed.

This location is not as crazy busy or packed as the Pacific Centre or Metrotown location which I greatly appreciate. Don't need to fight to get through the aisles or extend my arm between bodies to try to grab a little product from the shelf to test. 
The staff here are friendly but are not overly up in your business about trying to help you or give you advice when you are browsing the different shelves. Store is well maintained, organized and clean and are usually well stocked except when they have special events where you are lucky they even have products on the shelves.

I'm upgrading to "Yay! I'm a fan" and I'm adding a star to my first review.

Since my original visit I've returned a few more times. 

On my next visit I once again ordered the Denial and once again I enjoyed it.  I also seriously enjoyed the BFK they serve from their "Drank" menu.  (Tip, when ordering make sure to indicate if you would like it hot or iced, if you don't you can sit back and enjoy the surprise, either way it will taste great and be strong!)

For the most recent visit I ordered something from their special menu, Spinach, Jack and Bacon Scramble served with Potatoes and Toast, I opted to spend an extra 50 cents.  OMG the Biscuit deserved it's own table, it was not only the largest Biscuit I've personally seen, it was a very good biscuit.  

The prices are certainly reasonable and the staff is always nice and friendly. The music is loud and the decor is fun and surprising.  

Make sure you check out the message on the Shirts and Underwear they sell, wink, wink.

Somewhat under the radar on the pizza landscape, but House Pizzeria is a little jewel on Airport with a diverse menu and chill vibe.  

As self-proclaimed pizza junkies, my friend and I polished off one pie each.  This is one of the only significant drawbacks of House Pizzeria: the pies are smaller than your standard pizzeria, frustratingly teetering between too much for one person and not enough for two.  The special (The Subterranean) was unique blend of potato, fontina cheese, fresh basil, mushrooms, and plenty of carmelized onion that gave the pizza a distinctly sweet flavor.  Though not a traditional offering, it was flavorful, even if a little overpoweringly sweet.

The pepperoni pizza was fairly straightforward, but it was saturated - literally dripping - in oil.  Holding up a slice to let the oil drip off may or may not be your thing, but it seemed a little excessive.

Though our two pizzas were fairly average, House merits four stars based on variables and potential.  They have some good beers on tap, the specials are great, and the place itself is relatively nice (great jukebox for indie fans, clean, mineral water served).  It's a solid value and it has a wide breadth of pizza types with the occasional special thrown in.  As some people have noted, they employ a more doughy approach to the crust, but it's nothing particularly detrimental to the food.  A nice addition to the Austin pizza scene.

The Boyfriend and I stopped by this afternoon because we had a coupon for $15 off a dinner! All of the waiters and managers and chefs were extremely attentive to make sure we had everything we needed. (A bit crowding, at least two different people asked if my meal was alright before I took a bite, but we were there pretty early and they were not too busy.) We were gifted a small sample of the Pasta BRAVO! because it was our first visit here - and it was super delicious! I probably enjoyed it more than my meal, which was the Baked Chicken Parmesan. I felt bad because I love cheese, but the cheese grater was sort of slow and I didn't want her grating cheese for forever. :( I ended up taking 3/4 of my meal home though, it was very good but just alright. The Boyfriend said the Chicken Marsala was just alright. We felt that the prices were a little bit high for the food, but with the coupon it was worthwhile.

I can't believe I've lived here for so long and only just tried this place.  When we were first seated they brought out some big corn nuts.  You use a thin wooden spoon to dip them in the spicy and oh so tasty dipping sauce.  

I had the grilled steak (Churrasco) which was good if a bit bland.  The salad that came with it was fresh & tasty.  I washed it down with one of their creamy strawberry milk shakes - YUM.  They have several other flavors including passion fruit & pineapple.  

My only complaint was the service was a bit slow considering there weren't a whole lot of people in the restaurant, but it was a nice introduction to Peruvian food for me.  I can't wait to go back and try some other dishes, especially the fish, and desert of course!

Lots of beatings, but people keep going back. We're talking M&S, not S&M, right?

I've been there (the restaurant) 6-7 times now and have never had a bad experience, in food quality or service. Tea refills and check service both quick as a whip. Generally I find the service to be above-average to excellent. The food's verged on great about half the time and disappointed once. Maybe I'm some kind of deviant, but this place is in my "good, reliable" crowd.

I'm pretty tied to the "under $10" section for lunch, but appetizers and desserts still creep in. They don't flog the extras, we just find them good enough to order on our own. Some items are extremely rich, so you're only hurting yourself if you try to finish the seafood mac & cheese or Kobe burger in one sitting -- punishment for gluttons, you could say.

I haven't had a bad mussell experience or poor service, so have to say I'm bound to go back.

Went here with a group for their Sunday brunch. It was a bit of a wait because this place has become awfully popular (what place that serves brunch in Austin isn't though?). Also, they don't seat a group until all members of the party have arrived and I am friends with latecomers. It was lovely weather and waiting on their front porch wasn't a problem at all.

We were seated at a large community outdoor table next to the dog playpen while there was live music. We were promptly waited on and given recommendations for drinks and food. Our order was slightly messed up when it came out (or rather some people's order was forgotten about) - however the manager came around without us ever having to complain and comped those orders and gave them free drinks.

Overall it was a great experience and I think we will be back for dinner or drinks!

Dinner here last night-YELP comments about the wings sold us on trying and we were going to take in a band at the Tilly down the street so this was an easy place to go to.

Atmosphere-definite family style-lodge look with both booths and open seating tables for big groups.  Se scored a two top right by the fireplace which was nice on a chilly evening, upstairs in the dining area.  Theres a "Den" downstairs at the front door.  No carpeting and a large room accents the noise...you wouldn't call this intimate dining.

Our servers (plural) were very efficient-the main waitress actually asked the bartender what single malt they poured for me, when none of the bourbons I requested were available..so I have to say the bar is not well stocked...but it is a blew pub so I guess I should be happy they had anything.

Appetizer of chicken wings came out very fast, but 8 wings for $10 and change seemed a bit steep.  They were, however, quite tasty but not stupendous.  I'll go back for a to go order only because the only other option out here is BW3.  FOTM still rules in the River City for wings.

A nicely sized side salad for $3. was a surprise but the bleu cheese dressing was fairly tasteless.  From a bottle perhaps, if it's house made, they need to be a little more generous with the cheese.

My date and I split a plate of baby back ribs with mac and cole slaw and fries and that was a good thing because it was a huge serving.  The ribs were excellent with a tasty sauce on them.  Fall of the bone tender.  This got the 4th star for what would have been a 3 star review.

The small portions of mac salad and coleslaw were perfectly sized, a good crunchy tangy aside to the  fairly sweet BBQ sauce.  Fries were large but seemed to be frozen french fries from Sysco.  

Neither of us had the beer so no comments on that.

Attentive waitstaff for a busy Saturday night.  

We'll probably go back again-the menu had a lot of standard American meals-Meat Loaf, Salmon, etc but the only vegetarian option was the ever present gardenburger and a hummus and veggie plate for lunch.  This isn't a vegetarians place at all.  Since I'm a 99% vegetarian, I'll take my i% with great ribs thank you.

I visited this "Korean" restaurant one evening when I was in town, wondering where any Korean food was located in town.  And I found this one!  I had the pork bulgogi, which was on par!  It came with the usual side dishes, Kimchee, pickled radish, and bean sprouts.  I also had the fried pork dumplings, and they were amazing too!  I was sad to know that they only made it with pork, and not with beef.  I was very satisfied with the dish, and will go back when I'm in town again.  The Miso soup was good too.  This is not the best place that I have been to, but for the northeast, this is only the second Korean restaurant that I have had the pleasure of sampling.  

I have lived in Korea, and I have experienced amazing food there, to include here in America too.  One of my favorite places that I have been, was in Valpraiso, FL, and the restaurant is called Suns Korean Restaurant.  I should post a review for them one day soon.  Another few others close by to that restaurant in Fort Walton Beach are called Korea House and Okki Dokki.  Simply the best Korean Restaurants that I've ever experienced stateside!  If you haven't tried those places yet, you must!  If I could give them 10 stars, I would!

Two words you only need to know, ham bao. And another two, bola bola. 

I've tried the restaurant. It's a standard Chinese restaurant. I don't think I need to elaborate "standard". It's as standard as they come. But for the sake of those who want to ask exactly what I had, I had century egg or preserved duck egg congee with chinese donuts. If you haven't tried it, then I suggest you do before you die. Who knows, it might be your soul food, in comparable to having a soul mate. They're non-existent, as far as my loveless life is concerned, but I'm sure soul food exists. I think the south has already proved, otherwise. 

Back to the ham baos. When I turned 19, I turned to Canada. There's a lot to explore in Vancouver than overstimulating your normal 19 year old overactive alky junkie appetite. There's lansones and rambutan which I try to courageously smuggle into the US but decides to inhale everything by the time I get to the border, and there's the ham bao. Here's how good the ham bao is, no one in Seattle can top it. I'm talking circa 2002 here, cos I moved to San Diego after and I'm sure every Chinese or Filipino bakery have sought every possible way to get New Town's secret ingredient since then. Everyone's neighbor's mum would ask if I can get them 10 dozens each. That's the downside of telling everyone you're going to Canada, but the border patrols are used to it by now.

My friend and I decided to try this place out at part of Dine out. I have heard good things and the menu looked good, so we went. 

The restaurant is quaint with a cool story behind the name, ask the waiters! Food was pretty good. Meat is cooked perfectly but my fries were overdone and too salty. Overall, the vibe was cool and it was a nice place to have dinner with a close friend!

I definitely want to come back for brunch!

I came here last week with my family and even though the restaurant was packed we were seated within 5 minutes. The prices are a bit high, around $15-17 a plate but the portions are MASSIVE. Definitely worth what you pay for! I got the salmon omelette and it was absolutely delicious. My dad got the chicken and waffles and hated it, there was way too much garnish on his plate and once you got past all of it, the chicken was all breading and no meat. I will say my sister has been there before and raved about the chicken and waffles so maybe he just got a bad plate?

I liked it but didn't love it. I tend to eat on the healthier size so thousands of calories per plate aren't really my style but if you're down for some good ole southern breakfast with huge portions this is the place to go!

I would give this place a solid 3.5-4 stars (so I went higher for this review). Honestly I was impressed with the decor and the level of cleanliness that exists within this place. I felt like I was at a posh spa. 

I got a gel manicure and deluxe pedicure. The pedicure was awesome and relaxing. I did feel a bit rushed during my manicure as the lady doing my manicure had someone who decided she was going to wait for her specifically. I can't fault her for that. 

The only thing I would change is the way the gel selection is set up. The color is a LOT different than what is presented on the bottle. I wanted something very neutral but I got something very light. Definitely not something I would pick on my own. I would like to see some type of sample wheel many other places have.

We came here as part of my birthday celebration. We bought the Groupon for the petting zoo and t was awesome! There were so many animals to pet and the feed wasn't bad (we spent $10 for a large bag and it lasted two of us for the whole time). Our tour guide, Chris, was lovely! She did a great job explaining all of the animals. 

To get to the petting zoo area you have to take a hay ride type vehicle. My only complaint was the process to get onto that and how infrequently it came around. There was no order and it was hard to tell who got there first. Being a group of adults, we let the families go when it looked like it was getting full and waited for the next one. 

Overall, it was a great experience!

I love this place. Every time I have come in, we sit at the bar for a few hours and have some drinks. The atmosphere is TV Cheers esque with dark wood wrap around bar, tables and high tops, tvs lining the walls with the local news on and a wide range of regulars. THAT'S what gives this place charm. I like coming in here and feeling like I am at a local hangout. It is very clean and they always have great food and drink specials.

Friendly environment, but one thing that stood out was the music. I know, kinda odd, but hear me out. I was singing along to every song they played (minus a Irish song I didn't understand)....and I was sober! It just showed me how comfortable of an environment this was. I felt friendly, wanted to meet the people around me and overall comfortable. As far as the food goes, the hamburger I ordered was the egg burger and was delicious. Nothing to run home about but it was good. However, according to my friend who ordered the wings, they were the best wings he had in his life. An exaggeration? I don't know, but they looked good. Great place to eat before going out, and after!

You can grab some pretty neat stuff here.  Two trips have netted me about 4-5 pieces of clothing with savings of ~80%.  Most of clothing is Large/XL so it can be tough finding stuff that fits.

No changing rooms, as others have said, but then again I've never bought pants from here.

I suggest that you have a very good understanding of brands (and their price points) before going here, it helps with the experience.  Many clothes I've seen are sold from Macy's.  Just saying, good luck finding a true diamond in the rough.

I'm not usually one to review hotels, but this hotel was a special case.
My family drove down to Orlando for a brief Christmas vacation. We checked in the night before Christmas eve and checked out Christmas Day.

Once we pulled up to the front of the hotel, we had so much trouble with parking. We had no idea where to go. The receptionist suggested we pull up in the back, since our room was closer that way. However, when we got to the back, that lot was filled with a Clemson bus, which I believe was staying there for their bowl game. My "suspicions" were affirmed when we saw all the Clemson banners and posters flying everywhere. Good thing I remembered to leave my FSU hoodie at home.

The atrium/lobby is HUGE. It is often used for conferences and conventions, as there are large conference rooms, auditoriums and ballrooms. There is a Starbucks located conveniently in the lobby, as well, but the prices charged have about a 25% premium over the usual Starbucks (the closest one is located about 1-2 miles away).

I believe this is noted in several other reviews, but if you pay the resort fee ($20 a night), you receive quite a few perks such as parking, TWO free water bottles (usually $3.25, I believe), free Wi-fi (good for up to six devices at one time), free shuttles to and from Disney parks and other amenities that will be listed out for you. Instead of paying for each item individually, it is a much better deal to pay the discounted flat amount.

Our room had 2 queen size beds, a couch (not sleepable), a mini-fridge, and a large TV (I can't recall the measurements, but it is more than enough). There are many available TV channels to watch. The beds are comfortable with plush comforters and pillows. There are many outlets for anyone charging their phones or tablets by the beds, which is a requirement for me.

Overall, my stay here was quite pleasant and conveniently located to many restaurant chains, International Drive and SeaWorld. I would highly recommend to any traveler with any group size!

This review is for their WAXING only.

This place is great. It's pretty cheap for the area (brow: $10, half legs: $25, Brazilian: $35.)  It's not fancy or anything, I usually leave still covered in wax and baby powder, but she always does a great job. She's super attentive, which I really appreciate because I hate spending money to get waxed and then having to finish the job at home myself. I also love the fact that I always make appointments the day of and they can always see me. 

I would definitely recommend this place to a friend.

Excellent lattes! My go to is an iced latte with almond milk and they make it to perfection: Not too milky, strong coffee flavor but not TOO strong or bitter. The overnight oats with peanut butter is amazing as are the yogurt parfaits. I also highly recommend the baguettes. All of the above sell out quickly so if you see them get them! Haven't had any of their other pastries or food so cannot comment on that but it all looks amazing! The only reason I am not giving them 5 stars is because it is expensive - my latte here costs more than Starbucks. I think they need to consider that if they want to remain "a go to" place. Also the seating can be awkward.

Came here because I saw that Boxer offers a more interesting vegetarian ramen then the average mushroom shio broth standard fare. 

The vegetarian comes with a coconut curry broth, I would say it's light on the curry. There's also a decent amount of black sesame seed paste which adds another layer of flavor. Was certainly delicious but seemed more easily possible to duplicate at home aside from the home made noodles!

My only issue is the poached egg which ended up breaking and kind of getting mixed in and lost in the soup. Why is it so hard to make a marinated egg??

I had a nice time at Bareburger.  My husband & I took our 6 year old granddaughter for dinner Sat. night because I wanted to check it out.  We arrived about 7:00 after finding a spot at a meter out back.  Our wait time was quoted as 25-30 minutes so we stood and waited while having a drink.  A booth opened up after about 20 minutes and a lovely booth it was.  Our server was very nice and efficient.  The kids' menu had nice selections, including a black bean burger.  My granddaughter chose the chicken strips, that come with carrots and apple slices, and one side (she chose fries) and drink (she chose the organic fruit punch).  My husband had the California burger and fries (they are fresh-cut!).  I had the Black Bean Vegan burger on a whole wheat bun with the fries.  It was very good.  I like that they also offer a quinoa burger.  They offer several milkshakes that sounded good (Hot Honey) but maybe next time.  It was a good meal, but it's not a place we will frequent because it is pricy.  The fact that they service all organic food is fantastic, though.  The menu is extensive.  Keep in mind that everything is extra.  The fries cost extra, and the dipping sauce, other than ketchup, is extra too.

I can only speak to the brunch, dessert, and coffee, but all are excellent.  The omelets are extremely fluffy, the coffee strong (in a good way), and the deserts are all to die for.  I love that all of their desserts are on display, making my selection even more heart-wrenching.  This place is not to be missed if you are a dessert-lover.  Nearly all of their tables are small, round 2-tops, making group meals a bit of a challenge.  The brunch and beverage prices are a bit high for what you get, but it's all very good and definitely worth it on occasion.

This is the second visit to this location. 

Both times we were seated quickly. Service has always been good. This last time Kyle was our server and he was just awesome. He was attentive, but not over bearing. Polite, thoughtful, and had impeccable timing. 

We ordered drinks, a frozen lime Cadillac Margarita for my husband JC and of course a frozen Bellini for myself.

We both went with the extra shot. For some reason this made my drink way way too sweet. JC mixed his drink with mine and the tartness of the lime did help but it still wasn't great. 

I love the Italian salad dressing they have ( I wish they bottled it and offered it for sale ) I really wanted a large mixed green salad with a side skewer if shrimp ( only 3.99! ) but the salad wasn't on the menu as an entree ( only as a starter )

I'm sure had I asked, they probably could of done it, but for once I didn't bother with my picky obscure ordering, and just went with the spaghetti with spicy meat sauce. Which was quite good. 

JC loved his Chicken Alfredo with Mushroom and Mascarpone Cheese Ravioli. He also raved about the ranch dressing on his salad.

As always, it also comes with sourdough bread, the salad, and Spinoni ice cream. 

Dinner for 2 was just under 54$ ( plus 10$ tip ) 
Thanks again Kyle - you were great, pushing it from a 3 to a 4 star because of your excellent service.

This place is so cozy! We arrived right as they opened, so we were a little disappointed with our service. She had us and one other table, but forgot our appetizer and only came to refill drinks once. Otherwise, the pizza was awesome! I wouldn't recommend anything with their "chipotle cream sauce" (as either a pizza base or on pasta). It was extremely spicy with too much (slightly burnt) garlic, so all I could taste was flaming burnt garlic. The caesar salad was also spicy, which I thought was a little weird. Stick to the pizza.

You have to try this place!

I went here with a couple of friends the other night, and I am so glad I did.  They only opened about a month ago, and I came here because my friends from Chicago happened have a TravelZoo deal from here.

We were greeted by one of the owners, and he was one of the friendliest people I've ever met.  We met Calvin later, who was also very nice.

I'm not sure how fusiony it is, but it doesn't matter because the food was really good. For appetizers we had:
- Duck rolls- basically a duck egg roll.  It was a little on the sweet side for me, but my party seemed to like it.
- Basil rolls- nice and fresh.  There was a slightly sour taste to it that was really good
- Calamari- this was ok- I liked that they had little bits of battered and friend onion in there too.
-  Cream of broccoli with truffle oil (on the house):  They gave us a little thank-you-for-trying-this-place soup.  The soup was not too greasy and the truffle oil was so yummy.

For dinner: 
- Green curry (with beef jerky)- not sure what this beef jerky thing was, but it was delicious.  It was nice soft on the side and chewy on the outside. The green curry was very well made and was my favorite thing there.  If only I could swim in their green curry with my mouth opened...
- Fried chicken with lobster mac:  Chicken breast was tender and well fried.  Lobster mac was ok.
- Crispy beef-  Yum.  You have to try this.  A little crispy on the outside and nice slightly sweet sauce.
- Thai meat meatloaf (not a typo):  Nice seasoning and served with mashed potatoes.  Very good.

For dessert- caramel Fuji apple crusted with Georgia Pecans.  Mmm.. Thinking about it makes me so happy.  The combination was phenomenal.  I don't really like desserts, but I could eat this thing a thousand times over.

The prices are not too terrible.  Entrees were about 12-14 bucks and appetizers were about 6-8.   No alcohol just yet since they just opened, but they are waiting on their license.  I'll definitely venture this way again, and hopefully, Poor Calvin will be Rich Calvin soon.

Burgoo is a pretty dang awesome place to stop by for comfort food. Nothing better to drop by here when you have a craving for warm food that just hits the spot. 

Setting and ambiance are almost perfect for what they're trying to convey. Love having booths to sit in and just relax. Lighting is dim but visible and makes it for a nice night out location. 

The beef bourguignon and biscuits are among my favourites. Their biscuits are so warm and filling. Always hot and toasty, and a delight to have with butter. The bourgnignon is great. The beef is prepared just right and the medley of veggies that come along with it make it a great meal to have on a cold night.

Can't go wrong with Burgoo in almost any situation. With food that always hits the spot and a great ambiance, it's has something for everyone.

The only reason why the place stays in business is because of the quality of the bagels.  They're great!  Unfortunately, the service isn't the same.  You'll wait quite a long time on a busy day to get to the front of the line.  I don't understand why the owners don't tell the employees to work faster instead of holding long conversations with one another while making orders.  I was quite disturbed one day when I went to use the restroom and noticed a few mouse traps.  Apparently they have mice problems.

JINYA is a wonderful addition to Thornton Park.  I have been here a couple times now.  Once for dinner on a weekend and the other for lunch on a weekday.  Both times I had a wonderful experience.

Service - B.  The place was busy both times I went.  Service was good, not exceptional.  Both visits I had to remind my servers about a couple things.  My first visit my party sat inside.  My second visit we sat outside on the patio to enjoy the beautiful weather. 

Food - A.  I have only been here twice so I haven't had the opportunity to try a variety of items.  My most recent visit I had the tonkatsu black, which is pork based.  It was full of flavor and the soft boiled egg was delicious. You can customize your ramen order; however, I went with one of their specialties.  My friend ordered the small California Poke Bowl.  It was huge!! It's officially on my list of items to try when I come back.

Another wonderful dining venue in Orlando that isn't going to break the bank.

Totally addicted to their BBQ Tofu quesadilla.  El Myr is a dive bar in the middle of one of the busiest parts of town for hipsters.  That comes with tight spaces (close to bathrooms), slow service (on the regular) and cheap beer.  Pros or cons?  Depends on the day. 

I love the place.  I can overlook the questionable service for that damn bbq sauce and a big, ass cold beer.  R. Land art is big BONUS!  I have never had a bad time in this joint.

We tried Masu sushi.  We being me and two of my kids.  I was more concerned that the place was going to be inappropriate for them (music too loud, too much swearing) than my kids causing issues for the restaurant.  So we walked in and up to the restaurant and it's a sleek trendy kind of place.  The music wasn't too bad volume-wise and this was on a Saturday night.  

We ordered a few lemonades, some nigiri, a Pearl Roll, a Death by Sushi, California Roll, some pork fried rice, some tempura shrimp, and some karrage.  I scandalized my kids by ordering some otoro (bluefin) as they've been brainwashed by places like Bamboo Sushi.  The food and sushi were very good, it was very relaxed, the music was less loud than some places (Bamboo Sushi), and we had a pretty good time.  My kids however, aren't very picky eaters and are pretty accustomed to having Japanese food.  Total food bill for the 3 of us, about $150 not including tip.  Pretty standard for sushi in Portland.  Only negative was finding parking downtown on a Saturday night.  That was not a whole lot of fun.

choke-cough-gasp-wheeze..... i can't believe we went in this place, but a few people in my group were smokers so the rest of us drunkenly agreed to stop in here. the cloud of cigar smoke was so extremely thick that it was worse than the foggiest day in san francisco. i survived though by drinking too much gin and partaking in a little tabacco myself.... end result, the next day my hair smelled like cigars and i had a voice like demi moore. just lovely.

First time trying it out and came here for breakfast. You order then find your own seating, so if there aren't any tables available, you'll just have to wait. I'm usually not a fan of biscuits but I wanted to try it out since a friend had recommended it. Gladly, they were delicious! I had a biscuit with bacon, egg, and cheese with a side of hash browns and friend had the reggie deluxe. Both were great and the biscuits itself were perfect in my opinion.

A+ service - and how often can you say *that? I brought in two watches for batteries. The 2 amusing men that waited on me whisked them away, had them changed on the spot and even updated the date on last day of February to the 31st so the next day would show up as March 1 - so I had to do absolutely nothing. Saved my mani. ;)

They didn't even charge! Might be their policy - not sure, as they made jokes of it. Some places get you for $20 and make you wait, sometimes days. 

Smart marketing as I will return and recommend.

Went on Sunday with some of my friends (we're all in our early 20s) and it was great! Events like this make me feel more connected to Portland and more cultured in terms of Oregon as a whole. A lot of my other newly-21 friends went on Saturday, so if you're not trying to mingle with that crowd, try Sunday! There were a good amount of people there but it certainly wasn't overwhelming. However, some of the more popular beers were out by then, but that only led to lots of cheers!

Went in around dinnertime on a Thursday. They were fairly busy and probably could have used just one more person working tables. The service was awesome but it was easy to see the server was stretched a little thin. 

The main reason I went was Portland Nacho Week. I have to say, the nachos were some of the best I've had in quite a long time. The balance of sweet and spicy was perfect. The toppings were plentiful and I did not feel at any time that I was paying too much. I know that nachos are not on their regular menu but I hope they consider keeping them on the menu. 

I also had a meatball pizza. The pizza was tasty. The crust was cooked to perfection and the toppings and sauce were in great proportions with a good mix of flavor. It was definitely knife/fork pizza as the crust was not cooked to crispy on the bottom.

I ended up getting one of their house-made sodas with bourbon pre-mixed and was really happy with the drink. 

The overall price-tag was pretty hefty (Nachos cost as much as the drink). The food was great and I'll be back on occasion.

I went into Alan Webb Chevrolet to have my new vehicle plates installed and ran into my sales consultant Mike Woods.  I told Mike about getting yellow road striping paint on our new vehicle (thanks to ODOT having no warning signs) and showed him the side of our car which still had yellow paint in places after hours of trying to cleaning it up.  Mike offered to have our car washed and see if their lot attendant Niles could remove the remaining paint, which he did!  Vehicle looks great and we really loved their great customer service!  Thanks Mike and Niles!

This place does look like a warehouse...but at the same time, feels sort of homey.  The service here is always friendly, and it's a place where both my wife and I can have a lot of fun!   I ogle the petite but quality beer selection, while my wife wanders through aisles of kitchenware.  Perfect.   

You can have your beer chilled for free on the spot, if you're planning to have some when you get home.  

If you sign up for their mailing list, you find out about cooking classes, and their latest sales on particular wines (usually Parker rating ~90+).

Five star's goes to In-N-Out only in fact reserved for them alone however in second place is Tasty Burger right in Boston. Was away on business when I found myself at the take out windows and one snapped open a tall man approximately age 28 greeted my boobs yes my boobs not once did he ever look at my face just my boobs so anyhow my boobs lol ordered their double double with cheese and I paid him and he gave my boobs the change dating with a smile thank you hope to see you again. Really and you know it men are just built this way but that's no excuse and I could be hating this place just for this but a girl cooked my burger so that's why I'm even telling this story. Okay sat down outside there's picnic tables outside and proceeded to devour this tasty burger and you know what it was an incredibly tasty burger and I suggest to everyone and I've already earned you girls easy here you'll love their burgers but girl next time in wearing an Eskimo jacket to place my order.

One of the most delicious pizzas in the Boston area! Flavorful thin crust, fresh diced tomatoes on top, meat bursting with flavor. If you ask for extra garlic they really do it. 

The restaurant is tiny--room for only a few people to sit and eat--and the ambiance is hectic and bustling. There's often a wait to sit and eat, and it's paper plates and self-service for drinks, condiments etc. You can always get take out but the pizza is so good I want to eat it at its hottest best!

I am not a burger person. I don't like the heavy, fat-pooling-in-your-stomach feeling I get after I eat them. And they're really just greasy sandwiches... I felt this way even after eating at In N' Out, P.Terry's, Mighty Fine etc. 

Hopdoddy changed my mind about this. The burgers are really good without having that strange 3-day-old frying oil smell on them and none of the heavy-ness after you're done.

My only complaint is their weird ordering-seating system. It seemed like there was a lot of dead time in between seating groups at their tables and the line out the door was ridiculous for how many empty tables there were. We sat down and ate next to an empty table for a total of ~30 minutes watching the line slowly move outside the window, all the while this table next to us stayed empty. long-neck-girl.gif

Crowds. Crowds of people. So many people. I had no idea that Mike's Pastry was so popular. It is, as evidenced by the throngs of people who flock here. You will wait. Be prepared.

We got on line and waited about 30 minutes to get a cannoli. Was it worth it? The answer is yes. I don't even like cannoli, but the one I ordered (chocolate chip cannoli) was amazing. It made me a cannoli believer. There are dozens of different kinds of cannoli, as well as other pastries (profiteroles, eclairs) which you can procure by standing in a different swarm of people. There is the semi-line-slash-swarm that is standing around for cannoli; then there is the semi-line-slash-swarm standing around for everything else. Cannoli is to the left and everything else is to the right. Got it? Good.

Mike's has tables inside, if you'd like to enjoy your cannoli while watching the crowds line up. It's just better to just get your pastry to go, though. Half of the enjoyment came from eating my cannoli while outside observing the city.

My first time at this DNB and I absolutely loved it! From the food, to the service, to all of the awesome new games I had an amazing experience! This DNB looks pretty new inside and the game area is huge. As you walk in you are greeted by their service desk that can help you get more points on your card. Behind them is the colorful bar and dining area with large screen tvs. Also, up front is a bathroom, so you do not have to run all the way to the back of the DNB to go.

It was super crowded because of the playoffs, but we were still able to check out tons of games. They had a few new ones, such as Monopoly, Rock em Sock em Robots, and Connect Four. All of them were super fun, particularly the Rock em Sock em as you had to physically move your robot with the controls and then press two buttons to hit the other robot in the face. I think something must have been wrong with the machine as  my friend kept hitting my robot in the face, but I kept winning--who knows?!? But it was fun--just a warning though your hands will be hurting afterwards, but just for a little while.

The food was on point as usual at DNB. I love that they had a texting system, so they were able to let us know we were on the list and then let us know that our table was ready. I just simply had to reply that we were still coming and they held our table for us. Our waitress was super nice and accomodating.  Because it was so crowded she brought us extra drinks. And even though it was crowded she still managed to check on us various times to make sure we were alright. The food was great. I ordered their new turkey sandwich, which had spinach, sundried tomatoes, aoli sauce, slices of thick turkey all topped off on this whole grain rustic rye bread. And instead of the fries I got a side of their broccoli which was cooked to perfectly,  but it did have a little too much butter at the bottom for my liking.

Overall I loved this DNB and if ot were not for the distance I would be back every couple of weeks to let out some stress and just have fun! They describe it as an adult playground and it so is!! So come, play, eat, drink, and be merry--leave the kidos with a babysitter!!

We started with the tuna nachos which, if I'm being completely honest, are elevated "comfort" food. They're very well done, but if it's possible to feel trashy while paying $16 for nachos, this is the appetizer to do it. That being said, I'd totally order them again.

The crispy pork is a wildly under rated appetizer. Beautifully crispy, the savoriness of the pork nicely offset by the kimchi and vinaigrette. 

The short ribs were good, but not fall-apart tender. Austin is a BBQ mecca, so your proteins better be on point. By far, my biggest issue with the meal was the sour mash. It was extremely sour. Believe me, I'm a fan of funky foods: kimchi, kombucha, sour beers, I love 'em all. This was not a case of "little bit of sour cream in the potatoes." More like "the milk was starting to turn." It didn't make me ill, but it was very off putting, especially juxtaposed with the other dishes.

The bar was similarly underwhelming. Our table ordered a round of blueberry mojitos, followed by the tequila francois. Both were just okay, dominated by the mixers, with seemingly little actual alcohol. My wife ordered a glass of prosecco, and for the first time in my life, I was jealous of wine. Be aware, Plate is extremely proud of their cocktails, in this case it nearly doubled our bill.

Was the experience good? Sure, it was good. But at nearly $100/person, it wasn't mind blowing. Don't get me wrong, I'm glad to have true high-end dining in the Lakeway/Bee Caves area, but on the rare occasions I'm feeling fancy, I might just make the trip downtown anyway.

After adopting a dog last week last week I started wondering what I was going to do with him on the days doubles had to be worked ? Keeping him in a kennel all day and letting him out on break just to turn around and put him back in just wasn't sitting well with me and started looking up day cares in the area.

Barking Hound was found, they let me take a look around and even said the" first visit would be free," oh and they have cameras so nervous parents can keep an eye on their babies o.k. sign us up. 
Our first visit -  paper work was already filled out, they made copies and he was  quickly lead off with me following behind I figured if he got to nervous or I didn't like what I saw he would be taken home immediately this was not to happen. After socializing for ten minutes he was then put in main room with all of the others in his "category" suddenly I was quickly forgotten & off he went. 

The doggies get report cards when you pick them up, he made this "mama' proud. Vino had a ball, made some new friends and was told he was" very vocal," hmm weird haven't seen this side yet.  He was there just under six hours apparently he had a good time cause he was passed out in the back seat in under five. The staff is helpful the owner Stuart put me at ease and the rates will fit into my budget, the fact that this location is down the street from where I work makes this so convenient it's a "no brainer."
We cant wait to go back next week.

This is the more aesthetic side of the Common on the west side of Charles St.

There are many flowers and other landscaping that beautifies this side of the park that is far more congested because there is less open space.  While there are many signs saying to keep off the grass I see many not really paying attention to those signs.  

There are people everywhere and in the middle of the park they have swan boats (paddles) and some of them hold a lot of people.  

There is a really nice shot that can be taken of the George Washington statue if you are at the west side of the park near Arlington street where the shot can be had facing east towards the financial district.

I really enjoy their tantan ramen and the fact that they have Yelp check-in. Throw in some cha shu and an egg and BAM, that's a delicious bowl of $16 ramen. Fragment, spicy, and yummy. 

Yelp check-in is pretty convenient and if you know it's a 2-hour wait, you can check-in, then take your sweet time getting there. It's located in a questionable building and this place is probably the only reason the building is still standing. There's an ample parking lot in the back or take the T and walk 5 min from Coolidge Corner.

I blame South Street Diner for a recent unhealthy obsession I've developed: buffalo fingers. All the spicy goodness of hot wings, combined with the ease of chicken fingers!

On my first visit to the South Side Diner last year, my considerate cabbie dropped me at the entrance after I told him I wanted a snack before heading to bed. Luckily I had ditched my electric blue prom dress at the hotel, entered without shame and got a grilled cheese to go.

It was mighty tasty but nothing could compare to the joy given me by the buffalo finger I snatched off Leighann's plate on a return trip to South Side a few weeks ago.

If you have buffalo finger recommendations in your town, please send 'em my way. I'm on a hunt to find the best. So far, South Side is tops!

This is a nice sore tucked in on 23rd.   It is easy to find as There is a cow statue outside that advertises for the store.  It is always changing as it is painted in different ways. 

They have a nice selection of well made and pricy stuff.  They make all kinds of wearable items all from leather.  The leather here tends to be more simple lines and heavier then at Coach.  For me an added bonus is that they are an Oregon company.  

The staff here seems happy to answer questions about their goods.  

I was surprised when I first found it here as they have another store down near Powell's books.

Cat Grooming: 

Pet Drop Off - experience was just ok. Room for improvement in your customer experience interactions. I'm a visual person, it would help to walk pet owners through a check list of sorts explaining each grooming option, what is covered in those options & the price. As well as a place for the owner to write down any additional needs or comments before grooming. An online form could do the job well. Then implement all the basics of customer service and build trust with your clients & ensure them their pet is in good hands.

BE SURE to bring your cat in a carrier. They won't take care of your pet without it. 

Grooming - 100% awesome! My cat looks and smells amazing. He is very happy too. They take care of your animals here. I can trust that.

This is a bar/drink review:

Sam's has one of the best patio's in the city. My wife and I went there on a Friday night for some after dinner drinks around 9:30-10. It was a perfect 72 degree night out and they had a solo electric guitar player jamming. It was about as perfect as it gets. It looks like they have live entertainment every Friday.

They recently expanded their patio bar area which was a nice move as the indoor bar area is pretty tiny. The drinks are priced pretty much in line with the higher in market around $12 each. The wine menu has plenty of unique options with plenty to choose from by the glass. I had the "partyinthecity" something which was a gin based cocktail perfect for a summer night. I ordered from the bar which was pretty quiet, so my drink came out fast.

I haven't eaten here for a while, but the last time we went the food was delicious, and the menu looks really appetizing, so I know we will be back soon.

I went to the Castle for Wine Riot on 4/29/2011. Last year, I attended the same event at what felt like a smaller venue (very different space though - so I can't be sure) and thought that this space was ideal. The tables were spread out nicely, there weren't long waits to taste the wines, we were able to mingle and enjoy ourselves with ease. The only downside is that the bathrooms we were allowed to use were downstairs (which is not ideal when you're handing out wine like it's water!) ... however, that said, it was a fun space and very easy to get to via public transportation. 

I have to imagine that large events here (like a wedding) would be very lovely!

I looooove the coffee at Barista. I believe Barista, Heart, and Stumptown are my top favorite cafes in Portland! Bold statement, I know! :x

Barista is located in the Gadsbury building and there is limited seating INSIDE. Only about 3-4 tables that seat 2, a counter next to the cashier, and 1 table that could fit 4 people. However, there is plenty of seating outside which was nice... except for rainy days and when Portland is abnormally hot.

I definitely recommend the coffee here! A great place to hang out or do some work (if you can find a table). Great and friendly baristas with a cool and vibrant ambiance.

Another Yelp controversy to weigh in on! 3.5 stars rounded up to 4 because the -.5 star is largely due to the sour interaction I had with one of the older dudes we were interacting with, reproduced below.

Johnny's Hideaway is definitely *entertaining* and deserves appreciation for that alone.  And even though there are certainly downsides, it's UNIQUE.  I like unique places, as a rule.  I'm probably decently likely to return when invited because amusement in the form of familiar old tunes and male attention in varying degrees of unwelcomeness is all but guaranteed.  

I went somewhat spontaneously with two girlfriends after picking up one of them at the airport at 1:00 AM (flight delay due to ATL weather).  I was DD.  One of my two girlfriends was supposed to get married this weekend - Johnny's was quite sympathetic and let her in without paying the $5 cover.  Then the DJ immediately played a song I requested on her behalf.  The bartender was quite nice to us and attentive.  

The bar is well placed and spacious, and there are lots of places to sit down all over in the form of round cushy low chairs and little tables . This is GREAT.  I know it is cool to stand up all the time, but annoying - I like having the option of sitting down and somewhere to set my drink.  This is rather necessary, because drinks are Not Allowed on the dance floor.  If you step onto the dance floor with a drink in your hand, you Will be accosted by a smoky dude in a velvet suit who calls himself Elvis.  This got annoying, but it's nice to know you won't get spilled on on the dance floor, honestly. And the mirror wall was fun, but I was not so much about it last night, when I had flat hair, glasses and no makeup on and was wearing the shirt I'd worn to work and just spilled wine on while watching "Australia" on my friend's couch.  

As for the crowd, I had heard of the cougar/old dude reputation, and that contingent was certainly represented.  This late, though, there were plenty of young kids too.  I didn't dress for the club because I didn't know I was going there, but I fit in fine, and felt plenty attractive despite my schlubby dress and appearance.  More importantly, my friend had a good time :)

I feel compelled to relate the following negative experience I had with one of the older dudes, possibly a regular (based only on the fact that he gave a big hug to "Elvis"), who appeared to be there by himself.  We will call him "R."  So he seemed to be interested enough in all three of us.  He was not half bad looking either.  He started dancing with my would-be-getting-married friend, and I was glad he seemed to be giving her attention, but then it turned into too much attention and she bailed on him.  THEN a guy we used to work with showed up and we started talking to him, right next to R.  I think R felt a little dissed.  Then R bought my other friend a beer and she ran off and danced with this adorable young guy.  Then he tried to buy me a beer and I said "sorry, I can't drink beer, it's Passover" to which my friend responded, "really? You're going to try to explain being a Jew in *this* place?" And then I ran away too, and I think he felt a little dissed by all three of us.  So, when we got back, he said "you all are f#$@ing teases."  And I was like, um, that's not nice.  And then he was like "lawyers, f#$% lawyers man, the last thing we need is more lawyers."  (All three of us were lawyers.)  I said in a slightly more confrontational tone, Um, seriously, that's not nice.  He was like, "I know it's not nice, but it's true."  So then I said, "well what do you do?" And he said he'd been a [X] (redacted for privacy) for 17 years - I sort of got the feeling he might not be employed right now.  So I immediately said, "f$#@ [X]-s." and he seemed kind of hurt, even though I was just trying to demonstrate how his comment had been totally out of line.  Later that night though, I felt really bad about it.  Like, he probably just said that because he felt bad about his interactions with us, which I admit were probably not ideal.  So I'm sorry, R.  I still think your comments were out of line, but I should not have responded in kind.

So, that was my night at Johnny's Hideaway.  Definitely a good decision to go, will most likely have occasion to return.

There are several frozen yogurt places in Harvard Square, and Berryline is my favorite. Their frozen yogurt is creamier than the yogurt at Pinkberry and higher quality than those at YogurtLand. One downside is they only have 3 flavors on rotation at any time (and one is always the Original), but the flavors tend to be different at their different locations and are posted online, so you can see what they have in advance. My favorite flavors are three Nutella and Oreo flavors - the flavor is well-concentrated and the yogurt is creamy, almost ice-cream like. They have a nice variety of fruit and chocolate toppings, and I think their portion size is slightly more generous than that at Pinkberry.

I did take out from this place multiple times. The reason being that it is a ver small place with only 3 little tables. They do have a great variety of food selections and I m satisfied with their cuisines. I tried pork belly with fried rice, crab rangoon, drunken noodles and mango with sticky rice. 
My fav are drunken noodles and mango with sticky rice! Drunken noodle had just right amount of spicy and ingredients were fresh and came with generous amount. Mango with sticky rice was really good, and you should try it!

Every time I drive by here, I always notice quite a crowd waiting outside for a table. Luckily I was seated right away when we came around 5:00 p.m., though the place was already full and there was a steady stream of people coming in.  From what I can tell, small groups may be seated at the same table since space is limited.

We got the crab noodle soup, which was delicious.  The broth was clean and tasty, tofu and meat was good and also came with chili peppers so you could adjust the heat.  I don't think there was actually any crab in the soup though.  I would have personally preferred thinner noodles but still .. a great comfort food dish!  We also got a grilled pork and shrimp bun.   Admittedly, I couldn't tell the difference between the 2 to 3 grilled pork and grilled shrimp bun offerings, and even asked our waitress, but she told me that the marinated grilled pork and the lemongrass grilled pork were the same... but the pictures did help inform my choice.  I liked the noodles in this dish - I'm not sure if they were stir fried, but they had a nice texture... Different than the buns I normal get.  The fried chicken wings were also tasty and I will definitely reorder them again.  The side citrusy? dipping sauce added an extra pop of flavor.   Can't wait to try more things here.

Chick-Fil-A in a central Columbus location was a long time coming. They would have gotten a lot more of my money over the years had they had a location closer to me. I guess the best thing I can say is thank you.

Brand new place so everything is spic and span, but I don't think I have ever been in a dirty Chick-Fil-A. Not sure how KFC or Popeyes are going to continue with their footprint given the CFA expansion and growing footprint.

As expected they were busy, but they worked fast and friendly and never let us see them sweat. Service with a smile is a way of life with this chain.

I ordered a Spicy Chicken that was fried to perfection and was thankful for the extra pickles as a way to contrast the heat. The waffle fries were fresh, fluffy on the inside, and the right amount of salt. The fresh squeezed lemonade was the right amount of sweet and just enough tart to make me smirk.

Chick-Fil-A is all about their chicken and have the best variety of sandwiches in their industry. They have great kids meals (who else has grilled nuggets), awesome salads, fresh fruit cups, pretty good soups, and breakfast burritos and sandwiches that put McDonalds and Taco Bell to shame. My girlfriend is addicted to their shakes, they get me brownie points when I bring them to her with their fresh baked cookies.

The next time I say something bad about Chick-Fil-A will be the first. I highly recommend this chain to everyone I know except on Sundays.

I've gotten good service here. I get the "Diamond Wash" which is close to the top end. They sometimes miss a spot or two, but the car comes out much cleaner than it went in so I'm happy. It is a mass-production car wash so you don't get the same amount of care as if you were hand-washing it yourself, but it's a good value for the money. I think in the summer they employ a lot of teenagers, who tend to be surly, but the adults are always pleasant and I haven't had any sales pressure applied.

I live in the neighborhood and like this Cafe, a lot. Nice owners, nice staff, cute space.
They serve Stumptown french press style, and I have to say, it isn't my favorite, possibly grinding the coffee a little more coarsely would suit the French Press a little better.
The service is always excellent. The food is consistently prepared. I think the menu could get changed up a little (Nothing crazy). I'd probably come more often.
I've never been disappointed by the corn beef hash, and as a parent, I appreciate that the menu allows me to work my way through different price points and get my kids fed for a reasonable amount.
The coffee cake is always fantastic.

This place ended up being a great last stop on our afternoon trip to Icon Park.  As soon as I walked in, I could see this place had that classy sports bar sort of vibe.  A bar right in the middle of the room with TVs all over the place, yet very comfortable, spaced-out seating.  The booths were awesome too.  More comfortable than your average ones.  

We lucked out and arrived exactly as happy hour began, so we enjoyed $2 off our beer and cocktails and half off most of the apps.  We ended up just ordering all appetizers so we could try a bunch of different things and not break the bank.  

First off, the Pineapple Cider I had was pretty tasty.  It did, however, taste like I was drinking champagne while a large Hawaiian dude was smacking me in the face with a pineapple.  It was very sweet.  Still... not bad.  

The Boneless Firecracker Wings were on point.  They didn't come with a dipping sauce to cool them off though, which was easily corrected by just asking for it.  It definitely needed it.  They had a kick.  

The chicken lettuce wraps were interesting.  Impossible to eat... not bad.  The sauces were very strange though.  Not quite sure they went well with the dish.  The tofu was a nice twist though.

The Moo Shu Egg Rolls were awesome.  Definitely something I haven't had before.  They looked a lot like the south western egg rolls you find at some Tex-Mex places, but with Asian flavors.  The sauce it came with was weird to be honest.  It was like an apple sauce... but not really.  It's hard to explain but I kept going back for more of it.  

The fried calamari was decent, but I found the bread to squid ratio a bit off.  A lot of pieces just felt like I was only eating the batter.  Still, the tartar sauce it came with was pretty addictive and made up for it for the most part. 

The sliders are pretty great too.  The meat seemed like good quality stuff and the homemade sauce that came on it was really flavorful.  The buns were a bit of a let down.  I usually prefer a more potato roll-like bread with my sliders.  But that's just me.  Also, the fries were amazing.  Perfectly salted and really addictive.  

The star of the meal were the chicken nachos.  I couldn't believe it was an appetizer!  It was a huge plate.  Recently, the nachos I've tried from different places have been a bit of a let down.  These were a different story.   Loaded with tons of chicken, cheese, beans, and more cheese... they were awesome.  At a certain point I just avoided the mess and started forking off all the toppings and just eating them without the chips.  It was still really great.  

Dessert was no let-down either.  We got the sampler, which came with mini versions of three different desserts.  The chocolate soufflé was dense and very chocolatey.  Was more like a chocolate torte in a cup, but as a chocolate lover, I was enjoying every bite.  

The creme brûlée cheese cake was incredible!  I mean... two of my favorite desserts in one.  Nothing to complain about there.  

The peach apple cobbler was like an apple pie fresh out the oven.  The vanilla ice cream was a perfect little addition.  Also a great dessert.  

Service was all extremely friendly.  Even had one server come by and compliment us for our table full of food, saying "happy hour done right... I love it."  Food was for the most part pretty good.  The location of this place is great too.  Only a 20 second walk from the Orlando Eye.  There were a couple of other places to eat within a short distance from here, but I'm glad we chose this place.  Had a good experience.

First things first... their sushi rice is PINK! They use pink sushi vinegar as opposed to regular vinegar, which maximizes healthy nutrients such as Omega 3, Omega 6, Iron, Potassium, Vitamin C and Beta Carotene. 

It was a cold rainy day, when we came in (just another day in Vancouver), so we opted to sit next to the fireplace. This place is surprisingly spacious inside, with plenty of seating and tables on either side of the restaurant. 

I came in here with one other person and we split two rolls, an order of the gyoza, chicken karagge, and the oyster motoyaki. We loved everything except the oyster motoyaki. I normally like oysters, but this particular dish felt undercooked and I wasn't a fan of the sauce on top. I did really love the sushi well house roll (avo, cream cheese, prawn tempura, cucumber, deep fried spicy red snapper, imitation crab, yam crunches, and special sauce) and chicken karagge. The roll was generous in size, and covered in yam crunch flakes, which I particularly loved. The chicken karagge was perfectly juicy and crispy all at the same time - pair this with a chipotle dip, and we were in heaven! 

Service was very quick and our teas and waters never made it past the half way point. 

I'd happily come back here for more pink sushi! Yum!

What kind of hole have I been living in that I have not been to Lineage yet for Brunch, despite it being but steps from my door? I finally crawled out of my cave for Sunday brunch and loved Lineage as soon as I walked in the door, it is bright, airy, clean, spacious, minimalist but still warm. Whats more is that the staff are super friendly and service is always really great - smooth, accommodating, and with a smile.

- Bread basket - YUM - 5 piece assortment of scones, mini muffins, banana bread, all moist, light, and flavorful, served with delicious jams, and yes maple butter, I have never met a maple butter I did not like. 
- Prosciutto, Brie and Mission Fig Sandwich - loaded with prosciutto and cheese, the fig gave it just the right amount of sweetness, not too greasy. Wished I had some greens though.
- Polenta with lardons - creamy buttery polenta (again, I usually hate polenta, but this was good and not too heavy) - the lardons big and chunky, were not greasy and went well with the baby spinach. 
- Prime Rib Burger - Very Juicy, flavorful, cooked perfectly on a light brioche bun. Nothing fancy but very good. Fries are thick, crisp and not greasy.

...and while this place is a bit more upscale than any other place in Coolidge Corner, it all came out to only $20 per person, which includes tax and tip. I noticed that their menu is dated, so it changes daily - so I'll be back in the hopes they'll bring back the lobster tacos. Overall this is a refined and delicious dining experience, and for what you are able to get, that will leave your pocket pleasantly surprised.

If you are considering buying a car, especially a Honda, check out Holler.  I am obsessive when it comes to researching pricing, especially for big ticket buys, and Holler does a great job pricing with the market.

I'll admit, one of the favorite things to do is negotiate, so it took me a little while to wrap my head around the set price structure that they use.  That being said, I came out with a great deal that included brand new car warranty on a certified car - even covering tires and oil changes!

Give Holler a try, and ask for Gil - he took great care of me!

You usually can't go wrong at Korean BBQ's, and this place satisfied my cravings! Just sitting down at the grill excites me. Then I open the menu and it's game time. 

We started with seafood pancakes. My friend at the table was pretty adamant that he did not want pancakes. He had them before at other places and he didn't care for them. Well, he LOVED these crispy triangle patties filled with calamari and shrimp. He's converted now. He ordered a crispy tempura sushi roll in anticipation of not liking the pancakes. The roll was unexpectedly delicious. I was assuming it would be dry and fishy because we were at a Korean Bbq (can you blame me?).

Next came the meats!! Yummy! Jumullok Galbi (beef short ribs), Bulgogi (thinly sliced marinated beef), and Wine Sam Gyup Sal (pork belly in wine with a bean sauce). The waiting and watching as my meat grilled was killing me. I was careful not to fill up on all of the Kimchi "fixin's" around me. 

Our table of 3 polished off everything we ordered. The meats were so tender and well seasoned, none of the meats needed the sauces it came with, it was really difficult to stop, so we didn't.

So lucky to have stayed here.  My friend and I made plans to attend the inaugural Skookum Music Festival.  It was this last weekend and I just got home.  We found availability in June and secured the last room! Phew.  It has a classic look to the lobby, high end, sort of older.  Properly attired porters and doormen.  Location is very handy.  It was about a 50 minute walk to our Event. Loads of shops, bars, restaurants, grocers, to walk to from the Sutton Place.  A nice merchant is located right there if you need to grab some quality beverages.  We were so excited on landing and getting checked in we selected a sparkling wine and 6 pack of local pale.  The Sparkling Wine was very memorable, Blue Mountain from Okanagan Valley in B.C. it was delightfully dry and the clerk even suggested.  That's an affirmation.  We got to our room to discover a wide, generous view of the city.  Loads of large almost skyscraper buildings.  Who is washing all those windows.  Anyway, I could gaze out that window all day.  It was especially nice since the day we landed - it was bright and sunny.  The amenities were nice, no fridge in the room, though.  Bummer.  
The beds were extraordinary.  They were incredibly comfy.  TV was fine, we had it on for background, opening day of football - but the guide was dumb.  It stated channel IDs, but not programs.  The concierge helped us a few times.  I like their style and demeanor here, straightforward, polite. We ordered room service one day for Breakfast!  Such a treat.  It was perfect.  I had a simple eggs, toast, potatoes.  We were on the 17th floor.  The price was reasonable.  I think less than $200 night for two Queen beds.  So worth it, warm hospitality, great location.  Pretty city, just needed a few more days of sun. One other odd thing, we had empty bottles that just sat there for a few days.  Left a note for staff to remove, they did. I couldn't find the fitness center - but I think it's in another adjacent building.  Was allowed an earlier check in - bonus!

Of note: there was a Santa graveyard below us.  The rooftop of one of the buildings below had a pile of decorative Santa Clauses, clustered together in the corner.  Kind of funny.  We didn't do any research on this siting.

This review is for sitting at the bar for drinks and food. They have good spacing, dividers between patrons, dividers between bartenders and patrons, and staff are on top of Covid protocols. Staff have all been pleasant and attentive. The atmosphere is great because it is connected directly to the Casino floor. We have enjoyed drinks and appetizers. The meatballs are a must if you are a big eater. All the other apps are executed well. The bread and oil are great also. Deducting one point because the bar has been missing ingredients to a few of their specialty drinks. Why put it on the menu and not have the ingredients on hand?

Great little place with spicy Thai food!  We yelped it during our Disney Halloween trip.  The Fried Krab Cheese (Crab Rangoon) was melt in your mouth delicious with a light crispy wonton wrapper, and the potstickers were good too.  We tried the Combo Pad Thai, Thai Fried Rice, and Chicken/Shrimp Udon Noodle Bowl.  All were very good and spicy!  If you aren't into spice, order a level lower than you typically would.  The service was friendly and attentive, and price was not bad.  I would definitely  recommend.

I think I heard of Boiler Nine's concept over a year ago and ever since I've been so anxious to try it. It's nothing like I dreamed about in my head, but that's not a bad thing. I was told it was going to be multiple floors (it is) with each being a different food concept (it isn't) and have so much sq footage that it'd be hard to walk around it all (it definitely doesn't). What I learned from my experience is that I need new sources of information. 

What Boiler Nine is, is a small, modern, yet industrial, space with a small, yet powerful menu. So, almost completely the opposite of what I was expecting. It's loud and crowded on Fridays at lunch and only has two indoor floors. I hear there's a rooftop, too, but in 100 degree heat I had to pass. 

I ordered their burger, medium rare, and it came with house-made salt & vinegar chips. The chips were so good and even held their crispness after a few hours in my fridge. The burger was so thick and juicy that it should be in a rap video. 

Once the crowds die down, I'll definitely done again. I wanna see what they've got for dinner.

working in the area and wow I found a good breakfast place. I would put this place in my top ten for sure. super fast service, just the way I like it because I am on my way to work and don't have much time. I ordered bacon and eggs with home fries. this was the most bacon I ever received at a diner and it was nice and crisp. home fries were red bliss potatoes with very good flavor. ill be back! coffee was the only down fall, not that great. next time I will order orange juice.
