Phonatic has quite a few traditional choices from your typical pho restaurants.  Food quality is great.  Broken down, their ingredients are fresh.  That is the first step to a great tasting dish. Presentation is a little over board in terms of size but that's usually forgiven. :) Taste of the food prepared is middle to high in flavor. Paired with their clumsiness and friendly staff, this is a sure win for a pho restaurant in my book.  

Despite my review, I only awarded them 4 stars because for the fifth star to rise... I need to have the wow factor that makes it uniquely above others.  I await for this to happen.

This is a pretty legitimate place for seafood. We got the pick 3, crawfish, shrimp and blue crabs. The heat was just right, the spices weren't too overpowering, and the corn wasn't fresh so it was just ok. 

Knocked a star off bc when I presented my Groupon, she took my phone and laid it right on top of the butter sauce that splattered onto the table. You would think she would be more careful when handling someone else's phone. 

All I all the food was good but the service was meh.

Underbones (the bar beneath RedBones) is one of my favorite local haunts. Its walls are covered in these wacky acrylic illustrations of all kinds of bizarre scenarios, many involving pirates. The atmosphere is great, a little dark, a little loud, and a great place to walk home from with a nice buzz and a full belly. 

Must Trys:

1.) The wheel of rotating drafts. Don't know what you want? Let fate decide for you. 
2.) The Buffalo Shrimp served with blue cheese dressing for dipping. 
3.) The Corn Pudding. It sounds fucked up but it's one of the best things on the menu.
4.) The Caramel Custard (referred to by the employees and regulars as Liquid Crack). 

The portions are big enough to almost always leave you with leftovers, and they serve corn bread. I love corn bread.

You know I really like the Recess Arcade Bar and our most recent visit was on Saturday 6/15/2019. 

Its such a cool & very fun atmosphere..with the bar, arcade games, and the awesome music playing. 

They also have plenty of seating, the restrooms are clean, and they have a few TVs hanging on the walls, which played the music videos of the music that was being played on our most recent visit. 

The only thing that messes with me is that I'm always tempted to shake something because of the great music they have playing while also playing Pac-Man & trying to do both is no bueno for me..I need to be super focused if I'm going to kick a$$ on PAC-Man ;). 

Seriously though Recess Arcade Bar for sure is a fun spot to hang out with with your peeps.

-Rebecca our

I like Thai food and this place was pretty good. I do not remember the name of my order, but we started out with some cabbage spring rolls with tofu and veggies in them. They were served with a honey lemon grass dip and were excellent. My main entree was huge and tasty. I tried to pig out on what I had, but was quickly filled up with enough left over for another full meal the next day. The server was very well mannered and the service was quick. I had a few PBRs with my meal and it was a good night out with a few friends I had not seen in a long time. The atmosphere was friendly with some hipster types hanging out front on Alberta street. The aesthetic of the area on a whole was very much a eclectic art district with a mix of hipsters, hippies and Punk types. They also have a small bar attached to the building that is separate from the dining area.

I'm so surprised I didn't know about this restaurant until my friend from out of town said, "we don't have the restaurant in south Florida so I have to visit while I'm in Orlando"

Inside definitely gives you the New Orleans feel. Very cool decor! The servers were very friendly. 

I ordered shrimp and grits... HOLY SPICY! I don't know if I'm a wuss, but it was too hot. I had to request the cheesy grits bowl separately and Pick our the shrimp, because the sauce is what was spicy. 

So let's talk about the grits! Yes and yes! 

I will go back! And I really want to see if the shrimp and grits is really that spicy or someone messed up that night in the kitchen.... I don't know.... I would like to keep my taste buds though. So not sure if I'll risk it. Otherwise, I loved it

If you are in the N Druid Hills/Toco Hills/Briarcliff/La Vista/Clairmont quadrant, you can't miss this restaurant.

While a lot of over priced restaurants may have open in the former Lohman's Plaza shopping and where the N Druid Hills Walgreens shopping is, this restaurant is a gem.

Very reasonable priced lunch specials.  They offer Thai, Chinese and Sushi and they do all three cuisines very well.

Located next to the Target on Briarcliff they are open for lunch and dinner.  Worth the visit!

As far as diners go, this is the REAL DEAL here.  This is a 50s diner that really makes you go back in time.  Not only that, it's clean and shiny.  

  I had the pecan pancakes the other day for breakfast and these things were huge, no BS pancakes.  The syrup comes hot and delicious.  My friend had the guacamole burger, which he said was awesome.  I love the shakes.  They even have yogurt shakes, which are low in fat and cholesterol.  The food is big and tasty.  The atmosphere is splendid.  How can you go wrong with Elvis memorabilia and juke boxes lining the restaurant?  Why does it only get 4 stars?  The service is slowwww.  When we went, there was only 1 server for like 6 tables in the restaurant.  It's also a dollar or two more expensive than Denny's, but you get what you pay for.  As far as the quality and taste of the food, it far surpasses Denny's.  So, I'd be willing to pay an extra $2 for an actual good cheeseburger.

We had eaten there a few years ago off the regular menu and found it good but just better than average Chinese food. I became skeptical of the place when I saw the "All you can eat" sign go up. I find that the sign of a failing restaurant. But 4 of us tried the hot pot and were completely lost. We didn't understand the menu and checked off some things we knew we liked--beef, chicken, shrimp, vegetables. The waitress was awesome.  She guided us through our choices, suggested some unknown "whitefish" and mixed some sauces for us. We quickly got the hang of it and kept eating the courses she brought. I joked to our friends that this was very good, but we had no idea of the price of each course and might be surprised at the bill.(my only experience was years ago at a hot pot in Boston where every food was separately and highly priced). We got the bill and it was $19.95 each. The only upcharge was $2.00 each for giant oysters on the half shell and $3.00 for each of the soups (miso and vegetable) we got. I recommend it highly.

My boyfriend had been here twice with friends and kept telling me that he wanted to take me here as well. I was always kinda meh about it since it is "British" food, and I figured that would be a bunch of meat with some plain side such as mash. Finally I decided to give it a shot, considering it got 4 stars on Yelp. 

We came here on a late Saturday night. I was immediately excited when I saw how cute the restaurant looked! It was a little British looking house of some kind. We entered through the bottom floor and took the stairs upstairs to the main seating area. I was happy to see that it was busy, but we were still able to get a seat right away. 

One of the things that had me excited about the Fat Badger was the ever changing menu. We started with a Scotch egg and croquettes which were absolutely amazing!! Our mini Yorkshire puddings came out afterwards, making me want more. I had the rabbit on special for my main, and my boyfriend went for the bangers with mash. The portions were very generous, which is rare for these types of restaurants. I had to take some home as I was leaving some room for dessert. And am I ever glad I had room, because we ordered the sticky toffee pudding which was incredible. The hot toffee pudding with butterscotch sauce, mixed with the cold vanilla ice cream was probably one of the best desserts I've ever tasted! 

After this experience, I could tell why my boyfriend raves about this place. We are definitely coming back, and very soon!!

The ambiance is great for a romantic night, or special occasion, although the high rollers seem to love this place. The who's who of boston seemed to all have come out the night we went.

The food was very good, and the presentation was excellent.

My only complaint is that they are a bit overpriced. I mean, don't get me wrong, the food was great but you really are paying for the atmosphere. 

It's definitely worth trying once, but not a place I see myself returning to over and over again.

good location, well for me at least., orange line service, obviously the theater is new so I wont give them too much credit for the cleanliness, but it is clean. bar is a cool idea, im  not bothered by the assigned seating because its very rare that I just randomly decide to go to a movie. I agree with most of the reviews it is not your average movie seat .imax... some movies are just better that way and worth the higher price.... ps I saw American Sniper, it was worth it.

I went for lunch in November. The place wasn't that busy - so service was quick. They charge for fountain pop refills, so I'm taking off a star because that just seems unnecessary to begin with, and the cup they give you is about half the size of most fast food joints. Other than that, it was exactly what I expected from reading reviews and from having been to places like this in almost every city. They're usually hit or miss, and this one is firmly in the 'hit' camp in my books. 

They've got a good selection of fresh looking toppings, and sauces. My burger was basically exactly what I'd expected and hoped: nicely grilled beef with good seasoning/garlic hint (not sure if they put garlic in, or if it was the garlic mayo I added) - it's not a 'five guys' style patty where the beef is the star, but that's not what you should expect either. 

The fries were crisp, and they have seasoning salt if you're so inclined. The gravy was probably from a can, but again - to be expected, and works really well with the rest of the flavours. Good comfort food experience overall. Again, only problem I had was with the tiny cup for fountain drinks and charge for refills.

This is a very very cute place to go with your friends or a significant other. It is great to see a diversity in foods in Columbus. Walking in for the first time, I felt a bit lost. I should've know that this place was more like a food court than a grocery store from reading the reviews. Nonetheless, it was quite an adventure. I made 2 circles around the market and ended up with ice cream from Jeni's. Yum! That's basically all I got when I was there. The Indian food looked pretty delicious, too.

They have many great little shops in North Market. However, it is expensive and I would suggest not going alone. It is definitely a social place and I will go there next time with some friends.

Was really excited to try this place! The arancini balls were super good w melted cheese in the middle. The meatballs were amazing - good size, taste & texture. The Ceaser Salad was underwhelming. The swordfish w Orchette pasta was a 5/5. Now the bad - the penne alla vodka was garbage bin worthy. Pasta is my favorite thing in the world and I ended up throwing 1/2 of it away. To be fair, I don't like Al Dente but this pasta was undercooked so it was inedible.

I went here once for a team lunch and it's become one of my favorite burger joints. I'm pretty picky when it comes to how I want my burger made so I like the fact that they have a toppings bar where you can add whatever you want, aside from the cheese. The fries are tasty too and I feel like the amount of food you get for the amount you paid is well worth it. You can tell the building is kinda old and it has a kind of old fashioned fell about it, but other than that, it's a pretty good place to eat and relax. My old boss swears by this place and I do too.

Less than two blocks from my office makes this a great place for post-work beers; it's also good for plate sharing if you have an appetite. 

Decor and atmosphere are nice and space is relatively clean. Servers are friendly and accommodating -- one server remembered my beer order after only serving me one or two times beforehand. The only issue I've had here is when we ordered wings and they came out looking slightly under cooked. However, our server replaced the entire batch with a new one that was cooked perfectly with no extra charge. 

It's also a bit of a drag walking down a massive flight of stairs into the dungeon-area where the washrooms are located but if you time your bladder coordination right, you can use the handicapped washroom on the main floor. 

Overall, Elephant and Castle is one of my favorite pubs in Vancouver and I will continue to return for beers and light meals.

Usually when I lunch at Leow's, I go for the salad bar, but I finally got to try out Saltwood's burger bar experience that all my coworkers always talk about. Essentially, they have room for 8 at a long wooden table in the back kitchen where you sit facing the cooks as they prepare your meal. You order a burger (or shrimp po'boy) of your choice along with a dessert. I came on a Wednesday during lunch with 4 other coworkers. Just a note: this in-kitchen dining experience is ending in a month, so be sure to check it out before then if it interests you!

I got the Saltwood burger with goat cheese and mushrooms and it was delicious. The French was also a hit, as was the shrimp sandwich and the Southern. It comes with your choice of regular or sweet potato fries, which are just standard.

For dessert, I opted for the Bananas Foster-type dish which was unreal -- it comes atop 2 mini Belgian waffles sandwiching a scoop of vanilla ice cream and heavily drizzled with caramelly bananay chocolatey goodness (and of course, bananas). Super sweet and rich, but I couldn't stop eating it. The ooey gooey cake was also a huge hit, but a little too much for me.

The in-kitchen experience was a little weird -- you're just in the kitchen which isn't particularly glamorous watching someone put burgers on a grill and prepare other food while the dishwashers work behind you. I guess you do kind of feel like VIP when you're back there though. I'm glad they serve the burgers outside in the main bar area as well so I won't miss out once they stop offering this experience!

Convenience, check! 

Friendly Staff, check! 

Quality work, check! 

Pricey, check! 

I've been in three separate times for manicure with Julie. She does a wonderful job! 

On the last occasion, I went with a friend and she said her gel started to come off her nails. Meanwhile, my manicure is still holding on after 2 weeks (need to get them done again, im starting to scare people...).  My only complaint is that it is so pricey. 

My gel manicure usually costs $38 excluding tip. It's totally worth it, but not for every two weeks.

I'm not much of a department store junkie but I'm giving this place a thumbs up!   They have a pretty good ladies dress section and mens section if you are into V neck sweaters and polos. What I love most about this store, is that they like giving people discounts.  I never bring in a coupon and they'll scan one in for me and give me like 25% or 30% off. This weekend, when I walked in they gave me a $20 coupon to spend on any purchase that is at least $40.  I scored some make-up with that.    Good selection, clean store, and great customer service.

Good stuff. Quick review here. Came with colleague and they had a blast! 

Customer service: 10/10: I asked for a table for 10 for noon 10 mins before I arrived and they accommodated! Super nice. 

Food: 8/10: Could be better. Regular asian food. But great variety and fresh. We had mama's noodles, the beef soup, garlic mushroom noodles, pork belly rice w/ tofu and desserts! 

Desserts: 8/10: love the variety. Fav cheese cake is the oreo one! Free scoop if it's your bday! 

Ambiance: 9/10: chill and laid back. Good for large or small groups. Lots of noise when busy. You get to see the kitchen: open concept. 

Until next time!
Cherie

One of the good thing about Soho is they open til late. If you want a late night snack or drink or just wanna chill with friends, this may be a good hip spot to check out.  Their specials menu offer a good range of different choices from western to Asian dishes.  They  are pretty good deals which includes an entree or snack plus a drink .  Their drinks menu is extensive and also includes alcohol( but I probably wouldn't order alcohol at a bbt place) .  Their quality and presentation is pretty good for the price you pay for.  Location wise is also convenient with lots of street parking.

A friend suggested Elephants Deli for Happy Hour, which surprised me as I always thought of this as a place to go for prepared take-home meals, catering (I've hired them several times to cater holiday events for my team) and to purchase gourmet pantry items. Who knew that happy hour or sit down meals was an option? Obviously not me!

We enjoyed a cocktail and glass of wine, split a delicious margarita pizza cooked in their Italian open fire oven and then perused the various stations and offerings. There were so many sections of the store it was like a giant food and gift court under one roof:

- I was amazed at how large their gift area is, taking up a large portion of the store. So many items for that foodie in your life! And lots of cute things for kids. Elephants is on the "tourist" route and I'm sure many of these Portland influenced gifts make their way to other parts of the country
- Wine area with a varied selection, something for everyone
- Cheese, cheese and more cheese. Select 2 or three, grab a bottle of wine and baguette and a prepare salad and you have an instant picnic.
- The dessert area should not be missed! They have a "ding-dong" cake that reminds me of childhood and that classic treat. The Marionberry Chiffon cake looked divine and I convinced the person next to me gawking at it to buy it! He came back and thanked me - better the calories on him than me!
- There is an entire area dedicated to fresh made meats and salads with everything from orzo, couscous, potatoe, grilled flank steak, chicken cutlets, roasted veggies and more. Options are amazing!
- They also have a section dedicated to hot foods and their classics are all still there: chicken enchiladas, Mac & cheese, and tomato pic (get this when it's in season.) plus hamburgers, pizza and other hot foods made to order. 
- The freezer section is loaded with prepare but not cooked versions of the classics listed above and chicken pot pie, large variety of soups and so much more. Times when I have had to have surgery, I have stocked up here. And grab and go sandwiches and salads. Get the Jambon et fromage; classic and fab.

Throughout the entire store, on every conceivable counter, there are chocolates and candies and gummies piled high. Elephants reminds me of an adult version of Willy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory, with everything a foodie could want, in abundance everywhere you turn!

Prices are a bit high, imho, so rather than stock up, I tend to purchase specialty items or utilize for convenience when entertaining. Now I will also add Elephants to my list of lunch or HH meeting places to enjoy friendship over an adult beverage and really good food.

Came here last week with 6 other people. We love traditional Chinese food, especially seafood, but the place we were used to in Chinatown closed down. The ambiance is slightly weird, all the vent work is exposed making the place very modern and there is not much to the room, just a big room, not detail. The bar is huge and beautiful! I noticed the tables in the middle of the room are very, and I mean verrrrry close together. We sat in a back room area by orchards and some coral roots, which was a great big table. Music was Boyz II Men which we thought was so funny and random! Anyways, great food. We got the ginger scallion lobster, so good if you like lobster I recommend this! Everything was fresh, especially the cod and the black bean clams. We ordered wine, so did not get a chance to experience the bar drinks. Did not like the dessert, the fried bananas were so battered, but the other people at the table did enjoy them. I liked the green tea ice-cream. Well-priced, too. I will go back, especially for the Chinese seafood that I love. Great treasure for Malden.

What can I say, I'm a Maryland native going to a New York style salon, in Georgia!

When I need an inexpensive wash and set ($30) with a free deep conditioner (Tuesday through Thursday), I come here!  Vitalia is going to make sure your scalp is clean!  Don't let her petite stature fool you...she gets in your hair and washes the stress, tension...oh, and all the other stuff, away!  *Pretty sure I heard a choir singing when I left the washing station.* Erica is very friendly and always follows your request for styling.

It can get very busy in there, so be prepared for a wait.  Thanks to a more flexible work schedule, I'm figuring out times to go when it's not so crowded.  If you can, definitely do the same!

I admittedly have never had the "art house cinema" experience, but with that said I do embrace new things, people and places. So despite never hitting up the Dobie before it closed I was intrigued when I heard Violet Crown Cinema was opening on 2nd Street.

The first big plus is the free parking. If catching a movie at VCC, park in the AMLI on San Antonio between 2nd & 3rd street right by How Do you Roll?, bring in your parking ticket and VCC with validate it so you don't have to pay (good for up to 4 hours).

The second plus is they have a reasonably priced menu with lots of beer, wine and mixed drink options. The food menu is somewhat small and the only item over $10 is the Antonelli's cheese plate. I loved the cheese plate which had bread, honey, pistachios, and a generous portion of 3 types of cheeses. The mister had a pizza which was OK and on the small side. 

The movies do not have previews. It was nice to go watch a movie without the corporates forcing you to watch 15 minutes of trailers.

The Australian made seats are comfy and they have the old school table trays that pull out from the side. The one down fall is it is hard to find room for a plate of food and a drink. Speaking of food and drinks, you order outside the cinema in the lounge/bar area and carry it in yourself (although staff offered to help us carry it in).

Bad seat? One does not exist at VCC. Sitting in the front row will not put a crook in your neck but instead you get the lazy boy of the cinema chairs.

I adore this place and will be back.

Somehow managed to make it here with my love during happy hour or Monday madness -- something along the lines of cheaper drinks and lots of 'em. Let's just say half off all wine bottles under $50 is pretty super fantastic. 

This is your type A classy joint. Very nice, great atmosphere, after work hours drink, bring your secretary, knowledgable wait staff, friendly MGMT and hostesses. You know all the things you pay a decent dollar for. 

Order the edamame. So good! Pumpkin seeds and garlic and tons of butter. Basically, all I need in life. 

For the Main meal $33 steak and potatoes. Pretty standard and basic steak and potatoes. No complaints. Solid move on my part.

Over all good place. Will come back when the mood (or happy hour) is right. 

Go knock yourselves out folks! Dig in.

Extremely impressed with the atmosphere, food, and service of Veggie Galaxy (insert cool space noises here)

Not your typical diner, VG is modern dining meets old school service. Complete with classic radio, your standard bowling alley tables, and the ding of a bell every time an order is ready, they really embrace the feel of the restaurant.

The menu is what really blew me away though. A great array of breakfast, lunch, and dinner choices along with nice dessert options too. I ended up ordering the Chocolate Frapp with a club sandwich and a side of home made chips. A classic meal, all vegan.

The frapp was amazing, currently sipping on the last bits of it as I type this. The club was a perfect balance of "meat" and veggies, with a nice pesto to hold it all together. And the chips were classically sliced and seasoned. The sandwiches come with a side salad served underneath as well. My only hesitance was actually the salad. With a light vinaigrette, there's a great opportunity awaiting underneath my sandwich (literally). I'm imagining candied pine nuts or something else a little sweeter to balance out the savory of the chips and sandwich. Yin and Yang. Ya know?

Overall, very friendly service, great food, and a place I can see being PACKED on a weekend night or morning. Looking forward to returning soon!

Seedy and delicious.  This pizza place knows how pizza should be.  At least, I think they do.  It's not really clear, since they have 3 different sauces and 2 different crusts.  I recommend the Smokin' Joe's crust, which sort of has garlic butter pre-added for you.  Mmmmm.  They also have sauerkraut as a topping, and what's not to like about that?

If you dine in here... well, that's where the seedy comes in.  Their dining room is open 24 hours and the crowd is always colorful.  At 3am when you're up late with friends and you get hungry, you should go to Hounddog's.  Don't think, just do it.

Hello yummy vegan food!  Get in my tummy!

We tried this place for the first time yesterday, and I was impressed.  The menu was super extensive.  Many of the items were just variations of each other, though. There would just be a different sauce or a different combination of vegetables.  Stuff like that.   I was able to try four different dishes, and each one was delightful.  I liked Lucky Number 7.

The best part was after I had actually left the restaurant, though.  I felt wonderful!  It was just good, delicious food that actually nourished.  

Now, the reason for the one star deduction.  It's because of the space.  The restaurant is just too small.  They have too many table crammed in there and I didn't feel like I had much breathing/eating room.  I wish it would've been more spaced out.

Good frames.  Good pricing scheme.  Lenses included in frame price.  To get my annual benefit for insurance it costs more to use insurance than out of pocket.  Beautiful frames.  Especially like the limited edition frames.   No spring hinges so minus one star.  The suggestion that if you buy 5 you get one free kinda indicates that the type of clientele here isn't really me. For my 2017 benefit you'll find me at target optical. 

But I love the clearish shiny opalescent blue frames.   For that I might up my price point for my 2018 FSA use. 

The doctor is trendy.  Matches the store.  She is honest and kind.

This is one hota pizza piiie!  We had the ricotta fritter, awesome.  Crispy outside, creamy center, reminds me of the perfect chocolate chip cookie.  And the marinara wasn't to acidy. A great start 4 stars for the app.

We (4 peeps) shared a small "gourmet" Margherita and the grilled Bel Giardino.  Margherita came out so hot , I thought my tongue melted to the roof of my mouth.  Nice crisp crust, sauce lacked the some punch the marinara had in the app, cheese was tasty and not a drop of oil typically found with most pizzas.  The Bel Giardino, was the best grilled pizza I had in a long time, excluding my own backyard version of course.  It had the proper marinade to the veggies, and seasonings that explode in your mouth.  Margherita gets a 3 1/2 stars and the BG get 5.

Friendly staff and helpful with recommendations, not just your every thing is good b.s.  Overall a very good experience a return visit is required to try the sandwhiches and pastas.

After living in the North End for over 4 years, I had come to the conclusion that not only is it impossible to get a bad meal, it is also hard to say one restaurant is supremly better then another.  That is until  I came to Trattoria Di Monicas.  
I came New Years Eve and had the Chicken marsella.  It was delicious served with fresh motzerella and potatos.  I ordinarily would not have paired these two togeather but i am so glad they did.  It was a welcome change from pasta-which i get a lot of in this area! My boyfriend ordered the shrimp special which he loved.
It is a very small sitting area, which for two peopl is perfect, however I would never suggest this restaurant to anyone dinning with more then one other companion.
My ONLY gripe and unfortunatly for me this can be a make or break....is we were offered no bread! ughhh my favorite part of a north end meal! Since it was my first time here I wasn't sure they served it-or I would have asked.  Looking around when we left it appears they do, and we were forgotten about.  The fantastic food more then made up for this oversite, however it does knock them down a star.  I'm sorry I love me some carbs!

This is tasty, but because it has vegetables in it doesn't mean it's healthy!

These are hand pulled wheat noodles. If you have seen them in the making it's an art. All the stretching activates the gluten, making for a nice chewy noodle, unlike our noodles. Generally in the West, we boil our noodles. These are cooked in oil, and they absorb it, and all the flavors of the other ingredients. 

The chicken noodles, a bargain at $6.50 has a good amount of vegies and chicken, but the emphasis is on the noodles. It wouldn't be a bad strategy to take it home, divide into 4 portions and add your own vegetables. 

The spicy is covered with a nice coating of coarse chili sauce, but you will have to add more seasoning if you like heat. There is a large bottle of Sriracha sauce on the counter. 

It's great to watch the owner at the wok. Perfect timing. He formerly cooked at Du Kuh Bee.

Other countries discovered the allure of starch, oil, salt and spices, long before modern fast food, to captivate the tastebuds of their customers. That doesn't mean that  we shouldn't eat those foods across cultures, in moderation, today.

Brix kix ass!

This place is in the old T Flats location at Central and Magnolia. I think the room is a big improvement. It's small and cozy yet fun and lively and the high ceilings and large windows make it feel spacious. Great place to people watch and/or get out of the sun and suck down some suds. They have an amazing beer special: 12 Miller Lites for $10 all day every day. YES!

The menu is diverse enough to keep it interesting. Small pizza, burgers, fish sandwiches, and... fondue! My mahi mahi sandwich was perfect. They have the crispiest waffle fries you'll ever have in your life. Portions are a good size and prices are really fair.

The staff is attractive females and there are flat screens everywhere. I'm not sure if they're going for the sports bar crowd though. I need to go back when a football game isn't on. They might tune into CNN, which would be acceptable by this reviewer. 

I'll definitely return.

We never fail to get an amazing meal here!  Tonight's service was exceptional as was our food. The portions are huge and can never be finished that's for sure!  My scrod melted in my mouth as did the butternut squash!  The prime rib was humongous and came home with my husband as he barely made a dent in it!  His clam chowder was the best he's ever had!

Needless to say this place is fantastic. No reservations needed during the week. We just walked in and sat down right away. 

Thank you for an incredible night!!

The food was good, but the service was great. I had a margherita style pasta, and my husband had the house burger. The pasta wasn't exciting, but it was good enough. The burger was yummy. It was served on a hoagie-style roll, which was interesting. We liked the variety in the beer selections and tried a flight so we could taste several. There seems to be something for every taste, and we found a few we both liked despite our different tastes.

In the same buildings sushi yoko  (no sign outside?), this is the place to go for Japanese groceries on this side of town. It is small (and a bit creepy and eerie) but has a great selection of items (for cheaper than hmart for ex: japanese kit kats for $5 and pocky for under a $1) for cheaper than at the big supermarkets for japanese items. They also have more specialized items like fatty tuna and good instant ramen. There is another section for dvds and what not but I didnt look there. Also some cute girly stuff they bring in from daiso and what not. 

Overall, nice little grocery store for japanese items.

In terms of a GREAT Friday night dinner/ bar scene, I would definitely recommend checking out Estragon in the South End. Our visit here stemmed from a craving for a few drinks and some small plates. I had heard about the restaurant in passing from some friends, so really didn't have an idea of what to expect. 

First, parking was pretty easy. There are plenty of metered spots on the street and also plenty of resident parking if you're from the area. From my understanding, there are also a ton of bus stops nearby. The signage for Estragon is also very easy to spot from the street. 

We decided to sit at the bar for dinner, and honestly I'm glad we made this choice. The bartender Joseph was great the entire evening. He was careful to pay close attention to our needs from our arrival, all the way through our dinner, and with our final cocktails. The bar scene was also great throughout the night. Even with some very excited female patrons (someone had just gotten engaged), the atmosphere was well suited to a nice, intimate evening. 

In terms of food, here is a quick overview:

*** Queso de Cabra con Tomate (V) (Warm Goats' Cheese, Tomato on Toast) - This came with 2 long pieces of toast with a heaping amount of goat's cheese. You definitely have to cut the pieces to make them manageable to eat, but they are VERY good. 
*** Garbanzos Fritos (VG) (Crispy Paprika Chickpeas) - I think these were overrated. You can eat a handful as a snack and they're okay, but wouldn't order them again. 
*** Coles de Bruselas (Roasted Brussels Sprouts, Chorizo, Golden Raisins) - Very good side veggie dish. Would definitely order them again. Heaping portion too. 
*** Espinacas a la Catalana (VG) (Sautéed Spinach, Pine Nuts, Golden Raisins) - Again, really good choice for a side veggie dish. Good portion and well flavored.
*** Pulpito a la Parilla ( Marinated, Grilled Baby Octopus) - This was also a good dish, but you have to be okay with the whole head and body being part of the dish. Well seasoned and a good portion too.
*** Conejo a la Cazadora (Braised Rabbit, Tomato, Onion, White Wine) - This was a great meat dish aside from all the bones in the meat. It was a great flavor w/ the white wine and the pieces of meat were pretty big, but I spent a lot of time spitting out the small bones. It takes a lot of work to get through this dish. 

HIGHLIGHT****
DRINKS: We had a few different cocktails on the list and nothing really stood out as much as the Absenthe Special Cocktail with Absinthe and Angostura Bitter for $9 a piece. This was definitely something you need to try!! Again, our bartender Joseph was great with this part of our visit. He took the time to actually create an experience with the Absinthe cocktail, which made it that much more fun for us and other guests. He actually set up a tall glass holding pitcher which dripped the absinthe mix over two small glasses set up with sugar cubes. He also lit the cubes on fire to burn the sugar while the absinthe dripped into the glasses. It was really the best part of the visit, as I have never seen this done at another venue, ever. 

The total at the end of the visit was also expected. Although somewhat pricey (as tapas often is), we thought the value of the meal met the price well. If you're in the South End and looking for a great, unique dining experience, check this place out. And certainly try to go and sit at the bar when Joseph is around. He's fast paced, pays close attention to his guests and definitely makes the experience worthwhile with regard to the cocktails.

On a chilly, rainy December night, I met some new friends at Olympia Provisions so we could indulge in some of their legendary meats. No one left disappointed. The ambience there is top-notch: warm woods, moderate lighting, beautiful finishes. The wait staff was excellent and friendly, and then we had our meal.

Spanish charcuterie board - of the three varieties, the Spanish one spoke most to us and everything on it was delicious, from the meats to the nuts to the cheeses. Home run.
Sausage dinner - As much as many of the other menu items also sounded enticing, this place is known for their sausages, so for a first visit, I chose this. It was amazing. Flavorful and rich without being too heavy, the veggies and the fried egg made for a completely well-rounded dish. Yum!
Goat cheese cheesecake - A revelation. Well executed, perfectly balance and a non-overwhelming way to finish a meal. 

I can't wait to get back!

Chef Rob's certainly made an impression on my Caribbean palate. As a true island girl, it takes a lot for me to admit when island food is good but Chef Rob's was on point! I can only comment on the food as we had our food delivered. Overall, the food was great! I had the shrimp curry run-down that was very tasty! I usually don't like my food too spicy but this dish had the perfect balance where it wasn't too mild nor too hot - 2 thumbs up in that arena. I also had some conch fritters that came with a dipping sauce. These didn't blow me away. I've honestly had better but they weren't that horrible that I couldn't finish them. They were okay. 

The reason I give the restaurant 4 stars instead of 5 is for 2 reasons. 

Reason #1: They failed to make our substitution for rice and peas instead of jasmine rice. I was quite shocked to see a Caribbean restaurant have jasmine rice as their staple compliment to their dish. Rice and peas is the caribbean staple. You eat it with everything: chicken, shrimp, goat, ox tail, fish, beef. That jasmine rice just threw me for a loop. If that's the case, there shouldn't be an additional charge to swap out jasmine rice for rice and peas. It should be no cost for that. 

Reason #2: The prices are a bit up there for some Caribbean food. Don't get me wrong. The food is great but Chef Rob's will only get my business once or twice a month (and that's pushing it). For the shrimp run down and conch fritters, I was at about $25-26 and this was before tax and delivery charge. I consider this to be an indulgence, perhaps a reward for doing something good (eating well, losing some pounds, etc). 

Chef Rob's: Thank you for the yummy food on my trip to Atlanta but if I were a resident of the area, you would only see me on special occasions like tax return time or something :-) I still recommend that you try it and experience it for yourself. You won't be disappointed. Oh, and I also heard that the mango pie is to die for but I didn't get to taste it since my sis-in-law forgot to order it (why would she torture me so???) Happy eating!!!

I made my first foray to Lonesome Dove right about the time it opened, which is a tough period for any restaurant.  Except for Lonesome Dove, which displayed awesomeness right out of the gate.  Bartenders who were fast on the draw with some seriously tasty cocktails.  Crazy-inventive charcuterie.  (Don't miss the quail).  Unusual small plates that are worth constructing a meal out of, (rattlesnake sausage in particular).  BUT if you want to surf around the menu, 1) make sure you have a conspiratorial server and 2) hope chef Love ain't looking.  Apparently this is no-no, you're supposed to follow the order of the menu precisely, or else.  (You want your salad after your spatchcocked chicken? We'll meet you in the alley....). Other random comment: why the heck are the barstools too low for the bar? Does no one try before they buy these days?? Just don't take my usual seat in the middle please.  I'm the one with the booster.

Food: Pretty good.  The Sabzi Challow (like a lamb saag, but Nepalese) is delicious.

Service: Despite what other reviewers have experienced, I thought the servers were very kind and helpful.  All of my experiences there have been positive.

Ambience: The place is almost always empty, which is its main downside.  The table set-up can make you feel quite exposed, especially if you are one of the only parties dining in the place.  I think they'd do better with booths, which offer more privacy.  

Other: They currently have an EXCELLENT discount on take-out: 50% off the entire order.  Without this deal, I'd give the restaurant three stars, but this bumps it up to four.  We just ordered two dinner entrees, naan, and veggie pecoras for $19 including tax, and we have enough leftovers for another complete meal.  Go in and ask for a coupon.

One. Word: Samosas

Honestly, that's all you need to know. They are freakin delicious! Buuuut I guess I'll be a little more informative. I ordered take out for my work, and everyone's responses were positive. When you think of indian, you automatically think of curry. This place is not known for their curry. They do more sandwiches and salads. Many of my coworkers were skeptical, but once they tried their food, they were very pleased and pleasantly surprised. One coworker got the kale and let me tell you, that think is fried to the core. It's more like, can I get some kale with the fried batter. it was still really good, but really heavy and more than enough to share. I enjoyed my tandoori chicken salad, What I can appreciate is that the chicken portion is pretty large, compared to other places, that give you such small meat portions for salads. Overall, a good solid indian spot if you are looking for a cuisine other than curry.

We had a much better dinner here than we could've found in the theme park. Delicious food - two of us enjoyed the flatbread pizza & another the fish & chips. Fish was delicious & obviously fresh, not frozen. The $10 beer sampler was a great find. They had live music the night we visited so we ordered more beers & hung out for the rest of the evening. The only reason I gave 4 stars instead of 5 is because the service was a little slow.

We like it here, coming back for a 2nd time. We are not owners but enjoy it nonetheless. We had a 1 bedroom villa and it was perfect for us. Lots to do here and we like the short 9 hole Faldo practice course. All our needs were met and staff is friendly. We were missing a TV remote and an hour later we had a replacement and a call from the desk to make sure we had a replacement. 
Only issue is the paper-thin walls and floors. There are a lot of kids and families here and if you have an unruly bunch nearby, or a group who doesn't understand they are sharing walls with others, prepare to hear every scream, yell and stomp.

So the wife and I actually had a night out without the baby. A friend of ours offered to watch our little diva while we went out for dinner. It was just the wife and I. We were in the mood for sushi, no naturally my wife wanted to go to Saburo's for dinner. We drove out to Sellwood and as I was looking for parking I saw no lines, you think, great! But they were closed for the weekend and we got stuck with no sushi.

I quickly pulled over and looked at my Yelp app and asked the wife if she felt like anything, she thought about having a burger. I remembered driving by a Mike's Drive In and saw that it came recommended. She agreed and we went there.

It's a small little tiny place, reminds you of a place that high school students would hang out after the football game.  The wife ordered the Mike's Special Deluxe and I ordered the Applewood bacon burger. She upgraded her meal for a Marion Berry milkshake. 

The food did not disappoint at all. I thought it tasted really good. The burgers were not too greasy and the fries were cooked very well. That Marion Berry milkshake...oh yeah that was some really good stuff. 

A few weeks later we went here after playing basketball, this time her brother and my brother joined us as well. They ordered their meals but got soft drinks instead. Wife asked them...why didn't you upgrade? It's like $0.99 more. Her brother was like...really? So he upgraded his as did my brother. And the reaction was..."wow...that milk shake is really good".

I can defiantly see me dragging my daughter here for food in the future when she's old enough to hold a burger. Forget sushi...give me a burger!

Eat here! In an industrial complex, go all the way down to the end and you will find the Soursop truck and yard behind the fence adjacent to St. Elmo brewing company. Food can be ordered outside and eaten inside (to get away from the heat). While you're inside, catch a refreshing brew. Water dispenser is inside and complimentary.  Ordered the glass noodles (spicy just right) with a side of Som Tam....oh so good! The menu does change so was told Instagram posts updated menus all the time. I almost drove away as I couldn't figure out where this was, but so thankful I did not, because this is delish!  Worth the search for sure!!!

They serve slices, but I prefer ordering a whole fresh pie.  Has nice back patio for summer months.  Its definitely NYC style - thin and a large will serve 4 adults, 2 large slices a piece.  The salad was stellar here - v. large.  The bad news was our order for the kids "blew away" with the fan and was lost and we had starving anxious kids as we were served well before them.  We were given slices in place of the lost order, but I believe we should have been credited the pie or maybe its just because I couldn't stand the hunger meltdown of 4 kids under the age of 12.

Great new place in Boston! I had the lobster hole and mac and cheese. Both were delicious! The mac and cheese had a nice bread crumb crunch.  The lobster hole is their take on a lobster roll. I loved how buttery the brioche was in the lobster hole and the smell of the truffle mayonnaise. My only complaint is I wish it had more lobster meat. Ward 8 doesn't have a dessert menu yet but hopefully will have one soon. The drinks were great too!

Location, Location,Location!
Atmosphere, Atmosphere, Atmosphere!

I Loved It! I can go on and on to what makes a restaurant great! This place is hitting on all cylinders! From the Cool Entrance, to the very Social and Welcoming Host! To the Very Cool and Hip Decor, a Very Sexy Vibe comes over you when you walk into this place.

The open kitchen works in this space! The staff is a compilation of all the beautiful people in ATL, Loved it!

A party of 8ppl! 9:15pm, Saturday Night! The drinks were flowing, they pay attention the cocktails here, quality and presentation matter!

The food was great, presented well! Portions were just right! Salomon was amazing! The signature dish was the Steak and Pomme Fritte was perfect!

Pretty much looked like all high schoolers/college kids working but their customer service was outstanding. The owner of this location should be very proud of their employee selection. This was my first time at chick-fil-a restaurant.
We came because they offer an inside play area for children. Sadly not many places offer them any more. Food was good and the spicy chicken sandwich was way better than Wendy's. They have salads as well for any vegans out there. Great milk shakes and their lemonade isn't sickening sweet. Kids meals come with pretty good portion. 
Kids loved the play area and had a great first experience.

Being paleo is NOT fun when I think about never eating Gourdough's again, so I save this place for girls' nights and birthday treats, because there is NO WAY I'm missing out on the Nutella doughnut! It's not the only little slice of heaven either--pretty much everything on the menu is fantastic. 
I love the new brick-and-mortar place. The trailer was fine, but they were able to expand their offerings and service is so quick! I love how they managed to turn "the old Kerbey Lane" into a stand-alone place with it's own unique (hipster) vibe! They carry my favorite cider, and I always enjoy visiting. Worth the drive down South Lamar!

Reading the reviews of this place on Yelp, I was a bit hesitant to go.  I like to make my own decisions and with that I have to say my experience here was much better than most of the other reviewers.  I also never got here before they changed owners.  

I am originally from the east coast.  Some of you know that.  When I was younger, I wasn't a big hot dog fan.  The only place I would eat hot dogs at was Nathan's on Coney Island.  There was something about that place that made the hot dogs taste like the best things in the world.

Now I live in Portland, and don't get to Nathan's as much as I'd like to.  The mall versions just aren't the same.  Bring in Nick's Famous Coney Island.  Ok, I didn't expect to get the same thing I got at Nathan's, but the name still made me want to go.  That and the 2 for 1 coupons they offer that can be found in the local papers.   

The friend I went with likes to eat.  I like to eat.  This is a good place to do that and not spend a ton of money (with the coupon, that is).

The Coney dog menu has a few options.  The single, double, triple, home run and veggie Coney.  Prices range from $6.75-$15.  I'm sure you can guess the single is one dog, the double is two dogs and so on.  We went with...........wait for it................wait for it.............two triples.  In hindsight, two doubles would have sufficed, but when you have 2 for 1, you go for it.  The dogs come with a side of mac salad or potato chips.  Fries can be added for a buck.  Side salad for two bucks.

I should go back a bit.  The service tended to be a bit on the slow side, but everyone was super friendly there and I wasn't in a rush.  The bartender had a bunch of people she needed to take care of, but seemed to do it with a smile on her face.  The guy who ultimately brought us our dogs came by a few times to see how we were enjoying our food.  These are the little things that most places don't do that made my experience that much better.

With the knowledge that dogs were on their way, we ordered a few beers, took in the Atlanta Hawks-Miami Heat playoff game (Hawks won.  I am a fan.) and waited in anticipation for doggy goodness.

They arrived.  I wasn't quite sure how to eat them.  Covered in chili and cheese with a huge side of crispy potato chips, I decided to go with the fork and knife option.  I am usually a hands on eater, but there really wasn't a neat way to pick these up without dropping most of the contents on my shirt and subsequently on the floor.  Much rather the food was in my stomach and not on said floor.

I am not going to say that these dogs reminded me of Nathan's on Coney Island, but they were pretty good.  Had a nice snap when cutting into them and the chili with onions was very tasty.  This is also a meal I couldn't eat all the time.  So much food, but that isn't a bad thing.  I finished every bite much to the amazement of my friend as well as the bartender.  

So, hot dogs and beer.  Sounds like America.  Or something like that.  I enjoyed my experience here and plan on getting back again soon.  Hmmm.  Not the greatest ending to this review, but it is an ending.

Stayed at this property while rocking the 2011 Walt Disney World Marathon. The location was rather good, with striking distance to Epcot and the parks.  The bonus was that there was daily shuttles to Epcot and connections to the other parks thereafter from the hotel. While I didn't stay too long, I enjoyed my stay. 

My room was spacious and could fit 4 people no problem. The beds were comfortable and the rates were good. Did not use the hotel pool though.  Service was good.

We went to Maggiano's for the first time yesterday.

Good ambiance, good food (the bread is excellent!), and good service.  I must agree that the choice of ice-cream or lemon cookies for the kids meal dessert is a nice touch, and pretty good, too.

The only negative thing is the price.  It is a bit on the pricy side.  For 2 adults and one kid meal we ended up paying around $60.  I think that about $40 would've been a fair price.

All-in-all it was a pleasant experience, and we'll go again.

All the staff is genuinely very friendly.
And this place is a bit more affordable than other places!

I was recommended an earring that promptly came off my ear however when I returned, the piercer took care of me with no issues. Kind people.

Just note although you may have a bad problem with your piercing, you will wait the same amount of time as everyone else. The place closes at 10pm, they will not accept you past 7pm and the wait is 1 hr to 1 hr and 30 minutes. Fortunately, they have cozy seating, coffee, and games to play. They are also often out of ball earrings and have small selection.

Worth the hype and we enjoyed our dinner very much.  The staff was friendly and very knowledgeable about the menu.  The food was great and the flavoring was balance and strong. We tried a variety of dishes and enjoyed the majority of the dishes.  Oaxaca influences are apparent in the dishes and drinks we had. 

We had four dishes "para la mesa ( for the table) and two entrees and 1 dessert for two people.  You need to bring people to share and eat. My favorite is the octopus tostada because it had the most flavor out of all the dishes we ordered.  

The entree dishes, it was great but I would love to have a side or two with it or even tortilla serve with it.  I order a la carte the tortilla to eat with the entree as they don't really come with anything but that one fish or pork...just need something extra. 

Otherwise food and drinks - no complaint.  Happy Sharing!!

Been meaning to stop here for quite some time. I dig the whole industrial, concrete, steel gig they have going on. Nice street presence as you pass making you want to stop. (unlike one of the best Thai joints in town where every time I go I look at the outside of the place and can't believe I eat there. The inside is fine)   I digress 
So what does a person order at the Cafe? How can you not try their chipped beef on toast?  Out it came, perfect amount of toast to gravy, great flavors and texture. Side dish of fried red pots were exceptional- cooked to perfection. Crispy edges, soft inside. BUT here it comes- I'm not salt sensitive, if anything I find myself adding salt here and there- but not here! Put the industrial salt grinder out on display and return to a regular table sized shaker. Wholly cow was it all salty. Tongue pissed off on the way home salty.
Oh but- I was given such a good portion I had left overs and the next day wooo weee was it excellent. Still salty but the layering of flavors in the gravy is exceptional. I think they make this fresh for each order (?) if that's the case have them back off the salt a bit and you'll be happily lapping up the gravy.

Dessert- They called it chocolate pie. It was somewhat 'old' seeming very thick chocolate pudding in a cup over a chocolate crumb dust/not crust. Eh. Not my thing for $5. 

Service was great, place was clean and you could tell it's a neighborhood joint with some regulars at the counter. Nice

Yeah I'll go back

Well I went there today for my birthday.  Overall the food was great.  I repressed my urge to question how clean the kitchen was and just focused on the food.  I ordered the meatbahl calzone and it was damn good.  I also tried my friend's sausage one and that was great.  The space is small but it has a nice environment.

My biggest problem was that I asked if they could make a birthday cake and they said "let me tell the baker to call you," they baker never called.  I called again and was told that there wasn't anything.  I go in an BAM there is a poster saying that they make vegan birthday cakes!  Ok I feel cheated.  I got no birthday cake on my damn birthday.  That blows.  Do you understand how much that blows?  I was sooooo looking forward to eating a vegan cake that I didn't make myself.  So I'm leaving that to the damn dirty hippies not remembering.

Although I will eat there again.

Love the atmosphere, great for a quick bite or a leisurely dinner. The food was well presented and the staff was attentive. The limited parking lends itself to the person on foot walking the drag or for carpooling groups. The egg rolls were sweet, savory, and a great size for the price. I had the tofu stir fry, which name escapes me, and it had a lovely balance of salty and sweet. The fresh ginger slices cut through the salty fore-taste well and the rice served really filled it out. The fried banana puffs and coconut ice cream were to die for, honestly. I'm not a sweets person usually but I wanted the full experience and this is what sold it for me. The staff was also kind enough to let me take pictures, so that was nice. Great place.

I have been in here quite a few times, and each time has been a delight. I have tried their vegetarian tacos, and I appreciate that they aren't just comprised of beans and cheese. Their vegetarian tacos are truly one of a kind, and I never felt like I was missing out by trying them over the meat option. The portions are small (each taco is tiny), so I suggest the taco plate, which has 3 tacos and beans, rice, and guac. Be warned, it can be spicy (especially if you add the sauce). However, you can wash it down with some delicious horchata :)

Used clothes seemed a little gross at first, but this place is amazing. First of all, it seems like they must be pretty picky when they buy people's clothes because they're clean and look pretty close to new. The best part though is that the whole store is this collection of cute clothes, stylish clothes, strange clothes, racks and racks of them, shoes, jewelry, purses, everything; and most of it is pretty cheap, because it is "previously owned." I found this black v-neck with giraffes drawn in pink glitter on the front, tell me where else I would've been able to find something like that. I always end up buying a a lot of clothes here, and I get some good laughs just from looking around at some of the crazy stuff they have.

Culinary Dropout is a fun establishment right smack in the middle of the Domain. It felt very Austin to me and not so big box cookie cut for being in the Domain.

I will forewarn - it's busy here. Every visit was in the afternoon and felt like a late night party! They have so much going on it is not a place to relax at unless games are you thing.

The drinks are good but the prices to me seemed a dollar or two too high - prolly the domain tax. I have enough to know these bartenders make them so regularly that it is muscle memory at this point.

The appetizers were the first thing I ordered. My rule of thumb is you always get the Pretzels if a menu has them. They were amazing. The dip was fantastic as well. I'd got them every visit thus far.

The main's weren't memorable however by now I had enough alcohol to embalm an elephant! Looks like I'm about ready to start shopping at the domain now!

All in all it's a cool joint and one worth bringing a few friends to between stores for a drink and a pretzel. You can even waste the day away playing all of the funs games they have! :D

nomnomnom.  As my screen name implies, I truly heart sushi rolls.  I have been searching Austin for good sushi since moving here from LA in November and this place really hit the sweet spot in my tummy.  

My boyfriend and I shared a few dishes including the grilled chicken spring roll (nice and crispy, delicious dipping sauce), seaweed salad (standard but good), a spicy tuna roll (oh, LOVED this little one), volcano roll (oooooooooohmy), spider roll (crispy, hot, perfectly cooked) and the scallop sushi.  They had a lot of rolls with crawfish and the volcano roll looked the most appetizing to me - it was a California roll inside with crawfish cooked outside.  It was really tasty and had a slightly spicy/sweet sauce on top.  The scallop sushi was really divine.  It was buttery and completely melted in my mouth.  

This place is a little out of my price range to enjoy regularly but as a treat on a Friday night it was perfect.  Parking was impossible downtown so we valet parked which I completely hate but got over.  We arrived early enough (about 6:30) to be seated at the sushi bar but the room was packed by the time the normal dinner hour so I would definitely recommend reservations.  The service was great - everyone was so nice but not overbearing.  

I checked out the happy hour menu as we were leaving - they have a normal early hour happy hour AND a late night happy hour.  I will definitely be back during one of those time frames so I can eat twice as much sushi.

If you're looking for a fun themed breakfast joint - look no further! I came here a few weeks ago with a friend and we were immediately greeted by the friendly staff. I love that they let you put your now down on the No Wait App (not sure why everyone can't have that)! They have a lot of options on their menu, so it was hard to make a decision. Honestly, I wanted to try everyone on the menu. We ended up getting the homer pancakes and chicken and waffles. Their pancakes - WOW. Some of the best pancakes I have ever had. They're super fluffy and chewy and the cream cheese frosting was delicious. They were decorated like pink sprinkle donuts. The chicken and waffles were also pretty good. The waffles weren't anything to rave about but I did really enjoy the chicken wings. I would definitely come back here, but just an FYI they don't have very much seating to accommodate a large group.

I feel embarrassed to even write this review.  I don't get four stars for my actions here, maybe not even two.  Let's relive it anyway.

I had the boyfriend place an order here while I was at the store so that I'd go pick it up after I was done.  The only mistake they did make was to leave out the order of fried shrimp.  That made me think that the order of . . . something else, I don't remember what at this point, was something we didn't order.  So, I told him it looked like we got one wrong thing.  The man up front apologized, put in an order for the fried shrimp and left the "wrong" order in the bag (well, box, we ordered too much!).  I texted the boyfriend and found out I was wrong and he did order what I thought he hadn't.  I felt bad and tried to pay for it, but he was very insistent that I didn't pay for it and helped me on my way.  One small misstep on their part (leaving out the shrimp), but a much larger misstep on my part and they handled it much better than they should have.

So, when I got home, I really wanted to be able to give this place five stars.  Unfortunately, I couldn't quite do it.  The food was good, but not good enough for me to feel justified in giving out a five star review.  There's nothing wrong with it, but it's not better than Chinese food we've had at other places.  We'll go back and hope to be able to give them the extra star.

Oh god, this place will be the end of my wallet. I go here almost every pay day (for some reason) to just "look around," but I almost always end up with something as I walk out the door. Unfortunately (or fortunately for my wallet?), a lot of the stuff here are still too expensive for me, or actually, I could afford it, but I'd just feel extremely guilty if I do get it. 

However, compared to the original prices, you still get really, really good discounts. The last time I was there, I found a Kate Spade handbag for around $100 and it was originally around $260+ (ohhhh I was so, so close to getting it...) You can still find a lot of stuff that are affordable if you check out the clearance racks. They also have awesome deals on makeup and body and bath products. $20 for an Urban Decay palette that was originally $50+? Awesome! 

Can't wait for my semi-weekly visit to Nordstrom Rack to "look around..."

Wow, what a nice place to eat while visiting the museum! You'll find a few different counters here, one for quick pizzas and one for the rest. Pick out what you need, pay and they will give you a number for your table (if you ordered something requiring preparation).

Especially of note is that at the pizza counter they also serve Salt and Straw ice cream! Score! I don't need to go to the actual location to try some!

The food was good, I enjoyed the kale, potato and chorizo salad (although it was heavy on the dressing). The sandwiches come with chips and a dill pickle.

The place was clean and inviting and as soon as we were leaving, someone was already wiping down the high chair, which was nice to see knowing how well they take care of everything.

For what I am about to write may seem like a "two star"  review however, I beg to differ. So last night my friends and I went to Guilt and with the flashing lights and house music blasting.. it was just not good for the brain or my friend's slight cold SO we left some other friends behind in search of CURE. Got there at about 1 am and there were still people standing in line to get in. With my sometimes passive behavior I stood behind my friend while she talked to the bouncer to try to get us in right away. He told us to wait and we did. Two minutes passed and it felt like forever.. patience running low. Another bouncer steps out and said the club was over capacity - doors close - and told everyone to remove themselves from the line and sidewalk. We were not in line and actually hid right behind the bouncer. Another five minutes passed and some group of guys were let in before us! I was a bit paranoid but the bouncer reassured us to give him a second. A minute passed and we were let in - the bouncer ushered us in and told us not to pay the cover charge since we waited for SO LONG (total of 10 minutes or so) LOL Not long at all and I thought the men at the door handled it pretty well. I elt they accommodated us as best as they could while still following orders.

We got inside and thank goodness there were no flashing lights. The music was more hip hop and the room was actually quite tiny. I would have to say that the crowd here is more working professionals and the attractiveness level was higher than Guilt. Over all I would come here again.

Went here for lunch today with Lauren H. and baby C. Called ahead and made a reservation, which I would advise doing as the place is small and we still had to wait a few minutes for our table. Once seated, we placed our order. I got a pot of the hibiscus tea and it was delicious...and since it was raining on and off outside, perfect for the weather. I ordered the rustica salad, which was plentiful and flavorful. Lauren ordered the chicken salad sandwich. The portions are healthy and the service was superb. Certainly a great way to have a ladies lunch this rainy afternoon!

My wife and I had dinner reservations at another place with some time to kill, so we dropped by here to try the Spanish coffees that I've heard so much about.  We sat right at the bar (which was definitely the seats to be in) and watched the bartender razzle/dazzle us with making the coffee drinks.  They are very alcoholic tasting, so not really my cup of tea, but we still enjoyed the experience and were glad we tried it.  The ambiance also is nice with a really old room, neat woodwork, and small cafe-style seating.

This place is perfect for a post theme park chow down. Enjoyed a foot-long chili cheese dog and fries here. I've had the corn dog nuggets in the past and they were wonderful. The foot-long hotdog is definitely a good size to share unless you're starving and the fries are extra crispy with a nice coating and flavor. You can order on the Disney mobile app and skip the line and just wait for your food order to be called out. That's a much more convenient process and I would suggest it if possible. I felt like all the counters and tables smelled like onions and sauerkraut, were sticky too, but I guess that's what a busy theme park has to deal with!

Excellent happy hour.

We came in just before it ended and ordered spicy roasted cauliflower with pine nuts, a simple margherita pizza with home-made mozarella, and fettucine with pistachio pesto. Yum. Yum. And yum again!

Between the tasty food and the warm decor, we were surprised that we were the only ones in the place. Weird!

Our server was very nice. Attentive, but not smothering.

The only reason I can't give five stars is due to the music. Techno. For the entire time we were there. Maybe, with a few more drinks in me, I could've tapped into the sound and ran across the tables, but it seemed a bit much for a 5pm light dinner.

Feets don't fail me now!  When your dogs hurt,  your whole life can suffer.  No jumping jacks, no jump lunges, no stairmasters, no dancing in high heels.  Oh, wait, only one of those sux to be without.  Still, sometimes just walking around can be painful, and even tho I do enjoy laying about with my feet up, it can make you cranky to have work all day on your ouchy feet.  

So, thanks to Dej (who is in my shoes, so to speak), I checked out Dr Godhania yesterday.  One thing I have learned firsthand is, when you are searching for a doctor, don't pick one based on name alone.  I thought my last guy would really be able to sympathize with me as his name was Dr Payne.  Wrong, wrong, wrong.  He spent months on me and made me some "custom orthotics" that did not address my issues at all (he thought I had bunions, the catchall diagnosis for toe pain).  

Dr Godhania on the other hand (foot), did a little mashing around (ouch!) and some x-rays and nailed my diagnosis, sesamoiditis.  Great!  I already knew that as I have the internet.  He was very straightforward about the treatment options, very explanatory about my films, and very encouraging about my future in exercising.  He has sent me on to get yet another set of custom orthotics made, but he swears these will be the be all, end all of, well, them all.  

So I am reserving a star for future results.  I really, really hope he gets that 5th star!

I liken Casey's to Tony Parker of the San Antonio Spurs. A total diamond in the rough.. you wouldn't know it was there unless you literally drove down 51st or by hearsay. The place is kind of obscured by trees and is sort of behind/next to a convenience store. If you're driving down Airport, all you see are a bunch of people lined up to a decrepit looking building! I for one, never knew this place existed until a friend told me about it while I was waxing about Sno Beach. Apparently Casey's has been around over 15 years!! WTF?? 

Anyhow, after letting me try about 20 different samples and combinations, I decided on the Boston Creme Pie.. wow.. really good! It tastes just like it!! The only problem I have with this place is that they put way too much syrup on the ice to the point where it's kinda disgusting. The only ones I can tolerate are the creamy ones b/c they put less syrup in those. In fact, a good tip is to eat half of your snow cone in the hot weather and letting the syrup concentrate in the bottom half.. then get some more ice for free! It tastes so much better with the syrup diluted!

I'm in Austin for work and found this place while driving around.  For some reason it felt like a good place to eat plus they had valet.

Upon entering I was greeted with a friendly smile and seated immediately.  My waiter came right over and brought me some popcorn to nibble on.  The popcorn was seasoned and delicious.

I ordered tortilla soup and a chicken salad.  The soup was brought quickly and it was yummy.  The small size soup was a nice portion and seasoned to perfection.  I was warned the salad may have a little bite.  I waited for my food and people watched.  The customers were a mix of mostly corporate with some casual.

My food arrived and the salad was super good! and came with jalapeño muffin cornbread.  The only reason they get 4 stars is because you gotta knock my socks off to get 5 stars and I don't typically go goo goo over just a salad.  Awesome spot!!

A friend and I came here for lunch after hearing about the restaurant's creative "Tip" and "Tap" concept. The open, airy atmosphere with large front windows still gives the location a cozy feel. Service is very attentive and welcoming, and the staff knowledgable. The menu is inventive and caters well to all palettes, including meat lovers and vegetarians alike! The beer selection is terrific and pairs well with any of the dishes. I loved the Tofu Tips. Well-seasoned, flavorful, colorful--tasty bites from beginning to end! Definitely worth a visit!

"I cheated on Kure and all I got was this stupid cashew milk."

No, that's harsh.

I like this place, but their cashew milk doesn't measure up to the bottled magic at Kure.

I had a really tasty smoothie here once (Avocado Dreamin') and usually the employees are extra friendly but the last time I popped in for a bottled cold-press, the girl working was a bit awkward.

I want to try more of their juices, though! Definitely not writing Greenleaf off, I'll just keep getting my cashew milk elsewhere :)

If there were half stars, they'd get 4.5. The only reason they lose a half a star is because the tables for two are microscopic! I felt guilty about taking a table for four, for our party of 2, so we were kind of squished. 

But onto the food! 

Sandwiches here are above par, way above. I had a tuna melt, my standing Tuesday lunch date had the special panini. Both were fabulous, on ciabatta bread; grilled to perfection but not so much that they produced the "cheese grater" effect on the roof of your mouth. Both were accompanied by chips and pickles. I had an Italian soda that was nice, and we shared a really yummy brownie with peppermint crunch on top. 

They also have great soups and other sandwiches. 

A nice shop, clean, comfortable, but the tables for two could be more user friendly. Also - there is a bar seating area and the assortment of bar stools were positively odd looking. Given that the rest of Rosemary's is so tastefully decorated, one wonders what happened. I'll be back again...maybe for breakfast.

I alternate between giving my clothes to Sig's and to Professional Cleaners in the shopping center across the street, both of which are on my way from home to just about everywhere. I'm not sure why I won't just pick one.

I'm not quite as enamored with Sig's as everyone else, but I do leave it feeling warm and fuzzy, and I've never been disappointed with my clothes.

However, I'm not a fan of the not accepting credit card thing. They accept any check, which mitigates it slightly, but you can really rack up a huge bill on dry cleaning, and I don't want to have to think about bringing my checkbook or a slightly unpredictable amount of cash.

I came to SoulCycle at Beacon Hill for my first SoulCycle experience. I absolutely loved the class that I took with James -- it was nothing like any other fitness class I've ever taken. The 45 minute spin class literally flew by in the dark and packed room of blasting music. It was like a giant spinning-dance party with a central theme/focus (similar to a yoga class where the instructor talks you through your class). I felt connected to my thoughts, my feelings, and my physical being all while getting in a great workout! You really have to experience it for yourself to understand what SoulCycle is.

The staff was very attentive when I checked in and they were very helpful in helping me get set up for my first class. 

My only complaints are how crowded (and small) the locker area is between classes and how little instruction I got during the class itself. Luckily I had taken a general spin class before so I was not completely lost, but there was another person new to SC next to me who seemed confused about several movements during the class.

I honestly can't figure out why this place has gotten bad reviews. I live in the neighborhood and have been there several times. The BBQ won't make you think you're in Kansas City or anything but it's on par with other things in the area. Their smoked wings are really good as well. I think the price is a bit high on some stuff but then again, prices are up everywhere. 

The place went through a full renovation a little while ago and the inside is beautiful. The service has always been good. I sat at the bar one time during happy hour and they had a great late night happy hour menu and good drink specials.

I never really went beyond South City but this week for a reason which I won't disclose I did and I saw - Lure, it's own by the same corporation as South City, they are more focus on seafood.  The place is nice, easy, which works for people like me who travel and get out of the office late (9pm) and want some tasty food before head back to 4Seasons/Marriott.  The oyster were fine, the cocktail was a suprise and the Florida grouper was my favorite regardless where ate them.  In FL, they are the best, it's a suprise to find them outside of FL, a must have if you eat fish !!

I have never been inside the bar for more time than it takes to use the bathroom, and during my limited visit indoors, I observed very little because it's incredibly dark. There are stuffed animal heads on the wall wearing comically oversized medallion gold chains, think Run DMC circa 1986. There are projection screens, presumably for sporting events. I can imagine this is a different bar when a game is on.

So, you may be wondering how I am enjoying this establishment if I don't even enter it. Oh, my, let me lay it on ya. Hitting up the River Pig and finding a stool on the loading dock is where it's at. It's your own little perch on which you will enjoy people-watching first and foremost, but also Portland's Finest Bowl, a Pickle Back, and the stiffest drinks this side of the river.

The Portland Bowl is the epitome of a good warm weather meal. It's light and packed full of flavor. It's the right amount of perfectly healthy food to curb your appetite for something tasty while simultaneously allowing you to consume more booze calories guilt free.  Which is good, because the barkeeps here really do sling stiffies.

As for the Pickle Back. It's yum. Trust me. I am a pickle fan. I am an even bigger whiskey fan. Combined, the two develop an almost super power. Delish.

Disclaimer: I've only been here once.

Setup: This is an all-you-can-eat where you walk in, throw ingredients in a bowl, add some sauces based on either several suggested guides or whatever you think is a good idea, and then they cook it on a huge metal surface with swords (seriously).

Recommendations: PAY IN CASH, follow one of the suggested sauce guides with minor variation, and I'd go heavy on veggies rather than proteins (less meat/tofu, more veggies).  Get a very full plate as many of them (especially leafy greens and tomatoes) will cook down to a much smaller pile.

Pros:

* Lots of great, fresh ingredients for a variety of palates

* A remarkable number options in the way of stuff to spice and flavor your food

Cons:

* Be aware that at checkout the default "suggested" tip is WELL above the generally accepted food service minimums (18/20/25%).  My food was great but really all you should be giving is 15% for a place that's only doing drink service.  Also, I give the guy at the grill $1 because that dude was on point.

* The spinach didn't look great when I was there.

Wishlist:

* A little clearer explanation about how things work for newcomers.
