* Would like to see partial coverage of the various sauces (e.g. the top half of the container being covered).  I know all that stuff is very stable in an open air environment and gets cooked anyway, but it just seemed a little *too* open.

Continuing our 2013, "Around the World in a wheelchair tour" the only reason I give Le Cellier 4 stars and not 5 is due to the poor interior design coming from a newbie wheelchair user.  At the entrance there is very little seating/waiting area for a chair, while I did find an area somewhat out of the way, I ended up waiting outside so that other visitors wouldn't have to brush up against the chair or knock over my crutches.  

Access to the dining area was okay, but tight between the tables, I can see why this is one of the harder reservations in Epcot to get, there just isn't enough seating, even with tables crammed in together to keep this romantic and inviting.

Our service was stellar, the light up menus was a nice little techno-nod to all things Disney.  Started with bread basket, Charcuterie plate and Canadian Cheddar Cheese Soup, it all matched perfectly.  Fine dining for sure.

My MIL and I opted for the Filet Mignon we both inhaled the meal, the Mrs. had the Lobster Macaroni & Cheese along with a salad and cheese plate for her meal.  That Lobster mac was amazing!!!  I was lucky to snag a bite prior to the elbows coming up to protect the rest of the plate.

The littlest one had the kids Seared Salmon, really we should have sent it back, frozen fish and well, it tasted like the freezer.  Coming from the land of fresh wild caught salmon of the Pacific Northwest, this was a major let down.  But it was made up by the kids Chocolate Moose, just google the image, it was cute and tasted pretty darn good.

Staff was very friendly, spot on with the refills of water, bread and oh my the butter....

Yup, we'll be back!!!!

For me there are only a few things that make a gym good: quantity of routes, diversity of routes, and the people it attracts.

MetroRock really does a great job on all three. The route setters aren't just technical crimp climbers or jug setters with huge dyno moves. These guys dream up some of the weirdest and coolest sh!t ever. Sometimes I look at routes and think they can't be done and after a while working on them I can only see beta. This gym is great for that. Lots of opportunity to grow your mindset on how to climb. 

The quantity is good as well - as others have mentioned this place can get busy but more often than not you can find plenty of climbers to share beta and that's a huge part of climbing. Learning how you climb and taking bits from equal or stronger climbers is a great way to push yourself and become a better climber and everyone here is pretty cool. It's rare to find a climber that won't cheer you on even if you are just working V1,2,3. 

Although I don't often find myself utilizing the whole gym - I have tried out some of their top rope and lead and even on busy nights I can usually find a few open lines to work and they seem to be pretty unique/diverse as well. 

As a side note - they run a shuttle from the Wellington T stop for free so even if you live in the city and don't have a car there is an easy way to get out and back.

My friends and I were hungry around 10 and this was one of the few Thai food trucks that opens late until 11. We specifically wanted to try a food truck but the only things that were open were all shwarmas which we weren't craving. After a quick search on yelp we came to this. We ordered a mango smoothie, crab puffs, pad Thai tofu, pad sew ew chicken. The mango smoothie was so refreshing after a long day in the city. The crab puffs had actual crab in it unlike other places where it's filled only with cream cheese. Everything was so affordable and delicious, gotta love Oregon for its no tax. The old man serving us was so nice and sweet too, I would gladly come here again to give him business.

Hi, I do not agree with the other review for the Monarch building by Charlie.
I love living there!
People at the front desk and office are very nice.
The maintenance people are super helpful and on top of anything that goes wrong.
They have changed the dog rules and are very strict about pets urinating by the front entrance.
The carpets do suck, I agree, but they provide with free carpet cleaning twice a year.

I've been there for over a year and if you renew your contract they are very generous and willing to re-negotiate your lease.
It is perfectly located and so close to everything!!
Yes, they charge for parking, but who doesn't in downtown!!!
I have never had any experiences with anything falling from the building/other apartments into anything or anyone.

Remember that this apartments were originally built for sale and not lease, therefore the walls are cement thick and you cannot hear any of your neighbors most of the time (no people walking loudly on the apartment above!!!)

I really recommend the Monarch if you can afford it and are a pet lover!!

We dined last Saturday night to celebrate my father-in-law's birthday Disney Style - watching the Magic Kingdom Fireworks from a window restaurant overlooking the lake.

The restaurant is beautiful - decorated in soft creams and lighting. The bar is small but served a variety of fun cocktails as well as descent wine. Not sure about beer but I think the selection was small. Nice atmosphere.

We started with little neck clams in a broth of cilantro - perfectly cooked and seasoned followed by several snapper dishes. My husband had a whole deep fried fish, while I had a crunchy skinned filet! My 8 year old ordered a steak from the kid's menu and finished off with "Make your own S'Mores!" 

Our served was great and my father-in-law left with a BIG smile on his face.

We will go again next time we visit the Mouse!

Coming from California, I've seen some of the greatest botanical gardens...Huntington Gardens in San Marino, The Arboretum in Arcadia (famous for the legendary Tattoo yelling out "Da plane, da plane!" in the 1970s Fantasy Island)...but enough about those other more spectacular gardens.

It's true, Zilker does not stack up to those California beauties, but for Austin it's not too shabby, it's free, and it makes for a whimsical adventure with your folks from out of town, your significant other, your imaginary friend... 

Regardless of who you're with, it's always a pleasure to gaze at the enormous koi in the Oriental garden, or attempt to cross the pond using the stepping stones without falling in.

p.s. If you don't want to pay for the parking and don't mind a short hike, try parking at the Stratford Lane entrance to the Town Lake Trail.

Delicious veggie friendly food.  I came here for breakfast and ordered their breakfast burrito with a side of hash (which has yam in it!).  My burrito was HUGE.  I could only eat about half of it and ate the rest of it for lunch later that day.  I wished there was cheese in it because as soon as I cut into it, it would fall apart.

I also had a bite of my friend's Hick's benny and I loved the addition of the yam in the benny.  The cornbread was good too.  

Service was pretty good, granted we were one of three tables the whole time we were there.  They also have free wifi and a bookcase of boardgames and reading materials.  Will definitely be back to try some of their other offerings.

Not a big fan of French food but it was pouring rain, so we stopped in to check it out. Our server (Travis aka Leroy) was great and made us feel welcomed. Extra plus he was tall, handsome and generous.

I ordered the lamb chops and they were wonderful. Cooked to perfection and very juicy. My coworkers ordered the Coq Au Vin and Salmon, which I taste tested and those dishes were also great. Menu has alot of options.

The crowd is mature and very well dressed.  Seemed to be coming in after work. 

The bathrooms were separated and very nicely decorated.  Weird point but I like when restaurants have nice bathrooms. 

Very close to the Buckhead Marta.

I stopped by when I visited Austin for a weekend. I saw this place from other Yelpers checking in. I got one french macarons of each flavors. They were delish!!!! they were exactly how it should be. Crunchy outside and soft inside. You get one or two mini macaroons for checking in. Sometimes they run out so don't always expect it. Service was great and friendly. This is such a cozy cute place. I see myself spending time here on my next visit!

Located on South Cobb Drive not far from the Windy Hill intersection in a shopping center shared with Dollar Tree sits this Autozone location. 

I will start off by saying that if you are in a hurry, you may want to re-think a visit here. This place is ALWAYS busy, so be prepared to wait! One reason they are always busy is the next closest auto store has very limited hours, so the line here builds pretty quickly, especially after 7:00 PM. 

Service wise, they are pretty decent. Seeing that they are always so busy, it is word to the wise that you know what you are after before making your way up to the counter, as they are ready to help and get you moving. The staff are always multi-tasking and running multiple registers at one, showing folks where things are, testing batteries, going outside, etc...it's a site to see. 

Overall, this is the run of the mill Autozone. It is a tad bit smaller than the free standing, so definitely look online before coming in a their stock is not as expansive as other locations. 

Seeing I live right around the corner, this location will continue to be my "go-to"!

I came to sunstone on the recommendation of a roommate who took classes there regularly for about a year. It was my first hot yoga experience. I signed up for the 10 for $10 deal and took 6 classes over 10 days. After the promotional deal was over, I received a couple calls for them about signing up for a membership, but refrained on account of not being able to justify both a gym and yoga membership.  A few weeks later, however, I purchased a 10 class card which I JUST finished, over a year later. yikes. Lately, though,  I've been going to hot yoga twice a week and practicing 3x a week.The key for me, I think,  is going in the morning. I love arriving a few minutes early and napping in the hot room on my yoga mat in Shivasana before class starts. I was initially a little skeptical of the who hot yoga/bikram thing, and I don't think all the sweat your toxins out hoopla is correct, but something about the heated room is really awesome. Now that I do both hot and not-hot yoga regularly, I can attest to the fact that hot yoga does help you stretch further, deeper, and better. You leave feeling invigorated, and your skin looks awesome. 

Sunstone's strong points are that it is clean, quiet, and really convenient for me. I've heard people complain about smell in hot yoga studios and that is NOT the case here. The instructors are really nice, enthusiastic about yoga, describe the postures really well, and correct you as they see fit. The studio provides mats and towels, sells water, has tea in the waiting area, and stock the showers with bath supplies and clean bath towels. I also like that they offer 1-hour classes in addition to 1.5-hour classes that are more typical of the stricter bikram. I can't sit through 90 minutes, but 60 is perfect. 

The rooms leave a little to be desired...the air conditioning is a bit loud and I've was dripped on by condensation once, however, I don't know that these things can necessarily be helped in a room that has to be maintained at almost 100 degrees and 60% humidity. I also wish they had more classes,  but I'm sure this must depend hugely on the volume of clientele at the studio. Also, initially, I was turned off by the sales-yness and the high cost of yoga, but the class cards work really well for me, and I haven't received any calls or emails since immediately after my promotional deal ended. Sunstone's prices are cheaper than or comparable to other non-donation based studios, and they discount your membership if you are under 25, which I really appreciate since I am not a student.

My fellow Yelpers never let me down! I needed a florist to send a bouquet to a friend at her office. Looking at the reviews on Yelp, I chose Blooms of Dunwoody and was not disappointed.

Scrolling through their floral arrangements, I saw an option for "Designer's Choice Special" - this option allows the designers to choose the flowers but gives you a bigger value for your money. Sounds good to me, so I selected that option...the process is very simple: select your price point, occasion and recipient (you can choose to add extras like chocolates if you want) and provide the zip code. That's it...you then go to checkout and done! 

Not only was the process efficient, but the flower arrangement was lovely. My friend sent me a photo of it on her desk. Two thumbs up for Blooms of Dunwoody...

Oh how I LOVE Piece of Cake and how my waistline despises me afterwards. I frequent this location and the one in Decatur. I prefer this location because it has a swankier feel. Piece of Cake is great for ladies like me who can appreciate a great cake slice and not a wimpy cupcake. (Don't worry they have those too) Strawberry, white chocolate, caramel, pound, banana, key lime, carrot ugh I've never had a piece I didn't like. Plus the slices are massive, it can easily feed a good two or three; or a greedy one. For the non cake lovers, which I don't see how you would come here searching for something other than cake...they have ice cream pints/gallons, cheese straws, cookies, bars, probably lots of other things but I head straight for the cake. Thank goodness they're closed, I would go in my pj pants right now and get a slice lol.

As per closure of another place I wanted to try out, roommate pointed us here. Came in about 15 minutes before closing time; staff didn't seem real enthused but was cheery (enough) anyway. Prompt, generally friendly, service. Inside of Arleta is very homey, like your weird friend's parents' kitchen: weird paintings, lots of wood, slow-cooking style vibe. My companion and I had some sort of bacon-y scramble with a bunch of awesome vegetables. Better than average fair. Came with toast and potatoes I think. Price about $8-10. Jam or whatever it was that came in shot glasses was ridiculously good. Seriously, like buy-it-to-go good. Found the portions a little small, but still very filling or my poor hungover stomach. Not too greasy, not too dry. I have had better breakfast potatoes however. 

Overall, will probably be back.

We came into the Ginger Man for a few rounds of beers before dinner and were not disappointed. They have a great selection of mostly Texas beers with almost any type or style to fit what you desire. The bar is long, spacious and comfortable enough to keep you there a while. Our service was perfect as any bartender was eager to refill an empty glass. Also, out back they have a cozy open air space with great views of the downtown area. Thanks!

--Out Of Town Visitors Burnside Pubcrawl stop #4--

Three votes for best sunset view of downtown Portland. 

I wasn't sure about a winebar fitting into the theme of our outing but there was talk of a rooftop bar with a view and it sealed the deal. Oddly enough I have recommended Noble Rot a few times for the view but had yet to be up there.

The bar is swanky and dark but much less daunting on this slow summer Monday night. We ordered a round of Jameson and sipped them till the sun went down and our ride to the airport was due to depart. 

The view is nice, and a fitting end to this impromptu tour of East Burnside and Portland.

Little hard to see this place since there isn't a large sign. Small chalk board sign that says "Craft Hot Dogs." Service here is incredibly slow. After ordering t cashier was over chatting with her friends and the other worker was playing on her phone. The hot dog itself was ready in a few minutes after getting started. Why the 4 stars with such bad service? Because the hot dog was just that good. I went with the "Hangover." They have primo beef hot dogs just bursting with flavor. The egg on the hot dog I got was an incredible touch and added another layer of complexity and texture to the hot dog. The crispy pancetta is a perfect addition to the dish. Overall, highly recommend this place if you're looking for a good hot dog. Will definitely be returning to try another menu item.

A pretty cool spot that has a modern design and trendy vibe. The service can be a bit slow (while waiting in lounge area) but was pretty good once we were seated. The menu here has both Anerican and Italian fare. We ordered a wide assortment of dishes to share as a group as we were not too hungry. The standout dish for me was the special prime rib eye of the day and the short rib pappardelle dish. The beef carpaccio and fried brussel sprouts were also good. The best & burrata salad was refreshing. My friends enjoyed the calamari more than the tuna poke. Overall, a cool place to check out. I will come back and enjoy some cocktails here.

I really wish I could give 4 1/2 stars because Benihana's was so close to being a 5 star experience. 

We arrived during the lunch service, lucky us because it is way cheaper to eat here during lunch hours! The bad part about this is that I think we arrived at a time when staff was still arriving and prepping for dinner service. There was only one table sat, yet we waiting close to 10 minutes for a table.

Once we were sat there were no more complications. Our server was very friendly and attentive to us all throughout our meal. Our chef was very funny, not too loud and obnoxious, and talented (of course). His comedic timing was perfect and he really put on an entertaining show for my kids. They really enjoyed him. I think the funniest part, for me, was when he tried to launch some shrimp tail into his hat...but they went into his shirt instead. I guess they were a little hot. Poor guy, but it was funny non-the-less.

The food was very good, a little gristly fat in the chicken that I couldn't eat, but other than that good stuff. My son said it was the best restaurant he can ever remember eating at ever. Ha, cracks me up! I took him to a 5 star restaurant before with the 5 star food, and he likes Benihanas more. lol. Funny thing is, he usually doesn't even like rice, but he devoured it at Benihanas. 

I could tell management wanted to ensure happy customers. I believe the manager or owner was watching the dining area from afar. Love that. Would be even better if he casually greeted customers and asked them how everything was. We would have said "excellent" and given some big kudos for the staff who catered to us.

We'll be back, but definitely hitting the lunch service if we have the kids in tow. Lunch portions, by the way, are plenty big enough for most people.

Had lunch here on a Friday.  Arrived at 12:30.  Parking was a breeze.  Receptionist was warm and eager to share her favorites off the menu.  The waitress was close behind and equally enthusiastic.  So far so good.  Then I noticed that the ambience was conducive to conversation.  My lunch companion and I talked for over two hours and unlike most Austin places, we were not bothered by loud music, noise or a staff that wanted us out the door in a hurry.  The pleasantness of this place is key but the food is worth mentioning.  There were several great choices on the lunch specials menu.  My companion had the Shrimp Tostada and I had the salad with calamari.  We couldn't resist the cauliflower flan and roasted butternut squash.  Both side dishes were excellent.  Overall, the food was a cut above the usual Austin lunch fare--- if you want highly structured, well presented, complex flavored food.  In other words, if you are a hamburger, taco or pizza lunch person,--this is not the experience you are looking for.  I would say this is a Foodie's place.  Having said that, I would return 60% because the atmosphere and service are perfect for lunch.  If you are solely interested in food quality, then you can find fancier and more expensive but as a whole, this place is a good Austin option with personality.

Awesome place to watch the fireworks on July 4th. The Esplanade is a long stretch across the East side of the river. It's closed to car traffic and so pedestrians have free reign over some prime spots to just hang out along the water. There's access to it if you walk down from the Convention Center or if you head down from Belmont. 

Some sculptures to see along the way and just great night time views of the city.

*Certain bridged areas are pretty close to the water level and probably will get you splashed on a bad weather day with strong currents!*

(- 1 *) Needs food carts!!!

17 4-star reviews, including mine. 

Milk Bar is becoming a cool hangout, away from the idiocy of downtown and the cig smoke of so many other bars...

The beer list is growing nicely, with probably over 100 beers to choose from. A menu will help you decide what to pick, because this is not a Bud Light/sports bar. It's a place to meet a couple friends, listen to some music and talk. Imagine that, a place where you can have conversations. I've been a few times, and it seems to be getting better, with better music, cool movies and interesting patrons. The artwork is getting better too. 

The only key drawbacks I find are the limited space for mingling and the lack of a proper outside hangout area (for the puffers). There's only so much that can be done with the space, but they are making the most of it. I'd say it's best to go with a date or with a small group.

Check it out some night, and enjoy a nice craft beer. Staff is friendly too.

I normally don't go to nail salons inside a mall for one reason- overpriced. I came to South Shore Plaza to shop but then saw this and thought to myself #TreatyoSelf! Recently getting another job on top of my full time was definitely calling for a spa night and pampering!

As soon as I arrived I was told to choose a color and was seated at the spa for my pedicure. I usually get a regular mani/pedi and almost always get the pedicure packages when the manicurist asks and indeed she did and I said yolo! to additional $17 to a regular $28 spa pedicure. The spa pedicure deluxe came with foot/leg scrub and massages it thoroughly then gets hot towels for your legs and then a stone foot/leg massage (THE best feeling, I could have literally sat there all night!)--total worth the extra $17!

My manicure ($15) was alright, I showed a design (the tips to be glittered only) but the manicurist did not know how to do the design that I showed. But it's alright since it was a regular manicure and not gel. She pretty much painted my whole nail with the glitter then went back again on just the tips... but she was nice and very helpful, so I didn't mind it.

I would definitely go back here again. I had a wonderful experience! :)

Services: 4/5
Cleanliness: 5/5
Price: 5/5

I have been here in the past several years in January. I really like this place for lunch and today's experience was just as good as my past luncheon visits.

Most cocktails are $12 here. I enjoyed their peach sangria for $12. Kathy had a mimosa and a glass of silver peak chardonnay. We both shared and enjoyed the Fulton's seafood tower 2 for $45. Our total bill less gratuity was just under $100.

Our server Josh took care of our needs. I decided to upgrade my rating from 3 stars to 4 stars. Check out my most recent pics.

I plan to return here again next January.

I had a pretty good veggie taco here and a chicken tamale, which was out of this world and CHEAP. I'm ready for more. the boy working here were really didn't want to be there, but If i was a teenage boy i probably wouldn't want to be working at a taqueria either. Really the tamale was delicious, get me one now! (Plus they weren't out of horchata, which it seems like every mexican place i've been to recently has been). I also really like the tablecloths.

Carter's is crack for moms. They make well-made, soft, inexpensive, cute clothes for babies and toddlers. You can get the brand at most of the big box stores, but this is straight-up and direct from the source. Lots of good sales, coupons, and other enticements lure you in the door and make it impossible to leave without an armful of new duds for your favorite munchkin. If you have a little issue with buying too many cute things for your kid (and I'm not saying I do) stay far, far away.

Savor, as noted, is in the Westin Atlanta Perimeter hotel.  I can only review the restaurant as a hotel guest. Savor has a good menu with some variety.  My personal favorite is either the Tower Burger or creating my own grilled chicken sandwich.  The bacon on the sandwiches is very good and they have a very tasty chipotle aioli sauce.  They staff is relatively quick in turning around food orders, but the order is rarely 100% correct.  Thus 4 stars, good food, but could improve in accuracy of orders.

Once upon a time they were near Grant Park and I would have given them 5 stars. Their move to Poncey-Highlands renders them only 4 stars (largely because I hate change and I hadn't realized they had moved until one fateful day that had me making an unnecessary trip to Glenwood Ave.).  I will say this for them, they carry fantastic quirky and irreverent pieces by some of my favorites (they aren't the home of Urban Medium but carry it often enough to make it feel like their home). Their prints are definitely their best offering with their t-shirt coming in a cool second. I say cool because they even made this square a little hipper with my most recent purchase.

Such a cute and wonderful store!! With manikins sporting a wide variety of super pretty dresses, we decided to pop in here to check it out. We were greeted by two fabulous ladies and as we were carrying little plants with us, were struck up into conversation about them. Not only were the ladies very nice, but they were also super helpful with suggestions on where to get plant items on The Drive. Bonus! 

The shop is full of everything a girl needs to be swathed in femininity. You are greeted with tables and display stands full of trendy jewellery that matches not only with the theme of the store, but with all of the garments. The majority of the store consists of dresses of all colours and varieties, along with a few tops, sweaters, and skirts. There is even a small children's section in the back! Dresses are a little on the pricey side ($100+ for most) but they look to be one-of-a-kind's that you won't find at most stores. 

I'll definitely be back when summer finally shines through and dresses are needed for tea parties and general shenanigans!

That idylllic life as I knew it is gone....with life so sweet and easygoing, and I could reach work by simply biking 2.2 miles down one street to the Children's Hospital. Walking or taking a bus to destinations was accomplished with the utmost of ease.

Now, being back in the Bay Area, that sort of simple existence has faded and reliance upon a big ozone-harming, fuelly-dependent car has come back to the forefront (you like that one, didja now!?). 

5th Quadrant: a fun spot along the Van-Will (Vancouver/Williams) corridor that is in fact on the Portland biking route of the city! Large place for microbrews and pub grub both outside or in....happy hours that offer decent deals and above average food. Prices are greatly affordable, and the vibe is very cool. 

The offbeat nerd in me has done everything from coming with girlfriends to catch up on our lives during busy, LOUD happy hours, to playing chess (uh, yes.. chess) after dinner.....even take part in their goofy game nights... I recall one being a trivia night. It's great, because in Portland, it's all cool, and being yourself has never been easier, with societal pressures just off off off!!!!

The beers are rather yummy (read: C-Note), and the crowd tends to be younger 20/30's. Portions of food are generous, and the grill seems to get it right, most of the time. I miss it, terribly. This place was one of the foundational premier members that came to roost along the now popular corridor, before members like Lincoln and EaT (the oyster place) came. 

Pix Patisserie, the fine chocolatier, is just next door for super $$ splurging on sweets. now *that's* SUH WEEET.
NoPo (North Portland), live on forever! 

PS 5Q is part of the big Lompoc machine and opened up around 2007.

I had a really clever review in my head last night for this place - even did the whole "I'll remember it in the morning" thing.  Well, I don't remember...and am placing the blame on car bombs from the multiple bars we hit up before the Ambassador.  So maybe I don't remember the names of those places either..shut up it was Valentine's Day girls night out.  Maybe my brain is too full with calculus equations to have room for such trivial things.

This place has the most heinously (new word) amazing color scheme.  I had a roommate in college that used to say "there are only two colors in the world, teal and off-teal."  Well, this place is freakin' TEAL! No need for off-teal. 

Strong drinks, not that we needed them.

People on stage that were a little too into how awesome they thought their voices were.  It was like American Idol auditions.  

No one would sing "Paul Revere" with me.  By the time we decided what to sing (and yes I don't remember what we picked) they nicely booted us out.  Ambassador, I'll be back...my voice will be hoarse, my throat will be dry and I'll ask you for a sip.

OK, for anyone expecting a bowl of Texas/whatever style bend-your-spoon-because-it's-so-thick-and-hearty chili, this IS NOT your place.  Don't bother even stepping inside of the door.  

Skyline chili is better described as a sauce, not a "chili", but I digress.  This isn't gourmet food by any stretch of the imagination, but it is quite tasty if you accept it for what it is.  Skyline isn't fast food, but it isn't casual dining either ... really more of a "quick serve" restaurant.  Order and you should have food on your table in about 3 - 5 minutes tops.  I personally love the 5-way with tons of oyster crackers and habanero cheese.

This location is on par with any other Skyline that I've been to.  Service is adequate and food is consistent.

I tried out this spa while visiting family nearby. I have some health issues where I need to keep up detoxing and I heard they had an infrared sauna (they call it the iSlim). Having never been to a spa before, I wasn't sure what to expect, but from the moment I first walked in the chick who helped me out was fantastic. She walked me through everything and what to expect, making sure the temperate wasn't too high and I had enough water and cold towelettes. You put on this bodysuit to catch all the sweat, yea youre gonna need that, and then they have you get in this bed with heavy flaps like what you out over you for xrays. It worked so well. My family immediately noticed a difference and even that my eyes were clearer. I did the week pass and it was really reasonable for thentime I was there. One of the best things was you can watch Netflix while you sit there as it takes about an hour. My only complaint is that the top of each room is open and they do other things like spray tans, once whatever it was had such a strong fragrance it gave me a huge headache. Another time only 1 out of 5 different chicks I interacted with was all business and a little pushy and not over the top friendly. Otherwise highly recommend! Everyone was friendly and helpful, and its easy to find and park at. Go detox yo' self!

My boyfriend and I went to this place after we had seen their website. The price was ok, so we decided to check it out.
When we got there we had to wait in line for about 10 - 15. Surprisingly nobody was coordinating the line. As soon as a table were empty they would call the first person waiting and take them to the table. In our turn a guy, (with a tie) probably the person who should be coordinating the line, came up, asked how many people were in total and quickly find a sit for us. It was so nice having somebody explaining the place and telling us about the specials. He probably were busy, or during his dinner brake, but we did missed having someone up front. It is weird get in a place and wait in the line just because people in front of you are doing the same. So it was great when he materialized himself there. The service was great. A blond girl with an unsymmetrical hair (saved in one side) help us. She was so adorable and so helpful. She clearly knew everything about the menu, suggested some stuff and was very funny. I loved her. 
The food was fine. Not the best hamburger I ever had, but fair (I had the main one with fries). It wasn't memorable. Like, something like Tacofino's crispy chicken burrito (just an explanation what I consider memorable) that days later, after eating it, you can still feel the taste of the dish just by thinking about it. They probably have better things to try.

The 4 starts are more for the service and the place itself. Beautiful decoration, clean, great services, price ok.

I would go back again to try the food and maybe change my review about it.

TLDR; authentic-tasting Asian street food. I think the experience would be better if you went with a group so you can try more things. 

I was a little skeptical at first and didn't think it would taste that great. I assumed that because it was located in an area that wasn't predominantly Asian, it wouldn't taste authentic. Fortunately, I was proven wrong. 

Located on the BeltLine, which already sees a huge amount of people, the restaurant was poppin when I arrived for dinner. The bar is open seating and I managed to snag a seat. Hooks are provided underneath to hang your bags. 

The menu is pretty extensive, with multiple dishes from different Asian cultures. I wish I wasn't by myself...I could only get one item to try. Family-style seems like the best way to go, to get the best experience. There are so many small dishes to share. Since I could only order one thing without feeling too full, I went with the Mi goreng. My only experience with this dish is the packaged Indomie brand and I wanted to see if an authentic dish would taste the same.

My first thought after taking a bite was that this was nothing like Indomie's. The sauce is definitely different, tasting more closely to a pad see ew. Reminded me of Thai noodle dishes with the lime and the peanuts(?) sprinkled on top. But even though it wasn't what I expected, I enjoyed it. Ask for the chili oil to mix in for an extra kick! 

I'd love to come back with more people and try their other dishes. You really don't see a lot of Asian street food anywhere in the States and Hawkers can help when you're craving some.

Last stop before leaving Austin. This was one of my "must go to places" on my list. I read good things about it, and they were listed as vegan friendly. Stopped in for some lunch, first impressions were good. Popping hip place with an outdoor patio and nice view. Reminds me of something when I was younger.. can't quite put my finger on it yet but it was a great feeling.  We arrived and were immediately greeted by the hostess, I really wanted to sit out on the patio but we were on a time limit and it looked like there was already a wait. The hostess said we'd get faster service inside, after my boyfriend asked about the wait time. We were showed the way to our table and immediately greeted by our waiter Adam. I want to say that Adam was wonderful! Next time you're in there ask to be seated in his area. He was friendly, helpful and had vegan knowledge. He suggested some things on the menu. It's been a relief to me to be in Austin and have lots of vegan options. We started off with a bowl of the vegan chili.. it was very good. Spicy, fresh and tasty. I ordered the Veggie plate with green chili rice and my boyfriend had the Hippie vegan sandwich. It was all very good. I wished I would have had more time to enjoy the outdoor patio. Overall, it was a great experience at Shady Grove and I'm looking forward to exploring more of Austin the next we come down.

Revolutionizing the brand, Tony Roma's recently renovated their I-Drive location into a swanky space, boasting an airy outdoor patio with a fire place, an indoor/outdoor bar, and three state of the art private dining rooms. Equally impressive is their trendy take on small plates, glistening with global flavors and finger-licking goodness, plus excellent cocktails.

P.S: Hankering for an year's worth of ribs? Snap a selfie of your rib face (complemented by BBQ Sauce of course) and post with the hashtag: #RibFace to Facebook, Twitter, or Instagram!

This place surprised me. Before moving to Columbus, I always got good responses when I told them I was going to live in Easton ("Oh, that's a nice area. You'll like it there").

The Easton Town Center is like a mini Valley Fair, for those people who have been to the Bay Area. There's a Banana Republic, AMC20, Cheesecake Factory, PF Chang's, Melting Pot, Crate & Barrel, Panera Bread, Men's Warehouse, Trader Joe's, Apple Store, Lane Bryant, VS, Bath and Body, Coach, and Abercrombie. All across the street.

One more block away, there's a Target, Walmart, Office Max, and Sam's Club. It's super convenient having all these shops next to each other, and it's a really nice area.

I went to Allvera for a body wrap. I did the Power Hour wrap. 

Full disclosure this was my first experience with getting a body wrap so I don't have much of a comparison. I primarily went just to have a relaxing experience after a long stressful week.

I called approximately 30 minutes before I wanted to come in and the staff was very friendly and they were able to fit me in. I was led to a room in the back while was clean and comfortable. I was coming after work so was prepared with a swimsuit but they have little disposable underwear you can put on but you will be topless unless you want to sweat in your nice bra which I don't recommended. They then wrap you from head to toe and sit you in this small sauna machine where you head sticks out and there are little holes for your hands in case you want to use your hands.  

I put on some music and relaxed. They come to check on you about every 15 minutes. You sweat a TON. I was hungry when I went and by the end I actually started to feel queasy. They provide you with water throughout and apple sauce in the end if you need some calories, which was a life saver me

I'm not sure I really notice a difference in the way my body looks or clothes fit. But I did feel relaxed and overall it was a great experience and would definitely do it again!!

TOMS has a plan to take over the world, but they are doing so whilst running coffee shops and dishing out shoes to third world countries.

My evidence for their ambitions to pull off a lifelong desire of Pinky and the Brain? They own a coffee shop on South Congress, post-2009 housing crash. With Austin real estate skyrocketing, this philanthropic coffee shop snatched up a prime location. They now sling out their own beans in assorted beverages--alongside TacoDeli tacos of course (another company aptly prepared to run shop on corporate Austin).

The coffee quality is decent, the space eclectic, and the service good. For anyone who desires a funky shop, deeply rooted on a feel-good foundation, this shop fulfills those itches.

Took my family here on Friday night after not visiting for many years.  We moved back to the area so I was anxious to try the place again. Food is really very good, and plentiful. We did the family style, which is a great way to avoid having to make any real decisions, as you get to eat almost everything on the menu. The waiter let us sub out a few things too, which was awesome. They bring you more of anything you want.  It was all  seasoned and yummy. Baba ganouj (sp?) was hands down the best I've ever had.  Baklava was outstanding, not overly sweet. 
Service was very warm and accommodating. Feels like you're dining in someone's home, in terms of  both warmth and homey decor. Nicola, as others have
mentioned, is as gracious and friendly and fun as a restaurant owner could be. 
Very good food,service and value. We were there too early for the belly dancers, which was fine as we were just looking for a quiet meal. But they add a lot of fun on more festive occasions. We'll be back for sure.

Hi! There are a lot of good reasons to just go ahead and end it. This festival is not among them. This year they featured British Heavy Metal by the band Judas Priest as well as Satanic Heavy Metal by King Diamond who is from Denmark but lives in Dallas, TX! King Diamond brought his grandmother out on stage and said suggestive things about her and that was a weird vibe but the set was very good. There was also Yelle. She is from France and no speakey English but her songs are no less catchy as a result. One can dance to any language, you know?

The tobacco people are also very friendly. You will be treated to free Camel, Marlboro and even Hippie American Spirit tobacco should you opt for this. They are doing it right. In my mind it is believed that if you are going to promote cancer you should at least not be a dickhole about it. 

This festival does not serve 16 oz beers so I recommend taking many of your Xanax script to increase the effectiveness of these 12 oz Shiner Bocks. Also, Ambien and Adderall help as well. I practice Buddhism so it is all about balance and contemplating one's place in the world while on several drugs.

The ticket prices are reasonable so I don't feel financially fucked in the mouth the way that I do at some other festivals. I hate that feeling. OK. Thank you.

I went at dinner, and had the Gyro plate. Simply put, it's the tastiest Greek food I have had in Austin. The gyro meat was great, and the hummus was instantly addictive - I had to fend off two bus-people trying to take my plate. Luckily, no violence was necessary! I even liked the rice pilaf enough to finish it, and I don't usually care much for rice dishes. 

Beer selection is a bit sparse, but they do have Shiner and Fireman's 4, so I was satisfied. The service was friendly, and pretty efficient considering how busy it was, with the patio completely full on a beautiful autumn Friday evening.

Really loved my stay at this hotel.

The hotel is huge as it has a small convention center. There's an adjacent parking lot/garage next to it. The downside to the garage is that you have to pay/day if you're staying at the hotel. The garage is also a bit creepy and quiet at night. As for the rooms, we had a double Queen size bed room and it was perfect. The room was clean, tidy and spacious. Not sure why there are some bad reviews for this hotel, but I couldn't find a thing to complain about other than the parking lot and the daily fee.

Oh ... and most importantly, don't forget to get your DoubleTree cookie when you check-in!

Love the ambiance of this place!  Crepes are yummy!  What more could you ask for?  Perfect for a date night or an intimate get together with a few friends.  Didn't look large group-friendly.  Only thing notable - we ordered a nutella banana crepe and got a nutella pear crepe and didn't realize it until we were well into eating it.  Not what we asked for, but was still good.  I'm getting a nutella banana next time!  They serve Illy coffee but it wasn't brewed as well as I've had at other places.  Ambiance and crepes trump coffee though. :)

dynamite turkey sandwich

  On my dinner break I strolled down to try Au Bon Pain out for a sandwich.  I find them rather pricey, but considering the flavor it was well worth it.  I had one of the turkey sandwiches which had avocado on it among other things.  The sandwich was packed with flavor, just incredible to the very last bite.  One of the better sandwiches I have had this year and that is saying a lot since I do not typically like turkey.  I will definitely try them again.

A new hidden gastropub that shows a lot of promise for the Westside of Vancouver.  The interior is trendy, sophisticated, aesthetically pleasing and reminiscient of bars in PDX.  The menu has a southern influence and is not extensive.  However, that's not important if you can score well on most of the menu items.  I tried the salmon BLT which was tasty and it was accompanied with crispy skinny fries.  You can also have it with a side wedge salad.  The salmon is kind of a lox style and it worked well with the minced red onions, caper lemon mayo, and bacon in the sandwich.

Service was great -- you can tell the management cares about the success of their place and want to ensure satisfied customers.  I ordered their Gran's BBQ chicken wings which was a bit disappointment.  Wings were sparse and most where charred with very little meat.  When I mentioned this to the owner, she expressed appreciation for my feedback and offered me a coupon to come back in again and try the wings once more.  That's great customer service for a new establishment.  This place is really close to my work so am looking forward to future lunches there.

I have lived just north of Boston for three years now and in that time I've struggled to find a decent affordable sushi place.  That coupled with the fact that I used to live in Quincy, where great sushi and great Asian fare in general is widely available, made my lack of Sushi situation all the more unbearable.  I've tried the local standards, Yoshi and Snappy are average, Yoki is overrated and overpriced, and I've heard All Seasons in good but I spend about as much time in Malden as Ed Markey.  But after stopping by Genki Ya yesterday for lunch, I feel as though my long search is at an end.  The place has a nice clean and open look to it, probably seats about 25-30, when I was there it was about half full, with two servers and two sushi chefs all of whom did a great job.  The Sushi was excellent, I am a big salmon fan and the Salmon Rich Roll was right up my alley combining salmon, avocado, and rice, topped with more salmon and avocado.  The spicy tuna roll was also good, I find a lot of places tend to mail this roll in, using tons of mayo and tempura, but Genki Ya didn't fall  into that trap letting the tuna shine on its own.  In fact perhaps to much so, my one criticism was that it wasn't up to my level of spiciness, but still very tasty and also more to my S.O.'s tastes, which in the end is more important.  Price was very good for the quality, three rolls, and an appetizer was around $35 before tip.  All in all an excellent no frills sushi joint, I look forward to trying them for dinner.

I go to Yamato for the all you can eat quite often - they have a fantastic assortment of appetizers and sushi included and the special Volcano roll is INCREDIBLE. Service can get a little slow during peak AYCE hours, but that's kind of expected. More time to digest in between?

The fish is fresh and the quality of the rolls has never let me down. Sure, it's not the upper echelon of artisan sushi, but it's REALLY good for the price. No hard rice or soggy cucumber here. Among all the Brighton sushi places, these guys are pretty firmly up at the top. The AYCE is a steal on weekdays too, though the price goes up slightly on the weekends.

My 2nd time at Liuyishou, although different location, but I still loved it! This location is in the bustling plaza at Garden City/Alexandra. Therefore, parking can be quite challenging due to the existence of many restaurants within this plaza. If you go right at the start of meal time, you'd have no problem finding parking (fingers crossed).

The 3 of us chose the tom yum seafood soup for soup base. The soup base, tangy and spicy, came with quite a bit of seafood in the soup. We ordered the ring of meat, the veggie/mushroom basket, duck blood... The ring of meat, consisting of lamb and beef slices, encompasses the pot made my dinner especially beautiful. I also wanted to highlight the quality of meat we got at Liuyishou. I NEVER eat lamb slices due to its gamy flavor; however, I absolutely loved the lamb served by the restaurant! I didn't taste any gamy flavor at all!

One of the perks of Chinese style hot pots (mainland style, as this isn't the case for Taiwanese hot pots) is the sauce station. While there was a charge per person (must be the norm), you do have "unlimited" access to many different sauces, condiments, in addition to side dishes (pickled vegetables) and fruits.

While everything we ordered tasted extremely delicious, I must say the prices are on the higher end. Some reviews I read indicated that the prices were pretty cheap!? Sorry, but I cannot agree with this. For example, the veg/mushroom platter was $13, and all we got were some veggies and a couple of sliced pieces for each mushroom variety. Another aspect I didn't really like was the service. The servers were pretty rude, i.e. no customer service. I get that perhaps this is the norm in China; however, this is Canada and you are asking for tips! Therefore, give some service or, at the very least, smile at your customers!

On our trip from Seattle area back to Reno we wanted something sit down and relaxing.  Yelp helped find us something on the water.  Cool.

We put a reservation in, just incase this place was gonna get crowded.  Thankfully we did.  It was a little busy when we got there so it was nice to know we had a table.

To put it simply.  The food was pretty good. My wife was disappointed that the fish & chips wasn't a beer batter.  And I was happy because I got her leftovers!  The daughter got the pizza and it was good too.  (enough to help mom get her fill after passing on the remaining fish and chips.  We left satisfied so portion size was good as well.   

The service was overall good.  The staff seemed interested in the work and also seemed to like working there. I know, strange thing to say, but really I see it so many times where wait staff is just "doing time" to get the money. 

Atmosphere was nice too.  Would be a good destination place if I lived in Portland or Vancouver for sure.

Would I go back?  Sure.  Would I recommend it to friends?  Sure.

This place was packed for a Tuesday morning. My friend and I arrived here around 11:30 and there already seemed to be a 30-40 person line out the door. We went inside, put our name down, and the hostess said it would be about 45 minutes--no problem, as we had plenty to do since it's downtown with some shops all around. 

From what I could tell initially, this place is very very popular, with cute decor all around and a coffee bar close to the front entrance....we went on our way to meander around a bit and came back exactly 45 min later--and about a minute later we were seated! Perfect timing.

WHAT WE GOT:

1) I got the Mocha with white lavender pistachio rose with soy milk---actually really good! I really tasted the rose in the mocha, and it wasn't overpowering.
2) Poisson Lem Marrakech--poached egg, cured salmon,wheat berries, pistachio salad with sesame yogurt : my friend and I really enjoyed this, especially the cured salmon! For $17 it was a bit pricey but I especially enjoyed the crunch from the pistachio and addition of the wheatberries.
3) Avocado Toast: on grilled focaccia, with a tomato salsa and egg on side..this was a different version than what I was imagining but none the less good, I just which the portion was a bit bigger for $6.
4) Liege style waffle: with the white choc pistachio rosewater---we shared 1 which I think was enough since we shared everything else. The liege was piping hot, a bit chewy, a bit fluffy, but a very nice sweet snack. I do prefer the Blue Bottle liege waffles in SF though!


Overall food was pretty good, it was super busy so service wasn't great (our waiter forgot about our waffle and didn't really check in on us). But they were pretty spot on with timing and good about taking our orders.

If we were allowed half stars we would give it 4.5. Under remodeling but still open for business.  The place is huge inside.  I couldn't tell that from the front.  Clean too.  

We ordered an appetizer platter for 14.99.  It came with baba ganosh and hummus and cucumber relish and a yogurt dip with plenty of pita bread.  (The bread is very thin.) It was good and tasty. 

Then we ordered dinner.  My husband got the lamb shank called Baghali polo lamb.  The rice was cooked with a green herb and slivered bean. Not sure what kind. I ordered the Jeddo Prince.  This came with grilled skewers of chicken and beef and rice.  My food was delicious and flavorful. My rice had a subtle taste but it was buttery.  My husband's dish was good too. He ate all of it.  

We ordered waters and I got hot tea because I was curious of what Persian tea tasted like.  Also the tea is free to customers.  

Our service was good.  There was only one other table being occupied along with us.  So not sure how a crowd would do. 
Overall we will return and try again because it was really good.  But when the budget allows. 

Out the door our cost was 48.34 not including tip.  My husband gave 18%. So it was a little pricey for two people without the ambience and fine dining.

this is a duplicate review of the one I posted for Voila on SE 14th, which is where I met Jonathan and Tamara initially. Imagine my confusion when I see it listed as SW Washington St. 

The two initial reviews by Megan M and Samantha H could be off-putting. I have a much higher opinion of Voila Catering, who worked planning the reception for my daughters wedding. Voila made it a turn key event. All I had to do was show up on time, dressed and ready for her wedding.For a big day like a wedding, that is what should happen. 
Jonathon and Chef Tamara are professionals, which was evident as we planned the reception,discussed options, possibilities and costs. 
I rated Voila at 4 stars instead of 5 because of costs. This is my first time both walking a daughter down the aisle, and hiring a caterer. I really don't have anything to base my assumptions of what things SHOULD cost, so it is strictly opinion. Before you hire ANY caterer, I think its helpful to set a budget so you can at least have a measurement to judge by. I didn't do that. 
However, I am very pleased with Voila. With food preparation and rentals, and Jonathans insight, I believe our guests were pleased and enjoyed themselves. My daughter and her new husband certainly did. My wife and I were pleased that we didn't have to spend any time insuring things went well: Voila had us covered. All we had to do was enjoy the day.

Stopped by for drinks with co-workers and took a chance on the 5 dollar endless chips and salsa. 3 different types of salsa appear ranging in hotness and consistency that were all above average and done well. While no one likes to pay for chips and salsa I didn't mind after trying it. 

We sat in the annex portion of the building where a great, Nora Jones-esque, lounge singer was performing at just the right decible level to still have a conversation. We sat / stood around the bar where a long haired bartender was patient and witty with our group of people. 

I had a great happy hour experience here.

Buffalo Nachos are delicious and drinks are okay. Music be popping as well as the married men lol. It is sad because it seems like that is the spot they go to find side chicks. Ladies beware and look at the ring finger. These men are bold enough to keep it on and still try to get your number. Lol
It is cool though they keep it 100 for the beginning.

So, have fun and enjoy the night catch an Uber home and chill.

I've been a customer since they were on Northloop. I've always had a great experience until July last year.  I was tired of dealing with flats, so I decided to deal with it and brought in a set of puncture resistant tires, Mr Tuffy gold, thorn resistant tubes and sealant for the Peddler to install.  A year later, after 4,000 miles I had to replace a tire I wore out..  I discovered the tube liners never were installed, and they were never returned either.  I sent a note to the store email and after a week, I've not heard anything. I sent another email to the owner, and got a reply. The problem was taken care of. faith restored.  So if you have a problem, be persistent and your chances are good.

Great park! I brought my child today to the splash pad and the playground. 
Pros:
1) The splash pad has a fence containing it which is nice so little kids don't run off. There are bathrooms nearby for changing kids in. 
2) There is a big kid and little kid playground. The little kid playground has a fence around it. The big kid playground has a shaded canopy over it. There are lots of shade trees also in this park. 
3) There are sports fields and a batting cage. 

Cons:
1) The park is dog friendly but there are no dog plastic bag waste stations. I brought my dog and there were other people there with their dogs. 
2) I was waiting on a bench near the playground and there was no shade over the benches.

Quite nice! I stayed here for 5 nights during a work conference, and everything was pretty great. Check in was a breeze at 1am :P 

My room had a king bed with plenty of space and a balcony overlooking the pool. The room itself was modern and clean. The bed was comfortable and the linens were soft. 

The convention facilities were A+. They run a well-oiled machine. The food was great, and the staff is friendly. 

There are plenty of places to eat here, but since all my meals were provided at the conference, I did not get to try out the restaurants. There is a decent-sized grocery with fill-your-own-cup frozen yogurt in yummy flavors like dulce de leche. 

The only thing I think they can improve upon is the gym facility - it is super small for a resort of this size. There are maybe 10 cardio machines and very limited equipment. If you go to a gym at home even just semi-regularly, you are up for some disappointment. The bright side is that there is an outdoor running path within the resort that circles the buildings. One loop is about 1.5mi. Also, depending on which tower you are staying in, the gym and spa can be quite a trek. 

Overall, though, it was an excellent stay. I can't comment on prices since this stay was covered by my company but I would say that $200-300 per night would be a fair price.

Wrapture is great.  I was so sad when Tapas closed, but then this place moved in, and it's up to par.  I've had the Blackened Fish wrap, the grilled portabella mushroom wrap, and the grilled steak wrap-- all wonderful.  A little more expensive than I'm willing to pay for an average lunch, but extremely good quality ingredients and innovative flavor combinations.  Plan to call ahead and take it somewhere else as every order is made fresh and takes a few minutes, and they discourage eating on location.  Highly recommended!

I rented an ecv for 8 days of my Disney vacation. This is not an approved certified company Disney works with. So you will have to be there for drop off and pickup of your rented vehicle. I didn't know that Disney had preferred places to rent from that will drop it off and pickup at the concierge desk. So you do not need to be present. This wasn't an issue for my drop off, they arrived within the 30 min block of time and called 10 minutes before arrival so I could make sure to be at the entrance of hotel. It was much heavier then stated this was a problem since the 2 of us that needed it are disabled and couldn't put it in and out of car. So we had to beg and pay valets and strangers to lift it for us at each location. So beware if you d not have a strong person in your group. 
On the return the guy never called until 30 minutes after the pickup window and yelled at me for not being there. Ridiculous I waited for 1:30 minutes at the front of hotel the exact stop I was sitting when they dropped it off. He came with no truck and claimed I wasn't there. I nearly missed my plane (had it not been delayed an hour) waiting for him. 

Aside from that being my last interaction with them, which was disheartening, I was very happy with the price and battery life if scooter. I even received a 10% discount with the yelp check in offer. They do not nickel and dime you. Once they tell you the price that's what it is. No delivery fee, no tax on top no nothing. I really appreciated that. I wouldn't hesitate renting from them again if it is guaranteed to way much much much less.

The calamari was some of the best that I've tasted anywhere in Vancouver, and their pizzas are still pretty good. So I have decided to move this to third place on my pizza list! 

Any pizza is a solid choice here as it captures the perfect texture without being too soggy, so you could actually pick up the pizza without losing half of the toppings. The salad we ordered was plentiful and delicious complete with hazelnuts and delectable beets. The tiramisu was my only pass, but I somehow missed the panacotta with check-in which is disappointing since I checked in! You really don't need dessert here since the mains are all large and delish.

The atmosphere was a bit dead on a rainy Tuesday, and it's not the most interesting looking place, but it's extremely clean and the server we had was absolutely great. If we had more time, the movie + pizza special looked good, but choices for that were not our first picks, anyway.

Overall, I have no complaints, and when craving pizza on the west side, this is definitely the place to go. My prior review expanded on the pasta which was equally delicious. I hope that more people discover this joint as it's miles above another place I reviewed that's also quite near.

Went for the last night of Dine Boston week as we had a great dinner last year at the same event.

Unfortunately the ball got dropped this time for several reasons. Our meals were missing elements that were on the menu.

First the monkfish medallion salad had no trace of pancetta wrapped on the monkfish. Carrots were hardly visible as well. My beet salad "tower" consisted of three beets with goat cheese in between. Hardly a tower but was enjoyable just the same.

My bf enjoyed his mahi entree but I was searching for the missing "crab meat" from my shrimp/crab pasta entree. Also missing was zucchini.

Oh boy.....lots of errors here.

To top it off our pear almond tart as shown on the dessert tray arrived 1/2 the size as shown for each of us. Maybe they were running low.

It was a busy night and the restaurant full and nice to see especially when the owner is doing all the cooking!

We will return but please improve the experience as expected.

Second time dining at Lusca last night. Loved every single dish we ordered. House made charcuterie is some of the best I've had in the city. Also had a great black cod main dish that was cooked perfectly. 

Our waiter helped us pick a perfect bottle of wine to accompany our meal. They have a long wine list with some unusual bottles. Lots of great options. 

Dessert was a chocolate pistachio tart. Great combination. 

It was very quiet when we arrived at 7, but the restaurant was full and noisy by the time we left. 

A few glitches in service (asked for more bread to go with the charcuterie and has to wait a while for it), but overall a great evening.

Walked in at 4 pm - for late lunch and starving - to a fairly empty restaurant. Short menu, but all essentials are there: a little bit of Thai, some Vietnamese and some Chinese. Quick and nice service, complimentary edamame and 20% off with Yelp check in. A little pricey for a place like this, but excellent attitude, family owned and really good food. We had pho, pad Thai and banh mi - all fresh, greatly seasoned and customized to our liking. There was a little mix up with our drink, but in the end they took it off the bill.

This was a surprise. At the airport? Yes. The food was good, but at airport prices. On par, price wise, with other places though. The food was surprisingly good, for an airport. I'd say, maybe the best airport food I've had in a great while. And, the server we had was so nice! I even spotted her singing along with the music that was playing softly in the background. Shows happy staff. Nice addition. If you are looking for a good meal, this is a good place when stuck in the terminal. Note, this is four stars, compared to airport food, not the type of restaurant you'd find outside of an airport. I would remove one star compared to "normal" restaurants for the price and food quality.

I have been to yolks  several times and the food has been AMAZING and equality as good every time! 

I have gone with just one other person and in a group as big as six and the food came out hot, prompt and just as we ordered it. I have been there is many times some of the staff know what I order!

My one complaint is there are a couple of servers who complain when I had friends who wanted a harder poach. They rolled their eyes and made it seem as if we were asking for a flying pony along with our meal. Seriously some people don't like a soft poach but still enjoy eggs and bunch. I get that you are busy and find this request annoying but we are repeat customers! I'm fine with regular poached eggs but a few of my friends aren't.  They don't deserve to be scrolled for their preferences...

I saw these reviewed on the front page of yelp on April 18, 2015, therefore book marked it.

Firstly this shop is small, however, they pack a lot of punch in the personality department. There is a bohemian ambiance that is created. 

There is limited seating, however, there is a couch and a communal table. 

The table is for groups of 4 or more, however, the owner allowed me to do my art for 30 minutes before closing. 

This shop is only open on the weekdays between 8 - 5 pm, therefore, it was either this week or not at all. 

They have a lot of unique flavors and names. Very extensive menu. 

Bonus points 'cause they're one of the few coffee shops that actually has coconut milk as a diary alternative. 

I had the London Fog, sugar free made with coconut milk which added a unique addicting dimension. 

Price was $$$, almost $5 for an 8 oz. The coconut milk was an additional 75 cents, however, with everything else it was still an expensive drink. 

So why the 4 and not 5? Their hours need to be more accessible.

I came here on a Friday night and ordered from the Hibachi menu. I was a little disappointed that I didn't get the full experience and was seated in a separate room at a back table where everyone else seemed to be ordering sushi. The service was also a little slow - I ran out of water about halfway through my food and finished the meal with just ice and later sat around waiting for my check for quite some time. 

That being said most of my food was phenomenal! The ginger dressing used on the salad was so delicious that I could probably have eaten nothing but the salad and been pretty happy, but my salmon/scallops/shrimp dish was also incredible. 

The only miss food-wise was the fried rice, which was an absolute failure and tasted like cooking gas and oil. Absolutely no flavor in the rice aside from this and I was majorly disappointed because fried rice is usually one of my favorite things to eat. I have never had fried rice that bad before. 

I recommend this place for the salad alone as it was my favorite thing to eat in a long time, but definitely don't order the fried rice.

3.5 stars for Chang Thai. 

The service was quite good. Our waitress was both attentive and friendly. 

We ordered the Tom Kha in a pot, the catfish curry dish and Pad Kee Mao. The Tom Kha arrived unlit with a huge pile of goo underneath... once she lit it I thought I was instantly transported back outside to the 100+ degree heat!  Our soup started boiling and we were both choking down the flame exhaust. She came over and doused out the fire... too much! 

The Tom Kha was flavorful and (besides boiling) full of veggies and chicken. At $10 the Tom Kha could easily be a meal for two people. We didn't realize this but will have tons left over! 

My Pad Kee Mao was... good. It was good. I took most of it home due to being so full from the soup. It had a different taste too it, a bit of a sour spice versus the normal sweet peppery spice we see often here in Austin. It wasn't bad, it was just different. I prefer the more traditional black peppery spice serve at Tittyayas. It did come loaded with veggies which made me happy! I never can get enough veggies in my Pad Kee Mao. The catfish dish came highly recommended - I don't eat catfish so I didn't try it but The Fish Eater gave it a nice star ranking. 

Our waitress honored the 15% off checkin code offered on Yelp which was very nice, it actually expired June 30th. 

All in all I probably will be hitting up some of my favorite Pad Kee Mao places because we walked out with a $35+ bill for two people. That was a little bit more then I was willing to spend for lunch, especially when I know I can pay less for more quality at my regular stops.

Very good food!!! Out of all the Asian foods....I don't know much about Korean food...but I've eaten it a few times....so I normally stick to what I know.  

This place is a mom & pop shop....they were very nice! We watched Korean tv while we waited for our food....no clue what was being said but it looked dramatic like a soap opera.  ha!!

We ordered japchae---awesome noodles!  Hope you like sesame oil flavor because I do and it was quite good!  Had the beef bulgogi....lean, not fatty and tasted great.  Oh we also got the seafood pancake....which was awesome!  I would definitely get this again.  The meal came with little side items such as kim chee, sprouts, daikon etc etc...I think there was like 6 small items came with the bulgogi.  

I think they 10-12 tables in the restaurant so it was smaller than I thought.  We went a bit earlier than normal dinner time, I think just before 6pm.....guess Im getting old looking for a early bird special.  ha!  

A definite recommend!  The waitress and owners will help you order if you have no clue. I think Ill go there this week to get take out.

Happy Korean food eating!!!

I can walk to this place from my house, so that's a bonus for me. The food is not the best I've ever had and sometimes varies in quality, but overall is decent if you happen to be in the area and like Thai food. The service, on the other hand, is excellent and the people who run the place are SO nice. And I love the Thai tea they serve here. I would have to say that if you're visiting Salem, this is a pretty good choice. You won't be disappointed.

Started out with some appetizers. Crab cake and bacon wrapped scallops. The crab cakes were TO DIE FOR! They were both buttery and spicy and outshined the scallops. So if you can't decide between the two, go with the crab cakes.

Entree: Lobster Tail was just ok. Nothing special about it. The bone in cowboy ribeye cooked medium, was cooked perfectly, with a nice dark seat which is what you'd expect. Had it oscar style, which was also great. 

Dessert: The rocky road bread pudding had a huge marshmallow on the top that I feel was a bit overkill and hard to eat together in one bite. Better idea would be to add a few scoops of rocky road ice cream. The chocolate crunch was ok, it had an interesting "crunch" consistency, but overall it was not out of this world. 

Atmosphere was cozy and they had a live piano player, who was great.

As a self proclaimed ice cream connoisseur I was very excited to try out Tipping Cow after reading rave reviews online calling it a hidden gem within Somerville. My roommates and I decided to pay a visit Sunday night to give it a try. The staff was very welcoming and friendly and mentioned that the ice cream is made fresh every week and new flavors were installed once old batches ran out. There was a limited menu with 11 flavors to choose from and sizes ranging from mini to large with a very fair price to portion ratio (ordered a small for $3.25 two large scoops). We ordered the Espresso Chip, Ginger Blueberry, and Cookie dough. After finishing our ice cream 1 out of 3 of us were extremely impressed with the flavors. The Ginger and Blueberry was very overpowering and tasted as though you were eating the ginger on the side of the sushi plate. The Espresso Chip was very strong but since I am a coffee fanatic it ended up being a huge plus. Be forewarned if you do not like strong coffee you will not like this flavor. The one flavor that they did nail was the Cookie Dough, an absolute classic that we ordered with a melted brownie. Overall we were fairly impressed with our experience and would definitely be repeat customers when some unique flavors that make our taste buds tingle come onto the menu.

I was very impressed!  It was Mother's Day amd my wife had a craving for a BBQ sandwich.  We were near downtown do tried to go to La BBQ.  There was a 1.5 hour wait at 11:30 am on Sunday.  No thanks. It cannot be that good (or that much better than other good places).  

So we Yelped around for a close good place and found Kerlin.  We were very glad we did.  It is run out of trailer with separate smoker room.  It has covered outdoor seating as well as a store nearby where you can buy beer to go with ur BBQ (or they have Mexican Coke and other drinks).

We all ordered variations on the sliced brisket sandwich.  I had coleslaw on mine.  Brisket was excellent!  Tender, smokey and flavorful (extra moist).  Also sauce was good, a bit of sweet, spice and vinegar.  Side dishes were awesome and creative.  One proprietor is Mexican or Latin American and she brings el sabor.  Like Mexican street corn on cob, cream corn with bacon, a creative potato salad and more!  They also have BBQ Frito Pie, ribs, turkey, sausage, etc.

Definitely check them out. Don't you dare wait 1.5 hrs for any meal (life is too short), especially BBQ.  They were friendly, no waiting (though they had many customers).  Viva BBQ! Viva Kerlin!!

I cleaned all the stuff out of my car before I went, and got there early. Service took about an hour and everyone I talked to was friendly and professional. The interior/exterior clean I ordered cost way less than I expected and took about an hour. The job wasn't perfect, but I wasn't paying for perfect; I was paying for fast and clean. Everything was vacuumed, all the windows washed inside and out, the dash were cleaned, and all the little crevasses and pockets were swabbed out. I got a coupon that I will use next time on carpet and seat shampooing. I will definitely go back there; don't know why I waited so long.

Had a Bradford pear tree removed and wanted a replacement.  My research indicated that a Monterrey Oak was perfect for central Texas.  Called around and went down to Ted's Trees in east Austin to see what they had.  Talked to Chevo, the 85 year old man that started the buisiness many years ago.  He showed me a 100 gal Monterrey oak that looked staright and healthy but I procrastinated and it was gone when I went back to buy it.  So I picked out another tree and paid for it but when I came out I noticed some things about the tree that I didn't like.  Ted told me they were getting more trees in the next couple of days but they never seemed to come so I ended up picking a 45 gal tree that was straight and looked good and they refunded the difference.  Today Ted's crew planted the tree and I am very happy with it

I purchased 500 tortillas here on the morning of my wedding. Yes, they are made by hand but they run them through a big tortilla machine so they are uniform. I don't care about that, they tasted amazing - fresh, fabulous and still warm and the price was rediculously good. 

When I had gone there to arrange it the week before, I spoke with one really sweet older man who spoke English, but the day of the wedding when I called to confirm I could not get anyone on the phone who did. My Spanish is terrible so I had a slight heart attack at that point - luckily I had a friend over who speaks fluently and she got on the phone. Indeed they had my order as promised! 

The place is in this weird little strip mall in between a plasma donation center and a drive through cigarette shop. Not the most inviting location, but who cares? I couldn't have been happier with the tortillas, they really made our wedding buffet outstanding.

"Put you in a luxury car and you don't know how to act"....that's what was told to me just before I drove my X5 model off of the lot.  In truth, it was the second car I sat in (the first had cream interior thank you very much!).  

We went to Nalley BMW of Decatur on a Friday evening just before closing, really thinking of looking at models and considering purchasing something but not that day.  Who knew that we'd be leaving the lot with a vehicle all while getting a phenomenal deal in the process?

I worked with Anthony "byrd", who was somewhat new, but nonetheless took care of us.  There was haggling involved, which did help to get the car I wanted at the interest rate I needed and the loan term I desired.  

One of the main reasons i'm not giving Nalley BMW 5 stars is because although we came in late (and came back the next morning to pick up the car), we were told that it would be an hour at most the next day.  We ultimately sat for about 4 additional hours waiting on the finance guy to get freed up.  

Ultimately, I love my car, I felt that my customer service treated me well, and although I wont be back anytime soon for car shopping \, I definitely will be back!

I really love this place! To be fair, I've never actually eaten anything here besides their desserts. It's one of those places where I always go to meet up with friends after a meal, and never for a meal. Their desserts are delicious though. My favorite so far is the Oreo Cheesecake.

I really love the ambiance here. Yes, it's romantic and would be one of the first picks for a date spot, but it's also versatile in that it's great to get together and chat with friends over some good drinks. If you haven't been here yet, you're definitely missing out!

i tried Cupzilla at the Columbus Food Truck Festival. i wasn't expecting to like it based on the reviews but to be honest i thought it was pretty good. i had the Hot Cup level 3 hot. to be honest even when it was handed to me i had my doubts. so much sauce on it i thought it'd be  a mess, and it was - a tasty mess. once everything was mixed together it was real good and had just enough spice for me. i'd likely grab some more if in the same area.

Great meal, friendly staff!  Loved the chicken marsala, and the butterscotch pudding was to die for.  This restaurant was spot on for Portland Dining Month. Some places seem to have decreased portion sizes for the PDX Dining Month special but not here. Will definitely be back. Love the "In Our America..." sign in the window.

Update - I am disappointed to see the owner response to one negative Google review I saw. He or she responded with a link to Anthony Bourdain's rant about Yelp reviewers, as a response to in Google review. The first words in the video are "f$ck em", followed by a rant about how bad Yelp reviewers are.  Not really professional IMO, and professionalism matters when you run a business. Even if the reviewer was dumb, or whatever. No need to be disrespectful. Take the high road.

Great little boutique! Offers individual plants for sale as well as potted and decorated with other cute trinkets. They also have terrariums for sale. They also sell air plant fertilizer and materials for constructing your own terrarium if you want to put it together yourself.
