I picked up a few medium air plants and a succulent to fly back to NJ with me. I used the $5 off coupon from yelp! Very satisfied with my little babies. I wish I was able to pick up one of the larger ones but they were a bit too expensive for me $25-$40 dollars depending on size.

Overall all though I loved my purchase and experience there!

We usually head to Conley's Weds. nights for the prime rib special, 14.95 with a salad and side...you can't go wrong.  Plenty of TVs on the bar side to watch all the games and a good beer selection.  The pizza is clean and tasty, cheese fries, steak tips and scallops are all pretty solid options. 

Service is always solid, Maura aka Mo-town always knows when we're thirsty and is always smiling and personable which is appreciated.  They seem to always have a big group in the back and would usually lead to less service and an empty glass but they've always kept that beer glass full and food prompt so that you have to respect.  

Conley's is a solid bar and food option in the Watertown area.

Priced Right, Good location, Clean and Roomy.

We stayed in Parkway International Resort for a short trip to Disney World this January.  We found the location to be great - just off of I-4 outside the Disney Main Gates.  Our unit was clean and spacious.  I would guess it at close to 1300 or 1400 square feet with a private screened porch, kitchen with full size appliances, and a washer, and dryer.  It is a very livable condo for longer stays than ours.  We had one small maintenance issue with a missing coaxle cable for a bedroom TV and, after reporting, maintenance was there in just a few minutes with a new one.  No other problems.  The resort pool looked nice, but it was too cool in January for us to swim.  We would gladly stay here again on our next trip to Orlando.

It has been a while since I've visited a Bath and Body Works store but my good friend Glenn inspired me! I'm glad he did cuz I really enjoyed my visit here today! 
     I was greeted as soon as I entered the store. Several employees offered me assistance finding things. The store is well organized, very neat and clean. The lighting is good and the merchandise displays were eye catching. I found some terrific sale items. 
       The check out process was easy and quick. The cashier was friendly but I wished she had been a bit more careful placing my wall flowers in the bag. I bought four of them and every time she dropped one in the bag it sounded like they were breaking. Maybe she knows more about their durability than I do, because everything was in one piece when I got them home. Thankfully.
    I enjoyed shopping at this Bath and Body Works store today and definitely plan to return again soon!

Many of the negative reviews are somewhat accurate - the owner (Charlie Federico) has odd hours (closes at 5PM sharp), never answers the phone, it's a dingy shop, and owns the shop only as a hobby.  That being said, they're unfair.

This store has been in operation since the 1930's.  The owner was a former engineer for GE - so he knows his stuff.  He's says he's also been offered millions to sell the shop, but refuses.

Plus, he will charge you NOTHING.  He raised my seat, lowered my handlebars, fixed my girlfriend's seat, and raised her handlebars - for $10!  A woman that arrived at the shop before me, he charged NOTHING to fix her chain (she gave him $8 anyhow). Check out what a tune-up will cost you at any other bike shop - $50 a pop!

The owner was also smart enough to notice another little knock in the chain that needed fixing  - and he noted that you CAN safely raise handlebars even higher than the "minimum insertion mark", without damaging the bike.

He doesn't answer the shop phone (telemarketers he claims), so call his house where he'll happily answer the phone (617-471-5368).  He even opened the shop on Saturday for us.

The owner is 82 and religious, but he didn't say anything offensive to us whatsoever.  He'll remind you of your grandfather - he said to be careful out there and always wear a helmet!  He also GIVES AWAY a lot of the bikes in his shop to needy kids in the neighborhood.

Honestly, if you want your bike fixed on the cheap, and you want to support a local guy, I'd recommend him.


More here:
http://southbostontoday.com/federicos/

"If you grew up in Southie the name conjures up memories of summertime and fun, bicycles, scooters, bicycles, baby carriages, bicycles, wagons, but mostly bicycles.  Beginning in 1938 at Emerson and Fourth Street, Federico's has always been the last word in pedal power or wheeled mobility in general.

Charles Federico was born in South Boston of parents from Patti, Sicily.  His wife Mary is from Finnian Terrace, Ireland.  Family lore says the marriage was a perfect deal.  Mary taught Charles to speak correctly and he taught her to put her shoes on the right way.  They raised a family of eight.  Namesake, Charles took over the family business and has been a part of our community fabric for over fifty years.

Bundle boys, who wheeled groceries home, made their carts usually with baby carriage wheels from Federico's.  Seniors needing adjustment on their walkers still count on Charlie.  Above all, the hordes of bike riders still flock to the only licensed bicycle repair shop in South Boston.  It is more of a labor of love and a chance to give back to the community than a necessity.

A senior jet engine designer for General Electric, Charlie designed the fighter / trainer jet in use by Beijing, redesigned the Singapore Air Force and is a patent holder for a G.E. jet engine.

Charlie and his wife Carolyn raised four children and he keeps on ticking like he always has.  "Our job on Earth is to help," a deeply spiritual Charlie states. He recalls at 14 dreaming of his house burning.  Sure enough the next night at 2:30 a.m. his house burned.  Charlie believes miraculous intervention by Our Lady Mother Mary guided his mother through the flames to his room where they escaped from a porch helped by a couple of sailors walking by.

When asked of his Southie memories he first wanted to let me know he considers the New York Times reporter who tried to call Southie "SOBO", to be an intellectual moron.

"When I grew up every corner had a football team.  Military drill was held at the high school, and spiritual guidance was our directing influence.  My parents taught me pride in who I was and where I was from.  Southie pride stems from the idea of teamwork which we learned at an early age.  That teamwork of helping and being helped is the way I've tried to live my life."  South Boston Today would like to recognize Federico's for the institution it has become and to thank Charlie for helping to make our community what it has become."

After an early morning church service I along with my friends and wife made our way to Sweet Melissa's. We were told the wait would be about 20 minutes. With 2 infants and a toddler along with 4 adults in a small space I could certainly understand the wait. That 20 minute wait turned into about 45 minutes though. I ordered Sunrise grill with tofu which included home fries, a medley of veggies and salsa. Wow! That was an outstanding Vegan dish! The vegetables were a perfect match with the home fries, salsa, and Tofu. My wife got the pancakes with Nutella. She loved hers but it was a bit too much Nutella if there is such a thing lol. My friends liked their pancakes, french toast, etc even though one of their orders of sausage was sent back. Overall, we had a good experience here despite the wait. What a cool spot this establishment is in downtown Decatur!

I'm a bit late hopping on the pokè train. But I think I chose a good place to start my journey. This spot isn't too far from my house, so I decided to check it out for lunch one day. There was a steady crowd, but the Bowl Lab staff got everyone in and out pretty quickly. I made my own "experiment" since I couldn't decide on any of the signature bowls. All of the ingredients were fresh and paired well together, even though I was just picking random items to add to my bowl. Everyone was very friendly, which added to the experience. I'll definitely be making this a frequent lunch spot.

I've been a member of the Pluckers club for a while and I usually make a point of being sure to reap the benefits that come with membership. One of those is a free meal on your birthday (up to $15). 

Usually I reserve this meal to try something on the menu that I haven't tried before. The reasoning behind this: I didn't pay for it so I won't be disappointed if I don't care for it. The catch 22 thought that cancels out that reasoning: I'll consider it a waste of a free meal if I don't care for it and be annoyed that I didn't go with something I knew was good. Sometimes you just can't win.

I ordered the fried jalapeño appetizer. The actual popper is pretty run of the mill (though my actual jalapeño was matured, I don't know if they always come like that or if you might come across green ones) and comes with a strawberry chutney dipping sauce. The actual jalapeño isn't spicy at all. If the pepper were spicy, it would make for a much more satisfying appetizer and the chutney would be that much more effective, but it's still pretty good. I didn't stray into the unknown per se in terms of my meal (an order of 10 wings) but I did try two of the wing sauces that I've not tried before. The hallelujah sauce is very good. At first it tastes a little sweet but there's a hint of a spice in the after taste that grows a little. The other sauce I tried was the spicy lemon pepper sauce. It had a good flavor, kind of a mix between a barbecue sauce and your standard lemon pepper flavoring. Both sauces are rated 2 X on the spice level, but I'd probably drop one of those Xs from both. If you like spice, you can appreciate the tiny kick and taste the marriage of flavors going on in these sauces. If you're really sensitive to spice, I'd say you can consider it dipping your toe in. You're not going to burn off your taste buds and you'll be able to finish your meal without sweating bullets. I ordered the buffalo fries, which is just their normal waffle fry with some seasoning sprinkled on. It's okay, but overall not worth the upcharge. 

I tend to reap my rewards during the afternoon when the restaurant is quiet, but I've been here during some pretty raucous evenings. In both settings, the staff pay attention to what counts. They don't hover, they refill drinks, and they come by to make sure all is well. They're pleasant and want to make sure that you leave satisfied. Another year, another birthday lunch, another job well done by Pluckers.

I moved into the Brooklyn neighborhood about 3 months ago, and in that time have visited the Brooklyn Park Pub a handful of times. Each and every visit has been enjoyable, and the service is always friendly. After the very first visit, the bartender even remembered my name!

They have a great jukebox, and I swear my bf is addicted to their tater tots. I like the bloody mary's myself. (yum!) My one complaint is that I wish their beer selection was better (larger?), but they ARE a whiskey bar, after all. So I can't really complain. 

All in all, it's a great place to stop in for a drink or three! 

And, if you happen to be in the neighborhood because you're going to a show at the Aladdin Theater down the street? Make your way past the two bars that are closer to the theater. This one is BY FAR superior to those, and it's really just a couple of blocks father down the road and across the street. Well worth the (only slightly) extra effort.

This pizza is really good. I've sampled them over the years at various events and when I decided to go in, they were remodeling. Now they've reopened and I decided to stop in on a Saturday I believe. It was pretty slow and I honestly could have sat at the bar. 

My server was pleasant and made for a delightful experience. I ordered the apple martini, not the best but still tasty. The mixer they use isn't very good so that's what the issue was for me. 

The cheeseburger pizza is so yummy. I traded bacon for green peppers at no charge. I got the small for $12 and it came with 6 steaming hot slices. They don't have siracha sauce and is something they could possibly look into having in stock. I used Cholula sauce instead and still enjoyed the pizza. 

I ended up ordering the gluten free brownie as well to go. It came with ice cream and was delicious!!! I think it was about $7.  I will definitely come back here and sit at the bar, apparently they have $6 martini's on Thursday's!

I am stumped as to how the Arlington Heights location got a better review than the Arlington Center (this) location. I used to live in Arlington Heights and the Starbucks there was so gross (and the service typically careless or indifferent) I soon bought my own coffee maker and burr grinder. 

Now I live near Arlington Center and have coffee here (327 Broadway) every morning, when I can't get to Peet's. Not the best Starbucks I've ever had, but definitely reliably good! And the service is *always* friendly. I hate bashing on stores, but this store is much, much better than the Arlington Heights one. Though, I always get the same drink (soy misto) just to be safe.

This restaurant is really good and it is a must try! One note though...it is super small so either go really early (I went at 6) or get a reservation. Oh, and bring cash. They don't take cards. That being said, on to the food. Most places, I wouldn't even mention the free bread they give you. But here, the bread and olive oil was amazing. They put olives in the olive oil giving it a salty flavor which goes well with the bread. 

The waitress also gave my girlfriend and I free calamari which was a pleasant surprise. The calamari was breaded lightly and had decent flavor. It's not the best calamari I've ever had but uh...for the price....totally worth it. 

The entrees were amazing. I had the seafood fra diavolo and my gf had the tiger shrimp with red sauce and linguine. Price were extremely reasonable for the amount of seafood we got. My dish had everything from salmon, to mussels, clams, calamari, and shrimp. I would have preferred a little more heat since it was a fra diavolo but it was still really good. As for the shrimp with red sauce, the dish was just as good. 

So after we were full, we got tiramisu on the house as well. I'm not really a desert guy but the tiramisu was pretty decent. 

All in all, dinner cost $93 for a bottle of chardonnay, calamari, two entrees, and two deserts. Not bad at all. I'd go back for sure...hopefully with freebies again.

Delicious breakfast!!
The TURKEY (heaven) breakfast sausage are amazing. So grateful for that!
A way much healthier and tastier than the regular breakfast pork sausages.

Very common in a successful restaurant in this area: Line-up.Always.
But you will be happy, not sorry!!

So I recommend for breakfast especially during the week-end to get there around 8h30am.
I know, I know it's early on Sunday morning (as they open at 9am)... 
But this way you can you should be able to be seat kinda of quick.

Also I love the fact it's Old School decorated and the vibe is great.
Bonus: They are giving a ''rocket candy'' lollipop at the end of the meal!!

This place is pretty neat.  I was surprised when I arrived, as it's in the middle of nowhere and farm-like with roosters walking around and the dirt parking lot.  It's in a neat little house with so many eclectic things hanging up to look at.  There's even an old VW bus on the outdoor patio to eat in if you'd like.

Their menu is large with way too many delicious things to pick from.  I definitely had a hard time deciding what I wanted, but luckily for me, I overheard the lady at the register mention the special and then it was pretty much decided for me.  It was a waffle cone filled with bbq pulled pork, chili, beer cheese soup and bacon.  It was very good!!  They also have a nice selection of beer to choose from if you're looking to have a drink with your meal.  

I'd definitely like to go back again to try one of the many other things on their menu, since I don't think you can get the true feel of the place on just your first visit!

We walked in to Ben Darwish tickling the ivories, oh, now I understand why they named it that. I thought it had to do with elephant tusks.

Anyway,  the ambience is very nice, the colors are subdued, the sparkling chandelier lamps are fun. The bar is set up on the far side and the tables all are in the middle with the stage up front. They even have some comfy looking booths in the back.  Nice set up.

Servers were wonderful. One of them even squeezed between some tables to avoid my husband from accidentally taking a picture of her instead of the stage.  

They've got a nice wine list and the menu has some great choices. Oh and they have aviation gin.  I kicked back with my dry martini and took it all in. The sun was streaming from their windows and all was well so far.  We ordered an appetizer to begin and had broiled shrimp in a mornay sauce over half of an avocado.  Doug and I dug in to it and the shrimp were fresh and the avocado was ripe enough. The sauce was a little bland but that did not keep us from eating all of it.  There were quite a number of items that had fish, seafood, and even vegetarian on their menu for entrees. This was very encouraging since those items are what we order. I ended up getting the eggplant parmesan.  The eggplant was crispy and had good flavor. There was plenty of pasta and the tomato sauce was more of a fresh tomato vs. a cooked for days sauce. I finished my eggplant and left most of my pasta as I was full.

Very excited to have a new jazz space here in Portland. It's been too long. They've got a ton of live music lined up with free happy hour shows, and paid shows later on in the evening. I'm not sure what all the fuss is about cover charges. They just add it to your dinner bill just like the "other" jazz place down the road. It's normal business and musicians do like to get paid for a living.

I've usually come here before work or after a long day at school to treat my self to their PB&J smoothie! I'm guilty of being a cookie cutter and don't stray too often off my PB&J smoothie. 

I had to let one star go only because when I do decide to try another smoothie I don't really care for it. I tried their chocolate Elvis a while ago and honestly i am in LOVE with chocolate and I wish it was a little more chocolatey. 

But my bottom line I've tried other smoothie places and this place is the best!

I like the fact how I am surrounded by radiation. So cool! So many TV. If you are here for the game you won't miss a second of it. There is a TV at your table, tv along the wall, tv at the bar, tv on top of your table. TV EVERYWHERE. That is too many TV. So the color from the TV screen reflects onto the wall. WOW too many TV

OK now down to the food. This place is all AllStar Wings & Ribs. Well we came on a wednesday night to have wings. I have to say their wings are pretty good. $7 for a lb. You don't need to order drinks to have their wings for $7. As well, they have happy hour if you come in before 6pm. Their wings are not bad. Very yummy and juicy and flavorful. YES they do have 200 flavors of wings. I always like honey garlic and that is what I usually order. They are good. Chipotle was not bad. Honey mustard was also yummy. Salt and Pepper mmm mmm. 

Definitely coming back on a Wednesday Night for more wings.

This is a cute little spot and we'll definitely be back!! The restaurant only seats about 30 people so we waited about half an hour which was fine. We were greeted almost immediately and they offer you water and/or offer while you're waiting which was a nice touch! We ordered the Huevos Al Pastor, Hash of the Day, Biscuits & Biscuits & Gravy with a side of Sliced Avocado with S&P. Party of / and yes we were definitely hungry and ready to eat, dong judge!  Everything care out within 20 minutes and was well seasoned. We loved everything we ordered and only had about a half portion of the hash leftover. We'll definitely be back to try some more goodies in March!

Came here for lunch during restaurant week. Very classy vibe here. You can dress casual during lunch but I would get a little more dressed up for dinner.

Started off with a Riesling and it was very crisp and sweet. My sister and I didn't want a glass to ourselves so we split one. The waiter poured it in two separate glasses. How awesome and convenient. 

They gave us white bread to start. It was fine with the olive oil but nothing spectacular.

For appetizer, we got the Arancini. It was basically a mozzarella ball. I loved it. Crispy on the outside yet melting cheese on the inside. Marinara sauce was good. A bit tangy. 

The wait between appetizers and entrees took quite some time.

For entrees, we got ravioli and lasagna. The spinach ravioli was delicious. It had ham or something in it which basically reminded me of pepperoni. I liked it. Ravioli was not as soft as I would have expected though. But man, this dish super filling. My sister's lasagna was scrumptious. It had this amazing beef it it. Also, super filling. We could not finish. 

For dessert, we got tiramisu. So darn good. Light, fluffy and not too sweet.

Overall, two thumbs up.

We went here with a large group and they were able to fit us in no problem. We also enjoyed the entertainment they had. Our waiter was fantastic - couldn't have asked for better!  The Sangria and food were perfect and tasty. We got the family dish. Can't remember the name but it was the $55 version. 

The only draw back was that the music was really loud. We had to yell just to talk across the table. I would return but only with a small group.

As a homebrewer, it is hard to be happier with a supply store.

I have been homebrewing for the better part of 6 years and Bader's always has not only the supplies I need, but the knowledge as well.  This is the place where each of the folks that work there are always willing to spend some time with you explaining each stage, differences in grain and hops and how they will affect your brew.  If you have an off brew, bring it in and they can tell you where you need to change things (often, sanitation).  

For the wine maker, they have all the supplies you might need and once a year they buy a truckload (literally) of various wine grapes if you don't want to make your wine any other way.

Honestly, my review isn't higher because I barely have a point of comparison, but I can tell you that I have never left Bader's feeling disappointed or cash strapped (unless, of course, I did it to myself).

My husband, an Austin native, has got to be Rudy's biggest fan.  He hasn't lived in Austin for 8 years and still I have to hear about this place constantly!  Well, we just went there last weekend and yes I am sold.  Best part about this place is the samples - if you have never been there they happily give you samples of whatever meat you want to try before you order so you know you will be happy with what you get.  What a nice concept!  Even let us try the sides as well.  The extra lean brisket was fabulous, I was very impressed with the tenderness and flavor.  Their sauce blows the competition away, this is where they shine!

They got me in for a last-minute appointment when the government shutdown threatened to derail my USDA vet paperwork, so I was really appreciate of that. I also didn't expect the added bonus of finding a coupon for the first visit through Yelp! so that saved me some money too! The vet I saw, though I forget her name, was extremely friendly -- perhaps one of the friendliest I've met -- and was quick and efficient. Since I'd previously printed out and filled out the USDA paperwork, I was able to walk out of the office with the completed paperwork instead of having to pick it up in 2 hours. My wait wasn't excessive -- maybe 20 mins after my scheduled appointment. My only complaint is they seem to nickle and dime you a bit. I was charged separate fees for each item of paperwork I needed filled out, where other vet offices just charge you a flat paperwork fee. Oh, I almost forgot to mention, the vet I got is extremely experienced at filling out USDA export paperwork and fills out multiple per day. My other small town vet, Brookline Village Vet, only has one USDA vet with a sporadic schedule and less experience handling this paperwork, so if paperwork is what you are after, I would send you here first! Usually you have to answer tons of questions about the paperwork for your vet, but not here! They even answered some of mine.

I first checked this place out in the middle of July when Oregon was in the middle of a heatwave. The line was out the door and it seemed pretty busy, but people were popping out of the place constantly, so I figured it was worth the wait and service seemed to be working quickly.

I've tried it again a couple of times since and granted the line always seems to reach the door, but service is pretty fast and the cashiers are always super patient and nice. For a Friday night (at around 7 pm) in October, the place was still filled with people, but not super packed like how it was over the summer. 

Their prices range from $4-5+ and most add-on's like the boba's (regular or clear/crystal) are $0.50. Split cups are the best way to go if you're still trying to familiarize yourself with the menu and figuring out what you like/don't like from their options. Buying a mason jar from them only costs $2.50 extra (which is surprisingly cheap...most people charge up to $5 more), and they also have a travel bottle available--it's a glass bottle with several designs and sleeves available.

My go-to and favorite drink so far is their Strawberry Limeade with regular boba. It's semi-sweet, but has a tangy/sour taste due to the limeade and is super refreshing. Both fruit flavors emphasize the sweetness of the boba.

I'd also recently tried their Peach Blossom and Lychee Crush in a split cup...both drinks are very similar to each other. They both had chopped up fruit in the drink and most of it contained fruit juice. Both gives you a summer feel and is very refreshing. The Lychee Crush has lime in it, which added to the refresh-ness. I got them with clear/crystal boba, which is similar to the regular but just a little bit less chewy and more dense. They ran out of regular boba when I went--around 8:30 pm on a Saturday. 

Parking is not a problem. It's in a small plaza next to Dollar Tree and Mio Sushi, so there's plenty of parking in the lot.

The only reason I've deducted a star is because the place is pretty small and is not ideal for sitting around to hang out with friends. There are a few two-seater tables on the side and one table that can fit maybe four people, but other than that, it's a place that's best for going in and out. It just gets hard to find a place to stand/wait for your order when it gets pretty crammed in there.

Due to the popularity of the place, I'm surprised they haven't come out with a loyalty program. It would be awesome if they had punch cards--some buy 10 drinks, get 1 free like Dutch Bro's or other boba/coffee places. 

I have yet to try their Mangonada drink, which has chunks of mango, but my boyfriend has ordered the drink with watermelon chunks and Tajin and he absolutely loved it! If you're a fan of these types of Mexican snacks, you'll surely love and enjoy Zero Degrees. If not, there are plenty of fruit juice options as well as a few teas (milk tea, Thai tea, matcha green tea). It's definitely a unique place...kind of like boba drinks with a Mexican dessert twist. 

Give it a try! It's worth it!

Love:
- Really awesome flavorful chai and coffee that pleases my coffee enthusiast friends
- Good wifi with password on a little sign
- POWER OUTLETS EVERYWHERE including on a little circular 6-outlet station on the communal table omg
- Accepts what seems like all newfangled payment systems, including Apple Pay for that one awkward time I leave the house with my phone but not my actual wallet!
- Friendly service!
- All chairs with backs!

All that in a cozy atmosphere with fab Indonesian stylings.

A few things I don't love, but that definitely won't stop me from coming here regularly:
- Food is a little hit-or-miss for me. I enjoyed the roti when I got it before, but this time I had the gado-gado and it was a tad dry/flavorless. Will try something else next time.
- Restroom is weirdly outside and 'round back

I really wanted to give this place five stars but I just can't, at least not yet.

Having a young child of 11 months, we wanted to introduce her to swimming and after a few Google searches, found three nearby locations to this Michigan-based franchise, including their newest out in Norwood that opened recently.

I filled out an interest form and no more than 90 seconds later, my phone rang and the young one was booked for her first, mini class. A few days went by and off we were on a brisk Saturday morning.

The establishment itself is absolutely awesome. Bright colors, a nice fish tank and a huge viewing area which overlooks the pool, with chairs, for the family members who aren't actively participating in the swimming. There's some Tropical-themed changing rooms, a changing table and even a couple of centrifuges to help dry up towels and swim gear. They've thought of everything and it's all kid-themed and immaculate.

The staff is relatively friendly, especially the ones in the pool doing the classes and overall we've had a good experience. Well... except for the first time we went. The water heater broke so the pool was much colder than it should have been. No heads up, apologies or refunds. We had to check-in before our second class to make sure that things were back to normal and they were but it would have been nice to know ahead of time because we would have never driven out there knowing that my daughter would spend 30 chilly minutes in the water shivering and miserable.

So why only 4 stars? Mostly because of their front desk scheduling process and pricing models. Both times we've been they've been incredibly aggressive in trying to sell us on their $100/month tier good for 1 lesson/a week even though I've repeatedly said that because of scheduling, that we'd rather do the $25 walk-ins. They've told us many times that they can't fit us in many classes because they prioritize the people with the monthly plan which is absurd because why offer walk-ins if you're not going to honor anything?

Their schedules are also very limited on weekends with only 2-3 available 30 minute blocks per day which can make it tough for some people to make it. I was kind of hoping they'd have more per day but maybe that'll change over time? Who knows.

We plan on continuing to come for the time being and hope that they'll take a more passive approach to this whole $100 plan and let us do the $25 walk-ins. Rumor is they might get rid of it all-together at which point we'll probably go somewhere else since I don't want to commit to a lesson a week. They're aggressive to the point where we've had to walk out and get things scheduled over the phone which was much easier and quicker. Go figure.

But that aside, Goldfish is a great franchise and the staff clearly cares deeply about the experience they provide and the facilities are top notch. I'm a fan.

Steel is great for unwinding after work or pre-party meet-up. There is a sushi happy hour that happens every Wednesday from 5-7pm.  You walk right in and make a bee line to the curved bar, order a Mango-tini, get sushi=good times.  You and your friends are set for 2 hours. Watch carefully for the line that will appear for sushi-it's that serious.  Don't worry if you came alone, everyone is very friendly so you won't be alone for long :).  The place usually clears out by 6:45 and that's around the time for last call on sushi.

The food here was incredible. Tapas style deliciousness jam-packed with flavor. The service was very professional, getting close to standoffish without quite crossing the line enough for me not to want to come back. Here's a tip though. If you've just completed a 24 mile bike ride and want a place to comfortably rest your tush- this is not the place. You have a choice between backless metallic bar stools, and a pad less wooden bench that runs the length of the restaurant. Ouchies. But at least my stomach was appeased. 

I will be back!

We waited an hour and a half for this meal. Definitely not worth that wait. 

I got the Elk burger. This was well executed to the medium rare I ordered. The elk was not to gamey. The texture was more smooth than beef. The flavor was delicate, meaty and unadulterated. I appreciate that. The bun was soft and a bit chewy brioche. This was quite good. 

Despite feeling like a dinner-mill, the food was good. So I can't complain. I didn't want to like it, but I did.

This a fun little Mexican restaurant located in Point Orlando. They have a big happy hour party the last Friday of every month with great specials on Coronas and Margarita's. In fact you can get a huge margarita here that you hang around your neck, and they even have the strawberry variety. Adobe's has plenty of outdoor patio seating for some great people watching and a fun festive environment. My favorite day of the year for this place has to be Cinco de Mayo though. They really do it up right with an all day long festival with entertainment. Its normally on the Saturday before the big day. I would suggest checking it out for a great holiday experience.

I've been to this shop a few times and am generally happy.  They do good work and don't try to sell any extra services.  I've found them to have the best rates amongst other local businesses and dealers.  My only slight knock is that I've had to wait longer than promised for the repairs to be complete.  In my most recent visit, I was told the car would be ready by noon and ended up sitting in the waiting room until 3:30.  I'll continue to use Tech One, just won't count on the work being done until a few hours after the estimated time.

Heading back home to San Antonio, needed some food but didn't want to hit the normal breakfast places. I know Austin has tons of food trucks, so I went on yelp to see what was up. We found Killa Wasi and it definitely it Ely hit the spot. We shared the BOAR BENEDICTO and the berries and cream, both were really good. The staff is great and these young ladies got it going on, one small piece of advise, remember to add a touch of salt and a hint of pepper, it brings all the amazing flavors of your food together. Next time we are in Austin we'll come by and see how you are doing. Thanks for a great food start of my day

This hotel is nice and convenient if you need to stay at the airport area.  Amy was on when we arrived and gave us a ride in from the airport after we dropped our car off.  On the day we left, we got another ride in the morning at 5am to the airport.  Luckily, the airport is only 8 minutes away.

The lobby looked nice when we arrived and our room was very clean and comfortable.  The court yard and the pool is nice.  It's in the airport area so there's not many places to walk to for a nice meal.  But we had a car during our stay so it wasn't an issue.

I like this location a bit more than the one at Cordova. I didn't try their food, because they're not really known for their food. What I like about this location is that they have a chocolate fountain with 2 varieties; chocolate or vanilla. It's not really packed and they have a lot of seats. I had the earl grey tea and I loved it. When I took my last bite of the cone the vanilla chocolate melted it was weird, but tasty.

Bento Box: a neat
collection of all my favorite
Japanese flavors

I'm a dish-tination diner: I visit a particular restaurant because I'm in the mood for a particular dish. 
When I'm craving raw fish for lunch, I go to Sushi Sake. The Sashimi and Shrimp Tempura bento box delivers three pieces of salmon and two pieces of tuna sashimi, two tempura shrimp with a few tempura veggies, salad with creamy ginger dressing, two pieces of California roll, and steamed rice.  Oh, and miso soup to start.  All components are fresh and delicious. This isn't Uchi...the preparation is staightforward and not creative. But that's why it also isn't a budget buster, and at $12.95 it is hands down THE best sushi lunch deal in town. You will leave stuffed to the, um, gills.

You know those moments when you sit back in your seat and try to comprehend the amount of food you just ate? Yep, thats how I felt after my meal at Kyo. 

I went with a huge group of people, half of whom I did not know, and they had enough seating for all of us in the same area. Bonus. 

The All You Can Eat costs about $24.00 a person but, the variety and quality of food is worth the cost. And, that moment when you sit back and try to comprehend what you just ate, you've probably eaten more than $24.00 of food. 

This kind of meal is perfect for a large group, the more people, the more food options, and it gives you the opportunity to chat while you cook the meat and munch on sushi rolls. 

A huge bonus- if you order sake- they will ask you if you want it cold or hot. Always a nice option, but we know hot is the only way. 

The service was okay, it was a busy night but we did wait a while for drinks and found that we received some things we did not order. Make sure to check your order form when it comes back to you. Anything you don't eat, they charge on top of the base price. 

Lastly, beware that large groups have auto gratuity on the bills. Most of the group did not know and tipped on top of it.  Those servers made a lot from us that night. 

Live and learn I guess. I'll be going back regardless.

A chain for bahn mis? I can't say that I'd heard of Lee's prior to walking in but they have stores in California, Colorado and Texas to name a few states. Bahn mis have always been in one off stores with just Vietnamese families usually running the business. I've been to An Xuyen, Bihn Mihn a few other local places and love the food out of all of them. So how does a company with 55 stores compare? Surprisingly pretty good.

House made mayo? Check. House made pickled carrots and daikon? Check. A 12" French bread roll? Check. I was quite surprised, pleasantly at that. You even have the option of getting regular sandwiches like turkey or roast beef (they refer to those as European sandwiches) There's even a mini grocery store of sorts where you can purchase Vietnamese sausages, coffee, the house made mayo, desserts, bread and other ethnic items.

As for my bbq pork sandwich? It was really good. All of the above mentioned items, plus cilantro, jalapenos, salt, pepper and a splash of soy sauce. The last being different from other bahn mis I have had in PDX. The roll was a bit sturdier than some of the one off places and nice and crispy. There was plenty of pork and lots of crunchy veggies. The price was very much in line for this type of food and and the fried banana I got to accompany was really tasty as well. The two together was barely $5.

I keep finding new food up and down 82nd. If you folks living in inner Portland or over on the west side haven't found your way out to here, you should. You're missing out on some great Asian cuisine.

Enjoy.

We stopped in for a drink and a bite to eat after looking at the reviews.  Nice atmosphere, friendly service and good prices.  Now for the food!!!  The Reuben sandwich was unreal and a wonderful surprise!  Not like HUGE unreal or anything like that, but a nice size and good flavour.  My guy normally doesn't order these, but it was recommended by our server and he was so very happy that she did.  I had to have a bite and it was quite good.  Not what I would think of as a typical Reuben.  Well, I'm no Reuben connoisseur, so I don't really know, but I alway pictured them to be different...like stronger flavours I guess.  This wasn't like that, the bread was amazing and the sauce had a wonderful subtle flavour.  Nice melted cheese, chips and a very small coleslaw.  The only reason this place didn't get a 5 is because the salad (although reasonable in price) was kind of small for a meal, it is in fact mostly just lettuce haha and a touch of cheese and nuts.  It had pretty good flavours, but I was expecting a more substantial salad for $12.50.  I was hungry about 45 minutes afterwards and started thinking that I should have also ordered the Reuben.

My wife and I have been here several times and I have to say that I've never gone to a place that serves with as many variations and usually does them well and/or over the average. My wife and I stumbled onto this place awhile back looking for Asian type cuisine (for her) on a Sunday. This was one of few places open that day. 
Parking can be tricky at times as the parking lot is pretty small, you will most likely have to park on the highway or possibly on side street if there is a space.
The staff is very friendly and usually attentive. Although, they can be a bit slow once after you've gotten your food which isn't a big deal for me as long as they check up after the serve. They always looked out if I wanted a little something extra without charging the full price which is very nice.
So, now the food. My wife loves their Salt & Pepper Prawns and the Calamari dishes. She appreciates how Decoy does it fresh without overcooking the food, especially, the Calamari.
I've had their fish and chips, burgers, fish burger, and basic breakfast with sausage and a side biscuit and gravy. All of it was solid except for the breakfast. The breakfast was just...ok. Because the Decoy doesn't necessarily offer a breakfast that includes an option with biscuit and gravy , that meal got a bit spendy. Ran around $15-16. The biscuit and gravy didn't have much meat nor flavor, the sausage looked and tasted like something out of a Brown N' Serve package (in my opinion, of course). So, I'm not sold on the breakfast served there (at least, that one). However, that won't deter us from going there as they do very well in other food variations and looking forward to trying them as time goes on. Yes, I'm a fan!

Yea' boi! ;-) I love the sister branch of this restaurant, so I had high expectations coming to yebo and it met my expectations by far. The reason why its not a 5 and a 4 star review is only due to lack of variety/options in the menu. The menu is pretty limited, not much variety to choose from plus the plates are small portions/tapas style, but the limited things I did try were pretty damn good! 

Ostrich --- oh my! loved it! 
Tacos- very good 
bobitek?? the bread bowl with ground beef and fried egg-- super yummmy! 

Overall, I enjoyed each and every bite of meal, just wish there was a little more they can offer or make their portions larger so its like a meal instead of very limited small plates.

Miso Izakaya is a rather small restaurant. However that doesn't take away from how much character the inside has. Rustic wood trim covers the entire place, anime and traditional Japanese drawings can be viewed all around the restaurant.


The Sushi.. me being a connoisseur I headed straight for the sushi bar. 1pc per order, at first I thought the prices were high for what I was "going" to get. However I was pleased with the quality of the fish. The chefs are knowledgeable and friendly. All around I would definitely come back. I'm a sushi die hard... Nobu is my top spot.

We drove past some beautiful beaches in the Dorchester area (and an industrial street) before arriving at the JFK Presidential Library and continued to be astonished by our setting.  The building has a pristine and modern look with a gorgeous glass pavilion.  It's located on a peninsula by Dorchester Bay with a promenade (lots of joggers) and great views of South Boston.  Admissions is $14 for adults and $12 for students/seniors. There is free parking with admissions.  I like how the admissions sticker is the seal of the President of the United States.

We started off with a 15-20 minute documentary in the auditorium, which exits into the exhibits.  They have done an incredible job in designing their exhibits and included video footages so we can relive historical moments during JFK's presidency.  My favorite was the Campaign Trail section.  There's also a replica of his desk in the Oval Office with his personal items on display and exhibits dedicated to his brother RFK and his wife Jacqueline.

Having been to both this Presidential Library and the Sixth Floor Museum at Dealey Plaza at Dallas, I can say that they are different.  Although both do an incredible job at exploring his campaign and presidency, the Presidential Library is more of a collection (in a beautiful setting) whereas the Sixth Floor Museum has panels and video clips with an audio guide to keep us engaged in additional topics such as JFK's assassination and its aftermath (after all, it's in Dealey Plaza where JFK was shot during his campaign for re-election).

With good cocktails, a fun and large atmosphere, bar food, and a ping pong table, nothing is to not like about this bar. Upon walking in, I immediately noticed the size and how spacious the bar was. Even though people were buying drinks and the bar was well populated, I did not feel cramped or squished. It was easy for a group of six to find seating. 

We ordered fries and then found seats next to the ping pong table since some of us wanted to play. I did not want to play, so I decided to get some cocktails. Looking up at the cocktail menu, I was amused by their names. They were long, and I don't remember all the names, but I remember one was 'Started From the Bottom Now We're Peaches'. The sassy and tongue in chic names were unique and I had never seen names like these. Going along with the names, the drinks were also delicious and well made. I ordered one with rose flavor, st. Germain, peaches, vodka, and some other ingredients, and the fruity and floral flavors really popped. The cocktails were solid, so I ordered three different ones throughout the night. 

The bacon and pork gravy fries were also solid, and I had never seen them anywhere else. Tilt did a good job with the fries, and the gravy really worked with the fries. 

The atmosphere was casual and inviting. It reminded me of my favorite brewery/college bar with delicious beer and a good casual atmosphere for friends to hang out and catch up. Since the drinks and ambiance were awesome, I definitely plan to come back next time I am in Portland.

This was the first time I used Cooper Lake Automotive.  I had read many on-line reviews that were very favorable...so I was expecting a first class operation.

As a business owner I know that things do not always go as planned, and the true test of a great business is how they handle abverse situations.

I broght my Explorer (129k+ miles) in for brakes and a noise in the rear dirve train.   CLA called with an estimate and said they would have it finised by the end of the day.  Later in the afternoon they called to say that they had damaged the rear axle while taking everything apart to replace a rear bearing, and they would not be able to get a new axle until the following day.  CLA stuck to their original quote.

I noticed an oil leak under the rear end after I picked my Explorer.  I called and CLA asked me to bring it in so they could take a look.  Upon instection CLA said they must have damaged a seal while making the repair and I would need shedule a day where they could make the repair.  I asked if I could wait on it and they said they had to take the whole thing back apart and it would take most of the day to repair.

While things did not go as planned, Cooper Lake Automotive made no excuses, applogized for the inconvience, and made it right.  I will be back.

Pros: Good ball quality, lots of stalls, clean, good prices

Cons: No grass hitting area, empty lobby/pro shop, max distance 220 yards

I finally got my clubs shipped from my parents house in Omaha to my place in Oregon. Mind you, that's after four years of living in California and a year in Oregon, so I guess better late than never? I have a work golf event coming up, so I wanted to get my clubs. I also wanted to get some practice in before the event. Looking up places, I came up with Sunset Golf Center. About 10 minutes from where I live, and very close to Nike HQ, this place is a casual place for the casual golfer to hit a casual bucket of balls.

I was impressed by the quality of range balls I found. Most of them looked like fairly new Nike balls, lacking scuffs or chips. There are about 20 stalls, each with a clean mat to hit off of. I'm not a huge fan of hitting off mats, but they are clean and easier to hit off of compared to other mats at driving ranges I've been to before. The max distance is 220 yards, so hitting a driver full strength might not be the best idea. Probably a better place to practice irons, hybrids and wedges. They also have a putting green and a sand trap to practice those shots as well. $9.00 gets you 120 balls to hit, not a bad deal at all.

I always prefer hitting off grass than mats, and that this place lacks grass to hit off of is disappointing. Also, the lobby/pro shop area is very empty. Not much of a selection of golf items to purchase. They have some arcade games, a snack bar, and a big screen TV to watch. Seems kind of cavernous. The place also has a mini golf course and lessons. Since I haven't utilized either, I can't give a fair review of them.

Overall, hitting a bucket of balls is a great way to relief stress, spend some time outdoors, and even improve your golf game. Sunset Golf Center is nice to have close by and I'm sure I'll be back again, especially since now I have my clubs.

I have been coming here since I was a little boy (that would make it nearly 50 years!) 

Though we don't live as close to Antoine's as we used to, I still love going back there. Walking through the doors is like stepping back to a simpler time. The folks behind the counter wear old-time bakers shirts in blue or white with the Antoine's name embroidered on them. They have the old string dispensers hanging from the ceiling, ready to wrap your boxes of baked goods. The cases are filled with beautiful-looking pastries, cakes, pies and cookies and other confections.

Upon walking in, the smell is intoxicating, whetting your appetite for the treats to come. Oh, yes, and they are fantastic! You can't go wrong with anything.

Do yourself a favor and make a visit to "The Lake", mush, for some incredible Antoine's pastries!

outdoor drinking!! OK, that alone deserves 5 stars in this city. i haven't been to charlie's in ages...the last time i was there their outdoor drinking spot consisted of a few roped off tables on the sidewalk outside the bar. i made plans with a friend to meet here and didn't realize that the whole back of the place has been built out into a place reminiscent of zeitgeist in san francisco (it just needs a better attitude and a tamale lady but hey this is boston). i was so excited. on a beautiful day, this must be an amazing place to hang out. the beer prices were not bad at all, either. i see many summertime drinking sessions here in my future!
oh p.s. the service sucks but did you really expect *good* service at charlie's? c'mon now

Supposedly you need to live in Decatur and have a resident card to go to this park but no one asked me for one the two times I went...and I don't live in Decatur. oh well....oopsie! The park is huge and there were at least 20 dogs running around today. It was great. The people were all very kind and the dogs had a blast. The dogs have plenty of room to run around, the field is really long and pretty wide too.
 
A few frisbees and tennis balls laying around let us play fetch when my dog wasn't playing with other dogs. It also has a few "hills" which is nice for the dogs to get out that doggie energy! Only reason I gave 4 stars is because I wish they had more benches around the park. They only had a few towards the entrance, and then towards the far end of the park. 

It's OK though, what matters is that my dog came home exhausted and happy!

Also, they cut the water off in the winter so you have to bring your own water if you want your pooch to drink while you're there.

I love this place!!  I always go to Tentatsu nearby but switched over recently.  I love the decor inside it's simple but has a nice atmosphere.  I come here with my mom and we usually order two things and we're full to the max.

We get the dynamite combo which has cali roll, dynamite roll, salmon and tuna roll which comes with miso soup and salad.  The miso soup is a bit too salty but the salad is light and crispy.  

The dynamite roll is sooooo good!  We got beef teriyaki which was super fresh and hot but super oily so that wasn't so good.  The time before we got the beef teriyaki roll which was soooooo much tastier than Tentatsu since they put some green onion in it which brings out the flavour of the beef.  Honestly ordering two dishes is more than enough for two people to eat. 

I will definitely come here again with friends and family!

As a non hillbilly, let me just say that this place is worth its weight in gold.  Look, zoos in general are not high on my list.  They keep animals that should be in the wild in containment, and even when they're based on rescue/rehab, a good part of time is spent interfering with what nature would be sorting out on its own...survival of the fittest and all that.

This place has a TON of gators, and because they allow you to feed them, they are so bloated and overfed that they never even take a shot at the plethora of birds in the water with them.  Hell I saw a duck actually pull a piece of hot dog OUT of a gators mouth and the gator never freakin moved.

Not a big fan of the gator wrestling show.  I know it's done to raise money for the rehab of gators and whatnot but....I dunno...to me it kinda seems like you're not giving proper respect to these animals to first wrangle them, then tape their jaws shut and let people pose sitting on them.  Just...not a fan, rubs me the wrong way.

With all of that having been said, the attractions are fun, the opportunity to feed the "wild" gators (An upcharge) was a good time.  I like that the place is here and tries to behave more like a refuge than a zoo...and the gift shop...holy shit the gift shop.  The gift shop is a miraculous blend of hillbilly, gun nut, and psychopath.  I actually drank wine from a pouch...like a capris sun, but worse.  I was saddened to see that between my visits on 2014 and 2016, they apparently sold out of the onesie that read "I'll nap when the huntin' is done", but was THRILLED to see that I should thank my military for having a teacher that taught me English.

Seriously, this place is a do not miss, as long as you don't take yourself too seriously and have an hour to kill in the gift shop.

This is a great addition to historic College Park!  If you haven't tried it yet and are looking for a quick take out with friendly service and quality food you should give this place a shot. I had the big burger and I thought it was pretty good. It wasn't the best burger I ever had but it was cooked well and a good portion and good condiments. Waaaaaaay better than Micky ds. My husband got the gyro and raved about it. I took a bite and thought it was delish. My two kids both got chicken ringers which are fried chicken sandwiches. They were good quality but not as tasty as say chic fil a.  We ordered the nuggets for my three yr old but he fell asleep and didn't eat them so my husband had one and didn't think they were very good. Overall we liked all the food and the service was very good. We will definitely go back sometimes when we are craving a little fast food.

This bakery-in-the-wall (across from Starbucks and Anthem Park) has become a dependable place to go.  They have standbys such as scallion cheddar biscuits and various quiches to go (including vegetarian), as well as croissants, breads, and a changing array of treats. They even have carefully baked dog bones for your pet!  Outdoor seating, coffee on the go, tea, a daily  bulletin board . . .

Their service outside is friendly and attentive.  So nice to have French food with Vancouver smiles.

I would only suggest better service in the newly opened restaurant inside.  Good to keep things friendly and casual in this city, right?

The food was good. I will definitely come back. I order 2 vegetable sambusas, chicken tikka masala, lentil soup and garlic naan.  The lentil soup was DELICIOUS! Both myself and my 3 year old loved it. The chicken tikka masala was tasty and creamy but could've been a bit hotter heat-wise. The rice was fragrant and tasty as well. One of my two sambusas was warm in parts and cold in others, while the other was hot throughout despite it being eaten last. The dipping sauce for the sambusas was sweet and delicious which complimented the spice of the sambusas. We both enjoyed the naan. 

One of the restaurant staff approached our table and asked how our dining experience was so I informed him about the sambusa and he had a fresh one made for us. 

I would have preferred my sambusas before my meal but that's not a big deal to me. I'll be back to Layla's soon to see if they're worthy of 5 stars.

This is my neighborhood store that all my friends know I call "the nice mart"    If you think they have a good selection of beer, you can thank me (...partly).   I've lived in the neighborhood for 6 years and constantly asked the owners (husband and wife) to stock beer I liked.   With the exception of some high-end Belgian beer, they've gotten most everything (...like Hopworks...which he was selling for less than the whole foods down the street!).    If you want them to carry something, just ask!    How many corner stores will do that for you?     And now I see that have a ton of good wines as well!   This place rules.  

They have a small selection of other household items and typical convenience store stuff as well.  But the owners are great people and I really like supporting them.   They do charge $0.50 for debit, so use cash if possible.    

And if you have some time to burn, check out the display case in the front.   Such a crazy collection of items!

I usually grab some beer and a bite here when I am in town, and it's never disappointed. Beer is reasonably priced, wide variety available, and tasty enough. The food has always been good, and I have tried everything from soups to apps to burgers to sammies to entrees. I recall one day they had a poutine app and some steak special and both were actually quite outstanding. 

Overall, this is one of my favorite spots close to Fenway, as the rest tend to have mediocre food and even worse service (usually due to the volume of patrons, not the fault of the staff). Not the case here, despite the fact they could probably get away with it, just from being in such a prime location.

After all the raving I've heard about this place I finally was able to try it out on my last trip to the World. Everything we ordered was awesome. The Cheese Soup is a must try but its really heavy so I would share it with someone instead of ordering it on your own so that you're not full by the time your steak comes. 

This meal will definitely set you back some. For dinner it's 2 table service credits on the dining plan otherwise be prepared to shell out a decent amount of money. Because of this and the difficulty of getting reservations I don't know if I'll make it a point to come here every time I'm in Disney but I'll most definitely be headed back here on a future trip.

And yes you do need to make reservations as far in advance as possible. I made mine a whole 6 months before the trip. If you're staying at a Disney World resort you can make reservations 180 days in advance of the first day of your stay.

It is always nice to have some food from home when one is so far away. The interior of the restaurant is definitely cozy and there is a good array of items on the menu to try out. The tastes are definitely altered to be milder but the food is still pretty good. I had the tofu thote, which was very tasty! Portions are rather large but the prices are not very cheap. Would definitely come again if I happen to be in the area.

How does Pollo Norte take chicken, the wallflower of the meat world, and turn it into the bell of the ball? Your guess is as good as mine. Love? Gypsy Magic? Seasoning passed down from generation to generation? All of the above?! Sure! 

Rotisserie chicken is dope, so it's safe to assume a place that perfects that art would be likewise dope. Pollo Norte does one thing, and it does it right. You come here for the chicken, you stay for the chicken. Or you get it to go and gorge yourself in the privacy of your home, hopefully with your hands like an animal because that's what I always want to do but there is people around. If this place were closer to my house, my trash can would be filled with chicken carcasses. 

They offer a few basic sides. Rice, beans, slaw, potatoes and of course corn tortillas. I always get extra corn tortillas because they're on the small side and God forbid I run out while there is chicken to be had. Sides are good, not great. In full disclosure having grown up in a Mexican household, I can get on my high horse when it comes to beans and Mexican rice. For me it could stand a little more TLC spice wise, but that being said it is good and the price is right. I will say the corn tortillas are on point. 

I've heard they run out of chickens but this hasn't been my experience. Last time I was there they mentioned having increased production and that you can call ahead. So be smart, call ahead if it's your dinner plans and get that chicken on lock down.

A much more intimate setting than the upstairs or neighboring venues attached to the Vinyl. This place has a nice, waist-high stage, again with decent sound and a lot of tables where people can sit around and chill.

As with the Loft, if you're a musician loading in here is kind of shitty. They yell at you while you park on the curb and bring it in. Then there's not really anywhere good to park. There are pay area all around, but the only free that I know of is on the other side of the building, kind of hidden between two businesses.

I know a lot of people really like coming here, and I think the main reason I don't go is that there are very rarely any acts that come in here that I like. It seems mostly locals or bands no one's ever heard of (even on an independent level) which is fine, but I don't really go out these days just to watch bands. 

Ah, well, you know.

GO TO HATTIE B!!! The chicken is hot the way I like it. It is fried perfectly and the seat seeps through to the actual meat. Amazing. The peach cobbler is very good and you get a good portion for $3. The parking is horrendous!!! There might be 7 spots and the line is always out the door. There is a paid parking lot next door but why pay to park to pick up food. I mean I'll be there 20 mins max. All in all an def must go.

I love this place. The decor is upscale, trendy clean and zen. I have been coming here for - on average 3 times a month - 7 years.

 I'm still coming back although they took my favorite dish off the menu the black peppered seared Ahi and Bon Vie took the seared Ahi off their menu as well. 
My favorites: Firecracker Shrimp, egg drop soup, edamame, brand new roll the Nutty Almond Roll (Great) lays over 2 delicate sauces with thin strips of toasted coconut garnish. The steamed pot stickers are great the dough is thin and light not like other places where you can barely chew them the dough is so thick. Spouse likes the mango chicken. 

What I find insulting is you are charged $3.00 every time you get a new cup of tea with a bag. This was a first for me. Usually tea is refilled at no charge. The management may want to reconsider doing this - nicket and diming.

Service has always been great and I am so excited when they are busy , because that means - hopefully - they are doing well.

They rock...

there are a ton of ramen places to choose from, and they all have their own perks and flavors and whatnot, but this place has more than just ramen. it's more of an izakaya, which is great when you have a variety of tastes with you. you can get yakitori, ramen, poke, and a number of other things. i opted for the veggie ramen and added their yuzu bomb. guys. that bomb is NO JOKE. like, i mean, there should be a warning on the menu. i used maybe one full ramen spoonful for my entire bowl, and while it was slightly uncomfortable at first, somewhere into the middle of the meal, i inhaled something that sent me into one of those cartoon-like episodes a la roger rabbit. holy crap. i started crying and snot came pouring out of my nose. so, ya know, just beware.

the food was excellent. there's plenty of parking. and, if you check in on yelp, there are a couple of beer options you can get for $1.99. they have a great sake selection, too, if that's what you seek.

Small zoo but both times we've been we have been able to see most of the animals out and about in their exhibits. It was raining during our last trip but overall it wasn't too bad. We brought our infant daughter here and she stayed awake for a lot of the zoo and actually seemed interested in looking at the animals. 

I love their seal exhibit. I could sit there for hours watching them swim and dance in the water. 

Can't wait to bring our daughter back throughout the years as she gets older and can understand and interact more.

I heart trying on vintage dresses here..  even when I don't end up buying any. What could cheer you up more than trying on a cute 70's halter dress?  Ok, maybe there are some other things but this is a great vintage shop and I love the new location so much more than the cramped spot it was at before.  The dressing rooms are nice too which you don't find very often w thrifty vintage clothing places.  Good selection, & ok prices for the cool stuff you can get!

Donair Town is a reasonable spot to grab lunch while on campus.  I typically wander over for lunch at least once a week.  I've only ever ordered the platters (chicken, beef, or lamb) so my comments are limited to those.

The platters are a hearty serving of rice, the chosen meat, greek salad, hummus, and a pita.  Double up your meat for an extra buck or so on a super platter.  Always a consistent meal, and always leaves me satisfied.  

The couple that runs the place are a well-oiled machine that keeps the near constant lunch line moving at a reasonable pace.

My wife and I have been meaning to eat at this restaurant for a long time. We finally made plans with four others to have dinner here. We were greeted very graciously by the staff and first had a drink in the beautifully appointed bar. For dinner I had the lemon sole special which was outstanding. The server was a very well trained professional. we all had a great time. This is a cash only establishment so take that into consideration. A agreed we would return again soon.

Always great service - prompt assistance and ample samples. I also really like the renovated store. It seems more enclosed and united for some reason. Perhaps it's the shape of the store.
 They managed to pack the stores with tons of options to choose from and somehow wearing white lab coats make them more trustworthy.. (a victim of stereotype and social norm) I very much appreciate I don't have to play coy to get a free sample or two (which at most times 2). That's why I keep coming back!

So we just watched the Harry Potter Christmas show on the castle and we were on our way out when the kids wanted Butter Beer. We were informed that the cart was closed, so we were sent back down towards the castle to the other cart. There was an associate there that said THAT cart was closed. We went back to this original cart and told the big tall guy with long hair and glasses what had happen and he condescendingly told us to just get in the line. We did what he said and the associate firmly told us the cart was closed. We reiterated the whole story to her and she said she would let us in the line. THANK YOU, Sarah, for making the end of our kids' night a pleasant one.

I love this park!  It is a great place for your dog to run around, swim, and play off leash.  Lots of nice scenary and other dogs to play with.  Normally, I don't let my dog off leash anywhere, because I am afraid she will end up in the road.  The park sits far enough back from the main road that this is not an issue. It does smell, because unfortunately not ever owner cleans up after their pooch, but come on...it's a dog park!  It's bound to happen.

Other than the smell, the only two downsides I can think of is 1) The parking SUCKS!  Be prepared to wait a few minutes until a spot opens up.  And 2) Some owners do not watch their dogs and let then run wild.  However, this is a common problem at ANY dog park.

Overall, it's an awesome park..my dog loves it!

What a beautiful restaurant! The food and service are great. I had the Ebi Oshi, which was really beautiful and delicious. Given that the Aburi Oshi plates seem to be Miku's signature dishes, I would highly recommend trying one. I also had a Nigiri of Yellowtail that was refreshing. 

We ordered two desserts, the Green Tea Opera cake and Caramel-Banana Mille-Feuille. They came to the table looking a lot like the sushi: small, neatly constructed rectangles of goodness. I liked both desserts and thought the sesame ice cream was interesting, but I probably wouldn't order dessert again. The sushi itself is good enough.

Definitely a fan of this place. Obviously, I always get the fish taco every time - so I guess this review is a little biased. I guess I won't get into how they are made considering everyone else has done that already - but I will say they are pretty different. Sometimes this place can be a little off, but by a little off I mean a little off because it is still really good and satisfying nevertheless. I am a huge fan of fish tacos, and I can say I've run the gamut of the fish tacos. Probably not a great review because that's all I eat here, although I do remember once having the carne asada - SO good too! I definitely think this place is worth a trip. Everything is fresh, not too greasy, decently priced, always has a line (but isn't that a great sign?!). Recommended!

I went here yesterday for lunch, or a meal at like 3:30pm.  I don't know if that's still considered lunch.  After furniture shopping we decided to stop here for something since we passed it on the #1 bus on the way over.

It's dimly lit with lots of wood, big wooden chairs, huge wraparound bar, and a cool atmosphere.  It was pretty dead so we pulled up a chair at the bar.  The bartender was friendly and wondered why we were just having soda...hungover perhaps?  What I just downed 3 huge glasses of water in 5 minutes?  I'm fine!  What's dehydration?

I had a veggie burger that came with smoked gouda cheese (my favorite!)  It was good.  Really good fries also.  My boyfriend had the steak sandwich which lacked a little flavor but was still pretty tasty.  Mine was about $10 and his was $12.  A little expensive just for sandwiches but I liked the atmosphere enough to come back and check it out at night.  I guess there is live music most nights...

My new favorite spot. It's vegan y'all! They make their cheeses and breads in house which means I have non-diary cheese boards in my future :) 

I got there right after they opened at 5pm today. Didn't know that Tuesday's are $3 Austin brewery pint nights wooohooo! Started off with the Ploughman's Platter and Buffalo Cauliflower Wings. 

Ploughman's Platter - the three different cheeses were distinctly different and so very tasty. The butter - I swear it tasted like dairy butter. But it was made from coconut milk. And their breads (made in house) are divine! I am going to add this to my frequent cheeseboard list for sure!

Buffalo cauliflower wings - the best I've had and I've had many. They were crunchy, spicy and ever so delish!

I ordered the Gyro for my main entree and have had real gyro before since I eat meat. I prefer the vegan version for sure. Maybe I've had bad experiences with gyro meat previously, but the seitan was totally delish, the hummus, garlic sauce and tzatziki went perfectly with the seitan and pita. I'd be totally fine if I turned vegan and only ate here everyday!

The POS system was acting up and added gratuity to our bills automatically as well as didn't adjust off the Tuesday pint specials but management was great and comp'd a few drinks for us since it took them a while to fix the checks. 

This place was packed when we left so get there early. Or wait. The wait is worth it!

Perfect location for a large convention. I come here yearly for 'premier orlando', an international beauty show. This place has nearly everything for the show. From the large showroom, to the independent classes and 'theater' rooms. 

I'm always excited to come here for my classes. The only downside is that sometimes the workers don't really know where certain rooms or theaters are located. So you'll have to ask multiple people where something is before they can give you the right answer. 

Bring a sweater cause the place gets chilly! And stay in the hotels close to the convention (within walking distance). Bikers are also waiting outside to give you a lift so no need to take the buses or your car.

I was surprised to find meatballs on the menu of this counter-service pizza joint and even more surprised at the depth of flavor. The meatballs were tender and flavorful. The accompanying sauce had bite and balance. 

I would have appreciated pizza by the slice and the Italian Chop Salad was fine though uninspired. I don't know which quick-cook, personal pizza brand opened first (Pie Five and others come to mind) but the added menu items here and the wide beverage service make this a distinct choice in a well-populated field.

The Kohl's in Framingham is one of the best I have been to in a while. The store itself was well organized and the shelves were well stocked. This store had a ton of great clearance items, and the staff was willing to help me find a shirt that I was looking for. The only critique was that they needed more staff members cashing people out. The line at this store on a typical Saturday looked as if it was a Black Friday line.

Overall, this is a great Kohl's location. When I am in the area and am need of a new piece of clothing or home good, I will make it a point to stop in here at this store.

Always come to this location, and I only rate this 4 stars because of a guy named COLBY

Serving us we had carlos, Carlos great! I have a big family and we enjoyed his attentiveness and service. He was awesome about serving such confusing orders.

Now a guy named COLBY came to give cheese. Everyone wanted cheese and walked away after asking, and not having everyone respond. Then when our niece said she wanted cheese he turned around so rudely and asked very sarcastically "does anyone else want cheese?!" With a head roll. Once we pointed to her I said you can leave the attitude then he rolled his eyes and said "sorry" then blamed the fact that "they were running out of cheese" that experience was so bad it made almost all of us lose our appetites and decided to ask for to go boxes
Although once we asked Carlos he was in a hurry to bring us some. Very upset by COLBYS' response, but very pleased with Carlos.

I love the food... that you choose [spoon it raw] your meal from a variety of fresh ingredients that is grilled [rather noisily] and that you can go back and do it again and again... If you're not sure what you like from a large selection of veggies, seasonings/sauces, meat & proteins, noodles/rices... just make small portions and find out what you like! 

The best value is to park on a surrounding street [to avoid valet- unless on a proper date, of course] and go at lunchtime when it's cheaper! 

I haven't experienced the open-air seating, the flip up windows on the patio have always been closed when I'm there; but I suppose it would be amusing to see the Claremont more clearly, as well as Ponce traffic

But did I mention ~ I LOVE the food there?

My husband and I have eaten here numerous times. We've eaten as a part of large groups and also just the two of us. Each time, the service is very top notch.

Last night, the two of us had dinner there. We wanted to stop and tell management about how good the service was at the table next to us- the guy had such an amazing personality and kept a personal conversation going with the ladies at the table behind us. When the lady tried a soup for the first time and it wasn't to her liking, he took it off her bill and then brought them over a treat at the end of the meal for being such a highlight of his night. Great job mystery waiter!

The food:
- My favorite salad in the entire city is their Maggiano's Chopped Salad and that dressing- that house Italian dressing is SO yummy!! I would go and just eat this any day of the week!
- I tried the Shrimp Scampi - outstanding and a TON of food!
- My husband had the Crab & Lobster stuffed Cannelloni (sp?). He raved over it!

We've also had the Chicken Marsala (great!) and pork and chicken parmesan and a lot more dishes and recommend everything so far!

Hope you enjoy!

I really liked this space. Although I was a little confused about what it's trying to be (mostly given my own pre-conceived notions about what everything on Manor should strive to be), I think it's a great hangout spot and will return. They have a massive selection of beer, but it beats out the closer Flying Saucer for me because it also has pool, darts, shuffleboard, and TVs a plenty. The cocktails are very cheap... but also weren't the absolute best. Stick with beer and definitely chow down. I had the croque monsieur, and people I was with had things ranging from sausage balls, to some roast beef massive sandwich, to pretzel bites and beyond. No one left dissatisfied. It's a great spot for groups!! They have picnic tables and cocktail tables alike.. it wasn't too packed to find a place to sit with 5 of us on a Thursday evening around 8 pm. They also have the capability of opening the walls to make it an outdoor space whenever you want to take in some nice Austin weather!

What a beautiful store with a great location.  It has everything that you would need.  Everything is organized and easy to find.  Our cashier was friendly and fast moving.  They were short handed on baggers but Im sure it was due to the weather.  It had a Starbucks and the deli had many meats and cheeses pre packaged to save time.  They also food ready meals for you if you need a quick meal pick up to take home too eat.  It had a very well lit AAB spacious parking lot with 2 entrances.  Very nice.

No love for Totto in Boston? 

Yes, I've been to the NYC location and waited 2 hours in the freezing cold for a bowl of ramen. Yes, the ramen in NYC is noticibly better (maybe that's because the wait is ridiculously long). That doesn't mean that this Totto is terrible for what it is and where it is.  

I came with two friends and was seated right away (that would NEVER happen in NYC). The pork buns we ordered were super fatty and melted in my mouth - just the way I like it! I stuck with the spicy ramen and didn't regret it. Not as magestic as the Totto or Ippudo in NYC, but delicious nonetheless.
