My roommie ordered the mega ramen and kind of regreted his choice because it was HUGE!  

I'd definitely come back for another bowl of ramen. Heck, considering that I'd tolerate a 40 + minute green line ride from downtown just to get a bowl of ramen, that's a 4 stars in my book.

Had lunch with Winnie the Pooh and friends. Great buffet with variety and really friendly staff. We had to wait only 3-4 minutes before we got called for our reservation. Wife had forgotten her 'happy anniversary' badge and the reception guy gave her another one. We also had informed them of some dietary restrictions and they had prepared a special meal for us in addition to the buffet. 
We got great shots with the characters as well. Will definitely come here again!

Was visiting Vancouver with the fam, and my Filipino tongue kicked in. Yelped it, and found this place. It is located in a very tiny strip mall, busy cross streets, limited parking. The place is not too huge, but can accommodate a lot. I ordered the fiesta platter since there were the three of us. Also ordered the lomi on the side, and shrimp with veggies, and squid. Lotsa food I know- it aint gonna break my bank though their price were on the high side.

The wait time was ok, considering the amount of my order, but the waiting sometimes is not fun. I knew in my stomach that the food I ordered were freshly cooked. And the food arrived. The lomi, was actually good- it tasted just a bit salty, but I like it the way it was. The squid on the side was tender not chewy. The platter, omg, huge platter. The grilled squid on the platter came out chewy and hard, all other else were good, delicious.

Overall, the food was flavorful, very authentic Filipino food. If I ever come back to Vancouver, this is gonna be my first Filipino food stop. I recommend this place to ones looking for new taste.

So, I was stuck at the hotel for business (no car) in what, I am told, is not a safe area to venture out on foot. Even though it's a sushi bar, I was not interested in that for lunch, so I ordered chicken wings, which were really good. They had just the right amount of heat, but mostly just flavor. I also had the hummus, which was okay, but not the best. I returned at night to have a glass of wine, and was pleased with their red wine choices. I will say that their service is very friendly. Like super friendly. Genuinely cared about my well-being kind of friendly. It made being stuck here actually enjoyable.

Tried this place for the first time today, and I gotta say, I'm a fan.

 The place is right off of 62, and goes into one of those "Oh shit!" parking lots where it's suddenly upon you, and you suddenly have to turn into it. After parking across three spots and then across a handicapped spot to the stares of the people sitting in the hair cutting place, I finally found an actual spot and parked.

I had done some research of this place online before going, on, of course, Yelp, and I knew what I wanted to get when I got in there: this culinary concoction called "The Nest". When I walked in and ordered it, the boss (owner?) actually asked me if I was sure that was what I wanted. At first I was a little offended by that, but given the makeup of this sandwich, all is forgiven.

Quick service, friendly staff... that's all there. Now the sandwich.... The nest is a BRILLIANT sandwich, though surely not for everyone. Chicken Fingers, Mozzarella Sticks, French Fries, Grated Cheese and Tomato Sauce all in a roll. AWESOME. Since it's essentially a junk food collection of appetizers, I can see how this sandwich is probably more appealing to the high schoolers who are located right across the street, hence the warning I received.

I suppose a true test of this place would be to try one of the more mundane sandwiches and see how they stack up, but  they have passed my first test, and got me liking the place, looking forward to going back again, and trying more of their wares.

Recommend!

Our family goes here for occasions, typically birthdays.  We love the place but last night left me feeling like something had changed?  I will suggest, don't order the chicken mole.  The only thing I can commend them on here is the profit margin achieved in a 1/4 piece of dry baked chicken, covered in mole sauce accompanied by a scoop of rice and a dollop of refried beans-all for $19.  They win, I lose.  Mom got a relleno.   Small portion there as well.  Service was good.  Drinks were good.  I think they need to expand their entree menu options.  The best thing on the menu is the carne asada.  I'll go back, but will strongly consider other options for fine south of the border cuisine

A real Taqueria in Orlando. Easy to get to. Exit OBT, make a left at the first crack head, turn right at the next hooker and make a quick uturn at the second homeless drunk. OK so  its not in the nicest area, but the tacos are amazing. They are like true taco cart tacos in Mexico. They offer barbacoa, carnitas, adobado, asada, legua, cabeza, chicken. Small tacos but very tasty for only a buck and a quarter each. Great food. Highly recomend.

Sad they are not open on Sundays. Delicious and fresh Greek cuisine. Started off with the lemon Orzo chicken soup. It was good but not as hot as I would have liked it to be. Tender chicken , soft Orzo and light tangy taste. Followed it up by the moussaka, soft warm mashed potatoes mixed in with grilled eggplant and ground lamb with surprising layer of the lemon potatoes.  The entree came with a side of greek salad covered with feta. Next time I'll get the feta on the side, just way too much of it on the salad.  Dressing was full of nice herb flavors. Next time I need to save room for desert! Highly recommended. But cold inside so bring a jacket!

Came here on a Friday night around 7:30pm in a party of two. The place was pretty packed but we were seated immediately! The waiter was quick to take our order from the ayce menu but he was quite busy throughout the meal and we often had to flag him down to order more or to have our water refilled. 

We only ordered the crab rangoons from the kitchen and everything else was from the sushi bar. The crab rangoons came to our table within minutes of handing our order sheet to our waiter, but the sushi bar orders took a bit more time. If you're trying to take full advantage of the AYCE experience, I'd suggest placing your next sushi order as soon as you get the first order so that you don't spend time waiting. I was impressed that the sushi bar never got our order wrong even though we ordered a decent amount.

The rolls and nigiri were packed with a lot of rice. I wouldn't say I was mind-blown by any of the items I got but none of them were disappointing either. The sashimi had a good texture and tasted fresh. 

I saw some neighboring tables order their cocktails, as well as get other items from the menu. The other menu items seemed pretty decent but I probably won't try them because I'd only come back if I was in the mood for AYCE sushi again. For one of the few places in Boston which offer AYCE sushi, I thought that the $31.99 weekend dinner price was reasonable, considering that the non-sushi menu is pretty large and they have a decent selection of rolls, handrolls, and sashimi.

I haven't ordered a large amount of flooring from Floor & Decor, but they've been great for what we've needed them for. We almost ordered our wood floors from them, but another company was having a sale at the exact time we were ordering. Otherwise, we would have. We found great options at all different price points.

We have purchased tile from them. I initially went in because I wanted a square marble tile to make a table out of. Nobody else had an 18" square real marble tile, but they did. They have a ton of options, from traditional to trendy. One note: we had decided on a tile for our entryway and went back to get it maybe 1 - 2 weeks later and couldn't find it! It had moved to the sale/clearance section, thankfully, so we got the tile we wanted and we got a deal on it. But check the sale section if you can't find something you previously saw.

Checkout is always friendly enough but it's often very slow. Make sure you allot time.

Their prices are great and their selection is great. I've never had a bad experience.

Been going here since they opened, I actually put the phone wiring and jacks in the business before they opened.  Have been to many sushi bars and conveyor-train style restaurants, yet its the only bar that charges a dollar admission per person.  Waiting sign-in list during busy hours. Only 3 booths for 3 or more ppl along the train belt to help yourself. The plates were initially 1.00 depending on color plates now still decent cost of 1.50 a plate.  When you catch the eye of the sushi chefs, they welcome your calling out orders n promptly make them then hand directly to you.  Salmon, hamachi and tuna rolls are my favorite.  glazed eel sushi flamed to order.  Boyfriend likes the variety of roe, quail and fish eggs sushi, octopus and shrimp sushi.  Made to order fried calimari and tempura.  Hot miso soup delicious. Free hot green tea and tall ice water, other beverages available for sale in case. Need more wait persons to adequately serve customers.

good display of origami in case.  See the dollar bills folded up as animals !

Talk about a complete 180. I had a brunch buffet here a while back, and it was pretty close to the worst food that I had ever laid taste buds on in the wondrous food city known as Austin, Texas. Upon seeing that it was going to reopen as a reevaluated and revamped sort of gastro-restaurant sort of eatery, I was pumped.

I say gastro-restaurant because the alcohol menu sort of sucks, but they are not really just a "bar and grill"; furthermore, it also boasts some really interesting and tasty noshes. I very much appreciated the live music.

The outdoor patio is quite nice, and the happy hour is off the charts. With half-price appetizers galore, you could literally have a feast and get quite inebriated for under $15 a person. And by full and drunk I mean full and drunk. To put things in perspective: $4 flatbread, $4 onion rings, $4 guacamole... the list goes on.

I would recommend two appetizers specifically... namely because I got these, and I loved them. The roasted mushroom flatbread, with all its roasted mushroom goodness, boasts a nuttiness provided by the heavy dosing of truffle aioli, thyme, blue cheese, and some sort of shredded cheese. Does that not just scream UNCT. Not unctuous, but UNCT... like a grunt.

The charred corn guacamole was OK... nothing outstanding. But... the salt and pepper house chips are amazing. Super salty, super crisp, and a boat load to an order. This is a must.

More disappointing are the adornments that the entrees possess. The bison burger boasts a housemade aioli, which was a little lumpy; a spicy, but watery habanero ketchup; and a far-too pungent shiner mustard. The caramelized bourbon onions were sweet to the point of disgust. The pita bread that accompanied my chickpea chili was OK, a bit too dense. The mac and cheese was too runny, though the cheesy flavor was a nice touch. The chickpea chili disappointed heavily. It was too tomatoey in flavor, and the feta and grilled beet garnish literally added nothing, if not even detracting from the faux-stew.

Affordable is the grub here, and that truly counts for something. Other than that, I figure the quality on many items could be tweaked, but I am certain that I will return at some point for happy hour. I mean, $4 per order of whatever your heart desires? I shall not pass.

I went here Thursday night around 7 p.m. to celebrate a surprise birthday party with a group  of 6. We brought in a birthday cake and asked them to hold onto it after we are finish with our meal.

We ordered oyster pancake, xiao long bao, ma po tofu, a steak dish, a fish dish. There was a very long hair in our oyster pancake, but the server had no problem in bringing out a brand new one for us. Overall, the food was fabulous and delicious.

As for the service, it could be much better but definitely not the worst. They were quick in giving us our food, but even more quicker when it comes to giving out the bill. I think they could have asked us if we were finished before giving us our bill because we did plan on ordering a couple more dishes. Nevertheless, what we were most disappointed about was that they forgot about the cake. A friend of mine went up to a lady to remind her about the cake. We expect the server to take the cake out of the box and put the candles on and bring it over. At least that's what supposed to be customer service. Instead, they just brought the cake over that was still in a plastic bag, unwrapped, and smacked it right on the table like it was nothing. I guess they have never taken care of a birthday party before in that restaurant. 

I'm not sure if they do this to every customer's bill, but they charge a 15% service fee on our bill. Maybe it's because we look like those super young college kids who are too poor to tip, but that definitely would be a mistake if they assumed we were. The service fee is no big deal. We ended up tipping them more than that.

I've been here multiple times to enjoy a happy hour or late cocktail at their outdoor area, which is lovely. And always have had a nice drink, especially when it's happy hour, the prices are great.

So, we finally made it here to actually eat inside for a early dinner and cocktail last Sunday afternoon.  Luckily, we ran into some fellow yelpers outside and joined them for a bit and we munched on the beer cheese and pretzels, which I have to say was underwhelming.  After saying goodbye, we went inside to dine.

The interior is aesthetically pleasing, the noise is controlled by smart design, and the service from hostess, to server, and to the manager stopping by to check on us was on point.  Yay!

Food:  Well, I was a bit worried after our appetizer outside, but we proceeded anyway.  My husband was in the mood for steak and after showing him a yelp review of the Delmonico steak on the menu, that was his choice without hesitation. He ordered it medium with the au gratin potatoes. When it came out, it was beautifully seasoned and charred, and the temperature was a perfect medium as requested.  He and I both thought it was an excellent steak.  It was juicy, not too fatty, but enough to give it flavor, and tender as heck!  Really, it was SO SO good.  The au gratin potatoes were also perfectly crisped on the outside and not too greasy or cheesy.  He and I would so get this again.

I opted for the angus meatloaf sans the portabella mushrooms (which I don't care for). It came out with two generous slices that were meaty and tasty, a gravy that was good, but not fantastic, haricot verts (delicious and crisp), and I opted for the mac n' cheese, which was simply awesome.  

Definitely will be back for not only cocktails and happy hour outside, but dinner inside.

visiting here from Seattle we were looking for a great bfast spot. We'd heard about Tastee and Alder and tried to get in there each day of our 3 day stay here but each time the wait was at least 45 min. 
Instead of wait we decided upon Mothers and so happy we did. The food was outstanding (even though we had to wait here too). The kale scramble, the mushroom scramble and the daily frittata were excellent and fresh. Service was outstanding and the owner was even walking around filling coffee, etc. 
We finally did get into T & A today and now don't understand why the line is so long here as our overall experience at Mothers was much better. 
Enjoy!

Very reasonable place to stay if you're looking to visit Atlanta. The rooms are comfortable. 

    The customer service is great, I called the office to ask for milk for the baby. They told me they would check to see what hey could do bc the kitchen was closed. They were able to accommodate me with 2 small cartons of milk. They definitely went above and beyond. 

    The only negative was the highway noise if you can get past that then it's fine. Maybe an interior room would cut that out.  All in all nice hotel stay.

Fun, funky tea house in Harvard square. Prices are bit less than Starbucks, and the quality is way better. 

I ordered one of their tea-infused hot chocolates. My girlfriend awkwardly stared at me while I ordered it, but it tasted amazing with their coconut blend. Like having the warm tropics in my hand. 

After feeling sick from all the chocolate and cream, I came back 30 minutes later for a detox tea. Much better for a stroll around Harvard Square. 


Good tea selection and visually stunning. Lots of tea paraphernalia for sale too.

I LOVE PANEERRRRR

Anyways, I've been wanting to come here for a while and I finally popped in yesterday!
My friend and I were on the 49 to metro after lectures and we impulsively got off to go here.

What the heck $10.95 for the vegetarian buffet that is pretty good?? SO CHEAP
Service was good, everyone was really nice, the food was really good...

the paneer tho.........

and the naan............

Plus the samosas are so cheap like 75 cents what even I pay like $3.50 for crappy yucky samosas at school....

When I went around 8pm on a weekday there wasn't a line. There was just one party in front of us ordering donuts. Coming from Southern California we have a lot of donuts that are creative with different textures and flavors. So I wanted to try this place from all the hype it's been getting. 

Don't get me wrong, the donut was pretty good. I got the one with Oreos and peanut butter. I remember I was talking to a local Oregonian, and she said most of the time locals don't really like to go to voodoo anyways and just see it as more of a place on the average.

CASH ONLY. 

It was kind of pricey though. For 3 donuts it was around $9.

Since voodoo is open 24 hours, my suggestion is come at a later time so it's less busy and less congested with tourists trying to get a taste.

Great location, good space... especially if you get a "two bedroom"... it's actually two separate hotel rooms.  We booked through timeshare points and were not informed that we would have to pay "cleaning fees" for each room because we weren't staying a full week, which was annoying for the resort to even do in the first place. 

Especially because we paid for a two-bedroom and a one bedroom for 4 nights each, so it's not like we weren't spending our money or only stay one night. 

Employees were nice and typically helpful when we had issues with getting into the room or keys not working!

Love love love the atmosphere at Freddie's! The outdoor seating makes you feel like you are on your best friends porch, except with dozens of other people. The staff is super friendly and helpful! They even switched one TV from a Cowboys game to the Packers game for us, no questions asked. The food is decent, not amazing but not horrible, and drinks are reasonably priced. 

Pros - awesome atmosphere
Cons - sometimes people let their children run wild, which can ruin your relaxing evening

I usually come here after waiting in line @ Tasty & Sons for locally sourced free range organic lardons (wtf is a lardon anyway). Usually 1/2 way into my digging I B line it to the Fresh Pot (next door) and get rid of some bad energy. Someone should open a food cart on Mississippi St. and call it "Gentrifried" and served fried cat fish & jo jos. Eric is a really nice guy who doesn't use the internet and I think he needs to get a store cat named Cat Stevens.

I'd been dying to try this place since I started working nearby, and finally made it. The place is cute, but pretty tight space- the line and tables leaves minimal room to walk between. There were 3 staff working on a busy Saturday night, and while they were friendly, they were running around trying to make coffee, cocoa, milkshakes and fresh cones. It took around 10-15 minutes to be served- I got my ice cream in a bowl but it took another 5+ minutes for hubby to get his milkshake. The cornbread sweet butter ice cream was amazing, and the banana pudding was also delicious. The blood orange creamsicle barely tasted of orange, and the chocolate as #!*? was too intense for me though I love chocolate. The chocolate also had ice chunks through it. I enjoyed trying several unique flavors,and would consider returning to try some others and maybe one of their cones. Be prepared for a wait and an above average price though.

Go On Tuesdays for their $8 Mussels. I have to say that I saved room for this meal... and I could've shared one plate with my lovely friend I was catching up with.. but we were both starving so we each ordered the special.

We also got a beet and pear salad which, at regular price, I thought came in a rather smaller portion. I wish the beets had cooled because the salad was a little warm (I don't know if they plan to serve it that way). The decor is so cute... with one long banquette and tables of 2s and 4s. It is a little crowded as everytime the server spoke to the table next to us, you'd pretty much get someone's rear a foot away from you.

Service was friendly and informative, patient and not overbearing. The mussels came with fresh bread and a combination of yam fries and regular fries - what a lovely surprise. The plate of mussels were beyond massive. The plate /bowl it came in looked like an upside down sunday hat. The cream sauce was heavy, but in a good way. The bread was perfect for dipping as it soaked up the sauces as I savoured it in my mouth.

I ate every single mussel, and every single fry and couldn't walk or eat until lunch the next day.... but good conversation and good food can lead to great things (even if it means being full for a very very very long time).

I heard the main chef specializes in pastry.. if I had more room - I would've grabbed dessert for sure. They have $25 3 course meals with a glass wine / beer on Sundays.. definitely want to check it out!

I come here way too much. I guess because it's the closest one to me. I really can't wait till the Brookhaven one is done being built! 

Parking - There's a huge lot. You can also go downstairs to park. But I've never had trouble finding a spot on top. This WF is so freaking busy that people are constantly coming and leaving. I only come here during dinner/post work out dinner, so I get lucky with spots.

Steps away from YourPie & same lot as Northface.

Space - I'd say similar size as the one on Ponce I think. I see all WFs the same. Well, except the one in Druid Hills - that's the smallest one I've seen. 

People are extremely nice here. Every question I've had - done politely and quickly. I can't complain

The hot bar is awesome. Love the size & variety. I manage to always get like $14 dollars worth of food. Sigh. I need to lear to make it 10 bucks. But... I love the food here. So good and healthy. If you're working out at Flywheel, come here & eat!

I've been sleeping on this place for years and finally decided to bop over for a visit. Turns out I'm a fan. We ordered two items: The bf went big with the Hot Mess + cheddar, and I ordered the Savory, adding a sausage patty and egg. 

The Hot Mess is HUGE with double portions of sausage, egg, and bacon. It was definitely more than one person should eat in one sitting, and sure enough he only got about 2/3 of the way through. It was super tasty, though, so I swooped in for the last few bites.

The savory was so good, with the toast in a garlic and herb batter, topped with goat cheese, bell peppers, chives, and balsamic. As I mentioned I asked to add egg and sausage. I was a bit bummed that these things ended up on the side rather than on top, but that was easy enough to fix on my own. But I probably wouldn't have ordered my egg sunny side up had i known.

We were happy with out breakfast, and it was nice to try someplace new. I'm sure at some point we'll come back, but it's not a place I'd rush to. 4 stars for the win.

When I first moved to Boston, I lived in Brighton and thought that Sunset was amazing. They have 130 some-odd beers on tap, plus hundreds of bottles (including a 40 oz. bottle of Schlitz). It was perfect, until I actually went there. It felt like a Ground Round. Not Beer Mecca. And I was unhappy.

Fast forward to now and there's the Hobo. I haven't found a place in Cambridge that rivals their beer selection. This place doesn't have bang-up food, but it's not terrible. I'd put it just above Tavern in the Square but well below Garden at the Cellar or Green Street. Last time I was there with friends, we ordered two BBQ sandwiches, a roasted red pepper soup with grilled cheese, and fried calamari. The soup was the winner, though the grilled cheese was pretty much a grilled cheese you could get anywhere, including your own kitchen. I tend to shy away from pulled pork at non-cue joints because I usually end up disappointed. This one wasn't bad, but I remember not being a giant fan of the sauce (full disclosure: memory a bit fuzzy due to too many beers). The calamari was good drunk food, not too greasy, and had a couple of deep fried peppers tossed in that I wasn't 
really expecting.

Need to go back to sample more beers, but also to try out their pretty extensive cocktail list. They've got some of the favorites (Dogfishhead, Stone Brewery, Bear Republic), plus a bunch that I've never heard of, along with a bunch of seasonals that you won't find in most package stores.    

Pro-tip: if you're sitting in the back corner near the waiter's computer, take a look at what's on the screen. The first time I went, the buttons said "Joey has" "irregular holes" "bearshark keeps" "raping harry." The last time it said "more passionate" "bang-bang" "sweeter" "finger-bang." I think that was from Valentine's day. Anyways, good conversation starter.

This is a Sunset for grown-ups. More of a bar/pub feel than crappy restaurant with a gimmick.

Went on a Saturday morning with my boyfriend. We got seated in seconds! It was at the bar, but we were eating within 2 minutes! All of the carts were making their rotations around the room. Everything I love was available, except steamed pork buns or lotus rice, but it did not matter, because there is so much food available! It will give you the opportunity to try new foods. They know how to turn tables over quickly, and all of the food is delicious! Bigger groups wait a little longer, but it's so worth it.

A great place for lunch and brunch. I've been here a few times now, and have had great food each and every time!

It's gonna be busy on weekends for lunch and brunch. Expect at least 30 mins, possibly an hour. But the location is great because its in a shopping center that allows you to shop around while you wait. You receive 3 hours of free parking in lot. Just be sure to keep your ticket when you enter the deck. 

The decor is simple and clean, with lots of light coming in. It's a chill vibe despite it being a full house. Service is top notch. Some of the best servers I've come across. 

Food wise: The Double Burger Stack. It's simple, yet legit. One of the best burgers in town for sure. No frills, just two patties with American cheese, pickles, lettuce and onions. Sides are a la carte. 

I've also had Avenue A, which is smoked salmon (nova), schmear, avocado, grapefruit, cucumber, onion, and dill. It was fresh and delicious. Their iced coffees are also solid too-- nice and smooth, not bitter, not too sweet. 

I would also highly recommend the Pastry Basket. The first time I went, I made the mistake of getting it as an appetizer. These pasties are HUGE! But they were all so freakin delicious! I think it contains a cheese Danish, cinnamon roll, and maybe 2 different muffins. Needless to say, the second time I went, I got these as a to-go order, so I could snack on them all weekend. 

There's also an extensive list of brunch staples and deli style sandwiches. I can't wait to go back and try them!

Great food, great atmosphere.  I went here with a friend on a Saturday and there was a packed bar, live music, and lots of little kids in the seating area.  To my shock, none of this proved annoying: kids were rapt with the food, musician was enjoyable, and bar patrons were well-behaved.  Food and beer selections were varied and tasted great.  Portion sizes are reasonable, which is selfishly frustrating, because the food is good enough to leave you wanting more.  I recall some signs on the wall proclaiming the blueberry pie to be award-winning; I wasn't floored by it, but it was certainly very good, and you've gotta appreciate a restaurant that lets you finish off a meal with a nice big slice of blueberry pie.  Great for dates and for families, a rare -- and winning -- combination.

I had been meaning to try Panza for a long time.  For one thing, it's on the site of my former favorite restaurant in the North End, Cibo.  It's right across the street from The Wine Bottega, a sensational store that hosts free wine tastings every Friday night from 5-8 PM and several excellent events each month.

Panza was always crowded by the time I got to the North End.  Fortunately, my friend and I were in the area earlier (around 5:30) and got a table immediately.

We started off with the Italian Chop Salad, designed for two but could definitely be shared by 3 people.  It came in a large bowl and we served ourselves with tongs.  Its ingredients reminded me of cold antipasti and the pepperoncinis were an excellent touch.

For my entree, I enjoyed the daily special of pappardelle with lamb ragu, a sumptuous feast of broad, filling noodles and tasty tendrils of meat.

Overall, an exceptional meal.  We were disappointed that they wouldn't let us open the bottle of wine my friend purchased across the street and it did take some time to receive our entrees, given that it was crowded.

Definitely make a reservation or get there before 6 PM if you want to snag a table on a weekend evening.  This is a must visit stop in the North End!

We live about 5 minutes away but had never tried this place until last weekend. The pho was really outstanding. I got a large, thinking that would be plenty for me and my two-year-old son, but we ate it all and he would have had more. Now I can't stop thinking about it and I think we'll get some more for tonight.

However, we will be getting take out, since the restaurant atmosphere itself is not great. In particular, the air conditioning...or lack thereof.

Baci!!! Travels for Baci!! Pet hotels #19!!

Since we've been doing a lot of four seasons and fairmont chains, decided to try the Hyatt with Baci! Normally, Hyatt is my goto with points and membership perks!! Now Baci get to try it! 

Sooo! Vancouver downtown is kinda like downtown Seattle. Impossible to park/find parking / expensive overnight. The hotel valet suggested I park in the garage right through the hotel valet: it's used for restaurants/ shops etc and which would be cheaper. Ended up being $24 for a whole day/night. Valet was $42 I believe. Thanks, Valet dude! 


Normally pet floors are lower but I love high floors and well platinum membership got us a room on 20th. It rained the whole time but we enjoyed staying in and hanging out in the balcony. People watched in the rain and cold! 

The bed was comfortable. Room was nice size: a little on the smaller side. Just a tiny bit but still nice. Roomy. Baci love the bed and the couch! :) 

The lobby has Starbucks, a bar and hangout area with plenty of umbrellas for that crazy rainy weekend. We walked around in the evening for a bit but coming back was the best part! Especially for Baci. He doesn't care for the rain. 

The only complain was lack of microwave for my pups food. The room service can come and get it and do it for you. But seems like too much hassle. Ended up ordering new rice for his meals. A lot of food deliveries were ordered too!

And that 2 pm check out! Great for us to explore the Robson street the next day, walk the Canada place and the harbor. All within 5 -10 minutes walk!! Baci loved it so, I did too! Woof woof!

So first of all it was raining out and when i walked up to the door a team of black-hooded ninja assassins jumped from the roof and attacked me. I was tired and not in the mood for their attitude, but luckily their fighting style lacked creativity, and i still had my throwing star belt buckle on, so they were dispatched without too much effort. 
When i walked in the bartender knew my drink order, offered me the food menu without having to ask (i like that). He listened to my stories of my day with understanding and grace. Then some loud people in the corner tried a shot at me with a blow gun. Dusty easily blocked it with a bottle of Jameson's Irish Whiskey and served me a simple but well executed chicken parm sandwich. 
Sometimes the music sucks but most of the people reading this have such bad taste that this shouldn't be a problem.
But then i went into the bathroom some drug-dealing biker gang of circus jugglers thought i was a narc and it got pretty ugly. But the bar boys were pretty nice, and while Jesse held the saline bag and Dusty stitched me up, Noah held my hand and told me about his day and upcoming trip to South East Asia. Nice work gents!
They don't take debit fyi, but they can usually make change for a hundy, and they also accept priceless artifacts, gold and diamonds (no Ruby's though), and freshly harvested organs that are compatible with O+ or AB blood types. 
Overall a good evening...

Yay! An awesome place right next to my house! I'm a HUGE Korean/Japanese/Thai/etc fanatic. So I'm a pretty hard judge on Asian places. This place is pretty good! I am definitely going to be a regular!

Their service is great. Very attentive staff and very clean and bright place! We never had to ask to have our drinks refilled. The waitress was on top of things!

I had a create-your-own bibimbap and my man had the yasaitame. My bibimbap was great! Not the best in Atlanta, but very delicious and light. (I got to pour on my own sauce, so it was very healthy!) I can't wait to try more or their dishes. So yummy and such great options for vegetarians!

I always forget about Victory because it's kind of tucked away a few streets up from the hubbub of Highland Avenue in Inman Park.  But each time I go, I'm reminded why I like it so much.  First, you can't go wrong with their classic Jack and Coke slushees.  I appreciated the pro-tip from our waitress this past time, who pointed out that you're better off buying the smaller size because it's not any cheaper to get the larger one per ounce, plus the smaller ones don't melt as fast. A good tip!  The other alcoholic sodas on the drink menu are fun and different, and on busy weekends, they serve froze out of the shipping container bar in the parking lot.

I also really appreciate their food menu here.  The sandwiches are all small and slider sized but packed with interesting fillings, sauces, meats, cheeses, and accoutrements.  And at $4, they're that perfect little bite to nibble on when you want something to eat while drinking but don't want a whole meal.  Each slider sandwich comes with a small handful of potato chips.  If you want something else to round out your drinking nibbles, I highly recommend the very pickle-y and dill filled dip for your chips.  The portion size of dip is huge - you may need extra chips!

They have a large indoor bar area and high tops, a covered patio, a game room, and an outdoor patio area with picnic tables with umbrellas.  And, they ever have a small parking lot (maybe 10 spaces) with free parking, which is basically unheard of in this area.

All in all, as drink spots on the Beltline go, Victory is worth a visit!

I came here a few months ago and had a pretty bad experience. The Manager contacted me and convinced me to give it another chance and I'm sure glad I did. This time the service was fantastic from our server, to the busperson, to the manager! Everyone was extremely attentive without being annoyingly so. My friend and I ended up ordering a meal pretty close to what we ordered the first time and the food was amazing. The scallops were cooked and seasoned perfectly and my friend raved about the salmon she ordered. 

I definitely recommend checking out this restaurant. Good location, good food and good service.

Super chill place with great food (real good), brunch on Saturday and Sunday, great coffee, and good beer. $3.50 mimosas too! Chill vibes tons of patio space, and they have loud enough music to drown out he conversations of people around you (it gets kind of loud). The only weird thing is that the side of the cafe with the tv drips water from the ceiling. So be careful of moving the tables. It got in my oatmeal. Parking is a little tight but there's some down the road. Overall, recommend! :)

This review is only for the pub side, since I was there after their brew shop hours.

The pub's not much to look at, but it feels pretty cozy, especially if you sit in the little separate room off to the right side of the front door. 
I drank a couple of pints of the house IPA, and it was light and refreshing. 
The guys working behind the bar were friendly and accomodating, and they were playing old live Grateful Dead tapes, so it was nice and mellow. 
I'm withholding the 5th star until I've had a chance to fully check out the shop.

Love Tasti D-Lite. My husband and I first discovered Tasti in NYC a few years ago, and managed to stop in every day on our trip. I was so excited to see a franchise open in Boston!

We stopped in tonight for the first time to the Boston shop, and it's as good as I remember! I had a small serving of chocolate macaroon and my husband had a shake. Both were delicious treats. And even better, reasonable for our waistlines as well. 

The shop was nice, new, and clean. The staff was friendly and helpful. Definitely a good experience, and although it's not far from home, I wish it was closer!

A cozy restaurant located on Cambridge street in Cambridge. A small bar area for seating and a bunch of tables that can be made for small and larger groups. On a Saturday night, it was busy but not full. 

The wait staff was polite and helpful. Provided explanation to the dishes, menu and good recommendations. 

Ginza G + T was a typical gin and tonic. Strong and classic
Toro flight - was the nightly special so pricy at $28. 4 different cuts of toro. The best was the fatty fish as the other prices were more 'tougher' and resembled beef. 
Uni and rock crab hand roll - also a nightly special. Lots of rock crab and sufficient amount of uni. Probably one of the best dish of the night 
Kanpachi- good flavor with the pineapple sauce. Fish was thinly sliced 
Hien bronzini - not a typical fish on sushi menu so worth a try. Felt the sesame oil drenched the fish and overwhelmed the dish. 
Kalua pork onigiri- great presentation and loved that you had to wrap it yourself. Lots of filling - a plus. The pork was flavorful
Spam musubi- ate this at the end so was getting full. The spam was way too small for the amount of rice.  The proportion was way off. Definitely had better elsewhere. 
Short rib grilled skewers - did not come with skewers and there was no bone attached to the meat. This was nice. The flavor was good with lots of ponzu but meat seems dry. Usually short rib is a bit tender being close to the bone. 
Waygu beef dumplings- soup dumpling with 5 pieces. Soup was good. The dumplings weren't bad, maybe a bit dry since it was boiled. This cut of meat is better to be eaten seared, grilled instead. 
Loco moco - beef was tender and maybe a little undercooked. The egg was perfect and the sizzling aspect is a great presentation. Rice wasn't sticky enough to keep the shape from becoming a hot delicious mess. 

The general comment About the rice is that it's not sticky enough to hold the add on. 

Overall a great experience at Momi nonmi. Really liked the unique dishes.

This was my first trip here and figured I'd go along with some of the recommendations of some of the other yelpers.  

I ordered takeout and given my initial impression of the restaurant wasn't too hopeful for what was inside the bag.  While the restaurant was clean, the mix of scents just didn't seem to work.  

The contents of the bag were MAGICAL.  I ordered Vegetarian Rolls, Vegetarian Pancakes, and Pad Thai.  I was not disappointed. 

The Vegetarian Rolls were perfect.  Not greasy, equally filled, and the sweet chili sauce was great.

I was amazed by the Vegetarian Pancakes-- I wasn't expecting them to be thick.  A little greasy, but mixed with the ginger soy sauce, it was perfect blend although slightly spicier than I expected.  

The Pad Thai was very good as well.  The noodles were cooked to a perfect level of tenderness.  The dish wasn't soggy, and there weren't too many bean sprouts.

I will definitely go back to Tamarind House.

I had lunch today 9-19-12 with my Romeo friends (Retired Old Men Eating Out). We meet each month at a new restaurant and share camaraderie and current events. I started off with a Pasta Fagoli soup that was delicious. I then had the Shrimp Fra Diavlo (8/10) with big portions and spicy red sauce. The waitress (Ann) was very attentive and brought bread, drinks and meals to the table quickly. The owner Vinny sent over a complimentary plate of pizza squares which were just delish. This is a friendly neighborhood Italian restaurant in the rear of a deli takeout counter. The others in the group had mixed reviews and ordered Chicken Picatta (10/10), Pasta and Littlenecks (6/10), Shrimp Scampi (6/10), Shrimp Fra Diavlo (10/10). We also had a good selection of beers and wines (8/10). Although we ordered hot meals off the menu you could also select items from a cold antipasti buffet table. The average price of entrees was $13.95 but drinks, dessert, coffee and tip added to the final cost of $35.00 per person. There is limited meter parking on Broadway due to street construction.

At here in a rush at the airport only to find out my plane was delayed.  I had to forgo the beer too, but had I know I was going to be sitting at the gate for 2 more hours, I would've definitely tried a brew!  I had the roast beef french dip here, which was yummy (though I didn't taste much of it well since I inhaled it to try to catch my plane).  The service was very amenable to my time crunch and I thank them for it!  Definitely wanted to try the local brew since I know this is a big portland beer, but perhaps next time!

Well the quality and service at Lefty's are top notch.  A little pricey, but I'm willing to pay for it.  Now, I'd just like t address the recent review by Nicole M.   Nicole - when you are not online writing reviews, do you really refer to your husband as 'hubby'?  And do you really describe portions as 'ginormous'?  So cute and original.  Your review was not cool and it was not funny.  Maybe I'll give you a 'useful'.  Too bad there's no 'annoying' option.

We made a reservation and we were determined to feed me some prime rib. We had a huge snow dump on Sunday so it made it extra beautiful up there. The view was amazing. We valeted because it was so snowy and the roads were gross so why not spend some more for the convenience of letting someone else handle it? 

We came in and it was a gong show. There was a private event waiting for their room to be set up so there was well over 30 people crammed into the lobby bar area waiting for their room. They were snooty and obnoxious and had no desire to move even an inch to let people through. I ended up shoving a few people who had drinks in hand. Sorry not sorry.

We were seated with a fantastic view of the city. So beautiful! 

I got the prime rib combo. I was so looking forward to it. The mushroom soup wasn't as thick as I like it but it was ok. I wouldn't order it again. The prime rib was cooked perfectly but lacked any depth in flavor. The Yorkshire pudding was delicious as were all the veggies and mashed potatoes (less the tomato). The highlight of my meal was the sunburnt lemon pie. Yum!

My girlfriend enjoyed her beet and papaya salad. She wasn't a huge fan of her striploin as it was underseasoned. 

Our server was fantastic. It was already a lovely evening with an amazing view and her service was just the icing on the cake. 

I am giving it 4 stars for the experience as a whole. If it were just the food that night, it'd be a 3 stars. The service would be 5 stars. The view would also be an easy 5.

We ended up taking a stroll outside to see the view some more but quickly went to get our car because it was so cold. 

Suggestion: it's cold out so if you valet, please consider tipping them generously. Consider it a convenience tax for not having to get your feet wet or slip while walking to your car and freezing your butt off.

It's a sports bar with some big tables.  Honestly, what do you expect?  It's not fine dining, but I've never been offended by the food, and the prices for drinks are pretty damn reasonable, especially compared to some places in Salem.

Depending on what's on the juke, talking can be a little difficult, and, as with most sports bars, you won't hear a friggin' thing on the TVs, but who needs commentary to Boston sports anyways?  The patrons usually supply it all themselves.

I've never been here when it's way too crowded, so I can't speak to the atmosphere under those circumstances, but I've been on an average Saturday night and the crowd was varied, and numerous enough so that the place seemed full without being oppressive.  Our expectations were low and it was a good time.  That's enough for me.

The food is really good on busy nights but catch them on a slow night and good luck! We went on a Monday at 8:30pm. I got my wings - they were cold - but I was so hungry I ate them against my better judgement. I was sick the whole night. The bartenders are all really nice and the service in the bar area (where we always sit) is usually good. I wish they would alternate beers on special. It seems like Coors light has been the "beer of the month" for about a year.

1) if you like whiskey drinks, order the irish honey. hot damn it was delicious! our server told me it was entered into a drinks competition but didn't win, but it was one of the better whiskey cocktails i've had.  my mom said it smelled like perfume (it had honey and bitters in it) but she doesn't like whiskey, so if that isn't your thing i'd suggest chatting with the servers. they are very knowledgable and helpful. my gf asked about a wine pairing and our server let her sample two reds with her meal and then pick.

2) the service was great both times i went.

3) i had a steak special about a year and a half ago and it was awesome. served with some sort of herb butter, and i think potatoes or fries. however, my new favorite is that chicken. everyone raves about it on yelp and while i don't typically order chicken, i had to try it. you will not regret it, it is crispy and flavorful and simple but done perfectly. 

4) they have a surprisingly robust vegetarian menu! my friend got the beet and goat cheese napoleon and really liked it.

Nothing but positive things to say here- the food is always great (chile relleno, chorizo quesadillas, ensalada de la casa, queso flameado, you get it) and the service very, very friendly. Austin is a city full of Tex-Mex, but El Chile is just so consistently good, it's hard to pass up. And reasonably priced. Also, their patio upstairs gets a nice breeze and gives you a little view of downtown which is nice in this lovely weather. Get the michelada to wash down your grub and you'll be muy happy.

Out of all the restaurants in Ponce City Market, I enjoy this one the most. They offer rustic Italian with items such as pizza, seafood, pastas and nice starters. My fiancé is absolutely in love with the brussel sprouts that have ricotta and pancetta mixed in. Tonight we had the smoked trout dip which was very good, not too Smokey and a nice consistency. We also had the mussels which were good but the broth was a touch too salty. If you are going to Ponce and want to have a nice sit down i would highly recommend Brezza. For the most part you cannot go wrong with any item on the menu.

Food: 4 stars
Service: 3 stars

Boys night out, b*tches!

I came here with three of my bros to grab dinner. I know park has amazing appetizers so we got the tasting of toasts and fried mussels. Both amazing, the fried mussels are a must have when you come. Tasting toasts was also decent and great presentation. They are able to mix the ingredients on the toast very well to come out with unique flavors. We wanted large entrees to share with the group. The server was helpful in helping us pick out the pork shank and the chicken sandwich. The pork shank was truly gigantic and came with a lot of veggies- mushrooms, spinach and potatoes which we enjoyed. Pretty easy to share as well as the meat was quite tender. But I thought that the flavor and marinate was a little bit lacking. 

The chicken sandwich was pretty standard. It came with a lot of fries and the buns on the burger were interestingly prepared. I think that they were actually deep-fried for a short period of time. The only hiccup in terms of service was at the end when we were paying the bill the server lost one of our friends credit card. Turns out the server had put it in their own pocket by accident. Took a little bit of time but it all worked out. They also have really good drinks!

On a Saturday morning in downtown Portland after a great run, I wanted to find a breakfast option near my hotel.  After a quick Yelp search, I came across The Good Earth Cafe.  If you didn't find this place on Yelp, I don't know that you could pick it out from the street.  However, the food was delicious and inexpensive.  You place your order at the window, are given a number, grab a table, and the food is brought to you.

My friend ended up joining me for breakfast, and we split a PDX ($6.50) with Bacon, Cheddar, and Sourdough, along with a Croque Madame ($6.75).  The PDX was simple, as expected, but all of the ingredients were good.  I particularly enjoyed the Croque Madame, which was festive for a post-run breakfast.  The sandwiches also came with potatoes.  The prices for both were crazy reasonable.

The other food looked good too, and the place was full with no wait for a table on a Saturday morning.

We stayed here and it was a great spot. Just a few minutes from the airport a large outdoor shopping mall and Ikea. It was also just an 8 minute drive to downtown Portland. I would definitely stay here again. I read several other reviews that people complained about noise from airplanes but when inside the building I never heard one airplane. The only reason for 4/5 stars was because the water didn't drain very well in the sink or tub and the remote for the tv was difficult to use. Otherwise I'd still come back here.

Braised beef noodle with handpulled noodles9.95
BG: braised Lamb in soup with biang biang noodles9.95
Like just look at the width of those noooooods  the one in the background was actually double the size of the front! The braised beef is such comfort food. Tastes exactly like the braised beef my mom would make at home  it's just missing the beef tripe. It's laid on a bed of dry handpulled noodles. The lady told me not to get biang biang noodles with the braised beef .. not too sure why ‍ I enjoyed it, as it was very flavorful. But just a tad oily like most braised beef. Especially since there's no soup with it just the sauce so you see all the oil. 
As for the braised Lamb in soup its very comforting and light. Someone I would opt for if I'm sick  wasn't a big fan of the lamb as there wasn't much flavoring. And was a bit gammy. Now onto the biang biang noodles they were pretty good!! It was literally one long and wide af noodle  nice and bouncy texture you can definitely tell it's handmade without having to watch him make it. 
We also tried the Chinese pork burger 4.75 not pictured. It was pretty good nice and juicy like dripping with juice LOL. Was a bit messy. The bun was thin and kind of like a mantou in burger form LOL. Not bad

On a whim of our first night in Portland, 2k18 vacation hobos edition ~ after careful planning of how we were suppose to be enjoying the nightlife my bum friends decided to take a nap and it was 9:30 pm and I needed to do more things in Portland so I made their lazy *ss get up and we rush to get ice cream so we can made the 10pm for Searching. 

Got there and was super annoyed since it was literally across the street from Gumba where we had dinner. So I would advice that a smart planner would had dinner at Gumba then go straight to S&S to get ice cream.

Line was long for 9:45pm on a Wednesday night or is this normal. We got to try some flavor before committing. 
I tried a bit of the honey lavender and thought it was very nice and light. I would have gotten that flavor but the thought of PEAR w/ BLUE FRICKEN CHEESE intrigue me.  My friend also tried the bone marrow flavor and was hilariously not into it so I encouraged them to get the lavender while I got my Pw/BFC.

How do I explain this to a normal person ~ ok ok I liked it. I liked it a hella lot. The pear was a nice bit of fruity fun mix it the occasional saltiness of a mild blue cheese. The flavor dance back and forth give your taste buds every few minutes a fun surprise. We ate our ice cream while speeding to the movie theater hoping to make the previews (I love previews) while I secretly hope we take our time so I 100% finish my ice cream, which I did. If anyone know of a trick to sneak ice cream into the movie theater lemme know, next time I'd like to enjoy it slowly.

They just opened this past week, and my husband and I were so happy to see a new restaurant on this side of town! When we got there at 11:30, the doors were locked even though the website says they open at 11. A few more people showed up, too so I was able to get a bartenders attention from around the corner who confirmed they open at 11. So they unlocked the doors. That was weird. When we left at 12:30, the place was packed. 

It's an upscale sports bar with a pretty good wine and beer menu. I had the buffalo chicken wrap and it was delicious. My husband had one of the burgers and enjoyed it. We didn't have an appetizer or desert, but the orders the tables around had looked delicious! We will definitely return.

Small World, Peter Pan, Dumbo, and more!  It felt like a time warp to walk through Fantasyland....I instantly felt like I was 8 yrs old again...so much fun!  Many the rides were for little kids though, so we didn't get on them.  The Better Half wanted to ride the Carousel though, so she had a good time on that...LOL
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/fantasyland-bay-lake?select=ejF8nuFM6fkwE4MNu1jh0w#ejF8nuFM6fkwE4MNu1jh0w

My favorite part was the Storybook Circus and the Goofini and Donaldo characters in the big tent.  It was a photo op and these characters didn't disappoint.  Goofini took some fun poses with us and entertained everyone.  Donaldo was just as fun too.
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/fantasyland-bay-lake?select=5mP4Nhg8v9lUMQEIkjZdjg#5mP4Nhg8v9lUMQEIkjZdjg
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/fantasyland-bay-lake?select=EhkpWDd8m13iRQX8ls66HA#EhkpWDd8m13iRQX8ls66HA

There's a lot of new construction happening in Fantasyland, so there was a big section blocked off...don't know what's going to be built there, but I'm sure it's going to be fun!

Return Factor - 90%

Finally another shop on Cambie that I can go to for dessert! After a number of failed attempts to get into its neighbouring bbt shop, with sub par service I might add, I'm glad TMix is able to capitalize on their overflow. 

There's so much they offer that I wasn't even sure where to begin. A few friends and I tried a couple of different things: 

1) Macaron - pretty good not overly sweet and had a nice buttery filling. 

2) BBT - the London fog was done really well. Just enough sweetness and was very flavourful. Presentation was also quite adorable.

3) BBT Pineapple slush - I am kind of a pineapple slush connoisseur and usually it ends up being a miss more than a hit. The one here was fresh, not too tart and was very refreshing. I will definitely come back for this again.

4) S'mores bubble waffle - Nicely toasted marshmallows, chocolate chips, whip cream, graham crackers, chocolate sauce.... My goodness!! Dare I say more??? Very good but also very sweet! (I don't even want to know what my dentist would say about this) I'm glad I was able to share this with my gal pals!

This is a pretty new shop so I know they're still working out a few efficiency kinks but I really enjoyed my experience at TMix and would defiantly come back again. 

And I did.. the next evening.... (I'm serious)!

I had been a long time patron of this EG until recently. I have been going to Jill Hanson since at least 2008 and have never thought to go anywhere else because she is terrific. She's always on time (never more than a 5 minute wait, for sure), she has a great sense of humor and tries to make her waxing session quick and painless- this is for both lip and bikini. 

Going to EG is a little expensive and parking in that area on a weekday can be difficult (they're not open weekends). The Devonshire garage is only $5 dollars if you get there after 6pm, but if you're there before that time it's $7 for two hours. That's not a lot of money when you consider you are parking in the heart of Boston's Financial District, but when you add it to the cost of waxing sessions every 5 weeks or so, it adds up. This is kind of the reason I am not returning to this particular EG; I work outside of the city and Jill is no longer offering appointments after 4:30PM. 

I kept going because I love her-- but it's been too difficult to meet her appointment times. I highly recommend using her services if you work in that neighborhood.

I wish her and the Winthrop Square crew the best-- I will be back if I can't find anyone as good as you. :)

Overall: highly recommend the outdoor deck for a nice meal or celebratory drink. Go for the happy hour if you are looking for a nice deal!

Location: Departure is the top floor of a hotel. The elevators actually won't let you up until the exact time they open (4PM on Sunday). Ask for the outdoor seating! The view is awesome for a nice afternoon, either with a group or a date. 

Service: Our waitress was incredible. She helped us order the right amount of food, was super attentive, and our water glasses were never less than half full. 

Food: We ordered solely off of the happy hour menu, and it was awesome! For two, we ordered the edamame, maki roll of the day, departure wings,  crispy pork belly, and kimchi fried rice. The crispy pork belly was out of this world - we almost ordered a second one. You need to try it!! The edamame was as expected. The maki roll of the day and fried rice were fine. The departure wings were flavorful and crispy. But back to the pork belly...it made up for any potential complaints I would have of anything. We also ordered the weekly rotating cocktail - super flavorful and thoughtful!

Went Sunday April 6 for dinner. We didn't realize we missed end of happy hour and were seated in the small corner alcove in bar. Since happy hour was over we went for the dinner special. Our server was Nate and he was fabulous. Professional, good at his job. I had a salad and it was large and tasty. My prime rib was ordered rare and it was done perfectly. The fresh horseradish was a nice touch. The baked potatoe was served with all toppings on the side as I requested. I upgraded to the chocolate mousse for dessert per Nates suggestion and it was spot on. We had wine and martinis and it was an excellent lemon drop. I would go back when I visit portland.

Classic American Breakfast spot.  This diner in Winter Garden is a great lil spot.  This review is for their breakfast.  Went one Sunday morning.  The options are classic choices with a decent variety.

Ordered a breakfast platter that included two eggs, bacon or sausage, and 2 pancakes.  The sausage patties looked a lil skimpy but really weren't.  Just the way they looked I guess.  The pancakes were huge and fluffy.

The service was also pretty good.  Unlimited coffee kept on coming.  I don't think my glass ever got empty.

Prices were good too, almost all breakfast item were easily under $10.  WIll definitely go back for breakfast and possibly lunch some time soon.

Been on Boston - NYC acela express 3 times, twice first class, once business class.

Don't remember what 'business' class was like, that was many moons ago.

First class is decent really. Decent food, decent seats, decent service. 

I think most importantly, if you were to add up travel time between Logan-Boston and JFK/EWR-manhattan, the acela express is awesome.

If you're used to travelling on a larger jet however, the comfort onboard the train is rather lacking. Travelling on the acela between BOS and NY is like travelling on a plane with constant little turbulence for 3.5 hours...

Despite this I do think this might be the best way to go unless of course you have someone to chauffeur you to and from the airports, priority check in and all that.

A lively, sophisticated dining and drinking venue in Kenmore Square, Eastern Standard offers a good variety of offerings that's good for groups large and small and occasions intimate or festive. 

Menu items feature typical American bistro fare like oysters, seafood, steaks, salads, and burgers. Everything is of good quality given the price, and items like the chicory creme caramel are exquisitely plated, not to mention super delish. 

Boozy offerings are also quite extensive, with a number of quality domestic and foreign beers, and a solid cocktail program. Service is also attentive and friendly. Worth checking out for a variety of settings, whether for a drink in a classy setting before or after a game, or even for a business dinner.

I can see why this place draws such a crowd: its a trendy, open-aired atmosphere with a great view of the greenbelt in S. Austin. What a prime location for a place like this!!

I went around 5p on a Friday evening and there was still some parking to be had--- not much, but some, which is impressive for how many people were already at the joint. And there was actually a happy hour going on--- (and I use the word "actually" because it seems that Friday HH's can be nonexistent at some place). $3-4 for a marg or beer, ok.

Then we were seated for dinner. The menu is pretty broad. What my fiance and I ordered were both just alright, hence the 4 stars and not 5. And the place is a liiiittle pricey for what you get, I think the price is paying for the view mostly anyway.

Clean theater with stadium seating and semi-reclining seats...a big "YAY!" for a city theater. The concession area has evolved into a serve-yourself wonderland with a bulk candy section and the mother of all soda machines (the Coke dispenser with a touchscreen and one million different sodas that allows you to add the flavor of your heart's desire to ANY kind of soda you choose...the permutations of soda options are limitless). The prices are the same as any movie theater you go to nowadays - expensive, but that is to be expected.

"Do you guys have regular milk?" I asked the barista after receiving my coffee and getting ready to add a little milk and sugar. The barista, a typical Portland hipster, who prefers not to speak in too many words, replies "oh uh, no just that."
"Why is that" I asked, in a flatline tone.
"Oh uh, um. Uh--" he seems unprepared for such a direct question, but also is looking for something by the cabinets.
"The owner wants to keep the milk plant-based"
"Ah" I said.

Thanks plant-based vegan (most likely) owner for dictating what milk your customers should add to their coffee.  

The coffee is very high quality (competing with koava, case study, and extracto) but 4 stars for two reasons:
1. Don't allow dogs in the cafe. It's annoying when they bark.
2. Don't force your "plant-based" philosophy onto your customers. Oat milk and coffee don't mix well at all!!

I was pleasantly surprised by this place. After waiting in lines and enduring the heat you want a nice, cool place to sit and enjoy some good food. This is a really good size restaurant. We were there for lunch so were looking for something quick and easy for us and our kids. Chicken blt was really good, fresh ingredients, good portion and great roll. My wife had the turkey club on the croissant which was bland and not as good as the chicken blt. The artichoke dip appetizer was fresh and good but they should serve it with crackers or even tortilla chips. It comes with 4 pieces of Italian bread so without double dipping you would need to consume 1/4 of the app on 1 small piece of bread. Service was average but passable. I would go again if we were in universal and wanted something quick that wasn't a hot dog or microwaved burger.

I've been to the original Whit's Frozen Custard location in Granville,OH a number of times and was excited to see them open a store in Westerville.  I've been here several times since they opened and have tried both a standard cone and their variation of a Dairy Queen Blizzard (I forget what they call it -- something with Whit's in the name). Frozen custard is not the same as ice cream (other than the fact that both are cold and delicious).

If you love ice cream -- give Whit's Frozen Custard a try -- it's super.

Good little hole in the wall place, their build your own burritos are pretty good for the price point! I had mine with tuna, spicy tuna and seaweed salad which all were extra price so I do wish they had some fish options included in the price of their BYO burritos. The flavor and quality of the fry a was really good though! 
Their regular rolls were a little overpriced for the 6 pieces you would get unfortunately. Overall the whole environment of the store is pretty cool and I like how they are doing all the orders on their little kiosk stations even if it took a little longer than we expected to get our food.

I have to admit I might be a little bit biased towards The Reef and have fallen in for the Caribbean theme of the Restaurant, just like any Caribbean regular would who is stuck in Vancouver. I have visited 3 times. 
The first time I went to their location on Main St and ordered the fish taco with Plantain Chips, both done to perfection. The second time I went to the location on the drive and ordered the same dish because it was so good but was disappointed, it was poorly done and had a microwave feel to it. 
The third time I was more hungry and went for the Jerk Salmon. That was a clear winner. A huge serving of rice'n'peas, slaw and the salmon soaked in a very hot and spicy jerk sauce. Add some of the house made hot sauce and you will be reaching for the water jug!!!
As for the cocktails, I haven't tired them yet as I am always driving but I opted for the virgin Jack Sparrow version. So good. The Ginger Beer taste like actual Ginger Beer! 

Overall, the service has always been very good and the staff welcoming. I like the little complimentary fry ball with coconut butter, which is a guilty pleasure for the celiac diseased!!! 

The Reef is a fun place with a nice atmosphere and I will go back there again.

Don't walk, RUN to Motivated Fitness.

At $35/month, I can work out whenever I want, have a good shower, and get ready for work.  I don't go during a rush time, so I always get my turn on the machine and never feel like I have to wait.  I've been a few times in the early morning when its pretty crazy, but still no complaints.

Locker rooms and facilities are always clean.  There are plenty of spray bottles with cleaners and paper towels and people actually use them to wipe down machines.

The owners are super friendly and really make the extra effort to know their members.  I've only belonged since October.  It took over a year before the BSC staff knew me by face.

My membership doesn't include classes, but they aren't really at times that mesh with my schedule.  If I did take classes, I'd still only pay $55/month.  

If you live in Southie, don't waste your time at Gold's or BAC.  I hear they're both anonymous and over crowded.

Ate here on a Saturday night after booking with opentable.  We walked in and were seated immediately.  Our excellent server Justin was at the table almost instantaneously and suggested an excellent Sauvignon blanc from Greece.  I had the saffron risotto which was both cheaper and better than any other I've had in Austin, and the wife had the trout, which was excellent.  Food, wine and service were all very good at a relatively cheap price.  I would give it an overall 4.5 if that were an option.

I don't go to a lot of breweries as I don't drink a lot of beer. But I do on occasion enjoy going with friends because there's nothing like the ambience that many of these breweries provide. Usually you get a large space with different types of craft beers. There's generally some great music and food nearby. It just makes for a fun afternoon.

We came to Orpheus to celebrate a friend's birthday. We had trouble with parking (there's barely any) and most weekends it gets busy here. I suggest you Uber there. That day we went, they had over a dozen different types of beers and multiple people working the bar so you were never standing in line for vary long. On the screens above the bar they describe the flavor profiles in depth. For those who are non alcohol drinkers or just don't like beer, there are Jarrito sodas in the fridge. 

Every 30 or 45 min or so, they do a tour of their brewery in the back and actually provide cool information about the process (I find the science fascinating). They are the first brewery in Atlanta to make sours and of course now they have branched out into all types. Orpheus beer is sold not only in Atlanta but in different countries as well. If you stick around Atlanta long enough, you'll see their beer is pretty well regarded.

On occasion they will have a taco truck outside. They have a souvenir/branding store in the building and they also have someone who sells artwork. I do really enjoy the branding they use for their cans. It's genius!

There's nothing more fun than a carefully curated, thoughtfully organized kitchen store full of everything you need and even more you want. I can wander around in a place like this all day long, debating the aesthetic vs functional merits of three kinds of rubber spatula or hefting utensil crocks to find just the right weight. And on and on....

I hate shopping at big-box chains so for that reason alone I'm thrilled that Kitchen Kaboodle is local and in my neighborhood! They carry many top brands so some merchandise is pricey, but there are plenty of basics here as well that are budget-friendly (less so when it comes to appliances perhaps, but good deals appear nonetheless). 

Surprisingly, I wasn't hunting for kitchenware but for furniture on my visit yesterday. And there's a whole section of it upstairs: not just kitchen-related, but for the living room as well (couches, tables, floor rugs, and so on). In terms of look, I'd compare it to something like Crate & Barrel or West Elm: modern and comfortable with an edge of safe eclecticism. Additionally, Kitchen Kaboodle's sources are smaller and more conscientious manufacturers, which is a plus. 

When I'm furniture shopping I'm fairly demanding (it took me months to find the right dining room table). I don't mind spending some money for good sustainable construction, but I lack an unlimited budget; the aforementioned shops are typically doable only with sale prices, plus I prefer to buy more locally and independently. And when furnishing a small space, a piece has to function within some pretty exact parameters (and look just right doing it). In this case, we were looking for just the right storage bench, and I was delighted to find it - on substantial sale - at the back of the store upstairs. Excellent construction from reclaimed wood, with lovely clean lines, and all at a price less than what the national stores advertised for a similar - and inferior - product. Happy!

Service couldn't have been friendlier or more helpful; the man assisting us had the bench wrapped up and outside to our car within a few short minutes. On furniture purchases (or at least this one) you still have a week to change your mind and return it, a nice option since sometimes you have to see how something looks in your home before you decide it's really what you want. No second thoughts here though!

Aside from all that excellence, Kitchen Kaboodle provides an hour of free parking behind the store so you don't have to lug your purchases blocks to your car or home on the bus. This is my future first stop for anything kitchen-related, and a nice option for furniture too (especially when there's a great sale happening).

My husband and I never get out but have gone past this restaurant a million times.  Our way of trying out a place is to stop in for a drink and a few apps.  We ordered mushroom risotto that was  creamy & flavorful, crispy calamari which was light crisp and tasty, the special app of the night was pumpkin ravioli with sage and brown butter sauce..definitely as good as it sounds (just wished there was more sauce) and I must say the parmesan garlic fries...YUMM!  We would definitely go back and try them out for a dinner in the diningroom.  And the bartender was very helpful about wine and beer selection.  Good experience all around.

First, do not let anyone tell you that Watershed has the best fried chicken in Atlanta.  I've had it and it's not that great.  The best fried chicken in Atlanta is at The Village Tap.  It tastes like someone's southern granny is back in the kitchen cooking it for Sunday dinner on the grounds!  I also had the stone ground grits with it - they were nice and creamy.  My husband had the pot roast, which looked delicious - he certainly cleaned his plate.   At 6:30 on Thursday, the place was relatively quiet, which was nice.  Several couples were on the covered patio and some were on the uncovered portion.  We were the only ones who opted for inside seating, though a few people were at the bar.  

We'll definitely be back!  The only reason they get 4 stars instead of 5 is because they totally forgot to bring me my second side (though did bring it once prompted) and the beginning of the service was a little clumsy.  However, everyone was really nice and the food was really good.  

Go and check them out!

We went to the Salmon House for my friend's birthday the other day. The appies were awesome and the seafood was really good! (I'm a huge fan of seafood, so it's not a huge surprise that I enjoyed this place.) The service was also exceptional, and they also have quite an extensive wine list. 

My one friend at the party isn't a huge fan of seafood, but the spectacular view of the city made up for it. It's honestly one of the best views you can look upon while sitting down for a fancy dinner. 

It's a little pricey here, but definitely a great venue for a nice birthday dinner or special event.

I haven't been here in a long while. Remembering those good old days when I was a youngster, the sales person was very nice, very helpful, intuitive and really "professional". While time goes by...Precision seems to change...

The same guy always seems to be standing by the front door greeting customers. He shakes his head and smiles at us, yet doesn't say anything. ?!? Am I supposed to start the conversation? I thought to myself, "Do I need to take a number?" Do I just walk to the counter in front of me and ask for help? Do I just go get what I want then pay? Or, should I go to the other counter and ask for assistance? I try to make eye contact but everyone just seems to turn away.

Since everybody seemed so busy (which they weren't), I grabbed Josh (he couldn't escape cuz he just checked out a customer). I told him allll I need is 4 (damn) filters! One for each lens and a circular filter (then I'll get outta your hair!). He was very helpful and saved me some money on the filter deal. Cool!

The second time, I went back with hubby to get another battery, the same incident happened to us...We patiently waited for a sales person who was working at the computer on the counter. He saw us, but just kept minding his own business while we just stood there and waited.

All and all, they've got everything you'll ever need/want for all your photographic needs, whether it's new, old or used cameras, lenses or equipment. I'm not even going to talk about all of the professional camera equipment they have in there. They also provide photo copying/printing services, and have lots of "How to" training resources from classes, to books and to videos.  Anything you want to know about photography, they got it. One stop shopping for allll your photo needs, how bout that! 
   
Of course, I will definitely be back, since this is the only "professional" camera store in town. They have the best selection on all things "photography" anyway. (Even though I have to put up with SOME of the attitude here, hopefully that'll change) If it weren't for the professional advice they gave us "rookies", then, I'd rather go someplace else. Hubby disagrees though. It's not just me, is it?

We wanted a place to spend a Friday evening chilling out and enjoying a conversation with friends and one of our friends suggested this place. The atmosphere was really great. The staffs were friendly and recommended us with Chef Mon's specialty on the menu.

For appetizer, I loved "Moo Ping" (Grilled Tenderloin Pork) which tasted like what I had in Thailand. You have to try this with sticky rice as it's common in Thailand. For main dish, I could recommend "Pla Lui Suan" (Crispy Fried Fish with Herb Dressing) - this was another dish I have never seen in the U.S. that this restaurant could really bring the taste of Thailand here. Two thumbs up for the Chef!

This isn't the kind of Starbucks where you'd want to hang out for a few hours, but it's super efficient, very pleasant, and has parking in the back. The staff are very friendly and smart - no space cadets as far as I've seen so far. It's a sheer wonder how they get through the long morning line so quickly. The first time I went in here at 8:15am, the size of the line made me think it would be a disaster, but before I knew it I was ordering my usual (grande iced americano in a venti cup with extra ice and water), a drink that very few Starbucks employees across the country have ever gotten right. Normally, I either get a blank stare, a quad-shot americano (I'm not looking for a heart attack, but thanks), or a grande americano at the price of a venti. This has become of a pet peeve of mine, to the point where I now judge a Starbucks by how well they handle this drink. Sometimes you have to wait a little bit to get your drink after ordering here, but the staff members go as fast as they can without messing up your drink, so I give them credit.

Not only are the people here extremely organized and "with it," but they also go out of their way to give you what you ordered and be nice about it. Today, my drink somehow got lost in the shuffle for a few minutes (not even that long), and they presented me with a certificate for a free drink next time. They even said they were sorry. Normally, when my order gets lost at a Starbucks, I get an annoyed glare for daring to ask where it might have gone.

Visited this place on a trip to Atlanta. Really glad I checked it out! Great atmosphere. Really enjoyed the food and the service was top notch.
