They were super swamped and it ended up being almost 2hrs after we sat down that we got our food. The manager was super nice and gave us our appetizer for free. We hadn't really noticed it took such a long time because we were enjoying the atmosphere and the beer! They had a special for margarita gummy bears (gummy bears soaked in tequila). We gave it a try and it was interesting. Fun to try once, but not something we'd get again. Definitely recommend this place if you're in the Atlanta area!

I was fortunate enough to spend five nights here this past November.  The building was built at a combination hotel/condo with the hotel taking up the first five floors.  One advantage of this is that the rooms are really designed as small apartments with plenty of space including a huge bathroom.

The ceilings are at least 10 ft high and add to the sense of the space.  I was lucky to have a great view of the midtown skyline from the floor to ceiling bedroom windows.

The fixtures and appliances used were top notch.  I'm no expert on bedding and thread counts but suffice to say it wasn't lacking.

It was too cool to use the outdoor pool but the gym itself was a pleasant surprise with the amount of equipment available.  I later found out that this gym was shared with the tenants of the condo portion so it made sense why it was so well stocked compared to other hotels I've been in.

Can't say much about the food or room service, didn't take advantage of it. 

The hotel is right in the middle of Atlantic Station with is a mini-city filled with shops and restaurants that will fill all your food and shopping needs.

My favorite Bon Chon I've been to so far. The only one I haven't been to yet is the one in D.C.

The chicken size and flavor is on point. I think this location has the best spicy wings recipe, which is why this is my favorite location. 

The service is usually friendly and accommodating. I haven't had many bad experiences here. Definitely more good than bad.

The only thing that is troublesome is parking! It can take forever to find a spot. But I think its worth it.

I love the Hazel Dell Planet Fitness as it is always clean and the equipment is well maintained.  It is a great place to work at your own pace and follow a routine that meets your needs.  My ONLY complaint is people talking on their cell phones!  Even with my head phones playing music the constant talking of the person next to me drives me nuts.  The facility rules say phone calls should take place in the lobby.  I wish people would be considerate and use the lobby area if they are going to talk non stop for 10 minutes.

Firehouse Subs is my favorite chain sub place. I love the Hook and Ladder and the Engineer subs. Both are stuffed full of meat and served toasted. I get them "fully involved" which loads them up with lettuce, tomato, onions, mayo and mustard with a dill pickle.

Ordering is a snap, then you wait while your subs is made. They have an assortment of hot sauces available to try. This location has the new touch screen soda machine. It allows you to make hundred of mixes of drinks- it's fun to just stand in front of and try samples of a few dozen before you chose! I ended up with strawberry Sprite one time and vanilla Dr. Pepper another. Yum!

At this particular location the staff seemed to have dropped the ball on the whole, "Welcome to Firehouse" they usually shout when you walk in. They weren't overall very friendly either. Maybe they need some better management or a little retraining.

Having lived on the Mississippi Gulf Coast for a number of years, I now miss the Gulf style cuisine.  When I found the Crawfish Shack was run by Asians rather than by a Cajun ... I was doubtful ... but they really do have a great selection of dishes!

My only complaint ... although very good ... their Po-Boys are not traditional.  For that, you'll have to visit Atlanta Highway Seafood Market in Gainesville, GA.

In all other respects, this is a nice clean place with communal seating and a great menu.

We took advantage of Doubletree Hilton's Ultimate Waterpark Package this past weekend, Friday 3/22 to Sat 3/23. What a fantastic mini vacation it was!!! The package price was extremely reasonable considering it including a twilight pass for friday night and daylight pass for all day saturday, for 2 adults and 2 children...two $20 arcade cards...free breakfast buffet...and a night at the hilton!
I just wrote a 5-star review for the Hotel but our experience at the Waterpark was also great! Although saturday was a little crowded, the lines moved quickly and there were many lifeguards. I was impressed that none of them were talking to eachother like you often see, they each had assigned stations at which they were always moving and scanning, and they rotated stations often! 
Yes the chlorine smell was a little much but seriously, isn't it always in a waterpark? especially an indoor one? 
The food & drinks were delicious and honestly, compared to many parks, the prices were very reasonable. And once you bought a drink, it was free refills! (We saved our cups from friday to satuday!) 
My daughter had a blast and even my husband and I enjoyed ourselves on the big slides and the hot tub. 
I do think next time we will bring watershoes, although the molded floors are "textured" a slipped a couple of times....
Overall it was a fantastic time...my daughter wanted me to add that she had only one complaint......"I had WAY too much fun!!" --she's too cute!

Thank you so much, we WILL be back!

Went here last night on whim. I remember going to Smokey's when I was a small child, sometimes trekking from North Portland with my mom just for their pizza. They had the best pizza ever and I was tentatively hoping their current pizza could still live up to my memory of it. 

First off, the place is a bit "divey", located in the strip mall, and has seen better times, decor-wise. The room partitions are a bit shredded, the tables and chairs are probably the same ones from the 70's. But, in all, the place is clean and kept-up for what they have to work with. (Note about temps - the front is colder (a/c) and the back of the restaurant is warmer.) 

Being a Friday night, we thought the place might be packed, but it wasn't. In fact, it was kind of a ghost town in there. Not sure why. Friday night, pizza and beer....should be plenty of people. But I think there was only about 6 people total here. 

The employees were super-nice and friendly. Ever so helpful, too. This is one of the few places offering a gluten-free pizza (small size only tho), and they made sure to tell me about the sausage and the burger mix not being gluten-free. Any pizza joint willing to attempt making gluten-free pizza gets high marks in my book! (FYI, for those who don't know, gluten is what makes breads, etc, light, doughy, & fluffy. When left out, the result is often cardboard.) From what I could tell, there was no extra cost for the gluten-free option (another big plus, since GF stuff is EXPENSIVE!). 

My husband had their Smokey's Red beer. Super great, he says! If he had known it was going to be so good, he would've ordered a pitcher. LOL. Myself, I had lemonade. It may have been from a mix (they store it in a "Tupperware-like" container behind the counter), but it was really good, too.

The pizza took a bit longer than we were told (doesn't it always seem to, tho?), but we found it was worth the wait. The pizza was Small, but it was enough for us 2 people, plus a few slices to take home. The crust was, well, pretty good as far as gluten-free bread items go. Since it had no gluten to make it "rise", it was more like a thick cracker crust. They get points there for it. As we found out on our way out, they are fairly new to the whole gluten-free stuff. Since it is so expensive, it's not like they are able to make a bunch of "practice pizzas" - it would be really expensive to do so - and they are still figuring it all out. But it was definitely edible and palatable, even tho the workers that night all admitted that none of them had ever made one of the gluten-free pizzas yet. They did good. 

As for the toppings, we got the meat feast options, with added olives and pineapple. When the pizza arrived, it was heavy! LOADS of toppings! Heck, if I wanted to forgo the crust, a full meal could still be made from just the toppings alone! More points to them!

Our total bill came to $26.73. I guess that's decent these days for good pizza joints (why the heck is pizza, any pizza, so expensive nowadays?!). So, that's not too bad, really. As for flavor, taste, etc, they certainly did still live up to my memory of awesome yummy pizza! I am looking forward to dropping in again and making this our regular pizza place. It's like "pizza crack". Totally good and still worth a trek cross town for it. 

The bathrooms were clean, so that's another plus. Especially in older places, where they are often hard to keep clean. 

Keep up the great work, guys! Thanks for not being afraid to offer the gluten-free crust, and willing to keep working on it to make it even better!

Had been hearing about the service, but ours was great and quick (which we needed) when we popped in here for breakfast one day. Very nice egg sandwich on great wheat bread and no problem with substituting for egg whites and fruit on the side. They also had a lot of meat options, like turkey sausage, chicken sausage, veggie, etc. I'd love to give them a shot for lunch sometime as well. I bet if you stay on them the service may be better, being that we were in a rush we made sure they were attentive and I didn't get the feeling that the waiter had other tables at the time we were there.

The bathroom is really poorly designed. Whoever decided to color a bathroom BLACK must have been a man.

Michael Scott: Why is my office black?
Dwight: To intimidate my subordinates.
Michael: That's stupid.

The Dwight of the Hilton's design failed to recognize that since the dawn of time, bathrooms are kept white or off-white for a reason. The result of a  heavy black bathroom presence is that it's almost impossible to get ready in front of the mirror because the lighting is so terrible. It's like trying to do your hair, makeup (I'm told) or other regimen during a power outage. The low-watt vanity lights that they have built into and over the mirror stand no chance against the light-sucking black tiling of the shower. I think the easy answer is: BETTER VANITY LIGHTING. Redoing all the showers seems much more expensive. I assume they tiled the showers black to make it look "modern" while covering up any chance someone would notice that the shower wasn't cleaned.

Having stayed here now on multiple occasions over the past few years, however, the location's proximity to my office leaves few alternative viable options. The room service is also pretty good, much preferred to any of the in-hotel dining options. Although if you're willing to walk 1-3 blocks down N. High Street you'll quickly find the hotel's cuisine to be far inferior to the local options.

I have come to enjoy the bed a great deal here as well, it makes for a really comfortable sleep. The HVAC leaves something to be desired, however, as the room doesn't circulate air very well.

I was a walk-in for a gel polish manicure and needed an old gel polish removed. The salon is a little run down, but great value for money. They do charge $5 to remove old gel polish, but they do it carefully (I've been to Katie's Nails on Keefer Street and had old shellac removed by the tool used to shape acrylic nails!) The girl that did my nails was friendly, paid great attention to detail and left me with the best gel polish manicure I have had in a long time. I will definitely go back!

A tiny Mexican restaurant in Waltham, this place churns out some delicious authentic Mexican dishes. The chips and salsa come out right away, the chips are a bit on the crunchy side but the salsa is very tasty.  I usually order a Mexican coke to enjoy with my food. I've ordered steak and chicken dishes and the meat is always tender and perfectly cooked. They do get busy on weekends but the servers are always friendly. The decor leaves something to be desired, and you'll need to get driving directions before you go, but the food is most important and it is yummy!

Went here last night with the boyfriend. I was very happy. We both were. I had seen for a while that a shabu was opening here because I drive past it every day. I enjoy a nice hot pot. It is very social and engaging, and as a chef myself I love to play with food :-)

We started with kimchi and shumai, both were a good start to a great meal. Not filling but very fulfilling. 

I got the seafood delux platter, it came with calamari, really nice looking salmon, clams, fish balls and a few other fun fishy items. My boyfriend got the surf and turf platter, which he chose lamb. Our broths were a Mongolian (spicy Chinese) and the other was an herbal type of broth, I can't remember the name. We both had an excellent meal. 

We each had two drinks from their menu. I had a pink flirtini followed by a pomegranate martini. They looked very much alike, but they both had different awesome flavors. the drinks took some time to get to us, but server was very apologetic (manners still count for something in my book at least) so we had no problem waiting a few extra minutes. I understand that is is a new restaurant, and it may take a little time for people to settle in their positions and to fine tune themselves.

It's cool to have a neat shabu just down the street... I definitely reccomend.

For nearly three decades my husband and I followed the Korean gal who owns this place as she moved from one restaurant location to another. The reason? The flavors of her dishes are outstanding! When I was at her current location for lunch yesterday, I realized that all of the customers except myself were Koreans speaking Korean. I'd say that's a pretty good testimonial from people who know. Par for the course, the unlovely but functional "decor". The only demerit was the scanty quantity of meat in the Kimchi Chi Gei (the hot flavored soup brought to the table boiing furiously in a large, black flanged or stone bowl). It's a craving that I get when stuffy with a bad head cold, and it never fails to open the pipes. By all means, get the "purple rice". It's traditional and flavorful.

El toro is a perfect quick neighborhood mexican restaurant.  We've tried many others in the area, like Los Brovos, but El Toro definitely wins out.  

They have warm chips and WHITE cheese dip, while many others have yellow.  The salsa is usualy very good, too.  Based on the variability of heat, I think they make it themselves.

Margaritas can be a bit weak (depending on the night), but not too bad. 

The service is always very attentive, quick, and very friendly.  

Price is unbeatable, without drinks you can eat a full dinner for under $10.

I was introduced to Bedford Farms by a friend since I live in the Bedford area and this is the closest Ice Cream shop around.  My first visit, I ordered the Cookie Dough since this has been my favorite for a long time.  I thought the Cookie Dough Ice Cream had too much chocoloate chips and not enough cookie dough.  To be honest, I couldn't really taste the cookie dough at all.  So I was a bit disappointed, but I still enjoyed the ice cream.  The small size alone was already $4.75.  I really thought that I could've bought a half gallon tub with that much money instead of a small cup.  I still really enjoyed the ice cream, but I personally didn't think it was worth it.  The best Cookie Dough that I've had was the Blue Bell Ice Cream and the one at Bedford Farms didn't compare well to it.

I liked it. It is on the smaller side, but there is still a variety of genres. While it is called frugal, just be aware that the prices are not super frugal unless you're buying from the sale section (however, you are buying from a local and black owned business so if you are avid reader like myself you may walk out of here with at least two books and be supporting your locally owned businesses in the process). I bought a Selena book in Spanish from sale section $7 and a James Baldwin novel for ~ $8. 

Also, the Saturday evening I came, there was a book club meeting in session which is great. They have a little kids section too which is awesome. I also really liked the other items the store sells: super cute hand bags, personalized bookmarks, and clothing items). Go check it out!

Had a really good meal here a few days after it opened (maybe the second day actually?) I really love the decor and ambience. The giant open front wall is great, and the bar that runs along the patio, no tables, perfect for people watching, is a catch. 

The tables are high tops, which can sometimes be annoying, but made for good visibility up and down the long length of the establishment. This is a big step up from Tavern Old Town for the owners, but they're doing it well! The food was great. We loved the sweet potato tacos, so good! I got the bahn mi and it was spilling off the bun the whole time. Stacked! I also ordered a bowl of the veggie chili. We mentioned passingly that we were going to split it, and the waiter brought us two cups instead of a bowl. Thoughtful!

The service was attentive, there were TV screens everywhere (basketball was on...score!) and for goodness sake, there's a frickin' pool table! GENIUS. Will be back. A lot. My only complaint was the chauchy crowd the open wall was drawing. Lots of popped collars wandering over from 16 Bit.

A solid place for Latin American food. Great place to go for meals or for happy hours. I've come a couple of times for happy hours and enjoyed the appetizers greatly. They also have great mojitos and other cocktails too. 

The arepas and empanadas are always solid choices. The yucca fries and plantains are probably my favorite thing there. I've had their quesadillas before as well, which is very filling and comes with lots of fix-ins on the side (salsa, sour cream, guac). 

Service has always been great too.

Forge is a quaint little bakery and coffee shop that I've come to a few times. The atmosphere is fun, with several window seats, and even a little viewing spot to the bakery.

The menu is pricey-- don't get me wrong, but the work that goes into everything on the menu is unreal. Meat is always going to cost you extra, so expect this. This makes my bacon-loving soul hurt, but the breakfast sandwich I just had was so amazing that I really can't complain. 

Also, forge makes a mean cup of coffee. They know what they're doing.

Jenna is one of the best and the business and very talented in her profession.  I have been a brow and makeup client of Jenna's for years ! I have since moved to Seattle but I come into town to see Jenna when in Ptld for work or just visiting quite frequently. I have recommended her to numerous friends for brow shaping and makeup application.  I have seen first hand some of her clients who have undergone eyelash extensions and they look fabulous !  I hope to soon have them done as well !

So an unfortunate accident forced my husband and I into buying a new car since his was totaled. We weren't getting much in the insurance settlement and didn't have much in savings to front for anything super special. We did our own research online and went to look at one specific car at Hatfield Kia. When we arrived, someone else was taking it for a test drive, but we made it known that it was exactly what we were looking for. The salesmen all seemed to be "on our side" - so to speak - and updated us when the other couple said it wasn't the car they wanted. We went on a test drive with Manuel and he made sure we were taken care of from start to finish. He was personable, ready for the sale, but not overly pushy. We wouldn't have been the right people to give a "hard sell" to, which is what made us leave another lot earlier in the week. We did end up purchasing from Hatfield Kia and are happy, so far, with our vehicle. The only complaint is that the sales guys there are working their tails off - they were all super busy. If there was a lull with our decision making, the salesmen were off helping someone else. It could've been insulting, but we realized that they were stretched too thin.

The location for Midtown adventuring is premo.  I love the setup of the rooms, but what I like best is the water pressure!  The bathroom was VERY nice, and I enjoyed the separate tub and shower.  It seems some folks had problems with the water pressure, browsing some other reviews.  My room had NO issues.

The bed is heavenly and the staff is friendly.  I don't necessarily agree with an upcharge to park and another one to use wi-fi....but overall, this was a very nice stay.

In 1 of the innumerable outdoor shopping centers in Richmond.  Remarkably this center had ample parking.  From outside the shopping center &  Bistro look mundane.  

Upon entering Bistro greets you with a modern decor, warm colors & inviting comfortable chairs.  The floor plan is open with generous spacing between tables.  There is an outdoor patio facing Alexandra Rd. which may be used for seating in warm weather.  They played soft romantic music in the background.

After entering we were shown to our table promptly.  Service was friendly & good throughout the evening.

The menu was Italian inspired with Asian accents.  They started the meal with warm Garlic Bread.  We ordered Honey Squash Soup, Water Mozzarella & Tomatoe Salad,  Shanghai Seafood Pasta, Red Sauce Seafood Pasta, & Honey Squash Pizza.  The pizza, with very thin crust, corn, squash, & cheese toppings still leaves me wanting more.  All the food was delicious!  The house red wine was a perfect compliment.

An enjoyable relaxing dining experience...we will be back.

When I see an Italian Restaurant that features pizza on its menu my heart sinks, my head slowly descends to the table top and a gentle, rhythmic, banging begins. 
So we'd given Double Zero a miss until this weekend. We were on Roswell Road at 5:45 on Saturday and decided on a whim to give them a try for an early drink and antipasti. 
We self-parked, although there is a valet, and sat at the bar which is a little gloomy when coming in from the bright sun . Initially we had some difficulty reading the menu, fortunately Allie, our first server, had just bought some small flashlights, which helped until our eyes adjusted. Also behind the bar : Nick, from Grimsby UK, Chris, the beverage manager, and Trey. All the staff are friendly and helpful. 
One of the things I look for in a new restaurant is a wine list that contains wines that are unfamiliar to me, it's a good indicator of return visit potential. The list here is impressive with an Italian focus. Of the 80 plus wines on offer, at least 70% were unfamiliar to us and , most importantly, 50 or so are available by the glass. 
We called a friend we were meeting later to come and join us and had a couple of glasses of Soligo prosecco while we waited- the bar had one or two people seated and 20% of tables were occupied.
Our friend was feeling in the mood for something with a germanic profile (some weight and a clean finish). Chris was very helpful finding a wine with a profile he'd like - I Greco Filu Bianco.
We ordered a couple of small platters of cheese and meats, these are things that we serve at home so we had a basis for comparison
-Salame Toscano 
-Speck 
-Pecorino Grand Cru 
These came served together on a wooden board with a small bowl of green and brown olives, a couple of pieces of rustic bread and a spoonful of pepper jam. The arrangement was a nice touch - we've often ordered in this way and ended up with a separate plate for each dish.
All these were excellent with the Pecorino being a particular standout.
By 6:30 the place had started to fill up:  more people at the bar and the tables were around 50% full.
With another 45 minutes to spare we decided further investigation was warranted- we changed up wines and ordered more food. 
Wine:  a few reds from the House list: Barberani Polago Umbria and the Double Zero Pedirosso Campania. I like Barberani and this glass was a steal at $8 - highly recommended .
Food: 
Lamb Polpettine (sous-vide lamb meatballs)
Pork Belly Risotto served with a slow poached egg
Arancini

I went outside to check out the small patio: most of the area is occupied with a couple of small bocce courts (bocce in Sandy Springs!) one of which was being used by a family group, it's worth saying that I didn't notice any kids inside the restaurant,
The food arrived while I was outside so we didn't immediately catch the one error of our visit - instead of the Arancini we ended up with the Orrechiette. Time was too pressing for us to wait so we skipped the Arancini, and tasted the pasta - a little bland . The restaurant backed the Orrechiette off the bill.
The four meatballs were good - the mild flavor of lamb shone well through the seasoning and the crust was a fine contrast.
The belly was excellent - with the egg a great addition - certainly our favorite of the three dishes and something I would go back for. 

We left at 7:15, our total was $75 (excluding tip) - not bad at all. 
By the time we left the place was at 75% capacity and people were arriving for reservations. Age range 35-60 . Noise level acceptable. Pizza forms only a small part of the menu!
Rating: four stars - "on the list to visit often"

I've been having my eyebrows threaded at this Threading Spa once a month since 2007. Yes, it's in the middle of a Ghetto Mall, but the price makes up for it. $10 for my eyebrows. 

I used to have my eyebrows done by a lady who worked here on Sundays, but in the last year I discovered this other older lady who is there on Saturdays and she has exclusive rights to threading my brows ever since then. She does a great job shaping my brows and I'm a constant happy customer. Unfortunately I don't know her name.

I can't believe I haven't Yelped about this place sooner. Solid 4 stars.

My hubby is a huge fan of Pho and we always have Pho when we want a simple quick lunch.

We tried many Vietnamese restaurants in Vancouver, my hubby picked this one to try... But, I really suspect if the restaurant open for 24 hrs and how good it can be???  

Well... I may be wrong this time and this is the exception!!

The restaurant was simply decorated but looked ok.  I found the floor and table was quite sticky but the staff was so friendly.

We noticed the menu slightly different than other Pho places and it has a lot of varieties such as deep fried fish cakes and crab paste pho.  

Anyway, both of us ordered pho and roll combo:
Bun Bo Hue (Pork Hock, Beef Flank in hot spicy soup) The soup flavour was different, the meat was good, the noodles was great, it tasted not like those you have in the normal beef noodle soup.  (Very similar in LA Pho flavour)
Pho Tai, Bo Vien (Rare beef and beef ball noodle soup)  First thing I did was taste the broth while it is still the hottest. The broth was light and full of flavour.
Cha Gio, Goi Cuon, Nem Cuon (spring roll, shrimp salad roll and minced pork roll) It was ok coz the salad and minced pork roll was premade and a bit too cold and dry.

It's good to find another good pho place to go!

My wife and I booked a self-guided dinner cruise for two through cloud9living.com and were delighted with the experience. The boat itself has probably seen better days, but we were impressed with the friendly service, excellent food, and all around great experience it is to leisurely cruise around the lake during the sunset, check out the bats from the water, and enjoy the scenery.

The staff was friendly and helpful in getting us set up and going. When we returned, the staff person was attentive to us and even went out of his way to clear up a problem with some misinformation we had from Cloud 9 regarding parking.

The food was outstanding (we ordered the fajitas). Our only disappointment was that we didn't have something in which to take home our leftovers.

Overall, a great experience that we would highly recommend. We will probably book the same self-guided cruise again in the future and bring some friends.

Once upon a time, I went to see the Hunger Games (the first one) and my arm was viciously mauled by Bedbugs residing in the armrest of the theater's chairs. I discovered this as I was driving home and promptly returned and calmly declared that they had an infestation to take care of. Well the next morning I called and reported them for a health code violation and had the theater shut down for two weeks for fumigation. YES Houston friends, that was me. I don't think it is necessary to call out this super popular theater as I'm sure the forcible fumigation was enough. 

Regardless, why is this important? That bedbug mauling is what gives me trust issues when it comes to movie theaters. I've reached a point where I tend to only gravitate towards leather seats or make sure to wear long sleeves and pants if I'm in doubt. 

Regardless, I ended up at this theater to see Sin City: A Dame to Kill For. The theater we had planned on going to had a later showing, so we figured it wouldn't hurt to drop by here. 

My takeaway is that the theater seems to be trying to be a nightclub. It kind of reminds me of Lucky Strike in Houston, only instead of the gimmick being Bowling, it's Movies. Regardless, I like the pool tables, I also liked my decision to wear shorts and not a dress. Ain't nobody trying to be all cute and sit on the table to make a shot in a short skirt. I errr.... no longer try to use my feminine wiles to win competitive games. Wait, I take that back, all holds are off for my random occasional games of beer pong. We save those for ratchet nights. 

HOWEVER, what matters is the free blanket upgrade for the Premium Plus seats. I like having a blanket and a seat that reclines during a movie. But the premium plus seats have this weird microfiber cover that feels.... nubby? The way microfiber feels when it's slightly dirty. Which again brings to surface my trust issues involving bedbugs and movie theaters. Ironically the Premium seats have actual leather covers... aka bedbug deterrent. Come on iPic can't I pay $1 for the blanket? Or can the premium plus seats at least be smooth leather?!! I'm at a Catch-22; I want to be comfortable but I am super paranoid about bed bugs. I guess you can't win them all. I suppose I'll only get the premium plus seats when I wear long pants and long sleeves.... I can live with that.

I ate beforehand this time since we didn't plan on going here, but their menu looks pretty solid. I'd definitely be tempted to get food here next time!

I wish I have this place in Seattle! I was in the area and stopped by here before heading home. We ordered a thai tea, Ube and Lychee Crush. All the drinks were flavorful and not super sweet. My brother ordered a box of popcorn chicken and it came with fries and veggies and a drink at an affordable price. TASTY too!  

This place gets busy, but the staff knows how to handle the crowd. They are organized and the food gets out quickly. 

Coming back in the future!

I am truly impressed by CCC.  I got in a fender bender about a two months ago.  I went to CCC, they quickly did an assessment and hooked me up with Pam who oversaw all my work.

I have to admit, I was a bit of an annoying customer.  Pam ordered the parts for me and then it took me six weeks to finally make an appointment to get it into the shop (my ambivalence because I didn't want to be without a car).  Pam was awesome through this process.  She kept saying that she understood and that she'd wait for a time that would be more convenient for me.

Had I known how little time it would take CCC to fix my car, I would have taken it in ages sooner.  It took them approximately 72 hours to fix my car.  I was shocked.

Their work was impeccable.  If I ever get in a wreck again (knock on wood), I will definitely take my car back to CCC!

* Special Combination Beef Noodle Soup (C1): Pho is always good when its cold outside but it tasted especially good this time. The beefy broth with the tendon and tripe was flavorful. It had the typical onions, green onions, and cilantro as well. It's a pretty basic pho but it satisfies the cravings!
* Chicken Sate (A7): This appetizer consisted of juicy grilled chicken with a peanut sate sauce for dipping. It was nice and hot when it came out and not surprisingly, it was gone within 5 minutes. 

The service was fast and friendly. I'd recommend getting hot tea instead of water. This place isn't usually busy on the weekdays so there's plenty of parking. Lastly, there's a decent amount of options for rice, vermicelli, and pho. Overall, I'd come back again!

Back in October, I went to WE Day with Sherman and we decided to finish off the day with a bit of sushi. It's hard for two foodbloggers to go to a place neither of us has been, so thankfully, he was willing to do a "revisit" to a place that I hadn't visited before. This is what led us to Zipang Sushi. All photos are courtesy of Sherman. "Thanks!"  

Given that this was midday (and they were about to close after lunch), and he had already had lunch, we wanted to order light (and quickly). We started with their Assorted Sashimi. The salmon was amazing, and I really enjoyed the tako. The slices were cleanly cut and care was taken with the presentation.  

We wanted to try their rolls too, so we gave two of them a try. On either side is their Triple S roll, made up of Salmon, Scallop and Shrimp. I enjoyed the rice to filling ratio on this and could taste the sweetness of the scallop and shrimp quite clearly. The other was the East Meets West, filled with unagi, avocado and topped with prosciutto. As with most fusion cuisine where they pair Western flavours or ingredients with Asian flavours, the result could be a hit or a miss. The prosciutto seemed a bit dry and out of place with the roll. However, this would be an excellent choice for those who are squeamish when it comes to raw fish. 

I love Salmon Kama and when I saw that they had it, we had to order it, and boy, I'm sure glad I did. The skin had a good crispy char to it, and the fleshy collar was juicy and flaky. They served it with some grated daikon. Add some soy sauce to it and make a paste to dip the salmon into. The sweetness of the fish and the saltiness of the soy is a great umami sensation.

Although I wouldn't normally order Assorted Tempura, Sherman wanted to to give us another hot entrée to try. The prawns were really sweet and I loved the light coating. I normally have to peel apart some of the coating, but it was unnecessary here. The veggies were a bit heavy, more because of the thick portions they were cut into, rather than a heavy batter. Overall, this was a good place for a nice light lunch and I'd definitely come back if I was in the area again.

Take Note:

Closed on Mondays, and closes between 3-5pm.
Lots of options for non-raw fish lovers
Give the Okonomi a try, mini-pizzas. or the Takoyaki!
- See more at: http://xmasbb.blogspot.ca/#uds-search-results

Finally it has happened to me
Right in front of my face
My feelings can't describe it

FINALLY! I 've had Carver's Grocer-E!

(anyone get the reference??) 

I love Southern food and heard a lot of positive things about Carver's. After two years in the A, I finally made it to Carver's. They have pretty limited hours, 11-3 M-F, so I had to wait until the stars aligned for my day at Carver's. The area actually seems kind of desolate so I was nervous I was in the wrong area, but Carver's signage is prominent enough to not be missed. There are no parking lots, so you'd have to park in the neighborhood. 

We were merrily greeted by a gentleman at the cash register. At Carver's, you make your selection, get your food, take a tkt, and pay when you're finished. It's cash only. Also, it may become communal seating. There's 1 toilet. 

The space is intimate, but welcoming. I love the signage. They're funny and a lot of them are endearing gender bias remarks: adorable! 

If you order a meal, it comes with bread and 2 sides. The portions here are generous. I ordered brisket with green beans, and corn bread and Mac N Cheese. Do you remember the scene for Ratatouille when the food critique took a bit of the ratatouille? Well, my first bite didn't bring me back to my childhood, but it gave me complete satisfaction. I'm glad they gave a heaping too. My friend ordered pot roast, cheese bread, sweet potatoes, and broccoli casserole. Although the pot roast was slightly dry, the dish was still delectable.  

Show your student id and get $1 off.

After a hearing rave reviews about this place, I was finally able to stop into one of the locations. I'm originally from Jersey and I love my NYC pizza and have just not been able to find anything like it up here. This is still no NYC pizza, BUT it probably just made my list of top pizza places in Boston.  It's definitely a different type of pizza, its not greasy or heavy. Also, what's really great is that everything is organic and they locally source the ingredients. Even the drinks! 

Now that I know this place is down the road from HMart in Burlington, its gonna be hard to not come back!

Excellent! The food and service was wonderful!  The bourbon crawfish sauce over the blackened Mahi Mahi was out of this world good! We brought home a Black and Blue Burger and my husband loved it. The drinks were well made and the calamari was excellent.  The breads tasted fresh and like they were made in house.  

We'll definitely return! Beautiful ambiance and our server was terrific! 

It's definitely a posh seafood place but the turf options were great too. My mother really enjoyed the Filet Oscar.  

I've only been once but would bet it's solid choice and consistently good.

Phnom Penh's definitely 1 of the highlights of my Vancouver trip. This small place's incredibly popular, so get ready some wait time.

Marinated Thit Bo ($16.50) - Butter beef, cilantro, fried garlic with sweet, salty & sour sauce. This rare beef dish's excellent! The vinegar sauce's quite sharp. It'll hit you the strongest, but it's not too sour. The sweetness and saltiness of the sauce along with the cilantro will decrease the acidity. The fried garlic'll serve as the perfect complimentary to the dish. This butter beef'll just melt in your mouth - it's a must order!!!

Bo Luc Lac ($19.50) - Sauteed cubed beef, lettuce, tomato, lime juice. A solid beef dish. It's a very safe yet delicious dish, you can't go wrong with ordering one.

Conclusion: Their butter beef's incredible & that dish alone's worth the wait. Phnom Penh's a must-go restaurant if you're around!

A small hidden Greek restaurant in the middle of nowhere (a side road in East Cambridge) but if you are in the area (work/home), its a must eat to me.  Very casual and yesteryear decor inside.

The service here is better than excellent as the waitresses are very friendly and quick.  I find many dishes are well above average compared to other Greek restaurants.   You get a lot of food as most plates have a starter salad and fresh bread prior to your meal coming out.   A very nice lunch place that will run your group approx $10-15 person and everyone should leave smiling.

I haven't had a fruit tart in forever (too long) and I contemplated ordering one this morning because I'm trying to not ingest so much sugar (worst idea). But my sweet tooth won out. I ordered the raspberry and orange with a bottomless coffee. I really like that they have soy and almond milk in the self serve area. The medium blend I got was really delicious, the flavors melded perfectly together, not too strong or intense. I also hd the lake austin blend and I really enjoyed it (the lighter blend). The fruit tart was amazing. I could sing its praises for hours. The tart shell is thin and coated in chocolate, the pastry cream was ABSOLUTELY to die for, it wasn't too sweet. I don't like thin crusts and I loved this one. 

Today was perfect for sitting outside and just enjoying the weather/watching the water. I like Mozart's vibe, atmosphere and  coffee.

Jamaica Pond offers a serene oasis in Boston.  As part of the Emerald Necklace chain of parks and green land, the pond is the culminating experience full of joggers, dogs, kiddies, and paddle boats.  

It was approximately a 20 minute walk all the ways around the pond and we were strolling rather slow (enjoying the fall foliage!).  And on that note, what better place to view fall leaves?  Gorgeous blends of firey red and electric yellow offer a backdrop on a chilly day's walk around the pond. 

The boat house is a community magnet that regularly hosts events including music, children's parties, and fall festivals.  The day I went it was swarming with children in costumes for a lantern parade and I made sure to get the prerequisite hot apple cider to watch the festivities.

I'm constantly thankful I live close by.

So why 4 stars?  I saw a dead duck in the pond and it was emotionally scarring....

I was drifting through Richmond Center looking wan and distressed today, because I needed to buy some clothes. Not just any clothes, either. I needed some work apropro clothes. My part-time, work-at-home research gigs have spoiled me silly, and I found myself brutally underprepared for my first week of work at a new position. But I didn't have a plan of attack!

Enter Plenty (aka Plen+y, I suppose). It caught my eye (as I walked on by), because I was familiar with the store...I had purchased some things from their other locations, but never from this particular one. I was pleased to be greeted immediately by racks of trousers, blouses, and skirts, AND signs that informed me of their 50% off everything sale going on right now.

Needless to say, I went a bit crazy. I started flinging items over my arms willy-nilly in an attempt to finish the task at hand ASAP. A sales associate noticed my burden and asked if he could start a room for me, so that I could continue to rifle manically. It also helped that this store is about a quarter the size of their other locations, eliminating that lost, overwhelmed feeling that I'm prone to. Decent selection of casual and dressier options for the "young, modern working woman" (no, my new job isn't in advertising). Service was there, but sort of indifferent. I didn't mind - I walked away with enough items to keep me semi-presentable for the next few weeks, mitigating any future nightmares about showing up to work in pajamas.

We dined at Grain & Gristle last Saturday night and we were pleasantly surprised. We did a lot of research on different restaurants before we went out that evening and Grain & Gristle seemed to have the best prices and yummiest selections that night.

When we arrived inside the restaurant the lady that greeted us wasn't the friendliest. When we asked approximately how long the wait would be to sit outside (which doesn't seem like an outlandish request, right?) she snapped back with "we don't give out times - just put your name on the list." The man behind the bar wasn't any better. At one point he snapped at us when he asked if we were on the wait-list and we answered yes, instead of stating our name. Kinda strange, but everyone inside seemed to have an "I'm-too-busy" attitude.

We ordered a few drinks, sat there and thought, wow - not the best first impression, I wonder if this place was a mistake?? About 15 minutes later we were seated outside & got very lucky with a super nice waitress. She was very helpful and even made some suggestions on the menu.

We ordered the summer salad with tomatoes, stone fruit and whipped chevre with basil. It was so delicious we wanted to lick the plate clean! Next up was the Fressen pretzel w/ spicy mustard. This was also delicious. The mustard had a strong kick and you could feel the heat rising in your nose. We loved it! 

For entrees we got the Mediterranean sausage with cous cous and yogurt & the burger with a fried egg. We split both & once again wanted to lick our plates when we were finished! We couldn't have loved our food choices more.

I would definitely recommend this place for the food (the beer choices were great, too).

I go to this spot quite often. They serve pre-made taiwanese hot pot (so all your ingredients are in a large bowl). What's the bottom stays lit  to cook your food and will go out at the right time, although you can always ask them to light it out if it gets too steamy. 

They have a menu of about 10 different types of hot pot. My favorite is the curry fish ball. There are spice options as well from mild to "flaming" spicy. Great spot for a cold Day. They also serve side dishes and bubble tea as well. Each hot pot comes with a rice or vermicelli noodles but you can order more if you are feeling hungry (I recommend getting an add on of udon noodles). The hot pots are large enough to share as well and there are vegitarian options.

Overall the service here is quit good and fast considering how busy it gets around lunch and dinner. They don't do split bill at this location though as an FYI but they do take credit.

TIP: come during lunch cause you get a free black or green tea and the hot pot costs less for the same portion that they would serve at dinner!

What an awesome hotel.  The type of place you want to stay when you're treating yourself or treating your significant other.

I've now stayed at the Boulderado (Yelp reviewed 9/2/12) and the St Julien.  Both offer wonderful accommodations, both are walking distance to all cool things downtown Bolder...but you will pay (and get) more from St Julien, if it jives with your budget.

First class service.  You can experience this right when you pull up to the hotel for the first time: the bellman and valet attendants can't do enough to help you.  They even provide concierge worthy suggestions for dinner reservations and lounge locations.

Spacious and inviting lobby area.  People were lounging around reading their books, or sharing cocktails with a group of friends.  Theres a fireplace to sit near and warm yourself in the cold weather.

The bedrooms include the heavenly type bed...and the spa-like bathroom with the luxuriously deep bathtub was a hit with the lady.

Jill's restaurant - did it for room service and breakfast.  Both were delicious.  Meaning, I'd make the effort to eat there even if it wasn't attached to the hotel.

The indoor lap pool was actually one of the few I've seen on hotels that would compel me to take advantage of it (though I did not).  There was an indoor hot tub...and a small gym facility (which I thought was kind of weak).

Unfortunately didn't be a chance to try out the spa, as it was fully booked while we were there...and my slacker self didn't make an appointment in advance.

Got there at around 10:30pm on a Thursday night, after carousing and boozing elsewhere. I had been meaning to try this place since every time I drive by as  it is always crowded / popular.

Seems to stay open a lot later than it's neighbor Verde. I was impressed with the menu and the crowd. Ordered a draft beer (Harpoon UFO draft at five bucks a pop) and hung out and chatted with some semi-regulars.

Went back the next night with a buddy of mine and it was very crowded - perhaps given that it was a Friday night. I really like this place. The crowd is decidedly upscale (as is the decor / ambience). The bartenders are attentive and friendly. There is plenty of space along the bar as well as the standing area adjacent to the bar with a long table /  islandy thing with which to rest drinks on. Great people watching spot with a crowd age rangeing from the mid-to-late twenties on up to late forties-ish.

Have night tried the food yet; however, the menu is indeed a Kaleidoscope of options. Good variety of beer and wine choices as well as a full bar. 

I will definitely strive to make this place my go-to spot since it is oh so very close to the crib.

I just had a great experience at Hudson. The staff were very friendly and willing to help me with an issue that could have been ignored or brushed off. They did not dismiss my request and instead worked to resolve the issue at hand. I am thankful for their consideration and time spent to help me out. 
In addition, I learned that the new owner is someone I've had prior experience with by being a customer at his former food establishments. I trust my meat is in good hands.

First time ordering from Ruchi. Delivery service was fantastic. On time a the delivery driver called to make sure he was in the right place.
Chicken 65 was spot on. Flavorful and spicy.
Aloo daal delicious. Mild was spicy for my palate, but also perfect.
Chicken Tikka Mooshala (sorry if I'm spelling this wrong, I typically eat Indian) was also delicious. Not oily, not overly salty. Unfortunately it was very skimpy on the chicken (not enough for two) and thus the four star rating.
Rice came with the meal, which was perfect. I don't like restaurants that charge for rice.
I will definitely order from here again and will probably try a sit down meal as well.

Stopped here when we came to drop my kid at the University nearby . Parking problem as there is only street parking and the streets are small . 
Small shop, welcoming hosts , very clean , Decent menu with coffee, tea, smoothie varieties . I ordered some lattes and it was good ! They make hot and cold sandwiches and the menu is small but decent variety . The hot caprese panini was very tasty and my husband enjoyed it .  Will definitely recommend folks to stop by if driving through that area .

Went here for brunch after the Race for the Cure...we sat outside, which was great for people watching. The staff was friendly, but a bit overwhelmed by all the business. We got menus and our drinks came quickly, but it took awhile to get cream for one friend's coffee, and sweetener for another friend's ice tea. The food took a very long time, so it was a good thing the staff kept the drinks refilled and kept us up to date on the arrival of our food. it was a beautiful day and we had just walked 5 kilometers, so we were content to sit and talk. When the food came, it was amazing. Three of us had the garden scramble (I had mine with a side of bacon that was big enough to share). It came with fried potatoes. It was soooo good! The other person in our party had the corned beef hash, which she also enjoyed. It. Came with toast that wasn't buttered, though. She had to ask for butter. The table next to us ordered the breakfast burrito, which looked scrumptious. All in all a pleasant experience with good food. I'll be back!

I should have written this review when it was more fresh in my head. I have been to this sushi place a couple of times, and I'm sure I will go again. However, I usually go to the Sushi Train across town. This place is nicer than that on the inside, and well the sushi is just the same - that is to say "normal" in my opinion.  As I recall when we went there my wife had a Groupon or some other deal, and they were happy to accept it. There is a friendly staff which was very kind to my baby.

From the doorway the space appears massive, with an ambiance in contrast with many of the zip code's trendster establishments. Tall, stark walls. Bright lights. Plush arm chairs in front, but a dining room  made up of tables and plastic-backed chairs reminiscent of the small mid-western eateries back home. Dozens of wine bottles in varying states of emptiness sit on one of these tables set against the open kitchen's half wall. The overall feeling is one of uncertainty. But the smiling people, drinks in hand, affirm that yes, it's open. 

Drinks were ordered and brought first. It's the usual progression of things, so why not. We sip, talk, comment, generally lose track of time. Then, after Bek's stared at the bottom of her glass a while, and it seems I'm destined the same, we're asked for our order. Slow. Understandable, but slow. The restaurant is full. Nearly every table and chair taken. Not bad for a weeknight. Doesn't look like they expected it. There's the one waitress, a sous chef and the husband and wife owners. She's cooking, and he's preoccupied with some corner shelving; the waitress scrambling, looking deeply unenthused.

We order food and a refill for Bek. Should've ordered one for me to. More talking, no sipping (for me), more commenting. Now two empty glasses, no food. The owner stops by, gives us his spiel, "Indian food how it's made in India!" Great personality. No food. 

Eventually it comes. Two rotis, representing most of what is available. Chapatis and six bowls of various dishes. I like mine, Bek likes hers. We're happy and decide that we weren't really in any hurry. So, why not.

We leave full.

. This is a favorite spot of a very good friend of mine. Great bread basket (cornbread and biscuits). Menu is clearly southern, but more upscale, defintely a good place to go if you like southern food (I do not) but also enjoy a nice space and presentation, etc. If you really want down home southern cooking in atlanta, you can hit many spots for much cheaper. Menu is somewhat limited in my opinion but I have a laundry list of things I don't like or eat, so it could be just me.

First off, I'd like to say that this is a very nice bar/club!! The staff is very friendly, so were the bouncers. 
My friend and I are from out of state, and we randomly found this bar. We are both happy that we came across the good life bar! It's not full of underage kids trying to get in, and they also had a DJ playing upstairs and downstairs, even if your not into dancing you could sit in a different room away from the music! All three rooms have a full bar! 
Second off, they are a bit pricey so if you are looking for a cheap way out, I would go elsewhere, but if your looking for a classy not so crappy bar to be, then go here!!!

I love Twist. I would say it is my favourite restaurant after the good italian ones (yeah, i'm obsessed with italian food).

If you're going on weekends, just make a reservation a couple of days in advance; this place it's always crowded. 

Food is really good.. i love steamed mussles and calamari fritti. The bread they bring before food? Awesome! I think it's the only place i can find a real italian bread.

Anyway, 4 stars because rules are too strict sometimes. We can sit at the table only when all the people show up and it has to be within 15 minutes. I understand they have a lot of customers, but in a party of 15 people it is "normal" that somebody might be late.

After 800 reviews, they probably don't need another  but I am going to just give a couple tips for the heck of it.

1. Remember to order milk, you'll regret it if you don't once you're downing the fudge icing and need a cold bev to compliment it.
2. Grab a handful of napkins because even with the fork and knife, your hands will get dirty.
3. Share with a friend, these doughnuts are HUGE.

The Black Out was the most delicious, chocolately (if that's a word), fudge-covered doughnut and although I thought I'd be in a chocolate coma after a couple bites, I managed to walk rather than roll back to my car. 

My uncle got the one with the bacon, not sure if I liked the maple doughnut and bacon together but separately, it worked.

The falafel pita is very good.  

The other pitas they serve are also good, but I pretty much always get the falafel.

The teanade is good, though I'd rather pay more to get a larger serving with more ice.

None of their pitas travel well, so plan on eating there for the best experience.  That way you also have a large supply of their spicy green sauce.

So far I've never had a problem finding a free parking place within sight of the food cart. 

It is sort of wheelchair accessible.  No major barriers, but it is in a graveled area about 40 feet from the sidewalk.  No problem if you have someone to help provide motive power or if you are OK on rugged surfaces.

I really like this place.  We came for a late Sunday brunch, and it was still quite busy for so late in the brunch time.  The space is lovely and modern!  I wish the seats were more comfortable, though.  The outside patio seating is all wooden benches/chairs.  The fennel sausage pizza was delicious!  The crust was nice and crisp, no sogginess in the center of the pie (like so many other pizza places).  We also had the brisket hash, which was really tasty and hearty.  On our way out we grabbed a lemon bar and a s'more snowball from the bakeshop.  The lemon bar was much better than the s'more snowball.  I love sweets so I'm sure we'll be back, at least to try other bakeshop goods.

I showed up at 9:30pm on a Friday night and was the last of three sets of patients who all arrived around the same time. Even though they were busy, you wouldn't have known it. I got in right away and was there for two hours tops. I passed the time by watching tv in my own exam room. 


**********UPDATED**********

It's worth noting that this is an ER and will be billed to your insurance as such. My dr. recommended this place after hours when I thought I had influenza. However, this is a trauma center...not an UrgentCare/Emergicare Center. Don't make a costly mistake and visit for a non-trauma issue.

Since I live close to this location, I of course go there out of convenience. But the MOST fun thing about this store, are the closeouts and odd items, marked way down! Think Big Lots, or Dollar Tree, inside of a grocery store. The selection of groceries isn't bad, either, considering it's a small store. The close out browsing takes the sting out of grocery shopping. I only gave it four stars because of the slow check out times. Do not, I repeat, DO NOT go in right after work, especially if you're in a hurry!

It's been a while since I've done a full trip to the Museum, but I did see one of the latest IMAX movies - Journey Into Amazing Caves - and it was pretty cool. I wish I had time to see the museum as well, but it was closing (IMAX runs later than the museum hours on Sundays). 

The film was interesting - and of course visually stunning - especially cool (no pun intended) was the section on Ice Caves. I don't think I'll be caving any time soon - but it's nice to live vicariously!

I couldn't figure out why I kept coming here. 

Obsessively. 

Withstanding the TORTURE it is to come here:
- Cold patio. Warmish upper body, frozen ankles. 
- How the shack has nothing I want.
- The endless, endless, forever-feeling, tap tap tap, watch paint dry, excruciating wait for food...
- Ohhh, pile on some more wait... while intoxicatingly delicious garlic smells permeate your olfactory bulb and seduce your senses sooo baaaddd....
- Faackkk... the swirling thoughts like, "Why don't these fuckers deliver.. Why do I have to come all the way here... You know how hard it is for me to come here...!!"
- More empty-stomach wait. You can feel the hunger scrrrratch the insides of your gut. The lime drinking vinegar only exacerbates the feeling.

So.. what the crap is it about pok pok that got me hooked? Obsessed? Enduring ^that shit up there when I have hugely better and more high leverage things to do?

Is it the lime drinking vinegar that brings me here? (It's good! But no... it can't just be a mere gimmick that turns "tasty" to obsession..)

I was pushing around food in the pok dining room last night, and... I had an Anton Ego moment. 

You know, that one climactic part in Ratatouille where the evil food critic takes a taste of Remy's ratatouille and drops his pen. Dilates his pupils. Whooshes back to his childhood, countryside memories of his delicate countryside mother, cooking a delicate countryside meal... and it pierces away all those years of his wretchedness, and makes him feel human?

Yes! I had that moment! That WHOOSH. An amazing space-time bending whOOOOOsh back to my past. It's the fucking Kaeng Huh Leh. Which has the PRECISE exact flavor, texture, and taste of the only thing my evil filipino grandmother ever produced that lightened the burden of her evilness: Her pork adobo. 

And this revelation poured in both fear and delight. Fear that my grandmother was there. Delight when I realized she wasn't. Then bigger delight when I realized I closed a loop in my mind. I don't ever need to visit my grandma ever again! I realized the only reason why I went is so I could have pork adobo. And now, smacking me in the face in portland oregon, is a better ingriediented, unfathomably delicious, far superior version. 

Kaeng Hung Leh. Fuckin get it. It will change your life. 

I admit, that wasn't the dish that got me obsessed with pok pok. Owe that to Cha ca la vong. They put crack in that dish. Or some sort of people-catnip. 

When you read this: "Catfish marinated in turmeric and sour sticky rice, fried in turmeric oil with scallions and dill, served on rice vermicelli with peanuts, mint and nouc cham. Our stab at the famous dish from La Vong Restaurant in Hanoi, Vietnam." 

Beware. 

Even when you speak or think of it, all the tastebuds from the back of your tongue to the front will long for this, and pollute your brain with a hypnotic "go to pok pok. cha ca la vong. mmm. now." drone. And you'll skip out on your homework, or work-work, or whatever is important, and endure some fucking mean torture (see above), and then... 

Then you have it. 
And its really really good. 
And then its gone cuz pok pok's portions are fucking small.

As a college student, what's not to love about inexpensive, delicious diner food on a Sunday morning? 

Wilson's is filled with charm and the smell of greasy breakfast meats. Arriving at around noon today, parking was a bit of a hassle, but my party of 5 only had to wait about 5-8 minutes before a booth opened up. Certainly one valid complaint is that the booths are small and, while we did manage to fit all 5 people, it was a bit cramped. HOWEVER, bodily comfort notwithstanding, my cheese omelet ($6, with a side of homefries and whole wheat toast) and coffee ($1) were entirely worth it. 

Wilson's provides excellent value and a unique diner experience. The man behind the counter, grill master, and presumably owner, was very charming and made a funny old man joke about our booth of 5 girls ("each one prettier than the next").

I will certainly be back to Wilson's- nothing cures the remnants of a Saturday night like some good ol fashioned eggs, taters and toast.

The food here really is great,  Not subtle or refined, but earthy, with the best ingredients and attractively plated.

Service is the problem.  Not terrible, but it doesn't match the quality (and cost) of the food.  Our waiter did not refill bread without asking, (and then forgot) nor did he pour the wine after the first time.  He visibly changed his attitude from cheery to indifferent when we ordered a modest bottle of wine, appetizer portions  of pasta and only one dessert to share among three people.

The hostess was at best perfunctory- however she did seem new and nervous. If so, she should have been better trained before she started 

Once the service issue is addressed, La Campania gets 5 stars.

We came for the RW menu on Saturday evening at 4:00.  We sat at an outdoor table since it was sunny.  They don't take reservations, but we figured that time of day wouldn't be too busy.  We were right.  I took a peek at the inside - cute interior.

Our server was great.  The menus are available by scanning the bar codes on the tables.  I chose a cocktail to start - the King's Jive made with bourbon, and tasty.  I had a glass of wine later.  For my 3 courses, I started with the Thai Noodle Salad - yummy.  My main was the Salmon Salad, which was a piece of salmon, hummus and salad.  I'm glad I chose the Panna Cotta for dessert - so good and a touch better than the other dessert choice that my husband had, which was the Peach Crumble.

It seems to be a mostly sandwich and pizza joint, very casual.  I'm happy we checked out this new place by the owner of Local Cantina.  Another great addition to German Village!

I had lunch here with my boss after enjoying a quiet dinner here one evening with my girlfriend. Both times have been pretty good so far. The food is surprisingly high quality for a pub, and the pints go down well. There's a decent selection of the more common beers, wines and spirits. 
I think my favourite meal is the Armstrong cheddar and Irish gammon bacon burger. A juicy, beefy patty draped in cheese and bacon, with a load of fixin's. I had a hard time trying to finish the side of fries after wolfing down the burger. I kept nibbling though because the seasoning on the fries is pretty good.

What an awesome discovery during my time in Portland! 

Among the four of us we tried a selection of dishes. I had the southern platter with BBQ tofu, mac & cheese and a selection of veggies. The tofu was fantastic! But it did get a little salty by the end of it which is probably why there was the mac and cheese to go with it. Otherwise that was a bit bland. Another had one of their specials, the falafel burger. A third tried the Ty plate which is a thai inspired dish with tempeh, rice and beans in a peanut sauce. The fourth built her own plate with a coconut curry and stewed greens. I think the table favourite was the coconut curry though. Really tasty. 

The gentleman running the place (I forgot his name!) was great and super helpful. When he found out it was our first time visiting, he gave us a great breakdown of all the dishes and gave selection options when one in my party wanted to build her own plate. He was constantly checking up on us to make sure we were okay. 

I really enjoyed my meal here and definitely will be back the next time I'm in Portland with vegan travel buds.

The service is great! They will tell you all about the menu and each has item. I had the Bangkok duck noodle. Large portion @$18, made for 2 meals. The duck was tender and not greasy. I also had a Cocorita from their drink menu. It was pineapple coconut Margarita. It was tasty and strong. 

Also at our table was the short rib, Bangkok old fashioned (Thai tea with bourbon), lychee mule (Moscow mule but with lychee rice vodka), and several chicken and chrome dishes. No complaints on food except for some uncooked sticky rice. 

Will return. Delicious.

Great people. Great market. Decent lunch. 
I've now been a few times for lunch. First I got the blackened salmon. It was okay. Nothing special. The rice is good. The broccoli is too tough/not cooked enough. This was the case with the broccoli the second time around too. When I had salmon again. I added fries, which were great. But the third time the fries weren't that great. I got the fish and chips. The fish was good (outside of the breading). The corn on the cob was cold. How did it have time to get cold?  Should I try the lobster? Probably. Maybe one day. But I'll probably skip the sides.

Came here for brunch on a drizzly Sunday. The covered seating is not very covered, so if the weather is bad you'd probably be better off ordering to-go. 

Solid food trailer with a very Austin-y feel. They grow their own chives in the drums holding up their covered seating.

I see that other reviews mention half-orders, but I did not see that option on the menu, so I ordered a full order of the Johnny Hash. It was delicious, but definitely too much food for one person. If I make it back again, I will definitely check on the half-order option. A regular portion would be a great affordable breakfast for two, because for around $8 you can get a great brunch portion to share.

I'm glad to have found a good Mexican restaurant in the area because I have been craving for a burrito for quite some time. Which to my delight, they had one on the menu plus countless other options to choose from. 

We ended up getting a Beef Fajita, Chalupas, and a Combo Plate which comes with one enchilada, tamale, taco, beans and a guacamole salad. All were exceptional but our favorites were the fajitas and taco. I like how they pack a lot of ground beef in the taco. You're definitely not eating Taco Bell portion anymore (nor can you compare the two with each other).  

I also really like their salsa here which has that kick of spiciness in it that paired well with the warm tortilla chips. Overall, friendly staff and quick service, we will definitely return in the further to try other items on the menu. Restaurant is spacious and the frozen margaritas definitely hits the spot after a long day.

I was driving through Casselberry and used my Yelp app on my iphone to find this little Greek café. I stopped by for a to-go and the lady who took my order was pleasant and friendly. I decided to try the Gyro which is my barometer for judging Greek restaurants. When I got my sandwich is was HUGE, too big even to hold. I had to eat some of the filling before I could bite into it and even then I couldn't finish the thing. The meat was seasoned well but a bit charred around the edges, otherwise it was delicious. The filling and sauce were both very flavorful. 
The place is fairly small and painted inside like a typical Greek restaurant, Greek themed murals abound. (Why do all Greek places have murals?) If I'm ever on this side of town again I'd stop by, this time to dine in and explore the menu a little more.

The food is good. It is definitely a level above your typical Chinese take-out/delivery spot. The quality is there. Green beans were freshly cut - I know this because as we walked in there was a large basket of green beans with the tips cut off, seemingly left out to dry on towels perhaps. Odd to have where you walk in, but maybe they needed the space to dry them out? We had a shrimp dish, soup, and chicken dish as well, and they were all pretty tasty.

I thought the prices were a little high for what they had, so I wouldn't eat here every day, but if you're craving Chinese food and you're in the area, it's a win for the stomach, and a small dent in the wallet.

I do not eat fish and chips often, but Best fish and chips I have ever had anywhere, but when I am in the mood for comfort seafood, this is my first choice. After I happen to find this place few months ago, Fish and chips have never be the same for me :-). This are, to my experience, the best, most authentic, really British style, fish & chips in the entire Portland area, it is not that close to where I live, and it is hard to find parking, but its is well worth the trip out here if you like the real Fish and Chips, the fish is fried to perfection, not heavy, light, flaky, the fried potatoes are thickly cut, the portions are great and generous,
The first time here I had the battered red snapper and fries, for only $9.50  and it was a big enough portion,the batter was light and crispy, not soggy, and my boyfriend had the large battered cod fish with french fries for only $11.50, amazing! the service is good, and prices are really fair.
Also, it is one of the very few places in the area where they also serve haddock.Once though we waited several minutes before they came to take our order
I also have noticed that ...sometime, rarely, but sometime the fish had a bad aftertaste, too fishy, maybe because they used same oil over and over, to fry it, and the fries can have a plain taste. The dipping sauce is always good tough, even though, they don't give you enough of it even with the large orders. I hope they improve in this!!

This place is good. I ordered the shrimp desfina. Which is a bed of rice topped with shrimp, tomatoes and feta and garlic sauce. It also served with a side salad and bread all for 15.00!!! The food was very good. The potion is decent it's not huge or small it's just right and they gave me like 12 shrimp which made me happy. My only thing is that with the shrimp on top of the rice it was a bit greasy other than that the food was VERY good

G & S Lounge is pretty cool.
its always described as a dive bar, and sure the place has probably never been dusted, but what kind of dive bar has a selection of beer like that. its great, i feel like a kid in a candy store looking at the coolers of all the different beers. i try to make it a point to at least have one beer i haven't had before, and i've been there quite a few times and don't think i've tried them all.
i remember the first few times about being hesitant with the popcorn, but its fine.
things i like
*the awesome selection of bottled beer
*the fact that they keep a freezer full of ice cold glasses that is customer accessible (the freezer next to that weird beach head game)
*the ms pac man table, which has the code on it to turn it into normal pac man... although ms pac man is vastly superior
*the fact there are two jukeboxes
*the lego aircraft carrier over the bar
*lord of the rings pinball
*the fast service

it seems everyone has something to say about jimmy, and i agree with one of the previous reviews that he's just as much a character as leslie, but i think jimmy is really a nice guy. he may seem a little gruff, but he's cool, he's always hustling behind the bar, picking up glasses, restocking the cooler, he usually has help but he pretty much could run that bar by himself even on friday and saturday nights, i don't ever think he takes a night off. he's two dogs are great, and anybody who has dogs as nice as his must be a good guy.

one of the funniest things i think i've seen at a bar was once at the G&S lounge around 7, before it was crowded, he threw an empty beer box on top of a pool table, one of his dogs, the bigger one, hopped up on the pool table and just played with the box, swinging it around and tearing it up with dog barks of joy... i think i even saw jimmy smile, and every time jimmy smiles, an angel gets its wings.

Guava BBQ Burger is delicious.  If you're a fan of good sandwiches and burgers and want to fill up then Pour House is perfect.  Sit outside if you can and enjoy the people-watching.

From a food standpoint though there is a chef behind their bar-assumed food menu.  I would recommend this as a stop especially if you're not optimistic about it. It's a place where you'll be pleasantly surprised and leave fat and happy.

I also recommend going Wednesday night around 7 or 8. There's usually a good group of Winedown Wednesday Wackos who are just letting the party roll.

Randalls is one of the cleanest and friendliest grocery stores in the state.  This one in particular is always cheerful, well stocked and easy to navigate through.
Full disclosure: I used to be a bagger/stocker for Randalls as a teenager, but that was when they were independently owned.  Now they are part of the Safeway corporation, which has some plusses and some minuses.  The biggest plus is they now sell beer and liquor.  Their beer prices always seem to be less expensive than other grocery stores.
My only complaint with Randalls, and this is more a trend now with all grocery stores, is the use of less real checkers.  Self checkout is okay, but I always prefer a real human being.

The best wine spot I have ever been in. But it's also the first using the storage technique that allows sampling without causing the wine to deteriorate. I've heard of a store in San Francisco doing the same thing but haven't been there. So that's the bar. 

About the restaurant. Great service and great personalities in the service staff. The food? Very rich. We found the menu a little limited. We both only found one item we each would order. Both were a little heavy on salt. Good, but not great. I really appreciate chefs who show restraint. We found the food a little heavy handed. I would go back for the wines, but I would watch the menu to see if something changed and then maybe try it again.

I'm happy this is so close to us. I find it odd that many people cannot find decent "Mexican" food in Boston. That's because it's just one stop into Eastie, where nobody would dare go! Get off at Maverick, turn your pretty little pale face 360 degrees and you'll see 4-5 places in the square alone that are equal to or better than (in variety only, quality is about the same) this place.

Do yourself a favor and get pork torta and some papusas.

Stayed here about the same time last year. Really enjoy the property - it's a nice hotel, good location. My only two issues with this hotel:

1. They only have valet parking.
2. There's no pool.

Accommodations are quite nice and the rooms are always clean. I really appreciate, too, that the hotel gives patrons a happy hour at the venue immediately next door (wine, finger foods).

All-in-all I recommend this hotel for anyone staying in the Atlanta area, and wanting to be conveniently located to lots of things to do.

You know what this place has? Vibes for days.

By this point in Portland, most any coffee shop is going to be able to pour a quality shot. They definitely do that here at Push X Pull, and they get bonus points for roasting their own beans from right inside the shop. Every coffee drink I've had here has been awfully good, though I'm somewhat cranky that their only non-dairy alternative is oat milk. I'm an almond milk guy and don't like how many carbs are in oat milk. Then again, I totally destroyed a pizza last night, so maybe I shouldn't be such a raging hypocrite? I digress...

So how's a coffee shop to differentiate themselves? For me it's all about the atmosphere, which Push X Pull has for days. I live for this open and airy shop. The blonde wood and turquoise accents are modern and different than anything I've seen in a Portland coffee shop. That plus the massive walls of windows make this a really lovely environment in which to spend some time. Oh, and they're currently playing Chance the Rapper, so I'm feeling pretty good about the music vibes, too.

This place has been open for a minute and somehow only has 6 reviews? I feel like maybe Push X Pull is still under the radar. Hopefully not TOO under the radar, however. This little corner of PDX is all that much better because of their presence.

Pros: My experience with the customer service at spud.ca has been positive. The processing of my visa update was friendly and convenient and the delivery man never fails to bid a good day. Occasionally there are steal-for-it discounts, and new members for the first few weeks get 5 dollars off their invoice. The groceries are always carefully packaged and frozen items are kept fresh in an ice bag. The plastic bin is also useful to up-cycle your Save-on-Foods and Safeway bags and other recyclable items you forgot to put out for collection in the week. The grocery versatility is also quite appeasing and their website is easy to navigate. 

Cons: Items are generally a few dimes to one or two dollars more expensive than my organic grocery store a few blocks down. Always look for the weekly specials. Some items are over priced. I ordered a package of micro-greens arugula last time and it came in a plastic container barely enough for a single salad topping. The mango I ordered were 40 cents more expensive and 1/3 the size of ones I got from Donald's market. Sometimes the white mushrooms come with brown spots and salad greens are already decaying. 

If you are ready to invest a few extra dollars a week but save the half hour driving and carrying your groceries, and risk a few grocery mishaps, spud.ca is for you. Other wise, I would suggest running to commercial or the farmer's market and save spud.ca for one of those there's really no extra time weeks. I switch between trips to organic markets, green earth organics, and spud.ca to get the best offers. I would suggest not to be too dependent on the site, always have your alternatives.
