I searched for a dog park in the area and saw that the Scioto Dog Park was a 25 minute walk along the river from my place downtown. It was well worth the walk. At 9:30 am on a Monday morning, the park was quiet. Two other well-behaved small dogs came along and my dog had a great time. I was told by other owners that this park is extremely busy on weekends and because of that there are a lot of fights/behavioral issues. However, on weekdays your dog might not have a playmate. The park is very clean and there's two separate areas for large and small breeds. Lots of fun agility equipment to play around with. If you live along the Scioto, check this park out!

Really unique place that serves great coffee, friendly staff and amazing atmosphere.  This place could be a 5 stars but with all those great things there are some flaws.  

Their hours are very inconsistent, they also are never open early enough, when I actually want coffee.  

The owners are the employees,  so I understand that they are trying to make things work, but I hope eventually Propagation will have consistent and earlier hours and then it will truly be a 5 star place.

I was there last week for dinner with my family.. I am a huge fan of spicy food. Take it from an Indian guy.. this food is quite close to the authentic stuff!!  Obviously the gravies are a bit rich & decadent.  Tried the following:

1. Chicken Lollipops (high recommended if you love spicy food)
2. Chicken 65 ( pretty good)
3. Baby corn 65 - quit good. 
4. chicken biryani - also quite good. 

Loved it all.  Next aim is to try out their famous lunch buffet. 

Minor comments: decor can be improved. I think they do serve Beer, but it was not advertised on the menu. Maybe they can expand on it.

I agree with the other reviews.  The exterior rooms here leave a lot to be desired.  However......

We have stayed here several times (just got back today from a quick trip there) and only once was I moderately disappointed.  We usually purchase deals for this hotel through Groupon and have learned to pay close attention to whether or not the deal is for an exterior or interior room.  

Looking to save as much money as possible on this last trip we opted for an exterior room again and crossed our fingers.  The exterior room we got a year ago was in the back of the property.  It was musty.  It was dark.  It felt dingy.  Overall we felt isolated and did get that motel like feel.  This time we lucked out and got an exterior room toward the front of the building (facing Hotel Plaza Blvd) and overall did not get that same feeling as last year.  The room felt cleaner and brighter.  I didn't feel "unsafe" and it wasn't as loud as the rooms toward the back of the building.  

We love how close this hotel is to Downtown Disney (a walk across the street).  My kids love the character breakfast (on select days), even if it is only Goofy and Pluto.  I can't say anything about the pool as I'm not a fan of public pools in general and usually avoid them.

Overall I prefer this hotel MUCH more to the Disney "value resorts" (All Star Resorts) which definitely give me a motel feel and are slightly more expensive.  We are definitely planning on staying again and will try to book only interior rooms from now on.

We came in as a group and have to wait a bit for our table. Reservation recommended.

Ordered the following:
Taiwanese Sausage - this is a must-have
Marinated Appetizers consisted of marinated tofu (delicious), pickled seaweed (nice) and pork intestine (not my choice but was told it was good)
Beef noodle (I didn't have any)
Eggplant with chili and minced pork - this was good
Fried fish cake - a must-have
Stir fried cabbage, fish cake and pork - this was good
Oyster and egg - tasty

This place is awesome.

Parking - the lot in the back is quite tiny so look for street parking if you can

+++++ Unbelievable hand cream - Hemp Hand Protector - Very Dry Skin

At first you may not like the smell but to me it is the smell of blissful relief.

I've been using this hand cream for years and now have my daughters hooked on it too.  It has become a night time ritual for them to get a warm hand massage.

They excitedly wait for me to bring the magic tube.  Made with Hemp seed oil and beeswax this thick base works wonders on their little dry hands.

It is a bit greasy at first so we try not to do anything or touch anything once we've put it on.  I guess that is how it became part of our quiet night time ritual.  

Who wouldn't enjoy having a massage?  We let it do the work and soak in deep while we sleep.

My hands use to look cracked and would sometimes bleed.  I tried all different types of ointments, lotions, body butters from a variety of places and none of them really worked.

One tube of 3.3 oz is $18.50 and you may think this is expensive but a little goes a long long way.  I've had one tube for 2 winters and it is well worth the money.

They just had a holiday sale so I got two tubes free.  My little 1 year old nephew has very bad skin so I am hoping this will help soothe is red chafed chunky legs.

They also have Hemp body cream, chap stick and balm.  I haven't tried these others since the creme works so great.

They have amazing Peppermint foot scrubs, soaks, and cremes too!

This store is in the mall and I haven't found the service to be overwhelming but I also know what I want and buzz in and out.

5 Stars for the products but given the location I'll go with 4 just because going in and out of the mall off route 9 can be a buzz kill.

Talk about a wonderful date night spot.  I had been to Brio in Dallas before but this was our first visit to the Austin location.  We came here on a wim around 6pm on a Saturday.  When we walked in, the place was less then half full and we were seated right away.

We started off with the top shelf margarita and I will say, it was the low point of the meal. It may have had a splash of Patron and next to no flavor.  It just seemed to taste like a watered down strawberry juice. While it was only $8, I still would have expected a little more.  

Luckily, the meal went way up from there.  Starting with the warm bread served to the table, how could you go wrong? It was amazing and I would have been happy stopping there.  Good thing we didn't though.  We proceeded to share the spinach dip which was a massive serving and probably should not be shared with only 2 people.  We then finished with the balsamic, bacon, and chicken ravioli from the specials menu.  They accommodated us nicely by splitting the dish in the kitchen. The pasta melted in your mouth with all of the wonderful flavors.

I can definitely say this meal was filled with every last carb possible and I wouldn't change it for anything.  Don't know if I would come back for bar/drinks but the meal was a solid choice.

This is fast casual Peruvian Latin Food on the run. It's awesome. The portions are perfect. If you're very hungry, the 1/2 chicken lunch plate will do the trick. If you're craving something messier and slightly lighter, try the A lo Pobre Sandwich. Don't confuse this place for the sit-down restaurant Machu Chicken - they're affiliated but not the same place. This place also stole my heart by being one of the only places in Union Square open on Christmas Eve last year. Thanks, guys!

Inspired by memories of a wonderful meal at Panca in Greenwich Village, I was looking for Peruvian fare in Boston and found Ruka. We loved it, though it is more a multicultural tapas bar than a Peruvian restaurant. Don't get me wrong, they can do Peruvian. The prime ribeye cap and char siu chicken anticuchos were, in my wife's whispered voice, "sooo good!" The Japanese and Chinese were also tasty, but for us the anticuchos will long be remembered. Ruka also had a notably friendly and helpful staff. We'll go again.

Two hours before the movie started, I dialed the theater number,

Me: "Hello..is the theater stadium seating?"

Guy: " Oh yes, all our theaters are stadium seating."

Me: "Oh cool! Thank you very much."

I went there, used my free ticket from my Regal Card (Yes I watched too many movies). I walked down to the theater, went to the concessions. I got a medium pop corn and medium soda. The nice lady told me that free refill on the pop corn and also the soda! Wohooo! 

I grabbed my pop corn and soda, walked inside the theater 1 and......... it's not a stadium seating theater! I think the guy got confused, or I'm the one who got confused. All the seats are on flat surface, there's no seat higher than other seats. I prefer stadium seating since I'm such a short person, I don't like to seat behind tall people (no offense talls). Some of the seats in the back have mini tables which is kind of cool. 

The theater is HUGE. I'm very picky when it comes to my seat. I like it to be in the middle and not to far down, not to high up. Anyway, I got my seat since there were hardly anyone in there. I dig the theater, but seriously, this is NOT a stadium seating theater.

Ok I'm a vegetarian, poser, ok watever I like eating veggies more than anything but that doesn't mean I wont pass up a good burger!! 
I walked in and I have to say I loved the place already. Its very inviting! An awesome take on modern and rustic.
Ok back to the burger! So I was reading all the reviews and saw there was such thing as a quinoa burger. Woah! I've had black bean burgers and even shiitaki burgers, so this was a must! and it gets better...... you can do halfsies! as in half quinoa and half meat... sweet! You get the best of both worlds. 

It. was. amazing. 
My suggestion is get the garlic mayo! +grilled mushrooms +grilled onions = BURGEREXPLOSIONSINYOURMOUTH. 

I tried the urban fries and the salt & vinegar fries, wasnt wowd by either and was overly stuffed at the end, not feeling so well. Next time I think i'll prob bag the fries and just go with the delicious burger!

Pretty decent place. Not stroller friendly as the obstacles require you to go up and down steps, which is fine, just giving everyone a heads up. TAKE AN ADDITIONAL 2 BALLS PER PERSON, they will get lost in certain obstacles especially for the little ones. 

Overall we had a blast and we would definitely do it again. 

I don't recall seeing beverages being sold and possibly rightfully so not to get their greenery dirty. 

Only thing I didn't like was the long wait at the cashier line. There's only one register.

I love indian food, i don't eat it quite as much as i want to but i still have had my fair share.  This place is awesome, ambience is typical of an indian food place which is pretty lax in my opinion.  The food more than makes up for it though.  I ordered several dishes and naans for me and two others and there was more than enough food to go around and last for two days of leftovers.  Everything was great and cooked to perfection!  I would have given 5 stars but ambience does alot for me and here i am glad the superb taste of the food took my mind off the decor.

This might sound crazy but the water tasted so good. Idk what they did to it but it was refreshing. I was assuming it was because I drank last night but the others with me said it tasted good. 

Anyway, for starters I ordered the wings, they were just ok. Then I did the 3 meats 3 sides called pit ($26) split between 3 people it was filling and it's so worth it! The three meats I got were ribs, brisket and burnt ends, The sides I got were sweet mash potato, cole slaw, and Brussels sprouts. I liked the ribs the best, the meat fell right off the bone. The burnt ends weren't really burnt or smoked, I thought the brisket was more burnt and tasted better than the burnt ends. The three sauces: gold, hot, and sweet all tasted good. The hot wasn't that spicy but I prefer it to be that way so I can still taste the food. Now on to the sides. I liked the Brussels sprouts; they were not too bitter & just right! The sweet mash potato kinda tasted like mash squash it was just ok. The coleslaw was labeled spicy, but it didn't even have a spicy taste to it just tasted like the generic coleslaw. I enjoyed my time here and would definitely come back!

A small establishment with a large presence, their building is easy to spot from the turnabout as they have a large pyramid-like hat as their roof -- parking is available sometimes on the street, but if that's taken, try behind their bldg. 

If you're a falafel aficionado like I am, you would get excited like I did when approaching their establishment, but it doesn't last. As soon as you walk in, you see the entire kitchen prep area crammed behind a buffet bar and a small table desk. This allowed for some seating inside the location, but you would think they could use the extra space to prepare their menu items.

Instead, what you get is a quickly made falafel that was churned from an assembly line of ingredients. Don't expect a Chipotle-style experience, as this assembly line has a mish mosh of ingredients, half of which have strong Asian roots. The ingredients are fresh, but they are the basics and nothing more. 

The location is confused with its menu items, and this is evident when you see their name does not match up with the focus of their offerings. It's more of an Asian-Mediterranean fusion, which is cool and all, but the name "Falafel King" is misleading.

As for the food taste, their falafel needs improvement but it is a solid sandwich for its worth. This location does the bare minimum when it comes to respecting what it could be, and I think if they tweak some of their current offerings and add a few more, it could make their falafel sandwiches something worth boasting about. 

Oh well. It's too bad, they have great potential with that location to make killer profits. Overall, good food but their poor execution is holding them back from being a memorable eatery. Instead, they seem bland and blend into the mix of food offerings nearby.

 Message to owner: Need help? Consult with me, I have clear ideas that will improve your customer experience and loyalty.

Made a reservation and used a Gilt City coupon for 4 people for a Saturday brunch. It included one drink per person, one entrée per person, and four sides, all for around $70 I believe. What a deal omg. But if even without the coupon the dishes range between $11-15 and sides are optional since the plates are already pretty large. We all ordered different entrées from the house smoked pastrami hash to the spinach and herbed goat cheese omelette and everyone enjoyed their dishes. They make changes to their menu occasionally since the lox bagel I had when we came (mid-July, sorry super late post...) isn't on the menu anymore even though I thought it was tasty too.

Our waitress was very helpful with recommendations and overall had a really great attitude which made my morning even better. The restaurant is right across the street from the Broadway T stop so very easy to get there by T.

My bid was accepted by Priceline which I resorted to when I saw the high rates of downtown Austin hotels. I travel on the cheap a lot so I know I'm not getting luxury accommodations and The Holiday Inn provided good value at under $80/night. It's not really in the hub of activity in downtown Austin but it was only a cheap $5 taxi ride away. The hotel provides free shuttle service from/to the airport and you can even schedule a ride to downtown Austin...all complimentary. Don't forget to tip your friendly driver though! This is great for someone like me who travels on the cheap and tries to use public transit as much as possible. Rooms were clean and provided standard accommodations. I hardly spend time at the hotels I'm at...only use them for shower and place to sleep. Lotsa airline folks (pilots, attendants) stay here so it's a good sign of value.

This is the best dining you will have at the Walt Disney Resort (if you like or are willing to try Indian food). Nestled within the Animal Kingdom Resort, you can watch zebras, giraffes and more animals as you dine, courtesy of the windows that look out into their habitat.

The menu is Indian -- we started with the potato pea samosas (spicy and tasty). The Bread Service is pretty amazing. A choice of 3 breads to choose from (naan, roti, etc) and 9 dips. The breads were very tasty but not 100% authentic tasting but close enough. We opted for our main course to be Butter Chicken and Spicy Shrimp with jasmine rice. All cooked to perfection.

Items marked spicy really are, so make a note of that when ordering. 

The service was super slow but I think the fine dining places at Disney do that for the experience. If you want quick service go to a burger place in the park (although that is not guaranteed either!)

Count on always having a good time at O'shucks!! This is a total dive bar that will easily make you a regular and be happy to see you again. There's a room full of billiard tables and then in the main room it's karaoke from 9pm to close EVERY SINGLE NIGHT! My favorite hosts are Bowman and Sean. They always make it fun and everyone gets a shot to sing. The book of available songs is massive; it'll be hard not to find something you want to sing. Prices are great and they offer a hospitality discount. The bathrooms aren't always spotless and expect to smell like smoke when you go home but at least you had a great time! And don't forget nickel beers on Wednesday's!

Like any great park or public center it is mostly magical based on the people who are interacting within it's boundaries.  This is a very blank slate kind of space.  Which is a big factor in how much I love it.

Don't get me wrong, there's one of our most charming Starbucks on the block, as well as an amazing array of steps which make you lovingly hope that someone doesn't try to enforce handrail codes someday, an amazing water feature and the visitor's center.  But where the magic comes in is on a nice day during lunch, or Flicks on the Bricks events and other things that bring people together in this massive city center open space.  I for one am glad Portland set aside some of these places early on as infill has already taken so many amazing spaces away.  It's important to preserve some of them and know they all have social value.

Obviously this is an oven of a space on a hot sunny day, but it's Portland so most of our time is lovely... shhhh, don't tell the tourists that ;)  If our secret gets out more folks will want to live here.

It's a nice break from what "normal" folks do downtown with lots of shopping and things to do around.  Take a moment and just enjoy watching those folks from a great perch here... on the bricks.

I moved it to Lumina apartments from Northern California almost a year ago. I love the location. I have a beautiful view from my balcony to an open field where I can watch horses run, I have a fabulous fireplace and a washer and dryer. The community has a lot to offer such as a dog spa which I absolutely love, indoor and outdoor pool which my grandkids get a lot of use out of, a weight room, A playground and a fabulous dog area. The apartments are very up-to-date and if anything does go wrong maintenance usually comes out right away. The girls in the office are very helpful and always very sweet. I Enjoy it enough here that I just re-signed another year lease.

Came here via Scoutmob (50% up to $20 off), not that it did much damage to our final bill.

Super trendy / kinda noisy / cool date spot sort of place. Ya know how it is. So that being said, this restaurant is kinda on the small side.. not a good place for a group.

As with many other sushi places, they provide for you a list of all the sushi rolls / sashimi that they have, and you have to write in the quantity of each one that you want. On the average, I'd say that each roll will set you back about $10 (6-8 pieces per roll). So we settled on four different rolls, plus this sweet potato thingy (that's cause we were craving some tempura!). Also ordered a couple of bowls of miso soup, and a sparkling sake to share. 

Sparkling sake - I've only had warm sake before, so this was interesting! Surprisingly tasted very refreshing and was enjoyable. A 250 ml bottle cost $14 HOWEVER, we were there on a Sunday, and our server somehow forgot to mention that they have a BOGO hot sake deal on Sundays. Uhh, not cool. 

Miso soup - I guess I'm supposed to be a miso soup pro cause I'm Asian or whatever... so yes, the miso soup was quite good. However, they failed because I found all of TWO little tofu cubes in my soup (last time I checked, H Mart sells tofu for pretty darn cheap), and also because they must not know that real Asians like to have their soup along with their meal, not before as an appetizer (that's a white people thing). 

Sushi rolls - All excellent! Fish was very, very fresh - could taste it melting in my mouth! Oh, and it turns out that the "sweet potato thingy" that I ordered earlier was a sushi roll, not tempura. I'm not sure how the idea of a making sweet potato into sushi came about, cause it sure tasted... strange. Don't get it, even though it's only $5.

Tempura - well, the sweet potato was not a tempura, so we ended up ordering some extra. Comes with 3 pieces of shrimp tempura, and 3 pieces of veggie tempura. Nothing special, just the standard stuff.

So a couple of mini blunders here and there reduced it to 4 stars. Really, I wanted to give 5... our server (Kate E) was very attentive to us (pluss her super cuteness didn't hurt!), and overall I had a great experience.

Got the classic elote, hot cheeto elote, hot cheeto fries, spicy watermelon, mangonada, strawberry limeade, and peach blossom. I know way too much but wanted to try it all. 

Classic elote and hot cheeto one were both good, only thing I would do differently is ask for less cheese. Way too much for me but I just scraped it off. Hot cheeto fries were good too. I feel like you should have one or more toppings to add to it as well tho. The presentations for all of these were all very nice. 

My favorite was the spicy watermelon and mangonada. So fresh and delicious. Love how they add the chunks of fruit in your drink. The strawberry limeade is very refreshing as well. The peach blossom had a strange aftertaste to it. Tasted a little syrupi? Irk what it was overall I'd be back! I gotta try their popcorn chicken. And chicharrones next time.

I would've given Truluck's 5 stars were it not for the fact that I'm hardly ever able to actually dine here.  Trulucks has set up their system to discourage solo dining for whatever reason.  If you go to their website or their open table site, there is effectively no option for reservations for 1.  You can only reserve a table for 2 or more people.  If you try and reserve a table for 1, you'll get options weeks into the future at inconvenient times like 5:45 PM. 

I'll often walk in and ask for a table only to be ushered into the first-come-first-serve lounge area.  That's all well and good, but I walk into the lounge and realize there's 0 seating available.  That's the point where I walk right out of the restaurant and head over to Fleming's or Jasper's in the domain.  I eat out a lot and I try to eat at Trlucks a lot but I just don't get the opportunity.  On rare occasion I'll walk in at a reasonable time and they'll be able to seat me right away or they'll give me a 10-15 minute waiting time which is perfectly fine.  

I can't tell you how many times I'm craving Truluck's only to think "Well, will they really be able to seat me?  Nah.  Let's go to Fleming's or Jasper's or Driskill or Carillon instead."  It's just part of their culture I suppose.   I just wish they would have reservations available for solo diners on open table.  

Other than that, the food is good.  I love their parmesan mashed potatoes and they make a pretty good filet.  Their crab cakes are pretty pedestrian.  I think Bartlett's does crab cakes the best in Austin.  Their bread is excellent.  It comes to the table freshly baked, warm, and moist.

Visited 8/11/19  What is a great ending to a Birthday Weekend for a Shopaholic?  Shopping! Duh!  Who doesn't love Marshall's? I would love it even more if it was more clean and organized. But  I understand that it is the Eve of the First Day of School for man Major School Districts. However the Store was not packed with people and I can appreciate that. 

Options- The options here are great from clothing to home items 

Makeup-  I love Makeup in general but the options here were great the affordable prices for high end makeup like Bobby Brown and  NARS brands your would find at Sophora in Marshall's PERFECT

Customer Service- The Customer Service was great, the Ladies at Customer Services were very helpful and was very pleasant. 

If and when I am in the area I plan to return to this location .

This place was great. Centrally located within walking distance to a number of good restaurants. The staff was friendly and helpful directing my colleague and I to places to eat or get a drink. I didn't try the on site spot "The Original" partly because of the mixed reviews and partly to get out of the hotel and walk around. Overnight parking is steep at $30 but that's life in the big city. The room was comfortable and clean. Only reason it's not getting five stars is the lack of a tub in the bathroom. I wanted a soak and all I got was clean.

My husband recently took me here for my 30th birthday and it surpassed expectations.  It was the middle of the week, a Wednesday night, so you do not expect the top service or chef to be in the kitchen.  However, the meal was flawless.  They had our reservation from open table and figured out exactly who I was since my husband arrived before me and sent us upstairs promptly to get our table.  We ordered a glass of prosecco to start and it was delicious and served promptly.  My appetizer, the fried artichokes, was perfect.  The batter was light enough not to overpower the artichokes and the aioli was a perfect compliment.  My husband's barbajuans were also delicious but I preferred the artichokes.  Our server was very attentive and there was always someone right there to bring the next plate or remove the old one.  Then came our entrees.  My husband had the pork special with a piece of pork presented in an artful way and some pork belly to accompany it.  I didn't taste it since I don't eat pork, but he enjoyed it immensely.  He particularly liked the pork belly.  I had the Beef Daube with Mashed Potatoes and we shared a side of the Broccoli with Garlic.  My beef was perfectly cooked, it was fork tender and the mashed potatoes were an excellent pairing with the meat and the sauce.  The broccoli was done perfectly and the most delicious broccoli I have tasted.  I couldn't stop eating it.  I do like my mashed potatoes with a bit more oomph, these were very light and thin and I prefer mine to be more solid.  The taste was very good, however.  We did not taste the desserts because we had birthday cake waiting at home, but we will be back for another special occasion and before that for the bar menu and to sample the desserts.  The decor was very classic with one exception we noticed, the ceramic beehive shapes in many colors above the fireplace in the dining room.

After a couple of amazing meals and dining experiences at Daddy Pok Pok across the street it was a pleasure to find, after moving back to town, that there was a new type of Pok Pok experience and without the crowds. The Soda Lounge is exactly what I was looking for. The same amazing food in a larger, more spacious setting. We had numerous selections for the menu including the famous sticky wings and was impressed yet again. The Thai stylings of owner Andy Ricker are to continue being a Portland staple for many years to come.

Solid food! But in my opinion, was not memorable. 

We came on a Sunday afternoon for brunch and the wait was about an hour. The decor inside was nice and modern. Tasty N Son's brunch menu has a something for everybody type of vibe and ranges from traditional breakfasts, to sandwiches, and fusion foods. They serve their food family style, meaning that the food will be served once its out the kitchen as opposed to serving the entire table at once. I am used to eating family style, though the portions are not what I consider family style. They are individual portions and on the smaller side.

Burmese Red Pork stew - Just okay. It was a braised sweet pork served over a bed of white steamed rice and topped with an egg both ways (fried and boiled). Having grown up eating Burmese cuisine, there was nothing reminiscent of Burmese flavors and spices. The marinated boiled egg with the sweet pork reminded me more of the Taiwanese pork rice dish. 

Breakfast Board - Good! I liked the simplicity of the ingredients that all came together. Awesome bread, crostini, boiled eggs, pate, bacon, and lebneh. 

Shakshuka - Okay. Nice tomato flavor bubbling together with eggs. It is enjoyed by dipping some bread into the sauce.

This place is amaze-balls! The owners are so friendly and make us feel so welcomed every time we go. Their shrimp and crab leg combo is delish and so are the corn and potatoes that accompany it. Since I'm not a fan of spicy, I stick to garlic style. be sure to order at least 3 loaves of their French bread ( baked to order and always warm) so that you can soak up all the juices in the bottom of the pan. The portions are hearty enough to split with 3. One of my faves in the city.

Great, little cramped place that felt like we were in an underground dining hall, but the service was good and the food creative.  The wings - the most popular item - are very good.  I ordered them spicy and found that the build up of heat in my mouth was almost too much.  I also had an order of the coconut milk corn on the cob which was a nice balance to the hot wings.  Overall a solid experience.  I wish I had ventured further with the menu - but was full quickly.

I used to come for dinner at Jardin Corona and always was very satisfied.  Great service, yummy food.  I just heard they are serving breakfast, and decided to try it out.  I was disappointed.   I received a very large plate of chorizo and eggs, with potatoes and beans, however, the flavors were very so - so.  I left most of my food, as it was not so yummy.  It's even hard to describe what was wrong - kind of nothing, but nothing good either.  I will rate my breakfast as one star, but dinner as five.  Since I've been coming here  for years for dinner and was always happy, I am putting a total of 4 stars.  And staff here is very hard working, always smiling, and very helpful.

Want to beat the touristy area? This is the place for you. It's currently in the middle of a cow pasture!! Plenty of parking,too. The place was not very crowded,but it was a weeknight. We were told it could be an hour wait and I was aware that if the people in the golf bay before us wanted to extend their time, it's an option. No worries,off to the bar/ grill we went!!! We were immediately greeted by Yogi! He was very nice, attentive and genuinely seemed happy to be there!! I loved that!! We ordered cocktails and a plate of nachos oh, they came out relatively quick and then we ordered tacos a BYOB burger and a black and blue cheese burger! Everything was great! I was really surprised by how good the food was because it was very reasonably priced as well. I thought we would get a little bit less but we did not I was pleasantly surprised. Now for the reason for only four stars. there seems to be a lot of staff and a lot of empty bays when we finally got outside, so I'm wondering why we had to wait over an hour when they were plenty of bays, and once we got into our Bay we had some technical difficulties that ate up our time and we were not offered to have that replenished. We had an idea of the concept but the variations in games were not explain to us very clearly and before we knew it our game has started. We still had a great time even though our scores were not being kept properly but we weren't there for scores we were there for the fun and we had it! We will be back.

In town from San Diego, and tired from a long day of walking around the city, we decided to out the Union Oyster House for some good seafood, a nice lunch break, and even a bit more city history while we were at it.

Yum!  Didn't know that the way to eat chowder was with cornbread, but by God, they're on to somethin'!  The cornbread is outstanding, as is the fish chowder, and, of course, the clam chowder.  Oysters were also fresh and tasty, and the raw horseradish was a nice touch.

Our server was fun, efficient, and great at keeping 5 full tables happy at rush hour lunch time.  Reasonable prices, good selection of beer, and tasty food.  Thanks for the memories!

Oh, and the "Freedom Trail" is mapped out on the wall of the front dining room with artistic dioramas - kinda cool!

This place is everything the reviews said it was.We arrived in Atlanta on Sunday and I resigned myself that the place might be closed. No worries I walked around the food court to locate other great spot, I wanted to try during our stay.  Well Monday came and I get to the place only to find a sign saying they would be open tomorrow and that we should enjoy the solar eclipse. What the flick!?! Thanks to yelp I went to the Noodle shop.4 thumbs up.
Okay so finally Tuesday YES these pies are all that. And the price is reasonable. We first  tried the Thai chicken and the spinach and feta cheese both were great, and the  crust was flakey.
We went back the next day and tried the tomato and mozzarella cheese which we wished we got two of. The beef steak onr was good but the texture was not a hit with the wife. We will be going back and hopeful taking a few back to NY with us.
Heard there was an eclipse party hope all the staff was invited and enjoyed their day off?

I'm writing this review as a traveler who primarily connects through ATL and has only had to deal with arrival/departure here one time. If given the choice of connecting through ATL and several
other airports, I will choose ATL. It's generally a very clean airport (restrooms included) that is fairly easy to get around by either walking or talking the underground train. I typically take the 5-10 minute walk between terminals, but the trains come often and are easily accessible. Food options here are above average with pretty good prices for airport food. The one time I had to go through security it was pretty fast and efficient using TSA pre-check. They were opening new lanes to accommodate the number of people moving through.

A real pleasant surprise.  I've driven past here so many times and never gone in.  I buy most of my music from various L5P stores.  But after calling all of them and asking for a specific CD which no one had I was pleased that Decatur CD a copy and held it for me.  They don't carry all of the genres I'm normally looking for but they do have a good range of CDs, records, books and DVDs .  It seemed that they had all the garage vinyl re issues I'd pined over for years.  The staff were super friendly, almost too friendly.  Another plus, they have a parking lot and stay open until 9pm.  They weren't on my list for finding music but now they're definitely in the rotation.

So glad I decided to give this place a try! I ordered the pastrami/corned beef combo sandwich and it was mouth watering good! The meat was perfect and then topped with cheese, coleslaw, and Russian dressing on light rye bread! I also ordered a side of French fries ($4.95) and a drink. The French fries were steak fries and had a corse salt on them, perhaps sea salt?! They were equally delicious! I only knocked off 1 star for the price! The food is very tasty and service is fast (you order and pay and they give it to you right away) for the sandwich, fries and a drink my total was almost $22 that's a bit pricy for lunch, however the portions are big, so I would recommend splitting! All in all a great experience and I will be back! Just not too often as it is again quite pricy.

Pretty great! Disclaimer -  not an expert in BBQ but had a few Texas friends that were with me note that it was notably better than their experience at Sweet Cheeks. 

We went in a party of 6 for a birthday celebration. The waitress handled our order for food/drinks nicely (though sometimes she was hard to flag down... especially when we were trying to pay the check).

I had the burnt ends plate with 2 sides (included): cornbread (yum!) and collards/bacon (meh). Friends had good reviews for the mac and cheese. The waitress was knowledgeable enough in the beer selection to recommend a sour beer, which she kindly brought a sample of before asking if I wanted to commit to a full pint. (Lost Nation Gose).

Overall I enjoyed it, I would come back but perhaps just on special occasions since the price is high (but not abnormal for Kendall Square ranges). Sandwiches around closer to $12, plates around $18-20 with drinks (that I can recall) in the ballpark of $10/pint.

Went looking for coffee and a breakfast sandwich this morning, and the long line of contractors and police officers suggested this place would be legit. Loved the combo of typical greasy spoon choices (fried or scrambled eggs, American cheese) and Irish touches (want that with Irish sausage? brown sauce?).

Didn't try the baked goods, but had an impressive-looking selection of breads, pies (many flavors), and pastries. Scones come in raisin and cranberry, but also treacle and rock sugar (!). Small shelf of Irish groceries (salad cream, mushy peas), candy, and deli selections (black and white pudding, Irish bacon). Local flavor emphasized by the patron behind me who ordered tea and porridge with a very Irish accent.

My husband couldn't resist checking out the day-old pastries on the way out, so we left with a big bag of bargain hot cross buns and scones.

I've always been very overwhelmed by Jordans. It's like a casino - kitschy themes, in-house restaurants, no windows, no clocks - and it's nearly impossible to find the exit once you get fifty feet inside. But we needed new furniture and were striking out elsewhere, so decided to give Jordans a try. We were pleasantly surprised. The salesguy, Sean, was helpful, patient, not at all pushy. He didn't pressure us in the least and we were so thankful for it, particularly after being hounded by salespeople at all the other stores. We were able to find some nice stuff in our price range and style and the purchase process was painless. While it is still an overwhelming place, Sean helped to make it manageable and we left feeling great about our purchase.

With a get-together on the horizon, I needed great pizza and I needed it fast. I turned to my ever faithful buddy Yelp, and I was not at all disappointed.

After procuring sixty dollars worth of pizza for this shindig, I didn't know what to expect. We ordered a variety- even ordered a garden salad for one of our less meat-friendly friends.  All told, we got three large pizzas (one specialty) and a bunch of little add-ons. 

CRUST. FLAVORS.  That added touch makes a big difference.  Their pepperonis are perfect - can't really describe them, just little and bubbly.

Really solid pizza, delish breadsticks, and even the salad was great.  If you are going to order pizza, skip the big chains - Pizza Paradise is a great bet.

Omg so this CVS had all things Charlie Brown for Christmas but kind of pricy, so I had every intention on coming back for after Christmas half off sales. I had already been to one CVS the day before & all I found was the leg from "A Christmas Story". But this location had so much leftover Christmas stuff! I was like a kid at a candy store!lol I got as much of it that I could afford but had I had more money I would have cleared them out.
The staff wasn't the nicest well the gentlemen wasn't I should say. No customer service skills at all. The lady  that was there however scanned something while we were still  looking to get a price for us. 
I only go to this location because it is close to my mother's house but other than that I would never come to this specific location but I am glad I did just for the simple fact of all the cute Christmas stuff.

This coffee shop is located in the Atlanta Tech Village. Entrance to the parking garage is right before Lenox on Piedmont and can be easy to miss if you're trying to find this place for the first time. Their parking garage has free parking for 30 minutes and paid parking after that. The coffee shop does validate parking so remember to ask them about it if you parked in their garage.

Coffee here is good and has a great atmosphere for hanging out or doing some reading.

Was on a trip to Vancouver, and Finch's was on my list of places to check out. We walked into a old fashion looking cafe that was nicely designed as so. I ordered the Prosciutto baguette while my girlfriend got the avocado one. These sandwiches are absolutely stuffed with ingredients, and its impossible to eat properly. This is certainly a good thing, but each bite makes stuff squirt out at all angles. The sandwiches were definitely good as all other posters have pointed out. The coffee was pretty good too!

It is very difficult to find this place since you cannot see it from the street and the sign is small.  So you really need to know where you are going before you go.  I headed to Five Bites on a weekday to use a Groupon, since I knew I didn't have to call ahead to redeem a Groupon on a weekday.  However, I should have called ahead anyway, as some of the flavors I wanted were not in stock.  I had gone to their web site and written down which cupcakes I wanted, but at least half of them were not in stock.  :(  I do have to say, however, that the woman working at the store was very friendly and helpful.  The real reason I am giving this place 4 stars is that I thought the cupcakes were unbelievably delicious!  The cake itself was very dense, which I liked.  The red velvet was the only "flop."  Otherwise, all other flavors I tried were delicious.  But if you want specific flavors I'd call ahead to make sure they have them.

I went here for Christmas brunch.  I was excited that there was a place that was open, and that they offered a couple of vegan options.  They were packed and they offered something for everyone.  The ambiance is quirky and fun.  The service was on the slow side, but that can be expected when there aren't many businesses open for Christmas day.  My vegan hash consisted of sweet potatoes, apples, arugula, and it was good, but I'm thinking maybe I should have tried the savory crepes instead.  I was there with a mixed group, a vegetarian that got the eggs benedict and an Omni that got eggs and bacon.  For some reason, we thought toast came with her meal, but sadly when we mentioned it, the waitress brought the toast, but we were charged $2 for the side of toast.
I would come back to try their regular menu and see what vegan dishes they have.

Was meant to go to Olive Garden but the wait time was too long so ended up here. We were seated right away and the kids were promptly given activity sheet and crayons. 

The kids menu is great. For less than $10 you can either get a cheeseburger/steak/tenders accompanied with a side, fruit and drink. 

I shared an entree with another person along with a side and that was plenty. 

The wings are worth trying as well as the fried pickles. The onion rings were pretty good too. 

Service was very good. Our waitress was friendly and helpful!

Big Peter is my homie. Don't personally know him, but his (or her) pizzas sure are good!
The pizzas are made with a chewy crust and a real good tasting cheese. These are "Italian Style" pies, but not much like the "North End" or New York style of pies. Lots of different toppings (always love the pepperoni) but you might even want to try margarita-no sauce with fresh tomatoes feta, mozzerella and tons of garlic. 
They have great deals here-2 medium one topping pies for $12 and 2 large one topping pies for $14. Oh yeah, they also offer the biggest pizza around-a 28 inch beast. This will feed a whole bunch of hungry chaps. 
They do offer other sub shop style items, but I haven't tried anything else besides a chicken kabob salad-which was really good. I do hear that their roast beef sandwiches are proper. 
Their location can make deliveries take a little longer if you are on the other side of town, but it's worth the wait once those lovely pizza boxes complete with discount coupons arrive.

Ok so I am a fan of cheap and tacos, and this place NAILS both. The tacos here are awesome. The place is small and basically like a house, and when I was there, there was only one other guy picking up a to-go order, and two people sitting at another table.

You walk in and immediately order at the front, no menus to look at, just the chalkboard style, and then they bring you your food and any additional sauce you may want. I recommend the tomatillo! (The green one)

This place is great, if you are in the area and want taco's I'd go here, there are definitely better taco's out there, but this place will definitely take care of your taco needs!

Momma Goldberg's!! Yes!! If you are looking for a fantastic sub shop for reasonable prices then look no further! It's a bit of trouble living upstairs from such a great sandwich shop! My personal favorite is the pastrami sandwich you can get a combo with chips and a drink as well! On my days of not wanting any carbs I would indulge in the fresh salads! They are never really busy and the wait times for your food are always fast! They do have dine in options with limited amount of space... The facility itself is always kept clean with very professional staff me members working which we all know enhances the overall experience! Now for those of you who do not find a parking spot right in front may struggle finding a spot but if you live in midtown you know how the parking can be! Walking here would be best!

So, I have mixed feelings about this place. Whenever I come here I am overwhelmed by the smell. I think it's the fact that they serve food and beer in the dark but have carpeting. The stale beer smell is nauseating.
However, I got over this the second time I visited. The first time I made the mistake of A.) not ordering alcohol B.) went on a super crowded night.
Second time around we waited till the movie was no longer sold-out nightly, and I ordered the grasshopper milkshake, which has alcohol.
The alcohol will make you forget the smell of stale beer on carpet and fewer people means I didn't have to strain to hear over my neighbors annoyingly crunching away at nachos, of all things.
Anyway, go when it's deserted and get a milkshake.

We are local-ish, from Cedar Park/Leander. 

Headed down here for an evening with some girls.  After a day at the W pool (because we got massages there) we wished we had hung at this pool instead.  Really pretty outdoor area. 

We arrived to check in at 5ish- and were greeted with a complimentary glass of wine.  Nice touch.  The room was nice, the restaurant had a great breakfast, and overall a great night. 

4 stars because the Valet is $49 per vehicle....which for Austin is STEEP.  We didn't in and out once, so literally we paid $49 for 18 hours. Pretty crazy.

I was next door buying a magazine at the Inventory Stockroom and passed by Sea Monstr along the way. The storekeep's coworker is a regular here and recommended I give it a try. 

By the time I sat down (5 pm), there wasn't much of a raw selection in the display case- which is weird considering how early in the day it was. I originally wanted their Uni/Ikura bowl (sea urchin & salmon roe, a steal at $13.50), but was told they don't serve uni when it's off season. Fair enough. 

I ordered the Chirashi Don instead and was pleased to see the unconventional presentation of the dish. The sashimi were cut into bite sizes and dotted with salmon roe and small slices of tamago (sushi omelet). The slices were layered in a haphazard way, reminiscent of a godzilla-esque sea monster on a rampage- or maybe that's just me. 

The sashimi is fresh, and according to the menu the establishment uses the "finest locally sourced seafood". 

The service was efficient, and I like how Sea Monstr serves water that has been distilled using equipment provided by Vivreau Pure Water- hence the specially designed bottles they serve water with. 

The decoration is simple- apart form a wreath of Sapporo beer cans hanging on a brick wall, way past Christmas but still pretty cool. 

Overall, it was a fun experience. A chirashi don for $12.50 is already good value! I'll be back to check out their rolls, and to see whether they are better stocked on other days.

I had the Melanzane Pizza tonight. The crust was great - crunchy and tasty! It tasted a lot like it came out of a coal oven! The toppings were also great! 
 
I would definitely order from here again.
 
If you're a fan of Angela's Coal Fired Pizza on Rt. 1, try this place. And they deliver!

Edit: I tried it again the next day with a spouse on the way out of town for business, I didn't see the use in cooking for one. I ordered the margarita and the pollo. It was just as good as the night before! This place is absolutely worth checking out! I can't wait to try one of their meals, like the grilled chicken, or maybe one of their pastas!

I went for the first time two days ago and I can say it is very cute and cozy.  This is a great place to go on a date.  The food was great.  You have to try the red velvet waffles and chicken and my friends say the salmon is outstanding.  Although I dint think it's fresh salmon.  The drinks were great too.  What a great new place we've discovered on Edgewood.  The prices are a little too high for this this type of place.  The food was good but not 5 star good.  My ticket for myself (my meal and two drinks was $47). Well at least the server was great eye candy and professional.

Why 4-stars? Because it's a dollar donation to enter and a small gallery that you can quickly browse and enjoy some art before you are on your way. The staff are very kind as well. 

I admit, I was not a fan of the current exhibit...but hey, everyone likes different kind of art and the exhibits change over time, so don't let my opinion stop you!

This is also located next to that famous tea house, so have a meal + tea, then browse some art and walk a bit to burn off calories!

BOKX 109...the posh, secret underground restaurant at the Hotel Indigo.  Not really, but this place kinda has that speakeasy vibe.  Probably because it is situated in the lower level of the hotel, and only accessible by the hotel elevator versus an outside door.

Definitely upscale.  Definitely not jeans and T-shirt.  I was only here for a drink but took a look at the menu.  It will set you back a few bucks.  The type of place where you'll spend $60 on a steak.  Comparable to a Del Frisco's.   

Not the type of place I'd associate with a mid-tier hotel, but I think it attracts the locals more than the hotel guests anyways.

A perfectly good "middle of the pack" dinner option straddling the expensive Back Bay and the more foodie-friendly South End, without being a boring bar. The portions were quite good, and we were able to be seated without a wait on a weekday. The fries were delicious; my dining partner and I split the mussels as an appetizer, which were delectable with delicious bread. I ordered the burger without a bun, and while it's probably one of the more expensive burgers out there (adding "extras" such as the egg, etc are additional costs on top of the base cost of $14). We had a pleasant dinner and were easily able to catch up in a non-stuffy restaurant.

My husband and I went to ChenZ early-evening today, and really enjoyed it.

There were so many choices that sounded very tasty and interesting, we had trouble deciding what to get.

The service was great... food and hot pot concept thoroughly explained, water glasses kept full, very pleasant, attentive and prompt.  The young lady that served us was quite helpful with food recommendations and sauce choices.

We tried the sesame pockets appetizer.  The spiced pork, sesame pastry and cilantro were a great flavor combination.  All gone quickly, and plenty to share.  We'll try the onion crepes or lamb skewers on our next visit.  Or might get more adventurous and try the jelly fish salad.

We tried the hot pot, and will definitely go back to try some of their noodle dishes.  For our hot pot (ChenZ had about 40 items on the hot pot menu from which to choose), we chose the tomato broth and then lamb, chicken, quail eggs, shitake mushrooms and baby bok choy.  The broth came out simmering hot in its hot pot, and we were ready to go.  The tomato broth was a very pleasing combination of delicate, yet very fragrant and flavorful.

The lamb and chicken looked, smelled and tasted fresh, as did our veggies and the quail eggs.  Once all were simmered together in the hot pot, the combination of those together with the tomato broth was a delight to enjoy!  Everything we got was fresh, of good quality, and nicely presented.

Also, the restaurant and ladies' room were absolutely squeaky clean.

I do notice a good deal of fuss here about prices.  We eat at a variety of restaurants, so perhaps I'm used to a broader range of prices, but I did not find prices out of line at all for the quality and flavor of the foods we tried, and for the prompt, friendly service.  We had more than enough food for two adults, very much enjoyed our dining experience, and left happy and full for just at $50.00 including tip.

My only complaint is I did not save room for dessert.

Stayed here in August and I loved it. I loved the location, walking distance to a lot of restaurants and shops, right next door to BC Place. Modern boutique hotel with very comfortable clean rooms. The room offered a Nespresso machine, smart tv, galaxy tablet with charging port, refrigerator, and USB ports. The bathroom had a life of its own since it's the main attraction to the room but once you pull the curtain down you got use to it. The only draw back was that the shower didn't have anywhere to hold onto so it made things a little tricky. The staff was all very helpful and very friendly checking in and out was very easy and fast. Really liked the fact that they always offered cold lemon cucumber water and green apples in the lobby and they also rent bikes to the guest at no charge (while supplies last of course) This hotel made my stay in beautiful Canda that much more special!

I love hot dogs so much and finding a decent dog is hard to do. Spikes is good at filling the void. 

Pros: awesome topping combos, flexibility to add any toppings you want, great signature mustard, bite to the dogs, fresh baked bun

Cons: can be really slow at service, the bread while delicious can sometimes overpower the taste  of the dogs and toppings, Pepsi products (personal peeve!), dogs tasted rollered or griddled and should be grilled would add a lot of flavor. 

All in all, I am in contestant craving for a hot dog and Spikes delivered. Their take isn't a traditional dog, I would def love to see like a spike junior which would be a normal size hot dog on a traditional bun with choice of toppings to get a more traditional, off the grill, all American hot dog feel. Would still recommend if anyone asked. Happy hot dogs!

I've brought my 2006 Honda CRV into Beaverton Honda for several repairs over the past two or three years, and each time I've found their Service Dept personnel helpful in explaining what work they did, and if anything else requiring future service was needed. When one repair was going to take several days to complete, they gave me a loaner and accommodated my need for a CRV so that I could haul my work items around. Recently one of my headlights was burned out and I stopped in without an appointment and they not only fixed in within 10 minutes, but they also did it for no charge, and they left a chocolate chip cookie on the dash for me!  Great service!

The Capital Grille dining area is beautifully decorated in dark wood, low lighting at dinner, jazz music piping in over the speakers, with paintings on the wall.  The dining chairs are very comfortable leather dining chairs. Crisp white linens adorn the tabletops. Black napkins are provided for dark clothing. After having the warm bras with salted butter, I had the cast iron shrimp which are delightful beyond words. The shrimp are completely peeled, served in a small iron skillet, over soft crostini, cherry heirloom tomatoes, basil, and covered in a butter, garlic, and lemon sauce. Soooo tasty! The lump crabmeat is served with a mayo based sauce with a tiny amount of horseradish. It is an ample serving - be sure to ask for additional sauce. 

The filet mignon with the peppercorn preparation is divine. We eat out five days a week and have had meals in many cities in the US and Europe and the filet mignon here was by far one of the most tender and flavorful cuts of meat (aside from my mom's slow roasted garlic stuffed  rump roast) I have ever had. Our waiter, Kenneth, was fantastic. 

The seasonal berries with crème Anglaise are refreshing, the flourless chocolate espresso cake is wonderful, and the warm chocolate with port wine infused cherries and ice cream are scrumptious as is the cheesecake.  The cheesecake is very light and has the taste of creme brûlée. 



The lobster bisque is more of a cup of soup, not a bowl by any means, and to be honest it tastes like hot goo and extremely thick. It is the soup du jour and was highly recommended by the waiter. I sent it back and ordered the French onion soup. The French Onion Soup was as delightful as the lobster bisque was bad. The onion soup had a rich brown base with abundant onions, cheese and bread. It could benefit from being served in a larger vessel. A lot of the rich broth flows onto the saucer and is sinfully wasted. Very nice course.

We decided to try this place for dinner after some of the great word of mouth and reviews.   We started off with the Brie in Puffs and the Caesar salad.  The salad comes with fried anchovies (which I was not a fan, but the others in my group who liked benefited from getting mine).  The Brie in puffs were surprisingly full of flavor with the apricot filling and very well balanced.  They would be ordered again for sure!

For my entree I ordered the roasted mushroom and burrata flatbread.  It was the perfect size for one and it was delicious and full of flavor. I really enjoyed the flavors that were combined on the plate topped with the truffle honey balsamic (could have used more of that).  

While they don't show it they do offer kid's options, so they had pasta and chicken tenders.  They had salad to start and enjoyed all of their items.

Good drink and wine selection to choose from as well and the service was prompt and professional.

You do park in the parking garage and there is no ticket to take so be sure to ask about it so they can give you a card to scan when you leave so you don't have to pay.  Looking forward to another visit in the future.

OMG, I turned into.. A tourist... We have this restaurant in Time Square and when I walk by, I laugh at the long wait line. 

Guess what? In Orlando, this place friggin' rocks the house!

We came in for dinner and started with the "Shrimper's Net Catch" and fried calamari. Both starters were outstanding!!

I had the Shrimp Gumbo as well as the Kentucky Bourbon Skewer dinner.
Cooked perfectly, it was really tasty.

The kids had burgers (They aren't fish lovers) and my wife had the "Dumb Luck Coconut Shrimp" why they call it Dumb Luck, I haven't a clue. She also gave it a thumbs up. 

So when you come to NYC, I won't laugh at you on line waiting to get in. Hmm.. Yeah maybe I will. Haha, you can do the same for me in Orlando ;)

Tasty Korean fried chicken! We ordered a Half & Half Soy Garlic and Extra Hot King, Boneless Soy Garlic wings, and a side of the Rice King. The wings were freshly fried, packed with flavor, and crispy on the outside. The Extra Hot wings were delicious, but definitely spicier than I expected. The boneless wings tasted great, but were a bit too dry. The Rice King was the perfect side to accompany the wings! It consisted of white rice with some kind of seasoned seaweed mixed with anchovies on top. Our order also came with pickled radishes, neatly packed in small containers. The service was also friendly and we got our food extremely quick.  I definitely want to come back and try the other sides!

On a warm September evening it  was great to sit outside at The Daily Catch, with a panoramic view of the Harborside.  We were seated quickly and received reasonable service throughout the meal.  The highlight was the food.  We were not especially hungry but fancied the lobster dish with pasta and other seafood.  Our waitress suggested that we split a portion sized for one person, and also recommended that we upgrade from regular pasta to the house special black squid ink pasta.  The recommendations were right on point.  The lobster and other assorted seafood had been cooked over the pasta in a pan and were brought to the table in the pan.  The taste was outstanding.  Highly recommended.  The dish with the black pasta was about $50 between two people and we thought it was well worth the money.  I tried one of their selection of beers and that was good also.

I adopted two dogs from Northeast Animal Shelter just down the street. They recommended this clinic and I am so glad they did!

Both of my dogs have their own special needs. I have one who lost a back leg due to being shot in the leg (this was before I adopted him, and we don't know who did it or why). Needless to say, he is pretty nervous around strangers and doesn't really like to be touched. I would muzzle him when I brought him in, just out of caution, but I'm not sure that I needed to. Dr. Ingram was excellent with him! I don't recall him ever growling at her, which is what he does when someone he doesn't know approaches him too closely or touches him. She was always very thorough and explained everything she was doing. She would even call to follow up after every appointment!

My other dog was a stray for the first 18 months of her life, and while she is better with strangers she still does not enjoy being picked up or taken away from me. I'm fairly certain she give some of the techs a very rough time whenever they tried to take blood or give her a shot, but if they were ever frustrated or annoyed, they never let it show in front of me. After a few dramatic visits on my dog's part, they asked if I wouldn't mind coming back with them for shots to help calm her down. I know that most places don't allow this, but ever since then everything went very smoothly!

I have since moved across the country, and NEVC and Dr. Ingram are some of the things we miss most! I would highly recommend this clinic, and especially Dr. Ingram.

It's worth noting that one evening I had to come in for an appointment and it was not a night that Dr. Ingram was working. We waited for 50 minutes to be seen, and an additional 35 once shown into the exam room. I could hear the vet talking with other staff in the back about the clothes she bought for her own dog, and then about how badly another one of their (canine) patients smelled, for about 10 minutes before she came in to see us in the exam room. After such a long wait, I was not impressed that the staff was goofing around while I was stuck in the exam room, particularly at the expense of one of their patients. I also was not overly impressed with this particular doctor - she acted as if our appointment was an inconvenience for ehr. Thus, I recommend this clinic and Dr. Ingram together.

I'm not familiar with Indian cuisine but the Grill came recommended by a friend.  I thought the buffet would be a nice and leisurely way to experience the food and savor the tastes. The server was very helpful and took me through the offerings of which I took several small plates with two items each time. I was impressed that we were instructed to take a fresh clean plate at each pass through the line and returned to a cleared and clean table.  The décor is delightful and seating is not cramped and the entire dining area was filled with natural sunlight. What a wonderful way to enjoy a relaxing long lunch.

Kerbey Lane is an interesting place.  It somewhat reminded me of Cafe Luna (in D.C.) with allowing local artists to display their works on the walls.  If you're interested, you can purchase them.

The food was good as the place claim to use only organic and natural ingredients.  My partner had some breakfast platter that came with eggs, sausages and French toast.  I'm not a fan of French toast.  But, I have to say that his French toast was fabulous!

I had the migas.  I was surprised that migas was even made in restaurants.  My mother used to make them.  It was one of the meals that I missed from Mom when she passed away a few years back.  So, I ordered that.  It was alright.  I think it would've been better if they hadn't put in onions.  Of course, the menu didn't say anything about onions.  Otherwise, I'd ask them to leave out the onions.

The service was ok.  Just a tad bit too long to wait for our food.

I wouldn't mind coming back again and see if Kerbey Lane is really the place to eat as everyone brags about.

I love to find new spots to stop for a coffee and sandwiches. I was surprised by the variety of speciality coffees they have to offer. I had the Nutty Knight and my wife had Toffee Bar of which they both were good. I do like my coffee piping hot because I like to enjoy it over time this having it piping hot allows me to do so but it was at perfect temp for my wife. The sandwiches we had both were great as well. 

Definitely will be coming back! Nice little hidden gem in the back of Waterford Lakes!

I really didn't want to give this place four stars, but I had to, because it's just that damn good. 

I'm not exactly an indian food connoisseur, but I'm no indian food virgin, either.  And this is the best indian food I've ever had, especially for the price.  The shrimp masala (acutally, anything with masala at this place) is absolutely divine, and I really appreciate the condiments that come with each meal.  The condiments make the main dish what it is, and what it is is really, really good.

Mango lassi - also good.

What is not good is the wait.  I know, I know, I just have to suck it up and deal with it, it's part of the place's charm, blah blah blah.  Well, sorry.  Just because the wait is worth it, doesn't mean that I have to like it.  I don't.  Your food takes freaking forever to come (we're talking 20-30 minutes here).  This is by no means an unreasonable time for food to come at a normal restaurant, but at an "Indian Roadside Cafe" where there were no avialable tables, it was too much. The downstairs is tiny, so the only place I could perch while I waited was RIGHT in front of this guy who was peacefully sitting with his back to me, eating his food.  Let's just say he turned around in his chair and got an eyeful and loudly expressed his displeasure.  That was not fun for any of the parties involved. 

Also, when I went there recently, it was around 5:30ish on a Tuesday night.  I stood at the counter for FIFTEEN minutes (the only one in line) waiting for someone to take my order, but the phone kept ringing, and I kept getting ignored.  I finally left.  I know the guys behnd the counter are busy, and they always look harried, and they've never been anything but nice to me, but - come on.  Fifteen minutes is ridiculous.  And I really wanted that indian food.  

You still get four stars, Punjabi Dhaba.  But it hurts me to give them to you.

Being one of the silly folks that choose to live on the south part of town, I pass Hapeville on my way home.  Needless to say, the variety of culinary options somewhat runs into a brick wall at some point below the split of the Connector, leaving us southsiders as somewhat of invalids in popular opinion.  Furthermore, Hapeville does have some interesting dining options, but considering they all almost exist solely for the Delta lunch rush and those who are stranded at the various lodging places nearby, the hours of said places are often in question.

I'd passed Slideways for literally months, intrigued by the idea of a place that specialized in sliders that wasn't a Krystal.  However, the hours of the place confirmed that they existed primarily for lunch, and went into the evening on Fridays and Saturdays.  Finally, an opportunity presented itself to where I could give the place a shot on my way home from work on a Friday with no genuine plans.

The location is a tad bit tricky if you don't know what the surrounding area is like, it's fairly easily accessible via the Virginia Ave exit off of I-85, or if you're like me and actually heading south, then probably the Sylvan Rd exit is the most expedient.  It's on the southern side of the train tracks, and has a fairly generous amount of street-adjacent parking spaces, that are thankfully free.

The interior is cozy and modern, and perhaps not something to be expected out in Hapeville, but then again the Which-Wich and Willy's on the same road have ushered in a similar modern restaurant aesthetic too.  Anyway we're greeted promptly by the friendly staff that doesn't rush us or pressure us to order, since being first-timers, we have no earthly idea of what to expect.

I ended up getting one of the specials (beef, mushrooms, bleu cheese) and a fish 'n chips slider.  Now admittedly, the prices stand out somewhat, because the sliders all seem to range from $2.99-4.99 that I noticed, and it should be made aware that this is for ONE slider.  I ended up paying $11ish for two sliders and tots (soda would have made it more), and IMO, that's close to almost unreasonable for a lunch cost.

However, when the food arrived to the table, both sliders looked good, and it put to ease the concerns over the price.

Basically, take a Krystal slider which is two sponges, with a centimeter-thick square of "beef" in it with like a pickle and some translucent caramelized onions.  You could mash your hand down on it and have maybe an inch-thick square puck of an edible sponge with the essence of meat in it.

Slideways' sliders were vastly larger; slightly too small to be called a burger, but noticeably larger than what Krystals and White Castles have led us to believe are sliders.  The buns are fluffier and still have some chew to them, and the meat portions are generous and cannot be contained by the edges of the buns.  The beef patty was slightly thicker than a half-inch practically.

The flavors of the sliders were good, but I have to say were not perfect.  The beef I suspect is handled way too much; perhaps it's in order to grind in the spices and seasoning into the beef, but in the end, the patty has a slight toughness about it that I think comes from it being handled too much, probably in order to get it to its almost picture-esque circular shape.  The flavors are good, but the consistency of the beef was slightly off-putting.

The fish 'n chip slider though, was fantastic.  The fish was fried perfectly, and had good flavor on its own, and had a mix of both vinegar and some tartar sauce on it, with some fries jammed in there.  I'm definitely getting this again the next time I swing by.

Not to be ignored were the tots.  Tater tots are obviously big in Atlanta, and there are so many places where they can be had.  I don't know what Slideways does differently than most of the other places throughout the city, but theirs are more flavorful, and awkward as it is to describe it as such, but more tender.  It's like chewier, in a flavorful mashed potato kind of way.  I know I'm doing a poor job of describing it, but I'll be damned if I didn't want some right now.

Overall, I like this place a lot, and I want it to do well.  Hapeville is somewhat of a bridge between the city from where I live and where I work, and I'm all for more quality restaurants making their way south of the city.  The prices might seem a little, but it's worth noting that you'll be getting your money's worth in product, and the bottom line is that you'll probably not be leaving hungry.

After apartment hunting all day in Boston, we treated ourselves to a cozy dinner at the Squealing Pig. It's a small restaurant with a great atmosphere - and the beer menu is great. I ended up getting their special brewed beer which was quite tasty. 

Since it was raining, I needed some comfort food which came in the form of their chicken, brie, tomato and pesto toastie with tomato soup. That meal really took me home, and it was made with quality ingredients. Ill definitely come back, especially because for their reasonable pricing.

My first Max experience was during Restaurant Week, and I have to say I was pleasantly impressed. The server didn't treat my friend and I like we were scum because we were ordering off the RW menu, and the food was quality...not just something thrown together for the special menu. The shrimp and grits were great. 
Been back since, and have not been disappointed, with one exception...they've got killer lamb sliders, but they're not on the regular menu..they're a special now and again. They won't tell me when they're offered, so I have to keep calling and hoping...but they're probably the best ones I've had in town. When I can find them I'll always get them, the little devils! 
For sports pub food, everything is good and the crowd is fun during games. Good place for me to go by myself, sidle up to the bar, and check out the scenery without getting creepy advances, plus its close to home so I know I can get back safely and not spend a fortune on a taxi.

Man, there isn't much love for Fuddruckers!  It's not going to be gourmet food, but you know what to expect when you go.  I also enjoy the staff here.  They're really friendly!  I love close to this location so I've walked there to eat a few times.  

The positives include good burgers, a friendly staff, and a nice selection of toppings for your food.  I've ordered several different burgers and they've always cooked them the way I want.  The toppings bar is well-stocked and seems fresh enough.  They have lots of options so you can make your burger the way you want.  The staff is also a high point - they are friendly and helpful.  I looked sad the last time I went in so the clerk gave me a free cookie!  She was sweet!

Overall, this isn't a bad place.  It's inexpensive, the staff tries hard, and it's clean.  You could do worse, and there aren't that many other options in the immediate area at the same price point.  I'll definitely walk back from time to time.

We wandered in before a show at the Short North Theatre, which is next door.  We caught a Thursday HH, and Thursday happens to be half-off all bottled wine.  Lots going on!  We chose a very acceptable Nebbiola, and a couple Mexican Cokes.

It's a loudish bar situation, but the star here is pizza.  I'd been to the original location in Brooklyn so my expectations were high.  Expectations met!  

We had two pies, marghareta and  pepperoni.  Both excellent, with a great crust cooked in the 900° wood oven.  TJ, the owner, allowed me to chat him up as he was placing pies in the oven, so I know some facts.  He's a hardworking friendly guy, who serves up Top 10 central Ohio pie!

Not easy parking but if you're lucky there are open meters.

If you ahem not realized by my recent posts, I am a huge Jurassic Park fan so naturally, I like to visit Jurassic Park at Islands of Adventure. Recently I learned the Jurassic Park section is doing special desserts to celebrate the release of the Jurassic World Fallen Kingdom movie. The one I wanted to try the most was the Dinosaur egg. I have to say for the dessert you find in a theme park, it was awesome and detailed. The egg is a white chocolate shell, over chocolate cake and vanilla frosting at the bottom. The best part was the dinosaur claw coming out of the egg. It looked awesome and cool but taste was a little weird. It was like tootsie roll material, very chewy. The dessert was great, especially if you are a Jurassic Park fan. The only thing I did not care for was the dessert is served in a bowl and on a plastic plate. Had to make sure my raptor egg did not go flying on the floor when I was walking to a table.

I still give Fuloon four stars even though many things have improved since my last four star review.  I go to the Malden library every two or three weeks and when I leave there I treat myself to lunch at Fuloon.  I learned a long time ago that you just do not depend on their buffet because it is hit or miss.  Lately I have been getting ma po tofu with meat. Trust me it is delicious.  Tofu is a love of mine right up there with spicy things so the dish is just perfect.  I just had it yesterday and I am already looking forward to my next library run.  I think next time I am ordering the Szechuan beef noodle soup though.  Since I visit regularly i notice the staff is very friendly and they recognize me and pretty much know what I want when I get there.  A lot of people think they are rude to Non-Asians but last time I checked I was black and I get great service there.

I'll confirm again that the fried chicken was amazing -- crispy on the outside, moist on the inside. If you don't want to get the fried chicken meal on the online menu, they also sell by the piece.  I think it was $2.25 or $2.50 depending on if you wanted drumstick, thigh, etc.

Cabbage was delicious. We also got some beef ribs, but I honestly would just rather eat all fried chicken.  The ribs were tender but not falling off the bone. The sauce was a big sweet for my taste.

I called in my order, and they told me 20 minutes.  They were pretty much right on target with the timing, which was good because I left my car in a handicapped parking spot on the street.  Even with a Cambridge parking permit, it wasn't easy to find a spot right outside at 7 pm. I'm sure I could have found a spot if I circled around on a side street, but I was hungry!

I totally agree with other reviewers that the worse part is smelling the chicken during the drive home! I might have broken off a few bits of crispiness to nibble on during the traffic lights.

I love supporting non-profits, so I'm naturally attracted to this theater.  There's just no other like it.  I just get a little warm-and-fuzzy feeling when I come here, knowing I'm doing something to encourage local film making.  I haven't had the chance to volunteer here yet, but if I lived closer, I would...if for no other reason than the free passes and popcorn.  :)

True, the seating is not really comfortable and my knees are usually sore by the time a movie ends.  Sure, they don't serve beer or wine, like other popular theaters.  Yet the friendly people who volunteer here draw me in.  So do the easy-on-the-wallet admission fares ($6.50 adults, $4 kids and seniors).  The architecture is also nice to look at, but the selection of films is always top-notch (the ones I most want to see), so that's why I keep coming back.  

p.s. Last year, this is where we saw the incredible Spike and Mike's Sick and Twisted Animation Festival...so awesome!  So be sure to look for special film festival presentations like this at the Hollywood.

I made an appointment after reading the raves on yelp. I love my new cut and color. I got full highlights and cut for $130. Of course I'd love to pay even less, but this is def less than what I've paid in the past for the same quality (other salons were $160).
