My stylist absolutely listened to what I wanted and seemed to understand my hair right away. She took her time and made sure it looked just as I wanted before I left. My only gripe? My appointment started 20 minutes late, and I thought it was a little odd that no one - not even the receptionist - checked in to let me know that the appt would be a bit behind schedule. Do I kind of sound like a diva saying that? I don't mean to be - just would have liked someone to tell me that they hadn't forgotten I was sitting there! :) But once the appointment started, it was really terrific.

Solid option for work lunch. I've mostly gone to Chipotle, but I feel like Boloco's bowls and burritos are a little healthier (of course, it depends what you put on them). The rice seems less greasy and the chicken is softer and fresher. My bowl was fresh, hot, and tasty.

This location is particularly good. Aside from having lots of seating, both indoors and outdoors, it has a lot of natural light from big windows and being on the corner of the building. It is right next to a construction site, but there was no noise from it today. 

The staff were attentive and they seemed obsessive about keeping the place clean. The tables were clean, the soda fountain was clean and lids/straws/etc. were well organized, and they were mopping the floor in the middle of the day. Very nice to see, especially since some of the downtown/FiDi lunch places can get pretty grimy after the lunch rush. 

The only annoying things were that the music was cranked up really loudly, blasting non-hit music. Also, the employees sometime shout across the place to one another, which was especially pronounced because there were few customers and no one was talking (maybe because of the loud music?). 

Overall, though, a very decent and fast lunch spot.

Many reviews on Iacono's... went for pizza/salad bar buffet (M-F lunch)...$10.75..walked in and you enter at the take out/to go portion of restaurant... sat down at 1130... 3 fresh pizza's up.. cheese, pep/sausage and Hawaiian ... salad bar had fresh greens, Mac salad, peas, cukes, eggs, ban peppers, and other assortment of items to add to your salad(3 dressings)... really surprised how fresh everything looked... as I finished my first plate of greens & pizza another fresh pizza brought out and my server(Sean) filled up my drink... I love supporting local places like Iacono's...great place to go for lunch or dinner - pizza is good (cracker crust) service great and you feel like your supporting the community... check out Iacono's on Kenny Rd in NW Columbus, good food at affordable prices..

Easy brunch with the girls on a crisp Fall Saturday, and Glowbal delivered.

Complimentary strawberry banana smoothie shot and sugared beignets to start the meal. Excellent touch, although that smoothie was a wee bit thick! Top marks for server Rob and his apron fully lined with pens, and the hostess who seated us quite promptly in a nice spot on the "patio" when we strolled in at around 11:30. Our table was perfect for people watching, and we weren't melting under a heat lamp.

Re: the food.
Good deal on the sandwiches for the amount of food you get. Friend had the chicken sandwich and it was definitely sizable and came with a side salad and a bowl of hand cut fries. Yum. Then came three plates of some variation on eggs benedict. Benny was top notch, although the consensus at the table was that the muffins were a bit thicker than preferred. It didn't quite match up to the eggs benny at Season's, but lots of extra points for the hint of parmesan in the potato hash, and the perfect crisp and flavor of the pancetta.

Best surprise, I thought, was that their drinks are reasonably priced for such a hotspot... I suppose it might be because it's brunch? Nevertheless, that was one tasty mango mojito for $8. I'll be back next time I'm in Vancouver; that lobster grilled cheese is calling my name.

2 times in one Week after going for the 1st time this Sunday ! I got the melt. It Was Amazing! Everything About the place was great. I Would have Gave them 5 stars s but I was Very disappointed in my waitress last night. She .t00k a while to greet Us, got my side order wrong 1 / And shockingly For a place with Such popularity as Wahl buyers , She had zero personality' r I've been inthe industry for 10 years. I've never ever come across this issue. Legit nothing. No personalization. Like a robot.

Went here for a very yummy breakfast sandwich. sausage eggs and cheese on an everything bagel. Two eggs is always a power move without needing to pay extra. The bagel was doughy and seasoned really well. For cheese I got cheddar which is the best (in my opinion). The sausage was so thick but I loved how there was always a ton of meat in every bite. It was also so filling. The outdoor seating is great for people watching. The homefries were also really yummy with a little salt, pepper, and ketchup!

Really nice place, and walking distance from where I was staying, so that was very helpful. Of course the main feature is the lobster sandwich, which really is packed with lobster meat. Unlike some places where they have to mask lower quality or lack of good lobster with lots of mayo and seasonings, they had just a little bit, enough to complement the taste of lots of fresh lobster. I also liked their shrimp and corn chowder, and the fact that they have dog-friendly outdoor seating.

On one occasion, we bought several live lobsters to steam at home, and they really were alive and kicking... these were no half-dead things you see lying in tanks at inferior places. However, and I'm no lobster expert so I don't know if it's an issue of certain types of lobster being tougher than others, but the ones we got had the craziest, thickest, hardest shells I've ever encountered. Our home-cooked meal ended with pieces of shell, meat, and juice scattered all over the apartment -- we even found bits of lobster stuck to a coffee table half a room away from the dining area! The meat inside, when we could get to it, was perfect though :-)

We stayed at this hotel during our lazy long weekend in Portland...certainly a very swanky, hipster hotel with rooms to match, but rooms are on the small side. We ordered coffee as part of room service one morning it was very weak (though the beans are from Stumptown) so it was a waste of 20 bucks. we hung out in the lobby bar for drinks a couple times which was cool & tried to go to the rooftop bar one evening but it was too packed...

we've now stayed at the Heathman a couple times, at the Lucia & also now at the Nines. i'd say Heathman is my fav & Lucia is the least fav. want to try Monaco & Ace next...

Harvard Square provides a lot of options for tourists all in one location: entertainment, food, Harvard, sightseeing, etc.  Mr. Bartley's Burger Cottage (a must-visit) is nearby, there is ample street entertainment (some acts are actually really good), there are a plethora of shops and it's definitely a nice place to walk around in when the weather warms up.  

The COOP store is a fun spot to visit because it has a ton of Harvard University gear and merchandise you can purchase.  Public transportation makes Harvard very convenient and accesible as Harvard is one of the stops on the Red Line.

Shanghai River definitely specialises in XLB as it's one of the best I've tasted so far. They have the crab variety "Dumpling with Crabmeat" which is more expensive and comes in lesser quantity than the regular pork XLB - 5 pieces for lunch time.

We also tried a few of the lunch menu dishes including:

"Deep Fried Black Cod" which was marinated first and arrived with a side of mayo. Although it was very tasty, the skin could have been crispy as well.

The "Black Vinegar Spare Ribs with Nuts" has a nice strong burnt caramel flavour due to the thick sauce of black vinegar and sugar. The spare ribs were crunchy outside, then soft and chewy inside. It is also topped with pine nuts which I would have preferred to have been toasted first to it embarks a stronger flavour. However, this is still a must try if you want something on the sweet side.

"Deep Fried Crispy Tofu" has a nice crunchy batter filled with silken tofu and served with some watered-down soy sauce. I think they should come up with a more imaginative and tasty condiment with a mixture of XO sauce to make the dish stand out.

We also requested to see the dinner menu which they will happily take orders from so we ordered our favourite "Pan Fried Prawns with Walnuts". The prawns are coated with light batter so it gets a crunchy shell amidst one juicy bite after another. It's then tossed in mayo. It's topped with candied Honey Walnuts and sprinkled with sesame seeds. This is my all-time favourite Chinese dish which I'm critical of it's taste. So far everything has been perfectly fried except that the mayo sauce could be a bit more tastier and a tad bit sweeter like other restaurants that seem to have perfected the dish.

Overall it's a good experience if only you are able to skip the long wait which we were able to do by arriving an hour before they close for lunch. Ambiance is modern and feels clean especially with the open kitchen.

Despite the language barrier, our server tried to help us order what we were looking for since there were only a few photos that matched the extensive lunch and dinner menu.

Private parking allocated for the restaurant is available in the building they reside. As other reviewers have mentioned, make reservations before you arrive.

Came here with a new friend that I met at an industry conference while visiting. My friend ordered the crab appetizer and a butter lettuce salad as she said she had eaten a late lunch. I had a bite of her salad as she said I had to try it. I love butter lettuce - mild, creamy, and the herbs du Provence and red wine vinaigrette complemented this well, and the candied walnuts added the right amount of sweet to the savory. I ordered the sirloin steak medium rare and it was cooked perfectly. I asked to sub sautéed spinach instead of frites since these were not gluten free. Boo. But spinach was quite good. I'd come back here again when in town.

Cat - with gross infection.  High temp & needed surgery.
1st surgery went well but the bandage fell off the second we got home, so we returned to have it replaced.  New vet (not the one who did the surgery) advised further surgery as the wound was already worse in that short period of time.  I was reluctant to do another surgery on the same night but I agreed to it.
2nd surgery was great - the Dr. is a very good surgeon. 
Each time I brought her in for a check up or stitches to be removed everyone was very nice and the cost was low or nothing.
I will use them again.

It feels a bit out of place with the rest of the Village, but different isn't always a bad thing. You couldn't have two more different places with Graveyard right next to Gravity Pub. One's a dive and proud of it, the other is exceedingly clean and open with big windows and high ceilings.

The food at Graveyard is good, if not a little overpriced for the portions that they serve. The small plates on the menu are interesting, but very small. The sandwiches are good, but nothing special. The drinks are what you would expect, and there's a nice open area for pool and live music.

So, why four stars? I guess it's more for the idea of a new business taking over a long vacant spot in the Village than for the food or drinks being anything special. It's different from what you would expect from East Atlanta Village, but adding a new wrinkle to the 'hood is fine by me. Sentimental attachment to my neighborhood and wanting to see it thrive can get you at least one extra star...

Excellent choices of candles and other candle-related items.  I was able to find a nice collection for a friend.
My only problem with this and other Yankee Candle stores is that there are not pre-arranged packages to pick up and go.  I had to wait at least 15 minutes for someone to shrink-wrap my gift while the friend waited unknowingly.  But Donna put together a very nice package.

This is a good place to put together a package for someone, with a variety of scents.  A little pricey, but worth it.

This place serves Italian food.  This place uses the 'small plate' model.  This means that the meal is on a small plate.  The plates aren't very large.  This means that the meal is of a higher quality.  This place focuses on the flavor and the cheap prices to each meal.  It is odd that such a quality can equate to $7.00 or a large sausage pizza with mozzarella cheese is valued at $8.00.  

The place also focuses on décor.  There is a greenhouse covered with vines.  There is a wing where you can see the street  Then the bar sits in the middle.  The staff are always helpful.  The list of alcohol is more of a long chant of wines.  These wines are rather nice.  There is a list of alcohol that isn't wine.  I had the hard cider.  The hard cider isn't as sweet.  If one wants to have the alcohol in a medium sweet cider, then the drink that I have just described will do the trick.  I was quite surprised by the pizza. I want to say that.  The pizza was rather nice.  It is amazing on how such a confined space can lend itself to that level of quality.

Good Service, really good spicy falafel ... Terrible hummis

The lady that works the front is super friendly and makes all the food fresh to order 

The falafel sandwich is made with wheat flour pita, which doesn't taste too flavorful.  The spicy sauce is really good, and the falafel is crisped fresh.  The wrap includes fresh pickles and onions with tahini and lettuce 

The hummus was gross, overload of garlic, a slight drizzle of olive oil and some weird chunks of curds through out = skip it

Cheap? check!
Delicious? check!
Satisfying? check!

Great place for a huge bowl of noodles.  The bowl is more deceiving than you think and is quite full.  The wontons are large and have lots of flavour.  The brisket was for the most part fairly well cooked - the larger pieces were "tougher".  Service was quick and efficient, but not very friendly - but that is typical of this type of restaurant.  We were there during afternoon tea time so our noodles came with our choice of drink - 50 cents more for cold.  I got the HK style milk tea - delicious and my companion got iced lemon tea which was okay.

This place has a great variety of Dominican comfort food from fritters of all kinds to good old fashioned rice and beans with meat in sauce ir stewed. My favorite here and I think the best in Boston is the Beef Tripe Stew if you are partial to this dish this is the best place to get it. The Stewed Goat is also really good everything else is good enough to eat. They make great milk shakes here as well. And they are the best value in Metro Boston. Lots of bang for your buck. 

This place gives a true and authentic representation of Dominican food with a great variety always and their standbys which people go out of their way to get. Mondongo (beef tripe stew) and Chivo Guisado (braised goat).

For white people tacos this place is aight. 
I just went to their new location, no happy hour-- yet! Ordered the grilled chicken taco, 3.75, which has lots of flavor and they didn't skimp you, though do wish the taco was doubled with tortilla, like most true Mexican restaurants you can clean up the scraps with your extra one ;) and their special veggie one of the day which had potatoes, shiitakes, kale or braised greens, and this beet crema sauce. 
Honestly, the creativity was there the greens were just a bit overdone and didn't taste that great. 
This place is a bit pricer than what it should be but you do get a loaded taco.

I have been coming here for over seven years.  I have brought many people with me over the years and have turned them into fans as well!  The food is well priced and you receive large portions.  There was only one time I had an issue and the BBQ Pork I ordered was extremely dry, when I brought it to the waitresses attention she took it to the back and brought me out a new one that was delicious!  I usually order the family dinner A with Happy Family and 10 ingredient Chow Mein.  The Happy Family is always delicious as is the Chow Mein, although as several people have pointed out, it is a little greasy.  The only reason I did not give it five stars is for the oily Chow Mein, the horrible decor and the waitresses leave a little to be desired.  Considering I usually get our food to go, it is not that much of an issue for me!

Oh god. I think I'm in heaven. A good consignment store. An upscale consignment store. Yes, it can be pricey, but when you're looking at a mint-condition Vivienne Westwood coat that was originally $1,000 and is now $375, you better thank the fashion gods that you stumbled upon this little piece of heaven. I have found the most amazing dresses in this store--most are new pieces that just didn't move off the floor of the boutiques on Newbury, so they got dumped at this store. One man's crap is another woman's treasure--this woman, right here! If you have the time to dig, do it. This is a treasure trove worth the work. The only reason I don't give it 5 stars is because it can be pricey; but, like I said, you really are getting a good deal.

This place was nice. I ate here with a friend last night and ordered the pino grigio from Italy, and it was very crisp and smooth.  We split the brisket sandwich which came with FF and we ordered an extra side of cole slaw.  The brisket tasted good, but there was too much fat on it.  It really should have been a little leaner, but other than that the meal was good, and the waiter was very nice. 

We sat outside since it was 87 degrees out, and there was a roomy outside seating area.

nice experience!

I've wanted to try this place for a minute. Appears they are run by the same owners of Sushi Village. Hubby and I had the fried scallops combo, the shrimp and catfish combo and 4 piece chicken wings. 

The chicken wings were probably my favorite our of the meal. Full wing and seasoned. 

The catfish came in easily at 2nd place (maybe even a tie for 1st) as it was also flavorful and cooked just right.

The shrimp and scallop get no place. They are both breaded but to me sense neither the breading nor the seafood have seasoning what's the point in the breading?

The lady taking the order at the front was very pleasant and patient with me. I will be back for the Catfish and wings!

We were looking for something to eat in Etna Ohio.   We were referred to the Dragon  Village by a friend.  Very happy with choice.   It really is a local joint. Price was reasonable.   Food was good and hot.  Owner came out to check on us.  The two of us ate for $20.
Second visit.   Food is always fast and hot.    They really try their best to make sure that our visit is the best it can be    We will come back and make sure our friends come too

I tried the pupusa and it was good. I am a sucker for anything with avocados! The burrito was good but not out of this world. The food was simple but good.

This place deserves five stars because of the amazing staff. They are so friendly! There was a huge language barrier with the lady working there but she tried her best to recommend dishes to us until one of the English speakers could take our order. Both of the staff members I spoke to seemed very happy. The man who took our order even checked up on us while we were eating. He seemed very passionate about his food.

This place is a hole in the wall restaurant. Don't expect it to be absolutely spotless and have amazing decor.

We didn't wait too long, maybe 10 to 15 minutes since we came before the dinner crowd.

Tender lamb kebabs, plentiful portions of kofta, and fresh vegetables---basic tenets of any Mediterranean cuisine. Happy to report this place has scored positive in all these aspects. I have engulfed myself into this place numerous times so my review would be complete and all the times, it has been consistent.  The lamb was soft, juicy, and flavorful.  the bread was served warm and fresh, and the entrees were presented aesthetically pleasing and fresh--all the times I went.  Service was friendly, and professional, not to mention unbiased. I suggest the kofta sandwich with a side of baba......or for a more hungier soul--I recommend the lamb kebab platter...served with rice and a side. You will leave satisfied, full, and happy that your money was well spent.

My boyfriend and I were in the area and we couldn't decide what to eat. We are always looking for new places to try so we decided to stop by this tiny restaurant. We got the "Meat Lovers" and it was absolutely delicious. 
I would 100% go back, however, the only reason I wouldn't give this restaurant a five star rating is for those who prefer privacy when going out to eat. 
At first, we were seated next to a group of friends but one of them just kept talking so loud. Nothing offensive or anything. Just loud. That would be my one and only complaint. Definitely recommend!

The Macaroni Grill is a staple dinner/drinks stop for me and has been for a couple of years now.  I've been there a few dozen times.  It's definitely a favorite.

I'll categorize:

Food: the food is basically great.  I've had the opportunity now to try most things on the menu at least once, and even though I have my favorite dishes I'm rarely disappointed with any of the other options.  One very disappointing thing to note, though, is that my favorite dish of all time was removed from the menu about a year ago and I miss it very much.  Sausage and Pepper Classico, you will always be fondly remembered.

Service: this is usually good, sometimes great, sometimes not so good.  It depends on what night of the week you're in and who is working.  Sad to say, I've had lousy service here just about as often as I've had fantastic service.  The good news is that even the worst service at Macaroni Grill is still not too bad. 

Atmosphere: the atmosphere is pretty good and definitely feels Mediterranean Italian.  I like the atmosphere, especially in the bar area.  Fake plants, and paper table clothes?  Sure.  Have you been to Italy lately?  That's how they do it.  The point is, it feels like Italy and it tastes like Italy, more so than Olive Garden could ever hope for.

Prices/value: the price is moderate.  It's not a fancy restaurant so don't expect fancy prices.  Do, however, expect food that is frequently more fancy than the price you'll pay for it.  That is what you'll get.

Handy tip #1: you get better service in general in the bar area, on the stools.  The crew they have slinging the alcohol is the best in the place.  Probably the best in town.

Handy tip #2: don't bring groups of over 6 people here, especially if some people will be paying separate.  The wait staff is just not prepared to handle that, for some reason.  We had a shindig of about 10 people, all going dutch, and we were most displeased with the hassle we had to go through to get all the bills taken care of.  It's Keystone Cops for sure, so stick to small groups at most. 

All in all, if you're interested in a nice dinner and drinks, at a moderate price, Macaroni Grill is never a bad choice.  It's often the perfect choice if you're in the mood for Italian.

I'm kind of a pizza snob. I won't eat at chain "pizzerias" because they are so gross and most neighborhood pizza establishments serve passing pies at best.

Bianchi's is good, I'll give them that.

Large portions 
Delicious sauce
Perfect cheese-sauce-dough ratio with oil dripping off of the slice

Minus a star for the following:
1. I have a personal vendetta against places that refuse to accept cards. Get with the times.
2. The people who work here act like they are doing you a favor by allowing you to purchase pizza. They are NOT friendly. But I've been told that's just how people from Revere are.

The Baseball Tavern is one of the best places to grab a beer when the Red Sox are playing at home. It's cheap ($2.50 for some drafts) and they have several floors and a rooftop bar. The pub food is also decent, not particularly good or bad.

During the late fall and winter, however, the Baseball Tavern is pretty quiet (although it fills up for Eagles games on certain Sunday's). It would be easy to blame Fenway in general, but other places nearby stay open.

Very positive experience here. Noticed some of the negative reviews comparing this to the old Rosebud diner, which is simply just without value. This is a completely different approach in every way except for name and address. 

Gets busy for good reason - so try to make a reservation if you can. Great bar with good selection of beers and cocktails, but on the weekend you'll still need to bob and weave with servers as it gets quite crowded if you are standing. 

Menu well spread out, southern influenced for the most part. I got the Texas Rachel in a Skirt which was fantastic. Wife got the pork chops which were good, but not mindblowing. The Atomic poppers were also quite tasty. As with most restaurants in the Davis area - and in general in Camberville - its not cheap, but I thought the food was quite impressive and look forward to other dinners/dishes here.

PIE is phenomenal. I wish I had bought an entire banana cream pie to go.

After recently beginning a new job across the street, I am delighted to know that Sweet Tomatoes offers an exceptional selection of healthy meals. Whether you're looking for take-away, or planning to eat-in, there is most definitely something for you!

I would highly recommend getting to the restaurant before noon, since the fast-casual style of dining is popular. There are great booth-styles of seating with windows, and plenty of dining tables with privacy throughout. 

Lastly, the service was excellent, and I loved the privacy of the fast-casual experience. I will definitely return when I inevitably forget my lunch, once again.

I'm on the fence about this review. Really it was a 3.5 star meal. If this restaurant was on Park Avenue in Winter Park  it would get a 3 star rating from me for sure. Being that it is in lowly Apopka it should get 4 stars for being one of the best restaurants in town. This may be Apopka's only "special occasion" restaurant located, oddly enough, adjoining a Beef O'Brady's. The place is tiny so I would definitely recommend a reservation. At 6pm on a Friday evening we watched the place fill to capacity within 15 minutes. The layout is tight. We were seated at the table closest to the door so that every time the door opened we were blinded by sunlight. This would only be a problem until the sun went down, of course, but was annoying none the less.

Service was a little slow, especially at first. Our drinks took a while in the making but were good once we had them. Our server had limited knowledge of the types of alcohol available and squinted to read them at the bar from our table. I was starving and it took a bit to get our appetizer. Strangely they bring the bread and dipping oil only after the appetizer. It sure would have been nice to have when we first sat down. Anyway, the scallop appetizer ($16 but half off with a Yelp check in) was decent. The scallops were cooked nicely and flavorful but there was just too much oil. They ended up tasting slimy. My Chilean Sea Bass tasted better than it looked. My hubby's lamb chops would have been perfect if they hadn't been a tad over cooked. The three layer chocolate cake we split for dessert was rich but tasted dry, like a slice that had been precut then left out for a few hours to dry. 

So overall if was a good experience with a handful of small let downs. It definitely has potential to be great, and as far as Apopka goes is probably one of the greatest in the area. It isn't cheap though, as entrees will set you back in the $20-30 range. Still, if you plan it as a night out you'll likely leave satisfied. On a side note, the night we dined we saw the newly elected mayor Kilshiemer celebrating with newly elected councilman Sam Ruth. Word about this place is getting out!

On my way to the airport to catch my flight back to SF I realized that I was in Austin for five days and hadn't sampled the famous Texas BBQ yet.  Luckily, Salt Lick BBQ has a location inside the airport.
The food was well worth the wait-chopped beef brisket served with a tangy BBQ sauce on a soft roll and a pickle on the side.  
Of course I needed a Shiner Bock to round out the perfect Austin vacation...four solid stars, mainly because $14 for a sandwich (no sides) and a beer seems a bit high.

When you can impress your New York City friends with an outstanding Indian restaurant you know it's good!  Thanks fellow Yelpers!

If you always order Curry or Tanduri when you dine out for Indian food, break out of the rut and try Biryani. Now I don't know how you pronounce it, but I'll tell you that you can't go wrong with saffron rice, raisins & cashews, coconut garnish and plentiful shrimp (or chicken, lamb or veggies). 

The curry dishes were outstanding and the appetizers were perfectly fried and tasty. The tikona-think samosa with ground lamb re-heated nicely the next day. Naan is always good and was totally fresh. Take a walk on the spicy side and try the gobi paratha.

Between the prices and the amazing food we will be back. In fact, my husband and I can't stop talking about it. As for our NYC friends they'll be back too :)

I'm a few months late on writing this review, but the tail end of 2013 was just bananas for me.  One of my late 2013 complications was our home PC computer was moving at a snails pace, I couldn't even check gmail without some issue.  It would randomly shut down.  We thought we had a virus.  

My husband wanted to just chuck it and spend 3K on a new macbook (still does).  But I found midtown Metro Computer and said, "lets just see what they say, our home PC is only 3 years old".  Turns out our hard drive was going bad.  So they replaced our hard drive (preserved all the content  that was on it), and we were back in business!  Our computer now runs super fast again, and all we had to do was replace the hard drive for just a few hundred dollars (we had a terabyte hard drive)!  Much cheaper than buying a new computer and upgrading all our software!  

If you are having computer issues, take your computer to metro computer, I was very impressed!

This review is for the raw bar only.
My friend and I were originaly plan to have dinner here, it was friday evening at the peak of dinner time, and we did not make reservation, of cos the wait was longer than we expected, so we decided to have some oysters at the bar since two seats were just emptied.  we were served w 1 dozen of native oysters pretty quickly, It was quite a thrill to watch bar/rawtenders (yes, i just made up this word) cracking up our oysters in front of us. oh my goodness, those oysters are as good as it can get me, they're combine of med and large shells, not too small, so fresh and juicy we ended up ordered another half a dozen. The clams look really fresh as well but i had to resist them to save our stomach for dinner.  Raw bar also serve beers, short list of white and red wines. Overall, the service was quick and friendly, yes it could be tourisy and crowded but i'd love to come back here again for more oysters.

Love it here!  As a big wine drinker, and somewhat of a wine snob, this is a great place to go, get great wine suggestions (and not the most expensive ones either) - the staff typically know their regulars and will make suggestions for them.  They have a great beer selection also, and they don't sell cheap wine - so you don't have to sift through a collection of disgusting wine to get to the good stuff!  While they do have a lot of wines that are inexpensive, they are great with avoiding the cheap stuff.  Their wines of the month are great - they always have a selection of wine for around 5-10-/bottle, and they tend to be interesting and great wines to try.  Their quarterly sales rock - 20% off cases - and they have great cheeses and cured meats as well (salami, etc.).  The one criticism I have is that the people who ring you up tend to not be the nicest.  But who cares. This place is awesome.

When you go there, do not expect a fancy Thai restaurant. This is a very cozy family owned casual Thai restaurant, the owner is always very friendly and nice. The food is authentic, home style Thai food. Their Bangkok curry chicken is very good. We also always get pad seew(stair fried rice noodle). Some dishes can be quite sweet, but they will always adjust for your likes. When we ask for spicy, they really make it spicy with lots of red peppers! 

We keep going back there because it's just a nice comfortable little place to be and we know what to expect. If you want an upscale fancy Thai food I recommend maenam on 4th or one of those bigger Thai restaurants downtown(like sala Thai).

Short & sweet:

Service: 3
Coffee: 3.5
Pastries: 4 (Ham + Cheese Croissant!)
Wait time: 4
Price: 4
Cleanliness of bathroom: n/a


I only recently started to go to Espresso Roma Cafe. My sister and I went once a couple years ago; an employee there saw us, threw a fit about us being Asians. She told us to go back to where we came from and made other rude, ignorant comments. We were given apologies and extra punches on our little frequent user cards... and yet, for some strange reason, I didn't really want to go back. (She was a little hazy in the head, we were told.)

Anyway. 

I went back, having such a magnanimous soul. The off-kilter employee was still there, but she didn't say anything. And to my surprise, I found out that they offer 8oz of wonderful brewed coffee for just a dollar. Perfection. (8oz happens to be the perfect amount of coffee for one sitting, if you didn't know.) 

Espresso Roma is the size of my left pinky. Men, if there is a woman (or another human being) you're lusting after, bring her here. By sheer necessity, you'll end up invading each others' personal space. If breathing on your ladyfriend is your idea of a good time, make sure you shower the day of: she'll be able to smell you too. Because it happens to be small, the vibe is homey but a little claustrophic; I'd never be able to read/ study/ talk/ hang out here. 

The service is all right - the workers have the cool, hippie-hipster thing going on (how Boulder!). I do feel a little out of it sometimes and am tempted to return sporting a semi-bedhead look with a wicked tattoo. I'd also get a nose piercing and talk philosophy while smoking pot. 

If you do go into Espresso Roma, try their stuffed croissants; I've had the ham + cheese (warmed) and it was delicious. I also hear their zucchini bread is good. 

Hooray for the $1 8oz coffee!

I've been getting my art on lately. 

Atlanta has a fantastic art scene actually, and I'm really beginning to re-appreciate art like I used to back when I was a teenager. I become a member of the High off and on. This year I'm off, but its okay because they actually have one free day a month... its crazy packed on those days, but hey it's free. 

LOCATION:
Off Peachtree, its hard to miss... its a huge white building. Parking is $12 or you can try to park on the street somewhere and walk. There are also lots off 14th street that are about $5/$6 you'll have to walk a little, but if you aren't in a rush and want to save the extra cash thats an option. (there's also some down 12th street, and one on crescent ave). Oh and don't forget you can also take marta... it's "smarta", lol. 

PRICE:
$20 tickets, $8 for audio tour. If you plan to go more than a few times you may come out cheaper just buying the membership. 

EXHIBITS/ART/ETC:
There are the pieces they always have and there are the special exhibits. I've been to the last two main ones-- KAWS and GO WEST. I can't wait for the car one next month. 

It's a beautiful space, a white blank stone canvas ready to adorn itself with art from around the world... as a museum should be. 

They also have jazz nights here each month which are fun too!

Visit there website for more details on the current happenings, high.org

I'd give this place 3.5 stars if I could but I'll be generous. This is a really fun place. The donuts are fun, the gold glitter sprayed brick outside is fun, the excitement is fun, the box is fun, etc etc. This is totally a tourist trap if you like cutesy semi unique things - making me a giant sucker for this place. 

I came here on Sunday of Labor day weekend so naturally the line was ridiculous. I'm sure its normally ridiculous though. I spent an hour in line. For donuts. Kind of crazy but I knew I was in for it. We had stopped by around noon but decided to walk around and get coffee first, and then came back around 330. The line was still the same length but thats what I was expecting. They really could use some signage or a greeter to direct people to where the line starts. It was confusing and I wasn't the only one who felt that way. I also feel like it would have been more useful to post the menu on the window in addition to their sign telling you to check the menu online. 

This place is cash only, but there is an atm if you forgot. I got a dozen donuts that I picked myself and it cost me 25 dollars and some change. I didn't get any sort of discount for getting a dozen, so don't feel pressured into getting a dozen unless you want that many. 

Voodoo Doll - I was surprised by how much I liked this. I'm not usually one for filled donuts, but this was good. The chocolate and the raspberry married well together. I was glad that I got two of these.

Bacon Maple Bar- Yuck. One of the people in front of me in line was raving about this and how you had to get one. I figured I'd like it because I LOVE maple bars. I like bacon. I like when my maple syrup gets on my bacon. But I did not like this. I had half of it and threw it away. Wish I had only got one of these.

Fruit Loops - I was really excited about this one but the fruit loops were stale. Buh. =[

Marshall Mathers - Ok I had to get this one. Plus I love m&ms. Very sweet, but what I expected.

Memphis Mafia Donut - I really liked this one, possibly my favorite out of the bunch. It was also really sweet and intense though, this ended up getting eaten in four different segments. I think this was sort of a banana fritter with peanut butter drizzle and chocolate chips. I'm not usually a peanut butter person but this was great.

Chocolate Orea and Old Dirty Bastard were pretty standard and what I was expecting.

I had a couple more that I gave away because I prioritized the others for eating myself. I really wanted the peach fritter, but they were out and I was super disappointed about that. As far as service the girl didn't really smile but she wasn't grumpy with me - but I also rattled off what I wanted and didn't stand there trying to decide. I mean really we were in line for an hour, the menu is available online, and some people seemed to have no idea what they wanted. 

The donuts overall were really delicious, there were tons of fun options, and for specialty baked goods I felt like the prices were pretty reasonable. Don't feel pressured into getting a full dozen unless you want that many. Don't forget your cash, and be prepared for a stupid long line. If you like donuts and silly cutesy things give this a shot at least once.

Great place to refuel during a shopping session at Millenia. Located inside the mall at the main entrance, this is a convenient location... and a great option for people looking for a table-service dining experience instead of standard food court fare.

I stopped by here recently with a couple of girlfriends (my bridesmaids) after a very productive shopping day where we found bridesmaid dresses. To celebrate, we figured this might be a great place to visit for a little bubbly and light bites. It was a great selection! While the mall was very busy with holiday shoppers AND Brio had 40-minute wait for a table, we were able to immediately find a high-top table in the bar area, so we sat down immediately. 

We split a bottle of prosecco and then ordered soups and salads. I had a cup of the Italian wedding soup, which was hearty, with plentiful portions of sausage. We also devoured the complimentary bread, which was delicious. Everything really hit the spot!

Service was quick, despite the busy scene. At one point, the wrong soup was delivered to our table by a food runner, but the error was corrected immediately.

Overall, pretty sold dining experience!

You can find a whole bunch of pho on Buford Highway but Pho Dai Loi stands out for their overall tastiness. Their pho is cooked just right. The noodles are always al dente and the broth is flavorful. 

Pho is not the only winner here. Try their vermicelli dishes (called "bun" in Vietnamese) and you'll love it. The  rice vermicelli noodles, mixed with vegetable, serve with your choice of BBQ pork, shrimp or lemon grass chicken. I prefer the BBQ pork topping because it gives a balance flavor to the dish. The rice dished (or "com") are also a good choice here.

These guys get an A for takeout.  Day 5 of Snow 2011, we ordered online for 7 of us.  As soon as we completed online, we called to confirm.  They had already started our order!  

At pick up time (15 mins later), they were jammed and our order was ready.  All seven were there and the order was 95% correct.  This is much higher than one order I've placed at a drive thru.  

Moe's is consistent in quality & taste.  It was good (salads w/chicken, taco, burrito) especially since we had not eaten out in @ a week.  A good lunch place and I hear they are adding organic options - yeah!

This brewery was a little tucked away and hard to find but I definitely consider it a hidden gem. I'm not much of a beer drinker so I ordered their herbal cocktail from the cocktail trail and my boyfriend ordered one of their beers.
It was a Saturday night around 6pm and the place was very surprisingly slow. As soon as I walked up to the bar I was able to order and I was able to easily find a seat anywhere I wanted. So definitely no complaints here. I chose to sit outside in their beer garden. I loved how quiet the place is, very easy to just hangout and have conversations. They had a food truck available and they look as though they constantly have rotating ones. 
I personally loved my cocktail. It was very pretty and delicious. The butterfly pea ice cube was my favorite part and I'm glad that they didn't overpower the cocktail with lavender. My boyfriend liked his beer but said he wished they had a better selection because the ones they offered were t quite his style!

Describing Double Happiness to my boss, a Taiwan native, I said it felt like I was in a China Town, in a movie, in a bar where the Chinese Mafia hang out in a hidden back room. 

This place is freakin' sweet! This is why I feel like I can ignore all the issues we encountered on our Tuesday night visit. First, their website says they close Tuesdays at 9:30PM. The sign in their window says differently, I believe 2AM. They also have lots of funky Chinese character lights in the windows to let you know they're there. We knew they were open because we were going to see a friend in a band that was playing there. 

Second, no one could use the bar because they had just set it's resin and no one could touch it while it was curing. The poor bartenders were kept on their toes as people still tried to put drinks on the bar. Because the bar was unable to be used, that cut their seating in half. Obvs, this is a temporary issue! 

Third, for some reason, they were unable to take credit cards. Luckily, I had cash.

Fourth, some staff seemed confused about the band getting set up, like they don't do it often. 

The stage set up was really awkward, but we got the one of two tables they had set up. My friend remarked it looked like they got it out of the dumpster.  I didn't care, it worked. There were also some random covered long tables that served no obvious purpose. Also, dispite this place being relatively new, it was really dusty. Most of their decor was covered in dust. Seriously, check out the Buddha by Fresh Street. 

Bottom line, this place is really cool. Fresh Street is a great addition to this space. My friend got a bulgogi rice bowl and said it was freakin' amazing.  You order and pay at their section of counter and they bring it to you. It definitely smelled really really yummy. Well drinks were $5, they charged a $1 for my club soda, which is pretty good. 
It's got some cozy upstairs seating for dining, the bar for hanging out, and the stage area, which if no one is engaged in the band or DJ, would be overflow space. When were were there it was practically empty, but we still had a great time. 

I'm looking forward to going back to this sweet hangout spot. I hope they address some of their "issues" in the mean time.

Not much chance of beating Amy D to a new restaurant opening, so I settle for the next best thing - "Hey, you wanna meet up there?" I did hold the door open as she entered, so technically she was here first. You either have manners or you don't. 

But Karma will reward you with occasional moments, and this new Hanabi is one of them. If you're familiar with the original location on Anderson Lane, you'll walk in here, go "Wut?" and then mic-drop. It's a remarkable renovation, the interior is deceptively huge, and it has the most complete array of seating options I've ever seen - booths, tabletops, banquette, counter, and party rooms. There's also a unique section that looks exactly like Japanese sitting tables designed for Anglos. Wut? You'll know it when you see it. 

I sat at the sushi bar because I enjoy watching Chef Choo work. The Oyako app with wasabi mayo is fried and comes from the kitchen, but it's a pleasure watching a pro make your sashimi plate. What caught me by surprise here was his "Oil & Haemul" dish - I don't even know what that means, but it was stunning, beautifully presented, and a total delight to eat. 

I tend to shy away from "who has the best sushi" debates, I think it's just easier to agree on which places to avoid. So I'll put it this way: If you're up north here at the Gateway complex, with the need for impeccable Japanese-themed food and service, in a casually upscale ambiance, then start spreading the news - Hanabi has opened their doors for you.

Mike is awesome!  Was welcoming from the second I stepped in.  I was the only one in there for a moment so we chatted about how he was from Chicago and has been here for 11 years and was like...that's it, Orlando needs some Chicago flavor.  Seriously, after having the staple beef sandwich, I am so glad Mike put his foot down.

I went with the regular Italian beef and subbed the peppers with onions, im a sucker for fried onions.  I also topped the amazing meaty deliciousness with a thick coat of melted sharp provolone cheese.  Score!

Now, being from Philadelphia I am a cheesesteak snob and when I compare those type of sandwiches here to the ones in Philly...mu #1 complaint is... Where's The Beef?? As it seems that anywhere south of PA they seem to skimp you on the meat so I usually end up ordering double meat.  Yes, a female ordering double meat...looks so sexy I am sure.  Well here, at What's Your Beef?  They load you up with the meaty goodness so no need to order double meat because that would be basically ordering an entire other sandwich...which actually here, isn't a bad thing.

The meat was just so tender and juicy, it had a little kick which was a nice surprise.  The roll was as awesome as the portion of meat, crispy on the outside and soft on the inside.  Being this was my cherry-pop for an Italian beef, it was not as messy as I was expecting.  The au jus was perfect, moistened up the roll perfectly.  I believe I inhaled my sandwich it was so good and like I told Mike, if I was not heading out downtown, I would have gotten another one.  It was THAT good.  

I know I will be heading back to grad another Italian beef but I am also going to sample my usual go-to...Meatball Sub!!!

Their ingredients are all Chicago style so you must stop in to get this great taste of a northern city here in our awesome southern town...Thanks to Mike and his wife for opening such a great spot in DT Orlando!

This is my favorite thrift store. They have quality brands for the best price, good selection, friendly service, and they have a cat in the store. I love cats!

Once I found a latte machine, brand new in the box for 25 bucks, but last time I was there the household section was a little lacking. They always have fantastic deals on the sale rack outside. Designer tops for 2 bucks? YAY! Another time I picked up a pair of barely used designer leather boots for 5 bucks.

The people who work here are very kind and the service is great. They also guarantee their work. I'm told that a stain in the upholstery can actually resurface because it sometimes runs deep in the cushioning. So when my staining resurfaced I called and they retreated it for free. It's expensive for my budget,but as a treat to myself it was worth it.   My only complaint is that there was greasiness left on the plastic surfaces of the interior which I had to wipe down. Also I noticed a few crevices that still had some dirt. This could have vacuumed up with a small device, which sadly I don't own.

Having grown up down the street from The Scarlet Oak Tavern, I was a little reluctant to try the restaurant since memories of the Whiton House with it's floral wall paper and stuffy clientele still resounded in my memory. I am very happy I gave this place a shot. It was my mother's birthday and she wanted to check it out after hearing positive reviews from her friends. We stopped in for lunch, my father and I split a salad and both had pizzas. My mother ordered the skewered shrimp. All of our food was delicious. The hostess and our waitress were professional and friendly. The ambience was great and the decor is tasteful with a modern chic. It's a place you can go with your family or with a date. The best part of the meal was that when the staff learned it was my mother's birthday, they brought her a blueberry cobbler on the house. I would return in a heartbeat, a nice little gem on the South Shore.

First off, what's not to like about this place. It has been around for a number of years now and is well-known by most of Boston's residents. Conveniently located in the Back Bay on Boylston Street, this venue is a great selection for tourists and residents alike. Whether sitting inside or outside on the patio (which often has heat lamps available), I've always had good services and great food.

For whatever reason, I have always started off with the lobster mac n' cheese when I am here. It is a generous portion with large macaroni, generous portions of lobster and a golden brown bread crumb topping. if shared between 2 people, this usually works well as an appetizer. The jumbo lump crab cakes are also a good option as a starter. With two large cakes seated on lettuce and the fresh fruit salsa, the combination of the crab and sweet salsa is excellent. In terms of salads, I would highly recommend the Traditional Hearts of Iceberg. It is a large wedge of iceberg lettuce covered with bacon and tomatoes. If you dislike blue cheese, you can also opt for 1000 Island dressing instead. 

In terms of entrees, I have always gone with a steak (of course) and have chosen either the typical filet or the Filet au Poivre (pepper crusted). I typically have the steaks prepped medium-rare. For sides, I would recommend the Grilled Asparagus with Hollandaise sauce, the Creamed Fresh Spinach, the lobster mac n' cheese (of course) or the mashed potatoes. 

The ambiance at this place is great for romantic dinners, a quick bite with a friend when shopping on Boylston or Newbury, a business lunch/dinner, or a celebration dinner. They do a great job to accompany larger parties when you call in advance and the service has never been disappointing. I would absolutely make this venue part of your steak house exploration in Boston.

Cuba Libre is beautiful. I still can not get over all the detail that went into this restaurant. The first three stars are for the decor alone. 
Other than being aesthetically pleasing, the service here was fantastic. Our server was on top of his game, explaining everything in detail, helping us decide on entrees, making suggestions for drinks. 
Then comes the food- it was average. The appetizer was too much, too heavy, too greasy. It tasted good, but then again, most things covered in oil and cream do. My friend ordered the Churrasco a la Cubana. It had a nice flavor, but was tough (not what I expected for that price) and I ordered a rice, chicken and chorizo dish. I am not a fan of smokey flavors, and this was way too smokey for me. We had flan for dessert. It was nice, cool, creamy and the side of berries balanced it perfectly. It was a nice end to a nice experience.

Nothing quite compares to the feeling I get when I walk into a good beauty supply strore.  I just love row after row of items geared towards beautification.  Not all of stores do the job properly.  Some are too small or too cluttered.  Some need to get the lighting together (lighting is very important).  Some don't have enough merchandise.  

This Beauty Master suffers not from the above afflictions.  Large, clean, neat, spacious rows, appropriate lighting, and all the things a girl could want and need to look like the Georgia peach that she is.  

Did that sweet Asian lady that works in the wig section whip out a flat iron and style that lace front that that lady just bought?  Hells yeah she did.  

The people that work here are always friendly and helpful and I love that about this place also.  I'm a regular.

This is the first Whit's location I have had the pleasure of stopping at, and while it's a tiny place with minimal seating, that's no reason to turn a cheek without trying some of their tasty flavors of frozen custard. 

Frozen custard, frozen yogurt, ice-cream, italian ice.... yeah, there are a lot of frozen treats being thrown at you in today's world of frozen desserts, but Whit's, despite it being a small chain... has captured my tastebuds, and I am in love. 

My only sadness is the weekly flavors that come and go, and some I wish would just stay forever like their Buckeye Flavor, but even if you're not a flavor enthusiast, Whit's still carries the basics of Chocolate or Vanilla. 

It's worth a stop if you're recovering after a tasty dinner in Delaware looking to satisfy a sweet tooth attack, or even if you're about looking at the shops and need a break. There are plenty of public park benches on the sidewalks to rest on, and take in the ambiance of the old Delaware buildings.

We had the pleasure of visiting RusTeak this past weekend.  Great menu selection-food and wine.  Food was great! My husband got a burger and I got the fish sandwich-delicious!  We also got a piece of cheesecake to take home and it was really yummy!!!  We sat at a table in the bar-next time I will sit at a table in the restaurant.  The server was good put pulled to a lot of tables.  We ordered the shrimp appetizer-but he forgot to put it in :(. We will have to visit again to try it-the server raved about it-so we are looking forward to trying it.  Can't wait for y'all to come to Clermont-we will be regulars for sure!

In the past 3 years we've stayed at this hotel to celebrate the New Year's 2014,2015 and just recent 2016. And I just took the time now to make a review on it. Best recommended place to stay no matter where you end up, either Disney World or Universal Studios here in Orlando. Just a great location. When you wake up in the morning there's breakfast downstairs that start from 6AM to 9AM. And in the afternoon a Kick Back Dinner Meal from 5:30PM to 7PM. Typical food you would eat so take advantage of it! If your Vegetarian for some such and wouldn't like the food, there's a Whole Foods right across the street. And for pop-corn lovers. Yes! There a pop-corn machine right next to the elevator. There's a Indoor/Outdoor Pool, and a Mini-Gym. All I can say! Great service from the crew that works here and keep up the good work! Never stop improving. My second home! We'll be surely back in 2017!

Number #1 Con.. Don't do laundry on the 7th Floor the Dryer doesn't work that good on one cycle. Clothes damp.

Overall, a great experience, and I'm looking forward to trying more! 

The cons: the waiting room is small and there's not much seating. Also, we didn't start on time...maybe because they were putting clues back?

The pros: fun game, Ashley (our game master or whatever they're called!) was really friendly, patient, and gave helpful clues when we asked. We did the Rec Room; there were only 4 of us, and we almost figured the game out before we ran out of time. We definitely got waylaid by some "distractor" false clues, but we each had the satisfaction of figuring out at least one clue each.

Love this menu! It does poke in Texas justice. Definitely reminiscent of food trucks off the road in Hawaii. Always fresh fish. Probably the freshest I've had in ATX. Makes it worth the $14-$17 meal. My only gripe with this place is the setup is eh. They get really slammed and you can tell the kitchen staff is struggling to keep up (cannot blame them though, it gets crazy during rush hour) and then seating is just not ideal.  Also, I guess the beers are a lil overpriced for canned beer at such a casual spot. If the setup is going to stay the same, it warrants a $4 beer.

I feel like I have the right to actually review this place since I'm an actual China man. First of all, this place is pretty genuine... there's actually Chinese employees here!! You can barely understand their Engrish, and that's how you know it's going to be good food. When you walk in, it doesn't look like the nicest place but at least you can watch them cook everything so you know it's safe. Best time to come is when it's busy so you know the food is fresh. And make sure you read your fortune in your cookie!! You can actually learn Chinese!!

This place is a little hidden due to the minimalistic exterior decor and it's located on a small street albeit across an extemely popular restaurant. They have a large wine list and quite a few unique beers and cool cocktails. Beers start at $7 and cocktails at $10, which are typical for this type of social tapas style and western-traditional type of restaurant. There is a large seating area with private tables and large community tables. They have a unique menu along with old favourites; please take a look at their menu for a better idea.

Go for: cool atmosphere, a nice list of liquor and a relatively "fresh" menu, socializing over flavourful dishes 

Don't go for: everything being perfect as some dishes are a little plain

Great little breakfast restaurant. The food is very flavorful and never had a bad thing on their menu. Their egg Benedict's and hash out of this world good! It's got the classic decor inside and plenty of seats. The wait usually is pretty good but there is really no space to really watt. But now you're able to reserve your name on the app for the next available table and that's a game changer in my opinion because you've able to put in your name on the way there or wait in your car. 

The only reason they're getting four stars is due to the parking lot. If you're going on the weekend it's a little stressful getting a spot

I would say that this place is definitely a winner winner chicken dinner! However, some kinks need to be worked out. Now, down to the nitty gritty. 

-The wait was about 15 mins to the cashier. There was a line outside of the door and a short line inside. It made sense because the area where you order is not that big. If they didn't have this system in place, everyone would be squished in a confined area. 

-We waited about another 15 mins until we received our food. They give you a buzzer and will track you down at your table which is fantastic seeing as there is basically no room inside to wait around. The only issue I noticed is that the seating is so staggered between the outside and inside, that the limited wait staff is zipping around all of these tables until they find the correct number on the buzzer. It's a good idea in theory, but having four waiters come to your table with the wrong food was a little imposing. Again, the system is not the wait staff's fault it's just the way it is until maybe the kinks are worked out.

-Now the food. I had the three piece chicken tender meal (combo) with fries and a drink. I will say that my chicken tenders were not plump and juicy. They were thin, the breading slightly brittle, and not exactly what I expected. The dipping sauces (the meal comes with your choice of two) I chose were the peri peri sauce and the garlic parm sauce. The peri peri was a warm heat that stayed in the back of the throat. It had a strong red pepper taste (like Sabra red hummus). I liked it even though I'm not a spicy fan but do NOT eat this if your stomach is sensitive. The garlic parm was sharp and there was a prominent garlic flavor. I was disappointed in the tenders; decent flavor (mainly salt and pepper and probably another spice I don't know) but not plump. If I go to a chicken Guy, I want plump! The sauce and mixing these two sauces made the tenders taste pretty good. 

-My fiancé ordered the chicken guy classic sandwich. Now that was T-H-I-C-K! It was reminiscent of a very famous chicken place's sandwich. The bun was buttery and slightly toasted. It came with cheddar cheese. We both agreed that a lukewarm square of a cheddar cheese did not jive well with a crispy and warm chicken breast. The condiments it came with (LTOP lettuce tomato onion pickle) were okay. I personally thought that the temperature differences in the sandwich kind of took away from the big bite. 

-The fries were lackluster. Reminiscent of Wendy's fries. The fried pickles were excellent--crispy and salty. The buttermilk ranch the pickles came with was creamy and definitely had a homemade taste. 

-OUR FAVORITE: the Cinnamon Toast Crunch milkshake!!!! Crunchy bits of Cinnamon Toast Crunch and a creamy vanilla base made it a sip from heaven. It was topped with whipped cream and crushed cinnamon toast for garnish. Delicious and DANGEROUSLY good. 

-Misc: packaging and branding was super cute. It's fun, colorful, and original. Other reviews show the example. Most eat with their eyes and I thought that their packaging was thoughtful on this concept. 

-More seating needed! We had to sit outside. Inside was ridiculously crowded. I think that the seating choices should have been more booth like; I noticed lots of families struggling to seat themselves at the small round tables. The place itself is pretty small though so it's hard to get around. 

-Overall, try it Guys! It's pretty good. $29 got us two decent meals with drinks and a milkshake. Fun experience.

After arriving in Vancouver we were cold and hungry and went straight to Japadog for a hot dog with Japanese toppings. I wanted to go there after I saw Anythony Bourdain bite into one on NR. I picked this location because it had seating and was close to our hotel.  We ordered the Okonomi Kurobota, Love Meat Dog and Butter and Shoyu fries.

The Okonomi dog had the nice snap to it when biting into it and I loved how it had lots of shaved bonito flakes. I topped it off with the wasabi mayo and made it even better. The Love Meat Dog had yakiniku meat, cheese and mayo on top of a pork dog and was also delicious and filling. The butter and shoyu fries were okay, it just tasted like salted fries to me.

I'm glad I tried Japadog, now I can cross it off my list. I'm not sure if I need to eat Japadog every time I go back to Vancouver but maybe every other time.

As a local, I enjoy coming here from time to time. I've never had to wait, the sushi rolls are flavorful, and the service is pretty decent. I especially like the brown rice option for my sushi since I'm attempting to be "healthy". Basically any roll with a lot of ingredients in it will be a blessing to your taste buds. The more ingredients the better the roll. Keep an eye out for those with tempura or eel in them such as the Alligator roll, for those are especially good.  I wouldn't say that this is an authentic Japanese restaurant but it's pretty well done for a non-japanese owner. Honestly, if you're craving for lots of flavor and fish Genki Ya is the way to go.

All Star Burger is by far my favorite place to get a burger in the Lake Travis area!

There menu has goody variety and there are options to make everyone happy! My favorite is The West...it comes with cream cheese and is just so good!! I also absolutely love their sweet potato fries! They are a definite must try! 

On my most recent visit the burger seemed thinner than I remember, but it was still good. 

The price is the big downside of All Star Burger. My burger and fries came out to $12.75 which really seems like a lot. I wanted to add onions and tomato to my burger but at $0.75 for each I decided to skip it! I hate how expensive it is, but just reserve my visits for "treats."

This is a super cute cafe, home to many locals in the area. Their specialty is super simple, super delicious, organic ingredients. 

FOOD--
Warm Brie cheese plate - the cheese is warm, comes with super cold grapes and nicely sliced whole pear. Fruits were sweet and the cold was a nice contrast with the warm cheese. They also slice and lightly butter baguette for you. It was warm and crispy! Great to share (or not!) would order again.
Simple egg, avocado, toast plate - the eggs were bright orange, that's how fresh they were! Really simple, really good.
Iced coffee - hit the spot

SERVICE--
staff is nice. Quick. 

AMBIANCE--
Casual. No AC. Small groups better. 

I'd be back!

Never thought I'd find Memphis BBQ in Texas but the county line is serving up just that! I can't stand sweet BBQ sauce so I was thrilled to find this place. Food is good- personal favorites are peppered turkey and lean brisket. I hate coleslaw but not theirs, it's so fresh and crunchy, potato salad is good too. Only complaint is that they only serve limes- no lemons they said they were "too expensive". So no lemon for teas or water which is a bit ridiculous. If I'm paying $20 a plate I'd like to have the option of lemon water. Jesus even subway has lemons. Overall good eats.

place to go for the Bahn Mi. it had a lot of flavor but was still refreshing. they had an awesome pho and bahn mi combo that my boyfriend got but just getting the sandwich is cheap and more worth it. 
i got the bun bo hue and tried my.boyfriends pho. both wasnt bad but the flavor was a lot more milder than other pho places. 
i give it four stars cause our waiter was nice (quiet but nice) and the bahn mis were the bomb. 

parking is ample and the place is a little bit tucked in the plaza next to the gas station. 
price is super affordable and it may be also the bowls of pho are a bit smaller than other places.

This is a very popular place... at least on the weekends.  We waited for 2 hours which might sound bad however the waiting area is very nice and we enjoyed drinks and appetizers (spring rolls---very good) while waiting.  We committed to waiting that long because the food is truly wonderful.  And what a great variety of dishes.  It's Asian fusion (I think that's the right way to describe it) and is spicy or creamy or all sorts of things.  Very interesting selections.

The place is decorated very well and utilize all sorts of different tables and counters.  And the place is loud.  I mean really loud.   They boom the music and it makes it difficult to interact verbally with your party.   You end up yelling a lot.  I suspect they do that for the cool factor.  I think I'm finally an "old guy" in that it bothered me but that's the only thing that bothered me.   Service is great, the food is an adventure, and the restaurant is very nice.   Put in the ear plugs and get there.

This office is easy to locate and it's in a place with great parking (even though I got a ticket for not feeding the meter 2 extra minutes). I like the doctors and nurses here as well as the receptionists. My only complaint is that for an office so dead (the most I've seen in the waiting room were two patients) the wait time on the phone is ridiculous. It would help to have an automated telephone system. Whoever handles the answering service also needs to be trained in customer service to fix their attitude.

Moody's gets 4 stars from me for being a consistently tasty place for a quick bite.  It is the kind of place I enjoy going to when I don't want to be fussy about what I am going to have for dinner.  The chicken shawarma is moist and super flavorful.and the portions are quite large.  I must say some people are more precise and generous at making the dishes with the perfect ratio of meat/falafel, tahini, and veggies than others.  Overall, a great option for a quick meal or a late night bite!  Happy eating! : )

Oh man what a dangerous discovery this place is for me. I recently had my first meal there (dinner) and was thoroughly impressed by the experience. We arrived just after six and there was absolutely no wait, although it got much busier within the hour. Like, crowd in the lobby busy. A lot of people on here have complained about the noise, but we actually had no problem with the volume, although were seated by the windows with sound-absorbing cushions above us.

Onto the food: we ordered four dishes and that was just enough to fill up two girls. We had the sunomono, the Kome chasuke, the tako-wasa, and the love for sale roll. Everything was great, but we particularly enjoyed the chasuke (and emptied out the entire teapot of broth they brought alongside it) and I really loved the tako-wasa. The food was fresh and I only wish we could have ha a few more items from the menu!

Service was very good and at the end of our meal, our waiter brought out our check and let us know that Kome had taken care of the chasuke since it had taken so long to come out (we honestly hadn't even noticed since we were snacking away at everything else). I really appreciated how seriously they took their customer service and am pretty excited about the fact that our whole meal came out to $20 (for two people!!) as a result. I expect to spend much more than that on my next visit,though.

Overall, great experience and will definitely be going back ASAP.
(four stars until I have had more experiences there to match my first impression)

I go to Jeromy for haircut and highlights.  So far I've gotten one highlight (great great great- natural and bright but expensive- $135) and one haircut (pretty good, wasn't in-love, but then again my hair is dry and thin and impossible- $50).  Jeromy made me an americano coffee and told me funny stories about all the times he's gotten a concussion.  I like it here, i feel like I'm supporting a small east austin establishment that is really worth it.  When I look around everyone (mostly young women clientele) seems to be getting good cuts and leaving happy.

It's relaxing to walk in there and have everyone be friendly and hip and to know you're about to be taken care of.  

I liked the online booking system at first, but for my cut next week it booked me for the wrong date and time, so beware.

This has been a hometown favorite of mine since I was a kid. So my review might be a little bias but I'll try to keep it as real as possible. 

Recently, my fiancé and I hosted a small engagement party here with about twenty guests. Our waitress was phenomenal. She helped me get the tables set up, stayed very attentive to piling plates, took pictures for us, and took some time to congratulate us.

The Food here is mostly southern home-style cooking. They have a little something for everyone. I'm a huge fan of their salad bar and fried chicken. They also have a carving station that serves Ham, Turkey, or roast beef depending on when you come in.

An added note, the drinks are included in your meal and they are self-serve so you can get refills.

THE BAD:

One of my guests had requested some shredded cheese for his salad and the staff that he asked told him they don't serve shredded cheese. They gave him a bowl full of shredded cheese from the kitchen but I was shocked to see that they didn't have it on the bar anymore. Who serves tacos and a salad bar with NO shredded cheese?

This place is as unique as they come for a diner. The atmosphere is very hippy and the decor is politically charged. They have a little bit of everything. There's a stage for musicians, a lounge area, and bar. They have a breakfast and afternoon menu. 

I normally get Vic's Breakfast there which is your basic 2 eggs, sausage/bacon, hash browns, and toast. The bread is always fresh and delivered from a local bakery. The highlight of the meal is the hash browns. They mix in a little bit of sweet corn. Delicious.

The best seats are at the bar. The place has a great crowd of regulars. The bar is where you can usually find some interesting conversation and a great place to read the morning paper. The staff is very friendly and nice to talk with.

Key information to know. Don't wait until your super hungry to go. On a busy morning it can take quite a while to get your food. The place is regularly packed on weekend mornings. 

Vic's is an experience more then the food. It's a local staple for the neighborhood.

The burgers here really are delicious, with quality ingredients all around.  

However, why oh why did they have to tease me by including potato chips with the burger and not fries, and then not allowing me to pay extra to get fries instead???  This makes no sense.  Essentially then, you can pay extra to get both chips AND fries (dumb) or not pay extra and just have chips (unsatisfying).  Really, getting fries and only fries with your burger should not be a difficult thing, dammit!

Still, if I'm craving a good burger this is the first place I'll turn to in the area, as the saying goes, "you can't beat their meat."

I haven't tried the frappes, sweet potato fries or onion rings.  I plan to try them all soon.

I went here for dinner with coworkers while visiting BVN. 
I love the Peruvian take on dinner, you always get fries with your meal in addition to rice. I ordered the shrimp saltado and it was very flavorful. It paired well with my purple corn drink, which may sound suspect if you're American but I enjoyed it and recommend you try it. It's a sweet drink though, so be prepared to drink water along with it if you're not a fan of sweet drinks. 
Service was good. There's nothing pretentious about the restaurant, the decor is very basic but clean. Enjoy the food and the folks who work here. 
I'd definitely eat here again if I'm in the area.

Delicious food, great portions, and a cozy atmosphere.
If you want to get in on the weekend, be prepared to wait at least a half hour. We have waited up to and hour for both brunch and dinner. Plan to put your name in early and go for a walk or grab coffee down the street, since they don't take reservations. It's definitely worth the wait! 
The bottomless french press coffee is superb, and everything on the 12 dollar brunch menu is worth trying.

After years of suffering with asthma, allergies and nosebleeds, I finally received the news that I needed Endoscopic Sinus Surgery. I put it off for 3 or 4 years, because everyone I asked about it advised me not to do it. After having the worst nosebleed  (it took an hour to control), and 2 days of nasal packing, I knew I needed something to change. 

Dr. Joshua Downie assured me that while all surgeries have risks, a septoplasty and turbinate reduction would help. I had my surgery 2 weeks before Christmas 2015. 

My recovery period was not that bad. For the first week, it's important to take all of your meds and rinse your sinuses ON TIME! The antibiotics, pain meds and steriods do a number on your tummy. But lots of soup, smoothies, jello, pudding and Icees will keep you full.

Keep plenty of lip balm. A light swab of mineral oil and your saline solution every hour or so will keep your nose moist.

After day 3, I could tell the immediate difference. It's been almost 10 months, and I haven't had an upper respiratory infection or sinus infection. I still have a runny nose associated with my allergies, but an occasional neti pot rinse and Zyrtec do the trick every time.

Dr. Downie is young, efficient, and knows what he's doing. You will love him and won't regret any treatment he recommends.

If you aren't going to beat yourself up the next day about how much you spent on sushi, then this is the place.  Not even in NYC have we paid $18 for a Spicy Tuna roll.  However, it was great and well worth it.  One thing that wasnt so good was the avocado ball with spicy salmon.    It tasted like a spicy cheese on top with little salmon inside.  

Salmon nigiri was good, but small and $6 for 2 of them which isnt too bad.  Also, they Spicy yellowtail was good, also $18.

This is a once a month type of place and well worth it if you can handle the sticker shock.  Will be back

Oh yeah Baby, knock it out of the park.

Really didn't know about this place until this week. Well, it's a good summer to make up for lost time.  

The night I went, you get a 2$ dollar R&B pint (one per sandwich) with your cheesesteak - WIN.  The cheesesteaks are themselves are a bit on the pricier side but you quickly forget about the prepaid cost once you sink your teeth in and drench your hands in SAYCE!

I will be back.  I will bring many friends that eat sandwiches and dont drink beer so I can triple up on those pints. =P

Gator's is a solid three something from me for having one of the area's better burgers.  I don't know how they do it, but they do it and that's all that matters :)

Of all the swamp house fish camp river restaurants on the St. Johns, this one's my favorite.  What a fun rustic spot to kick back and have a few beers on the river.

Expect slowish but friendly service and the occasional raucous and foul table of revelers.  Mosquitoes at dusk can be unbearable.  Hidden in the marina where the 415 bounces over the St. Johns.

Gator bites for tourists and locals alike lol

Bun bo hue (pronounced boom baw way) literally means beef noodle soup with origins from the city of Hue in Vietnam. If you're not already familiar with bun bo hue then I recommend you give it a try. Unless you're Vietnamese I'm going to make the assumption that most people were first introduced to Vietnamese food with pho and now they're interested in exploring more options. Teo serves a decent bowl of bun bo hue with really high quality ingredients. The broth is decent although not as spicy and flavorful as I like it. I usually add extra shrimp paste to mine. You have to ask for extra shrimp paste as they don't keep it on the table. The blood cubes are some of the best I've had. Super nice location and very clean. I've only ever had the bun bo hue here and I think they only serve two items, I think the other one is pho. They've never actually given me a menu when I come here so I'm not sure. And what's the deal with only giving me two napkins? I mean they're decent napkins and two is an adequate amount of napkins but I just like to have the option of more napkins. I don't want to be the guy that's always asking for more napkins so sometimes I'll just internally stew and then do nothing about it.

My first restaurant at Hollywood Studios. I'm excited!
