This place is one of the upscale dining spots in the Theme Park. I didn't take any chances so I made reservations for my party of 3 for an early dinner. Thank goodness because it seemed like it there was a considerable wait even though the place was not full. We checked in and waited a few minutes while they were preparing our table. While waiting I checked out the walls which are full of caricatures of family Hollywood stars. There's a ton of them so watch where you're going. Our buzzer went off and to our table we went. 

We sat in the Bamboo Room back in the back, a nice little private room. I love the decor and the intimacy of it. We all agreed that we wouldn't order entrees because we were still full from our lunch. I started off with a Margarita flight with the flavors of a Classic, Cherry, and Lemon I believe? Nothing bad about these drinks. I enjoyed them. i decided to get two appetizers. The first one was one of their offerings leftover from Thanksgiving so they might not have it any other time of the year: the Oyster and Brie Soup. I love oysters and I love brie so why not put them together? There are 3 fried oysters swimming in a creamy, brothy sea for cheesy goodness. Can you tell I loved it? The taste was very much melted brie and not like the taste of the spreadable cheese variety. Blech! I also ordered the Togarashi-Pumpkin Seed Crusted Ahi Tuna. I loved that this came with sushi-rice and seaweed on the side. Such a simple appetizer and just enough. It was very delicious.

I must came back and try an entree. Check them out!

Service is always friendly, and the food is consistent.  The chicken kashmiri and  malabar are awesome.  The tandoori chicken is great too - not dry like at most places, but not as much spice/flavor as I would like (it's basically just grilled chicken IMO).  The saag is good, but I personally prefer the saag at Clay Pit.  

The atmosphere is really comfortable and welcoming - great for dates or just hanging out with friends.  I love that they're BYOB and that they don't charge any fee for cups, which they could if they really wanted to.  Definitely one of my favorites in Austin.

I met up with some dear, old friends on a frigid Saturday night and I was hoping the meal would be as lovely as the company.  I was not disappointed.
We initially did some damage by getting a bunch of appetizers - short rib, scallops, bacon wrapped dates, beet sliders and the shrimp.  The short rib was saucy sweet and so tender, you could cut it with your fork.  I was so excited about the bacon wrapped dates (filled with goat cheese), I burnt the top of my mouth.  It was still bacon goodness worth burning your mouth over.  The beet sliders were interesting and I was trying to leave my comfort zone. I kind of liked it - it did not seem like a beet at all, really.  The scallops were good, but not my favorite of the bunch. I am not a shrimp person but be forewarned, they come with the heads still on and looks daunting for a novice (I heard they were yummy).
Believe it or not after all this goodness, we moved on to the dinner menu. I had their take on grilled cheese and tomato soup.  The grilled cheese was so simple but done with Vermont cheddar and an artisan bread. The tomato soup was light and creamy but not in a heavy way.  I opted to also share the "tater tots" - it is not the usual shredded potatoes but a mashed potato almost fritter -like. My friends split the venison dish -  this dish takes 25 minutes to prepare but apparently worth the wait.

Ate here today with my wife for lunch. We both enjoyed it. I had the Cashew Nut Tofu ($6.50) lunch special while my wife had the Red Curry ($7.50). Food quality was good. Service was good too. We ate around 1 pm. Food took only a few minutes and our server regularly kept our water glasses full. I realize there are several Thai places in Portland and especially in the Alberta area but I would recommend checking this place if you are in the neighborhood.

I love Waterloo for 3 perfectly valid reasons.
1. The playground. Great place for happy hour for those of us with energetic kids!
2. The happy hour prices are the shizzy! 50 cent wings, 2 dollar Texas Lemonades. The drinks are nice and stiff. I like.
3. They actually have a really good breakfast menu... decent. Nothing stands out other than the mimosas.

The food at Waterloo is nothing to write home about. I've never gotten sick off of it, not to downplay it, it's good.  That's always a plus. We keep coming back because we can relax while the kids are having fun and the atmosphere is friendly. We can get a good buzz and still behave like responsible adults by providing our child with a social experience. Thank you Waterloo SPM!

I was pleasantly surprised the first time I came here.  For some reason, I thought this was some sort of Asian restaurant.  Far from it!

This is a very laid back place with a large menu that consistently pleases.  Lots of options for lunch and it's a great place to come if you're nearby on the weekend.  I like coming here to eat on the patio on Sunday (well, I've only done it twice, but I feel like it's something that I would like to do more often).

Nice employees and good bar service.  I give it two thumbs up (and four stars).

Located in the heart of Steveston serving up a fancy brunch menu that's beyond just breakfast food. Spacious patio that's fairly secluded from the road, yet you can still feel the bustles of the wharf. A perfect combination with weekend sunny weather.

Not sure why Yelp has listed Tapenade Bistro as Mediterranean. The menu is decidedly French. Their website confirms that it is "French inspired West Coast."

On to the food now:

Dungeness Crab Duo - beautiful plating with vibrant colours. Crab cake was moist, fresh, and flavourful. 

Mussels (Pernod) - fat and fresh. The broth was a touch under-seasoned and missing the depth compared to the mussels at Salade de Fruits. But it was still nice, and I happily slurped it all up.

I came here to study today to get out of the limited & sometimes over-populated coffee shops in San Marcos. i was looking for somewhere that wasn't located in a busy area and was a good place to study. there are tons and tons of coffee shops in Austin to choose from, but i was very happy i went with this one. it's location in east Austin meant that it was a little closer to me. the place was pretty small and had a vintage vibe with really comfy blue velvet couches, plenty of tables, and nice lighting. i got a cardamom latte which was delicious and my friend tried their iced chai which she liked, but wished it was a little more potent. the barista was friendly and i was SO happy that it never got loud or crowded in the three hours we were there. the only thing i wish this place had was a minimal food menu (like simple sandwiches and salads that most coffee shops offer if their customers get hungry, although i did notice food trucks right outside that i would try next time i visit). also, parking was not the most convenient but it was doable (limited customer parking so most people would have to resort to street parking if it got crowded). other than that, this place was pretty good and i would definitely come back!

Went here last night with some coworkers, and had a fabulous time. The Miller Lites were $1.50, so there was a good crowd for a Wednesday night. We pulled together a few tables, ordered a couple of HUGE pizzas from Hog Island Deli, and had a few drinks.

Service was great all night. Yes, the staff is a bunch of hotties, but they are also really good at their jobs! This isn't always the case (it's actually rarely the case) so I really appreciated it. Everyone was super friendly and looked like there were having a good time. It seems like the kind of place where you could go alone, and still have a good time.

I have been a patient at Fenway since moving to Boston in 2004.  They are genuinely a one of a kind healthcare center dedicated to meeting the needs of Boston's LGBT community.

As a whole the care I have received here has been thoughtful, in tune with my needs and respectful of the issues I face as a LGBT person looking for health care.

They also have a lab, pharmacy and mental health treatment on site, which makes for great convenience.  

Like most community health centers, they have their short comings.  The billing department can't ever seem to get things correct, and keep your records straight.  They also seem to experience unusually high turn over, which can cause your primary care experience to feel disconnected as you start over with a new provider.

That said, this is truly a wonderful place or anoyone looking for sensitive, thorough healthcare for our community.

So 4 stars for being and keeping it so real here...and Classic too!  4x8 plywood panels hung vertically with 1 by trim on the walls. Some of you will know what I'm talking about.  Painted high tray ceiling with Uni-Strut hanging 60's decor lamps. TVs mounted everywhere and kitschy beverage (alcoholic) company neon signs and mirror plaques on the walls. Some games in corners, like Hoop Fever, and several bar billiard tables. Oh, the empty kegs are staged under the Hoops! Many tables and the bar is huge. 50 or 60s style with seats (chairs and stools) that'll remind you of relative's houses with the chrome tube frames and glitter vinyl coverings. But it's cool. Real cool. 
The beer selection is diverse as to not drive the yuppies away but if you don't like this place it's because you forgot where you started.

I've been to The Varsity more times than I can count. I always stop in whenever I'm going through Atlanta. Just a neat place.

What do I always say re: fast food? What are the 3 things you want? Cleanliness, speed, and affordability. The Varsity has all three of these things. But, what puts TV over the top is its uniqueness and culture. The people behind the counter that are screaming at you - "What'll ya have!" - to the names the employees give to the items - "Nekkid Dog Runnin'" - to the mistreatment of someone that "did not have their order on their mind and their money in their hand."

Just a really neat place. And the food is a terrible, greasy mess of wonder. How could you not love it?

The Clay Pit delivered really, really tasty Indian food with great service.

We ate dinner around 8:30 and the place was bustling. We ordered a ton of food. Potato bondas and Samosa chaat to start. Then, 2 mango lassis for our group of 3. 

Then for the main dishes, we tried the jalapeño & cream cheese parathas (I'd recommend passing on these...), the paneer parathas (delicious!) and the plain parathas (good too). We ate these with chaana saag (very good), vegetable mirchi curry (delicious - the best item on the table), potato kofta (too creamy) and saag paneer (delicious...and NOT too creamy which was a blessing for me!). We also ordered some jeera rice (which was AMAZING!).

Coming from Houston, my standard for Indian food is very, very high (given the number and quality of restaurants we have). So, I doubt that I'll be coming back or coming to Austin JUST to go to the Clay Pit as many other reviewers have indicated. 

But, if you're looking for good, vegetarian Indian food in Austin, I would definitely recommend going to the Clay Pit!

Welcome to the neighborhood Poke Bar! Having just opened up 4 days ago, I was expecting mild chaos when I went in at noon for lunch, but the restaurant was surprisingly calm and under control. Seating inside is not very abundant (a few tables for 4 and some 2 seaters), but tables were filled with patrons noshing on their sushi/salad/rice bowls. The space is clean, modern, and has easy signage for first timers to figure it out. 

Ordering is set up like Chitpotle: stand in land and pick your size (small/2 proteins, medium/3 proteins, large/4 proteins) and base (salad, rice, nachos??, etc.) and then move on to step 2 where you pick your proteins (tuna, shrimp, octopus, salmon, etc.), and so on and so forth. It's a little overwhelming the first time, but once you get the hang of it, it's pretty straight-forward. They had a great variety of toppings ranging from pineapple, to corn, to seaweed salad, to avocado (extra $1). Sauces are also abundant and you can choose 1 or many. Depending on who is mixing your toppings, they might be heavy handed with the sauce. I had to tell the worker to stop with my wasabi shoyu cuz he just kept going and going. (My mom did not stop him and said it was a little salty because there was too much sauce.) Anyway, after you get toppings, you get ... more toppings! Toppings for everyone! And after that, at the register to pay, there are ... more toppings! I opted for a sprinkle of sesame seeds and fried garlic because, yum, garlic.

We ordered 3 bowls and they were tasty and fresh. They also have loyalty cards so I immediately got stamped for 3 bowls. (11th one free.) I will say the small with 2 toppings left me hungry after an hour. I'd advise patrons to go with medium or large if you want something more filling.

This poke brand is a global franchise. So while some things many not be within their control, I offer some notes for the business owners. (The entire staff was very nice, btw.)

-If possible, I'd invest in bigger bowls. We got 2 smalls and 1 medium and they were all in the same size bowl. Even with the small, it was hard to mix and eat without making a giant mess and getting rice/salad everywhere. Can't imagine ordering a large and eating from the small bowl.
-Possibly look into ordering sheets where patrons could mark what they want in advance so they're not holding up the line figuring out what they want. Not an issue if it is not busy, but I can see it being very slow going during a lunch hour rush.
-You may want to change your social media handles from Brookhaven to Chamblee. Chamblee residents get VERY defensive about being called Brookhaven. (I've seen the threads on NextDoor!)

Located in the new Solis Parkview condos/apartments next to Big Daddy's Burger Bar. There's a small lot in front of the restaurant and parking deck across the way. Overall, great experience. We'll be back!

We went to Sagra to celebrate a friend's divorce settlement. My friend and my girl both ordered the Bistecca and I ordered the Frutti di Mare. The steaks were cooked to order with a blue cheese sauce. The pasta dish was bounding with seafood- calamari, clams, mussels, and shrimp. The sauce was a spicy red sauce. Needless to say I cleaned my plate. We saved room for dessert- the Cioccolate cake with Blood red orange sorbet. My girl went gaga for the sorbet. The flourless chocolate cake was to die for. We will definitely be back. The service was flawless.

Finally tried the last of the big 3 on my list and I was definitely impressed.

Service: what I expected! super friend staff with cheery attitudes and big smiles. 

Food: loved the "organic"  and "natural" of the ingredients. Was a little skeptical at first but after the first few bites and slurps I was believing all the power words they used on their menu. Instead of ordering the gyoza, we ordered the pork (not the side, but the actual appy) which was port "butt" and shoulder. It was served with a bit of sweet sauce on top and ... seriously.. I would put this up there with my filet mignon from Gotham. It just melted in my mouth and my tastes buds were def happy. I like how that they give you options of adding things to the soup base to make it taste more rich and flavorful!

As previously stated, its a little more pricy then Kintaro and Benkei for the standard bowl w/o toppings but for some reason.. after eating here you dont get that super heavy feeling in your stomach where its just screaming up to your brain to take a nap right on the table!

Why does this place only have 10 pictures? Their food is gorgeous!

I've been to Sugar twice, both times for breakfast. I'm so so glad it's a short, easy drive from my apartment in Jamaica Plain. It makes for a perfect place to get an awesome breakfast in the am!

I've only had the breakfast sandwich to remember (eggs, cheddar cheese, panchetta, and fig jam on a biscuit). DELISH. The second time, I ordered the same, but they were out of fig jam so I asked for strawberry. I know. Weird. But tasty!

My boyfriend got the french toast and said it was one of the best he ever had. It only comes with 2 slices (albiet large slices), however. But he loved it (and he is the pickiest eater I know, bless his heart). 

OH. Oh yes. Their hash browns. YUMZO. Though very dark in color, there is no burnt taste. They're salty and a little crispy and always cooked through. I don't even put ketchup on them (but you should feel free to).

The second time I went there was a 20 minute wait. Use that time to check out the menu, and the bakery in the back. 

My two gripes are the price, and service. $8 for a breakfast sandwich? This is sad-making. Also, their service ranges from bad to fine. It's hard to get ahold of the waiters occasional. HELLLOOO? Yes, I'm waving at you.

They have a creative menu with fresh ingredients. Delicioso!

Lunch is definitely the best time to go to Bubba Gump. My husband and I have attempted to come in for dinner but there is always a long wait. We came in for lunch on Sunday and there was no wait, the service was awesome and quick and the food was tasty. My only complaints are there aren't prices on the menu for drinks and prices for food are pretty pricey. Two drinks and two entrees cost us over $60. If you are looking to splurge then this is a night treat. I had the seafood feast which comes with hush puppies, fried shrimp, fried fish, coleslaw and fries. The fish needed some flavor but thankfully lemon and cocktail sauce took care of that. My husband had a variety of shrimp which included coconut shrimp, fried shrimp, tempura shrimp, bacon wrapped shrimp and fries. Each shrimp was paired with a special sauce which my husband loved. We each also had a watermelon Coronarita. You do get a souvenir shaker with the purchase of a drink. We will definitely return for lunch when we want to splurge on a meal.

Mellow Mushroom.... Where to begin? The pizza here is FANTASTIC. Fresh ingredients and a competent kitchen staff makes for one helluva pizza. The decorations on the walls provide an excellent sense of atmosphere which is always important when dining on a slice of pepperoni. 

Things like trivia nights and loyalty points always excite me when trying out a new restaurant. Unfortunately, the live music was a little weak, but that's to be expected every once in a while. 

The pizza is incredibly cheap when bought with one of the numerous discounts Mellow Mushroom offers, which was  a huge plus for me. The wait staff was also very friendly and on top of our refills here at the UCF location.

Maple bar is usually my go to so I was excited to try their bacon sprinkled maple bar.  Unfortunately, they were out. :(
However, my disappointment soon turn to excitement after taking a bite of Maple Fried banana bar!  So decadent! Old fashioned and raspberry filled donuts were also delicious!  A dozen disappeared in the blink of an eye between the six of us.   
Blue star have their place in my heart but Tonallis certainly have made their mark!  Thank you yelpers for leading me to Tonallis!   
Now, I have done my part.  Your turn... Go have some donuts already. :)

I love buffets like this. A good assortment of food, hot and fresh, and most importantly everything was very clean. It's very unusual not to see buffet tables a complete mess, but on my visit even though it was busy everything was being constantly wiped down and cleaned up. 

Also I have always, always, always found that service at these places are not good. It's hard to get your drink refilled or your plates taken away because they really want you to lose your appetite. Not here. My water was being refilled every few minutes, and whenever I went to get a new plate of food my dirty one was already gone when I got back. Every time.

In fact when I got some crab legs and I got back to my table there were crab leg crackers already there. Are they psychic?

As usually I won't pretend the food at a buffet is ever better than the food you will find at a traditional restaurant, but it was all very decent, and most was above average even for a buffet. I will definitely come back the next time I feel like eating way too much.

Hubby and I went to the Grilled Cheese Grill in SE today. Oh, it was delicious. I had the Grilled Cheesus and he had the Grilled Quesus. Both are 1/3 lb burger patties between grilled cheese sandwiches. HUGE! And so very tasty!

The bread tasted very fresh and was perfectly grilled, the burger was nice, if a bit overdone for my taste. The only drawback is that they have no mayo. I like mayo on my burger, but just mustard was ok too. (Since I cannot stand ketchup). The burger comes with a bag o' chips. The BBQ flavor is quite tasty.

I was completely stuffed and couldn't even finish my burger, let alone eat dessert, so no review for the yummy sounding dessert sandwiches.

The Grill has recycling and composting bins as well as one for trash. They are clearly well-used and I think that rocks. :)

In sum, I will definitely be back.

Dear sweet delicious Upper Crust. Why do you hate me? You are the cheapest, tastiest lunch to go in my hood, why you gotta keep forgetting parts of my orders :((((( WHYYYYYYYYYY I just want to eat your sweet (cinnamon) buns! Sink my teeth into them! But you forgot them! & I only noticed when I arrived at work 3 miles away :( WHYYYYYYYYYYY So I called you up & got my name in a book, which is not a very promising thing, if there is a book of people who have had their orders messed up. But you know what? The people who work inside of you, Upper Crust, though they are forgetful they are attractive, & the food is delicious. So even though you are mean to me, I love you. I will be back. But I'm not giving you five stars! A FIVE STAR PLACE WOULDN'T FORGET THE BUNS!!!
Love Always,
Debby K.

On the recommendation of one of my Turkish friends , my husband and I dined @ pasha this weekend. We are ardent fans of the middle eastern cuisine and had high expectations. We have been to other Turkish  restaurants in the area - Bosphorous and Istanbul both of which were good as well.

First of, the decor of this place is beautiful- they've paid attention to aesthetics and that adds to the experience

Secondly and most importantly, the food is delicious and worth all the stars it has received here. They have a yogurt based appetizer which was yum! I ordered a chicken entree and my husband ordered a poke+beef mixed entree, both of which were served with adequately spiced Bulgarian rice - all of which was really tasty 

And finally the staff - they are pleasant , polite ,friendly and will take time out to explain what a particular item on the menu is (especially desserts)

We loved the place and highly recommend it.

Best,
Sneha

Before leaving Orlando my family wanted some breakfast hot, healthy and good. I pulled up my trusty Yelp app while my husband headed in the direction we needed to go and this place popped up. It's located in the outlet mall area and shares a lot with multiple businesses.

We were sat quick in a nice both, they didn't offer Vegan dishes specifically but there was items I looked to turn Vegan but asking if they would do a eggless Veggie omelette and just sauté the veggies and a side of potatoes. My husband had the chicken and waffles and our son had a children's waffle with turkey sausage. They don't have freshly squeezed juice so I opted for water and my husband and son had the orange juice. I mentioned to my hubby that they had strawberry butter made in house so he ordered some and said it was good. The server (I wish I could remember her name, I'll update my review when I locate the receipt) was amazing. She was very accommodating and patient with us and my many request and questions as well as our toddler indecisiveness.

I'll definitely recommend this place to others as the service was great and the food was good.

Fall = knitting time!

Finally had the time to check out Gina Brown's Yarn after living in the area for almost a year and I loved it! I didn't really have a project in mind, but the owner (?) was able to decipher the vague concept I had in my mind into a free pattern online and a decently priced ball of mossy green yarn! She was very patient with my indecision as to what to make and what yarn to pick, offering lots of advice and yarn/pattern choices. 

She even said I could come back for help (if they weren't too busy) in case my knitting skills turned out to be rustier than I had imagined. They have a knitting pow-wow on Thursday nights too! I can't wait to finish this project just to go back again. :)

This taproom has a very minimalistic and industrial aesthetic that makes it a perfect place to catch up with a friend. It's quite small, but there was ample seating when I was there. Their cider is different from most of the dry ones I've had before - my favorite was the common with citrus-y flavors. The Apple flavor wasn't as strong as I was expecting (or used to with other ciders), and maybe that's just the case with a "true" dry cider. It tasted almost like a wine, which is great if you're a wine lover, I suppose!

There are certainly more 'off the beaten path' places to get your Southern Food Fix, but Mary Mac's has a few advantages in certain situations: you're already in Midtown, you've got a boatload of out of towners and need a huge table, you're meeting people there (it's easily located), or you just want to experience a very 'Atlanta' thing to do. 

They'll keep serving that sweet tea up until you beg 'em to stop (the menu proudly bills it as The Table Wine of the South), you really can't get away without eating something fried and if you don't enjoy invasion of your personal space, the sweet lady that comes by and rubs your back may freak you out. 

If it's your first time, they'll give you a bowl of Pot Likker to try out for free. I won't ruin it  for you, and let you be surprised when you get it. 

For the most part, every time I've been here, the food is as expected. My only one sadness on my plate of Southerness is that consistently, the macaroni and cheese is not what I would expect from an upstanding meat & three. . . but watery and disappointing (see review for Busy Bee Cafe for some amazing mac & cheese). But otherwise, I've enjoyed every piece of fried okra and spoonful of potatoes I've stuffed down here.

Take out is really easy to facilitate too (you can even place an order online!) . . . which could actually be quite detrimental to your waistline if you live too close.

Fantastic restaurant. Great patio and service. Make sure you try the sujouk and chicken cedars. Amazing. Full of flavor and very tender. Great place to get some small bites and share them with a group. Bread with the hummus is great too. Made in house (at least it appears). 

Hookah offerings are small unfortunately. Only a few flavors to choose from. However, the staff are that serve the hookah are extremely attentive and they use real coals instead of the charcoal ones with all the chemicals. Nice touch. 

Have been multiple times and will return again!

I'm giving this place three and a half stars because it's better than Roppolo's, closer than Home Slice and cheaper than ordering pizza at a sit down restaurant.  Rounding up to four stars because of its sheer convenience relative to my office. 

I ate here at least once a week for lunch when I worked downtown. It is consistently good New York style pizza. I like anything with lots of veggies and they have a rotating menu, so it's nice to have choices. The sauce is a little spicy but not too bad. One slice is just enough to not be hungry anymore but two gets me stuffed. 

Bonus points for always stocking canned Nestea.

I can eat for hours as long as I have a boiling pot of broth, a pair of chopsticks, and a metal net. 

We have been here several times for birthdays and special events. My first tip is to bring a credit card with a good limit on it. No, it isn't astronomical but you should really be willing to pay. If you are, then you're in for a treat.

First of all, I am pretty sure that they have employed the same service staff for years. Every time we have come here, I have seen the same servers. They are very pleasant, well dressed, and are fantastic in their service. I give a two thumbs up for that. 

As for the food. WOW. There might not be anything more fresh than this. When I think of Landmark, I think of fatty beef slices, cuttlefish balls, and geoduck....amongst many other things. Absolutely Fantastic. It is hard to stop eating. When you do, you are satisfied and not at all unhappy with your experience. 

As for parking. WOW. The free parking in the back is a fuster cluck. You will find your car blocked in by a dozen other cars and when you try to leave, the management calls the owners of the cars to have them move their cars for you. You can imagine that this takes a while. Meanwhile, there are normally 2-6 other cars waiting to park anywhere near. Not a good idea to try and drive down that alley way! 

Overall, for hot pot, this is the real deal. I give 4.5 out of 5.

Came here a while back with 2 friends, using the scoutmob coupon (which they honored with no hassle).

To maximize our usage of it, we got 2 pizzas, the Steak and Blue and the Southwest Baja. To start off, I kinda just expected the toppings to all be thrown on like most places, but I was proven wrong as even the presentation of the food was nice, even, and symmetric. Of course that's not a huge deal if it wasn't, but it was a nice touch.

Anyways, the Southwest Baja pizza definitely was what it implied, and had black beans, corn salsa, grilled chicken, and jalapeños. It had a nice kick of spice too, but not too much for a pizza, and they didn't skimp on the amount of toppings, neither for this pizza or the Steak and Blue. Speaking of which, that the Steak and Blue was also pretty darn good, there was enough steak on it and it wasn't dry either, so it had a good flavor along with the blue cheese. One thing about the pizzas we had though was that they were really thin and crunchy; now I usually don't like thin pizza since I feel its a lot less filling, but that Maddio's kinda gave me a new perspective since it made each slice be crunchy, but not too hard. It wasn't moist either, or greasy, which shows something about the preparation, too.

To be fair, this is obviously an Americanized place, but that doesn't even matter honestly, because the food here, at least the pizzas we god, are MAD GOOD.

I'm probably coming back this week actually, totally worth the drive.

As a friend and I pulled up to park, a sign caught our eyes for "Free Valet parking". Why park along the busy N. Highland Ave on a Saturday afternoon when you can have someone do it for you? So I handed over the keys and walked to the front door below the giant "Fritti" sign. A tattooed guy was walking out of the door and though he looked busy, he was nice enough to open the door for us.

I went with the Vegetariana pizza without cheese. They asked whether I wanted it the traditional way with the different vegetables in sections, or if I wanted everything thrown together. Together may have given me the opportunity to taste everything at once, but I went for traditional. It's funner that way, and a bit more of an experience to attack the pie from all sides.The crust wasn't as crispy and charred as I like, but I still loved it!

It was awesome pizza and a good price. I was impressed with the service and intend to come back soon!

-Andrew "VegMuffinMan" Morrison-

Full review and photos: http://tinyurl.com/26oderb

Tried out Velvet Taco today - the location in Rock Rose is next to Thai Kun and across from 77 Degrees.  If the price was higher would have been a three star experience.  

Velvet taco had super large Orange Fanta's which was nice so me and VGP could share.

I found the corn to be very tasty - a bit more spice than the similar item at Dos Batos. I think they used fresh corn on the cob to make the item.

I had two tacos - the Tofu and the Shrimp.  The tofu I rated as a 5 and the shrimp was too salty and I rated as a 2.  I couldn't even finish the shrimp in the taco because it was so salty, but the grits were good.

I'd go back, but probably only for lunch.  I'm not all that fhancy however I would have preferred a plate over a brown napkin spread on my table. Almost forgot the cashier was quite possibly the nicest service person I have encountered in months. She was short(er than me) and had highlighted hair, she mentioned they get free tacos every shift.  What lucky workers!!

This place was one of the most popular places on yelp that we saw for Portland so had to try it out! In a nutshell: I definitely liked this place (taste of everything was amazing), BUT i do think it's overpriced asian food. I would still recommend it overall but our bill was ~$85 for lunch for 4 people. Tip: Get there early, as we had to wait at least an hour for a table since the restaurant is small and it's so popular! Our orders: 

Fish Sauce Wings: 4/5
I don't like wings cause they're too much work LOL but these tasted amazing! It's also one of their most popular dishes so I would recommend it. HOWEVER, be sure to eat it with rice! Otherwise it's too salty (hence mixed reviews on the fish sauce wings) but if you eat it with rice it's really good! 

Neua Naam Tok (Flank Steak Salad): 5/5
This was my favorite dish at pok pok! It's basically steak with lemongrass/mint/greens. It's small but your mouth literally explodes with all the kicks in the salad dressing. It's good to eat with rice too! 

Pok Pok Special: 4/5
This comes with papaya salad, rice, 1/2 roasted chicken and some sauces. Chicken was okay but the sauces were pretty good and it's just nice that it comes with the rice and salad to eat with your other orders. 

Kung Op Wun Sen (the noodle dish): 3.5/5
These noodles were nice to have with the meal but I wouldn't say it's out of this world. 

Overall our meal was very delicious and booming with flavor, I just wish they gave more (amount is pretty small) or charged a little less. Still worth trying though!

YouTube is handy for showing you all the foods you are missing out on from around the world. Thailand has rolled ice cream, cold and packed into a cup. I wouldn't have thought we'd get it in Winter Park but Sweet Fifi is serving up hand rolled ice cream. 

For $6.50 you can choose one of their standard rolls or you can choose your own with 2 toppings. I got "Get Sticky" which comes with butterfingers, Carmel, and whipped cream. My brother got the latte one and my sister in law and roommate got the s'mores. 

It's fun to watch them make the ice cream. It is so cold that it doesn't melt as fast. I liked the one I got best. While tasty for $6.50, it is an expensive treat. I don't know if I would go back but it's fun to try and watch. Now I don't have to wait for Thailand!

I love stopping by for lunch. I've only ever ordered their sandwiches but I've never been disappointed.

Their turkey cuban is absolutely delicious, and they've never had a problem switching out a few ingredients for me (replacing the Swiss with provolone). The breads they offer are phenomenal too. 

Sometimes service can run a little slow but they're always friendly. To make sure you have your pick of the breads available try to get there with the first half of the lunch rush. If you wait too long you're usually limited to just the baguette.

Very cute coffee shop tucked away in downtown Lake Oswego. 

I came in at 10:58 and they still served me breakfast with a smile (breakfast ends at 11). 

The coffee is about 20% less than Starbucks (I had a quad latte) and it's at least as fast. I got my coffee and freshly cooked waffle in less than 5 minutes. 

There is a pretty sizable inside seating area (for a small coffee shop) and a great little patio area with about seven 4-top tables.

Portlanders love Andina, and once you eat there, you'll understand why. This is a must-go place whenever I'm in town.

Your meal begins with delicious homemade bread and three dipping sauces that are bursting with flavor, and it just goes up from there. The ceviche is out of this world. The meat in the entrees is succulent and cooked to perfection. Everything is not only mouth-watering, but also vibrant in taste.

I love the brightly-colored linens and the atmosphere is great whether day or night. This is the kind of place you can take your mom, celebrate a birthday with a big group of friends, or impress a date. Basically, just stop wasting your time reading reviews and go eat there.

Uhhh...who knew that the Japanese culture has an affinity for the hotdog? I'm glad they do, because I had what could only be considered a step closer to culinary genius.

Japadog delivers Kurobuta Pork Hotdogs with Japanese flavors out of several locations in the Pac NW. I stumbled across mine in Vancouver and was glad that I did. I had the Kurobuta Terimayo dog. 

The dog was packed with flavor and topped with teriyaki sauce, Japanese mayo, fried onions and seaweed. It was awesome! Go try it!

I've been to Krog Street Market a few times now, and this time it was a Friday night. I valet parked my car for $3 plus tip. I have been there before where I didn't have to use valet, but since it was Friday, that particular lot was packed. 

This time, a friend and I tried Fred's, and we were lucky enough to find a spot at the counter. I ordered a veggie burger and a side of the garlic fries with ranch. The Veggie burger was a fun mix of a bunch of things that turned out to taste delightfully similar to falafel but a little spicier. The order of garlic fries was really fresh and pungent. If you're going to get these fries, I suggest you get one order for two to three people. It's a lot of garlic, and you'll need less than you might think.

A delightful surprise: The drinks there (all bottled or canned - including glass bottle sprite and coke) were super cold. 

After Fred's (even though I shouldn't have) I went to Jenni's and had a scoop of the Savannah Butter Mint Ice cream. It was excellent and a great way to finish off a meal. 

If you're going to go to KSM for the first time, I highly recommend visiting on a week night. You won't have to pay for parking, and you'll be more likely to get a seat wherever you'd like. It's a pretty fun outing, though, and a great potential date spot.

With a great view of the water, this hotel is conveniently located close to the Vancouver Airport. There's a frequent free shuttle that can take you to/from the airport. 

We stayed here for one night. Rooms are modern,spacious and clean. Bed is comfortable and we didn't hear any airplane noise. There is no free wi-fi and there is a $14 parking fee. Also, there is a 24 hour fitness facility on the top floor which gives a panoramic view. 

Would recommend to anyone looking for a place to stay near the airport. It's not the best accessibility in terms of transit options, but one can make use of their free shuttle to the airport to connect to the Canada Line.

Atomic Bean is not near my house, and it is located pretty much in between Central & Harvard stations, guaranteeing a walk from either, unless you're lucky to catch the #1 bus. BUT. ABC is THE place I go when I need somewhere to work. 

Why? I gotta get real. It's the free WiFi. That, and the ample tables and plugs -- I haven't had trouble finding space.

You'd think that a coffee shop with complimentary WiFi (a shockingly rare breed in the Camberville area) might breed a hushed atmosphere of laptop zombies, but the Atomic Bean manages to avoid this somehow. 

The baristas are friendly, if laidback. People-watching on Mass Ave through those huge windows is #1. And everyone's friendly about letting you finagle around their chair with your laptop cord. 

I head here when I need to get work done outside of work, so I usually am there at the end of the day; this means less-than-fresh pastries, so I can't comment on the food really. But in the summer, I love the mango iced tea with an almond croissant. 

Things to watch out for: no free refills, and no AC from what I can remember.

Came to the restaurant today with in-laws and an infant. At 2:45PM (on a Saturday) there was 15 minute wait. Those folks sure know how to turn seats - impressive!
Proprietor is very attentive and makes sure everything is running smoothly.

This was my 2nd time here and as always I walked out happy. Really recommend coming here in a larger group, so you can order as broad of the selection as you can. Food is good and so far I only didn't like one item. That is really notable for dim sum.

Heard about pupusas for the first time about a week ago. Headed straight to yelp to find the best place to give them a try. Once again Yelp delivered, went yesterday afternoon to this humble looking establishment. We truly enjoyed our taste of Central America. 

Taking a queue from Kit F. we ordered the small shrimp cocktail and a few pupusas (pupusa regullta, pupusa de loroco con queso, and pupusa de queso y frijoles). The pupusa regullta was our favorite. I would recommend against the pupusa de loroco con queso, I think it must be an acquired taste. Loroco is an exotic flower, indigenous Central America. Pupusa regullta consist of cheese, pork, and beans. Pupusa de queso y frijoles contains cheese and beans.

I'm a big fan of this style of eatery.  LOVE being able to make my own choices (control freak? maybe) as well as the sauces, and starches, etc.  I think there are basic things you just have to KNOW for your first trip, and you can improve on your experience in subsequent visits, like PILE your bowl high cuz everything cooks down.  I was very pleased with my combo and can't wait to come back with my caveman, who I will counsel to pile his bowl high with protein and then plenty of sauce.  Like the throwaway spoon option for tasting the sauces...which can make or break your whole deal!  I've been to "low rent" versions of this, and didn't get to try the "high rent" version because my Mongolian Grille groupon expired before we got to visit downtown, and I've been anxiously awating this opening in South Austin, YAAAY for not having to cross the bridge for mongolian grill experiences!  Yes, it was loud, not sure why with the lunch crowd, and our waitress was a little familiar, but that's okay too, sometimes that's fun!   I like that staff is excited about what they do, that can be contagious in a good way!

3.5 stars rounded up because the place is really new still. 

No alcohol as of yet (I think they only opened two or so weeks ago) -- so I am excited for the warm sake next time. 

The place is all really new and nice. The one thing I appreciated was that there was very little wait time before we got started with the food. I hate when hibachi places wait to fill a table before the food starts. Only half our table was full and I saw them start tables with only one couple at them. There were no chopsticks (in their defense I didn't ask so they may have them available). 

As for the food, it was pretty standard hibachi fare. Nothing too notable in the negative or positive spheres. Prices were very fair and portions were large. Chicken with teriyaki was well done (not over cooked!). The fried rice and veggies needed a pinch more flavor (salt mainly) or the sauce dishes need to be bigger. I'm pretty sure everyone at our table had at least three refills of the two sauces. 

Hibachi entertainment was actually pretty awesome -- there was fire (woo!) and the chef was pretty entertaining in the beginning. Either we were a bad audience (not as responsive as we should have been) or he ran out of tricks because the entertainment ended in the first half of cooking. 

Their service is still in training -- they forgot to ask for dessert before bringing out final checks in a rush so we had to order it when we sent our credit cards in which made it take much longer. 

We will definitely be back to try their sushi next time and we are excited to have a decent hibachi place close to us !

Yeah, it's in a strip mall.  Don't let this deter you.

I walked in, exhausted from two hours in that FANTASTIC Goodwill around the corner, expecting a quick meal of overpriced soup in an uppity atmosphere. 

Not so!

Keeping with the thrifty theme, I opted for a $3.25 "cup" of white bean chili and, not realizing how much soup I would get, the complimentary-but-you-have-to-ask-for-it bread.  The soup came out shortly afterward in a bowl as big as an average person's morning cereal bowl, garnished with crispy tortillas, with garlic bread on the size.  It took me half an hour to eat it all.  But eat it all, I did.

Everything was very good.  The soup had nice spices, a nice chili consistency and tasted healthy.  (Well, except for all the cheese and sour cream, which I could've opted out of - but when have I ever opted out of cheese?  Come ON!)  The bread was good... although had I realized it would be garlic bread I wouldn't have asked for it - it was an odd mix with chili.

I was dining alone and appreciated the magazine selection in addition to the usual used newspapers tossed aside by other patrons.  I had no issues with the decor but I usually only notice that if it's uber cheesy or otherwise off the wall.  

I rarely venture into Beaverton but now I have two reasons to go back...  or at least a new lunch spot on the way to the coast.

I had been eyeing a beautiful Vuitton for quite sometime... my boyfriend suprised me and told me that he was going to buy it for me as a gift... SO happy.

We went down to the Downtown Seattle store and to me dismay, they did not have it! UGH!
I ended up calling down to Portland and they had it, the SA was SO wonderful... I am spacing on her name right now unfortantly.  There was only one left and I asked her to put it on hold, we wouldn't be able to head down there until the weekend.

We went into the Portland location and I felt as if the SA's we slightly rude (the lady I talked to on the phone was not there) and even when we went to purchase the bag they acted as if I couldn't afford it... very snobby.  (Minus 1 star!)

I was very happy over all, saved my boyfriend sales tax and got my bag!

This place is solid!  My husband and 7 year old son were riding Flight of Passage and my little girl and I didn't have a place to go so we decided to stop over at Satu'li canteen to grab a bite to eat.  The problem is, they were INCREDIBLY busy. It was the opening day of Animal Kingdom's 20th anniversary and the weekend of the Star Wars marathon so the place was packed.  It took over 30 minutes for me to receive my mobile order.  The food I ordered was really good!  We had the cheeseburger steamed pods - bao buns pods with chips and the quesadilla for the little one.  The buns were delicious and I could have ordered another serving but by the time I received my order, my son and husband were back from riding Flight of Passage and it was my turn to go on the ride.  

Definitely a MUST try when you're in Pandora.  The pods are delicious and the inside seating area is air conditioned so if you're looking to beat the heat, a good place to eat as well.  Highly recommend.

2nd visit....many many months apart
 
The first time I went, they were close to closing-limited selection- so maybe that's why I wasn't overly impressed one way or the other.  

Both donuts I had yesterday were quite tasty!  Both thumbs up!  More expensive than DD or KK but I guess they should be given the boutique nature of the place.

Worth the price sand special trip over the big boys -- DD or KK!  Great that a mom and pop place is thriving.  Good job sublime!

After reading the reviews from Yelp. I decided to make an apt. I told them what I wanted and they suggested a consultation first, which I think show's great professionalism. 
I met with Lanescia  (I'm not sure about the spelling) who looked at my hair type to determine what would be best for me and looked at photos I had with me.

She was great! She takes pride and time in her work. She listens to what you want and gave me extra time in case I went home and decided I wasn't happy with it.  I have gotten many compliments and I will definitely go back.

The staff was cool and helpful, even right before the kitchen closed at 2AM. Wings were OK, maybe a little pricey at $1 per. I had the lemon pepper and they were well flavored and not too oily. Tried one slice of Soul Food Pizza since that seems to be what everyone is talking about. It was a very interesting slice of pizza! I ate it all so it must be tasty. I had mine to go, but Jack's seems like its designed for group outings that involve lots of beer and loud conversation. I'll come back with friends.

This place is cheap. SO CHEAP. I like cheap food, and when food is cheap it doesn't need to be five stars, it can be three and I am more than happy because it's cheap and that is the extra star.

They have this INSANE combo here that is 3 rolls and miso soup for $6.25.... I KNOW RITE. 

The service was slow, but I was paying $6.25 for sushi and had nowhere to be. If you are poor and on the drive you should hit this place up for dinner. My roommate and I are poor now because we are moving so this is our new cheap go to sushi joint.

The place is small for the crowd that it gets, so I had to wait outside in the cold unfortunately. The ladies that work here are all gorgeous (at least the ones that I've seen), so there's some good eye candy here. The food was as great as it looks in the photo, I was actually surprised how excellent the food was! This is my new breakfast spot for now on, but I'll be sure to place my order over the phone next time so that I won't have to wait outside for it.

This isn't the mom and pop shop I expected it to be. It's done up so modern, wow! They even have a microphone to announce when they're seating your party. 

The menu is pretty straight forward. My only problem is that they say not to plate share. A bit controlling, if I wish to share as I'd like. They allowed us anyway if we got two extra sides which were priced at $3.75 each. 

They come out with a basket of bread rolls, cornbread, and cinnamon rolls. I was really excited for the cornbread but it was alright. The cinnamon rolls are good though! 

You write down what you want on a piece of paper with everything clearly labeled: appetizer, entree, sides, bread, drink, dessert. We ordered 3 legs of the fried chicken with whipped potatoes, fried okra, pot likker, and cornbread dressing & gravy. 

The chicken was phenomenal. It made everything that wasn't worth it, worth it. The fried okra, pot likker, and whipped potatoes were good but the cornbread dressing & gravy were alright. We didn't finish it.

From the bouncer to the bartender, great customer service and friendly interactions. The Chile Margarita was a perfect blend of spice and sweet. They certainly have a color palette - teal/blue - so if you don't like blue stay away. A variety of mish-mashed decor but lots of spots to claim and get comfortable in. Oh and, best part -Franks!! Waffle fries and a Jackalope - cherry on top. Can't wait for warmer weather, I am going to have many a girls night in the back yard.

I love this place. I work in the neighborhood and have been many times. I'm amazed at the reviews. I can't tell if the place is erratic and we were just lucky or if people don't actually know what flavorful Indian food tastes like? Been to too many dried out buffets I guess.
The woman who said it was so oily...its ghee...clarified butter. So many of the dishes are wonderfully flavored....like they've been cooking all day. The Ginger Chicken is amazing. Love the eggplant dish too. The bread is amazing and the owner always so welcoming.  
Wish they had a better location.

I have been to this place a few times & haven't ever been disappointed. It's usually pretty busy but they will extend their seating out into the lobby of the hotel where they are located which offers a more laid back seating style. 
Drinks are on point & food is great. 
Their Happy Hour Menu is one of the best I have had recently. 
We revelry tried the Calamari, Bacon wrapped dates & the burger and everything was cooked to perfection and delightful. 
I'll defiantly keep this place on my list of great downtown spots.

Pro
- I tried Bibibop on Polaris Parkway on Friday...and liked it so much I returned on Saturday.  Obviously, I am a fan.
- There was no wait either night around 6:30ish.
- Very Chipotle-esque in format, efficiency, and price.
- I got the purple rice spicy chicken bowl with everything (except no lettuce) and Yum Yum sauce.  i got Teriyaki the second night - I would recommend the Yum Yum sauce. 
- Great fast, casual option.

Con 
- I could have had a bit more food, but the bowl was adequately filled and appropriate for $6.40.

Thanks to Jamg C. and Daniel B. , I have a new found love for Baldino's.  And even better- I have found one a wee bit closer to my house...

This location is standalone alongside Buford Highway (almost across the street from the farmer's market). 

It can get busy as hell, but by the time I get there (usually late afternoon) the dust seems to settle and things go pretty quickly...

I like this location because: They have cannolis, a working pinball machine (25 cent play!), and table that has direct access to the napkins and sauces (which if it is taken when I arrive, I will bully you out of your seat)!

On the most recent visit, my friends and I decided to get a 6 footer for the super bowl (all we did was call the night before, we picked it up next day no prob)... It was spectacular!  Do note that with the purchase of a party sub they add a $10 deposit (refundable upon return) for the board that is sits on.  We also got all of the "wet" ingredients on the side so it wouldnt make the sub soggy...  It was a great value and kept everybody full.

Hell, just writing about this place is making me hungry, Baldino's- I will see you at noon ;)

I've been a Jamaica Plain resident for two years, and sadly I will be moving elsewhere in Boston in just a few weeks. Upon reflection of my time here, Camilo Market has been my favorite business in my neighborhood. 

Beer and wine selections are plentiful (so are the spirits, but I usually buy the aforementioned more frequently.)

The staff is friendly, hospitable and always willing to lend a helping hand (no literally--I'm 5 feet tall so I always get a hand when I can't reach the high stuff--thanks y'all!)

So, Camilo Market and Liquor store, I will miss being in walking distance from you the most.

But this is just a toodooloo, not a goodbye.

Me and a couple of friends decided to visit this place based on a recommendation by none other than YELP! It was very easy to find and all trails from the parking lot will lead you to the quarry. We're not professional rock climbers, so we climbed what we could as a shortcut or used the trails to go up. Although, there were a few groups that had a team climbing day there!

Also, don't be an asshole and break your beer bottles there. It's a nice place, so don't ruin it for everyone else. I was climbing and my hand landed on a piece. Secondly, ease up on the the spray paint, it makes it quite slippery for my footing.

First Impression:
I had an amazing experience at Anthony Vince Nail Spa - Easton! As soon as I walked in I was kindly greeted by the receptionist's warm smile and offered a beverage from the bar....yep! The bar. This nail spa offers a full bar (though I cannot comment on it bc I opted for the strawberry-lemon infused water). 

Atmosphere:
The overall atmosphere in the salon is calming and very relaxing. The day sky mural on the ceiling, the waterfall over the sinks, and the open and organized stations create a welcoming ambiance and spa like feel. While the decor is pretty amazing, my favorite about AV's atmosphere is their ventilation system. The ventilation at this place is great! There's no nail salon or chemical smell like at most shops, and I could actually breath the entire time I was there. My second favorite thing would have to be the pedicure chairs Bc they not only massage, but they also recline. I've been to many salons but I don't recall ever going to one that had reclining pedicure chairs. 

Service:
From the moment I walked in the door I felt welcomed and catered to by the staff. After telling the receptionist I was there for a pedicure she informed me that I have the option of doing a mani-pedi combo and I would receive $5 off the combined service, so that's what I chose. AV offers a plethora of nail polish options, both regular and gel polish. While in the process of choosing my nails colors, my nail artist came over to greet me and took me to the pedicure area and began immediately working on my pedicure. I opted for the basic pedicure or the "Spa Pedicure" and the No-Chip Gel Polish Manicure. The basic pedicure includes a hot towel wrap for your feet and legs, which most salons consider an add on. My manicure was done very well and my nail artist was efficient with grooming my nails. My only qualm is, when shaping my nails all of my nails on my left hand were filed at an angle, but before proceeding my nail artist asked me if I was satisfied. I informed her that I felt my nails were shaped at an angle and she immediately fixed them. I appreciate having the same nail tech for both my hands and feet. I've been to other salons that will give you two different nail techs, which can be a pain when tipping. Speaking of tips, ANTHONY VINCE ONLY ACCEPTS CASH TIPS PAID DIRECTLY TO YOUR NAIL ARTIST, so please remember this of you decide to visit.

Overall, my experience at Anthony Vince was great! I don't want to ditch my old nail salon Bc I love them too, but I think I may have to make it a point to visit AV more often. For my gel manicure and Spa Pedicure combo I paid $73 after tax. The prices at Anthony Vince are a little higher than other places in the area, but you get what you pay for.

What a great experience! I was slightly uncertain about having my car repaired by a smaller shop as I started my search by visiting a few of the bigger franchises - Kirmac, Craftsman and others. At all of these chains, the experience was similar - formal quote procedure, busy, impersonal service, waiting for various staff, long estimated times for a simple repair and quite costly. 
When I walked into Big City  I knew immediately that this would be service with a personal touch. Amy, Tommy and Andy knocked it out of the ballpark!
Great value at roughly half the price of the big shops, very accommodating in making the logistics simple and an excellent car repair. My car looks terrific. Throughout the entire process they were friendly and professional. I have pretty high expectations, and they set a new standard! I encourage anyone with an Auto Body repair to check out this well kept Vancouver secret.

Noureen is a beauty brows n' beyond expert!! She is beautiful inside and out, with an inviting spirit that will put any nervousness at ease. The shop is clean, sanitized and beautifully decorated with a calming spa feel.

I've been a client of Noureen's for over fours and I wouldn't dare let anyone else touch my eyebrows! Hands down she knows her craft. She is a sculptor who has the ability to shape the most amazing arch that compliments your face. However her expertise goes beyond just brows, she is experienced in makeup, skincare and waxing. I recommend giving BBB a try;m, you won't be disappointed!

We came to Granville Island this afternoon to do our big shop and support local businesses when we came and re-discovered The Grainry. We'd last visited about a year before in search of authentic Portuguese piri-piri (which they have, FYI) and decided it was time to restock the spice collection at home with all of this home cooking. While the shop is closed to customers as a precaution against COVID-19, the staff were extremely attentive, friendly and helpful in helping find products or giving recommendations as I wasn't sure what we needed to restock. 

I'm pretty sure it was the owner helping me out (as he seemed to do the buying for the shop) - it was awesome as he's clearly a foodie and passionate about using the best quality ingredients. He gave me about 5 different suggestions for different spices to use on steaks, beef and chicken all based on some of his favourite combinations. We tend to go for more Latin and Iberian cuisines, so it was cool getting new ideas on how to incorporate Middle Eastern and North African flavours! We only ended up buying a couple of staples this time (onion powder, garlic powder, green oregano, chiles de árbol and liquid smoke), but we're planning on looking in our cupboards and going back to restock in a couple of days with a comprehensive list.

We're happy to support small local businesses, and we're happy to add The Grainry to our repertoire. Super friendly, knowledgable staff, great selection of products with new stuff coming in all the time, and the prices are totally reasonable. Definitely check it out!

My only constructive feedback would be that, since customers can't go into the shop at the moment, to have a full list of products both on their website and available to look at onsite. Most folks may already know what they want when they come, though I think there are a few of us who get inspired by what we find! :)

What a great place!! A small Jazz Club that is very intimate and fun. Because of its small size, you're able to really enjoy the show! We saw Big Bad Voodoo Daddy and they ROCKED IT! There isn't a dance floor...so if you're looking to dance during the show, that isn't really an option (although we saw one couple dancing off to the side). 

We dressed up in vintage swing dance clothing...but everyone else wore pants and button up shirts (both males and females). We saw a couple people in jeans. We felt very comfortable being dressed up and felt like that was the way everyone should have dressed. But obviously you don't have to dress up to come here! 

We would definitely come back! It was a fabulous evening full of good food, great company, and an awesome show! We made great memories this weekend. 

Thank you Scullers!!!

i'm a big burger gal. huge! honestly have never and will never find someone who can out eat me (in burgers specifically). this place- wow it's the first place to really challenge me. i walked in the door and it was like a breath of fresh air. WHEW. amazing vibes. fantastic burgers straight up. it's expensive so i cant go too much but i usually save up so i can pay in quarters. way more satisfying and makes it totally worth it. also, my server Quinton was awesome. plus he is so cute. i probably made him really uncomfortable but hey- i was just shooting my shot . (he knows what i'm referring to)

From beginning to end, 9 Elm is the perfect restaurant.

At the risk of being accused of being morbid or over dramatic, I'll say this, if I were on my death bed, and I had a last meal request, 9 Elm would be a [sic] good option!

The night started off with a dirty martini.  Now for the past month, I've been enjoying dirty martini's from various locations.  I have yet to have a bad one, thank god.  9 Elm made a very good dirty martini to start off the night.

Appetizer:  My date (wife) and I started off with the Butternut Squash Ravioli.  It was very good, to say the least.

Both my date and I ordered their Grilled Filet Mignon medium rare.  The blue-cheese butter along with some kind of au jus (perhaps it was a reduction or something, I can't tell, but it was good) mixed with the mashed potatoes was out-of-this-world fantastic!  There were carrots, green beans, and asparagus included, and-despite not being a major part of the course-were also cooked perfectly and paired extremely well.

Desert: My date and I shared the Warm Chocolate Cake, which was simply delicious.  It would be a sin not to try at least one of their deserts while dining here.

Summarize review: 9 Elm is simply perfect.  The wait staff is excellent, the atmosphere is simple...yet comforting, the food is nothing short of excellent.  What more can I say other than, it took me 2 years to finally come here, I hope it doesn't take me 2 weeks to come back!

This place is a gem, hidden inside a semi-sad suburban mall. Make no mistake, though - this is no mall sushi. It is legit, fresh, delicious sushi and Japanese food, served in an impeccably clean space, by lovely people. We've now been a few times, and tried a good variety of rolls and appetizers, and never been disappointed. It's priced in the mid-range for sushi joints, and I think it is very good value for the quality of food they offer. Four of us ate, until we were stuffed, for $100 (including tax, before tip). Of the three sushi restaurants in the immediate vicinity, this one is our top pick by a huge margin. My only wish is that they were open a bit later in the evening, but given that the mall is basically a dead zone after 6pm, I can see why they aren't.

I've been to Hawkers several times and am never disappointed. As always, we ordered a ton of food last night. We got the dumplings, twice fried wings, beef lettuce wraps, some crab dish, duck and pork belly baos, and four different noodle bowls. Everything was absolutely delicious with great flavor. If you like crispy wings with lots of flavor, these wings are for you. I typically don't like fried wings but I can't deny how yummy these are. The lettuce wraps have always been a favorite item of mine. While I usually order the duck, I went with beef last night and omg so good! Again, full of flavor and the lettuce was very fresh. The noodles were the pad Thai, beef haw fun, some curry rice noodles, and another that I forget the name. They all were very good with their own spices and flavors. My favorites were the curry rice noodles and the beef haw fun, but really and truly they are all so good. There are peanuts in many of these dishes so be weary if any allergies. I recommend going with a group of friends and ordering a bunch of the small plates to share and taste everything.

Was it really 2012 when I reviewed Flawless Lashes last?  Well - THEY ARE STILL AMAZING!  I LOVE waking up in the AM and feeling pretty without makeup..  My fluttery gorgeous lashes have make me a lash addict! 

The staff are all  professional, knowledgeable estheticians who treat you with kindness and sincerity.  I was impressed to know that as products and technologies change (YES! LASH TECHNOLOGY!) that Sarah and her staff are always learning and investigating ways for you to look good and feel better in the spa - when you leave- for weeks after!

Thanks ladies!!

SWEET LORD JESUS YOU HAVE ANSWERED MY NOODLE PRAYERS.

The basics:
Tsurumen is located right in the heart of Davis Square, in the old Snappy Ramen location. Their menu changes, and on the day we went, had 3 items. The menu had the Paitan and the Shoyu, both ramen dishes, and a Date Soba noodle dish. The ramen was $15/dish, with an upcharge of +$2 if you wanted an egg. The soba was $12.

Let's just put it this way... I would push little children out of the way for the Date Soba again. Even the cute ones. That's how freaking amazing it was. The noodles were so damn memorably delicious. I'm salivating just thinking about it.

So please ignore Yelpers like Jeffrey L. and his review on 5/9/2018, who is offering his advice on how to run a restaurant and cook ramen. If he knows so damn much about making world class ramen, then why doesn't he just open his own restaurant? As the kids say, SMDH.

Great Thai food!! This restaurant is very clean and the staff are friendly and helpful in selecting menu items. I ordered the pad thai and it was some of the best pad Thai I have had. Ingredients were fresh and flavorful and there was enough for left overs. The pad Thai did not sit heavy on my stomach either. This makes me think that they use just enough fat for a flavorful dish but not so much that it is greasy it heavy. 

The food was brought out quickly as well which was nice. I will be coming back again to try some other dishes! I would recommend to anyone wanting Thai food at a good price.

I absolutely LOVED my day at Sea World! We went on May 20, 2012, and the park was not crowded at all as far as theme parks go! We basically walked on both the Manta and the Kraken. The Shamu Show "One Ocean" was fantastic, even though the trainers don't get in the water anymore (understandably so after the last sad occurence) I also really enjoyed the dolphin show, though my family weren't really fans of the "cirque de soleil" type feel. I thought the divers were awesome! Since we weren't there for the official summer season, we didn't get to see the Shamu Rocks night show, which was my favorite last time. Overall the day was awesome, I got a stuffed Shamu which actually seemed reasonably priced! Also, GET THE MEAL PLAN! for $30 you can eat all over the park, get free bottles of water at all the restaurants, and pretty much all you can eat. In 2 meals you will have gotten your money's worth. Add in snacks, and waiting to have breakfast at the park, and you have gotten a FANTASTIC deal! My family who live in the area all got season tickets, which are also pretty awesomely priced! Make sure you buy your ticket online if you are doing a single day, you can come back again within 7 days. I got my ticket at the gate using my family's discount through their season pass. Turned out to be the same price as online, but without the ability to come back for free! Lame! I won't take a star off, since that's really more my fault, and my one day was awesome enough to make up for it! 

Also I don't know how much it costs to get the little thing of food to feed the dolphins, but I hung out on the free side, and patients won out! I was able to pet a dolphin without paying, though the people on the pay side did get more personal time, and pet more than ONE dolphin, you can hang out for as long as you want right up by the water on the free side, so eventually a dolphin will come close enough!

Best breakfast spot, it's what you call a hidden gem!!! I had the most incredible arepas, pan de bono, and coffee. The owner was nice enough to customize my order since I'm a vegetarian... my arepa with cheese and avocado was just delicious. Simple but a true gastronomic experience. 
-------------------------

El mejor lugar para desayunar, es lo que llamas una joya escondida! Tuve las arepas más increíbles, pan de bono y café. El propietario fue lo suficientemente amable como para personalizar mi pedido, ya que soy vegetariana ... mi arepa con queso y aguacate estaba deliciosa. Sencillo pero una verdadera experiencia gastronómica.

This theater is on the smaller side but it is really, really nice. The facility looks brand new. It's located right next door to Miller Union so a great excuse to have a nice dinner beforehand. Parking is both on the street and in the small lots surrounding the building. We went to a matinee and there was free parking. Not sure what the evening situation would be.

I was blown away by the talent at the production of Willy Wonka the Musical. As an elementary school teacher, I can say that it is no small task to organize an almost all child cast. However, to not only organize and teach the children but to have them give incredibly professional performances that upstaged even the seasoned adult actors- wow! The entire cast was outstanding but the children really were the stars. The sets on the show were so artistic and detailed that they really helped bring Wonka's factory to life. The tickets to the show were $30 but Goldstar.com had half off tickets too. The theater is a non-profit so I will definitely not complain about the price. At full price, the show still would have been well worth the money. The summer series looks great and I can't wait to go back.

I stayed here for one night while I was in town to visit family. Everything was perfect. From the welcome gift of wine with the nice little note to the comfy bed. The staff is so helpful, even when you walk down to the lobby at 9:30pm in your sweats asking if they have hot tea. I like that you have to have your key card to go up to the floor our room is in, made me feel safe. Especially because I was there by myself. And how can you beat free WiFi. Check in and out was quick and easy. They even gave me a late check out. I will for sure stay here again next time I'm in Portland.

Dion was great to work with and did an excellent job replacing our cedar shingle roof overhang.  It was a small job and he fit me into his schedule in a matter of days.  Most communication was via text or phone tag but he was extremely careful to document his work and the quality of materials so I could feel secure that the job was done properly.  Everything from the scheduling to the payment was very easy, and his crew did a terrific job cleaning up our yard after the work was done.  Highly recommended.

We live within walking distance of Penguin and have avoided going in there for some unknown reason since we moved to Sellwood in July. Last Friday night we figured, "Ah what the hell, why not?" and we were so happy we went in.

We love divey places like this! The older couple (I assume they're the owners) that tend bar are SO genuinely nice and make you feel so welcome, like you're at grandma and grandpa's house. 

There was a karaoke session going on. The female KJ was nice, fun and full of energy. We don't sing karaoke but we love watching it. The diverse crowd was so much fun and so happy!  I'm upset we avoided this place for so long but we won't anymore!

P.S. If you don't want ironic shirts made about things you say on the internet, maybe you shouldn't purposely offend people by calling them a  "putz" ..after calling them "nice" ... like by calling him nice first it's supposed to make it okay that you're also calling him "a stupid or worthless person."  Just flat-out rude.

Fun auction every Saturday. Can find some great deals just set a limit so you don't spend more than you want.  It is family owned & operated. They are firm but fair and treat everyone in a friendly but professional manner. They answer all your questions with all the information available to them.  Items are new & antiques, collectibles, tools, appliances, indoor & outdoor furniture as well as cars, trucks, motorcycles & more.   Auctions are also held on Monday's.  Each auction is all new merchandise as everything must be sold.

I'm so excited for this place! Just what the square needed. 

I dropped in a few nights ago for a quick foot massage. I was so glad they were able to accommodate me as a last minute walk-in. The atmosphere wasn't much (which should be expected with such great prices), but it was peaceful, quiet and comfortable.  I got the 30 minute foot massage and ended up adding additional time because it was too great. 

Everyone was so friendly and I can't wait to come back!

Stumbled upon this place via IG the day of their grand opening. We promptly went the next day and it was superb! Im so excited they are so close and easily accessible! We had been wanting to try Hattie B's and Nashville hot chicken in general so we jumped at the chance to try this place. Conveniently located with lots of parking. I was afraid of a long wait because of going the day after the grand opening but it wasn't bad at all. They have kiosks to order your meal, hand sanitizer at the entrance for your convenience and they only allow a certain number of people inside to help with social distancing. Employees were friendly and kindly gave a warning about the reaper sandwich when our order was ready. The pickle and coleslaw that came on the sandwich were perfect compliments. It's only an extra $2 to get the combo which includes fries...and make sure to add the garlic aioli dipping sauce! I love the simplicity of the menu as it allows them to really focus on making a quality meal. And the price is just right, both my husband and I filled up on a combo meal each for online $20. This place will definitely be going into our rotation when we got a hankering for some spicy bird!

The best dining experience I have had in a while. Yes their prawns are incredible, the barbacoa was insane, and and the cocktails are creative and delicious, but what I can't get over is how amazing everything they do with Masa is. The masa is part of every dish(including the blueberry & masa sorbet, which you can't miss), and is just such high quality and so delicious. I want to just go into the kitchen and eat handfuls of it, it's just amazing. Such creative dining, an amazing experience, awesome wait staff, 10 out of 5 stars if I could.
Don't miss this awesome Austin dining experience

If you need tires, get them at Tire Man. Seriously. I can't say enough good things about this business. 

First of all their prices really are better than anyone else's in town. After getting quotes at Costco, Discount Tire, and the Toyota dealership, I called Tire Man. They gave me a great price on better tires than any of the other places I talked to. They put my new tires on with very little wait, and my car has never driven/handled better. It honestly feels like a new car again. Additionally, the owners of this shop are really friendly and helpful, as are the two resident Boston Terriers. And finally, it just feels good to support a local, family-owned business.

In fact, I was so pleased with my experience at Tire Man that I decided to write up a Yelp review, and when I looked at what other reviewers were saying I discovered that not only does Tire Man sell tires, they also do brakes! This was great news for me since Toyota had just told me I needed front and rear brakes at a cost of nearly $300 per axle. Tire Man came through for me again! I had called a few other places for price quotes, and all were in the $200-$250 range. Tire Man charged me much less, and informed me that I only needed rear brakes. Yes, please! I took my car in today, and in no time at all they had my new brakes installed and I was back on the road. They have earned a life-long customer in me based on my two recent interactions.

As ridiculous as this sounds, I have literally in the last week said "I love my new tires." about 5 times. Is it weird to love your tires? If it is then I don't want to be normal.

My boyfriend and I have been here probably a dozen times, but last night our service was the best we've ever had here! Isabelle was extremely attentive and very kind. Normally, when we come here, we don't receive a single drink refill or only get checked on once when we get our food. We don't really mind because we're both in the industry and as long as we get our food, we're happy. But Isabelle is definitely worth the time to write a good review. Food is always amazing and when we go back, I will be requesting her everytime!

I don't know why this place has such low ratings. 
The ladies were super sweet and stayed late to finish my nails. They made sure I was very happy with the final result. The basic pedicure included a really lengthy massage, which I though was nice considering other places only do it for two minutes. 
My gel fill was way better than the place I had previously gone to. She fixed the shape of my nails and made sure I loved the design. 
They are offered me a drink and were very polite the whole time. The best part is that they are open late until 8! I'll definitely be coming back.
