He came and helped with a smile on his face and like always was able to throw in some history and useful knowledge. The  company is great and I would not use anyone else.

I love the sandwich called "the Rachel." It's a Ruben, pressed perfectly. Like all the sandwiches, the bread is perfectly toasted in the center always comes together like a warm cheesy hug. This establishment has been consistently putting out flavorful sandwiches for many years. This is not the type of place you bring shenanigans to. Live by the Golden rule and you will find the environment delightfully inviting and inspiring. It's a great place to sneak away, a perfect rendezvous. Great staff and amazing ownership.

This place has a great vibe. We were here on a chilli Tuesday night for drinks and dinner. We were greeted by the host who informed us about their COVID-19 rules. We order upfront and pay, we were given a number and then waiter would bring us the food. You can take off mask at the table. There was a decent amount of crowd but every one was socially distant. 

We had a combination of tacos that consisted of carne asada, carnitas and chipotle chicken. All of them were very delicious. If you don't like cilantro then please say that upfront when you order otherwise you will be surprised to see a bunch of cilantro and onions on your taco. Nevertheless I really enjoyed my dinner and drinks here. I felt safe and had a great time.

I adore Dr Snowden at Orchards Veterinary Clinic. He took care of my lab when we found out she had kidney failure and was going downhill fast. He was fantastic with her all the way through her treatment and he was the only one I would allow to put her down when it was time. He was caring and empathetic. He cared about Teddy as much as we did. The office staff was caring and hugged me when I needed that hug. I felt she was in the best possible hands all the way through the end. They didn't push unnecessary treatments either. Since then I've taken my other two dogs. Again he was fantastic with them. He got down on the floor with my pup and scratched and petted him until her relaxed. He is a GREAT vet and Orchards will be my only vet going forward. Thank you so much, Orchards!

I woke up with a sore back and typically I would be dreading any type of workout but knowing I was booked for Shea's Core & restore class I couldn't be more excited to attend. Not only did I feel like I got a workout in, I was able to stretch out and really take care of my back with the preplanned spine recovery routine she had planned. I feel refreshed and my body feels taken care of with no worries of powering through this week!

I bought my '98 Saab 900 S from Atomic Auto and had a great experience.  

After looking on Craig's List and finding the right second car for our family, I was surprised to find it was being sold from a mechanic's shop.  But I figured that's a great place to buy a car from - there shouldn't be any hidden problems and there's an actual place to hold accountable if anything goes wrong.  I really didn't need to be so paranoid.

The salesman at Atomic was super laid-back, no pressure, and friendly.  Their policy is that you can take a test drive overnight to make sure you're satisfied.  I noticed some vibration when braking and they had a mechanic go for a drive with me, then added new pads and rotors to the sale.  To top it off, my blood sugar crashed right after we agreed to the purchase and I had to leave.  We sealed the deal on a handshake and I came back the next day to pay for my new car.  They also took care of the title for me, too.  Not bad.

It's been three months and I'm still happy.  They don't have a huge selection, but they'll be the first place I check when I want to upgrade.

The other day, my wife and I met a friend of mine for lunch at the Parkstone Wood Kitchen,near the Portland Airport, and Jill Keller was our server.  I remember the name because of the impact she made on us.  My wife is Gluten Free and Jill made sure that she was absolutely pampered and taken care of.  Thank you Jill!

She also spent the extra time to make us feel right at home, even suggesting the Citris and Pecan salad that indeed was amazing.  

The food was great we all agreed, but it was Jill that made it a 5 star event for us.  We will be back.

This is the Gold's I am currently going to during the week because it is the closest to my work.  It has recently gone through some renovations and I'm really happy with the improvements.  They've redone the indoor track area, locker rooms, updated the equipment, and replaced the TVs with flat screen versions. The women's locker room does have a sauna which might be a plus for some. The dark TV room is great as it takes my mind off being on an elliptical machine, and I like the separate women's area although it's a bit small.  

It's still not as fancy as the MoPac or Tech Ridge locations, but then I don't have to deal with the monster crowds of muscleheads and cardio whores found in those places either so there's no pressure to speed through any part of my workout because there's a wait for a machine.  

It's been ages since I've bought a membership, so luckily I haven't had to talk to any of the staff at the front desk.  The class instructors, however, have all been really helpful and very encouraging.

if you're looking for POSH Nails, this is the same place, just a new name

This is my second time visiting the studio and let me tell you I've found a place to call home for my nail needs! I moved here from out of state, so I've done my research on nail places and came across here. I decided to give it try and have no regrets what-so-ever. The first time I came in was as a walk-in. Cyenna was able to take me for a gel manicure. She made the experience so comfortable, I felt like I was with one of my girlfriends from having such a good time. Along with that, she was also very professional; asked me if everything was okay from shape, color, length, you name it. 

Everyone around me seemed to be in a good mood which made the visit all the better. They have a great selection of colors to choose from (which is nice to have so many options). 

The studio also offers other services as well. My first visit I got my eyebrows wax and if you're like me, you're very hesitant to try a new place for brows, but again Cyenna listened to what I wanted and I was extremely happy with my brows. 

Look no further, and give this place a try.

One word...phenomenal!  Jenn was extremely gentle and patient with my 18 year old, long haired kitty who had developed significant matting on her tummy and, for the first time, required shaving.  I was extremely nervous about having this done, but I certainly didn't need to be as Jenn is very experienced and had everything under control. Although my kitty was significantly angry, she was not harmed in any way.  I am so happy with the end result.  I would recommend Jenn to anyone needing kitty grooming of any kind.  It is obvious Jenn loves kitties and taking care of their needs.

My neighbourhood pool.
It's not fancy. It's a dated building, but what more do you want? It's a pool.
Admission is dirt cheap and public swim times are plentiful and convenient. 
Change rooms are always clean. Staff are helpful and laid back.
The kiddie pool is nice and warm and at it's deepest it's only 2.5' deep, makes a great little spot for the wee ones to splash and play. It's a great option for the kids when the weather is crappy.

I had an amazing experience today with DANI. I usually go to Kara, who is also amazing, but I was late and missed my appointment. When I was given the option to go to another waxer or reschedule, I sat and contemplated for a couple minutes because I was SO SCARED to get a full bikini wax from another waxer, but I am glad I went with Dani! From the very beginning, she was super professional and warm, explaining the wax process and everything she was about to do. She made sure I felt comfortable and talked me through personal care in between waxes. Usually, I feel embarrassed/judged when EWC waxers talk to me about that and push EWC products which are so expensive (especially for a student), but I did not feel that way with Dani. She even gave me samples of the products that she spoke about during my wax. I am glad I missed my appointment because I found my new go-to waxer! :)

I've only been to Bluefin a couple of time and it was during lunch hours. They offer $10.00 lunch special and you can choose between two items on the menu which comes with a complimentary salad (ginger dressing). I was amazed at how large their lunch portions were, because usually $10.00 will get you nothing. It was a full portion meal for a low price! I highly recommend their salmon garlic butter yaki, or their japanese seafood ramen. Very delicious! They also have good sushi here, and very decent portion. I highly recommend this joint for lunch.

While looking for recommendations for a "refresher" tattoo, my colleague told me about her experience with Juli. She shared the amazing work she had done and told me about the beautiful, non-typical studio.  I decided to give it a shot and I am sooo happy I did!  After getting one tattoo re-worked by Juli, I then got a watercolor tattoo from Chris and then went back to Juli for a cosmetic tattoo too (amazing eyebrows!).  I get so many compliments on them all! I highly recommend Juli Moon Studio for tattoos in the Boston area!!

My husband and I visited for our 3rd wedding anniversary. It was such a good time and very relaxing. Everyone was incredibly friendly, it was easy to find, the boat and shuttles were constantly running so you don't have to wait for long to get back to your car. Expect to get wore out from all of the fun your having and the walking from the dock to your shuttle! This is a great family activity. However, you have to be taller than 45inches and 7 years of age or older. This can be an inconvenience, but they do it for your safety.
There is an obstacle course that you get a 45 minute time slot to go on as many times as you want, and then after that you are able to swim on the slide, diving area, trampoline, and rock climbing area for the rest of the day. They have bathrooms, a food truck, a bar for those who are 21+ and plenty of chairs. They also have cornhole boards to pay as well!

I estimate about a third of my yearly earnings gets dumped right into the wonderful land of gaming that is Guardian Games. The staff (all of them) is always quick to greet me with a High Five and sometimes even a shouting of my name, like it's my Cheers. Sure, they mostly cater to Magic and Board Games (the latter of which is a vast collection indeed!), but they have to make money, and that stuff keeps them afloat! And yet even with that heavy focus on those kinda of games, they also have an enormous RPG section, and quite an impressive collection wargaming items as well. And a Lego section! Who doesn't love Legos?

I host several of my regular weekly game nights there (from AD&D2E to Dungeon World to Fading Suns and more), either out in the open or in one of their numerous private rooms (if we need some more quiet focus). While gaming in the back areas, the staff is always attentive, regularly refilling our drink orders and keeping us caffeinated and/or boozed up, whatever the event may call for.

The place tends to get pretty loud during events, and there always seems to be at least one large gathering at any time. But that's because they have a very active community, which welcomes gamers of all ages, genders, and other choices of personal orientation. It's an extremely welcoming place, of which I'm proud to call my self a loyal patron.

Arrived at Delmonico's about half an hour before close; although, there was no one else in the restaurant, we still felt very comfortable.  After inquiring if it were a nuisance for us to dine in so late with the hostess, we were pleasantly greeted by our soon-to-be server, Kristin, who proceeded to escort us to our table. She really made us feel right at home. She briefly explained the menu, daily specials, and offered us a variety of drink options. Drinks were delivered promptly. We decided on her food suggestions, the salmon special and the filet Gorgonzola Alfredo and were nothing less than impressed! The manager also stopped by to make sure things were going well. Will highly recommend this restaurant to everyone we know! Thanks again, Kristin!

Half Raspberry Half Pineapple Dole Whip - Great combo, glad they had it. The raspberry is really really good, and mixed with the OG, even better. 
Kakamora Float - really disappointing. 

Dole whip rankings 
Pineapple - great flavor and creamy smooth texture
Lemon - Pineapple Lanai - tart and refreshing 
Orange - Sunshine Treat - excellent both as a creamsicle and on it's own. Get the lava burst thing. I lava float. 
Raspberry - Aloha Isle - great flavor and creamy 
Lime - Pineapple Lanai - great flavor but sherbet texture. Little icy. UPDATE - last day was creamier and delicious. So, could be hit or miss. 
Lime - Storybook Treats - great flavor and creamy taste. Could be soft serve and not dole whip. 
Pineapple with Coconut - Simba's sunset - Tamu Tamu - best coconut flavor mostly because of the syrup. This was light and refreshing, but ours was very melty. 
Cream Cheese soft serve - Storybook treats - This was really weird. It intrigues you more than anything else but it isn't very good. Better when mixed with the coke but again, not great. 
Strawberry - Refreshment Port - too much like ice cream, did not taste like dole whip.  
Coconut MK - tastes like vanilla with a hint of coconut at the end.

*Disclaimer: I didn't personally buy anything from them. Why? Because I'm too damn blind & it's never affordable when you're blind. FYI - they don't accept insurance.

Where else can you get frames, lenses & have them shipped to your front door for as low as $95? This is includes tax! Probably not even Walmart. We hopped on their bus on W. 6th a few minutes after they opened on a recent Sunday. Because what can't you get out of a trailer or bus these days? And yea, they have AC in there! Fun fact, if you're stupid tall like my boyfran, you won't be able to stand up straight in the bus (sorry giants). I was concerned once we got inside that their selection of frames was too limited in quantity and a bit too hipster for what we were looking for. I was wrong. We had success! They even offer a good amount of sunglasses. 

Within 25 minutes we (and by that I mean me) found some cool grey frames that fit his face and personality. They measured his eyes/face (for where the prescription goes in the lenses), paid on the iPad and we were done. We were informed glasses will be mailed. If an adjustment is needed you can bring them in and they will do it for you. Pretty standard 30 day free return and 12 month free replacement if you break them. 

When it comes to glasses, I believe you should wear them loud and proudly! If you don't have some stupid outrageous prescription you can definitely get some affordable frames here. Unfortunately, it would cost me about 3 pairs of frames here for just the lenses I need. But I appreciate what WB is doing here. Hip frames for a low price without the pain of your typical optical experience.

This place is fantastic for a great sandwich.The Cuban and Italian subs were spot on. The bread is fantastic as are the meats and cheeses. Unless you are extremely hungry, opt for a small. We could not even finish the small sandwiches.

Note this is a small place and there is no where to sit. If it is a nice day, get a sandwich and find a nearby park or go to the greenway to sit and eat. 

You can come in and get meat and cheese sliced to take home to make your own sandwiches. They also have a small grocery store attached with various sauces, homemade pastas, etc. the homemade pasta looked very good.

We will definitely be back.

Qui is a perfect dining experience. Even non-foodie hubby raves this was one of the best meals we've had...and that says a lot as we are lifetime world travelers. Go with an open mind - it's not about one dish--although all seven that we tried were wonderful. It's not even just about the meal. It's the unique hand-crafted cocktails made by a bartender who clearly takes pride in her work.  It's the quirkiness of the amuse bouche. It's the quality local ingredients presented beautifully and served by friendly waitstaff. Everything-even the architecture of the space-works well together.

Was late for our appt but seen within 5 mins. They were very busy on a Sun afternoon, so glad we had an appt. They seem to turn around a mani within 15 mins or so. Had a good experience for my first acrylic nails with french tip gels, $35 (about an hr) - a bit steep but supposed to last 2-3 weeks vs 3-4 days (I was told) if I am hard on my nails/hands - which I am. Since it was my first time I let my s-dtr tell the tech what "I" wanted. My s-dtr got a regular manicure for $12, she's been here before and liked it. I liked my tech, she was patient and answered my questions. I'm supposed to come back every 2-3 weeks for touch up to the acrylics as my nails grow out. I'm not sure I have the time in the long run to do this, but for now I'm looking forward to my nice looking nails.

Make Westlake Hills Vision Center your one stop for any of your vision needs! By far the best customer service experience I've had in the Austin area! The staff was warm and friendly and took care of all of our needs. My husband and I both had eye exams and ordered glasses and contacts. They have a quality selection of frames for you to choose from. This place is one of the few that still has the "old Austin" friendly atmosphere while being upscale and professional. Big thank you and happy holidays to everyone on staff!

What a great facility! I brought in a baby squirrel that my neighbor's dog found in the backyard and decided to bring inside the house to her dog bed. She was treating it as if it was a puppy of her own so luckily t was unharmed.

The staff said its about 1.5 months old and will be transferred to their main facility in Elgin where it will be rehabilitated and released with other squirrels it"s age. 

The gentleman at the centet was
very friendly, helpful, aswered all of my questions and explained how the squirrel would be rehabilitated and how long they would have it.

They have incubators and bins and are fully equipped to take care of this cute little furry one. If you happem to find a wild animal that is injured or abandoned, be sure to bring them here and please make a donation to help with the cost of feeding and care for the animal.

I'm so glad there are facilities like this one to help save the animals. I would highly recommend them.

In Boston for business and will be here for some time. Finding good places to eat is essential. Pizza was my craving and Yelp searching began.

I love tradition and Regina's fit the bill. The ambience of this place is exactly what I love. Nothing fancy. Just great service and food.

I had the 10 inch #14 Classico. The dough is outstanding. Lite sauce and great toppings. It was heavy on the artichokes and next time I will try a different pizza.

There are many choices and I didn't count all of the them.  Something for everyone. The 10 inch could easily serve 2 people. 

You can't go wrong at Regina's. I notices a lot of folks ordering simple pizzas with 1 or 2 toppings. The sauce and crust is soooo good, I understand why.

If your looking for pizza, stop in at Regina's, you will thank me.

I always shop Autozone.  I remember they were Autoshack, just bought from RadioShack.

They have continually improved.

My wife had been several times before me. And had great service.

It is about relationships. 

This store is tops.  I hope upper management allows Emil and Jesse to grow with the company.

These two are excellent with working to achieve the customers goals even when the customer is not fully sure of the route needed to have a cost effective repair.

I always go back to this AutoZone!

This place is legit delicious! I have had two different orders from here, pork tacos (taco al pastor - pork and pineapple)  and a fried fish burrito. The tacos were tender, juicy, and SUPER tasty, I brought them home and wished I had ordered more after gobbled them up. The fish burrito was incredible, really spot on for flavor and HUGE. Well worth the price, it was more than a meal for me. 

I cant recommend La Taqueria enough, they are friendly and the prices are great!

This is now my go to for my weekly grocery shopping trips.

I live in Melrose near a Shaw's, but this Super Stop and Shop has a MUCH larger selection... AND is ~40% cheaper...AND it's on my way home... AND super convenient to get into and out of off the Fellsway.

The aisles were a little confusing at first, but I have a pretty set list I run though each week so after like 3 trips I got the lay of the store pretty good.

I've moved around the last few years and seen the gas station / grocery store combo before... but the layout of this one is awkward to me.  All the lanes being are one way only?  I've never seen that before and definitely skipped ahead in line the first time I got gas here because I didn't understand the setup.

We are coming up on the one year mark for having our adopted pup, Ralphie, and we could not imagine life without him. 

Thanks to the great people at PRBJ that rescued his Mom, who was turned into a kill shelter while very pregnant. PRBJ oversaw the birth of the litter and fostered the puppies until they were all adopted. These pups knew nothing but love from the time that they were born, instead of the sad alternative seen by many dogs and cats.  

The adoption process started on the PRBJ website, where we filled out an application and fell in love with our pup's picture before meeting him. The foster moms oversaw the last stages of our adoption and helped to screen us, they were very informative and had a wonderful rapport with the pups. 

I attended several workshops at the PRBJ storefront at the Oviedo Mall, which were helpful for a new puppy owner and gave our 8 week old pup a chance to socialize with dogs of various ages. The storefront also had new toys and various items for sale, at a deep discount. 

If you are considering adopting an animal, please check out this great organization. I know many friends who have adopted animals from this group and all of us agree, that Judy and her team really have a special touch...and the animals seem to know that.

We come here about once a month for AYCE sushi. We have noticed the dishes are getting worn with almost every piece of china with a crack or chip.  There is also a lot of graffiti in the booths.
Makes everything less appetizing and you wonder about pride of ownership.

Since we were last here the place had a facelift. The dishes replaced, no longer chipped as in my last review. Service was outstanding and the food was great and plentiful. Recommended.

Having been through my fair share of airports, I have a deep love for PDX.  Pianists play live music near the security gates.  Lines move quickly. Food is decent to good - Laurelwood and Flying Elephants provide much better grub than every other airport I've visited so far.  There's a Powell's for your literary needs. Free wifi! Cute little shops to find last minute gifts for folks who want a souvenir from Portland. Oh yes, and a Dragon Tree Spa right in the middle of it all.  I love their northwest location so I've happy they have one way out here at the airport. All sorts of yummy things here to keep you going and the free water refilling stations make for a peaceful journey.

Life sure is easy in Portland, compared to LAX or SFO at least.

Cathedral Eye Care makes going to the doctor enjoyable again!  I recently saw Dr. Sarah Chewerda for an eye exam and new prescription.  She is really friendly and down to earth. I had experienced a serious retinal issue in the past, and Dr Chewerda put me completely at ease with her engaged, knowledgeable approach to addressing my concerns. She is truly compassionate and takes the time to really explain the often complex landscape of the eye and how it works. The staff is warm and welcoming too!  The coffee they offer you upon arrival is a lovely touch, and simply wonderful! If you're looking for a first rate eye professional with a relaxed, genuinely caring approach, look no further than Cathedral Eye Care!

Having spent almost no time in the Gulf Coast region, I've never developed a taste for Cajun food, so when I see shrimp and grits on a menu I worry that I might be in the wrong restaurant. At Lucile's, that fear would have been totally misplaced.

The restaurant is a converted house so it genuinely feels like you're just in your grandma's breakfast nook, which will either feel cramped or intimate or both depending on how you look at it. We ended up seated at the communal table which was set for eight people, so you can make a new friend or two like we did, having a pleasant conversation with some locals about the merits of Cajun cuisine and the weather in Rocky Mountain National Park. The servers are all suavely polite, almost to the point of being smarmy, but they were taking good care of all the patrons.

The food is tremendous. We started with an order of the beignets, and I strongly counsel you not to skip these light, airy, powdered-sugary delights. My scrambled eggs were a little watery and weak, but the perfectly seasoned potatoes, savory andouille sausage, and enormous sweet flaky buttermilk biscuit more than made up for their minor failings.

Maybe I wimped out by avoiding grits or seafood or anything super spicy, but even if you go that route at Lucile's you'll wind up with one of the best breakfasts imaginable.

Features Canadian artisan-made inuksuit and carvings.  I really didn't know about inuksuit and I was drawn into the store by the interesting looking sculpture of rough stones stacked in the form of a human figure.

Here's a little history: The people of the Canadian Arctic are known as the Inuit. They used to be called Eskimos, which came from a Native American word for 'eater of raw meat'. Now the Arctic people are officially known as the Inuit, which means 'the people', or singularly, Inuk, which means 'the person'.

The inukshuk may have been used for navigation, as a point of reference, a marker for travel routes, fishing places, camps, hunting grounds, places of veneration, drift fences used in hunting or to mark a food cache.

The store itself has quality art with a small section for the usual Canadian touristy stuff.  They are able to answer questions about the history and the artists.

I would return for their beautiful Canadian indigenous art.

Everything about this place was amazing! The food, the wine, the service, the atmosphere, everything.  I think we had the best server I've had at any restaurant, Alex.  He went above and beyond what you would expect even at a nice restaurant. His descriptions of the specials were very detailed and convincing. He made sure our little one was taken care of and happy the entire time.  We were nervous about going to a nice dinner with our 1 year old and he made it a wonderful experience for my husband and I both.  Our food was absolutely amazing, we had the swordfish special and the fettuccine, both had so much flavor and melted in our mouths! I could not ask for a better experience, worth every penny! Thanks again Alex.

Seriously Mike & Patty's? Seriously?

Why is it that everything you make is so freakin' good? Oh, you little hidden jewel, you. 

I've been goin' here for years and have never had any issues with Mike & Patty's, except for somewhat longer than average waits during peak hours, but it's cool. My Bacon & Egg Fancy is worth the wait anyways; add an ice coffee to that, and I could wait for days. Not feelin' the Fancy? That's fine, go for the Egg Torta with Chorizo. It's my #2 go to, and it's solid.

Not a fan of eggs in your sandwiches? Umm... then you're just not my kinda guy. Eggs are the perfect food... Still, lucky you -- Mike & Patty's can and will make you happy yet. They've got lots of cold cut subs galore,  and hot dogs too!

Although I no longer live down the street from Mike & Patty's (oh, the good 'ole days), I would still make the trip for their Fancy any day. Everything's cooked to order, right in front of you in an open face kitchen. It's a neighborhood joint. Good food. What more could you want?

Yes. Yum!! 

A few of my coworkers and I gathered and chose Talat for the first location of our dinner club. What a lovely backdrop (delicious food) to this magical night. 

At the suggestion of the waitress and the fact that it was "family style", we ordered almost the entire menu. Choosing the fried trout over the steamed one. Because: The South. 

Each dish climbed in flavor, the squid and dessert probably being our standout favorites. But not a disappointment in sight. The squid broth I would happily drink by the pint. Pour it over rice, noodles, or my waiting body. 

Visit Talat before they leave Gato but I believe they are aiming for their own storefront now - which I'll happily patronize. 

All the stars.

I'll give this 5 stars because it's one of my favorite places in Davis and my go-to. The food is consistently good, they have a good drink list, the servers are nice, and most importantly, they let you bring dogs if you sit outside! And they bring said dogs water and treats.

I've been here with between 1 and 16 people. Even though they don't take reservations, I've never waited more than 15 minutes for a table. It's not great for late-night, as the bar area gets really crowded, but that's fine with me.

Hotpot is my favorite, I always have Hotpot with my friends and family. Simmer Huang Restaurant provided the different type of Hotpot experience for people. You can eat your own Hotpot in three different ways, which is really cool.  I have been to Simmer Huang Restaurant two times in past few months. Simmer Huang Restaurant is located on Kingsway street, Burnaby. It's right across the street from Crystal Mall, and the location is very easy to find.   The ambiance is modern. The servers were nice and friendly. In this restaurant, you can order directly from the menu or create your own combination hotpot. After you ordered the food, the servers would bring all the ingredients on the table. Then, they began to put all the ingredients into the pot for you.   You pick a creation off the menu or create your own combination. The staff then proceeds to cook the food in front of you. First, the server really organized putting all meat and vegetable in the pot to steam them. Once everything got all cooked, it's the time to put the sauce on top of food. Waiting for another 5 mins, we could eat the food. When the food in the Hotpot was almost gone, we dipped Chinese pancakes with the left ingredients in the pot. Also, we ordered vegetable on the side. Once we have done Chinese Pancakes and the food in the pot, the server put the water in the Hotpot. We began to use the normal way to cook Vegetable in the Hotpot. The sounds like lots of works for eating Hotpot at Simmer Huang, but food taste was great. It was a very different experience for me. I love it.

I have no idea why all of these negative reviews have appeared on your site. I have been using Earth20 for five years now, and have never had anything other than prompt, efficient service. They have suspended delivery when requested, every time I have had extra water on hand, and have delivered quickly whenever requested. I have never had any problems dealing with their customer service people whatsoever, and as to the comment that their water "tasted like swamp water" that is just untrue. The fact that they provide BPA Free bottles is an added plus.

Wow. Going to Barbara Christman is unlike any other doctor visit that you've ever been on. She's an outstanding healthcare provider. Barbara is a thorough, caring, and thorough nurse practitioner. From OB/GYN to nutrition, Barbara is thinking about you, the patient, from a whole body perspective. I was really pleased with the care that I received AND I felt stoked about taking control of my health, my life. She recommended some great dentists, derms, and other docs too to help me get my healthcare team in order. Barbara is really fabulous - this is high-quality healthcare at its best.

I was looking into companies to hire to help with my move from a 1 bedroom apartment into a newly purchased condo/townhome. I had researched a handful of companies, and was getting ready to settle on one in particular when I came across this company being reviewed on Yelp. I scrolled down to read the different comments, and lo and behold, one of my friends had used them back in May. She left a glowing review, so I decided to call them. Man, am I glad I did. 

First, their customer service representative on the phone was great to deal with, and I was impressed with their charge structure. So many other companies charge for driving time to and from your place, and many charge for a flight of stairs. Priestley & Sons charged for neither. 

Second, I knew I was going to like them when they were right on time for my move. The two men pulled up in a big red moving truck, which was incredibly clean. Scott and Tony were the guys who then got out and made the magic happen. They were incredibly nice, efficient, and professional, and had the entire move done in less than 2 hours. Nothing broken, everything wrapped and carefully stored on their truck, and delivered with no worrying on my part (I wanted only my furniture moved, my friends and I took care of all my boxes and loose items). 

There was only a 1 hour minimum move requirement, whereas most companies had a 2, 3, or 4 hour minimum. My final bill was only prorated for the last 45 minutes, so I decided to leave a larger than usual tip as I was really impressed with the move. 

I highly recommend this company to anyone looking for a great experience from start to finish.

This place is authentically Italian. They use 00 flour for the pizza and breads. Super crispy and delicious crusty. The Italian guys for Orlando City FC are regulars and there a lot. That's a pretty good endorsement that this is a Taste of Italy and not New Jersey.

A quick update. We had been a few times and had great service. This last time the Futbol Soccer team were actually dining in and not picking up. We were definitely not experiencing the same level of customer service we had before. I'll give them another try before thinking of adjusting the rating.

Love love love this place!!  We used to live right down the street from Heirloom Market and every time we went, the food was consistently good.  Their Korean pork sandwich is one of my favorite menu items (but it is spicy, even for my Korean tongue) along with the fried sweet potatoes.  Chefs Cody and Jiyeon do a seamless job of combining true Southern bbq w/ Korean bbq.   Apart from my fave sandwich, the smoked wings, pulled pork, pulled chicken, and brisket are all delicious.  I really like how they do not put sauce on the meat before serving it to you.  I usually have decision paralysis when it comes to sauces so I am always taking turns between each bite dipping it in the table sauce and the korean bbq sauce.   

Yes, finding parking can get very annoying, as well as finding a place to sit.   Do not go with a big group if you plan on eating in.  If you really find the parking/seating a hindrance in making a decision to go there, just order to-go.  They do a really good job of packing the bread separate from the meat, with all the sauces you want, so none of it gets soggy by the time you get home.

After getting Rick's (http://m8ryx.yelp.com/) highest recommendation, I knew it was only a matter of time before I made the short trek out to SE 122nd a few blocks south of Stark to give Puerto Marquez a try. I too grew up in Central Valley Cali and share his relative disappointment with the "midrange" chip 'n salsa Mexican restaurants in pdx, so I tried to temper my high hopes with a little cynicism.

All that cynicism went out the window within minutes of stepping in the front door. From the outside it's a very humble looking establishment (as are most on SE 122nd) squeezed into a little parking lot with a 7-11, a Panderia/Mercado, and a Mexican Furniture store - but once inside it's actually a fair bit larger than it appears.

They have a couple TVs, as well as the familiar painted mural walls, but here their depictions of a seaside Mexican village, complete with fishermen casting their nets into the surf, is actually relevant - Puerto Marquez definitely specializes in mariscos (multiple pages of fishy goodness). But for those of you not down with critters from the sea, they also offer a fairly comprehensive assortment of ground-bound food items and more "Tex-Mex" style dishes and combos - and aesthetically you're not left out either, as the north side of the restaurant has portraits of Gauchos and other standard Mexican-themed decorations.

Wanting to see Puerto Marquez doing what they do best, and always game for good seafood, My Lady and I both ordered up some Camarones platos - mine a la Diabla (upon the recommendation of Pablo, our server), hers Mojo de Ajo. Don't let the fact that we both ordered shrimp give you the wrong impression - their menu features bass, halibut, salmon, squid, octopus, scallops, even lobster - basically if it's edible and comes from they sea, they serve it! They've even got at least 3 different varieties of ceviche!

With mouths watering in anticipation we both enjoyed the chips (which tasted fresh and crisp, if not house-made) and to a lesser extent the salsa (decent, though pretty standard and not hot enough for our tastes), and My Lady really appreciated the bean dip, though she found it a tad too smoky - and vegetarians beware: it DOES have pork in it; in fact non-pescetarian veg-heads may be disappointed overall with the menu at Puerto Marquez, but those who partake in seafood will likely find exponentially more options here than most other Mexican restaurants.

As is common in many Mexican restaurants, the plates are huge but shallow, creating the illusion that you're getting more than you actually are - but fear not, the portion sizes on both our platters was more than ample. Taking a cue from Larry David, yes, we did count how many shrimps we each got - I got 8, My Lady got 9 - but these were very large, butterflied, tail on "jumbo-shrimp", so neither of us left hungry. In fact, these were some of the freshest, most succulent shrimps I've enjoyed anywhere in pdx!

My Camarones a la Diabla were terrific, and while it was prepared with more fire at Puerto Marquez than at many other places in town, I still found myself wishing it had a touch more heat. The spicy, red, tomato-chile based sauce was divine and contrasted perfectly with the sweet shrimp, and had no other veggies to get in the way. My Lady's dish was more of a garlic, butter, onion, and bell pepper affair - equally outstanding!

We both were really impressed by the rice - seasoned simply, with just a few tidbits of carrot and peas, and a mellow yellow color, it was way more pleasant to look at and devour than the often unnaturally orange-colored Mexican rice you find at many other places. I DO however wish they offered black beans, or at least whole beans, as I've just never been a fan of refried beans; they did let me sub in extra rice so it was no big loss.

The service was attentive, personal, and very friendly - and without resorting to the stock (though charming) "Hola Amigos!" that greets you in many other Mexican places. Pablo asked us how we'd heard of them, talked a little about their menu, and was happy to describe anything or make recommendations. They've been in business since 2000, apparently catering almost exclusively to a Mexican-American audience, but since being featured in The O and Willie Week last year, they've begun modest advertising (see their ad on pg. 18 of WW's "Cheap Eats 2009" guide) and have seen increased business from gringos and Latinos alike.

While their seafood prices are a little higher than the rest of the menu, it's right in line with (or even cheaper than) what you'd expect to pay for such fresh and expertly prepared dishes elsewhere. Really, I think the only area I'd say could be improved is to offer more than just refried beans, and maybe some more inspired salsa. Despite this, I'm gonna have to join the club and declare this one of my favorite Mexican restaurants in town!

This is hands down the best and most consistent Vietnamese in the Columbus, albeit not the most conveniently located. I have been going to Mi Li for four years and have yet to find a Pho that I like more or a bahn mi than is more savory and delicious. 

I have taken multiple out of town friends here and have never had anyone leave with a less than satisfied full belly. The only criticism I could even muster is of their bubble tea which only comes frozen causing the tapioca balls to become so tough that, before you reach the half way point of your drink, they are no longer able to navigate the straw.

Simply put, Mi Li is a delicious diamond in the rough and worth the drive to Cleveland Ave every time.

Bunn has chronicled our life and has been our photographer for over a decade. She has this style that can't be learned and creative vision of a photo setting her apart from others. 

Aside from being an outstanding photographer, she is a great person with a funny personality that will remove any anxiety you may have when getting photographed. 

She had done:

1. My dad's family portrait ~2004
2. My wife and I's engagement photos in 2010
3. Our 2011 wedding in Bali (which has been blessed to be featured in a global wedding magazine and several wedding blogs.) 
4. 2012 Photos of me that we used to rent a full size billboard as a bday present to my wife in Indonesia. 
5. My wife's boudoir photos in 2014
6. Winter family portraits in 2015

Point being is that you develop a trust with someone that will capture moments in your life and say yes, these photos captured who we are.

Went for my two year anniversary and the highlight was definitely how we got the shittest table in the restaurant (the closest to the door) and it was not a big deal somehow. I am a big disliker of tables close to the door but somehow it was still romantic and special. Hats off to them. 

They had escargot which made me change the 4 star review into 5 star cause any place that makes snails taste like that is unbelievable. 

Service was excellent, the food was fantastic. The price can be left for interpretation based on your social status (aka how much money you make). 

Not somewhere you just decide to go on a night out and eat but for those special occasions highly recommend. 

The Yaletown restaurant area is incredibly competitive. Out of all the restaurants in that area - this is probably my favourite one.

I also saw Pamela Anderson LOL

If you need a home inspection, do yourself a favor and call Tri-Value Consultants.  Two weeks ago (late July) Michael and Joseph Scaduto inspected a 3-family home in Salem, MA for me, which I will be moving into in October.  Simply put, they are the best home inspectors on the North Shore.  

Personality - This was my first home inspection as a buyer, and it was like having family members or close friends perform the inspection.  Michael and Joe are in your corner and have your best interests at heart.

Performance - A+ Michael and Joe are incredibly detailed.  Their inspection and written report will be more comprehensive than any other home inspector (I've since asked around).  Michael literally crawled into attic spaces, was hanging off porch railings and got dirty in every corner of the home.  

Cost - Less than the big named companies, and remember, they'll stay longer and do a better job finding issues (and potential issues).

My family and friends will be using the Scaduto's.

Always such a guaranteed good time here. Exceptional acoustics in a cozy rectangle of a bar means you always feel the music (in more ways than one - this is jazz we're talking about). The bartender pulls off the superhuman feat of always being here, so you feel like a regular even if you don't frequent the place. It drips with cool in the place at all times, and they feature live music - get this - 365 days a year. The only thing that could make the place better? Get rid of the very distracting TV screen in the place, which jars you out of what would otherwise feel like a first-class ticket to another time period.

I get food from El Coyote at least once a week and every single time I've ordered something from here, they haven't let me down. This place makes delicious, cheap, and filling food that satisfies my rather constant cravings for Mexican food.

The Chimichanga here is really, really delicious. It is a generously sized burrito with a heap of guacamole and sour cream liberally drizzled on the top. Out of everything that I've tried here, I would have to say that this is my favorite. However, the Chorizo Nachos are a very, very close second. If you're a hungry person like myself, I'd recommend getting both and sharing some of the nachos since everyone loves nachos :) The tacos are also excellent and pack a whole bunch of flavor in each bite.

El Coyote also has really yummy hot sauce so I'd recommend to ask them for a bunch before leaving! It goes really well with their rice as well. 

PS: They also sell a guacamole burger, which comes with a side of fries...it's really yummy and got my boyfriend on the guacamole train!

I usually order all of my photography and printing supplies through another large photography store in New York City. I now live in Portland so I decided to try out Pro Photo Supply, and I couldn't be happier. The entire staff is kind, professional, passionate, and most importantly supportive of their community.

I recently purchased a professional Epson inkjet printer, which I was going to order through the other store and have shipped to me. Pro Photo Supply was so friendly and easy to work with. They had the printer in stock, for which I was able to pay with ease and security through a direct link online, and was personally delivered to me the next day. Chris brought the 50 lb. machine up the stairs to my studio without hesitation and it is already up and running. I would still be waiting anxiously for it to arrive on my porch. Instead, I was able to get what I needed easily, at the same price, and faster than having it shipped! Thank you!

Wow, Kimberly is an amazing amazing teacher! Came here for the noon class for the first time to try Kimberly's class and she was all that I expected and more! The studio is gorgeous: small, easy check in, stones through from the Whole Foods and near the orange line.

Kimberly explicitly explains every single move but her real gift is probably more in humble demeanor.  She gives awesome assists, plays really nice music, and also has a very nice transitional flow.

Her diction is great too; some yoga teachers have GREAT voices and Kimberly is def. one of those--she is easy to follow and has a perfect balance of pushing you but also making you realize NBD it's just yoga!

For sure will be back for her Mon and Wed classes at Charlestown Yoga. Thank you, Kim! 

~Tamara W.

My house is always stockpiled with a selection of Celestial Seasonings teas. And as an avid tea drinker, it gets consumed rather quickly.

But as tasty as is it when you buy it in the store, there's nothing like getting it from the source. For whatever reason, the tea shop at the factory always has flavors I've never heard of or seen in stores.

And if you ever get the chance to take the tour, take it. I used to work for an ice cream cone factory, and basically this is the same thing, except with tea. But nonetheless it's a fascinating look behind the curtain of one of the country's most popular tea manufacturers.

This place is amazing. It was the best healthcare I have ever received. Every single midwife who works there is dedicated to helping pregnant people have the best possible birthing experience. I had a hard first birth, and every single midwife I had an appointment with made sure to tell me positive stories about Second births that had gone really well. The women who attended my birth truly celebrated with us and made it such a special experience. I'm approaching my daughters first birthday and am always going to be glad that I had the opportunity to give birth here. It was a healing and transformative experience for me. Now more than ever, I'm so glad to know that women still have access to this care.

This Walgreens is wonderful and you can tell it is because they have a great management team.  The employees are pleasant, positive and always so quick to ask if they can help you find something.  The Store Manager Marcia is always present and she is clearly the one that sets the tone for the positive energy of this store.   

The photo department is well run and the Walgreens app makes it easy to print photos immediately from my phone and Facebook.  The pharmacy is also well run with a  positive, professional staff.  

There are two employees that deserve special mention because they greet each customer as if the store was their families business. Whitmis and Jayshree are often working the front and my children look forward to seeing them.  We love this store!

Blooming Moon Wellness Spa is the best place I have been to in Portland. I have been going to the Blooming Moon for 4 years and I have NEVER had a bad experience, bad treatment or not come out feeling better than when I came in. 

The establishment is clean, calming, and reasonably priced. I have had brow waxes and every kind of facial/foot soak from Ginny. She is truly a zen master. This place gives a whole new meaning to relaxation and can melt the stress away! 

All of the staff are professional and friendly. Reminder calls about appointments are greatly appreciated! Free parking on the street & is never hard to find. Plus you can go grab some wine at Hop & Vine next door or some lunch at Delphina's on the other side.  

If you have been looking for a place to go that gives awesome spa treatments that are reasonably priced and would like to do it with nice knowledgeable people...look no more! You have found your spa oasis!

Whenever I'm in town I HAVE to stop at Lazy Moon. I love that the environment is so relaxed. I have yet to try bocce ball but its definitely on my list. Ordering is usually a breeze but it can be PACKED around dinner time on the weekend. My go to is a slice with caramelized onions and applewood smoked bacon with a side of ranch. Their pizza is absolute heaven. I wish they would expand to south florida but until then I'll just keep returning to Orlando to get my fix.

This place is fun. I love their space and open kitchen. Their menu is easy to read and I like their options. The staff is patient and knowledgable with giving suggestions or information. My friend was excited for their gluten free options, as well as a vegan meatball. Everything we had was made fresh to order and tasted amazing. My meatballs had just enough kick. The sauce was fresh and well balanced and not overdone. I hate too much sauce, and their portions were just right. I felt their price point was spot on. I didn't have to wait long and enjoyed watching the men cook my food. I look forward to returning and trying all of their options. I'm so glad this spot is in our neighborhood.

No words can completely do justice to the wonderment that is the Cantab Lounge. In a city with no shortage of generic Irish pubs, college-kid meat markets and overpriced, underwhelming dance clubs, the Cantab is a breath of fresh air (even if it sometimes doesn't smell quite as nice as that  metaphor might imply - part of the charm, right?).

The Cantab is a live-music venue for all those people like myself who prefer to drop $5 on a well-honed bar band than $30 on a over-hyped HOB show (Thanks, TicketBastard!). Its music runs the gamut from blues and country to funk and disco, but it's (almost always) live, and (absolute always) amazing.

There are two undisputed stars of the show here. Free Tuesday bluegrass is a Happening - yes, capital H. Come in, cozy up to the bar with the throngs, throw a couple bucks into Geoff's donations hat, and tap your toes away to the best fiddlers and banjo-pickers offered by the city of Cambridge (well, let's be real: Berklee College of Music). 

But for my money, there is undoubtedly no better night of dancing in Boston then the Chicken Slacks on Thursday. This funk-soul outfit brings together twentysomething hipsters, soccer moms, and a plethora of goofily grizzled barflies. Singer Diamond D is an endearing mish-mash of James Brown, Al Green, and that sketchy homeless guy that cat-calls weekend partygoers on the corner of Mass Ave and Prospect. Ladies: don't stand too close to him if you know what's good for you. (Where "What's good for you" = not acquiring syphilis).

I hear good things about the poetry slams and blues jams, as well, but I'm afraid to go, since spending four nights a week there will severely empty my bank-account and leave my social life unacceptably non-diverse. But I'll keep coming back to the Cantab as long as it offers feel-good music and an intriguingly varied clientele.

I went with a group of friends (7 total) at dinnertime on a weekend, and the wait for a table was pretty good. Inside, we were seated in the basement area. The complimentary basket of chips was perfect for a group of hungry college kids, and the only appetizer we ordered was guacamole for the table. I got chicken enchiladas, which were great and filling. The size of my friend's chicken quesadilla was huge--enough for lunch the next day. Our waiter was friendly and funny. The price was more than cheap college kids typically pay, but definitely reasonable and normal for a restaurant. Overall it was a great experience and we all definitely want to go again.

I recently found this store mentioned in raving terms on the Community of Richmond's facebook page...I thought to myself "my husband use to go there" so I looked them up online and booked an appt.  Samson emails and asks a few questions and we converse back and forth. He solved my problem by email...re: snow tires and all season.

I got in the next day...his wife drove me home so I didn't have to sit around. He gave me a discount for keeping me waiting...what!!!! unheard of!!! He explained everything and was obviously very honest.

I go back in a week to tighten the torque, then tire rotations every ? km, free repair of a fixable flat tire...all for free!!!!

By the way, I was mistaken, my husband never went there but I'm sure glad I did.  Thanks Samson!!!

I recently got new insurance that required a PCP in their network who would also do referrals, so I had to leave my primary doc of many years. (She doesn't take insurance, but to me she was worth it, and before this year didn't have to have referrals for specialists.) I was very nervous about getting a new doctor. Well, there was no need to worry, because Dr. Velasquez is fantastic. I truly didn't expect to like a new doctor that much, but she is thorough, down to earth, intelligent and knowledgeable. I'm extremely impressed. The referrals process is a pain, but Dr. Velasquez and her staff do their best to streamline things as much as they can. I recommend Dr. Velasquez wholeheartedly.

Found this place last minute! We were wanting authentic mexican and we were not disappointed! It's Friday and so they had a Sangrias and Margs 2 for 1 special. I ordered the sangrias and I was not disappointed! Left feeling great lol. We were immediately greeted by our hostess and server. Super friendly guy but I did not catch his name. Either way he was great and seemed to be the only male server on the floor so hope that narrows it down lol. I ordered the pollo rico, SO. GOOD. Chicken breast smothered in onions, peppers, and cheese. Yummm, it comes with tomatoes but I took them off. Overall the food was AMAZING, the restaurant was so quaint and cute, gave me a real mexican atmosphere. Definitely recommend!

Great spot for a quick pastry. Their selection is really large and I wish I was hungry for more so I could try every one. They have a lot of unique twists to classic pastry items too (i.e. the everything croissant, which I wish I wouldn't ordered too). 

We ended up ordering the almond croissant and the leek quiche. Almond croissant was sooo flakey and crispy. I loved the texture a lot. The taste was good too but not the best almond croissant I've ever had. The quiche had a wonderful, buttery crust, and the inside had a salty and savory flavor. I would get this again. At $5, it was priced fairly too. If I lived in the area, I would give their breads a try.

This place was so nice after a long beach day. I mean what's better in the summer in New England than some fresh seafood?! Especially when you're seated on their very nice balcony. 

I admit we only ordered a few things from here. I had the clam chowder and we split a small raw bar tower and the crab legs. But everything was so fresh! The oysters were delicious, as were the shrimp and crab legs. Their clam chowder was so good I wished I had also ordered the chowder fries. The table next to us had them and I was definitely feeling a little envious. Ah well, next time.

Super close to my house so I loved coming here to study. The employees were always super friendly and kind, perfectly fine with me crashing for 4-6 hours at a time. Sometimes it does get busy during weekends but you just have to come early. I love the atmosphere, absolutely so clean and refreshing. I love seeing the wall of manga and the little drawings everywhere; kinda reminds me of some place they'd use in dramas. The waffle here is actually really good if you don't mind the wait, same with the hot drinks; they're reaaaaally aesthetically pleasing. Overall lovely place to come, just know the right times and the right people

This is our favorite restaurant.  I'm sorry to hear that one of the folks below had a bad experience; however ours has never been anything but excellent.  We visit Portland Prime at least a few times a month.  

We typically sit in the bar (Ask for Stephanie and tell her Jennifer sent you) but all of the servers are marvelous.  The drinks are amazing... Michael, the bartender has created a few wonderful drinks from his own recipe and my fav is the white apple martini.  It's not too sweet and his magic recipe makes it perfect!  

Happy hour is the best - super great food, reasonably priced.  Dinner is awesome as well; their seared Ahi tuna is one of my favorites.  

We love it so much, we bought gift certificates for a number of friends and family.

We're going to be there tonight!  Hope to see you there!

I absolutely love love love this place! Angela is the best she was able to save my lashes from a previous lash artist that wasn't aware on how to safely give me a lash set. She has been able to work with my difficult natural lash line. She is sweet- cute as a button- and honestly makes me feel so beautiful inside and out. I love her and beyond happy I found her. Please go see her she will change your life. Has a soft touch and I fall asleep in our appointments.

I called on Friday evening and talked to Terry.  He accurately described a car that he had on his lot that perfectly fit my needs.  I got there around 11 AM on Saturday and he very patiently walked around his lot and showed me lots of cars and answered my many many questions.  Eventually I drove off around noon in my almost new car.  He helped me with financing and he gave me a great price on my clunker that I traded in.
I got home and checked out all the other cars for sale in Austin that were similar to the one I bought.  He gave me a really great deal!
I love my car!  For the first time after buying a car I didn't have that nauseating feeling that I was making a big mistake or paying too much for something that was losing value while I watched it sitting on the lot.
Terry followed up with a phone call to make sure I was happy with my car. That has never happened before and I've owned lots of cars.
I am so happy with my purchase and will definitely go back to this group!

Sarah Moss is amaaaaazing!!!

For myriad reasons this girly girl hadn't had her hair touched by a professional in well over a year. Cancer/chemo hair loss, a lost pregnancy, and other reasons contributed to the desperate state of my locks. 

Sarah greeted me immediately upon arrival and offered me a beverage, then proceeded to analyze my hair with her trained eye. She saw my vision of piecey layers but I needed her expertise with the color--I was going to leave it completely up to her. I have never, EVER marveled at my own hair color (I have gotten my hair colored in a salon religiously since college--20 years now--with the exception of the last year+) but she nailed it. She looked at my grown-out roots and skin tone then asked if I was okay just letting her do her thing. What I have now is a gorgeous warm chocolatey brown with a touch of red and gold. How she managed to add dimension in a one-step color process is beyond me, but she simultaneously brought out my hazel eyes and complemented my face shape while maintaining my natural summer highlights. She also gives THE BEST scalp massages In her shampoo. 

I had gotten to the point of almost dreading having my hair done in my former city with my former stylist--long and slow appointments, cold and industrial environment (going for a trendy, avant gard vibe, I suppose), lacking in basic customer service from the staff and overall experience as a whole, stylists chatting among themselves....we've all been there. 

Not only is my hair amazing, but the entire experience was a forgotten joy. It had been a while since I had allowed myself to be totally pampered. I almost fell asleep several times ("that's okay! you're not the first and you won't be the last," Sarah said) and she appropriately conversed/let me doze, taking my lead during the 3 1/2 hours I was there. Is there anything worse during hair appointment than having to entertain your stylist?

The ambiance is soothing, the entire staff is friendly, parking was a breeze (street parking at just $1.20/hour) and I left relaxed and happy. Can't ask for more. 

Thank you to ROAR! and Sarah Moss :)

I've been meaning to leave a review but life got a little busy. However, this place did such a great job on restoring my boots and had such great customer service that I had to come back weeks later to leave a review. The store has a new owner who is very friendly and helpful. You can tell he is really trying to turn this place around. I do not know what it was like before but i had a very good experience with them. I had a pair of boots that i love so much but had been worn for almost two year and were giving up on my. The owner was able to restore them back to pretty much new! On top of that, he had quoted me for a Wednesday but was able to get it to me quicker. I really appreciate the quality, customer service, and timeliness of this shoe repair shop. Thank you.

I was in town for a wedding and forgot my contacts (and had an expired prescription), but was able to book an appointment with Dr. Torre the same day. 

He and his staff were efficient and knowledgable. We didn't have to wait more than a few minutes and, during the exam, Dr. Torre was personable and helped me understand why the subscription contacts I'd been wearing were drying out my eyes. 

He took the time to explain the differences (and prices!) between a variety of openings, gave me a few prescriptions to try, which more than got me through the weekend, and was funny to boot. 

If I lived in the area, I'd definitely return. Great doctor, great office.

Three of us ate at Puritan & Company tonight for the first time. All of the food was delicious. I had the pan roasted fluke with spring succotash, fennel and guanciale; my husband had the roasted duck with mushroom, sweet potato and pear; and our friend had the roasted chicken with peas, carrots, quinoa, and onion. All were fantastic!  Appetizers were Island Creek and Wellfleet oysters, deviled crab biscuits, smoked bluefish pate and swordfish salami. All were delicious and the service was impeccable. The room is really funky in an Inman Square casual way. I highly recommend it.

Max is a fucking superhero.

An abbreviated version of my home-buying experience:

After a few months of searching, I finally found a condo that fit all of my needs. I was using my bank as my lender, and made an offer on the condo, which was promptly accepted. After accepting it, the bank realized that the condo wouldn't qualify for my VA loan, and it wasn't an approved condo for traditional financing either. My bank said I was pretty much stuck with an investment loan, with the wonderful terms of 5.75%, 5-year ARM, up to 11.75%. They said that it might be possible to get traditional financing, but this would require the HOA president filling out a ten-ish page questionnaire to determine eligibility. 

Since I was three days into my option period, I started panicking. I called four lenders within the hour - Max being one of them.

After talking to Max, he said it didn't sound like there would be a problem, but he would need to check a few things.

The next day, he had a loan application ready for me to sign. He had determined that the condo was eligible based on the mailing addresses of the owners (to see if they lived in the condo), and calling the HOA president (he might have done more, I'm not sure).

Two weeks later (over half-way through my contract period)  - my bank and one of the other loan agencies STILL didn't have enough information to determine if it was eligible. They were still twiddling their thumbs, waiting on the HOA president to fill this paperwork out.

About two weeks into the process, it comes back that there's a problem with the HOA's insurance. It was an umbrella policy that covered many condos throughout the US. This, according to new regulations, meant that it wasn't available for traditional financing through Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. Max immediately went to work.

He spoke with the HOA president, then his insurance agent directly, to see if this could be resolved. The insurance agent said that she could not provide an acceptable policy, after a week of stalling. Max then contacted several other insurance agents, got quotes for comparable policies, and submitted them to the HOA president. He even called the HOA president several times to make sure things were going smoothly. Without him doing this, I would not have been able to get a loan for this condo.

And, to top it all off, he extended my rate lock-in for eleven days past the original period (since the contract had to be extended) without any charge.

So, yeah. If you're buying a condo, I would definitely recommend Max. He is a badass.

This place is delicious! It pops up under vegan on Yelp! I have been twice now when in Boston and both times for lunch. The staff is very friendly. The food is served a bit differently than other Ethiopian restaurants I've been to in that they serve it in a dish with sides of rolled injera instead of on injera with sides, too. It's a bit more "fancy" this way, though I do miss eating the injera that has stopped up all the yummy goodness!

I have loved both vegetarian platters I got and also the injera rolls appetizer. So delicious! 

Plus, the decor tells you all about Lucy, an Australopithecus afarensis found in Ethiopia. Even the art is all about it! Neat. I also love how they have written Amharic sayings on the mirror so you can learn a little language and culture while you're there. I can't wait to go back!

Ate our NYE dinner here before heading across the street to the Eagle Lodge dancehall for their end-of-the-year party. (Of note: SH was also hosting a F*CK 2016 party and offered a flight of themed shots named for this past year's dearly departed music icons as well as $10 bottomless sparkling wine. Which was Andre, so, no thanks.) 

Really nice cocktail menu -- variety of liquors represented and they're nice enough to break it down into "put hair on your chest" and "other" categories, as well as some bartender specials and classics (and wine and beer). The food menu isn't too large, but you'll find a variety of proteins, salads, a meat/cheese plate, burgers, desserts. They also happened to have my all-time-favorite appetizer: bacon-wrapped dates. Husband really enjoyed his steak, particularly the potatoes au gratin on the side.

Not a huge space, and they don't take reservations (but will put your name on a list). Romantically casual vibe; candle light and cozy intimate seating. Really convenient to the 14 bus.

Will plan on coming back!!

I've been here a handful of times and I'm overdue on giving them a review! I've never had any complaints here and each visit has filled my stomach and warmed my soul! During the weekdays, they do get a bit of a lunchtime rush, but they are always quick on serving food and people continually come in and out. It can get a bit noisy when it's packed, but that's bound to happen with their popularity in the area. 

Their pho has a really nice refreshing flavor and is huge! Their crab rangoons are filled with a lot of cream cheese and their sweet sauce is delicious. They also have a good variety and additions for Boba Tea. They also serve alcohol! 

They are mainly a self-serve place which is nice. Utensils and napkins are placed on each table and the tables are reserved based on your place in line, which comes in handy during their lunchtime rush.

The food always comes out quickly and they have a mini-topping bar which has all the veggies you could want in your pho! They also have all of the to-go containers placed on the counter next to the drinks so no need to wait to cut in the line to get a to-go container. 

Based on my overall experience with all of my visits, I would definitely give them 5 stars and recommend you give them a try!

I hate a lot of things, including exercise and fake perky people. Thankfully, Brilliant Body PDX tricks this cynic into the former with none of the latter. Rebecca is amazingly genuine, enthusiastic, motivating, and talented -- damn, girl can dance -- without being an obnoxious cheerleader type. It's amazing. Zumba (specifically this class) is the ONLY kind of exercise I've stuck with for more than a month. I've been going for almost 6 months now and LOVE it.

It's fun! That's really all there is to it!

It's not all rich, skinny white ladies either, which I appreciate. And I'll never stop being grateful for the low lighting and lack of mirrors. THANK YOU, Rebecca, for not making me watch myself flail around ;)

The only downside I can think of is that the (very rare) subs just can't match Rebecca's awesomeness. But on the plus side, they made me appreciate her more. I can't imagine doing Zumba anywhere else.

I have bought many flowers over the years, but have to say that Ali Bleu offered me the absolute best customer service I have ever received.

I called and asked if they had a specific novelty vase and Donice, the owner, said she would check and let me know.
Right about 7:00pm I received a call that she had found one. I could not believe she was still working so late and she said she really wanted to let me know before she left for the day. 

Two days later I got a message from my daughter saying it was an absolutely beautiful arrangement.

It's not every day one has such satisfaction from ordering flowers.
Thank you Donice for going the extra mile. It made all the difference.

I HIGHLY recommend this shop!!

There are two China Kitchens in this area. This review is for the one inside of a supermarket in asian square, not the one in Chinatown foodcourt. This is the best authentic Chinese restaurant in ATL. I recommend the xinjiang dapanji (stir fried whole or half chicken, it comes w noodles), their dry pots are to die for. Steam dumplings are also the best in ATL. On top of that they offer free all you can eat rice. Mostly chinese people eat here so if you want a real cultural experience in Buford Highway this is a must.

Delicious! First time ordering--I wasn't disappointed! :)
Sauce was perfect, not overwhelming. Crust was thin and slightly chewy, but totally delicious--not doughy and inedible like most North American styles. Toppings were sparse but fresh and packed with FLAVOUR! Actually, I reminisced about my time in Rome while I ate my "Pizza Speciale". I honestly think this is what real pizza is supposed to taste like!
Settings were simple, clean and unassuming, and the sit down area small but adequate, considering the small space they're working with. I can only imagine how packed it will get (line-ups out the door?) when they receive more attention! Staff was attentive and personable. Water was available on tap (carbonated, too!) while I waited. Service was quick from ordering to presentation...10 minutes, tops! 
I have no suggestions for this place. Can't go wrong if you keep it simple!
If they go bigger down the road, I hope they maintain the rustic charm and simple recipes and they'll continue to have followers! 
When you eat a pizza like this, don't wait too long to eat it! The thin crust and toppings will cool quickly and while some might like eating cold pizza the next day, this pizza is best eaten fresh from the oven!
YUM! I'll be back soon!

Credo is a perfect place to sip on a great cup of joe and get stuff done. The atmosphere is relaxing yet stimulating. There are plenty of tables and comfy chairs to claim. The music playlist is just right if you forget your headphones like I did. 

With their pay-what-you-want system, you never feel constrained to one cup of coffee, but you can keep going back for more and more. I am definitely a fan.

Credo is also available to rent on evenings when they are closed. My church rents it out once a month and it's a great meeting place!

I've been to Oga numerous times, and it is always a good experience.

I've tried their Bento boxes, and their noodles, numerous different apps, and of course their sushi. They are all good, but I especially like their unaju. It is sooo good! Generous portion of the eel, very moist and juicy, served over perfectly cooked rice.

Once in a while, I'd try their special from the special menu. They are always very good, different from the usual you get at a japanese restaurant, using interesting ingredients.

Finally, the service that I receive here is always very courteous. From the moment you come in, and throughout your meal, I find that they are very attentive and polite.

This place is so stinkin' cute! If you went to the Fork & Vine before Jack Allens kitchen moved in, you'll be pleasantly surprised that they kept the same layout and decorations. Which I think is great because decor like that shouldn't go to waste ;)

Came here for brunch, they have a good amount of options to choose from but the options are very home-cook type of food. 

You can see managers walking around making sure their guests are satisfied, or the food is still fresh.. servers constantly checking in on their tables. Really great. Would recommend.

Came here with my husband for a quick dinner since we ran out of time to cook dinner and it was getting late. We both ordered the "Tacos Al Carbon." Hubby ordered the grilled chicken and I ordered the steak tacos. The Tacos Al Carbon comes with a side rice and a cup of beans. My steak was cooked to perecftion (medium-rare) and was really tasty. The beans had a nice taste to it, because I usually I find beans very bland but these were nicely seasoned. The Tacos Al Carbon came with red onions and cilantro - simple, but very tasty, and my tacos were very yummy! I will  definitely have those again! (My picture doesn't do it justice). Try it, you won't be disappointed.

I went here a few weeks ago with a friend and was blown away.  I am the biggest fan of mexican food and Chuyes certainly hit the spot.  I had the combination platter and it was the biggest plate of food that was ever put before me.  It was flavorful, hot, and delicious.  The thing that impressed me the most were the chips.  They are the extremely thin kind of chips.  Not the thick kind.  Salsa was awesome too.  The thing that really blew my mind was the dessert we had.  I dont remember what it was called but it was cakey and made with three different types of cream.  It was so huge.  There was a table of six who ordered the same dessert we did and i thought it was so big because they were a table of six.  WRONG.  It was the normal size of the dessert.  All in all a great experience and great atmosphere.  Will definitely be back.

I had an unbelievable experience at Quirk. I drove two hours to Quirk and do not regret that drive at all. I had only one car in mind, and I left two hours after arrival (including test drive, quick negotiations, and signing of all paperwork) with that car. My salesman, Victor, and his manager, Rachel, were incredible throughout the entire process. I was shocked to see some of the negative reviews given my experience as my experience was excellent. I would consider driving back to Quirk for my future VW needs!

Stonington's came through for our party tonight at the very last minute. Due to unfortunate circumstances we were unable to stick with our original dinner plans for our Grandfather's 80th birthday dinner. I called and asked if they could accommodate our 12 person party, which they said they could do with ease. The whole team was friendly and service was exceptional. We interacted mainly with Shannon who was so sweet and went out of her way to make sure we had a great 80th birthday dinner. While the food was great and we had no order issues, it's the service that the whole team gave us that will keep us coming back. Most restaurants would not have greeted and served us the way this location did with only an hour left of business, and for that we are so thrilled to have chosen your establishment.

I been eating Korean BBQ for a while now as I use to live in a Korean Neighborhood (Fort Lee, NJ). Across the bridge, I would go to K-Town in NYC to eat at some great places as well.  It is fair to say that I been around when it comes to Korean BBQ and Bulgogi is one of the best Orlando has to offer.  When you enter, the restaurant seems pretty unassuming.  K-Pop plays on a TV in the background and you are seated quickly. 

Things started off well when I saw that the menu said "All you can eat" which I did not see coming (the only exception to this is the Rib Eye which is only one per person).  I ordered the LA Galbi, Bulgogi and the marinated pork.  They were excellent and the waitress helped cook the meat since I am not the best chef. If you are looking for great K-BBQ at a great bang for your buck value, look no further.  I plan on going back again soon!

You would never guess by looking at this conservative looking suit wearer that I've been inked 8 times. The last four of those tats have all been done at Memorial. 1 from Mikey, 1 from Gary and 3 from Phil (including my very first tat done 17 years ago when Phil was at another shop).
