I found out about Picnik from a website called Mark's Daily Apple, which is dedicated to the Paleo/primal nutritional lifestyle. I follow the principles but I also indulge and cheat from time to time(I'll eat rice, drink a Mexican Coke once in awhile, but I am gluten free).. Well my cheat days will now be fewer and far between, because Picnik has some really great Paleo compliant food. I try not to get too hung up the terminology, I just want to eat REAL food that tastes great. The mocha coffee was probably the best tasting cup of coffee I've ever had in my life, and the pastries were really good as well. I'd recommend anyone to give this place a shot, regardless of your dietary ideology, it's real, great tasting food. The staff is super friendly as well, and it's always great to support local business.

Brittany has been doing my hair for years and I have always walked out feeling great about the results! She is genuine and really cares about the job she is doing on each client. I moved from the area several years ago and tried several new  stylists closer to where I lived. None of them could achieve the same results with my color/highlights.  I receive countless compliments on my hair and would travel any distance to let Brittany take care of me!

I called Jules Catering after getting the name from the coordinator at the venue we had rented for a college graduation party with 36 guests. After a brief conversation with Bobby, I was sent a proposal and pricing. Bobby nailed the menu, and the pricing was within our budget... I sent the deposit check immediately!

Not only was he super helpful with a few additional requests, like one guest with celiac disease (therefore gluten free) and one vegetarian, but everything was perfect! 
From the wait staff to the chef, everyone I dealt with was professional and pleasant. The food was FANTASTIC, and many guests have told us that this party was the highlight of graduation week. Best of all, my husband and I were able to relax and enjoy our own party.

I will definitely use them again, and I am recommending Jules Catering without reservation.

Before my wedding I wanted to have my engagement ring cleaned and have a tear in the gold repaired. I found Jb based on their location and Yelp reviews. Before going in I did some research to get an idea of what it would cost. We took in my ring and the estimate they gave us was very reasonable (even under most other estimates). It was late in the day so they told me I would need to leave the ring overnight but that it would be ready first thing in the morning. After reading people's horror stories about jewelers (not this specific business) swapping out diamonds I was apprehensive to leave it. I'm really glad I decided to go ahead with it. The next morning my ring was ready as promised. The repair job on the gold was done perfectly. They managed to get years of lotion (I know, I know) and grime off the ring and it sparkled and shined like the day I got it. I also asked for the prongs to be tightened which they were. When handing it back, the jeweler did a final inspection and noticed one of the tiny side diamonds must have been blown out when it was cleaned. It was replaced quickly and I was on my way! The work they did was great and I loved how fast I was able to get the work done. While I wasn't thrilled about the diamond falling out during cleaning, I did appreciate their honesty and attention to detail. It was such a tiny diamond that I probably wouldn't have noticed! I would definitely use Jb Jewelers again!

I searched online and found what I wanted and today visited the store location at Barton creek mall. I was promptly greeted by Debbie, who was knowledgeable and friendly. I vaguely described the charm and she took me right to it. She then helped me pick the right size chain and length and did not try to persuade me in the direction of the more expensive. She also did not try to upsale me, ask me to join a club or any other form of harassment. She clearly saw I knew what I wanted and was there to purchase the item. Debbie remembered to offer me a gift card, which she placed in a professional holder and gently stuffed it into the beautiful gift bag!

One of our top two burger restaurants. The beef is top notch, cooked perfectly, great flavor combinations. The West is my favorite! I get it skinny style - YUM! Really awesome concept & great employees - all friendly.  It is worth the drive to the Hill Country Galleria. I would bet they have more locations in the works - it is ALWAYS busy in there & we can't seem to get ourselves to try any of the other restaurants out there because we love it so much! You can tell the owner believes in his business and makes you a believer after your first visit! Hoping they open a location closer to downtown! Please.....

I've stopped in here a few times now. The staff is a happy group of people. Everyone is friendly and up to chat. I have been in there when they were super packed and busy. I didn't have to wait for service, they work well to accommodate everyone. The juice bar has a lively line up with some leading U.S. Brand juices which is awesome! The show case is fully stocked with a healthy array of mods and RDA's. I love they carry some pretty unique ones!

Probably one of the best ramen I've ever had. The shio deluxe was not too salty, and the pork chashu had a nice sweet, nutty and smoked flavor to it. Super spicy ramen is the type of spicy that hits you immediately, but dies down as you get used to the broth. It's a little too salty, would have preferred it to be less salty and more depth in spice.

Portion sizes are good and the price is slightly more affordable than other ramen shops. 

The wait is not too long here. We had fourteen parties ahead of us and we waited 30-35 minutes. I'll definitely come back in the future!

I have been going to Salon Femia for well over a year now, and have been nothing but thrilled with my experience.

Daniela cuts my hair and does a fantastic job.  She is the first hairdresser I've been to that has given me solid advice on what works best for my hair.  She gets it.  She doesn't push the latest product down your throat or cut your hair the way she wants to.

Linda does my eyebrows and also does a fantastic job.  She knows what works for your face, and I swear is the first pain-free waxer I've ever seen!

I highly recommend both Daniela and Linda... you will not be disappointed!

This place has good food and a good atmosphere.  It's also quite expensive.  Brunch was about $45 per person.

Originally, I hesitated to come because I thought of it as a hotel restaurant.  It doesn't look like a hotel restaurant, though, because it's not next to the hotel reception desk. The food is good, which isn't always true with hotel restaurants that think they have a captive audience.

The crab frittata (short of like an Italian omelet) had lots of crab, not just egg.  It had big chunks that were clearly crab and not rubbery crab.

The place is not noisy so whispered conversation is possible.  I tend to like either quiet places or places with such good food that they noise level is deafening with dishes clanging and people yelling.

Outside, you can see them prepare food.  It looks clean, no rats seen running around or people picking their noses.

My experience at this Boston Sports Club has been nothing but great! The staff are super accommodating and friendly and I could not have been happier.  I did the 30 days for 30 dollars deal because I was only living in Cambridge for the summer and I honestly feel that it is the best deal around.  This gym has plenty of cardio machines so you never have to wait, and their weight room is separate making the whole gym feel more spacious.  They offer a wide variety of classes and the facility is extremely well kept and clean. You should join!

Mana Culture makes me smile! I can't go in without finding 10-20 pieces I can't live without... All of the jewelry is so original, sexy, fun, sunny, and irresistible. I have never walked out of the house with a Mana purchase on and NOT gotten a compliment. The fact that you're supporting local artists is an added bonus. Jahnavi (the owner) and Lana are amazing as well; always willing to help you find just the right piece but without pressure or the icky sales feel.  I honestly can't say enough good things about them. If you haven't already been, it'll be the best thing you've ever done for your jewelry collection. I almost forgot they just got a clothing line in from Hawaii too! Perfect for the hot Austin summer :) Enjoy!

I have experienced many styles and approaches to massage. I am particular about what is useful and nourishing for my body. Todd is the best practitioner with whom I have ever worked. He is innovative and intuitive, and he "got" my body and its many aches and challenges. I intend to age as healthfully and resiliently as I can. I am in my mid-70s, and maintain an active and athletic outlook on the challenges of aging. I want to make Todd a regular part of my self-care.

My husband whisked me away for a special night at the Four Seasons.  The hotel is fabulous but so is their restaurant, the Bristol Lounge.  We had an amazing dinner here.  Each table is spacious and located so far from any other table that you feel like you have a private dining area.  The service was outstanding.  Our waiter was very helpful at answering questions about the menu, attentive, and friendly.  Everything from our generously poured cocktails to dessert was mouthwatering.  Friday and Saturday evenings they have live jazz playing in the background as well as a dessert buffet.

I got married here in January, and I could not have asked for the wedding to go more smoothly.  Not only was the staff at VV incredibly helpful and organized during the months leading up to the wedding, they were totally hands-on during the entire event.   VV is very flexible on changing your event from indoor to outdoor (or vice-versa), and having hotel rooms on the premises definitely helped the family and friends coming in from out of town.  And you can not find a venue this beautiful for this price. Trust me, we looked.

i love the inside of this bar, the outside of the bar, the upstairs, etc. this place is wonderful.

the outside was perfect for drinking and catching up, and smoking, though i am not a smoker. the upstairs was really neat to watch everyone walk in and out and sing their favorite tunes.

i wouldn't know how to get here from the other bar, but i sure am glad an atlanta native took us here.

they had karaoke which was really fun to watch from upstairs.

this place was the most laid back bar i've been to. i had a lot of fun here with my friends and look forward to coming back here to check out some of the regulars belting out their fav. tunes.

Patti helped me replace an irreplaceable family heirloom with a wedding ring that is simply spectacular.  I made another purchase based on this experience.  

I stop in to have my rings cleaned and inspected regularly at Lake Oswego Jewelers and recently, the jeweler detected a small diamond missing in the fine detail.  They took care of it for me immediately.

It is rare to find such personalized, efficient and friendly old-fashioned service.  If you're in the market for a wedding set or other fine jewelery, I recommend you stop here first.

This activity was awesome, we did the Game Show Show - we received this as a Christmas gift and were unsure what to expect. They recreate the gameshow experience with vests, a cool name tag and a 'get to know you card.' Our hosts, Bucky and Samantha played their parts very well and brought a lot of charisma and excitement to the hour long event. 

They also do a variety of game show like things such as wheel of fortune cookie, family feud type rounds, jeoporady type trivia, charades and tons of other surprises throughout the hour. Another bonus, is your family or friends can watch you live when you go.

The game show hour went way too fast and would definitely do this again. It's great for date night, team building or just a group of friends who want to have a goofy time. 

Highly recommended - the experience is definitely different!!

We've been to Uni a few times now and every time it's been excellent. Drinks are always enjoyable; loved the Swizzle Smith - came in a pineapple glass with crushed ice which is always an exciting touch. (I'm a sucker for kitsch). The ramen was out of control and we can't wait to try it in the winter. The Mongolian beef was perfect and the gnocchi in the dish was like small pillows from heaven. I would eat a dish with just the gnocchi. Surprisingly the Sake Nigiri was one of the tastiest bites of all the raw seafood we had and it was the least expensive at $9. The Uni was exciting. I've had it before but served warm, so this had a completely different texture and taste. I'll admit I'm not usually an adventurous eater and usually have to have several drinks in me before trying something like uni nigiri. Loved it! It was my fiancé's birthday so I got him a surprise dessert - the Buttermilk Chess Pie. I'm not one for sweets but this was awesome. Slight punches of sweetness balanced out perfectly with the peaches and caco nibbles. Service is always excellent. We arrived early so we stopped at Sonsie for a quick drink where they had 9 employees huddled around the bar chatting and we couldn't even get our check (after asking for it) so we had to physically interrupt a personal conversation to thrust over our credit card to pay. This would never happen at Uni - the moment a plate was empty it was gone. Drinks 3/4  done, you're asked if you would like to order another. 10/10 recommend and can't wait to go back again. Extra points for the weather being perfect and while that had nothing to do with the restaurant it certainly added to a lovely evening.

I stopped by this place with some friends during a visit to Austin.  My friends and I were instantly greeted by Kallie.  She ended up being our waitress as well and was quite delightful.  She was very knowledgeable about the menu and gave us some great suggestions. 

We thoroughly enjoyed all that we tried, tasted and drank.  We tried several dishes...the smash fries, fried pickles, hummus trio...crab crake fritters.. OMG.. all of it was delicious.  I also had one of the Candy Girl drinks..again delicious!  

I tried the salted caramel cakeball.  It was good no doubt but the best one was the red velvet that one of my friend's had.

Overall, I really enjoyed this place and will return again on my next visit to Austin.

I moved to Vancouver from a city with a large Vietnamese population, so this is my go to when I'm craving Vietnamese eats.
It's located in the downtown area, so you'll often need to park nearby and walk to it as it doesn't have on-site parking. The restaurant is in an old house, and the interior is a well lit, slightly worn, casual eating location. They have a really nice exterior patio that's great to sit on during good weather, and has a nicer ambiance than the inside, but it can be noisy with the street.

I've been here three times and had few complaints each time. The service has always been polite and pretty good. I've had their bahn mi sandwich (decent) the traditional beef pho (pretty good) and the bahn xeo (frickin delicious). I'm looking forward to my next visit to continue to enjoy the great Vietnamese food.

This is a great local place for fabrics, in a cool little white stone house on N. Lamar (across from Central Market). I wanted some silk for my wedding dress and flowergirl dresses and was overwhelmed (in a good way) with their selection - floor to ceiling dupioni silk for $15/yard, in every shade imaginable. I had a nice chat with the owner because I was worried about the environmental impact of silks. She advised me that the higher-quality silks from India (which is what they carry) is not formadehyde treated before shipping, plus its a natural fiber. The only downside is a long shipping distance from India; but I was very happy with my purchase. My sister made my entire wedding dress for about $75.00 with the silk we purchased here. 

They also have an incredible selection of buttons of all kinds wonderfully presented in little baking tins in the glass case. 

My only suggestions to Silk Road would be to carry more organic fabrics (they have a limited amount), like hemp silk and more organic cotton and linen. Most of the linens they had were a blend of synthetic material and linen. Also, they don't have much in the way of notions or patterns, so do your catalogue-looking and zipper buying somewhere else before coming here. They also have many many catalogues of fabrics to help you look up what you might need for special orders.

Best Mexican in Quincy.

The salsa deserves its own mention - so fresh and tasty. We'll often order a tub of it for take-out at the end of our meal.

I hate to lean on pricing to compliment a restaurant, but Paloma provides a lot of value here. Huevos de los Charros is my stand-by order, and it's one of those dinners I crave on a winter day, and for less than $10.

My only complaint is the ownership. There was a point during the cold months where my boyfriend and I patronized once a week, and the owner (or the gentleman that I assume is the owner) never showed a glimmer of recognition, never tried to shoot the breeze, etc. Come on, buddy!

10/5 Stars. Sex shops can be awkward, even if you're familiar with the industry. The shop was clean and well-organized, but the customer service is what really shone: Archie was friendly & professional, showed me a variety of options, but never made me feel like I was being upsold. I definitely felt at ease, and it was great to have an open, chatty conversation about fun toys! They provided good information, and I'll definitely be back when it's time for me to make major purchases. I would recommend this shop to anyone in the area who's looking for standard sex shop fare.

A++! On Monday I made a Thursday appointment via email, an option that I really appreciate because it means I don't have to make a receptionist suffer on the phone while I flip through my calendar. 

--They didn't have to dilate my eyes which is always a plus since it makes me nauseous. 
--Dr. Chavez was super thorough (and friendly!) I love that he let me turn the dials when deciding which of two prescriptions allowed me to see better. 
--The tutorial on how to put contacts in/take them out was helpful. I put them in on the first try (which is a testament to Rosie's great technique because the last time I thought about wearing contacts, I gave up when it took me 1 hour to put just one in!)
--I thought $140 for the exam and $15 for the contacts tutorial (required for first time contact wearers) was pretty fair.
--I will say that if you're in the market for new frames, this place might not have as many options as you'd want. That said, this didn't bother me a bit as I always always always by frames when I visit my parents OKC at a magical place (Sam's Optical!), anyway.

I don't plan on being in Austin forever, but while I'm here, I'll definitely stick with Eye Capitol for eye care needs!

Some places like to experiment and do unusual preparations, and then get so caught up in the idea of "I CAN MOUSSE THAT!" that they forget to actually make, you know, GOOD food. 

Roe is not like that. Yes, there were savory panna cottas, a German style octopus preparation (out of this world), and various other unique ideas that showed the the chef was both having fun and very very good at what they do, but at no point did the flavors or overall concept of the dish get lost. That, more than anything else, really impressed me. You have to go in with a bit of an open mind, but you will be amply rewarded. Additionally, on the tasting menu, you get at least a couple of options to choose from for each course, so you can easily find SOMETHING there that will please you.

In addition to the great food, I can't talk highly enough about the service. We ordered the wine pairing, and the gentleman that explained the wines did a great job. There were a few things that stood out. First, he clearly knew his wines. He knew where they were from, he knew the tasting notes, etc. In some places (read: most of Portland), this sort of knowledge can lead to arrogance and condescension. However, he would explain the wines to us and then make some joke. For example, at one point he stopped and said "how's this level. Too nerdy? Want more information? What do you think?" I really thought that was great, and set a very good mood for the place. Additionally, he would not only explain the wines and the tasting notes, but also explain WHY they were selected for a particular dish. Specifically, he'd talk about why he thought which flavors of the wine paired well with which flavors of the food. That sort of connecting the dots was really interesting. Finally, we unfortunately did not understand that the dinner would be a bit of a time commitment, so we had to leave early. You could tell that it was very unusual for them to do so, but the waiters very kindly and graciously helped us box up our desserts so we could get out the door. They never made us feel bad or made us feel like we were putting them out, which was really fantastic.

This place is great! Not pretentious at all. Quick. Reliable. Helpful. Friendly! No judgement about how much you do/don't know about bikes. No judgement about you leaving your bike outside all winter and then needing a serious tune up. I'd recommend this place to anybody in the Boston area, even if it's not your closest bike shop. Reasonably priced, as well. The owner and employees (there's always multiple people staffing the shop) are all helpful and will take the time to answer any questions you have.

We took a sunset cruise and it was a little on the cool side for memorial day weekend it was still a great time. The crew was friendly and personable. They were interacting with everyone onboard all throughout the cruise. The cruise was on time both leaving and returning to the dock. It was a nice slow sail allowing you to see the various islands and also get a look at planes taking off and landing if you want to. We saw a really nice sunset on the way back to dock which made for some great pictures. I'd definitely go with them again for a cruise.

I like the fact that at this location you are able to go up to the register, order and then pick a seat.  I like this concept because it tends to move pretty fast.  There are plenty of seats available!  Super clean place, you are able to grab as many chopsticks, napkins or utensils right at the fountain drink station; which I love b/c you don't have to keep asking the server for this.  My food has always come out as great as the other Bento location.  You can also place order ahead and pick up, I have never had an issue here, staff is always friendly.

If you are a parent to small children, you know that most "play" places in Portland fall into two categories:
A) Places kids like, and
B) Places kids don't like.
Do you know where YOU fall in the picture, as the parent? NOWHERE. It doesn't matter if you like the place or not. You just need like one solid hour of surfing iPhone for Pinterest recipes, amiright?! Laydies? Anyone?
So, I have two boys. They are currently 4 and ~3. (Yeah, REALLY close in age... that first year was a doozy. I don't even remember it.)
THEY love Play Boutique. They love all the little cars you can "drive" around. They love the huge, new-park-grade play structure. They love the bounce house. The kitchenette. The train table. ALL of it.
But you know what? *I* love Play Boutique too. 
Yes, this place falls into the illustrious and mythical category of "Places We All Like." Even my husband likes it. Can I stop beating around the bush and just tell you why?
A) It's clean. The play area is clean. The bathrooms are clean. The cafe is clean. Lobby. Etc. Not musty-germ-smell-indoor-pizza-place "clean" but Clorox Wipe Worship clean. I can support that.
B) There is ALWAYS seating. Inside the "arena" (which is encased by a half-wall) there are benches and chairs for Mommies who need to be hands on (or are "helicopter" parents... no judgement. Well, kinda judgment: give the kid some space, he'll figure it out. But then again, what do you care what I think, you don't know me.) There is also seating APLENTY, around the outside of the half-wall.
C) Good coffee. Like that brand "ILLY" that always makes me think of skinny Italians on mopeds. And you can drink it there, while watching the kids. Not like some places where you have to set it on a special ledge and sneak to and forth for lukewarm, unsatisfying sips.
D) THE KIDS LOVE IT. I know I said this before, but "kids love it" falls into its own sub-categories:
  1. They "like" it for little 5-10 min increments, in between which they have to come and whine to you about something, declare their boredom, try to get your attention, or convince you to leave, after which you have to rile them up / threaten them into staying. (Not Play Boutique!)
  2. Places they like so much, they will LEAVE YOU ALONE for the entire two hours, and have to be convinced to come home with you, by being shown evidence that all the other kids are also leaving. YES Play Boutique! This, right here, is why I think $7 is worth the play. Because every other place is at least $5, and my kids do D-1 (see above), and for that extra $4, I can actually relax, keep an eye on the kids, and look at my phone. (Isn't that all we want? To look at our phones? Oh, don't even pretend otherwise, I will call BS RIGHT NOW on whatever pretentious lie you're about to tell. Look at your phone. Looks like you have a "like" on the pic of your cute kid you just posted. You know you wanna look. At Play Boutique, you can do so... leisurely.) 

The only thing I would change is to make the play time earlier, rather than the current 10:30-12:30. However, I'm sure this isn't some crazy nouveau idea the business has just never thought of... there is some reason for it (they have a preschool there, etc.). And now that my kids are post-nap age (booooooooo! booooo to no naps!), it works for me.

I've never bought anything other than coffee there, but I know they have food. Truthfully, my kids wouldn't stop playing to eat, and why the eff would I make them?! I see in some of the reviews that mommies think it's spendy. Maybe it is. But can I suggest something to all y'all mamacitas out there?... if you have a problem with something at a small business, reach the owner and voice your opinion. They WANT to hear from their customers. (To the person who was bragging about putting "dirty" shoes on in the infant crawlers area: beyond disgusting... and shameful. How about calling and asking them to put a bench near the cubbies? Gross.) Leaving negative reviews that may prevent a business from succeeding more quickly (or at all) does NO ONE a favor in this case. It's an indoor play spot... which we NEED. 

One more tip: Groupon / Living Social/ Sharing Spree "deals" are to help businesses gain exposure and develop a customer base. I'm always surprised at how entitled some of the people with social deals are. This is a BUSINESS. Be respectful. You don't have to keep coming back if you don't like it, but stop treating the businesses you buy groupons for, like a Walmart. Ok, go to timeout and think about what you've done. Mommy needs to read a blog... "read" = drink, "a blog"=wine.

this place is GREAT... I got the boneless wings..(altho i was told the classic style are out of this world).. and i was very pleased not only by the flavor.. but also the general size of the wings.. to go along with my meal i also tried the fried pickles. i had never tried them before so im glad my first try was a good one... they seemed to be the small pre sliced burger topping style... but fried to perfection...the staff was friendly and full of smiles... next time i will have to try the classic wings.... even tho im not sure they could taste any better.... AWESOME WINGS!!!

I cannot thank Toodie's enough for the most exquisite experience I have ever had buying jewelry.  My most recent purchase (3 months ago) was an emerald engagement ring.  I have shopped many stores from local town shops to the Big Apple, New York city, in search for a special ring.  In my experience I can tell you that Toodie's provided me with the largest selection of gems to choose from.  They set the quality bar for others to follow.  They take their time to get to know you as a person and work with you until you are 100% thrilled with your selection.  

I am a person who takes the road less travelled and make choices others don not see.  In fact, the very setting I bought was a one-of-a-kind design they custom made.  Every day I am blessed to see that sparkling emerald on such a beautiful setting upon my fiancée's finger.  She receives many comments about it.  Believe me when I tell you that Toodie's is the real gem.  (just behind my fiancée of course. :D)

I'm always so skeptical of Asian fusion places, but Koy does it pretty well! The yellowtail sashimi was amazing and came with a dab of gochujang. Super yummy and my favorite item of the night. 

The jjajangmyun was also tasty and came with lots of chewy noodles, black bean sauce, and pork. Super grateful that they even offer this dish considering how few good Korean places there are in Boston. 

Drinks were amazing. It's so hard to find places that do Soju cocktails, and the ones here are so good! The lychee one has yuzu sorbet in it, and makes it super refreshing. And the watermelon-mint one is similarly perfect for a summery day. Or really any day heheh. 

Very excited to come here again. I've been eyeing their Bang Bang Cauliflower since I last came.

I've overhead Brian say to prospective customers, "All I need is one time, then I gotcha hooked!" Boy is he right about that. I absolutely love this food cart, and frequent it (probably 3 times a week, there, I said it) when school's in session. 
The brisket is pretty good, but nothing to write home about. The pulled pork is where it's at; I recommend getting it with both spicy mustard and spicy BBQ sauce on top. Juicy, tender, big flavor, the pork hits every note. The macaroni salad is also phenomenal, and I--in literally every other instance-- absolutely dislike macaroni salad, and can't stomach more than a bite of it. Not too much to say about the rice except for that it's tasty as well! 
Overall, it's the best BBQ I've had in Portland; 5 stars, grade A, highly recommended!

Having moved to Austin not six months ago, I was really worried about having work done to my car because mechanics are always painted as bandits and I had absolutely no idea where to take it. Luckily, I have AAA, who recommended me B & B (as they are a AAA certified garage).

All the guys at B & B were SO amazing to me. I came in pretty frazzled and displaced by my whole car situation (I had gotten in a fender bender a couple of hours prior that then caused my car to die in the middle of the highway), and I feel as though they really did everything they possibly could to make me feel at ease about it.

As I had suspected, it turned out my radiator was cracked pretty badly and had to be replaced. Once we settled all my paperwork and everything, I went out to my car to grab my book while I waited for the results of their inspection, and a few of the guys went out with me and popped the hood right there and quickly identified/actually showed me where the radiator was cracked. It made me feel a lot better about the situation for them to physically show me what was wrong with my car, instead of disappearing for an hour and coming back with a laundry list of things that needed work.

I found that, at B & B, they really try to make you part of the process and feel like you have some control in what's going on.

Afterwards, I went back inside and they offered me a beverage and chatted with me a bit. They are seriously the friendliest and most welcoming staff ever.

Richard at the front desk walked me through my quote and was really, really great about it. They were unsure as to whether or not another part of my car would have to be replaced as it was bent in my accident (which they also showed me), so Richard quoted me the worst-case scenario and the best-case scenario because he didn't want me to have any surprises - which I REALLY appreciated. He has got to be the nicest, most genuine guy ever, which goes a long way when you're a worried customer.

The guys even offered to give me a ride home, a complementary service at their garage.

I called early the following day to see what the deal was because I was pretty nervous about my "worst-case scenario". My car wasn't ready yet, but they explained to me why and what they still had to do. They gave me a time to call the following day and said it would be ready then. They actually called me before that time, earlier the next day, to let me know my car was completed. (As well as sending me a confirmation email!) They didn't have to replace the other part on my car and were able to work around it just fine, so my final bill was the low-end of the spectrum Richard had originally given me (huge relief!)

When I went in to pay my bill and pick up my car, a different gentleman helped me, but Richard came out from the back just to (SUPER sincerely) tell me to be careful from now on. (Did I mention these are the nicest guys ever?) Since then, my car is running really great; you wouldn't even know the whole fiasco had happened!

In conclusion, I have definitely found my go-to garage in Austin. I will absolutely be back to B & B.

Having just relocated to Austin I needed to find a new dental clinic so I checked out my trusty Yelp and I'm so glad I did. Rose has got to be on of best clinics I've ever been to. The facilities are top notch with modern state of the art equipment. Everything is nice and clean and very welcoming. The most important part is the the staff and everyone was wonderful, from the person at the front desk to the billing department made me feel comfortable and answered any questions I had. Now I have to give an especially large shout out and thank you to my hygienist Emily, she was amazing! She is fantastic at her job, skilled and knowledgeable and made me feel at ease. From X-ray's to cleaning and polishing she was great! I've had my teeth cleaned over 100 times throughout my lifetime and I've never had a better job and experience thanks to Emily! I definitely recommend Rose for your dental needs as they will be my dental clinic from now on!

I've been going to Johnny Fox's for the last 2 years but never got around to writing a review until now.Since its an Irish pub, I'll start with their beer.

 Many of the bars in Vancouver serve Guinness but, as advertized, Johnny Fox's serves the best. Not only is it on tap (unlike many places that serve it from a can) but they use the proper pour method. It may be the pour or some other magical secret known only to them, but I've never tasted Guinness (and i have a pint of it at pretty much every bar that i go to) as good as at Fox's. On top of the black stuff, they also pour Smithwick's and Harp, 2 more fantastic Irish brews. On top of the straight beers, they do mixed beers as well, all of which are delicious and poured with the proper separation of beverages in the glass.

On to the food. 

Johnny Fox's used to have a rather extensive food menu, but it was recently revamped and downsized. In this change they removed one of my absolute FAVORITE dishes: the Irish Patchos. The dish is essentially nachos but with slices of potato instead of tortilla chips, topped with cheese, green onion, tomato, black olives and jalapenos; certainly big enough to feed two people.  They held on to the Guinness burger and the Guinness and beef stew, both of which are superb. My final item that tops the food list are the Irish spring rolls. Even though they're not traditionally Irish, these crispy little badboys are a fantastic adaptation and a perfect starter to share. 

All in all this is one of my top spots to eat and drink in Vancouver. Its affordable, delicious and the beer cant be beat.

My only issue with Fox's.......BRING BACK THE PATCHOS!!!!

This little place is amazing! True New Mexican food! My family and I moved to Oregon a little over 2 years ago...we have been searching the whole time for a place that serves hatch green chili...needless to say we have been disappointed until now...my oh my! This is so true to the flavors of New Mexico...we are so incredibly happy to have stumbled upon this awesome place! I was in heaven! You will not be disappointed if you eat here! I ordered pozole with green chili and it was delicious! My daughter ordered the stacked enchiladas Christmas style and she loved  it! My husband ordered the stuffed sopapilla and he also had it Christmas style and he loved all the flavors! We even had dessert which included a sopapilla sundae, coconut flan and a sopapilla with honey..all were delicious! The chips and salsas also a must!

The idea of having tapas for a birthday brought us here. Having everyone together talking,  sharing a meal together, enjoying themselves - ten ten tapas provided a GREAT environment to do so. I came here after much research for tapas places in Vancouver and I'll be coming back again. We had a reservation for around 6 and arrived to an almost empty restaurant. Quickly it began filling up and before we knew it there was a live performance - a singer. It made the night that much more special. We ordered a few different appies to share and I must say they were all great and had us wanting more. Roasted bell pepper and garlic hummus, fried potatoes with chorizo, mussels, calamari were the appies we ordered and it was good for five of us. Everything tasted delicious no complaints! I ordered the meatballs and crab cakes after as I was stuffed and didn't want a full meal but I was glad I did. The sauce the meatballs were made in was so rich and delicious, by far some of the best I have tasted! We were there to celebrate a birthday and management knew and they surprised the birthday boy with a desert and Pierce director of management took some great photos and emailed them right away. 

I would definitely recommend ten ten tapas for anyone looking for a great atmosphere, great food, and amazing service. I will definitely be going back!!

Also for all those Life with Derek fans, Edwin bartends here! Another treat for us when we arrived.. seeing him, pretty cool!

As experiences go Vancouver is undergoing an enlightenment on the frontier of food and beverage - Flavours, flavours, flavours.  A visit to O5 is the kind of event that reinforces this movement and are we ever blessed to have this kind of place to experience excellence in tea knowledge.  These guys Pedro and Brian who have put this place together are remarkable tea hunters and you need to check them out when you are on 4th.  Very cool concept and remarkable and interesting teas!!  Savour the moment because they're taking it to a whole new level right here in Vancouver.

I've been to the south side location a number of times, and was so excited when I heard they were opening up one in grandview that also served brunch! We came here on a Sunday late morning and got right in. We split that tacos (added in bacon) and the power bowl. The tacos were good, not amazing. The hot sauce definitely helped. The power bowl was delicious. I loved the pesto sauce, next time I would probably add in protein. We also split a smoothie bowl and they even divided it up for us, which is always a nice touch! 
The atmosphere is really clean and cute! It's small inside, but there is still plenty of seating--even a big table for a larger group.

Love taking classes at this studio! Me and my friend love exploring new yoga classes and this particular studio will forever remain in the rotation as a go to spot for our hot yoga fix.
  
The studio is very clean and more spacious than a lot of other heated studios I've been to in Atlanta. The instructors are all very friendly and the pace of the classes are good for all experience levels including the "I haven't been to yoga in 3 months and now I can barely touch my toes" group like we were. All of the classes I've taken so far, the instructors have been great at providing modifications and also alternate moves in the flow for the more experienced yogis. Also I LOVE the lavender soaked cooling towels at the end....I honestly look forward to the end for it...not just because I'm dying by the end. :-)
  
The parking situation can be a little tricky if you're going for evening classes but I haven't had many issues with the morning classes. It would prob help to say I usually go to this studio on a weekend. It is also worth noting they (I'm sure the building owners) are implementing a paid parking system so it will no longer be free but the cost is not bad it was approx $5 for 1.5-2 hours.

Not only was the food fantastic, but the service was unbelievable. Before we had even decided to eat here we were offered falafel and humus samples, they were delicious. I ordered something that took longer than what my friends ordered to prepare and the fella behind the counter offered me a salad to tide me over until he brought it my meal to me. He then ran back inside and brought me a special spicy sauce that was fantastic and brought us baklava. Everything was delicious and I really felt like he cared about our business.

I decided wedding dress shopping would be a one-stop experience for me. Barbara helped me out and it was a fabulous experience. The second dress I tried on ended up being the one, and Barbara glitzed me up with belt/straps/veil/jewelry during the appointment (ended up with it all!). I chose a custom made Matthew Christopher lace gown and made several changes (backless, added gorgeous straps and belt). I lost 30lb between the purchase and my wedding and the in-house alterations dept made it look flawless, which was a TON of work. I was told dozens of time that my gown was the #1 dress people had ever seen. Custom work was gorgeous. Had a major malfunction with the straps and they snapped off from the gown during the reception. Allegria worked with the straps manufacturer and sent me replacements as well as a small gift and were so kind in working with. Highly recommended!! Also got my girls' Amsale bridesmaids dresses downstairs (go with floor length tulle, they were stunners).

I am a huge tea snob.  Saying that I love Ku Cha.  Their selection is great, Location is convenient and their hours are extremely reasonable.  Although their prices are a little steep, the quality and artisan-ship more then makes up for it.  Unlike most tea houses the employees at Ku Cha seem to really enjoy there job and view it as an art (which it is).  The flavors are incredible but more than anything I enjoy watching these tea lovers craft a great cup of art.  If you like tea, Ku Cha is really worth a stop.  I hope you love Ku Cha as much as I do.

I finally got to try the truly yogurty flavor of frozen yogurt when I visited a Red Mango in NYC this summer. I was so excited to discover that Portland had a Red Mango of its own in December. I visited it twice before it closed up in January. I scrambled to find another place serving up this same style of frozen yogurt in SE Portland. Oh man, Tart was everything and I was looking for and more! The black currant was delicious and their mochi is way tastier than the Pinkberry or Red Mango mochi topping for some reason. Also, they have frozen custard (which makes it way easier to talk my husband into going to Tart). THANK YOU TART!

I visited a few other chiropractors before finding Elevation Chiropractic and Rehabilitation. It was immediately apparent this facility is a step above the others, especially compared to those in the area. They worked closely with my insurance to ensure I was able to get the most out of the treatment process. The value of what I received here far exceeded anything I'd experienced with other chiropractors. 

The 1:1 time is always very specifically tailored to my back and spinal issues. I never feel rushed and Dr. Davis takes careful notes to ensure we can pick up exactly where we left off after the last visit. I was impressed with the home care options I was provided, which included specific stretches and exercises with careful explanation of each. Dr. Davis seems very focused on long-term improvements for his patients and not just treatment of symptoms for immediate relief. 

I was able to quickly see improvements in areas I've had pain in for many years. It has overall been a life changing experience. The facility is always very clean, quiet and the treatment is done in a private room. Dr. Davis is very personable and obviously far more concerned with helping people than in drawing a profit from them. His staff is just exceptional as well! The office manager always greets people with a smile and a cheerful welcome. I would highly recommend Elevation Chiropractic and Rehabilitation!

Love love love love love this place!  God bless the gayborhood.

I am not a dog owner (I'm a Cat Lady), but my bf is, so this weekend when the weather was gorgeous we decided to take his dogs on a field trip here.  Great decision.

This place has a beautiful iron fence with a double-gated entry to keep the kids corralled.  The gravel is great for clean-up and there are no muddy paws at the end of the day.  There are trees and benches for us people, and there is a special segregated small space for tiny dogs lest they get trampled by larger ones (though we had a pug with us in the big space and didn't find it to be a problem).  It was a pretty popular spot on a Saturday afternoon, and I was really impressed at how well all the dogs behaved together.  The people were all very friendly as well.  I think if you're single, this would probably be a great place to meet someone.  The location is fabulous as the South End is so dog-friendly in general, and there are lots of dog shops and friendly small businesses in the vicinity to walk to.  And there was tons of street parking, even on the weekend. 

My only complaints: 1) the water fountain was out of order (we assume it hasn't been turned on for the season yet?); 2) the bag dispenser was empty (we forgot ours, but thankfully didn't need any); 3) I only wish it was bigger!  Regardless, we'll definitely be coming back.

I cannot express how much i really enjoyed this place. The ambiance and the mood of the staff was awesome. I really recommend sitting outside during the summer you wont regret it. The food was delicious i got their famous Baby Beluga and another time I got the Heartless Artichoke, I'm not sure which was my fav, but i do know that eating their was like getting a warm hug, it's comfort food but of a different kind.
P.S if suffer from separation anxiety from your baby/pooch/mans best friend thats okay because they are allowed here. If you have encountered insufferable businesses that don't consider dogs to be people/children too this is the place you've been waiting for they have a small menu for your dog that i'm sure they will enjoy.

Italian Meats.  Cheeses.  Basically all of the good stuff from Italia, and I believe I've said it here before - everything good in this world comes form Italy.

But Carfagna's only brings the best of the best to the table.  The have all sorts of stuff that I love, and a bunch of stuff that I don't even know about yet and probably will love as soon as I try it.  Once a year during football season my friend's mother flies in from New Jersey to cook us Italian sausages and other sorts of good stuff that Italian moms know how to make - and it all starts with a shopping cart full of Carfagna's.

The two gripes I have are frivolous in comparison with the goods... the place ain't cheap and it is always packed.  If you are planning on going during peak hours just plan on waiting around half and hour just to get checked out.  I would not recommend going here during peak grocery store hours if you are only picking up one item - too long of a wait for just one thing.

Last time I came here (on my birthday!) I got a $90 parking ticket (the on-street parking changes over at 4pm to a no parking zone and cops start handing out tix immediately!) BUT it was still worth the ticket -- that's how unforgettable the Miso Disco fries and duck banh mi are. Add a Stiegl Radler (grapefruit wheat beer) to your order and you have a party in your mouth the likes of John Travolta shooting his gun in a white leisure suit. Go NOW! Do it, do it . . .

Rita and I have scored three 5-star veggie restaurants in 3 weeks.  Vedge in Philly, Teresa Carles in Barcelona and now Leaf in Boulder for her birthday.  Leaf was named one of the best veggie restaurants in the US and we agree completely.  Starting with the service.  Rebecca is a phenomenal server - knowledgeable, personable and efficient.  Stefan, manager and sommelier, paired some incredible wines with our 3-course meal - 2 from Argentina and one from Mendocino.  And to go with the wines, he told us their stories - elevation, appellation, history.  I haven't encountered such a knowledgeable restaurant wine person since Joe McCanta (who taught me so much) at the late (very missed) Counter in NYC.

Stuffy nose?  Sinus problems?  One dose of Tacodeli's Habanero or famous Doña sauce should clear it right up!  Seriously... I can't eat one of their tacos without my nose running.  And the tacos are fantastic.  Definitely the best in Austin (and this is coming from a self proclaimed taco connoisseur...) Austin Chronicle voters agree-- Tacodeli has taken the best taqueria award for the past two years!!

That being said, there are a few cons that I cannot ignore:

1. Tacodeli stops serving breakfast at 11am on weekdays..... It breaks my heart a little every time my mouth is watering for a potato, egg, and cheese taco only to find that I am minutes too late:
     (SUGGESTION: if you want breakfast, call and place an order at 10:55ish. so you can pick it up a bit later)

2. Tacodeli is full of yuppies-- I usually like the yuppie crowd.... but on the weekends, the line is out of the door, and there are just too many dang yuppies for me to have a relaxing taco experience.  They are usually pretty cool people, but their range rovers take up more than one space in the already crowded parking lot parking lot, they have a tendency to be overly pushy, and a tendency to yak obnoxiously on their iphones in line.

3. No dinner-- it is seriously a bummer taco deli is not open for dinner.... I would go for a Tacodeli dinner on the reg, but they close at 3pm daily.

4. The parking lot sucks-- I have always managed to find a spot somewhere, but the parking lot is poorly designed, there are not enough spaces for all of the businesses in the area. I frequently have to go look for street parking nearby.

All this being said,  I still love Tacodeli dearly, and I consider myself a Tacodeli loyalist  Best tacos in town, they use high quality ingredients, and the service is pretty good!

My cat would freak out whenever I took her to the vet clinic and yowl so loud when they had her in the back that I felt both sheepish and concerned. A friend recommended Dr. Mullen very highly, so the last time my kitty had something arise, I had him come to the house to check on her. He just sat down on the couch and waited for her to come to him, and she quickly crossed the room to go sniff his cowboy boots and immediately decided he was a good person. She let him examine her thoroughly, while I held her and petted her. He was great at explaining his diagnosis and the various options for treatment, and he was very open about the cost-benefits. His fee was extremely reasonable. I also really enjoyed talking to him in general, he's one of those interesting people who reminds you why you decided to live in Austin.

A beer lover's dream!!

This place is amazing. Moving here from the micro brew capital of the world (Portland, Oregon), I never thought I would find a spot that would rival some of my favorite haunts in Stumptown but this place takes the cake. 

Once you walk into place, you automatically feel welcomed and cozy in the wood paneled interior. Mosey up to the bar and you'll quickly be overwhelmed by the number of beers on tap. Open the beer and wine list and you'll be even more blown away by the number of bottled beers available. 

The service is attentive and knowledgeable. They're more than willing to offer a recommendation as well as provide you background information on any of the beers. 

With so many beers available, could it get much better? While the variety of music on the jukebox doesn't top the beer list but it comes close. Pop in a couple bucks and the selection will surely rival your iTunes library.

Great beer selection, great atmosphere. This is definitely a place where I will become a regular.

Quickly becoming one of my favorite spots to work, read, and get some great coffee. First, love all the natural lighting that pours in from the huge wall of windows along the entrance. The place just feel airy, bright, clean...but not overly sterile. There's a great energy to the place. You can feel the bustle of the community that gathers here as part of their daily and weekly ritual. 

The coffee is great. They take the time to feature every roast on the menu with the corresponding drink option, like where the beans are from and the flavor profile. Such a simple meaningful touch that many great coffee shops don't take the time to do. They have an ample selection of pastries from a couple of my other favorite spots in town, Crema Bakery and Little T. 

Best part about this coffee shop is their small food menu. They have a small kitchen that serves up some unique food options, making this a place a really great blend of roaster, coffee shop, and cafe.

Just finished a 3 day juice cleanse!  It was the first time I had done a cleanse and Matt was very encouraging about the process. As a result of the cleanse, in just 3 days I have a clearer complexion and more energy. I also am sleeping better, even did during the cleanse!

FYI- to do a juice cleanse you need to place your order about 24 hours ahead so the kit can be prepared for you. You get 6 different juice blends per day, to consume in order. First is a green blend, then a lemon blend, another light green blend, another lemon blend, beet juice, then an almond milk blend. They are all good (beet was not my favorite, but to each their own). Very fresh, very clean, and not too hungry during the process. I recommend giving it a try if you never have. As a result of my experience I plan to come back and do 1 day flushes and another cleanse in the spring!  Thank you, Matt!

Super big fam of Texas road house. But I you go to this one ask to sit in Ric's section. The food was "as always" great! I ordered fried pickles and a 11oz steak which I was going to take pictures but everyone knows texas road house, but this specific review is about the excellent service. I'm picky about water being kept full and Ric didn't let us reach the bottom at all. On top of that his effort to make sure we were satisfied was always on point. So if you need a great server and you happen to be at this Texas road house make sure you ask to sic in Rics section!

Checked this place out last Saturday and had a great time!

There was a cover, which sucks, but it was only 5$. 

Music: Super on point, I was dancing for most of the night. At some point around 12, they brought at a sax player. I also like their mix of high tables in the center, booths on the right and a small area for dancing closer to the band 

Food: split a shrimp po boy from the food truck out back, it was delicious

Upstairs: Very sexy vibe, all the walls and lights are red. No entertainment or anything up there, just some booths, and a bar, but it got pretty crowded. I also liked the crowd, no one was really getting too drunk and yelling, which was refreshing!, just people old and young getting a drink and making conversation. 

Worth checking out! It has a very loungy feel so it was more of a date spot to me, but you could also come with a few friends.

I love this place! I bought a groupon to Brass Ovaries because I was wanting to take classes here and had been looking at the place for a while.  I was so excited for them to be up on groupon.  So far I have done two Pole 101 classes and one Aerial Hoop class.  I fancied myself a tad stronger than I actually was in that first and second pole class, and a little more graceful.  But I had so much fun in the class.  The second class we strung together some moves into a routine and had a ton of fun with it.  I feel a lot more confident with the moves and spins and "lifts" - not sure what to call them but I'm quite pleased with myself for those.  My instructor for the pole classes was Natasha and she was fabulous.  She is so sweet and is always smiling.  She makes it easy to have a great time.  The aerial hoop class was AMAZING!  I was doing tricks the very first class.  My shoulders are incredibly sore today (terrible idea to have done yoga this morning after last nights hoop class).  I had the best time - I've never felt so strong and graceful in my whole life!  It does take a lot of strength but I was able to do everything she showed me.  I'm saving up to get my own hoop!  It was awesome!  My instructor for the hoop class was Sophie.  She was so sweet and encouraging and helpful!  I can't wait to do more classes.  I highly recommend this place to anyone - in every class I've had women of every size, shape and age and it was a blast!  Definitely try this place out, it's fantastic!

I got recommended this by my mother while visiting Portland. I have no idea how this restaurant possibly has below a 4 star rating but the food is excellent, the atmosphere authentic and the server we had was very friendly and took her time to go over the menu for us as first time visitors. 
We got the octopus dumplings- something outside my comfort zone but amazing. Two sushi rolls which were both excellent and ramen which was also amazing. The saké recommendation from the server was great (note many of their saké is served chilled as I hear is common in Japan, but they will heat some like the house saké).

i have a best friend who is a professionally trained chef, she was visiting from portland for her 40th birthday and made the request for a great meal for her present. i read reviews and made reservations for self portrait...

this beautiful little gem of a restaurant was perfect. the staff were so lovely and offered helpful options. the FOOD was divine and it soothed the fine tuned pallet of the jet lagged west coast birthday girl with ease.

i can't wait to go back again!

This was honestly one of the best sandwiches of my life. I've eaten plenty of bagel sandwiches in my time, but something about this particular bagel sandwich made the magic happen. Was it the excellent bagel from Block's? Was it the fact that the sandwich was steamed, softening the bagel and melting the cream cheese? Was it the obviously fresh and high-quality ingredients? Was it the friendly owner's neon-green tye-dye momentarily dazzling my senses? I may never know.

What you should know, however, is that this is a new (and impressive) food cart that (despite the name) can currently be found in the Short North, Clintonville, and Downtown depending on the time and time of day (see http://shortnorthbageldeli.com/locations/). You should also know that the particular sandwich I got was the $6 Good Ole Goodale, which has Turkey, Cream Cheese, Tomato, Colby, Avocado, Lettuce, Sprouts, and Honey Mustard on your choice of bagel. I should probably also mention that the Goodale is kind of messy, and, if you are like me, you will probably devor it in a primal and predatory manner that will result in it being all over your face. Or maybe I just have bad table manners in the face of a great sandwich. Regardless, you should go here!

069 / 100 - 2017 YELP 100 CHALLENGE.

CRYSTAL IS AMAZING!!!

I was looking at different waxing locations near Vista and came across Sugar San Diego. I had never heard of sugaring before, so I read up on Crystal's website and did a little bit of Google-fu. She had a discount going for first time customers who wanted to get a Brazilian and seeing as how I had always wanted to try, I thought, "why not!?"

Sugaring is an all-natural method of removing hair and is often compared to standard wax. A lot of people say it's a lot more gentle than standard wax, so seeing as how I wanted to get a Brazilian, I thought this would be the best route to go.

I scheduled my appointment online. Super fast, super easy. The day of my appointment, Crystal texted me with some directions so that it would be easier to find her office. Really sweet and helpful of her to do that!

Once I filled out the new customer form, she took me to the back and we got started. It was my first time doing this, but Crystal was totally cool about it. She walked me through each step, explained what she was doing, and so on. I'm a bit of a baby when it comes to pain, so sugaring was a little painful for me. At one point, I had to ask to take a break LOL. Crystal didn't even blink twice at that request HAHAHA. She kept me distracted by chatting with me (she's so sweet and funny!) and gave me advice/tips & tricks on aftercare.

The session itself didn't take that long and she did a very thorough and fantastic job! Sugaring does get easier the more you do it, so I'll definitely be coming back. Crystal's prices are definitely fair and reasonable - especially since you don't need to come back for 4-6 weeks.

Definitely recommend Crystal and Sugar San Diego if any of you ladies are looking to try out sugaring! It was a great experience for me.

I found this cool restaurant and concert venue one evening when we brought some out-of-town guests to see the spectacle that is The Oasis. We took a detour around the perpetual line, headed up the stairs, and went straight into Uncle Billy's. There was virtually no wait!

The restaurant is huge inside and has a lake-view deck that sits parallel to the overloaded one of its gaudy big sister next door. There are plenty of indoor tables, but we headed out back to sit on the deck.  I felt positively sneaky that we had landed a table so quickly while people stood in cue next door. This must be the best kept secret on the lake.

Uncle Billy's offers a BBQ menu and an array of somewhat offbeat appetizers (white queso, fried pickles, etc.) and the usual Tex-Mex fare. The food is good, as in better than next door's. Then there are the beers...Uncle Billy is apparently a microbrewer, as well. There are a number of beers on tap, a sampler to try several at a time, and some that are unlisted (see the chalkboard at the door).

Whereas the aforementioned next-door place books cover bands, Billy's seems to book the local original acts. I saw Ian Moore, Bob Schneider, Jimmy LaFave & Joe Ely on the upcoming list of shows posted in the restroom (which was very clean, btw). The concerts take place on the rooftop for an additional charge, but it didn't seem exorbitant. They do serve food up there, and I haven't yet tried out that arrangement, though I've recommended it to others with good results. Check out their website for more details.

I'm just excited to have such a cool Austin venue out here in the sticks. And now you're in on the secret, too. Pass it on...

**update 12/3: A quick review of Uncle Billy's website says they've closed for the season, most likely meaning winter.

I hired Chris Kirker for a very narrow scope of services.  Despite its scale and unbeknownst to me, the issue I was facing was extremely critical and could have had extrodinarily bad implications for my children. Chris identified thie plethora of potential bad outcomes from limited information supplied to him and rescheduled his day to meet with me urgently.  Upon meeting him, he was incredibly knowledgeable about the matter (which had international implications) and had devised a strategy that was not only cost effective but was far reaching in its implications and could be executed with ease. Chris engendered enormous faith and trust in a short period of time.  From the outset, he was heavily invested in my case and I felt that he was genuinely concerned and wanted to ensure the best possible outcome. Going forward any issues that come up I am squarely placing in his corner. Super bright, agressive, strategic and caring are the order of the day when it comes to issues of this magnitude. Only address in town thank you...

Have you ever heard of David Vendetti? If not then you're missing something in your life. And that thing is David Vendetti.

David teaches the all levels yoga class at SBY. It's targeted towards moderately practiced yogis but every movement can be modified for the beginner or the advanced. After a 90 minute session with David you will be drenched in sweat and sore in places you didn't know existed, but you will be glad about it.

David is an AMAZING instructor. He keeps you laughing through the class and is very encouraging when you feel like giving up (it happens, trust me). It's very hard to describe David. He's kind of someone you just need to experience. I think I fell in love with David before I fell in love with yoga.

I've also taken aerial yoga classes here with Joanna K. She's a really good instructor who walks you through the steps at a comfortable pace so you don't feel like you're going to fall out of the sling and die. The inversions are so much fun and I personally find doing yoga in the air very cool.

I've heard great things about the Pilates classes taught by Hanneke but haven't had the time to take any of them. I intend to if my schedule ever changes.

***************************************************
I forgot to add some things:

As more of a testament to David's amazingness, he knows a lot of his regulars really well. I'm sure these are people who come to all of his classes (I can only go once a week) and have been seeing him for years (I've only been practicing for six months). 

But after class a few weeks ago he extended a brunch invitation to anyone who wanted to come. My friends and I went as well as some yogis he knows well and a yoga instructor from New Jersey who was visiting. He and the regulars were super nice and treated us like old friends, despite the fact that we'd only really been introduced that day. They were so genuinely nice and welcoming and I had a great time.

Also, David and Todd (the advanced level instructor) are the cutest couple ever. No dispute.

As a testament to the great yoga practices at SBY, when I started in January I had scoliosis that had gone untreated since I was 12. It was minor, but it caused one of my hips to be an inch lower than the other and gave a slight curve to my spine that caused lower back pain. 

Last month I had to get an x-ray done due to a head injury. The x-ray showed that my scoliosis had improved since my last x-ray in August 2011. My one hip is now only a quarter of an inch lower than the other and the curve has straightened out a bit, causing me to grow half an inch. And while I still have some back pain, it's now more mild instead of moderate. 

The only lifestyle change that occurred during August 2011 and May 2012 was starting yoga, and I really can't think of anything else that would have improved my condition.

This place was super cute ! I got a matcha latte and it was amazing and they also have halva which is something I always had as a child. The atmosphere was really laid back and casual and there was a lot of people there studying it made me want to bring my books and study there (even though I was on vacation in Boston) I really recommend this place and it seems like a great study spot because they serve food drinks and even breakfast !

If I can get breakfast in the Back Bay for under $10, it's a steal! I've been here a few times and it has beat out most other fast options on the block (Dunks, Starbucks). The flat whites are awesome, and they have a good cold brew as well. The smaller sizes are perfect for what I prefer. Today I got a sausage roll for breakfast and although I've never had an Aussie one before so I can't compare it to anything, I'd say it was delish! There is only one staff member on, so if you're in a huge rush it might not be the place for you, but they're conscious of the line and move as fast as they can.

I have been to three different locations for Laser treatments and I have to say that there is no doubt that I will remain with All in One Laser!  Here are the reasons that I feel All in One has an edge on the competition.  1- During the first session- she really takes the time to explain all about hair, growth, follicles, and different lasers.  2- she keeps a file with extensive notes on your visits. 3- she actually changes the laser depending on how thick/thin the hair is. 4- her rate are very competitive and 5- They are extremely nice and personable.  If you are looking for a serious laser tech... this is your spot.  Only 3 appointments in and I already have great results!

This is my go-to place, I;ve been a member for 2 years and I love it. Kim and Russ are very welcoming and  agree with other reviews that is has a very homey atmosphere that you don't get in most places. I've taken Zumba, yoga and Zumba toning and all of them were good. Truly feels like a very unique, comfortable place to work out. It's close to my house so i go a lot and the membership is very inexpensive. My son loves going there too. Wonderful place!

Currently living about 1.5 hrs from this restaurant, we decided to make a special trip here for a birthday girl's celebration. We tried making reservations in advance, as it was a Friday evening... But my date tells me someone on the other end said they don't take reservations. When we got there... They said we needed reservations! 

I'm inclined to believe my date, but regardless... They seated us in under 5 minutes and the manager even gave us his business card for next time we want to make a visit. Our server was Fairy... He was excellent making great suggestions! 

They were out of a few things ... Like the oysters and something else I can't recall, but our dining experience was A+ and the food was delicious! 

If you like ankimo, I would highly recommend their ankimo appetizer!! HIGHLYYYY... :)) 

Amazing sushi and fantastic drinks as well. I would definitely be a regular if it weren't so far away.

I love this brewery, great people and excellent beers!

While trolling around Boston, my wife found that the Harpoon Brewery was located here.  I was mildly familiar with the beer as I had tried one of two in the past.  I definitely wanted to check out the brewery though.

We arrived and tried to book a tour, but it was booked solid.  I was a bit discouraged by that as we had to leave town the next day (I live in Nashville).  I explained the situation to the lady organizing the tour and she apologized.  However, in about 30 minutes she came back to let me know that had moved some things around and would fit us in.  How great is that!

In the meantime, we sat at the huge bar that dominates the main room of the brewery seating area.  I tried the darker selections and my wife tried some of the lighter IPAs.  They were both excellent.  Harpoon does a great job crafting their beers and they have a terrific variety.

If you're in Boston and a beer lover, do check out the Harpoon Brewery.  The employees are knowledgeable and very accommodating.  The beer is also very good!

Most interesting sub roll award goes to Larry's.  The roll is amazing spongy, but in a good way.  They toast it up and smother it with amazing meats and I am hopelessly addicted!  

I am currently stuck on the Pastrami and Corned Beef combo.  I go there about twice a week.  I used to order the Animal when I frequented this chain 15 years ago in Florida.  I used to go there every day when I was in college.  Some things never change.

I seems like the place may have changed owners in the past year or so. The people who work there now are very friendly.  The guy who hands me my sub every time I go is always smiling, making my day just a little bit brighter.

Last minute panic when we were traveling and daughter decided to go to her junior prom- my husband called Chris after locating him on yelp.  Chris was responsive and flexible putting us at ease that we would be able to capture photos of our daughter despite us not being in town.

Our 17 year old daughter had great things to say about Chris, had fun with the photo shoot and we were truly AMAZED and incredibly thankful to have found Chris. His work was delivered to our inbox in less than 24 hours, professional, and STUNNING photos.

Thank you Chris- we applaud you for your work.  Chris also has amazing photos that we enjoyed viewing in his Instagram page!

Bravo!

Wow, this is one of the closer restaurants to me and I only recently went there.  Even though I watched it being built and saw that it was open...

Really amazing food, made by people who love food and love the farm to table idea (even if that's not quite what it is here).  Really great food, a variety of types of food to order - are you having a vegie sort of day?  Need some protein?  Need a lot of protein?

Hints for eating there - try the free water, they put various things in it to give it a little flavor.  They have alcohol if you feel the need.  Sometimes the 'buffet' items on the counter seem to be slightly less fresh, perhaps look at it before ordering and base your decisions with that in mind.   You can order from the menu OR from the counter items, so don't feel boxed into just the visible choices.

I'd bring a girl here for a casual date, simply because it has an interesting/causal atmosphere and interesting food choices.

Only thing is, you can make quite a large bill for yourself if you get too carried away with ordering options, drinks, etc...

We skipped the traditional dinner when we visited Portland and opted instead to try Food Truck Row. My husband was in heaven. Lol 
PoBoyz caught my eye, but lured me in after a sample. I love samples. 
The owner was definitely personable. In fact, probably the nicest we met the whole day in this town. 
I had a tough time picking between shrimp and sausage, so he mixed me an amazingly delicious bowl. Perfectly cooked. Perfectly seasoned. Perfectly done. The bowl was very hearty and I couldn't eat the whole thing, but trust me, I tried. 
Won't disappoint!

When you consider the kinds of parks we have here in central Florida, this one is pretty awesome. Not only are there plentiful amount of benches for you to sit and eat at, but there' s also lots of green grass areas for you to place a blanket down and have an old fashioned picnic. 

This park actually has a pretty trail that allows you to see Florida at it's core. The marshes, tree's with hanging moss, snakes, rabbits, (yes we saw these things).

I don't understand why there are people saying this park doesn't have flowers because I saw plenty actually (see pics) and its free so... gotta love that!

Yan is very knowledgeable about skin and your skin as it ages, as well as different types of skin. She makes me feel comfortable asking any embarrassing questions !  After consulting with several other clinics, I trust her and find her to be business savvy with a heart. I don't feel over sold or just a number when I see Yan. Even if she finds more you need more services than you thought, it has been worthwhile, and I'm happy and comfortable with the suggestions. The office is also peaceful, pleasant, minimalist, and therefore clean. Thank you, Yan and Savanna, both.

Don Sembera went "above & beyond the call of duty" while representing the Seller on a home that we purchased in West Lake Hills. He had a excellent knowledge of the neighborhood, city regulations and the history and intricacies of this particular property. He helped the Seller understand the value of a buyer like us that wanted to preserve the home versus many others that wanted to raze it and build yet another McMansion. I'd wholeheartedly recommend Don for those seeking a home or looking to sell a home - especially in West Lake Hills!

Clean, organized, and welcoming shop with only the most professional artists working there. There are a lot of less than stellar tattoo shops in the Boston area, and The Painted Bird is certainly NOT one of them! I've only been impressed by their work and how they conduct their business.  Plus, the tattoo Andy did for me has garnered some serious compliments over the last few months (including someone who pulled over on Comm Ave just to get a better look at it. No joke. You can't make that up!) Looking forward to my next tattoo by him.

I love this salad shop! The produce is delicious; it is clear that they are careful about what they provide to their customers. I think the combinations of salads they suggest are amazing. Of course, a person can do the "create their own". My favorite is the spicy Caesar. Adding mozzarella and salami makes it even better. The customer service is fantastic. Yes, there is usually a 15 minute line if you go during the peak of lunchtime but I usually slide in a little after one and I'm able to walk right up with no line.

Since I have not been in the store or seen any of their product, this review is purely a customer service review.

I live on the island, knew exactly what I needed and over the course of a month, just could not find it anywhere but the Obusforme website. Lots of places over here carry Obusforme products  but only one was willing to spend a couple of minutes checking cost of ordering one in...uh, uh.

Then I Googled the product with "Vancouver" in the title.
Up popped Chairlines with what I was looking for.
On sale, cheaper than anywhere.
I emailed, they were out of stock, would not be restocking but could order one and would honor the sale price.

Nicole was fantastic through the whole process.

Doesn't get much better than that.

What can I say, when you bring your mom in town and take her here, she will feel like a princess. We sat down for some bottomless mimosas and the manager went ahead to buy the appetizer. I truly felt special when I was dining here and the experience alone should count for the five stars. However, even the food was amazing. An assortment of tapas with Spanish style influences made this a very cultural and memorable experience. If you have not tried this restaurant yet, I highly advise you do since it will make your day, and raise your standard for future restaurants.

Coming from NYC I have been spoiled by being able to take numerous Barre classes (Pure Barre, Physique 57, Flybarre, Exhale and others) and FINALLY I was able to try Bar Method (thanks to Classpass)  

Upon entry you are greeted by a very friendly staff who gives you a quick tour of the studio.  The studio has a decent sized changing room and 1 shower (which is a plus as that is not always the case in NYC)  

I like that the instructor read my profile sheet before class so she didn't have to ask about injuries (recovering from a car accident so I have wrist and lower back issues)
She did a great job of prompting me to the bar when it was time for pushups and other needed modifications.
