Getting service from the Genius Bar was very quick when my laptop battery died, and they had it replaced in under an hour for around a hundred dollars - cheaper than ordering the battery from a third party and doing it myself.

I'm very pleased with the service I've received at this location and will continue to frequent it as a customer in the future.

It's a Saturday afternoon with a snow storm looming. I can't get work done on my car during the week because of work, so I was determined to make it happen today. I'm new to the area, and had no references for mechanics or auto body technicians. I thought that, combined with my Missouri plates, would do me few favors in this search. 

I called Mike and he was the only person I'd called that said, "sure, come on in and I'll take a look". He charged me less than anyone else quoted me, despite the 'on the spot' demand. He went past the mirror replacement I came for by also repairing my loose door panel. Mike is a professional and competent guy who, from what I observed, cares a lot about what he does. I was communicated with clearly and honestly, and am completely satisfied with the work done. that's what makes this a five star review.  

I recommend anyone in Boston/surrounding areas that may be looking for an auto body guy to give Mike a call first.

Michael came to my house and did interior details on 3 of my vehicles. He took his time and didn't rush even though it took a good portion of his day to get all 3 cars done. He was on time, friendly, and most importantly - all 3 cars looked and smelled brand new at the end. I'll definitely be using Lux again next time my cars need to be freshened up.

Side note: he was able to get rid of cigarette smoke in one vehicle and an ink stain on the seat of another...I was impressed!

Excellent team of lawyers that I highly recommend to anyone who is looking for a closing lawyer! The staff are extremely knowledgeable and thorough with everything they do which is so very important when you're making a purchase like a Condo with lots of complicated documents that need to be carefully reviewed. 

All of our communication was via email and the team did their own negotiations with the seller's lawyers during escrow. This was extremely convenient for me because I was living in Manhattan and buying in Boston so needed to minimize the amount of times I would be needed face to face. Luckily, that was only ONE time during the closing. Ali was so accommodating and professional. He even kept his office open late on my closing date (which also happened to be his birthday as well) so he can accommodate my complicated schedule. Wonderful experience!

I have been a customer at the Chelsea location back to when the smaller, old store was here.  Tonight, after a long day at work I stopped in to grab dinner and Paulette, the cashier greeted me with "hello dear how have you been?"  With a friendly smile on her face.   Paulette's excellent customer service is something that you don't see often - an employee who remembers their customers face and name!  Paulette is the adorable lady with glasses and short black hair check out in her line for a smooth top notch experience.   Also, kudos to the entire seafood department they are always helpful, smiling, and give great tips on what to purchase and how to prepare the fish.  Especially, when the scallops are on sale they say " you must buy them they are cheaper than in a restaurant " HELLO SOLD l buy 2lbs.   Did you know they will also steam your fresh lobster for you = no cooking after a long day at work yahoo !!!!
It's a great place with afordable prices and the freshest,  delicious produce

Finally a deli like place that serves fresh eggs and breakfast all day long outside of Waffle House and IHOP!

This is my first time actually making it to one of their establishments. My job often has breakfast catered from here and I've never tasted anything bad so I wanted to come here for myself and try them out for brunch. 

My boyfriend, brother and nephews came here on a Saturday afternoon during the worst weather. I'm not sure what happened but when we pulled up and started walking to the restaurant it started to look like a tsunami outside. lol. 

Parking is $10 valet, public parking right across the street (they'll validate this one) or free around the corner. I didn't know anything about the parking so we valeted. Luckily when we came out the attendant didn't even charge us. We just tipped him and went on our merry -  get it? ... MARY lol - way. 

I believe I had the quadruple bypass sandwich. This sandwich has pork roll (which is one of my faves and i can't find it anywhere but Publix), sausage, ham and bacon.. I think. 3 fried eggs, lettuce and mayonnaise on a roll. Seriously.. after half of a half. I was completely full. The sandwich also came with some potatoes that were seasoned to perfection. I believe they had lemon pepper on them. Whatever is was had my taste buds Uber satisfied. 

The breakfast sandwich was awesome. Next time, I may try a burger or something because the one my brother had looked delicious as well. I just had a taste for breakfast and knew what I kind of wanted. 

Definitely worth the drive through Atlanta traffic. I'll be back sooner than later.

Wow. What a find. Tiny hole in the wall (don't plan on eating in) that packs in a ridiculous amount of flavor into each dish. And it's all traditional home cooked Chinese...nothing even remotely Americanized. 

The braised beef noodles are unreal. The broth is rich, the noodles perfectly cooked and the beef comes in big chunks to start, but is so tender that it easily shreds apart in the bowl so that you can have meat in every bite. 

Also try the cucumber salad (that comes soaking in a refreshing soy and ginger dressing) and the soup dumplings (best I've had).

Expect a wait, we were mid line at 8:30a for brunch.
Micah, our waiter, plus his teammate coordinated very well to ensure our table was taken care of. Coffee and water were refilled throughout brunch.
We started with lemon ricotta hush puppies. There were 6 to a plate and it is delectable as an app. Hints of lemon in the pups and the dipping sauce was sweet too.
For entrees, we ordered the shrimp and grits with eggs, and the cat head chicken biscuit. Both we're good, but the cat head platter came with 2 super large biscuits encasing a ginormous piece of chicken topped with peppery gravy coupled with a side. A side of grits doesn't have much flavor, I recommend going for potatoes instead.
We also saw the behemoth dish with 3 chicken breasts on a sweet potato waffle. Goodness, that was beastly.
All in all, come with an empty stomach and expect a wait. Food is great, service is prompt (Micah was attentive through and through). Screen door is a superb place to grab a meal.

I dislike visiting dealerships on days when they're open. I like looking at cars when there are no salesmen to bug me! But last time I was scouting around, I actually WANTED information. Which gives me shudders, because my dealings with salesmen make me itchy. BUT, the guy who waited on me, Rob Wilkes, was very friendly and helpful. He knew what he was talking about, got me some links and information. Showed me a nifty app for my phone for all kinds of car stuff. I liked him a lot. 

I didn't buy a car from Rob, through no fault of his. The right one just turned up elsewhere. But I felt strongly enough about his helpfulness, that I wanted to leave him a positive review. Seek him out, you won't get a bad "salesman" vibe from him! :)

Our waitress Ashley was so sweet - she happily recommended several entrees and appetizers for us. We ordered the potato leek soup, bacon wrapped dates, beet salad and the duck legs. Everything was wonderful: the flavors were robust and complimentary so not one thing felt overwhelming or disproportionate. The duck was a mouthgasm: the meat literally fell off the bone and melted in my mouth. It was a borderline sexual experience between the food and I. 

I know this sounds a bit personal for a Yelp review, but I would be remiss to exclude what an explosive and sensational experience this was. The beets were succulent and fresh and the potato leek soup had perfectly crispified bacon bits embedded in the creamy and viscous velvet body of the soup. The bacon-wrapped dates blended perfectly with the chèvre in the salad and the dill yoghurt perfectly complimented the pistachios and arugula. 

The dinner was so enjoyable I felt a sense of Catholic guilt afterwards. I need to repent for this meal so my soul doesn't burn in hell with the other heathens.

My mentor took me to lunch here today. At first I thought it was gonna be like your typical Italian restaurant chain (like Olive Garden) but it was way better than that!

Started with the calamari, which was soooo good! Crispy and tasty (but not chewy). I almost ate the whole thing. The complementary bread was warm and soft. Pairing it with olive oil & Parmesan cheese made it a great experience.

I tried the Famous Rigatoni D. I usually don't like Marsala so I was pleasantly surprised. But I couldn't finish the bowl because I was too full from the bread & calamari, but they made good leftovers. Definitely would recommend.

My mentor got the Gnocchi in vodka cream sauce. I got to try and it was so tasty.

This location has a really nice banquet hall area downstairs! The bathrooms were clean and the whole restaurant was really nice. So was our server (I think her name was Rainy). I think I might come back next week!

Sunshine in your mouth even if its raining outside. One love. I had previously visited Roxy's and had some so-so kalbi chicken. For one the KC isn't my favorite dish but they were out of Kalua Pig, their famous burger, and a number of other items. I can't complain about a place that's so good they run out of food. I geddit. 

Walked in today and got a 50-50 order of Kalua pig and Kalbi Ribs. The latter of which I love with little char. Everything was perfect, just the best grinds from a wonderful ohana. 

Prices are lower than the surf in Oregon. Some of the best Hawaiian food around, and one of the best places you can possibly go to in Beaverton for a nice casual spot. 

If you're laid back and looking for great food, Roxy's is it! If you're not laid back, you should probably work on that. :)

This was the BEST latte I've had in years and I drink a lot of lattes.

It was smooth and full of flavor. I loved it. 

They offer all sorts of beans from everywhere around the world and various brewing styles from pour over to aero-press. 

The atmosphere is craft, but not pretentious. It was clean and there was lots of space to sit and talk.

I LOVED it! It's just too bad there's not one of these in Knoxville, I would visit it ALL the time.

I arrived early for my 1:30 hair appointment, and was promptly greeted by name. I moved into the waiting area and was offered a cup of tea or a glass of champagne until they were ready for me.  Between the music, therapeutic fragrance, and the flickering candles it was hard to feel anything but relaxed.  

Sharifa was kind, efficient, and thorough.  She listened to what I was looking for, asked appropriate questions, and I walked away a happy customer.  I'm looking forward to visiting again for a manicure and pedicure.

5100 acres of forest in a city--amazing.  Forest Park is exactly as it sounds: it is a park that is a forest, in Portland.  And like all the forests in these parts, it is lush and green and full of startlingly large trees.  

Definitely worth a visit, though if you're pressed for time, know that the woods in Washington Park are basically an extension of Forest Park, and you can see those easily and thoroughly by walking around Hoyt Arboretum, which is free to enter and is very near the Washington Park Max stop.  Note also that you can get a feel for what Forest Park is like by going on the 4T Trail, which, while not running through Forest Park proper, will take you through beautiful forest paths in Washington Park.

It's easiest to drive here to any of the trailheads, but you can also walk here from the Washington Park Max stop.  The easiest trail to get to from there, as far as I could tell, is the Wildwood Trail, which is the centerpiece trail of the Park, ~40 miles and winding through its entire length.

You have now until Monday, November 18 to have a taste of the Feast: Asian Dining Festival. For my last stop, I invited my friends to join me at Continental Seafood Restaurant to enjoy a $178 set menu for 6 people. 

it is my first time dining here. When I was selecting which restaurants to go, the menu from Continental Seafood Restaurant immediately attracted me. It is a 7-course menu that can feed 6 people. I invited four friends to tag along, and it was exciting for me because it has been a long time since I have such a fancy Chinese meal. 

The first two dishes are Crab Meat Fish Maw Soup and Roasted Pork with BBQ Duck. The soup is beyond my expectation, with a generous amount of crab meat and pieces of fish maw in it. The big bowl can fill up to 7 small bowls, so my friends can go for the second round! I love the crispy skin from the roasted pork, and the ratio of fat and meat is perfect. 

The Sautee Jumbo Prawn with Superior Soya Sauce arrives next. Again, I am surprised by the portion, which I believe it has more than 10 jumbo prawns in the dish. It is flavorful, but unfortunately, I wish the prawn itself can absorb more of the soy sauce flavor. It tastes somewhat bland on its own. 

The next dish is the one that excites me the most - Braised Lamb with Bamboo & Chinese Mushroom in Hot Pot. Lettuce is included on the side. Putting lettuce in the braised lamb hotpot is a common thing to see, as it can absorb all the flavors from the sauce. This type of hotpot is rare and often expensive in Vancouver. Therefore, I am surprised to see this on the menu. The lamb is tender and flavorful! I would totally order this again next time I am here. 

The last two dishes are also as fabulous as the others - Pan Fried Black Cod with Soya Sauce and Sticky Rice with Preserved Meat & Sausage. The black cod is cooked and seasoned perfectly. It is soft and flaky, but I hope it is more "pan-fried" than deep-fried as it looks they dipped the fish into corn starch prior to pan-frying it.

The sticky rice is one of the best sticky rice I have eaten in Vancouver. You might think I sound exaggerated, but I love the egg strings are so thin that the flavor is in every ingredient of the dish. It is not overly seasoned, and I won't feel too heavy after eating more than a bowl.

Unfortunately, we didn't get the dessert, which is also included in the set menu because we were too full with quite a bit of leftover. The server offers us red bean sweet soup and fortune cookies. 

*** Overall Impression ***

Continental Seafood Restaurant is rated at 3.9/5, and I think it totally worth at least 4.5/5. Almost all of the dishes are perfectly seasoned and cooked, and with this $178 set menu, it can probably feed more than 6 people. If you do the math, each person is paying around $35-40 after tips and tax, which is reasonable for a fancy, high-quality 7-course meal. The restaurant is spacious and clean, with good service. I will definitely return on my own time to try their dim sum and get the Braised Lamb Hot Pot once again. 

Taste : 4.5/5 * Service: 4.5/5 * Ambiance: 4.5/5 * Quality-Price: 5/5

I am EXTREMELY picky with my nails- I am talking OCD, striving for flawlessness, overly critical in my post nail examination to the point I roll my eyes at myself (in my head).  I was born with this and have always painted my nails myself- trapped in a perfect polish hell.

Then I want the gel nail polish and recognize that this is a service that is beyond my capabilities.  So I visit a few places, let them know my OCD nail sickness, and frustratingly stare at my imperfectly applied gel polish for a few weeks until I cannot stand it and start peeling off the polish. 

Then comes along Amy and her salon Poised.... 
I have never had the a more perfect application without the usually orange stick and alcohol to fix all the mistakes.  The thumb by thumb then fingers by fingers technique won me over before I even saw the polish. 
She cares that her customers are nailiciously happy and trains her staff  have the same care and attention.

This is it... my Nailvana!

5stars service and food!

In town for work, we stopped by for breakfast, my husband have been to this place a couple times and he said it was good and I'll love it!

My first time here and yes! I got my French toast (my favorite to go menu everrrrrr) I got the banana and fruit berries and asked them if I could substituted Nutella instead of caramel sauce: the answer is YES!
My french toast was good but I prefer wet(?) toast, I hope they soak the bread longer, it's a little bit dry for me but maybe a lot of people like it. Also it was good with all the berries and banana, even the whip cream was good too!

The most important: HOT CHOCOLATE, it's the real deal! I love their hot chocolate so much and it came in a mug that so cute and looks so cozy!!

My husband got Chilaquiles Verdes, just to be honest I don't know much about Mexican food but this one was good. He said he got this every time and never change! I tried a bite (or more than that!) and it was really good, the chicken and everything went very well together, it gave a little bit of spicy but just tiny to gave you more taste and not too cheesy.

This place is awesome please come and order some food, your day will be happy eating.

Awesome! Beautiful hotel in the  of the waterfront. Walking distance to lots of shopping and restaurants. Close to South Station if you are taking the train. We walking to dinner (Babbo) and the Movies. We were given access to Equinox gym which was last cared across the street. Rooms are beautifully and simply decorated in soft off white and light wood tones. 

Very nice bar and vibe. Great drinks and attentive bartenders. Good food as well. We had a delicious breakfast at a lovely window seat overlooked ng the Barking Crab. 

They offer "igloos" at the rooftop bar which are see-through heated teepees/ tents with seating and bar service. We popped in Friday night after dinner to check them out. Interesting concept. The offer heat lamps for those unfortunate souls who do not get a seat in the igloo.  A line started forming in the lobby at about 4pm for this sought after attraction.

My 4th trip to O4W pizza for lunch and brought a co worker.  We both had a slice of the Grandma's pie and a slice of the supreme with peppers, sausage and mushrooms.  As usual both slices were fantastic.  The Grandma's pie slice nails the trifecta of pizza attributes..the crust, the sauce and the cheese.  All three of these are executed to perfection and blend themselves into as close to a perfect slice as I've ever had.  Equally well balanced was the supreme pizza.  You can taste the quality of all the ingredients that goes into making that pizza.  The thing that gets me is this is how good the re heated slices are so I can't wait to order a pie made fresh to order.  The only downside is the ambiance of the actual inside eating area...pretty non existent.  But overall nice job O4W on bringing N.J. style pizza to Atlanta!!

Fantastic little Chinese garden in Portland's Chinatown. Easily accessible by MAX and much closer than the Japanese Garden to the city the center.

Having visited multiple Chinese gardens (Huntington Gardens in Pasadena, Sun Yat Sen in Vancouver) I still really enjoyed the visit here.

When we came it was during the Chinese New Year's festivities and there were plenty of things for kids to do.

Great place to take your family!

For any BoA card holders, remember the first weekend of every month is free entry into the garden!

Haven't been here in a spell, but decided I'd like lunch with a view now that the lake is full again (thanks you texas storms). As always the entrance is over the top with natural beauty. Our table overlooked the lake and i was instantly relaxed. But you already know all that, here's why I'm writing the review...the food has improved tremendously since the last time I'd visited. Both entrees ordered were absolute perfection. I would seriously eat the tuna salad everyday if I could. Well worth the drive and well worth the price.

I had a really positive experience at the West Roxbury location. I was a walk-in and was asked to wait for about 10 minutes until a chair opened up. After about ten minutes I was greeted by Marianna who asked me what I would like done to my hair. I told her that I would like long layers and some shorter ones in the front, essentially mimicking hers. Before she cut took much off she checked the length with me to make sure I was comfortable. She took her time and was very precise with the cut. 

She was very focused the entire time and was incredibly friendly. I would absolutely go back and get another cut from her. I have grown accustomed to expensive cuts from high-end salons but it was nice to get a similar cut from someone who took pride in their work and not feel the hole in my purse at the end.

Today's visit to PDQ is solely for the chicken tender milkshake available today only! I went through the drive thru and whispered "I heard you have a chicken tender milkshake today only", she laughed and I was able to get one easily. 

Honestly PDQ is underrated and I feel as if they deserve more credit. Their sauces are phenomenal and their tenders are really good with just the right amount of spices. 

The milkshake was vanilla with whipped cream and a cherry, there was half a tender placed on top as a garnish. The shake was cold and sweet, mixed with the tender (yes real chunks of tender) it had a salty flavor which was the perfect balance of salty/sweet! 

You wouldn't think it would be good, but it is! Hopefully they bring back this treat again. I will be there!

Man, I loves me some fishes...

Not just the ones that go well with a lemon-wedge and some rice pilaf, but some stress reducing swimmers in the 30 gallon tank...Of course, Having just started my first tank about a year ago (salt water, no less) I needed as much help as I could get...Thankfully I found it at Aqua-dome...

As others have said, the folks there are very "fish-smart" and super friendly...Patient, too, especially when dealing with a none-too-bright customer (ahem) who walks in the store looking for the "Finding Nemo-fish"...They took the time to show me the best way to set up my tank as well as which fish would get along best in a tank that size...Thanks to their information and helpfulness, my Lawnmower Blenny, Dragonet, Yellow-fin Damsel and Ocellaris "Nemo-fish" are all happy and healthy!

...Now if I can just get them to stop glaring at me when I have grilled Tilapia for dinner...

I really love this park. I think mainly because of the lake as I always enjoy being by the water. The front part of the park has baseball and soccer fields (and probably other sports during the warmer months). Once you go further back, there's an underpass to walk under and then you find the real gem. Here, there is a fairly large body of water. Apparently large enough to qualify as a lake though its kind of like a giant pond. Anyway, there's a nice balcony that sits out over the water where you can sit and enjoy the view. The water always looks nice and clean and I believe they stock it for fishing. Or you can hit the sandy trail that surrounds the lake and enjoy a mile long stroll. There are several benches along the trail as well. The path is well maintained and fairly even. We saw lots of dogs out today and a few people fishing as it was the perfect day to get out and enjoy the weather! 

The only downside to this park is that it's right next to 315 (you literally walk under the highway to get to the lake area) so you can hear the highway sounds. However, it's still one of my favorites.

Greg wilde is a genious with hair! i couldn't believe how amazing my hair turned out after I went to him. before I went to him I had roots 5 inches long and every person I went to before greg did not do what I asked for nor did they make my roots go away! As soon as i went to greg he got rid of my 5 inch roots and he did exactly what I asked for. Hes smart he knows his colors and he is a funny guy! I will defiantly be back!

I meaaaaaaaan....it's the greatest place to eat in austin.

Get the Brussels & fried ice cream.  O.M.G. 

We let the waiter pick our courses for us and it was the best idea..they will ask you your likes and dislikes & make wise choices based on that. I particularly liked doing that because I am a picky eater &  I think I would get turned off by some of the combinations, which ended up being my favorite. Love this place with alllllllll my heart.

ISABELLA STEWART GARDNER MUSEUM ....5 stars!

Without a doubt, this museum is splendid, a gem, a beautiful experience. It's a shame they don't do weddings because I know hundreds of girls walk in this place and say--this is the castle I've been looking for for my dream wedding. However, it's just an elaborate tease--this museum may be a beautiful mansion, but it's mostly an art museum and the Gardner wants to keep it that way. I will definitely come back with my family and friends to show them this gorgeous house.

GARDNER AFTER HOURS ..... 4.5 stars!

However, I'm not writing about the museum which is 5 stars, A ++ . I'm writing about the NEW Gardner After Hours event, a brand-spankin' new night time soire every third Thursday at the Gardner. Overall, I was impressed with the way that the museum was able to handle themselves with such a gigantic influx of people. The museum was the perfect place to relax while sipping cocktails--languid, romantic, and inspiring. However, I would have liked standing in line for cocktails less and also, some appetizers circulating. Perhaps samples of the treats in the cafe?

 The Yelp Elites got into the event free, but if you're not a member the charge is $12 to enter the museum, and $23 for a night among the arts, art-enthusiasts, and a performance (based on the theme of the evening). The concept is absolutely brilliant and I think Gardner will do well if they just change a few minor things. I'm really excited for them and oh, if you can, don't miss the Ginger Ice Cream in the cafe-my tongue is still tingling!

My background is in endurance sports, especially biking and cross-country ski touring. I've been training with Hua since October 2019 and winter cycling with Maren since 2020. Both are incredible athletes who practice what they teach. Hua always finds clever ways to keep your body guessing and fitness building, and Maren is great at improving your endurance and mental fitness. TR has done a fantastic job adapting to online training and classes during the pandemic. My TR workouts are keeping me sane and pushing me to do things I never thought I could do, even from my home gym. I'm proud to say I'm the strongest and healthiest I've ever been. TR will transform your relationship with gyms, help you reach your fitness goals, prevent injury, and keep exercise fun and challenging. Best of all, TR is a community made up of great people.

This place serves incredible pizza! I have had pizza in several different places of the world, including Italy, and I have to say, this is hands down the best pizza I have EVER eaten!! If I lived closer, I'd likely be here on a weekly basis. In addition to their amazing pizza, their service is impeccable as well! Upon entering the restaurant, we were warmly greeted and didn't have to wait long for a seat. The wait staff stayed on top of our needs and even gave us two homemade cannolis on the house!! Fantastic place, highly recommend!

Seito Sushi is the jam!

I've been to the Winter park location, and was somewhat impressed. Today we went to the Baldwin Park location, and I was pleasantly surprised... it is simply gorgeous. It's a feast for the eyes I tell you! Like a fine hotel dining room. 

Everything I tasted was a knockout. I chose the Bento Box with Hot 'n Spicy Pork. It came a generous portion of pork and sauteed onions, rice, 3 fried dumplings, Miso soup, Ginger Salad, and a 1/2 order of California roll. Plenty of food for around $9! 

I also tried the Korean short ribs, Coconut shrimp, Bonzai roll, and Edamame. So good all the way around...

The seating is well thought out. There are different sections, which creates dimension and ambience. Plenty of outdoor seating too, in view of the lake. Ultra-lounge music plays over the sound system. Service was very attentive. 

Seito is now tied with Amura for my favorite Japanese restaurant in town.

Highly recommended!

If you have never had flash nitrogen ice cream, you got to try it at least once. They offer 3 bases for ice cream: Ice cream, yogurt, and coconut milk. Then you choose your flavor and items to add.  My kid went for the ice cream based, chocolate flavor, cookie dough and peppermint patties. In her own words and quote "This is the best ice cream I have ever had" Those are big words for an ice cream addict. I ordered coconut milk based, vanilla bean, and nestle crunch. The ice cream texture is smooth. Both were not super sweet. Yummy!!!. We also tried the dragon breath (think its called that way), you can do rice crispy treats or some other cereal. Both brought super cold that produce smoke when you put in your mouth. My daughter thought it was cool. Its was ok for me.

This is a must try at least once. Since every order is handcraft, when busy, be prepared to wait. They can only make 3 ice cream orders at a time and takes time, but worth the wait.

Five people in our family, they sent us a nice mini van, great driver, accepted our credit card with no problems.  
Cab was on time, actually early.
Cab was clean, non smoking.
Driver was so nice and helpful.
We needed two cabs for our return and that was even better.  Having just been burned with New Years surge on UBER, this was not only stress free with flat rates to and from the airport, but it was nice to spend money with a small local company.  Yellow Cab you have my business but will need to earn it each and every time.  781-648-1000 was the number we used both ways.

ABSOLUTELY AMAZING! This is my morning stop whenever I'm in Vancouver.

Pros?
-Two separate rooms (I'm not sure why so many reviews say it's a small place, because if you combine the two rooms it's really not)
-Excellent service
-Creative and delicious drinks
-AMAZING food
-Interesting flavor combinations
-Delicious mini waffles (unlike any you've ever had, chewy and vanilla-y) with great dipping sauces, such as my favorite raspberry caramel
-Fun atmosphere with lots of people
-The cassoulet is my FAVORITE
-The hot food comes out in a fry pan so it stays hot

Cons? (more like tips)
-Well, get there when it opens and there are no cons! And get there with all of your party or you'll be waiting with the rest of them. This place has a line before it opens, and the line never dies down until it closes. If you get there when it opens though, you'll be sat as soon as they can get to you and smile when more people show up just a bit too late.

I can not stress enough how much I love this place. After moving back to Dallas I have had full on cravings for it! I always come have lunch or dinner here when I am in town.

The location is by a somewhat busy intersection (on the drag, across from UT's campus) so of course the restaurant will generate a lot of traffic. Thankfully I always go during their dead times so I can easily grab a seat right when I come in. The place is fully decorated to fit the atmosphere. I always get the spaghetti with beef and it's spicy, which I love. I mean, why would you go to a thai place and not eat spicy? Their pad thai there is also amazing, would easily recommend that as well. Their service is not the best, I hardly ever get refills but honestly the food is so great I don't really care. I wish there was one in the DFW metroplex!

My first oysters on my trip to Boston! They were delicious!!!

I came on this trip with a friend who is allergic to seafood, so I didn't think I'd be able to go to any seafood restaurants. But when we came to visit Quincy Market, I saw this place and jumped on the opportunity to try some oysters. We had dinner shortly before so I wasn't very hungry and bought 3 oysters, planning to only eat 1 and share the rest with a friend flying in that night. However, once I had the first oyster, there was no turning back. I finished my plate in a matter of seconds.

These oysters were so fresh! Fairly large and given with fresh lemon slices. 

True, I don't have Boston seafood to compare these to, but I HAVE tried oysters in various other states and these were definitely the best by far.

Food (5/5): Please note this is a review for the dinner and not the brunch. I have had both, and the dinner trumps the brunch by far. I have been here twice, both times with the boyfriend. We always start out with appetizers, and I can say some personal favorites are the Gulf Coast Starter, Tempura Maine Lobster Tail, and the Crab Cakes. They are all amazing, but I personally like the lobster tail the most (you seriously cannot beat the contrast in textures and tastes of the crunchy tempura with the hot and juicy lobster meat). For entrees, I have tried the pecan salmon with lobster bread pudding as well as the cocoa-espresso ribeye on two separate visits, and I can honestly say both are FREAKING DELICIOUS. Really tender salmon meat, soft and buttery lobster bread pudding, easy-to-cut yet full-tasting ribeye. My god, I have dreams of these entrees. The desserts are sort of an afterthought - I have had the bananas foster and the bread pudding, and it's nothing to write home about. Still, Green Pastures gets 5 stars from me for really hitting the head on the nail with the appetizers and entrees.

Service (3/5): For such a nice place, I sort of expected better levels of service. It wasn't really anything special. The waiter assigned to our table seemed to be gone for a good amount of time, and I had to summon someone else half the time just to get more water or place another drink order. I think I'm speaking from one bad experience though as the young fellow who did help us out was extremely courteous, and I'm sure our dining experience would have been a lot better had he been our waiter for the night.

Atmosphere (5/5): The entire restaurant gives me the feel that this used to be an old Southern plantation home. It's your typical white Victorian home with vintage decor inside. My only regret is that dinnertime is much too dark to explore the grounds and the peacocks. Otherwise, this is a very lovely establishment and it's perfect for an intimate night out with your significant other.

Overall, the food is amazing and the service seems to be wavering dependent upon the servant you get. This is a great place to celebrate a special occasion with a spouse or significant other. If you have only been here for the brunch, I urge you to try the dinner. It is one of my favorite restaurants in Austin, and I will definitely be back.

By far, this was one of the best massages I have ever had. I had a deep tissue massage and it was relaxing with a perfect amount pressure to alleviate my tension spots. I will definitely be heading back to this location in Wellesley! The staff were friendly welcoming and helpful.  My massage therapist, Deena was intuitive and knew exactly how to apply the right pressure in all the right spots on my back. A lovely experience from the moment I walked in until the moment I left.

We love it here!  The menu is vast, and we have been slowly making out way through it; we have yet to find anything we didn't like. To the point that we had our wedding's rehearsal luncheon here. Everyone enjoyed the food, some fun comments were made about the eclectic decor (my aunt and cousin are avid Volkswagen lovers) and again, no one had any food they didn't like. We wish the information about booking for the in house catering had been more clear, but it was such a great experience that my father (who was the one that paid for the luncheon) cannot wait to go back when he visit again. We've never really tried any of the baked goods, only because we are usually too full from the food. Great portions, (and the specials will blow you away!) fresh, and wonderful service.

ANH AND CHI IS THE PLACE TO BE!! Overall, the food is great, the atmosphere is amazing, and restaurant staff is super polite. Pre-Covid they are known to be super packed, however during Covid they have nicely separated every table from each other and it feels a lot safer, especially if you dine outside in the heated patio area! The food here is definitely on the more expensive side for Vietnamese food, however you're also getting new school flavours that make this place so unique. First off the chicken wings are to die for, so juicy and delicious and these guys do it right. Next, their beef pho is solid; it wasn't my favourite of the bunch but it was packed with flavour and the beef was nice and tender as well. Also the grilled pork vermicelli dish was amazing, this was by far my favourite dish. The pork is super flavourful and charred to perfection offering a complete bite when paired with the vermicelli noodles and salad mix. Overall you have to check this place out if you haven't already!! Make sure you call in advance to see what their wait times are like as they are often super busy :)

"..and they're always glad you came."

After visiting Cypress Street Pint & Plate for the first time to gather with fellow Yelpers to play UNO a few weeks ago, I came to think of Cypress as Midtown's Cheers. Everyone knows everyone's name and if they don't,  they'll quickly try to get to know you! By the end of your visit you will have had to remember more names than you did at your very first AA meeting!

The special on this particular dreary Saturday was an egg sandwich. Which I can honestly say: Rocked My world! What better to have with an egg sandwich than a bloody mary (or two). Perfectly served in a tall high ball glass with three olives. Service was fast and more importantly,  personable. 

The owner, Billy and Manager, Andrew L. are very friendly and genuinely personable. Seeing them out at Ecco on Friday night, I was completely surprised that they both remembered my name and were more than willing to give me a big hug and welcome me back to Cypress Street Pint & Plate. If that's not convincing, I don't know what is. After shutting down the bar at Ecco, I walked over to Cypress St. where I was pleased to be greeted by friendly faces. 

I took one quick look at the menu and didn't need to see anymore once I saw corn dogs on the menu! Six to an order, the all beef corn dogs hit the spot! I ate my order and half of Camille B.'s order!

Gordon, one of my favorite Atlanta bartenders, gave me a big hug when I left and asked Camille and I both to stop back in a see him sometime. 

There's not very many places you can go at 2AM where the bartender, and management are more than willing to offer up a hug and sit down and chat it up with you!

Yes, they have PDX carpet ice cream (and it's great, and very minty; those who are 'meh' about mint need not apply). But you know what else they have? Salted. Caramel.

I love salted caramel anything with every fiber of my likely-cholesterol-clogged heart. And Scoop's salted caramel did not disappoint. 

First, it is salty. Not in a 'oh no, there goes the Morton salt girl spilling salt all over stuff' way, but in a way that you can definitely taste it and it is a perfect counterbalance to the sweetness of the caramel and the rich fattiness of the ice cream. I only got one scoop (and one scoop is still a lot of ice cream), but if I hadn't just had breakfast I know that a second scoop of that salted caramel ice cream would have been just fine.

And oh, the waffle cones. If they're baking, you're buying them, because that waffle smell wafting from this little truck is nigh irresistible.

Taco Tuesday and National Tequila Day equals a perfect dinner!!  Decided to try another new restaurant and I'm so glad I did!!  Luckily the place wasn't crowded very nice atmosphere, nice music playing friendly staff waiting to take my order.

Upon walking in you place your order at the counter you get a number and sit where ever you like.  Monday and Tuesday they have all you can eat tacos.  That was the  perfect choice for me because I couldn't make up my mind.  I ordered the grilled chicken, blackened chicken, beef and crispy fish.  Waited about 5-10 minutes for my order everything was freshly prepared, hot fresh and delicious!! I didn't have a favorite because they all were so good!!  

I gave this establishment 5 stars because the service was outstanding, the cleanliness of the restaurant and the food was amazing!!

YESSSS...5 Stars for one of my favorite brewpubs in Oregon!

I worked a block away from this awesomely located brewpub in NW Portland for the past 2 summers.  I would smell the beer brewing bright and early in the morning and once I had a whiff of that I knew it was going to be a good day. This place also probably takes up an entire block.

Im not going to lie, I might be a little biased towards Bridgeport beers but that's because they ROCK.  they make one of the best IPA's in my opinion and now with Hop Czar on the shelves I cant stop drinking beer.

So what if im biased towards the beers...Beers aside, this place is awesome, I never been in it before its remodel but have been there with family or friends a few times. Its like 3 stories tall and depending on how busy it is you're seated accordingly.  If its spring or summer you should check out the back patio, which is usually full but nothing beats drinking a micro on a nice sunny afternoon in NW Portland! Go there during peak hours and its a great social environment, everyone is happy and the atmosphere is bumping.  I've stopped by the bakery in the mornings a few times to get coffee and a pastry and im also impressed with their baked goods.

The food is upscale and presented well. It seems that they make most of their stuff from scratch. Its not your cheap brew pub burger and fries crap (cough..McMenamins). this place knows how to make food and probably has a good chef back there.  I usually get one of the Pizzas which are all named after different Portland bridges.  The pizza has never let me down especially with a pint in my other hand.

If you want a taste of one of Oregon's best micro's along with good food and a lively atmosphere (in and around the restaurant) this is the spot. period.

Although I've had massages before, for the first time in my life I reached a point that I needed a massage ASAP!  I had a pain in my neck and my back just ached.  I call on Monday and Tuesday afternoon I had an appointment with Craig.  Like others have said he really listened to my problems and really worked on my body.  I paid $90 for 90 minutes of heaven.  The next day I was soar, but that went away as did the previous pain.  I've been telling friends and co-worker left and right.  As an added bonus, I when I filled out the form they asked for my birthday (this was the very end of June and I have a July birthday).  On Saturday morning, I had a postcard inviting me in for a $40 hour long massage during my birthday month!  No need for Newbury prices, I'll definitely be a regular at this wonderful Allston joint.

We decided to give sweet Melissa's another chance and boy am I glad we did! We went on a Sunday (again) and there was a 20 minute wait. After what happened last time, I was pretty nervous but we were actually seated in about 15 minutes so we were off to a much better start. From there it only got better. Our server was super friendly and attentive. I ordered the lox BLT and it was more than worth the wait! It was hands down the best BLT, maybe even the best sandwich, I've ever had. We will definitely be back!

Finally, my love for Boloco extends out of the city!

I've been going to Boloco for years in downtown Boston, and this location is actually a lot nicer than others. You can order quickly via touch-screen instead of waiting in line -- or if you're low-tech, you can still order at a register. The store is super clean, and there is a trendy downstairs seating area with TVs and interactive games. For example, you can respond to questions that pop up on the TV, or play games on your smart phone with other guests in the store.

The staff is super friendly, and I'm a huge fan of the loyalty card -- free burrito on your birthday, or for spending a certain amount in stores. And I like that Boloco seems a lot healthier/fresher than its counterparts in the area (like Qdoba and Chipotle). It seems like less of a chain, and more of a "real food" place.

So far so good. I'm not complaining at all. For the price & how conveniently location wise to almost everything especially 10min to Disney World....Staff is friendly & helpful to my experience. Will def be back..! The pool is the hi lite of this hotel. We paid $104 per night & we were on the highest floor (6th) & had an awesome view of the pool. For this kind of price & this close to Disney World? You can't beat it. Highly recommend this hotel..

Let's just say this review is over due. My sister recommended this place and I eat here at least once a week (if not more).  I always get chicken and waffles so I cannot tell you about anything else on the menu. My meal is always fulfilling. The price is reasonable. Every time I go I have a 5 experience. 

This place has great customer service and now they know me by my name. The staff is always jolly and if you eat at the restaurant it's a good atmosphere.

This is a great burger! We had Bonedaddy cater our wedding and it was a marvelous experience - the chicken burger is amazing, and I was shocked at how good the quinoa burger was. All of our friends and family told me how much they liked the food - it was fun, tasty, and everything went incredibly smoothly. Can't wait to go visit the truck downtown and try some of the specialty burgers - I've got my eye on the Die, Muenster, Die!

This is a fun tasting room with great service and small plates, cleverly disguised as a hip neighborhood wine bar. All the wine is from their winery, and it's all tapped--no bottles--so there are infinite tasting and glass options.  They offer some pretty reasonable bottle and glass prices, as well as flights of reds and whites.  

We weren't sure what we wanted, and our server brought us tastes until we settled on a bottle we all liked.  We also dug into the roasted garlic in olive oil. 

I'll be bringing my mom here when she's in town, because Mom likes things that are awesome.

Wow I love this place! It is the ONLY place I will go for tires and shocks and even wiper blades. The staff are friendly and extremely competent. Recently I brought my car in for a wheel alignment because it had been something like 5,000 miles since the last one, and a little while later the service guy came out and told me that they had tested my car and all four wheels were right on so there was no need for an alignment. They didn't charge me even though they had spent probably a half-hour doing the tests. That is excellent customer service. I highly recommend them.

The locals say avoid Voodoo, and I'm glad we did. Blue Star is fancy in the way of being classy, innovative, without the wacky that is Voodoo. It's clean and modern inside, with a few window seats. It's a gem! 

The line at 11am was probably 5 minutes. They've got incredible choices of donuts, it was difficult to decide.  Blueberry basil bourbon donut- pretty and delicious. You can really taste the basil, but it's so subtle. Great balance of tart and sweet. Chocolate almond ganache was rich towards the end and can be messy. Their donuts are light and airy, very high quality made. Having thought about these donuts everyday I was in town, I made a power walk right before close at 7 to find they were sold out. I look forward to coming back and trying more.

Sushi by Yuji is amazing.
Before I start, I have to say make a reservation!! We tried to go here before and they had a sign up saying they were only taking reservations today. The second time we went we called ahead on the same day and it was all good, they ended up being full when we were there (it's a tiny place!). Also, both of these instances were on weekdays so I imagine you'd have to call even earlier for weekend reservations.

All of the seafood here was so fresh which just elevated the taste of everything.

We started with the carpaccio, half tuna and half salmon, and it really set us off on the right foot. The flavour was amazing, something I still think about the taste of even though this was weeks ago. The tuna was just a bit better than the salmon, maybe because it was more thinly sliced and was able to absorb the sauce better, but they were both amazing.

The shiro/house roll was really delicious as well. I think there was something in it flavour wise that was similar to the carpaccio, but whatever it was made it taste so good.

We also got the spicy bc roll, kura roll, and the chopped scallop roll. The only thing that disappointed me at this place was that they did the thing where they made the roll "spicy" by just putting a spicy sauce over it, but the inside of the roll tasted the same way it normally would. Their spicy mayo did have wasabi infused in it though, I'm personally not a huge fan of wasabi so I wasn't a fan of this roll but my boyfriend didn't mind it. The regular rolls were pretty standard, but definitely tasted a lot better with the fresh seafood. Really appreciated that the seaweed was easy to bite too and wasn't the kind that you get stuck chewing forever.

I think this is the kind of place you go to if you want to stray away from your regular sushi order and get dishes that are more specific to this restaurant.

The hostess was kind to seat us even though we didn't have a reservation, just cautioned that we needed to quickly order since our table was reserved in 1 hr and 15 minutes...  This fortunately was more than enough time to have a wonderful meal...

We tried both the muqueca completa and the seafood casserole.  The seafood casserole puts the paella to shame, all the paellas that we've had here in the US haven't been as delicious and luxurious as this seafood casserole.  The muqueca was simply fabulous, I loved the abundance of vegetables in this seafood dish.  

The waitress was so sweet making conversation with our 2 year old (she has a little one as well) and perhaps because of the pleasant interactions, I have never seen our daughter eat so much!  She loved the coconut shrimp as well as her fish dinner with mashed potatoes and rice.  

We have one month left in Cambridge and quite tempted to stop cooking and eat out every day with such wonderful restaurants in the area...!

Once again my second trip here at Russian house for dinner ordered the lamb with specialty sauce and appetizers are eggplant rolls, portabella mushrooms with melted cheese , then ordered  vodka shots and a white Russian . First of all it was the best I ENJOYED EVERYTHING including the salad was like a potato salad but better. The waiter was attentive and beyond. Every single dish we ordered was amazing!! Yes I go back sooner than later. You do have to find a parking for downtown is hard to find any parking but we were lucky since it was early afternoon. The ambiance is so delightful and colorful the ceiling is truly artwork. I like the stuffed bear while your walking into the restaurant. I will be a regular at this place and free vodka. Love it!!!

The largest aquarium in the United States of America!!! This is indeed a must-see destination in Atlanta, GA.
There are so many things to see including sea lion show, dolphin show, whale shark feeding, etc. Also there are 4D theater shows such as shark show and even seasonal animations (e.g., Polar Express 4D).
There are about four main wings of traditional aquarium tanks including tropical species and cold water species. Comparing to other aquariums, the Georgia Aquarium approves on these tanks on all aspects, from grandiosity to unique designs. Many exhibits give you multiple views at different angle perspectives. There is a tunnel pathway that goes underneath one of the aquarium tanks providing an impressive immersive view of whale sharks, manta rays, etc. 
*indeed quite a number of photo ops available  here

There is a cafeteria providing a good selection of a la carte of burgers, fries, pizza, chicken tenders, salads, and various bottled drinks. But as always with these types of places, prices are often exorbitant when comparing to outside the venues.

When you are welcomed in to the Georgia Aquarium, you are recommended to download the app so that you can have a map and the scheduled times for shows, events, etc.

No issues/complaints about the staff.

Marriott is our Hotel chain of choice for this family that travels often!

I particularly love the Residence Inn chain because of their mini kitchens and of course free breakfast! (who doesn't like free) We're talking substantial HOT breakfast! fresh waffles, eggs, sausage, toast, fruit, etc... 

This stay was one of the best that we have had! 
Front desk staff - Bruno and Daniel were excellent.  

Being in the heart of the nightlife and blocks from DT shopping on Robson, the location and value are great!

Overall one of the Greatest Marriott experience we've had!

Been to many Pubs/Taverns/Bars/Breweries/Restaurants in Boston. This place was by far....the absolute best. Owner Adam knows how to treat people. Greeted us and each and every
guest that came through the door he was near.
Came and talked to us. Even gave me a sample
of their made-from-scratch Chowda (damn good btw). Being an outta towner, felt right at home with the what we were told by many bartenders in the area as locals' favorite. If you only visit one tavern/pub...this should be it!!!

I went into Hawthorne Cutlery & Gifts to find a Christmas present for my boyfriend yesterday. I'd also brought along 3 of my daily-use cheapo kitchen knives to get sharpened. The two older gentlemen behind the counter were super helpful and helped me find the perfect gift for my budget. They also sharpened my knives for free because their regular guy wasn't in that day. They never made me feel stupid for not knowing exactly what I was looking for and were respectful and courteous at all times. They carry a lot of knives for every budget and they'll be happy to tell you details about the ones you're interested in. I'll definitely be back to support this local business.

We made a last minute decision to try this place...what a great decision!!  Is in a nice little neighborhood.  Restaurant is cozy and was very clean. They also have sidewalk seating.  We were there at just after 5pm and were seated right away w/o a reservation.  Service was very friendly and attentive with great input for my mother, who had never had any type of Indian cuisine.  Everything was delicious!  I was a bit disappointed that they do not have any type of vegetarian korma on the dinner menu but the other options were still fantastic.  Can't wait to come back again!

The staff at Millworks is amazing. My daughter moved in yesterday and the boxes we had shipped from home were already in her room. It was a great pleasure working with Kenda, Marlin, Desmond and Annie. They gave us the tour of the property and informed my family of all the amenities. They even supplied the apartment with beverages as a welcome. We love that the property offers socials for new and current residents. They were like concierges also in giving restaurant suggestions. Our other daughter was a resident there 2 years ago and loved Millworks also. My daughter that moved in now is very happy with her new residence.

Stopped by this place for lunch on a weekday - I haven't been to the Shops at Porter in years, so I was glad to see the little restaurant storefronts are still there!

Tampopo serves traditional dons (bowls), curry, and udon - kind of like Japanese comfort food. I've never really seen this kind of food served at typical Japanese restaurants in the area so I was happy to try it out. I got the chicken karaage udon, and my boyfriend had the soboro don. Both were solid and good portion sizes. We also got an order of gyoza and a surprise complimentary orange jello!

The gyoza was great - fried, but just enough to be crispy and not deep fried and oily.

The karaage was crispy and tender, and the udon was nice and chewy! I also really liked the sauce, which was tangy and just a little spicy. I really appreciate the vegetables they put in to make a more balanced looking meal.

Will be back here whenever I am in the area.

The Festival of the Lion King is a wonderful live show. The line for the show is mostly outside with no cover, so that wasn't fun in the heat, but the wait is worth it.  You start off with funny hosts that get the various groups of people to rival other groups in the theater.  This production has great music from the movie and excellent acrobatics that rival the Cirque.  The show was really great that we saw the line was short and entered the theater for the next showing.

This dealership has redeemed itself. 

I've always been a little leary of getting auto repair work done at a dealership. Over the years of having several different cars, Its been mention to me more than once, by mechanics, friends, and by my ex who was an auto sales representative for several years (now retired), that they are not to be trusted. So when my uncertified used (not under warranty) Hyundai Sonata's engine light started showing up on my dash about a month ago, I went to my trusty mechanic and he at that time, hooked that device up to my car to find out what was going on. It showed no code, he tightened up the gas cap and said to bring it to the dealership. OMG! On the way to the dealership, I stopped at the store, came back to my car, and lo and behold, the engine light was gone. THANK GOD! About a month later it appeared again, like a bad dream. Ok, I replaced the old gas cap with a new one, the light went off again. Another prayer of thank you crossed my lips. That last about a week, when for the third time, here it is again! Ok, ok,  I've had enough. I bring it to my trusty mechanic and he finds a code this time. Finds out what the problem is, Harness, sensor to the transmission needed attention. Although everything on a car is expensive, gone are the days of windshield wipers that use to cost under $10, or working on it yourself, the technology is so advanced now, even the auto technicians probably need to go back to school every six months or so to keep up. I say to myself anything to do with the transmission and/or engine is big dollars. My trusty mechanic told me how expensive this 4 to 5 hour job would probably cost. He called the Hyundai dealership, explained what the problem was to the service advisor Mike, and Hyundai agreed that it was under warranty and would do the job. Unbelievable!!! I called again just to verify and got the same answer, "yes its under warranty and we'll do the work", but they're busy and don't know when they'll be able to do it, but said if I bring it there now and can leave it for a couple of days, they'll work on it. I was there in less than 20 minutes!
Couple of days later I get an early morning phone call from Mike, telling me my car is ready! No charge at all, and here's the kicker, upon arrival, my car was washed AND my wheels were waxed.... My wheels waxed! What dealer does that! 
I love you guys! Thanks for the superb service!

Absolutely delicious. Came on a Saturday so was able to have eggs Benedict for breakfast and it was so good. I asked for the eggs to be medium so that was fine. I enjoyed the friendliness of the server. She was so nice and recommended everything in such an upbeat way that I tried it all. The tofu scramble was truly delicious. The table and surrounding areas were clean and inviting as well. The restaurant is adjacent to a vintage Embassy Suites. The hotel has a vintage play area for children too. Expect lines and lines of people and get there early for weekends. The eggs Benedict and cinnamon bun is only on Saturdays. Also Voodoo Donuts is diagonal from this spot. I will hit up Portland again next month and try other things. And the pricing was not wild. Tofu scramble, 2 coffee, eggs Benedict... under $30.

This place only gets a good rating because of the location. It's beautiful for its close by mini-park and its oceanview. There is outdoor seating, but the service is terrible and slow. I personally think it's the reflection of the manager. It's a great place to bring your puppy to lunch while meeting with people. Parking garages are nearby but street parking is difficult.

The food is overpriced and not that great for its fancy location. The bar scene is a bit older it seems - more young professionals lingering than usual. Great overall atmosphere though.

I give this Panera another shot every once in a while after vowing to never return because the food is pretty tasty.  Unfortunately, I think I may have finally had it with them.  To give you some perspective, allow me to tell you about my experience there this morning.

I walk in and place my order with the guy at the counter as follows.

Me: I'll have a steak, egg, and cheese bagel, a four-cheese souffle, and a small coffee to go.

Guy at the counter: Is all that to go?

Me: :-I

He proceeds to get my souffle and hands me the bag along with my coffee cup.  The souffle is upside down in the bag, indiscriminately tossed in with no regard to gravity.  I get my coffee and it is dreadfully watered down and bland, a true crime against coffee everywhere.  I try a different one, same result.  I leave once again vowing to never return.

I wanted to like this place. Such a cute name, cute location, cute concept - but none of it came close to what I thought it could be. 

From the name you would think they specialized in dumpings. But no. They have maybe 4 or 5 different types, nothing special, all generic ones you could probably find in the frozen aisles in an Asian grocery store. The shrimp dumplings I had were so bland. If not for the slight texture change, you wouldn't know where the dumpling dough ended and the shrimp began. I've had MUCH better at mediocre dim sum places.

They have a few variety of other Asian entrees like rice bowls and ramen, but nothing to write home about. If you're in the area, don't have time, and you absolutely need to satisfy your Asian food cravings, then make this your last resort - and don't get dumplings.

Came in on a Saturday. Nice ambience. Ordered the Corner breakfast. Was told I could not substitute the meat for anything without an upcharge. No big deal. 

My plate was brought to me with a side of fruit. Figured they changed their mind and it was on the house. Nothing to write home about. Small portions. Tiny toast and soft potatoes.

Received the bill and saw their was a $3 charge for the fruit which I never ordered. I kindly asked the server to remove it. She came back and said that the manager said that since I ate it, they cannot take it off. Wow. So because they messed up the order, the onus is on me. Awful.

Have always been a fan of Bar Louie. Tonight @Polaris was very disappointing. Came in for some 'after movie' bite to eat. Sat at the bar. To our left, the bar was covered in dirty dishes & glassware. The bar in front of us was dirty & sticky. When we asked the bartender to wipe it off, he was unbelievably rude!! Asked me "Can you see that I'm busy and have my hands full?" Lollll, I almost fell off my chair! Uhhhh....okay then. He finally came from behind the bar & wiped up w/ a smelly, dirty rag. GROSS! We ordered our food from another bartender. When we asked what we could substitute for the fries (i.e., fruit or a vegetable?) she screwed up her face and said, "We don't got any fruit, only broccoli."  I mean, you just can't pay for this kind of entertainment! Food was fine, timely and warm. Service--terrible. Will not make this a regular stop. Matt the Miller is a thousand times better!

We arrived for our reservation and we were told that we could wait outside or in the bar until our entire group arrived...annoying since we were happy to order drinks and appetizers while we waited for friends who were running 10 minutes late. The staff were not particularly friendly and the food was totally mediocre. Also, we noted that we were celebrating a birthday in our online reservation and reminded our waiter, but he did nothing to acknowledge my husband's birthday other than say "happy birthday" as he handed him the check. There are so many options in the North End, skip this one.

Had a regular mani pedi here and it was not-so-great. I was definitely left with rough edges around my nails and cuticles, which I had to deal with when I got home. Also, I don't think they sterilize their utensils before/after each use. I saw the technician just rinse them with water and place them back in her bin, then spray them with a little bit of disinfectant before use.
Gorgeous Nails across the street does a way better job for slightly less money, they're salon is just slightly run down.

When I entered I mentioned I saw a $2 off coupon on the website and if they would honor it. I was told "It must be printed. If we had everyone pull up here and say they saw the coupon on the website then we'd all be broke." He printed my receipt and said "Here you go, now you've got $2 off your next wash when you bring it in."  What a complete douchebag comment. First off your margins are ridiculously high where a full service wash costs you less than $10 with your labor. That is a $13 profit if you get the lowest end wash.  You could have just said sorry, company policy is that we have to have a physical receipt. I think I'll go somewhere else next time.

The place is immaculately clean and Shauna knows what she's doing... Except when it comes to dealing with people. She alternated between being nice, rude, snappish, and yelled at me once because I "closed my eyes too hard". It was like dealing with someone with split personalities. When you're in the chair and someone is tattooing your eyes, this is a very vulnerable place to be! Normally if someone spoke to me like that I'd let them know right away that is NOT ok, but I didn't want to make her mad(der?) when she's perfirmind delicate work! The experience was so bad, I'll NEVER go back here. Also, I wanted cat-eye eyeliner and she said she couldn't do it; at the time, she had a photo of it on her website. So that's false advertising as dad as I'm concerned! The liner turned out ok but it wasn't worth the experience of dealing with Shauna.

I went for my birthday and enjoyed the food and music.  However I choose Boogalou because I thought it was a restaurant/lounge but they treat the tables like clubs.   It wasn't busy (there was over 3 tables empty) and they made us get up from the table before all of my guest got their meals and finished their drinks.  I was over charged for my drink because the bar tender didn't know how to make it.   My drink was mostly ice and I was charged $17/drink.   Boogalous has potential but service has to improve.

Pros: 
free street parking
good service, but then the servers are only taking care of drinks
good drinks

Cons:
*extremely loud-couldn't even hear my wife right across from me-not really a date place

*you sit very close to your neighbor, which doesn't help with the decibels or comfort

*you have no idea about the order of when the food is coming out or how long it will take-we waited 20 minutes until the first dish came, which looked disappointing.  We had to wait another 20 minutes before another came out, and even though it also didn't look great, we took it just to eat something

*in typical Gillespie fashion, all the food portions are tiny and overpriced e.g. $13 for a tiny portion of lentils

*They will try to bilk you by offering an item that "isn't on the menu" so you have no idea of the price of it.  Once you agree to take it, they go right to the place on the menu where the $40 slot is and mark it.  Seems they knew all along it was on the menu. .We ended up paying $140 for two people with 3 drinks and 4 of their tiny portions, and were left severely disappointed. We walked out  feeling we had just been punked by Gillespie again (see Revival) and still a little hungry.  

There are much better restaurants in Atlanta, especially for that ridiculous price.  In general, you would be wise to avoid the Gillespie over-hyped joints.  If you want to spend the money for a nice dinner, Ford Fry and Castelluci places, for example, actually live up to all the flattery.

The Galaxy Cafe has a good concept for a local diner, however, there is a failure to deliver.

Quality of food:  I had the French Toast with fresh strawberries and bananas - it was good, but the FT could have been a little less soggy.  The upgrade for pure maple syrup was not, and I doubt the claim of pure maple.   My husband had 'The Big Wrap' it was ok, but having egg shell in the wrap was not ok.

Atmosphere:  the noise level was identified as "average" --- it was pretty loud.  Definitely not a quiet / quaint place for a leisurely brunch.

Price:  for the location, the atmosphere, and the food it was overpriced.  

Would I recommend the Galaxy Cafe to a friend, probably not.  Would I discourage someone from going, probably not.

It's a middle of the road place, with prices that are a little higher than average.

This place is no longer what Iit used to be. I came back today, and was sorely disappointed. Unfortunately, everything has changed. Apparently some Americans can't stand the fire, spice, and sweetness of authentic caribbean cuisine so they complained until, like many other places I once loved, they changed the flavors. Watered them down. Americanized them. Let me just say the whole point of trying cuisine from other parts of the world is to experience the true flavors and something new. If you can't stand the heat, then don't go into their kitchens. What I had today was nothing more than very garlicky baked chicken that was too salty and regular rice and peas. Nothing with the coconut flavor, thyme, or anything in their that I'm accustomed to. I asked for cabbages and got mixed vegetables instead. I'm tired of people complaining and forcing those who serve international delights to change their gem of a recipe just to suit the taste of those who truly don't want to try anything new. I asked her what happened and she did admit they had to remove the spice and change how they make their food due to complaints. She did ask me what do I think and I told her it just isn't the same. She was very nice about it and did offer me a discount for the next time I came back, but I'm just too afraid. I don't want to spend the money and can't get authentic traditional food like I once did when I first became a patron. I hope they go back to the way things were. 2 stars for the service and courteousness of the staff(they are always nice) but the food was nothing special. I could make garlicy baked chicken myself.

I stopped by to try a burrito because one of their signs says "TACOS BURRITOS" and I would like to eat those. 

I should mention their signs. There are so many that I have no idea what the restaurant is really called. The take-out menus say "Pollos a la Brasa el Chalan" which aparently means "chickens to the live coal dealer."

I ordered the steak super burrito, because I always like to try out super at least the first time. I waited for about 5 minutes, and then food was ready. $7. 

I carried it home on my shoulder like a kid toting a 30-rack. 

It was MASSIVE, I think it honestly was about 2lbs. 10 inches long and maybe 5 inches in diameter. There were no thoughts of hand-to-mouth feeding with this thing. Knife and fork time. 

The taste was really quite good, with sweet morsels of steak, spiced rice and veggies. It really wasn't much of a *burrito* though. It was good food in a massive portion, but it didn't have that juicy, slurpy spiced meat and veggie flavor to it.

I try and avoid chain restaurants like these as much as possible. I was just really hungry and drove by. I dined in and ordered the tropichop and a side of plantains. The food is ok and not terrible. But it's still not Chipotle.  

I ordered at the counter and sat down. 30 minutes later my food comes. Now remember this is suppose to be fast food/fast casual. 

The kitchen area is a mess from what you see ordering at the counter. Trash and food all on the floors. Employees could give a shitless about being here. I don't blame them. They probs get paid terribly. I get it do the least amount of worm possible and burn out the clock. 

Food was decent. Won't talk bad about the food. It is one of the few places with plantains and I love love love sweet plantains. 

Going forward I'll always remember to avoid places like this.

Oh man, Bollywood Bistro is another one of those Indian places that I felt was a complete waste of my money. I don't know if it's because I got takeout here a couple weeks ago, and didn't eat in the "bistro" (HA it is NOT a bistro), but add this to the list of places which, if you like authentic Indian food, you should for sure avoid. 

The chicken pakora was soggy and gross and was basically the equivalent of chicken nuggets. The chicken tikka masala was rather like Campbell's tomato soup. I remember being very sad that I actually ate my food, but I paid for it and was hungry, so... not as bad as Curry & Hurry, which is the most epic fail Indian food in Columbus I've tried thus far, but certainly not *good.* 

It's sad because Bollywood Bistro is a great name, so I had really high expectations. The terms "bistro" seems to me quite misleading. FAIL.

This place had very insta worthy dishes, but flavors were mediocre. The service was slow but the owner was very nice, she asked us if it was our first time, told us a little about the restaurant and when they opened up. The conversation made it feel very welcoming for my friend and I. I specifically came here for the bone marrow pho, in which they would offer it to you but is not actually on the menu. I don't get that. The flavor of the broth wasn't bad but I definitely have had a lot better, I enjoyed every bit of the bone marrow but the main concept of pho is the broth and if you can't perfect that then it defeats the purpose of the restaurant. My warm also came out warm, which wasn't pleasant because I like my pho steaming hot. But I must say, some of their dishes were very unique and you can get that anywhere else! The pomelo salad was our favourite and I had wished I captured a picture of that! Really refreshing to have! I personally liked their Banh Mi but my friend said it was alright as well.

Do not come right at 4pm dinner time opening. Most everything either was prepared too early or leftovers from lunchtime seatings. The fish on the sushi buffet looked dry and tacky. They had Inari sushi that was dry, I never seen that before. The dim sum dumplings in the steamers were dry and hard on the pastry edges. The selections were average with some things you normally don't see on a buffet (crawfish, frog legs). Food was luke warm and a little bland. The best part of the meal was them having soy sauce on the table. Disappointing since my wife and daughter went there on grand opening week and raved about them. Will likely not be back to try again.

Looking for a good restaurant near my hotel, I stopped in Atlantic Fish Company after seeing the good reviews on yelp.  I was solo so I sat at the bar. The service was a little slow but that's pretty typical when you sit at the bar.  

I had the sea bass chowder. I was a little disappointed in it as it was a little bland for my taste especially since the description featured poblano peppers. There was one slice of pepper which is nothing for a Texan. Also, the bacon appeared to be packaged bacon bits instead of fresh bacon. I had a small salad as well but I can't tell you what it was because it wasn't the one I ordered. And since the salad came out 10 minutes after my soup, I didn't send it back.

Great location and that's about it. Service was slow, slow, slow. Slow to take our order, slow to bring 2 glasses of wine, slow to bring the food. I ordered a glass of pinot noir and the server brought a glass of white wine. I explained that I ordered pinot noir and he just looked at me. I had to add "It's red wine" before he realized the error. (Then he blamed the bartender.) The food was average at best. I had a pizza with ahi tuna and although the tuna was just barely seared, it was not a high quality piece of meat. The pizza was a little more spicy than the menu led me to believe. My husband's crab cake sandwich was a little mushy and too much bread. We will not be returning.

Awesome that they deliver. BBQ is acceptable. Small dining area and the sun will be in your eyes if facing the window because their window coverings aren't very effective at keeping sunlight out. 

2 Star rating because they don't even have a sink to wash off BBQ-hands. I can live with walking to the convenience store to use the restroom; but, what kind of BBQ joint doesn't have at least a sink. The employee advised me to use hand sanitizer when I asked to use a sink to wash my hands... not cool.

About a year ago we had Bamboo Grove cater my sons Birthday but the food was awful. Yakisoba was dry, Pork and Chicken Teriyaki had no sauce to it and the green salad we ordered they forgot to give us dressing for it. When we called to advise them of this mishap we were told, 'Oh sorry not sure what happened"

So needless to say we figured we'd give them another try cause as I stated above, they used to be 'Da Bomb"!!!  

My mom and I ordered a Large Kehei Rib plate (to share), a plate of poke' and Spam musubi. The ribs was $19.00 and only had 6 pieces of ribs, 2 scoops rice and one lump of mac salad that was all mayonaise. The poke' had no taste and came with a piece of white paper on top, which when we brought to the attention of our waiter all he said was, "oh so you want another one?". Ummm....Yeah!!!  When we got our poke' back it had absolutely no taste at all. We also ordered the spam musubi to go and it came out with our meal. When we asked for them to put it in to go containers they got a bit irritated. 

I hope they get things together because us locals from Hawaii know what good food is and willing to pay the price but gotta get this place back to where they used to be.

We've sampled vinegars and oils at several locations, in Austin and other cities. We enjoy the freedom to wander and taste the wares, but Vom Fass is a bit skimpy with the samples which are only available with the assistance of store employees. Flavors are very diverse, but the balsamic lacked the sweetness that defines them, and the oils (particularly nut oils) had thin flavor and a bitter after-taste.  We decided on a bottle of oil and one of vinegar, and we're still reeling at the price. $165 for the two small bottles! We STRONGLY suggest that you inquire about pricing, and consider making a trip downtown to Con Olio. There, you can taste the offerings freely, the flavors are considerably more intense, and the prices won't give you a stroke!
