Yes, turnover in childcare is high. I get it. But I think it's a red flag when the person (including center administration) with the most longevity still has less than 5 years at the center.

Some staff are fantastic but no one stays for very long. We saw 4 or 5 different directors in just a couple years, and the lack of continuity for our child combined with ever-increasing rates led to us switching to a different center. Even escalating to regional management for issues was frustrating and we felt like we had very little resolution. 

Pros: Location is highly convenient. Facility is large and has a great outdoor recreation space.

In the land where Melt is king of the melted sandwiches, Tom+Chee is a peasant.  I ordered the Hot and Spicy which was $4.95.  It was horrible.  You would expect a grilled cheese to be crispy on the outside and melty on the inside.  The top was crisp but the bottom was extremely soggy.  The flavors didn't blend well at all.  

I ordered a cup of the chunky tomato basil which was $3, about $2 more than it should have been.  I expected something like Wolfgang Puck, what I got was a watery tomato soup with some chunks of flavorless tomato and no hint of basil.  So glad I didn't pay $4.50 for a bowl of it, even the small "dipper" size of it is $1.50.  This brought my total to about $8.50 with tax, not including a drink which would have been a couple bucks more.  

I don't believe there is much value in the meals here.  This meal should have been about $6 or $6.50 at most based on the quality of ingredients and portion sizes.  $8.50 was way too much.  

As far as service goes, they bring you your meal and that's it.  You dump your own trays and get your own drinks.  I don't have a desire to ever go back but if someone else was dead set on going back I would give it another try.

Great cider but you'd never know it from the poor quality of the customer service.  We've given them 3 tries, now we won't come back. 

1st experience was super great, so naturally I wanted to come back and bring friends.  

2nd experience, brought friends, had good cider, brought 3 growlers but they wanted to charge $45 for a growler full.  Screw that.  We went to Albertson's for a $12 growler fill.  

3rd experience we were greeted then promptly ignored for quite some time and passed up for other customers, even ignored when I tried several times to wave the server down, so we left without ordering and will not likely return.  Psst...I'm a great tipper and a low maintenance customer so you're kinda dumb for ignoring me.  Get over yourselves, its cider, your poop still stinks.  

We went to the Growler Guys where they were more than happy to serve me a pint of cider and fill my growler for $15.  They even serve Portland Cider Co cider except without the attitude.

I've been to this establishment a number of times for sit down dinners as well as drinks at the bar, and I'm just not overly impressed.
I mean the surroundings are cool in that it was once the actual train depot, but I'm just not a fan of the entire make-up of it in terms of food.
While the meat and fish dishes are decent, the prices are on the high-end.
I'll go again if friends suggest it, but it certainly wouldn't be my first choice.
Everyone raves about the salad bar, but to be honest, while everything appears to be fresh, it somehow reminds me of one of those old fashioned salad bars that Star Market used to have; and the selections are pretty limited and basic.
Side note-stay away from the appetizers; have had all of them, and again, just not impressed.
If you do go, try the steak or lobster casserole (tell them to be light on the breadcrumbs and butter so you can enjoy the full flavor of the lobster, as they tend to overload the dish with those items).
I agree with a previous poster that the service does tend to vary.
Also, be sure there's enough cash in your wallet or enough available room on your credit card!
Update: Just read "Shopper M's" review and I totally know who he/she is referring to at the bar!  The Bartender is not friendly at ALL and I can't believe that this place keeps her.  She totally acts like she's above everyone else, is rude, and acts like you are bothering her when you order a drink (god forbid that I pull you away from your conversations about how many miles you ran today in training for your marathon or whatever it is).  On top of that, from what I've witnessed, she hassles other employees when they come to the bar to get a drink for their table. I can totally relate "Shopper M", as I've experienced the same.

This place has really gone down hill! I came here for my lunch break today and I got the soup and sandwich combo. For $12 plus tax you'd expect the sandwich to be at least fresh. It was two pieces of cheap white soggy bread with cheap Swiss cheese and the worst part lettuce, lettuce in a hot sandwich! The soup was also so salty and had so much white pepper in it, I had 3 spoonfuls and had to stop. I will not be back - Thierry nearby offers a lot better quality food than here. If you do come here - stick to their pastries.

I've been to my share of luxury day spas and since it was my birthday, I decided to treat myself to a facial. I had been following the reviews on  Buckhead Grand Spa for a while and decided to make an appointment for a facial.  

So on to the actual review . . . 

You might ask, why just two stars when everyone else has ranked this spa higher? Well, when a company puts the word "Grand" in their name, I think it should live up to that... unfortunately, Buckhead GRAND Spa did not live up to its name.  The spa itself is actually relatively small, particularly the rooms where the services are provided. I was hoping for a very relaxing experience, but something was missing. It was unfortunately one of the most un-relaxing spa experiences that I've had.  For the type of service I received (a facial with an added masque and exfoliation) I felt that the service was extremely over-priced.  

The facial itself was mediocre and typically most day spas will include a brief shoulder and neck massage with the facial and I didn't receive that with mine.  At check out, I asked the receptionist is this a normal practice and she replied that it depends on the type of facial I received.  When I told her the type of facial I received, she said, "oh well, you should have received a shoulder and neck massage." Then, she said, "well, maybe she just ran out of time."  Although some people might see not getting a neck and shoulder massage as something small, for me it adds to the relaxation factor of a facial. 

Needless to say, I won't  be back. Usually within a week after a facial I can tell a difference in my skin.  With my facial from Buckhead Grand Spa, I saw no difference in my skin, at all. At the end of the day I was felt cheated and disappointed that I had wasted my time and money at this spa.

Based on other reviews here, we didn't have high expectations for the place, and I have to give credit to the power of the Internet for softening the blow of mediocrity.  Based on the prices on the menu, without Yelp I would have expected much more from the place, and given it one star out of spite.

Fortunately for us, we only came here because we had a gift certificate, and didn't have to spend any of our own money.

To start off, let me recount the good things about Sibling Rivalry.  We had a very nice and sufficiently attentive server.  No complaints at all there, and admirable given how little the poor guy had to work with in terms of food.

Also good was the cocktail I had, called "Summer Breeze" or something like that.  Delicious actually.

Heading down the scale was the fried calamari appetizer with green papaya salad.  It was pretty good too.  NEXT!

The rest of it was so completely dull that I can't even describe the flavors involved.  So I'll use colors instead.

Beige.  

And that's exactly how I felt after sampling 4 dishes and dessert.  Beige.

The patio was nice, and if you also have a gift card to spend, I'd recommend sitting outside rather than the dining room, which was decorated like a hotel restaurant.

If you don't have a gift card, I'd recommend going somewhere else, unless you hate food.

Cissi's is for sissies, I think. People who buy groceries because they're cute and because they must be good if they cost so much, at any rate.
I liked the layout, I liked the displays. I was there right before closing time, so the made-to-order and bakery items were looking a little slim/poor quality (no more than a pound of each cut of meat, one to three pieces of each sweet item), but we decided to skip it for post-date dessert. The eclairs, while yummy looking, weren't enough to dissuade me once "Amy's Mexican Vanilla with strawberries" was mentioned.
I can't imagine ever coming here for grocery shopping or to pick up an emergency staple. There are drug stores and a 24-hour H-E-B not too far down the road for that. Maybe if I got a better look at their luxury foods, I'd have a higher opinion.

What is disappointment. After waiting for "The Yardhouse" to open in PDX after years of enjoying them in CA, I find out they've been sold a year ago to a conglomerate. Not the same place I loved.  Some dishes remain, albeit smaller portion versions. Others are new and bland. I've visited twice after a so so first visit, the second was worse. Service was good the first time, very spotty the second.  It has lost it's appeal and become just another mediocre chain.  I won't be back.

NEGATIVES
1. Maintenance! There is ONE maintenance person for the entire complex and he is completely overwhelmed and under-qualified for these old apartments. I have had a hole in my ceiling for months with no set date to repair it. When repairs are finally made the workmanship is shoddy.
2. THE WATER/SEWER BILL! Every resident splits the cost of community water and sewer. So, in other words...you pay for other people's personal excess, car washes, sprinklers and filling up the pool. These bills are about $100 bucks a month. Once this is added to the price of your rent, the rent isn't as low as you thought. In this bill you are also paying $6 bucks for a "gate fee." The gate is 90% of the time broken. This bill is barely mentioned when you sign your lease because they know it is absurd!
3. LATE FEES! There is NO GRACE PERIOD for paying your rent. If you turn your rent in on the 2nd, there is a $100 late fee!!! If it is not paid by the 7th, the fee goes up to $250!

POSITIVES
1. The neighbors are amazing! There is a great feeling of community here. I have met so many wonderful people here. People sit around outside at night and talk when it's nice outside. Very friendly.
2. Location. Right in midtown, close to 85. On a residential street that is nice for walking your dogs.
3. VERY pet friendly!! Most residents have animals and there is a dog park within walking distance.
4. The staff members are very nice but generally inefficient.

The only reason for two stars is the food last time we ate there. The service has gotten a little worse each time we go. This is gonna be our last visit. To many other Mexican places with good food. First of three families to be seated. Both other families had their food on their tables before we had even had been asked for our order. Had to get up and ask for menus and drinks for table after 25 mins of being seated. Finally after 40 plus minutes we packed up to leave. Had still not been asked for order only drinks and chips with salsa had been delivered. I asked the lady at the front counter for our check and she asked why we were leaving. I said after 40 mins and the restaurant only half full we couldn't wait any longer ( little kids). She then gave me an $8 ticket for Lemonade and chips & salsa. I asked her if she was serious about the ticket. The manager finally waved the ticket after I explained this issue. 

No apology or even a hey well make this right. I wouldn't recommend this place.

I really like this place and I wish I didn't have to write this review.
Service was awful. From two different servers. 
The girl server was so rude to me when I asked a recommendation for a cocktail. She made me feel like I can't read. Best feeling you can give a costumer.

I get it. It was a busy night, hard work. But what can I say, I came here to have fun but got so upset from the service. 

Expected more from this place and was highly disappointed. There are other places with great cocktails and beer.

Food is definitely overpriced for what you get. It gets 2 stars because the food tasted pretty decent. Ordered the "chicken wings" which looked and tasted like it was made out of some kind of bean curd. The vermicelli Singaporean noodle dish which was pretty flavourful. Food was not bad, definitely not amazing. I really was kicking myself when we sat down because I didn't have a great feeling seeing there was only one other table who was eating in a sad looking restaurant. The service was pretty bad and super slow. It looks like it might be owned by an asian couple (the female was not particularly friendly, however the male was much more welcoming). I'm pretty sure it was just the 2 or them running the front of house and kitchen. When we ordering the lady questioned our orders by saying "that's it? You think that's enough?" Which to me is a bit rude and presumptuous. In my head I was thinking "yes that's it. Your menu doesn't look particularly amazing so it would be in our best interest to order as we go". I think I replied something like "yes, that is enough for now". 

We had to ask for water which seemed odd that none were offered as we arrived (only until after we ordered which took about 10 minutes of deciding and having to ask for water did we get water). The odd thing was the waters were given to us in black mugs. Mine had a white powdered substance around the mug and at that point I decided I wasn't drinking from this dirty mug. So major points off based on poor cleanliness. 

So based on pretty poor service and the lack of cleanliness, this place gets 2 stars. One star each for the okay tasting dishes we ordered. Price point wasn't cheap and you would be better off ordering from a food court in a mall (like crystal mall/Aberdeen centre).

DO NOT GIVE TIPS WHEN SWIPE your card
1. The waitress says she never get the tips when you swipe your card ( only the tips in the jar) 
2. It's a SELF SERVICE place that require customer clean after the meal. Dare you try to walk away, because they will chase after you to clean it up. "Wait, I paid 20% tip when ordering". Doesn't matter, clean the table up!!!

The 2nd time I went there for take out. After The cashier swipe my card, she flipped the screen to select tips. 
15%,20%,25%,other... I'm confused, if this is a self service place with a tip jar next to the cashier. WHY 1) even ask your customer to select tips? 2) set 15/20/25% as the first few options??? I doubt the owner has a degree in human behavior and try to trick people pay tips, then force them to clean up after by pointing a notes on the wall somewhere : customer to clean up the table. 

Oh, the food... awful but eatable. A slightly better than the service. 

What if you already paid the tips by accident and they chased after you to clean it up. Argue with them in English rather than Chinese. I have friends experienced the same thing. The table with American Chinese argue with them in English got away and got refund back.... don't ask me why, I'm the proud Chinese speaking table, unfortunately.

I didn't like this place, at all.

Came here with a coworker for lunch, met our server in five minutes, was served our drinks 30 minutes later, our lunch 30 minutes after that.

Normally, two people can do lunch at nearly every place in Polaris in an hour or less. Larger groups? Yeah, maybe a little longer. here? Two people. No crazy requests. Ordered from the lunch menu, and it took over 90 minutes.

The food was meh, but filling (I had the blackened chicken sandwich).

Plain and simple, I'll be skipping it for lunch from now on.

I used to like this place but there was a very interesting mishap that I just can't get over and I won't be going back.

The waiter took my order. I waited 20 minutes. The waiter brought my food. The food wasn't cooked. I flagged the waiter to complain. The waiter took my food and I specifically asked that they just heat up the part that's not cooked and bring it back because I was fine with that and I didn't want to wait for it to be cooked all over again. I waited 15 minutes. The manager came back to say they were out of the dish I ordered. I said but I asked for the food on my plate to be heated. He said he will not charge me for it and walked away. So, disappointed and confused, I left. Sheesh.

I was excited to try this place, as some of the reviews were good.  I have only been here once, and based on what I ate, I may not make it back for a second time for severals months.  

Pro-
Plenty of seating and choices, having both tables and booths.  It looks like they could handle seating a large party with ease.
Padded chairs and booth seats.
Fairly decent decorations.
Serves Asian alcohol and spirits.
They have a fish tank.

Con-
Smelled like my great aunt's house (but to be fair, it might have just been a booth of older women near the door).
Atmosphere and decor was late 80's, I'm talking teal and salmon colors.

Since it was my first visit, I decided to try the ambiguous General Tso's Chicken lunch special, staple of all "American" Chinese restaurants. My soup selection was egg-drop, and I should have had the miso.  The egg-drop was very thick and very yellow.  I ate the soup, but it was nothing special.

When the chicken dish arrived, there was plenty of steamed white rice on my plate, along with a standard Chinese egg roll.  The chicken was cut into fairly large pieces, that did not seem to have any breading on them.  I was able to cut the pieces of chicken into 3rds (that's how large they were) with my fork, but it took some effort.  The chicken was overcooked and dry. I was not offered chopsticks until I was already into my meal, but I probably would not have been able to use them due to the chicken's texture. The sauce was fine, and had a good flavor.  The dish was accompanied by several pieces of steamed broccoli which I didn't have any problems with.

The thing I found most unsettling was our server was wearing shorts.  I'm no prude, as I think shorts are fine for restaurant employees, but only if the ocean is nearby. Needless to say, this wasn't a good first impression of Dragon Court, but I will try them again in several months, and hope to have a better experience.

The only thing good here was their famous chicken. It's one of those places that I've been to and don't need to go back. Our server was absolutely terrible. Some of the worst service I've ever experienced, especially when you're spending $50+ a person. There were multiple times when our waiter just said "NO." My friend asked for a specific cocktail and he responded with those two letters. we were shocked. He didn't even follow it up with an explanation of why we weren't allowed to have this drink. After we enquired he said it was because they ran out. He didn't even offer any recommendations. The second time we were just told "No" is when we were ordering a certain dish that they were sold out of. Again, no recommendations he suggested to replace the item they didn't have. The cocktails were good but lacked in the amount of alcohol, almost made me question if there was alcohol in it at all. My friends and I decided that the service was so bad it wasn't worth the meal.

Truly the worst eggs I've had in my life. And I've had a lot of eggs. My rubbery, overcooked omelette sitting in a pool of orange grease was unworthy of the smoked salmon it was stuffed with. I think the potatoes were previously frozen, they had a funny after-taste and had not been salted or seasoned. They did have good service which is the only reason why I've given them two stars but unless you really are stuck, I'd pass on trying to eat here.

I'm a fan of Taco Mac - I'm a brewuniversity member and I visit the Dunwoody location quite a bit.  This one is much closer to my house so we decided to check it out.  

The first time we went, it was so crowded we just turned around and walked out.  It was 6:30 on a Thursday.  I'm assuming it was because of free glass night?  The second time, it was about 4 on a Saturday.  We ended up finding seats at the bar but it was still very crowded.  

Beer list is good, but it is good at every taco mac.  Service was just not up to par with what I normally get in Dunwoody.  She asked us almost right away what we wanted when we hadn't seen the list yet.  Then the bartender didn't come back over for at least 20 minutes.  I had to ask her if we could place our order which I hate doing.  The other bartenders completely ignored us.  Its just not the same atmosphere as the other Taco Mac....disappointing.

Interesting concept, generally tasty food, but wayyyyy overpriced.

To start, cocktails were tasty but were on the small side. The "Kirin slushy" was an interesting concept and cool presentation, but pretty disgusting-tasting IMO.

For food, the waiter suggested getting one or two large plates and a few small plates to share, so between three of us we tried a few different dishes. Upon recommendation, we ordered the large plate fried chicken, which was nicely executed but way too expensive for what it was- 4 nicely fried, nicely flavored, boneless chicken thighs (aka one of the cheaper cuts) and a large scoop of just-OK mayo-ed potato salad with a touch of seaweed, for $28. 

Next up was the small plate of corn, which was essentially a tasty coconutty (vegan) version of elote/Spanish street corn, 2 half ears for $~8... fine but not worth the price. The small plate kale salad was OK but again, not worth it for the price (~$10?). Last up was small plate roasted potatoes with ground lamb for ~$15, which was yet again way overpriced, and had some good flavors but weren't incorporated enough IMO (each ingredient- lamb, potatoes, yogurt, spices, pomegranate seeds- felt like it was added to the plate completely seperately, and it was only if you made sure to have each item in the same bite that the dish really came together and popped). 

On the plus side, they have a nice patio, cool interior, and attentive service. But the price point and portion size means I'm not eager to return.

The decor was fun, but the place could use a cleaning - the cushion seats had lots of fur or white hair (or both). I cleaned it up and washed my hands - its hard to eat with hair around food! (Never had that experience before!) The service was cold and aloof. When I went in, I had a 10 min wait and was told to wait outside - the tone and the attitude was off, like I am privileged to eat here. Not to generalize, but I was expecting warmth from such a place (teaches me to judge a book by its cover). I had their special - the pumpkin pancakes - they were great - light and fluffy, and you could tell that the pumpkin was not canned. But 2 medium pumpkin pancakes without sides cost $8.00- (regular cost $4.25). Wow! I wonder what year the NY Times praised their pancakes (as according to the menu). This is one of the sad times when 4 star food quality is overshadowed by lack of friendly/attentive service and cleanliness.

NOT VEGAN FRIENDLY/FOOD ALLERGY FRIENDLY
The restaurant is not food allergy friendly. Bring a snack, it's impossible to get through in under an hour and you will be starving. The "allergen list" has only about half the things they have available and some random things they don't. I bought a salad thinking they'd have a salad dressing that I could eat, and I ended up having to give it away because they had only two dressings and I couldn't eat either (I had to go through the line again and wait for them to find the packaging, and they didn't offer to refund me or replace the salad with something I could eat). I would have been able to avoid that had they had the dressings in the allergen list, or the dressing with the salad bar. Everything has cream in it except the french fries and the chicken breast, vegans beware.
The store is a huge maze. We took three hours to get through it and we were skimming. There are shortcuts, and you can grab little maps, but you have to walk through the entire thing to get to the end, so stopping for one thing could take you over an hour even if you know what you want. Prices are decent, there are some things that are radically expensive and some things that are insanely cheap. It's great small-apartment-living stuff.

I want my $15 back.  Seriously, this place was lame.  Admittedly, I wasnt really sure what to think of the place before I arrived, but I do know that I was expecting better.  If they charged $7.50, then I'd say it's okay, but $15 for what we experienced was just silly.  There were a few cool parts (see below), but overall I'd have to say it's certainly not worth the admission.

    There is a 3-D movie that's a bit hokey, but pretty cool.  Very similar to the 3-D movies at Disney World or Universal in Orlando.  Then there was a short animated film that was SO BAD, I think it's embarrassing.  We were told that it's "new" and seriously, it's SO BAD I'm fully expecting it will be pulled.  
    I got my picture taken with the Coke Polar Bear, which was cool and there are lots of displays of coke art.  The around-the-world soda tasting room was cool (just like the one at Epcot) and filled with sodas ranging from good to disgusting, but it was interesting to try them all.  There are a few rooms packed with the history of Coca-Cola from inception to modern times.  Interesting thing though, while the entire history of the soda is covered from scratch, I did not see any mention of the fact the original Coca-Cola recipe invented by John Pemberton used to contain cocaine, which is a fact!!  For some reason, I suppose Coke doesnt want to advertise that?  Hmmm,,,,, I wonder why?

This attraction felt like it was something Disney would construct to entertain you while you're waiting in line.  When it was over I heard a woman ask, "That's it??" and I think that sums it up nicely.  I waited forty minutes in line for this and it absolutely was not worth it.  After you make your way through the line you're corralled into a room where a talking skull on the wall prepares you for your adventure.  All good so far.  You enter a fairly large room that is themed quite nicely.  There are pirate skeletons, gold doubloons, a wrecked pirate ship, etc.  After seeing that you would think you're about to be impressed.  You're not.  You literally spend the entire time watching a floating skull projected on a screen.  At one point Johnny Depp (who is on another screen) makes an appearance.  JD never leaves that screen and nothing remotely substantial happens.  Animatronic skeletons?  Nope, just projections on the screen.  Fire?  Nope, just projections on the screen.  I could have stayed home and watched a Pirates of Caribbean blu-ray and been more entertained.

Pretty much had a bad experience the second I arrived. 

Parking was 10 dollars. Thats absurd for columbus.

I ordered the margherita pizza, which didn't have enough cheese on it. I think they were just going cheap on the fresh mozz, they put one piece on every slice, instead of covering it from edge to edge. 

While i waited for said pizza, i had to listen to a bunch of screaming children playing in the fountain across from the patio. 

Perhaps sitting inside would have been better, but im still upset about my pizza and the 10 dollars for parking.

The first time I met my friends to eat here, the food was super good, the drinks were very good and strong, and the waiter we had was super nice! The next time I went however, while the food was still good, I got the wrong sides for a meal that I had ordered the first time I went there. I also ordered the mango margarita, but this time it was extremely sweet and it was clear that there was not much tequila in the drink. I kindly asked the waitress (who seemed to have an attitude the whole night) to see if there was a way I could switch out that mango marg for another flavor. As we watched her approach the manager, her body language showed that she was extremely annoyed with having to do this, and it was clear that the manager was also annoyed. She came back to say that I was stuck with the terrible drink and that I couldn't remove it from my order at the least. The manager walked by our table, so my friend kindly asked him why we weren't able to exchange the beverage and his response to us was since there was already alcohol in the beverage he can't take it back. Never have I been told this; if you receive a bad drink you should never be obligated to pay for it. At this point none of us felt the need to make a scene or argue back with the manager so we just said ok and continued on with the rest of our meal. This overall experience was so disappointing to the point that I don't know if I'll come back. Me and my friends are on the younger side, and I feel as though the matare and the waitress took advantage of this. I've also worked in this industry, so I know that this is not the proper protocol. I hope that they resolve this issue for future customers because the food is good.

To being with the meal started off on an odd note, as the server indicated that they could not bring any salsa out, because they had run out and were making some.  This struck our group of four very oddly because it was prime time on a Friday night (10JAN, 7:30PM), but we went ahead and ordered some guacamole instead as we were looking forward to some sort of appetizer/beginning to our meal.  The guacamole arrived and then we were informed that there were no chips either, as they had run out of them too; again, super odd for prime time dining and presumably we were supposed to eat the guac with a spoon?  Not 2 minutes later our server, returned with our beverages and had an accident, dropping water and beer on the table and onto the floor, with the beer bottles breaking and glass shards going everywhere.  The server came back 3 minutes later and cleaned the table up, but 3 of the four people were REALLY wet, most of us looking like we had "accidents" with the front of our pants soaking wet.  The evening did not get better, although apologies were offered, since the manager was not called over to address the service issue, nor was the hundreds of glass shards on the concrete floor cleaned up.  We finally requested an audience with management, who did come over and offer more apologies, but no recovery to the event(s) were in site until we expressed our dissatisfaction.  Ultimately we were offered the guacamole (with no chips, mind you) as compensation for the errors.  We eventually moved to a new table, after asking, and the evening did not get much better as the manager became somewhat snappish with our utter dissatisfaction  As our food arrived later, mind you still no chips nor salsa was ready yet, only two of the four meals were served, and had to wait an additional 5 minutes for the remaining food to arrive at which point the first two meals were getting cold.  Then to make matters worse, the final 2 meals, sizzling fajitas, arrived not sizzling, and the server then accidentally dropped the tortillas on the floor, thus delaying our meal even further.  In the end, accidents occurred, no legitimate service recovery was executed, and the food service/food itself was very disappointing.   Many valuable lessons were learned this evening!!! :)

Disappointing experience for brunch.  The food was actually very good, but the service was not up to par with what Portland has to offer.  After being seated, our hostess never brought menus as she said she would.  Luckily a couple at a different table left after not being served, so we took the menus from their table.  After about 15 minutes without service a waiter arrived and asked if we had ordered drinks yet.  When we indicated we had not, he asked for them without apology.  One of us ordered bottomless mimosas, but don't let the adjective fool you - multiple wait staff walked by without acknowledging our presence or asking if we needed a refill.  Luckily our waiter checked in on us when we were more than halfway done with our meals and agreed to get another refill upon our request.

The food was admittedly very good (we had the Florentine omelet and classic benedict), not to mention we were given complimentary donuts that were very tasty.  Unfortunately the poor service trumped good food, however, and despite being a couple of blocks from where we live we will gladly walk past this restaurant to have a better dining experience elsewhere.

OK it does eventually get me where I'm going, but does it have to be so ugly?  First they took away the low-flying airplanes when they moved the airport.  I miss that!  Best way to wake up an early morning commuter or big rig long hauler with the thrill of impending death!  

Now, they have that massive rock and debris pile right by the upper deck that once was the green, collegiate Concordia.  What is the image we are putting out there for visitors??  Post-apocolyptical??  Welcome to Austin!  Home of the H-Bomb??

What happened to our green city???

First our server Brad was great he was prompt and professional. The problem was our food took 30-40 minutes and the two tables that were seated after us by 10 minutes received their food first. The maui maui sandwich was a bit bland, the cobb salad was great, the fish and chips were good but the fries were cold. The final salad was not prepared as requested and the kitchen tried to say it was and Brad was great in making the issue right.

The manager/owner (tall hairy man at the St. Johns location) is pretty terrible, but everyone else is great and the food and drinks are fine.

Nothing too fantastic about this place, but they offer other milk options other than Soy or Cow and they have a few gluten free options.

Edit: I was contacted by the business owner after leaving my initial review. I found it inappropriate and uncalled for as my review was honest about my experience there. Every other time I had ordered a food or drink there, it took time, but wasn't too long. The review was posted because the owner/manager (it was a tall, older, hairy man) took my order, charged me, made my smoothie (which was the worst tasting smoothie I have ever had) and forgot my food order. 30 minutes later... I got my bagel with cream cheese.

This was over a year ago, so hopefully, for their sake and the communities', they have stepped up their game and stopped allowing him behind the counter. If not, at least there are plenty of other quality coffee shops within a block walking distance with great food and drinks!

I had horrible experience with Indian women vet, she didn't want to see my dog without assistance, then told me to go out because my kid is getting my dog nervous, then she said that my dog is aggressive and she's afraid of her safety and can't continue. I was surprised, I have a very sweet Boston terrier, 3 yo never ever shown aggravation in vet office. When I came in he was in a muzzle, all red, and at the and of it when he started to walk out I saw a blood trace he left behind and they said, oh don't worry we dropped him from the table (because he was so aggressive) and he just broke his nail. 
The doctor we've seen before was awesome and always got along well with my dog, rewording him with a treat after they done.. hope they fire her

This is very over rated. Ordered surf n turf-steak was cooked perfectly but over seasoned and salty. The lobster was over cooked and dry. Very surprised at this after paying soooo much.  The other order was pan seared chicken, over cooked and dry seasoned ok. Ordered asparagus had some sort of citrus sauce, not what we were thinking. The menu is NOT very descriptive. Also ordered Brussels sprout salad and had a Dijon dressing and was NOT listed on menu. The sweet corn pudding was awesome. The service was great.

Again, while visiting universal studios, we decided to catch dinner here. When we arrived, it took about 10 plus minutes for us to be acknowledged or offered some drinks. I went inside to ask for a waitress and then finally our waitress arrived. But once she arrived, she was pretty nice and stayed one top of things. But once again, city walk, the food here was just ok. I ordered spaghetti and meatballs, my other friends ordered fettuccini and lasagna. The only thing that was good was the lasagna. All else was eh. My friends fettuccini was undercooked. My spaghetti noodles were a bit to thick for my liking and the meat sauce was bland. I just expected a little more based on all the good reviews but I just didn't get it. Definitely not coming back here again. I should have ate at the Three Broomsticks instead.

This isn't a very good place. I was the only customer in the whole place when I walked in, and it still took several minutes for me to place my coffee order, because I had to wait for the guy behind the counter to get off the phone. I then proceeded to order several things, only to hear the guy behind the counter say "We're out of that right now." I finally ordered a frappe that took at least six minutes to make. I could have made it better myself at home in my own kitchen. It definitely wasn't worth the $4.55 that I was charged. 

There were a number of people sitting around the store, but none were eating or drinking anything. They all seemed to be known to the guy behind the counter, and were just there to hang out. 

I sat in the coffee shop for about an hour doing work on my laptop, and there wasn't a single customer other than me during that whole time. 

I hate to talk badly about a small business, but this one isn't worth patronizing. 

Consider a different coffee shop.

I've been to this theatre more than a few times with the understanding "You get what you pay for."  The other reviews mention the dilapidated condition of the entire theatre and restrooms.  Those reviews are very accurate... So, know before you go what you're in for...  However, I'm mostly discouraged about their popcorn...  It's clearly not freshly popped at the theatre, it is stale and a huge disappointment...  I'm sure it's the kind of bulk popcorn that comes pre-popped and arrives at the theatre in large bulk plastic bags.  Even pumping in extra "butter" can't improve it...   REMEMBER... CASH ONLY & "You get what you pay for" and you'll be fine.

I'll start out with what I did like, although there's not much to talk about. Decor is nice, the giant window brings in a lot of great lighting, the service is snappy, and I appreciated being able to get a side of avocado with my omelet. 

As for what I disliked, and why I won't be dining here again anytime soon, the list goes on and on. Upon arrival, no hostess greeted us, we were instructed to write down a name on a clipboard and just hang out, with no clue as to how long we'd be waiting. After finally sitting and ordering, my boyfriend's homefries were burnt and so bland we had to drown them in salt and Tabasco. My Popeye's Favorite was borderline inedible, as the spinach was greasy and dripping, the bacon was mostly fat and not flavorful, and the onions were almost entirely missing. Eggs were rubbery and again, not seasoned or flavored with anything, and the cheese blend promised was mostly absent too. My boyfriend ordered extra mushrooms with his ham and cheese omelet, and the mushrooms managed to be sparse and mostly raw. 

I had heard good things from friends about this place, but I won't be passing on that recommendation. Very bland, poorly cooked food, with a disappointing front of house.

I was going to leave 1 star but since the management took care of the sloppy service at the end, I am leaving 2. I have been getting my car washed here several times and it's been an ok service like at any other automated wash services. Basic car wash includes vacuum but don't expect a "vacuumed" car:). You would need to pay extra for real vacuum service. About 6 months ago I gave it a try for their best wax service as well, paid around $100. Job was done well, I was a happy customer! Today I decided to return for another best wax service expecting same quality (over $100 service). Well, this time it was obviously a sloppy job, spots were missed on trunk, hood, roof etc. Detailer, who I tipped generously ahead of time ( my fault ), did not apologize but mumbled that my car needed clay treatment to get it completely clean. I explained and showed him how I was able to clean the missed spots with my fingertips and made him understand that I was aware about clay treatments and when it is needed and in this case it was just a sloppy wax job. Detailer then disappeared and his supervisor showed up. We went over the missed spots again. He explained they are not able to remove all? :) I demonstrated once more how easily it was coming off clean with just slight touch and asked how come some areas of the car are clean and some not. After-all, I paid for their premium wax treatment. Supervisor did not seem to believe I had purchased their premium service  until I showed the receipt. There was no apology, just a quick reply: ok, we'll get it fixed within 2 minutes. About an hour later my car was re-finished and looked like brand new without clay treatment:) 
I doubt I will go back for premium services. I just don't feel like spending all day at the car wash justifying why I should receive the service I had paid for and especially do not appreciate being up-sold unnecessary services if there is no need. My suggestion to management: QA your services and be aware what service was purchased before handing back the car to their owners. I bet your ratings will start improving then.

I grew up on the border, and I just can't get my head around New England's Mexican food. The stuff isn't even close for the most part, so I'm either cooking it or on the lookout for a new place. Enter El Sarape. One of the nice things about Mexican is that it's cheap, and it is cheap here at lunch time, just not at dinner. Oh, and expect a wait. Apparently townies can't get enough bland Mexican food. My wife and I came out down $45 (minus tip and no alcohol) for two entrees and a few sodas. I was baffled. Not worth the wait or the cash at dinner time. I mean, their lunch prices seem fair if you've got the tastebuds of a 5 year old, so by all means, hit 'em up.

My buddy wanted to try this new restaurant and asked me to join him for lunch.  I love cajun/creole cuisine and was expecting that the food would be good.   Unfortunately, the burgers we ordered were not good  We both ordered our burgers medium well and they came out really well done to the point of being dry with not much seasoning. Plus the burgers were expensive (gourmet burger prices). Some of the other non burger dishes that we saw other diners eating looked good; so there is a good chance that the other dishes on the menu may have been better.  The service was good though.

My husband and I were pretty disappointed when we went last week. We sat at the bar, and were pretty much ignored by Brennan the entire time we were there. Reading the menu was not entirely exciting, so I asked Brennan what his favorites were, explicitly saying "no bowls". He recommended the fisherman stew (bowl), the pasta (bowl), and the bisque (bowl?). We ordered the tuna poke, and the peppers to start (a Brennan recommendation). Both were pretty flavorless. Our cocktails were delicious, once emptied Brennan continued to ignore us. We were all set to spend the evening eating and drinking, but instead we paid up and left. We went to an establishment a few yards away, where we were catered to and ate a delicious meal. We have been (and will continue to be ) loyal patrons, but this was not the experience expected from a Cameron Mitchell Restaurant. I will definitely give it another try.

The staff overall was very nice and helpful. They helped me pick out some new products. Victoria is very nice and had a very helpful idea about how to blend my hair as it is growing out. She added color to the bottom and partial highlights on top. I do have to say that my bangs ended up too short and that can ruin the joyous feeling of a new haircut and color, especially when I have a friend visiting in a couple days. Now I am just self concious about it and it is runing my week. They were first cut mid-brow and I said slightly shorter. the bangs should be touching the top of the eyebrow. They were about 1/4-1/2 inch above that. They don't even touch the eybrow when wet. You really don't need me to tell you what too short is if you are a professional. I said everything was ok at the time because it takes time to really get home and see the difference I think. So that is my fault. At first it always looks different so it is like, ok. The more I look at it the more it upsets me at this point. They are so clearly too short. Also wish the blonde highlights were more visible. I came in primarily for highlights so there should have been more and not so thin. Now I may have to add more somewhere else and will have to try to weigh my bangs down as much as possible. The rest of the haircut was good but messing up the bangs ruins the entire thing.

If you are planning a baby or bridal shower at this restaurant I would not recommend it.  I could never talk to them on the phone so no communication. 3 days before the shower after I had called in the final count they told me that I could not have 15 people only 12! They finally added a table so we could have our 15 quests. When we arrived at the restaurant at the time reserved the table had dirty dishes on it. We had to wait 1/2 for the table to get ready and I had to help set the table as only 1 person was assigned. In the same room another shower of 18 was scheduled 30 minutes later. I ended up having to be the waitress. I had to take orders and clearing the table.  Unfortunately they make you pay in advance so they don't care what service you get. Food was very good but a TERRIBLE place for a shower.

I was very disappointed in this location of Suzi's. Their South Lamar restaurant (which is now closed...temporarily?) is closer to my downtown office, so I usually go there. The lunch specials are always tasty, with fresh vegetables and good cuts of meat. I tried the Anderson Lane location recently and was very, very disappointed. The food was heavy on the oil, the vegetables were limp and overcooked, and the meal was just all-around unappetizing. Too bad they can't live up to the sister restaurant's performance. I doubt I'll be back...there are many other (better) Asian/Chinese joints in town!

I came here for a nice dinner to celebrate a small event. Our dinner ended up taking three plus hours. Im not really sure on what happened. They also tried to sit up in the "front" of the house. On such a beautiful summer day with the patio full I asked to sit at the back and there was a far nicer room that had one six person party seated although the back room slowly did fill up I felt as if we would have been snubbed. By the end of our meal many people had come and apologized but I didn't want to cause a scene. They offered us free dessert and  brought us something straight from the freezer and still completely frozen. When I asked what in the world was going on they told me they were still new and appreciated the feedback that the dessert was frozen!? Still new after they had finished a whole season. They also were not new at running a credit card for a dinner well over $150. I thought it was pretty disgraceful imo. I only give them the extra star because the food was delicious. It was everything else that was horrible.

I may give this place another try sooner but the other reviews are pretty spot on with the zero presence of good service. I have to holler at the bar tender to get a drink. That's not normal when there's less than 15 people inside the establishment. 

Miss Lady server acts like she could not be bothered and can't even make an eye contact. That's the thing when you know this place is a bit off. Too bad, it is local and they serve good beers. 

Their Vanilla Porter is amazing. The food is bar food. Service? I bet if you train bums on the street to serve, they can do a better job than who's employed inside.

I am not one to usually leave a comment when it's like smedium, usually only if the service was garbage or the food horrific. I can say that is neither the case here. Food was meh... My son who loves sugary goodness was blah about his french toast and my pancakes resembled maybe a fast food consistency, bland and dense, not light and fluffy. Eggs were poached well but in a puddle of water because it wasn't dried. Like that's cooking 101. Bacon was good for what wasn't probably farm to table but I didn't ask. Over-all food experience C-

What made this trip interesting was the server. Older 50's and probably very nice. Unfortunately that was not my experience. She was pushy with us. Asked us 4 times within the first 2 minutes if we were ready to order to the point where I had to assertively say no. Then she came back when my son went to the bathroom and asked again. Umm, did she notice the table was missing one of the two people and probably not the best time to take an order? I observed her with other tables and it was like night and day. Appropriately checked in, was gracious, made suggestions, and didn't seem to rush them out the door. Odd to say the least... I have assumptions but not going to assume the worst. 

I would say it's worth the extra drive into Portland where culinary is artful, delicious, and when a hipster server is rude you know it's just because they are misunderstood.

Went here with some of my friends. Had drinks to begin with and appetizers. It did take awhile but they seemed to be getting quite busy. It took more than 45 mins for the food to come out after we ordered and the food wasn't that great. There was really no seasoning and I feel like I had to dump a lot of tabasco for me to really taste something. I got a west side boil with house sauce spicy. It was just spicy. We then wanted to order more and someone that wasn't our waiter said they don't have side fries (even though it's clearly on the menu). We then waved down the waitress and said she could put in that order for us. It was just an odd experience. For what I paid, it wasn't worth it.

I've been to Blackfinn a couple of times, first for a happy hour, second on Wednesday evening to sip some wine with a couple of friends.  The Wined up Wedensday is a good deal.  However, get ready if you sit inside.  IT IS LOUD!  To talk with your friends you basically spend a lot of time yelling.  The music is pumped up like a dance club.  Also, at both happy hour and wined up wedensday we sat at the bar, we had to wave and flag down the bartenders.   Not the greatest service.  The food is typical chain restaurant grub with a menu the size of a novel, and the food comes out resonably fast.  If we go a next time I go, I'll give the patio a shot.

Food is pretty good but the service and attitude of the staff is really poor.  The hostess  made us feel as though we were inconveniencing her by asking about the upstairs vs downstairs.  We opted for seating up stairs and began "the wait".  We had to go to the bar ourselves and order drinks as no server ever came over to assist us. We kept thinking this must just be an off night and tried to enjoy time with our group. Once we were seated, the service didn't improve.  Our server was obviously stressed with too many tables or maybe just poorly trained. Food was OK but the overall experience poor.  After talking with other friends, I learned they too had experienced either bad service and or mediocre food at this restaurant.  Fun location to people watch but the poor service and so so food make it not worth the effort. Lots of better options in Austin!

Bad night for service. We waited over an hour for appetizers and the nice young waiter was clueless about the food and the wine menu.  This was a shame because the restaurant has a great cellar that is not well represented but the wait staff. We had brought guests and were embarrassed by the wait as hosts.  The staff was good willed but inexperienced even though the restaurant was not full.  Maybe the problem was in the kitchen.  Interesting that others had a problem with service.  It is hard to enjoy the food when it come an hour late.

I went to this restaurant with my wife the day before Thanksgiving. When we entered, a lady usher directed us to a table attached to the wall with both the chairs facing out of the window - killing any hope of a romantic dinner. I requested to be seated on any other table where we could face each other. I was rudely informed that since we were only two and since most tables could host four or more, she couldn't help us. Shocking, especially because the place was empty! Anyway, the young owner/manager who saw what was happening rescued the night and rearranged a table for us. Plus two stars for him. Alas, I can't give any stars for the food. We ordered fried calamari, which wasn't very good, slightly rubbery tasting. I went for the baked cod, which was done very well, but was utterly bland since the gravy separated from it very easily. My wife ordered a chicken marsala which she didn't find too bad but was nothing to write home about either. Overall, our bill was 80 (including tip) which I would consider expensive but wouldn't mind occasionally if the food is good. Unfortunately, the food here tasted average.

The only reason I'm giving this 2 stars is because of my manicure/pedicure experience. 

The first time I ever went here I went to get a haircut. The guy I got paired with was a total jerk. He thought he was hot shit and did not do one thing to my hair I asked for. Just needed a cut and layers with a side bang. Nothing too out of the ordinary. He said he would do it but then kept saying "this will look better" so I trusted him since he was cutting a lot and my friend had said this place was great and I welcomed a little change. The hair cut took FOREVER and my hair ended up looking almost identical to how I had come in. Then it ended up costing way more than what I got back. The guy (I wish I could remember his name) was rude the whole time and I refuse to ever go back there for a haircut.

I only ever went back there to get my nails done with my friend. They women were nice and good. It was a little expensive for a mani/pedi, but not bad. I just go to a place on Beacon now that's a little cheaper and closer to home.

I called Maquillage about my awful experience and they got me in right away to fix it.  I was very happy with this service.  I, again, felt confidence when I left.

Today, I washed off the bronzer & the issues on my legs persisted.  My wrist does look better.  I am attempting a quick fix with a mild self apply foam.  

Anyway, I upgraded from one to two stars because of the customer service.  It is unlikely that I will cash in my other groupon.

My rating went from a 5 to a 2 for one reason. The mall has made a move to make all parking anywhere close to the mall pay only. $10.00 just to park or you can opt for $15.00 valet. When we were there last week 80% of the pay parking was empty and we had to walk right past it from the "remote" parking for those unwilling to fork over the cash. My wife and I are seniors and went often to buy things for family members. I refuse to pay for reasonable parking at a mall that is supposedly a place to save money. We won't be back until they decide to restore the majority of close parking to first come first served and remove the fees. Too bad, it was a nice mall and I'm not sure how we'll know if they change back.

If you're looking for a lackluster meal then this is the place for you. There was no hostess at the desk when we walked in. The hostess was cleaning tables. They were out of the wine I ordered, and the Sprite my husband ordered was carbonated water with no syrup. The waitress was polite but not overly friendly, and the whole staff seemed unhappy at being at work today. 

Food wise it was good food except my husband's chicken parm was plain sautéed chicken covered in cheese. My lobster ravioli and the kid's fettuccini were good, as was the calamari. We were not offered dessert, just boxes and the check. 

Overall I doubt we will be returning to that location again.

When my car broke down, the husband and I needed to rent a second vehicle. We picked this Enterprise because it was conveniently located halfway between our house and my office. 

We pulled in about five minutes after they had opened, to a lot that only had 4 vehicles - a compact car, a truck, a van and a Cadiallac. Now, we had reserved a mid-size car... but ok. Whatever. We'll take the compact. 

But... the person ahead of us in line had ALSO reserved a mid-sized and also didn't want to drive a large and gas-guzzling truck or van. How do you only have 4 cars available to rent, none of which are what your earliest pick-ups reserved, and accept the reservations? The employee even said that they weren't expecting any cars to be returned for several hours, so it's not like someone else was just tardy with their drop-off.

So the employee said he would give us the Cadillac for only $10 extra a day. And then quoted us like $340 for 2.5 days of driving it. So then we had to peel back all these extra things he had added on without asking to try to be able to afford to rent a damn car to drive to work and back for 2.5 days. Eventually the other customer decided he wanted the truck and we got the compact - which, for 1.5 days rental WITHOUT the crazy insurance to be driven a total of 52 miles was still $130, which is stupid. 

As we were leaving, 5 more people were arriving to pick up vehicles they had rented, and no new rental vehicles had been dropped off.

the only times i'm really ever in here is to go to the bikram's studio... i've explored it a tiny bit and i know it has a fruits & produce market, a clothing store (actually it might not even be there anymore because the last time i visited it, it was having a closing sale), a safeway, and a parking lot. it's a tiny "mall" (i don't know if you could even call it that) and there's not much to it. it's cute i guess.

Stop by this place after the Orlando gay parade. We sat in a table for 5 to be able to see outside and the server did not want to take care of us because we were only 2 and a baby. They were too busy dancing outside and seem to care less about their customers. We have to waive at a few servers to get a menu and server. Finally after 15 minutes we got a server. She was good though. We ordered immediately because we were hungry and we knew dishes will took a while. So we went simple and we ordered their ribs. They arrived very fast. They were good but not great. BBQ sauce was decent. Their potato salad was ok. Nothing to crave for just decent fast food. One of our drinks were spilled and got replaced but got charged for it.We got full immediately I guess it was too much carbs at once. This is not a place a will go on a regular basis but maybe to grab something quick if I am ever in the area.

I've held off on reviewing this place for a while, but feel like I need to write something up now. I came here for an evening dinner date, and had a fairly mediocre time. 

During my meal, I ordered a salad, fillet, and a baked potato. 

The salad was good, but nothing to write home about. Quality ingredients, but nothing incredible. The steak was not cooked well. The outside had been burnt, and was hard when it arrived. Powering through that, the inside was cooked to medium as indicated, but I still felt like the taste was a bit off. The potato was bang on average, and trust me, I know my potatoes. Fairly small in size, and definitely skimpy on the toppings. 

Additionally, our service was relatively slow and inattentive - there were not a lot of people eating there at like 6:30 PM on a weekday, yet we were stuck waiting for refills on a couple occasions. This is unacceptable at a place that charges $50 for a steak. 

If I'm being completely honest, I would much rather go to Texas Roadhouse or Longhorn for my steak dining experience in Columbus, because I can get 3 BETTER meals for the same cost as the one I had here. 

And in saying that, I do not discredit these fancier steakhouses. I have been fortunate enough to be able to travel to Chicago for work for about a year. While there, I've eaten at places like Chicago Cut, RPM, Benny's, Chicago Chop, Remingtons, as well as a couple others. In all of those places, I paid upwards of $100 for my meal, but left feeling like I had just eaten one of the best meals of my life. 

I spent $75+ at Hyde Park and felt that I would have enjoyed my meal and had better service at a chain steakhouse that shows ads on tv. That is not okay.

This restaurant took over space previously owned by a Japanese restaurant. I was excited to see a unique restaurant to open so close to my house. Inside the restaurant looks pretty nice and it's quite spacious(even though from the outside it looks very small). 

I ordered Jerk Chicken wings and Goat Curry to go. I felt the flavours were bland, It wasn't seasoned well. The wings were ok after I added a bit of salt to it. Still wasn't good enough! The curry was very disappointing. This dish lacked both basic seasonings like salt and depth of flavour. I feel that this restaurant needs to make major improvements to make their dishes more flavorful.

No chance man.  The lamb was way over cooked, under seasoned and the presentation was dreadful.  The asparagus wasn't even prepped or cooked correctly.  It was soggy and the white dried out part was still on.

I'm awful at cooking (hence why I eat out a lot) but I do know how to prep asparagus.  The bartender claimed the cook had all these accolades.  But who serves well done lamb and dirty asparagus on a plate that looked like a reject from first round of masterchef.  This doesn't seem like just having a bad night.

I'm sure they will blame the Rainey st area when this restaurant goes under, but it will be the food.

I knew the place was cheap and I also know there are other places that I have stayed at for the same price and didn't have any issues with it. But this place is broken down. We got 2 rooms the first room the tv didn't work the phone didn't work and there was no batteries in the remote. Second room the tv didn't work, the alarm clock stopped working in the middle of the night the toilet didn't flush. I had to call down 2 times to get theses issues looked at. Once they looked at it the tv worked but then the remote didn't. After being in the park all day I didn't want to get up to change the channel! Also the tv were from the 1980. The room smelled like mildew! I will never go back!!

Okay...maybe I've been spoiled as a native New Yorker, but these "xiao long bao"s were terrible! The amount of tears I shed for their mediocrity far surpassed the amount of soup in these so-called soup dumplings. They didn't even give us spoons to eat the dumplings with. Which was fine because there was so little soup. They tasted like frozen soup dumplings.

Other dishes we got included the scallion beef and the crispy tofu. Boston, what are your standards for Chinese food?! The scallion beef was, I admit, fairly good but you can make this at home if you have soy sauce and scallions. Crispy tofu looked like the tofu version of chicken fingers with sweet and sour sauce. Also, the sauce turns pink after you leave your leftovers in the fridge for a day. My roommate tried to explain the chemistry of it to me but I was too grossed out by the fuzzy pepto-bismol looking back at me.

One tip, they do take credit/debit but you get a discount (5%, I think) if you pay with cash and your bill is over $25 dollars.

I really tried to give these guys a little time before I went (in to get there stuff together, but it still hasn't happened, yet).  At least they've brought Pearl district snobbery to the East Side!  The pretention was very thick as soon as we arrived.  Party of 4, with reservations, still a half an hour wait, only to get sat next to the kitchen.  Which I was cool with, but my friends not so much; I like to get to see a little action!  However, we waited for everything.  It was fairly painful.   Bottle wine...15 minutes, take our order...another 15 minutes, first course...20 minutes, next bottle of wine...another 15 minutes, and then the creme de la creme, main courses... a full 63 minutes (I timed it from when our appetizer plates were removed.).  The place is nicely put together and the food itself was pretty good, but I can cook up a storm at home in the time they took.  I mean really, three and a half hours from our reservation time to have dinner, please!  This is exactly why you don't give big accolades to a restaurant until they have proven they can deserve them.  Willamette Week should be ashamed.  I wish these guys luck, because they have a lot of potential, but they have to get it down.  And they certainly haven't yet.

I spent $70 for a spa pedi and a french manicure here. I greatly enjoyed the atmosphere and we were served promptly and pretty well, but the mani/pedi results left something to be desired. I asked for rounded nails left even on each hand, but she cut them real short and left them too square.  The polish started peeling off within 24 hours, and the french manicure wasn't particularly good in the first place. For the price, I expect to get exactly what I want and to have it last. If you're looking for a nice spa experience and don't care about the polish lasting, this is a great place. They have other services including hair, massage, facials and such, and if I didn't mind spending a lot of money, I'd go back.

This has got to be one of Panera' worst locations.  But to their credit, they've gotten much much better since the Windermere-location manager joined the team.  Unfortunately, he cannot be there all the time.  

I typically frequent this location when I visit the area in the evening before/after shopping or on weekends for the past 4 years.  In the morning the service is excellent, but don't go after 6:00 p.m.  Things get pretty nasty and shabby. 

I was very sick and waiting for my appointment at the Centra Care.  I needed to eat so I ordered a cup of soup and salad.  Who can ruin salad?  If I wanted to eat out of the garbage, I would have gone to McDs.  

Bad service, old food, smoker employees, smokers on the patio, and dirty restaurant.  There are years of dust on those self-serve clear drink dispensers.

Don't believe me?  Here's a photo.

We used to frequent this Pub almost daily when we lived across the street and it was great.

But, wow have things changed!

Dropped in there tonight around 6:30pm for some dinner and it wasn't really busy as it used to be.

The greeter could not be less enthused to seat us.

Our waitress took the "Meh" down to a new low; we asked ourselves, "who did we piss off"?

She begrudgingly took our orders, appie and mains.

The mains came out half way through the appie so our table was loaded up and the mains were cooling as we rushed to finish the appies.

No chit chat, no "hows your evening"  the waitress could not be less engaged if she tried.  Everything was almost tossed onto the table with nothing more than a grunt.

The food was "meh" to match the attitudes of the staff. In fact I think the "stir-fry "special" they tossed down in front of us was a mish mash of leftovers from the day before...it certainly tasted like it was!

When we paid the bill and yes I tipped a very undeserved 15%, nothing from her at all.

Needless to say, we won't be back and I urge anyone to avoid it and try Glowbal around the corner.

i LOVE the hotel. So many great things. The History, the space we had, and more! So why only 2 stars?  Well - the service let us down HUGE

So I recently got married, and we wanted a hotel that was nice, had space for my wife and her bridal party to get ready, and also would be good for pictures. Our reception was in Boston, and after looking at the Omni Parker House, and others, we decided we wanted to look for something classic, great for pictures, affordable, and not generic (example,w e could get a suite chain in quincy, but its generic)

WE booked a room block for guests (with 11 guests staying for 1-3 nights), booked a room for myself for the night before, and then also the Garden Suite for two nights (her, and then us the second). 
The suite was amazing (and at the cost, it should be). 1200+ square feet, living area, full kitchen, dining area, and a 600 SF balcony outside. it was PERFECT. All the room for her to get ready, plenty of room for guests to stop in, a fabulous outdoor space, and perfect for pictures.
My room was as expected. Small, since an old hotel, but up to date, clean, and well appointed. no complaints on it at all.

So where did we get let down

1. Housekeeping. When we checked into the hotel, the balcony had not been cleaned, with empty beer cans and cigarette butts abound. We called and asked them to clean when we were at the rehearsal dinner. They didnt.
We asked them to come twic eon Sunday, even if a cost to us, so it could be clean for pictures and then after. They came at 7am, cleaned for pictures, perfect. didnt come again
Despite several requests to several people, it just didnt get done. Although to the hotels credit, they did refund my prt of the room cost since it had not been cleaned as needed.
2. AS with a lot of weddings, we had gift boxes for our guests. Snacks, aspirin, Bottled water, champagne,etc. We arranged before with the hotel, who advised us it would be $2.50 each box to deliver. annoying, but in the big scheme of things, it was fine. We brought everything in, reviews. Good to go
right?
Well, 2 boxes got delivered to the wrong rooms. Two guests did not get them the first night. then the four guests arriving the second night, didnt get them at all. Despite several conversations with the manager, they disappeared. they said they were delivered. said our guests must be mistaken. said they didnt have them
THEN, the next day, after everyone checked out. THEY FOUND THEM! apparently, tucked away in teh bell closet.
well, great. not these boxes we made for guests, spending $40+ each on, didnt go to the guests.
The manager, Jeffrey, offered to ship them to the guests. I provided the address. and good to go. Better late then never, right? well, no
All the guests got the boxes. destroyed (I am guessing they got destroyed and crushed in the bell closet). All were missing items. (funny enough, teh same items missing from all four boxes - Bottled waters and homemade granola!). Now,w e know all boxes had them, so how was the same stuff missing from ALL the boxes!
To the hotels credit, they did ship (although incomplete), and did not charge me the $2.50 per box room delivery (which is good, since some went to the wrong rooms or not at all!)

Why am I posting this all now when they have tried to help? Well, three days later after emailing FIVE people there, including the group even coordinator, and the manager that helped us, about the missing items, and such, I have not heard back from ANYONE

I love the hotel. I really do. The suite was amazing. teh decor, and common spaces great. I love the history, location, and more!

But with such bad service, when spending SO MUCH money, how can I recommend it or go back?!

I wish I could give this place 2.5 stars because that's really what it was: average. I had read that it was supposed to be trendy but have to disagree. The food was very basic; more plain "American" than "American new". The place was also very loud so I could barely speak to the two people I was there with.
What upgraded the place from bad to average was that service was quick, we were seated immediately, the staff was very nice, and the décor was different.

CVS in Stoughton is interesting. More and more of the CVS stores in the area are laid out in the same way. The Stoughton location is different and has an odd layout, and some of the signage throughout the store isn't exactly correct. Additionally, prices are always higher than Walgreens and other stores like Stop&Shop and Shaw's (both a minute (or less) away). Selection is limited and staff aren't ever too friendly. Not a good pharmacy.... Major work needs to be done to flip around this store to be one of the better. 2 stars.

Today I went to Golf Galaxy to get my irons re gripped because I just got a new set of irons and the grips that were on there I did not like. (I did not purchase the irons at Golf Galaxy) When I asked to get the clubs regripped after I bought the grips which was over $100 they said I would have to leave my club a there for about 4 days because there so many orders placed already. I was a little confused about this because I had already been there for almost half an hour and saw no one working on regripping clubs. But I didn't mind too much because I understand there were already a lot of orders ahead of me so I couldn't control that, so I just bought my own regripping tools at the store which was about another $30. After that I asked a worker if I could hit on the TrackMan because I just bought new irons so I wanted to get my distances, at first they weren't really sure, so I said I would pay for the hitting bay on TrackMan because I understand that they charge to hit on those bays. He then said actually you can just hit on it, it's a slow night so don't worry about it. I really appreciated that so I started hitting on the TrackMan. After about 5 minutes of hitting, another worker (could have been the manager) that I have not talked to yet asked what I was doing, so I explained. He then said I couldn't do what I was doing and I told him someone gave me permission to. He then said that this is a retail store, you can't just come in here and use us for a range (with attitude). I then didn't really know what to say because I literally offered to pay because I understood that they didn't want people using the store for a range. He eventually said it was fine because it was a slow night and there were no other customers in the store. He still didn't seem very happy about it and had a lot of attitude, and made me feel very uncomfortable/unwelcome. I hit for just 2 more mins because I could sense this dude was frustrated about this so I got my stuff and left. 
I was pleased when I first got there but then it switched to making me feel very unwelcome. I wish the workers were on the same page. I left very frustrated because I already bought multiple things there and even offered to pay for the bay, which eventually ended up with them acting like I was trying to use the store.

I was visiting a friend in the area and we decided to try Bamboo Nails & Spa. I was displeased with my service; I'm only giving 2 stars because the young man (didn't catch his name) who assisted us was friendly and welcoming.  My technician said nothing to me (save for "wash your hands") and started on my nails without verifying what I was looking for... I had to stop her from doing something I didn't want; she also walked off without a single word to work on the next customer... no "everything look okay, etc." My friend had a technician who was friendly but insistent on her receiving a gel manicure, his saving grace was he fixed my nails after I accidentally bumped them... seeing as my technician was no where in sight. Also, my nails had a ridiculous amount of paint on them (coated 4/5times.. I lost track), in fact as I'm sitting here now 5hrs later they're almost dry.... I'll be taking them off tomorrow at the hotel spa. For the price it was what I expected.  I'm a seasoned nail "goer," as I go every 2 weeks, friendliness of the two employees was great... they're service not so much.

Being from Southern California and going to John's out there vs. here was a big difference. In CA there are multitudes of people, a long line to get in, hard to find a place to sit and crowded areas where it's hard to get through. But there is a wide variety of choices and bins are constantly changed, so the food is fresh. Here, there was no line, seating was readily available and it was great because you could actually walk without bumping into someone. But, food choices were limited, food was not fresh and seems like it had been sitting for a while and items ran out and were not re-stocked quickly. We will most likely not be returning, as none of us found the food appealing. If it's not one thing, it's another.

Got a Groupon and went today for around 2pm and that place was empty. First bad sign among many, next we ordered: two one meat plate and two sides. I got pork ribs, potato salad and pinto beans, boyfriend got turkey, spicy potatoes and mac & cheese. 

My plate: just three barely cooked pork ribs, and barely any meat, not even with the fork it will come off the bone...yeah that bad; potato salad was decent and beans tasted just right out of the can.

Boyfriend's plate: about and ounce of turkey that was so-so, mac & cheese was VERY dry and bland, forget the spicy potatoes, besides the yucky look they had also a yucky taste....didn't even touch them after trying one. 

Nope, not coming back to this place again. Owners were friendly but definitely not real worth nor delicious BBQ place for the prices. I personally would not recommend it to any of my friends. :(

P.S. The way the put the bread out for people to serve themselves is just nasty. Bread is IN the plastic bags so anyone that didn't wash their hands before getting in that place can stick their hands in it and grab their bread or...just at the last minute change their minds and just leave their germs!

Called Wednesday to try to get someone out then, but due to the hot weather, Empire was unable to get anyone out that day, so we were told Thursday between 12 and 4. Around 3:30 they had still not arrived, so I called and was told it would be 1 to 1 1/2 hours. Around 5:30 the weather had gotten bad with thunderstorms, so the technician decided not to go, and we were bumped to first thing Friday morning.
When I talked to Empire on Thursday afternoon, I requested that because my wife was at work and needed to not be involved in trying to work things out, to please make me the contact, and I gave my phone number. However, my wife called me from work early this morning to say that Empire had continued to call her, apparently ignoring my request.
I called and asked to speak to someone about the situation because I didn't feel I would be able to give them a high rating, including very positive comments, like I did on several previous visits.
The owner, Martin Hoover, called me several hours later. After listening to me, he asked what could be done to help out. I replied that some type of discount on the bill would be greatly appreciated. He replied that he wouldn't do that because he felt Empire had done everything they should in a timely and responsive way.
The technician was not there long, having found corroded batteries in the thermostat. The corrosion could have been cleaned out with soda water or vinegar and fresh batteries installed, and everything would have been fine, but he elected to replace a perfectly good thermostat with a new $178 one.
