The economy is still bad, and everyone is trying to survive these days, but I won't be able to partner with Empire again because they have apparently forgotten how important dedicated and satisfied long-term customers are.

Had a work  lunch takeaway from here and frankly it was just horrid. Definitely not a big fan of their flatbreads, which is what unfortunately work ordered for us. I took the vegetarian flatbread and it ate so heavy and I felt so stodgy afterwards. I wish there had been more grilled vegetables and rather than the weird-tasting plastic cheese they used, I wish there had been some fresh feta instead. What made it worse was a funky oily aftertaste left in my mouth after I finished eating the flatbread. My salad box also contained two (yes, only two!) pieces of tomato and an inordinate amount of raw onion (I did mention I was at a work lunch meeting right?). Anyway left more than 2/3 of my lunch in its box and was hungry for the rest of the afternoon. Not the greatest experience. 

Note: #385 of Yelp 100 challenge for 2016

Some friends of mine and I were treated by this company during their training day, so I don't want to complain about kindness and hospitality!  The staff was very nice and eager. I am not really sure what the difference is between Tex Mex and other mexican food is-  with that said, I found the food to be very bland and unappealing. I only ate about 1/4 of my spinach enchilladas- they had no flavor. My preference for chips (thin white style) and cheese dip (white) was not what they offer here, so it could be that this restaurant is not for me. The atmosphere is lovely and they have a patio- I only live two blocks from this location so I was hoping it would be a great addition to the  neigborhood, but I will have to pass in the future. Thanks for having us in for lunch though!

I am only able to give this a 2 rating due to the terrible service and lack of flavor in the food. If this was to be reviewed based on ambiance it would get a 5 Star! I was excited to try this place out based on my husbands friend review. If you plan on eating inside be prepared bc it is very loud! We were asked if we wanted a table outside bc music was about to play and of course it was a gorgeous cool night so we jumped at the chance! The ambiance outside was amazing, musician was terrific! If it's a cool night I highly recommend only sitting outside! Now for the food, my husband got the prime rib which was actually very tender. It came with veggies that I think might have been microwaved? I got the chicken franchese bc every Italian restaurant I have to always try it! The portion was huge. This meal could have been split bc it also came with a salad as did all the dishes. The appearance was perfect so I assumed the flavor would be amazing...man was I disappointed, the angel hair was mush, zero flavor at all. I definitely do not recommend getting this dish. I will say the chicken was so moist! But it lacked the butter lemon flavor that it is supposed to have, it's as if it was a water sauce...so idk if they had an off night but it wasn't good. The side salad however was great! Our server was slow, unresponsive, took forever to bring us our check or even come back for asking for dessert. I will go back bc of the ambiance but I would try a different dish. I feel they need another shot to make up for this time and I saw a surf and turf that looked amazing so hopefully that dish tastes as good as it looks...but you would think for Italian that would be the food to get.

Alrighty, let's start with the service: I came RIGHT at 8pm for oyster sunday so they were pretty packed, so I don't blame em for being pretty slow.. I mean, for $1 oysters how can I complain? The waitress brought over our own personal carafe of water.. i LOVE when places do that! It took a while for us to get the waitress's attention after that but oh well, they were busy.

My brother and I decided to start off with a dozen oysters each (http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=h5UrFxN1bejk5oiRL3LWsw&select=Sa7jYg00NTIu3u6Dm5GdmQ), then proceed our way day the asian-fusion inspired menu. They serve their oysters a little bit differently here.. they don't give you cocktail sauce (after all, it IS an asian-fusion restaurant).. instead they gave you this sauce which to me, tasted like a vietnamese fish sauce-based migonette (nuoc
 mam). In my opinion, a little too overpowering for the oysters..

Now the bad part. the oysters my brother and i were eating tasted a little off... it didn't necessarily taste BAD, but it didnt taste so fresh.. we thought it could have been the type of oyster.. but after finishing our dozen oysters, we didn't feel so good.. We decided to opt out on trying the rest of the menu and GOOD THING we did. A few hours later we both started throwing up. Now I know once in a while a restaurant can't help but get a bad oyster, but what are the chances that BOTH of us got bad oysters? I'm hoping it was a very rare thing and that their other customers felt fine, but i'm a little hesitant to try myers and chang again. Had only ONE of us gotten food poisoning, i'd for sure be down to try again, but the fact that we BOTH got it makes me a little uneasy..

I know it's not completely their fault, so I'll give 2 stars and maybeee in time I'll write an update!

I really wanted to try the blowout bar today so booked an appointment online. It was fast and easy. Friendly people greeted me and my stylist was nice . I didn't get the sense she was very confident in her ability and I feel like she struggled a little with the blowout. The back of my hair looked great and the front not so much so I fixed it when I got home. I don't think the stylist are dressed professionally at all and I really did not see one person walk out of there with hair that wowed me. If they are charging top dollar then the skills and presentation should match that also. I gave 2 stars mostly because the scalp massage was pretty great. Next time I need a blowout I will just visit the nearest great clips for half the price and a better result.

The all you can eat is a great deal if you can eat that much food and aren't a foodie. They also do not offer a child price, and I am not paying $21 for my 8 year old peanut niece to eat a roll or two (if I'm lucky) of sushi!!! None of the dishes that we tried were memorable.The service left an incredibly sour taste in my mouth and it's why we will never go back. The waitress was rude and inattentive. At the end of the meal we were also told that they charge you for uneaten food, but he'd let us pass this time! So I am very socially conscious and understand they want to limit waste, but the rolls that were left weren't appetizing AND if you won't let me wrap it to go then piss off!!! And also if that's your policy then have it posted on the menu and or have the wait staff inform you at time of ordering. So I guess thanks for not trying to charge us twice for food?? The only reason I gave it 2 stars instead of 1 is that the male wait staff that checked on us towards the end were polite..

I think that I have written about Neptune Oyster previously and perhaps more glowingly.  I debated between 2 or 3 stars as my experience this last time was less than stellar - but I decided that "I've experienced better" sums up my last visit.  

I get the feeling that perhaps this place is riding the wave of their past popularity and have lowered their standards, both in terms of service and food quality.

We arrived right when Neptune opened on a recent Sunday morning.  We immediately got a table and after some time given menus and after some more time saw our waitress for the first time.  Even though the place was half-full at this time, she certainly seemed frazzled and having no time to wait for us to decide.  In fact, she walked away several times if there was a lull in our ordering.  This reflects the service overall, hard to get someone's attention to order another glass of wine or even get the check.  The staff definitely has an attitude and I am not sure that they buy into the customer always being right thing.

The food was ok.  No question it was fresh...but people come on...it's oysters and lobster...not the height of culinary sophistication.  Having said that those are two things that I love and crave on a regular basis.  Somewhat disappointed by the lobster roll...sure it was big...it should be for $28.00...but the lobster was tough and too much mayonnaise.  Would much prefer the lobster roll at James Hook & Co.  I can also say that the Shrimp Cocktail was horrible...the giant shrimp were tough and rubbery...should have definitely just ordered more oysters.

I think that everyone in my party came to the same conclusion...it was alright...not sure it was worth $300 for 3 adults and 1 small child.  There are so many great restaurants in Boston...not sure I would rush back anytime soon.

This mall reminds me of Gateway Mall in Springfield. It's small, boring, and unappealing. I've never been a fan. 

The one cool thing about it is there is an ice skating rink inside. Although that seems like an odd thing to put inside of a mall. It really does. Can be fun to watch families enjoy it though, and little kids as they learn to skate. I've never tried it here myself though. 

The shops all seem to be disappearing as time goes on, and they're never replaced. There are just empty spaces in here, and more of those than actual stores. It's honestly depressing to me, watching stores move out and nothing replacing them. 

The food court is much the same, everybody disappearing. The ones that are left, just seem to hate it there. Like, they know they'll be next, so why put any effort into it. 

Would I return? Probably in a few years, after it's been long enough for me to forget how bad it was the last time. With the hopes it has improved. 

Review 174 of 2017.

It was a very mediocre stay. At no point during my stay did I think "I'll definitely book here again". Rooms and hotel seemed dirty. The area around the sink was covered in a few inches of caulk. The toilet was also loose. They do serve breakfast which is decent. The options change daily for what they serve for breakfast. It's not anything special. We went to a few parks, got back around 2pm and our rooms still weren't cleaned. We had to wait at the pool for another hour before our room on the first floor was cleaned. Check out is 11am and about 10am room service was already pestering me on when I'd be out of the room. I stayed with my parents who left the room about 10:15 and I stayed to watched TV and room service came in to clean, so I had to leave. It's a cheaper hotel so you get what you pay for.

Sometimes I really think your timing at visiting a restaurant is everything. Clearly I chose the wrong time to visit here.  My husband and I visited RMF on a Sunday afternoon. There was one other couple there. We thought that would guarantee us quick service. But, sadly it did not. The servers were busy filling salt and pepper shakers and working on other things.  We finally got some menus and *Yikes* was it expensive. But we realize that organic can be pricy, and you get what you pay for..etc, etc., etc.  So, undeterred I ordered the flatbread special.  My husband ordered the same and with soup (coconut curry soup)

The soup was ok, but you know when something is missing an ingredient and you don't know what it is? That's what he thought the entire time he was eating the soup.  They gave him a piece bread that was a bit too salty to go with it. 

When our flatbreads arrived I was famished. They were tasty, but average. Good cheese, mine had bacon...bacon is always good. Just not amazing, and quite forgettable.   I would love to try it again, but it's way too pricy to experiment here. I won't be going back.

Came here with three friends to try to enjoy a brunch on a Saturday morning. There were four of us and we were directed to sit at a table with six seats so we did.  We were given a coffee I'm giving her water in three minutes later a large party walk through the door and the waitress asked us if we would move. There was a gentleman in the restaurant who was screaming at the top of his Longs when he spoke and we only see that was available was next to him so we decided that we didn't want to move so that caused a bit of a problem. 

The food was not good at all I ordered a Greek omelette could not identify the meat in it and it  had literally no cheese in it and was not very good.  The potatoes were OK and so was the bagel. Other than that I would not recommend this place.

A cool, multi-level environment with funky Asian decor ........... 1 star

Decent sushi that's half-priced on Sundays ...... 2 stars
(but they get you by adding 18% gratuity .... minus 1 star)

Making fun of how hard the place tries to be something it's not and persuading one of the waiters to demonstrate origami on a table napkin ...... Priceless

Seriously, take a look at the other reviews and you'll probably see why you should skip out on this place.  It's probably best for a quick drink or two.

Went to Kore and specifically explained to my stylist that my hair is tricky to cut and so often hairdressers cut it lopsided which is my pet peeve of all time here in Vancouver, plus I hate anything wispy because wispy hair makes my fine hair look even finer. Well, I have lopsided hair and it is wispy - again! I've spent the last week trying to fix it myself and it is looking pretty good now, much better than what it did when I had it cut at Kore, and paid $75.00 plus tip plus bought a can of mousse that is no good for my hair type. How is it so hard to find a stylist in Vancouver who knows how to cut hair properly, and who checks to make sure that the haircut is even? Sheesh. On a plus side, the fellow who cut my hair is gorgeous and very nice. I almost feel bad leaving this review. PS. I could have gone back there to get it fixed but if the first cut was so lopsided, I have no faith in the next one.
PPS. Lesson learned that I won't be tipping until I can check the haircut at home, and if the cut is good, then I'll tip double next time. This particular haircut is turning out to be in the top three of worst haircuts ever. Sigh.

I arrived between 4:30-5:00am on a Wednesday and this TSA Checkpoint was a cluster, long lines and inefficient probably best sums up my experience. About the only positive I can say is that the one friendly employee who was pulling people out of line who arrived an hour before their flight and putting them into a faster line, which really made me wish that I had done the same. What really frustrated me was that they continued to open up new check points and splitting the line off which resulted in nearly everyone behind be getting through security before me, WTH! 

Needless to say it took about an hour to make my way through security and up to the most unfriendly and overly aggressive female TSA agent who must have been on a bit of a power trip. She barked at me and every other traveler in an unfriendly tone, so much where she pretty much ignored me and continue to call other travelers through before allowing me to pass, not sure what I did to upset her but I managed to keep my mouth shut and was just happy once I made my way to the other side of security and onto my gate, so glad I am done with that!

First of all, this place is a mess....period. The valet parking is $20 and for what? It's literally next to like 5 dumpsters and it smells like trash. In order to get inside of the actual establishment, you have to show ID. In order for me to use the RESTROOM I had to show my ID again??? Like huh? then I get to the bathroom and they literally only have 2 which is supposed to be enough for the tent and restaurant extension outside lol yikes.... anyway my friends and I ate in this tent structure that they have in the back and it was hot and our food took forever. The food was pretty good when we got it though!

I've been going to sally's for years.  I get my hair done professionally but I buy toner and some random things from time to time.   Never had an issue before now.  

Two weeks ago I went in on Saturday to get the toner i wanted.  They were out and i almost got a different one but I asked the pretty tan girl if they had any of the one i wanted and she said no that they would have it on Tuesday.  I asked her if it would do the same thing and she said no and that i wouldn't be happy if i used it.  So I took her advice and everything was fine with my encounter with her. 

Then Tuesday came I went in and two workers told me that they had a big truck the night before and were still stocking.  I told them I specifically was told to come today to pick it up.  They told me to call back later.  I was already mad at this point because i made 2 trips there and still didn't have it.  On my way back through town a few hours later I called a lady answered told me to hold and a guy got on the phone.  I asked if they found the toner yet and he asked me if i just called. I said NO i was in there a few hours ago.  He told me no and that they probably didn't even get any because the truck is auto ordered.  Which made me think he was just being lazy and not wanting to find it. he told me he would look at the invoice and let me know if they got it. about 5 or so minutes later he tells me there wasn't any on the truck and that they wouldn't have any til they get their next truck on the following Tuesday

There was no way I could believe that.  I called corporate and spoke with a man who was nice and understood my frustration and that i felt the guy was lying about having any.  He gave me a 30% off coupon code to use.  he called the store and talked to the guy and told him the same thing.  However the rep told me that he seemed nervous about the situation and that he would send the complaint the regional something...

Guess What!?  it's been a week and I just went back to sally's  and Still no toner.  I spoke with a lady who didn't know about the issue and i didn't bother explaining because it doesn't make a difference.  She was nice and called the warehouse to see why they hadn't received any.   It's not her fault im frustrated with going 3 times out of my way and leaving empty handed.  

So I had my boyfriend go to another store and pick up the toner I wanted.  They had at least 20 of them.  That's not the end of it though. When he gave my phone number to checkout and use my $5 OFF COUPON i received when i renewed my membership a few weeks prior they told him they don't have my information and that i don't have a card. even though i have the receipt that shows I renewed and the coupon.   not only that but they wouldn't accept the 30% off code that corporate gave me because they said it expired a month before.   (it has not even been a week since they gave it to me.)

I called corporate to get the membership straightened out and that was easy but when i asked her about the 30% off code she literally argued with me for at least 5 minutes saying there is no way that i have a 30% off code because those don't exist. she looked it up and said it doesn't say anything about giving you a code when you called last time, then she said it did but doesn't show how much.  she put me on hold to ask him about it and came back a few minutes later saying that he gave me a 30% mothers day code to use and it expired on Sunday.  Which I don't care that much about the code but I can not believe she accused me of lying about having a 30% off code and the others misleading me and causing me to have to wait over 2 weeks and making 4 trips for one product.  

If they would have just told me the truth from the start or told me to call before coming to make sure they had it none of this would have happened.  I am still Mad.

I've been going to this place for years ! Most of the staff are very friendly listen to what your asking for on the cut front and make it happen .. Equals more often than not a great cut !
Today walked in put my name on the list . 30 mins later walked back in to take my name off the list as a courtesy .. Asked if I could put my name in for a later time .. The Girl at the front desk was pretty rude telling me yeah you'll have to resign in later .. We don't do that with a condescending smirk !
Crap customer service skills .. I will not be back .. Lots of choices in this town ..

I went to Sitar a couple weeks ago together with a friend who recommended this restaurant. Let's just say it was ok but I experienced much better and to be honest I expected much more from an Indian Restaurant in Vancouver (well, Gastown...) but even compared to my 'hole in the wall' Indian Take-Out in Los Angeles this place lost by miles.

The food was ok but not overly tasteful. I ordered mild but that the Chicken Tikka Marsala has absolutely no taste was a new thing to me.

The biggest let-down was the waiter service. The Lady was nice but the guy (the owner?) was downright rude, forgot about half of the order and they did not even offer a refill on my soda that I ordered next to the Kelpi.

The bill in the end was like 70$ for 2 people plus tip, which - I have to admit - was little after this experience.

Will definitely try something different next time!

Cheers
~S

Low Bar has always been a little hit and miss, but you could always count on a few things to be standard... Particularly hot toddies with house infused cinnamon whiskey and breakfast sandwiches. Disappointed now that the misses are a lot more common than the hits. Maybe it's the new ownership trying to get their feet under them, but the hot toddy was truly terrible and their biscuit tasted like undercooked cornmeal. (And some friends just mentioned their even worse disappointment after they went for Dining the Couv, but that is technically hearsay.) 

Hoping they can get it together. But for now, I won't be back.

I can't comment on most of the food, but based on the items I tried, I wasn't very pleased. I decided to try this place out for a quick snack based on the great reviews. I had the guacamole and chips. I was expecting the guacamole to be full of flavor, but unfortunately I've had better guacamole in the refrigerated section of the supermarket. The tortilla chips had an unfamiliar and strange texture as well. Maybe other items are better, but I probably wouldn't order guacamole here again.

I really wanted to like this place, but they were just okay. I got a couples massage with my friend. First, we asked if we could use the bathroom before hand, and one of them seemed mad. Then, they didn't ask what level of pressure we wanted...they just started massaging. The worse thing was that they were chatting to each other during the massage, which was unprofessional. The massage itself was so-so. I left them a 15% tip even though the massage was not great, and they were pissed. I will go elsewhere next time.

I originally found Major League Maids on Craigslist.  They were calling themselves something else in the beginning but have since changed their name.  The first time I used them I was SO extremely happy!  Thrilled.  I spoke with Chelsea who is the owner along with her husband.  Only thing that wasn't perfect was the kitchen counter top not being cleaned.  They're granite.  The lady that came to clean was Hispanic and spoke broken little English.  This wasn't a problem for either of us. We got along just fine and I really liked the girl.  

I told Chelsea about the counter tops because she wanted to know if there was anything at all I wasn't happy with. She really wanted to make sure her clients were happy with their service as they were a new business.  So, on the next visit, Chelsea sent her husband to come in with a new girl who was a white English speaking girl.  She did a great job as well and the husband wanted to make sure I was very happy and I was.  Again, thrilled!  So happy to find a good cleaning service that wasn't just interested in making money.

Well, after that, everything went downhill.  Third visit, 3 Hispanic ladies show up. Only one speaks broken English.  She gave me a pre-printed list to fill out that shows everything they will do while there and I was to check off anything that I didn't want done.  This was great.  A detailed list.  Perfect.  

I left the girls to do their thing.  I paid them their money cash.  When I got home, I found the windows in my living room (which I have a lot of) were not cleaned at all. Underneath my dining table it had not been cleaned, tons of dust underneath. Two of the bathroom floors just weren't swept at all which also means not mopped. Two closets, not swept either.  No one swept behind the doors that were open in rooms or closets.  I was just really, really unhappy.  I took pictures of 2 things and sent them to Chelsea.  She was very apologetic, offered to clean the house with a $20 discount on the next visit.  Okay, fine, just as long as I don't get the same girls.  She said there were only suppose to have been 2 women there which was odd.  Why was their 3?  Were they paying someone on the side.

Next scheduling Chelsea tells me she's sending her best girl to me, they show up 1 hr and 15 mins late.  No phone call to tell me they were running late. After 3 calls to Chelsea and telling her I had to leave and forget it, 3 girls show up as I'm leaving my house. It's the same girls as last time.  The one who spoke English remembered me as well.  I was VERY unhappy.  

Chelsea then started sending me weekly texts offering a special house cleaning for $50 due to other clients cancelling.  This was weird.  This happens all the time now and she wants to fill her schedule?  If she can do the whole house for $50 why does she charge $77 normally?  It was just too gimmicky for me and I felt they got into the money making mode and quit offering just really good service.  I was willing to pay $100 each time for the service I got on the 1st two visits.  It's really a shame.  I was so happy to begin with.

Be careful and stay with the girls and watch what they do.  And no they do not all speak fluent English as her website advertises.  Good luck Yelpers!

After experiencing original blacks, smittys, and franklin bbq I'd have to say this place did not hold up to Texas bbq standards. The brisket was not tender at all and the cut was an inch thick. From experience brisket cuts are 1/4 inch. The sausage was grainy to the point that once bitten into the ground pork would fall out of the casing. Tsk tsk. Stood in line for what I thought would be something stellar but total fail. Oh well, on to the next bbq joint...

"I was very satisfied with your product but the service made me never want to shop here again."

That's what I said to the lady that worked there, anyway. I LOVED the diamond jewelery I got there. Zales is great for beautiful, sparkly diamonds that are reasonably priced because of minor inclusions/flaws that are not very noticeable. But be careful to examine any diamond thoroughly before buying. The lights in the store make it hard to examine, and my diamond had a small black spot on the edge that I hadn't noticed before. I wish I had returned it, but then again, the diamond was big and clear and sparkly and you can't notice the inclusion unless you get up close so I didn't mind. I still love the diamond.

Now about the service - it sucks. It's easy to buy here, but if you ever need any repairs or assistance, forget about it. I waited for 45 minutes to get my ring sized 
(which they charged me for .... Who charges to take gold OFF a ring and make it smaller?) and was treated with a very rude attitude by the middle aged blond-ish lady that worked there. When I got the ring back, it was still too big. Thankfully they agreed to correct the problem for no fee. 

Zales is great, just not at this particular location!

My first experience with Belmont Pizza was good. A friend ordered us a plain cheese pizza and, as an adventurous eater, I was surprised how satisfying and flavourful it was. My second experience was not so great... the meat-lovers' pizza arrived without the appetizers I had ordered - and it tasted like a greasy heart attack on dough. My third and last experience made me want to cut ties... we live just up the street and it took our order (a large combination pizza) 45 minutes to arrive. The mushrooms and peppers made a soggy mess out of the crust and the flavour was mediocre.

Server was awesome!!! The wedge salad with romain lettuce was to die for!! The dip for the bread my partner and I agreed was not tasty. Medallions were undercooked to what I requested and somewhat  tasteless. Sent back because it was undercooked and they further cooked it for me. Creme brûlée was cooler in temperature than it should have been. Potato Au gratin was tasteless as well. I don't plan on coming again. The ambiance was beautiful and the cocktails were very good as well. Food ruined it for me. They did take off price of dessert because of the undercooked food, which just showed how good the service is. Wish I could give 2 1/2, but not a three. Maybe it was the cook for the night.

We were quite disappointed with this salon.  My three adult daughters, our two older grandchildren (ages 8 and 9) and I came to Atlanta to find gowns for my husband's and my 40th anniversary celebration in January 2019.  We made an appointment at Lori's, arrived on time at this lovely shop (free plentiful parking) and were happily greeted by the receptionist staff.  It went downhill from there.  The young woman who was "helping" us clearly didn't want to be there that morning.  We basically "helped" ourselves.  Any questions we asked were often met with rolled eyes and her responses were in "valley-girl-speak."  There are many beautiful gowns here and two of us actually found dresses we were interested in although there were no samples in our size.  When we asked our "assistant" to take one of the dresses from a display mannequin which was in the proper size and color, our "assistant" told us that was absolutely impossible because those are "the rules" -- you'd have thought we'd asked for the blood of her firstborn.  She finally did remove the dress from the mannequin and practically threw it at us.  It turned out to be perfect and we were nearly ready to make a purchase, but we wanted our measurements taken and the exact measurements of the gowns we'd chosen.  That, too, was impossible because unless we've handed over our credit card and made the purchase, no measuring because, well, you know, "the rules."  We questioned this policy, trying to be logical - how do you know if it'll fit if there are no measurements? - but we had to abide by "the rules."  So we abided by OUR rule - the customer is always right - and left Bridals by Lori never to return.

Whoops! Should have checked the reviews before rolling in here. The staff is very nice. None of this is their fault. But...great, YET ANOTHER serve-yourself spot in Portland with prices as high as a sit-down place. The food is unimpressive (the jicama salad is the worst--soupy and cinnamon flavored; the tacos varied between good and dry/flavorless) and definitely tiny/overpriced (two-bite tacos for $2.75+). This place is lazy to the max and feels like a touristy theme restaurant. They didn't even redecorate after Sen Yai closed (RIP to that actually good restaurant)...at this point, I don't think they should bother.

Recently left the Linc after 4+years. Very bitter sweet. Some of the staff are great and they are very responsive regarding up-keep and Maintanence. However, be prepared to be treated like a criminal if you violate any of their rigid rules regarding parking, damages when you move out, and monthly utilities. Also be aware that they will raise your rent every year even though the exact same apartment that is vacant will rent for less then you're paying. They have no loyalty to long time renters. 
they have turned the visitor parking and monthly parking arrangements into a money making scheme. Don't want to go into details, but you and your guests will come to hate those $44 parking tickets. Scheduling a simple dinner party is hell because you have to explain how every one has to move their car by a certain time or get ticketed.
Also, the moving-out process is so unfair. They use very cheap materials (particle board cabinets) in these apartments and blame you because they don't hold up. Your furniture will dent the fake wood floor and they will charge you hundreds of dollars to replace the cheap flooring. 

The "utility" company they use will charge you $50 for being more than 30 days late.... which on a practical level means that if you pay monthly, every month with 31 days means you'll get a nasty note on your door charging you $50. 

They are ridged and anal about a lot of petty stuff....then they put on "parties" for the tenants. I would have gladly traded the silly parties for more respect and fair policies.

I expected so much more with all of the reviews of this place but I was completely disappointed. 

I came here for lunch on a Friday with a friend. We searched Yelp and found the glowing reviews of this place. Once I stepped into the restaurant, I knew the restaurant was more about ambiance than the food. 

For appetizers we ordered the monkfish pate and nasu dengaku (eggplant in miso sauce). We got the eggplant first and my immediate reaction was a little disgust. The eggplant was completely covered in the dark brown miso sauce. It didn't look very appealing, I didn't even bother taking a picture of it. When I tasted it, the miso sauce was waaayyy too sweet. You can't even taste the grilled eggplant. My friend and I had to scrape off the sauce to get a decent flavor. The monkfish "pate" was really good but not what I was expecting. When I hear the word pâté I was expecting some type of spread. The monkfish liver came out whole, I didn't mind this at all because that's how I like it. I just didn't like how they tried to make it fancy on the menu. 

I ordered the sushi and sashimi lunch combo for my meal. My friend ordered the yellowtail roll and a dragon roll. My lunch combo came with sashimi pieces of red snapper, salmon, and tuna. Then my sushi pieces were just repetitive with the red snapper, salmon, tuna, and oh yay they added shrimp! What no yellowtail in there?! If I knew the sushi and sashimi were going to be the same type of fish I would have ordered something else. The cuts of the fish were ok but the quality was not very good. The red snapper was dry and the salmon was too chewy. I tasted my friend's dragon roll and it was ok. They had tempura sweet potato in the roll and that was different. However it made the roll pretty heavy. The eel was good and the sauce wasn't too sweet. I didn't get to try the yellowtail roll but my friend said it was good.

Unsatisfied with my combo, I ordered a toro handroll to hopefully lift my spirits. The toro handroll wasn't impressive for $17. There was supposed to be scallions inside but I didn't get any. The toro wasn't the best quality and the seaweed it was wrapped in was so chewy.

Our total bill came out to be $71 pre tax and tip. I couldn't believe how much we spent on the quality of the food. The monkfish liver was the only saving grace of my meal. The service was ok when it came to clearing our plates but we did have to ask several times for lemon and water refills. So sad this had to be my last meal in Boston. I definitely won't be back, I'd rather spend my money at a good hole-in-the-wall sushi type of joint than this place.

Not a lot of options here in this specific area of the airport but I think if I had time, I would visit a different concourse to get food as the tacos here made me a bit sad. This is pretty much like fast food with a very high price and even lower quality than Taco Bell.

The carne asada taco and shrimp tacos were very over priced and soggy with little to no flavor. It was like eating wet cardboard with some chewy bits. I don't think the ingredients are very fresh and the tacos are wrapped quite poorly even though they don't have many people ordering. If you've never had a taco before you might enjoy this but I'd rather eat a cold prepackaged sandwich from an airport vendor.

The chips and salsa were decent although the salsa a bit spicy and the chips were crispy which were a nice addition to snack on the plane. However, I don't think I would come back solely for that but definitely giving an extra star for the chips!

I visited on a whim for a quick meal on a Friday night. I'd love to know which street they visited to find these "street" tacos, because as a visitor in search of "Boulder's best taco" I've been unimpressed with my findings. 

Chips and Salsa - the chips are the highlight, they're nice and crispy and exactly what a tortilla chip is. The salsas lacked kick - Mango salsa was very sweet, salsa verde was missing acid, and the red salsa was about where I'd begin to place "mild." These were not bad tasting, but were not necessarily what I was looking for. 

Tacos - I had barbacoa and carnitas, they were about 4x the price of a normal street taco. I was very surprised that there was no al pastor, cabeza, lengua, or even chorizo on the menu - traditional street taco staples. My tacos were not bad tasting by any means, but were not necessarily flavorful - bit more heat, seasoning, and maybe a little extra sear would've gone a long way. I was also surprised to find so many toppings, but that's personal preference - I like the meat to take center stage. The tacos were very juicy, which is a great thing, but that caused the tortillas to become soggy and rubbery. 

Overall, I was unimpressed. I feel like I'm definitely getting hung up on the "street taco" name, but these are very different from the tacos you get on the streets of Mexico City or Los Angeles.

The only reason I am giving them two stars is because the guy that did my gel manicure was really nice. Overall, I would never go back here. I told them lady that welcomed me at the door that I was in a rush. She said ok and that I should sit at a pedicure chair. She ran the water and poured the typical blue "substance" in the water. It took them 35-40 minutes to begin on my pedicure. Before she could start on my pedicure I started to feel itchiness on the bottom of my feet. Im not sure what the problem was, but she ended up draining and re-running the water without the blue "substance". I do not believe this salon is very sanitary at all. The pedicure was ok at first, but the manicure left black nail polish on my finger...And since this was gel polish it could not be simply wiped away. The kicker was they charge the same price as much of the higher quality salons AND my pedicure only lasted 2 days before BOTH of my big toes chipped. I will not be returning!

Honestly, I believe that most nail salons are either using cheap polish OR deliberately providing shotty work in order to make sure you have to return quickly. From now on I will invest in the proper materials to do my manicure/pedicure at home. Its ridiculous to spend $50-70 on a manicure/pedicure only to have it last 2 days!

Went with a group of 6 for dinner. We did the all you can eat option. Servers were grouchy. Inattentive. Reluctant to give us more cards for ordering. Hard to wave anyone down for drink orders. 

We had several members of the group arrive at slightly different times and the server tried to not give us another ordering card. You already did she said. Ummmm ya. Now we want more. There are more ppl now. WTF is up with this place. It's all u can eat right? 28$ each. Soooo you want me to pay to sit here and NOT eat dinner? Idiots. And might I point out that we were 5 girls who didnt eat much and 1 guy. So it's not like we ordered a huge amount at all. I Probly ate 12$ worth of food. Partly cause it was hard to order more. 

Then they want a tip. Bahaha ha sure. 

Ridiculous. Avoid it. Way better options in Vancouver. Many many options. Like. Go ANYWHERE else.

I was very disappointed. My expectation was that I would get North End quality Italian food. This was Bertucci-type of dining. The decor has vastly improved. Atmosphere was bistro-loud and happy. We all had something different and each dish offered nothing special in flavor or quality. 

Caprese  salad was on a small plate. There was too much dressing and there didn't appear to be any basil. Peppers were too much. This dish should be fresh, simple ingredients that speak for themselves. Kind of hard to get this wrong. 

Caesar salad was flavorless and light on dressing and appeared to have balsamic vinegar on it which was overpowering. 

Pasta dish with chicken and broccoli was too light in sauce and chicken was very dry and over cooked. 

Shrimp scampi was the best dish we had but the shrimp was over cooked, dry and rubbery, not light and fresh. 

Ravioli had a very heavy sauce which tasted fine but was too heavy. The pasta was very thick like a puerogi, not light and al dente 

Bread was cold, tasted ok but would prefer an interesting dipping oil. 

Drinks were a good price but not a great selection of wines by the glass. 

There was grated cheese on the table in a jar. Hated that. In a good Italian restaurant the cheese is parmigiana regianno and grated fresh at the table. 

Waiting staff while friendly was not attending to the water glasses being filled. 

Overall, it was a very average experience with nothing gourmet about it. It felt like eating in a Bertuccis masked as Giacomo's. 

They should take some tips from Papparazzi which has a nice experience for a chain. I also think they could learn a lot from Alta Strada in Wellesley that has really great food, and cooked well. 

Im hoping to see some improvement because I would like this restaurant to be a success.

Really upset with the customer service experience here. I had walked by one day and the line was out the door so I decided to see what the hype was all about (on a day with a shorter line). I ended up going in before noon on a Wednesday and the line wasn't too bad, so I placed my order "to go" and sat down to wait.  About 20 minutes had gone by and I had seen a couple people who were behind me in line get their orders.  I walked up to the counter and looked around and the woman behind asked me if I needed help. I told her I had placed my order 20 minutes ago and hadn't gotten it.  She asked me my name and looked at her screen and told me that "It had only been 7 minutes". I was a little taken aback by this comment because I had actually been waiting there for 20 minutes. About a minute later they called "my name" and someone else grabbed the food. That lady who grabbed the food had the same name as me-and it was her food. Then the woman behind the counter looked at me and decided to check the shelf of food for call ahead/pick up and said "my food must have been put there by accident" and handed it to me. I totally understand it was a mistake, however no apology was given to me after she accused me of being in the wrong. Based on this rude customer service experience I have no reason to go back to Life Alive.

Sadly, the people who work there sometimes seem to want to be somewhere else, anywhere but at work.  Their prices are very high, (i.e. Draper Chicken is more expensive than Whole Foods.) and their product doesn't turn as fast, so you have to use it that day. But the biggest pain is that they're not open normal hours for a market.  They don't open until the middle of the morning.  Why bother to sell eggs and bacon.  And when you turn away pissed, they have a good yuk at your expense.

Great food. Horrible service. We go here often and I'd love to see some attempt at delivering all meals to the table at roughly the same time. Typically meals arrive over a 15 or 20 minute period. My wife and I even asked if we could get our two meals to arrive close to each other so we could eat together. The server said, "probably not, the kitchen doesn't care about that."

We return because the food is good. However, if the service was even marginal, we'd return far more often. I wish the owners cared about providing decent service.

My initial experience here, was seemingly great. I came in to make an appointment and the staff was extremely helpful and friendly. When the time came, a week later, I returned for my appointment and the staff and doctor were all helpful. Then came the sales...I was treated so poorly and condescendingly by a gentleman there who was pissy I wasn't buying his offer for "upgraded" lenses. I then realized that he was trying to charge me for something that my insurance covered and when I pointed it out to him, he was smug and told me "oh, well I guess I can add that". I'm now waiting up to 2 weeks to receive my glasses and hoping that they are what I'm supposed to be getting. This may be my last time using this shop...

*****UPDATE (ORIGINAL REVIEW BELOW)*****
Changing my rating to two stars based on my second visit. A different woman did my brows, and i specifically stated i wanted ti keep them thick and to just clean them up. She didn't listen. She gave me an arch that i didn't ask for, and they came out MUCH thinner than my previous session. I didn't notice it until i had left the building and happened to glance in my rearview mirror... If every employee can't consistently give good results based on what the customer is asking, i do not think this establishment deserves a high rating. I've already purchased a series of 3, so i will make sure to only let the same person handle my brows next time... After they've had time to grow back in properly. 

***** ORIGINAL REVIEW *****

Ladies, you know that feeling when you can't stop checking your brows out in the mirror because they look SO good? That's the experience you'll have after a trip to Mona's. I've been growing my eyebrows out for a couple months, and i finally caved and decided to have them groomed somewhere. They were a mess, but i was convinced they were still to sparse to be cleaned up properly. I was wrong. I just mentioned that i'm trying to keep them as thick as possible and she just worked her magic while threading my brows into submission. They now look better than they have in years! I'll definitely be going back, as it's difficult to find someone who actually listens to and DOES what you want. There is a special where you can purchase a set of 3 brow threadings for $15 (versus $6/individually). Also, they do very nice henna for those who are interested.

I have used this place for convenience to mount and balance 2 sets of tires.  Mistake!!  Both times they have destroyed my rims.  Besides what I discern as a lack of concern for the quality of their labor, I am always given the sell on services and repairs I don't need (once actually exceeding the value of the car!).  The employees are not bad people and I pity them having to deal with some of the customers I have overheard, but I will forever again avoid chain stores for auto work that I cannot perform myself.

yep, I sure have experienced better. 

So, my boyfriend and I decided to take up the "Free to MA residents" Sunday morning admission. I read the reviews and didn't really expect it to be large or modern. And man, it sure wasn't!

This is more like a couple of rooms of collections. No real hands-on stuff.. and hardly any information, facts, etc next to the display items.

The taxidermy area smelled like a great grandma's attic. The animals were falling apart. 

The glass flower exhibit was set up like a school library... I mean, sure, it's awesome work... but I mean, I just wasn't into staring at fake plant/flower anatomy for more than 5 minutes. Also, these are mostly plants/greens. No brightly colored flowers or anything like that. 

The Mineral Hall is a large room with many minerals on display. Some were amazing. But again, I don't think we spent more than 15 minutes in that room. Kind of repetitive. 

The Arthropod exhibit is what I was mostly interested in seeing and ended up slightly disappointed. They didn't really have the vast collection I thought they would. There wasn't really anything to read when looking at them, either. 

The Climate Change Exhibit I can't really vouch for... we only went in there because a massive amount of kids stormed the gem room and we needed to escape. 

I am with others - I don't understand why Harvard can't update its collections... I mean, the animals were literally falling apart.

I also have no idea how kids would find this exciting for more than 5 minutes.

But hey, It was free.

Despite having ads for all the other Firkin properties at the back of the lanes, it is not part of the Firkin portfolio. This might explain its current condition. They still haven't fixed external damage from recent hurricanes, and the signs on the outside are in need of cleaning or replacement. The staff is friendly, at least the ones I've dealt with. Food is decent, but usually takes a while to get to you. Some of the lanes have broken and chipped boards right by the foul line where balls keep getting dropped over and over again. 

This place had a lot of potential when it opened. But they have closed the full-service restaurant, pro shop, and the billiards area. There are also no leagues at this bowling center, which explains the condition of the lanes. Almost every monitor for each lane has some black spot on it. There are lots of upgrades and updates that need to be made to fully realize its potential. 

It's good for what it is, but don't expect to be blown away. If you are a serious bowler, this might not be the place for you. But it is on kidsbowlfree.com, so that's a plus.

Looks fancy but isn't.

We arrived early for our 7PM NYE reservation and were seated late. No one even took our drinks order for 20+ minutes, and then took another 20 to bring the drinks. At that point, we had not been served our first of several courses in a Pre-Fixe menu, so my fiancée complained. The hostess then came over the explain their "system," and how they don't serve tables while someone was in the restroom. I pointed out that I had been away from the table for only 5 minutes. The Hostess didn't apologize.

The service then improved moderately, but no one ever asked if I wanted another drink until I'd finished the last course.

The food was just bad. They used excellent ingredients and mangled them. Beautiful foie gras came out covered in raw nuts that were impossible to chew. The final rib eye was nicely cooked but adorned inexplicably with nuts and flavorless dots of foam. 

We took the dessert to go because a Glade scented plugin nearby (!?!?!) was making the whole area smell foul and after two hours we were just done.

They said they comped my drink and foie gras but the check wasn't itemized and the cost didn't seem to reflect those deductions, but I just wanted to leave.

I came with 4 friends, we wanted to be seated outside so we had to wait a few mins. We sit outside and there's plenty of umbrellas covering the tables. Our waiter was informative and explained the how the restaurant works. Our food was good and he did well checking in on us. 

Then a turn for the worst happened.

 We split our checks, most used cash, half wanted change back, and the other half didn't. He forgot who wanted change and who didn't, so he returned with the cash and said he messed up and forgot. So we begin to explain and he continues to look as if he's trying to remember. So I say "the Oaxaca burger and single burger are the only ones that need change". Calm and helpful right? Nope! His response "ma'am I've been doing this for 8 years, I just need quiet to figure this out." Then he walks away and I'm left stunned. I'm talking at the table about how rude he was and he returns and says "I'm sorry for being rude..." me "yes that was VERY rude" him "well I said I was sorry so you can either take it or leave it". BRUH!!! What in the entire hell?!?! So naturally, I begin to examine how my tone was and I was very calm, so then I realize hey it was just him with his panties in a bunch. I must have reminded him of a girl who broke his heart, circled "no" on his "will you go with me," a girl who cheated on him with his own brother, the girl who packed up her stuff in the middle of the night and left him...who knows! But I KNOW his anger was misplaced. The manager just so happens to come outside, I tell him the story and he apologizes profusely. I still believe he could've done more. I tell him I want all of my change, every penny. He returns with just the dollars...and in ones at that as if I was going to leave a tip. They kept my 23 cents. It seems like all restaurants are doing this now and I don't mind, but in this situation I was pissed. I decided not to be petty and didn't ask for it back though.

SLOW.  I live close by and avoid this place because it is slow and a pain to pull in or out if you want to turn left.  I actually get annoyed at all the people turning in here that slows traffic down.  The only redeeming quality is that it has a play place which is great for people driving on trips that needs this for their kids.  I would advise going to the Chick Fila for a playplace in the winter but this works in the summer.  The playplace is outside but under a canopy.  This place is just slow in drive thru and inside.  I went in to get an apple pie the other day and it still took 5 minutes to order and receive food.  I wouldn't advise the slow drive thru either.

Beware of this establishment if you are a person of color and or have family that are of such... these people are racist, especially the waitress that my family and I had. The food was okay, not as good as it used to be but that's besides the point.. this woman would only acknowledge me (i am white) and wouldn't respond to any requests that my boyfriend and his sister asked for. They both asked for boxes and she ignored them, walking away and then came back to me and asked if I wanted a box but didn't seem to care about what they wanted (the same thing with their drinks she never once asked if they needed a refill the only time she spoke to them is when she took our orders.) the location in St.Cloud is better! Don't come here.

I DO like shopping at Forever 21. Its cheap and perfect for those fad clothing styles you wont be wearing forever. Its a beautiful store, its two floors and its done very well. I've been to the one in Metrotown which in my opinion is very unorganized and very hard to shop at. However the staff at the Robson location are HORRIBLE!! I understand they probably pay minimum wage and this is obviously not their life goal to work here, but put some effort in. I had tried on some jeans and went to purchase them. I was also returning two items I had bought a week ago (nothing wrong never worn tags still on.) The lady was so rude and kept questioning me why I'm returning them. They also don't give you a refund just store credit. When I asked her if the jeans would stretch she said "I don't know, haven't you bought jeans before?" what kind of answer is that?!?! So when I said I wanted to buy them in a size smaller she smirked at me and said "well go ahead, go get them." Did not even offer to grab a runner to bring me the size. Ill still go there since I live 5 mins away but I will just be rolling my eyes at these girls.

I'm kinda done with Andina. Might bring out of town guests here, but I'm otherwise done. 

I have a real problem with having a 7pm reservation and not getting seated until 7:30. 
The noise level in the bar is out of control. 
The menu hasn't significantly changed in years. The vegetarian quinotto has been on there as long as I can remember. Maybe they change it a bit seasonally, but come on. It's good, so don't get me wrong on that front. 
There's no place to wait. So, when you are told your table isn't ready, you have to fight the loud band and 100 other people hoping for a bar table in a walkway used to run food from the kitchen. Then, you have to fight the band, the servers, the other waitees, AND  people trying to get to to bathroom once you pick out your eight square inches to stand. 

The drinks are great. The service is generally attentive, except for the time I was told a dish was vegetarian only to bite into a chunk of ham.  But, to be fair, that was years ago. 

The food on my last visit was meh. The asparagus tasted like grill, not like asparagus. The fried yuca was tasteless.  I know yuca isn't the most flavorful veggie to begin with, but this was like eating deep fried dried blah. The green salad wasn't anything special. 


Every time I go, my stress level goes up about quadruple normal.  The restaurant is SO enormous now, it feels kinda like being in a huge cafeteria.  A huge cafeteria that you are supposed to like because everyone else does.  They are booked out well in advance and I can get more bang for my buck at other places.

I went here with 3 others after a long hike.  It was mid-afternoon, and the place was tucked in a well-hidden plaza near the Arthur Laing bridge beside Penang Delight.

The first comment I have is about the name and concept of the restaurant, which has a distinctly French name... in fact, the name would lead you to believe that it makes several products out of oranges.  However, the menu is a big mismatch - I would describe their cuisine as classic Japanese-style Italian.

I ordered a hamburger steak on beef hash stew spaghetti.  I never really understood hamburger steak; isn't it just a fancy way of saying meatloaf?  In any case, this was ok meatloaf and the stew was ok, but it wasn't unique by any standard.  The flavour lacks a punch of citrus that usually marks a good stew... maybe they could have included an orange wedge?

My sister had tonkatsu don with curry and it was an average dish.  The pork cutlet was just slightly past golden brown, and tasted good.  The curry was strange; it tasted like the spices were not cooked on their own before they were added to the sauce.  My comparison is always to Glico curry cubes which you can buy in any store.

I'm certainly not too impressed.  Maybe the forte of this restaurant lies in its desserts?

Ok.....this place started strong and has ended horribly. Discovered thru a friend and then used the Scoutmob for lunch and later a Groupon offer.....but this last full price meal visit left a bad taste in my mouth. There were only 2 other people in the place when we arrived, yet, it took the waiter over 5 minutes to wander over to our table to ask for our drink orders. It was obvious the waiter was avoiding eye contact with us in fear he'd have to come WORK.... then we get our food and wow. The pho bowl was 1/2 empty and devoid of broth....or flavor. My overpriced bahn mi ($9 freakin $$$, really folks?) was salty and poorly constructed. I could've gone to Buford Hwy and had a sackfull of bahn mi for the price of this one lackluster version. I will not be returning, even if someone was going to pay my way.

I picked the place for a friend's pre-bday dinner - thinking it would be a great place to get in and out of on a week night, not too fancy since the fancy pants dinner was later in the week. The food came out over the course of 45 minutes. Some people sat without food while others waited allowing their Pho to get cold to be polite and thinking it can't be that much longer... The pho was good so they have that working in their favor. The staff were over worked and understaffed. The restaurant was not even packed! But all the to go orders overwhelmed to the point that those eating in suffered in consequence. The manager did her best to right the wrong and refunded items that were charged to the wrong ticket and those that took way too long to come out but the overall experience was already ruined for us at that point. It takes a lot for me to write a bad review but my friend leaving unhappily on his bday did the job.

Service is very poor. We were a family of five at 8:30pm and we waited over 20 minutes for anyone to even address us. We literally were on the countdown for walking out when someone finally came over to take our order. The bread was fantastic along with the chilled vegetable topping. Ambiance is great, food was good, service was far below acceptable especially for this price point of a restaurant. We were very disappointed after the restaurant came so highly recommended. Not a great start to vacation.

It's very convenient, but the "fresh food" never really looks fresh. The liquor store has good selection and pricing but it takes way to long to get checked out, there's usually a long line, always only one cashier and it seems customers either don't have ID, are paying for their purchase by counting out change or are already drunk. They have a big display right in the middle of the aisle in front of the register that you have to manuever around. I guess what I'm saying is that the location is conveneint, but forget it if you are in a hurry. 

And the sushi contains carbon monoxide  to keep it looking fresh, gross.

Bar staff was excellent. Clams were excellent and fresh as expected. The Truffle Oil Lobster Mac N Cheese was tasty but lacked the lobster!!!  Five very small pieces (about nickel sized) were mixed in. Oh and it was priced at "market price"!!!!  The dish was about 6 inches in diameter. After I complained about lack of lobster meat, manager came over and gave me a discount. He took 6 bucks of a "market price" of $30.95.  So essentially I had a glorified bowl of Mac N Cheese for $25 bucks. Needless to say I won't be going back. LTK thinks they can charge outrageous prices in their name. But when they rip off customers with bogus "market price" they will see their clientele go other places.

This place is very cool looking and the food sounds good. But we the all you care to eat. If sounded good and looked good. First their is six of us and the table was way to small to fit the large plates of food. And the food was just bad all of it. Well the corn bread was good. The only thing that was ok was that the server was very nice and had a nice talk with her. I would not go back again.  We did not get dessert it may be good.

CRAPY staff! Good selection of military surplus at a mid to high price (no real deals here). Lots or odds and ends if your going into the woods or reliving a Rambo fantasy. Again though staff sucks! The walk past you with not even a hello, they make you wait for no reason, they are dismissive and generally they just SUCK! on the up side if you need no help and dont mind moderate prices they have a lot of great stuff.

So if you've read my reviews, I'm pretty positive. I'm trying to look for the positives for my experience at this restaurant and they are limited to the service (good service), ambience (nice decor and location) and food presentation (very nice, above average (see attached photo). My wife and I both ordered the "Bun That Nuong Cha Gio Tom"...the restaurant was a little busy, we waited about 20-25 minutes...my chicken and my wife's beef were barely warm and our salad was wilted with quite a few pieces of salad with brown edges. Now you ask, did we mention it to the server, no we didn't...in most cases I would have but we were with our son, were very hungry and on a bit of a time constraint. To sum it up; location, service and decor very nice but someone wasn't doing their job and ensuring the food was hot and salad fresh...I was disappointed however may try it again

I'm been growing more and more disillusioned with this place over the last year or so. They used to be AMAZING - quick service, big sushi rolls, etc. Lately though the rolls I've gotten have been falling apart and TINY, and the wait was always ridiculous, even when there wasn't a line. I was a way bigger fan of the Subway-type service they used to have, where you watched the chefs make your roll.

I kept wanting to give this place a chance. I'm a vegetarian, and hdyr has the best sushi options for vegetarians that I've ever seen. Last night was my last try though: I bit into one of my rolls to find a big shard of hard plastic. Since it was a to-go order, I couldn't exactly ask for another one. Absolutely disgusting.

The view was beautiful but the food and service was terrible. We were sat down and given menus but it took around half an hour for the waiter to come back to ask about drinks!!! The water messed up our drink orders. When we finally ordered our food after an hour in the restaurant it took another 45 minutes to get the food. When we received it the pasta was undercooked and the "spicy" sauce was not even spicy or flavourful for that matter. My entire table was disappointed with the attitude of the waiters and the quality of the food. It was also very over priced. I would be able to make a better quality bowl of pasta for under $10 but I had to pay $40 for a tiny bowl of pasta. We had a party of 8 people and none of us enjoyed the meal or experience. But the view was very pretty.

Went on a Saturday night. It was quite busy but got seated at a high table in about 5-6 min. Ordered a kale Cesar salad to share and a Margherita pizza. The salad was tasty. The pizza was OK. Service was less than we expected but we didn't order alcohol. Waitress tried to take away the salad bowl before we had finished and removed our plates with one of us still eating a slice. Seems they needed our place to seat a party if 6. We got the message loud and clear when they set the space for 4 next to us for 6 and squeezed two extra chairs in. Oh, wiping our table with a damp rag while we were still seated was another clue. 
 All in all we were out in 35 min. Didn't need the hour parking! Won't go back. Too bad it isn't nicer. Kerrisdale needs more restaurants.

This review is only for Club16 Seawall Bike rentals

The bikes we rented were great, comfortable and made cycling around Stanley Park a breeze. I just disagree with their salesman. We asked how long it would take to get around Stanley Park and they sold us 2 bikes for a 3 hour rental. 

Although we stopped many times for photo opportunities around the Seawall, it only took 2 hours to tour around. They wouldn't refund us for the 1-hour we didn't use the bike!! So, if we rented the bikes for just 2 hours and brought it back for 3 hours, I'm sure they'd charge us for 3-hours so why can't we get our money back for the 1-hour we didn't use the bike x2?? You feel ripped off

Last time I came to this location was about a year ago and had no problems with the service or product I had purchased. Came here around 2 pm today and ordered 1/2 a dozen donuts (5 sprinkled donuts and 1 chocolate Creme filled). Customer service was fine considering I just through drive thru, after I had paid and went back home I peaked to see how the donuts looked and saw that they gave me the wrong Creme filled donut and one of the sprinkled donut looked crappy. Guess quality went down since my last visit. You'd think they'd put more effort considering I paid around $9 for half a dozen. :/

I'm super bummed with my sns dip. I usually get my nails done in NH, closer to home, but I was in a pinch in the area and found Waltham Nails and Spa. Everyone was super nice and accommodating-- no complaints there. I'm just not pleased with the finish on my nails 3 days later. Typically, I get 3 weeks out of a manicure. I've gone 3 days and the clear finish looks like glue was used instead of clear. The surface is all scratched and bumpy and the skin surrounding my nails is cracking and super dry. Not sure if I had some weird reaction to whatever chemicals they use. For $40, I expected a little more longevity.

Hi, my name is Riley.  I went to check out the facility last week and was not impressed.  The front desk staff was completely occupied with paperwork and who knows what else and barely side hi, and did not wear a smile nor seem very happy to work there.  Maybe the person was having a bad day or something.  A gym is supposed to be upbeat and positive energy and vibe.  I don't think I'll be back to this location even though its fairly convenient.  After seeing the facility I can say that the cleanliness was not a problem.  Some of the equipment is very nice, while other pieces are very old.  maybe 10+ years old and should be updated.  parking is ok, but plenty of trash on the ground!  Dang!  Hopefully management sees this review and get the parking lot cleaned.  First impression is often times a lasting impression; I don't want to step out of my car and step onto multiple pieces of garbage and what looked like to be remnants of an old dirty poopy diaper.

I'm not one to complain about Vietnamese restaurants as I don't expect much but I'm slightly suspicious this place is a front lol.  They did not provide us with bean sprouts, mint, or lime.  Nor did they have any chilli sauce at all at any of the tables.  Just very odd as I'm pretty sure those are all standard ingredients in pho.. lol. Also the they were quite chincey on the meat and the broth tasted like nothing except some sugar. Which I appreciated as it had literally no taste to it.  My girlfriends rice was hard and chewy as if it were 3 days old LOL. Oh yeah she got sick from that night until the next day from her food.

Oh boy, I had such high hope for Uchiko since it blew me away the first time I had it when I used to go to UT. So when I came back with my friends celebrate a birthday, I really hyped it up for the group. For short - Do NOT waste your money on the Chef's Tasting menu - instead, order from the actual menu.

As many people have raved about the Chef's Tasting menu at Uchiko, we decided to "Go big or go home" and give it a try with our group. Usually, we'd love Omakase or Tasting Menu since the chefs would be presenting the best/signature dishes in a most creative order, to create an experience for the guests. However, I felt that Uchiko's Tasting Menu was just slapping on average dishes from different sections of the menu without much thought. There wasn't even a list for us to really know the dishes contain as the waiters/waitresses spoke as quick and as soft as they could, so sometimes we just tried the food blindly. 

Overall for the Tasting menu: everything was average (from the Crudo to raw oysters to the suhi). The worst item was the sushi roll - the look was comparable to the taste. The best items were the Chutoro sashimi (melted on my tongue yummy!) and the Peach Okashi (light and refreshing).

Usually you should be full after having a tasting menu--but we actually had to order items off the menu to satisfy our hype for the night. But actually, I was glad we did, because the remaining dishes of the night tasted fantastic, and my face as a foodie was saved! We really enjoyed the Short rib, Pork belly, Brussel sprouts - they were delishhh!!! The foie gras and otoro nigiri were amazing as well! And of course, the Milk & Cereal dessert was out of this world! :) 

It was quite strange that one of our friends got a really bad stomach ache towards the end of the meal - seems unlikely to have been the dishes at Uchiko since everyone else was fine, but I did have to tap into my pharmacy knowledge running to the pharmacy after our meal was over to rescue the poor guy!

Tl;dr: Overall, it was such a disappointment to have tried the tasting menu. I would stick to ordering from the menu!

WOW.  This place is like an old girlfriend you used to date but then you dumped her because she was boring even though she was cute and then years later you see a photo of her on facebook and you think "WOW She got FAT!!!!  And UGLY!!!"  And we all know what that's like, right?  Right guys?  Fat ex-girlfriends?  Dodge the bullet?
-
I played here last weekend.  I had a really nice time but holy smokes this place is overpriced.  A lot of damaged fairways and greens.  It was just utterly unloved.  The holes are all right - none of them were particularly memorable.  I only played the front nine.  But wow.  I mean I'm not going back here unless I have to and since none of my friends have the guts to play golf - then forgetabout it.
-
Although they do make a nice turkey club at the little bar/restaurant on-site.

Ok this is probably an Austin thing and everybody thinks it is so cool.  You drive up and find there is very little parking and you are going to order your crepe from an old air stream trailer in a dirt lot.  You are going to sit outside in Austin's delightful104 degree heat with 95% humidty and don't go hungry. They only take cash and the drinks are not refillable and do not come with ice or in a glass and trust me you need lots to drink when you are baking out in the dirt parking lot sitting at a rickety little TV tray sized table on a folding chair that has seen better days.  Then after a extremely LONG wait you get your crepe.  It is ok but the best crepe this side of France?  I think not.  As I said don't be really hungry or plan on ordering two and spending 15.00 or so for them.  The drinks do not come with ice so in the wonderful Austin desert like heat it gets hot long before your food is prepared.  If you are dressed for work it is a disaster as you sweat through your clothes that you then get to stay in all afternoon long.  This may be an Austin experience but like everything else in this town it leaves a whole lot to be desired.

Yelp claims it's economical, but $30 for a two items with no drinks is only economical by Los Angeles standards --- that makes sense, since this is ultimately a Los Angeles chain started by a couple white dudes who once visited the middle east. In my experience, Doner meat should be crisp, carved off the spit to order and served with just a hint of sizzle on the edges, but all the meat here is soggy, like it's been soaking in fluid for hours. This was not ideal.
The decor is trying hard to be hip, but the result is pretty unwelcoming. Uncomfortable furniture, jumbles of lights clumped together hanging from an exposed surge protector and a rat's nest of cables, and artwork with theme or style. Pretty underwhelming. Tastier, and more economic, options are available food carts all over town. Don't bother giving these Californians your money. I don't think they deserve it.

I recently got a house inspection from Tiger.       I chose Tiger because i saw good reviews on yelp and other sites similar to yelp.  Most importantly, the inspector i worked with was on vacation.  So i gave it a shot.  The inspector was decent but seemed a little half assed.  After the inspection, I was given a hand written report which I can hardly read the writing.  Assuming a typed report will be email to me but nope.  The inspector gave me a business card with his cell phone.  He even informed me if you have any questions please contact me.  I contacted the inspector the next day to ask him a question that the seller broker brought up.  The inspector didn't answer so I left a voicemail.  Never got a call back so Ive decided to call again the day after and left another message.  Again no call back.  That's unacceptable and unprofessional.  I would NOT recommend this company to any of my family and friends.

Because of a delayed flight, Southwest put me here. 
Customer service, shuttle service and proximity to the airport are a plus. 

However, here are a list of things that led me to leave the place even though it means I was signing up to spend the entire night at the airport.
1) room had a bad smell -1 star
2) couple of hair strands on the bed -1 star
3) as soon as I turned on the air conditioner, the smell got worse -1 star
4) my phone didn't have good reception. I was afraid to stay in the hotel I didn't like, and which had a bad phone reception. This didn't influence my rating, however this significantly effected my decision to check out of the hotel. 

I recommend doing basic renovations that improves the customer's stay significantly.

I was so excited to try out this restaurant since my husband loves eating pate. We thought their sandwiches would be reminiscent of the one he had in Paris since the reviews were so incredibly high. 

There was plenty of parking out in front around lunch time. The shop is pretty small but cute. It was rather busy around 1 pm. 

When it was my turn to order, I asked if their Brie cheese was pasteurized or unpasteurized. He said it was but I did a quick search on my phone to find out that it usually isn't. I also asked if they could cook my lunch meat either in a microwave or on a grill and his only reply was "we don't have a microwave" in a tone that it was beneath him if they did. I get that they are an artisan store and probably wouldn't have one but he made no effort of accommodating to my dietary needs. He should have asked another coworker if the cheese was pasteurized since it was important information to me rather than causally guess that it was. I shouldn't be ingesting unpasteurized cheese as a pregnant person. I was a little annoyed. They should really be more careful on what information they provide. 

The sandwiches were less than memorable. My turkey panini was dry and didn't have very good flavor. I could have made it at home myself in throwing some cheese, turkey and cranberries. I just didn't think it was too special to deserve 4.5 stars worth. In fact, I wished I went to panera bread since you at least get a soup with your sandwiches at their prices. My husband's pate sandwich was also disappointing since the bread was so hard. He said that his jaw and teeth hurt after eating the sandwich. Each bite was a battle with the bread. 

Overall, I was immensely disappointed with my lunch and surprised that Yelp was so far off the mark on this one.

This place is centrally located near any hospital you could dream of.  Therefore, expect a lot of ambulance sirens, which you actually get used to after a couple of hours.

My main issue with this hotel is the lack of customer service.  Only at one point did the concierge hail a cab for me and I gave him a tip because I didn't want to be completely rude.  However, the day we arrived, he saw us (two women) getting out of the cab and struggling with our luggage but didn't even go outside to offer to help.

The lady at the front desk was on the phone when we arrived to check-in and throughout our whole interaction, it seemed like she wanted to be somewhere else.

The rooms are basic, the beds are hard, and the bathrooms are somewhat small.  The only great thing about this hotel is that it is directly connected via elevator to the Longwood Galleria, which is a convenient collection of shops.

If you walk a few blocks (past Harvard Dental school) you can catch the T's Green Line, which I needed for some business.  The area itself seemed safe enough, I never felt threatened or uncomfortable.  You will see a ton of students and doctors or nurses running around in scrubs; I've definitely seen worse.

I lived in a Braden Fellman property for 2 years at their Springdale location in Decatur. The location was great, and the company was pretty responsive to urgent maintenance requests. The property could have been great, but the general location of the place was definitely lacking. The roof was leaking in several locations (stains on ceilings) which resulted in moisture issues in the place that was extreme even for Atlanta. It smelled like a basement, and I had to buy a dehumidifier after many of my belongings developed mildew. The company was aware of the issues, but only offered mildew treatments, and no long term solutions to the problem.

Overall, Braden Fellman wasn't the worst, and my experience was mostly fine, but there are definitely much better options out there for the price.
