Edit: in response to the comment from Braden-Fellman below (just for the sake of more information), the mildew didn't become apparent until December (I moved in mid-August), so not totally an issue from summer heat/humidity. When I got my dehumidifier, the humidity said it was 70%. I mentioned this to my property manager at the time, but hopefully this will be useful if you decide to update the roof/window/any other sources of moisture.

Seriously, Roka? Rice does not come with the Vegetable Curry?? I paid $2 extra for tofu (over $12 for the dish) and you can't spring the 25-cents for a little thing of rice???  I eat here all the time (it's mighty convenient) but I may have to make more of an effort to BYO lunch. This is ridiculous.

While some things are tasty enough (the rice-less curry is even tasty, if seriously oily, and the sushi is usually quite decent) this place can be SERIOUSLY short-sighted.  Tons of form, light on function. 

(Ironically, one time I ordered the lo-mein and guess what? It came with a huge side of WHITE RICE, which made no sense at all but was good for a laugh.)

This is actually a brunch review.  I bought a Living Social deal for weekend brunch, and being avid brunchers we gave it a try.

They open at 9, we got there at 9:05.  There were already a few tables taken, but not many.  The hostess was nice and showed us to our seat right away.  Our waitress was nice and attentive.  

Plus: food was decent priced, portions were adequate. I had the veg benedict, it was OK - and veg, so yay there.

Minus: very few veggie options, decaf coffee wasn't brewed (really?  In the morning? On a Sunday?), "house potatoes" - yuck, were still partially frozen.  Hash browns are my crack so I was hoping, and sorely disappointed.  Pepper.  Black pepper.  TONS of it on the potatoes, and no salt.  So, um, I eat fire - so this isn't a "spice" thing, but black pepper is about the most boring seasoning and if it's there alone, and piles of it, it can be overwhelming.  Throw in a little salt for balance, or better yet some jalapenos?  No, just partially frozen, thick cut potato shreds with piles of pepper.  Yeck.  

Unfortunately, we won't be back - unlikely even for the bowling.

Boo. I should have known - I was  warned away from here, but I had to learn it for myself. 
We were told we'd have a 10-15 minute wait on a Thursday evening. So we hung out "downstairs" to munch on chips and salsa (free until 7). This place is poorly lit and super loud, so trying to make conversation before dinner was difficult. Our party (of 3, not difficult to accommodate) was seated after 25 minutes. This entailed struggling through the solid mass of people that populate the hostess station and bar area (likely also waiting for tables). The dining room was a little quieter, but the atmosphere was still pretty oppressive. Once seated we were asked if we were ready to order  3 times in the first 10 minutes. Yeesh, give us a minute to look at the menu!
I tried the Baja tacos with shrimp and a creamy jalapeno sauce. They were ok. It came with beans and rice on the side, but I hardly touched them, since they were old and not especially tasty. Beans and rice are prepared vegetarian, if that is important to you.
Once we finished eating, we didn't linger. 
Overall the service was fine, even with the poor start. Overall the food was fine, but generally uninspired and could be fresher. It was the atmosphere here that closed the door on a positive experience. There are hardly any windows and low light, plus it was jam packed with people yakking their heads off. The decor is meant to be zany, I think, but with all the other elements, is really just crazy inducing.

Marylou's earned their two star rating by having great service from their staff but the absolute worst coffee I have ever had. It was not strong, very watery, and hardly had any flavor. We got an iced coffee with blueberry cinnamon crumble and another one with cinnamon hazelnut. Both taste like water!! We also got a pistachio muffin that was great. But spending $10 on two waters and a muffin isn't right. 
I would have liked to given more stars because the staff was kind and the muffin was excellent but as a coffee shop, I really feel that the coffee should be much better.... It really was awful... 
This is the third time coming to this location and all three times I have been disappointed and will not be coming back. I'll stick to my Starbucks, Honey Dew, and Market Basket coffee.

The old school atmosphere from the 50's outfits the servers wear to the red leather chair decor is awesome. The atmosphere gets 5 stars all the way. Everything else is 'OK' at best. The service is slow. Their grits and Waldorf salad are actually quite good. Everything else was average at best. 

OK Cafe offers a lot of healthier alternatives and organic options which is fairly unusual for the area but they loose any health benefits on some heavily over salted foods.

They do have a seperate take out section of the restuarant with a full bar of take out items.  

Overall, OK Cafe totally lives up to its name.. OK

I was looking forward to trying this place as I had seen it plenty of times driving by and when dining next door at Chuy's. A friend and I decided to give it a try for our weekly Wednesday dinner and I was very disappointed. The restaurant itself it nice, it's very modern and trendy. My only complaint about the set up is that it is very dark in the dining room. It was almost hard to read the menu. The few lights they do have have these wicker shells around them which block most of the light. 

I got there first as my friend was running late from an appointment. I was seated right away because they were not very busy and our waiter asked what I wanted to drink. Once he brought the drink he never came back to the table, I was starving and would have liked to order an appetizer to enjoy while waiting on my friend. I sat there for 30 min til she arrived and not once did he reappear to ask if I wanted something while I waited. I figured once she arrived he would come back finally, wrong! We waited another 15 min before finally asking the hostess as she was passing by if she could please find out waiter. He never appeared, another waiter came by and said she would take our order because they weren't sure who our waiter was?? Once we ordered he finally came by after another 10 min to ask if I wanted a drink refilll. I had been there about an hour by the time he reappeared. Once our appetizers finally arrived they were ok, the avocado egg rolls were decent, but the deviled eggs were very runny almost like a soup was places in the eggs.  The runner who finally brought our meals to our table apologized for the wait because the kitchen was "really backed up," strange since the place was pretty empty and It's an open kitchen so we could see our meals sitting under the heat lamp for well over 20 min. My pasta was luke warm by the time it was brought to our table which really ruined the meal. We finished eating and it was another long wait for the waiter to bring us our checks he kept walking right past us but not acknowledging us at all. Once he brought the check he set them down and said, "ok I just want you guys to do one more thing, have a great evening." It was nice of him to say but was weird for him to be saying parting words, when he still needed to return to get our cards and run them. We wondered if he was gonna come back. I don't think he intended too until he noticed us still sitting there waiting 20 min later. I think the restaurant has potential to be good, but this experience did not make me want to give it another try. I felt like I had been there all afternoon, by the time I left.

Did not even go in because the bouncer was so rude. He gave us a hard time with our ids, though there was no line behind us. He also made a rude comment when he noticed we were from Los Angeles. After his rude response when we asked him if ESPN was on, we decided to leave. (Keep in mind, we still hadn't entered the bar.) As we turned around, he yelled "Now you want to leave? whatever!" As visitors in this town, we were disappointed. He may have been trying to be funny, but he came off as insulting and rude.

My fiancé and I were so very much looking forward to supporting this restaurant and business- so much so that we make a reservation almost a full week in advance to dine in their newly transformed tavern in the tent! We were so excited that the tavern was offering an outdoor eating option! We stalked the menu almost everyday, and looked forward to our Friday night date night reservation. Even better- the weather was perfect and the view of Boston is unmatched. Well after a week of anticipation, we finally made it to our reservation and the tent was empty. We knew something wasn't right. We walked in the restaurant and the (very nice) hostess said that there was an electrical problem and the tent was closed. We were very confused. All I ask for is a courtesy call to let us know about the situation. I am VERY disappointed we didn't receive that. Even an email would have sufficed. We aren't comfortable eating indoors yet, so we left. We know times are tough, but a phone call should have been made. Very disappointing.

The selection is wonderful. The service
 was less than stellar. And I didn't like paying 7$ for one cup of tea! I bought a three ounce pack of tea (I'm guessing 3, it doesn't say on the package) for 7$ and said I'd also like a warm cup of that same tea - I was charged 7$ again , the price of the packet. When I asked about it, because I thought she had accidentally charged  me twice , she said 'oh - that's a special tea so we charge the same price as the packet.' I'm sure I'll get 3 or 4 cups out of the 7$ packet I bought! Not cool.

I went to Torchy's about 4 months ago.  Didn't like it then so I decided to I would go again to maybe go with less expectations but I still think the Tacos are a little less than average.    I wouldn't call myself a taco expert but I've been eating tacos since I was a boy.

First thing you want to do is smell the tortilla(smelling it gives you an idea of the freshness and tastefulness of the tortilla), then taste the meat, wetherer beef or chicken, and then taste the extra stuff.   The tortilla failed the test, the meat was average and the extra stuff(like salsa, cheese,etc.) was decent.

Our cab driver recommended that we try this place (she said it was better than franklins).  We went in and there was a Buffett to pick your sides out.  We went with the mac and cheese and coleslaw.   Ordered some brisket and the beef rib.   Since the bone was so large the beef rib was VERY expensive for what it was. 

I can say from eating franklin the day before that this brisket here was not good at all! It was very dry and chewy.  The beef rib was good but not worth the price tag.  Sides were nothing to write home about.  Disappointing experience for the cost.

I went for lunch yesterday and I found this place to be just ok. I ordered the green curry asked for it as spicy as they could make it and I still had to add crushed red peppers and chili sauce to make it spicy. Also the curry paste they used just didn't seem to have much flavor to me seemed kinda bland. I guess maybe I had higher expectations after reading some of the comments here. I hope I can find better thai food in the area if not I guess this place will have to do.

What are all these people giving four stars???
One person even said it was the best asian restaurant in town?????

Are you nuts?

As my Lord, Jesus said. "Forgive them God, for they do not know what they do...."

Amen!


This place is a very forgettable place.  Sorry New Englanders.  You don't know good hibachi, nor good Japanese restaurants.

This place is packed with people and you would think the food is good.

NO.

The restaurant is owned by Chinese people who pretend like they know what Japanese food tastes like.


I'm from NY where the food and service better be good or you pack up and leave.


Even the moderately good Hibachi places have better Hibachi chefs. 

All who are interested should check out real Hibachi chefs.

The only highlight for me was that on Valentine's day, my girlfriend was given a rose(as was all ladies).  

Don't waste your money on the Hibachi.

If you have a girlfriend who has never been to a Hibachi, you can impress her and trick her into thinking you took her to some fancy place.

but trust me....this place is like Burger King pretending to be Red Robin.


save your money. save your time.  save your pride.

Lack-Lucster. You're first welcomed by giant chalkboards yelling at you what "don't" and "can't" do. Why not just sit people with a menu? People are packing in trying to figure it out, and when you do the host says "Do you know how to order?" Then you place your order and you're told to get get your own chopsticks, silverware and water. Why? 

The pho is not authentic and bland. In my opinion, if you're going to be a soup nazi (from Seinfeld) then you'd better have some damn fine soup. I'd like to say that they do, but if you've eaten there you know they don't. Cloudy dull tepid broth. Dense balled mat of noodles. Crudely cut rubbery brisket. You know the paper thin rare beef that's supposed to be on top? All grey and lumped in the bottom. The herbs on the side were paltry and oddly stacked so the bean sprouts covered the sprig of basil, lime, and very largely cut jalapeños. This ensures that you have to dig around to get to the then soaked in water herbs. I will on a positive note say I think they make their own meatballs. This is applaudable, but I also know that it's most likely a powder they mix with the unsold tendon.

The place seems to popular. Lots of folks taking pictures of their food. I just think it's good that they take their pics before they eat, because I doubt they'd be that happy about after. Or maybe they're just gluttons for punishment?

Two stars, because they at least served me my food.

My recent experience is based on ER experience.
My whole family had some good time at ice-rink skating. Unfortunately, my wife fell on the ice and it was so unlucky. From pain and quick arm check - it looked like she had an elbow fracture.
So, we quickly left the rink, took 2 our kids and departed to Vancouver General Hospital. At arrival, nurse without any empathy told me - you'll have to wait 4 hours to see the doctor.
I didn't see lots of people with broken arms or legs. I was really unpleasantly surprised with such quick assessment.
So, we left and went to St. Paul hospital. For some reason, staff there gave us fast track and we've seen the doctor after 40 mins. Feel the difference. I'll never visit GVH and won't recommend it neither.

Off and on I have been coming here for years, i do like the taste of the pastries, but the barista training over the years has been sub par. In my previous profession, I trained and taught baristas the skills they would need to work behind an espresso machine. I would be willing to bet, they do not calibrate their thermometers, because If i order their milk chocolate mocha, and they serve it to me below 135 degrees, that is just unsatisfactory. I am not a baby who wants a tepid drink and for safety reasons you want that mocha hovering between 150 and 160, as it also tastes better. I was served warm chocolate milk. I asked for it extra hot, it was written on the cup, 180 degrees. It didnt even get close 140, as i was able to drink it down in 2 minutes. You might ask how could i know this with out a thermometer? Well when an individual has made as many lattes, aulaits, macchiattos as i have, you can tell. I can pace myself when my beverage is 160 because if i tried to gulp it down it would burn my mouth, at 180, it basically will fry my tongue and render my tastebuds useless for the rest of the day. Now when I pay over 5 dollars including tip, I expect more. The girl at the counter was lacking in customer service skills, especially when I asked for the bathroom key. She just gave me an annoyed look and only said "Make sure you bring it back." Next time try saying when you get done, if you wouldnt mind bringing it back to the counter it would be appreciated. Try smiling. Please Please, stream and properly aeriate you milk and get it to the sweet spot between 150 and 160.

My husband and I had dinner here during restaurant week and we were quite disappointed. We made reservations, got seated right away, but our waiter did not come around for 30 minutes. Took 90 total for the main course, and the restaurant wasn't even that busy. The portions were smaller too so it would have been a better deal to order from the main menu. Additionally, the bread came out after our first course , which seemed weird. Finally, in recognizing our long wait, we were offered a free appetizer voucher for our next visit. The table next to us was offered this before they ordered. We will not be coming back to use the voucher. Compared to other restaurants during restaurant week, McCormick and Schmicks was not up to par. 2 stars is given for food only -- everything tasted good, which is expected.

The food is great. They have Lobster Mac & cheese that that is not on the menu, but it is phenomenal. My complain is not about their delicious food  but rather  customer service.

Incident 1) I was ordering twice a week (I know I am chubby) but they keep forgetting the soda. Last time the delivery guy said, I will be right back and never came back, I called twice and they kept me waiting and never came (I can't have dinner without soda, it ruins the experience). I called the next day (it is about the principle more than the actual soda) they were not apologetic, and told me that if I want my soda, they will deliver between 4-5PM because they get busy after that.  Really ticked me off so I hang up.

Incident 2) My wife loves their delicious grill chicken dinner so now we order pick up from my phone because she is afraid to order from hers (that's where I argued from regarding the soda).  I know I have an accent but I am not hard to understand at all. I order a grilled chicken dinner and she was like, what you want fish. She kept asking me to repeat myself like 10 times and at the end she still didn't get my order right. I corrected her and she gave me some serious attitude.  

Although we love their food, I told my wife that we are done with Nicks. Too bad because we were spending about 250 a month so about 3K a year. I know it is probably a drop in the bucket for them but I won't go to them out of principle.

They really do judge a book by its cover here.  I am always getting the newest products, but every time I come here I can't get any service.  I imagine it has something to do with them hitting numbers.  That is why a lot of people have mixed feelings about most tech shops.  I was not told how long my wait would be or that they could text me and I come back while everyone after me was told that.  I am guessing they just want me to switch to Android.  I will not.

Really wanted to love this place but I was sadly disappointed with their food. They are still in their soft opening, so only two pages are available for food.

Walking up to the restaurant I was in love with all the decor, definitely throwing the Miami vibes with candy skull art, neon art and faux grass walls. A cute little sign next to the front door, "Feed me tacos and tell me I'm pretty". Inside the space looked almost the same from the old Carmel (the restaurant in this space before), although there were a few cool additions, the funky art, cool blue toned walls and an impressive black and white mural on the right wall.

A friend and I visited for lunch, we were given the menus and were told only the small menu was available. Chips and salsa were a given, points for that lol

Since we only had limited options, I just went with the quesadilla, I know in these fancier Mexican restaurants tacos can be on the small side. My hope was to get a more satisfying meal than small tacos but to be frank even my quesadilla was a kids portion size for $11. It was accompanied with a small lettuce, side of salsa and sour cream. It was so unbelievably thin, I thought it was just a cheese quesadilla, the cheese they used was almost nacho style, really runny when biting into it. The dish presentation was really sad.

My friend ordered four tacos, she tried the Chicken Al Pastor, Lava Shrimp, BBQ Pork Belly and Chorizo. Although the tacos weren't too small the filling in each of these tacos were really scarce and cold. I only tried a bite of her shrimp taco and it was really chewy with a poor consistency.

Service was very attentive though, always asking if we needed anything or if we needed more water. I'd give this place 4 stars for the overall vibe and sevice but I'd rate the food as 1 star. Hoping the food will improve once the full menu is available.

My family and I always come to Thumbs Up, but the Marietta St. location is our usual. We just wanted to avoid the midtown traffic since the SuperBowl is in town. This location was not at all like the Thumbs Up we know and love. No one was there to greet us and we stood around for about five minutes before finding the sign in sheet. Also, our waitress was very abrupt and not very warm unlike at the Midtown location. The food was okay, but I'm vegan and I didn't feel that there were a sufficient amount of options. THE WORST PART of my experience this morning was that a ROACH was on the booth behind my brother and we were seated close to the kitchen, so who knows what it was like in there. We were all disgusted and had to leave immediately. The only reason for a second star is because we were served really quickly. We'll be sure to stick to the Marietta Street location from now on.

First time eating here. I ordered a breakfast burrito and cinnamon roll to go. Cinnamon roll looked very different from your typical cinnamon roll which is due to a different flour they use. The cinnamon roll was gross and the bread was tuff and they used a cream cheese frosting which I really didn't like. I was very disappointed in my "burrito". On the menu it says the burrito comes with corn, bell peppers, eggs, beans, and corn. It was basically two small tortilla shells with eggs and corn inside and a little bit of cheese sprinkled on top of them. The beans where thrown on the side of my to go box on the brown liner (they could have placed them in a cup). I literally only seen two small chunks of bell pepper inside my tortilla shell. It was tasteless and soggy. I was very disappointed to have spent 14.00 on this meal. I won't be eating here again. Also parking is a hassle.

With all the great reviews I was super excited to try this place out . However I was greatly unsatisfactory with the Ramen I got . The place was not busy whatsoever when I walked it . And had a table for 2 people. The ramen was not even that hot . The broth had no flavor. I didn't get a seasoned egg , so there was literally nothing in the bowl except for noodles,plain steamed corn , onion and two pieces of very fatty pork. Usually when I eat ramen I like to slurp the broth, it's my favorite part but I just had no desire to, the broth tasted like nothing and it was really thick and grey . Spent 55$ there and my friend and I both agreed it wasn't really worth it . Left the restaurant honestly looking for somewhere else to get a snack from before going back home.

Short and sweet.

Abu Omar is just okay. The evening I visited the truck, they seemed to be out of half their menu. The menu which has no prices and isn't complete. :/

Also there was only one person working who took large breaks from making food to take orders... slowly even though other people were waiting for their food.

Chicken shwarma had a bit of odd texture...  likely being overcooked at a low temperature.

Also they use a grilled tortilla style bread rather than a pita which was unexpected and not preferred. 

I didn't hate the wrap but I won't be back either. 

Every truck isn't for everyone.

Kind of a cool restaurant with outdoor dining.  Fun place to have a drink after work. But don't go with kids - they don't have a kids menu. Don't order a frozen margarita - that "insults the authentic nature of the experience" according to our waitress. But they serve fajitas - the most Americanized and least authentic menu item in "Mexican" restaurants. And, if you don't like the wait staff petting one of the many dogs in the restaurant immediately before being handed your food, well tough. 

Is the food pretty good? Yeah, but I'd prefer my Mexican food without a side of pretentiousness and dog hair. 

We're still looking for great Mexican in Lake Mary. F&D Cantina ain't it.

This location has really let its standards go down hill. Naturally you can still purchase all Targets typical items. 
What is needing attention is the cleanliness. 
2 different employees were in the bathroom while I was in there. The first was washing her hands when I came in and left, the second came in used facilities and left while I was clearly taking photos. 
Neither of them seemed concerned with the state of this raunchy bathroom. 
The parking lot was also littered and appeared to have not been tended to in quite some time. 
It is not a pleasant situation to have to use a public bathroom as it is. To add to it overflowing toilets, dirty used toilet paper all over the floors and toilet seats, water on floors etc simply lazy. This is an insult to your customers Target.. You can do much better.

Looks like I should have tried the sushi!

There is a definite bait and switch with the rest of the menu. My husband and I ordered Pork Katsu and Yaki Soba, but we got Chinese food. I like Chinese food, but not when I'm trying to order Japanese food and moreso not when the food is just meh while being quite expensive. The Pork Katsu was flat and tasteless with a sweet n sour sauce rather than bulldog (Japanese BBQ) sauce and the Yaki Soba was an odd chicken lo mein (Chinese brown sauce) made with soba noodles. Not good, and I won't even bother coming back to try the sushi.

Maybe I'm a masochist for trying out very "traditional Americanized" Chinese restaurants, but part of it reminds me of my childhood. At any rate, I dragged my boyfriend to this place, and the experience was very subpar.

After getting seated in the corner, it took them about 10 minutes to come back and take our order. Okay, whatever, you have a lot of takeout orders. I guess I can forgive that.

After ordering, it was a good 15 - 20 minutes before getting the food. I know how a wok works, so it shouldn't take that long unless you're prepping your ingredients alongside. Maybe it's the amount of takeout orders slowing it down, but who knows?

We finally get our order of almond chicken and mapo tofu with two tiny bowls of rice. The food's pretty decent, though you can definitely taste the "cheapness" of the chicken. The mapo tofu was pretty solid; using black bean paste in the recipe is a nice variation. As other reviewers have mentioned, the portions are huge, so we easily had leftovers for the next night. 

After some more waiting, we finally got our check, and to our shock, we were charged for two tiny bowls of rice for $1.00 each. I can forgive waiting exceedingly long for service, and I can overlook the flavor in the chicken. I cannot accept them not informing us that rice cost extra.

tl;dr: If you do take-out, which I would probably recommend over the dine-in experience, make your own rice.

Visiting town and thought I'd stop by since I've heard good things about their ramen. The experience was sub par. 

We waited for over half an hour for a table while people who came in after us were seated before us.  We weren't given any napkins or utensils with our food--we ended up walking up to the counter to grab it ourselves. For the entire meal, we didn't get any attention after our food was given. We walked up to the counter to refill our waters ourselves and nobody came by to ask if we wanted more of our other drinks. 

After we got our checks, it took another 20 minutes for them to process our cards. There was a lady who was waiting for a seat for a good portion of an hour--she could have easily taken our seat if they had processed our cards quicker, but she ended up just walking out when they would not seat her at one of the already open tables. 

The food was decent, but boy, I hope their service isn't always like this.

The food is okay other than the obvious fun Chipotle staff seems to have pouring on loads of sour cream but stingy on $2 guacamole. The total experience is not so good. Once I decided I was going to eat in I went to grab a seat- inside. EVERY SINGLE TABLE is dirty. Very nasty. I managed to grab a corner of a table without crumbs since I am so hungry but it does not feel clean in here. I am here on 7/22/17 at 3:55pm. Not a customer in line and only myself eating. Several staff standing around and no one has cleaned a single table in the 30 minutes that I've been here. It will be a while before I come back, if ever. I am huge on a clean eating experience and prefer not to have the remnants of other people's food in sight or on my arms. You all will have to get it together in this location.

Also known as Shannon Beach.
Pros-Has free parking, although highly competitive. Be prepared to circle many times for a spot. Ice cream truck along grassy side bank was super cute. Does have bathrooms, though not the cleanest. Nice sand although beach is on the smaller side. Not a far walk from lot to beach.
Cons-No lifeguard. No rules seemed to be enforced. We saw two cop cars in the lot when we left, unclear why. Highly packed beach of chaos. Loud music/people chain smoking on and near the beach. Lots of yelling swearing conversations, hard to relax. Multiple kayaks and large floats (someone had a four person float in the water) in the same area where people are swimming. When we went, the water even out fairly deep was completely mirky brown with what looked like floating wood chips from a playground-other reviews note similiar observations of the water. Roped off area is small, you can swim outside of it into the lake.

We were heading to Disney for a couple of days so I asked my husband to book us a water park hotel (just stayed at one the previous month in Orlando). He found this on a booking site and it looked like fun. 

When we got here they said we didn't have to pay the $13 resort fees, which we thought we had to pay, based on the booking site. So that was a perk, but we soon discovered nothing is really free unless you do their sales pitch breakfast.

We had a renovated room which was really nice, had some ants and was an odd shape since it was in the corner, but we liked it.

We planned to spend check in day at the water park. 6pm we walk over there to be told it's $20 a person to get in and they close at 7! 

We went back to the pool next to our room.  It was nice and warm, but wasn't the waterpark we anticipated.

I am self employed and went to answer emails really quick and found that you must pay $10 per device to log in. We weren't told this. 

I needed to call the front desk and found the phones, while connected, had no dial tones. This probably saved us from sales pitches though!

The bed was super hard and killed my back.

Also our room overlooked the pool on the ground floor and the master room only has blinds, not black out curtains, which made it hard to sleep-in with the 24/7 lights lighting up the pool and yard areas.

The tram to the theme parks seamed like a great perk, but you can't come back on any tram headed here, if you get on the 10am to the park, you have to come back on the 6pm tram, you can't take the later one.

Our building seamed half full if that, bit parking spots at night were hard to come by.

The room was a great price on goseek.com, $62, but we were expecting a lot more based on the listing. They should have been more up front about fees, we would have gladly spent $20-30 more per night for a hotel that had a water play area.

When I first dined at Nava in 2009, the prickly pear margarita contained alcohol, the food was good and the blue cornbread served hot.  However, on my most recent visits earlier this year I was disappointed.  The prickly pear margarita tasted like it contained a store bought, pre made mix.  The bread was not brought to the table until after the entrees arrived and the bread tasted stale and was cold.  The cheese dip was full of grease.  It was basically cheese melted in the oven and served with tortillas.   The service has declined during each visit. The patio chairs had bird poop stains and there are too many bugs out there during the summer. The bugs flew into the food, drinks, and into my face.  The lamb taco was my only reason for returning but the prices do not justify the slow service, sugary drinks, and flavorless food.

Had a Groupon but didn't catch that we needed to make a reso. I never sit at a table and only at the bar anyway at restaurants so even if I did know, I still probably wouldn't have made one since what restaurant takes resos for the bar?
The server made it seem like she just conquered the world in order to be able to serve us using the Groupon without a reso, and also seemed really pissed. Would mention things like "your food is going take a very very very long time."  ok got it lady lol we are still sorry! We knew what we wanted to order before even getting to the restaurant, but she wouldn't take our order right away because I think she still wanted us to feel indebted to her lol.
Anyway long story short it took an hour and a half to get a pizza and everyone around us who sat down (without resos) wayy after us got served before us.
I get that Groupons are annoying but the point is to get new customers back in the door, which won't happen for us.
I'm really not one to care about the service at restaurants because I go to eat the food, not make friends or judge people's character behind it, but this experience was actually quite awkward enough to ruin the restaurant for me.
2 stars because I was starving and the food filled me up, despite the pizza being as thin as a piece of printer paper.

I have been a regular patron of Earls for years and have had a love hate relationship. Just visiting them last week with my brother. We were there for lunch i should note. I had the kung pao chicken and a beer. I am  very versed on value for money and quality is not cheap. I am shocked to see some noodles and rice with a little spice and a few chunks of chicken for $33. Plus the obligatory 20% for the hot little thing in the tight dress. I must say they do hire smart funny and very cute wait staff. But wayyy overpriced food. If you are looking for value don't go here.

I am new to Georgia and was nervous about starting over with a new dentist. I had a routine checkup and cleaning back in February at the Roswell location. Everything went extremely well. The staff was very friendly and accommodating! I left that appointment feeling relieved about finding such a great team. 
Last week I went to the Buckhead location after a piece of my filling fell out. The office was great at getting me an appointment right away. Once again, the staff was very warm and welcoming. After the x-rays and exam, I was presented with a bill and told that 100% was due upfront. Apparently they charge their patients upfront and then file the insurance claims. I was not made aware of this. I left that appointment disappointed and unhappy. Now I am back to where I started and looking for a new dentist.

While the food was quite good, this restaurant definitely has some growing pains it needs to get over if it wants first time customers to come back. We were first time customers this weekend and we won't be going back. We pre-paid for our food at the counter and dropped a generous tip in the tip plate which I wish we could take back, as half an hour later, we still had no food. Two of the self serve soft drink spigots were out of order and the root beer came out as soda water. I mentioned it to one of the servers and she said they would refill the root beer in a couple of minutes. It still hadn't been refilled in the half an hour it took to get our food. We spoke to a manager about the long wait and he was appropriately apologetic, saying they just put a coupon out and did not expect the response they got. While the restaurant appeared fairly busy, it did not seem to be filled up and we've never had to wait this long at similar restaurants in the area with the same type of crowd. As I said at the beginning, the burgers were pretty good, but if you go, take your chances on the service.

If we had seen the 71 posted food score, we would have walked out. We noticed it too late! Ordered child's noodles with butter only, no cheese, came loaded with cheese, so we had to wait for a corrected order. I ordered fettuccine with Primevera sauce, completely inedible! Dry, no flavor, pasta was gummed together. The chicken panini was super thin, like eating a cracker. Also had chicken Marsala & mushroom ravioli with 4 cheese sauce. This was the only good dish.

This Cactus Club doesn't do happy hour. Super disappointing. 

We sat on the patio and the patio really doesn't get any breeze from the glass which makes it pretty uncomfortable, even at just 20 degrees. The server told us once you order you can't move inside lol. We shortly found out why! Our service was also terribly slow. 

It's the same food and same drinks as the other Cactus Clubs, but I think the prices are slightly higher. 

It's a nice view of the ocean.

Went last night to this store front on Burnett near Hancock.  We almost did not go in because there was nobody in there at all and it was 7:30PM.  The next door restaurant had at least 10 people. We almost went next door but I had been wanting to go to Man Bites Dog for a long time and decided to venture in anyway.  I ordered the Danger Dog, and the Pulled Pork Mac and Cheese.  First the Danger Dog was supposed to be wrapped in bacon and no bacon was found.  Other than that the Danger Dog was quite tasty and the bun and cheese complemented each other with the right amount of fresh and crunch engulfing a flavorful, juicy beef frank. One of the best gourmet hot dogs I have ever come across.  Now the Pulled Pork Mac and Cheese was less to be desired.  First, I am very disappointed when i find out that a restaurant uses fake cheese that is $H!% in a CAN.  Many people like it, and i do to when i get it from a cart on my nachos at a ball game but it really pulls out any quality a restaurant might have when they use that cheep, fake cheese.  Next the mysterious meat they said was pulled pork was mixed up in the cheese when it came out.  I think it would be better if they put the pulled pork on top.  The taste of the pulled pork with the fake cheese was not right and it really tasted like canned tuna fish.  Maybe I had ordered the Crap Cheese and Tuna Mac and did not know it.  Anyway if it were not for the bad experience with the Mac and Cheese I would have giving this cool trendy place a better review for the the great tasting Dog dressed up with the best condiments ever.  Well, yelp as always it is always a good indicator that if there is nobody in the place something is wrong.

We go here mainly because it is close by and has a playground for the kids to play on while you sip margaritas on the patio. The food is ok, but not outstanding. Some chicken dishes and beef dishes with a different sauce and name. I like the queso and and the enchiladas. Last week we went again and it was pretty bad. They had the server working all over the patio as well as inside. My biggest complaint is the kids meal- $7.00 for a bowl of macaroni! No side, no drink. With milk it was almost 9.00! We felt gouged, although when we complained she comped our queso. 
Go for the happy hour and then go somewhere else!

I walk past this place daily so I thought I would give it a try. It was a mistake I can't take back.

Services Done: Spa Pedicure & Dip Nails 

Pros: 
- They have wine and they don't water it down
- They always have availability 
- They have a large dip nail color selection 
- They didn't charge extra for not having nail kit

Cons:
- My Pedicure was essentially a polish change and cuticle cut. 
- The price went from $25 dollars to $30 while I was sitting there. 
- During my manicure she started using a dirty cuticle trimmer.
- All of my nails are misshaped now & uneven. 
- For a regular manicure and pedicure the price is $40 I wanted the dip manicure and my total was $75. When I asked why it was $35 more for dip (poorly done dip) she couldn't really answer. I've never paid $45 for dip at any salon I've ever been to and this salon was certainly not worth it. 

The staff was nice, I appreciate that they got me in quickly but be prepared to over pay and to not love your nails.

Well I'm planning to go on vacation in about a week and went to L5P for some shopping! My first stop was Cherry Bomb, because I have shopped there in the past and they tend on having cute pieces. Some pieces are a bit overpriced. 

Well when I entered the store the staff was not very friendly and watched everyone like a hawk. They even patted down a customer before she left the store. It took the fun out of my shopping experience. 

I ended spending a good amount in L5P but not in this store.

The service as others have said is pretty terrible.  First the hostess was nowhere to be found.  There were plenty of servers at the empty bar who saw us but paid no heed (the only people that acknowledged us were the guys who cut the meat).  Had the same run in as Carlos with the tall blonde waitress.  She was rude and unhelpful.  When I was there last they had a list of non-alcoholic drinks but when I asked her she said they had no list and did not offer any suggestions as to what they had.  Had to wave her down for anything whereas the table next to us seem to get her undivided attention.  The meat is still good but it seems like their salad bar, which failed to impress last time, had gotten even worse.  The service by the guys walking around with the meat was great, the rest of the staff could really learn from them.

Okay I was pretty disappointed.  I only went because of all the hype on this place.  Food was mediocre at best.  If your here simply because it's a historical landmark then take your picture out front, browse the gift shop, then go eat somewhere else and save some $$ because this place is expensive.  My fish was over cooked and not very exciting, desert was boring and cold.  The only thing I had that was decent was the oysters on the 1/2 shell and my glass of water.

I heard great things about this place, but I can't say I will go back.  I had the ribs, and they were tough.  The flavor was okay, but overall, this was quite disappointing BBQ.  The ribs were tough.  A barbeque place that cannot cook ribs well is not a good barbeque place.  I didn't try the brisket, but a friend with me did, and he was thoroughly unimpressed with it as well

I have enjoyed barbeque in the Boston area before.  I would go to another place if you are looking for good barbeque (or a good dinner).

Went here for father in law birthday. The selection is very small and the food isn't that hot. Took the food prep forever to refill the food. Probably did this on purpose. The hot food was bland and some dishes were very salty. The dessert selection was sad. Pudding, jello, banana with a red sauce and a few fruits. The sushi section was okay. For $16.99 per person I expected soft drinks to be included but it is extra. The servers looked like they hate their jobs. Don't know if I will be back but this place has potential if they actually listen to customers  comments.

I enjoy going to concerts at most venues, but not the Biltmore. Every time I hear of a band I like coming to town and then see they are playing there I let out a long sigh as if to resign myself to having to be in that space. Knowing if they played somewhere else the experience would be so much better. 

Perhaps part of the problem is that this space does not appear to have been designed for playing concerts. The stage is centered between two hallways which lead to the washroom facilities. The stage itself is very low and is usually curtained along the sides.  Another issue I have is that the sound is ok when it is good and terrible when it is bad. I have actually left a concert early at this venue due how crappy a particular band I really like sounded. Trust me I need a good reason to leave a concert. Also, yes the décor is 'funky', but the space is also funky in the sense I don't want to touch anything. I would hate to see the place when the turn the ugly lights on. That and what is with the line up situation outside. More than once I have shown and there is a huge line up outside of people with and without tickets that isn't moving. Then have walked up to the front of the line feeling the daggers in my back from the people I pass to ask if it was ok to go in as I had a ticket. The door man quickly steps aside and lets us enter only to find out there is hardly anyone inside. They need to coordinate the front door a little bit better. A sign or two would suffice.

I do like how you can get up close and personal with the band. Although I have seen bands that look a bit uncomfortable and have commented during their performance on how distracting it is to see people walk past to the bathroom in their peripheral vision. However, the price must be right to put on a show here or groups wouldn't keep coming back. That and the bar tenders are always fast and efficient and the selection isn't half bad or overpriced.

Menu looked amazing.  I ordered the seared tuna with fingerling potatoes special. Unfortunately had to send it back.  Was overcooked and tasted fishy. As much as I hated to do it, but after three bites I could not eat it, and I sent it back.  Second round was much better....properly cooked and not fishy tasting.  Now of they could just get the presentation better...it would be a great meal.   Good news...the waiter was fantastic and very accommodating.

P.s.  brussel sprouts we're AMAZING

New to the neighborhood, we'd been looking forward to trying Kome, hoping we could add it to our regular roster. Food was fine, but the behavior of the host and management made sure our first visit would be our last.

5:20PM on a weeknight, my wife arrives with two hungry, summer-heat-wilted teens. I'm on my way separately, about 10 minutes out. She asks to be seated and is refused (incomplete party). She asks again -- look, it's really empty; we're hot, hungry and tired, and really want to get our order in. Host consults with management. The verdict: "Yeaaaah ... that really STRESSES us, so ... no."

First ... we're a family of four. They'd seat the first three of us at a four-top anyway. It's not like we were a gaggle of office workers trickling in, pushing tables together and slowly expanding over two hours. And they're a small-plates restaurant -- ostensibly they WANT us to order more! So seat my family already and let them get started!

Second ... why should I care about (or even HEAR about, for that matter) the "stress level" of any restaurant, let alone a premium-priced one?

Finally ... you know what stresses ME out? Arriving to find my family huddled in the hot waiting area while 60% of the tables sit empty, no food on the way, and an awful lot of non-stressed staffers lining the walls.

Food was tasty, waitress was competent but distant. No manager stopped by to see how things were, nobody asked if we enjoyed our experience. Dropped our 75 bucks and left.

You know, you can love your policy, or you can love your customer. Thankfully, Austin is rife with other restaurants who go out of their way to let you know your business is appreciated.

I have been here about 10 times and I've felt increasingly disappointed with each visit. This weekend was their last shot with me. I have serious questions about the sterilization of their tools and the cleanliness of their work stations. I have never seen them actually take a tool from a sterilized packet or machine, they always just take them out of a drawer. The technicians are also pretty rude and aggressive with grabbing your fingers or shoving your hands down. It's like they hate you and this is how they get their feelings out?

I went a few weeks ago and was unhappy with my manicure immediately but the girl who did my nails was so rude I didn't feel comfortable saying anything. I went back (don't ask why) this weekend and a different rude girl did such a terrible job on my nails that I had no choice but to go back and get it fixed. The look on her face when I walked back in the salon was one of horror and disgust. Same girl, same. 

I'm done.

Not bad, but not the greatest. I've been able to be somewhat of a regular here by making friends with a few workers that help provide some of the services I need, but  other than those four, or so people, I haven't been able to get so much of a "hello" out of the cashiers, or people in electronics. They just usually walk by and pretend I'm not there. I've worked retail, and I understand it sucks sometimes, but that's no reason to ignore the customer.

I do like however, that they have been working to improve their market and grocery sections. I just wish that there was actually a tofu selection for those of us veggies. And more of a beer selection would be nice too. Also, the bathrooms could use some cleanliness work as well. I usually find toilet paper on the floor, and often chewing gum on the toilets themselves, so I have to wait until there is a clean toilet available.

I was pretty psyched about this place because of all the hype my friends gave it, so I decided to give it a try. I didn't know what to get but knew I wanted a wrap, so I decided to get the special they had of the day which was the lamb kabab.

When I ordered, I asked the cashier what was inside the kabab since I don't really tomatoes and what not. She told me there was lettuce, onions, and tomatoes, so I asked her to only put the lettuce inside with my kabab since I don't like raw onions or tomatoes. My boyfriend got the beef shawarma, and we also ordered hummus, an extra pita bread, and fries with the sauces on the side. After I finished paying, I looked at my receipt and saw she charged me for the lamb kabab on rice. When I went back to the counter to tell her, she said she would just change it to the kabab. I'm not sure how much the price difference is, but I feel like $9 for a lamb kabab is p pricey.

When I got my food, she forgot to give us the sauce on the side for the fries. Once I got home, I was pretty disappointed that the wraps weren't labeled. I basically opened it and hopped it was mine. Once I took the first bite of my lamb kabab, of course, there were onions, tomatoes, as well as cucumbers in my wrap. This would be absolutely horrific if I was actually allergic to any of those instead of just disliking it. Not only did the cashier get my order wrong and charge me for the lamb kebab over rice, she still got my order wrong and it had the onions, tomatoes, and cucumbers in there. As for the beef shawarma wrap, the meat was cold. It was so strange, but it was. It also didn't come with lettuce or anything. It was just the beef shawarma, tomatoes, and sauce. 2 stars. My boyfriend didn't even finish it because it was so below par (and he usually finishes everything including my food). The fries were okay. It wasn't crispy. It was p soft and p thick. The only thing I actually enjoyed was the hummus and pita bread. It had a nice flavor and creamy texture.

Tbh, the lamb kebab wasn't too bad, but I won't come back again because my order was wrong, the beef shawarma was cold, and the cashier honestly didn't pay attention to anything I said or asked for. This place has such good ratings, but for me, it was mediocre at best (which is a shame because my friends raved about it so much).

Just finished eating dinner at Asta and all I can say is HUH?
Service and ambience were 8/10, but the food was one of the most underwhelming we've ever had. 
My boyfriend and I came in an hour earlier than our reservation and were seated because the restaurant was quite empty. The waitress poured us some complimentary sparkling because it is the holidays after all and we were excited to start the meal.
We both had the 8 course tasting menu and it took roughly 2.5 hours from start to finish. The time between courses were long and the portion size was tiny (yes, tiny even for someone who can barely finish an entree size pasta at another restaurant).
The amuse bouche was salty, the turnip dish though garnished with truffle did not smell nor taste anything like truffle, and the venison was covered in burnt ash that was way too overwhelming and bitter. The cheese dish was great and I wish there was more since it was ONE ravioli. Apart from that, I can barely remember any other dishes because they all tasted the same. 
The menu was mostly vegetable dishes, actually, 6/8 were vegetarian.
I don't want to give such a bad review, but for $110 a head without drinks or tip, it is insanely overpriced. I have had 8 course dinner before for much less and the quality of food that I experience today at Asta is inferior to say the least. The vision was there but the food was not.
I hope they will change up the menu, or hopefully do something different to reflect their price point and vision, it's safe to say I won't be back any time soon.

4 star staff. Very nice and helpful.
Problem is in the establishments limitations.
The guy working behind the pins goes out the back door to smoke, but leaves the door cracked invade a lane gets stuck (doing his job well) but when the front door opens the air is suctioned into the lanes and we could smell the smoke the entire time we bowled!
The food was a typical cheap choosing. Not bad but nothing special, there are fewer lanes than the other bowling alleys in the area, making it the smallest option as well.
I wouldn't say don't go, but there are some better choices.... I WILL SAY, they have some great and unmatched specials. Like quarter night! So if you're ok with smoke the. It's maybe a 3.5 star for you

Tonight I had the worst service I have ever had at Spagio. First the server disappeared for 30 min after bringing us our drinks. Then our food took over an hour to come to the table. I ordered all of my food with no cheese as I am allergic and the server neglected to tell me that there was cheese in the meatballs in the pasta dish I ordered. Then it took him another 45 min after we had gotten our food to come clear our plates and leave the check. It was an incredibly disappointing experience at a place I usually love dining at. The server Josh should be let go.

I would give this restaurant a better review if It wasn't for a few issues. First: Do not sit near the Hostess Stand/ Server Bar Area, especially when they first open. All the employees clump together there to talk about what they did the night before after work and it gets very loud!!!! At one point there were 8 employees clumped together. Second: Do not let the server talk you into their house filtered bottled?? water. They put in into a Vero bottle and charge you $5.00, that is a rip off. Third: Do not let the server tell you that the starters are small and you will need 2 to 3 for a party of two. They are big enough to share.
What we ordered:
Pharmacy Manhattan- wasn't very good.
Caprese  Salad- Excellent
Caesar Salad- Excellent
Octopus & Squid Salad- Excellent
Skirt Steak- I would not order again, It was flavorless and chewy 
Pork & clam Alentejana- Excellent , I loved this Dish

Having only eaten Ethiopian food once before (at Addis Red Sea), I was excited to take the plunge again. A friend suggested trying Fasika at its new location after lamenting it's loss from JP, so we checked it out early on a Tuesday evening.

Just to reiterate what's already been said - the service is a little slow, but the food itself is fantastic. Unfortunately that in no way compensates for the Bizzaro World environmental battle between the bar and restaurant. Barely separated by a small divider, the place is an aural nightmare, with the bar's jukebox playing Rod Stewart, Boston, Def Leppard, etc. accompanied in full voice by the aforementioned besotted patron at the bar. Mildly amusing at first, then progressively grating. As if to compensate, the TV volume was on relatively loud - I kept expecting Brian Williams to stop his newscast to tell our singer to clam up. The (only) restaurant waitress was doe-eyed and charming while the bartender looked like she had cornered the market on peroxide and fake-tan-in-a-jar. Good food can only carry bad aesthetics so far.

I went to Frank Ski's on two different occassions.  The first time was at the bar.  The service was great, the appetizers were good.  Loved the happy hour!  However, the second time, there was not much to brag about.  I made reservations for a group of 10, during happy hour.  I knew we would not be able to get seats around the bar due to our group size.  But I did not know we could not take advantage of the happy hour prices sitting at a table.  We were told we could not get the prices at the table but if we ordered and paid for our drinks at the bar and then came back to the table we could get the happy hour prices...crazy.  The food was not that good.  The salmon was very bland.  The salmon at Longhorns is a lot better!  One of the people of the group order a piece of the chocolate and red velvet cake.  The cakes were very small, extremely small pieces, for $7 and not very good.  

As for the staff, they are very friendly.  We had some great service!  Not sure I will go back, if I do, I definitely will not be eating.

This is one of the messiest and poorly staffed Macy's I have ever been in.

I grew up with Dayton's and Marshall Fields.  Macy's has done a crap job of maintaining the bar that those 2 stores set.

It can be difficult to find help here.  In returning a pair of shoes, it took 20 minutes for a manager to come down and process my return that I ordered online.  20 minutes for a few extra buttons on the register.  Ridiculous.

They work on commission in the shoe department, and it shows.  You have to wait for the person who helped you to check out, so if you get Mr. Sales McSales, you end up waiting for an eternity to pay for your shoes.  Forget it,,,,I will order it online instead.

I have had good experiences in the jewelry department, and at the Lancome and Clinique counters.  The staff there is very friendly.  I had a person check me out at the Origins counter, for Origins product, and she barely said hello.  Let's just say that her makeup job did little to cover up the permanent snarl on her face.

Unfortunately had a pretty disappointing experience here my first go around. Ordered a 20 oz Americano and it tasted really burnt. This rarely happens but I didn't even finish it. I had to accept it was a sunk cost, which isn't something you want to consider when you're drinking coffee. 

The service wasn't the most engaging or welcoming. The place was completely empty and the barista didn't make an effort to strike up conversation or anything like that. Seating was pretty uncomfortable, so we didn't stay inside very long. I was hoping to spend 30-45 mins talking with my guest, but we decided the car would be comfier. 

It's very hard for me to justify returning when I know I can go across the street to Starbucks for a cheaper and better experience.

"That was the most ridiculous meal I've ever had" - My girlfriend

We had been wanting to try this place for awhile, given the different choices for meat. My girlfriend had the water buffalo burger and I had the wild boar burger. Both were just mediocre. No flavor at all. Her bun was soggy. Surprisingly only mine came with fries. So you can imagine her reaction when getting a full size plate without fries for $8.50 + $1.00 to add cheese. No side? Really. Just sad. She left hungry. 

Like she said...we could have eaten somewhere great for the $25 we spent.

Quickies:

Pros: They open later than most salon. The wait is quick on my visit.

Cons: Not what i wanted/ Language barrier.

The story:

After getting a foot massage from Yuren I decided to get a hair cut as well. But it was 7PM on Sunday so most hair salon has been closed. I used Yelp and find out this place is still open. I decide to give this place a shot. The location isnt hard to find but be aware of parking. When i walked in there are no client there and the front desk mid age lady also the hair washer was playing with her phone while listening to an old fashion Chinese music. She saw and look at her phone to pause something on it and ask me wash and cut? i said yes. She then direct me to get my hair washed. While she was testing the water temperature, she kept looking at her phone. When she was washing my hair she constantly looking at her phone as she was multi-tasking. She washed 2 times and condition one times as it supposed to be. I can tell she has been doing the for pretty long time but she didnt use at least 70% just plainly muscle memories though times. There are still some part i would still like to work on but there are no words, she was too busy to play slot-game on her phone. (I found out later while she was washing other client's hair and she put the phone straight up.) Anyway the person who cuts my hair doesnt seems to speak English as well. So i spoke Mandarin with him in-case of misunderstanding and my hair suffer. But then i think they spoke Cantonese but understand a bit Mandarin. Anyway, as usual i told the hairdresser to leave my side longer to cover my ear, he cuts it a bit too short and his cutting style isnt smooth. Based on his movement he is probably at intermediate level who only cut less than three years. I have thick hair and he didnt thin it enough. I probably will have to thin it more after i go home.... 

I have to admit, My hair isnt the easiest to cut and I am pretty picky on my own way. I feel like the stylist strength is army cut hair style. Anyway in the end i still tip the hairdresser and the hair washer. While i gave the tips to the hair washer lady, she was eating dinner. She did said thank you but in an in-sincere way. Personally i cut myself hair better than the one he gave me. But i don't want to make a mess in the bathroom and i have no time... ok i will be honest, there are also laziness in the factor. I will not recommend this place however i will also not discourage because everyone is different, they may be a good match for your style but not mine. Good thing that they open late, that is their asset, if you need a quick hair cut with ok looking or just make it short when you dont have major parties or showing your appearance in front of social media you may consider this place, after all, hair will grow back! Good luck out there adventurers!

I'm not really sure I've met a pizza I didn't like... until I was introduced to Inbound.

I really hoped this place would be my pizza spot--having a pizza joint within walking distance from home that serves slices is the holy grail. I've come here on two separate occasions and tried both the pepperoni and the buffalo chicken slices, and each time I felt deeply unsatisfied. I can't even really put my finger on what I don't like about it. It just wasn't that good. To put this in context, I'm totally fine with pizzas from all the major chains--Pizza Hut, Domino's, Papa John's, even the cheap-o Hot 'n' Ready pizzas from Little Caesar's--and this pizza just didn't do it for me.

There was nothing wrong with the service or anything else about my experience. I don't love giving negative reviews on Yelp, but in spite of the convenience factor I just can't go back. If they ever re-tool their recipe, I'd be happy to give them another shot.

I am still looking for good Tex-Mex in Austin.  And I feel stoopid saying that.  Maudie's Cafe isn't it.  

The service was indifferent. In...  out...  buh bye, kthxbye.  

The margs were good, but $4.75 seems steep for the size compared to what I'm used to paying at my local haunts in Houston.  And when I ordered a second, the server took my glass and disappeared even though it wasn't empty.  WTF?  

The salsa. was heavy with chipotle and tomato.  I'd like to see some cilantro, some tomatillo...  It was like chipotle-Pace.  OK, but pretty stock.  

We ordered queso and sliced jalapenos as a starter. The queso was actually beschemel sauce with cheese in it.  I guess flour, butter and milk is cheaper than cheese.  It was fine for what it was, but it was not queso.  The jalapenos arrived in a bowl, with no plates or anything.  The small slices were fine, but I wanted to cut up the bigger ones to make them go farther.  I did that on the table surface.  The server came by twice and saw me doing this and didn't offer a plate.  Yeah, I could have asked...

 The flour tortillas were factory mass-produced, rubbery and perfectly circular.  They felt kind of waxy and tasted bland.

My wife ordered the shrimp fajitas, which were pretty expensive.  She liked them.  I thought the dish was heavy on bell peppers and that the shrimp were really unseasoned.  

But the shrimp fajitas were great compared to my chicken enchiladas.  The verda sauce was tasty, and it's a good thing, because that was the only thing in the dish that was seasoned.  The tortillas were the afore mentioned mc-tortillas.  The shredded chicken was basically boiled chicken.  No seasoning at all.

Like I said, I'm still looking for good Tex-Mex in Austin.  And judging from the reviews on Yelp, so are a lot of other folks.

So I am going keep this to the point. Service was slow. Everyone came in at once. Took 15 mins to just get a drink order. When we had someone come up to us they rushed us into ordering our food before the drinks. The service was friendly but I did t enjoy being rushed. There where plenty of servers but they seemed very overwhelmed. The food came out fast and hot. So the food was good. However I ordered the country fried steak. Barley any gravy came on it. I spread it around on maybe a quarter of the steak. I asked for more. The kept forgetting. I was still waiting on my toast. When the toast and gravy finally came separately after asking multiple servers the toast was not toasted and had no butter. At the end they charged me for the gravy and I politely explained I should not be charged for the gravy due to the kitchens mistake of not properly adding the correct amount to the dish in the first place. They removed it no questions asked. Bathrooms where disgustingly dirty. Someone was even bathing there kid in the sink....literally washing his hair. I just don't think I'll be back for a while.

Every time I pass this location, the line is out the door. My interest was piqued. So away I go and make plans with my group to go. They opened at 5:30p and we got there at 6p and the line was already out the door. Once inside we realized the reason for the line. You place your order at the counter and pay. The inside is not that big causing the overflow outside. Prices are very reasonable. Service was quick. No one in my party including me thought highly of the food. It wasn't nasty but mediocre. I would eat here again if someone invited me but I would never make the choice to go here.

Really want to cater to vegans? Might want to stop the video loop of captive elephants doing tricks. Gross. 

I had the chive pancakes. Tasted like chives and raw tofu flavored batter. I love spicy, and the sauce the pancakes came with blew my face off with heat. Not really in a delicious flavorful way. 

Also tried a bowl of miso soup. Freeze dried mushrooms, previously frozen carrots, giant chunks of silken tofu - is it an oxymoron to say "extremely mediocre"? The good news is that the miso broth was insanely good. Worth a star by itself. 

The other star is for the (mostly) cool ambiance. Inviting green walls, creative lighting, mod condiment holders made me want to sit in there even after I was full of foods' mediocrity.

Buddha Thai at 28th and Iris will deeeeeply satisfy cravings for Thai food, and I am totally certain I'd hit Buddha Thai instead.

True story: My first week in Boston and freshly arrived from California, I descended into the Dugout with my new school friend, Carl, an old-fashioned redneck from North Carolina.  Carl ordered a Bud; I asked for a pina colada.  The bartender, a tough-looking guy with arms like a stevedore, leaned across the bar, set his face inches from mine, looked me in the eye with obvious distaste and said, "We don't serve pussy drinks here."  A lesson learned: For the next three years, I never asked for anything but Bud at the Dugout.

While it may be five stars in my heart, the Dugout's a dive and it doesn't pretend to be anything but a dive.  You can't give a dive five stars--it defeats the whole purpose!

But this is no one-star dive like PJ Kilroy's.  Two stars all the way, baby!

I went in for the first meeting and met with the owner. He was very nice and I felt like he really got to know me and what I was looking for. We chatted for about an hour. He then told me that two women in his office would be working to find me matches based on what I had told him. I was annoyed that these women hadn't even met me and they were the ones finding matches for me. Not him. 
I was then set up with a couple of guys who were really nice but I wasn't attracted to them. I only had one bad date with a guy who lacked social skills and with whom I had absolutely nothing in common. It was then that I started to realize that they weren't taking my profile into account when matching me up. They definitely would not have matched me with this guy if that were the case.
I had been told that they would take my feedback and use it to make better picks in the future. This was not the case. When I told my advisor about my experience with Mr. No Social Skills, she quickly replied, "well, how about this guy? I just happen to have his file on my desk right now." This was another guy that I clearly had little in common with. I truly think they just match you up with whoever they have to give more dates to in order to reach their membership minimum within the shortest amount of time.
While I met a couple of nice guys, I ended up putting my membership on hold and never went back for my two final dates to reach my guaranteed 5 date minimum. I was too annoyed. I spent way too much money for this service ($630) to be arbitrarily set up with guys who were obviously not right for me.

Went for brunch today.  Got there right at opening.  Worst  service I've ever had here or any other downtown Louisville restaurant.  Waitress kept telling us she hadn't worked brunch in a while.  I ordered stuffed French toast, which came with a meat.  I asked for chorizo.  Husband ordered potato and salmon hash with poached eggs.  Five minutes later she came back to tell me I couldn't have chorizo - only ham or bacon.  Didn't offer to ask the kitchen.  Seemed overwhelmed by the computer.  When our meals came, my husband got fried eggs not poached.  She dropped he plates, husband called out to her, and said he'd ordered poached eggs.  Her response - the computer doesn't let me order that.  So two requests, neither addressed with the kitchen, or in any way - and these were not complicated requests.  She never came back til she brought the check.  Husband had to leave table to hunt down hot sauce.  Two stars because French toast was good.  Potato salmon hash was all potatoes and very little salmon.  Would never order again

Although I have a busy schedule I called ahead of time to see if they could get me in, they were which was great, I show up and told them I called not too long ago and the lady said "okay" so I was standing there for like 5 min and no one told me what to do said I sat down and waited about 10 min. No biggie I know I just called in.. finally the last asked me to sit in chair 1, she talked soooo quietly that everything she said I had to ask her to repeat, she had a rude demeanor and acted as if I were an inconvenience. Usually I come in once in awhile for their great pedicures and a glass of wine which is awesome. The guy with all tattoos have done my nails before and he is very detailed and extremely nice and funny which is why I came back, but this experience was not the best, rude, raised her voice to make me wash my hands again, but then explained why a little later. Wasn't pleased so I won't be returning unfortunately Even though it's close to my work.

I really wanted to leave The Pecan saying, "This is one of the best meals ever!"  All our family could say was, "That was way overpriced, and Golden Corral would have been better."  

The wait staff was excellent.  The before-dinner muffins were wonderful.  The side items were good.  The main entrees were not good.  Three of us had fish, and the fish tasted bad and/or mushy.  

Unfortunately, this is not a place I will return or recommend.  Oh, family of four with 3 entrees, just sides for my picky son, 2 soft drinks, 1 beer, and mandatory 20% gratuity on a gift certificate:  $145.

Not a really big fan, I'm afraid.

We came here because Tamarind was, at the time, the highest-rated Indian food within a reasonable distance. It really didn't live up. 

The main issue we had regarded the service which usually, my wife and I don't care about. We like spicy food and asked for our meals to be spicy. The waiter not only refused to believe my wife could handle the spice, but actually brought a completely different dish than what she ordered. This, he claimed, was because she wouldn't have liked the original. 

I got exactly what I ordered, by virtue of my having a penis. Also, it wasn't that spicy. 

The food, like all Indian food, was flavorful, but the potions were disappointingly small. As an American I demand one gallon of Daal and at least 12 pieces of Naan. I'm willing to take as little as 1/4 that figure. No less!

Brought my 2002 Mazda Tribute in when it started getting rumbly. I already knew cylinder 2 wasn't firing properly and something needed replacing. They replaced my spark plugs, a couple other minor things and charged me $190 for a new ignition coil. 
When I got the car back it was still doing the same thing, so I took it to a mechanic I had used before and he almost immediately notice that yes #2 was in bad shape but #4 looked brand new! They had failed to look up the proper number order and replaced the wrong thing. My hometown mechanic went ahead and replaced all of the other ignition coils (at $70 each) and I got the right fix for about $150 less than what Honest-1 charged me to not fix it.
To their credit, when I informed them of the mistake they offered to fix it properly for free but by that point my confidence in them was not high and the car was already with shop #2 so I didn't bother.

We don't shop here much, but it is a decent place to find specialty items and different things than the chain stores offer. If you're after routine items like milk, produce, pet food, and box dinners, go to the chain stores; they'll be much cheaper.  If you're after local-grown produce or odd items or smaller brands, Weilands might have them.

(Seriously, they sell major-brand cheap pet food at a higher cost than their competitors. Even the nearby IGA on Oakland is better-priced. You'd think with billing themselves as a specialty grocery, they'd offer specialty pet food brands. But I digress.)

With that said, buyer beware. We've caught them twice now in substituting cheaper cheese for a more-expensive brand -- unfortunately, we didn't catch the sub until the cheese had been grated or sliced, which was too late to return it.

Specifically, what they label as "parmesan reggiano" IS NOT PARMESAN REGGIANO. It tastes NOTHING like real PR, and I'm guessing it's either asiago or a mild romano -- maybe a domestic parmesan from Wisconsin -- but it's not the real Parmesan Reggiano. The real PR has a very distinctive flavor & a hard, dark-yellow rind with "parmesan reggiano" engraved into it.  Some stores cut the rinds off & sell them separately, as most folks will throw them away anyway (tip: simmer the rinds in spag sauce), and that's ok, BUT that rind is the ONLY way to be sure that's the real deal, without opening the package and tasting before you buy.

Weilands, of course, didn't have the rind in the package. That didn't set off any red flags with us at first, for reasons stated above. BUT the cheese in question was the wrong texture/consistency (real PR is a semi-hard cheese that grates easily; what we got was distinctly softer), wrong smell, and wrong taste. In other words, WEILANDS WRAPPED A CHEAPER CHEESE AND SOLD IT AT THE HIGHER REAL-PR PRICE.

TWICE. TWICE.

The first time might have been a labeling mistake. We didn't want to accuse a store we liked of fraud, either. But the second time, a month later? No. That's deliberate. By International Law, only one type of cheese can be sold as Parmesan Reggiano, and that's the stuff straight from Italy, which is NOT what Weiland's is labeling and selling.

Shame on you, Weilands.  We're not regular customers, but you've still lost our business.

Questionable. A certain saleswoman invited me to connect via LinkedIn: "Hey Jeremy! Surprised we haven't met yet. I work with some of the guys in your industry. I save them time and eliminate the hassle of shopping by making them feel great in their clothing. Shirts, jeans, sport coats, shoes things like that. We should connect." I assumed she was a personal shopper. I accepted, and she immediately started calling and messaging me demanding to set up a Zoom call that day. I told her I was busy, but ended up agreeing. Big mistake. It took a damn hour. I love shopping and told her so. I'm a sharp dresser and sent her a photo of one of my outfits laid out to prove it. In fact, my first job was working at a tuxedo shop. I'm complimented often. I personally think that sitting for a fitting and all of this might entail more time, not less, than my own personal shopping routine. She did not send me promotional materials, but shared her screen to set forth the store's outlandishly expensive programs ($5,000 suits and $400 dress shirts). WTF. Told her I'm not in the N.B.A. and need to pay off my educational loans, so could not justify the expense. She then asked me--incredibly--whether I could refer anyone to her. She was visibly disappointed. I told her no--that my friends were either thrifty, or I did not know their fashion preferences or habits.

Not a good experience moving with these guys. 
They were scheduled to move my furniture on Aug 25. They called on the day of the move and said their trucks were in repair shop and they wouldn't be able to move my stuff that day, but they would show up the next day at the same time. The next day when I called them to confirm (they didn't have the courtesy to call me) they said they were going to be delayed, maybe an hour or so. I figured this being the last week in Aug, may be they were telling the truth. So I waited. 1 hr AFTER the delayed time they called to they would come in another 2-3hrs later. By then I didn't trust these guys anymore and called my friends.
