Every time I spoke to Andrew, he kept saying he would give me an extra guy to move my stuff at no additional cost. He apologized and said the truck breakdown was totally unexpected, they were losing business too, etc, etc and promised to give me a good price next time.

On the plus side, they did quote me a better price than anyone else the second time. But they were again late by more than 2hrs. On the day of the move, Andrew called me and said he'll be an hour late (scheduled time was 1pm). At noon he said maybe 3-4pm. This time his excuse was that someone else's move was taking longer, and what did I expect him to do? 

I've certainly dealt with movers way more professional.

First the good

Right next to the airport literally 10 minutes
Staff at front desk super friendly and allowed us to check in early

The bad

We had a king bed with twin pillows 
As you can see from the picture the ceiling is molded and coming apart
The room was small bathroom if you shut the door it was over.
Definitely not what I expected from the Hyatt. When you walk in the front desk is right where the tables are for dining.

If felt more like a motel 6 btw parking is not free 10.00 a night, however the gate in the back is broken so they shouldn't charge you until that's fixed.

The airplanes at night fly low in dirty so be warned it went until about 1130 by then I was sleep. 

They need to do a serious cleaning very dusty around the ac units .

Bottom line it served it's purpose we stayed one night if I had to stay longer we would have asked for a different room don't stay in 102 until they fix that ceiling and throughly clean.

Nong's does an excellent job in replicating the Thai chicken. The protein is tender and juicy with nice succulent softness. The rice is cooked perfectly and the soup is such a warm comforting broth. There's a lot of potential in this dish. 

But for me...this is a dish I grew up eating my whole life. I've spent years watching my Dad make the sauce and spices for the brown sauce poured over the dish. And I'm sorry Nong, but you just don't do it for me. Nothing beats a family tradition. The sauce was lacking in robust flavor. It was more sour and sweet than the savory component I was looking for. 

For all the reviews it was underwhelming. To the point that I called my Dad and told him I missed him because that's just how Thai food works for me in a new city. I end up craving a home cooked meal rather than a restaurant reproduction. 

Although the similarities were there, the portion size are also lacking. It's more of a meal that's great if you're trying to count your calories.

ya, I have to agree. My partner and I woke up early on a Sunday to head out and get brekky in our new neighborhood.  I read some reviews and had passed by a few times, thought I would give it a try.  In hindsight, I should have either driven into the city or eaten at the village inn.  First of all, Im gay. So is my partner. Its Portland for gods sake. But you would have thought we were making out in leather jockstraps with the stares we got. 

anyhow. Coffee was decent, I was a little disconcerted by their "ribbons of eggs" (not sure how you make that and the toast was kinda bland and kinda cold.  I would not return again, even though Im all about the mom and pop shops.  

The hash browns were scary. Thats all Im going to say...like they hash browned last nites mashed potatoes.  Youve been warned!

After reading these reviews I can see how a good number of people in the country will vote for Trump.  They are suckers for a decent sales person. Easy things are done well here, and quickly but be careful if its anything more than a tune up.  All the stereotypical used-car sales person models are alive and well here.  If a mechanic you don't know tells you he loves you on the first visit, a red flag should wave in your brain somewhere. Then the list of savings and things he has done for free will come out.  Your fault if you buy it.  This is a business  that exists to make money, and that's fine.  But that's all it is.  I could drudge up all the details of my experiences at Alewife Auto.  I'll leave it alone. I will only use a dealer going forward.

I've been going to Silk for years because they were always accommodating for walk ins but their customer service has gone way down. Lukewarm at best foot bath water, not nearly enough soaking time, and my tech chatted under her breath in her language to her coworkers the whole time. It's awkward. The services have started to just feels very rushed and inconsistent. During the part of my manicure where she was supposed to be massaging my hand she was doing it one-handed while scrolling through her cell phone that she had in her lap. Can you imagine?? It is always clean and bright in there but that's not enough. I won't be back.

I go here when I wake up too late on a Saturday and I just need to ingest caffeine - no matter what it tastes like.  The coffee is generally crap. The pastries tend to be okay, and not mangled or stale like you see at some Starbucks. 

But, what makes the place a good spot for those moments right before the withdrawal migraine sets in is that the staff here are great. They're friendly but not pushy. It might be that dealing with the "special" customer traffic you get from being a Starbucks with a bus 72 stop  and a WalMart right next to it has made them all hyper-aware of people's personal head space and how to navigate their way through a lot of tough conversations and transactions in a pleasant way.

I had high expectation as everyone else in Vancouver since this is the only udin specialized restaurant. Very disappointed by not only the food quality, but also their operation and customer service.

We ordered beef udon and cold dipping one. Beef one, they shouldnt be saying its beef udon, cuz there were only scraps. Dipping one, the portion was so small though I ordered large. Both of us came out hungry. 

Topping bar was empty at 1:30pm. 90% were empty tables. 

I will give another try next yr. Hope things get better here.

Not recommended.

My husband, father and I went here after visiting my mother in the hospital nearby. I was pretty disappointed, with prices that are fairly expensive for the quality of food they offered.  They had no vegetarian options on the menu, but when asked, offered several things that are not listed on the menu. 

I had the beet salad. It was extremely small, and the arugula was wilted. The blackbean burger, which was not on the menu and the waitress didn't know they even had, was good and bonus points for grilling the bun. However, the fries were soft, cold, and no seasoning. 
My husband ordered a second beer that never arrived. We needed to leave to return to the hospital, and my husband asked if we could get the check and to remove the beer. The waitress looked up at the bar, said "There it is!" And returned with the beer he no longer wanted. It also remained on the bill. 

In short, not worth the price or poor service.

The nail salon was clean and neat. People there were very kind and helpful. My sister and I both received gel manicures. They came out great and we really liked them. My sister got these little studs on her nails and it was nice, but an hour later, a few them fell off. She wasn't even doing anything and they fell off. Few hours later, one finger of mine, started to peel. It was really disappointing. I think if you are going for a basic manicure they are fine, but do not go for gel.

I came here based on the history of this place I had heard about. Since i have heard about this place I have become vegetarian. I dont eat animals because i love and care for animals, not because of any health reasons.

We ordered Vegetarian Enchiladas. Freaking disgusting. They actually had the audacity to use Gardinera from a jar as the vegetable filling !! It was pickled nasty with cheese melted on it.. The machine made tortillas were doughy and pasty..

Yuck... we are not going back.. Perhaps the ribs are good who knows..

Ill wait for a Chinese place to come back..

Pancakes are delicious, but the fry game is decidedly weak (both potato & sweet potato). While the burger and sandwich were hot and crisp, the fries were literally cold and soggy for both of us. The fries were half of the dishes we ordered (i.e. worth ~$5 per dish), so that was quite disappointing. Other than that, we came at an off peak time and the food came out really fast. Oh and this is really random but my menu had coffee in it. I opened it and drops of coffee rolled down the menu into the table. Probably a one off experience with the coffee though. I recommend you order queso and pancakes and open your menu with caution.

This was the first place I got take-out from when I moved to Cambridge in July 2013. I found the food to be decent, especially the pasta as well as the marinara sauce, although slightly overpriced it was the closest tasting sauce to the one I make at home. 

Not too long after that, something changed, new chef or new owners. The sauce changed and so did many other things, for the worse. The food was mediocre and flavorless.

Now with the recent remodel I had hoped the food would improve again, especially with all the talk about a new chef. Unfortunately this has not been the case. The pasta has not improved, and I recently ordered fish and chips which turned out to be prison style frozen fish bits. Utterly disgusting and a huge disappointment as they are so convenient. I'll order from Skampa from now on.

Sad to say, a disappointment 

Came in and ordered coffee and water.  That took 15 min.  Frankly, the coffee was not that good.  

Finally they took the breakfast order

The food was disappointing too.  Fruit bowl served in plastic container like you'd expect at the airport.  Poor presentation. Potatoes were as if they were warmed over.  Toast was one slice when it seems two are typical. Eggs?   They were good

Friend ordered cheese on a bagel.  What a fright!!   Cheese looked like it was made In a computer, half draped on a cold, wrinkled, stale excuse for a bagel.  Yuck!!

Asked for jelly for my toast. Had to ask twice.  So that makes food and service substandard.  For that matter they forgot the potatoes on one of our orders. 

Oh, well.

This was my fifth time here through the years. When I first came here many years ago I was blown away by the hugeness of the buffet with a great selection of Chinese, Japanese , Korean and American foods.
It still has a large selection of different foods but the quality has taken a toll to the point where I don't desire to go back anymore.
Orlando is known to have an abundance of Chinese buffets, all mediocre at best.
Koy Wan was different. It had quality.
All of these buffets start out great and go steadily down hill until customers stop coming and eventually the restaurant dies and goes out of business.
I gave Koy Wan two stars due to the shear abundance and variety of foods.
About thirty five kinds of sushi, sashimi and negri. These were pretty good but not great. Soups including egg drop, wonton. miso and seafood. Wontons were very heavy with meat that was tasteless and too starchy. Hot foods like clams in black bean sauce were bland. Frog legs were deep fried and over breaded. Spare ribs were slabs of fatty pork or beef, not the usual type of ribs often found in Chinese restaurants. Lo mein and chow fun were good. Korean beef was thin and tasteless.
General Chow and Sesame chicken were tasty.
Tea was one dollar per person extra.
Service was mediocre as well. I had to get up numerous times to flag down a waitress for more water and tea.
Ambiance is nice with multi rooms to dine in.
In all fairness, I cannot recommend this place.
When in Orlando, be smart and stay away from buffets. A sit down Chinese restaurant is a better choice and search out Yelp for reviews before venturing out to eat.

An almost dead or sick crock roach crawling on the floor 10 mins. after we stepped into the room on the check-in date.  I called front desk right away and security guys came in quickly and did 10 mins investigation.  The conclusion was: this was just one crock roach and it must be coming from outside when house keeper left the front door open and room was free of any other crock roaches.

The room is on the ground floor and hotel person told us it's an delux unit as it was remodeled.  Though, we suspected that this room could have some problems before.  The recent remodels of new carpet, new counter tops, and some new kitchen appliances were to correct those problems.  We decided to change to a standard room on the 3rd floor. 

Some other issues I think hotel can make improvements:
- No "Do not disturb" sign.
I was in bathroom and heard somone opened the door without asking for permission to enter (or maybe I didn't hear).  Wish there is the sign so that I can hang on the door knob.
- 2 shampoo bottles instead of 1 shampoo and 1 conditioner
- no hand lotion
It's cold at night in Nov. With air condition on, hands are really dry without the lotion.
- no eggs in the included breakfast
Even boiled eggs will be very nice as my son loves eggs.
- breakfast is ended at 9am.  
Wish it can be a little longer to 10am.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

Above review was written by my wife Jenny C.

Ok, I'm going to be a Debbie Downer. 

I recommended this place for brunch and it was a pretty big disappointment.  

First of all, me and my buddy were most excited about the pretzels. Why is it so hard to find a good pretzel in this town? I think it's because lye is pretty unattainable these days (THANKS METH LABS) and apparently that's what makes a good pretzel.
So, if you like pretzels, don't order one here. It's not a pretzel. It's bread. In a pretzel shape. AND to make matters worse, mine was incredibly under-cooked, I'm talking raw dough in the middle. My friend's pretzel was cooked through, but we were both bummed that we just got bread and cheese. Hmpf.

Also a culprit in my mediocre experience:

We decided to sit outside because it was a nice day, there were three open tables and they were all dirty. So we ended up bussing our own table. Eh. 

Duck confit nachos: great idea in theory, totally lacking in execution. They were kind of cold. Lacking a lot of duck. Could have been waaaay better. Especially for $12. 

Since you have to go inside to order (I knew this before coming here, so whatever) my darling boyfriend let me order on his behalf. I got him the quiche of the day, however I left the menu outside. In my opinion, quiche is quite heavy and tastes the best with salad. Which is what I thought it came with. The bartender asks me "Do you want it with hash?" and I reply "what are my other options?" and he goes "You want it with hash." But the thing is, I DIDN'T WANT IT WITH HASH. However, since I didn't have the menu, I didn't really know what to do and kind of panicked and the bartender disappeared.... sigh. So, my boyfriend was disappointed with his meal. And the hash. Ugh. 

We also tried the grilled ham and cheese, and the hot dog, and those were both considerably good. Pretty much the only thing that saved this place from one star in my book.

While I don't mind going inside to order, I do mind having dirty plates and glasses sitting on my table for an extended period of time. We had an obscene amount of flies that wouldn't leave us alone due to this. Not very fun. 

And then there's the tip situation. What do I tip? You brought me the food, yes. You bussed my table after we got the check? No one really waited on us? But then I hate tipping low? And our check was super high for what we received, this place is not exactly cheap.

Sitting inside here for a snack and a few drinks would probably be a way better experience. 
If you're looking for a sit-down meal, I would pass this place by.

So, we're feeling gluttonous.  We order a pizza from Regina's for $25 (those nightowl's and their delivery fees!) and jump over to foodler to order some apps and dessert.  We settle on Sorento's.  Needless to say, it ends up being more like Shitrento's.

We order calamari, a caesar salad, cannolis, and a piece of chocolate cake (I know, I know, I said gluttonous, remember?!!?).

The calamari literally smelled like it had been sitting out for two weeks.  The stench almost made me vomit.  Then there was the caesar.  What can I say?  Disgusting.  Utterly, unwaveringly, disgusting.  The lettuce was limp, the croutons were soggy, but the dressing was the worst part: it smelled and tasted like the inside of an anchovie's asshole.

I'm going to go ahead and give these mofos two stars just because the desserts weren't half bad and the delivery girl was a sweetheart.

We would have been much better off with the Regina's and bribing the nightowl girl to stop by 7eleven on the way to pick up some zebra cakes.

So disappointed!  This was our one stop in Quincy Market, and I thought I'd picked a winner.  But...

We split a lobster roll, which was ready when we got there.  I know, I know, I should have asked for a fresh one.  But how?  It was nicely filled with lobster, but the bun wasn't as soft as I wanted, and it was cold... and the lobster didn't have enough flavor.  I had to salt it.  Oh the sin!

We each got soup, Ken had the clam chowder, and I chose the lobster bisque.  Ken's chowder was the better of the two, and it was only slightly better than average.

I was really excited to try this food, and I walked away disappointed.  I loved the eggplant rolls and the cheese bread, which I got as a two piece combo for $6.  Unfortunately, it was not like a lunch at all. It was like a snack.  I knew I wasn't crazy when a coworker who had recommended it the day before looked at my pitiful open plate and asked, "Where is the rest of it?"  I ate it before I even left the block of food carts, and I was still hungry.  That's pretty sad considering the other options available in food cartlandia.

Have been to Vinotopia many times and thought we would give its sister restaurant a try before going into Argo. Ehat were we thinking! The  waiter who took care of us was very nice,only been there for a short while so he had not tried alot of the items on menu.The female bartender (11/4 9pm) have no smile at all.Our Veg and Coruvian burgers were quite delicious and made to my husband's diet specification. Then we decided on half salad to finish our dinner.Boy, what a disgrace for the portion.Literally, 2-3 small mouthful and when the bill came, the price tag of that salad was shocking!!! Almost $7 for that shamefully small bowl of salad. The reasonings by the manager were not quite convincing. It is not a exclusive joint, people can come and go into the restaurant  and plenty of decent places in the mall to eat(best do not feel ripped off). We thought that was a disgrace on the part of the  ownership and executive chef to price the half salad and god know what other "half" dishes at such astronomical price!
Go somewhere else to eat if you want to enjoy your movie and the rest of the evening.

I bought a Groupon and went here last week. Zagat rated??? Hmmmm. I'm reconsidering my trust in Zagat; this is my 2nd disappoint from them this year for GA recognized. Zagat NYC is not much better. 

My husband and I ordered 3 dishes (tilapia, curry, and pad see ew) between the 2 of us and a soup and a salad. The Tom Yum soup came out hot but nothing to write home about. The atmosphere was bland and IKEA looking, walls were a little too yellow and made me feel like I was in a bucket of mustard paste.  The tilapia was overcooked and expensive for such a small portion. The Masaman curry sauce was pretty decent but it's typical Thai fare you can get at any other restaurant. What disappointed me the most was the Pad See Ew. I was so excited that I saw this on the menu bc I haven't had it since my Seattle days. Pad See Ew has broccoli in it. I asked the server 4 times if it did because that is how I remembered it. She says "YES": it is broccoli stirred fried with noodles. The Pad see ew I got that night had 1 very small slither of broccoli, noodles, a few very thin slices of carrots. I looked at my one piece of broccoli in astonishment as it was slightly yellow and cut so thin. This one little cut of a broccoli crown was sliced probably in 8 ways before 1 of the 8 slices got to me. I was floored. My husband looked at me and laughed and said, I guess that is what the server meant by 'Yes' it has broccoli. Are you kidding me?

I don't recommend going to this place; not worth your hard earned dollars. Also, the location is almost scary. We had to go to two different parking lots to make sure we parked in the right place and had to bring my husband's laptop inside the restaurant because there is a BIG sign that says "We are not responsible for any belongings". (AKA beware because this neighborhood is not SAFE).

So we have ate here twice in the last month and we should of not gone back for a second time. The first time we ordered a new sandwhich and it seemed like they actual had to make it. I say this because when we went for a second time and I realize why now they have a drive-thru. These people have taken the word microwave to a entire new level. If you are going to a restaurant (which they claim they are) and not a fast food joint. My food should not come out from the back in under 4 minutes! My mozzarella sticks, crispy chicken sandwich and my girlfriends burger all microwaved and the food was absolutely dreadful. This place has completely lost its way and it's right on the same level as Burger King and McDonald's ( they actually might be better) but the over reason I give it 2 starts is cause the icecream wasn't bad and that's just because it's the only thing they can't stick in a microwave, but I have a feeling If they could...they would. Rant over

Service was typical of any other fast food restaurant. I'm not so sure why everyone loves it because it tastes like all the others. I needed a quick bite to eat while driving home because I knew I was going to be stuck in traffic. Got the steak burrito and a cheese quesadilla. Both lacked any type of flavor and the steak was dry. The tables were fairly clean as well as the floor. 

I surely do not understand why there is an extra charge for chips and salsa??  I highly doubt if I will be back to one unless it is necessary.

My review is specifically for the banh mi as I have not tried anything else in this restaurant. The reason I discovered this place is that I had been having a huge craving for banh mi and went on a search for a Vietnamese place in the Davis/Porter Square area where I work. I decided that my craving warranted the semi-long walk over to Pho House. I got there and ordered the pork banh mi to go. And I was highly disappointed. The sandwich was mostly all bread and barely any filling. If you're going to use so little filling then maybe serve it with a smaller piece of bread. Eating the sandwich was so dry due to bread to filling ratio. I've never had a banh mi with so little filling. Definitely don't recommend. I might come back in the future to try the pho, and I hope it's better than the banh mi was.

Located in a small storefront in EAV along with some other vendors.  Limited selection - couple of cakes, 2 -3 pies and a bunch of fruit squares and brownies.
Tried slices of the two cakes they had that day - chocolate with chocolate buttercream frosting and an almond cake.   Presentation could use improvement - they dump the slice sideways into a too small cardboard container so the frosting gets messed up.  The cakes were pretty dense, but both didn't taste fresh, and the perimeter of both were dried out and hard.  Frosting was too sweet.  
Slices were HUGE, enough for 2 servings -- too bad the cakes didn't taste better.

I was looking forward to a nice dinner with my husband, but the service totally killed the experience.  We each ordered three items (the whole menu is small plates), three meat items for him and three vegetarian items for me.  After an hour, he had eaten his entire dinner while I'd only received a salad.  One of the items wasn't even what he ordered, but we were running short on time so he decided not to send it back.  I informed the server that we needed the check, since we were leaving for the theater.  She quickly brought out my second plate and comped us the third one, which arrived just as we were getting up to leave.  Still, even with one comped item the bill was over $100 (and we didn't even have drinks!)  At that price I expect solid service, and the kitchen has serious issues with timing.  It wasn't even a Friday night, we were eating early on a Tuesday.  As I was leaving I overheard the server apologizing and taking something off the bill for the table next to us too, so it seems like we weren't a one-off.  Food is alright, standard fancy-ish New American with middle eastern accents.  Music is loud and clubby, what you would expect at a bar but hard to have a conversation.  Tons of people talking loudly and taking selfies, just what I like with dinner.  You can have a better date, for less money, elsewhere.

This is a review for their delivery service. 

When we looked online at their menu, we were really excited because they have a great variety and a ton of wing flavors. The prices are also pretty decent for Boston. Moreover, their online ordering system was easy and convenient. 

The guys ordered 24 wings (spicy BBQ and mild buffalo) and fries; I got a grilled chicken pesto spinach wrap. 

First of all, it took over an hour. Nbd. Their site says they have long wait times because of how fresh they are. 

Fresh my you-know-what. My wrap was cold. While the chicken was good, I actually wanted to salt it because the pesto and tomatoes were lacking flavor. It was also very very messy and watery, dripping everywhere. They brought us the wrong flavor wings and totally left out the dipping sauce (ranch). The worst thing by far was the fries: TERRIBLE. They were soggy, cold, and flavorless. 

To boot, the delivery guy was rude. 

I would not order from here again. Disappointing.

The first time I went here, it was okay. I got a new set of acrylics (stilettos) and the young girl doing them was kind and took her time.
The next time I went I was appalled by the experience. I went for a fill and I had a broken nail and obviously needed it repaired. I had an older woman doing them this time and she barely spoke to me, which is fine, but literally rushed through the fill so fast that it was done in 15 MINUTES. Not to mention halfway through the appointment, she was on her cell phone!!!
When I was sent to the drying station I was looking at my hands and realized she didn't shape them at all and the repaired nail was this big misshapen blob and that other nails you could see my old polish on them.
I asked another woman to please refile the repair nail and it came out too thin so she sent me back to the first woman. I sat down and she was purposefully making it obvious to me that she was angry to have to do it. She was sighing and rolling her eyes, then looked at me and said "you want them to match?" and laughed with another technician. After she was finished she just got up and walked away. I tipped her before going to the drying station so this was just unacceptable. Never returning and I advise you to avoid this too unless you want a botched job and no one to help fix it.

I just ordered 2 breakfast tacos (bean and cheese) in the drive-thru. Easy huh? Well, the beans were so watery they leaked out of the foil and caused the paper bag to burst. A mess in the car. I cleaned it up and opened up a taco. Liquified beans dropped out making more mess. So, I returned the tacos to the drive-thru window. I spoke with a very courteous manager, Gabriella. She exchanged my tacos for something more solid. Potatoes. What a mess though. But on a good note, the manager was able to help me quickly and professionally.

I was sure I would buy my wedding dress from Charlotte's. They have a great selection and a beautiful space. However, my consultant made me feel very uncomfortable purchasing a dress from Charlotte's. She was insincere and only ever spoke to my family to shut down any opinions that did not match my own. I did, however, find a dress that I loved. We had half an hour left in the appointment when I found "the one" and everyone loved it. My future mother-in-law saw a dress on a mannequin she wanted to see me in, because she thought I would love it. She was so nice to come and only ever said sweet things so I wanted to try the dress for her, but the consultant interrupted, asking if I felt like I had to try on more dresses and completely disrespecting my future mother-in-law's wishes. I was so embarrassed. The consultant then kept pressuring me to take measurements and fill out the paperwork to order the dress. She told me I had to order the dress that day because ship dates were changing and if I waited I'd have to pay a rush fee and may not get my dress altered in time. My wedding was eight months away and I would be shocked if the gown wasn't delivered, altered, pressed and beautiful by my wedding, even if I waited the few days  the consultant said I couldn't afford. At this point I was already starting to feel like a dollar sign and an inconvenience and now I wondered if I was being taken advantage of.  I could tell my whole family was uncomfortable and I wanted to leave so I filled out the paperwork and went to order the dress, but my mom took me aside and asked if I would mind purchasing the wedding dress from a different shop. She was made uncomfortable by the pushy and insincere consultant and also worried that we were being misled  about the delivery time
so we decided to buy the dress in a shop out of state.

I will not be going back to Charlotte's as I do not think it is an honest business invested in treating its customers with respect and integrity. They do have a great selection and I did find my bridesmaids, mother of the bride and groom, and flower girl dresses at Charlotte's, but will be buying them from different shops. I feel bad, but they are not inexpensive purchases and I want to feel secure working with stores that will be supplying such important things for our wedding.

This is an "ok" apartment run by very unintelligent people. First, it's just faux nice. They're so obsessed with conveying class that they put embarrassing carpeting in the elevators that say "Style follows you home." In fact, the walls are extremely thin, the cabinetry looks and feels like Ikea, and the amenities are just not very nice. For instance, the grills are always disgusting, and the pool is only a couple of feet deep. Also, my view is of a giant Phipps parking lot. And the blinds do nothing. And cell-coverage in this concrete eyesore is virtually non-existent. While they suggested once they would "consider" installing a solution to this cell service issue, it appears that since this might not be a concern of prospective guests (only actual residents), they declined to address the issue.

More importantly, despite this mirage of class, the property management team is really just ill-suited to manage anything. In a maintenance request where I suggested that I thought my toilet was not working properly, they chose to inform me that this was just the nature of the ultra-modern ultra-low flow toilets they installed. In fact, there was a crack in the base of the toilet which ultimately resulted in poop water spilling out onto my floor.

They have also instituted very bad parking policies because they seemingly enjoy messing with their residents. While the previous management team actually attempted to make new policies known (albeit, only via Email) with prominent subjects like, "Parking Changes," the new manager, Jim Stabler, opted evidently to impose new policies in a "Community Update," next to very crucial information like, "One of our property managers is leaving! Wish her well!" and "We are having a dinner!" and "We have Yoga!" This new policy made it so that, despite the ample parking in the building, guests need to park their cars, walk inside to the concierge, get a pass, and walk back to their car to put the pass in their car --no matter where they park. Indeed, despite announcing this policy so prominently in "Community Updates," they chose to leave "Visitor Parking" signs up misleading unsuspecting guests into thinking that this distinction might actually be meaningful. Apparently "Visitor Parking" signs are left up because they prefer people with guest passes to park in those spots first.

Indeed, although they are capable of physically posting signs about the unbelievable amenity of mini-muffins on Fridays, they couldn't actually take the time to post signs explaining that "Visitor Parking" actually doesn't mean that visitors can park there without a pass. I suppose a sign that says, "Pseudo-Visitor Parking" might detract from the faux classy aesthetic though. And yet, Jim Stabler evidently thinks that not only are these signs appropriate, there's no issue in casually booting Residents' guests and forcing them to wait 90 minutes. It's strange to live in a building where the management views current tenants as adversaries.

I really wanted to like this place since it is located near our home, but their really isn't anything good to say about our experience. The service was awful and the night we went their it was uncomfortably hot and they would not do anything about it. The prices are definately too high for the quality of food which was sub par. The pork tenderloin my wife and I both ordered was so salty we could barely eat it. The drinks we ordered were also not very good. The wine selection was awful and we neither one liked the mixed drinks that we ordered. I guess to sum it up it was a waste when you have so many good restaurants to choose from in Austin.

Pretty disappointing. Flavours are bland as other posters have written. I ordered the elk medallion eggs benedict which was gamey and somewhat interesting but my wife's crabmeat egg benedict came out cold. There was only one chef in the kitchen and maybe this was simply due to the long weekend, but it seemed she was getting pretty overwhelmed with just a half-full restaurant. The crabmeat is clearly canned which honestly shouldn't even be on the menu if you're not going to take the effort to get fresh stuff. The orange juice is freshly squeezed and the coffee was OK, but nothing to write home about.

Went out of our way for lunch today to this place from Boston. Due to overwhelming reviews on opentable 1000+ with 4 stars and about 600 on yelp.
My wife and I weren't very happy. All I can say is that the service was great thanks to our server. However the food was just ok. The plating not very appetizing it's like getting lunch in a cafeteria or having hospital food served. Just plain blah! Taste was ok really nothing great. I had the terrine for apps and my wife had the chowder 2.5 stars it was ok something you can get at panera. We had the pot roast and my wife had the turkey pot pie again it's just plain and simple. This place is good if your around the corner and if you want to spend $60 in lunch( discounted for restaurant week).

I had such high hopes for the Beehive.  The reviews suggested good food and a fun evening out.  I went for dinner with a friend and soon after being seated realized it was far too loud for dinner conversation.  We ended up yelling across the small table for the remainder of the evening.  The food itself was very good but the price was what you would expect to pay at a classy restaurant with white tablecloths--not a pub with brown paper laid on top of the tables.  We ordered the NY strip and the other steak option and both enjoyed our dishes.  Halfway through dinner, a loud party was seated next to us and it got even louder and more impossible to hear each other.  We requested to move to the next table over for some relief and the waiter was very helpful with the move.  The worst part: we got to dinner at 8:30 thinking we could enjoy the meal, or at least finish it off, with live music but by 10:30 the music hadn't yet started and our meals had long been finished so we couldn't continue to hold the table.  We left before the music began--disappointing!  I would expect $12-$14 entrees for a loud, pub type of venue like Beehive but our dishes came out to much more.

Expensive for the quality... The place smells fishy (no pun intended), and its not because its all prepared center stage, I really think its the moldy humidity of the local.  I saw a lot of asian folks going, so I figured if judged by native diners, then it should be a safe bet.  Definitely mass produced sushi, and relatively pedestrian Chinese food.  Dry pastries.  If you are in a rush for lunch, it makes sense to do the quick buffet.  But nothing to write home about.  Average food, ok service.  Pricey.  Quite frankly, the Natick Collection food court sushi is actually better, they are fast and its more affordable - IF you want to go into the mall.  Very spacious, so if you are in the mood for going out with the lunch crowd from work, you have enough space to create your own setting, stuff your face if you don't mind so-so for lunch price, and then say "adios amigos" time to go back to cubicle city and burp it up for the rest of the afternoon.  Lately when really pressed for time, I've been doing take out - but at 15-$17 a pop, I think I should stick with cold cuts in my fridge or a happy meal (hey, I love Micky D fries!) and wait for better sushi elsewhere.  If I'm going to part ways with my dead presidents... might as well enjoy them.

I was not impressed. I went here as apart of group, but honestly, I would been better trying my luck at the food court on the other side. On the up side, the waiting staff was friendly, and the service was prompt. I'm just no into charging an arm and a leg for food that is not that great. 

On top of that, they didn't have wifi?!? I guess they didn't want people getting online to complain about the food! But seriously, I just feel like they could have done better that's all. The food lacked flavor and zest that I was expecting for the zesty prices.

My favorite Mexican food cart was closed, so I looked around for another one, but was surprised there were no other Mexican carts. I decided to try Poco India since I like both Indian and Mexican food (which is an odd combination but thought I'd give them a try). I ordered the elephant burrito which is a large flour tortilla filled with your choice of meat, beans, sauces, vegies, etc. It took 15 mins. to get my order though I was the only customer. The burrito was average, consisting mostly of meat (spicy pork) and rice with not much of anything else. I was looking forward to more sauce, vegies and spices. However, it was dry and bland. Perhaps their other dishes are better, though I doubt I'll return.

The food is fine.  Two star rating due to relatively low value:  example on my visit today was Greek salad for $11.99 (on the web it says $10.99, so don't base your price expectations on the on-line info they publish http://www.allmenus.com/tx/austin/14529-hoovers-cooking/menu/).  Salad was a broiled chicken breast with a small amount of artichoke hearts, a very small amount of feta, sprinkle of black (canned, pre-sliced) olives, and a pile of average lettuce.  More like a $10 value than a $12 value--even being generous. Also, $9.99 catfish fillet was SMALL.  

If you like good food but are not sensitive about price, you'll be satisfied.  But by no means is this place a bargain.

I've visited the place twice. And the only reason why I gave it 2 stars is because the first experience was good. I ordered Kung Pao Chicken the first time from Grubhub and it tasted good.

Today I order pickup for Picked cabbage fish soup. The entire dish is pretty much not edible. It has so many round peppers and those peppers make your tongue numb. I didn't eat any of the peppers. The soup and everything in it makes your tongue numb... Usually Chinese restaurants will deep fry these peppers so they don't have the numb taste. From looking at color of these peppers, clearly these peppers weren't deep fried or cooked properly. And they put so many peppers in it! 

Another thing that bothers me is that no one wears mask. I saw at least 3 staffs there and not a single mask :(

Bleh....

Signs outside say Holy Smokes and the inside branding says Barrel & Boar. Confusing.

Won't be back. The employees inside were super nice so I truly hate to give this two stars but the food was just.....not that great. Particularly the sides.

Ordered ribs, pulled pork, brisket, turkey, collards, cheesy potatoes and beans. They didn't give us the ribs. We went back later and got them - free of charge which was good but we already had company over, etc....

Greens had this whole sweet vinegar taste going on - not what it do. Cheesy potatoes were so plain and boring. Beans were okay - different. My ole man didn't care for them because they were all sorts of bean types mixed but the flavor was good. 

We got three sauces - carolina, spicy and sweet. I guess spicy was the best but I didn't like any of them. Super weird flavors. 

Ribs and pork were okay. Meats were a bit drier than preferred.

Tim Hortons in the Guildford area.

Parking is available in the strip mall lot.

The location looks a bit dumpy from the outside, but the interior is modern with all the other locations.

This location ran out of decaf coffee, and for some reason the guy behind the counter refused to make some more. Um, isn't this place a coffee shop? Knock one star off.

The ice coffee I got instead was served in a plastic cup with a sippy lid. Interestingly enough I still got a paper straw. Tasted fine.

Wow, this Chuck E. Cheese has definitely changed since I last stepped foot in here as a kid, to the point where I barely recognized it. I came today for my nephew's third birthday party.  Granted it has been over 15 years since I've been here, and I understand change is inevitable, but this place looked so empty and not like the fun and exciting place I looked forward to as a kid. 

The amount of games and play structures have decreased tremendously. I would say there are about a third of the machines left that use to be there. The huge jungle gym structure and ball pit have been removed. This place honestly looks sad. 

A lot of the machines and games were out of tickets and one of the machines that take photos were out of the paper. There use to be game attendants on the floor replacing these things. The birthday boy wanted to take a photo on the machine that was out of photo paper, but even after asking for it to be replaced, it was never replaced. A lot of game credits were wasted on these games/machines. 

Food is not really good here either, and it's also expensive. $20 for a medium sized pizza that tastes like it came from the frozen aisle of a grocery store. 

Also, the back half of this place where the reserved tables are held was extremely cold in temperature. It was just that one particular area, everywhere else was normal temperature. This was really odd. 

Two stars because I kind of feel bad. It is not really the staff that is at fault. I think the chain/franchise itself has gone downhill. I would recommend Dave & Buster's over this place. I don't plan on coming back here.

When you talk about World of Beers, you're really talking about the Good, the Bad and the Ugly.

First the Good: This place has a good selection of bottled beer. 

The Bad? Service is a tad slow and the decor, with an assortment of 10 dollar framed chessy rock posters makes me feel like they ran out of cash. 

Bringing me nicely to the Ugly. You pump this much money into a place but don't put in a kitchen? Yes that's right, the only food available is via take out from an assortment of lame BD eateries! They have to be kidding me with that!

Totally disappointing! I ordered a chorizo cemita as the description at the front of the food cart was compelling and I don't often get to enjoy chorizo. There was no one else around, we can thank COVID-19 for slow business. So slow that while in an attempt to order more, I was curtly told "no - no have" when I asked for horchata, too. The hand written sign was a failed but promising marketing attempt. So anyways, ten minutes later, I took the sandwich 50 feet home, unwrapped the sandwich from bright red grease soaking through the double layers of wrapping (plastic wrap and paper). The amount of chorizo in this thing was insane. Honestly, too much, too messy. The jalapeños were flavorful. The cheese was not melted since the whole sandwich wasn't even hot. And, where was the avocado? One teeny tiny sliver in the middle. Oh, and the bread that the sign so sweetly described? Stale. I don't get this food cart, I wouldn't go back nor recommend. The only positive is I legitimately had two cups of chorizo leftover for use later. Breakfast burritos at home anyone?

I take my fried chicken pretty seriously. First of all, outside of Church's and KFC, fried chicken is surprisingly difficult to find. Sure, there are plenty of restaurants serving fried chicken breast or chicken fried chicken, but that's like kissing your brother. Real fried chicken has both meat and bones. Together.  On each piece. Emphasis on meat. 

Secondly, I can't make a habit out of eating fried chicken if I want to maintain this girlish figure. So I consider it a special treat for those times when nothing else will satisfy that ubiquitous craving. 

It was for these reasons that I decided to venture down to SOCO for some MRS P's. I had tried this place once before when it was on Rainey St. But that was a while ago and I think alcohol was involved. Mostly, I remember my son telling me how great it was. So I was excited to go pick up a 12 piece bucket to share with the fam. Key word here is bucket, which per the KFC precedent would imply an assortment of chicken pieces like breasts, thighs, drumsticks and a couple of superfluous  wings. 

You can imagine my disappointment upon returning to my home and unpacking the "bucket" only to discover 12 pieces of overcooked chicken parts that included 8 wings, 2 tiny drumsticks and 2 mystery pieces of boneless hunks. To be more accurate I wasn't disappointed so much as pissed off. Considering I paid $37 (which included 2 things of Mac n cheese) I expected more. Wouldn't you? No, because you are smart enough to read reviews BEFORE rather than AFTER trying a place. 

So, if you're a tourist hanging out around SOCO, likely enamored with the food truck concept, and you want a little chicken snack then by all means give it a go. It will be made to order and hot. But if you like traditional fried chicken with recognizable parts both meaty and bony, you best go elsewhere. Like your home town.

I enjoy going to steakhouses for a specific reason: karaoke.  The girl who DJ's karaoke on Saturdays is awful.  She caters to her close friends and allows them to sing much more often than the other patrons.  Karaoke is something that should draw a lot of paying customers but this girl is just driving them away.  I've had the food here a couple of times and it's pretty good but in the greater Boston area there are a lot of good choices for Japanese steak houses and something like that bad DJ will keep me and my friends from going back.

I was there last night for a wedding reception for my good friends.  The food served at reception was good.  Bartenders were good.  The staff at the reception were all great.  The view outside was amazing.  But the problem was.....

My husband, 2-month old daughter & I was there last night for a good friends wedding.  We were very disappointed to find out there were not changing stations available in restrooms.  My husband went to take care of her & came back to get me from reception because there was nothing available in men's restroom.  The women's restroom did not have anything available either.  An employee directed us and another mother to restroom downstairs.  We struck out their as well.  We went to front desk to ask if there was anywhere we could use to help us take care of the children in private.  The employee directed us to sitting area in lobby nearby saying the chair was pretty comfortable.  An employee told us the changing stations had been removed before a recent remodel but had not been put back in after they were finished.  We ended up taking care of the children in the lobby.  We felt embarrassed.  We felt others would judge us but that we did not have a choice.  The next time we needed to my husband used the floor in the corner of the reception.  Another parent at the reception told me they had used the floor in corner of reception room as well.  This wedding had quite a few very young children in attendance.  I guess we could have gone to the car.  Or we could have left her with a baby sitter but I many guests wanted to meet baby for first time.  Or I could have stayed home.  I know you are hotel with private rooms but I feel you also invite the public who will not be staying overnight in because you have coffee shop, restaurant, meeting rooms, wedding reception facilities you invite the public in and should provide changing stations in the restrooms.  We were disappointed and expected more at otherwise such a nice place.

I hate having to give this restaurant only 3 stars when it really deserves 5 stars, but ... I ordered takeout/delivery one evening.  I thought the prices were reasonable so I ordered Pad Thai and samplers that should have totaled $16 including tax.  When the order came the driver told me the order was $23 but he didn't give me a receipt.  I told him my concern but he insisted it was $23.  I gave him $23 plus $2 for delivery.  He had the audacity to ask me for more!!!!  I told him, no that his tip is included in the $25 I handed him.  I won't be visiting nor ordering from this place again.  

The food was delicious, by the way.  However, I felt ripped off by $7-$9!

I gave this place 3 stars a year and a half ago and went back today.  Their food was good but service was crazy slow.  There were 2 servers at first in a dining room that needed 4-5 for breakfast.  2 more appeared later but spent most time behind the counter poking at a computer screen.  I noticed there were 2 people in the kitchen - when tables are walking out because they sat down and no one got to them it's time for the kitchen to start delivering food.  The waitstaff appeared  inexperienced - that's cool, my first waitress job was a diner - but they need more people or a manager or someone to pitch in if they can't keep things moving or if they're short staffed because someone called out.

Free parking near downtown at a trusted brand of hotel. But..this is not the Omni we know. They have no control over the surrounding environment of the freeway and pan handlers, but surely they could do a much better job at making this an oasis once you enter the grounds- covered parking or not making the cars visible from the street,  clean windows-idk if they're cloudy for privacy or just dirty- There are other options. A big improvement would be getting rid of that worn brown carpet in the entrance and putting down some tile maybe? Does it always smell like cologne? Just, no.
I hated to do it because I've grown to love Omni and you get points toward a free stay if you're a member, but I just couldn't stay here.

I really found nothing special about this coffee. I noticed it walking by and saw a crowd of people so I figured I'd give it a try.  As I was trying to decide what to order, a patron was saying how great it was and he made a recommendation to me.   I forget what I paid but it was expensive but hey, we all know coffee is expensive these days but I wasn't impressed and I would definitely not go back. Oh well, you've gotta try new things and experience them for yourself!

only reason why I'm giving these place a 2 is because just the Carnitas chunks in my burrito tasted good other than that it was poorly made. We ordered 2 burritos one was steak and the other carnitas. The steak was filled with mostly smushed beans and a little bit of steak. why do they soak the burritos in sauce???!!! It was soggy and not pleasant to eat. We are now both sick. Our stomachs are not happy. Should of driven to Annas taqueria.

I've been here twice already and I'm not impressed. The first time I had tacos de asada and pastor. The meat was over cooked and hard on both. I love that the tortillas are handmade but they seem to fall apart after the first bite or 2. The salsas are good just not a big selection. I also tried the menudo, it was bland. I decided to give it another chance and try the tacos again. Same experience, meat was hard and over cooked and the tacos fell apart. The handmade tortillas were delicious though as was the agua de horchata. The supermarket part of it was great thought. Had a really good selection of Mexican products.

I visited for my monthly haircut. Was taken in immediately by Monica and she asked what kind of haircut I needed. She went to work and it felt like she was raking leaves! She was using so much pressure with the comb that I thought half my scalp was being torn off. She used the #3 clippers and was rough and moving the razor too fast. I was lectured on various haircare products I need to purchase from them during the "special event".

Granted, I was in and out in about 5 minutes, but the level of discomfort during this haircut was uncalled for and unnecessary. She was in a hurry as it was the $7.99 haircut special and with the amount of people waiting, she probably wanted to serve as many customers as possible.

I'll be back, but Monica isn't touching my hair! (The only way I knew her name is from my receipt. I didn't see her DBPR license on display at her workstation.)

I'm a hair snob. Maybe I'm vain, but I appreciate a truly good haircut. I thought the staff at DeKwa was wonderful, but now that I've discovered what a difference a truly fabulous Asian hair salon can make, I must say that the haircut I received did not meet my high expectations. If you have hair that requires precision sculpting, razor detailing, or just the right amount of youthful edge, I would not recommend DeKwa. I approached DeKwa with high hopes that I would fall in love with it because the staff was great and the reviews here were good, but I will continue to seek out a better Asian hair place.

These folks get two stars because, well, technically here I am, and nothing is broken. And I want to be as fair as possible.

Three years ago I used Eagle Lines to help me get from the Boston area to Austin TX. They were very good--so when I was looking to do the same move in reverse, I had no question about who to hire. A lot can change in a few years; I know that more than anyone.

Eagle Lines acknowledges that moving across the country is stressful. I believe they even market themselves as being a company that takes stress out of a move. If you're a go-with-the flow, flexible type of person, that's probably true: but then again if that were true, you wouldn't be very stressed about a move anyway, would you?

What I mean by flexible is this: If you don't really have to be out of a place within a certain time-frame (e.g. need to coordinate being out for a lease or a house closing), if you have a few grand or so extra to plunk down (without solid explanation as to where it's going or what forms of payment are acceptable), if you're not big on estimates or communication about what's happening (without investing your time in repeat emails / phone calls, etc. that may or may not be returned), if you're cool with multiple, random people contacting you as part of the move (without much identification or without leaving messages when you're not available), and with lots of pretty beat up boxes that make you cringe upon opening, then this is probably a good company for you to hire.

To end on a positive note I'll give some kudos to David, the main guy on delivery. Of course none of this was his fault--he was friendly and he did a good job. Another positive is that the time it took for our things to arrive was pretty quick. Good luck.

Came for Valentine's Day and was disappointed that they didn't tell us prior to reservation it would be such a prefixed menu. The first server told us the menu was $45 / person (seemed inexpensive). Then our actual waiter apologized and mentioned she was incorrect, the appetizer, first course, second course + dessert would be $65/person. Seems reasonable and I can appreciate the prefixed idea...just wish they would have told me when they called to confirm like the other open table restaurants.

I'm not a 'rich' food person, so meals like the very creamy soups, tuna tartare with puréed creams, and buttery dressings are just not my preference.
I was looking for more of their seafood selection and flexibility since I am picky : )

Nice waiter though.

Would not go back.

Ahhhh Monumental Movieland. After calling just about every single hotel in the area and finding they were completely booked we ended up here. If I were to sum this hotel up in one word it would be cheap. As we are walking down the stale smelling hallways I'm staring at the movie and show posters. They were covered in dust. Why not clean them up a little to look presentable for the guests? I know they're old, but sheesh.
We finally enter our room. It had the same stale smell as the hallway. To be expected. Now comes the inspection.The bed frame wasn't an actual bed frame. You could see they've built it themselves. Not that this matters, but maybe that's the reason the bed was so uncomfortable? To make matters worse before bedtime I hear "what the heck is this?" And I turn to see my friend holding up what is supposed to be a pillow, but looks like a sack with a bunch of clothes in it. Seriously. Shower time might have been the funniest part of the hotel. I am totally aware hotels give you the crappiest little bottles of soap but this was just ridiculous. The bar of "soap" stuck to my body and the "body wash" smelled like plastic. Not even pretend soap, just plastic. My friend said he recommended staying far away from it because it must not be healthy or even safe. I couldn't help but chuckle.
I definitely regret not bringing my own towels because they provide you with sandpaper. The towel was literally scratching my body. 
I probably wouldn't stay here again unless I brought my own things to make up for this. Actually, I probably wouldn't stay here at all. I did not have a completely horrible stay, but there are far better hotels for the same price in the area.

Quite disappointed. I was looking forward to an upscale, tasteful meal but what we ordered was terribly disappointing. My husband ordered the scallops lemoncello, which was cloyingly sweet and didn't seem to be made fresh ... like the scallops may have been pan fried, but hours earlier. The asparagus and risotto too. My Chicken Lazario was drowning in olive oil and also not very hot. The piece of garlic bread it came with looked good, but one of the bites I took I could literally feel the oil run into my mouth. Only my son's tiramisu was any good. Not very friendly staff either.

Food is pretty good, but insanely pricey and they have also now instated a new courtesy charge to "protest" the minimum wage increase. Not surprising for a place where the wait staff is rude, the clientele are so self-absorbed they will sit on you without noticing and steal your spot, and where looking for a window seat means taking life into your own hands. 

This is not a "Portland" spot whatsoever. The views are great, but food, people and atmosphere are way better elsewhere; where you won't get elbowed by random strangers for your seat! Come for a drink, but don't come for dinner.

I really wanted to like Darryl's, but I came here with some friends last weekend, and we had the following experiences:

--My friend ordered the mussels, and one of them was bad.  She vomited.  (I could probably stop my review here.)

--I also ordered mussels.  There was sand in a lot of them.

--We had made reservations for dinner (and there was no mention of a cover charge), but when the bill came, we were charged for the cover.  (As a group, we spent $200+ before tip.)

--We had a bar tab before we were seated, and when we asked for the bar tab to be transferred to our table, the servers/hosts could not manage that.

--Moreover, my friend had left his credit card at the bar with the bar tab, and they wouldn't even return his credit card to him when he asked for it.  (He asked for it *so that he could pay the bill.*)  In fact, my friend had to get up and discuss the situation with several employees.  (They offered him a free drink for the confusion, which seems like an odd response.  There were six of us waiting for the bill to be figured out, and they offered one person a free drink?  So we would have to sit around some more?)

--Two members of our group ordered burgers cooked medium-rare.  The burgers were actually cooked all the way through and were very salty.

--Our table was about three feet from the band, so we felt like we were seated in the middle of the dance floor--there were people dancing on three sides of our table.  At one point, the *hostess* (not a customer!) was leaning against my friend's chair (she was gripping the back of the chair) so that my friend couldn't lean back!

The only reasons I rate this place two stars instead of one: the music was fun (although loud); the drinks were strong; the host was friendly to me; and our waitress was fine.

This was a subpar hotel, and I would not recommend. For some reason, there are multiple Double Tree hotels within the Austin area, two of which look alike and are the same street. We must have spent an hour trying to locate the hotel just because of its awkward location. Though, the lady at the front desk was helpful in directing us and informed us that the hotel was conveniently located behind Denny's. The front-desk staff were definitely very nice. 

If you're afraid of elevators, this hotel is not for you. The elevators seem to move at a snail pace, for some reason, and it is very inconvenient. If you're in a rush, sucks for you, because the elevators will slow you down. Our hotel room also had a pungent smell, and we weren't really sure what it was from. It was also right off the highway, adding to a lot of noise. The bathroom was nice and spacious (one of the few positives), but alas, the beds were hard, uncomfortable, and left me waking up with back pain.

Yet again another Magic Kingdom let down. I just don't get it, with all the stellar restaurants throughout Walt Disney World why does the Magic Kingdom always seem to fall short? Well here it goes..... after reading reviews from trusted yelp friends I probably should have just cancelled my reservation and went elsewhere. Here's what I was expecting..... mediocre food with great, fun service, corny jokes and one liners. We were fine with this. 

Here's what we got..... we were seated and eventually greeted by our server or skipper as they are called at this restaurant. He bearly introduced himself and asked what we wanted. We placed our order and off he went. To start our meal we were given a loaf of sidewalk chalk with maple syrup. Oh sorry I meant bread with honey, it was hard to tell the difference. For dinner I ordered the fried chicken and my husband had the lamb chops. Fried chicken was tasty but not worth the $23 price tag for one piece. Lamb chops were edible but tasted like the one's that are frozen on sale at the grocery store.

The whole time we were there we were listening to other skippers and tables laughing, joking and having a great time. Ours wouldn't even come back to get us a drink refill let alone tell a joke or hang out for a minute. I never finished my meal because I was dying of thirst with an empty glass the whole time.  Couldn't flag down anyone because no one would even make eye contact. 

We paid left and will never return! Come on Magic Kingdom get it together.

My review is relative to other hibachi grills i have been to

I was on the fence to do a 2/3 rating
Ultimately i went w/2 rating, but either way i was not impressed

Everyone was friendly and the restaurant seemed to be clean.  However, that's where the positive feedback ends.

Constructive feedback:  
-don't rush people to order
-food was way too salty
TOO MUCH food for one person (give a rice/noodle option, but please don't throw, literally, both of too much my way)
-the cook was sloppy when he served; he just threw all the food on my plate
I can't stand that bc i hate having my food mixed
Every other hibachi i have been to, i have had the cook carefully place the food on my plate

This pains me to write since DryBar is my go to place for EVERY occasion!! The 2 stars is for the super sweet front desk receptionist. I always have great results from here so I am thinking this stylist was having a rough day.
I needed my hair ultra perfect for an important meeting. The stylist seemed a bit nervous & expressed that my hair was difficult. Yes, my hair is long but that's never been an issue here. When she was finished I was shocked at how FRIZZY it was. Usually I walk out feeling fabulous & this time I was a hot mess. Once I mentioned something she just added a whole bunch of product & hair spray. I ended up putting it in a pony for my meeting.
My blow dry usually lasts 5 days before I wash it. This one I had to wash out as soon as I got home.

There was a dark time last year when mice ran wild throughout our apartment.  They came in through a little hole behind the fridge and took up residence in all the dark, secluded spots in our home.  We got home from vacation and there they all were...having a little vacation of their own.  

I called maintenance and it took them a week to come and fix the hole.  A week!  The reason it took them so long?  They had to answer calls of people who had lost their heat first.  Death by hypothermia trumps animal kingdom, I get that.  But the woefully understaffed maintenance is just the first example of the problems with the Samia properties.

The heat in winter is a huge problem.  Whenever it's really cold, it doesn't come on.  The rest of the time, our apartment is so hot we have to open all the windows.  I loathe wasting so much energy but I also loathe dying of heatstroke.

The bathroom is kind of ridonkulous.  There's no ventilation and as far as I can tell their solution is to paint over the mold that accumulates.  But since it hasn't been painted in three years large swathes of paint break off and litter the floor, exposing the grodiness beneath.  Also, the toilet doesn't really fit so there's a piece cut out of the bottom of the door so you can shut it!

They do reactive repairs, but I'm willing to bet this whole building is full of places like mine that need some serious renovation.  One of the walls has a jagged crack starting 1/2way and going all the way across to the ceiling.  The walls are thin and I can hear everything my neighbors are doing - luckily the woman who had sex in her extremely squeaky bed every Friday night (when I was working Saturdays) from 11 - 11:15 exactly has moved out.

Most of the time this place is OK, and I guess I'd rather be sweating in winter than freezing.  It will be nice, though, when we eventually have a place where we can have the toaster and the air conditioner going at the same time.

My last experience was pretty weird. I used to go to the store on Powell fairly frequently enough, and never really had a problem, but the older woman at the new location seemed to follow me around the store and watch me as if she was expecting me to steal, which made me feel uncomfortable, and frankly, I'm a bit insulted. Every minute or so, she would peek around the corner and watch me and then ask "You need help with anything?" No ma'am, I don't need help. I didn't need help 40 seconds ago when you asked the last time while watching me closely. Maybe I can help you learn some profiling skills, though. I had mentioned when I first walked in the door that I was on my way to work with my giant work bag, and needed to stash it behind the counter. Obviously, this is eliminating a great chance of me stealing anything by leaving my backpack with you. This also tells you I have a job. The fact that I was in a nice, clean dress and wearing fancy heeled boots with full make up and made my visit quick and unlingering should prove that I am a professional type and likely a good paying customer. So why on earth was I followed around and watched as if I was suspected of petty theft? Jeez louise! I have all my teeth, I wasnt holding my hands in my pockets or looking around suspiciously and leaning closer and closer into the shelves to sneak something, and I very clearly have a job that I even mentioned I was on my way to. I don't even look like your average 82nd ave tweeker. I don't even look like one of those punk ass teenage girls that try to steal because they spent all their allowance trying to get some old white dude to buy them fuzzy navel. Shit, man! Get it together. You spent so much time trying to make sure a harmless, small, employeed woman wasn't going to steal that you could have been robbed by three other customers and wouldn't even realize they were there at all.

Initially I was really excited when I found this salon via Yelp and other online reviews.  My experience however was lackluster.  The salon itself is cool and everyone I met there was nice and accommodating.  It is awkward when you get a bad hair service.  Maybe they were having a bad day?  I don't know.  My cut was OK at best and the blowout was one of the worst I have ever had.  Ever.  I actually had to go home and restyle my hair which was a bummer because I always look forward to leaving a salon with shiny, bouncy hair that is ready to go out on the town.  ~sigh~  I guess my quest for a new hair salon continues.

I've been to this Subway two times now and have only one complaint: they need to actually toast their toasted subs.  I went in the evening both visits and each time, the store was dead.  This Subway is located near the corner of Powers Ferry Rd. and Northside Dr. in a small shopping complex with a funky one-way parking lot.  The store itself is clean and in good condition.

I've had the $5 footlong Cold Cut Combo and the Spicy Italian sandwich here.  The Cold Cut Combo comes with three pre-sliced, turkey-based meats: ham, salami, and bologna.  The Spicy Italian comes with pepperoni and salami.  Needless to say, both come with plenty of cured meats, so if you order a footlong, get ready to digest almost 100% of your recommended daily intake of sodium.

I like to get my subs with a little bit of everything: spinach, shredded lettuce, sliced tomatoes, green peppers, red onions, pickles (sometimes), black olives, cucumbers, jalapenos, and banana peppers with oil & vinegar and oregano sprinkled on top.  The ingredients during my visits have been fresh and crisp.

Toasted is the way to go, but if someone handed me two subs from this place, one toasted and one not, I would not be able to tell the difference.  I'm not sure what the issue is.  Either their machine is broken or the temperature/time needs to be tweaked.

Service is fine.  The store closes at 9pm, Monday through Saturday, and 8pm on Sunday.  (Subway's web site has incorrect hours posted for this location.)

This is one of the most disappointing restaurants in Portland metro.  $10.00 for 3 tiny oysters supposedly cooked in olive oil and part--tasteless.  A "soba noodle bowl" with shrimp:  literally a single tangle of spaghetti.  Soba noodles are not spaghetti!  So spicy as to be inedible.  Cost:  $12.00.  So I spent $22.00 plus coffee for a meal that could not have been prepared by a professional cook.  Second (and last) visit.  The fish tacos are good.  Stick with those if you must go there.

I have been in here 20 min only to get chicken they out in a microwave they assured me the wait was for fresh baked chicken. This place is a joke I barely stop in due to the long lines and lack of urgency when making your meals. The southern comfort food is good yet the service is terrible. Never been to a restaurant that takes this long to serve food that's already prepared. They are in need of new management and employees

I usually *love* Milestones but my experience at this location this morning was totally sub-standard from what I expect from this chain.  (I've been to the Robson and South Surrey locations a few times each, and have always had a fab time.  With Bellinis, it's hard to go wrong, right?)  I hope it was just a one-off for the Denman locale, but I think probably not.  Our waiter was less than lack-lustre.  Not fast, nor efficient.  He said he was extremely busy, but looking around, I didn't understand how since there were only a few tables occupied.  He was less than engaged with us.  Brought tea but no milk/cream.  We asked and received it, but several minutes later as our teas grew cold.  He was just cold.  I'm not asking a lot, I don't think... not looking for a best friend, but I'd like someone who took in an interest in serving me my food.

Pet peeve: The new-ish "credit swipe at the table" machine is a great piece of technology... but as a waiter, please don't hover over me as I input your tip into the machine (or discuss it with my partner).  I don't like the 'pressure' or vibe you give off.

So, all that said.  I wonder what will happen when Catcus Club opens up across the way.  Still, Milestones is a great chain, and I will be back.  Just not the Denman location (as I recall the last time I went about a year ago, I was similarly unimpressed).  Make the walk and go to the Robson Street location instead

I came here on two occasions recently, once on a Friday evening and once on a Saturday. Both times, I had the same female bartender who proved to be rather rude and not friendly at all. I went up to the bar on the second level around 1030 that night and asked for a cocktail menu. While I understand it may be an inconvenience for her to mix involved cocktails at that time, I surely didn't expect the eyeroll that I received. No words were exchanged after we got our cocktails either, despite the four cocktails putting me over 60 dollars including tip. In that regard, I was a bit disappointed, as I expected a better attitude for the decent tip she received for 5 minutes of her time. The bar itself is nice and the atmosphere is good. Despite this, the dance floor was sloppy, especially made so by the individuals above the stairs repeatedly pouring drinks on dancers below, which made for a very discouraging experience. I haven't tried their food yet, but all in all, I don't believe I will be returning.

1) I'm really sick of the staff trying to sell things at the end of class (shoes, meal delivery service, etc). I am marketed to all day, everyday. It would be nice if I didn't get it at my workout class too. 

2) I don't want to hear the instructor singing along with the songs. I appreciate the enthusiasm but if I wanted to serenaded, I'd go to a concert. Stop singing, start coaching. Speaking of music, they played a Christmas rap song last week. In October. WTF. And enough of the "mash-ups" for crying out loud. Just play a full song already. 

3) I ride the bike instead of doing the treadmill for orthopedic reasons. When I'm on the bike, I'm totally ignored. No coaching, templates, instructions whatsoever. $170/mo to be ignored? Nah, I'm good. Maybe they could charge less if they didn't have 5 girls working at the front counter at the same time. 

4) Classes are too packed and you are herded in like cattle. Good luck trying to do burpees in your tiny little space on the workout floor. And don't even think about stretching on your own or focusing on something other in the class. You'll get weird looks from everyone.

My wife and I tried this place tonight as it had good reviews.  We wanted to see if it was really as good as the reviews.  We found it to be just shy of terrible.  I'll explain:  we were politely asked if we were eating in or take out, we were staying to eat so we seated ourselves.  We were the only people in the restaurant at 6pm, I should have known.  The waitress had no personality and took our drink order.  We reviewed the menu and ordered a house salad and a small Milano pizza.  The salad was literally all lettuce with about 8 grape tomatoes halved and red onion slices with balsamic drizzle topping.  I like my salad but this was just way too much lettuce, apologizes for no pictures.  The pizza came out it a square and only sliced into four pieces. I would have thought they could have cut it into eight smaller slices, but that's ok.  The pizza was fresh and delicious otherwise.  Service was not friendly, felt like she didn't want to be there.  Finally from Yelp, it had a 10% discount and she only deducted it off the salad not the entire meal.  I didn't say anything as I would have normally said something.  I just gave a smaller tip.  We will never be back.

Don't be fooled by the "prettiness" of the website. The service gets worse and worse overtime they change management companies (now on #4) and managers (now on #...I lost count). A few things:

1) The inside hallways are never cleaned. They are dirty! The carpet is soiled. The walls have dents and marks. The stairwell has stains.

2) The pool is nice, but is in the shade for about 3/4 of the day due to poor placement of the building. The hot tub has been down for repairs so many times, I never know if it is working.

3) The online payment for rent (which they encourage you to use) charges you a $100 convenience fee. Really? Its 2017. Why do we have convenience fees to use our debit/credit cards to earn miles?

4) The maintenance folks are not nice. The director Vaughn is actually rude. 

5) The walls are paper thin. I can hear everything in the hallways and stairwells.

6) With the addition of the restaurant, which is a nice addition (albeit way too expensive), there are tons of people going in and out of the property, leaving trash and cigarette butts and taking up every space in guest parking. 

My lease is up in November and I am already starting the process of figuring out where I can live. The beach amenity is nice, but is only available like 3 months (if that).

I needed Pho during my visit in Atlanta and decided to go to Pho King because it was closest.  Although, ultimately, it satisfied my Pho Craving- I had a couple of issues with the food.  Ordered Spring Rolls and they came out without mint to roll into the lettuce and there was only one piece of lettuce.  The Spring Rolls were also cold. 2.  The Pho was not really all that hot and it was covered in red onions.  I have always had it with white onions and prefer it that way. 3. The Fish Sauce was overly sweet and not fishy enough.  Overall, it was not a super authentic flavor, but got the job done in a pinch.

Sadly, this is an update to my previous 5 star "glowing" review of A&B, once my favorite place in Salem. I've been there as AB has grown from counter service to table service to full fledged "restaurant" with full bar and outdoor seating. Their menu grew but was always good and the service was always top notch... Until now.

On my most recent visit - a few weeks ago, the experience was SO different that I actually thought AB had been sold to a new proprietor.
