AB started out super vegan friendly- 3 vegan burgers, vegan shakes... It's was truly the coolest place around and I thought it was amazing that they were so in tune with catering to all diet types (veg, vegan, gluten free, meat free, traditional) ... Bit by bit things began to change. The vegan shakes were the first to go. "We can't find a supplier, but we are looking for a new one" they told me; that was 3 years ago I think! 

Back to my most recent visit... I quickly noticed the menu had changed. 3 vegan burgers were now 2 and the lineup of traditional burgers was different. The sweet potato burger, which was amazing, was gone. I reluctantly ordered one of the vegan burgers, though had to get a lettuce wrap since they were "all out" of the gluten free/vegan buns. My friend ordered a bacon cheeseburger. When our food arrived, my little burger sadly wrapped in a warm, limp piece of romain was all alone - no chips. I inquired only to find out that the homemade potato chips are cooked in the same oil as all the fried meat and chicken and are therefore not vegan (not even vegetarian)! My friend didn't even finish her burger - she said it was just "ok". 

I spoke briefly to a manager about the changes. It was obvious she didn't really care and used excuses such as "seasonal produce" -- hmm, pretty sure sweet potatoes are not seasonal, also pretty sure that vegan/gluten free buns are available all year as well ... And frying potato chips in chicken grease is a business decision and not one dictated by season.

She thought I would be pacified by knowing the spring menu would have new "seasonal" veggies and more salads. It makes me sad that in a city as cool and progressive as Salem, what once seemed to be the coolest place to eat has succumb to typical corporate greed and money saving shortcuts regardless of whether or not they compromise the integrity of the establishment. Fortunately, Salem is always changing - so if AB has had its "15 minutes" there will soon be someone else to take over as the cool place to go in town.

I need to remember to go inside. I waited in the drive thru line today for a whopping 18 minutes. Either the car that was two in front of me ordered 6 of the entire menu or they were chewing someone out. The guy in the window was nice and acknowledged how slow it was but offered nothing to make up for it. Not cool. I also almost side swiped my  jeep (which isn't a huge car) trying to maneuver around the itty bitty drive thru corner.. Go inside people! The staff is great but why in the world they decided a drive thru was a good idea here is beyond me.

I really don't understand how this restaurant has 4.5 stars. I got sick here tonight and I wouldn't be surprised if the food was to blame. 

I made a reservation for 8, but when we arrived the hosts was not paying attention. After a few minutes she turned to me and I tried to tall to her about my reservation. Then a manager came over and used the register with us just standing there waiting for help. After 10 minutes of being ignored, the hostess is finally ready to pay attention. She has lost my reservation but told me it would be a very sorry wait for only 2 people. She seemed very confused. Sat other groups before us and couldn't remember the order people came in. We were finally seated by 8:40.

The waitress was in a bad mood and she kept bringing 8 dishes of starters despite there being 9 people at the table. Orders were mixed up very frequently and none of the staff really understood how to do their jobs.

As for the food, everything was weird. It was not at all what I expected from hibachi. The seasonings were lacking and everything had a char. I can't say I enjoyed anything. Some of the flavors were okay even if they were not traditional, but that was over shadowed by the tough, low quality steak, chewy scallops, rubbery shrimp, and tough lobster. 

I will not be coming back.

What a strange piece-shiv "spa" this place is.  

At Frenandez Spa
YOU CAN GET:

Liquor
Beer with liberal-as-fuck use of rubber bands for anti-clinking of your six-pack of High Life on the walk home.
A Frisbee
Strange Looks
A foam glider
A gigantic avocado 
An ATM, which may or may not be working
To see a strange old man lecturing six 7-year-olds about who-the-fuck-knows what
A gumball
Those Jesus Candles
Cigarettes
Matches, and they're free unlike the boo-hoo-frowny-face sign has you know at Forest Hills Liquors!
Other produce
Nothing "spa"-related as far as I can tell.

It's rare I throw out the 2-star weaponry, but Fernandez Spa really deserves it, and I don't mean that in a negative way even.  It's just a real honest-to-goodness piece-shit.

I've seen only one Ayoub's store which is on Denman. This is a true dried fruit and nuts heaven. Huge area with just great selection of all the yummy stuff. I was completely lost and happy like a kid in a toy store. At the other side, I am not a big fan of loose anything, open to everybody and anybody's touching and tasting which I personally saw. What I also did not like was that there were lots of products without a name tag. I asked a few questions, but than both the salesperson and I got quickly bored going back and forth with my search for knowledge (basic information). The name of the product, where it is made, the main ingredients, does it have any added sugar, salt, oil, let alone the nutrition content. There was also no info on best before or expiration date. All of this missing information does not seem to be difficult to incorporate and it is really important to me. Especially when I am buying something that I am going to put in my body and that is so expensive. For that reason, I will not be coming back and I am really sorry. On the bright side, I found Yupik online with all the missing components to my shopping experience, plus they are cheaper - so it's all good.

We were famished after shopping and decided to try this place.

Plus - huge portions. Great location.

Cons - server was hinting or promoting to make us order more; pad sew was just low quality rice noodles (trust me on noodle quality) doused in dark sweet sauce. Crispy pad thai was very mediocre where the corn starch gravy was forgettable and lacked identity. I guess it made enough impression for me to make this review. Their siew mai appetizer was expensive (4 pieces) and extremely poor quality.

Only eat here when convenient.

This place has really nothing to do with the show Cheers. It's a tourist-trappy kind of bar with an old tv show's namesack (somehow - I have a feeling some marketer somewhere lost their job over this one...)
 
We managed to find it at night without a map (we're awesome) and only stayed long enough for one beer each at the bar. The musician was good, but kind of creepy when he used some crazy deep throaty voice - and the bartenders seemed a bit burned out. 

We ordered Sam Adams Oktoberfest. Tasted different than the same beer at other bars - made us wonder how often they clean their lines...?

Wish we could've seen the gift shop, but it was closed by the time we go there. Not an all together terrible experience, but we'll never go again. Definitely overpriced for what it is. And again - has NOTHING to do with the show Cheers.

If you're looking for good BBQ I wouldn't waste precious time at Stubb's. Ate here on a week night evening. The app was good, drinks were good. Got the 3 meat plate. It came out within 3 minutes of ordering and everything on the plate was room temperature. I would've said something but the waiter didn't stop by for about 5 minutes after I got my food and didn't bother to ask how it was once he did. I just don't get how you can be a BBQ joint in downtown Austin and not even serve hot BBQ. The hard part's smoking it, seasoning and giving it that great taste (but that was lacking at Stubb's too). The easiest dang thing is to keep it warm until you serve it. Check out another BBQ joint in town if you want the goods. Nuff said.

First time here, not pleased at all. I ordered a grilled cheese, while my boyfriend ordered a Ruben. We waited over fifteen minutes before we were told they were out of meat for the Ruben and asked if he wanted something else. My grilled cheese sat there, getting cold, while they made his sandwich. The whole time the waitresses sat and chatted with a table of regulars, all the while we were trying to get their attention to order something to drink. They over charged us, and when we got to the car we realized that the cheese on his sandwich wasn't even melted. We went back in and they remade it, but STILL the cheese wasn't melted. In a hurry, running late, after waiting over a half hour for two grilled cheese sandwiches, we just accepted it and left. Most definitely would NOT recommend. Your money is best spent elsewhere.

South Congress Cafe has a great location and a great vibe-upscale diner with a nice bar. 

My boyfriend and I were wandering SoCo looking for a place to eat on a Wednesday night and were drawn in by the curb appeal of South Congress Cafe. Unfortunately the appeal stopped at the curb.

We were sitted and asked what we wanted to drink. We seemed to lose our waiters interest the moment we asked for only water to drink. (Lots of folks had full bottles of wine on their table and what waiter doesn't want 20% of that!). He was apathetic and seemed uninterested in answering questions.The menu is interesting and looks chef driven so we were trying to generate a bit of conversation about it. But maybe because we are older and tee totallers, he didn't seem interested and gave us shortest answers possible.

We shared the lamb enchiladas. (Maybe another thing that annoyed him was our sharing a entree.) All I can say is "Eww".  For starters the sides were plain white rice and squash. When I say PLAIN, I mean plain white rice-like not even hot and not so much as a grain of salt on the rice for seasoning. And the rice tasted better than the squash. I don't know how to describe the squash dish except raw and rancid. The squash was cubed and crunchy-not sure it had actually been cooked. Then the taste would best be described as "rancid". Either what the squash was "cooked" in or the squash itself had gone off and it was clearly "off". We did not eat either side. The lamb inside the enchilida was stringy, salty (we found where all the salt went!) and unrecognizably lamb. All gross.

We told our kindly waiter and he replied (over his shoulder), "I'll tell someone". Sure you will, kid.

Work right down the street from this place so we were all thrilled when it opened, since there is nothing really around on Middlesex turnpike to eat other than the 99's, the what use to be the Naked Fish and Pedro's (now both out of business, wonder why????) location location location..... and now soon to be Max & Dylan's so other than those places for us office people there is Wendy's down the other end towards the mall. Went to the BB allot when it first opened. Owner is from NY, trying to get the NY "deli" experience to Mass and non less to Middlesex Turnpike, he was nice. Got to know me with a hello from all the staff, I'm quite unforgettable I've been told. It's definitely my gorgeous red hair !!  Anyways, friendly staff, place is clean too. Food is ok, they advertise in NY your lunch would be over $25, but for Bedford/Burlington $15 + is still pricy. Some nice salads and some unique items like the Jersey Joe. Corn beef is bland, lacks in flavor, nothing to write home about, and the pastrami is fatty. Coffee is VERY expensive. I haven't been in awhile so maybe I'm due back for a visit :)

I gew up in Brighton and my parents would take my siblings and I to Daniel's Bakery all the time while growing up. Back when Daniel still owned and ran the bakey, everything was great and reasonably priced. When Daniel retired in 2007 and sold the business, the quality of food went downhill. Even though the original recipies are used, items don't taste quite the same anymore. And baked goods don't stay fresh for more than a day after purchase. Plus, everything costs at least twice as much and the size of the baked goods has shrunk considerably. I remember eating huge hot cross buns as a kid but those are now barely the size of a mini cupcake and filled with way too much candied fruit. Some of the employees aren't friendly. My parents still live in Brighton but rarely go to Daniel's anymore.

Lines are too long due to their popularity. 
We tried getting the ice cream twice but decided against standing in line for over an hour. 
Finally, the second time, I decided to buy a pint of their most popular flavor Sea salt caramel (@ $9) and eat at home. 
Ice cream was only average. I have had this flavor at other speciality ice cream store and loved it. 
It was too high in salt and the ice cream base was at the best average. I would rather eat baskin robins or cold stone than pay premium price for their average ice cream. 
Not sure what all the hype is about.

It's not bad, and sometimes it is good.  That's my impression of John Harvard's in Framingham, the very popular and busy restaurant in a corner of the Giant Strip Mall now known as Shopper's World.

I've been there about a dozen times.  The beef stew is rather good, the blackened steak tips are hard to chew.  There was  a spicy dish mixed with sausages that I was indifferent to. Nachos are a mess. In general, the food is tasty, the service is good, and the price low. The Old Man Winter (Ale) was bitter but full, and the brown ale smoother.  My one main complaint about it is how unnecessarily noisy it is - the tinny music that can't really be heard raises the din level to make sure you won't stay too long, and perhaps that's the point.  I keep going back because it's next to the craft store and never has been bad. When the weather is warm you can sit outside, and it's really nice!  I think if the kitchen wasn't so formulaic I'd give an extra star.

Rented from Alamo at the Orlando Airport. Prior to arrival, I contacted Alamo to find out about a second driver (spouse) at no extra cost. Received an email from Alamo stating that spouse could drive at no extra cost. There also was a free upgrade advertised and I checked that out with the company as well and they advised that if I rented a standard car, it would be upgraded to a full size. When we arrived at the desk, the gentleman serving us was very rude and suggested that there could be no extra driver unless the cost of 10.25(?) per day was charged. He also informed me that the upgrade had already been applied and I would get a standard car only. He offered to show me the message on the computer. I again advised him that this had been checked out before we arrived and then I asked to see the manager. The manager attended and told me that the response that I had received from Alamo was incorrect but he would waive the cost this time. He also allowed the upgrade "this time". I thanked him very much but while finishing the paperwork, the original gentleman serving us made a negative remark to my wife but we let it pass in order to cause no further delays. All else went well with the rental. The car was clean and the parking lot staff were very helpful and professional. It seems that the staff at the desk need some customer service training as they turned me against the company from the first moment we arrived at the counter.

Super fun spot with great food, drinks, and atmosphere! 

However, last time we went we had a rather sour experience.  We came for the Sunday night 9pm-close happy hour.  All of the food we ordered was off of the happy hour menu.  When we received our bill we noticed that the happy hour prices were not on our receipt.  We questioned this with our server who told us that our food orders were put in at 8:55pm so did not qualify for the happy hour cost!!!! Are you kidding me?!! She said that the computers were automatic so there was nothing she could do.  If the computers are that strict and do not have an override system then you would've thought she would've given us a heads up to wait LITERALLY FIVE MINUTES before placing our orders.  Especially odd since she handed us the happy hour menu when we sat down....Very disappointed and hopefully I don't have this experience again.

CHECKED OUT

I love the Homewood Suites.  It is one of my favorite hotels for many reasons.  In fact, when I'm working in the area this is the hotel I typically stay at. 

I've decided to update my review because I was generous  on my last review.  I was still in the infatuation stage of my relationship with Homewood. Now don't get me wrong I haven't lost that loving feeling because I'm still in love with the brand but I may be on the rocks with this location. 

Everything started out great.  I was able to grab a room because if my status with Hilton.  So after waking up at 3:15am in Chicago and jumping on the first flight to Boston, I was able to freshen up and unpack my bag, before hitting the office. 

I started noticing things in my room.  Like the handle to my bedroom door was literally falling off.  The screws were totally stripped. My kitchen sink was dripping water every time I turned it on.  I could hear Justin T. singing "Cry me a Waterfall"!  I was going to call down but those were a couple of major fixes. First I don't want plumbers and locksmiths working in my room, while I'm at work.  What if they put my underwear on their heads and start making funny uTube videos.  Hey it could happen! Or they decide to take all the cash I hid under the mattress. Don't judge me there's no wall safe here. 

I've also noticed the heating wasn't working great. I was really cold the first night and it was set at 70.  Then I set it to 85 and it was still not pumping out major heat. I noticed in my last review I had issues with the AC.  I can't catch a break here when it comes to climate control. 

My final straw was when I returned to my room at midnight and it was not made.  Yes the maid seemed to ignore my room. It's not a good feeling.  I went down to see the night manager and he didn't seem very concerned. He then asked me if I left the "Do Not Disturb Sign" on the door! Wow! It's midnight and you are gonna pull the old...it's my fault! Dude it's not my first night in a hotel. I asked him for some fresh towels, which he grabbed for me in back. I just wasn't happy I had to go down to inform the staff about what they usually do. 

The food quality was also not great. I know everyone is trying to cut corners.  I was happy the first day for breakfast with hard boiled eggs.  Then on day two the hard boiled eggs disappeared. I asked and was told that they don't have them. They were serving the most gross looking egg soufflé. Two minutes later, the hotel worker that told me he had no hard boiled eggs offered to make scrambled eggs for some other hotel guest who was grossed out by the egg dish they were offering. Hmmm! Couldn't he had boiled me two eggs? In fact, he went on to offer scrambled eggs to other guests, who grossly looked at this dried out egg soufflé.  That's great but where's my hard boiled eggs.  It was the only healthy option. 

Last but not least the water in the shower here sucks.  You feel greasy when you get out of the shower. No matter what I do, I can not get the feeling of slime off my body.  I have no idea who's fault this is but it's just not a fun feeling in the morning. 

I love the concept of Homewood Suites.  In fact, this is the only location I usually have issues at. I just had to say something.  I just hope somebody is listening. 

PS The room with the issues was #114. Avoid it at all cost.

Sam's club use to have great prices for everything, that's no longer the case.  Their prices are now about the same as everywhere else, plus everywhere else you don't have to buy in bulk.  They started offering organic items a couple years ago which is why I renewed my membership, then they cut out most of the organic items.  The store is usually crowded and cashiers and very slow, if you need assistance in store you're out of luck.  No one there seems to know anything or how to get an answer and the employees at the customer service counter are rude, it is obvious all the employees would rather be anywhere else.

The food was good for this type of food.  It was painfully obvious that some of the staff really didn't care about customer experience, however. We arrived about 15 minutes prior to closing due to faulty information on a website, so this was partly understandable. But one employee was advising that all the tables were taken when this simply wasn't true.  We thus switched to a takeout order and another employee made the most minimal effort to locate us outside when the food was ready. The informality was refreshing, but carried a step too far. Not clear if employees need more training, a pep talk or better salaries, but the experience was rushed, chaotic and not unfriendly --'but not smooth or welcoming, either. Be prepared to be a little pushy.

As soon as I landed in Vancouver I was too eager to check out all the holiday activities. First stop was the Christmas market since it was closest to the hotel. Entry fee is $10/person. Was not worth it. You don't get anything but the opportunity to purchase food, drink, and merchandise at quite a hefty price. One small cup of spiced apple cider was $4. Wasn't even any discount for purchasing more than one. Each food item was about $10-$12. By the end of the night we should've just eaten next door at Cactus Club. There are plenty of other places to see Christmas trees and lights for free... like at Canada Place a block away...if only I had known this earlier.

I'd never heard of this place but im always excited to try a new spot. Upon walking in the place was nicely decorated and the DJ was poppin. However, it fell short in the most important areas (food and service) that I can't think of a reason why I would go back. 

Pros: 
The ambiance is very pleasant. 
Dj was really good and the music wasn't so loud that you couldn't have a conversation, yet loud enough to enjoy 
The biggest pro was the lyrics to You're All I Need on the wall of the ladies room.

Cons:
The bar service was unreasonably slow. The restaurant was only 20% full, but it took 15 minutes for the bartender to actually take our orders and make our drinks because she was busy socializing with the wait staff. The drinks are watered down

The seating isn't the most comfortable. We were sat at a group of wobbly tables with stools that didn't have back rests. The restaurant was pretty dark, we had to use our phone flashlights just to view our menus. (I guess that's the thing though bc I have to do that at other places too)

Our server came to our table and without greeting us or introducing herself, she asked us if we wanted appetizers. We had to probe her to find out what was good on the menu or if they had any specials. For the price of the food and drinks, we expected a higher level of service. She barely came to the table to check on us and the restaurant wasn't busy at all. Our food took almost 40 minutes to come out. I'd be afraid to come to this restaurant when they're actually busy because you may never eat or drink anything. 

It tasted like they put room temp tap water in fancy bottles and that's what was served (no ice or offer for ice)

I ordered chicken and waffles. While it looked good, the menu doesn't say that it's dark meat and the server didn't mention it either so I returned it.  $8 mac n cheese has to be amazing so I tried it, I wasn't impressed. It wasn't bad but it definitely lacked seasoning. To replace the chicken n waffles I got the strip club wings.....they should just call them jerk wings as they were not reminiscent of any strip club wings I've ever had. After not eating all day and having sent one dish back I ate them. They were flavorful though. The theme of the dishes was that they were all bland. The other people in my party ordered the etouffe which needed salt, and the blackened chicken pasta which she was underwhelmed and left most of it. I'm not sure whyyyy they would disrespect the sanctity of a real strip club wing. But they did. Their "strip club wings" are a jerk type of flavor drizzled with a sauce that looks like ranch, but isn't. For $12 you get about 8 drumettes. 

We were a party of 4, and our server added gratuity to our checks. I'm not sure if this is standard practice for all checks, or if they add gratuity for "larger" parties. Again, there were only 4 of us, so we were all surprised by the gratuity already being added to our bill. Our service was so bad, that we wondered if she added it because she knew she sucked and probably wasn't going to get a good tip. Nonetheless, I thought that was odd. We had no issue tipping, but she would've gotten 18% instead of our standard 22% in this type of place but hey, I get it, not everyone tips accordingly. Well, tipping accordingly would've been like 10-15%. Again the place was bare and we barely saw the server.

I give this restaurant 2 stars solely for the ambiance and the DJ. Everything else was a fail. Maybe the brunch is a better experience but I'm skeptical about that unless there's a different staff with a focus on service and timeliness. I don't want to imagine what the food wait is when it's at least 70% full, forget full.

Dr Brooks has no bedside manner.  He is rude, sarcastic, and uncaring.  During a visit, he will not examine you.   You need to speak very slowly in order for him to understand you.  I've used this practice for 10 years and mainly saw an NP who was more knowledgeable than Dr Brooks, or she appeared to be more knowledgeable .  She left the practice so I then saw Dr Brooks and Garcia.  Dr Brooks will only address 1 item during a visit and then you will have to wait another 6 months to see him.  If you need to make an appointment with him in between, forget it.  You will see an NP.    There are current changes in this office and there is a very large turnover.  Dr. Garcia recently joined the practice.  He is young and caring but not knowledgeable.....as he ordered the wrong test for me and if ended in an emergency that wasn't an emergency.  You will not get good care at this practice.  ........CR

It's a Walmart Supercenter. 
This means lower prices (hopefully not at the expense of their employees....)   Walmart hasn't had the most positive publicity over the years and for that reason I'm not a regular; I think employees should be treated fair and paid accordingly. 

Today I went with a friend who needed something specifically from this store so I walked around and purchased more than I intended.  

It's quite big.
Their fresh produce department looks reasonable, not everything is cheap (oranges $7,49?!?? Really?!!!!)  

It's a one-stop shop which makes life so much easier.
And they do carry so much, that's absolutely true. 

It's not a store I'd visit frequently but when I'm in the area I will drop by.

This hotel appears to be undergoing renovations, however its current state is pretty poor. The shower was literally falling apart around me, and the water pressure and temperature depend on who is using the toilet or sinks in other rooms. It jumped from normal to chilly to scalding hot multiple times in one shower.

The safe in the room was broken when we arrived and was never fixed despite notifying the front desk every day, the beds were uncomfortable and hard, and the door would fail to latch unless slammed shut.

Additionally, parking is limited and the theme park shuttle broke down on the highway.

You can do much better for your vacation dollar.

Captain EO....it was our first time on this attraction and I didn't know what to expect.  I remember as a kid hearing about it, but never went because the lines were too long.  Many years later we're at EPCOT and there was nobody in line, so we decided to give it a try.

The kid at the entrance told us that it would be the original Captain EO version...we didn't know what that meant.  When it started, it looked like a combination of Thriller and Fraggle Rock meets the Muppets....yes, I am a child of the 80's.

This attraction is seriously outdated...I'm glad I got to see it because I've always wanted to, but I don't know if I'll do it again.  Also, it seemed like the little kids that were in the attraction weren't impressed by 1980's technology...they probably think it's cheesy in the same way I thought watching the Godzilla movies from the 1960's was hokey.  The theater was only around 30% full...that should tell you something.

This is a one and done for me.

Return Factor - 0%

My wife and I went here for the first time tonight and I have to say we were disappointed. I ordered the beef ravioli with meatballs and meat sauce. The meatballs were very tasteless and luke warm at best. The sauce tasted burnt and the ravioli tasted like store bought frozen. My wife ordered the cannelloni and thought it was better than the ravioli but still nothing special. I am not not certain if we hit at a bad time or what. The place was busy and people seemed to be really enjoying their food. I must say that I will give it another chance in the future and hope to have better results. After reading several good reviews I had high hopes that this would be our go to for Italian food.

Not worth the wait, in my opinion. Our orders took FOREVER! The cashier didn't know which number corresponds to the drink so we had to look it up for her. She looked like she doesn't wanna be there as well, lol. Tried ordering a thai tea, they're out. Then a milk tea, they're out again. Wanted a green tea.. third time's the charm.. NOPE! They're out. Disappointing.

Spare your time and go to Coco's Cafe instead. 

... that rice ball deserved a star, tho.

Soooooo..... 

I hate to do this but I did preface my initial review with I'm picky. Sad to say, I don't think I'll be visiting this Salon again. I had my nails done on the previous Friday and took a color suggestion based on Diane's input. I do my normal gel manicure and deluxe pedi as normal. As they start polishing I ask was this a different color because it looks so light. It's Fall, I don't like pastel polish in the Fall. She says she doing multiple coats so it'll look different. When she finishes I'm not impressed. It looked really "gawdy and I voice my discontent with it. I ask if I can come back on Sunday and have her re-polish because it was 7pm on Friday and I didn't have time and was tired. She said yes. 

Fast forward to Sunday, come in for color correction as agreed. When I'm done she says, I'll check you out. (Scooby-Doo face appears in my head) 

I get up and she says "Sorry, I have to charge you.  it'll be $33.00." In my head, I went the he double hockey sticks  off. Like all the way off. I just paid you 63.00 plus tip on less than 48 hrs prior and you want me to pay you for a correction to your error? Then to add insult to injury, she says "it's rainy and messy outside " while I was eyeballing that receipt. Now it was messy but the mess going on inside this edifice is much more entertaining. "No Bueno, girlfriend" 

Nevertheless,  it's Sunday and for the sake of my religion, I paid the $33.00 (no tips for her trickey) instead of arguing because I wasn't in the best of moods and exited stage left. Hope she took a Polaroid with her eyes cause that is the last she will ever see of me as a patron. 

I will be taking my 10 fingers and 10 toes back to Polished in West Villages and this time I won't stray. 

Hot Mess, Squared... Glam Nails. Smh!

This is my neighborhood target and I find it adequate during the week, but this place is an absolute disaster on the weekend. My family and I were there on a Sunday  at 2 and they only had 3 registers open with lines 8 people deep. I hate self check out bc why should i do a job for free and it wasn't even an option today bc I had to price match a wrongly marked item. We were in line for what seemed like forever and the cashier was super nasty. I could tell Sue thought that she as funny in an "old person who lost their mental filter" way but she was just nasty. When we got to her, we said hello and I said "i need to price match bc the game is $7 cheaper on the target app" she replied "yeah? So?" And I looked at her dumbfounded. She repeated herself and my husband replied "so, we're going to get the cheaper price". She continued with her meanness the entire time. I went to bag something with a bag I already had "don't bag that! I'm going to do better than you anyway" 

I couldn't even come up with a reply, bc what I wanted to say is entirely too nasty. 

I really want to rate this place 1 star but bc it's usually not a sh*tshow during the week, I'll give a bit of mercy.

"Keep Portland Weird," reads the wall across the street from Voodoo Doughnut, the eccentric and beloved doughnut shop in Portland, Oregon. Judging from the dreadlocked ginger, dirty hippie girl with ring worm (seriously), obese monstrosities, various speed geekers, aging hipsters, and other creatures occupying the block-long line to get a doughnut at 3:00 p.m. on a Tuesday afternoon, weird is exactly what they're keeping it.

Among the weird was I. I'll admit it, I waited in the ten-plus minute line to try what authors Chuck Palahniuk and Anthony Bourdain once swooned over. It wasn't my choice to go or wait; nevertheless, I was there and I was intrigued. I'm not a big "sweets guy" (excuse me while I throw up in my mouth for saying that), but I'm all for decadence, and decadence is definitely what the people at Voodoo Doughnut are doing. Along with weird.

I tried four doughnuts: The bacon maple bar (maple frosting and bacon), the dirt doughnut (vanilla frosting and Oreos), the sprinkle doughnut (vanilla frosting and sprinkles), and an Old Dirty Bastard (chocolate frosting, Oreos, and peanut butter), the last two which were vegan. I only took a bite of each, and every one, even the vegans, proved too rich for me. As comedian Robert Kelly would say, "What the fuck does that mean, it's too awesome? You diabetic boring ass face."

I may not be diabetic, but I guess I'm a boring ass face. I just couldn't eat them; they were too rich. I'd rather trek the mile over to BUNK and eat a pork belly cubano with a side of bacon and egg potato salad and a "Mexican" Coke instead. (Like I said, I'm all for decadence, it just depends on what kind.)

Something that pleasantly surprised me was how supple and moist the vegan dough was. I've had vegan doughnuts in the past and they were abominations. Like eating chalk. Why bother? It was nice to see people doing vegan right when there is so much wrong in the world.

Ultimately, Voodoo Doughnuts is not a great place, nor is it a bad place. Simply, it's proof that if you deep fry it and put Oreos, Cap'n Crunch, or actual strips of bacon on it, curious people will come. So will weird people and, evidently, so will I, even though I'd rather be eating my pig with vinegary red peppers on toasted, gluten-full bread, not a maple bar.

I'd been looking forward to trying Zendako for awhile now, however the experience was not the best. I had a wait of 20 minutes to finally get my order, while the 5 people behind me who ordered after I did received their order ahead of me.
When I politely inquired about my order after a couple of people who were behind me had received their orders, the person looked a little startled and said it would be 4 more minutes. I think they gave my initial order away to someone else but offered no admission or apologies for the mistake.
When I did get my order the takoyaki was fine, but admittedly not worth the wait. I have had other takoyaki before, so was perhaps expecting something more based on what I had heard, but the overall experience was a little deflating.
Maybe they had a bad day based on what other reviewers have said but I am just putting my own experience out there.

Very nice atmosphere and decor. 
We liked all of the sandwiches but none of the desserts. 
We were excited that we were able to choose  as many teas to try as we wanted but the waitress never ever came back to our table. No water refilled  or offers to try a different tea.  
Our excitement of trying high tea was snuffed out by the fact that nobody ever came back to our table. Maybe they were understaffed and just didn't have time but the lack of customer service ruined our experience here

I came here for the first time for a game. Nice arena. However, employees are rude. I do not like to give a bad review, but my experience here was not one I care to repeat. The ushers were beyond rude to the paying customers, that is unacceptable in my opinion. I do not buy tickets to in turn get yelled at nor talked down to. I will never return here. I am 56 yrs old and respectful to others, I expect the same treatment in return. Also, concessions are too expensive.

We sat at the bar. I got nachos with chili and she got the chicken fingers and fries. The first few nachos without chili on them were good, but the chili was very watery and tasted funny/old. Halfway through i couldn't eat anymore because it turned into a moist, non-solid mixture due to the watery chili. The chicken fingers were fatty and greasy. We both got pretty sick that night and were sick for the next few days. The service was fine and the food came fast, but the food wasn't good.

Marges is packed with stuff, a lot of it quite expensive.  You can get many of the items online, for less.  Nevertheless, I've shopped here. In my last experience, I had moved, but on a return trip to Florida stopped in at the store and bought several items, and asked they be shipped.  When I received the package, a glass item that was bubble wrapped, and placed INSIDE a larger item that was also bubble-wrapped, was cracked.  Clearly, the glass had been broken before shipping and was packed that way.  When I called, Marges swore that all items had been shipped in good condition and blamed the shipper.  Quite a feat for a literally insulated item to crack during shipment.  The moral: if you're willing to pay their high prices, then be sure to carry your items out the door yourself, since their packing department is not trustworthy.

We're fairly new residents, been here about 5 months now.  The rent is pretty cheap compared to other parts of the Pearl, this is why I rented it without ever seeing it from NYC. 

Points are docked for the following:

- yes the loud mail trucks are annoying as hell all hours of the night but I lived in NY, I can deal but really annoying to be woken up 2-3 times in a night.

- NOT eco-friendly AT ALL.  All of the heating and cooking in the units are done by electricity, not only is this probably one of the least energy efficient way to heat your home or cook, it will add an additional $200 of utilities to your cost of living.

- blasé would be the best way for me to explain how they responded to by bicycle theft - it was stolen from its INSIDE courtyard which for some reason is open to the public during the business day (when I'm at work) without any other security present. They simply said this is why we ask you to have renters insurance, oh and report it to the police so that they will patrol here more often. Kind of gobsmacked.  

- really sour old maintenance lady who is constantly scowling and hates her job. Don't tell me to take the elevator down from the 6th floor because "I'm still young" - I have my coffee and heels on and just trying to get to work!

Points gained for the following:

- all my packages do get delivered and don't leave with UPS/USPS/Fedex and do that whole dance of re-delivery

- if I report a maintenance issue, they are prompt and the guys are awesome.  

We are planning on moving out of here as soon as the lease is up even though we have a couple of lovely neighbors. Well, the pearl just doesn't have much personality at all really.

I've been here twice - the people that work here have personalities of dead moths.  In the morning the last thing you want to do is be served by a person that cannot smile, can hardly even say "good morning," and acts like you are bothering them.  The selection at this "bakery" is awful - cookies and muffins is pretty much all you get.  If you want a real bakery experience, go to Upper Crust Bakery off of Burnet - so worth the drive.

Only getting 2 stars for the fact that NO ONE was there and they were able to get my dog in and checked. Came in the door was unlocked and the first thing the girl up front says to me is "those doors are supposed to be locked" with a big sigh of annoyance. My dog had eaten something and was throwing up a lot throughout the night and shivering. The actual vet doctor came in and seemed annoyed that my dog was scared and barking at him. Eye rolls, big sighs, comments about her behavior made me feel that I was more of a nuisance than anything to them. He made an effort to constantly drop the cost of the procedure as if I wouldn't be able to afford it or that it would change my mind about keeping her there. Please, if you're going to be a 24 hour emergency animal hospital, don't work there if it's going to be burden on you.

Glad to see another Italian ristorante hit the burbs as there is a dearth of them OTP.

We arrived on time and our party was promptly seated in one of the banquets, however the  padding was slighlty firm and there was not padding on the painted wooden backs.

Our waiter asked for drink orders but we had brought our own wine.  So he brought out some nice stemware, an areator and decanter.  

Yeah we had the cut your own pizza which in my opinion is at best the 4th best pizza in the ATL.  (Fortunato's, Antica & Varasano's) 

We also had four other unmemorable entrees.  

Can say much more......cavaet emptor.

It's a nice trendy atmosphere with nice designs. However, this is about the end of the good.

One thing you should know is that if you plan on reserving a table for a group, you can only stay for two hours. It does matter if you are still eating, ordering more, or having a good time...they will make you leave. This makes no sense to me and I have never heard of a restaurant turning down money. I would never again go here to have a event because of what happened. Management was unaccomdating and rude when tried to get another table because our "time limit" was up. TERRIBLE.

Guess these reviews were on the mark! Set up an appointment for 9 am to get a check on why my fan blower isn't working. Told that the "master mechanic" won't be in until 10am. Why allow appointments for something that only one person can do and you KNOW he isn't in til 10 am. 10 rolls around and my car is still sitting there and no mention of the mechanic will get to it. After sitting around for 35 minutes, I approached the guys at the counter and was told "he's working on it" but guess what, he wasn't! My car was still sitting in the same spot untouched but my keys and folder were moved to "complete". After another 10 minutes my car was finally moved into the garage area and checked. The service person about an hr later came out and told me it was an electrical problem. When I asked if he could order the part for repair, he gives me an attitude saying he would have to price it out and that I should just go to the dealership instead. So lets get the facts here, I WANTED to give them more work and my money and was still turned away!? After all said is done, he didn't even write down on my paperwork what was done or the diagnosis so 
 I can take it to the dealership and say "this is the problem can you change it out". Instead just charged me 50 bucks and pretty much said good luck and rushed off to the next customer who will probably be just as frustrated and thought of as a hassle than a real customer. 

NEVER coming going to this pep boys again and NEVER recommending anyone go within 10 miles of this place. I will probably not get a resolution just a canned message saying email us here for them to give me another canned message saying nothing but they are sorry but not really sorry.

UPDATE:Went to a REAL mechanic and guess what. Pepboys did NOTHING. Literally was just an unplugged wire and they charged me 50 bucks to park my car in a garage and then shoo me away. So please tell me how hard is it to replug a wire or is that a 100 dollar surcharge? This place is such a scam and terrible with customer service.

I have only eaten here once and typically wouldn't review a restaurant on that basis, but my friends and I were disappointed to the point that we would never go back, so I thought someone else out there may think it's worth knowing.  We went to this place because our usual spots were closed due to being on vacation in Thailand, we all wish we had just waited a week or so.

Specifically; our food was overly salty and for the price our portions were very small. Maybe not even for the price, in general - our portions were very small.

end.

I went with 2 stars instead of 1 because it is McDonald's. you don't go there for quality food or service; you go for fast food cheap. Unfortunately they  miss the mark almost every time on the fast scale. Last night I waited for 30 mins after I had paid for my food for me to receive it. After I had paid for my food I was stuck at the first window due to cars in front of me so I talked to the girl in the cash window. I was rather impressed by the dedication when she told me "I don't know why everyone has to complain when they wait; there are 2 other fast food restaurants in town and I am sure they don't have lines". That was impressive. I waited 30 mins for my food and when I got to the window they started to give me the wrong food for one of the many cars that pulled out of line due to the wait. I corrected it and they got me my food and it was correct. 
  I have tried to let the owner know what is happening by filing a complaint at corporate and asking for a call but I have never received a call back from anyone. I figure that the owner not caring about this location is the reason that it is the pit that it has become. It will continue to survive in Johnstown due to the fact that there is really nothing else here but if you are in the area and want fast food, just go across the street to Wendy's and you will save yourself about 30 mins of your life.

Poor flushing toilet. Low pressure in shower heads. In the sink, the water doesn't come out fast or far enough to even get your toothpaste spit down the drain. The front desk employees; left little to be desired. The first night, Knowledge acted as if we were ruining his day. The second day; our keys to our room didn't work. My fiance'; who's name was on the room as well, wasn't allowed to get replacement keys, because according to the plump deskman, 'he's not on the account'. I went back down; to get the replacement keys (told sometimes the system kicks folk out their rooms; and their keys stop working); and was told, "your fiance is on the room account, 'sometimes our systems just don't show us everything'. Had to wait over 20 minutes to get replacement keys; and that's with just one couple ahead of us, who the plump dude was skinning and grinning with. So, this 'brother' was nicer to an Asian couple just checking in, way nicer than he was to us, who were scheduled to be there for like 5 days. The only good service was the bellhop; and the valets. The servers in the bar; acted as if they hated their jobs too. Spent the evening talking to each other; rather than waiting on us and taking drink orders; so the six of us left; and believe me; we spent a lot of money that night. Took us over 10 minutes to get two drinks; and when they came; with no smile, no thanks yous, we were out. So, it seems to me as if from the top down at this location; there is an attitude of apathy; or people are annoyed with customers; or simply don't like their jobs. I worked at Hilton Portland Executive Tower; and that type of attitude; mistakes; and poor service are not of the HILTON culture. Do better!

I typically do not shop at Market Basket for a number of reasons. Today, i went in to get a fresh turkey that was advertised in the 2 week sale ad. And there were none to be had. I asked a person behind the meat counter. They go to where they should be to look (hello, I've already done that). Went into the back, we are getting a truck today, maybe there be some later. The staff tend to be less friendly than other stores, including other Market Baskets. When one of my items wouldn't ring up, the cashier just made up a random amount - which I believe was an overcharge. i just asked if she could void it. She seemed bothered by that request. I know remember why I only shop here once or twice a year. Shaw's has better customer service and overall appearance of the store.

With 260+ reviews and an average rating of 4 stars, this review is certainly in the minority and I'm sure it will be dismissed by many. I know if I saw lots of great reviews and came across at bad one, I'd negate it too. Still, here goes...

My daughter and I were seated at one of only two tables in the entire restaurant without any lighting. Also, our table was in a little alcove, and with my back to the rest of the restaurant, I could only see my daughter and a wall. I felt very disconnected. As for the food and service? A big fat MEH!

Here's a list of all the hiccups:

1. They did not have lemonade. 
2. The bread wasn't great. It was some garlic hybrid.
3. Grilled octopus was very tough and had a bitter tangy sauce that overwhelmed it.
4. The waitress brought us more bread and it was nearly burnt. Super crispy and dry.
5. We waited way too long for the main course.
6. Waitress never asked if we wanted another drink.
7. Waitress wasn't very attentive. Not rude and didn't go MIA, but I expected more.
8. Main course was pasta and lobster in a bowl of butter (yuck, too much butter).
9. Lobster was chewy.
10. My daughter's salmon was undercooked.
11. Her dish was supposed to come with risotto, but it was just cubed potatoes.

Positives:

1. Pecan tart was delicious.
2. The pasta was cooked to perfection. Probably the best I've ever had.
3. Father/daughter bonding time (that's why I never complained to the waitress...I didn't want to spoil the mood).

Considering the way this place presents itself as high end dining, I was not at all impressed. I'll take The Capital Grille any day. There I feel special, hence making the expense worth it.

This is a consistent experience. Not a one off situation. Every business has a rough day. But this is always the experience Regarding online orders for pick up. We've been at this now long enough to figure it out by now. 

The pick up time has never been achieved in my 5-7 experiences. Today it was 20 minutes after the selected pick up time that I received my two salads and a bag of chips. 

Either adjust the algorithm or staff appropriately. I will always be fine if you tell me I have to wait longer at home or running errands but standing in your seating area for 20 minutes is unacceptable. You get one more chance from me.

I have eaten at Taverna 3 times now.  The first two visits were very good.  The third was miserable.  The highlight of my visit was going to be the chef's focaccia.  Not so.  It was late in coming and was obviously raw when it arrived.  I ate 2 slices and asked the server to ask the chef to cook it some more.  They cooked it.  When it returned the bottom was crisp and the top was still raw.  I also order lasagna.  That was a bowl of thick, tasteless cheese soup with a curious little glob of what was apparently overcooked pasta in it.  Oh, and there was a streak of brown stuff across the cheese soup.  I told myself that it was meat sauce.  I also told myself that I will never return.

My boyfriend and I decided to try out Kimura after reading so many good reviews about their omakase.
We made reservations and the place was pretty packed when we got there. Service was extremely slow, but we let that slide because it seemed like every table in the restaurant had omakase. My boyfriend had the $50 omakase, while I had the $40. 

In the middle of our meal, there was a long 30 minute wait. The table next to us who arrived over an hour after us, had already received their entrees while we had not. It turned out they had made a mistake and delivered our entrees to them. We had to wait another 10 minutes for our entrees. 
But my entree never came. They didn't even realize they had missed my entree until I asked about it. The waitress almost didn't believe me, she had me name every dish I had thus far. She then came up 5 minutes after I had told her about the missed entree, telling me it was last call, and I needed to place my last orders in if I wanted any. I reminded her about my entree, and she almost looked shocked, like "Is this girl gonna let the missed entree go?" After speaking to the other waitresses, and the chef, she tells me my entree will be coming in the next 10 minutes. My boyfriend finished his meal, while I waited for my entree. 
By the time we finished our meal, we had been in the restaurant for 3.5 hours. We were the second last table to leave, and the last table left came in half an hour before closing. Eight tables had come and gone during meal - three of which had omakase. Ridiculous. When our bill came, I asked if we could be given a discount for the inconvenience they caused with the mix-up. No can do, said the  waitress. 

Brief overview about the food, as I basically rated this restaurant on its service. First up was the baby spinach salad, which was extremely salty. Next was the raw oyster and oyster shooter with the monkfish, which was alright - your typical oyster shooter dish. I also had had the quail and salmon - salmon was tasty, but the quail was very, very bland. The soup, which I believe was squash, was good. My entree, the lobster and cod, was good - but certainly not worth the wait. The tempura was not so good, and the sashimi was pretty fresh. Nothing special.  

Needless to say, I will not be back. The food was mediocre, but it is not good enough to bring me back. I've had much better food and much better service elsewhere.

I wanted to like him- I really did. But the whole experience was so unprofessional and pushy. 

Firstly, I left work early to get there, and was made to wait 30 minutes past my appointment time to see him. Secondly, they wasted my time asking me verbally to fill out a form that I had already taken the time to fill out and scan in during my lunchbreak. Then, I saw him for about 20 seconds, we took an xray and was asked if I could come to a group educational xray session (I mean really? I am paying money for your PERSONAL attention). I was not educated on the fact that my spine health would be a group exercise until after the xrays were taken. I also witnessed him yell at his cheerful front desk receptionist and it left a bad feeling in me.

His confidence and demeanor was cutthroat and quick. They used a bunch of fear tactics in the their marketing and images around the office. However, at the very least, he seemed competent. I was scared to see a chiropractor though, and his demeanor did not put me at ease.

I left feeling really flustered, and emailed immediately saying I wouldn't be coming back for a group appointment. I was then greeted with a barage of emails in judgmental tones saying that they never would have taken the xrays if they had known I wouldn't go to group therapy. These words didn't even match the font used for my name or Joel's sign off (i.e. they copy and paste).

Not a great experience. I wouldn't recommend.

=== 1. VERDICT/VALUE
Wide range of Chinese food available 24 hours - great!  But high prices, takeout only, slower service, and a payment requirement for only cash have taken the lustre off the golden child that the No. 9 Restaurant was in the past, especially with so much competition nearby.

=== 2. FOOD
On this day, we enjoyed:
 
- BBQ Pork on Rice ($12.63): it was alright - asked for 50% fat and lean, but it was more like 30% fat and lean :S

 - Prawns with Mixed Vegetables ($19.31): costs a pretty penny but they did not scrimp on the shrimp or sauce!

=== 3. SERVICE
It's short/curt and OK for Chinese food takeout, working in English, Cantonese, and Mandarin.  Food prep seems to be slower than before, considering the level of busy-ness and lack of dine-in patrons.  Be sure to bring cash!

=== 4. ENVIRONMENT
Operations have changed from dine-in to solely takeout at the door facing the parking lot, where one no longer goes inside any longer for the most part.  Speaking of the parking lot, there's typically plenty of this available these days in the time of COVID.

I've gotten into the habit of bringing my own mugs & take out containers with me since I've moved here as sustainability & the environment don't appear to be a concern in Boston. I brought my own coffee mug here & they charged me for a large coffee even though my mug is a bit smaller than their large coffee. Way to be greedy & discourage efforts at lowering your global footprint. No other coffee shop I've been to so far has done this except here. Not to mention I'm saving them money on take out cups. I'll stick to Haley House. The atmosphere at Haley is much better as well.

We waited at the bar for half an hour for drinks. I don't mean in line, I mean AT the bar, pushed up against it by the other people, and everyone around us getting served. Only so long you can stare at a bartender who isn't looking at you until you're discouraged. We even split up and my friend who left our initial spot was served first! She mentioned it and the bartender said she was just going in order. WHAT ORDER?

Anyway, getting in was fine. Yes, there was a line, but it moved fast enough and when our friend wasn't back with the cash yet they didn't care that we just stood there waiting. Coat check ran out of room so we were told we could leave them on top of the beer boxes and she wouldn't charge us. Gee thanks.

Music was okay, I remember thinking it was a bit too much of a certain person, but can't recall who.

Great atmosphere and menu. BUT do not order anything with the risotto... Hard, chewy, literally got stuck in my teeth like glue. Very hard to get out of my teeth. Not edible. They did make good with a fantastic lobster fettuccine. Excellent cannelloni for my friend. When the Chef came by to check on dinner, I mentioned all of this (good and bad) and he immediately became extremely defensive and yelled at me (literally yelled) saying I had no idea what I was talking about, he was a chef and knew how to cook then stormed off in a fit (without filling our empty wine glasses next to our highly priced bottle of wine) I couldn't believe it! So extremely rude. It will be hard for me to go back.

The chefs are nice and funny but this is by the far worst Japanese steakhouse I've been to. The presentation of the plate as the chef served us our food can be compared to a dog. Just dump into our plates with rice falling to the table. There is just no appeal whatsoever. Vegetables are soggy and beef is over cooked. The review here about the miso soup being salty and salad dressing too oniony is sooo TRUE. For the price you pay you should expect variety. But this is what you get: two rubbery shrimps, overcharge fried rice, so so flavored chicken, rubber feel like beef, soggy vegetables and a sad ambience.

So first I probably need to say I'm a bit biased towards this movie theater. I've been watching movies here since 1989 and it's been 10 mins from my home most of my life.  

So when they first opened the food side I was the first to try. I loved that I could reserve good seats in advance.  The food wasn't bad, not healthy, but better than popcorn. 

A few years later I've probably been over 100 times and I can say my biggest issue is the service.  The staff is not diligent on contacting you when you press the button. I'll say 50 percent of the time the order you give is not what you get. Now I'm a vegetarian so allot of times I require them to leave things out of my meal.  I went last night and sure enough same issue. 

I'm not sure how crazy I am about the new parking garage. I'm so used to parking next to it and walking in.  Tip, to enter the movie theater area you have to goto the second floor so try park there. I parked on the first floor, had to go up to the second just to come back down to the first.  Pain in the you know what. 

This has Soooo much potential. Either way it's still the best place if you want to reserve seats, just prepare for bad service.

This 99 is OK I guess, never had any real problems with it . Service can be really slow at times. I kinda wish that they would automatically bring you popcorn instead of having to be ask for it but not a big deal. (My memory goes back to when the 99 at the Liberty Tree Mall used to be a Ground Round with all you could eat free popcorn and peanuts :)

My problems are twofold. Firstly, I find precious little on their menu that interests me. The menu is boring !!! Potato skins are obviously frozen that they deep fry and they are usually mealy sometimes they seem like they're left over and heated in the oven. Food is average for a chain.

My second problem concerns the 99 in Seabrook, NH. My mother and I used to stop there when we would go to Cow Hampshire for the day.
The first time I got the New England Roast Turkey there ....IT .....WAS......AWESOME!!!!!!!!!!!   So much turkey, I don't even care if it was "Tour-kee Brand Turkey flavored Turkey substitute" , it looked, smelled and tasted fantastic ! It was moist even without gravy. The portion size was huge, kind of like you would get at home on Thanksgiving. A BIG mound of corn bread stuffing, very tasty. Nice gravy. Sweet honey\buttermilk biscuit. Tasty squash and cranberry sauce. YUMM.....next time we went..still good food, but smaller. next visit good but smaller....next time....smaller. In a nutshell, each time I went it got smaller and smaller !! The taste of the food remained good but it was the case of the mysterious shrinking portion !  At 10.99, I think there should be a platefull. In fact, the first time I got it, there was so much food that they had to bring the sides on the side. They side plates would not fit on the dinner plate !. Now they bring everything on one plate and there is still room. The side bowl that held my squash is now a tiny ramekin that sits on the plate glued in place by a buttload of gravy. 

So, the 99 gets a big ....ehhhh from me

Patronized this establishment last week with my family.  Really warm, cute and quaint environment.  My fiance worded shrimp and grits that were like soup.  Asked one of the employees if the grits typically come like this, he replied "yes" because other patrons have complained of them being too thick.  Our waitress came to the table and my fiance asked her the exact same question and she replied,  "no"  Okay so someone isn't being honest.  Cool!  

So we went back today because we truly wanted to give them another try and unfortunately, it was an epic fail.  Our daughter ordered chicken & waffles and sadly the chicken breast wasn't cooked all the way through.  My fiance and I ordered baked wings that were not fully cooked so we had to send those back to cook more.  When they brought the chicken back out, it still wasn't cooked thoroughly so we boxed them up to take home and doctor ourselves.  The sauteed spinach and broccoli was good but all and all, they certainly need to tighten up on some things.  I had coffee and just like my first visit, the coffee was scorched and you could tell it had been sitting all day.  Gave both servers nice tips because they were good, the food just wasn't.  And the bottled oregano that they sprinkle on each and every plate as a garnish is over kill and completely takes away from the flavor of the dish.  Try FRESH parsley, basil or rosemary.  


We may try again in the near future but after failing a second time, not so sure about it!

I got an $80 haircut at the spa salon and was really disappointed. Nothing about the service was "spa like". The hairdresser was really opinionated and negative and talked too much. The haircut itself was too fast, with no attention to detail or high end products used. At that price point I'm expecting a little scalp massage or something extra. The room you get your hair cut in feels like a closet that was turned into a "salon". There are only two chairs in the tiny room with no natural light.

Afterwards I had lunch. A very dry turkey club sandwich with no condiments or seasoning.

Overall: mediocre to poor and way overpriced.

Two stars (versus one) *only* because the staff is excellent.  Honestly, every single employee I interacted with was courteous and seemed genuinely happy to help.

But, oh, goodness the rest.

I only stayed here once, for a conference, and while I generally enjoy travel for work, one of the perks is usually staying at a fancy hotel!  Not a hotel that just charges a lot but fails to deliver.

So, my issues:

The rooms are dark.  Even with all the lamps on, it just felt dim.

The rooms smell weird.  You know when you walk into a room, and you know it's non-smoking, but it still kind of smells like smoke?  And it's just kind of the scent of the weird industrial soap they use?  It smells like that.

They! Have! Bugs!  Okay, just crickets, but honest-to-gosh there is a sign by the front desk that just basically says, "Austin gets swarmed by crickets this time of year.  There's nothing we can really do about it, and they won't hurt you."  I could hear crickets chirping the entire time I was there.

The walls are paper-thin.  Tissue-paper thin.  I heard someone sneeze, I heard my neighbor hanging things up in the closet, I heard a cell phone alarm at 6:30 am.  

There was a special event with a band that was directly below my room, so after work I got to listen to country music for four hours.  After the first two, I called and they said it should end at 10 pm.  At 10:30 I called, and they said it should end at 11.  Really, they have 463 rooms.  They just shouldn't rent out the ones directly above that ballroom if they're having an event there, because it wasn't just the dull thumping base of loud music.  I could hear the drums, bass, lead guitar, and singer clearly and distinctly.  Or they could just rent those rooms to the people organizing the event.

I'm not sure where other reviewers stayed but I was not in a room with two flat screen tvs, I was in one with one small, old television.

The mattress was too firm.  It wasn't comfortable for me.

The room didn't have a refrigerator or microwave.

I hate how mid-range hotels offer free wifi but the pricier hotels charge for it.  This one charges $13 a day.

The water pressure was not great, and the light in the bathroom buzzed.

The chicken pot pie was just not very delicious.  It was much more vegetable than chicken, and the vegetables were strangely (disturbingly?) hard and crunchy.  Also, my entree was ~15-20 minutes later than everyone else's.  The waitress was nice enough to offer me a free beer, but making the entree free would have been more appropriate, I think.

This brings me to the positives... the beers are generally $5.50, and there's a very cool selection of them.  The pitchers ($15) come in fun glass cylinders, and are a pretty good value - especially considering the quality of beer they serve.

Nevertheless, the beer selection isn't remotely near that of Cambridge Common's.  Actually, I think Cambridge Common wins on basically every front except location, which is Tory Row's obvious benefit.  It's right in the middle of Harvard Square near the T stop.

***If you have a timid dog, this may not be the park for you.*** Our Mastiff is the most gentle animal (still only a 8 month old puppy) and is NOT a fighter. A few dogs caught on to this and basically attacked him while their owners just stood by and watched. I had to pick up my son and go in to get my poor dog that was laying down, terrified. The other day my husband literally had to grab a pit bull by his collar, that was attacking him, as his owner casually jogged over. The dog was still trying to get ahold of him as he held his collar. Also, a lot of small dog owners use the large dog section making for a lot of small dogs yapping at big dogs. So in conclusion, my rating is based on OWNERS and not on the park itself. The park is lovely. If owners paid attention to their dogs this would not be an issue. We won't be going back anymore because of this.

The food was fantastic, my low rating is not due to that. I was with two friends, both ordered different specialty pancakes and I ordered eggs, toast and bacon. All three enjoyed what we ordered. I would love to eat it again. However, the waitress we had was incredibly rude. She barely gave us the time of day even after everyone cleared out. She at one point scolded me for drinking my soda out of the bottle and not in the glass. She proceeded to take the bottle from me and ask in an aggressively condescending way, "why don't you do it the right way? It's called a raspberry lime Ricky because of the lime" and poured my drink in the glass that contained ice and a lime. I'm a 23 year old woman who was in the area presenting research at a national conference. I don't need you to tell me how to drink something. 
Also, when we came in the door was propped open and we didn't see the small piece of paper taped to the window that states it's cash only. However, when we saw the ATM and the amount of people using it, I asked one of the waitresses if the place was in fact cash only. She said no and that they took cards. When our bill came and 2 of us put cards down our waitress told us the cash only rule and my response while standing up to go use the ATM was, "oh we're sorry, I asked and one of the girls said it wasn't". She immediately snapped back with a terrible arrogant tone, "absolutely not, there is no way anyone in here told you it wasn't cash only". We were all caught off guard so my friend described the girl. It turns out it was that girls first day. It was a simple mistake, we weren't mad that we had to take cash out, we weren't trying to get the girl in any trouble but the way our waitress spoke to us over a misunderstanding was really out of line. She did not even apologize after she realized she was wrong. We are disappointed that she spoiled our first experience. Maybe I will try to go back next time I'm in Boston. The food might be worth another shot.

Great atmosphere, but pretty disappointing. Now because I'm a waitress, I give more slack than most, knowing how difficult this business is. Seated infront of a window which was nice, immediately brought garlic bread and had our waters filled. We order drinks and shrimp cocktail, which was just whatever, tasted like it had been sitting out and it wasn't chilled at all... Then we ordered a lemon drop martini... It came with a salt rim on it? Very unpleasant surprise. It took about 10 minutes for me to grab a different server to ask for another drink made properly. Then we get our entrees, boyfriend gets a huge baked stuffed lobster which he enjoyed. I get the seafood linguine... No flavor. Just a bunch of pasta in a broth with unseasoned seafood. The calamari was overlooked and chewy. Scallops were bland. Nobody came back to check on how our food was and all I wanted was some parmesan cheese or something to add for flavor. Overall unimpressed.

Got a weird vibe with this place.

Tried to schedule my appointment online with ZocDoc, but was unable to do so, so I had to call and make the appointment over the phone. No big deal, but why have a ZocDoc link on your website, if it doesn't work?

Upon arrival the medical assistant who took me back seemed to have the wrong patient's medical history. She kept referencing family histories of conditions I had not indicated on my medical history form and asked for additional information which I had been sure to include on the form.

The actual appointment took all of 3 minutes. I was seen by the Physician Assistant, not Dr. Bhatt, and she seemed extremely rushed. I scheduled my appointment to discuss my adult onset acne. The PA looked at my face for about 5 seconds and proceed to prescribe 4 different medications. She didn't ask about what products I had tried using, what worked, what didn't work, my lifestyle, or anything. She suggested that I start all of them at the same time... how then, would I be able to tell which ones were working or not working? Or am I just supposed to take all four of them for the rest of my life?

The prescriptions she picked for me had to be ordered through 'special' online and over the phone pharmacies... she wouldn't give me the script to bring to my own pharmacy/pharmacist but insisted that the required pharmacies were "cheaper." Sounds like inducement to me.

After the PA took her leave, the medical assistant returned to the room with samples of only two of the four items I was supposed to purchase... apparently I was just supposed to take their word for it that I wouldn't be allergic or have an adverse reaction.

The Medial Assistant then proceded to contradict the instructions given to me by the PA, saying that "she usually tells her patients to do things differently than the PA because she thinks they work better that way." Very professional.

All in all - just a weird vibe. Didn't feel like I was receiving great care and felt super shady having to call all these 'special' pharmacies to fill prescriptions that I couldn't try out. I will probably utilize a different practice from here on out.

Years ago we had dined in at Shogun and I remember it being really good! However,  ordered take out last night and was pretty disappointed. 
Ordered, their spiciest sushi, which was deep fried, had jalapeno, cream cheese and spicy tuna, forget the name but it was pretty good. Got the tuna vs salmon sushi, it looked fresh and my son said he enjoyed it. Got another spicy tuna roll which I didn't realize was fried too, wanted something raw and fresh, this roll sucked! The spicy tuna in the fried rolls resembled cat food..... I never remember this from other sushi places, not sure but it's not the most appealing. 
My daughter got the shoyu ramen, it was mediocre at best and was missing a few ingredients she was looking forward to (the egg and fishcake.)
We also shared the teriyaki chicken entree, the salad it was served with was watery and lacking flavor, miso soup was the best part, but kind of watered down, and the chicken was chewy and overcooked. The sauce was terribly lackluster,  I had to doctor it up bigtime.
I won't take another chance on this place. I had high hope from the pictures on Yelp. Unfortunately my fav sushi place was closed so I ordered here. I'm bummed, I'd recommend taking your chances at another sushi place.

I returned to this restaurant in years . 
The service here leaves a lot to be desired . I stood at the entrance for a while and there were two women at the register helping  a customer but neither one of them greeted me  or even looked up to acknowledge my presence . Later ,the hostess came after about 5 minutes at the entrance and she took my family to the table .
We sat doe another 10 minutes before our waitress came to our table . The waitress did not introduce herself. We ordered our food and when she brought us the appetizer the 3 of us had to eat from the appetizer plate because she did not bring us plates . We had to ask someone who was cleaning the table next to us for to go plates and the check because our waitress was no where to be found . They did not give us a bag for our containers .  Over all the food was good but the service was poor .

Normally I'm not much for reviewing, but I was having lunch with a friend this weekend and she had the same exact comments I did. 

This place has the potential to be excellent, but it seriously needs to work on its customer service. We went on a Friday night around 7. It wasn't busy so we assumed the crowd came in later. It took us 2 hours for a meal for 2 people!! I wouldn't have minded the time if the service was quicker and we stayed to drink, but the majority of the time we waited for drinks, water, or to spot the server in general.

There was one bartender making all the drinks. It took about 15 minutes for us to get our drinks. We ordered 2 rounds and stopped after we realized it wouldnt be worth the wait time. The waiter looked unusually perplexed, as if he was in a completely different time zone than us. He would always have a pitcher of water with him, but never refilled our glasses unless we specifically asked him. Also, no one ever cleared our dirty plates. We would even slide it to the end of the table as a huge hint. Nope. Nada. I would be more understanding if it were busier, but being as slow as it was I couldn't excuse it. We also noticed that the staff kept running across the street to black olive. I can only conclude that the staff was running 2 restaurants at once. Lol. Maybe that's why the waiter was confused, he didn't know which place he was at. 

As for the food, it was really good. The only saving grace for this place. The dishes were exotic and different. We order a few sushi rolls, appetizers, and I believe 2 entrees. Each was delicious and presented well. I would come back to this place if it had better service. Hearing that my friend had the same experience, I think I'll pass.

I love the vibe of hula hut, I love the boozy drinks. The food is just okay. What brings it down to 2 stars is the filthy restaurant and lack of enthusiasm from the staff. We sat here today at the out side bar that's farthest out. We were here for about an hour or so. There were more dirty tables than clean. Not a single person stopped to bus them...except the customer who bussed her table so she could sit. No less than 5 employees walked passed her without offering to help. We saw tables piling their dirties onto other dirty tables because they couldn't get bussed. The place was not busy. Steady, but not busy. Nobody seemed to care or notice. Its as if they didn't realize that the more people you wait on, the more money you make. Maybe it was about to be a shift change and the morning people didn't want more tables? I don't know. It was just filthy. As we were walking out to our car, we noticed one out of ten tables were clean. The rest had stuff all over them. The braless waitress eating and sucking sour cream off her fingers before touching straws and serving people was pretty disgusting too. But I'm certain that a manager that allows this will not care enough to even read this.

Our server Justin was fantastic! He was very patient, and answered all of our questions, from the wine menu to the entrees. He took time for conversation with us as well.

The food was okay, but not remarkable, certainly not for the price. There was no wow factor that would make us want to return. There are many other restaurants in the vicinity that serve better food for a better price. 

Our credit card was charged 20% more than the total bill even though we had written the tip amount and total amount on the slip. A message was left with management, but the call was never returned, so we had to call again. The manager was not polite and acted annoyed by our concern. His reason was they add 20% as a security measure in case the charge is not approved. This is odd considering a credit card was used, and immediately charged to our account. There is no mention of this additional charge on the menu, nor were we notified of this at any time. We did get the 20% back a few days later.
