He did not apologize nor act like he cared about our concern. He hung up on me without saying a word in the middle of when I was talking as well. Very disappointed and we will not return.

The quick review: Atmosphere and service much better than the food, which doesn't come close to the best barbecue in the region.

Atmosphere: Wide open, lively decor, tables spaced out so you're not on top of each other like in too many places.

Service: Super friendly and accommodating on two visits. A real plus.

Pulled Pork: A huge pile, but almost entirely gray meat under the sauce with very little smoke. More of a crock pot feel, and very mushy. If volume were the only consideration, 5 stars. Taste and texture matter, so it's closer to 2.

Ribs: Tried twice. Mushy the first time. Mushy, grossly fatty (unrendered), and an obvious reheat the second time. To add insult to injury, they had little signs on the table promoting a ribs deal with an appealing photo of ribs cooked perfectly with nothing but dry rub. What showed up: an oversauced, undersmoked mess (see photo).

Wings: Tried twice. Both times, the wings were very large and the smoke came through. Not much flavor otherwise, and not tender, but not a problem. Crisp enough, and six sauces on the table perked them up.

Cornbread: Decent one time, very dry another.

My sister and I both got the lavish pedicures and the gel manicures. My sister's pedicure and service started about 20 minutes before mine yet somehow I was done with my service only 8 minutes after her. 

I wish I asked who did my nails because she was very rough in the way she handled me and was trying to speed through the process as if her life depended on it. A pedicure is supposed to be relaxing but all the steps she did were just apply and then immediately removing the scrub or what have you. There was no massage like my sister had. She simply applied the scrub and then removed it. Applied the mask then removed etc. There is still obvious dead skin on the bottom of my foot and toes that any good pedicure would have removed.

When she was cutting and shaping my finger nails she kept doing the almond shape although I asked for round and now they are a mix of both round and almond but in varying lengths and shapes. None of the tips are actually centered to my nail. When cutting the nails she was trying to go so fast that she at first pinched my skin and nails in between the clippers a few times almost cutting me several times. Once gel was applied she didn't want to wait until the 30 second timer on the lamp went off either. Even just the way she would grab my hands was so rough. 

It's a shame because the salon has a wonderful selection of colors and seems to have a nice owner and atmosphere.

The crowd here is awful.  Everyone looks like they just rolled out of bed, including the staff.  Service is slow, music is so loud that the bartender couldn't even here my order. Parking was also a nightmare.   I went here as part of a bachelorette party and we ended up leaving after one drink.  If you want to be "seen" in Columbus, this wouldn't be the place to go.  Since we were in the Short North, we ended up going to Eleven which was awesome and then to Sushi Rock which was even better!!! I won't be going back to 23 any time soon.  And to the staff: comb your hair and iron your shirts.  Thanks.

I've came to this dairy queen before and it was decent, but today I came with my girlfriend and when we walked in we found the manager yelling at an employee in the front of the store. She continued to do this while we were ordering which was very distracting. Me, working in fast food myself, know that if there's a problem you have to handle, do it in the back. NOT in front of your customers. The ice cream was decent though.

I would have given five stars, however I had an unfortunate experience with the billing dept., not over billing or anything like that. I called to let them know that I was there, in the parking lot, ready for my appt. as I was instructed in a text message.

When I called the number, I ended up in the billing dept. and a lady answered. I told here I was the for my appt. She let me know that I was calling the billing dept. I let her know that the phone message was confusing and said maybe they should change it (so people don't end up calling the billing dept).

The lady yelled at me like a drill instructor. I thought patients were to be treated cordially. Not with the Billing Department. I'm sure that they are familiar with is this lady and know who she is.

Second time here and I'd say the food is good, but overpriced.  Loud music, almost like we were at a night club vs a restaurant which made it hard to talk.  I had to ask for wasabi multiple times when usually that's standard at every other sushi place I've been.  Not a bad experience but for the price and mediocre atmosphere I feel fortunate to be in portland where we have many other options for good sushi - won't be coming back.

My first year lease is coming to an end. Here are my experiences at Halsted(previously Avalon) Danvers Apartments:
The good: The property is beautiful. I mean, beautiful. It's safe. It's quiet at night. I've never had an issue with parking and it's free. The concierge is AWESOME. They are so nice and helpful, I can't even tell you. The new fitness center is really nice if you're into that kind of thing. Halsted buying the property was a major improvement. 
They did a great job with snow removal all winter. Maintenance shows up relatively quickly during business hours and they are polite. They'll even take off their shoes if you ask. 

The bad: Everyone uses every inch of grass for a dog toilet so my child can never run on the grass and must be confined to the play area. Shouldn't that be the other way around? My car was accidentally left unlocked and someone rummaged through it and left the door open. The walls are very thin and you hear everyone in the hall, upstairs, and out side. (I have very loud and rude downstairs neighbors that argue outside) The paint is CHEAP. Fixtures are CHEAP. Windows leak. Construction is CHEAP. Utility bills are high, due to leaky windows and bad insulation. Maintenance's window "fix" was caulk. A water heater in another apartment burst and flooded my master bedroom and bath. I had to insist they removed the soaked insulation and drywall to avoid mold. They attempted shortcuts in the whole process.  After hours/Emergency maitenance people are very offputting, RUDE and inexperienced. And.... my rent is being raised over $100 after only 1 year. This is what REALLY irks me. Over $100? I'm just not happy about this and I don't think it's a fair amount for the quality of the apartment.

Hadn't eaten at Saltgrass for over a year.  A friend and I decided to try for dinner since we were both in the mood for steak.  I had the 8 oz Top Sirloin and  friend had the Porterhouse.  Both steaks were tender and done to our liking but the issue was the amount of salt used on the steaks to the point you were unable to enjoy the flavor of the meat.  I also had the baked sweet potato that had a huge amount of butter, sugar and cinnamon to the point again the flavor of the potato was hidden. It out server has too many tables, as he did not have time to check if all was acceptable and showed up when time for the check.  Definitely will be at least another year or more before I would return.

Asked the bar server (she doesn't rate to be called a bartender) what pale ales were available on tap. She hands us the beer menu and says "everything we have is in here"...we pick a beer and she says "oh, we don't have that, we're in the middle of changeover."  I suppose she was technically correct--everything they had was in there, but everything in there was not on hand. A bartender worth 2 sh!ts can run the on-tap list from memory...and tell you when a keg has kicked.  

We get our beers and "poof"...all the BW3 bar employees vanished. I've never been to a bar where, despite a full house, there was no-one behind the bar. No bartender. No barback. Nada. For 10 minutes the back of the bar was a ghost town...

3 stars for decent wings and cold beer.  Minus one star and plus my lasting scorn for putting Clueless McHuh behind the bar and serving room temp fries.

It's disappointing how bad service can really make you have a bad experience. My two friends and I went to The Lawrence for dinner on Saturday night with reservations. The atmosphere is gorgeous and trendy but after being seated, we didn't get water or even see our waitress for about 20 minutes. She arrived at our table, clearly flustered looking like she was about to cry (she mentioned it was only he second night working there) and apologized for the delay. She took our drink order and gave us water. It then took another 20-30 minutes just to get our drinks. We even went to the bar to get our own drinks (which took way faster) while we waited. We then ordered our dinner, which took about 45 minutes to arrive. Our waitress barely came back to check on our drinks to see if we needed more while we waited for the food. The wait for the food would've been bearable if our drinks just kept coming! The food was good, nothing amazing or worth the price, and my dinner came out cold. Overall, I think this is a cool and trendy place to get drinks or just hang out, but definitely not good for dinner. I would not come back here or recommend The Lawrence to any of my friends until the service gets significantly better.

Although I took one quick bite to try the chimichanga  because I was so hungry.. this is exactly what the food looked like when I opened it. Not appealing at all! The presentation of the food is not okay. I've tried many Mexican restaurants and this is the first I went to that I did not like. The beans were super chunky and thick, did not look appetizing! The meat in both my items had a weird odor and was not good... I tried to eat my meal that I spent $20 on but I simply couldn't. I threw the whole box away because it was just so gross!! Made my stomach feel so weird. Really disappointed :( Hopefully the cooks can try to package the food in a better way and make their food more presentable.

Having come from 2 years of college in NYC, Cherry Mart is naturally kind of disappointing compared to the myriad of other Japanese marts I've come across in NY/NJ. It's small, dimly-lit, and doesn't carry all that much stuff. I also find it really strange how some items are overpriced (i.e. Pocky) while others are on the cheaper side (i.e. Gummy). I hate to be bitchy but when you think about how rent should be at least fifty times more expensive in NYC, prices at Cherry Mart really should be lower...

I participated in the National Karaoke League in 2008. You may get to sing 4-5 times during the season, but for the money, you should get more. I always find it better to just go to Ego's (the bar they hold the league at) and do karaoke on my own. The league doesn't attract too many petite or better girls to whisper sweet Richard Marxs' too either.  It's not bad, but sometimes you really don't feel like hearing Chumbawumba, you'd rather hear a kick ass version of Endless Summer Nights. KNOW WHAT I MEAN VERN?

the wait this last time we went was horrendous. not a wait to be seated, a wait for our entrees which took around 55-60 minutes to arrive after the appetizers. This after the waiter telling my mother and I the paehla (paella) dish was a poor decision because it takes around 45 min to make. If we would have to wait that long anyhow, than we should have ordered what we really wanted. Oh and thanks for no explanation or apology for letting us wait that long and not even refilling our water glasses or bread basket in the meanwhile. HORRIBLE service this time around=not an amazing experience at all.

This place has a great location and is super convenient for us, but the top deck is understaffed. 

We went there to eat tonight and were at a loss for words. We sat down and ordered food, which we didn't get half of until asking for it again later. Basic eating utensils never made it to the table and we had to ask for any napkins at all. The cups we got were just about thimble sized and despite being that small were empty the whole meal and never were refilled. It took forever to get the bill. 

I feel bad for the waitress, because she's got too many people to serve. 

We won't go again.

Not impressed. I've been here on several occasions - usually unwillingly dragged here by friends - and have never been delighted with any of my meals. I've tried a variety of things on the menu but nothing blows me away, or even makes me want to come back without having been forced to. 

I've even ordered the pad thai (one that everyone apparently raves about) and just could not make it past 1/3 of the plate. Personally, it's too sweet of an entree for me. I've tried things friends have eaten ...also no luck. I guess try this place out but I don't really care for it.

the Vladimir Krutov of Vancouver Shwarma.

around 8:30pm, i stopped in to grab a chicken plate, which i've done many times over the last ten years at Falafel King. dude cut some chicken from the spit -- but then put it in a bowl and microwaved it for two minutes. he disappeared into the back and came out with a plastic container of rice before loading up my takeout box with salad, hummus, sauces, pita. 

the rice was mushy and clumpy, bordering on wet, while the meat was unforgivably bland (possibly due to being nuked?). somehow this unholy combination neutralized any zing the sauces might have brought, and the entire meal came off like an over-cooked $2 no-name microwave meal.

Been to Midway twice now so that qualifies as reviewable. The patio is decent if a bit utilitarian. Table service has been overall acceptable, bartenders a bit full of themselves. Had the jerk chicken philly (not much taste and the bread to filling ratio not good, ie. lots of bread) and the turkey burger (which I can only describe as disturbing - do not go there). Midway shines in the craft  brew department, however, which so far has been the best reason to drop by. Go for the beer - hopefully the food will improve over time.

I called to check my warranty on a computer I purchased from them after it broke. The employee on the phone told me it was still covered for two more months. I double checked with him to be sure and told him I was coming from New Hampshire and didn't want to waste my time.  I drove an hour to the store based on the representation that my computer was still under warranty.  When I arrived, however, the repair employee told me my warranty was expired. He was also very condescending and sarcastic and said I must have dropped my computer when a piece on the computer had come loose on its own, apparently a very common problem with this type of computer.  When I asked him how much the repair would be, he quoted me far higher than my local store in New Hampshire.  The only reason it's two stars not one is because the General Manager was accommodating and compensated me in cash for my wasted gas money. Still doesn't really make up for the wasted time, and the fact that I could have already had my computer fully repaired at my local store if I had not waited until I would have time to bring it to micro center based on their employees false representation about my warranty. I would never consider shopping here again.

You know I didn't really enjoy this location. Mainly the atmosphere was very lacking for some reason, food was ok and drinks not tasty or strong for the price that they're asking for.

I bought 2 drinks here and neither got me slightly buzzed. For $15, Trudy's margarita can do the trick for me. 

Waiters were busy so had to constantly flagged one down for something like a straw or some other condiments.

I think I prefer to go to Chili's if I had to pick between this and that.

Pretty disappointed in our first experience at franks tonight. After reading reviews and hearing it was a good place to go we probably won't go back. We ordered tips and a sirloin, both were ordered medium and both were well done and burnt a good amount. We got our steaks and saw they both were burnt a little, so we decided to try them and both were sent back. We never send food back but when all you can taste is burnt meat and there is no flavor to the steak then that's ridiculous. This is a steak house, messing up steak is unacceptable. We got our "new" orders back and they were maybe 10% better. I hate sending food back but a steak house not being able to get a medium sirloin and tips right? Come on absolute amateur hour. After eating we got the bill and noticed their menu was not updated because house wine is listed at $6 a glass but when the bill comes and two glasses is $16 that's not $6 a glass. We asked the waitress and she said "oh I put in you wanted house the menus just haven't been changed" oh okay thanks for letting us know when we got the wine real helpful. The only reason they are getting two stars is because the mashed potatoes and rice were outstanding plus the Guinness was fairly priced.  Give it a shot if you want but we won't be going again. Just look at the charred tips. Ramsey would flip

First time eating in this place, the food was okay... huge lack in customer service. We ordered two mofongos stuffed with chicken and shrimp, two flans and one soda; the bill without tip was 35.00.. I found it too pricy for the quality of food and the service. The server brought the food, she did not ask if we wanted anything else, she did not checked on us, did not ask if we liked the food, she didn't even offer dessert... we asked for it. 
The dress code in my opinion it is more oriented to the guys, as the server was wearing a black thin leggings and a t-shirt. I am not finding this place suitable or family oriented mom-pops restaurant.

Almost every time I go there I struggle just to add as little more rice .. I'm willing to pay for it but they don't allow it coz its not on the menu .. So I ask for extra on the plate .. They make you feel like a homeless guy who is getting free food .. My last visit was the worst .. I asked for 4 burrito bowls .. I asked for the extra rice he added just a little .. Then they pass the bowls to the next person .. Now they want you to hear what both of them are saying and respond at the same time .. I responded to one of them and the other response was the wrong answer coz that wasn't what she asked me .. So she repeated herself again but with a higher voice as if I'm one of the workers .. At the cashier I paid then one of the employees asked the cashier how much is that .. He said 37 .. Then he replied with "wow that's a lot if money" .. Weather I'm right or it was just me .. My visit wasn't pleasant at all .. And I'm not going back here again .. Don't get me wrong .. The staff is ok .. But they just need to pay attention to what they are saying in front of the costumers and please don't rush costumers .. Some of us only can concentrate on one thing at a time .. I'm giving it two stars coz if the amount of rice they put and the way the staff dealt with me in my last visit. At the end I went home and found the order wasn't the way I wanted .. They added Lettuce to two of the bowls which I said they shouldn't .. And it was like three layers .. To cover up the shortage in rice.

Went with 8 girlfriends at 8pm on a Sunday. We were the only table in there and you expect the service would be quick. Nope, the service was very slow. Our server was friendly and cheerful, however she s on the slower side and I wouldn't be surprised if she was still in training. 

Food is good but I don't think it s worth the price tag. I can have equally amazing sushi rolls elsewhere with 2/3 or 1/2 of the price. To top it off, when we're about to leave we saw a little rat running around in the seating area. 

Wont recommend it to my friends.

Went here for the steaks and i got boneless ribeye and my wife got the bone-in ribeye. My first bite i thought, "wow what a juicy steak!", but then a few bites later i realized that all the steak had was juice and no actual flavor. It was so watery I wondered if the cow had recently drowned. My wife's was the same as well, and they got her order wrong by cooking it medium-rare instead of medium, and the mashed potatoes tasted like they came from a box and not with fresh ingredients. It was a busy night so i expected the service to be a little slow, but when the waiter says things like, "umm did i already come by and talk to you about the specials?" , you really start to wonder how they can charge the same price as Ruths Chris which does a much better job in both service and quality steaks

I visited this place frequently when I worked at Lenox Mall right across the street years ago.   Though it hasn't been a regular hangout of mine for some time, I found myself here to watch a couple of the NBA Finals games the past couple of weeks.  While I had a fairly decent experience here the first time I went (if you do go, request the waitress with the short red hair - she's great), last night's experience ensures that I will never set foot in this place again.  

Being out on the patio with only one TV per side was bad enough (not ideal for viewing unless you're directly facing it, which is hard to do with rounds) but we had the rudest waitress I've possibly ever encountered in any restaurant.  Not only did she ignore us and the two tables next to us for most of the night (to the point where we had to go to the bar to get our own water refill and additional napkins), but when we did manage to get her attention, she was both abrasive (getting upset with us when we informed her we did not order the beers she forgot to put in "for our table" - our table had no alcohol at all) and condescending (when we decided to order something else, she responds "I was just here a second ago, but what do you want?").  Really?  The food that my table did order took forever to come out - over an hour- and was mediocre.  I am sure the kitchen was backed up (typical for a sports bar on a big game night), and I would have been more forgiving if she had not been so rude, had at least apologized for the wait, and if other tables (who had different waitresses) hadn't gotten their food pretty quickly after their orders were placed.  

One of the tables next to us finally asked for the manager, who didn't seem overly concerned until he realized it had happened to multiple tables, and he did end up comp'ing our table's bill.  Between him and the awesome red haired waitress, I added a star back, but based on last night (and my overall "meh" impression of the place), I will go somewhere else next time.

Overrated and overpriced. Went on a Friday night at 8 pm, it was so crowded and waited over an hour for a table of 2. But I didn't mind since I was excited to try the restaurant. I just got a drink from the bar and drank it on the outside patio. Once seated, the service was a little slow but that was to be expected as it was a busy Friday night. I ordered the salmon Alexander ($33), my boyfriend ordered shrimp and chicken tenders ($20) and it was all just mediocre. Definitely will not be back.. there are so many more delicious restaurants in the area with way better service.

Great coffee, great food. Very convenient location. Friendly staff. However there are two minor annoyances I have: one being that the ventilation from their kitchen is so terrible that your clothes literally ALWAYS smell like food once you leave (in fact that's very annoying). You WILL smell like a burnt piece of toast once you leave, guaranteed. Second is the music. They've very effectively established their coffee shop as a conventional laptop friendly/productive environment where you can get things done and/or have casual/ professional conversations in various tables or corners of the shop, however the music is constantly WAY too loud. 

Update: Just tried it again. Only this time I could barely breath. You could literally see the smoke floating around the shop. Absolutely ridiculous. Unacceptable.

I can't remember what I had here, so basically the food isn't too memorable. Fajitas are the dead giveaway that this is an attempt at Tex-Mex and since I don't live in the South, I'd really rather prefer my Mexican left alone the way it is--good.

The wait wasn't too bad considering it was a weekend. The (loud/lively) atmosphere makes me think it might be better in a group setting. Preferably with enough cocktail drinking to make you forget why you came here instead of some other better restaurant.

Pad Thai...comfort food.  I was feeling slightly hung-over and exhausted from braving Washington Square the day after Christmas, thus I needed a little comfort.

Hangover food should be a little on the heavy side, maybe a little greasy or oily.  Sadly my hangover was not properly nurtured.  My Pad Thai was rather on the dry side and was surprisingly lacking in flavour of any kind.  My order came with a little pack of nearly flavourless peanut sauce and one slice of lime that did not even come close to moisturizing the abundance of noodles.  

The scallops were nice and juicy and I polished those off right away.  But once those were gone I had little incentive to go near the unenticing pile of noodles before me.  Come on, lure me in with some spice, some egg, and heck some moisturizing and tantalizing sauce.

On the up side, the guy behind the counter that took my to-go order was super nice.  He brought me water while I was waiting and even noticed how dehydrated I was (goes with hangover) and brought me more water.

Alas, next time I am looking for a scrumptious Pad Thai, I will probably look elsewhere.  As lovely as the service was, really the food only rates 2 stars as "I've experienced better."

I'm generally a fan of Pollo Tropical, but I'm only giving this location 2 stars because often times the counters, floors, tables and drink stations are filthy. On my last visit, I wouldn't even touch anything in their condiments and salsa section because of how filthy it was, and the "fresh" onions looked horrible sitting in a slimy puddle of liquid. They have black mates on the floor next to the drink station and the salsa counter; and to me, that's just being lazy and avoiding having to mop up spills, and of course it looks terrible!

The only reason that I'm giving them 2 stars is because the food is always good, I just wish they would keep everything clean!

A nice meal, but nothing so amazing (in the context of fresh fish) that I can say is worth trying. I dined on a swordfish, which was served fairly bland but of solid quality. A caesar salad to start was OK, but nothing out of this world. Service was fairly good and knowledgeable. 

I do have to say that this place was extremely busy. You must make a reservation. Also, the noise level is quite loud and reminded me of a Red Lobster in that way. 

Atlantic Fish is not first class, but may be a place you try when you need a more casual indulgence of reasonably good fish and side dishes. Prices are decent.

Good luck!

Hubby was craving pasta... friends recommended this place. Was very optimistic when we walked in... great space, packed, got seated at a great table right away.
Took a while for our server to arrive at our table. It was packed after all. Finally got our waters and put our drink order in. Server seemed like he didn't want to be there. Food also took a while to arrive... calamari and squid appies were delicious... a bit pricey but really good. Drinks finally came, after we asked about them and after appies were served. Menu seems very authentic. Unfortunately took me a while to find something that interested me. Buddy recommended a pizza so that's what I ordered. Mains finally arrived. Pizzas looked great... mine was bland... was bored after 2 piece and didn't finish it. Hubby has pasta... said it was delicious.
Not sure I will go back. The room was great but service and food did not impress me.

So I'm notified they have a low mileage Smart Car on Lot, that's what I want for round town wheels. I state in email it MUST have power steering option, First answer is it doesn't, my reply no thanks. Bit later, well come on down , it does have it. So I'm coming ready to buy. But nervous about it. Call back and get internet manager (Wheeler?) , other guy Brady. Most definite it does. I even went through how to check with Brady guy.  ROUND TRIP 134 MILES, Got wife along to  drive it back if I buy. Yep, I don't even sit in it cause it don't have power steering Total Lie- to get me in the door. I give 2 stars cause the actual sales guy I saw- was a nice guy who didn't have a clue. This place gives sales a bad name.

Ugh, I feel like I'm cheating on my secret lover (so secret even he does not know), Paul Qui, by writing this review.  I've been such a big fan of everything he does.....Top Chef, when he was at Uchiko, all his food trailers.  But the new menu [April 2013] at Shangri-La was not great.  Collectively our group probably tried the entire menu and there were no "wow" comments; some said their dish was okay and others left their plates unfinished.  Half the menu contained either kimchee or nori (dried seaweed) and admittedly those items may be an acquired taste for some.  I tried the "ESK Grilled Cheese" and was anticipating unique and tasty.   It was unique: sliders style with the bun mimicking a King Hawaiian roll, containing slightly melted brie, green apple slices, nori and kimchee.  The brie and apple went well together as you might expect, but the kimchee definitely fought with those flavors......and well, the kimchee won.  It over-powered the delicate, the tart and the sweet.  Paul: whatever else you change with the other ESK trailer menus, please, please, please, don't ever replace the Liberty's delicious Brussels sprouts salad!  p.s. - I still love you!

YIKES. 

I don't like when people review an establishment based on the clientele, but in a tiny pub it's hard not to comment on the atmosphere/culture of the place. It's flooded with 20-something new Southies. We had a girl sitting at the bar next to our table who was falling out of her chair, went outside and put her mouth on the window to taunt her friends and continually tried to make phone calls, but was unable to because of her level of intoxication. We were there at 4pm on a Saturday. Again, I know this isn't necessarily a reflection on the pub itself, but we could not wait to get out of there. Her friends were doing little to contain her and they were not exactly the most well-behaved either.   

Our server was pretty nice. She ended up giving me a larger beer than I ordered and acknowledged that, but then charged me for the smaller, which was cool. I don't think I'll ever step foot in here again, though.

I saw a scout mob for this new place and I had to try it. My friends BLECK! 

Let me start with my experience. First of all the place was real that'd to find. I drove around that shopping  center 10 times before I finally found it. 

When I walked in I ordered a dozen cupcakes and used my scout mob coupon. The dozen cost me $26!!! I know that my scout mob only gave me $10 off but wow those are some expensive cupcakes. 

Now on to the cupcakes themselves GROSS! They seem to have marshmallow fluff for the frosting. It was disgusting. The actual cake part was mediocre at best.  So much so that  I pawned them off on the hubby's work guys. 

Bottom line just avoid this place.

Meh, just meh.  I continue to be underwhelmed by the food and service at Pok Pok.  To be fair, I'm a vegetarian and I think they are known more for their meat dishes.  I had the coconut curry soup and while it tasted ok, it was rather dull.  I've also had the Thai herb salad a few times and it wasn't anything all that spectacular.  Even though the food was "ok', I don't think I'll go back just because the service has been horrible each time.  On this last visit, I waited 30 minutes for a drinking vinegar and it was just kind of tossed on the table with no apology for the wait. The soup came out fairly cold and then soup bowls, spoons, and chopsticks weren't delivered until ten minutes after we received our food.  On each occasion, the servers have been abrupt and indifferent (not at all representative of the outstanding service I've come accustomed to in Portland).  I asked for a variation on the drinking vinegar and I swear my waiter rolled his eyes while replying with a snarky "soooorrry, but no."  If you're a meat eater or here from out of town and want to experience Pok Pok . . I  say go for it and you'll probably be happy.  Their drinking vinegars are lovely and I do recommend trying them out if you go.

TL;DR: Tried to rope me into unnecessary work that I didn't ask them to look into in the first place. 

Brought my Accent in for a manufacturer's recall. I didn't even expect or ask for them to diagnose the vehicle in any way. They said the car would be ready around 2, at which point I sent a text through their system asking for a time estimate. Got a phone call about a half hour later saying the recall work was done but that the tech flagged a number of issues and he would send me a list so I could sign off on the work - didn't explain what the issues were or give me any idea of their severity. 

I get the text and much of it is valid - new wipers, oil change - I knew that when I brought it in (although again, I did not ask for them to look at any of this, I have a mechanic I like already). Some of it was extremely suspicious, like brakes that I know work just fine. Some of it seemed to be outright nonsense, like the transmission flushing procedure that I knew I had done a year ago - and I have not driven anywhere near 60k miles this year, I've barely driven at all due to covid. I decided I would take it to my regular mechanic because I'd rather have them work on it regardless, as they are much closer.

So I go back to Beaverton Hyundai, and they say they need to get the car ready for me to take it (I can see it parked right there, I'm capable of backing out of a spot). The guy I talked to on the phone comes in and somewhat resentfully says, "You didn't confirm any of the work, does that mean you don't want it done?" Yes, you didn't communicate with me at all so I didn't think I had to inform you that I was on my way to get my own car back.

Then he says he has to do some paperwork, which is fine, records are good. After a short wait, I go to sign it and he says, almost spitefully (the tone of the whole interaction was bizarre and off-putting) that the brakes are a safety issue and that if nothing else, I should get them looked at immediately.

Well guess what! I did get them looked at, and the mechanic I trust says they are fine but they squeal a little from some warping. This matches my experience perfectly, because the brakes do in fact work just fine.

So thanks for the recall work, but I'll be sticking with my regular mechanic for everything else.

We'd been wanting to try Waffle House for awhile, and our other choice this past early Sunday afternoon meant driving a little too far.  So we picked last week to go for the first time.  We got menus right away and the waitress took our drink order.  The place was busy, but it wasn't swamped and there seemed to be plenty of people working.  I got coffee with cream as requested, but no spoon.  

The workers seemed busy enough, though distracted, even sitting occasionally.  We apparently were invisible.  We waited and waited and finally asked if someone was going to take our order.  We weren't at some far away table.  We were right by the gap where the waitresses came out from behind the counter to the tables on the floor.   Eventually, someone came over to us. 

Then we waited and waited for food.  We had to ask for silverware to eat it when some of it- not all of it-  came at last.  I got my scrambled eggs long before my waffle came, so I ate them before they got cold.  They were good; not overcooked or undercooked.  My girlfriend got her All-Star Special without her bacon or waffle.  We had to ask about the rest of our food.  We had to wait for the waffles.  It's not unreasonable to assume that when they came to the table, they'd be hot.  However, the margarine (not butter) didn't melt; they were just warm.  

My girlfriend said the food was good, they knew how to cook over-easy eggs, but the bacon was definitely a cheap cut.  The waffles tasted good, but they were a little too sweet for my taste, and rather thin.  I got one cup of weak coffee; no refill.  I didn't feel like asking once more for something, and it wasn't good enough to want more.  

The food was kind of like home-cooked food, and the workers were like one of your good-natured but absent-minded sisters of whom you could ask, "Hey, while you're up could you get me x?" "Oh yeah, sure."  We were never rude; just puzzled that we didn't seem to merit attention.

I've had better, more abundant food much faster for a better price.  The restaurant seemed messy, the staff didn't seem organized or trained to notice when customers needed something even though we were right there in front of them.  I gave two stars only because the food was good enough for what it is, but paying money for absent-minded service spoiled the experience.  We won't be back again.

It's tough to write this review because I actually like the store. With that being said the customer service was terrible. The staff was not welcoming and didn't seem interested in being of service.  I like to support local, small businesses but I don't think I'll be coming back to this store. There are other vintage/resale stores in the area and they manage to deliver the goods and provide excellent customer service. If the staff could just manage to do the basics, I think it would make a difference. Be Best.

Kerbey Lane was fair.   With most of the egg dishes, egg whites were available for 65 cents more and tofu scramble could be subbed for 75 cents.  Not a bad deal, considering I'm used to paying up to $1.50 to substitute egg whites.  I went with the Kerbey Scramble, substituting tofu scramble for the eggs.  Oops... I'd noticed that the tofu in another dish was mixed with nutritional yeast (eww!!) and didn't realize that would be in my tofu scramble as well.  The consistency was weird and gummy.  I needed my beloved Tapatio for this one, but the only hot sauce on hand was Tabasco.  Grossed out by the tofu/yeast scramble, I focused on the breakfast potatoes (very good) and whole wheat toast, making for a very carb-y meal.

There were two staff there at 6:30am, the gal at the register was very pleasant. She's the reason for the second star. The girl that opened the door was NOT pleased to see anyone. Giving her the benefit of the doubt I handed her a generous tip as she handed me my latte. She sneered and said what's THIS for? I said it was her tip and she shrugged and passed it to the other girl. Guess her blue hair wasn't elevating her mood. Coffee was good, however.

Basically the only reason I was at this store was the pleasure of returning cans and bottles! However the machines (of which there was only 3 and in such a busy location, I would think they would request more) if they took the cans and bottles, mostly kept jamming. So what should've only taken a short amount of time for 3 bags, took almost 2 hours. We didn't even get through all the bags!
The only positive things I have to say about the whole experience was the poor guy who had to keep coming out to unjam the machines. But I also want to mention the girl at customer service gave me the greatest tip on where I could take my returns to in the future. So I just want to give her a great big THANK YOU!!!

Today I took my dog in just to clean her ears and put some drops in for mites. Also got some spray for her hot spot rash. Total $209. $58 just to walk in the door. Spent unreasonably amount of time waiting. 1 hour and 45 minutes.  The vet is nice and knowledgeable but since it changed hands the price keeps going up. Time to move on and find another vet.

Just got a text when I got home to remind me about Canine cough vaccination in two weeks. Why didn't we take care of it then?  

I also inquired about Claro Otic Ear Solution for my dog. She is a cocker spaniel that frequently get mites in her ears.  $30 to look in the microscope to confirm what I already know. $29.50 to clean her ears and $67.20 for 2 vials of Clario. Why can't you just prescribe this for her and let me do it?

I ordered the oven baked salmon ($27) with baked potato instead of rice. It was a small piece of wild salmon that also comes with some asparagus. When I cut in near the center of the piece of fish it was tender and I thought this was going to be a great entrée.  However the outer edges of the salmon were dry and over cooked (which is a good portion of your small serving which could probably fit in a burger bun). The worst part was that some of the salmon had a fishy smell that you get when fish is not fresh. I could not tell right away because it was not smelly for some bites.  I ate about a quarter of the salmon and gave up on it, complaining to the server.  

The server apologized and brought me a Caesar salad instead. Apparently I took too long to complain because when I took my first bite From the centre of the fish I told him it was good. So I paid $27 for a salad, baked potato, and 3 pieces of asparagus. 

I will not go back to the Richmond Keg for a long time after such a bad experience.

I was all around pretty disappointed with my experience at Jades. 

First, the place was very dirty and terribly decorated (I'm not a stickler for this at all but Christmas tree ornaments, really?). The manicure I got ($17 for a french) was bubbly and just not done very well. I expected more for $20 (including tip). 

The one plus is that its ventilated well (probably because of the industrial vaulted ceilings) and so it doesn't smell. Because I'm not from the area I can't compare to other places around here. However, I don't plan on going back unless I try other places and find worse ones. In that case, I'll do it myself. I also don't think they do the thing with the boxes anymore because I didn't see them and the person doing my nails didn't mention anything about that. 

In short, not worth time or money.

I went for lunch, sat at the bar.  It was Wednesday.  The place was almost COMPLETELY EMPTY.  They have a very nice bar.

The bartender had 3 people besides us.  You would think that we would get warm, friendly service with a smile.  NOT SO,  This lady bartender was so unfriendly, almost ignoring us.  Her bartender service was terrible.  Of course, we got the friendly smile when she brought the bill, Tip time.

Where is the owner or manager.  

This is quite a beautiful restaurant; but service staff ....NOT SO GOOD

If you want a warm environment and friendly place for lunch, this is not it.

The apartment we stayed in was beautiful, wish we could've stayed but the rent was hiked tremendously- for a 2 bedroom they wanted $1606/m for 10 month lease- we got that awful notice right before xmas! On top of that, you'll pay $75 for unsecured parking, you're utilities are based on collective usage of the whole apartment community, and are extremely high compared to the rest of Hillsboro. 

The management keeps changing as well. I think it's changed 3-4 times in a year span. They can't get their accounting situation straight. After doing my own accounting, I found out that I've been overpaying for a few months. Since parking is expensive everyone parks in uncovered spots, including myself. I travel a lot for work, and I left my vehicle in the parking lot while gone. They tried purging vehicles deemed "abandoned" by having them towed. Luckily I came back and saw the tow sticker on my car, and had a couple of hours to move it. I confronted the office about it, they said its in my contract that I have to move it within 72 hours of notification, but they never notified me - that manager has since been replaced. Her successor was also replaced.

Their package receiving is also bad- they've mislabeled packages before and I've been given other people's stuff. There's a lot of other small things, but bottom line - you're overpaying at this place, and you won't feel that welcome here, but your apartment is nice.

Staying at the hotel and I'm glad that I get free breakfast with the room. Walk into restaurant and there are 4 people there and wasn't created. I had to ask if I seat myself. Waiter was just ok. I ordered the $15 omelet that comes with one side and no bread- can't believe that. I ordered a bagel and he never brought it out but did charge me for it. The omelet was way over cooked but the grits were the better part of the meal. Honestly a sausage biscuit and coffee from McDonalds for $2.00 would be better.

Teatro is a decent, but not great, place for Italian food. The bright spot of my visit was the service, which was outstanding; he was knowledgable and very funny. I ordered the Gnocchetti with kale and pine nuts. It is a creative dish, but turned out to be a bit bland. The gnocchi was too doughy and a tad underdone. This by no means ruined the dish, but the dozen or so gnocchi on the plate were not worth the $22 I paid for them. There are many Italian restaurants in Boston that serve better food at a cheaper price than Teatro. This city is chalk full of great Italian restaurants, but, unfortunately, Teatro is not one of them.

I had the brisket the flavor was ok but it was dry almost like barbecued shoes. The staff is a bunch of young kids from the local High School/College they were very overwhelmed one girl even yelled at another one of the employees. It was like $15 for the meal and 2 sides a bit pricey for a place that has a drive through. My mac and cheese was pretty much yellow water. For that amount i can go to a nicer restaurant with better food.

Soooo me and Yolanda P. was in the mood for a good place to sit down for burgers and wings on a weekday after work, I had booked marked this place based on her review (granted its about 3 years old). 

I am still pissed off about how horrible it all was : ( The wings were a decent size but flavorless and the burger was burnt to a crisp and just plain nasty. I did get an order of Cajun fries that I finished off just to be some what satisfied with the experience. 

Needless to say this place is scratched off my list.

* Stress leads to prematurity problems *

I had heard their pulled pork was superb, so I had to shuffle on by and give it a try.

One couple gave me an evil eye when I walked in the door and got seated right away - which confused me until I heard their conversation later.  They were lamenting how long they had waited for a table but that, "It emptied out so quickly now."  Thankfully I missed that joy of a line by coming a bit off-hour.  But seriously, giving me a nasty look because I happened to get lucky on my timing?  Sheesh.....

The customers all seemed stressed out.  I'm not sure what it was, but there was a definite stressful vibe to the place.  Perhaps it was the wait they had been through.  Perhaps it was the ghost of Guy Fieri and staring at his graffiti he left above the door.  Who knows?  

The waitress also seemed stressed, and brought a half a cup of water.  That was odd.  In too much of a rush to fill the full glass?  Odd.  

After ordering she quickly brought some condiments which were basically signaling to me that the pulled pork would likely be on the milder side for the West side target market and that they offer ways to kick it up a bit in case you like spice.  Photo:  http://www.yelp.ca/biz_photos/YlIyVA-wkv20VhzuJrVkzA?select=-73Pt_oW8asE-oH79_4ofg

The sandwich arrived.  It was a generous portion of shredded pork.  It did not taste like it had ever seen a smoker though.  I think this was more of an oven method.  That was disappointing as I really like the smokey nature of a good pulled pork.  It also was underseasoned - I don't know if it ever saw a spice rub prior to cooking?  Or perhaps it was rushed and not allowed to season long enough before cooking?  It basically didn't have that long and slow rich smokey spicy flavouring I would look for in good pulled pork.  The bun was warmed nicely and had a nice texture at least.  The slaw also had not marinated long enough and tasted rawer than I would prefer.  And there was MAYO on the bun?!?!?  WTF?  Mayo with pulled pork?  Meh.  Fries were fairly standard commercial variety, but served nice and hot at least.  Overall it was nothing I would come back for.  Photo:  http://www.yelp.ca/biz_photos/YlIyVA-wkv20VhzuJrVkzA?select=nvE5XwIuy6YvyqheYoXJ3g

I'm really glad I didn't wait on a line to get it, as then I would also have likely been just as stressed as all the other customers.  Instead I was just disappointed!

I was traveling and staying at the Boston Harbor Hotel at Rowes Wharf. Interestingly, I noticed his sign/office across the street. 
I had been a patient of his when his office was in NH. I'm sure he had to relocate after taking advantage of patients such as myself when he recommended I do a certain procedure to correct my teeth. It failed to work and did not straighten my teeth. I spoke with (2) other dentists later  who did not know each other and they both concurred that this recommendation was never going to work for what we were trying to accomplish. 
He probably had other unhappy patients in NH and had to move the office. Since then a new Dentist has completed veneers on my front teeth and they look great. 
Make sure what you are considering is the best way to achieve the results you desire. No matter what they recommend. I tried to take action action against him but his insurance company was in Cali ( whole different time zone) very difficult trying to phone back and forth w/the rep.

Decent pizza delivered hot if you live nearby.  And usually my order is accurate, prompt and hot.  Stick to the basics:  cheese and pepperoni.  Even sausage kinda sucks because it's some sweet sweet local thing.  Sausage on a pizza should be *spicy*.  At any rate I digress.  Tonight the person on the phone while sickly sweet, insisted my usual 12 dollar pizza was 16, even after I insisted she had calculated it incorrectly.  "Well how much is it usually?," she asks.  YGBFM, we're asking the customers how much the food should cost?  I actually had to stop to help her calculate the 4 dollars she was over charging me.  She couldn't be more put out.  No tip tonight for this reason sorry.  The delivery guy was prompt and friendly.

I don't get it.  I read a ton of great reviews about this place, but it was just meh. 

Service:  The hostess had a "why are you bothering me" type scowl/attitude.  Our servers was nice but was being berated by the hostess I think, because she looked like she just listened to a recording of her dog getting run over.  Poor girl looked about 3 seconds away from crying the whole time, although she was attentive. 

Appetizers:  Both our appetizers were great, I had the crispy soy nugget, which was amazing, probably one of the best appetizers I have ever had.  You get a star for that.  

Main Dishes: Meh.  I had some sort of dish that ended up tasting like poorly made kimchi.  It was actually pretty boring.  Just not good. At all.  My partners dish was equally bland, although they enjoyed it more than I did.  I couldn't even bring myself to steal bites of it when she wasn't looking, which is rare.  

Dessert: Tried rice pudding and I think a cake or something they had special, I can't remember the 2nd dessert exactly.  The rice pudding was...bland.  Like no taste.  The cake was clearly one of those ones you get in the fridge case at a supermarket, only warmed in a microwave. 

Atmosphere: Noisy millennials shouting at each other.  I don't know if everyone between the ages of 20 and 33 has hearing loss from a life of wearing ear-buds or what.   But really, there's no need to excitedly shout your boring stories about your boring pointless lives.  You're not making up for lack of personality or character by amplifying the volume at which you render your mundane milquetoast recollections of some awful craft-beer you had.   Even the older people that were there were shouting constantly.  This one lady pulls out her phone, puts it on speaker at full blast and starts having a conversation with what was apparently her partners.  I kept whispering "dump her" at an elevated volume to try and plant the seed in the other person's subconscious.  After that riff-raff cleared out, it was actually decent inside; tables were cleanish, artwork on the walls was nice, etc. 

Bathroom: The toilet was leaking all over the place.  Which is gross enough on its' own, but here's the issue:  Since my last review some time ago I have become incredibly wealthy.  You know when people find those half-unfrozen mammoth or mastodon carcasses in the tundra?  I pay to have a chunk carved off from whatever mega-fauna is thawing out and ship it to my cobbler.  On this particular day I was wearing my mastodon leather shoes.  Which were subsequently coated in the spewings of the toilet.   I may have to get on my private jet and fly to a desert island you've never even heard of just to get them to dry out.  Not good times.  Really though, the toilet leaked from the bowl when flushed.  Gross gross gross. 

Overall: It wasn't terrible, but other than that amazing appetizer this was nothing I saw here that even reached the bar of 'average'.   I would probably go back again and order completely different things, and also wear cheap shoes in case the crapper is still leaking.

"Two hearts, two hearts that beat as one...."

Is it just me, or does anyone else zone out to the muzak in these places? The listless cruising of the aisles wouldn't be so bad, but sometimes I start singing along. In the produce department.  

In another store, that might be cool and you might even get the produce guy, or another shopper to sing along, but:  (1) Freddie's employees tend to be a little surly and (2) Endless Love definitely falls in the guilty pleasure category and probably not what you want to serenade the produce guy with while you're squeezing the melons.  But that's just me -- boundaries.

I've been coming here on a weekly basis for over a decade and they cover most of the bases. The natural foods/organic section is surprisingly good and I can get decent produce and most of my household items. And thank goodness they have the sense to stock both Tillamook and Umqua ice cream.  

One thing I should mention is that I've had two bottles of wine I purchased here in the last couple months go bad. One of them was the cheap stuff, but another was a nice Napa Valley Chardonnay, so beware.

I still can't believe they offer free daycare in this store. I only used it once or twice, but still a neat option.  They miss the boat in the prepared foods section and I don't think I've ever gotten food to go.  Something they really should expand.  Nice that they offer free cookies to the kids in the bakery and have a large clothing section with Levi's, Dockers and Columbia.

Still can't figure out the whole family friendly aisle concept. To me family friendly isn't the removal of magazines, but the absence of toys and candy bars at the check-out.  

The key to the whole Freddies experience is to size up your checkers.  Some of them are excellent and others I know will take a really long time. 

-------------

Update: I've dropped my original four rating, since it seems that I prefer almost every Fred Meyer location to my local branch. Sigh. But, convenience is key and I know this store like the back of my hand.

They tried. Came to this place for the first time at 5pm on a Saturday in January. I ventured out from my home wanting to sit somewhere nice after a long hard week of work, eating tortilla chips and having some good drinks. Tried a few chain restaurants and places by the Vancouver waterfront , all of which were jam-packed with people: most restaurant availability (mcmennamins and Wild Fin and   Stack) at this time on 1/16/21 were at a 45 minute wait, even for a party of 1.  Ended up here, due to having a $10 gift card from December.. The building looks very suspicious, with no windows, and a hard-to-find door. I found the door (no minors allowed), and was greeted by a bouncer who wouldn't let me enter without seeing my ID. He informed me they were "full", but that I could order my drink and food and take it with me to the "smoking section" (he didn't mention it was unheated) and that he was sure a table would free up soon in the tables in the tent (heated), in which case he would come get me and seat me there. This never happened, btw. Ended up freezing my butt off in the "smoking section" which is a carport with benches in the back of the building outside, for an hour. I don't recommend eating here for a good experience with ambience. However, since it wasn't raining, and I had a $10 gift card, I was hungry and thirsty, so I stayed. The fried shrimp basket and fries were "pub quality" decent. The Cadillac Margaritas were quite good! Kudos to the bartender for that.  The signs all over the smoking section said it was a no service area, so we needed to bus our own tables.  Bottom line? great drinks and accommodating bar service, but probably not worth the price.. I don't want to pay $30 to bus my own tables, bring myself my own drinks, clean up my own dishes, and have to sit outside in an unheated area at 48°, at a community bench staring at a trash can.  They don't have Cointreau, BTW. All I ordered was 2 drinks and a shrimp basket.  I left having paid $20 for dinner  $5 tip (after the $10 coupon was applied from restaurant.com.) Pub quality food at best, but good drinks help you forget about food quality. However, I made a better Margarita at home and ate my chips at home, and realized I would never go back. $30 is too much to pay for that kind of UNservice.

This location doesn't come close to the Bridgeport location. 90% of the rolls that came out were gross. We did happy hour and got a variety of different rolls and it was hard to stomach them. The special rolls that are on the happy hour menu aren't really worth ordering in my opinion (western, dynamite, Vegas) were the names I believe. The special rolls on the menu at normal price range from about $15-$18 - totally not worth spending your money on this. You'd pretty much be better off going to conveyor belt sushi. 

To give them credit the salmon and yellowtail nigiri were good. And pretty much the only roll I liked was a super basic spicy tuna roll. Also we were in the bar area and the waitress/bartender was super awesome. 

If you do go here, come for happy hour and take advantage of cheap drink prices and just eat appetizers and fresh (not fried) sushi rolls.

Went on the first day of the end of prohibition. Poorly managed. Wait to get "inside" the pharmacy was at least 45 minutes. People kept leaving after signing up and being told the wait was 15 minutes. You could hear a lot of noise and buzzing coming from inside the showroom. Decided since I had already waited so long I would stick it out. Once "inside" there we only 2 customers and ONE open register and at least 5 young female budtenders giggling and chatting amongst themselves behind the counter. Once I made the only choice there was (7 grams of flower, nothing else) I had to then wait to get rung up. Adult male appearing managerial kept running to and fro in a semi frenzy occasionally shouting out "thank you for your patience" . A lot of people showing up on my stint were newbies and there was nothing telling them what to do so the people waiting had to tell them. Wont go back. Too many other opportunities locally to spend my hard earned $.

I really think you guys should close down for a day and retrain everyone.  My English teacher will roll in her grave right now but there is never NOT lines flowing into the aisles.  Maybe its under staffing but either way anyone going here should leave extra time for what ever else you have to do that day.  

If training day is not an option can you please at least put the competent cashiers on the 10 item or less lane. 

Sorry to go overboard but I was in there today at what would be considered a non peak time and you would have thought it was one of those days before a snow storm was coming.  Not because there were that many people but the lines were backed up that far.

Cute location and generally kind server, the rest of the staff however, classically Canadian coldness and lack of all signs of affect, and  , as well as the lovely Treaty of Paris cocktail, all save these 2 stars I leave this place. Being told over and over again how 'particular the chef is' about any modifications to the dishes, temperature of the proteins, etc, we were utterly unimpressed with his particularities. The cod was disgustingly fishy despite our server's assurance that it was the freshest fish possible (the particular chef), the romesco was barely blanched (not cooked) and boringly bland, "The Steak" (ribeye) was recommended at medium, and when we requested it medium rare, the server again insisted that the very particular chef strongly recommended medium so that fat would properly render, of course it was over cooked and loaded with unrendered fat anyway (someone needs to help this chef learn how to cook). I had a ribeye at Flint Creek in Seattle last week that was on the rare side of medium rare and was cooked to perfection! My hanger steak was fine, medium rare, but poorly seasoned. Additionally the wine, and this is a foux paux that far too many restaurants make, is stored up high on the warmest shelves of the venue, so my glass of wine was hideously warm, heavy sigh. We couldn't stand the idea of staying for desert and hearing anything more about the very particular chef's tastes.

I come here to chill, without having to be worried about parties of families or kids running around. A decent place to have a beer and relax. They specialize in wings, but also have lots of other food options. 

The wings here... aren't good. Sure they may have lots of variety, but the flavors aren't "awesome". It also kind of bugs me that their quality isn't consistent. I'm pretty sure they use whole wings and separate them, hence my 1lb of wings with tiny wings and probably not even a pound since another order had the same amount of wings but where bigger. The wings are doused in sauce of your choice... but when it makes it to the table it's cold and soggy. Ugh. This has happened 3/4 times I've come here. Their nachos are good though, sometimes soggy, but lots of ingredients, so it's ok i guess?

Service is meh. They aren't very attentive... usually too busy not doing their jobs. I'd rather go downtown or even coquitlam for better wings and service. Where servers can put on a smile. But hey, if you don't want to be bothered and don't mind not having your drink refilled... come here!

While this store is very convenient for those who live in the area, as it is quite large with a wide selection of produce, prepared/takeout food, natural foods, an Osco pharmacy, and a health/beauty products section, this is much that could be improved.
Sometimes the produce is acceptable; other times, not so much. I've had green beans go bad in a few days, opted to skip buying entirely wilted heads of lettuce, and the cucumbers are often too soft for comfort. If you're a vegan like me, shopper beware - you might be better off going somewhere else.
The prices are quite high compared to many other markets just outside the Boston area (MarketBasket in Waltham has the same products for nearly HALF the price. Examples: veggie burgers, pineapple and cantaloupe, tomatoes, tofu, and cauliflower -  $4 a head? Really?).
There never seems to be enough people working there, so the lines always move incredibly slowly. This has been the case for at least the last 2 years since I moved to this area and began shopping here. Despite there being about 8 checkout lanes, I've never seen more than 3 staffed, even during the busiest times. Sometimes the self-check out lanes are also closed down. On numerous occasions I've also witnessed employees walking around the front of the store seemingly aimlessly, while they could be helping bagging large purchases (there are rarely baggers helping here FYI). 
Why do they have such high prices if they are so poorly staffed? My guess would be building rent, and for those who don't have the time or the means to travel elsewhere, you're stuck with paying the high prices.

Went there for the first time on a Sunday, they are supposed to open at 11 AM. At three minutes before 11, an employee walked up and could not get into the store because management was not there yet. She walked away. 15 minutes later the owner walked up, making excuses, not apologies, and did not have a key to get in, she called someone else that couldn't arrive for who knows how long? Would love to give them another try, but probably will not.

Oh Bikinis, Bikinis... I think it might be time for us to break up. You are the funnest place to watch the Steeler games, and being from Pittsburgh, thats a bold statement. The management and rudeness by your staff has finally come to an end. I bring large groups to watch the games. You shouldn't have to order a beer when your halfway through just so you don't have to wait. And whats up with running out of mugs and serving me in plastic? That has to violate some sort of sanitation, taking my mug back to the bar to fill up. Am I sure that I got mine back? Your food is terrible, yet I continue to put myself through the torture  every Sunday, looking at that menu. There are 4 other Steeler bars in Austin, I think it might be time to try another one next Season and for the SUPERBOWL! I am giving you 2 stars because its still a fun environment.

Decided to give this place a try because it was a gorgeous day to sit on a patio. When it comes to a patio this place does not disappoint. On this particular Sunday afternoon it was practically empty. There were 3 other tables but then a very large party was sat. The problem with this place was that there was only 1 server for the entire patio. That meant that everything was slow. Waiting to be greeted? Slow. Waiting to place your drink order? Slow. Waiting for the straw you asked for? Slow. Once you get your drink and then asking for straws for that? Slow. Actually, no it didn't happen. I just got up and got one from the bartender myself. Ultimately, we decided that, although the patio was super nice, we would continue drinking and get food on a patio somewhere else. Honestly, I wasn't even mad about it. At first, I was annoyed with the server but then I felt bad for her for having to be the only server up there. It totally wasn't fair. Maybe I'll give this place another shot one day. I just hope they get their service issue straightened out.

My bf and and I were looking for a new place to try and had driven by this place a few times and said why not.  The outside decor seemed hip and inviting and well lit.  When we walked in on Saturday night (around 6pm) the bar was somewhat busy and the dining area so so.  We were greeted with a smile and brought to our table.   

First off, I grew up in the restaurant business and for over 20yrs have seen the ins and outs of how to run one.  One thing I learned is to keep the patrons happy.  So I think it's quite annoying that we were seated right next to a large table when there were clearly other open tables that would have kept us at least a table away.   I understand that if we were seated at this open table there is potential of another party sitting next to us but at that time it would have been the smarter choice.  

Our server arrived promptly and service overall was 4 stars for me but it's not just about the service.  

We ordered the broccoli spring rolls as an appetizer.  They were just ok.  They were a bit too greasy and could have used another touch of salt/pepper.   My bf ordered the short ribs which were tender and juicy but again lacked seasoning.  The sides with his dish was mashed potatoes and brussel sprouts.  The mashed potatoes were ok but the brussel sprouts were under done and had no seasoning and all.  I ordered the scallops over the parsnip puree.   The scallops were a smidge under cooked and the puree was way too sweet.  We also decided to get dessert, also a disappointment.   The brownie sundae and apple crisp were huge and the menu should indicate the size of these desserts.  There also were nothing special,  though the apple crisp lacked bring crisp, it was basically a scoop of vanilla ice cream over apples.

The one thing I will say is the pricing was worth the ratio of food you received.  

Overall the atmosphere and ambiance of this place is great, I would recommend going to hang at the bar and meet up with friends but not for the food unfortunately.  

As always never take my word for it and give it a try yourself.

Really wanted to love this place since I'm all for korean snack shops but at my first visit, the 12$ seafood pancake was so salty I had to toss it out. It was also soggy instead of crispy (literally ate it in the parking lot after picking up. The seafood in the mix itself tasted almost rancid. Not sure why it took as long as it did to make because the whole thing was pretty disgusting and burnt instead of crispy. At my second visit, tried the TWELVE DOLLAR tuna kimbap (yes 12$) and the rice was hot? It made the tuna rolls taste really sticky and warm when kimbap is supposed to taste almost cool. I think this is the most I have ever, ever paid for kimbap. Average price for kimbap is 6~7$ MAX at any given korean snack shop in Atlanta. For 12$ I was expecting something pretty amazing but as expected, 1 roll will absolutely not fill you up and 24$ is not worth getting full on kimbap. We also ordered the bulgoggi which did not really taste like bulgoggi?? Each bite got progressively boring and a single order is way too much for one person?? Ended up throwing away almost half. Not sure why the portioning and pricing is so all over the place. Korean snack shops are usually not "family share" style unless they offer items in multiple sizes and in varying "sets" with other items. I found the menu to be pretty limiting and this is the first time I ever saw ddukbokki as an appetizer and again only coming in one size. This location will have to be a pass for me.

The ATL was slammed with travellers and we found ourselves sadly heading towards the TGI Fridays and its long line when Intermezzo appeared...and only a two minute wait. I ordered the Chipotle chicken panini with "baked fries". It was described with "smoked, pulled chicken" and a "creamy chipotle sauce". Not too bad sounding, right?

The panini arrived on very soft bread...no typical grill marks or indication it had been "panninied". Lots of dry, flavorless pulled chicken, a couple of tomatoes, and a hint of what must have been the chipotle sauce. Overall, it was bland and the fries were a waste of space.

Unimpressive service including asking the patrons to help them clear dishes!  Practically throwing dishes into the clean up bin RIGHT next to us before we were through with our meal.  We were in a group and ordered family style, but then we were asked to share a TINY plate of desserts.  CHEAP.  the food was fine, i've had better.  I would not go back, mostly because the service was so terrible.  I felt that the waiters were angry that we were there!

I also live around the corner from the hub, & I've been anticipating the grand opening on this place for quite a while...The old tenants were "the Pit"- possibly the worst BBQ joint in Austin and back then it looked like the building was in real bad shape...

THANKFULLY the new proprietors really cleaned the building up- its nice & clean with new bathrooms too- perhaps a little too sterile, though. It just lacks the cozy atmosphere you'd expect from a good neighborhood joint..

on to the food

all i have to say is one big "EHHHH"

What I mean is it's utterly mediocre and lacks any uniqueness whatsoever...Sorry.  I really wanted to like this place.

the menu is really small- like what you'd expect from a golf course pro-shop grill or your average pub-grub kinda place: burger, chicken sandwich, BLT, club sandwich, salad, shakes & malts, and that's about it.

I ordered "the Flatty"- a 1/4lb burger with avocado & tots.  The veggies were fresh and prepared just fine, but the meat was overcooked and bland.  The bun was the whitebread, concession stand kind- a little stale and cold.

the tater tots were cooked just right, but too salty, and i usually don't mind salty stuff...just WAAYY too salty.

They had like 4 different bottled beers and 2 wines available - so its not really a place to go drink, or I'd have given them a little credit for the lackluster food. they did have like 4 flat-screen tv's though.  so maybe cool to take the kids there on a Sunday after their soccer games or whatever...just not my scene.

Sorry to be ripping this place...but I'm just disappointed.  I mean- have some friggin pride!  don't just cater to the lowest common denominator.  We don't need more mediocre restaurants in this town...but this neighborhood DESPERATELY needs a quality, reasonably priced restaurant with good atmosphere...

Unfortunately, The Hub is NOT up to the task.  If you want a decent burger around this neighborhood- try the Boulevard Grill on Far West (actually they have great burgers), Waterloo Ice House down at 360, or pony up for some great food at Che Zee.

The sushi quality has been lacking for quite some time.  The rolls are smaller and the fish is not as fresh as it used to be.  As far as the Thai food is concerned, you can get better quality at Thai Chili down the stree.  My biggest complaint is that the food never comes out at the same time for the whole table.  So if you have 4 people, they'll bring out a steaming hot entree for 1 person.  Then 10 minutes later...a lukewarm entree is brought out for another person at the table.  This happens every time, it seems.  Someone is always waiting to eat and someone always has lukewarm food.  I wish they would PAY ATTENTION and make sure that everyone at the table (especially if only a group of 3-4 people) has their food at approximately the same time.  And the food should always be served hot...but without fail someone's entree is always the one thats been sitting, getting cold in the back.  Ugh.  There are plenty of Thai and sushi places near Thaicoon...so they'd better step up their game if they want to survive many more years.

If there's any consistency to this location, it would be consistenly bad, consistently rude staff, consistently greasy spoon kind of food. Yuck! If I didn't mind grease I would just pay half the price for Waffle House. I am amazed this location isn't one that was shut down due to the company cutting some store locations. I don't know how it does any business. Every time I come here there's not very many people here and there is so much staff they are falling all over one another. Will never go back to this place. Again....yuck!

Is 26 West worth the overpriced rent? No.
Is 26 West the best apartment you can find in West Campus? Definitely No.
But is it as bad as other reviewers make it out to seem? Eh.

Prior to living here, I felt like I had made a big mistake after reading all the Facebook memes and reviews about this place. After living here for over a full month now, I feel that I can give my honest opinions that may help others who are deciding on a place to live.

THE GOOD:
The 4x4 is very spacious and I like how the rooms are divided into two sides. The gym is nice, and there were free school supplies in the computer lab downstairs. The location is very close to campus (and the food trucks!) and the pool area actually isn't too shabby. My roommate requested a bathtub resurfacing and she was able to get it completed a day after she called them.

THE BAD:
Walls are really thin! You can hear everything and even people walking above you. The exterior doors to get into the building are constantly broken and therefore do not lock properly. The door leading to our unit has broken over 4 times now in the time that I've lived here so anyone can just walk in. When I moved in, the lock to my room was also broken and although maintenance has come to examine it, I have yet to get it fixed. Speaking of maintenance, someone had come in to fix our light in the kitchen but for some reason also felt the need to replace the eyehole in our door even though it was not broken and no one had placed a work order for it. 
The trash disposal is also located in the parking garage and is really far away from some of the units. The exterior hallways sometimes have throw up, but in my experience this is usually cleaned up within 24-48 hours. 
The mailing system here is a bit whack. Sometimes I receive packages but do not receive any notice from the front office, and they have lost a package that I had delivered before. They are also really inconsistent about requiring photo ID for pick up. 

I think the weirdest thing that they just implemented is the wristband rule. Supposedly if you are to have a guest over, you must have your guest wear a cheap rubber wristband to use the amenities. They also give you a wristband for yourself, and if you lose these wristbands they make you pay ~75$ (wth? these are literally those cheap bracelets you get for free y'all). I have not personally seen this rule enforced, and I find it to be just another sleazy tactic to rob college students. 


Overall, I don't regret my decision to live here as I feel that a lot of these problems occur at many other apartments in West Campus HOWEVER I will say that I lived at The Ruckus last year and did not experience any of these problems. Despite all the cons, I'm still able to enjoy being at my apartment and do not constantly agonize over the "horrible conditions" that many others have lamented about. If you really cannot find another place to live, I don't think it would be a bad idea to live here, just be aware that some of these things do happen.

We ended up here one night when we tried to go to Foreign and Domestic and the wait was too long for our time table.  Both my bf and I have been vegetarian at one time or another so we were up for trying one of Austin's famed hippie eateries.

I wouldn't say the food was yucky, but it was seriously lacking flavor.  He ordered the bueno burger, I ordered the spinach mushroom enchiladas with spicy cashew chipotle sauce.  If I had been eating a $3-4 frozen dinner, I might have been more impressed, but there was nothing special about the flavor in either dish, and my enchilada dish had obviously been under a warming lamp or the plated dish had been tossed back in the oven for a bit because the sauce had developed a bit of that telltale skin on top.

The best thing about our evening was the solo vibraphone player in the corner - that was one of those "only in Austin" type moments...

I was looking forward to lunch here on Sunday as my friend hyped it up, but sadly it's going to get only 2 stars from me on this review. Food was 3, but service sucked so 2 is it. 

We arrived and it was busy, but we were the only ones waiting. We waited a few minutes and then were brought to a table where a server never came over to us for 10 minutes. Everyone around us were ordering and getting drinks. I called the hostess over who went and got the server.
