We ordered an appetizer, but they never brought it.

I did enjoy my sandwich, the Sonoma Chicken Wrap with roasted chicken, hickory bacon, spinach, marinated tomatoes and guacamole, wrapped in grilled flatbread. But I had to send back the cold fries it came with for a new order. 

This place was fair and that's being nice.

Unfortunately for me the food was awful! I have never had this issue before with this place however the steak and cheese with extra cheese and mushrooms I ordered looked like this! Dry bread, over cooked steak and no mushrooms... cold cheese? The Italian sub was on dry bread without the oil I asked for. On top of all of this when I called to let them know their food was less than acceptable the young lady on the phone wanted to argue with me!! Customer service NOT GOOD! I am giving 2 stars only because they did deliver the food within 30 min as they promised

I live locally but haven't tried this place until I picked up a buywithme coupon.  Went there recently and left a lot to be desired.  I wasn't paying attention when I first walked in and didn't see the sign to hand the coupon to the hostess when you arrive.  I was actually on yelp while I was waiting to order and saw the note that someone else posted about having to do that.  Once I saw the note, I handed my coupon to my server next time he came over.  From there on I noticed a big shift in attitude towards me and the service got much worse.  WHY did you sign up to offer the coupon to people if you get annoyed when they use it????

Drinks were ok.  Kind of small and very standard.  I love chips and salsa and usually eat more than my fair share when I go to mexican restaurants.  This salsa was awful and after one bite, I didn't eat anymore.  Weird consistency and almost tasted more like a chunky pasta sauce with cilantro..

Parts of the meal were good and others were average.  First of all, please bring food that is HOT and not barely warm.  I got a combo platter and the fried quesadilla actually had some good flavor but was missing cheese. Burrito also had some good flavor.  Rice and beans needed to be much warmer.

Disappointed with Ton Ton's ramen game especially when there are so many other great options in Atlanta. Ordered the tonkatsu and I felt there were toppings missing. The description stated there was mushrooms and I couldn't find a single one. But the most offending part of the bowl was how beyond salty the broth was. My mouth was blistering salty. The pork slices were too flabby for $13. My favorite place that I've found ramen at is Hajime... I feel they've perfected their craft with those handmade noodles. Plus coming to Ponce Shitty Market is like going to a freaky mosh pit. Pass.

I used to like getting a quick meal from this place when they were located next to Dave's Fresh Pasta before Dave's first expansion.  I know they weren't really crepes even then - as a few other reviewers have noted, they're more like thin somewhat crunchy pancakes - but these semi-crepes actually stood up well to the hearty amount of stuffing put into each one, so I didn't mind.  But after they reopened in Someday Cafe's old spot after some months without a store, I tried them again, and I just can't believe what a difference the bigger location and new staff has made.  I had to wait a half hour for my crepe each time, even though there were usually quite literally no orders ahead of me at all, and additionally, sometimes the staff was actually dismissive or snobby towards me.  After about five tries of having the same disheartening experience every time, I finally gave up.  (The other people I know who used to go to their old location have similarly quit trying.)  Food has to be really really good, to me, to warrant that kind of wait, and while this food is pretty good, it's not at that level.

I read several reviews and thought I'd give this place a try. The staff was friendly and helpful (they would get 5 stars). It feels like a chain inside but there's flat screen tv's to keep people occupied. I got some food to go. It took a little while but that's okay. I tried the 101 egg roll which I liked fine  and the tofu spring ... Which I didn't. It had a wide flat piece of fried tasteless tofu, some greens and tons of noodles. It was huge but tasteless and not tightly wrapped. For entree I got the brisket pho. The meat looked strange. I usually go to PhoThaison across the street and get the beef pho. It's raw and cooks in the broth which adds to the flavor. The brisket pho at phoNatic comes cooked (which makes sense: ) but it looks like machine process/cut meat. It reminds me of gyro meat (the look, not taste). When I put the pho together, it just wasn't great. Edible- yes but missing lots of flavor. I'm glad I tried it but I will be going back to PhoThaison!  Their pho is great! And they give you a cup of tea with a cookie while you wait!

Felt compelled to write my first ever review. I would not recommend this restaurant. The portion sizes are extremely small for the price and I am not a big eater. The seafood risotto was black and literally swimming in a pool of oil. Granted it was "special" seafood infused oil but it was very oily for risotto. there was about 3 pieces of seafood. You actually had to pay for the bread! I was very nicely offered another option but I declined as I had a bad taste in my mouth. Bad introduction to a city who prides itself on good food. Service was good, however.

3 of us ordered dinner at Chen's. Kung Pao Chicken, Beef and Broccoli, and egg rolls. Both entrees were very bland. The Kung Pao didn't have a trace of heat at all, literally none. The Kung Pao was super heavy on celery without much else. The Beef and Broccoli was ok but again, bland. The egg rolls were decent size but lacked anything that made them stand out.

We weren't expecting too much from Chen's and I'm pretty sure the food isn't going to make me sick. But, other than that, very unmemorable even for this type of Chinese restaurant.

The service was ok although we were the only ones in the restaurant. Portion size was average. Strangely, at the end of the meal the waitress tried to sell us a cheap-looking Chinese calendar for $25. Odd.

Well, one thing is sure, I'm not booking at this resort again. Here's why:
1. Poor WiFI connection. This is a business trip so WIFI was absolutely necessary. I had to call Guest Services who connected me to their WIFI Department several times since my connection was running extremely slow. My first evening was the worse. I was not able to get anything done. As luck would have it, my Hotspot was not working either. Talk about major frustration.
2. Horrible parking at night. Must be because it's Spring Break so this place was packed with families. With that, came lots of cars. Good luck finding a space if you drive in late at night. I made it a point to use Uber on nights my co-workers and I dined out at a risk of coming back to our resort without any parking. 
3. Hard to reach Guest Services. I was able to reach them but it took several attempts. Lines kept ringing.
4. Finally, my cable went down. So no TV this
morning. Guess what, this will require another call to Guest Services!
5. Fitness Center is wonderful but they close at 8 PM. Not bad for those on vacation but certainly not convenient for business travelers who tend to drive in a little after 7 PM.
Too bad considering it's in a great location. It's close to Whole Foods which I frequented. This resort also looks like a great family vacation spot with all the amenities and activities they offer. On a positive note, they are upgrading their rooms and they are constructing another building. Then again, this will create a worse parking nightmare. I  hope their management team takes all these reviews seriously. At the end of the day, they are up against other resorts and hotels in the area. I would have switched hotel after my first night but there were slim pickings because of the time of year. Lesson learned.

Are you there, Tap?  The lights were on, but nobody was home.  

We had dinner here (with a Summer Swag coupon, 50% off) on a nice night, so we sat on the patio.  The service was spotty, but eventually we put in our drink and dinner orders.  I had a glass of wine and the Mediterranean flatbread ($8), and both were decent.  The vegetables on the flatbread were fresh, and the lemon confit was a nice addition.  Overall, the menu seemed to have something for everyone and was definitely priced right.

But, the service was bad.  No one refilled our waters.  No one checked in with us, and we actually had to hunt down our server just to get the check.  They weren't that busy, so I guess they weren't looking to turn tables, but really?  Really?  One other thing that I didn't understand- Whose idea was it to put the restrooms on the 2nd floor?  I had to walk up the stairs and through a private party before I found them.

The cocktail menu and wine list were appealing to me, so maybe I'd commit to a happy hour here, but that's about it.

Dang that's some expensive queso. 

Yes, the proximity to the Convention Center is strategic, as who else will dine there besides those with expense accounts?  Personable hostess and wait staff, including a cute backwaiter who looked like he doesn't  yet shave reguarly. After a tour of the labrynthian dining rooms (with some interesting looking private cubbies) my 5 girlfriends and I chose to sit in one of the large round booths in the bar area, hoping that eventually the place would start filling up on a Tuesday night (no such luck; the place was dead and decidedly NOT happenin') .

I found the choices  - cheese vs broth vs boiling oil vs chocolate; appetizers vs meal more than a little confusing. But they brought us our Titos N Cranberries quickly and often, and that made everything ok. 

I just wish I had a client I could expense it to.

I really hate giving out less than 3 stars for even a mediocre experience, but this place warrants it. 

1) I ordered the moscow mule which had jalapeno in it.  I knew this going in, but the jalapeno was so overpowering i had to send it back.  I requested a beer instead, which was just ok.  

2) I had the filet-o-fish which also had jalapeno on it...but in thick slices so they weren't really a part of the sandwich per se, but rather a nasty surprise which I had to take off.  I had about 6 thick slices of jalapeno on the sandwich, which seems a bit crazy for a small sandwich. 

3) The desserts were too cold and the buttermilk pie was way too sweet.  

4) I was charged for my untouched moscow mule.  

This was the icing on the cake of a forgettable meal which I sadly won't repeat, which saddens me.  Cool atmosphere and great music.

My packages got shipped.  That's a plus.   

The $35 I spent to send two stuffed animals to New Jersey and Pennsylvania from Massachusetts?  Kind of pricey but I liked the insurance/tracking/peace of mind.

The 40 minute wait I had while I was not helped or even acknowledged?  Not really fun.   To the store's defense, there was only one cashier on duty on the Saturday I was there, and the person she was helping was sending a tube.   Yeah, that doesn't sound too crazy to me, either, but maybe sending a tube at the UPS Store is the equivalent of the logic games on the LSAT.  

The fact that the doors to the store were open and the sign outside said it would be open until 4pm, but yet once I got in at 3:45 I was told they were closed and was handed a lollipop for my trouble?  Well, that's just one of those amusing yet disturbing stories I can tell my friends... so thanks, UPS Store!

I used to love this place and completely agree with the other reviewers who complained about their downfall.  I went in this afternoon after craving a savory crepe all weekend and was very disappointed to find out that they are no longer on the menu.  I asked if it would be possible to put the ingredients of one of their sandwiches into a crepe and the worker laughed at me and said "yeah, we don't do that anymore."  For the life of me, I don't understand why they wouldn't be able to put ingredients that they already have with one another!  To make things worse, we were forced to sit at a communal table with strangers and it makes the whole dining experience completely awkward and made me want to get out as soon as possible.  What if someone wants to have a semi-private conversation?  Impossible.  Sorry Cafe Nation, you were once one of my favorite places but I will not be returning and will have to find another place where I can get a decent crepe.

I'm not entirely sure I get this place.  They advertise as if they have the best fish tacos that have ever been presented on a plate; however, I certainly beg to differ.  The sauce they use tastes like McDonald's special sauce, which actually makes it taste like a fast food fish sandwich, rather than authentic fish tacos.  Maybe it's because I'm from Austin, but fish tacos should NOT taste anything like that. 

The one plus I give to them is the selection of salsas.  Everything from tomatillo to roja to verde is available, and they're all pretty good.   Problem is, the food you put the salsa on leaves a lot to be desired.

I dont mind hot pot every now and then, but I hate the loud chatters of people..it does not help when you are attempting to get a server's attention.  Its not the best place, but its not the worst. 

We had a reservation at 8:30, we got there a bit early and the manager asked if we had a reservation, he snottily replied "OH, you're too early, tables not ready yet".  I can see that, I realize we were early, but its cold out!  Douche.

I'd much rather do hot pot at home, comfort of my own home where I don't need to pay extra for the soup/soy sauce/hot sauce and things..why would I go to a place just to boil my own food basically?

We had a larger group of 15, one of the guests at the table asked the manager to get 6 bowls of soy sauce.  He was like "6!?"  We re-assured him that we needed that many more..hesitant/cheap-ing out on things like soy sauce now?  Good grief..

Do it at home, you can buy better things and not have to deal with people being ridiculously thrifty with big tables and have better service.

Extremely unhelpful. I called a week ago because my refrigerator stopped properly cooling. They said the soonest they could get to me was a week later, so I said fine and waited patiently for my appointment. Finally, they called to say they were on their way. The very nice technician that showed up was dismayed that it was my refrigerator, as he was not a refrigerator technician. Wow. What?!?! So he left, saying don't worry, we'll get you taken care of. A little while later I get a call from someone at their office telling me to call the maker of the refrigerator!!! Seriously?!?!? I wait a week for my appointment only to be told to call the manufacturer?!?!? Absolutely ridiculous. Two stars because the young man that showed up was very nice and professional. However the overall experience was just absolutely worthless.

So let me caveat this review as I'm surprised that I haven't reviewed JCT in the past. Normally, I would give JCT 5 STARS based on my previous (3) experiences. The food is amazing as is the ambiance. Last night must have been an anomaly, but the folks seated next to us seemed equally annoyed. Not sure if the kitchen was in the weeds or not enough servers staffed or just an issue with our server. It was a lovely evening out and we decided to sit on the Patio. It's a great space and we still had fun, but it took 45 mins to get our food (standard fair - dates, mussels, truffle French Fries, & Pimento spread) - it was all "lukewarm" when it came out, but by that time it was 9PM and we were starving. My steak tartare came out 15 mins later which was equally strange. Maybe it was just an "off night for them", but hoping this feedback can help them get back on track. I'll definitely still come back and let's see what my review is next time. :)

The actual work that Magic Beans does is very good. However the business practices make me unable to recommend them. Their first engagement was for a spring cleaning. They came out and did an estimate and I approved the work. Halfway through the work they told me it would cost roughly double the estimate, or they could stop work and leave the project halfway completed.  Everything was visible during the estimate, and if these are true professionals, they would understand what work is required. In retrospect I believe they low-balled the bid and planned the up-sell, as I have seen other folks making a similar statement that the work price changed mid-project. 

Following this, there was miscommunication where Megan sent a text that implied they would be doing ongoing maintenance. While the text stated they would be coming out weekly, the price was about the same as what they quote in their monthly contract at $220/month for maintenance of a mid-sized yard. (Their actual contract document shows a somewhat lower price). Regardless, Magic Beans actually did not do any work, and after a month the place was growing significant weeds again. I asked Megan to look at this and advise me what was needed. 

A short time later she replies that they have already started work and want almost $1400 - and that the previous quote of $220 was per week. That is utterly ludicrous. $1000/month for maintaining a Martin Acres yard? But she was going to discount it by30% because of the communication problem. Since she already started work, she wanted me to pay the whole price or "half and they will stop work then." This all happened within an hour and a half of my message. There is no way that more than an hour of work had occurred at that time. At no time had I told her to start work. 

In the end, I paid her for one hour of labor at her absolutely unfounded labor rate of $75/person for 2 people for an hour. I feel this was still an extortionate amount and especially since I had not approved the work. 

As I said at the beginning, the actual work is good. But they are way beyond expensive, and I feel that they use deceptive business practices. If you use them, be sure to have an absolute agreement as to scope and prices.

The food is great, it's extremely delicious. However, Terrence is extremely rude. I came in one day, he didn't even acknowledge me. I had to speak to him in order for him to greet me and as a paying customer I should be greeted as soon as I walk in. He will shut down the restaurant in the middle of the day & not let customers know that he won't be in and t customer service was horrible. It makes me not want to return. The food is delicious, but the customer service needs to be worked on.

Got the Groupon deal as well. I REALLY wanted to like this place. The people all seemed super nice and friendly, for the most part.

Chiro:
The Groupon didn't even include a chiropractic exam, they offered a free 15 consultation along with our massage - why not? The chiropractor was definitely a pushy salesman type, pushed the discount x-rays, pushed for follow-up exams and kept nagging about the follow-ups even after I was done with my massage and checking out. 

Massage:
I've had 2 hour massages and 20 minutes massages and backrubs from bored partners. In my opinion, 30 minutes isn't really much to write home about, no matter where you go. My massage was meh-worthy. The gal was nice, the massage was ok, the room was warm and very calming. 

Float:
This was our first time floating, we really had no idea what to expect so we went in with open-minds. The lady that got our tanks prepped was telling us about how the heater in the one my husband was going in kept cutting off, but since we were just doing the 30 minute float - it'd be fine. She tried upselling us to the 60 or 90 minute floats, but we said we were fine with 30 minutes to start. She said she'd knock 5 minutes before our time was up, then knock when it was time to get out. 

We put in our ear plugs, waved bye to the outside world and closed the door to our separate float tanks. Blackness. Silence. Warm water. Lean back. Float. The places my mind took me were amazing. I literally tripped the eff out. I was meditating at first and then just friggen left the planet. It was so relaxing and warming and loving and amazing. GREAT GREAT GREAT! Then I started thinking, "hrm. it seems like I've been in here for a really long time.... Crazy how time sort of stands still when you cut out the senses.... let's count seconds... 1....2....3" You get the idea. Then there was a knock. "ok wow! so now i have 5 minutes. lets see how long that feels!" I think. Then a LONG while later, I hear/feel the second knock. "Ok! I'm done!" and I get up slowly,  open the door and my husband is standing there wide-eyed looking at me. He asked me if I'm ok and told me that I was in the tank for ONE HOUR AND FORTY FIVE MINUTES!!!!!!! The lady forgot about us! He got out on the first knock, took a shower, went to the steam room and started to worry about where I was. That's when the lady came back and knocked on my tank the second time - 20 minutes after the first.... 

I got out and felt like I was on a mysterious planet. Naked. Dripping. Smiling ear to ear. I was a friggin prancing faerie. Took a long shower and was so excited and happy and soooo relaxed. I loved it!

The gal came in to apologize and seemed very worried that I'd be upset. I said it was totally fine and loved my experience. I'm thankful she sorta forgot about me! I had a blast! BUT, if i were someone else, they may not have appreciated wading around in the friggin water for almost 2 hours.

By the way I stepped on a piece of glass while walking around naked and barefoot. Word to the wise - bring slippers.

By the way pt. 2: Yknow how the lady mentioned the heater cutting out in my husbands tank? Well it cut out and his water got cold and he was shivering by the time he got out. Yknow - an hour and a half later... Pretty lame.

2 stars are mainly for the nice people that worked there. We will not be coming back to this establishment. BUT heck yea, we will be floating again!

The stars are for the friendly staff, the very clean look and ambiance, and the profit-sharing business model. It's a nice place with nice people so I want to be nice, but...

I don't want to eat here. 

The "egg and piperade" is $11 for what can't be more than 50 cents of food. One scrambled egg, two pieces of white toast, and four bites of lettuce.  You will leave very hungry. In fact, the first thing I'm going to do when I leave is... go out to breakfast.

The piperade, which sounds like a big feature based on the name of the dish, is one teaspoon of pickled onion and pepper that was gross and ruined both the eggs and the lettuce. The terrible value would be more palatable if the food were amazing, but the dish wasn't even enjoyable.

Bottom line: they're not making anything you can't make, and they're charging 20-25X what it would cost to do it yourself. 

Time to go find some breakfast :/

I had a bad experience consigning here. Once my consignment period was over I called to give them a 24 hour notice that I would be coming in to collect my unsold items so that they would have time to prepare them. I picked up the bag they had waiting for me, took it home and found there were about 10 items missing that were not accounted for either through sales or through being returned to me. I called the store about 20 minutes before close that day, but no one answered the phone. 

When I later went into the store with a list of the missing items, the woman working said that she hadn't been able to find all of my items before leaving for the day and had left a note for the other staff to look for the items and they seemingly ignored it.  she was gracious enough to suggest that I look through the racks myself to see if I could find my items. I spent almost an hour, without any assistance from her, and eventually found all but one of my items. 

I found the entire experience disorganized and unprofessional. I will never consign here again.

This place made me feel like I might need to re-take kindergarten math because the numbers just weren't adding up.  There were 2 customers in the whole store (us and someone returning something) and 3 employees.  This means, only one set of people were actually in the market to buy a $100 pair of jeans (that would be us, thanks for following along).  3 employees, and we had to ask them to get us a fitting room, they didn't offer to help find any sizes and just sat around and talked while we dug through sizes for 20 minutes.  They were out of common sizes in many of the jeans.  Not that anyone offered to look in the back for us or anything.  We ended up buying nothing, no surprise.  3 + 2 = $0.

The fried chicken and gf waffles were a delicious treat. The server was overly eager and rushed. The atmosphere was vanilla and suburban. The host tried to make us leave our table and sit at the bar after we'd been seated and served coffee. She did offer to pay for our coffees, but it was a poor trade for a downgrade in seating, so I declined. Our 2 breakfast orders took 45 minutes to get served. As good as the food was, I won't go back for the mediocre overall experience.

I've only been to BJs 3xs ever. Never had an issue but today I wasn't too happy. Perhaps they they had an off day. Everything I ordered came back wrong. The churros didn't have cinnamon and sugar... so it was bland fried bread, I ordered sweet potato fries as a substitute to regular fries and I was charged a full side order. The hamburger was cold by the time it came to me. Just not a good experience. I was so annoyed I didn't say anything to the waiter because honestly it would take too much energy. I just know I won't return here.

My friend and I had a reservation here for breakfast and it's a very different type of process...One that Disney must be testing for future quick service restaurants but I truly hope that doesn't become the norm. It's clunky, confusing, impersonal, no bueno. You have to have a reservation for breakfast, then you check in once, check in again, are given a rose so they can find your table (now this was the cool piece of the meal), pick your meal from a computer, then go find a seat. The whole process was confusing and wasn't explained to us nor were we offered help. We didn't know if we could sit anywhere, we didn't know we had to grab our own drinks, ugh to the whole thing!

This all made my dining partner a bit crabby first thing in the morning which wasn't fun. Breakfast is $26 each, no cheaper options for people like me who can't eat a lot...and we just were not impressed at all. No character interactions to justify the price. And the food wasn't amazing. We tried the breakfast sandwich and Feast A La Gaston. They actually brought us a platter of pastries to start out our meal which we picked at a bit but couldn't find any we loved. The feast a la gaston includes scrambled Eggs, Herb-Roasted Potatoes, Apple Smoked Bacon, and Sausage served with Fresh Fruit and a selection of pastries. The breakfast sandwich was open face with poached Eggs, Applewood Bacon, Brie Cheese, and Arugula on a Croissant served with Fresh Fruit. Everything was fine but just wasn't worth our confusion or the price. 

The dining rooms are very cool though decorated with various Beauty and the Beast themes. I recommend exploring the entire castle!

 I'd like go back at some point for the lunch and dinner but it'll need to be with someone new because my best bud said he'll never go back again! Wah wahhhhh.

I went here at the suggestion of a friend. Great atmosphere and lots to look at. Good music and feel. I found the service horrible though. Took about 10-15 Minutes just to get someone to ask if I wanted something. Then when I ordered a margarita it took a while came with no lime etc. (I did see some others had them), and the bartender said something about  my drink being "a well drink from a gun." Really? I've never heard of that and it's a red flag for me that I'm getting all mix, which it was. Also you tip a bartender depending on the service you get and a drink that requires no mixing or anything makes it hard to justify tipping especially when it takes a while just to get their attention. I also heard the guy next to me complaining about the portions of his meal and that they left out part of his order. Said he had come there for years and never seen such small portions. Although, I had no food, I have little incentive to order with bad service, drinks with no alcohol, and portions that leave me hungry. Maybe it's for the regulars. disappointing...

Heard some negatives from Japanese friends and positives from American friends. The Japanese friend's were right. I am biased having lived nearly a decade in Tokyo, but the best thing was the edamame. I really was looking for some good ramen and since iti s called "noodles" was hoping I had found the place. I was wrong. The ramen was horrible - could make better instant ramen at home - although the toppings they put on the ramen were actually quite good. I had thinly cut steak which was delicous. Everyone else thought the sushi was pretty decent. Actually, most annoying thing about the restaurant was that they had valet parking that actually parked my car right in front of the restaurant - the same spot I pulled into and all he did was turn my car around... Not sure what the Atlanta love affair with valet parking is, but definitely wasn't necessary here.... Won't be back (but not cause of the valet - because the noodle suck).

Seeing as how the prices start at around 9 dollars for a burger you would think it's going to be great, well, that wasn't the experience unfortunately.

I ordered a chorizo burger and it's supposed to have spicy mayo but honestly it tasted the same as store mayo.  The burger was just a tad overburnt as well.  I also ordered a kale slaw and it was a pile of bland slaw and slivers of kale.  I even asked for pepper just to make it somewhat edible.

The decor is quite fabulous and reminds me of an art museum.  I just wish the food was good, overall it's style over substance.

First impressionsimpressions weren't that great. I came with my brother and my step mom. It wasn't so busy, they wanted to seat us by the door I asked about seats away from the door and the hostess said they were all full. 

I saw an empty table in the middle where the cherry blossom tree was. Actually, there were a few empty tables. I don't know if they were reserved or the hostess was lazy.

It took awhile for us to order. Food took awhile to come. My step mom's miso and Sunoco came shortly after we order, my main and her main came 10 mins later. We had to ask about my brother's Osaka combo. 

Food is alright. On par with all the other sushi joints in the neighborhood. I probably won't return.

I was excited to walk my lab/collie Starbuck from Hill and Memorial to this park so that he could spend some long-delayed quality time running around with other doggies. We were met at the entrance by a membership registration table that was quite frankly unhelpful. We learned that were were expected to have proof of vaccination (vet records) on hand, and fill out registration paperwork (the stapled corner suggested at least two or more pages), that we could not take home with us to fill out and was not available online (it's 2019, what gives?). Two stars because the park looks nice (from the other side of the fence), but the lack of a sufficient system to complete the required registration from home, something that even the most basic kennel has nowadays, is absurd.

If its a warm, sunny morning in Union Square, I'd love to be on the tiny patch of grass abutting Bloc 11.  They serve what I consider to be the perfect cup of coffee (dark roast that isn't simply torched and then watered down) and I love the staff (Hi, Steve!)

HOWEVER...

A perfect cafe these things do not make.  

Not being a sweets person, I don't jump for joy at the sight of pastries, muffins or donuts and being a blood-thirsty animal "lover", I don't care if they're vegan or soaked in pigs blood for that matter.  If I'm going to treat myself in the morning, I crave the perfect breakfast sandwich.

To sum up the bloc 11 sammich: Flavorless, unseasoned, overcooked, CRUMBLY eggs on focaccia bread that absolutely cannot hold up to it.  You CANNOT eat this sandwich on the go and frankly, you can't eat it at a table, either.  Ham cannot save this sandwich and even the default cheddar cheese just sits there.  It cools and becomes firm almost immediately because the bread is hardly toasted.  May I suggest an orange, melty and somewhat salty Gloucester Cheddar?

In my business, if you can't cook eggs, you shouldn't be cooking at all.

Bring me a sandwich I can eat without having to pack a fork (or a net to catch all of the eggy bits jumping ship) I'll change my review.  

Oh, and talk about overpriced wifi!  Go to the Sherman Cafe, instead.

This place was a recommendation by the UBC student I was chatting with on the ride from Seattle to Vancouver.  I like to incorporate the local flavor to my touristy vacays as much as I can, so of course, I looked for a Tim Hortons so I could try it out.

This place wasn't what I was expecting.  It was kind of like a new and clean low-end place, like a gas station you stop at in the middle of the night on the way to where you're going.  The coffee is pricey, not very strong, and not memorable at all.  Doughnuts were cheap, a dozen minis for $2 something.  Doughnuts weren't spectacular, but better than the coffee.  No  need to say so, because their logo says it...but for good measure, all these places are 24 hours, so students study there.  Think Starbucks meets gas station mini-mart.  Weird right??

A while back, I read an article called "Cheap Steaks" listing the non-steakhouse restaurants with a cheap, but good, steak on the menu.  Brick was listed as selling a baseball cut steak and loaded potato casserole.  

My husband chose the steak, but substituted mac and cheese for the side.  His steak was really good and cooked perfectly to medium.  He didn't have a steak knife, but had no trouble cutting it with his butter knife.  

I chose the Big Fat Italian burger with brussels sprouts for the side.  I was really surprised at the sprouts.  They were fried and sauteed with onions and bacon (I avoided the onions) and lightly dressed with an orangey vinaigrette.  The sauce balanced the bitter sprouts with some sweetness.  I thought the burger was good, but not great.  It had some nice flavor with salami, tomato sauce, and banana peppers and it was moist.  I liked how the bun had a toasted, buttery, garlic flavor.  

My husband convinced me to share two of the mini cheesecakes for dessert (I didn't need much convincing).  One was bacon and chocolate and the other was plain with berry and chocolate sauce.  Each was about 4 inches in diameter.  One would have been enough, really.  He liked the plain one with berries better than the bacon one; the bacon was weirdly chewy.  I thought they were both rather bad.  The cheesecake itself had a gummy texture that was worse on the outside and top.  Nothing like cheesecake should taste like.  I would not order them again and do not plan on helping eat the leftovers.  They didn't taste good enough to warrant the calories.  Overall, I thought the main meal part of the dinner was fine, but not enough to go out of our way to eat there again.

I went here about a week ago it was around 4:20pm. They close a 5pm. I wanted the sandwich with Turkey and avocado. Well at this time I was informed they could not make sandwiches or pizzas because they already turned off the machines for those but they could make me a wrap with the same stuff as the sandwich. I got that and it was mediocre. I think the hot sandwich would of been better but I'll never know. Had way too much onion, over powered the wrap. It was extremely small. Only thing I liked was the bacon(Of course). Overall the guy taking my order was rude and pretty much wanted to get out of there it seemed like. I'll take a pass on this place next time.

We used to love this place but they slowly started to lose their quality. The final straw was 3 days before my wedding day (after two other questionable visits). I had made a manicure and pedicure appointment for my wife and I about a month prior. When we came in for the appointment, they said I only made an appointment for one person. I showed them my email confirmation showing two people and they essentially said they couldn't honor the email because someone failed to write it down in there calendar and they had a 'large' group coming soon. After a lot of back and forth, they said they could squeeze us both in in about 30 minutes. We agreed because we didn't have time to find another salon and we knew they typically did a good job with nails. Our nails turned out fine but their service was dreadful. I don't go to salons often but when I do it is a treat to myself and this salon felt like a punishment.

Business is Business. That's what I have to keep reminding myself when I see the Einstein Bagels signage plastered over what only last year were my favorite Kettlemans and Noah's locations across PDX. Einstein Bagel's has gone on to close 3 area restaurants after acquiring the two above local chains. As with any corporate take-over, the independent local vibe these bagels joints had is now exchanged for a boring and banal interior. At any rate, this location, close to campus offers cheap eats for the student body, and there is seating conducive to cracking open the books. The boiled bagels that were popular at Kettlemans and Noahs are long gone (save 3). Granted, Einstein has expanded sandwich offerings with a variety of deli style lunch options. All and all this place was what I would expect from a corporate bagel chain, so in that sense it was fine. But I'm left grumbling at the fact that these guys swallowed up my favorite local bagel spots and now offer what I'd argue is an inferior bagel experience. Grumble. Grumble.

Some of the food is good, but the service is just ok. They're snobs in a lot of ways, no reservations, no accommodations for allergies or dietary restrictions, the wine selection is super limited, the waiters are smug and the food is hit or miss. This was my third time there, it likely will be my last.

Ordered the Orinoco salad, which had chicken that was chewy and dry. The Portobello arepas were good. The Jardinara was a little dry and the steak came with like a sauce which had fish (or something similar) and it was definitely not medium-rare like we ordered. Meh.

It tells you quite a bit about a restaurant when the dinner menu says "$7 minimum per person"!! Will have to find another place that makes good arepas :/

I was really excited to try Taqueria after all the raves of yelpers and friends, I was really excited to read all the great descriptions of their unique tacos on their menu, a little too excited I guess...boy was I disappointed after eating there. 
Now I can handle bad service and long lines(with out my 4 year old son anyway) but that was not my reason for a two star review. The food was not great, really not even good... at all.
We ordered 4 different types of  tacos, the salsa trio, and a cheese dip and the only thing that was somewhat good were the chips! The idea is good, the execution, in my opinion, bad.

It might just be this location. I've been to Walmart stores in other states/cities, and this one is not the best. Some employees are rude, clientele are rude, and I cannot seem to have an enjoyable experience here. I usually come here for cleaning supplies if I'm running low.

Now I just go to Target and spend a little more on things that I need. It's better than being snapped at all the time when coming to this store. Not a huge fan, and I won't be coming back.

Deviating a bit from the Chinesebites.com Signature Dishes Tour, we were invited to try out a new Japanese-fusion restaurant in Yaletown, KiBo.  I was joined by Romina, Rick, Grace, Alvin, Kevin, and Sherman for an intimate tasting of their dishes.

A few of us also ordered drinks.  I found the drinks to be quite sweet to taste and not that interesting.

We started off the evening with garlic toast served with negitoro ($8), which was served with toast.  The negitoro was pretty standard and was heavy on sesame oil, green onion, and tobiko. 

We sampled the Kibo set, a platter of three types of sashimi ($24). Each one had their own sauces on them already.  I enjoyed the tuna since it was fairly light on the sauce, but did not like the heavy seaweed taste on the salmon.  The fish seemed to be fairly fresh.

The beef carpaccio ($9) was a weird combination of parmesan cheese and wasabi dressing.  I didn't enjoy it because the cheese was too heavy, covering the beef itself.  The kibo salad with tuna, mango ($13) was also unexciting for me, especially since I had quite a decent mango salad the evening prior at Indochine.  I disliked the dressing, and this unfortunately seemed to be a recurring theme throughout the meal for me.

We tried a variety of aburi kibo sushi set ($17).  I sampled the salmon and the scallop, both of which weren't bad. 

The chikuwa cheese ($6), which is essentially Japanese fish cake stuffed with cheese them deep-fried, was alright.  Not sure what the cheese inside was, as it was not stringy (and hence not mozzarella).  The Japanese short ribs ($7) were pretty good and not tough at all. I liked the grilled taste of them.

Any meal would not be complete without bacon; we sampled the ebi bacon ($9) -- skewers of prawns wrapped in bacon.  These seemed to be grilled and was pretty good.  The bacon wasn't crispy, but that was alright since the prawn itself was crunchy.
 
The hamilton roll ($14) was essentially a dynamite roll topped with a variety of sashimi.  By this time I was already really full due to prior froyo consumption.  The volcano roll ($12) was pretty different from the other rolls since it was deep-fried.  I thought this was pretty interesting.

The caterpillar roll ($12) was also of the dynamite variety, except topped with unagi and avocado.  The Philadelphia roll ($12) with salmon and cream cheese was not bad.  I'm not huge on cream cheese in rolls, or rolls for that matter actually.

The marinated sablefish ($14) was quite good and soft.  It wasn't overly oily despite being an oily fish, and I really liked this dish.  At $14, this was well-priced.
 
The kibo beef ($15) itself was good and not thought at all, but I really disliked the sauce.  We wondered how the rack of lamb ($16) was Japanese because it was cooked with mustard seeds and cumin. Not to mention lamb isn't really a Japanese thing.  I only had a bite of it, but I thought it was a bit overcooked to my taste.  I like lamb quite rare.

To end the meal, I thought we were being served green tea, but it was actually soup.  A really delicious soup.  The seafood dobin ($10) tasted like a beautiful umami combination of shiitake essence, with clams, fish, scallops, and prawns.  It was really tasty and probably the most enjoyable part of the meal.

Before coming into this which wich, i was debating between this and taco bell.

Walking in, i assumed that offering a sandwich wouldn't be that difficult. I was wrong. They have definitely over complicated the sandwich ordering game. You grab a brown bag with whatever meat you want then mark off what you want on it.

I decided on the Philly cheese steak because i love philly's. I added provolone, banana peppers, onions, crushed red, and mayo. I was disappointed because this sandwich was 0% spicy when that's what i really wanted. 

The sandwich was pretty alright at best. Lacked flavor and the bread was very crumbley. Comparable size to a 6in sub from subway. But for $9 for a sandwich and drink is dumb! 

The place was clean and the people were friendly but i still can't get over that their motto is superior sandwiches and this sandwich was alright at best. 

Step up your sandwich game which wich.

I can't comment on the food, because we left before eating here.  We came to have a meal and conversation with some old friends, but after we sat down, we discovered that Taverna is not so much a restaurant as it is a Greek-themed circus that serves food.  The inside of the place was mostly filled with with parties of 15 people or so who were all yelling at the top of their lungs.  We opted to sit in the glassed-in patio, hoping it would be more quiet.  It wasn't much more quiet than inside, because the restaurant blasts really loud, over-amped, distorted music throughout the place.  The clownish waiters run around yelling OPAH!, lighting cheese on fire, and throwing napkins in the air.  I've traveled extensively in Greece, and I can tell you that I've never seen anything remotely like this in any restaurant in Greece.  Greeks would never eat in a place like this.

We were there at 7PM, and it was already chaotic.  I can only imagine what it would be like later in the evening.  If this is the kind of silliness that appeals to you, go and enjoy.  If you want an authentic Greek meal that you can eat in a grown-up restaurant, look elsewhere.

I really want to write a good review for this place, or at least, a better one.

This was the first place in Austin that I've seen carrying the Hangar One Vodka line, of which, I am a huge fan. So when I walked in and saw my favorites sitting on the top shelf of the bar, I was immediately excited.

Unfortunately, what I received with my drink order... wasn't Hangar One Kaffir. I'm not sure what it was. It could have been well, or Tito's, I'm not sure. It simply wasn't what I ordered. The two other people with me didn't get what they ordered either. A Hangar One Buddha was... again maybe well, but clearly not what was ordered. An order of Crown Royal somehow magically turned into Patron Silver...

In the wait staffs defense, it is damn loud in this place, really, really loud. A normal conversation at a table is hard to keep up, so mistaking an order could be rather easy. Also, when the mistakes were pointed out, the situation was quickly solved. Good job on that, honestly, I had hope again.

The menu is a bit overwhelming. Lots of choices, and paragraphs describing each piece. It was super hard to choose, lots of the food looked good.

I went with the special of the night which were lamb sliders, and the scallops which were wrapped in bacon and bazil.

The scallops were good, not great, but a cool concept.

The lamb sliders were overcooked, dry, and served on a piece of bread about three times the size of the lamb. Super sad panda.

In the end, I'll probably go there for the huge bar selection. It was also dead at 7:30 on a Friday night, not the best of signs. 

The whole place feels dated, big time, which it can't be because of the building it's in, that's basically brand new. The plates are unattractive, the chairs are uncomfortable. Paper napkins are a bit sad at the price level and atmosphere.

I'll give it another try, but the first impression, as my friend would say "It was not readied."

The entire experience as a whole, was 2 1/2, maybe 3. I began by calling Mary, and her business to set up a surprise Spa Party for my friends going through a breakup. Everything seemed fine, until the actual day of the party, she came, was on time, (had her son assist in bringing equipment which I wish I was privy to earlier) after that, my front door was left open multiple times upon set up and breaking down equipment, this allowed one of my cats to almost escape. Not a huge deal, I looked it over, I know there was a lot of equipment and it was heavy. The equipment scratched my hardwood floors, again not the worst, but irritating and I took note of it. After this she did inform me that they would be doing mini facials, after I had already only requested two treatments to keep my costs down, I thought that was very nice. Things slowly just went downhill from there. Upon arrival she said she forgot her extension cords, so one foot bath (these were both just store bought machines, not even the same ones) so one foot bath has warm water and bubbles, and the other had just hot water form my sink (I wish someone would've informed me they'd need to use that) after the water became cold, that was it. I do not own a microwave, they couldn't really heat up their stones. So by this time I'm fairly just annoyed, but I'm still going forward with services because why not. Two of my friends start off with the foot baths, two of us start with the massage. This is what was truly just irritating and disgusting to be quite honest. I had Mary, deep tissue, it felt amazing. What I did not enjoy was the singing, the story of her husband leaving her when my best friend was just broken up with, I'm paying you to provide a nice, quiet, ambiance for my friends and I. And then she began coughing on me as she was massaging me and not once stopped to wash her hands, or even apologize for literally hacking all over me. It was disgusting. Once again, I looked it over and bit my tongue, this was a day for my friend to be relaxed. She then proceeded to tell me she forget her essential oil kit, and I said I had mine she could use. Throughout the remainder of the sessions she CONSTANTLY put down my oils that I had so kindly let her use throughout the spa treatment she failed to be prepared more. This is was changed my mind completely to be honest, the fact she consistently said hers were better, better grade, whatever, you shouldn't have left yours at your place of business and then ask to use mine only to put them down, it was rude and very unprofessional. After that she attempted to push her DoTerra oils onto me and my friends by giving us samples and catalogs and by saying that 'Can you smell the richness, and the difference) it was again just rude and I was done by this time. Finally everything was done. I wanted just them to be gone to be honest, and then she sat down, called her son to come get them, and then sat and waited, this again was rude because you shouldn't be in my home when everything is done, and just unprofessional once again. She then asked the group where she should go eat, on the phone she very obviously said 'We're going out tonight' after I handed her the payment. Tactless in my opinion, why blatantly just be rude and ignorant as you're still in your clients home? Upon breakdown, once again her son left my door wide open for my cats to potentially run out. The second lady wasn't all bad, I did not get a massage by her so I cannot honestly review her performance. Mary seemed to bark at her a few times throughout the process, if she wasn't finished when she was and what not. She was quiet which is what I would've preferred from the other. I couldn't wait to get her out of the house. I also wish they would have uniforms or some type of united-ness or professional look. They were very casual, and to be honest Mary was a little larger than what I felt was comfortable to be moving and hanging over me. I felt a little closed in when should lean over me. The total services came to $466 I gave her $500, and asked for no change. I feel I should have tipped less. I would use the service again, but not form Mary, and I'd be much more frugal and specific with my orders. I'm not pleased at all, but I'm sure other people have been or else they wouldn't be in business. I'd just be careful with this business, I feel it could go either way and my experience just turned out to be horrible.

I've given 2 stars because we did have an outstanding server - Jeremy F. - who did his best to recover for the entire restaurant experience. In short, we will never return. Here's the recap:

Dinner Reservation at 9:30pm on 2/14/15 (yes, I know it was Valentine's Day- all the more reason for this restaurant to have been prepared). 

We arrived via Uber at 9:25pm - it's a good thing. They offer valet but apparently it's around the block and there were grumblings about this. 

Hostess was polite enough, checked us in and said it would be a few minutes before they could seat us. She offered us a menu and said we could wait at the bar -- lol!

Ok, so I'm looking around for the bar and realized she meant the make shift "cluster" bar they attempted to establish. 2 high top tables backed up to a counter with a trough/well on top for ice. I question the validity of food safety on that. 

Anyways, the bartender's back was to us the entire time - she never asked to take our order. We were
Seated at 10:02pm- still no drinks--
At the "chef's table" facing the open kitchen.  Server greeted us almost
Immediately and brought water. We ordered 2 aperitifs + 2 appetizers. Appetizers were delivered and complete before I complained about our drinks. At 10:28pm, we finally received our cocktails. It's obvious bar was understaffed and not having a worker friendly station - a real bar- Is also wasted time. 

We ordered dinner. I had the kale Caesar - which was fantastic and the steak - lovely. My husband ordered the duck - smallest portion of duck ever and we wonder if it was something ordered in bulk from say Sysco. 

Poor wine selection although we did settle on a bottle of Pinot noir for dinner. 

As the restaurant began winding down the kitchen staff began to get a little lax. Meaning, I watched the kitchen staff eating and or drinking various things in front of us! Remember, we were sat at the fancy "chef table." For the untrained eye, it probably wouldn't matter-- however, I've worked in the industry before and eating where food is prepared/cooked is a hazard.  

We went on to order dessert, after dinner drinks and have conversation with Jeremy about the restaurant because in the 2.5 hours we were there - no table touch from a manager. He listened well and made apologies as best he could. 

It was pretty disappointing to pay $$$$ prices for a 2 star experience. If you turned the lights up in the restaurant and really looked around -- it's a diner at best.

The food was delicious i really enjoyed the Bay wings and fish tacos. The service was ok however i ordered 3 HOUSE shots of tequila when i got my check it came up to be $48 for 3 shots. When our server came back i asked the server she said " patron is the house tequila here " I'm no bartender nor alcohol connoisseur but i 1) know those were not shots of Parton and 2) Patron is not your HOUSE tequila! They say they open at 3 however was not open until 3:15. Overall the food was good but everything else needs major improvement. If you go be patient and prepared to have some issue. 

Our high hopes was shot down. I will never go back !

We had a party of 15.  It was pre booked and the had a week notice.  Quality of food was good but the service was severely lacking.  It can be described as Slow, slow,slow.  We started at 7:30pm and they served our last dish 10:15pm.  Excuse that they had a big party just show up is not an excuse if we were pre booked!  Wow!  Reading the other reviews here you would think upper management would do something.  I attend this party as a guest and I hope our party host received some compensation for the poor service.  Oh well guess we'll find another closed restaurant soon.  #ripbucca

Not sure what Lamberts is supposed to be.  As a barbecue restaurant it is only fair, and Austin has other places that are far superior.  It is located in an old building, which means nothing, except that during our dinner the AC dripped on one member of our party. We brought this to the attention of the waitress and finally the manager. Their excuse was that the building was old! We asked to be moved but were told they didn't have another space? They brought out a mop and mopped the condensation during the rest of our dinner! Clearly, they realize they have a problem, but don't seem to care.  The food was OK, but not special.  When you say barbecue to a Texan we have high expectations. Lamberts falls short. It seems to appeal to a lot of people from out of town who don't know any better.  If you are looking for good Texas barbecue, or food in general. then keep looking, it isn't hard to find in Austin.  If you want a drink and music, maybe Lamberts fits your bill?

I've always heard great things about this place. Good quality and great portions for the price you pay. And with this beginning weekend of September, I heard there was a special 50% off for a couple of days. 

So, I decided why not go ahead and try the place out?

Went there and looked at the menu real quick. I decided to order a regular portion of the house special with rice. It was only then did I find out that the 50% off only applied to certain items. I definitely admit that it was partially my fault for not noticing that detail, but then again they could've just made that clear on their promotion. 

Waited for a while and got my order. To my surprise, I got fries instead when I definitely know I said rice. Then when I looked at my wings, they were boneless instead of bone-in. I know these might seem like nit-picky issues for some people. But why offer choices when you're not even going to get them right? 

The wings themselves were alright. Good flavor, sizeable portion. One major criticism is the crispiness. I wouldn't know the wings were "fried" unless you told me. Tasted grilled if anything. 

Overall, probably won't come back again. Though I can understand why some people enjoy it. The day I came was maybe an off day.

The store was nice. Ok selection on regular size shoes. Abysmal selection of 15s. It is a outlet store after all. My issue was with the people at the front end though. While ringing me up I asked the clerk what the price rang up for a pair of sneaks he just rang up. Instead of scrolling on the mobile register he 're rang the item. I ok'd the price then I figured he would delete the second entry. When prompted for my card I handed it to him then asked about the total. Well he had already swiped my card and charged me twice for a pair of $90 kicks. Then a person I assumed was the manager assured me the total wouldn't end up on my card while returning the item charged incorrectly. I knew my card would charge me the full amount then refund the $90 at a later date which it did/has. Essentially putting that $90 in limbo for who knows how long. My advice here would be to hang on to your card until you've verified what they will be chargjng and make sure it is accurate. The initial error was obvious and I just assumed the clerk would right it with out specific direction. I was wrong which in the end is really my own fault. Next time I'll visit niketown.

So this is tough. It amazes me, when a company you believe in and support as an online entity only, decides to open up an 'antiquated' brick and morter store, and they take such drastic steps backwards in customer service and you have to think if it is worth going elsewhere from now on.

I have been purchasing clothing from Indochino since 2013. I have purchased I believe 8 suits and 10-12 shirts. to say I like their fit, choices, quality, etc is obvious. so why the negative review? I have spend in excess of $5,000 on clothing with them

Until 6 months ago, I have always done everything through the website. Take my measurements, submit them. design and customize, order, and receive. I have had to have things tailored a little after the fact, which I did with a local tailor I trust very much (see my other reviews)

So what changed?

My sister is getting married, and her Husband to be wanted suits from Indochino. Great! But I had to go into the store to order it, and get the accurate pricing, I couldnt do it online.

This is where the first issue happened.
I was measured, ordered, etc. all fine. 
I customized the suit to my liking, as Indochino allows. I talked with my future brother in law, to make sure what I was doing was ok - he was on board. I would match, but be able to customize a suit i would end up using for work after the wedding. 
Well the suit came in, and it was not customized as I desired. and as I ordered. When I called indochino, the girl said she had to change my customization, because she reached out to the Groom, and he said to. I called him, and he refuted her story. he was fine with what I did, and never spoke with her. She LIED to me, and took it upon herself to customize the suit. When I said I wanted a new one made to my specifications, she refused

ok, upset. it happens

Fast forward to the past three weeks. I ordered another suit, using the same measurements. I increased the jacket wrist measurement to fit my watch and cufflinks for french cuff shirts (yeah, first world problems). It came in a little bigger then expecting (I think they increased the diameter versus the circumference). No biggie, Customer Service said I could bring it to my own tailor and get reimbursed, or to the studio and have it fixed for free. Hindsite is 20/20, and I should have gone to my tailor even if paying.

I went to the studio to save money. was told 1-2 week turnaround. fine! I have a wedding this weekend (the 20th) and it was the 2nd of May), so worst case scenerio, 2 weeks I could pick up on the 16th when I had a day off.

then the issues pop up
1. The clerk helping me with new measurements wants to change this, that, etc. no, please just change what I am asking do not retailor.

2. I call on the 15th, since it has been two weeks, and I have not heard. no suit. they said it should be there on the 16th at 7pm. to late for me to pick it up, but ok. they said they would call and I would get an email when it was there. On the 16th, no call, no email

3. I called on Wed the 17th. time getting close. I called again. Girl on the phone said she would check on it, and call me back. no call. no email. no jacket.

4. i called again today. The guy on the phone said he would check. That he didnt know what tailor it was with, but it wasnt back (going on 2.5+ weeks now). He called around, and said 'hopefully' it might be there Friday the 19th - too late for the wedding of course.
He said they were busy, and busier then last year, so alterations can take 3-4 weeks

WHAT?!?!

to say I am frustrated is an understatement. To say it strains my belief in the company is an understatement. Having in person assistance in a brick and morter location has made the location WORSE, and has led to me getting product that is not how I want, not customized how i want, and left me very unhappy.

With a lot of other made to measure studios, both online and locally, it is hard to support a company that doesnt seem to want to support their customers or stand behind product. I have purchased product online with House of Bespoke with success, and with 9Tailors locally, and been happy. I guess I have to push any future business their way, since Indochino does not seem to value customers and proper service.

Ate hear Saturday evening. Good things first.... Hostess was attentive, we went to the bar to get a drink before out table was ready as we were early. Wine is reasonably priced.  All staff was really nice. Brought water and drinks as we needed them. 

Bad things... Our appetizer was a prosciutto and pear salad. Honestly it was pretty bland. We expected something on the pears but they were plain. It left us thinking with a bit more effort it would be something. For our main course we had the tagliatelle Bolognese and tortellini stuffed with cheese with pesto and chicken. For the tagliatelle the sauce was underwhelming and also very runny. The pasta was ok but I think based on the thickness it was more fettechini sized. The cheese tortellini was so plain. There was no much taste to the pasta. The chicken was very plain and just placed in a light pesto that it tasted like plain chicken. Wasn't happy. 

Our dessert we had the chocolate cake and creme brulee. The cake looked great but was low on taste. The creme brulee didn't have the correct consistency. It was like ricotta rather than smooth. 

Overall I'd rate the food 1 star.

As a consumer that has free will and the ability to make decisions we have to take some of the blame when it comes to making bad choices.  Most Americans do not have the slightest clue when it comes to making a good choice on a supplier of a must have utility.  Knowing the per cost of therms, kilowatts, etc is the most important detail.  If a supplier claims they can get you lower bills overall in comparison to your current supplier, that could be true but it requires work.  Most of these details are not readily shared anywhere when making this choice.  As a renter or an owner, if having to pay for electricity or gas to heat or power your home, take some time to understand your bill.  Call your local providers and ask customer service to explain the bill to you and what is necessary to know.  First talk with the major supplier of the utility.  Most of the time they would provide you with all the details you need.  Go online  and do some research.  Most often there is some sort of free website to gain details about utility providers and must know information provided by ex- employees of these companies, local government and npo's that want more information out there for the common consumer.  I.E Citizen's utility board, etc.  

Know that if having gas service you are charged per therm.  These rates rise and fall all the time.  Calling in and asking to be "locked into" this rate gives you 12 months at that rate.  Call in any time during that time period to make use of changes if the rate reduces.  Providers make money on you.  Your rate will only change if you call your service provider in a timely manner.  They will NOT undertake lowering your rate.  IGS requires a phone call to make changes.  Its an easy way for them to make money on your irresponsibility.  Imagine if after your first 12 months you do not call, they adjust it to whatever rate is available at their discretion and so forth.  Most consumers assume a lot of things; like that rates rise and fall and that it reflects on their bills.  NOT true.  At anytime you could be paying more or sometimes less than any of your neighbors.

When the sales person for IGS told my parents they could lower their Nicor bills they agreed and signed on.  The salesperson put them into some sort of "budget" system without explaining all the details or the fact about rising and falling rates.  Seniors tend to hear what they want, so when sales guy said "lower rates than Nicor" that's all my folks needed.  What IGS did was take the average number of therms used throughout the year and charge for that all year round.  Their claim is that it saves you money.  Call your local major utility provider to find out exactly how much you average in the summer versus winter.  These numbers are grossly different especially living in the Midwest.  Some years are colder and some warmer and you may not need that many therms but are being charged for them.  Imagine your neighbor is paying $50 dollars in the summer and your bills are over $200 year round.  With this in mind, say if its a very cold winter and would expect higher bills, according to Customer service since you are budgeted you would still only pay whats within your budget right?  I don't think so, at least that's not what I saw in looking at all of their monthly bills for a year.  There were rises  and falls in cost.  Some details are not clear and when calling customer service much information is not clearly shared.  There is a lot of bicker about what the major provider charges which is charged on top of the charge from IGS.  Which is why its important to understand your bill.  You know whats not cool..? When you type IGS Energy in Google and the first six or so entries are about ripoff reports or other websites where concerned Americans are bitching about service and unfair business practices.  I'm from Chicago.  One call to understand the bill with Nicor and I learned A LOT.  Three calls to IGS where one was useful but the other two were talking circles around me.  Realizing you have been overpaying for over two years hurts the heart and mind.  Also note that if you opt to stop services with a secondary provider it can take up to two billing periods or so they say.  They can continue to get your money at a high rate till the change back is made.  WTF right.

Another thing to keep in mind is the energy is still coming from the major supplier.  These major suppliers have options, pricing options, the same deals to save you money as the secondary suppliers do.  Also if you ever have any problems with service, you never work with IGS but are told to call customer service at the major provider.  Isn't that crazy? Other than collecting your money, what else is IGS doing for you???

Read my review once or twice.  If you like, contact me via Yelp and we can talk about it.  Hopefully I'll remember all of the information I learned in the last few days.  I would rate them a solid 2.5 stars if I could.

I found this place to be more expensive than it's worth.  I'm no stranger to high prices for small plates, but there's usually something special that stands out about them.  We started with queso fundido, which was tasty and of a decent size.  We ordered two dishes:  Pastel Azteca and Tinga Poblana.  The former was unique and tasty, but could have used some more spices to kick up the flavor more.  The Tinga Poblana, I'm afraid, was a very poor dish.  It was basically a small portion of pulled pork in a watery tomato stew with very little flavor.  $26 is far too expensive for that dish and it's the most regrettable purchase I can remember in recent history.  I tried two different drinks:  The Mezcalina is very, very tasty and I would recommend it; the El Naranjo Martini with tequila and mezcal was a decent martini, but nothing outstanding.  If I was to recommend this place at all, I'd have to say it's a good place to have drinks and an appetizer or two.

Unfortunately, I didn't have a good experience with Olla. I wanted to support a new business in Gastown so I gave them a try. I was disappointed with the flower arrangements they put together for my wedding.  One set of vines were so miniscule they only covered a quarter length of the wall.  I couldn't believe it.  If I had to do it over again, I should have gone to Flower Factory or some other well established flower shop. They didn't deliver what they promised and I would not recommend them to any bride.

Food was fine, probably 3 stars.  Service and pricing/menu was not good.  I can't help but get the feeling they are nickel and diming you on everything.  From the $2 chips and salsa to the additional $1 for charro beans even when it says beans included on the menu.  I think a la cart and giving options to the customer is a good thing, but at least tell the customer when they will be charged for something when it says it's included on the menu.  At least ice in my water and extra napkins were free.

I enrolled my 5 month old puppy "Charlie" for basic obedience with Tara based on her yelp reviews.

Our first surprise the first day of class was the fact that Tara was not the trainer and it was a lady named Lisa. We don't think she has the skills or sufficient training experience to teach a class. She was always reading a paper to see how to explain the 3-4 commands for each class. We asked her a couple of times on how to address certain issues with our puppy and her answer was let me ask Tara or Savannah how to resolve the issue. In two occasions the shed where the class was held had a horrible smell due to the fact that they keep dogs in kennels there and how know how often the kennels were clean.

My wife and I decided not to finish the basic program, we didn't even go to the last class.

I wish we could experience Tara's experience and that's what you are paying for and not for an apprentice or somebody that doesn't have the knowledge to teach the class. Lisa is a nice person don't take me wrong but lacks of experience and knowledge.

If you enroll to train your dog here, make sure Tara is the trainer, we feel that we paid for something that was completed different of what Training by Tara offers and we wasted our money there.

"On Oster, On Waring, On Hamilton Beach..."

There is the occasional frijole, grain of rice, or scrap of vegetable that narrowly escapes the clutches of the blender, but they are few and far between.  Don't bother looking for the meat, because they are still chasing it through the woods behind the restaurant.  I think if there ever would be a market for Taco Smoothies, this place wouldn't have to change any of their food prep to add them to the menu.

The place is really not that bad, it's just that the food barely passes for, well, food.  And, when you peel back the wrapper and open the tortilla, no matter what you thought you had ordered, the guts inside are pretty much all the same mushy goo of ingredients.

When it comes right down to it, all the Yum! Brands franchises are very much the same in terms of quality and satisfaction.  You eat there because it's fast and convenient, not necssarily because it's good.  I shouldn't take it out just on this location, but it's the closest one to my house.

Don't let appearances fool you here, friends: waterfront view, modern decor and an open sushi bar so you can see all the fancy methods the chefs have up their sleeves; it's all a delightful show that, sadly, didn't translate to the food. 
To be fair, 2 orders of rolls does not a complete review make. However, both were enough to leave me feeling unsatisfied.
My date & I, still full from an earlier meal, ordered the Oshi Salmon Sushi (as per everyone's reviews) & the Crunchy Surf & Turf Roll. 
The Oshi Salmon sushi is the clear favourite here, as theyve got boxes of them behind the counter partially prepared, waiting to be blowtorched. And it was good... But I dont know if it was good on its own, or because we were so disappointed in the other roll that the Oshi was good only in comparison.
The Crunchy Surf & Turf roll was a HUGE disappointment. It was so bland and boring, I may as well have been eating plain sushi rice, that had a bit of crunchy tempura batter sprinkled on it. We hinted our disappointment to our server, who didnt seem incredibly interested in our dissatisfaction. 
Dont know if Id come back here, there's definitely better sushi to be had elsewhere, especially in Vancouver.

Wok on Fire would normally get 3 stars from me simply because of lack of any decent competition here in south Austin, however I'm giving them 2 stars because their customer service and attitude in general is crap.  I've been there more often than not simply because of proximity.  I've never had a disastrous experience with Wok but they're certainly not impressing me and again their employees seem more bothered with the fact that they have to work than with helping you.  I admit I've been spoiled coming from San Francisco where there are great Chinese restaurants seemingly on every corner.  It seems to me that here in Austin people feel the need to cater to multiple genres of food.  A lot of places like to combine Thai, Vietnamese, Chinese and even Japanese cuisines all under one roof.  This is funny to me because they usually can't even get one thing right, let alone multiple cuisines.  And I'm not talking about fusion here, I'm talking about having Pad Thai, Pho Ga, sushi and General Tso's chicken all on the same menu.  I guess for what the options are, this place is all right...

Very nice displays and great selection.

The prices are WAAAAYYYYY to high. I'm not one to come down on businesses about prices, but it's ridiculous.  The only time I shop there is when a 40% or more sale goes on which brings their prices to normal!

Also, I have been steered wrong several times. I got two ocellaris clownfish and asked what anemone they would host, I was steered towards a bubble tip...After months of them not having anything to do with it I researched and found it's the carpet anemone that they'll host and they'll rarely host a bubble tip!  

The worst misguidance I received was a while back when I got a large hermit crab. I specifically asked if it would harm my feather dusters and the employee said "no"...well...it ate my feather dusters within days!!!! I took him back and told the manager who said that there was no way one of his employees would have said that the crab wouldn't harm my dusters...so the guy pretty much called me a liar....hasn't he heard the phrase "the customer is always right"? He did exchange the crab for something else, but my feather dusters were a loss. I guess thats better than nothing...

So, inexperienced staff & high prices are my complaints.

Going to college in Boulder, cheap, late night food is always near to the top of the priority list for nights on the hill. Being one of the places that stays open pretty late into the night / early into the morning, Tra Ling's is often the first choice. I usually get fried rice, orange chicken, or general tso's chicken, and it is always pretty good, nice and hot, flavorful, plentiful, the way Chinese food should be. However, bear in mind that 98% of the times that I've dined at this establishment, I've been at least a little bit drunk, and good drunk  food is a lot different than good food. Looking back, their entrees are decent, definitely some of the best Chinese food you can find in Boulder, but that doesn't really account for the fact that the morning after eating Tra Ling's, you get the 'Oh, god, probably should not have eaten that last night' heavy, greasy feeling in the pit of your stomach.

We went to G'Vanni's in Billerica for dinner because we bought a coupon through Buy With Me.  We recently moved to the area and are trying to test out the local restaurants.  Overall, the food was just okay and we will most likely not be going back.

We started with a Caesar salad and their version of mozzarella sticks.  The salad was very good with fresh Parmesan and the size was huge.  This was actually the best part of the meal.  Their mozzarella sticks are more of a mozzarella sandwich (mozzarella between Texas toast) and it was just so-so.  It was pretty bland, I felt like it needed salt.  It was served with red sauce which was pretty good.

For dinner, we got the pumpkin ravioli and shrimps & clams in white sauce.  The pumpkin filling in the ravioli was really good, but the butter sage sauce was bland (again, maybe salt would have helped?).  The seafood was cooked well and tasted fresh, but the white sauce was bland and tasted like plain oil and butter.  Again, the portions were huge and we each took half our dish home.

Overall, the food was just okay.  The bright spot was our server, who was very sweet and attentive.  But unfortunately the food was not worth a return trip.

Such a great, relaxing spot! Great food, n friendly owners, only problem after they talked about the wine from Italy, they insisted on us tasting some grappa, so we did thinking since we just bought 2 flights n a $50 bottle the grappa they insisted upon wouldn't show up on our bill, well, when the check came, both grappas were on it, and they weren't even good! It was upsetting to have the owners insist on grappa n then order & charge it without telling us it was not comped! Otherwise good food but owners should be respectful if they are leading the customer down a expensive path!

My roommate and I are renting an apartment from Miller Properties for the coming year. We explicitly said that we needed a new place as close to July 1 as possible and they initially said they'd have one July 15.
