Then they said they'd only have one August 5 (they told us this two days before we're supposed to move out of our current place). The delay is annoying, sure, but it's more that they lied about it that makes me angry. Like, just be straight with me. I like the leasing agent that I worked with and he seemed genuinely interested in helping us find something in the meantime but I would have preferred it if he had been honest with me from the beginning. Or at least to understand why it happened. I hope that this does not continue when we actually live at Miller, but I'm prepared if it does.

Moshi has been on my "restaurants I want to try" list for a really long time, so my hopes were pretty high.  Maybe too high.  The initial impression was good, as the tiny restaurant has interesting art and fixtures, and the glasses are neat, but it went downhill from there.

Mostly, the food here is just overpriced.  My wife and I paid more than $36 for five little pieces of nigiri, three unusually small rolls, and two bowls of miso soup.  At most sushi places, when you order a combo, as I did today, you get both miso soup and salad, but here you have to choose.  I had to pay $2.50 extra for my wife's soup, even though the two rolls she ordered were more expensive than my combo.

The food ranged from average to no good at all.  My nigiri tasted almost exactly like it does at every sushi place from Columbus to the West Coast to Tokyo, which is to say, good.  My wife said her banana roll had no flavor and was like "mush," but added her O-H-I-O roll was good.  I was hungry again less than two hours later, and I'm a light eater.

But I'm not coming back here.  Not when Akai Hana, Mr. Sushi, Edamame, Tensuke Express, etc. etc., are all in the same city.

So my review is from the POV of the tables in the back of the restaurant, not the circular belt bar seating area. I have a feeling many stars were lost in translation for this review based on geography of your table. 

You fill out a card saying what you'd like. Prices were fair and the food was good. It just took SO. EFFING. LONG. First of all, we went here because we were legit hungry, not peckish. We waited maybe 10 minutes to be seated. Then another 10 minutes to have a drink order taken. Then another 10-15 to have our orders taken, only to realize (from the other table not attached to the bar) you take your card to the chefs who compile your order. After eating, the check was slow and the cashout process was slow too. 

How was the food? Fine. How were the prices? Fine, great, even! But for experience, I can def imagine a more on-the-ball place existing. Not in a hurry to go back. Oh and we walked here from Ground Kontrol, so it's a viable option for pre- or post- gaming sessions. 

They take cards. I don't know if there was a minimum. But they sell candy up by the registers. People were friendly, just slow.

The staff here are so lifeless and rude, it's frustrating!!! I say this because there aren't many other immediate options. So to put up with this staff's dirty looks and personalities is NOT the way I want to start my morning. Most people who eat from here are employees of the building upstairs which houses about 5 different companies which I assume is why they stay in business. Otherwise, the food is OKAY. Typical sandwiches, soups, literally a last minute stop if you've forgotten to bring in food or something.

This Starbucks is loud and small and very uncomfortable to relax at. I'm used to a very nice environment to study in and could not find that here. The wireless internet is slow and laggy even when just using a search engine such as Google. Don't bother watching YouTube videos or listening to podcasts because it takes literally an hour for streaming content to load. They also didn't have all the ingredients for a special that they just started advertising and making, so I left disappointed.

Wow so disappointed in this place. When I first moved to Orlando I wanted to find a Korean restaurant that could satisfy my cravings whenever I felt homesick for my mom's home cooked Korean meals (and love of course) and this place ruined it for me. The food is far from good. I ordered spicy beef soup with greens and all that came out was spicy broth and literally one small piece of beef off the bone and scraps of greens. The service is even worse, no one knows what they are talking about and you have to call them over for them to notice that you need refills. Also they know nothing about the menu. Given that most of them are not Korean I don't expect them to know everything about the menu, but as an employee they should know basic information to share with customers trying Korean food for the first time. Anyhow, never going back.

I have visited this restaurant for lunch and dinner. The lunch buffet was just ok. Nothing special to distinguish it from a lunch of higher quality at Memories of India. 

My dinner experience left a lot to be desired. There were two people working at 5:30pm (typical dining time). It took over 30 mins to get a samosa appetizer and we were left waiting for drink refills throughout the entire meal. Unlike there indian restaurants there were no "indian chips and salsa" served prior to the meal. 

Service was very slow, the rice was very gummy, and the food was edible but not good. Next time I will stick with Memories of India for Indian food. 

If you're looking for good Indian food, great service and a Restaurant close in proximity go to Memories of India.

I must agree with the reviewer who wondered , "Do any of the people who give Central Sq. 5-star reviews actually live here?" I am thinking that as well, because I certainly don't get the charmingly bo-ho, Williamsburg-y feel they get. Perhaps things just look prettier from far away ...

Take it from someone who has the misfortune of waiting until their lease ends, so they can move out of the smelly crotch of Cambridge: there is very little "charm" in the scabby bum who sleeps in front of 7/11 and once prominently displayed his own fecal matter for passersby. There is very little charm here at all, just a lot of crappy post-war housing with faulty plumbing and a whole lotta bum fights.

Now I've lived in a city, so I'm not some frightened country bumpkin in her first apartment. I'm used to Philadelphia (also known as both Killadelphia and Filthadelphia) but for God's sake, parts of Central Sq. make Philly look like the Hamptons. It's the amount of dirt and garbage that lines the sidewalks (I'm not sure where it all comes from) and the crowds of loud, crushing people--homeless and otherwise; again, not sure where they all come from--and the fact that during the summer, it smells like rotting milk and human feces. At first, it was appealing, like a miniature Mission tucked away in Cambridge, Land of the Ivory Tower and Hemp Pants. But really, I think it's just a dump, masquerading as a very hip place to live. It's similar to being Amy Winehouse: for a few seconds, it sounds great, but after that, you realize it's just a receptacle for crack-cocaine and insanity.

The pros, and the reason it gets two stars, are the fantastic ethnic eateries within a two-block radius. There are some great cheap eats (Moody's Falafel is the cat's pajamas ... the cat's falafel ... the shwarma's pajamas?) And I love the produce at Harvest Co-op. I'm also of the opinion it's generally a safe area. There is a police station literally off Mass Ave. I was only threatened with grievous bodily harm once, and I think it was by an Emerson student. But at the cost of having to deal with some of the most unpleasant homeless people in existence? (They're honestly disgusting. See also: the time that lady proceeded to eat her own leg scabs at the #1 bus stop.) Or what about the time that I stepped on a bloody maxi pad? The ridiculous apartment housing costs, for pretty shite living conditions? 

Nay. This bitch is moving to Brookline. Deep down, I too am a yuppie Jew. I'm done with the fauxhemian life.

(11/4/2019) I came by for a very late dinner, still plenty of cars in the drive thru. Order was taken efficiently.  The lanes are def tight.  There's 2 lanes, side by side, and then merge to one lane for the pay and pickup windows.  The turn is obviously so tight that it looks like plenty of people tag the wall on the way in.  Food was piping hot when I got it. The McRib was sloppily thrown in the box (see photo), my Happy Meal came without the sauce I asked.  It's in a convenient location.

We came here on a lazy Saturday afternoon, looking for intoxicating drinks and good food. We ended up sitting on the patio which was very nice. Our waiter was friendly and prompt and he let us know about the happy hour menu, which is what we used to order our food and drinks. I must say the drinks were good and my husband enjoyed his saki, but the food failed to impress. We ordered a sushi roll, pot stickers and the margarita flatbread. I don't do sushi, but my husband didn't like his roll. I've only had steamed pot stickers and these were deep fried. They just didn't taste right to me, but my husband thought they were pretty good so maybe I just prefer them steamed. The margarita flatbread was by far the biggest disappointment. It tasted like something I could make at home with store bought frozen pizza dough and Kraft cheese. Eventhough the drinks and service were good, I get hungry when I drink so Kona you're not the place for me.

Two stars for good food! Lack of the others based off of a few awful customer service experiences. When calling in a to go order, on multiple occasions they have put me on hold and forgot to come back to answer the phone. This is especially annoying since  their version of hold is putting the phone on the counter so you can hear them talk to other customers. 

On another occasion, my boyfriends order took an hour instead of 20 min like they said. They really need to do something about their output problems.

I was very excited to experience this restaurant -- I came here with my fiance for a romantic dinner. The decor is rustic -- lots of stuff on the walls, seems reminiscent of the old "Public Houses" of Europe, but with white tablecloths and wine glasses on each table. Seems like it started out country but then changed its mind and became fancy.

That, however, was where the fancy stopped; this was mostly to do with service. Our server, Joseph (a young man in his late 20's), seemed to know about as much about the menu as we did -- right from the initial greet he was stuttering and soft spoken. He went into the hors d'oeuvres specials, seeming as though he was asking us about them ("It's a lobster macaroni and cheese? Served in a carafe? Big enough to share?") My fiance asked for a beer recommendation for the steak; he seemed as if he had never been asked that question before, and stammered that he would go and ask the chef. I requested a wine recommendation as well, and he once again stammered (questioningly) a wine which was delicious if only he had recommended it with confidence. I felt nervous about ordering it because HE was nervous about me ordering it. 
About halfway through our hors d'oeuvres, the server finally asked if we wanted our wine and beer right now, or with the meal. This was around 30-35 minutes after being sat. Halfway through our hors d'oeuvres, and around 15 minutes after we had given our entree order to the server, he came up and rather tactlessly informed us about the entree specials AFTER WE HAD ALREADY ORDERED. Kind of like an "oh....and if you wanted to order this....sorry..."

To start, we ordered the escargot and the onion soup. The escargot was simply seasoned, but the sauce was great -- similar to another reviewer, I too dipped the bread in the sauce because I really enjoyed it. The onion soup was AMAZING: I actually tipped it to get the last of the soup out because I didn't want to waste any. I ordered a glass of the German Selbach Reisling, which was delicious and went with everything I ordered; my fiance ordered the Durkel, a dark German beer that he raved went perfectly with his New York Strip steak. 

For our entrees, as mentioned before me fiance ordered the New York Strip steak medium rare -- he was obsessed with the au gratin potatoes, and we both agreed that the carrots were cooked wonderfully. The steak left a bit to be desired -- then again, obviously this isn't a steak place, but the cut of strip did not seem to be the best, with a lot of fat and a bit tough. We both wished that the pepper sauce had a bit more kick to it, but it was very good as well! Another suggestion for the service -- when the steak arrived, Joseph then stated, "let me go get you a steak knife." Three minutes later, he arrived with it. Since this restaurant brags a fine-dining feel, having to stare at a delicious-looking, hot steak for three minutes not being able to cut into it seems a bit amateur. I won't eat until he can, so why not have the steak knife as a pre-drop, so both of us aren't watching our hot food become cold while you get him the proper utensil to eat it with? I ordered the coq au vin, and it was GREAT -- one of my favorite dishes to order, and the reason why I came here. My chicken was cooked perfectly, the sauce and mushrooms were great, it was the highlight of my evening. The coq au vin and the food are the reason for the two stars that I did give

We did decide to order an additional side of the truffle fries, just to see what they tasted like and they did not come out with the meals. I reminded the server about them, at his first (credit given: diligent) check-back: he informed me he would get them immediately. 20 minutes later, he checked back with us twice and informed us they were coming -- 25 minutes later, we were finished and asked for them to be cancelled. 

I ordered the creme brulee for dessert. I also ordered a cup of coffee. The coffee was delivered, and it was then that the server asked if I would like cream and sugar. I replied with the affirmative. My creme brulee arrived (with only one spoon for a couple....thank goodness my fiance didn't want any), and I reminded the server about my cream and sugar -- once again an item getting cold and untouched because of the server's inability to plan ahead for his Guests.

The flaws in service were ignored at the time because I will not let a bad server destroy my romantic evening. I definitely think that Joseph should be put through some additional training (wine/beer knowledge, food knowledge, and maybe a serving class) and next time in order to receive a better, classier experience I may request one of the older more experienced servers. The steak was nothing to write home about, but everything else was great and I would definitely eat here again if not to try more items on the menu. Especially my truffle fries, which I was looking forward to trying but then never received.

Had a similar experience to another post on here visited this restaurant yesterday, a Tuesday night in January where it was not overly busy in the main dining area and was seated out in the closed in patio area right under a blower that was blowing cold air on us. It was freezing server came over and watched us put on our jackets and say it was cold. After trying to bare it we finally asked to move to a high top table to warm up. I had the salmon burger and French fries not long after eating I developed a terrible stomach ache. Very unimpressed with this place and will not be returning.

Pros: 
-This place has a really cool ambiance and decor. 
-The vibe and the whole place really comes together well. 
-As far as food, the fried mozzarella appetizer and salads were good. 
-Hostess greeted and sat us promptly. 

Cons: 
-The place was slightly hard to find, but not impossible. 
-Our server seemed as if she had a chip on her shoulder and was semi snooty. Not sure what that was all about. The place wasn't all that busy, so I doubt it was because she was overwhelmed. 
-The pizza was slightly better than alright. Mostly bland (I had Margarita and one of my other friends had one with peppers and sausage.) Again, both bland and not worth the price.

Overall, for what you're paying you're better off finding someplace with tasty flavorful pizza.

Exasperating.

This isn't a coin laundry. You have to buy a stupid card. You can't buy the laundry card with a credit card, you need two $1 bills. Then this $2 isn't even loaded on your card. If you want to top up with a credit card it won't let you choose the amount, it's like $10, $20, $40.  We came with a bunch of quarters but you can't load value on the card with coins. And there didn't seem to be an ATM inside. We eventually found a $5 bill and then the wash was $4.50.

So overall for 1 wash this cost us $7. We went here  because we were going to get some things from Assembly square and it was the closest. Certainly won't be going back. Maybe if you live in the area and can load $20 on the card (which gives you a $5 credit) it might be worth it. But still more expensive than elsewhere and the machines weren't awesome.

Unimpressed.

So my experience was not soo good. Waited a really long time,  almost 4 hours for a table and only did it because it was friends birthday. Later in the evening about 7pm, they were turning people away because they could not accommodate. We ordered drinks from the bar downstairs and hung-out outside....for a really long time. 
The food was okay, (not worth the wait) we waited another hour+ for food. I ordered the catfish for appetizer, came out soft and salty, questions the freshness, not going to lie, tasted like it was microwaved. I tried my best to be reserve because it's a new establishment, but there's a lot of work that needs to be done. There was no flow, no service. The service team needs work, as well as the kitchen. The looks on everyone's face, "where's my food!".
The parking was terrible. Pay $10 for parking in the back or get a ticket parking in the front. We tried to get our money back when we found out about the 3hr wait, the attendant said he informed us about the wait-which he did not because we would not have stayed.....but we decided to stay anyways.

The positive was that Kandi and Todd were very friendly and we got to meet them and theirs friends. I think they have the support from the community, they just need to tweek the rest. Maybe have some outside professionals come to evaluate and provide recommendations to fix and improve. This is a good place to be, but not if you are not getting service or food.

Good luck.

Can you say disappointment?  I've been to this location many times, and it's never been disappointing.  Sure, the food seems pretty meh to me, but the good company and decent service usually makes up for it.

Wish I could say the same for the last time I was here. Even the best company couldn't save this visit because of the awful service -- err, I mean, no service.

Granted, we came in on a late night -- Thursday, just after midnight, to be exact.  But isn't one of the selling points of this place round-the-clock service?  Well, what they don't tell you is you get no service if you come in then.

Me and the date were seated promptly, but it all went downhill from there.  It took us at least 5 minutes to see our server, and then at least 10 more minutes for him to come back with our drinks.  Speaking of, the fella I was with ordered a sweet tea, and they said they didn't have any sweet tea.  SURELY YOU JEST.  So, the Mr. had a chocolate milk; me a water.  And yes, 10 MINUTES.

We couldn't decide if we wanted an appetizer or dessert, but fortunately (or unfortunately) we had plenty of time to figure that out.  We never saw our server again.  I mean, we did, but he was tending to every other nearby table except ours.  On the bright side (if there is one), I learned that I have the power of turning invisible at Kerbey Lane.  Oh, that's not an advantage?  Darn!

After a few more minutes of trying to be patient and understanding, me and the Mr. decided to get scooting.  He was waiting for our server to return so he could pay for the milk.  I looked at the menu, saw it was $1.97, told him to leave a couple bucks on the table, and said "Let's roll".

Pity we left our server a three cent tip.  That seemed far excessive.  And turns out, the fella I was with said his chocolate milk wasn't really tasty.

Kerbey Lane, y'all did FANTASTIC that night.  For those who have trouble reading sarcasm, that was sarcasm.

So, you've been warned.

I brought my bridesmaid dress here, based on great reviews of their wedding alterations. My dress was way too long, and ever so slightly too big in the waist, and way too big in the bust. She refused to take in the top, saying it wasn't possible (I assume because there is pleating on the bodice) and told me she would move a bone that ran up the side to run up the center of the bust so that it would conform to my shape. In actuality it looks slightly worse, and the gapping still exists. She did do a good job on the hemming, however, which was pricey at $45. I just felt like it was laziness that prevented her from doing the job properly on the bodice. I'm very disappointed! She was nice and I wanted to trust her, but my dress looks like crap.

It's OK.... I guess. 

But, it's those old 1990s style "outlets" the 20th century building construction booms came up with to make cash fast off of corporate brands... only they no longer have discounted pricing like back in the day. 

They have a Sephora, but it's not exactly an outdoor mall. In order to get around, because walking isn't always safe, you often need to drive from one place to the other which wastes gasoline. It also seems to be extra bad in winter because it seems extra windy there in the winter months, and very cold. 

Honestly, I DO NOT understand the allure of shopping here. It makes more sense to drive 1 exit over to the Hanover Mall which has free benches, and air-conditioning as well as heated in the winter, and its easy to walk from place to place after walking, with excellent security, and very kid friendly... But, this place doesn't have that. 

It's also really strange that when I speak to people, locally, about whether they shop here or the mall more often they usually say here. But, when I ask them why, and point out all the issues with it, they seem perplexed because it's actually true, and they don't know why they shop HERE more often, and it makes no sense.

Pros: nice area of town. Okay atmosphere. Sometimes good pastries?

Cons: unfriendly staff. Overpriced. Poor customer service. Pastries are a hit-and-miss. 

Review: my husband and I have tried this place a few times over the last couple of years and I think tonight was the last time. We walked in and the place was dead. Not one person in the restaurant. That's ok, maybe it was just a slow night. The guy greeted us with about as much energy as Ben Stein. Two cups of black coffee and two pastries were around $15.  I've never had dinner her but I won't be going back to try it out.

If you like trying to check in 30 minutes early and finally getting your room about 45 minutes after it's suppose to be ready - than this is your place.   Walked up to the front desk to speak with the staff and was quickly shuffled over to a self check in computer.  Then 1/2 way through that process was told the room still wasn't ready.  Come back later.  Nice bar though.   Good thing.  Looks like I'll be sitting at it for some time to come.

Pretty disappointing food and service...

Service:

We went around 8:30 and they had already shut down patio which made us feel unwelcome at the get go. While we waited for our food, we saw almost 10 people that were turned away or turned off from coming in because it was almost 9, which is when they close (super early considering it is next to a university). They continued to close up the entire time while we were having our dinner, which made us feel awkward and rushed to get out, again, even though it wasn't even 9 pm yet. 

Food:

The food was pretty lousy. I order the Japanese flavors with noodles, tofu and vegetables. Not much flavor at all in any of the components and not much food regardless. I'm not really sure how adding vegetables on top of the dish adds much considering one of the vegetables was a cole slaw. The cole slaw was actually decent on it's own, but it was really something I wanted to mix into my noodle bowl? My boyfriend got a kale salad on his and same thing, just sort of random for a topping. He ordered the chicken, which he barely touched because it was chewy and just generally unpleasant. 

Kind of a bummer since the concept is fine. 

Recommendations:

More sauce, more flavor, rethink arbitrary vegetable toppings, replace weird frozen chicken with real chicken strips, don't make patrons feel unwelcomed especially when you are still open.

This was our first time coming here for dinner. First and foremost, our server was great--no complaints there at all. The kitchen really needs some help, though. 

Long story short, it took 20 minutes (conservative estimate) after ordering for them to let us know they were out of the fish and chips two of us had ordered, at which point we had to order something else. I can understand coming back right after we ordered to let us know, but 20 minutes later?? We were promised 25% off our replacement entrees due to the wait, which was appreciated. Food arrived another 20 minutes after that. I ordered a medium steak, which arrived a textbook well-done. The server agreed it was beyond overcooked and removed it from our bill. When the bill came, the other replacement entrée wasn't 25% off, but we'd been there for over 2 hours at that point and were just ready to leave. We paid and walked out, then realized we forgot our leftovers on the table. We came back no longer than 2 minutes after leaving but they'd already thrown away the to-go boxes. That was mostly our fault, but it seems like they might wait 5 minutes or so to see if we came back...

Also, there is no kids menu at all. We had to pay for an adult entrée for our 3-year-old, who of course only ate about 20% of the meal. 

Again, our server was great and very apologetic about everything, but the kitchen was another story...

We have been going here for about a year and the rates have been ok for the limited amount of machines they have since this place is constantly busy. The basketball court is usually taken up by a lot of people playing games so your lucky if you can find time to shoot around. This I can deal with. 

  What I wasn't too happy about was the fact that we came to workout (my fiancé and I) and there were about 3 younger people working up front and one in the kids club. We took our 2 year old son to go play and the girl in the back said she only had room for one more. Great, that works out perfect. Not really. See, if you have a two year old they count it as two or three spaces not just one. She stated its because they need more "attention." You have a ton of games and toys, I can bet you money my son won't bother you for "attention" for one hour while I workout. You don't change them, or feed them so that comment seems irrelevant. 
  Anyway, I understand the person to child ratio but when she called to the front desk to ask for help they said they were all busy at the front desk. No, they were all talking and hanging out at the front desk. It's frustrating when you pay for a gym membership and for your child to go yet they fail to mention these details to you. Might as well go to LA Fitness now that they have childcare too.

We've given The Oasis two tries and were disappointed with both.  The place is unique and we really enjoyed walking around looking at the decor.  The view was nice even with Lake Travis being low.  The major problem is the food.  I can't even say it's so-so.  It's sad that the owners do nothing about even wanting to change the chefs they have.  I have read MANY comments about the food being bad, as well.  I guess because they are so busy on the weekends that's all they care about.  Well, they need to know that people are not flocking there for the food.  It's the view and sunsets.  If you picked that restaurant up and placed it some place else, it would go under.  They could have an even bigger gold mine if they served edible food.

We ordered delivery specifying that our pizza be cooked well-done. It arrived half-cooked. To its credit, Flying Saucer apologized and graciously sent out a new, properly cooked pizza. The low rating for this review results from the condescending attitude of the man who delivered our replacement pizza and who at the same time he acknowledged that we'd ordered a well-done pizza, admonished me that our first pizza had been cooked well-done according to Flying Saucer standards. Really? He took that back when I brought him the undercooked pizza and showed it to him. However, he then scolded that, in the future, it is my responsibility to order my pizza "well, well, well-done."  I would have laughed in his face, but I feared that if I got too close I'd catch his smugness. Badly done, Flying Saucer. If you screw up an order, just own it and move forward.

I really wanted to like PS Nails, after so many positive reviews I was excited to get my mani/pedi there. Unfortunately, I am deeply disappointed, and won't go there again. Yes, the place itself is clean and looks sanitary, and ladies there are nice and welcoming, and they do offer drinks.  
But, the person that did my nails deserve only one star. Pedicure was just OK, she scratched my foot when she was doing scrubbing, massage with hot tones -  nice feature, if only she did a better job doing the rest of the pedicure. She did lousy job on my manicure. while cleaning my cuticles, she was mostly throwing glances at the pedicure stations - for what? and therefore the nails did not look and feel "cleaned up" at all, when she put  nail polish she was not meticulous and went over the nail itself  and the nail polish was on my skin. CLeaning it with a brush with a nail polish remover didn't help much. The girl at the counter did try to offer a re-do, but I already spent an hour there, and was on a tight schedule so had to refuse. and why would I sacrifice my time for somebody's lack of professionalism or interest in just doing things right. 
I would like to believe that the other girls at the salon are more professional at what they do.  One additional star goes to the girl at the reception, she tried to be helpful.

If they say the wait is 20 minutes, that means an hour. Whatever time they tell you, triple that! Or quadtruple it. Heck, times it by 5. While waiting for our table, my mom and I sat at the bar and were ignored for half hour. Plenty of employees walking around and no one offered any service. We just wanted some drinks and chips while we waited. Had to flag down one of the bartenders to order after half hour. They had more employees in the bar area than customers and they were just talking amongst each other. The chips came out all wet from the oil and the salsas tasted rancid. The salsa came out warm as well which was kind of off putting with the oily wet chips. I went up to the host desk to ask how much longer the wait would be, and was told there were 6 parties in front of us. What?! How can that be after waiting half hour and being told 20 minutes half ago ago? Waited another half hour and I went up and asked how much longer the wait would be because we were thinking of leaving. She says Oh I can see you right now. WTF?! Weren't offered waters once we sat down and my mom and I knew it was gonna be another 5 hours before we see any food so we opted for EASY menu items- we both got soup and that was it. 20 minutes later, we get our food. The waitress was nice, but she kept forgetting things. Forgot my mom's Sprite refill, forgot to bring me water when I asked, forgot our togo containers (we took most of it home because it just was bland and figured to doctor it up later at home). Took forever to get our check. Super slow with everythingggg. We spent almost 2 hours here for two drinks and soup so plan to make a half day event ordeal if you decide to eat here.

Worst indian buffet I've had in Austin. And I've tried several around town like Bombay Bistro, Paradise Biryani Pointe, etc. You can definitely tell the rice, meat, dessert, and etc was old here. Also all of it was overly greasy and oily. Indian food usually is, but this was off the charts full of oil. I couldn't even finish my plate. I literally jus kept eating the salad they had. Waste of 10 bucks. Felt like I ate someones leftover 2 day old indian food. Even the naan was super chewy/stale. Also, my friend and I were the only people in there during lunch. Probably should've walked out when we saw that. Never going back.

We just left this place and Haley is NOT someone who should be cutting long hair!!
She's got attitude and totally ruined our son's long hairstyle.  Even after speaking to her she was adamant she doesn't have any attitude?!? I don't need a response to my direct disdain for your performance where I have to interrupt your craft and have another stylist complete and fix your absolute mess created!!! 
Caroline was nice enough to credit us for the haircut- Bonnie was gracious enough to fix the mess as nest she could... 
Unbelievable 
Will have to seriously reconsider recommending this place

I'm sure that this is akin to blasphemy, but I really do not care for Juan In a Million.  When it comes to Tex-Mex, I am very easy to please.  Throw some cheese, sour cream, chiles and cilantro on most anything, and I'll happily devour it.  We are soooo spoiled in Austin, because coming here from pretty much anywhere else in the world, our Tex-Mex joints blow everything else out of the water.  

Moving on...I have heard friends, tv shows, media, etc...praise Juan time and time again, so I feel kind of crazy not being able to agree, but I just think that...get ready...the Don Juan taco is gross.  Being from Atlanta, GA, I grew up on all things pork lard-infused, and DO love them, but pork lard in my tacos...no bueno.  Gotta draw the line somewhere.  Juan in a Million is the opposite of Curra's.  Curra's breakfast tacos are clean-tasting, bursting with flavor and let the ingredients stand on their own, whereas the Don Juan is like eating a garbage pail trainwreck.  

The only reason I give it 2 stars is because the Juan is so charming with his whole "i come to everyone's table!" schtick and the prices are really pretty amazing.  I truly couldn't finish even half of my $3 taco...but that's for other reasons.

I try to only leave positive reviews, but I just have to share on this one since cleanliness, not just quality, is a concern. I have been here twice. First visit got a pedicure and a gel manicure. The manicure peeled on two nails after only two days. I thought $65 for the service was a bit much for this area. I thought I'd give them another shot since they are so darn close to my house. This time I got a pedicure only. I did mention the gel manicure problem, but they didn't even apologize. Just said I should've come back when it happened. I told them I had to travel and didn't have time. No offer to do it again or even a discount. My pedicure is okay. Had to remove polish from my skin when I got home. The thing that bothered me the most is that after the tech put my dirty tools away she found some more skin she wanted to trim. So she grabbed some cuticle trimmers from the drawer behind her, used them, then wiped them on my towel and put them back in the same drawer without sanitizing them! That's scary. I won't be returning.

Blah. I can't tell you how man times I've been here and each time, just blah. I only go when we are asked by others and look at it as a social outing rather than a food outing. It is a good place to grab a beer and watch a game with friends. You're risking it to think the wings will be consistent though. We've had dry, wet, undercooked, overcooked, hard, pink... seriously. The Buffalo Wing Flatbread was the best thing going and they took it off the menu but if you ask nicely sometimes they'll make it for you.

After hearing positive comments about Toro Bravo, my boyfriend and I were truly looking forward to celebrating my birthday at this restaurant. For first impressions, the the ambience is appealing, space being limited and quaint, we opted to grab a drink next door while we waited for our table. The wait time was not anything ridiculous considering it was a Saturday evening (about 30-45 min), however, after being called for our table we realized the table we had waited close to an hour for, was a table lack thereof: we were seated next to the kitchen within a couple feet of the servers' pick-up window for all outgoing dishes. On any other visit this would not have been such a letdown, however we requested a nice table for our celebratory evening.

The hostess was nice enough to mark gluten free options on our menu for us, making the ordering process hassle-free. Considering we had never eaten here before, we were curious about portion sizes and how many tapas to order. Oddly our waitress seemed annoyed when we asked this. We ended up ordering the sautéed spinach and wrapped dates (both were very appetizing) along with some Spanish red wine. The raciones we ordered didn't take long to arrive either. Once the entrees arrived we were hoping to order another glass of wine, however, our waitress had disappeared since taking our order and never even checked in throughout the entirely of the meal. While we still had some food on our plates she asked if she could clear our plates several times, we definitely were clued into her attempt to move us along in order to bring another batch of customers to this "table." 

Considering the food was good, the atmosphere was welcoming (when not next to the kitchen), and service was lacking, we may not be able to justify a reason to revisit. Plenty of other good eats in Portland.

Four of us dined here on Wednesday, 02/25/15.  We went for the all-you-can-eat wings.

The good:  Our server, Daniel, was great.  He was polite, engaging and let us take a while to order since we all needed to catch up after having not seen each other in a while.  

The bad:  The kitchen.  We got our first order of wings in an acceptable amount of time.  The second order took nearly one hour to come out of the kitchen.  For a location advertising AYCE, you'd think the wings would be readily available.  The "Peanut Butter & Jelly" and "Thai Peanut" versions were not very good.  They were bland.  The Honey Garlic was nice.

The very bad:  The booth seating.  The hard wood benches are horrible.  Ask for a table where the chairs have some padding. 

It could have been so much better, and sadly it wasn't.

Ten Tables wasn't the best.  The annoying thing was that they made us wait for over an hour even though we had reservations.  So we ended up getting seated past nine pm in spite of an 8 pm reservation!  The food was pretty yummy but i've had better.  The wait was extremely annoying and by the time we got to order, they had run out of an entree and some desserts.  This place has a reputation for being "oh so good" but really, having exactly ten tables doesn't make you all that cute, although this place seems to think it is.  And apparently, they're too cheap to spring for a working AC because it was very warm in there and they only provided small glasses of room-temperature water seeped with some leaves.  My friend had raved about it but she herself was rather shocked at the sub-standard service which can only mean that this place is inconsistent.  Reservations does not a waiting table make and as a direct consequence, our menu was limited as well.  Not at all impressed, guys.

If you want to wax nostalgic about high school and do something merely because all the cool kids are doing it, then go to Stephanies on Newbury Street.  You can sit on the patio, feel like you're part of the "in" crowd, and along with everyone else on the patio, secretly be thinking about how terrible the food is.  To top things off, you can spend your hard-earned allowance on your overpriced food instead of on video games.   

In all seriousness, Stephanie's has a reputation for being a Bostonian staple for a great brunch spot, but after eating there, I think this reputation is highly undeserved.  Stephanie's has a great patio, but their food simply doesn't deliver.

Visited this weekend for the Barkhappy event. Great space, my friends raved about the drinks, there's one with pineapple cream and sailor jerry's which was a big hit and their cherry limeade sounded amazing. I feel bad reporting this because there's literally no way of verifying this, but I was getting a coke and a beer for a friend and I know I handed over a $20 because it was the only note I had, and the bartender gave me back a $1 and said I'd given a $5. Cash transactions are really hard to track, so I understand, but it was disappointing. However a fun space and the event was really successful.

This was my 2nd visit to Sweet Samba and have a big complaint - the service requested was not the service received. I had called in and reserved their version of a deep bikini. (As a side note, their waxing service menu is not as straightforward as it should be. Each style has cute names rather than clear distinctions.)

My service was excellent and painless. The aesthetician and I had such a good time chatting (I know some people prefer just to watch the overhead TV) that I wasn't really paying attention to what was or was not being waxed. For some waxing newbies, this may seem hard to believe, but I'm a veteran waxing customer and it just doesn't hurt anymore. I'm used to it and pain is a non-issue. Anyhoo...

Afterwards when I got to the desk to pay, my bill was more than expected. I told them I had asked for a deep bikini (The Barely Bare) but apparently had received the French Kiss (brazilian with a landing strip). I had the feeling there had been a little bait and switch. I know what I requested and was not happy that somehow there had been a miscommunication between the front desk reservation and what was told to the aesthetician. 

To sum up, the service is good & the place is cute but I do not like feeling like I had been tricked into an upgrade. My advice is to pay very close attention to the confusing waxing menu and be sure to reiterate to your aesthetician exactly what is being done so there will be no confusion.

I don't know if it was the hour long wait standing outside with my party of 5 or the cramped quarters and lack of elbow room we had at the table, but I didn't particularly care for Flying Biscuit. After hearing nothing but praise for this place I just knew it would be a hit with me and my guests. I think 1/5 of us had a meal they were just ecstatic about. I was told after the fact by one of the friends who had been shelling me propaganda about how good the biscuits were that I'd gone to the wrong one. She said I should have gone to the "other" Flying Biscuit. She even said that the biscuits at the one I went to were probably driven over from the one she prefers. This floored me. She couldn't have been serious...or was she?

We avoided any wait at all and had an early Thursday evening dinner at the Waterford location. We were warmly greeted and, based on the significant number of "full service" seats available, declined the absolute worst table in the restaurant that was first offered. Thankfully the hostess recovered nicely and seated us in a non-traffic area. 

Our server, Lisa, approached us with a smile and genuine greeting. She was a bright spot throughout the meal walking us (first timers) through the menu and checking on us unobtrusively 3 or 4 times. 

My burger was cooked exactly to order and was tasty. The "house made" pickle was a small but nice complement. My dining partner ordered the opened face "Mom's Sloppy Joe." She found it tasty as well. 

The downside...the food was not hot. My burger arrived "warm" but clearly (hopefully) not to the restaurant's standard. The bun had clearly not been warmed at all. And, the same was true for my friend's open face sandwich and our side of tater tots. Very disappointing.

All that said we concluded that, other than our server, the experience provided little compelling reason to visit anytime soon or to rate the dinner higher than a "2." And that number was driven by an excellent server. 

Don't be misled by the lines at the door. There are better options.

Great food. But the service in the bar here SUCKS. We've eaten here SEVERAL times and each time we vow not to go back. But their burger is awesome and we find we crave it. So we head back in, only to be disappointed by cranky bartenders and servers who literally throw our meal at us or roll their eyes. We're customers who are so easy to please too! Very frustrating experience but seems to be on par with many of the Portland restaurants these days. When did Portland become France, where you have to be mean to the servers to be treated with respect???

Honestly, the food here isn't that great and the service is lacking. We ordered two special big bowls of pho and fried egg rolls. Now I am not sure if it was just me but the pho noodles tasted a bit raw. The pho had a sticky hard texture and some of it were clumped together. The soup base was also a little heavier for my taste. Pho is suppose to be a healthy meal bit the soup was extremely oily.
I have to admit the food was served pretty quickly but if they just took some more time the food probably would've tasted better. 

Now the service, the waitresses all seemed out of it. We were sitting for a good ten minutes waiting to just order our food. The waitresses would come out to serve food and walk right back in the kitchen without looking around to see who needs servicing. Good thing the male waitor ( who seems to be the only one busting his @ss ) finally noticed us trying to get other waitresses attention and helped us. 

Now keep in mind I'm from New York, and there are plenty of Viet restaurants that will top this one.

I used to love this place.  My friends and I have always enjoyed the food, the wine and the great patio.  We went last night and everything has gone downhill.  The staff wasn't friendly or accommodating.  The service was barely mediocre.  We ordered a wine that they were out of, but instead of letting us pick another the waiter just brought a replacement, but it wasn't even the same kind of wine.  When we questioned it, she was rude.  However, we were happy to see that the menu had not changed, so we ordered our favorite salad and pizza. The food was nowhere near as good as it used to be.  We barely ate the pizza and I brought the leftovers home to my husband who eats anything and he thought it was disgusting.  The menu was had the same descriptions, but it tastes like they are using cheaper ingredients.  Sadly, this was our last time at The Grove. What a disappointment.  This place used to be our go to place for great food and great wine.

This a review by a vegetarian

I entered intending to get the happy hour $8 12" cheese pizza. But I saw they had ready made slices and after all the mediocre $3+ slices in this town, these $2.50pers looked pretty darn good. Well, they weren't. There a parmesean sprinkle or something on top of them and either that or a dried herb got seriously hard. At first I thought I'd caught an aberration but then it happened again. It felt like there are tiny little pellets of sand or rock on top of these.
It's a shame because the rest isn't half bad. But the only rock I eat willingly is salt so I'm not coming back.

One extra star for the sense that staff know the regulars.

Visited on a Saturday afternoon with my five y/o daughter. I don't understand why they have to text you when your table is ready, what's wrong with a pager like everyone else? Anyway, they first gave us a table in the "21 and over" area which is just dumb, so we had to wait a few more minutes for another table. Service was a little slow but the server was very friendly. 

I asked for just a regular cheeseburger with usual toppings, lettuce, tomato, ketchup, pickle. I got a burger with cheese and ketchup only! I asked for medium-well but the burger was medium-rare. By then I had waited so long (about 25 min) that I ate it instead of sending it back. Fries are good but nothing really special although I do like that you get unlimited fries. 

I may visit again but I think it's quite pricey for mediocre food and slow service.

Just came back yesterday from a spring break vacation trip with the family. We stayed here at StaySKY Suites, which also owns Lake Buena Vista Resort Village & Spa, so we thought this place should be good. 

When we checked in the guy at the front desk was Aaron, although he was just doing his job, he was not the most friendly guy. My wife has a disability due to her hip and I wanted to save her a trip from walking to the front desk and the guy would not allow us to check-in unless he saw her face, even though I had her driver's licenses and mine.

We stayed on the fourth floor, which was nice as we were very close to the elevator, which makes it easier for my wife. However, during our entire stay, we had to use the stairs about 90% of the time because the elevator is so extremely slow. My 7 and 4 year old son and I ran down the stairs and was always able to beat the elevator to the 1st floor and that is without it stopping in-between floors.

Overall, our room was nice and the beds were very comfortable. Unfortunately, one of the biggest problems we had at this hotel was that there is no hot water, only warm. (0 being cold, 10 being burning hot, it was about a 5-6). My wife was not happy about taking moderately warm showers. Internet... The hotel has free wifi, but it is very slow, less than 3MB download, and less than 2MB upload.

StaySKY offers free breakfast and like other reviewers say, it is nothing special. However, all of the ladies who handle the breakfast in the morning are outstanding, they do a fantastic job and were so very friendly and helpful. They were wonderful and are such hard workers, because this place gets very packed for breakfast. The first day I ate breakfast they had these powdered circle eggs and some nasty corn beef hash that gave me an upset stomach. On a positive note though, Saturday they have a very good breakfast, so if you stay here, definitely eat here on Saturday. They make freshly scrambled eggs and serve freshly cut ham, it was a total 180 compared to the other days.

Not to be so negative with my review, but during our stay the hotel lost its power for a minute or two and our hotel room door had a hard time opening. We had to literally hit the center of the door to get it to open, it kept sticking. We definitely had a lot of issues at this hotel, but I am glad we stayed here instead of their resort (Lake Buena Vista Resort Village & Spa) as one of their reviews say their truck got broken into. 

This hotel does also have a pool, it felt very nice and warm and they have a hot tub as well. Sadly, we did not get to use it though, but it was open. Also, if you need ICE, make sure you turn the ice maker on inside the hotel room, as the hotel charges for ice. There is no ice makers outside in the lobbies of the hotel.

The best thing about StaySKY is its location. It is very close to all the major destinations and the hotel is very affordable. When you visit Orlando, you will spend a lot of money, so you are better off getting an ok place to stay, so you have money to visit the overly expensive theme parks.

[Review #444] (29th Review of 2017)

Given the fact that there is only one review for GasWerks posted at this point I am assuming most of the Yelpers around here must have decent taste.  This is because GasWerks is an entirely tasteless bar, not worthy of one's time, especially if that time is coming on a weekend night (thursday included).  Young and trashy seems to be the theme here, but unfortunately not in the good way.

This is truly a Zero star place, but as you can see I gave it two stars.  Why, you ask?  Their happy hour.  None of the annoyance factor is there yet, and every bottle of beer in the place is $1.  Certain days even offer free pool on the large (non-bar) tables.  One trip here in broad daylight I stumbled across this discovery but my overall hatred of the place has yet to lead me back to take full advantage.

My wife and I were celebrating our 2nd year anniversary and decided to go to this place because of the way that it looked. We had always wanted to go and now had an excuse to go. I wish our curiousity didnt get the best of us. Our experience was horrible. 

There were 3 adults and 2 kids in our party and we were seated out side. The host that sat us was extremely helpful, but we sat for a while and 2 other parties were seated after us right next to us. They were served their appetizers before we even had gotten our drinks. Our dinner party turned into an endurance test. The other parties had already gotten their desserts before we had gotten our meals. HORRIBLE. 

Wife has a horrendous time, I was annoyed, and our anniversary ruined because of this hell hole! Food was great, thats why it gets 2 stars, but I recommend to anyone to get the food to go. Or better yet, go to Carraba's if you want a finer dining experience than this place. 

Will never go again, not even for take out.

Writing this review because I want this place to succeed as a place people go to get something healthy quick. I have eaten here a handful of times when it was VERTS and besides them taking some things I enjoyed off the menu, I had a usually good experience. Tonight I ordered using the noom app. I arrived to pick up my order 10 mom after it was supposed to be ready. I walked into a completely empty restaurant (around 7 pm) including no employees to be seen. I waiting for maybe two minutes until another customer walked in who seemed like they were friends of them employee working. She put some pita bread in the toaster for him, then acknowledge me (but not with a "hi welcome, sorry about the wait" or anything of that sort) I told her I had a pick up order. She looked around for it then started to make it. Again no "or sorry it's not ready yet, let me make that for you" just threw everything together and handed it to me. Again no apologies. Not until I asked her what her name was. Then she apologized. I was also excited to try the sweet potato hash, which did not end up in my bowl. Really disappointed in the customer service I received.

My boyfriend and I are vegan and are always excited to try new vegan places, so we were really disappointed by the food here. I want to support this place because the employees are really kind and there's a good vibe inside but the food is just so bad. I'm not sure how so many other people thought it was so great? 

We got the humble bao, tofu to you (which came to us barely warm), and ramen. The food came out too quickly to have been freshly cooked and was pretty bland to be honest. We saw reviews about the black forest cake and decided to give it a try but it literally tasted like a store bought cake - fake sugar frosting and no flavor. You just seem to be paying a lot for pre-boxed food that doesn't taste good. Super bummed and definitely would not recommend.

This used to be a 4-star venue but our last experience really soured things. My wife and I love to visit Boston. The ES in Waltham has been a a staple in our trips given its proximity to Cambridge and Downtown at a great price. We've never had any issues until our last visit.

Parking, which used to be free is now $15, which feels like overkill given that the hotel is in a pretty suburban area. That may have been a mandate from Hilton so I won't ding them too much on that. The problem arose when we had some pretty noisy occupants next door who  had kids running up and down their room, blasting music, yelling, and overall being very inconsiderate. When we called the Front Desk we were told that there was nothing they could do as "quiet" time starts at 10PM. 

Fine. When we got back from dinner and settled to bed we heard loud music playing at 11:30 at night (we have recorded proof). As soon as we called the front desk it all of a sudden stopped. We felt like the right thing to do there was to place us in another room rather than basically ask us to tough it out. We love Boston and the surrounding area, but we'll definitely look to book elsewhere next time we go back. Leaving it at 2-stars for the awesome breakfast.

I have never seen such a long line at any Dunkin Donuts! And this is with two cashiers working, and three staff behind them. I came in to grab a couple of donuts for my kids, and because it was my birthday, my free coffee. Well, unlike other establishments where your coffee is free (cough, Starbucks), adding almond milk means you WILL pay the up charge for it, even though it says free drink of your choice. Yes, it's only fifty cents, but it is the principle. The woman working the register was a little gruff, and yawned a few times while I was ordering, but who knows? She may have been there since dawn, and just ready to go home.  All in all, it took about fifteen minutes from start to finish. Not impressed. But the store looked clean, so I'll give them that.

Either way, next time I'll wait a few more minutes and visit another spot.

The first time I went to Palm Beach the employees were very rude but I decided to look past it because I loved the spray tan that I received. Eventually I bought a package and started going every week for spray tans. They were consistently good until about a week ago. My friend went a day before me go get a spray tan and they told her that the machine was not emptying out the entire cartridge and to come back tomorrow. Well I went the next day with her and my spray tan was noticeably not as dark and somewhat patchy compared to my previous ones. I went again today and the same thing happened. I'm pretty sure they never actually fixed the machine. On top of all of that, I really think they rip off their customers with all their different, confusing tanning packages. I pay $50 a month but I still end up paying $5 every time I go there for add ons. Doesn't make sense. They need to learn how to properly run a business.

Sadly this place has gone downhill. I used to love it, but my last few experiences have been less than positive. Went tonight (probably my last time) and the pho was not very tasty. There was hardly any broth and a big blob on noodles stuck together. The condiment bar/ veggies were not replenished. The seating area was dirty and the restaurant seemed very understaffed. Also, my friend tried to order shrimp spring rolls and was told they were out of shrimp- then someone who ordered after us had a full plate of shrimp spring rolls. I'm disappointed how the quality of food and service has gone down so dramatically.

We purchase two leather sofas and the Guardsman Gold Protection Plan. Our Leather sofa faded horribly and the seams are separating but Guardsman won't cover anything despite under their "gold" plan.The sofa is under three years old and the manufacturer has stopped producing them (most likely due to fabric issues).

This is completely joke of coverage. There is no reason to purchase this product. We have been loyal Haverty's customers for years but this experience is causing us to reconsider. In addition to poor coverage, the two sentence denial took almost three weeks to receive via e-mail.

I was directed to call their customer service to be told that they won't cover it or to view a sample plan which may or may not apply to my actual plan.I would rather spend my time advising others to avoid the disappointment that I have endured.

very dissapointed the menu has changed from whats online
the space is awesome but the prices were expensive and the service was AWFUL. Waited too long to get our order taken and too long to get our drinks and way too long to get our food and only a half hearted apology as we watched everyone else around us get served. One table even got 2 different orders of food while we waited for ours.  Happy hour was very dissapointing  food and drinks not very cheap, bacon fries ok, fried steak weird but the spinach goat cheese chicken salad was the best thing. Drinks were good too but there are so many places in portland that serve a good drink.   too bad the location is great but  i am not going to go back and cant reccomend  itto others and we really need good food and bars in st johns

We came here thinking we would get a decent meal while in the area visiting relatives. 

The food was decent for the price and location, however timing of food and service left a lot to be desired. 

Our appetizers were very poorly timed, and the rice came in under cooked.

Our service was barely acceptable with drinks going un refilled. When we ordered deserts 1 of our items came quickly and it wasn't until about 10 minutes later we were told out other item was not available. It amazes me that it took them that long to let us know. 

When we did finally reorder another desert it took another 15 minutes to get that dish. 

Overall I would not return unless I was at the mall.

I have been this place several times. But the the most recent one wasn't pleasant: 
Food was ok. Lamb skewers tasted good, but too little for the price. 
We also ordered big plate chicken, but we didn't see the dish, even we had waited 30mins after finishing all the other courses. They probably forgot our order, so we cancelled it. 

Extremely hot inside during this time, but temperature hot. They said AC is broken, but we customers had to endure the high temperatures.

So much hype, but the food just wasn't as I expected.  The service was terribly slow, but I can forgive that since it was the night of the ribbon cutting ceremony and they were packed.  But the food was "meh."  I ordered the chicken street tacos and it was nothing more than flavorless shredded chick in corn tortillas.  No limes, no avocado, no cilantro.  Very boring and uninventive.  The rice lacked flavor (in fact I put salsa on top to help it out).  Charro beans were good.  One of my friends ordered a salad and it took 15 minutes to get dressing for it.  Another friend ordered a chimichanga which he described as "OK" and same reaction from others regarding enchiladas and tacos.  So many fabulous Mexican and Tex-Mex restaurants in and around Atlanta, but this was just another average place. Disappointed.

Ordered a Khao Pad Krua Thai (basically Thai Fried Rice) for lunch, to go... My experience, aside from the food, was decent. The person on the phone was friendly and English-savvy, my food was ready on time and my pick-up and check-out was efficient. But... the food was terribly subpar. Fried rice is generally pretty hard to mess up... so I was really disappointed to find hunks of un-fried rice in my container. I mean, if you can't even make sure all the rice is fried....... Taste was also fairly mediocre; I agree with another review, this is basically food court quality. Not inedible, but you could do much better elsewhere.

Not good y'all, and I come from the home of Chik-fil-A. I gave that place up a long time ago after all the hate spewing.. Anyway...I stopped at Flyrite yesterday and ordered:
1. Chicken sandwich w fries & a chocolate chip cookie 
2. Chicken wrap w fries & the same cookie

First, the cashier and the woman prepping drinks must of had a beef Bc when I asked for straws from the non-cashier, she rolled her eyes at me and motioned to the cashier girl, implying the cashier girl should have given them to me. She basically implied the cashier girl was an idiot which I thought was rude. 

Second, I'm a cookie whore. I am fine with openly admitting it. Those cookies were a travesty!! $1 for a coaster sized cookie that tasted awful. If you can't get the glory of the chocolate chip cookie right, don't sell them!

Third, my boyfriend said the chicken sandwich was dry and bland. Sauce was good, but like sriricha mayo isn't ground breaking. My wrap was OK, but they put paper in the packaging and it stuck to the rice wrap so I had to eat the paper that wouldn't come off the wrap. Organic or not is prefer a chicken wrap hold the paper. BBQ sauce was tops though! For $22 though, I was pretty upset at how not good it was.

All in all, I'm super unimpressed... What I was hoping for was an answer to healthy fast food, what I got was a lot of boring, overpriced, dry, paper stuck food.

Maybe it's just getting its kinks out, but for now I'll "Fly Rite" past this place.

I went with some friends for Dim Sum as our weekend brunch once, probably will not go back.

The carts for Dim Sum got around okay, and the food ... some tasted fairly good, but the other tasted like your Asian market frozen food reheated. Also, I totally understand the hectic workload of the staff there but maybe - just maybe - the cashier did not have to be that rude when talking to us, when we took two minutes to figure out how to split our bill.

2 stars for the portion. Other than that... mediocre at best. I had ordered dinner for my girlfriend, her sister and myself. I had the pastrami. Wasn't bad. A little messy and the sauce overpowered the taste of the pastrami. But then again, I haven't had a decent pastrami since moving to the Boston area. GF had the Texas steak. Asked for the steak to be done medium rare. I'm no foodie, but my understanding of medium rare is a slight pink in the middle of the meat, not having the inside of the steak the same color as the outside. Supposedly was made with BBQ that neither one of us could taste. The Buffalo wings were flavorless until we added our own hot sauce to them.

2 stars for the portion. Other than that... meh.

The beer selection was great, but the food was mediocre. The crab cakes were not jumbo lump as claimed and they tasted like they came from a can. There was too much breading in the crab cakes also. The green beans were too salty. The tortilla soup and bacon and eggs appetizer were great. If I were to come back again, it would be purely for the beer selection and not so much the food. The service was slow, but the staff was friendly.

I went there with friends last night, with big expectations, and I have to say I was quite unimpressed. Maybe it's that Filipino food really doesn't appeal to me, but this is what it looks like: a little protein, a LOT of rice, and virtually no veggies. Oh, and very little in the way of spice. I imagine this is how the poor must eat in the Philippines, but we can do better here. And quite frankly, I encourage these guys to do better, otherwise they won't be here this time next year. Too many other good choices in this town.

this used to be one of my favourite breakfast spots in the area. however with the increase in price, that seems to mean there's a decrease in food quality. i used to come here when the breakfast special was $5 and done well. it's still pretty cheap ($6.29) but nowhere near as good as it was when it still came with a piece of fruit. super mangled and mushy hashbrowns, slightly undercooked sausages, and poor presentation. save your cash and walk up to Far Out and get their breakfast burrito instead.

Noodle Lab is located within Boston Public Market and the line was cray cray when I went (lunchtime), so my expectations were high.  Although I think they're build-your-own ramen style is different and they definitely have efficient service, the actual taste of the food was super average (if not below). 

I ordered their tonkatsu spicy miso broth with soft boiled egg, pork belly, and enoki mushrooms as my toppings.  The broth flavor was honestly comparable to cup noodle soup flavors with the blandest of kicks for spice :/  It felt similar to making your own late night ramen and tossing a bunch of random ingredients on top.  The toppings were average -- nothing to rave about.

It pains me to give their food one star (I feel so mean), but I'm generously giving two as a nod to their quickness because it really was amazing how fast they took care of such a long line.

I hate to disagree with the rest of the other Yelp reviews, but honestly, I've experienced better. Maybe it's because we ordered to go, so the two pasta dishes we ordered (spaghetti + meatballs and chicken parm) basically had no sauce. Sure they are generous with the pasta, but the meal was bland because of no sauce. Plus, the chicken parm pieces looked like they were filled with grease by the time we got back. We still ate some because we didn't want to waste the food, but it left us feeling sick for the night. Maybe the other Yelpers had better experience because they ate in the tiny restaurant, with the food served hot? 

I would be wary of spending $25+ again at Basta Pasta. It will probably take many moons before I will give this another try.

Ok, Garlic shrimp was amazing!  Hookah was great.  Customer Service....failed!!!!  I arrived and a young lady greeted me but i kindly let her know i wasn't ready yet....other guest came in and she greeted them and sat them.  I went outside, came back in 15min later and it was an older short man standing there (assuming he is the manager)  I say we are a party of 3.  He starts asking me questions like do u have a reservation, are we gonna have dinner...etc.  I stated the young lady that was here earlier did not ask those questions to other guest so why are you questioning me!!!  He didn't want to sit me and my friend Bc he needed all three and i stated that the 3rd person would arrive for desert.  After going back and forth....he ended up sitting us.  It felt like he was looking and talking about us the entire time.  I then look to my left and there is a man sitting alone at a 4 person table for at least 45min.l before his loud guest arrive.  But the manager wants to give me a problem and stare at us all nite long.  Not to mention the guest there were extremely loud and swearing but the manager said nothing to them, which he should have.  Almost everyone in there seemed upset about how loud they were.  Did NOT like that 1 bit.  Not to mention i came in December and had to complain to a staff member bc our food and hookah took FOREVER.  I'm done with this place.

2 stars based on take out. Ordered from gourmet garden in beverly tonight and now will always take the extra drive vs. Coming to the one in danvers. We always order the same food and each time I get my chicken lettuce wraps I get a smaller and smaller portion. I literally got 3 times as much at the Beverly location. My husband ordered General Gso chicken and got double the amount as well. If you're going to come here, eat at their resteraunt.  Food is good, and in person good portions. They really need to re look their take out!

Extremely disappointed. I was excited about a plant based meal service but some meals were missing ingredients and the dishes were so bland and dry. We ended up throwing them away and getting takeout which defeats the whole purpose of this service. The trial offer of "Save $25 off your first box" did not get applied until I notified the company as they charged me the full amount. The next damn day they charged me for the following week which I wrote them and asked them to please not send as we did not care for it. A week later there is a box on my porch and the charge posted to my account so. Hello Fresh is $13 cheaper per week and a million times better. Don't waste your time or money.

Admittedly, I am spoiled when it comes to Mexican and El Salvadorian food. I spent the past 10 years in California and nothing I've found elsewhere even comes close to the amazing Mexican and El Salvadorian I ate regularly there. 

A few weeks ago I had a hankering for some pupusas so I decided to check out Tacos Lupita. The entire experience was... meh. I wanted to like the place, I really did. But no dice. 

There are only two types of pupusas on the menu: cheese and pork. I'm used to having far more options like beans and spinich and loroco flowers. No such luck here. I ordered one of each type of pupusa and was totally underwhelmed by my food when it arrived. The pupusas were greasy and heavy, the masa too thick, the curtido old and wilted. Yeck. 

I guess I will continue my search for decent Mexican food in this part of the country or maybe just wait until the next time I visit CA to have the real thing...

We ordered Set B $12.45 (pan fried buns + mini wonton soup), Curry Beef Vermicelli Soup $7 & XLB $6.85. First off, the mini wonton soup refers to the size of the wontons (which contain literally no meat) rather than the size of the bowl. When I ordered, I thought maybe a smaller bowl or the entire wonton itself is smaller (smaller wrap but still decently filled) but I was completely wrong. Both the noodle soups were very bland, I would highly recommend NOT ordering either. The (smaller than average) XLB and pan fried baos are made to order so they took a really long time to arrive. We had already finished our noodle soups, and sat waiting for about 10min, before the pan fried baos came. And after another 20min of the pan fried baos arriving, the xlb came. Not to mention, our vinegar was forgotten, as well as our drink order and my tea was not refilled throughout the dinner (and it's only Thursday too). The only plus to this meal was that I can 100% vouch for their pan fried baos. In fact, they were probably some of the best I've had! That being said, I'd probably skip this place and just walk over to Dinesty for their consistency.

A 2 star because the pan fried baos were a solid 5 stars for me but everything else weighed it down from a 5 to a 2 unfortunately. Would not recommend and if I do come back, it will probably only be to order take out for the pan fried baos.

Unfortunately by far thee worst Dutch bros I've been to yet. And I'm from southern OR where it all began. So let's say I'm one of those Dutch brats that I know how a Dutch is supposed to be, from their drinks to the type of people that should be working here. I can agree with another gal and I'm sure others who have felt the same, I feel rushed and it's not as warm and welcoming here at this stand. I've now had multiple visits, enough of them to be negative to say something about this location, then go praise the locations that ARE doing it right. I've now had one of the butthead boy workers look at me because I wanted whip on my rebel like it was outrageous and the tone that was used when he said it was just not okay, so negative and rude. Then today 3/10/16, without knowing it, the boy working called my friend a "needy ass" for wanting the whip that she was asked if she wanted to begin with, on her drink ... She's pregnant mind you and I thought she was gonna rip through my driver window from the passenger side because she was so offended.. He tried to cover it up and say he was joking around but that could and did offend the wrong person. Regardless, that's not the type of people who normally work at Dutch brothers. Honestly, this location needs a new owner that cares seeing that the quality of people working here are just not up to standard and it's not terribly hard to be a good employee for Dutch, they hire genuine, fun, up beat and exciting people. Not rude little kids whom are actually probably older than at least 18 that act this immature and unwelcoming . Such a disappointing location. And the coffee at this location does seem sweeter than it should be and I like mine sweet. They really don't seem to do things by the book here or even close really, which again, isn't hard seeing Dutch is a great company to work for, I've had multiple friends work at one and all of them loved working there. The only plus side is the loop for the drive thru is large enough that you can park in the far back if you want to do the walk up window, and still get out which is fantastic.

It amazes me each time I've called in to order lunch for a group that A) they don't take email requests, B) they don't answer the phone in the morning until after 10am, C) I've talked to the manager and he won't take my orders the day before so I don't get stuck making a phone call that doesn't get answered in the morning.  This makes it hard to depend on a restaurant that doesn't seem to want more business.  It's unfortunate since each time we order it's usually around $180 to $200 and it has averaged twice a month for nearly 7 months.  I'd say if you want a single lunch make sure you get there before 11:45am or you won't find parking in their tiny lot.  So it's not like I haven't given them MULTIPLE chances.  So sad to you Ryan!

Dropped in after a post-dinner walk from Unchai to have a snack and dessert. We whiled away a half hour savouring a dessert before trying the calamari at the Happy Hour price.

As usual the server wasn't exactly thrilled especially as we didn't order any alcohol (none of us being drinkers). But the place wasn't exactly packed either.

Calamari ($14 or $10 during Happy Hour)
-We were informed the $10 happy hour portion is the same as the $14 regular menu portion. 
-Not recommended even at $10. Seemed flat somehow. Lacked seasoning? And price for portion at $10. 
-If you do get it, try to pair each piece with the fried jalapeño slices to get some bite to each bite.

Billy Miner Pie ($7) mocha ice cream on a chocolate crust with hot fudge, caramel, and almonds 
-Simple idea that's tasty. Ice cream is soft and easy to spoon through but doesn't start melting into a puddle right away. Still, if you're going to try more than one dessert I wouldn't ask for them all to be brought out at once.
-Seemed like a surprising portion for $7 so if you're dining solo or duo, plan ahead.
-Our server said their cheesecake was made by the Keg but offsite and distributed to the outlets so this was probably the same. So you can expect supermarket quality for their desserts in general.
-The portion is big enough that if you get bored midway you can experiment with the pepper and salt at your table. Go heavy on the pepper to get enough impact. For the salt to get that salted caramel taste, go easy as that salt grinder gives you rather large chips.

Iffy service...we were ignored for a long while before we flagged down a server rushing past us to get our assigned server.  I ordered a glass of sparkling rose', but was given a glass of non-sparkling...I ended up drinking it anyway, as the server didn't reappear until I was almost done with the glass.  Seems like this place is skating by with a fabulous location with a constant flow of customers...too bad, as there's a great bar, open and closed patio area that's great for sitting back to have a drink and people watch/eavesdrop.

Here's my problem: every time I order an iced coffee with milk and sweetener, they make it without sweetener. This has happened consistently for the last month. I've ordered it multiple ways to try to make it clear: "sweet", "sweetened", "with sweetener". But somehow, they always leave it out.

I usually don't point it out because I'm totally fine with unsweetened coffee, but when I'm craving an iced coffee, I usually want milk with sugar with a taste of coffee.

I have a hard time giving out such a low score because I really like having an almost full-fledged Starbucks on campus ("almost" because it's a pain to use Gift Cards, and they don't accept Square).
