On top of that, most of the employees are friendly with the exception of one or two. I can even handle the wait considering how busy this place is during the fall/spring semesters.

But seriously. What's with the word "sweet" that you can't understand?

Not a great Starbucks experience here today ... I ordered a "tall in a grande cup iced coffee with extra milk" (which I frequently order in Starbucks locations around the Lower Mainland without any problem; in fact it was suggested to me by a Starbucks barista to order it that way instead of asking for extra room and pouring extra milk in myself at the counter) and I was informed I'd have to pay for a grande, so I changed it to "extra room" instead of "extra milk" and poured it in myself. 

Then, I had to ask for my receipt, and it was a "treat receipt" so actually worth something and not just a regular receipt (which they should provide anyway).

I came here for my clinical skills exam. The good thing is the shuttle that takes you from the airport was on time. The front desk was very kind and friendly and got me checked into my room pretty quickly. Of note they got me to the right room first time. Unlike other reviewers have said. 
I stayed on the 11th floor which is apparently the club floor. My room was pretty clean. I did not have any issues with dirty towels or dirty bed. Everything look like it was supposed to be. 
My floor is pretty quiet, and I had no issues with malfunctioning sinks or doors.
The morning of my test was a different story. The night before my test, someone kept calling my room phone over and over during the tonight. I called the front desk and they blocked the calls for the room phone but it still went through to the room phone. I eventually ended up unplugging the phone and that solved the problem. By now it is 5am and I have to wake up at 630am...needless to say I was tired. 
There is a shuttle that takes you to the testing center but apparently they forgot about us and they end up sending us a shuttle  at 745 instead of 730. We are supposed to be the testing center by 8 o'clock. They got us there in time, but it's never good to have these last minute issues.
Same thing happened with the shuttle that was supposed to pick us up. It supposed to meet us there at 3:30 PM but they were never there. We called the front desk and they probably sent us a shuttle.
The continental breakfast on the club lounge is a joke. It consists of bread, watered eggs, and bacon. They also have some juices and such.
Overall, if you're coming to Atlanta for the clinical skills exam, just stay at the hotel that is right next door to the testing center.

When we arrived it wasn't too busy. I ordered a coffee and a yo holla stuffed French toast since I had my heart set on that from online reviews. The waitress was very friendly. She took our order and returned about 5 mins later saying their out of that French toast. I was bummed but ordered a Montecristo and fries. My coffee was just warm not hot. Even my refill was just warm. Out food came out. Everything was hot, but my fries and montercristo tasted both like the frying oil needed changed. My last complaint is it took forever to get boxes, our check. it got a little busy and there was only 2 waitresses on the floor. We left over looked out last 20mins in the diner. I don't know how I feel about returning here one day.

Something must have changed here as have had decent to good food and service in the past.  Today we were seated in a timely manner but watched as others seated after us were prompted greeted by wait staff while we were apparently invisible. The neighboring server said I don't know who your server is...  but I'll take your drink order.  And downhill from there.  Food quality not as good as it once was. Restrooms were filthy with sticky floors and dirty toilets   (Almost left after that). Of course after that noticed how dirty the rest of the dining room was.  Not likely to return.  This was a little after noon on Saturday, plenty of empty tables and no line. I would guess we were late discovering why others have stopped coming to an otherwise once thriving deli/restaurant.

Once again Yelp has let me down. This restaurant changed their location but when u route to the address it still takes u to the old location. I was in an Uber so it was very inconvenient to call another Uber to get me to the right location. 

The service was good. We were greeted with smiles and had water with a wedge of watermelon? That was kinda cool. She took our orders and food come out quickly. The Vietnamese hot and sour soup was on point but that wasn't my main dish. I ordered Beef Pho and it was terrible. Pho is first, all about the broth, there was no taste. It was like warm water with a little salt and sugar. Second, the noodles are totally wrong. It's like ordering angel hair pasta but getting fettuccine noodles. It's not the same. 

Maybe they should take Pho off the menu and just cook a few good items.

First of all, when you walk in there's a very funny smell that never ended up going away. Not a very pleasant smell. My gf and I were excited about the boba smoothies but then were let down quite badly. The tapioca pearls were hard and tasted of cardboard. 

The service was horrible. The young guy waiting on us was very friendly and felt bad and apologized for it taking so long but they still could step up their game. We had two servers and they still couldn't get it right. Pho usually takes a short time to get out, but not this time!

#28 and #25 were what we decided to order. I give the PHO 4 STARS and the rest 2. They did take our boba off the check so that was nice. The pho broth is good but I don't think I'll be coming back. I could get good pho without the smell.

Lets be honest here, you probably didn't come here cause you wanted gormet. 

The chips are good. Had a few tacos. Fish taco was covered in a weird sauce that I wasn't crazy about. Seared Shrimp was tasty but literally pooled oil on my plate. Which I guess I'm fine with. 

Cheap beer isn't. $5.25 for a pacifico or Dos Equis is just a bit steep for what they are offering. 

Their Margarita is crazy sweet, but I'm partial to just lime juice and tequila with a hint of triple sec or simple syrup. So take this part of the review with a grain of salt (heh). 

Don't get me wrong, there's nothing wrong with Papagayo, its just not really worth it if you have other options

After reading quite a bit of good reviews for this restaurant, my husband and I trekked over looking forward to some great beer and a  late afternoon meal. Unfortunately,  we were  sorely disappointed and wished we had gone elsewhere. The place was packed when we arrived but we were able to get a seat at the end of the  bar that was very tight and uncomfortable for dining    Anyway,  the place really assaults your senses on every level and not in a good way.   Once seated I just want to leave and go to a quieter, cozier  place to eat, drink and relax.   We went for the extensive beer selection as it sounded interesting.  My husband was happy to see a German wheat beer that he loved, however, it was poured in the wrong glass, a Pilsner glass verses a Weizenbier or Weissbier glass.  When we asked the bartender for the correct glass we were told they got rid of those glasses, and only use the pilsner!  She also tried to tell him that he is actually getting more beer as the Pilsner glass is slightly larger. But that is not the point, as there are reasons for the correct glass, as it is tapered to trap yeast at the bottom of the glass, and the correct beer glass should be used.  My husband is German and he would never come back here for this reason alone.  The manager really needs to look into this, go to The Barking Dog or the Grill Next Door and look 
ah how they handle a large beer selection with the correct glass for each beer,*** IF YOU ARE GOING TO CHARGE $7.50 A BEER THEN USE THE CORRECT GLASS!

Lastly, there is no bar atmosphere here, people should go in and sit at the bar to see what I mean....There were at least 10 bartenders, and each bartender had a small area, appeared to each have 2-4 customers each..  The moment we sat down we were handed a menu, as if we had sat at a table.  The bartenders were hanging around everywhere and when we decided not to order food,  she swiped up the menus and we had to flag her down for our second drinks, clearly she wanted us to leave for turnover sake.
Anyway, very disappointed.

Unfortunately, this place was a flop for me. I normally LOVE me some Chinese food, but... this was a disappointment. You get a LOT of food for not too much money, which was great! But my sweet and sour chicken was yuck. And I'm a HUGE fan of sweet and sour chicken, so that was a big deal for me. It had the sour tang, but none of the sweet! I ate maybe two pieces, then threw the rest away. I was actually really, really sad about it. I shared my husband's food instead (he went to a different truck). The veggie spring rolls were just decent, but the sauces included were not. I wouldn't go back. Cheap food, but you get what you pay for. I'd rather have Panda Express.

We chose this place b/c it was crowded and thought it would be great. The service was ok. We had to ask for olive oil and cheese to dip the bread. The bread seemed like it wasn't freshly baked although I really don't know. My eggplant parm would have been excellent if it was hot. It was barely warm. I've had much better in this area for the price.We spent $60 for both of us and I thought it wasn't worth it. Wouldn't recommend.

I was a little disappointed hopefully they will get better. I am a huge fan of taro and shave ice. When I heard a new dessert opened up I was super excited. 

Jumping to the point:

Reasons why I find the experienced distasteful: 1) no flavor in any of the ingredients 2) the taro ball had a hint of taro but no other taste. 3) they should use a new shave ice machine. The ice wasn't crushed properly and it became ice cubes. 4) all the ingredients didn't really blend together. 5) overall I thought was just bland taste in my mouth.

I would rather go to other desert shops instead.

I am pretty throughly unimpressed with Hey Cupcake!. I will preface this review by saying that I really love to bake (I make a mean key lime pie in fact), but even so, I still think boxed cake mix is the way to go. The cupcakes are always moist, rich and chocolatey, and fabulously cheap. Therefore, i went to hey cupcake ready to be blown away at how much better these cupcakes were than my 99 cent betty crocker chocolately goodness cupcakes from earlier. 

Hey Cupcake has a very small selection of cupcakes, I think there are about 8 in all. Now, I could see my way to forgive the limitation on choices if the cupcakes were at least amazingly moist and yummy. But honestly, they're a little dry. Also speaking as someone who doesn't much care for creamcheese I found my chocies even more severely limited since there was no option to chose one type of cupcake and another type of icing. 

All in all. I just don't think it's worth the hype.

I forgot to add, it's a little expensive for what it is. Again... not worth the hype.

The only positive thing about this Safeway is it's location. 
I don't live in Surrey, but I won't go to this Safeway again. Unfortunately, my friend lives near this Safeway and it's the most convenient store. We were at the pharmacy recently and she was asking questions about her medications like any other patient. She and I found that the female pharmacy assitants were very condescending and huffy to her, but we're very nice to the caucasian patients. (I don't know if it's because they're white themselves), but I stayed and assessed them more. And noticed the same situation happening. *sigh* what a sad occurrence that discrimination still occurs. 
I don't like giving negative reviews but I would've thought that having a Safeway where there's a lot of south Asians, the techs who are from a different ethnic background would be more accepting of people from other cultures. Luckily for my friend, she's stated that she now only brings in her prescription to the less biased and more welcoming staff. Maybe she'll have more luck in future.

I'm perplexed by the rave reviews here. My husband and I had the five-course tasting menus here (one veggie and one normal) and were totally underwhelmed. Half of the dishes had way too much salt, and none of them had very interesting flavors. For example, the fettuccine dish was just VERY undercooked pasta in a heavy, salty sauce. Hardly worth the price. The salad course was romaine leaves, watermelon, with a ton of salt and a bland dressing. One of the dishes had slices of corn still on the cob, which required a lot of work to remove the extremely small amount of corn with a butter knife. None of this seemed very innovative in terms of recipes. However, the dark chocolate dessert was tasty. The servers were also very nice.

My da' and I went here recently, expecting something romantic and authentic, so my review is based on that expectation. This was on a Saturday evening.  

Service:
This place is found above Paradiso Cafe in North End.   We had a reservation asking for a window seat, but we got a weird corner seat where we felt cornered. But otherwise, the service was OK, staffs were friendly.

Food:
we had...
Antipasti - Daily selection of roasted, pickled and grilled vegetables
Risotto del giorno (with pumpkins for that day's special) 
Veal saltimbocca
They were all OK, but not very authentic Italian.  It is American Italian food, not Italian Italian food.  Not really something that one would experience in Tuscany.  
We ate half sized dishes, which was more than enough.  I looked at the loud table and saw full sized dishes and they were huge.  And kinda unneccessarily oily.  

Ambiance:
S-U-P-E-R LOUD.  Drunk people on 2 of the tables.  The drunk people were hurting my ears with loud dirty jokes and unpleasant laugh.  My darling and I had to almost yell at each other to have a conversation.  This may only be that specific evening, and I guess this is not really the fault of the restaurant.  Even one of the servers came to us and said, "they are pretty loud, huh?"  

An acquaintance from Italy stayed in Boston area for a while and before going back to Italy he told me that the only authentic Italian place he found around here was Pulcinella Trattoria in Cambridge.  
More restaurants I try, more I agree with his view.

Among the few Whole Foods markets I visited(a few in California including the relatively new one in Cupertino where we used to shop, the flagship in Austin (TX) and the one in West Vancouver), this is the worst one I've ever stepped into.

The outside was nice and inviting with a living wall.  However, as soon as we stepped, we wondered if we took a wrong and went into a warehouse store.  However, the prices were definitely Whole Foods prices.  From the roof to the shelving to the product display, the store looks slightly better than a Costco store.  It's a far cry from the store in Park Royal Village in West Vancouver.  While I expect to pay a premium for quality groceries, I prefer my money would give me a better ambience as well if it is available and it is just across the bridge at a store of the same company.

The location on 82nd between King and Johnson Creek, the fans in room 7 have been broken for 6 months now, I've mentioned it on multiple occasions and have asked for a different bed more than once. I felt like a bother, but also I hated being so cold in the winter when I went there for some heat. Also the radio is rather janky . Once I was placed in a bed that was inadequately cleaned. The one on Sunnyside is preferable.

I change my mind completely! I'm sure the food is still great, if you can get it, but we have tried to eat here EVERY day this week and it has been closed for one reason or another. We went in and immediately asked for the manager. We were told "it won't do any good" and then that "there are other places you can eat if you're angry." The whole situation could have been resolved if they just had a working phone, a voice mail recording or even an updated website. I have easily spent $1,000 here but don't plan to EVER return.

I used to think they had some of the best Chinese food here but it's been a while since I've last had lunch here. Very disappointed with the food on this visit for lunch! 

First of all it looked as though all of their prices have increased and secondly the quality of the food is not what it used to be.

I had a combo lunch with egg roll, chicken subgum chow mein and pork egg Foo young.

The egg roll was obviously cooked from frozen and pretty much what you would get at most other Chinese restaurants.

The chicken subgum was mostly bland and had way too much celery in it and not much in the way of other veggies.

The pork egg foo young was the worst that I have ever had, obviously frozen from food service vendor, deep fried and the gravy also left a lot to be desired.

On a positive note, the portions we're huge.

I have found at least 3 other great Chinese restaurants since my last visit to Wong's and I will most likely not return here.

Summary: Glad I tried it and satisfied my curiosity, but I don't think I'll be back.  Kind of interesting(?), but way too pricey and just... not good.

Dumplings are one of my very favorite foods, so when I heard this place was coming to within five minutes of my office, I was excited.  I showed up the day before and sent pictures to my wife, I scouted the menu and reviews of other locations.  The concept looked great on paper, and they clearly had success in previous locations. Excited, I say.

You can get all the location and handmade bun details elsewhere.  The bottom line for me is that it's a ton of dough for very little filling, and at around $3 a bun, it's expensive. I guess it's more filling than other buns, but the dough is not why i get dumplings! Especially this dough.  It was like someone crossed a steamed pork bun with a parker house roll and under-cooked it by about 3 minutes. 

My wife and I had (thankfully) decided to try 1 each of three different kinds of bao (lobster, sweet potato, curry beef), and ate them in the park across the street.  We agreed they were "interesting" and quickly got down to discussing where else we wanted to go for dinner that night.

I was so excited to try their pad thai... 

Then I was so disappointed when I put it in my mouth. Do people still say, "that's what she said?". 

I had what is probably my least favorite version of pad thai at Titayas. And I'm not even a pad thai snob... I probably like mediocre pad thais more than the average yelper. Flavorless, dry, luke warm. Not a good trio of words when describing one's lunch. 

The soup that is served with the lunch specials was pretty tasty though. So that's a plus. The coconut ice cream with crushed peanuts was decent as well. 

it was probably the worst pad thai I've had in Austin. But I would give titayas another shot, because I did see glimpses of hope...

4 star sushi with 1 star service. Came here on a Sat night for an early dinner and ate at the bar.  It was only 6:00 and not very crowded.  Sushi was certainly above average although not quite up to Umi levels.  Service fell very short.  Water glasses not refilled, nobody asked if we were enjoying our food.  The bar staff were mostly texting or talking amongst themselves.  I've worked in the service industry, so I get it.  It's hard work and easy to take your eye off the ball when it's early and not crowded.  But when customers are sitting at your bar paying $25 for a wagyu beef roll it's showtime.  There are too many other options in Atl to settle for poor service.  Won't be back.

I was really disappointed with this joint because I've been so excited to try this place since they were building up. I'm not sure if I just came on a bad night but the experience wasn't that great. You can refer to Kim N's review because we ordered exactly the same thing. 

One thing that I would recommend to the owner is to offer a combo seafood boil platter on top of their selection. Maybe I'll come back when it's crawfish season if the place is still around. On a positive note, the flavors are very good and the service was superb.

Also, place doesn't have their liquor license yet. You can BYOB but they do charge a $10 fee.

Not really a Greek place.  Got the athenian special with stuffed grapeleaves, yogurt, spanikopita. For $11, I got grape leaves straight from a can.  The pita bread was chewy and unremarkable.  The spanikopita was very greasy but at least it looked like it was made in house.  I guess dining at a hole in the wall like this I can't complain about the quality but $11 is pretty outrageous for a skimpy appetizer.  Maybe Ill edit this if I feel like giving them another chance.

I'm glad I'm not the only one who had this experience - I was so excited to try a cupcake when I heard Sweet opened up so close to home....the website was cute, the shop is super cute, and I was overwhelmed by the amazing sounding (and looking) flavors in the display case. 
When first trying a new place, I always stick with the basics - if you can't get that right, I have no interest in venturing into more creative options.  I went with my standby - yellow cake with chocolate frosting.  Given the price, I was even more excited to get home and try this bad boy.
We get home...I open the box...I pick up the delectable looking 'sweet'....I take a bite....and I grimace.  The cake was dry and the frosting barely tasted like chocolate.  I took a second bite to confirm my distaste for it and then tossed it.  
I would have given them 3 stars since I only tried one flavor, but based on everyone else's reviews, I'll stick with 2 stars as I'm not confident any other flavor would be any more moist and tasty.

Food was good, came hot, but rest of service wasn't up to par. Ordered a coca-cola, & got a coca cola on the first try- but then it was refilled with sweet tea, then Diet Coke, then finally got regular, third times a charm I guess. Ordered some Queso dip & some Guacamole for appetizers, waited 20 min, got our entrees and then had to ask for the dips, which came 10 minutes AFTER our meal, by that time the chips were gone, took another 10 minutes to get chips.  Ordered chicken enchiladas with a side of sour cream, got cheese enchiladas with no sour cream. I like cheese enchiladas so instead of complaining I just ate them, as I said, the food was good but probably won't be back. Arrived on a Wednesday night at 7 and left at 8:15, and there were only about 10 other tables with customers. I'd expect that kind of wait on a Friday or Saturday. To have a meal take over an hour and mistake after mistake, I'd hate to see what it's like on a Friday night...

I chose this place because of the high yelp reviews, but I guess I went on an off day. 

I ordered the $8.99 fish, shrimp and wing meal. The portion was huge, but the food was just okay. The fries were the only thing that I enjoyed because they were hot. I tried to eat my food because I paid almost $10 for it, but I threw it away rather than stuff myself with mediocrity.

I don't doubt that they've earned the high reviews, but I certainly don't have anything to rave about.

When someone takes more than 2 weeks to respond when you ask for a simple question like rates, im not a fan.  Ive read some of the reviews about promptness, cancellation etc and I always want to give businesses a benefit of a doubt.  I did, and I decided that this wont work for me.  Ive already reached out to 4 different electrologists in the city and everyone responds within a day or two like Eva from Alter Image who I decided to choose.

Ordered takeout from here last week because we were excited about getting our fix of Indian food in Waltham. But the quality of the ingredients is average and the taste is below par. We ordered Panner chili noodles, Gobi Manchurian, Chole Bature, Aloo Tikki Chat and Mysore Masala Dosa. The noodles was super oily and had a metallic taste to it, probably from a old, unwashed wok?! We had to throw it away! Gross!  I don't mind the MSG in food but the Paneer in the noodles was also doused  in red, food coloring which not only made it look unappetizing but is extremely unhealthy. Also the cauliflower in the gobi Manchurian was literally uncooked, which is not how it is meant to be. Still I am giving this place a three star because the coconut chutney for the dosa was pretty good and the Chole, despite being over seasoned with turmeric was still edible. I will try again because I love to support local businesses but this one still needs a lot of improvements!

I will say this. Of all the churches I have been to, this one aims at a very specific audience. Hipsters that rely on knowledge. There is truth here. There is knowledge. There are even cartoons from great Portland artists. See "The Bible Project" headed up by one of the teaching pastors from Western "Tim Mackie".  The music is not original, so much as, The Original. As in the original versions. This place is beautiful and covered in art and flare and whimsical design that honestly rivals some movie sets. But there in lay the problem. During worship, not a tear was shed. Not a hand was raised to the father. It is a personal matter that worship removes us from our own mind and soul and takes us to a closer link to Jesus. The blank stares and attention to style were far superior to genuine believers. We all know that John the Baptist wore burlap rags and ate bugs, and was considered one of the greatest pavers for the way of Jesus. Jesus practically wore bed sheets with a higher thread count than most. He could afford it after all, he was a carpenter. But the people here walk in with euro punk boots. Beards. Skinny jeans and XL cardigans. Typical Portland attire. If you are an artist that likes the bible as a historic ancient text that wants to "know", but not "do" or "experience" God. This is a great place that is really just extremely easy to get sucked into. It's beautiful and smart, but empty.

Nada seems promising, but after my second visit, I'm not eager to return.

First, the good news: it's a beautiful restaurant and great space in which to dine.

Both times I've been here, I've found the food here to very underwhelming. The best things I had on the last trip was the trio of salsas and queso.

The tacos we had -- porkbelly, chicken and al pastor -- were meh. Encourage the cooks or corporate chef to get out and try some of Columbus' taco trucks or Los Gauchos (for pastor). Flour tortillas? No thank you. Porkbelly could have been chopped fine and needed some crunch and acid.

You get the point.

Nada is just too pricey... I'd pay it if they nailed the food, but currently I can feed three people at Taqueria Los Primos for the price of a taco entree at Nada -- and it will be a lot tastier.

Sorry, Nada, but you've got some work to do.

Gyu-Kaku is a Japanese-based chain of Yakiniku, or grilled meat restaurants.  With several dozen American locations and over 600 in Japan, they are the "Olive Garden" of Japanese-Korean tabletop grill eateries.

Similar to "Olive Garden," the operation is formula-driven; one of commercial-grade marinates, lower-grade proteins, inattentive servers and gimmicky promotions.  With a group and with alcohol flowing freely I can see how the social dining experience might be enjoyable.  As a businessman dining alone, and with evening work awaiting his return, my experience fell far short of that mark-- it was an genuine ordeal.

The dining room is large, yet partitioned into small dining cubicles. Seated in a back corner of the busy restaurant, I decided to use a coupon I'd received to bring the $49 "Ultimate All You Can Eat" (53 items / 90 minutes) into an acceptable expense account range.  The gas grill was ignited as I placed my first order.  Unfortunately, the grill had numerous and unpredictable "cold spots," a fact which plagued my dining experience throughout the evening.

Ordered on the first pass was fried pork gyoza, fried cheese wontons, Angus beef rib in sweet tare sauce, beef tongue, pork belly shio, garlic shrimp and shishito peppers.  The kitchen was out of the beef rib.

Both of the fried appetizers were very obviously pre-fried, then reheated when my order arrived.  The gyoza were tasty, but both were woefully overcooked and unappetizing in appearance.  Pork belly, shrimp and the peppers weren't bad-- once reliable cooking areas on the grill were found.  In each case the marinates used were soulless and poor imitations of quality Japanese grill preparations.  Further, the kitchen's attentiveness to trimming proteins of sinew was inadequate for this style of cooking.

My second order, garlic shoyu chicken and garlic mushrooms, revisited the same type of insipid commercial marinates, but were eatable.  The mushrooms were delivered in an aluminum foil packet, making it impossible to determine their cooking time without repeatedly opening the packet.  Both were considerably better than what had been served previously.

Service bordered upon slow for the duration of my meal, but the process of getting a check, then getting my credit card back, redefined all standards of slow service.

I would characterize Gyu-Kaku as a poor value for the money, and not a chain to which I would choose to return.

Fries are good. Burgers not so much. The patty is unseasoned and just really didn't have much flavor. Prices are quite high unless you go during their "Happy Hour"

The coolest thing they have is the soda machine where you can create different combinations of drinks. I've never seen these before in person and got to try out a bunch of fun (sometimes odd) drinks.

Service was ok (maybe a bit gruff but maybe it had something to do with the cashier/employee being a foreigner.)

I dunno but I like having my toppings out in the open (like a mini salad bar) for me to place on my burger. I don't want to have to request every single thing ahead of time (like ketchup? I have to ask for ketchup? Ugh)

When I first found Purple Carrot I was so excited that there was a vegan version of Blue Apron out there and couldn't wait to try it. I subscribed to the service for a little over a year and even upgraded to the TB12 meals as they are higher in protein and lower in sugars and processed ingredients. I will say that all the meals Purple Carrot cooks up are, for the most part, extremely tasty. They also provide colorful easy to follow recipe cards and even sent me a really nice TB12 binder to put all my recipe cards in. 

In March 2018 I decided to cancel my subscription. It seems that Purple Carrot's Operations team just can't get it together and despite several mishaps, I finally had enough. Also, the quality has gone down...way down. I'm sorry, but when I pay $78 per week for a meal delivery service, moldy ingredients, missing recipe cards, and missing ingredients is simply inexcusable. I have given Purple Carrot multiple chances to get it together and they're only getting worse. Every time I receive a box and there's something wrong with it I send them an email and I receive the same response, "I'll let my operations team know..." yet nothing changes. Today, for example I received a moldy onion and a green onion that's literally a day or two away from going bad. This tells me that their produce isn't being turned around fast enough likely because they're losing customers left and right (based on the reviews here). Prior boxes have had missing recipe cards and missing ingredients. How can you be a meal delivery service and have ingredients missing from the box?! Recently I have noticed mistakes in the recipes as well such as ingredients being provided but not included in the recipe...or it will tell you to chop something but won't refer to it again in the recipe so it becomes a guessing game. 

The quality is also declining. Part of TB12's slogan is "Eat Like a Champion." I highly doubt Tom Brady eats boil in bag quinoa and microwaveable minute rice. I joined Purple Carrot for healthy home cooked meals, not ingredients that are boiled or nuked in plastic. 

Lastly, every time I log into Purple Carrot, there's a link letting me know I can send a free box to a friend....so I did and I quickly realized that this a shady deal offered by Purple Carrot disguised as them being generous. In order for your friend to receive a "free" box they have to sign up for a subscription and enter their credit card info, which if they're not familiar with the skip deadlines, which most aren't, they wind up getting charged for a box. I see several people have complained and this happened to my friend and he received poor customer service. What really grinds my gears is that I thought I was doing something nice for a friend and really wanted to show him how tasty meat-free can be but now Purple Carrot has soured the situation. Additionally, I feel this shows how devalued I am as a customer of Purple Carrot...that they would provide my friend who I referred, poor customer service. The whole thing is shady and shows that Purple Carrot is desperate for customers but what they don't realize is they're losing customers by engaging in these shady practices. If you truly want to spread the word about how delicious and healthy your food is then do that...don't make people sign up and charge them for stuff they don't want. I can't stand when businesses do stuff like that...it NEVER works out for the business in the long run. 

Look, I have been vegan for over 3 years now and I'm pretty hardcore about it. Often times I struggle with what to cook and what to eat...or how much to cook...so this service was perfect for me. It sucks that Purple Carrot has left such a bad taste in my mouth. No pun intended.

Hair: Hair looks great, but the stylist just really didn't want to be there. Also, he really didn't listen on the color I wanted and kept talking about warm or cool black colors; very off-putting. 

Professionalism: Salon opened an hour earlier than he showed up, and he was the only one there, which was odd. 

Tone: Zero conversation, not even a "how'd you hear about us". Very transactional, cold and just generally awkward. I would tell you his name, but he didn't me; so have no idea. 

I won't be back.

I read great things about Canada Place. The brochure was colorful and had a list of tons of attractions- it sounded like a worthwhile place to visit with a limited amount of time to spend in Vancouver. It was, in fact, a complete waste of time. 

Seriously, I spent over two hours there and I'm still not sure what the hype is all about.

The brochure mentioned the Canadian Trail. I was intrigued. I like to learn about the places I visit. The Canada Trail was nothing more than colorful (somewhat muted) bricks inlaid into the ground that were labeled with Canadian place names. No explanations. No information. Just...boring.

Despite Canada Place being pretty darn lackluster, you may notice the two stars that I've given it. One is for the view. It's on the water's edge and it does allow for some beautiful views of the water, city, and nearby mountains. The second star is for FlyOver Canada. You can check my review for that ride seperately, but I have to give credit to Canada Place for housing the attraction.

Probably not the best time to check out a bakery, but I went on a Saturday afternoon for a pick me up, and since this is a bakery and not an Italian dessert place, I got myself an espresso from Counter Culture (their coffee of choice), a canele, and a scone for the Boo.

Espresso was fine. It wasn't incredible, but it wasn't terrible. The canele was delicious with a crunchy crust and deliciously eggy inside. The scone was a disaster--hard, dry, and probably my Boo's fault for getting it in the first place. Who eats a scone on a Saturday afternoon?

Probably should come back for another visit in the morning, on a bustling day when things are fresh. Shame on me.

I'm giving it two stars because initially the Alpharetta office assured me before treatments and during scheduling, that my groupon would be honored past its expiry date . I bought a set of 8 treatments at the Alpharetta office. After 3-4 treatments I received a call from the Buckhead office, informing me, there's a change in policies, and that the Alpharetta office will not honor the remaining 4 treatments. The Buckhead office actually called the Alpharetta office to ask them to dishonor my purchase and stop honoring any further course of treatments. I should have been informed by the Buckhead office, before the expiry date that their policies, apply to the Alpharetta office as well. I think that was extremely rude and plain bad customer service from the Buckhead office. They also wanted me to buy another deal to continue the treatments. So, stay away from their groupons even if they seem like a good deal.

Planned on eating dinner here tonight, but ended up with a plate of buffalo wings at the Ninety-Nine. 

Only thing sweet about this berry is the service, food is sour (literally).  Open tables on a Saturday night is never a good sign.  Based on the patrons on either side of us, this is a place for drinks, lots of them (nothing wrong with that), but not for food.  

Quick rundown - didn't touch the Bolognese after the first SOUR bite. No tomato sauce, just pasta tossed with tough meat and hard carrot chunks - a dead giveaway this "sauce" was just mixed together for a few minutes before serving (taken off the bill - classy service).  French Onion Soup, which a tavern should nail, was absolutely tasteless.  No seasoning, could've been warm water.  The wife, who was nice enough to escort me to the Nines afterwards for my buff wings, got the Turkey Tip special with mashed potatoes.  Again, no seasoning, literally could've been eating anything warm - like military or school cafeteria bland.  Other reviews are right, great service, tasteless food (unless you get the bolognese with the sour kick).  Disappointing for the wait staff and such a great location.

So everyone's review on here was about the same....GREAT view, ball park quality food and sloppy service....all are close but not dead on.
THE VIEW...its pretty, but you can enjoy the view by simply driving up the hill and getting out...just park in their lot then walk around and enjoy the ambiance. You don't have to pay 20+ a plate just to see the view folks.  Our server was friendly and knowledgable and had no issues with getting our order correct.  Poor waiters are generally going to happen at all restaurants and they usally dont last long. 
THE FOOD...I had the Grilled Shrimp Diablo which were tasty...but not 23$ for 5 shrimp tasty.  And the sauteed veggies...pretty limp and lacking color (signs of over-boiling) so they definitely were not only sauteed.  Thats ok, who is coming for veggies anyway right?  
If you are planning on taking a date here...think again.  she will not be impressed by the food, probably will like the view and the ambiance but in the end will still think your a jack ass if she sees the bill....and if she doesnt....your still a jackass!  
My advice....take a trip only if your already near by and don't plan on eating....just grab a beer or two and enjoy.

I was not thrilled with my experience at Stix. There was nothing specifically wrong with it but there was also nothing I left making me want to come back. 

The restaurant was mostly empty and they questioned the time of our reservation which was laughable. The restaurant looked nice but felt like they were trying to hard. I did like the wooden menu holders though, nice touch. 

I am not the biggest seafood/shellfish fan so the menu was light for my tastes but the food was fine. Unfortunately it took 20 minutes to get a gin and tonic in a close to empty restaurant. 

On a more positive note, my girlfriend loved it and wants to go back.

If your looking for a swanky lounge thats trying to be far more posh that it actually is, Minibar is your place. It's expensive, the crowd is what you would normally expect from a hotel lounge, and while the drinks are delicious, the service pretty much kills the mood. 
I ordered the ox-tail made with gin, St. Germain, rosemary, grapefruit, and lemon. It was refreshing, but the grapefruit was a little overpowering. Minibar is a fine place to drop in and have a drink with a friend after a day of shopping or hard days work, but it's nothing to write home about.

I really really want to give this place a good review because I decide to order from here based on reviews on Yelp, but....I can't. 

The lady that took my order could barely understand english.  And even worse, I couldn't really understand what she was saying when she took my order :-/

I ordered a chicken lo mein, veggie fried rice and scallion pancakes.  Well...that's not what I got.  Two out of the three things I orders were right. I went home and when we opened the bag we found the following:
1) Soup...
2) Plain white rice....
3) Scallion pancakes &
4) Chicken lo mein.

.....initially I thought she had given me the wrong order until I saw the scallion pancakes and chicken lo mein.  It was rather disappointing.

First, let me say that their food is probably worth three/four stars. It was decent pizza and their cheese is really good. However, as many of the recent reviews have stated their customer service isn't the best. I tried out Yelps new online ordering and I was very disappointed. On a Friday night around 8, I figured it would take about 45 minutes or so for a pie. That's fairly typical and I'm aware that they aren't a huge chain that delivers. Place my order and as stated above, it said around 35-60 minutes. As it got closer to 9, they updated saying it would be delayed and to expect it about 9:17. Ok, and hour and 17 minutes, I can accept that. It then became 9:30 and I hadn't received an updated. I call and was put on hold for 5 minutes, nothing terrible. The woman was nice enough but didn't seem to have an idea as to what was going on behind the scenes. I can over look that to... maybe she only works front end. The manager, maybe owner, gets on the phone. He's pretty abrupt and almost sounds as if I'm causing him an inconvenience by calling. Once he finds my order, he lets me know that it's just now being made and will be ready in 20 more minutes. I question the timing since it's been an hour and a half already. He informs me that if you order online or ask for delivery, your order gets out at the back of the line to everyone else. I was a little annoyed since it shouldn't matter how you order it should be treated the same (within reason and as to not totally eff your dining in customers). I told him that I would be willing to come pick it up myself since it may take less time then the 2 hours it was already going to take. No mention of, "I'm sorry it's taking so long; Can I get you xyz so that you're not paying for the delivery charge?" Simply nothing. Got to the restaurant and there were 3 people inside. It was completely empty. He was on the phone with another very upset customer whom was saying whatever they got was inedible and was asking them to remake them. Let's just say the rest of the conversation wasn't very pleasant either. He hung up and the woman up front started bad mouthing the customer. I got my pie and left. 

The food was decent. Better than a chain but not worth 2 hours. There are a lot of places to get pizza and if you're going to make it as a small business you need to treat your customers better. If they are unable to handle online orders from multiple websites, then they need to pick one and only one. I was really hoping to find a new pizza place since moving to this side of town. Alas, the search continues. Pitty.

Service was good. The atmosphere was nice. But the desserts were way overpriced. I had the tiramisu dessert and it was good but it did not wow me and make me feel that it was worth every penny that I've spent. The portion was very small which would be fine if I felt that they used fine expensive ingredients in it except it doesn't taste that way. I also had the white hot chocolate that was alright but just not worth $5. I think its a great place to have coffee and dessert with a friend but just not worth it for the price.

This is not the place to go to get a conventional prescription filled. I wanted to give this place my business, I really did. Now I drive a bit further down the road to the drive through Walgreen's. I always felt uncomfortable waiting at the counter to pick up my prescription. I'd be the only person there, and there would be pharmacists and assistants standing behind the counter up on their platform staring at me, but no one to come to the counter to help me. Then, I got a letter in the mail saying they stopped taking my insurance. What???  Never heard of a pharmacy not taking an insurance. It was a common one. My insurance has changed since, but I will not be bringing my prescriptions here again. 

That being said, I do buy my locally made 2,000 IU Vitamin D drops here. This place does seem to be a good place to buy supplements.

This is a mixed review,  I would have done 2 1/2 stars if I could. I went in as a walk in today,  I have been to the salon once before and they did a nice job.  I needed a partial highlight and a cut.  I explained to the girl that I had just recently had a hair cut, but that it wasn't shaped well and needed more layers.  She did highlights first, and they turned out WONDERFUL! Really nice color, she did them exactly like I asked.  HOWEVER....the haircut is a total disaster.   I'm super unhappy with it. She took it WAAAAAAY too short.  She never discussed length with me, I guess I should have been more specific that I didn't want much taken off the length but I thought she understood that I was just looking for a little more shape.  When I saw how short she was taking it, I got sick to my stomach.  I'm a bigger girl and need some length to shape my round face.  I said something to the effect of, "please don't go any shorter"  but the damage was done. She took 2 1/2-3 inches off the length!!  She could tell I was unhappy with the length and tried to explain that "the cut was very disconnected"  "it will lay much nicer now"  I know the cut was disconnected and it will lay much nicer now....but I've had a bob cut for 16 years and she could have blended it without taking that much off the length.  We also didn't discuss how short I wanted the layers, and they are too short.... basically....EVERYTHING IS TOO SHORT! I still gave her a nice tip and  I'm not gona cry about it.  I know in 4-6 weeks it will be back to a comfortable length....but I wanted to look and feel good for my anniversary trip this weekend, and instead I feel self conscious about my "too short" hair cut.

Karaoke starts at nine.  That's a load of elephant crap, because they didn't even get going until 10:30... after we had to ask SEVERAL times when it was going to start, and each time they lied and told us it was starting right then.

Karaoke selection:  TERRIBLE.  I mean, there were a few classics... but it was by far the worst song selection I've EVER seen in my entire Karaoke life.

Food -- decent -- not even worth elaborating on that.

Service -- far under par.   When we were practically the only table there... the waitress actually came over ONE time in a HALF HOUR.  That's just terrible.  And that isn't including the times we had to go and get staff to find her and send her over.

Secret Bathroom around the corner from the other bathroom -- good to know.

Sake Bombs -- don't hit the table too hard or the shot of Sake will fly into your lap.

Ride home from Roni -- priceless :)

I attended Biwa in larger group than normal (8+ people) and had a decent time there. Biwa was more than happy to accommodate for our group, however refused to split the check for individuals, there was also no explanation for why they wouldn't split the check which I thought was odd as that makes payment easier for guests and themselves. They had a very large alcoholic drink section, mostly sake and wine, however the prices were too high for my liking, upwards of $10 for what I think was a 4oz glass. Service was good, but food portions were small, as my gf and myself ordered 3 dishes that barely filled us. The food tasted good, but I was disappointed with my curry as it was so hot I couldn't taste much. Most of all, I was extremely disappointed with my gf's ramen, that seemed sub-par for something that costs $11 (anyone would agree that $11 for ramen had better be amazing). Also, the chefs were not Japanese or even Asian from what I could tell and the place really doesn't seem as decorated as they advertise, you can tell that your eating in a basement. Lastly the bathroom was located outside of the establishment and in the hall. Had a nice time, but could have been nicer.

Been here a few times and I go back and forth between 4 stars and 1 Star. I give 4 stars for their nice strong drinks, large portions, and friendly service. They always give huge portions along with endless salsa and chips. Somewhat authentic but I cannot promise anything based upon the following. 
I give 1 Star for the very long wait It can take depending on the day of the week. Monday or Tuesday night there's usually no problem but on a Friday or Saturday night one can expect to wait up to an hour for their food to arrive-- let alone wait 20-30 minutes for the first drink order. I also tend to take restaurant that offer a large menu with a grain of salt-- sometimes a large menu comes with compromise on the quality of food- that being said I think their menu is so large the authentic Mexican quality I was looking for has taken a hit. Between tacos, chimichangas, enchiladas and potato skins ( Yes. Potato skins.) their food really isn't all that good unless your needing something to put in your stomach that isn't Taco Bell. Again, I hate to give bad reviews but this is the 3rd or 4th time that I've eaten their food and gotten nothing but a high bill, long wait, and sour stomach.

Complete utter garbage that white people from Ohio and Mexicans that don't remember what food tastes like in the motherland think is good. This place wouldn't survive in any major city in the U.S. and it shouldn't be the gold standard in Columbus.

The al pastor is the most over-rated pork imaginable. Thinly shaved and lacking any real flavor from either the pork or the pineapple roasting on top of the source and dripping down on the pork. Admittedly most of the best al pastor I've had has been set up the same in taqueria's but this just tasted inferior. And the gringas taco that they add some cheese and the smallest thinnest slice of pineapple I've ever seen then charge you an extra $2 to make it $4 (regular al pastor being $2) is comical. 

The fish taco the lady at the register said I had to order was simply un-eatable. After growing up on proper baja tacos from the west coast this was nothing more then a fish stick with some shitty sauce and lettuce. 

The lengua didn't taste braised at all, it wasn't soft and tender like lengua should be, disappointing.

The interior is great, but the food seems over hyped. I like how they converted a giant warehouse to a really nice, high ceiling cafe. I came here on a Sunday morning around 10am and it was still relatively empty, but I've also dropped by here in the evening and it was packed. There's only a few parking spots in front of the restaurant and the back, but there are tons of tables and seats inside. Students pack the place as well as families coming in for brunch on weekends. When it was empty it was a nice place to read, but just be aware that they do have a sign saying max 2 hours (although I doubt people actually go by this).

I tried the matcha roll cake after seeing someone review it and to be honest, I wasn't a fan. Too much cream, and not the great kind. Chocolate croissant seemed a bit stale although for mornings I was hoping for fresher baked goods. Their macaroons are good but pretty pricey. I'd only go here when it's really empty like as soon as it opens, but if my goal is to get some work done, I wouldn't go here again as the food also wasnt anything special.

After reading the reviews here, I had to try out the buffet.  Boy was I disappointed!  I didn't find the quality to be "melt in your mouth" excellence (as stated by another review here).  A family member or friend of the owner must have written that.  There was a meat dish that had been laying there so long, it was was all dried out.  The tres leche cake mentioned in the reviews is not included on the buffet.  Nor was the beverage or any other dessert.  Dinner buffet (a small spread) was $7.99 and the drink was $2.35.

I was so horribly disappointed in this place.

It was busy. We got wings. My son (5) loves wings. Everywhere we go - if they have BBQ wings, he gets wings. This is the first place he made a face and looked at me and said "Dad... I don't like these wings."

They were crap. It's not the Rooster's I remember.

The service was mediocre. Forgotten drinks, mistaken orders, three times they tried dropping someone else's food at my table, and they forgot half my order.

No reason to come back, and I can't recommend it, but I have friends that love Rooster's - so I'd venture a second chance, but that's it.

I love halal food. Absolutely love it. And I used to love the Chicken & Rice guys, but it seems like as they expanded, the quality of their food dropped significantly. If CNR Guys are reading this, please go back to how it was a year or two ago. 

The Good: The chicken and rice aspect is still good. But it's hard to mess that up. The white sauce is good as well. The pita slices are nice and hot too. 

The Bad: The lamb has decreased in quality. It's no longer the chunky lamb you hope to find in a platter like this, but it's sliced up and doesn't feel substantial at all. 

The Ugly: The hot sauce. It's just awful now. It tastes like tabasco sauce which doesn't complement the style of food at all.

Honestly wasn't crazy about it. It's not like the pizza is terrible, but since it is billed as a "Chicago" pizza place, I must warn that it's not nearly as good as the actual Chicago stuff. And this is only like the second negative review I've ever left in my life, so you can't get me on hater status. The West Coast in general struggles with pizza, so again I'm not trying to be harsh. The service wasn't great which obviously doesn't help, but I leave my review stuck to the integrity of the food.

Beware! In the context of The Lakeside Inn, "historic" means:
* Moldy/mildewy-smelling rooms
* No curtains, just blinds that can't keep out the security lights outside
* No in-room coffee maker or cups
* No counter space in the bathroom (a free-standing sink)
* No modern plumbing (the shower water alternates between scalding and freezing every minute)
* No comfortable seating to watch television
* Only one nightstand
* Surly front desk staff
* Stairwell walls and ceilings covered with moths
* Wooden exterior doors that are rotting off the hinges

For our $259/night, the only real positives were a window that faced the lake, an air conditioner, and off-street parking. But in retrospect, we should have stayed at the Hampton Inn several miles away. Next time, we will.

The Yelp phrase corresponding to two stars reads: "Meh. I've experienced better" - and that's exactly how I feel about this place. For a girl who loves coffee shops & cute, independent stores, I'm totally unimpressed by this place, and I can tell you exactly why:


1. Speed of Service:
HOLY heck is this place slow! Since I work close by, it's convenient to come ... but I regret it every time when I'm twenty minutes in, and still food- and coffee-less. In fact, my team - which has been around here for years - has stopped going in the past few months, because they really just didn't have the time to wait around.



2. The Stock - or Lack Thereof:
More often than not, the real culprit behind the speed isn't the person making the food or coffee, but the fact that they don't have the things they need. Even though it's 3pm in the afternoon - aka that time when everyone starts to fall asleep at their desks - they'll be out of coffee, and have to brew a fresh batch. It's worse with food; here's my experience from yesterday:

I wanted a chicken caesar salad for a quick lunch. Hardly complicated - but literally fifteen minutes after my colleague and I had ordered and paid (she got the same thing), we are informed that the store doesn't have any romaine lettuce.

No ... lettuce? in a place ... that sells all variety of salads?!

(Why do I always seem to have problems with lettuce, in the bizzarest of situations?! Seriously.)

Thanks to that hiccup, my "quick lunch" takes 30 minutes just to procure (sigh)


3. Price/Quality Ratio
I'm not saying that every place has to have stellar service or always be on top of their game. But if you're not going to be top-notch, don't charge me accordingly. Mohr & McPherson Cafe is, from what I can tell, the most expensive cafe in this neighborhood ... and not only is the service slow, but the portions are small, its baked goods are often dry/stale-tasting ... not really a bargain.


Bottom Line: If you're nearby and too lazy to walk elsewhere (and also need to kill some time), then this place may be what you're looking for ... but if you're just a normal person who has a job to get back to, this detour may prove to be too costly (in all senses of the word).

My actual rating would be a 2.5. The food itself was fantastic. I'm a huge fan of their lamb and mint jelly. Their mixed drinks are also very tasty. If I had to rate on that alone I'd give it a 4. 

Unfortunately, most of the time my boyfriend and I went there we had to wait forever for our food. Not only that, but we were ignored most of the time we were there which made things like, getting our drinks refilled very difficult. 

The crowd itself is a fantastic mix and the overall atmosphere is great. However, I recommend going only if you are ok with having your meal take 2+ hrs.

My wife and I are from Oklahoma and came to Orlando to leave on our cruise. We have eaten at this restaurant before and was happy with the meal especially the salsa and guacamole which are extremely large servings. Once again we got the table side guacamole which was excellent. From our past experience we realized we would be too full from eating the chips, salsa and guacamole that we would be to full to eat a full meal so we ordered the trio and shared it. Very disappointed with this item. Although the enchiladas were tasty they were under stuffed. The chili relleno was terrible. From my experiences a chili relleno should be stuffed, dipped in a batter and deep fried. This poblano pepper was barely larger than a jalapeño, was barely stuffed with meat and cheese, then was probably put in a pan and fried. Not good at all. The rice and beans were combined in a small bowl with the rice on one side and the beans on the other. Definitely not a full serving of either and if I want them mixed together let me do it not the restaurant. Overall the guacamole and salsa is worth the trip if that is all you are going to eat.

this is my second time here. First time I just had drinks tacos and hookah. Drinks were good, tacos weren't bad, and hookah died quick. 
But second time, we ordered deviled eggs, crab cake, Mac n cheese, blacked salmon, chicken and waffles. 
Devilled eggs: not bad just really sweet. 
Crab cakes were cold in the middle. 
Mac and cheese was good. 
Blackened salmon wasn't blackened and when I told her she said well that's what the kitchen said and kept moving.
Chicken n waffles: dry. No dusse taste. Chicken nuggets pieces on top of four waffle pieces.

Went here with a gal pal for a small lunch after a shopping day. Nice staff, and we actually got seated pretty quickly. I got the fried mac n cheese and she had the Buffalo chicken tenders. The chicken tenders portion was extremely generous, which we were happy about. Our biggest gripe with the meal was that there was too much breading on both the mac n cheese and the chicken. On top of that, the mac n cheese didn't have a ton of flavor, which was pretty disappointing. This probably won't be my go-to place, but I'd come back and try something else.

MANAGEMENT NEEDS LESSONS!! Haven't been in here for awhile, so decided to eat here again instead of cooking. My husband had the burger & I had the French dip! Good was excellent! Then I discovered there are new owners & managers. The owners were nice, but the management needs improvement! Idk his name but he walked by our table at least 5 times, never once asking how we are doing or how our meal was! Instead he kept chatting w/ another table that I can only assume were friends of his. He did this to two other tables as well. Very disappointed, old management was much nicer!

Park Creek Kitchen is an odd congregation of contradictions.   There's definitely a neighborhood feel to the restaurant.  Several people were greeted as regulars while we were dining.  I could totally see a South of Lane UA dad putting on his hawaiian shirt, khakis and Keen Sandles (I swear I see variations of this outfit every time I'm out to dinner in Upper Arlington) and walking over for dinner with his family.  It's in an interesting space, too--formerly a bank building.

High concept entrees mix with classic sandwiches and burgers with varying outcomes.  My etouffee was pretty good, my wife's crab cake was a bit bland but we both agreed the mac and cheese was outstanding.

Smart decor (If you get seated towards the back of the front room you'll see the old bank vault--very cool) mixes with paper napkins and those nasty old chairs you see in fast food joints.

And fantastic bartending mixes with some off the mark cocktails--my Woodford Reserve Manhattan was spot on (and strong--holy moly), but my wife's Lemon Drop was a big miss.  

Mainly, we were a little surprised by the price of our dinner--two drinks, one appetizer, two entrees and a side ended up being over $100 with tip.  For that price, there are better options for a night out.

We have been here many times, always enjoy the wonderful food. 

Service is usually not the greatest, but tonight we experienced such rudeness that we may never go back again. Running late due to awful parking in the area, we called and were told "no problem". Once we got there, the host was exasperated and in disbelief that we called, since no note was made. They left us standing there awkwardly, seating another party of two that came in immediately. Finally and grudgingly tried to put us at the end of a large party in the middle of the room...no thank you!

Went to the Druid instead where they welcomed us with open arms, great service and a much better attitude.

There was only one girl at the counter, and two customers before me just ordered two slushies. She went ahead to prepare their drinks without saying a word to me. There was a guy behind me waiting too. My order was very simple. Just an Apple turnover. It would take just a minute.
After she finally got to me, she didn't say anything. Like "sorry for the wait". Nothing. She offered to warm up the turnover though. I agreed, not knowing that they have the oldest and slowest oven ever. I guess it's better than microwave. But so slow! 
I haven't tried that turnover yet, but I hope it was worth the wait.
I understand when the person is alone at the counter, but she had to communicate with her customers.

I want to give this place the benefit of the doubt or say it's because Colin was on vacation, but it seems like this place maybe used to be good and has gone down hill. went with my boyfriend and we each got a greasy below average grilled cheese and watered down tomato soup. My boyfriend got a hair slow cooked in his soup, which is when we decided to leave. Our drinks were okay, not so amazing that we would come back. Our dessert was stale and hard to eat. I think that if you've been a loyal customer since the start, you are likely treated better then new customers. I hope that this was just a bad day, because I feel like this place could be cool with a bit of updating and perhaps a cooking student or chef. Or for that matter, scratching the food and focusing on coffee.

Was on a bus trip to go Riverboat gambling in New Orleans- When I pulled the bus over to get Some flapjacks! However, I was disappointed when I found out what I was really in for... I ordered he Mozzarella sticks as well as a Chocolate milk, and of course a Grilled Cheese (Well done). The Sticks were solid, the waiter had a Mel Gibson-ish feel to him, and the Grilled cheese was a bit too crisp. The only positive was the chocolate milk, which was very satisfying!

I went for dinner on a Saturday night with some friends.  I hadn't been there before.

The Coronas were moderately priced at $4 each.

I ordered #24 which is a combo plate: burrito, enchilada, and chalupa.  The choice is beef or chicken, that's it for meat choices.  It seems like no matter which meat option, the chalupa is meatless (bean only) and is NOTHING like any chalupa  I've had anywhere -- not even Taco Bell.

I had it with beef and it was completely bland.  The food is, however, cheap.

The majority of the seating is on a patio, so the tables and chairs are plastic.  It's heated in the winter, but it just seems so chintzy.

started with a standard order; classic burger and fries.  no, i don't want it "crunchified", if i did i would have ordered the crunchburger, because i can read a menu and i'm not going to say "crunchified" out loud.  sat down and noticed a burger sitting on a plate at the pass, i was slightly ahead of the lunch rush with about five others.  that burger sat a solid five minutes, and i was thinking "no, it can't be mine".  well a few minutes later, yep up comes a bucket of fries and that burger that had been sitting at the pass for almost ten minutes now came over to my table like i hadn't noticed.  it wasn't bad.  it was a little cool but it was a solid burger.  well seasoned and cooked as ordered.  the fries however, they sucked.  so overcooked they just kind of went all powdery in my mouth.  the fry sauce was, i don't know, some chipotle mayo concoction.  meh.  i hate it when food comes in buckets too, that's just tacky.  the staff was friendly if not overly attentive, i barely stood up and they had swooped in and were clearing my spot before i had my coat on.  it's appreciated but no sweetheart, i don't need you to explain the condiments to me, they're condiments.  i'll give it another try, if the fries still suck then i won't be back for a third time.

We were really looking forward to trying the Captain's Boil since my wife saw the poster for the lobster roll deal starting on July 15th but were very disappointed when we went in today. 

The lobster roll had relish and mayo on it which was unusual and it also had bacon but the bacon was basically raw. The overall flavor of the lobster roll was extremely bland and when we asked for some additional sauce or something to put on it to give it some flavor they said they don't have anything at all in the kitchen that they can offer. 

Our daughter ordered the chicken teriyaki with udon and the portion of chicken was good but it too was totally flavorless and it looked like it was boiled. The teriyaki sauce came on the side to add some flavor but they only gave about 1 tablespoon worth of teriyaki sauce. 

Other people looked like they were enjoying their food but we clearly didn't have the same experience. 

The menu is quite similar to 'Holy Crab' on Robson street but the food, service, and experience is much better at Holy Crab

I'm bummed to say I wasn't impressed. Maybe I came in with too high hopes (this is fast food after all)... But with the price point at $5/ sandwich (not including fries and a drink) my expectations were right to be high. 

I got the spicy chicken sandwich with the sriracha mayo and ranch on the side. The sandwich itself came on a toasted bun with a few pickles and the meat. From my understanding the meat is locally sourced and no MSG is added - which definitely deserves a kudos for a fast food place. The bun wasn't too bad, the pickles were soggy and nothing exciting and the chicken wasn't crispy as I hoped my fried meat would be. I'll admit I did the drive thru and didn't eat my sandwich until 10-15 minutes after I got it. I will come back to try the sandwich in house for a fresher take. However, that ranch dressing was really good. They make it in house, and it's thick and well flavored. 

This being a new establishment I took my time reading the reviews before writing mine - and being a small business supporter I struggled with the low star rating, but I stick by it unless something (like a positive dine in experience) forces an update.

Great place, but be cautious at the time of payment since they based their gratuity on the whole total including tax. Which by law gratuity should only be based by the total before applying the tax. Talk to the waiter about it and the only thing he said to me is that gratuity is included if there are 5 or more people and left. 

Look online to be sure and found this: 
"The gratuity should be based on the pre-taxed amount. Your server will pay their tip-outs based on a pre-tax amount. If the grat is based on a post tax amount then you are tipping the server a much higher percentage."

Hope they don't stumble with a more stubborn guest.

I went here for lunch today, my second trip, and I do not need to go back. the meat is authentic as I had to spit out pieces of gristle and bone in almost every bite. I will admit it was a large burger and cooked right but I could not enjoy this for the chunks I had to avoid. the staff was fairly unfriendly in both taking our order and even getting a glass of water seemed to put out the lady behind the bar. the crowd was definitely an interesting mix.

Went here for lunch last month, while visiting Austin for the weekend. Many of my friends have raved about the food here. We chose to sit outside, since the decor was really cute. 

The dumplings appetizer was delicious. I enjoyed the sprinkle of crispy fried shallots on top and the ginger chili oil the dumplings were in. The oil sauce was not too spicy and had a tang of lemon. 

We waited 35 minutes for our food, after we had gotten our appetizer. Many people, who had arrived after us, had gotten their food before us. 

I ordered the specialty bánh mì. I like the bread of my bánh mì toasted. The bread was cold, and there was not anything special about its contents: pâté, roasted pork, and liver mousse. Overall, it was dry, cold, and lacked flavor. 

My boyfriend ordered the bún with flank steak. The steak was cold.

Food is pricy, which I had known looking at the menu, while waiting for our table. My bánh mì was $11, my boyfriend's bún dish was $16, and our dumplings were $12. I spent $60 on a meal that I felt was not worth $60. Our server only came to our table twice. I was very disappointed at the experience I had here.

I really don't see what all the hype is about. It's average. Yes they do have some very unique pancakes but I have not been impressed by anything on the menu. Breakfast burrito, Eggs Benedict, heuvos rancheros, and others were ok. People take about this place like its the best food ever, well if you are comparing it to Denny's then yes this place is the shit. Otherwise it's just another Egg and I or Breakfast club. Better than Ihop. But Silver grill and Grand Lux are WAAAAAY better IMO. oops almost forgot to mentions the hipsters, this place is like attack of the trendy fuckin hipsters part 2. So bring your vans, skinny jeans, and over-sized beanies. Also be prepared to see the food runners underwear (yep so trendy the management doesn't care if he is saggin his pants) and countless 30 somethings with a whitenuckle grip on their youth. PUT the bedazzled hoodie down and step away slowly!!!

My sub is good enough but I Had to get it with no lettuce because the lettuce was wilting and turning brown on the edges. The rest of the items appeared fresh enough. But VERY little selection on 'fillers'. The options were lettuce, tomato, onion, banana peppers, pickles & mayonnaise. I got a 'reg' size sub with roast beef, turkey & bacon (I think it was called the 'Mega Club' but I could be wrong) & the total came to ten dollars, seventy-something cents. It was a combo meal which included chips & a drink. With tip the total paid was $12.75.

I don't think I'll be coming back.

Two months later, and there's been no change in product availability for the items I requested they stock that are at all the other Austin area HEB stores I shop.  I didn't expect much more than lip service from the management, and sure enough, that's exactly what I got.

One bright spot?  The helpful employee in the water aisle who insisted on pointing out that the carton of water I grabbed probably wasn't what I wanted.  He persisted.  He was right.  He had read my mind.  Scary.

But, otherwise, HEB Minus.  Cue Kevin O'Leary.

A simple peanut butter and jelly was very poorly made for my son. The peanut wasn't spread on the bread, it was more of a glob and the same with the jelly. Clearly corners were cut due to the high traffic they were having during the lunch hour, but if you can't make a simple PBJ then clearly the sand which maker needs a new position. 

I have the roasted turkey and avocado, which was a very messy sand which too. This was my first time trying this so I'm not sure if it was the person who made it or if it's the sandwich itself. It was so messy that I needed a fork to eat half of my sandwich.

I swore I had written a review on Fellinis!! I use to live right next door to the Ponce location so it was definitely convenient and their late hours are a total plus. Unfortunately we began exploring other pizza joints and quickly realized that while Fellini's was convenient it was sub-par.

I came to this location recently and was quickly reminded why we stopped coming here for pizza. It's not that the pizza is over/undercooked or overly greasy. I have one problem with Fellini's and that is that they seem to cook their pizza and then after it is completely done they throw the toppings your ordered on top. They don't coat them with cheese midway through to get the proper cheesy-veggie mix. Nope they just throw them on top. So in effect, you have a cooked piece of pizza with raw veggies on top. 

I suppose if I was a raw vegetarian this would work (minus the whole cooking of the actual pizza). If you're not going to cook the toppings then why cook it at all??? 

Go down the street to Camelli's or Village Pizza.

It's a good place to watch a game and have a drink, but the food is REALLY bad and pricey.  The menu is very limited so I chose a cheeseburger.  The cheese was dried up, the burger was overcooked, and the fries were soggy.  I had this burger plus 2 beers and my total bill was $45...so it's quite expensive too.  This airport has so many food options so don't make the mistake by spending money unless you are there to watch sports.

Ok my experience was okay not the best Chinese restaurant I've been to the chicken was almost like fast food but with a high quality price I got the general Tsao chicken and I got probably three pieces of vegetables in my while dish but they do give you a side of rice my largest complaint is that they do not have vegetables with their dishes and it's way to costly not to - but i ended up paying $40 dollars for two people and two drinks. Not ok...

I REALLY don't understand the hype of this place. The sandwiches are so bland and plain. 

They don't even toast subs. They don't carry legit vegetables and for crying out loud. They only have 2-3 cheeses to choose from. 

How do you sell a roast beef sub and don't carry and cheddar. That blows my mind. Let alone toast subs. 

I mean just look at the company name. It's two first names  

I will give credit to freshness but seriously step your game up. I 

dare you to put jimmy John locations up north.

Wow, what happened?  I used to come here often, but since moving haven't been since last spring.  The menu no longer offers many of the basics (like the burritos), and I tried one of the new items and was greeted by oily fried dough and flavorless re-fried beans.  Also, the place smelled like someone vomited in the bathroom and they failed to clean it well (the smell leaked into the dining area).  And despite there being plenty of wait-staff, no one came to refill our water the entire time we sat there.  Too bad, this place used to be great.

This place has amazing food. The burgers are always so flavorful. And don't even get me started on the fries. I really love it because they have chicken burgers which at least make me feel like I'm eating healthy even if it's still smothered in cheese. I rate the location so poorly because on a Saturday at 2 pm it has taken 45 minutes to receive my food. I understand that they are full (no tables available) but for that wait I should have been warned before ordering! No one has come to acknowledge the poor service or apologize for the extreme wait. Fast casual isn't so fast anymore. Thoroughly disappointed since the food is so tasty. Make sure you visit when they're dead!

I was excited to read about West Coast Roofing because of their positive reviews. I set up an appointment for them to come give me an estimate through their website, which sent me two reminders this morning in advance of the appointment time. However, the roofer never showed up, never called, and their office is apparently closed today? Poor customer service. I'd suggest going with a company that will at least call you if they're not gonna show up to an appt that they clearly new about.

I've ordered from Beauty's for delivery to my office a few times, and the pizza is fine.  Nothing worth writing a tome about, but recently I ordered 8 pizzas for an office party 

...and they didn't show up.  

When I called Beauty's to ask where they were, the man told me they were delivered.  I pleaded my case for longer than I should have.  We have a very small office, and if there were 8 hot pizzas here, I would know it, and more-over, I wouldn't have called.  I'd be eating pizza.  Not scamming on Beauty's. 

I told him we didn't receive the pizzas, and he said they were delivered and his tone indicated this was the end of the conversation.  He told me they were delivered to the security guard at the front desk, a man with a mustache.  As far as he was concerned - the job was done.  I asked that the owner call me, and I don't think that's every going to happen.

Beware.  Horrible customer service.  They don't so much as care if they mis-delivered your pizzas.

Also, if you're in Technology Square, and you stole our pizzas, SHAME ON YOU!

You have to give one star to do a review...henna sent my husband a christmas card thanking him for his continued business and offering to buy his 2012 Chevy Cruze for120% of book value !!!!!!  my husband has never been a customer at henna and he has never owned a chevy...he drives toyotas (for the last 30 plus years)....the letter was from the service manager....i on the otherhand owned a 2012 cruze...have never been a customer at henna and never will be even though they are less than a mile from my home and my husband and i have different last names....looks like someone is delusional over at henna
