The absolute worst adoption experience you could ever encounter. If I could give zero stars I would!

After having a dog for 9 years, we decided it was time to get a second dog. We looked up Pet Rescue by Judy, read all of the information on their website about adopting, submitted an adoption application, notified our landlord and obtained written permission to get a second dog. After a few days we were contacted by the organization and began emailing back and forth with an adoption advocate and after answering several more questions, we were pre-approved to adopt a special needs dog that we selected. We made an appointment to pick her up and pay the adoption fees. 

When we arrived it was a bit chaotic but everyone was friendly and were so grateful we were adopting a "special needs" dog. We signed the contract and as I was handing over my debit card to pay, an old lady randomly asked me if MY dog was spayed. I was caught off guard by the question but was honest and said no. Suddenly the lady flipped out and said that we couldn't adopt one of their dogs and that it was their "policy". I was confused because MY dog is a female and so was the dog we were adopting. I tried to talk to this woman because I didn't understand her reasoning and she just kept repeating over and over again that she had been doing this for 26+ years and she wasn't making an exception. The other employees/volunteers looked downright horrified and embarrassed by how nasty she was being. They urged me to stay quiet and be patient while they tried to "convince" this woman to change her mind or at the very least let us foster the dog if we agreed to get our dog spayed. Nope. She only got more nasty and started talking down to my husband and I and then went on to lecture us and roll her eyes when she found out who our vet was (which by the way we've been using for 9 years). We pointed out that NO WHERE on the website does it say existing dogs in the home must be spayed or neutered, which she admitted to, but was VERY shady when we repeatedly asked her why it's not something they say up front. On our application we even stated that our dog was not spayed and we were still allowed to continue with the adoption process.

After finally realizing we would not be allowed to adopt (we waited an HOUR until the other employees/volunteers gave up trying to convince her), one of the volunteers apologized for the way we were treated and told us that if we took OUR dog to get spayed, we could come back and adopt. She also admitted that the nasty woman that made us feel like horrible human beings was THE Judy from Pet Rescue by Judy and that she's nasty to everyone and isn't a "people person". She told us that if we do decide to come back to do so because we care about the dog despite how poorly the organization's owner treats people trying to adopt. 

There are so many dogs available for adoption through other organizations, please do not waste your time, feelings, or money adopting a dog from an awful organization like this one. Here are some other organizations to consider:

Orange County Animal Services
Pet Alliance of Greater Orlando 
South Lake Animal League
Florida Little Dog Rescue

***UPDATE***
A few months later (October 2015 to be exact) we adopted a dog from Orange County Animal Services and let me tell you, the experience was beyond my expectations! The employees were sweet and friendly and the adoption process is easy breezy. They let you wander around as long as you'd like to browse from their huge selection of breeds, which to my surprise, included plenty of puppies. The price to adopt a dog is $55 but they often have promotions and specials if you're on a budget. By the end of October both my 9 yr. old dog and my newly adopted dog (2 yrs. old) were spayed/neutered...and we did it because we wanted to, not because it was forced upon us.

New to Atlanta, we had not yet established primary care for our daughter and when she woke up with a fever my wife took her to the Smart Primary Care in Brookhaven. With potential for a sore throat the doctor called in a prescription to the local pharmacy. However, despite being told of an allergy to a specific medicine, the doctor prescribed a derivative medicine that she was still allergic to. My wife was unaware the derivative could also present an allergic reaction and headed home with the medicine.

When I heard what was prescribed I recognized the derivative as potentially problematic and called the doctor. The doctor was busy and no one else could address our questions so I called the pharmacy. During that call it was made clear the derivative medicine could also invoke an allergic reaction. I then called the doctor's office back telling the person who answered what I had learned from the pharmacist. He confirmed that my daughter's medical record indicated the drug allergy and he said he would notify the doctor and call me back. Shortly thereafter he called back with a new prescription and confirmed the doctor had made a mistake despite clear drug allergy information in her medical record. We will not be returning to a Smart Primary Care again.

My company offers an amazing insurance plan with almost unlimited chiropractic benefits, so I thought, let's see what all the fuss is about.  I saw Ms. Zygmont for mild lower back pain that comes around when I start lifting stuff.  

The first red flag was how they insisted on taking extensive X-rays of my back as standard practice.  Generally, chiropractors should only take x-rays for patients who have suffered traumatic injury or are over 70 years of age.  I am neither.  After exposing me to high levels of radiation without a second thought, it turned out my spine was healthy.  I was expecting a mild adjustment, and maybe some preventative advice on back care.  

However, Ms. Zygmont recommended a long-term treatment plan for my intermittent "lower back issue", starting with my coming in on a daily basis for an entire week!  She had me do the whole shebang, including the electrical stimulation, adjustments, massage, and physical therapy.  The front desk was aggressive about scheduling me to come in the following day for another adjustment, and, giving them the benefit of the doubt despite a bad feeling in my gut, I came in.  Little did I know that I was to undergo the stimulation, therapy, massage, and physical therapy as well, without any justification.  They had the balls to try to reschedule me for the next day, but I put an end to it.

Looking over the insurance claims and seeing the $1100 they charged my insurer for those two days, I realize that Zygmont Chiropractic took maximum advantage of the generous chiropractic benefits of my insurer for a patient who didn't need these treatments.  

Zygmont is no different from any other sheisty chiropractor.  I imagine that with the increased overhead from their new location, such exploitative practices will just get worse.  Stay away.

I felt I was being misled, tricked or and cheated.                                                                                                                                                             

I was told I would not have any more pain, yet I was still in pain.  (later I had to go to another dentist, who told me whoever did the extraction did not clean it thoroughly, thus, infection was still there). 

I was told I only needed to pay $93, now, I am asked to pay extra. Had I been told your insurance might not cover everything, in which case, you may need to pay additional. I would definitely left, as I would not want to pay more than $100 to get a tooth take out.

WORST COMPANY EVER! My spring broke a few months ago and I called them out to replace it. The only good thing I have to say is they came out on a Friday at 4pm (which is the only reason I called them). Other than that, they told me I had circuitboard and motor issues. I fixed it with them along with other door "needs." They installed a keypad and threw away my other one without consulting me (that I bought 2 months earlier). Their keypad didn't work initially. They said to push the buttons harder. It has been spotty for the last few months. Just bought a new car (a 2020) and tried to sync it with the garage and it's not compatible. The garage door keypad has also stopped working. I tried to buy a new one at HomeDepot and nothing is compatible (shocker). I called them out and they wanted to charge me $89 just for a technician to come look at it! They are scammers who convince you to buy their products that are not compatible with anything AND when you have an issue, no one can fix it except them so you have to pay their ridiculous prices. Save yourself a headache and use ANYONE else. Run away from this company!

Paid $3300 for a move, it's now taken a week, "estimated 3-5 days, but they don't deliver on weekends. Tried calling and a very rude lady just kept saying it's "estimated, AGAIN, it's estimated. For this kind of money I'll definitely go somewhere else. My pod sat in Kansas City for 5 days. I started a new job and have no clean clothes now, and no washer and dryer. Will never use this company again and I will recommend others not to.

Is it a restaurant? Is it a food truck? It's mostly tortilla, not much flavor in the protein, and they say they're open when they are not. I called trying to find out if they were open for lunch, they were not even though their hours say otherwise. Stopped by on another occasion on my way home from work  for lunch and stood next to the food truck outside for 10min before seeing a person come out of it who didn't acknowledge me until I asked him repeatedly if they were open to which he replied "no" while he was prepping food. 

Long story short, they're rude, don't seem to adhere to any sort of schedule, and the food isn't great... wish I could give them less than a star.

Poor scheduling processes. We usually try to make an appointment and still have to wait 20-30 minutes. After waiting over 30 minutes for a toddler haircut last time (2 months ago) I decided I wouldn't bother with even making an appointment again. Yesterday, I brought my son in for a haircut without an appointment and was told it would be a 45 minute wait. There was 1 lady working and she appeared to be finishing up a haircut for an older gentleman (which was bizarre). A haircut for my son should take less than 10 minutes and it was at 11am on a Tuesday. So we decided to go over to Supercuts where we received very friendly, welcoming service immediately and for half the price. The Supercuts haircut was great quality and better value for my money and time. I love the idea of taking my kids to Cool Cuts for the "fun" experience, even if it costs more, however, the unwelcoming staff and dingy storefront will prevent us from being customers and recommending Cool Cuts to friends in the future. I hope that this store can make necessary changes to continue to stay open.

My first ever visit to Cabela's, and now my last. Two events or the prices of one. The facility is nice, nice decor, but I have never seen such bad customer service. When I ask for a specific product from a salesperson, the last thing I expect to hear is, "Check down there by the last aisle. It's somewhere over there." It happened to me three different times with three different salespeople while looking for three different items. Three strikes and your out! I gave up after spending forty minutes in this store looking for the right items. I finally became completely disappointed and left. These people are the most unprofessional floor salespeople I have ever seen

I couldn't be more upset with how I was treated but more importantly my son. This is truly when keeping it real goes wrong. My son grew up in a Barbershop until his Godfather passed away five years ago and closed the shop. His Dad was a barber and he stopped cutting. We moved to Florida and he struggled to find someone he trusted. I will not say any names but I was given a Black Barber name as a recommendation. My son loved how he cut so we would make the 50 minute drive. My son now goes to school in MD and plays Basketball. His team was getting interviewed by Steven A. when he returned. He wanted to cut all his hair off and chose this Barber to do it. I reached out and got a 10:30 appointment. We left 1.5hr early because a Saturday in Orlando has traffic. I got there at 10:35 and my son walked in. The Barber barely made eye contact and told him he was late and could not take him. I walked in to confirm if he said he couldn't take him now or not at all. He immediately got defense. Saying I should have called and so what if I live 50 minutes away, he lives an hour away. He told me when I made the appointment he could take me at 10:30 because he had a 10am. Then he told me I was his first and he came early for me. I honestly think he made a mistake and didn't apologize when he realized it. Instead he went on to tell me how he's a Barber and this is a Business. Then maybe he shouldn't have been raising his voice when I only came to clarify. I owned a Salon before returning to corporate America and have a huge respect for the art. I had my two year old in the car and was literally at the light at 10:30am so I didn't think it was necessary to pick up the phone. He was clearly half way through the client head in his chair. That does not take 5 minutes. He had to start him earlier then 10:30. My son was so upset because he has been preparing for this day to cut his three year hair growth off. So I went back in and asked if I could have someone else. He clearly sent me to a guy who was not as comfortable with Black men cuts or experienced in general. They only charge $18 but no matter what I always pay $40 so I don't understand why that guy was such a prick. I know this is long but I hope he learns from this. My son may be famous and he tossed the chance of being his barber out the window because of five minutes.

My wife and I went out to see our favorite comedian Bruce Bruce last night.  We have been to the Improv in Brea, California and Las Vegas, Nevada. We enjoy the ambience and sitting arrangements that the Improv venue provides to their guests.  The venue at The Pointe Orlando was very unpleasant to say the least.  It was a packed house. The 3 comedians were very funny and put on a great show despite the heat.  The ambience was like being in a "sauna". Most of the guests including my wife and I were using the menus as fan to cool off. My wife ordered "Bernie Mac and cheese with grilled shrimp, the food was below room temperature and tasteless. If Mr. Budd Friedman was in the audience, he would have been extremely disappointed with the managers on duty and their lack of concern, even after we complained along with several others.  The 3 comics on stage were also complaining and how hot and stuffy it was.

Where's the zero star option? There is NO management here.  They are simply token.  The common areas are not cleaned.  They don't work normal work hours.  Need something attended to between 6pm and 10am? Well forget it.  They often leave emails and calls unanswered.  I can't imagine if I didn't return messages in my job, I would be fired!

There is NO security presence.  Last week someone tried to get into our apartment while my wife was home alone.  Probably someone drunk and misplaced, but the point is, calling "security" means at least a 45 minute wait (based on past experience, they simply aren't around).  By then calling the cops would have been faster.  This is more than a "keeping the place respectable" issue, its a SAFETY issue.

The walls are paper thin.  I feel bad for some because having a small gathering and playing music a a reasonable level will cause neighbors to send in reports.  No one's fault other than the developers who decided sound proofing was optional.  Then there's the W construction next door, again if the build quality was better.   I won't even go into the finish quality inside the units.  Ok, I will, CHEAP!

They rent to college kids (via their parents) which treat the place like a frat house.  Again, this might be mitigated by some sort of security presence but, as said, there is none.  

I cannot wait to move out.  Do not rent here, no matter what the incentive.  You've been warned.

Letterpress is beyond disappointing and i caution anyone who considers going there to think again.

Saturday night, Magical Dining, we walked into a cavernous space that is best compared to a caferia. The section with the most desirable tables in the place were curiously closed. Apparently "set up from breakfast" 

The service was incredibly slow despite only 5 tables seated. Our waiter had an overwhelming scent of body odor that completely put us off dinner. True story -- how can a responsible restaurant manager not address that?

The food was just OK and the large portions... too large in fact.... did not make up for it.

All in all, it is resto that i wish i never attended and vow to never again. The best i can do is warn others not to repeat our mistake.

Pass, even with a  groupon. For an Italian restaurant ( or any that is suppose to be fine dining) they have one of the smallest wine lists we have ever seen. The restaurant itself had no atmosphere. A large room with three rows of tables. As far as dinner goes,we started out with the calamari which was so salty that we had to send it back. The foccacia which  was suppose to be seasoned didn't have any and came along with a spread that had absolutely no flavor. I ordered the Ragout of Lamb, the sauce which had a few slices of olives that were extremely salty, and if it wasn't  for the pepper , it wouldnt of had any flavor. Had some trouble finding the lamb in it.  I'm not sure, but it could of came out of a can. My partner had the grilled steak which was nicely cooked to a medium-rare, a few mushrooms ( rubbery) and greens that were also a bit bland. The one good thing is the waiter we had knew how to pour wine ( yes there is more to it than justing opening the bottle and filling a glass).

I have been to Jam a few times, each time a frustrating experience and after this visit I won't be going back.  They don't answer their phones. EVER. Wait time on weekends is hours to get in then an hour or more for food.  When I went there this time for breakfast (on a weekday) I waited in line for 1 hour 15 minutes.  Then after we were seated waited 25 minutes for someone to take our our order, we almost left except that we'd already invested so much time here.  The food took another 45 minutes to be served.  My food came out and the presentation was nice at first, then I took a bite, it was totally charred black on the underneath side.  I intended to request a new dish.  I sat patiently while my dining companions ate.  The server never checked back.  Finally when everyone was done eating the server brought the check, seeing that my plate hadn't (but one bite) been touched offered to get me something new.   I said I didn't want to wait for another meal nor make my friends wait while I ate by myself.  He gave me a coupon for $7 off my next meal after 4pm.  A better coupon would have been come back for the same breakfast meal but non-charred and you don't have to wait hours for it.  I did not enjoy my experience at Jam on Hawthorne at all and I don't understand why so many people put up with their wait times and service.

Did you know that these Sears outlets are really not part of Sears? They are franchised and owned independently. They have working relations with Sears but while you can get a great deal it can be a problem. Not only do they take Sears defective items they also purchase from other sources. So I purchased a Samsung dryer and they tell me I have a one year manufactures warranty. Four days after the purchase the dryer is installed and it has no heat. Call the store and they give us Sears repair number. Sears repair says they can't do anything and that we need to call Samsung repair. I asked why their outlet store would give me their number and that's when Sears said the outlets stores are really not part of Sears. I called Samsung repair and gave them the model number and serial number and they say that unit is not on warranty and that I had to send them a receipt. End up taking the dryer back and they credit my account. I asked them to sell me another dryer that's marked about $20 higher and the assistant manager said she has to get authorization. I asked her to call her manager and she said the person who authorizes the discount is her managers boss, a DM type person from Sears? Wait they are not part of Sears or are they? Great values but risky if there's an issue. Oh and if you call them, it seems like they put you on speaker phone.

Too many things that weren't great about this place. Definitely not a place I would ever go for a special occasion. It was just "okay" Drinks were good. Dessert for my birthday was not edible. When making the reservation, they asked if I had a special request and I said yes, it's my birthday please make it special! We were seated in the worst area next to a huge party and a table of wild kids! When I asked if we could be seated else where the manager said there was no where else to sit. Tables opened up but he never came back to check on us. Waiter had zero personality and we had to ask about the menu. Not sure why this place gets such rave reviews, but like I said it was just okay.

Man were we disappointed.  We had been here three years ago with our kids.  It was a winter's night in Boston and we were staying around the corner at the W.  It was warm and inviting, full of people and the food was good.  But this time, it was really bad.  The server simply disappeared after awhile, never clearing our plates, and brought the kids milkshakes that were not fully processed.  The waitress told the kids they "needed to stir..."  

My fish and chips were basically inedible.  The nachos were OK, but my wife's french onion soup was just awful.  Something happened to this place in the years since we were there.  My guess is that it could -- and should -- close soon.  Sorry, and I hate to say this, but it's time for this place to go.

Store #91 on LaVista Rd. OMG!!!! Doesn't this look good? Well, I wouldn't freaking know cause it's been 30 min since I got my meal but I hate to eat when the rest of my table is waiting for their food. No drinks when they were ordered and it was our friends birthday, 10 in the party and we had 3 servers. It makes no DAMN sense and I'm not happy at all. They don't do well with groups, I think it's too much for them and they can't handle them. It's been a long time since I'm been to a Red Lobster and after tonight, it may very well be my last or it will be a very long time before I visit again. NOT VERY HAPPY.

As a Preferred Avis First member for several years, I can easily say this is the worst Avis I have been to! After 3 of my employees were told they couldn't pick up the car, I had to create a new reservation. 

My Preferred employee with her infant child, and 8 months into her high-risk pregnancy was forced to stand in the elements for over an hour.

I had to return from my meeting 30 minutes away to address this issue when Nancy told us she could "now" honor my original reservation. 

Over an hour and a half later, you finally did your job and act like you want a cookie because you did me a favor?  Now can you compensate me for my time, or missed meetings? How about staying up all night with an employee on monitors.

This type of performance is why I would recommend you use any car company other than Avis in Orlando.

If there was a way to give zero, these people earned it.

Spoke with sales rep Sal who told me he would take care of getting me set up with internet, TV and phone at new house.  Installer Justin comes and installs my modem and 3 wireless receivers for TV and one receiver that is directly connected to modem.  For the first 10 days the TVs were very glitchy which made for irritating TV watching.  I talk to Sal who said get a wifi extender cause your house is too big and it should solve problem.  I go put and buy Google wifi extender 255.00.  I get home follow all the instructions and my internet is blazing fast and reliable.  I then realize all my wifi boxes are not working but, my wired one is.  I goto the gateway which gives signal to receivers and reset.  Still nothing, I run through all the trouble shooting still no TV.  Next day which is day 13 of service I call and spent 1 hour 39 minutes on the phone with att.  Just trying to get the wireless boxes removed and wired boxes installed.  Only to be told we value you as a customer and we will have someone out in 6 days to swap the boxes out.  I then feel that the solution is a horrible one and ask for them to pick up equipment and I will go with Spectrum.  Then I was told that will cost you 360.00.  If you go with att dont be surprised of you find yourself in my shoes.  See attachment and look at time I spent talking to them.

I'm not one to complain- but I literally made a yelp account to review this place. My friend and I came here to have our nails done (full sets). Both my friend and I had nail techs that had a very hard time getting our shape correct and even, and even after voicing our concerns, they did nothing to fix them. In fact, they proceeded to loudly (and obviously) talk about us. My cuticles are practically torn to shreds, and all in all, I'm extremely disappointed with the services here. I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone.

The absolute worst Publix in Atlanta. No matter what time you go in they will probably be out of fired chicken wings. I've been going here for several years and they are always out. You would think they would cook more plan better but nope! They have instead adopted the we're doing you a favor operations style. So when you mention something to them they get a serious attitude the deli manager had the nerve to say we're busy. I'm done with this horrible place. The whole management team is HORRIBLE FULL OF EXCUSES!

This is the worst hotel and it's sad because it's right on international dr I only stayed one night because I had no other choice but the tv was broken it smelled like cigarettes and other odors .i had my daughter with me and my daughter did not like it all we couldn't even take a shower because the bath tub was dirty so soap no coffee and the elevator was making weird noises that we thought we got stuck I travel to Orlando because we're annual pass holders so we do this very often it's just sad that I paid 80 and I couldn't even take a shower or enjoy my hotel stay .!!!!!!(NEVER STAY HERE) ohh and the front desk no help stall I asked to be changed and they said they were sold out and there was people leaving right in front of me .what is upsetting that they think were stupid but is there loss because my money won't be spend here again . Ohhh and I forgot to mention the hookers and drug use around the whole property...

Stay far away from this place. I've ordered through their "app" twice now, and both times I arrived only to find my sandwich wasn't even started - even though most of the workers were just sitting around outside since it apparently wasn't busy.  My last experience there will be the last time I eat at Subway, especially this location.  I was insulted by the employees as they made my sandwich, which should've been ready at least 5-10 minutes prior to my arrival.  In Addition, they made my steak and cheese sandwich with cold steak (didn't even heat it up) and barely enough meat to even be called a sandwich.  When I asked for more meat, which even another customer said was warranted because it was two small spoonfuls on a 12" sub, that's when I started getting stares and insulted by the employees, including the person whom I assume was the supervisor, even though she was on a personal phone call taking on her earbuds the whole time.  Needless to say, this Subway location ruined it for me.  I'll happily go to all the other local sandwich shops that don't charge $9+ for a crappy sub.

Came in with a friend today to ask about prices for touching up her commemorative tattoo. The owner belittled her staff in-front of us, bounced three figures around before settling on 120.00 as a touch up fee, and then proceeded to lecture my adult friend about 'legal' tattoo policies. She was very judgmental, aggressive, and confrontational from the beginning. Honestly, the only people who get tattoos on Hawthorne are kids who don't know any better, and tourists visiting for a week. Take the time to find an artist you can establish a connection and get a good rapport with. I doubt that will happen with anyone here.

I had a horrible experience at this restaurant - so I was compelled to join this website to talk about it. I was planning a dinner for 10 people that were flying in from out of town. I made a reservation and gave the host my credit card number to reserve a table. That Saturday we arrived and they didn't have my reservation on file. They did absolutely nothing for us. It was 8:30 on Saturday - luckily we went to Rocca and found space in the lounge. Double check your reservation with this place. Horrible service!!!!!!!!!!

I simply just came here for a wash & blow dry. Waited a half hour for my appointment. The woman who brought me to the sink realized there was purple dye in it from the previous client after the fact that my hair was already in it (awesome). Thankfully she switched me over to another sink. Brought me to her chair, then said my hair was too tangly and that I need to be under the dryer. I know I have tangly hair but I have never had this issue anywhere else. Everyone else has just brushed through it and blow dried it no problem. 
Still kept c/o about my hair. 

Floors are FILTHY. 
Salon is dirty.
Left with my hair still wet, paid $45 to go home and finish the rest!
Never again.

After doing some on line research on where to take my party of nine to brunch, we selected the Hawthorne Street Cafe based on good ratings.  Unfortunately, our experience did not match the reviews.  First, we waited for 50 minutes instead of the estimated 20 mins we were told when we arrived-had we known we would wait so long we would have gone elsewhere and I believe they knew this.  While we waited, parties of 2, 3 & 4 came in and were seated-completely ruining our chances of having smaller tables combined to seat our larger group.  When our meals came, three of the nine were not good. Not a single employee returned for water/coffee refills or to check if we needed anything else, not even the owner who claimed to "love everyone" asked how we liked our food.  And lastly, even though three plates of food were left virtually untouched on our table, because we were a larger party an 18% gratuity was added to our bill.  Ordinarily I would keep service separate from the food quality but none of it was good and deserving of 18%.  All around, a bad experience.  I would bet no one in our party will return to the Hawthorne Street Cafe.

This review is only for the hostess, since we didn't get to try the quality of the place itself. My partner and I came here at 9 pm on a Monday night for drinks. After standing awkwardly by the door for a minute, the hostess finally came out from the back and greeted us with an annoyed: "Can I help you with anything?" That's an actual quote. I should have known right there and then. Given the late-ish hour, most tables were empty but the bar was full. We asked her if we could be seated at a high table that's right by the bar (or literally at any other table, since almost all of them were available), but she said no. For drinks, she told us, the only two seats left were  in an awkard corner between the bar and the window. We actually tried to sit there because we really wanted to try out this place, but it was just too uncomfortable. So instead we left, wondering what crowds could possibly show up to have dinner after 9 pm on a Monday night to justify keeping all those empty tables and losing two customers. I sincerely hope that being a biracial couple had nothing to do with why she treated us that way (but the place had no diversity at all tonight, so unfortunately I did have to wonder). We were both still wearing business casual from the day at work, so I know for sure it was not that. In the end, we took our business elsewhere and had a lovely evening, but it's a shame that some places still make people feel uncomfortable like this in 2018.

By far the worst experience I have ever had at closing.  From a slow to zero response on questions and concerns to a misinterpretation of language in a legal court document.  Positively certain all documentation and actions taken at closing are illegal and complaints have been made to the BBB.

If your looking for a professional office I would look elsewhere.  Closing with this firm cost me thousands.  It seems they were more concerned with their time restrictions and commissions than what was laid out for them in black and white.   

If you are being helped by a Sarah lee Schroeder our Jacquelin hill I would strongly suggest other agents but more importantly if a firm is willing to hire incompetent, dishonest employees, go elsewhere.  

Too many good people here in Austin to choose from.

I wouldn't send my worst enemy to this dump.
I have had better clam chowder out of a can. Oyster stew had a bit more flavor but basically just a handful of oysters swimming in a bowl of cream.
Cajun shrimp app... 6 small shrimp on a skewer served on a plate with a piece of lettuce on the side, no individual plates, no silverware...
It was as if some kid was playing restaurant and this was their best shot at presentation.  Scallops wrapped in bacon... not too bad but the bacon was overlooked.... same presentation issues, however they did bring me a fork this time.
Wife's fish sandwich was served on a soggy roll that looked like it was salvaged from a defunct Howard Johnson's. The fish itself was edible but it looked like bad hospital cafeteria food. The top of the bun didn't last past the first bite before it crumbled into pieces and had to be discarded.
Guinness was the highlight of the meal. Kudos to whoever was pouring on the bar. All of this for the low, low price of $81. 
Needless to say I will never step foot in the joint... and will encourage others to stay away too.

We eat sushi fairly often - and we tend to avoid Aji - just because it doesn't feel authentic and the quality in the past has seemed only so-so.  Last night - struggling to find an option quick and nearby we hit up Aji again for take-away.  The food (again) only tasted so-so (not screaming freshness).  Last night at 1:15a my son woke up to some serious tummy-trouble (explosive diarrhea) - and when I woke up at 5a I had the same (and still have now - for two hours).  We otherwise feel fine - so I think it's safe to assume we had some bad sushi.  My wife and daughter - who didn't eat sushi were/are totally fine.  Uch...I hate to do this to you Aji...but that was definitely the last time for us at Aji and I'm gonna have to caution others on eating here as well.

My reservation was for 2:30pm. Food didn't arrive to my table until 4:05pm. It was a total of 4 tables 10 people. The service was absolutely terrible from the entry staff to the waitress who told us she was about to quit, Lord only knows what was going on in the kitchen. On top of service being less than, they didn't have soda, bloody Mary's, salad dressing just anything. This was the worst experience I've received at Del Frisco. Erica the waitress could've been more attentive. The manager Justin could've accepted more accountability for the lack of service that was provided. I will not be returning to Del Frisco and wouldn't recommend anyone to eat here.

I had the worst make up ever.!  I had to go to someone else to fix it. I wish I had taken pictures before and after to show the difference.  Fortunately, there was a miscommunication and didn't have to pay the $70 dollars for special occasions make up, but only the $45 for  the "regular" make up. I had called the day before and had been quoted $45 even thought I had said it was for a Gala.  I was shocked when they tried to charge me $70.

Yup. A year and a half later and nothing has changed. Tried it one more time and never again. The sauce had moderate taste this time at least (Spicy garlic). The wings however...the wings. Mushy, greasy, zero crispyness. Presentation is nil when taking out. Can't speak for eating in. Overpriced. And the s***s the next morning. There is still no contact form on their website, 18 months later. Attempted to contact them on Facebook. Their response was prompt asking for details of the die-in experience. I gave them time and date details. Told them is was a take-out. They never responded back after multiple prompts.

Very little to do only thing worth seeing is chef's table. Still expensive for $5 to get in event to pay $4 for a tiny plate of food. There weren't many free samples at all. There were tons of food trucks selling their food at normal prices, I don't need to pay $5 to get in this event when I can see the trucks any other time. 

Event has gone downhill. Better if I saved took my money to food cart festival, vegetarian fest or beer fest. Worth my money.

How hard is it to find a reservation and hand out a key? With an average counter time of 15 minutes PER CUSTOMER, you can imagine how long it took with only 7 people in front of us. If it's an employee issue, train them better. If it's a system issue, invest in better systems. Don't let the fake reviews fool you. No matter how good the vehicle is and the prices are, it still only gets one star because of the extremely poor customer service. Nobody wants to wait an extra hour and a half after landing at midnight to simply get the keys to a car we already reserved.

Flew in for a business trip and got in really late. This was the pizza place the hotel clerk gave me the number for and I ordered - Big Mistake

Order placed 1:25
Delivery Estimate - 45 mins
First phone call stating they would be another 10 mins - 2:10
Second call that they were right around the corner - 2:30
Pizza delivered - 2:45

Pizza is AT BEST Luke warm. The pepperoni is bland and the cheese/crust are average. Maybe it would taste better if it were hot, but who knows. Maybe carry out is the way, but do not get it for delivery.

Tusker House will always be the place I had to wait 40 minutes past our reservation time to get seated and broke down into pregnant tears in the waiting area (which had little seating) because I was dehydrated and hungry beyond reason. It will also be the place that never even apologized for any of this mess. 
The food is okay at best. The roast beef was overdone. Couscous was super bland. We didn't get to meet all of the characters because we had to rush to make it to our next fast pass because of the delay. 
Our honeymoon had to get changed last minute because I got pregnant and could no longer go to Zika infested tropical waters. So this was supposed to be the last meal of our substitute honeymoon at Disney.  We paid over $100 for the two of us for this crappy food and crappy consumer service. I can't warn people away enough.
I also just can't believe that Disney has gone so downhill that we didn't even get an apology.

Be aware of your insurance information! 
This place claims to be in-network, but also claims they use a 3rd party to appear in-network so they charge more than the in-network contracted rates. My insurance shows that a root canal on a molar is $840 with their contracts, but they wanted to charge over $1,000 for it (both quotes are just the procedure rate.) 
I filed a complaint with my insurance company to get them removed from the in-network list, but I'm sure my insurance company isn't the only one with this issue.
I did not end up using their services because that extra charge would have been out of my pocket so I cannot review their actual service experience.

I called the shop and explained I have a 3rd party warranty and an AC issue. Their inclination on the phone is "no problem bring it in and we will take a look at it". I brought my car in for diagnostics only. I was not informed there would be a charge for this service. They called me to inform me that my issue was not covered under the warranty and would cost me nearly $2000.00. I advised I would be unable to pay that at this time. They took it upon themselves to complete other things and charge me nearly $200.00 for services I did not authorize during "diagnostics". I wouldn't get my car fixed here ever. Shady crooks.

Holy crap has the customer service gone downhill. Actually it's in the toilet. Not that they were exceptionally friendly before but now it's like you, the customer, are a total inconvenience and they don't really want to be here (even though I think hey are the owners!). I did not believe this to be true. After our call completed I immediately hung up and called the store manager myself and was connected to him within 2 to 5 minutes. I've explained that I spoke to the woman that is the assistant manager of the bakery and he pauses and says "I'm unsure whom you spoke to, I do not have a woman that is an assistant manager for my bakery." So then I explain this is Lie number two. My cake was wrong, I was only half compensated, and now I was lied too about who I was speaking to. The manager sympathized and immediately offered me my full compensation. Mind you my story is not over yet. As soon as I left work immediately went to the Publix location to get my compensation. As I approach customer service the representative was very nice as I handed her the receipt and explained that Spoke to John the general store manager and was advised to reference our previous conversation. To my surprise John 
, the General store manager was having a conversation with another customer to my right. As the representative cashed me out he looked me in my face and did not say a word! Not even a single apology for what happened to me. I would've thought a face-to-face apology would've been in order however my cries and frustration was overlooked as a customer even by the lead of the store. I have never had this type of service at Publix as I will never be a customer at this location again. I can't believe this day!

I really wanted to enjoy this place as there were so many positive reviews. I am a bit of a foody and cook at home at least six nights a week so it's a treat to go out to eat and I have high expectations when going out to eat from the kitchens of professionals. I want the meal to taste more delicious than what I could cook at home. My parents owned a restaurant for over 20 years, so I know what cooked to order food is like.  

I had seen some negative reviews on google and trip advisor, but yelp is my go to, default location for restaurant recommendations. Our dinner was not, in fact, cooked to order, unless you consider microwaving to order as an equivalent. 

I read a review on another site complaining that they microwaved their french bread and was skeptical of the reviewer. We did in fact order the bread and it was definitely microwaved because it was warm, but the moisture had been whisked away. The music is low so it was difficult to have a private conversation at your table and I could hear the microwave multiple times in the kitchen. I kept imaging what Gordon Ramsay might have to say in an episode of Kitchen Nightmares. 

My bourguignon was ok, but my friend's rabbit was very dry, most likely because it was microwaved. Additionally, the rice that was offered as a side was dry and, again, microwaved. You could tell because of the chunks that were clumped together and hard and inedible. The bourguignon had some decent flavor, but the rabbit was not at all delicious. 

I just want to be able to offer another perspective for those expecting high quality French cuisine. If you expect the cuisine of French restaurants in New York or LA, you will be sorely disappointed. 

I do believe if they did have fresh ingredients, cooked to order, and threw away their microwave, there could be some delicious meals here at Au Rendez-Vous. Until then, I would steer clear.

My husband and I were refered to Aspire by my OB. We had been trying to get pregnant for the better half of a year. We decided to try IUI.

 I felt very rushed through every appointment. When the day came I asked them if they checked to see if I had already ovulated, as the IUI procedure was expensive and I thought I may have already ovulated. They scoffed at me and said the trigger shot would have made sure I ovulated. But right after I already could have? I would think they would go ahead and check just to ease my anxiety. That did not happen. 

The day I was suppose to get my period I received a phone call from one of the nurses. She asked if I started to bleed. Those were her words. I informed her not yet. She straight out says, you're not pregnant. Call us when you start to bleed and we'll figure out what you want to do next. Not only was this the most unprofessional, insensitive phone call, she gave me no further information. Being in a vulnerable situation I was beyond disturbed by the lack of empathy from this nurse. Clearly she and few other employees are in the wrong field of work. 

Fortunately, I had an appointment with the wonderful and amazing acupuncturist located in the office and informed her what had happened the day before. She gave me the information the woman who worked in the clinic failed to. 

I decided right then that we were done trying. We had been through so much emotionally for the last year and their treatment of me was the absolute worst. I DO NOT recommend using their services. Please find a clinic that practices empathy and gives you the attention and information you deserve.

Never come here! They tell you a lot of lies and have a very deceiving haggling process. 

I came in to search for new 2018 Kia Sorentos, because there is a manufacturer discount on those, up to $5,000 in cash. 

When I came in, the first thing I asked for were the 2018's Kia Sorentos. The seller (S****t), started lying.  Some of the lies he told us:
- Well, you know, our best deals are actually on the 2019's. Truth: he just didn't have any 2018's. 
- The 2018 is now considered a used car, you will not get the same warranty. Truth: it is not, is just a different model year. 

Then he showed us the 2019, we liked it, and the haggling started. 

First he said that the car cost $45,049. That is a lie. The MRSP for the 2019 Kia Sorento EX Premium which was the car that we were looking at is $42,950.00. There are tons of tire shops in this area of town, so there's really no need to use these guys.  I needed new tires, so I called, made sure the tires were available in-house, and made an appointment for 8 a.m., the first appointment of the day.  Even with an appointment -- and few other customers -- it took these folks an hour and a half to put four tires on the Honda, a job that can be done by any qualified tire jockey in less than 30 minutes -- without breaking a sweat!  So, why did it take so long?  Well, I watched my mechanic stand around in the office and talk for the first 45 minutes of my appointment -- with me sitting there.  After an hour, I looked through the windows into the bay, and saw the mechanic slowly turning a lug nut with one hand, while he kept his other hand jammed in his pants pocket!  Here's a little hint, guys: When doing manual labor, it goes a lot faster when you use BOTH hands.  It's obvious management allots an hour and a half to change a set of tires, and the mechanics are going to do their utmost to make sure the job isn't finished any sooner.  They jerked me around and made me waste my time, not because they were busy, but because they could.  I'll never be back.

I leased a new A5 Cabriolet from this dealership and had a very pleasant experience until I had to deal with their Finance Department. Do not go into the closing meeting by yourself, because you will be sold and sold and sold on protection packages that you don't really need, and that will jack the price of your car up thousands of dollars. Signing on the car was a phony and soul-sucking experience that defaces the Audi brand.

The A5 Cabrio also ended up having several leaks, a problem I had to bring the car in for four times over 5 months until I told them I wanted another car. Every time I was told the car was fixed and tested, and every time rain would spill in between the windows and roof line. When I did return the car none of the expensive maintenance plans I paid for up front on the Cabrio was refunded. And although the sales rep Jay Levy and the service rep Daniele Flanagan were great, and continue to be, I was for the most part made to feel like the car's malfunction was my fault (and I found exactly the same issue with another A5 Cabriolet owner online in about 2 minutes of searching). 

So buyer beware. Great selection, convenient location, super cars for winter weather (providing they don't leak) but don't close on a car without a wingman here. And don't forget to save all your service receipts.

On our last visit, we were asked as we sat down if we wanted chips & salsa.  Of course we want chips & salsa, it's a given anytime you sit down in a Mexican restaurant that they are included for free!  But no...we received the bill and were charged for chips & salsa -- charged for chips & salsa?!  This is unheard of of.  So I asked our waitress what the deal is with this little charge she snuck into our bill, and she replied that they now charge for chips & salsa unless you order queso or guacamole.  Wellllll don't you think she could have mentioned that when she flippantly asked if we'd like chips & salsa before we had even opened our menus and read about these new charges?  Based on principle alone, we won't be back -- we are THAT annoyed with how it was handled.

The 2 last visits were our last:
1 months ago my husband as usual tried among other dishes the carapulcra and he was trowing up all night and was sick to work next day. We also noticed in one of our past visits previous to us getting sick that one of the male cooks after lunch hours was cleaning the bathrooms without cloves and them going back to the kitchen still without cloves. Aghhh seriously? That moment we though of course that he could washed his hands in the kitchen which still aghhh gross and maybe that's why people get sick eating there. 
We will never ever come back, sorry Susana but your lock of integrity among your competition and for not following up to phone calls about your customers getting sick for eating are your restaurant it's a very bad way of doing business. 
And yes there are other better Peruvian restaurants in the area which we tried and the taste is wow completely different plus the authentic Peruvians people are cooking them. 
Be aware of going to this restaurant, if you want to eat popular taste this is the place to go but if you really want to try good Peruvian good please don't cheat your self look in austin south, central and round rock you will be amazed. 
We traveled to peru 2 times now and we can tell the difference in the taste and quality. 
Oh by the way most of Lima Criolla reviews are from their friends, family and related people around their owners circle as we had being informed during a get together at a latín/Peruvian event. 
We do not recommended this restaurant for lock of integrity, professionalism, service, cleanses and so so food.

The reason for this Bad review is because of the customer service!!! Tara who claimes to be the manager was not accommodating. My massage Therapist was great!!
