Ok that was the good part... and then less good was the skewer... it was cooked well and overall wasn't offensive but it walked the line as it was so caked with salt and other seasonings that I could barely identify it as a piece of meat at all. ... and then... the comedic "piece de resistance"... the noodle bowl I was so excited for.
This noodle bowl was literally nearly indistinguishable from a can of Campbell's canned beef and vegetable soups. It was full of overcooked  potatoes, gelatinous carrots, grey green beans and peas just like your favorite lunch you ate when you were five years old. It tastes like a can of soup and a few squirts of Sri racha. .. but the "hand pulled" noodles were great, right? Well, maybe at some point they were noodles but what was served to me was almost mush, they had been over cooked or perhaps sitting in water for too long... not sure but they tasted like... well like the noodles from a can of soup. 
Then it occurred to me- maybe this is a play in the classic childhood bowl of soup meant to tug on the nostalgic heart strings of a weary traveler like myself... nope- I looked on the restaurants website and the photos of the dish looks very different.
Something went wrong here, very wrong. Don't risk it and certainly don't make the mistake of going out of your way to try what sounds like an exciting Chinese style dining experience- it wasn't even a dining experience for me because I couldn't barely finish 10% of the dish before I threw it in a bus box.

I wish I could give this place negative 10 stars. My recent experience has left me completely disheartened, not for the horrendous service of this establishment alone, but for the general authority bouncers, managers and owners believe they have over their patrons. This review can pertain to both men and women, but as a woman who was accused of having a fake I.D., separated from my group of friends and dragged out by a man double my height and width, I am especially writing this in the hopes that someone else will see it and it won't happen to them. 

I was allowed in at the door with this supposed "fake I.D.", paid the $5 cover, and bought a round of drinks for my friends with my credit card. They held on to my I.D. at the bar, and when I went to close out my tab, the bartender immediately got the bouncer. This man held me by my arm and my back and I was not allowed to tell my group of friends. He pushed me through the crowd, and when I reached the door the manager, a squat, gray haired man, took my I.D. like it was trash and put it in his pocket. I showed him my passport, and he informed me that both my license and my passport were "the fakest ones he's ever seen". They did not call the police. They did not have any procedure. They simply wanted to victimize me, as I'm sure they have done and will continue to do. After 45 minutes, during which time my friends were involved and the police were called (by me, not the establishment), another bouncer came out with a stack of I.D.s and shuffled through them to return mine.

 The problem here is this: when I contacted the Operations Manager, he told me that they have no real procedure. They pick and choose whose I.D.'s they confiscate. They do not notify the police. They do not give the "fakes" to the police. They "throw them in the trash the next morning". I'm hearing through other people that they sell these I.D.'s. The Operations Manager has since refused to return my calls and no action has been taken against the bouncer. They gave me no explanation of why they pushed me out of the place, or why they selected my my I.D. as a fake, but I suspect it was because they supposed I was vulnerable - a woman "alone" closing out her tab. Easy target. Luckily, I am not one to play the part of victim, but I wanted to write this review as a lesson, a warning to all.

I'm relatively new to Yelp and I am trying to build up my reviews, so after numerous trips to Kickass I feel compelled to put my constant disappointment out there.

Kickass has a cool name, is in a great location, and has great SOUNDING cupcakes, yet they continue to disappoint me!  I've gone back several times because I didn't want to give up hope on them, but I gotta break down and say it.  This place kinda sucks.

Kickass? More like Blows Chunks.

They say to never judge a book by it's cover. In fact, I gave this place several tries. Ladies and gentlemen...some books should be judged by their cover.

First off, the ambiance. It's dark in there. And I'm not talking "sexy" dark, I'm talking "weird maybe I shouldn't sit down and eat in here because something un-sexy may happen to me" dark. So the majority of the time I just ordered my stuff to go. Next, the customer service. They aren't rude, but they're definitely not friendly. At first I just chalked this up to them being busy. But then I went in there when they weren't busy and got the same treatment. Basically, a "gimme your money, here's your food, now get the hell out" vibe. Finally, the food. The flavoring isn't bad at all and is just as suitable a gut-filler as any other Austin Chinese restaurant. However, when I'm presented with a plate overflowing with fried rice, I expect to find more than four tiny shrimp and two tiny packets of soy sauce. 

So my suggestion is that if you find yourself literally dying of hunger and can't possibly crawl across the street to McDonald's without getting hit by cars, then visit this place. Otherwise, I'd say stay clear of this place.

Don't waste your money or time. Fado's is blocks away and miles better.

My significant other and I are moving to a foreign country with our cat, and specifically called ahead of time to make sure that VCA could fill out the paperwork and perform the necessary tests on our cat. We informed them of our travel dates and they said they were able to do everything we needed and to come on in.

We went to Lori Feldman, who had some good reviews, but as soon as we started talking with her she told us the paperwork had to be filled in within 10 days of our flight. So, okay, that was the main reason we came, and this stipulation was NOT mentioned by the front office, but she assured us that she could still complete the necessary tests.

Lori then told us that Nietzche (our cat) had a heart murmur, which was very upsetting to hear. She recommended we come in for a $500 EKG the next week to "see if he could fly or not". Because we are not millionaires, we decided to get a second opinion before spending another $500.

Fast forward a few weeks to my significant other taking Nietzche to her family vet in Miami. Imagine her surprise to find out that they have to redo the $300 worth of tests because THOSE also need to be done within 10 days of our flight.  I wish Lori Feldman had filled us in on that before subjecting Nietzche to what sounded like some very painful tests (based on his yowling from the next room).

Oh, and they also couldn't hear any signs of a heart murmur after carefully examining him twice.  As we suspected, that $500 EKG would have been nothing more than a waste of our already meager funds.

Thank you, Lori Feldman, for attempting to weasel $800 (and successfully weaseling $300) from a young couple who just want to travel safely with their cat. 

I am also VERY attached to this cat and almost cried when I was told he may have a heart murmur. I hope she can sleep at night.

In the meantime, I would recommend that anyone who values their pet and their financial stability stay far away from this profitable clinic, and find a place that actually cares about the health of their patients.

We were there last Sunday (4/26/15) celebrating our anniversary. We had already been there once for Sunday brunch and we decided to give it another try, since the first experience had not been good.

We got there before 9 am and got in line. We asked if it was possible to sit downstairs at the bar and we were informed to we could just go inside (instead of waiting for a table), since the bar was apparently empty.
Yes - it was "apparently" empty. There were around 5 or 6 employees congregating at the bar downstairs. And the presence of customers did not intimidate them at all. From the time we got there (9am) until the time we left (10:30am), there were still a few of them laughing out loudly, as if that was not their workplace, but their living room, instead. 

We went upstairs to get some food and suddenly there is a waitress chastising us - in front of everybody else - because, apparently, we could not have started serving our plates from the specific table where we were. We should get in line, in front of the other table, and then move to the other tables from there. 

First of all, there is no indication/signal or anything whatsoever to inform the customers about where the line is supposed to start or from what table we are supposed to serve our plates from.
And the thing is: we wanted the specific food which was on the specific table where we went. And there was absolutely nobody else at that table. Which means: we were not cutting the line in front of anyone else. If there was a line for that specific table, we would have followed it.

Now: why on earth would I have to get in line at - what was supposed to be - the "main table" or the "starting table", since what we wanted was on the other table?

We are not to be blamed for the fact that the space is not well divided and well organized, and they allow the place to get so packed that you can hardly move around.

It was an extremely unpleasant situation and the tone that she used was extremely rude. I tried to explain to her why we were serving from the other table, but she just walked away.

Apart from the "incident with the waitress" and the "congregation of employees at the bar", the amount of people allowed inside while they wait for a table is ridiculous. While we were eating there were at least 3 different groups standing close by and staring at us in order to see when we were leaving, so that they could have our seats. It is uncomfortable, to say the least. And it is also a sign of mismanagement, just like having untrained staff.

Needless to say: We will not be returning. The experience starts with good service. And they lack it.

-I LOVE SPICY. I asked to make kimchi jijae extra spicy and was told "only regular spicy"
-they don't do raw eggs being dropped in the hot soup anymore

My oh My where do I start? My first time visitng Florida. It was late my flight got in around 11pm. This place was still open around midnight. Went in and the place was completely dead. We were the only customer inside so of course we were seated right away. I am usually not a picky person when I'm hungry late at night. Not sure if I was tired but right when I look at the utensil I wanted to walk out of the restaurant. 
I try to not pick at the disgusting utensil. Order my food and 4 out of 5 items my friends and I order. The appetizer was the only thing pleasing to eat. The burger was horrible, the steak was worst than frozen entree, the country steak was overcooked. All the side trimming that came with our serving was like cafeteria food. 
NEVER AGAINNNNNNN!!!  )=/

STAY FAAAR AWAY FROM THIS BOGUS COMPANY!!! 
The absolute WORST service you could ever get set up with, or at least the WORST we've ever had. Its been nothing but a constant nightmare side day one. Due to being far more trouble than its worth, we've given up on TV and basically watch netflix instead. Had an appointment scheduled with Reliable and got the time range of 10am-2pm arrival. Received a call around 1pm that he was due to arrive in 20 minutes. I requested him to text me when he got to my home as I was assisting my movers in the backyard and wouldn't be able to hear the doorbell.  He texted me and I went around to the front of my home and he was driving away. I called but got the office line so I quickly texted. He texted me back stating he left as he rang the doorbell 3 times and no one answered. So I'd have to call office to reschedule. Seriously? Customer service at its finest folks. Now imagine the workmanship you'd receive. Nothing like taking time off of work for that. I'm still in mild disbelief that people can actually suck that bad. 

So that's my experience

Masu has gone downhill. I was here about 8 years ago and it's not as good. The Panders bros mural is gone for one. 
Experience: It's expensive, portions are very small (don't get the wagyu), service was fine at lunch, and the music was awful. Don't come here with someone that has mobility issues.

The miso was too salty, edamame bland, the salmon roll was flacid and luke warm, did not taste very fresh. The ramen was ok, a bit salty too, nothing exceptional I'm afraid. My wife had a nice roll that had more flavour than just salt. 
I've eaten at most sushi places around town as well as a few in Tokyo and this place just can't hold a candle to any of it.  I expected more for what we paid and I won't be returning.

It's common knowledge that most mechanic shops try to charge extra for stuff you don't need when they think you don't know a lot about cars... guess it worked for them this time, because I really don't know anything about cars. That's why I come to a mechanic... that I trust will help me because they DO know what's going on. 

Asked for a basic oil change (expecting they would use normal oil)... I should have checked the receipt when I left but they put in the MOST EXPENSIVE OIL without asking me. Ended up paying a whole bunch of money I didn't sign up for because they took advantage of me.

Posting this so the next person who doesn't know a lot about cars will know to clarify what kind of oil they want.... instead of trusting the mechanic to fulfill the request to the best of their ability. :(

The moral of the story is, nobody at this McDonald's communicates with each other OR the guests.

It's my right to determine if I want to give the server tips depending on his/her professional behavior. What a joke! Asking for tips??? Worst nail job of my life. My friend and I went for the $20 shellac. I'm only giving one star because I have to to write a review.
The women were both servicing multiple customers at once, and were not friendly to us. 
My nails were filed, but not in any particular shape, and not smoothly. Several of my nails have weird angles on them now. She used cuticle clippers on my cuticles, and she did a terrible job of it. There are frayed (not white the right word...) edges on my cuticles now. I kept wanting to take the tools away from her and do it myself.
When she started painting my nail, I asked for #63, a bright rose color. She started painting and I said, "Oh wait, that looks really red!" She said, "Yes!", and kept painting. They look like Dorothy's ruby slippers.
The lady who was doing my friend's nails didn't even bring the right nail polish. She also chastised my friend for something she hadn't done in reaction to the light color of the nail polish (because she brought the wrong polish...).
After my nails were done, she wiped them down and started the massage. I literally was involuntarily yanking my arm back in pain. She didn't even notice. My arm still hurts a bit, an hour later. The lotion also made my skin start to itch, but she told me I could jot wash my hands. 
Then she left to do a pedicure, not even waiting for payment. I sat there for probably 15 minutes before my friend's nail lady finally decided to settle our payments.
One of my nails was painted to the skin. Once I peeled it away, I had to scrape off a strip of polish at the end and then file when I got home. I also had to clip several hangnails that she created.

I traveled down to Portland and really wanted to check this place out. I had read great things about it. However, the table had rice on it. No one bothered to wipe it down. Geez, give me a rag and I'll do it!
The menu had zero dietary guidelines on it. No GF or vegan options. Hmm. I wonder about that. Must be a legal thing.
The coffee was served in a glass, I burned my hand grabbing it. And the glass was scratched up.
The coffee creamer pourer also was scratched up. 
I asked if coffee came with a refill. I was told yes. My girlfriend was offered a refill on her cup. But I was not offered one on mine. I kid you not. Like ok, I'm paying for this....please some service. 
The bathroom doubles as the employee locker room. It hasnt been cleaned in who knows how long. The trash was overflowing and smelling awful. The kitchen is located just outside the locker room changing room/bathroom. Yikes. 
I'm sure he's making money not buying coffee mugs and emptying the trash but at what cost?

These people deserve a zero star rating. Walk away if your home warranty service company tell you to use them tell no. 

I took off an entire afternoon since our air conditioning isn't working. These guys never showed up and never called to say they weren't coming. When I called to ask them why they never showed they said they were here. We have cameras and they were never ever here. 

The worst part is when I called him out for lying he hung up on me. What a waste of my time and money.

My daughter is actively looking to purchase a vehicle and found a used Hyundai Santa Fe online at Mirak Hyundai.  I drove down on a Friday, met with a salesman, looked at the car and let him know that due to our schedules, we would both come in on Monday morning to test drive the Santa Fe.  Sunday evening I exchanged multiple emails with the salesman and confirmed that we would be there Monday morning around 10:30am which was fine.  We arrived with the usual pleasantries and he said let me go get the car, returning five minutes later telling me that the Santa Fe was sold on SATURDAY.  The next comment out of his mouth was "no problem.........we have plenty more to look at".  We left, never to return.  In my eyes either this was the old "bait and switch" or total incompetence as this is not a large dealership or superstore dealing in 1000+ autos on the lot.  Yes I have previously purchased at Mirak in the past, No I will not return again.

This place used to be good, now it's horrible. The entire place is filthy, the floors look like they never mop. Sticky, dirty, wrappers everywhere. Vinyl booth seats dirty. The bathrooms are atrocious, looks like they haven't been cleaned in weeks. Wasn't even close to what i was expecting. Personally looks like a stomach virus waiting to happen. I showed up with my family around 7 or 8ish..and viewed the layout..it looked bare. Very unprofessional. Im not sure how they got licensed. We have several rentals. I sent him to several properties. To our surprise the diagnosis was always the same. The lady taking the orders, preparing the food & taking the money was very rude! She raised her voice at me because I didn't tell her what kind of sauce I wanted on my rice fast enough. I placed an order here through Grubhub (to use my PayPal account). When i parked, noticed an email stating my order was cancelled. Hmmm. Ok. The email was very vague and generic. Didn't really explain why the cancellation occured. I called the restaurant to see what was going on. Phone number doesn't work. How unprofessional. Called Grubhub to get an explanation. The food is good, the waitress we have had a few times is fun and friendly, it's too bad she's moving to Australia. However, I won't be back.

The downfall of this place is that for somewhere that says "good for children," they don't seem to care about changing a baby. I obviously do not expect her to change circumstances beyond her control, like the lack of changing tables, but her attitude sucked. I wish I'd changed her on the empty table next to us, but I'm not an a**hole so I did it in my car.

Very disappointed! They don't have much of a selection in store. All their guns are in "the warehouse". I went to do a routine physical exam, but the physician added some other exams during the visit without telling me that not included in the routine checkup and needs extra charge until I got the bill. I felt so cheated and the staff was really unprofessional. When I discussed with them about this issue, the representative at their finical department had a bad attitude and immediately denied their responsibility. I am thinking about changing to another hospital, and would not recommend it to anyone I know.

Very disappointed in this location!  Long time Chipotle customers, but young kids make it difficult to stand in line so we started ordering online.  The first time we did this, we were given two burritos full of steak fat .., just chewy fat not steak.  The second time we did this, one burrito was normal and the other had only 5 small pieces of steak in the entire burrito!  As such one burrito was twice the size of the other, even though they were identical orders!  Never had this experience at any chipotle when ordering in person, and because this has happened twice with online orders, I can only conclude that they think they can get away with this because the customer is not watching them make the food.  Hopefully this is exclusive to this location but I'd suggest never ordering online and avoiding this location.  They did offer to remake it, but with a to go order you don't notice this until you're already home.  Not enough compensation in my opinion.

Disclaimer - review is for Newton Highlands location ONLY. Newton Centre is great - good selection of products, professional and knowledgeable sales people. Go here instead.

That being said, the Highlands store may have the absolute worst customer service I've ever experienced. I never even write reviews but felt compelled to for this as I sit here on my phone in my car shocked.  I just walked out of the store wondering what the  f*** I did to deserve such treatment. The woman who "helped" me look for a travel adapter / converter was actually mean. Rude, sarcastic, abrasive and kept cutting me off when asking questions. When I politely! declined to make a purchase because I just wanted to get out of there, she made a big show of abruptly running back to her counter and disingenuously wishing me a nice day in a very intentional way. I actually thought I was being punked or something. The whole thing was very bizarre. Ugh.

Sigh...I hate it when I really want to enjoy a night out of dining with friends, and the restaurant we choose seemingly does not want this to happen.  

A friend of mine recently moved to Quincy, and my man and I decided to go visit him, and dine at Fuji 1546, because we had all stopped in there once before, and thought it seemed cool.  sigh...

To me, Fuji is the antithesis of what a good sushi restaurant should be.  Most importantly, the ambiance is way off.  I think of sushi being a peaceful experience, if somewhat exotic at times.   Fuji was loud and strange on a Friday night, full of south shore dudes who may or may not have gone to my high school... with large flat screen TVs showing the Red Sox game.  The actual interior design was cool and modern, but this place has a pretty busy bar scene, and the whole thing just didn't sit right with me.

After waiting quite a while longer than expected for a table (thanks to the GIANT theatre-sized Red Sox-showing plasma screen in the dining room!?!?!) we finally were seated and ordered up a grand amount of apps, sushi, and a couple of entrees...which was not without debacle.  My husband ordered an acid-cooked NY strip steak entree, which our clueless waitress had no idea was on the menu, and kept trying to confirm as the filet mignon entree, which was much more expensive.  After showing her the menu to confirm that the dish existed, we thought things were fine.  Then another waitress came over to tell my husband that they were out of that, but that there was filet mignon...then walked away without giving him a menu.  When we flagged down our waitress again, my man grabbed a menu and ordered some pork dish...and we thought that was the end of it...until our freaking waitress came back AGAIN to ask my husband if he wanted the filet mignon!?!?!?  Maddening.

Long story short, the waitstaff was inattentive and clueless and our sushi and entrees ended up coming out so far apart from each other that all of us were done eating when my husband's food finally came out (which by the way was nasty and gristly, and cooked completely to death).  Also, did I mention that the menu here offers such yucky offerings as sushi hand rolls containing ingredients like mozzarella cheese, bacon, and hamburger...ack!   Cheese and sushi don't mix...at least not in my mouth.

To be fair tho, I should mention that the tetaki tuna was delicious (the only star i'm awarding goes to that), and my lemongrass chicken wasn't too bad...a bit bland but edible.

I did not actually receive the message I booked online. When I arrived I was informed that the masseuse I was matched to only gave very light messages, even though I had requested medium to firm. The receptionist is the one that told me I would not be satisfied with the message so I should reschedule. I can understand there could be a glitch in the online scheduling, but if they knew that was the case, I should have been notified before wasting my time driving there. I will not be rescheduling, and if I do visit a Massage Envy in the future, it will not be at the Quincy location.

Tried an online store first for glasses, I've had good luck with that but my wife had an awful time getting progressive lenses that worked. So we went with a traditional store nearby, and had an equally bad experience.   The clerk ignored us for a good 15 minutes, and then when we got the measurements and frames done we had a second shock at the prices; not at all what they advertise on the wall of the shop!  Even after insurance, we were out over $200.  

They never contacted us when the glasses were ready.  We ended up waiting an extra two weeks more than necessary to pick them up!  After all that, you would think that at least the glasses would be good; but while they are better than the online glasses my wife got originally, the frame was loose on this set so that one eye was focused at a higher horizontal plane than the other.  We only found this out after my wife went back to the eye doctor complaining that her eyes were hurting after using the glasses.  

Avoid this place at all costs; the location does not make up for the lousy service and prices.

I made an appointment 2 weeks ago for my bridesmaids to try on a handful of dresses at 3pm. We waited at the counter for at least 5 minutes before anyone (including the 2 women behind the counter) said a word to us. Once we were acknowledged we were informed that we would have to wait so that the associate could finish with another customer (who did not appear to have an appointment). Nonetheless we were fine to hang out and chat for a bit, HOWEVER when at 03:48pm we wanted to try on one more dress our consultant promptly discouraged us and told us to hurry because we were " Almost out of time" ( despite the fact our appointment started late). The consultant collected the styles I requested ( the ones they had, despite this being an official Alfred Angelo store and the only one in Atlanta,  they don't carry all of their Signature collection bridesmaids dresses). She placed 2 dresses in each room Room 1: size 6 Room 2: 8 Room 3: 12 and then asked my bridesmaids who would fit in each size, as one of my friends walked towards Room 2 Kierra, the consultant, stopped her and informed her that she was " Much thicker" than my Maid of Honor and should try on the size 12. My jaw dropped I couldn't believe someone who is supposed to help brides and their bridesmaids find a dress for the most important day of their life would say something so insensitive and down right rude. We didn't say anything about it and continued with our appointment, Kierra couldn't have been more disinterested in helping us. After they tried on the dresses without any help from her, she wrote up the style numbers we liked and then walked away. We waited for a while and finally decided that she was making herself scarce so we would leave and that's exactly what we did. My bridesmaids and I are fairly easy going we came in knowing what styles we wanted to try and fully intended to purchase them today; however given the terrible service we received and their limited selection we were very disappointed and although we will be ordering Alfredo Angelo dresses it will NOT be from their store!

Eye exams here are way overpriced.
Antoinette Dumalo charges $107 for a "complete" eye exam and updated prescription. But if you wear contacts, you are hit with an additional $80 charge when you show up for your appointment, for a total of $187.  She will refuse to discuss anything relating to your wearing of contact lenses during the so-called "complete" eye exam unless you pay the extra fee. This optometrist seems more concerned about profit than good customer service.

You chose not to take responsibility and cover your employee's "miscommunication." This in my mind does not reflect concern for the patient. When MSP stopped covering eye exams, we were told to expect to pay a fee of "around $80." Not two separate fees if you happen to wear both glasses and contacts and happen to have questions about your use of both. What next, separate charges for left and right eyes? I have ONE pair of eyes, not two. A basic exam should be an opportunity for a customer to discuss any concerns related to their vision correction.

Stay away from these people.  They automatically withhold a "cleaning fee" from your deposit regardless of how clean your place is.  They sometimes don't respond to maintenance requests for months at a time.  They increased the rent on my apartment in the middle of the first year of my lease.  Overall a horrible experience.


Edit in response to comment by Regency: actually, the the statute that you cited says that you MAY deduct the cost of carpet cleaning regardless of whether or not the carpet needs to be cleaned.  So yes, you are legally entitled to charge me for carpet cleaning even if you don't need to clean the carpet.  I'm not disagreeing with that. What I'm saying is that charging tenants for carpet cleaning when the carpet does not need to be cleaned is a bad business practice that does not put the customer first and reflects poorly on you.  Second, I am also aware that you did not officially increase the rent on my apartment.  I was referring to the $40 per month fee for water that you started charging me after I moved in.  I have lived in enough houses to know that no one person ever uses $40 of water in one month.  So, why were you charging me for water that I was not using? Was it maybe so that you could get around the law that prevents you from raising my rent in the middle of a lease term?  I'll give you this: you people at least put enough effort into your sheistiness to remain technically within the limits of the law, if not within the limits of ethical business practices.

I went in to find some bug spray and Heat (which I did not know what department to look in).  

The store looked dingy:  A little dirty and poorly lit.  The space between the racks was super large, and there was a lot of empty space.  It looked like the store had very little inventory.

I counted the people in there.  It was Thursday around noon, and there were 12 customers total.  It may be an off hour, but that is still not many customers!

I asked where the bug spray is and the person I asked sighed and looked bored and said, " Down there!" pointing somewhere vague.  "After the camping items and before the laundry items."  So, I walked a bit and then guessed where "down there" was.  I could not find the item. 

So, I asked someone else.  She showed me, but I did not find bug spray, only repellent, and she said that is all they have.  I asked for "heat", but she had never heard of it.  

So, I left.  

I would not shop at Walmart due to their store policies and reputation for not providing health care for their employees, but my friend who is fixing my roof suggested I would find what I needed there for the roof job.  Well, I did not find what I need, and I will not shop there again.  

I went to ACE and got good service and found what I needed rapidly.

Routes car rental company is very unprofessional in the way the customers are treated. upon arrival, i had to wait 3 hours for the vehicle and the reason given for the long wait was due to a lack of staff.

Upon returning the vehicle, an invoice was provided with 0 value beacuse it had already been paid for. 

3 months later routes decided to charge me through credit card of a sum which they would not explain to me what the charges was. i called the customer service hotline and they mentioned that they cannot assist and i would have to write them an email, which i did.

they responded with why they charged me was  for a shortfall without providing any information and did not respond to me thereafter.

i strongly do not recommend this rental company to anyone should you want a car rental. you will be best to go for a respectable company e.g. hertz, avis etc.

This is a place located in the middle of Atlanta. I heard that this place has a reputation of being a chef's restaurant. The location is open late, and it is a very intimate place. I found the place very crowded and hard to maneuver around. Additionally, a lot of the food is over priced and quite unhealthy for the heart. 

I had the pleasure of eating at this place multiple times, and I must say that the experiences were not consistent. 

The Pork Buns was too sweet for me. Most importantly, very greasy and fattening. The flavors were not mixed well together because it contained too sweet and too salty. Additionally, the greased buns did not help it go down the throat easily. 

The Bread Company Soft Pretzel was your typical pretzel, but over drenched with salt and grease. After consuming the pretzel, it left me wanting coke to wash down the salt and great out of my mouth and tongue. 

Cornmeal Fried Oysters were terrible idea because I should have known that if the restaurant is going to grease and fatten everything the place serves, the restaurant will take a full advantage with a fried food. 

Farm Egg and Carbonara pasta was actually filling for a small dish, and it was very good. The carbonara sauce contained a lot of cheese and butter, and it was very easy to spot the sauce's rich flavor and fat after the first bite. 

Bacon Caramel Apple was too sweet and greasy for me. It's more unhealthy than the movie theater popcorn. Instead of the butter the theater popcorn uses, this popcorn is covered with bacon fat. 

The Daily Raw Oysters were ok. It's not the most fresh tasting oysters, I was able to spot the taste and the smell of "sea." Real fresh oysters are not supposed to have that smell or taste of sea, but these did. 

Lastly, the almighty burger that the restaurant serves late nights for limited time and supply. Not worth the wait, money, time, and stomach. If you want a good burger, then try Bocado. I feel that Ronald had a better idea about burgers in McDonald's than these Holeman and Finch Burgers. The pickles in these burgers were so sweet that it overwhelmed the burger itself. Additionally, the bun were covered with grease, and the patty might as well been lard. The burger was flavorless and the fries that came with it was wet with oil. When I took a first bite, I felt as if a ball of grease was going down my throat. The patty was moist, but in a wrong way. It was so oily and fattening, that it had to be "moist." Making it "limited" raises the hype about the burgers, but the burger was very disappointing. I felt like I wanted to clean out my arteries after consuming this burger. Bottom line, this burger is tasteless, greasy, and too sweet. 

Overall, I wouldn't go back to this place unless I have to. The restaurant is very cramped, and the food is greasier than Varsity burgers put together with a fat kid's  skin. I find the place completely overpriced and over hyped. Additionally, the flavors of every dish is overpowered by the wrong ingredients. Either the chef has lost a lot of his or her taste buds due too much smoking and drinking or he or she just loves overpowering every dish with random ingredients that throw the entire dish off. 

Don't take your hot dates here because you're going to be wasting your money.

This review is for the new Reflections location on W. Morse Blvd. in Winter Park. The receptionist at their original location is super friendly, so I'm not sure what happened here.

I arrived for my 8:30 appointment at 8:15, so I'd have time to complete new patient paperwork. The front doors were locked, so I just waited outside for someone to arrive--I didn't knock, look into the windows or try to get anyone's attention. An older lady with short blonde hair and glasses--clearly annoyed and talking on her phone--threw open the door and accusingly asked me when my appointment was. By this time, it was about 8:20--a perfectly reasonable time to arrive for an 8:30 appointment--but she was visually annoyed and pointed for me to go upstairs. No greeting or acknowledgement, whatsoever. She didn't even stop talking on her phone to tell me where to go. 

Tip: Don't schedule 8:30 appointments if your staff can't arrive early enough. 

My wait time was short (during which I completed my new patient paperwork), but my appointment was shorter. I went to have some moles and a small scar checked out. The PA looked at them for about 30 seconds, then went on to recommend products for acne--which was not the purpose of my appointment. She spent the next several minutes up-selling prescriptions and products, taking no time to 1.) ask about my skin and its sensitivity, 2.) explain how these products worked or 3.) find out which products I was already using. The entire appointment was maybe five minutes long.

Finally, when I went to checkout, the receptionist was curt and told me someone else would take my payment, like wanting to pay was a total inconvenience to her. 

The only person who was actually pleasant in the office was the nurse who brought me into the exam room. 

TL;DR: I paid $75 to deal with rude staff members and listen to product pitches. Go here for zero help and a bunch of products you don't want.

The theater (Charles Playhouse) is HORRIBLE!!!!  We paid HUNDREDS of dollars for my wife and I to take our 3 kids here for our son's birthday.  We sat in the balcony, on the side.  We could not see a single thing!  At all.  Nothing.
My wife and I could barely make out the top right side of the stage...and my kids could see absolutely nothing.
At one point my kids stood up so they could at least see a little bit.  (We were not blocking anybody - there was nobody behind us).  The woman working there came and told us we had to sit down!  Why???  
So basically we threw away hundreds of dollars for absolutely NOTHING!!!

First, this is absolutely not New York style pizza.  Just because you have a similar crust doesn't justify the tag.  Second, every NYC joint I've ever been to has a case full of pizza you can choose from. You pick your slice(s) and BOOM a few bucks later, you're in heaven. I ordered fresh mozzarella on a slice and got it on top of a regular cheese slice.  The reason why I ordered fresh mozz is because I didn't want regular cheese.  This place charges an arm and a leg for some attitude and a label.  You want good pizza in Atlanta?  Go to Camellis.  Trust me.  Places like this who claim to be NYC style should be ashamed.  I lived in New York, I know.

I went through the drive-through on 6/3/20 and ordered a torta with some ingredients removed. When I got home, the torta was made completely unlike what I ordered even though the order was correct on the receipt. I called the restaurant and asked to speak to a manager and a young woman came on the phone named Angela R. She confirmed she was the manager. I explained what happened and said that it had taken a really long time to go through the drive through and I was tired and wasn't coming back to get a new order and asked for a refund. She was very nice and even offered to refund me AND give me another torta free which I said was not necessary as mistakes happen. She got my receipt number and confirmed she'd refund me and I should see it within 3 days. On 6/12/20 I still hadn't gotten the refund so I called them back and was told she was not working but said I could talk to the manager. 

The manager, Mario, came on the line and after explaining why I was calling, he proceeded to give me quite a hassle, why was I calling 9 days later, Angela is not the manager only a cashier, etc. I had to repeat the same thing over and over for several minutes and finally I asked him if he was going to give me the refund I was promised and he said he would be but only for one order. I kept saying I wasn't asking for anything else, only what I had paid for but didn't receive. I'm sure there was a language barrier because he was obviously struggling to repeat back what I was saying and that didn't bother me. What did was his accusatory tone and his insinuations that I was lying about talking to Angela because she's not a manager. 

After 15 minutes of his rude customer service, he said he would refund me and I should see it on my card in 2 days. I've already been told this by a much nicer employee than him, and given his tone and rude behavior, I don't have a lot of confidence he will actually refund me. 

I was going to also tell him about my experience on Sunday, 6/7/20, when I ordered the same item again, a torta with no guacamole or mayo. Again I got home but this time the torta I ordered which should have had carne asada, cheese, refried beans, lettuce and pico de gallo, only had a very small lump of steak and some grated cheese. There was a lot of bread that had no meat at all and the bread had been squished down to 1/16 of an inch. My friend who ordered a surf and turf burrito (and this was his first time there) got hardly any steak or shrimp. He was not impressed. 

Last week I called in an order at 10:00 a.m. from work for me and two coworkers and explained that I needed to pick up the food right at 12 noon as we only had 30 minutes for lunch. When I arrived at noon, the order wasn't even started. I asked why and the same manager, Mario, came out and told me it was because I didn't pay in advance. The woman who took my order didn't tell me that or ask for payment. When I told him this, he acted like he didn't believe me. So of course I was late getting back with the food and my coworkers and I couldn't eat our lunch because we had to get back on the phone. Of the 5 times I've ordered there in the last month, every order had something wrong with it. Twice I've had to deal with the manager and both times it was a negative experience. 

But the experience on the phone with Mario, the manager tonight, sealed the deal. I am never going to spend my money there again because there's no consistency with the food, they make lots of order mistakes, and then the manager is rude and hassles you when you tell him you didn't get what you paid for. Buyer beware, this is not a restaurant that cares about its customers.

I would have loved to write a great review about this restaurant, however, I never got the chance to. Apparently the cooking of their BBQ is not the only thing that's slow around here. I walked in through the take out door and there was a sign that instructed me to walk to the bar to place my order. So I walked up to the bar to place my order however there was no bartender there. I noticed a menu, pulled it out, started looking at it, and there was an employee walking towards me with her phone in her ear. I looked at her, not sure if she noticed my tiny 6'3" 265 lb frame standing within arm's length from her but apparently either she missed me or her phone conversation was more important because she never acknowledged me. I had to get to the airport, so I left. Businesses like this shouldn't complain about economic times when you keep failing to take opportunities for a sale, I'm surprised they're even in business. Maybe it's a Florida thing.

Waste of time and money. Ordered online at 10:18p for 10:40p pick up, arrived at 10:40 and waited 10 more minutes before receiving cold and disgusting food. Very unorganized pick up/to-go order line. Despite the long wait and crowd of people the employees didn't show any frustration or attitude towards customers but that wasn't enough to make me want to eat at a hooters ever again. I wish I could get my $20 back for food that was worth less than $5.

You get what you pay for... and maybe a little less.  My husband had been going here out of convenience and after his last visit we decided enough is enough.  His most recent visit left him with a stark line running around the middle of his head (not blended), much shorter on one side than the other, and the trim along the outer edges was uneven and way too high (clearly she had trouble making a straight line so she just kept buzzing higher and higher).   He said it looked like she was really struggling.   He couldn't go to work looking like that so I spent 30 minutes at home just trying to salvage the cut.  Previously he had told the stylist "I want texture on top and just don't want it to flip up in the front".  All she understood was "You want a flip? ok I'll give you a flip".  We're going to look around the area and try to find a real barber for the future.

I have to admit, I've never had a good experience at a Walgreens, why do i keep hoping that will change?
I went in to this Walgreen's Location to pick up a couple of items. One can of dog food, one can of cat food, a three pack of gum. I shopped a bit to make sure i got a sale item. I don't want to complain for 10 paragraphs so I'll summarize.
- no one was working the registers so I had to wait
-once someone came she acted like It was a huge inconvenience for me to buy something
-my emailed 20% off coupon wouldn't work and she tried her hardest to refuse me 20% off, despite the fact that this company gives out 20% coupons every weekend.

I understand that retail is not a fun job (I worked it for 6 years) but you really shouldn't treat the customer like they aren't worth the paper the 20% coupons that you mail out EVERY SINGLE WEEK are printed on. 

overall won't be back to this location ever again. Hope they have a staff change soon!

Oof, the ads got me and we decided to get KFC before the playoff game and what a mistake. The location wasn't super busy as there were 2 cars in front of us. When it was our turn to order, it took forever. Static and finally we asked if anyone was there and the employee taking the orders told us to wait a minute. If they didn't have the barrier I think we would have done a u-turn and left because we didn't have a great feeling with how rudely he responded to us and how slow the service suddenly became.

We ordered a large popcorn chicken, a large mashed potato and a three piece meal. It came pretty fast and seemed a bit expensive to me (which was surprising as in the ads things are presented as much more reasonably priced).

Got home and the food portions were ridiculous. The popcorn chicken box was just over half filled. The three pieces were not large - one looked like it came from a Cornish hen instead of a regular sized hen. Only the mashed potatoes looked right. As for taste - ugh, yuck. The popcorn chicken was way over cooked and most "pieces" were just breading with no chicken. The three pieces of chicken barely had any breading and it certainly was not crispy. Soggy might be a better word to describe it. The biscuit was good. The potatoes were okay if you got the gravy part but seemed gluey and over heated at the bottom. Very disappointing meal. We certainly won't be back to this location or any KFC location again.

I purchased a bike at this bike shop because a friend of mine recommended it. Paid a little more so I get free adjustments. Loaded up the bike to get an adjustment and took it into the shop off I 85. 
Waited about 10 minutes at the counter only to be curtly told that " no more service work can be scheduled until the middle of July". The tech was really unfriendly and completely unapologetic. Like this is normal for them. I guess it's real easy to promise future work when there is no time to do it. 
I have been in there before. Never the same people and the clerks don't know where anything is located or what product is better than the other. With so many bike shops around I suggest you go somewhere else. Can't stand help that does not care about customer service one bit.

I wish I could put negative stars! Drove three hours to look at a truck, drive it and it was a pile of junk. By then it was 8:30 p.m. on a Saturday. We found a truck we liked, it drove great. I asked if it had keyless entry when I saw that there was only one key. "Of course it does, the extra keys and key fobs are locked in another room and we can't access them until Monday. We can mail them to you." The passenger front seat belt had been chewed in half by a dog. "We will send you a new one next week". We bought the truck. Day after getting home the engine light comes on. I call Merced, he basically tells me it's not their problem. I ask about the spare keys and key fobs and seat belt, "they will be mailed soon". A week later, just after Christmas, we are surprised to find that $136 was taken from our account which caused a total of $252 in over drafts. Merced, the finance mgr, never gave us a heads up that out trade in payoff was$136 more. Merry Christmas to us.... yet, we still made the $250 payment on the 10th of January as the first half of the $500 cash down we got manipulated into promising. On time. Like we agreed. Of course we got the whole song and dance routine of "we aren't making any money off of this truck, the cash down makes us break even"  pppbbbbbbbb, whatever.... I call yesterday to ask about my key, key fobs, and seat belt, asking to talk to a manager. They transfer me to Merced. I ask if I can speak to a different manager or the owner and he raises his voice and tells me to talk to him or never call them again and promptly hangs up on me. I text our salesman asking about the spare keys and keyless entry fobs and he texts back that there aren't any. Sorry. I go to a local Ford dealership and they investigate, only to find that the truck didn't come with a keyless entry module. But they can order me one. Also, they can make me a spare key but it's $99.95! So now we have almost a $300/mo  payment on a $23,000 truck that has the engine light on, a ripped seatbelt, only one key, and no keyless entry! What's funny is that the car salesman laughed when I asked about it having keyless entry and replied "of course it does, the fobs are just locked up and I can't get them".  BUYER BEWARE!!!!!!!!!

Ever since Norm's Garden closed in May of 2015, I have been in search of a comparable  Chinese restaurant.  Sadly, so far, no luck!  Canton Phoenix was my latest try and unfortunately, it wasn't a hit. 

I ordered several lunch combinations (Mongolian Beef, General Tso's Chicken, Dry Sauteed Green Beans and L6, which included BBQ Pork, Sweet and Sour Chicken, Fried Rice and Sub Gum Chicken Chow Mein) so we could try a variety of items.  I also ordered a separate order of BBQ pork fried rice and an order of MaFa chicken.  Three of the lunch combos came with a spring roll.  Ugh, soft, squishy and not good at all.  The best of the three combos was the Mongolian Beef.  It was tasty, but the beef was a bit chewy.  The General Tso's chicken was super sweet and had no spice whatsoever.  That was disappointing.  The Dry Sauteed Green Beans had an odd flavor, almost like soap. Ick, really bad!  The BBQ pork and the Sweet and Sour Chicken in the L6 combo were good, the BBQ pork was actually the best item ordered, but there wasn't much of it.  The Sub Gum Chicken Chow Mein tasted like sesame oil .... just sesame oil, there was no flavor of the vegetables or the chicken, and the chicken was rubbery and weird looking.  One bite of that and it went in the garbage, along with the soggy spring rolls and the green beans.  Total waste of money! 

The MaFa chicken had potential, but it was so greasy that I had to roll it in paper towels to draw the grease out before tasting it.  Also, they line the bottom of a styrofoam container with slimy, stringy lettuce that then sticks to the pieces of deep-fried chicken.  Gross!  

The fried rice that came with the three combos was brown and flavorless ... in the garbage it all went!  The separate order of BBQ pork fried rice was a little better, but not a whole lot.  

Another thing that turned me off is the to go containers are all plastic or styrofoam.  Putting hot food into plastic containers is nasty.  Not a Chinese takeout box in sight!  Everything was put in a plastic container, including the whole order of BBQ pork fried rice, and the deep-fried MaFa chicken was in a styrofoam container.  Not good.  

Overall, very disappointing experience and a lot of money wasted since much of the food ended up in the garbage.  I certainly won't go back to Canton Phoenix, but I will continue my search for some decent Chinese food in the local area.  Norm's Garden, you are missed!!

I prefer not to give any star to the Hong Kong grocery store. Even before when they were 88 these employees here are just obnoxiously rude. 

The cashiers are the ones to look out for. It took me a while to get to review this place. But whoever that WORKS there or WORKED there are super rude and conceited. You're just a cashier, why do you have to act like you are better than everyone else??? 

I was helping my manager pick up some seaweed and this cashier was throwing the stick that separates people's groceries. Another one kept pointing and stabbing this poor Indian man's vegetables. 

I'm Asian and I find this place to be an embarrassment for our Asian community. Screams so loud and the produce is not fresh here. Restrooms are filthy dirty, the food court is disgusting. They picked up all chairs and tables from different restaurants and place them in the food court. There is also a huge hole in the parking lot ramp. Let's see how long it will take them to fix it.

If you have an oil leak DO NOT use this auto repair center. The issue was properly diagnosed but the work was not done correctly even after multiple "attempts". After 4 attempts and continuous smoking I took my car to another shop that was able to correct the issue on the first try. The main benefit is that their work is covered under a warranty but save yourself the time and go to another repair shop. They have done other work on my car that was great but oil leaks are not their strong suit.

After waking up at 4:30am and being at work for 12 hours, I decided it'd be easier to order out.  I got some dim-sum, which was fine, but also ordered an entree of honey walnut shrimp for $14.50. It came in the typical Chinese to-go box and was barely over half way full! Last time I ordered it, it came in one of the larger square styrofoam boxes full. 

**UPDATE: I was sent a comment (assuming from someone at Good World) asking if I counted how many shrimp were given to me because they always give the same amount, and that maybe the box wasn't as full because the amount of veggies they give varies -- Furthermore, that if I wanted more veggies I'd be given a full box. Excuse me, but this dish isn't served with veggies besides some sliced tomatoes for garnish! Take some accountability.

Beware of this place!  I do not trust their food safety standards at all. Incredibly irresponsible business, avoid this place if you can.  They sold me an expired juice, I called to alert them (also concerned there are more of these in that fridge and wanting to save another customer from experience) but they never even bothered to return my call. 

I bought (what I assumed was a "freshly pressed", or at least recently pressed) green juice and a muffin. My total came to over $15. I am happy to pay premium price--for a premium product.  You would think for the price of this juice it would be...idk, FRESH?  

This trip to "Nourish your soul" was right before heading out on a long road trip. My stomach began to hurt a little about 20 min after I started snacking on these treats---the juice did not taste so good, but really I assumed it was probably the muffin that didn't agree with me (as it was my first time trying that muffin, but I've drank green juices for years) Anyway, at this point I do not know what it is because I noticed AFTER drinking half of it :/ that right at the top it said "use by Oct 19th"...not best by, not freshest by--but USE BY.  I wanted to vomit.  As much as I'm a fan of raw juices and realize what the pasteurization process does to phytonutrients, etc --I'm also aware of what happens with harmful BACTERIA in un pasteurized products if not handled properly!   This place is a health hazard. **Avoid** and definitely DO NOT LET YOUR KIDS CONSUME PRODUCTS THERE, VERY DANGEROUS!   And that fact that it is such a challenge to get someone on the phone is concerning, very irresponsible business.

My boyfriend took me there for my Birthday last Monday and we got sick afterward. I called them the next morning and no one answered. I waited until they opened and called again. Spoke to a woman who asked about some details and asked for my information so someone could get back to me... Well no one did. For people who eat there, I just hope they passed on the message to the kitchen. When something like this happens a "fine" restaurant as this needs to really be a WHOLE lot more responsive. Especially when RAW food is involved.

It is only obvious that Bruegger's has changed its operational process.  For example in its previous location, when you ordered a bagel it was made right as you ordered it.  In this new location when you order your bagel you get put in a " wait status " and your order is filled at a later time.  Why do I care?  When I last went in, I ordered 2 bagels that I could see only 2 were left in the bin.  I then waited a half hour and then made an inquiry.  I was told that they were all out of the type bagels that I ordered and were in the process of cooking more, but it would take another 15-20 min.  I got pissed at the manager because I saw the two bagels that I ordered at the time I ordered them.  He told me that those two bagels were used to fill orders before me and when it was my time to fill my order there were none left so they put me in another wait period until they had cooked the bagels that I ordered.  I find this process very annoying and intend to let their corporate HQ know.  Currently I give them one star.

Where do I start. I leased an apartment from this company for a year and a half. Never once was my rent late and several months I paid it early. I have been waiting for my security deposit for 44 days. It looks like small claims court is our next stop. The Dad is the one I had to deal with and he apparently suffers from selective dementia to gain him additional time in addressing an issue, or returning money he owes people!. I would seriously run hard and fast from this company and anyone named Anani or Anami ( they use both which is questionable to me). You've been warned.

Too bad zero stars was not an option.  I have never experienced such bad customer service.  I dealt with Karen on the phone and in person.  When I described what I needed she said " That could be a million things".  OK, I get it,  there are variations.  When I asked where they were on Burnet, her reply was " Burnet is a very long road". Really, but there are cross streets to help narrow down the area.  I was able to get out of her it was between 2222 and 183 ( they are 2 blocks north of 2222.  When I showed up I presented her the sample. She said have a look around and see if you can find the match and " let me know if you need any help ".  Yes Karen I did need help.  I figured you might know the product you sell well enough to be helpful.  Never found what I needed.  But I do think the concept for Logan's Run was probably based on her.  No help to me whatsoever, wasted 2 hours of my time and made me realize why I pay for customer service that is helpful.  I wouldn't take free wood to burn from these jerks if I was freezing to death.

Today, July 17, 2013, at 3 pm, I was waiting to make a purchase while 2 cashiers were waiting on a young blond lady. It looked like there was a problem with her purchase. I stood there a few minutes and 2 young white men came up behind me also wanting to make a purchase. One of the cashiers, a dark haired lady, looked around me and told the 2 young men they could go to the other cashier desk because there's no waiting at that one. My jaw dropped. Was I invisible? One of the young men was nice to ask me if I wanted to go first at the other cashier desk. I said no because the cashier wasn't talking to me. Both cashiers just ignored me and kept working at the cash register. Finally, the young blond lady told the cashiers to wait on me and she could wait. The dark haired cashier gave an exasperated sigh and took my item. I asked her if I was invisible to her. She didn't answer and told me to swipe my card. If my son didn't want the jeans I was buying I would have walked out. Because I am Hispanic, I can only conclude I experienced a discriminatory act. I will never shop there or at any other Gap related store.

These people LIE!!!!! I had them move me and they talk the talk but DAMAGE YOUR STUFF!!! They say they have insurance and maybe they do.... Yet, they pay a $ 0.60 per lb. and with depreciation. Enjoy! ;)

The quality of the food was lackluster and there was a musty smell in the place that just wouldn't settle.

I ordered the Risotto. It arrived cold! Although the staff is extremely friendly, I would not come back.

I'm being rude by drafting this during lunch, but I'm still not nearly as rude as our server.  He took twenty minutes to take our order and his attitude was awful. Our beers sat empty for forty minutes at a time, and he forgot the waters we'd requested twice.  At least he apologized when he bothered to show up thirty minutes later.

Just kidding, he didn't apologize.  Instead, he rolled his eyes while watching my fiance hand us the waters we'd retrieved from the bar. Normally, I'd never consider going to the bar for a drink while seated at a table, but considering it was free and we were being incredibly under-served, I felt 100% justified.

We were the opposite of a rowdy college group (late tweties/early thirties professionals), and we were looking forward to having some nice beers and relaxing. Sadly, our server's complete indifference and incompetence cost the bar some serious dough and repeat patronage.  We left completely sober, underwhelmed and annoyed.

The nachos are good but nothing makes up for the awful and rude service.  

If you get the large guy with tons of tattoos, just do yourself a favor and leave.  You'll get better service at McDonald's down the street.

Six of us went to Hightower last night in just enough time to catch the end of happy hour on a Saturday night.  Which is always attractive.  

What wasn't attractive was the 5 dishes we ordered that, after one bite each, we couldn't stomach another bite.  I read great reviews about the chickpeas.  I'm a huge fan of smelt fish.  We all collectively seek out good brussell sprouts...  Every single dish we ordered was completely over salted (except for the ceviche) was rendered 100% inedible.  It's pretty baffling to me how you can mess up almost all the dishes at a table. Two bowls of the fried chickpeas, two of the peanut butter brussell sprouts, and the smelt fish...  Side note: Interestingly, the fish part of the ceviche was absolutely incredible (the smoke flavor was divine, the fish was perfect temp, cut, and freshness) but sadly, again, the sauce was so over salted that on the two ceviches we ordered, we had to move the fish away from the rest of the dish.  What a shame.  Most of my friends are much kinder than I and certainly not as fastidious in their desire for food to be good, and they were terribly disappointed.  

What continues to befuddle me, is that we had a table full of uneaten food and the waitress didn't once ask if there was a problem.  Wow.  We all felt so uncomfortable sending all the dishes back, so no one said anything and a very large bill later, we certainly did not order dinner, downed our acceptable drinks and promptly vowed to never return.

I remember when ABW was just starting out in austin, they should get back in touch with who they were back then.  Super bummed ABW super bummed.

The food was mediocre, the service was inappropriate and the wait was unacceptable. For the really long wait we were offered a free desert at the start when first told about the back up . No such desert was offered or came.

We used this company as recommended by American Home Shield Warranty company.  The technician came out to the house and checked our Central Air units. When he didnt show up, we tried to contact the company at both of their locations listed on the estimate.  No one ever answered the phone.  We tried reaching out to the warranty company.  They called the company and we were told that our technician was out sick and that Perry Mechanical had no one else who could come out to our house in Ocala.  When he finally showed back up, he gave us a bill for $385.00 in refrigerant which was not listed on the original estimate.  The estimate never gave the price of the refrigerant. When I called their offices constantly over 3 days, the only way I could get anyone to return my phone calls was to tell them I was issuing a stop payment on the check we gave them. I received an estimate which included a part for just over $200.
After they complete the work, the final invoice lists same part for over $500.

I know it is an ESTIMATE and labor may change, but I am confused how their parts price was so far off, especially when they claim to be "certified" by the manufacturer. When questioned, they rudely explained how it was only an estimate, and they use separate systems to create the estimate and the final invoice. I would hope/expect those separate systems to have similar prices. Maybe that's just my unrealistic expectations, but something seems a bit off to me. I got the impression they do not like being questioned after they had to get a supervisor out to fully explain their process, which I still don't fully understand. 

While trying to get the additional $$ from the responsible party, they threatened me with collections and gave me the spiel about how it was my responsibility, even though I was in frequent contact with them and they knew I was working on it. It was not even 30 days before they received full payment. Calm down guys. It would not have even been an issue if they had provided a more accurate estimate.

Visiting Boulder we stopped in for dinner. We ordered the guacamole table side which was good.

Just left it on the table with a tiny amount gone till we finally got up to leave, like we were gonna have a change of heart and eat the gross thing.

Asked our waiter,Alexander for water no ice, he brought water with ice.  I reminded him I asked for no ice. He decided to ignore my request and instead let the ice in my glass melt, seriously the water tasted like chlorine anyway. So I ordered a glass of Navern Cava Rosado Rose that had zero flavor like the bottle had been open for a while.
Not sure how this place got so many stars it was a total disappointment.

I have had chronic pain in my hand and wrist which has, in the past, resulted in surgery to remove a ganglion cyst in the center of my palm. The pain returned and it seemed like I would need to have surgery again, so I scheduled an appointment with Dr. Gadaria. At the time I scheduled the appointment I was in the very beginning of a pregnancy. I also had really awful insurance with a very high deductible- so basically everything was out of pocket. When I called to schedule the appointment I asked the scheduler if it mattered that I was pregnant. I didn't want to spend the money on seeing the doctor if the doctor was unwilling to operate on a pregnant lady.  The scheduler said she couldn't tell me whether or not Dr. Gadaria would operate on a pregnant lady and that I needed to come in and talk to him about it. So, I went in and immediately asked Dr. Gadaria if he would operate on me despite me being pregnant. He said that he has blanket policy of not operating on pregnant women except in life threatening situations. That question was the extent of my appointment. He couldn't help me. I didn't understand why this policy could not have been communicated to me by the front desk before my appointment. As I leave, I am asked to pay $200! I paid it but was so upset that I was in tears by the time I reached the elevator. I went back in and explained to the office manager that I really couldn't afford to pay $200 to ask a question to a doctor that could have been answered by the scheduler over the phone and that I would never have scheduled with Dr. Gadaria in the first place had I known he couldn't help me due to my pregnancy. The office manager was clearly annoyed, unsympathetic and unwilling to refund me the $200. I then asked to speak directly to Dr. Gadaria about it. He was far more graceful and understanding about it and told the office manager to refund my money. I was extremely grateful but the office manager went about angrily processing the refund all the while making it very apparent that she despised me for even asking. 

Fast forward a year later. I have given birth and finished nursing and the pain has intensified. I am now in a condition to have surgery and my insurance is now much better. I call Dr. Gadaria's office because he has the best ratings and because I remembered how he did right by me even though his office manager didn't want to. I try to schedule an appointment and after giving my name to the scheduler she puts me on hold. The office manager then picks up the phone and angrily says, "you came here last year and there was a problem. The doctor does not wish to see you as a patient" and then hangs up.

I can only imagine that the office manager had wrote some nasty comment on my file that was flagged by scheduler when I called. I highly doubt that Dr. Gadaria was even asked whether he would take me as a patient. In short, the office manager is petty, short tempered, rude, unempathetic and holds grudges. This is a small office so you will most likely have to deal with her as a patient of Dr. Gadaria. It is because of her that I give this poor rating, and as the office manager is the face of this medical practice, I do not recommend that you go here.

No matter which Lush Nail Bar location I go to, they seem to always disappoint and this location is no different. I will give them their credit on their level of cleanliness and sanitation of their facility. They seemed to really follow COVID-19 guidelines very well. However, there service is subpar. I got the lush coco pedicure. The tech that handled my pedicure was so rough. The skin around my toe nails still hurt from all her digging and clipping. I can tell they do the age old method where instead of buying fresh new nail polish when they start running, they just add nail polish remover and shake the bottle. The tech sprayed my toes with some much nail polisher remover that the skin around was burning. I got a simple white polish and the tech applied base, two layers of polish, and top coat. I sat there and waited a good 10-15 mins for polish to dry. Then I paid and departed home. I live 41 mins from this location and I ran into an accident so it ended up taking me an hour to get home. When I got home I got out the car looked at my toes and they seemed fine enough. Surely after an hour and a half they would be dry. Wrong! I change into another pair of flip flops to walk my dogs. I took off the paper ones from the shop and slip my foot into my other ones and when I tell you all the polish came off immediately. I rubbed my hand over my toe nails and the polish just rubbed off like it was so thin like the tech had put half a coat on my nails. I would advise to not use their polish and bring your own. However, this is the third location I have been to and I can't say I have ever had stellar service. I will not be going to this location or any other location for that matter.

Came here after watching the phantom gourmet.
I was aware that they make after ordering, so I was very patient after ordering the small combo. But, after waited 30mins, I saw people who came in after me already got their food. I asked the same waitress who took my order 30mins ago that how long I still need to wait and she was like "what u ordered?". I have to say that dumb, stupid and innocent face really moves me out of the restaurant.

Great service and definitely come back for that 2.5＄delicious Pepsi. I recommend you change your name to crave mad for service.

I hate to leave such a bad review but I was sorely disappointed with the taste and quality of the food. Butter beans were sour, all four kinds of protein (salmon, bbq chicken, turkey and smothered pork chops) were dry and over seasoned, corn bread dry and heavy, corn even tasted spoiled, greens were over cooked. The only thing tasteful was the dessert. Incredibly disappointed. We usually go to the one on Campbelton Rd that has never disappointed. We happen to be closer to this one and gave it a try. Never again. Maybe it was just the day we came in but so much being bad, we won't go here again.

Went here for lunch and had to make our way through the protesters telling us that there are rats and roaches in this brand new restaurant. I challenge them to point me in the direction of a restaurant or any structure in this city without a vermin problem. Thanks guys!

Next, the food was pretty good and the decor is fun. One annoyance was that they seated 5 of us at a table that barely fit 4 people, but whatever not a huge deal. I got the spicy tuna sandwhich which was delicious. Also, the portion of waffle fries isn't huge you might ge like 5 or 6, so if you ae one of those (like me) who order something in its place, get the fries! They were delicious. We had a veggie burger at the table too which looked awesome, will have to try it next time!

 Also, I wish they would have just used plates to serve our sandwhiches on instead of these long slabs of wood that clearly don't fit on the table.

Lastly, I would come again!

This review is directed towards the contact lens office specifically.  I went back after my AWFUL eye exam to get a contact consultation and order new ones.  I had different eye doctor today (I wish I could remember his name), and he was excellent.  He was incredibly patient and considerate, and he noticed a problem with my prescription and contact lenses that I had been wearing for the last 5+ years.  He quickly fixed the problem and was thorough in his questions and considerations.  I'll definitely go back to him.

Basically, if you're going here for glasses or contacts, you're golden, just don't go to actually get your eyes checked out.

The first thing you should know is this is not an British Pub.  This is an American mall version of an British Pub.  So it is bigger, louder, dumber and (in its defense) a lot cleaner than any version it sets out to emulate.  As others have mentioned, it is kind of like a Disney amusement park version of an British Pub.  Various English Premier League logos and flags are displayed prominently, as are the logos of british and european beers and whiskeys.  Perhaps more so than you would see in the real version.  The servers all wear kilts--which is actually Scottish (and, to a lesser extent, Irish) traditional dress.  So, a muddled message in execution of concept.

On the other hand, they have a lot of modern, customer friendly, conveniences like flat screen tv's and wifi.  They even have tables with built in beer taps--an interesting, but potentially disastrous idea given that most of the patrons will likely try to drive home from this suburban location.

All things considered though, this was a fun place to spend an evening on St. Patrick's Day weekend.  They had a couple of good bands booked and, with a boisterous, inebriated crowd, I think a good time was had by all.

Service was a little spotty, but that was probably due to the sheer volume of business they were doing on a busy weekend.  I'd be interested to see how the service is on an average day.

As others have mentioned, the Kentucky Bourbon Ale is awesome.  Give it a try if you go.

Went to visit Fifty Licks for the first time over Thanksgiving break. The ice cream was pretty good along with the homemade waffle cones. They honored our auction tickets we had bid on several years ago and with two toddlers, never had a chance to use until our visit. 

The major complaint I have were the two young women working there. They scoffed at asking for samples, they could hardly break a smile even with two very cute kids staring at them, and I'm really not interested in going back to a place where the staff were generally unfriendly.

3 stars because their fall festival was so much fun! Always a hit. But sadly this year, with COVID going on, there was absolutely no social distancing and masks were not enforced. There are multiple sanitation stations but all hidden. Many signs telling us to stay 6 feet apart and wear a mask when under cover or in lines, but no one enforcing this. Way too crowded in a time like this. No way to sanitize tables and nobody sanitizing them for us. Had I known there were no accommodations being done for COVID, I wouldn't have come. Just a warning for those who take social distancing measures seriously.

I have been staying at this locations for a decade and various Hilton name changes. Obviously, it must be okay or I would not continue coming. Through out my dozen or more so stays here I have always observed a blatant abuse of extending gold member perks (free breakfast buffets) that I can no longer ignore. It's no easy task to achieve gold status , ( as a matter of fact... It took me purchasing Hilton grand vacation property in New York City to finally obtain) and I resent "handouts" to those undeserving.  As I checked in and observed the person ahead of me handed a stack of cards for their family , or the request for 6 beside me , I couldn't help but remember just a month earlier i was checking into Hilton Anaheim and explained to the clerk that our third person checking in that night was our air force daughter flying straight in from a six month Iraq deployment and couldn't Hilton please include breakfast for her .... Which I was quickly reminded "no, Hilton has a strict 2 guests per gold member breakfast daily limit" . 
Guess that doesn't apply to non-gold guests in Atlanta. It wouldn't take very much math for the owner of this location to see...... Out of 100% guests.. 90% eat breakfast for which 5% is paid in revenue??   Really don't see how restaurant stays open.
Other than favoritism for guests.... My room has always been clean, the bed is comfortable, place is quiet and parking is good. Shuttle very convenient and covers mall and good restaurants.
