Also, if you are gold or diamond , don't expect your automatic room upgrade; they also allow slumber parties in their rooms so make sure you speak up and ask if you can move if you notice a ton of kids and parents toting large coolers on the elevator.

Decent burger joint- I really like that they're different than anywhere else! From the logo branded onto the buns to the extra huge onion rings and unique hot dog options (I had an apple turkey dog of some sort- pretty yummy), this place is cool. 

The service was great and the chill vibes were cool- not quite restaurant style, not quite fast food. Had to give 3 stars though because the food was just "good" just "alright"--nothing spectacular. This isn't where you go for an AMAZING burger in Austin- but if you're in the area and need a quick bite, this place is a great option!

Douzo is one of those places that you would check out once to see what the buzz is all about and then that's it. Unless you actually work in the area and crave sushi 3,4 times a week.
I came here during lunch and grabbed a seat at the bar. The place was packed with all types of business people. I don't think the fish quality here is that great. I ordered the Red Spider roll because it seems yummy. It is nothing special. 
All the suggestions from other yelpers are great but do add the Duck Ravioli (Gyoza). They are delicious! 
I also order Tuna Sashimi which came in 3 pieces for a price of $8.75. I expect really really fresh fish. It was not at all. The pieces of Tuna was not tight and chewy but easily fell apart in my mouth instead. 
Service is kinda snobby and wasn't as nice as I expected. After all, if I paid more than $30 for my lunch I should set my expectation a little higher, right?

Went to Nik's for the first time the other day. I have driven by it many times but never stopped it so my family and I decided to try it. It's a small place. Reminded me more of a bistro than a restaurant. It was small and cramped.  They were busy but not overly busy but the dining room dwindled down the longer we sat there.  Our server was kind. Friendly and smiling.  We ordered a chicken sandwich, bbq chicken and some flatbread pizzas for the kids.  My bbq chicken was really good. I got it with asparagus and that was yummy.  The bbq sauce was really tasty and the asparagus were cooked to perfection.  I had a bite of my husbands sandwich and that was good too. Fries were similar to McDonalds which is a GOOD thing. Who doesn't love Mc Donald fries? The flatbread pizza was good and perfect size for our kids.  Our food did take a while. I'd like to go back and try some other items. I try not to eat pasta but it is tempting me. Maybe we will go during a slower period also.

This place was okay, but a little disappointing.  I ordered the "Filet de boeuf grille, sauce au poivre noir Gratin Dauphinois et haricots verts."  In a real language (English) that means beef, gratin potatoes, and green beans.  The potatoes were delicious, the green beans were kind of nasty, and the beef was so-so.  So all of that averages out to A-OK.  My girlfriend got the duck dish and was similarly non-plussed.

For dessert, we got a cinnamon-apple crepe and the puff pastry with vanilla ice cream.  The crepe was pretty good but the puff pastry was not that good.  Again, averaged out to A-OK.

This place is a decent restaurant, but compared to some of the other places in Epcot's World Showcase, it just doesn't quite hold up.  Go to Japan or Germany instead.

Sometimes I forget how much people love brunch.  I mean, what's not to love.  So what I'm saying is when we showed up at noon we had to wait about a hour to seat 3 people.  They did however give us coffee while we waited.  After 45 minutes they even asked if we wanted a cocktail since it was after 12:30pm. The parking surprisingly wasn't bad, they had plenty of seats if you were  waiting for a table and the décor was nice.  Our service/server was excellent.  I wish I had caught his name because he was really friendly and just a great server all around (baseball hat, glasses, beard, some tattoos, I know it could be anyone).  My wife had the Shrimp Po Boy (she really liked it). Initially she planned to at half of it and bring the second half home.  That didn't happen.  I had the Folk Southern Fried.  It was good,  tasty but lacking something, not sure what it needed.  When I go back I want to check out the Roasted Pork Verde (my second choice that day).  It sounds awesome.  Oh, we were there a long time.  So we had a few cocktails and later ordered fries.  The bloody Mary was very good  as was the Johnny Appleseed.  My wife and friend had the Strawberry Fields and What's Up Doc, also delicious.  The fries were excellent.  So Folk Art, good setting, great service, good food, tasty cocktails , yes! This is a definite must try again.

My husband saw this spot on Man V Food so of course we had to come here. We made the two hour drive down from Olympia in the pouring rain. We arrived pretty early on Saturday and found that the line was already wrapped around the outside of the building. Obviously, in this part of the country you can't let standing in the rain for 30 minutes stop you. 

We used our line time to scan the menu online and choose our flavors. The longer we waited the larger our wish list grew. We settled on a dozen donuts for the two of us.

The Maple Bar was the best donut of the bunch. The Grape Ape and Mango Tango were good too. I liked the sugar crunch and the flavor of the powders with the icing and donut. Everything with cereal on top was a disappointment since all of the cereal tasted stale. Cereal on top of the donut sounds interesting, but just doesn't work.

Keep in mind that they only accept cash so make sure to hit the ATM before visiting. I want to say that there was an ATM on site, but I wouldn't count on that. At the time I visited there was also only one table inside because most of the space is used for the line. Plan to have somewhere else to enjoy your donuts.

These aren't the best donuts you'll ever have in your life, but the donuts and the shop are unique. Would you really want to visit Portland and miss the iconic Voodoo Donuts?

The ramen here is definitely different than others I've had but it was tasty nonetheless. My only issue really is the the large portion size, which I never thought I would ever criticize about a restaurant. The portion size is absurdly large and this is demonstrated by the fact that the majority of the room got an "almost". I typically can finish a bowl of ramen, but here I ate as much as I could and over half the bowl was still there and so many noodles left. 

You can't split the bowl, and you can't take it home which I understand, but looking around the room there was so much food that was wasted, it was pretty sad to look at. I've never wasted that much food before. I hate to be preachy, but there's a real need in the community for food and to see a place like this pretty much fill bowls over capacity and just throw everything away after barely anyone finishes is pretty disheartening. 

Either lower the prices and the portion sizes, or let folks take leftovers home. There shouldn't be this level of food waste.

This fitness club occupies five stories of a warehouse-like building right near Downtown Crossing. It is very convenient for those working in the Financial District. The club is clean and spacious, though there is little if any natural light. Because it is a relatively new club, it is not too crowded, and you can almost always get on the machine you want with no trouble. While the club has a full regimen of strength apparatus, cardio equipment, and group exercise classes, it lacks a sauna or hot tub or headphone jacks on the equipment. For people who appreciate privacy in the locker rooms, the private toilet/sink/shower stalls can't be beat.

My biggest problem with this club, which is why I cancelled my membership, are the hours. While it is great for after work, they are only open five hours on Saturday and closed all day Sunday. For people who live outside of the city, it makes it tough to work out on the weekends, particularly since they have no affiliated suburban locations.

When I registered, they charged me a $50 initiation fee and $45/month dues for a one-year contract, claiming it was a special for people visiting the club the first time. Who knows if they'll give you the same price if you return after comparison shopping. Membership includes a 7-day risk-free trial period, and when I went to cancel before the end of the period, they did not give me a hassle at all.

The Decor is beautiful! The food is really delicious but I think the portions are a little small considering the prices. I've been here only twice and I've order the enchilada verde and the enchilada with mole. Both were very good and flavorful but for two enchiladas, a tiny portion of refried beans, a tiny portion of rice and the price if I remember correctly was about 20 bucks. 

The chips and sauce they give you in the beginning is soooooo good. 

Although the servers are pretty good, the server we had the last time we went was so rude and stand-offish. 

The white sangria that I fell in love with the first time I went was nothing compared to the this time. It was so strong and bad tasting :/. 

I would recommend this place for everyone to try but beware of the the servers attitudes lol

I ordered fish tacos and Cajun wings through Yelp. The tacos were SMOTHERED with Cole slaw which I didn't like lol. It made the tacos soggy. So I had to remove the Cole slaw and eat tacos with a fork without the tortilla(which obviously wasn't my intention). The Cajun wings we're ok. Only a few of the wings had Cajun seasoning on them but they did give me an extra side of Cajun seasoning. I think the wings were a little overpriced for what I received. Other than that, delivery was normal. I'll probably order from them again but I will try something else.

Portland BLT review:

I saw a picture of their BLT and figured this would be the hands-down winner. More accurately, they sell a BLEAT (+avocado, egg). Everything tucked into a fresh croissant. The side view of this thing is something to behold.

The place was packed - always a good sign. I took a seat at the bar. I was served quickly, but then all service broke down. For such a hop'n establishment, I did not expect that. Back to the meal...

Unfortunately, presentation did not represent the dish. I noticed the romaine was fresh, just no crunch. It's difficult for me to fault the lettuce since it was fresh, but this is the filter I have - it must crunch - basics for a BLT. In addition, the tomato wasn't ripe. Fabulous bacon, and the avocado and egg were a great addition. Big kudos for the pesto aioli too. Alas, the basics come first... especially, if you call it a BLT. It's not like the sandwich sucked - no, on the contrary, it was definitely good. Just not a good representation of a BLT.

I really wanted to love this place, I really did. I made an appointment for my sisters and our mom to come here for a relaxing day, just to get away from our mundane schedule and everyone was super excited. While the facility is beautiful with topnotch reception service, our massages were cut too short. We each booked for 50-minute massages, but each of us received at most 40 minutes. We all arrived at least 20 minutes prior to our appointment time, changed, and waited to be called but only to be shortening by what was promised. It does not live up to the hype. Very disappointed!

My wife brought me here for Father's Day, partly because of coworker raves, partly because of my love for a good rib-eye, which was the Fathers Day Special. 

I will begin with the service, because I believe this was the best part of my experience. I found the staff very attentive, helpful, down to earth and quick to laugh, which are all qualities I truly appreciate

The meal? It was a multi-course "deal" but I want to focus on the main course: It was pretty good, but I have had far better rib-eyes. Mind you this was a price-fix multi-course menu, which I suppose are never spectacular by design, but the quality to price ratio was not good. The rib-eye was cooked perfectly, but was lean, and tough to cut at times. The mashed potatoes (although tasty) seemed somewhat watery and I couldn't help but wonder if they were instant. There was a blue-cheese popover on the main dish that was tasty. 

Would I come back? Probably not on my own, but if someone were to suggest it I would not be against it. I am giving the 3rd star for the wonderful service, but there are places in the not-too-distant area that serve locally sourced rib-eye that blows this place out of the water (or should I say pasture?)

We went in for the, what use to be $6 appies before 6pm, now $7. Still not a bad deal. We ordered the hot wings, bruschetta & the poutine. The hot wings were average, prob use Franks for the sauce. The bruschetta was way bigger than I was expecting and really quite delicious. Very nice & fresh, a really good balsamic. Mmm...  But the poutine... I was impressed by the added touch of bacon & the size of the cheese curds but I'm fairly certain I received the left over fries from yesterday. If they had fresh crisp fries I may have fallen in love.

This place is huge and when I say huge, they have their own parking structure and right behind it is parking for buses!!!  Since I was a stone throw away from the place, I decided to stop by and give them a try.

They have pull up service, where you can pull up your car to the car port and they will take your order or park and walk in.  When you walk in, just find the line that is the shortest, the lines will move quickly... 

I went with the #1 combo (two chili dogs) with onion rings and Diet Coke, also got an order of their fried apple pie.  I go my order, found a table and enjoyed the meal.

Chili Dogs - while they were good, but they are not as good as those in Detroit.  Being a Michigan native, I had share of my coney dogs and yes, the chilis are different depending on where you go, but their chili dogs, while still good, is not up there compared to chili dogs from Michigan.

Fried Apple Pie - excellent, if you have room, grab two!!

Onion Rings - great onion rings!!!!  Fried to perfection, crispy and delicious!!!!

The place is in heart of Atlanta and unfortunately you'll run into some folks asking you for some money, so be mindful and do know what you do not have to give them money.  If you are not in downtown, they do have other locations, so if you are in ATL, stop by for some hotdogs!!!

Super cute quaint restaurant. The tables are very close together. Apparently there is parking in the back but I just parked by TD since they were closed. We ordered the hot and spicy tofu, garlic wings, vegetable masala fried rice and this egg plant dish (forgot what it was called). Our server asked us if regular spice was okay and we agreed but our group was under the impression that it would be very spicy. We definitely did not want food that we wouldn't be able to eat. The tofu and the wings came out first. I did not detect any sort of spice in either dishes... The tofu was crispy but was kinda bland.... Wings were tasty but not spicy. A little bit of spice would have been appreciated. Fried rice had a kick to it and was good!!! The eggplant was definitely my fav dish. The chicken in it was tender and the carrots were a nice touch. We all got dessert which consisted of deep fried pineapple, banana and ice cream. Batter was great. I know some places have the Batter too thick (pastry like). The service isn't too great here and the tables were so close together that it made it very hard for our servers to come to our table. I wasn't able to try out the other dishes that were recommended on here but all in all it wasn't bad. 

Would I come back? Probably only if I was invited... I would still give it another try.

My family and I frequent this restaurant quite a lot and normally everything goes well... hence the 3 stars instead of 1.... however, we have recently had terrible service by a waitress named April.... she was very rude to my husband as he tried to order... and she seems to not like children very well... We left a tip and left, but have not been back in over a month now due to our bad experience... I really hope this was just an off day for April and that we can eventually return.

Negative star. Only because of one individual. And that would be the owner Brian. He is by far the most unpleasant human being to walk this planet. Whatever the drama or miserable life he leads, he is the owner of a company and needs to leave it behind when he goes to work. Mean mean person. After speaking w him on many different occasions, his rudeness was the only reliable source. Never ever would I let threes people into my home. I even requested, when I was at a desperate point in my life and just only cared if my shower door got done, that Brian NOT be involved in my work and did not want him entering my home. This guy is a joke. Move on people. There's a great place called image glass. Give business to them! Nice guys and excellent work!

July 2019

We saw a video online and we were tempted to take the drive from Boston to Texas just to try it.  We do random stuff like that so it wouldn't have been shocking had we done that.  I ended up booking a whole trip for his birthday.  I based the vacation around his wanting to try this restaurant.  

The wait is crazy long.  Its a pretty cool place and the story behind the start of the business is pretty interesting.  The food is just okay though.  The portions are kind of small.  I am assuming the wait is super long because the tables are long (seats at least 12 people per table) and there are no small ones.  My boyfriend and I went and waited over 3 hours for a table.  We were sat at this huge table.  We almost felt guilty taking up a huge table just the two of us.  They should consider seating another couple at the opposite end of the table.  

On another note, the wait staff was super nice.  They were definitely overwhelmed with how busy it was but still kept a friendly demeanor with the guests which was nice.    

What really surprised me was that they serve sliced white bread with the food.  I was under the assumption that corn bread was served with BBQ food.  According to our waitress, that is a northern thing.  So if you go, don't expect corn bread.    

We had high expectations of this after seeing the videos about it online and the photos.  It was a one and done type of place.  We are glad we went, we probably wouldn't go back.

We've driven by this place countless times, but have always been skeptical about trying it because it looks like it's either part of the auto repair place or gym that it's next to. We finally looked at the menu and confirmed they can accommodate a gluten allergy and we gave it a shot. 

The space is bigger than you expect, but they had a private party so all the normal diners were relegated to the small dining room off to the left. There were still tv's, but it felt a bit crowded and there were kids everywhere. It would've been nice to sit by the bar at a high top table. 

While they can accommodate gluten allergies, they don't have a specific menu or a dedicated fryer so Celiacs are stuck with sandwiches/burgers with no bun or salads. 

I had the honey and chicken almond salad, which was very tasty and a good amount of food for $12. My sister had the burger and she was impressed with how well it was cooked and how good it tasted. The breadless turkey club was also good, but not particularly memorable. 

Weak beer selection - not much interesting beyond the usual subjects on tap.

I took my cat in for the first time a while back, and I feel the overall visit was pleasant, the whole staff was very kind and helpful.  However our nurse Katie was trying to be a little too helpful. She continued to ramble throughout the whole visit, even occasionally talking over the veterinarian, which made me very uncomfortable. 
 On a different note, the rest of the visit was great.  The veterinarian was great, I feel he was comfortable in his decision making, which put me at ease.  I loved the feel of the old house, and as far as the pricing I consider it reasonable for that area of Austin.  Overall experience was good, and I  will continue to take my animals to Lake Austin Blvd Animal Hospital.

Came here on a weekday night for a friend's birthday party.  Strolled into the joint at midnight and the place was basically empty.  A friend commented that when he was here on a weekend it was packed, but i liked having the place nearly to ourselves.  The place had a good vibe to it, i really liked all the ample seating, even the bowling lane's seating was couches! 

Our bartender was mad nice, but maybe because we were the only people getting drinks he wanted all the tip he could get.... It was kinda pricey though, but it's friggin Lansdown and i completely expected it and don't hold it against them, but this might be a better joint for when times are flush.  They do have 4$ bud lights so my wallet didn't cry too much.

Overall, definitely a fun joint for groups, especially mixed age groups like mine was (it's a 18+ place).  Good service and atmosphere and no cover! what what!

I met up with some friends for dinner here last week.  They arrived before me and as soon as I took my jacket off the waiter was over and asking me for a drink order.  Uh, hey, would you mind if I sat down first and looked at your menu? Thanks. 

I can't comment on the beers since I chose not to partake, but I was able to see they offer  a very limited selection of their own brews.  I went with the a chicken picatta special.  That was actually quite tasty. Chicken medallions in a lemon sauce with capers, mushrooms and tomatoes.  One friend got the buffalo mac n cheese and seemed very content. The other got a burger and did not think it was anything special.  Although, my dish was pretty good, I don't think this is really any place that I'd return to.  Everything just seemed so average. I have heard they are a decent for drinks and apps, but I probably won't be looking into that.

This place was super fun! We went on a Monday afternoon so there was no wait - the place was pretty dead since it was within an hour of closing time. I saw Slappy Cakes on Unique Eats and bookmarked on Yelp for the next time I was in Portland. I could see where the griddle could get very hot at your table but we went on a cold day so it was fine. The service was decent.  There were so many choices on the topping for pancakes it was hard to decide! We also read so many great reviews about the huevos rancheros we ordered those, the chicken fried bacon, and made our own pancakes.  The pancakes we made were the best item.  I was not in the love with the bacon - it was definitely made earlier in the day and slightly reheated which was not good so maybe if you came at a time it is fresh it would taste better?  I will still give "a-ok" 3 stars for this place.  It's a cute idea.  I would feel nervous bringing a child but if they are still around this must not be a problem.  Again, really cute idea! I would take someone from out of town. Oh and they had several delicious sounding grown up drinks!

Might be because I'm not a huge BBQ person, but I don't think the quality of the food was worth the price. I shared a big cheeks tray with a friend and we got pork belly, brisket, and pork ribs for the meats and potato salad and collard greens for our sides. I was excited to try their biscuits-- they were yummy and the honey butter was delicious-- but nothing beats the biscuits at Buttermilk and Bourbon! Maybe I'll go back if I'm craving meat... but honestly I can eat better and more meat for lower price elsewhere.

If you are hungry when you get seated you will be really hungry when your Order arrives. The manager let one very good waitress handle the breakfast and brought in several others for lunch. Jessica was the best of the stafff!  Thank you for makinG our day. We worried about her when we left and wanted to make sure she got all of the tip. The pancakes eggs and bacon were delicious. The chicken fried steak was nothing special and a bit over priced.

I was able to try this studio thanks to ClassPass. Because of all the boutique studios on ClassPass, I was really eager to try Commit 2B Fit. There are definitely good and bad things about this studio.

Good
-The quality of Katie's classes are excellent. She focuses on form and sprinkles lifestyle and fitness tips in her classes.

Bad
-The studio is so small. There were about a dozen women in a tiny room, but the instructor still had us moving all over. I had to time my movements carefully so as not to bump into people. Too bad people didn't extend that courtesy to me.
-The studio is dirty. Sometime classes are held outdoors and the equipment and floors reflect this. 
-The other instructors don't really keep an eye on the participants and seem inexperienced. I saw a woman squatting head first and nobody stopped her. 

As you can see, the bad outweighs the good. I'm glad ClassPass has let me try so many different gyms and studios, but this is one I won't use again.

Food: we had the spicy broth and two meat combos. The quantity is pretty good, though the meat quality is just alright. The quality to price ratio is a bit subpar compared to some other shabu places in Boston such as shabu zen, kaze shabu in Chinatown and swish shabu in Fenway, but it's still decent. I also didn't like the sauce mix here because, personally, I don't like sweet soy sauce with spicy shabu. Perhaps in the future they could add more options. However, I was very pleased with the quality, selection and quantity of the a la carte vegetable items.  I also liked that when they refill the broth for you, they use the broth you purchased instead of the generic base broth (a lot of shabu places do this and it dilutes out the flavor). 

Service: we got seated right away and someone came to take our order pretty quickly after that. Our server seemed really busy (she forgot to bring us a few things until we reminded her). They seemed to be under-staffed for a Saturday night, even though the place was relatively empty. As a result, our server was running around all over the place and so we had a hard time getting her attention. She did get everything we wanted and was very friendly!

Decor: really new, modern and the space is huge! It's a great place for large parties!

Roomie had a friend in from DC visiting for the night. She is a former Bostonian, and so on her one night in town she decides she wants to go to John Harvard's. I'd never been there before, nor had my friend... so our 4some ventured out of the Dot and all the way to the other side of the river for JH's.

The whole reason we went here was because she wanted a Chicken Pot Pie. Apparently... they're amazing if you like pot pies. I do not so ordered some asian style chicken thing... sesame i think. It was yummy - very good. So for the main meal, everyone game two thumbs up.

Desserts..... not such rave reviews. The brownie sundae... not so terrific. The brownie was cold (hello, brownie sundaes where the brownies are nuked and warmed and then the ice cream on top are amaaaaaaaazing). The butterscotch bread pudding apparently didn't have like any butterscotch taste and like zero drizzlings of the advertised caramel syrup.

We had a reservation and were seated right away. We thought things were going well, but the waitress took for forever to do anything as if she were slammed! Why??? The restaurant wasn't overly busy. So, I have no idea what she was doing.

All in all the experience was OK so I gave 3 stars. I'd go back there again if I was in the area, but I'd skip dessert here and get something somewhere else..... and would never go here if I was crunched for time (i.e. - before a movie).

Pros:

Decently sized, quiet rooms.

Indoor pool.

Great breakfast area that accomodates large groups well.

Laundry facility 24/7 and very efficient and inexpensive (1 dollar per machine)

Located very close to great restaurants and shops.

Cons:

Water pressure.  Taking a shower in the rain outside would be easier.  It is a seriously slow, no pressure shower.  Just bad for anyone with long hair to rinse.

Parking is valet only and 38 bucks a night.  It is recommended that you download the city's parking app Parking Kitty to reload your virtual meter, but even that's a pain.  The hotel is in a two hour area so you are constantly reloading on the app which also comes with a surcharge for use - of course!

Staff can be clueless on who is at the desk.  Sometimes we got great advice and at other times a deer in the headlights look.

Other than that it was a decent stay.

This is not a Tex-Mex restaurant.  They really did a good job with renovating the old Home Grill restaurant.  Very spacious and the booth and table set up are almost the same.  

The staff here is very friendly.  I went here for lunch so my review is based only on business during lunch when it was not busy.

I ordered the duck belly quesadilla with mole.  The mole was very tasty, I wish they had just a tad more duck belly in the quesadilla but overall it was good.

The menu is very limited and I wish they had a little more selection.  I moved to Austin from California so I am still partial to the Mexican food in Cali.

Overall is you want to come in for Happy Hour and have a love for Tequila this place is for you.

With TSA in Austin getting slower and slower, and the worst TSA "mall cop" experience in the Austin airport, I decided to fork out the $85 for TSA pre-check. Once approved, this is good for 5 years and allows you streamlined access through airport security at the more than 150 participating US airports.

The paperwork is all online, and once submitted, it gives you a choice between an office at ABIA and these guys to complete your appointment. All availability is posted in 15 minute increments, so it was easy to sign up for a convenient time slot. 

Upon arrival, there was no waiting. I was 10 minutes early and after showing appropriate identification and handing them the credit card I was paying with, I was walked back to one of the appointment rooms. 

It is a little impersonal and "process" oriented, but I felt like I did not get the memo. The woman taking my info was all business. She had a foreign accent and as I tried to make out her name (she never introduced herself), her name tag was hanging from her lanyard, upside down, and she shot me a stern look. I mentioned I was trying to see her name, but it is upside down. It started with a "w" but was not a common name or one I would remember. 

I was asked to have a seat, and when I set my coffee on the table, I was told to place it on the floor. (Okay) 

I was in a small office on the guest side of the desk. There was a large computer screen to my left. Screen by screen, I was asked me to verify the answers of questions (that I had already completed on-line). Then came the digital fingerprinting. FTR, if you have small hands, this is not for the faint of heart. First came my thumbs which both had to be on the scanner glass at the same time, but the barely reached the scan area. I felt like the woman was torture stretching them just to appear in the glass. She would press them down hard so the camera could capture all the grooves, but was having some issues doing this. She said if it did not work the third scan attempt, I would not be able to complete the appointment. By some act of magic, the third time was the charm and my thumbs feel a quarter inch longer (not cool). Then came, one hand at a time, the digital scan of 4 fingers for each hand. Again, she pressed them down on the glass hard, trying to get a good picture. I couldn't help but wonder if this was old technology, because a scan of my fingerprints at the DPS a few years ago was much more efficient and painless. 

Once my fingers were tortured, ahem, I mean scanned, they processed my credit card, handed me a receipt and told me I would receive an email with a UE ID (Universal Enrollment ID number) and could check the status on the web. She said it could take 30 days. I was escorted to the lobby and sent on my way. 

Three business days after my visit, I checked on line and I have already received my KTN (Known Traveler Number) and was informed I should receive a letter in the mail within 10 business days. The next time I fly, my TSA pre-check will allow me to bypass the long security line, keep my shoes and jacket on, and my laptop and liquids in my backpack. 

I will say that the process to get a TSA pre-check is on-line and fairly painless. The in-person interview was cold and absent any feel of human interaction. A robot might have been more suitable. The fingerprint scan was painful, bordering on torture. 

While Identogo did what they were contracted to do, they could hire people who like working with the public rather than stone faced government worker types. I did notice that they seemed to have plenty of time to take walk-ins. 

Identogo does not just do TSA pre-check services, but offer a full array of identity/background related services including live scan fingerprinting, fingerprint cards, FBI and state identity history checks, notary services, and photo services for things like passports and visas. They are a private firm designed to take a little of the bureaucracy and line standing out of the equation, and they do that. Their bedside manner leaves a lot to be desired (but that was just my experience). 

With thumbs up on the fast process and zero wait time (I was out of there in 9 minutes), but sore thumbs down on the fingerprinting and bedside manner, they get are a the only alternative in Austin to having to pay to park at ABIA for the same service. 2.5 stars, rounding to 3 (because I am nicer than they are).

After driving by a million times, my sweet man-friend and I decided to head in for breakfast early on a Sunday morning.  Expecting a wait based on the reviews here on Yelp, I was pleasantly surprised to find a very short line, and we could have even sat inside if it hadn't been so nice outside.  

The biscuits are good - that is a fact.  I had the biscuit with cream and fresh fruit, and was treated to a delicious tender and flaky biscuit, unsweetened whipped cream (DELISH!) and beautiful huge marionberries.  

I had higher hopes for the grits - they were fine, I guess.  The texture was creamy, and yes, the little kick of spice was nice, but they were lacking in dimension.  They could have used a bit of extra-sharp white cheddar, in my opinion, or at least some SALT.  Totally bland, for all the hype I read about them. 

Man-friend had the Reggie DeLuxe, which looked like a heart attack on a plate.  A deeeeelicious heart attack on a plate.  I didn't try any, but he said it was pretty good.  

Stumptown Coffee:  always a fan.

Service: nothing to shout about.  I assume everyone working that morning had a raging hangover.  It seemed like it.  But hey, they were functional.

BONUS: If you get there before 10:30 am, Triple Nickel lets Pine State customers use their picnic tables out front.  Great for summer - winter? Probably not so much.

Over all, pretty okay.  I took a star off for the bland grits and blander service, and a star off for the inflated price.  Our breakfast was $20, which just seemed too high for what is essentially a one-trick pony take out joint.

This place has very average BBQ.  I can't really pick out a meat that just blows me away but the brisket and pork are just average.  The concept is really cool and no other BBQ place that I have seen does it cafeteria style.  They have a great looking bakery shop in there as well and I have had a few items from there before and they were decent.  I so much want to like this place but it just doesn't blow me away.

I've been a fan of Pei Wei for several months, and I wanted to try the big brother - PF Chang's.  Everything was good, the decor was nice, the food was fresh and tasty.

The service was fantastic!  Please ask for Diane if you go.  Let the management know that she is a good waitress by requesting to be seated in her section.

We had egg drop soup, crab wonton, lettuce wraps, mongolian beef and sesame chicken.  I thought the crab wonton was great, and the egg drop soup and lettuce wraps were good.  I wanted some veggies served with my mongolian beef.

I'm only giving them 3 stars because the food was good, but not great.  For the price difference I would have been just as happy at Pei Wei.

My friend and I came here on a Friday around 12 o'clock and it was extremely busy. The restaurant is fairly small which resulted in us being placed in a sharing table. My friend got a ramune drink and said it taste like the dentist office while I got an oolong tea that taste like dirt. We noticed that people who ordered after us got their food first. My friend also said the water taste like it came from the toilet. I got the spicy ramen which was very flavorful and the noodles were cooked perfectly. My friend got a ramen that was onion flavored and it looked like they gave her the entire green onion. The waitress took forever to give us our check resulting in we had to initiate a signal to let her know we were done. I don't know if I would come back again.

It's no coincidence that just the other day a guy with ear gauges rear ended my car on his fixie just outside Nelson the Seagull. This block is clearly full of hipsters who could be more attentive to people they should be focusing on.

At Nelson it seems it will take you at least 10 minutes to get your food or coffee, if there's a line or not. That being said, the food and vibe are really decent. They make stellar bread which I lust after every once in a while either by the loaf of as part of a sandwich. The Ploughman's is my favorite -- a great blend of creamy boerenkaas, sharp red onion and sweet chutney, complemented by the fermenty dark crust and chewy crumb of the bread.

It takes a while for the guys in the back to prepare it, and the prices have gone up while serving sizes have gone down, but it's still worth it.

Just watch out for beard hair in your food.

We chose this restaurant because it ranked four stars on Yelp vs most others in the immediate vicinity which were 3.5 stars.  I'm giving 3 and one of those stars is extra for the service which was very friendly and attentive.  If portion sizes are important to you, you might give extra stars for that, and if you read the tips carefully, you will see that is what most ravers valued.  It is true that we carried home literally pounds of pasta in a doggie bag, never to be eaten. Personally, I would rather have smaller portions, and cooking to rave about -the food was okay, but very standard fare, and a few selections were sub-standard (like the meatballs, which were basically balled up hamburger meat, and the Saltimbocca which was watery, and the pasta which was overcooked).  The calamari was crispy, and served with tasty marinara sauce, so we did enjoy our appetizer.  Will we be going back? No.  And that is consistent with the hit or miss luck we've had in the North End - mostly misses.

Easily one of the fanciest hotels I've ever stayed in.  Everything is very clean and well taken care of.  The staff is very friendly and always willing to help.  It truly is a top notch place.    

Why the 3 stars?  I'm sorry, but if you are paying as much as you do for a room here, why must they charge you $18/day for self parking and don't have a fridge in the room?  If my job wasn't insistent on me staying here, I would have stayed down the road, and saved the job a bit of money.  I get that they have a lot of folks on the payroll, which is probably why it's so nice there.  But $18/day for self parking?  Come on man!  The parking lot was full every day I was there, so if they charged $5-$10/day, they'd still make out on it.  The kicker, was when I got charged $19.17 (yes, they add tax too!) for parking for 4 hours.  I was told that if you are parked for over 20 minutes, you get charged for a full day!  UNREAL!  

If they get rid of the astronomical prices for parking and put a tiny fridge in every room, 5 stars all the way.

My absolute favorite part was meeting Spider-Man. The characters at universal are so personable. We loved the photos so much we invested in the $100+ unlimited photo pass. To be honest I didn't go on a single ride here. I am a total ride wimp and essentially spent the day meeting different characters. I felt that universal studios has a bit more to do in some ways. However island of adventure had tons of ride options and some cute themes as well.

I worked in a building across the street from Haru while they where building it and when it finally opened we were interested to give it a try. 

I'm going to be upfront right now and say I'm not a sushi fan. And you might as why the hell did I go to a sushi place. Well, most sushi places do have choices other than fish. And Haru does...although probably not enough to satisfy the majority of non-fish or sushi eating people.  

My co-workers ordered the lunch boxes and some sushi. I got a side of yakitori and a tofu dish. Both were rather good and I was happy with my choices. The downside was the cost as it was a bit pricey - for lunch. Granted we figured that would be the case and considered it a splurge lunch. (Yeah, we wished we had the corporate card to charge it to!). 

The decor is fun and they have some neat light fixtures in there. There is a bit of modern starkness that does have a bit of a cold feeling. Every employee was dressed well in suits or similar. As we exited the restaurant, it was like we were royalty or something as every single person who worked at Haru said good bye to us as we walked past them to the door. It was a bit much and a little awkward.

Overall, not bad.

My family and I were looking for a casual dining experience with great food after a long day at the theme parks.  Mannys did a great job getting us in and fed!  The food was ok- as I am a steak coniseur I was hoping for a little better.  My father ordered a T bone medium rare which came out well done and was poorly cut.  The waitress did correct the problem quickly and a new steak came out almost immediately.  Overall for the price and quality you're better off going to Texas roadhouse a couple minutes up the street.

I really don't need to write anything about Pour House really that hasn't already been said.

Decent bar food (which is a lot for the Boylston street bar area, sadly enough), easy enough  to get a seat, nice shakes, typical Boylston Bar (Patents Pending) shitty beer list (Sorry, I love me some Guiness, but Guiness alone won't save you).

Service is passable, I don't remember anything absolutely outstanding above and beyond, but do you really need that kind of stuff?

Avoid it during the SAWX games unless you want to be packed in like a sardine.

I checked Yelp before coming out to Zab E Lee, but yelp didn't really tell me anything about the sushi. So, here we go as you can see in my pictures the sushi looks fine for the most part. With the exception of the yellowtail. The yellowtail is poorly colored, to say the least. Each piece of sushi has a very small clump of rice, which would be fantastic at just about any other sushi restaurant. However, the fish to rice ratio is way off for this establishment. As the fish Is what I would call "sub-medium Quality", the rice portion should've been larger and the fish portion should've been smaller to hide the inequities. 

The yellowtail was also rather salty and the best way I can explain the texture would be spongy. The tuna and salmon were very brightly colored and looked great, but they just didn't have great flavor. In the case of the squid, it popped like cartilage, but it didn't have any creamy textures. Plus, again the flavor wasn't really there. 

The only piece of sushi that I remotely liked was the unagi, but even it didn't have as good of flavor as I'm used to. The only consolation about the meal was that for all you see in my photos, I only spent $31 (plus tip). 

Now, you might be wondering why I gave this restaurant three stars when I'm saying that the sushi was just god-awful...

I also ordered some of their coconut soup. Remember, this is not Hey Japanese sushi restaurant. Zab E Lee is a Thai restaurant that just happens to serve sushi. The coconut soup was pretty good. My personal preference would be for a little bit less lemongrass and more chicken, but it was a delicious soup.

I will probably order from them again... Definitely not the sushi... But I will probably order some Thai food from them as it seems like they'll do that very well.

My honest recommendation to the chef to prepare the sushi is, please look for a better fish vender... Perhaps ask the people at a Happy Sumo. I would also recommend that you cut the fish a bit more thinly. Sushi Is an art form that is all about balance in beauty and flavor.

I'm not rating the beer since I didn't have any. This is solely based on the food and delivery. 

First the NEGATIVES: The  sausage was burnt, very salty and honestly tasted like something I could have gotten at the grocery store. Hebrew national hot dogs taste better than that. The fries were a bit dry and I only had a couple because they didn't taste very good. The pierogies were very doughy and the flavor of the dough was lacking, very bland. They tasted packaged to me. The potato pancakes weren't very crispy and I just didn't like the flavor of them. I did like how they came with sour cream but wish they also came with apple sauce. The blueberry pierogies were very doughy and would have much better fried. 

Now the POSITIVES: The sauerkraut and the coleslaw are pretty good.  The creamy sauce that came with the blueberry piergies was DIVINE and make you think of Boston Creme donuts. 

Overall, this pace was interesting enough that I would try again one more time. But so far I am not super impressed with the food.

We went into the restaurant around 8:45 hoping that we would catch the 9:30pm happy hour but was too hungry so decided to order from the main menu first.

At first, we were going to order their deluxe sashimi platter but didn't felt like it was worth it as 10 pieces = ~$55. So we decided to go for some nigiris, beef hotpot, and one of their special rolls (don't remember which one but it was the one with spicy scallops).

Nigiris looked really good but was just ok. Same for the special rolls that we ordered. I guess my expectations have definitely heightened from dining at quite a bit of jap restaurants the last few years lol. The best part of the dinner was the beef hotpot. It was simple yet satisfying. It came with approximately 10 pieces of fatty sliced beef with a bed of lettuce and 3 types of mushrooms. We opted for the miso broth and it was quite good, along with the price of it (very reasonable for this dish).

Anyway, we expected a rush of people to come at 9:30 to take advantage of their late night specials but when we finished at 10:15, no one came in and we were the only table for the last hour and a half. The location's not the best so it may suffer from people seeing the restaurant unless they researched it on the internet beforehand. Be advised that this restaurant has changed its operating hours to open until 1:30am.

I've been to Ocha twice now. The first time I found it quite good. My drink was the perfect amount of sweetness and the flavors were good. However the second time I popped by, a few months later, I ordered the exact same thing and was not wowed. I don't know if it was an off day or something but my drink was too sweet and the flavors just didn't taste quite right. 
Their presentation is definitely on point though!! 
Overall they're not necessarily the best bubble tea in the Portland but if you are up in their neighborhood they are an option if you're craving boba. 
Despite being disappointed on my second visit I still plan to stop by again as they do have a vast menu and I hope that I will enjoy their other drinks.

I was very hopeful and ended up disappointed. I've had poke in Chicago and it's outstanding, here I ordered not knowing what i was ordering as this place works like a chipotle. It would be more effective if the offer preset combinations. Poke is all about combining flavors and I was lost. I guess that with guidance I could get something better. Ok. I get it. What I just also surprised me was the price. A large bowl with 4 proteins that are by the way hard to find - portions are very small and an order of 5 dumplings was almost 18. No drink. I had water. With that I would have paid almost 21. Not really worth it. In chicago an outstanding poke bowl would have been less. 
Nicely decorated, clean. They offer Keto, veggie options.

Smaller than other locations but the same friendly staff.
Advertising at the entrance enticed me to try the Elk burger with it's greatly reduced fat, calories and more protein than the other options of beef, ostrich or buffalo. Weighing in at $10.49 Elk isp almost twice the regular rice of the1/2 lb. Not wanting to be too healthy I made is southwestern with guac, bacon and pepper jack. The meat was good and I left happy and full.
I think I'll pass on the Elk next time and down grade to the Buffalo.

I'm in a Sunday afternoon bowling league that happens here, and it's a pretty decent setting for it. It's big enough to accommodate everyone, there's tons of tvs to keep your attention while waiting for your turn, there are great drink specials ($10 for a bucket of 4 PBR tall boys), and waitresses come right over to your lane to take your order. The food is not bad, fries and chicken fingers are generally pretty good, and the service can be spotty but not horrible. All in all, I have a good time here.

I was here for dinner recently.

Food 4/5: I was absolutely starving that evening and ordered the roti canai ($6) and the Malaysian style laksa ($9.95).  Yum and yum!  The roti wasn't greasy and was accompanied by a nice dipping sauce.  I don't have laksa often enough to distinguish between what's good or not, but whatever I have having was delicious.  Lots of toppings, flavourful, not too spicy, albeit a bit salty.

Value 3/5: Between the two of us, we paid $30, which was pretty decent for what we got.  Some of the other menu items seemed to be on the pricey side. 

Ambiance 2/5: Small restaurant, very quiet on a Saturday night, no music, no ambiance, too dark.

Service 3/5: Prompt, friendly, no complaints.

Overall, a solid 3.5/5.

We knew we'd get here eventually, since it is now the closest Ted's for us, but today was a surprise.  Sweetie had a craving for their mashed potatoes and sauteed mushrooms (and for Ray Ray's brisket, so I went on a trek...)  She used to work at a Ted's and we've been there a few times, so it's a fallback place for us, and always good.

This location just opened, and they are still working the kinks out.  Still, it was good, and I'm sure we'll be back and they'll have things together better.

It's in the "suburb" of Easton just to the east.  There is street and lot parking, though of course since it's Easton it can get pretty busy.  I snagged a spot out front, and they weren't too busy mid-afternoon on a Sunday.  It's decorated like other Ted's, with lots of wood, fairly fancy overall.  However, this one is far more bright and airy than the other Columbus locations.

Service was great, from several employees.  I sat at the bar to order our carryout.  Mashed pots and shrooms for her, trout dip and the chopped salad for me (hey, I have to eat healthy sometimes.)  The bartender asked if I wanted meat on the salad, so I said sure, bison, done medium.  I noticed the fresh lemonade jug at the bar, so had one to pass the time.  That turned into two lemonades, and one to go, because, well, it took forever.  None of that should have taken long; maybe the longest would be the bison, but still, half an hour for a to-go order?  The staff were apologetic, and offered snacks (and free refills.)  When the food came out we were missing the pots and shrooms, the whole reason for the trip.  That was swiftly corrected, and I was on my way.

The food was... a mixture of good and okay.  Sweetie loved the mashed potatoes and gravy, and the mushrooms.  I liked the trout dip.  I had expected bits of trout in a sauce, but it is chunks of trout, good trout, with a bit of sauce and seasoning.  Served with good tortilla chips, it was the star.  The lemonade was very good (though not as good as homemade.) 

 The salad... was just okay.  The salad itself was sad, and nothing like the description.  "Iceberg, roasted corn, garbanzo beans, vine-ripened tomato, green pepper, red onion, cucumber, smoked ham, basil vinaigrette."  Lots of iceberg, half a dozen chickpeas (literally,)  a couple dozen kernels of plain corn, a few small bits of tomato, no cukes, no peppers, a tiny bit of ham and a couple of slices of red onion.  And, missing the promised dressing.  The meat was another disappointment.  I figured it would be crumbled ground bison, and might add $3 to the $6 salad.  Nope, it was a separate bison patty, clearly intended for burgers, and added $9.  To a $6 salad.  I had a chance to pass when I saw the bill, and didn't, to avoid further slowdowns.  I would recommend passing on the added meat, and probably the whole salad.  Still, it was healthy, I enjoyed the trout dip, and (added to some Ray Ray's brisket) I was full.  Plus, Sweetie was happy.

So, ups and downs, to be expected for a new place.  I figure things will smooth out soon and they will join other locations with 4-5 stars.  Even with the wait and other issues, we had a good meal and will be back, to dine in or for more cravings...

I have only been here for lunch since I work at the Pru. However, it's a great little spot. The ginger pomegranate soda is refreshing when you can't have an alcoholic beverage. I love their pork and broccoli rabe sandwich. It is quite large but the flavours of the juicy meat and slightly bitter greens pair well. Their fries are always crisp and piping hot. The price is a little higher than I would like to pay for lunch but I always get two meals out of it. Four stars for the food!

I would give a higher rating if the service was not bad every time. I always go off hours in the early afternoon and it is fairly empty. However, it takes a long time for anything to happen and there are rarely check-ins so I am trying to flag someone down for more water or the check. I don't know where these servers go when there are only a few customers. Also, one time I was finally able to order and was only then told that they were out of the sandwich - it would have been nice to mention that when we sat down since now I'm rushing to find something else while the server is visibly sighing. 

I would suggest that the waitstaff is trained better to match how well everything else is done here because I sure do like the food.

The most delicious Thai dish I've tried was from this restaurant.... BUT, it's not a 5-star rating because I had a less-than-fresh piece of fish from here. 

I have a love-hate relationship with their "hot chili fish."  The first time I had it, I thought it was the most amazing dish ever.  The fried fish was crispy and not too oily and the sauce was perfectly spiced. However, the second time I ordered the dish, it wasn't so good.  I bit into a very fishy-smelling, not-so-flaky piece of fish.  It was so bad that I had to spit it out.         

I haven't ordered from them since the incident, but maybe when I'm in Weymouth again, I'll give it another try.  Hopefully, it'll be a 5-star review then.

My boyfriend and I decided to try this place for sushi Friday night and showed up at the restaurant a little before 8.  There were 3 tables of people seated and eating.  The place seemed nice and the waitress friendly. We ordered miso soup for him and edamame for myself. His soup came but my edamame didn't come until about half-way through our meal.  The sushi was tasty and fresh - I had the "I love salmon" he had an unagi roll and super spider roll.  Shortly after we got our food the rest of the place emptied out and we were the only ones there, so one of the ladies started vacuuming.  I thought it was a little odd and looked at the time, it was only 8:20 (it says they close at 10 on Fridays).  Soon she was vacuuming right beside our table. So rude!  The food is good, but the service pathetic.

I wanted a really good and fresh salad. And I got an okay salad, I can't say it was real fresh.

This is a fancy subway type spot where everything is out and ready to be put together.

I got a chopped salad, which you'd expect would be chopped...not so much. The chicken was good but not a ton of flavor. Overall it was good, not great; to the point I did t eat it all.

My wife's "make your own" was tastier mostly due to the brusssels which were tasty. The quinoa was good and the sweet potato noodles were real interesting. She was pleased and said she'd come back.

The fresh juice was indeed fresh and quite good.

The baked mac n cheese? Hard pass. This was noodles with warmed up cheese sauce, I do not think any baking happened.

Lots of options in this area, I'll keep looking.

I"m really not sure what to think of this place.

Granted, I only stopped in for a cocktail and to see the space, so I don't have much of a relationship with the place.

It looks really freaking cool in there. Every little bit of the place has been very carefully crafted together. The patio is okay, but compared to the inside, it doesn't really hold a candle to the definite vision that the inside has.

Our waitress was nice. Not always there, but always around. I'd been drinking tequila already, so I tried their Añejo Manhattan. Damn. It was really tasty. And it tasted like a Manhattan, to boot! Was it worth $10? Not sure, but I've been charged similar prices for crappier drinks.

I looked over the menu, and it's very interesting. However, it doesn't liken people to come here for snacking. I'd have tried the grits, but didn't know if I could justify paying $9 for grits. Plus, I wasn't that hungry for something heavy. Cheese plate? $14! Ok. Ok. Probably a really decent amount of amazing cheeses with acoutrements. Well, I wouldn't know because I didn't order it. 

The people across from us did, and it looked to be on the small side. Granted, I could see it's a really interesting menu and all, but I'd be more likely to try some things as a happy hour special then go back for it later at whatever price if I was really enthralled by the cuisine.

Lastly, and most confusingly, I thought this was supposed to be a Show Room. As in they will have shows of some kind? The site says they want to do this. And yet, I couldn't find a stage anywhere. Granted, I sat outside, but I walked through there twice and was paying attention, I think, and...no stage? Where's the show gonna go?

This place should get about 3.5 stars - it's good, but just slightly overpriced.

Trident is one of the only places in Back Bay that serves up a real breakfast selection on weekdays, which makes it an automatic go-to.  The atmosphere is laid-back, like a bookstore.  Waitresses are friendly, if a little rushed.  Table space is a minimal.  

Menu offerings are extensive for such a small operation.  The sandwiches all sound amazing, and many of them are.  Favorites include the Monte Cristo breakfast sandwich which is a hearty mix of sweet and savory, and the Cape Codder (turkey, cranberry mayo, swiss cheese, lettuce).  Trident fries are vegetable fries that are novel, unique, and well done.  Cheesy tots are overrated, as are some of their baked goods.  Most sandwiches range from $10-12, and breakfast entrees around $8.  It shooooould be a dollar or two less per item, for what you're getting.

All in all, a good joint for those of you in Back Bay looking for a nice, easy breakfast.

Let me just preface by saying that I have no basis for comparison re: Korean food in Columbus and I'm trying not to compare it to Korean food in other cities that I've had (which have been really good, so it wouldn't be fair).

Came here for a quick lunch and to check out the food. There were 2 polite and efficient servers running the roomy and very pleasant space inside. Ordered the dolsot bibimbap and a pork & kimchi soup and both were pretty good, standard, quality. The prices are a tad high especially after lunch so keep that in mind. Overall a solid selection when you need a Korean food fix in the university area.

Not a bad place to get brunch or breakfast with a friend. Seems like they have a decent lunch and dinner menu too. The environment has a nice Austin flavor--funky, vintage cafe.

I feel like I shouldn't be rating the Omelettry because I didn't get an omelette, but whatever. Get the gingerbread pancakes! So fluffy and delicious...yum. 

Bottom line: Nothing that will blow you out of the water, but solid breakfast food. 

Tip: Take a look at the vintage store next door! Some cool stuff there. :)

The food was delicious, but this place is overpriced. I mean the premium they must take is just insane, espeically when there's a Chipotle literally right across the street from them where you can get more food, very similar quality, more options for toppings and it'll be cheaper. I got the Niko and the chicken was amazing, and $11 for a sandwich is fine but not at a 'fast casual' place. There just wasn't enough food or variety within the meal for it to be that much both with the sandwich and the plate.

we came here for a nice light dinner with soup and salad.

the restaurant itself is clean and quiet. it wasn't busy at all, even for dinner. the wait staff and personnel were soo nice, i could pinch their cheeks! 

the menu is pretty basic with sandwiches, soup, salads and drinks. i got the caesar salad with a half club sandwich. pretty decent sandwich and basic. the salad was huge and slightly with too much dressing. my advice is to get the dressing on the side. they do have a condiments table with pickles and complimentary breadsticks (the hard skinny kind in a package, not like olive garden) and even capers!

the place is reasonably priced as well, so you won't break the bank coming here. it has outdoor seating which is nice. located in a great area so parking shouldn't be an issue.

The lunch special is well priced at $9.50+tax for 4 items (choice of noodle + choice of rice + salad/miso soup + side).

It can get busy during lunch time though the staff is fairly fast in getting your orders and serving them. The hot tea served tasted very diluted though. 

The food was average. The salad might be a better choice as the miso soup was very salty and tasted like it was out of a packet. The beef slices in the udon soup were very tender and that was the highlight, besides the raw salmon slices on rice. 

Just don't expect too much from this place.

YVR Poutine Crawl:
Like any hokey tourist, we love to try local foods no matter how stereotypical they might be. While poutine, I believe, is more of an eastern/Montreal specialty, I'm not going to pass up gravy, fries, and cheese curds. Since our layover was from 1am to noon, we were limited in our chance to explore beyond our hotel and thus the YVR Poutine Crawl was born. Here are our rankings:

1. Canucks Bar & Grill (USA terminal/AFTER security): Above and beyond the best we had, but we figured this would be the case. They offer a classic poutine, and a version with mushrooms and bacon. We got the latter and thought the mushrooms were chewy, but the bacon was a good addition. The only bummer with this was that Canucks Bar & Grill had surly staff and they seated us RIGHT in front of constantly buzzing kitchen door despite tons of other seating. They have no Canadian beers on tap, but a bunch in bottles.

2. A&W (National terminal/BEFORE security). This was our first taste and I actually really liked it. The cheese curds were squeaky and not too melty, the gravy was good and plentiful, but the fries were a tad soggy. I thought I would like soggy fries better, but crispy actually taste better!

3. Burger King (USA terminal/AFTER security) The cheese curds were melted and the stringy gooey mess was delcious, but a pain in the rear to eat. We basically needed to use our hands to pull it apart. The crispy fries were a bonus. They do technically offer bacon for $1, but they were out.

Honorable mention: White Spot (National terminal/BEFORE security): They serve poutine, but  only once breakfast is over at 11am. 

**Note: It is VERY easy to walk between the National/USA/International terminals. The YVR airport is wonderful with tons of shops, but quite small overall.

I'm a big fan of their bagels, and their English muffins! I love the jalapeno cheddar bagel, turned into am egg breakfast sandwich. Service could be a little more friendly; most of the foks that have helped me have had that non-chalant, angsty Portland hipster vibe, as though they would rather be somewhere else. It would be so nice to be greeted with a smile, and some sincerity, but I know that's asking a lot in this town.

It would also be great if they had time limits set on the tables, if only during busy hours. There was one dude, who was sprawled over a four top, all by himself. He had finished his food by the time we walked in, and was still there as we huddled in the corner trying to eat our food standing. It's a fine line, and I understand that's a hard thing to manage, but they could try and implement something so that one person doesn't take up a 4-top for an hour plus AFTER they've finished their food. I think to-go is a good option when they're packed!

**I'm editing my review to note the following: I am not recommending you don't visit. You should! The food was fine and fresh, just not to my taste on this visit. The owners contacted me afterwards expressing concern over my dissatisfaction; customer service is second to none.  **

New World Cafe is similar to New World Deli but just doesn't have the charm of its original Hyde Park counterpart.  Between the TV tuned to CNN, the dark lighting and the beer signs I might have mistaken the place for the Boulevard Bar and Grill a few doors down if not for the extensive sandwich curation.

I ventured down to this location tonight (a Friday night) and it was relatively quiet, save for a few patrons.  My guess would be that they see a big lunch crowd and the evenings are not as popular in general.  The server at the front recommended the curried chicken salad after I learned they don't carry eggplant parm at this location and so I ordered the 1/2 sand and soup (broccoli cheese.)

What can I say?  The food was very safe.  In my head curried chicken salad is usually served with melba toast to ladies who lunch (tm) on a bed of lettuce.  The salad, not the ladies.  This was served on my choice of bread (sourdough) with crudites.   Was the sandwich bad?  No, but it was bland, sort of old-style Southern charmlike in its 'exotic' curry flavoring and remarkably underseasoned (though that may be my sinuses talking).  

I lost my appetite after eating the broccoli cheese soup - definitely not canned, but bizarre in that it was cheese soup with bigger-than-your-mouth broccoli florets - and took my sandwich to go.  I think I'll come back for the burger but I need to do it during the day time when NWC doesn't feel so much like a poorly lit sports bar.  Some candles or possibly eliminating the glowing lights of the television would go far in giving this place a modicum of the charm of the other location.

The stars go to the server and the cook, who were charming and remarkably efficient.  My soup/sam were out in two minutes - yowza.

P.S. They'll be getting wine soon, for now only domestic bottled beer (and only one local, some beer with the Austin mural logo across the front). Meh.

Went here from suggestion of a friend after a long hot day. Parking is hard to find as it is a small shop. You can either park on the street in the front of the store or a couple parking spaces in the back. I got the honey green tea with 80 percent sugar and it tasted very bland like they decided to not add the sugar at all and nothing really special. My boyfriend ordered the iced mocha and liked it. I would say it's really similar to the iced mocha frap from Starbucks. Overall decent place, but nothing out of this world.

I would give it four stars if it wasn't so expensive. I opted not to get an entree because I thought they were too pricey. Instead I split two small plates with my friend. We got the fries...nothing special there but very good...and the cornmeal mushrooms...very good and highly recommended. My other friend got the fettuccine and she enjoyed it.

For desert I got the Napoleon. It was light and delicious. My friends got the chocolate cake and both thought it was rich and tasty.

We went on a Friday night around 8 p.m. and were seated almost immediately. Service was good. 

I feel like this review is so boring but I think it's because I found this place boring.

This past Saturday "Lucy's" lost its luster for me.  Sad because we often use Lucy's for cheat days and we love the delicious cocktails.  Saturday we took some friends out to the Lake location.  Our server was great, silly but no complaints there.  Our friends were interested in having a big party there.  We asked our waitress if there was anyone we could speak to about a party of 45+.  The response we got was shocking.  We were welcome to email but no one would personally talk to us?   They were not busy.  So disappointed, can't believe we didn't even get offered an email.  Thumbs down!!!

This was highly recommended by my supervisor, so once we got off our flight it was the perfect timing for lunch. We arrived 5 minutes before they opened and there was already a line! Once it was time, we got seated. The water they offer had hints of coconut in it. I'm not a fan of coconut water, but this was acceptable since it was a very light hint. 

The wings were a must order, we got the 1/2 dozen. It was good. In my opinion, I've had better. I think it was a bit too flavorful for my liking and not enough meat.

I really liked the coconut rice in the small container. it was cute and kept the rice warm. 

Overall, everything was maybe a little too flavorful for me. that's personal preference.

I'm leaving this review just as a helpful tip for other would-be kayakers (and as a nudge to management!) Despite the fact that the website says "tours daily 10 AM and 2 PM", and that kayak rentals are availably daily, this may or may not be true the day you show up. CALL AHEAD. We tried calling a number of times, but no one answered, so we just showed up and were told they weren't renting or doing tours this time of year. I suggested they should update the website so that the homepage doesn't say "tours daily" if there are no tours, let us know if we have to wait until April (or whenever). So just call and make sure they are actually operating! Good luck!

used a Groupon for this place, BEWARE, they said the deal was only valid after 5pm but this wasn't stated on the Groupon

there's both a casual cafe area & fine dining area where they have live music at times, but the chef brings the meats to your table regardless of where you choose to sit! you can also go to the kitchen to choose your own meats!

---FRIED YUCCA MMM cant get enough of this
---meats overall weren't nearly as tasty as at Oliveira's, but the BEEF RIBS were good! the meats here tend to be a bit oversalted & a few were overcooked (although we came when it wasn't particularly busy)
---large selection at the salad bar but again nothing compared to Oliveria's!!

NOTE there's a yelp picture w/ fruits but this wasn't an option when we came?!

The truck came weekly nearby our work. They seriously need help in their order taking. I don't understand why it's so hard. They are slow in taking orders. They mess up orders a lot. I heard stories from my co-workers, as well as my own experience.

The last one was this. I ordered a burrito, just a burrito. The guy who took my order asked me, did I want Guac & Awe or Guac Star. I thought he meant the guac that went inside the burrito. So I said the first one. Then he told me I owed $13. A burrito cost just $7 or $8 according to the menu. I asked, really? $13 for just a burrito? He talked to someone else and ended up charging me just $8. That's fine.

When I got my food, I got a burrito, a guac, chips & salsa. Which was the burrito + guac + salsa. Which cost $13. 

My co-worker ordered a nacho. The guy behind him ordered the same thing. But the guy behind him got the nacho first. My co-worker had to wait extra 5 minutes. When he brought up the issue with them, they said sorry the rain and all caused them to back up preparing orders (how did the rain affect them at all, since they were inside the truck?).

The food is good. The guacamole is very filling. The burrito is tasty. I am not much of a tamale person but I found their tamale quite decent. 

I just can't stand the ordering process....

The space is a bit tight (they will seat you with random people at times), they didn't have any of the drinks I wanted, but the show was funny.

I honestly feel the experience is based on the comedian there that night.

The service was attentive, but also stayed out of your way since you didn't want to be taking orders while trying to catch the jokes.


It was fun. Definitely a place to go in groups. Had my girlfriend and another couple with us, so it was easier to feel comfortable.

Franchise, yes. Looking past that, however. I got to the airport around 11 am. I needed to eat something to suffice for lunch, so when I so Charley's while headed to the security check point, I took a detour. 

Meats and toppings are cooked right in front of you. Fries are cooking behind the line cooks. Oh, and they put their buns through a conveyor toaster thingy to get is warm and soft. I chose the Chicken Philly & Fries special for $5. Sandwich? Tried and true. Fries? Well, I personally am not a giant fan of the thick cut design. They were fresh out of the fryer though, hot and soft. Could have used a bit of salt or seasoning. But not bad at all. 

The two gentlemen working the food counter were efficient and fast. No complaints. Hey, when pressed for time and /or destination, I'm glad this joint was a small detour off the main path.

I came here with my wife last weekend to see Black Rebel Motorcycle Club.  I had never been to the venue before, but I read a few reviews beforehand so I knew what I was getting into.

As far as the venue goes, it's all right.  Kinda old, kinda dirty, but that gives it some style and the dive bar feel that is starting to disappear in this town.  The sound system here, and the guys who work it are awesome!  I love when a venue takes care to make sure the bands that people are paying to see sound good.  The sound crew did an amazing job!

I loved that they had a seating area upstairs (where the bar is)... we grabbed a couple of seats, and were easily able to get another drink when the mood struck.  Prices are a little high on the beverage side, but that's true of a lot of venues.

I liked the Roseland, and would probably go to another show there if they were hosting a band I wanted to see.  I'd give them a 3.5 if I could, but I'm gonna have to settle for a 3.  Not a bad venue, but not fantastic either.  Some upgrades could go a long way for this place.

Tip:  don't stand against the wall upstairs.  Security comes through regularly, and they will make you move.  I saw at least 50 people get talked to during the show.

Solid Asian fusion restaurant, the only real disappointment was the initial service. We didn't have reservations on a Friday evening so we decided to stop by, and give it a try.

Initially seating a table of 4 wasn't an issue, we were given menus and almost led to a table. Then they took everything back and had to see what was available. We wanted to sit inside, but they led us outside to the 'patio' (3 tables behind a bush), but we reiterated that we wanted to sit inside so they said they would try and find something (we could see an entire row of open tables, so I'm not sure what the hold up was).

Once we were actually seated, everything else was fine. Our server was great - she gave us very good recommendations and the drinks were good, a little weak, but tasty.

Had my group come and not had such an issue right when we walked in the door this would be a totally different review. I don't think I'll be coming back here any time soon.

I decided to give this place a try since all the rave about vegan food. Although I'm not vegan, I've had some vegan food that was great so I was excited to try this place out. I had to take a "double-dutch approach of when I would go because some reviewers had consistently mentioned 1-3 hour wait times. I had absolutely NO interest in this so I figured after the newness wore off, I would be in the clear. I then learned that they don't open until 4 PM so that added another layer to planning. I figured that an early, weekday trip would spare me the wait. I was wrong. What added to my time was trying to find parking. I ventured out around 3:30 on a Monday and upon passing by, there was already a line forming. When I finally made it to the line, I realized that the long lines are sectioned off with dividers to prevent blocking neighboring businesses. From the time of getting in the line at 3:50 and getting my food, it was about 2 hours.  It's sort of like a catch 22. Once you've waited for 30-45 minutes, you feel defeated if you leave because now you realize that you wasted 30-45 minutes of your time which didn't include time you wasted for parking. Nevertheless, they have a rep that will periodically come outside to greet and inform customers of the burgers they will serve on that particular day. They have a limited amount of burgers that one person can order which is cool because I'm sure you'd have some people who are willing to avoid the long wait and have someone order for them.  They have this cool theme for first time "virgins" or people who's first time eating at the slutty vegan. Once inside, the service moves pretty quickly. I decided to try the Menage a Trois. All of their burgers comes with fries. There's their slutty vegan sauce they add as well. On my first bite, I was waiting for something to happen but it didn't happen. The burger wasn't bad but it wasn't worth the wait. It lacked flavor and the sauce was too spicy. The shrimp that came on the sandwich was pretty good but because I'm not a fan of spicy, I wish I would have asked for it on the side. The fries were seasoned well. At the end of the day, I came, I tried, and I probably won't return because of the wait time didn't balance out my experience with the food. Great customer service. Cool slogan/brand and they have a great marketing team. Also, they don't have indoor dining/seating options although we did see people showing up with lawn chairs.

My husband and I have been to Birch St Bistro many times in the last four years we've lived in Roslindale, and I've never had a bad experience. Unfortunately, we decided to take my grandparent-in-laws (is that a thing?) who were visiting from Maui last Wednesday night and had a really tepid experience.
