To summarize, the service was really scattered and disorganized and the entrees were mediocre. The latter surprised me the most, as usually the food is delicious. Perhaps this sub par visit is due to coming on a non-peak night, but I arrived wanting to impress my guests, and left feeling a bit let down. I'm sure we will give the bistro another try at some point, but I'm in no hurry to return...

This is my go-to gym during the week.  It is conveniently located within a short drive of where I work.  Since I drive to work, I do enjoy that you can use the parking lot, starting at 5:30.  Depending on how I hit the lights coming over from work, sometimes I get there as soon as 5:20.  Most of the attendants will let me park, though it is possible you may get turned away for showing up too early.  Getting street parking, as a non-South End resident, may be tough.  Just try to show up at/after 5:30 and you're good.  Enough about the parking lot.

The gym isn't enormous, but they have figured out a way to pack everything in there without feeling like you are on top of each other.  For the size of the gym, there is a lot of cardio equipment, particularly treadmills.  

The class schedule is part of the draw for me.  If I come after work, I make sure to sign up for a class, that way you're not spending a lot of time looking for empty cardio/weight machines to use.  There are several excellent spinning instructors at 6:00 (both am and pm) that I find to be some of the best I've encountered in the BSC system.  

The locker rooms are a bit on the small side, particularly when you show up at peak times, like 5:30-6:00 area.  But, magically everyone seems to find a place for their stuff.  When I've come in the mornings, it does feel like they could use a few more counters with hair dryers, as there are definitely some that take their time getting ready and kind of camp out at those counters.  I try to bring my own hair dryer just in case I need to improvise.  The only other comment regarding the locker room is that I find a lot of folks do not abide by the no cell phone usage policy at this gym, in the locker room, as compared to some of the other ones I visit.  On a recent visit, a girl was trying to arrange a phone interview while changing in the locker room...I mean really?!?!?

I'm going to give them three stars. They weren't bad, and for $19 I can't complain about the speed and service I received. 

However, after my adjustment and a drive home I was in worse shape than I started. I couldn't even stand. I'll blame that one on the vehicle ride home with an inflamed lower back. 

I really didn't like the rushed feeling I got. I don't like that they don't take insurance, and because of that, they are very keen to recommend a pre-paid package after the adjustment.  Without any X-rays, they feel comfortable telling you it will take several more adjustments to fix the problem. 

If you're in pain and need immediate help for and can pay the introductory $19 fee to get seen, then this is the place for you. Otherwise, find someone else.

Quick visit so I didn't get to try the food, but asked for 3 whiskeys that were menu items that they ended up being out of. Then the old fashioned was very subpar and had ice cubes like they came out of a coke machine and sugar at the bottom of the glass like it hadn't been stirred well. All stuff that the ownership and management should be keeping an eye on. However, the staff was super friendly and welcoming. I must say that the only great thing is the staff. Hard working and approachable. It's a shame they aren't being taught how to make good cocktails and are not provided a large inventory.

It could have been the waiting for months for this place to open that gave me over inflated expectations, but I really don't see what all the fuss is about. I live spitting distance away from here but have only been a few times over the past year. I wanted to give it the benefit of the doubt so I've gone at different times and had different plates each time. I've had most of the menu and my general review is a solid 3 stars. Fried and sauced, covered in fresh herbs (love), and raw onions (hate). Over priced and over hyped. Small but good selection of draft beer and house sake (hot or cold.) My favorite is the tako taco- but really the best part about it is the tobiko. The fried tortilla is unnecessary and the only purpose is it has is to boost the overall look of the plate and make it look larger. My least favorite is the Poor Qui Buns. No texture, only flavor comes from the sweet sticky sauce. Bleh. Cute place, cute outdoor shared area with Irie Bean. Friendly enough staff but limited involvement being that you order at the bar and they bring you your order. I know a lot of peeps love this place- more power to em. For me, it's a hard pass.

Fortunately, I get to enjoy fine dining along with my colleagues on company tab. And we really enjoy a nice atmosphere along with good food.
My recent visit to Boston brought us to Morton's at Seaport. I have dined at Morton's several times, however this visit left me less than satisfied. 
Our server was very personable and friendly, introduced himself and shook everyone's hand around the table. He had great recommendation.
BTW, we had lunch earlier that same day at Smith & Wollensky just around the corner. Great food, great service, great presentation; really enjoyed the experience.
Now, coming back to Morton's, the silverware was so basic, it could have been something out of a restaurant closeout sale. S&W's were stamped with their own logo. We had to ask for menus to be brought out! Our food was brought out late. We watched as on employee dragged out a large trash barrel through the restaurant to the back kitchen. A table of 4 guest that were sited a few feet away from us discussed their bill with one of the managers for about 30 mins - very distracting as they could not reach a conclusion.
Anyway, I feel that we you come to a place like Morton's, one should enjoy a great steak/seafood experience, as we did earlier this year in New York (5th Avenue). I will not return to this Morton's location and instead go to Capital Grill, Grill 23 or S&W.

Wow. Atlanta's Americasmart is quite large. There are three main buildings, with many floors, and it can be quite a challenge to figure out where you want or need to go.

I highly recommend International Optics in Building 3, 7th floor. When you exit the elevator, walk to the left of the elevator bank and around towards the back. Ask for Jenya Royter. She is expert at finding great frames to fit your face. They have a fabulous selection, and they offer eye exams on Wednesdays from 11 AM - 2 PM. Otherwise, don't forget your eyeglass prescription!

There are lots of shops for women, but the selection of menswear is limited. Like any of these places, negotiating skills are a plus, but you can find great deals even if you don't like to bargain.

To save on parking fees, take MARTA to the Peachtree Center station, and follow the signs to the Mart.

I have to say this place did get a shaky start, but recovered. My first experience was ordering a 9oz sirloin with steamed veggies, and stake came out really rare and veggies where mushy.
Returned 3 more times , 2nd time.. steak was perfect, service shaky, 3rd time ... fish tasted like stake so I guess they use the same griddle/ pan for fish... no good, service excellent , and last 4th time... moved over to Manny's from Colibri due to no waitress showing up, and ordered the chicken sandwich with some beverages .. I have to say, alone outside I hade my drinks within a few minutes and my food came cooked perfectly within the next 10 minutes... and my waitress was amazing and on point.

Food here is always great. I love their various takes on benedicts. And obviously the pannekoeken (sp?). This location has a beautiful view of the harbour and floatplanes. The huge problem with De Dutch, and not confined to this location, is consistently slow service. They need to hire more kitchen staff and severs. 3 times out of 4 that we come here you will wait 10-15 mins to get your order taken, then another 45 mins for your food, and your server will be always in a rush and never around to check on you. We put up with it because we really like the food, but we only come on rare occasions when we have a lazy morning with lots of time to lounge around and wait. 

Long story short, if you're in a rush, don't eat here. If you have time to spare, you'll enjoy the food.

Walking down Rainey we were looking for a bite to eat where we could sit down.  We decided on this place figuring Mediterranean would be good and fairly healthy. It's small but quaint and we were seated right away.  We wanted to have some wine and the waitress was willing to let us taste it to help us decide. The malbec was decent so we went ahead with the bottle.  I decided on the kabob plate which comes with your cover of 2 sides. I chose hummus and greek salad. The hummus was really fresh and yummy and the Greek salad was also very good.  My plate came with 1 beef kabob and 1 lamb kabob. The meat was flavorful and really tender. We asked for naan which was complimentary but did not taste authentic or fresh.  That was kind of disappointing considering how tasty everything else was.  I would try this again if i was in the area but i wouldn't make a special trip across town.

When I wanted to replace my ADA compliable cabinets with new, taller versions I contacted Kent Moore because they had put in the originals in 2013.  Noe came out and gave me an estimate and the price never changed.  He was helpful and understood just what I wanted with a number of new changes I decided to add.  There were no unexpected delays or costs, which I really appreciate!  The new cabinets went in as scheduled and the workers did a fast, clean job.  The tech came the next day to check everything and I have been happy with the workmanship and customer care.

Such a fun spot in general. Cutest store as you walk in and great service. I love the country feel and their options for breakfast. With that said, I love to visit and eat here ONLY when we vacation to Disney or up North. Reason being; the food is not the healthiest, YET very tasty. HENCE, indulging here can be dangerous. It is extremely cheap!!! Their portions are huge too!! I DEFINITELY RECOMMEND CHECKING THIS PLACE OUT, if you haven't done so yet, (just not on an every day basis)...  :) :) :)

my first visit to a taco truck! i've always wanted to try one, but every time i'd suggest it to my friends, they'd always give me the "ugh, tacos from a truck?!" response and i'd be outvoted by chipotle. eww.
 
chi! forget it. i'll go by myself! 

La Morenita is located on the parking lot of Allen Market (across from the old Beaverton Library). it's been here for awhile and every time i'd drive by there would always be a line.

they have tacos, tortas, burritos, quesadillas, and breakfast sandwiches. tacos $1.25 each, burritos $5, $1 for drinks. i didn't know what to order, so i asked the lady in front of me who seemed like a regular here and she said everything was pretty good, but that she especially liked the asada tacos.
i ordered the burrito pollo and it was good! i liked how simple it was and everything seemed fresh. next time i'll try the tacos.

there was only one cook and his daughter was taking orders. it was pretty busy so i had to wait awhile. the patrons were all mexican. i think it was the first time they'd seen an asian girl at a taco stand in this area.

bring CASH! and don't forget to tip the sweet girl!

(can someone tell me how to access the "food cart" option under categories?)

Luxurious decor (though my dad said the walls look like couch cushions ) and all the staff have bow ties!! We booked a table for 7.30pm, but didn't get seated till 7.50pm! So just a heads up, they'll likely run late from other seatings. 

Service was per usual. We tried their set meal for 4, with the pei king duck. That was delicious!!! Their shanghai xiu long bao was decent, other dishes such as dou miu, egg whites on broccoli, veggies, three layered meat and chicken were alright too.Price is slightly pricier than other restaurants as expected due to the ambiance they're portraying, but the portions are quite big too! Would come back for a special occasion due to the ambiance, but a bit too pricey for my regular dining preference.

Bitter, Sweet feeling about this place :/ 

This place was highly recommended by my husband as he went to school in the area. Therefore, I decided to give it a shot when we were visiting Atlanta. 

The service is TERRIBLE! Although this place is more like a self-service restaurant, the folks at the cashier/order area have a terrible attitude and clearly don't give any f**k about service nor how to interact with customers. I stand at the order/cashier area while the cashier girl was on her phone scrolling through the social media feed. She made eye contact with me but decided to ignore me...

The pizza is phenomenal though, that's why I rate this place a 3-star. I would recommend folks to come to Antico to get pizza, just prepare yourself for the bad attitude. Good luck :)

2. 5 stars would be appropriate.  It's unfortunate since the place has great potential.  However, it misses in several areas.  We sat in the lounge area for the LSU/Bama game and the big screen is crazy big - I mean 25 feet with great picture.  However, it is limited viewing if your too close to it.  That's the problem.  There are very few other TV's.  It wasn't crowded at all, so there is no reason for the service to have been so painfully slow.  I had to pull the server aside and tell him it was my friends bachelor party and to step it up. It helped a little.  He messed up our drink order, then made some crappy remark that he won't charge us but he has to dump it.  Ok on to the food.  The things we got were very good with some minor misses.  Seared tuna app was excellent, beef tips were average, bone-in ribeye was excellent (as to flavor and cut), but undercooked.  The server told us med rare would be more like medium so we ord'ered rare.  We got rare.  I didn't feel like sending it back.  $30+ (depending on cut) a la cart is simple too much.  This is not a Bones or Ruth Chris.  If they added Tv's, more sitting area and found some better servers I would make this a go to place for sports.  It could be a Dantanna's alternate.

This place has been around for a long, long time as have most of the items in the mall. If you have some free time, hop over to check out the unusual assortment of odd items, housewares, jewelry, old postcards and books, albums, etc. The place is never ending - turn the corner and there's another room of stuff.  Prices aren't as good as a thrift shop or garage sale, but it's fun to look around.  Take a mask and self monitor social distancing.

Pros: great for people who like sports, good for having a beer and talking, lots of items on the drink and food menu, portion sizes on my friends dishes were decent, prices were average

Cons: food was average, portion size on my dish was super tiny

I went here on a Sunday before a game and it was very busy. 

There are a million TVs all over the place so there were tons of people watching sports here. The place was clean. The service was slow but it made sense because she was busy. My friends got wraps and salads and they looked pretty big. The menu had so much on it and it wasnt all generic stuff - some of the different stuff I saw were: sandwiches with cole slaw and french fries on them, bison burgers, vegetarian dishes. etc. They had a variety of beer: cocoa beer, apple beer. etc.

My food was average. It was baked buffalo chicken and mac and cheese. It was on sale for 7 bucks because it was Sunday but it should have been like 4 bucks because it was so tiny. All my friends thought it should have been an appetizer. I dont know how they charge full price for that ever. It was okay tasting. I was sorta bummed because it sounded awesome. Everyone said their food was okay but no one was blown away.

I think they will do okay because of the sports crowd but really, i dont think I'd go here again unless someone wanted to go and I was tagging along.

I celebrated my birthday here last year. Kind of a sex in the cityesque  deal, three girls taking the cocktail menu by storm. Orleans Cosmo, Chocolate Coconut Martini, Totally Peach Martini, Mocha Martini, 24 Karate Martini, Mango Mojito, and Dark and Stormy ... no stone unturned.

I liked the set up of the place, couches in one area, defined dining area and bar area, with a spot right up front for live music.

So, about that live music... This guy was playing guitar and had a little backup with another guitar? I'm not sure, but the sound system was either jacked up or it was not good to begin with. Either way we tried to move further away so that we could enjoy our evening - didn't happen. In fact I'm pretty sure the music got louder and more distorted as the night went on. 

The wait staff was a little slower than I would have hoped and we had just missed the time of the year where they take over Comcast's parking lot and have outdoor seating (just last month I saw them start an actual patio, kudos Orleans!) which was a shame, cause as awkward as it was to walk outside and smoke a cigarette, the music was much more pleasant from the street. 

I would go back, cause the drinks were decent... I would like to try the food.

I have to give Gus, the owner, credit for sending me such an interesting message!  I wish HE would've been there when we visited!  As I said, I couldn't put my finger on it... and as Gus calls it, maybe its the "character"... I will have to come back and try again on one of my business treks over to MIT.  Or maybe its just me... But I don't want to think, that perhaps... Im too old for college town... But GASP! Could it be, I have become too old for ICE CREAM?!  

SAY IT ISN'T SO!

Went in for a quick bite on a Monday night. Place was empty and  we say at the bar. Nice inside. Bar tender was great. 
Tried a couple of cocktails, which were well made: tasty and not crazy strong or weak. 
We shared a seaweed salad (solid), dragon roll, seared ahi tuna, and spicy girl roll. The seared ahi tuna was on the sushi list, but was just tuna on some white stuff - not bad, but expected a sushi. The other two were tasty, but came on a thick sauce - almost like mayo. Not bad, but not typical for this kind of sushi. Overall good experience. A bit pricey, but reasonable for the area

I thought for a good ten minutes about whether I could give a better rating than a three. I just can't. 

The beer is solid. I like it. It's not the best beer in town but it's a nice line up especially for what this place purports to be. I would happily drink the beer again if the beer was served somewhere else. I just can't get into the venue.

Before moving on, I will say that I did not try the food but people seemed to be enjoying it. I don't know one way or the other whether the reviews criticizing the food are right or whether the ones professing adoration are right. 

Parking is a mess. There's not enough on-site parking and it's hard to find off-site parking without the risk of being towed. Once you finally steal a parking spot you have your choice of sitting at long communal benches outside or long communal benches inside. Outside is cool when it's cool outside. Inside is fine except it's also a music venue built out of steel and concrete so there's no escaping the very loud music. 

Ordering inside is relegated to the two line counter system that seems very popular these days. It's not efficient but I'm not getting bent out of shape about it. I could get a beer in reasonable time. The water is at self-serve stations which I like because it makes it easy to keep drinking water along with the beer.

The worst thing about this place is all the kids. Alright, I'm not from Austin where things are more kid friendly and I do think it's weird to bring kids to a place where people are getting drunk, spilling beers, having adult conversations, dogs are running around (which are not always friendly to noisy kids), etc. but it's not my job to parent other peoples' kids. On the other hand, it's not my job to parent other peoples' kids. The kids were everywhere with little to no supervision. Somebody else called ABGB a boozy daycare which is very accurate. The kids were running all over cutting through crowds, running into people carrying beer and racing around the servers carrying hot food. At one point some kid came down to where my wife and I were sitting and started throwing rocks at us. We couldn't even complain to the parents because there weren't any around. I can't blame the kids. There's nothing for them to do. Of course they get bored and want to run around. They're kids. 

I hate to criticize ABGB for the poor environment caused by all the kids because they neither encourage nor discourage their presence but it's also their business and they let the environment be what it is. If adults were doing the same things the kids were doing I would expect the staff to do something about it. It's no different just because these patrons happen to have their parents with them.

I came here on Saturday night with a group of friends, around 9:30 we walk in and the bartenders don't even attempt to make us feel wanted there, just throwing a menu in front of us. My friend orders a $27 glass of rum, neat... but then the bartender proceeds to fill a glass with ice and pour the rum over. When my friend told him he had asked it to be neat, he just strains it - if you pay $27 for rum neat, it shouldn't be watered down or tainted. He asked for a new one, which he felt bad about, and the bartender obliged, which was nice. But to continue, no one asked if we wanted our tabs open or closed, immediately running our cards, while also taking the food menu away while I was looking at the menu (I probably would have ordered some apps, had he not taken the menu away from me)... unfortunate experience. As someone that's had a lot of years in the industry, I cannot explain how much it means to care about your patrons and make them feel comfortable - so these bartenders clearly were lacking. 

Drinks were good, but the experience was ruined by the environment the bartenders created for us.

Came here around 9pm, they close at 11pm, it's a great concept but things didn't look as fresh because it was end of day and been sitting out. I build my pizza and waited. The woman that was tending the pizza was yapping in the phone so she burned our pizza so they just apologized and remake another, would have been nice if there was compensation for the mistake. We also order a salad it wasn't that fresh either. The place would a lot nicer if they cleaned the windows outside and inside but I guess for the price point can't expect much. This place could be busier if they put some effort.

Definitely make a reservation in advance - this place gets super packed and busy, even during the week. The aesthetics of the place are perfect for IG obviously, and the drinks are really the star of the show. 

The food was only all right when we went. The chips & guac were awesome and the chips were perfectly seasoned. We also ordered the fish tacos (slightly weird after taste), elote (a little too indulgent for me - and a bit messy so be forewarned!), and their black bean hummus (rich and a little underseasoned for me). Their churros were slightly overdone for me but still a nice way to finish the meal.

Overall - not a place I'd be raving about for dinner, but a place I'd come back to for drinks and a snack after work. Hoping to try their brunch next!

We tried In-N-Out, and we will try it again at some point. The hype associated with this establishment I am unsure about. It was fast, even though cars and people were knee deep. The fries were a little lackluster in taste (I only ate one on the five minute ride home, and that is saying something) and the burgers were OK, although the crisp lettuce in the burger was good. We did order some extras off the secret menu, but I think I can do without anything animal style in the future. Given a choice, I would head to Dan's. This is maybe the secret here - eating inside the establishment after picking up the order when it's fresh and hot hot. Maybe this is when the magic happens. Oh year - we tried a shake too. No better or worse than anyone else, but they are not "special."  A fast food joint with friendly service, so I cannot complain.

There are more people at the hostess desk than there were servers. We were told there was a 15 minute wait and the place was practically empty. They only had a few servers and didn't want to seat us until some guests left. Because it was so empty and they were gradually seating people, I would think service would be better. Service was rather slow, but I really enjoyed my meal. I had the smokehouse burger. It was delicious (after I sent it back to be cooked well done as requested). I had both the fries and coleslaw. Fries were better. As I was leaving, there were many people waiting. Still, there were many empty tables. They really need to get more servers. They could do better business. They did have a live performer who did a fantastic job. His set ended at 9. I'll give them an extra star just because of him.

We picked up 3 donuts while Smoke & Donuts was outside of Red Cypress Brewing. Madagascar Vanilla Glazed, Vermont Maple, Florida Blueberry and a RCB Death Roll.  The Vermont Maple was my favorite and my husband liked it the best too. The Blueberry one was so heavy on the some I couldn't even taste the Blueberry and Blueberry anything is a favorite of mine. 

The donuts are smaller than your usual donut chain and any other bakery around here. The cost was about $7 for the four donuts. Service was fast and friendly.

It's a motel, not a hotel, and is one of the cheapest options if you want to stay on a Disney property.  Rather than parking right in front of the entrance the way I would at other motels I was forced to park in a parking lot while I checked in.  It confused me because there were several other vehicles who were loading/unloading in the front.  We stayed in one of The Love Bug buildings.  The color scheme wasn't soothing.  The room was modest and could use an update (such as new paint as the paint was chipped in many areas).  There was a small refrigerator in the room.   There were two small, flat pillows on each bed.  The shower did not drain properly.  Like pretty much all motels, we could hear when everyone else around us were using their showers and toilets.  It's a good option if you want to save money on lodging while at Disney and spend most of your time at the parks (rather than in the room).  The front staff was always courteous.  On the day we left a male housekeeper knocked on our door (we had the curtains open so it was obvious we were there, but we had the "Do Not Disturb" sign on the door handle).  He asked what time we were checking out.  I said we'd be out before the checkout time of 11:00 AM.  He was very persistent on questioning me as to the exact time we'd leave.  It was rude, intrusive, and annoying.  I reported this (and the shower draining issue) to the front desk staff.  Since it's on Disney property, we were able to utilize the Disney buses to get around.  The customer service at breakfast was disappointing.  When I ordered the egg white omelet the female worker sighed heavily.  I asked her if there was a problem.  She said that everyone was working those that morning.  I again asked if that was a problem (since it was a listed menu item).  She said that the eggs were sticking together.  I told her she could use regular eggs rather than egg whites (I ordered the egg white omelet because I wanted the veggies in it, not the egg whites), but she used the egg whites, which appeared to be frozen.  My roommate was able to get hot water (to make instant coffee) for free.

I find it very interesting that the first review I wrote for RA has magically disappeared. I was coming to update my old one only to find it was removed. I guess it's because of how drunk the sushi guy was that night. However, my return trip for lunch today I am proud to say that everyone working was sober. Actually the sushi chefs were the only ones paying attention. After I was seated and sat there for 10 minutes with no waiter or anyone approaching me. One of the sushi chefs took my order. I started working and another 10 minutes passed and my lunch arrived. I still had not been approached by a waiter so still had no drink or any of the items that accompanied my meal. The sushi chef went to find someone. A very sweet young man came and brought me a drink. Then got me a soup and salad. He then checked on my often. His name was Lucky. Too bad I wasn't. I have to say that sitting at the sushi bar here is the worst place you can sit. This is the second time I have received horrible service there. If they could work on the service I might give them 4 stars. That is if I go back. I crave sushi all the time and this place is so close. But it is almost worth the drive to Gekko on North Ave. The sushi here has a higher quality then others. I just hope they can work on the customer service. PS my pricing is for the lunch special if you go to dinner it will cost more.

Saturday Nite- out and about Atlanta. Purposely decided to head over to Gino's. If  you recall the place prior to Gino's was caught in a fire and destroyed. Somewhere between then and now Gino's NY Pizza  Bar resurrected from the ashes. The place is spacious.  Two parking lots but they are difficult to maneuver to the movie driver. Watch for potholes and running water with a scent.!! There is a full bar in the rear of the design with poker fans playing with chips and brown liquor. Looked pretty impressive. Noticeably cooler back there. Sitting near the front of the restaurant from the inside joy can view the outdoor patio which was not to far off from the previous design before the fire. I decided to go here because it had been years from the last time I went. Same owners/same family. 
Very hot in the inside area near the desk where you place your order. Service was a bit slow but I guess that's part of the pizza game. The a/c setting must have been on the "budget setting." It was way to HOT!! It was hotter inside that it was outside. 
A plus about eating outdoors is that there are fans on one side of the patio that blow harder than the a/c indoors. The pizza- was just basic. I would give it 2.5 stars at most. The service once we got going was 3.2 stars. Just busy I guess. The specialize in pizza slices for the person on the go. We ordered a whole pie all veggies. The sauce had a mild sweet flavor to it. Just could have been the base sauce. The crust was thin and average texture. Nothing lite and airy. Overall it was a good experience. The drinks were GOOD- although the next morning I did have a tummy ache. Lasted about 9am the next day.  Not sure what that was about because I love Pizza. The service or at least our waitress was better when things died down. I would go back for drinks and maybe try a different  option on the menu. The owners daughter was at the cashier location. I did not get her name but she was polite. I did not get a chance to review the restrooms but that will be when I go back for drinks. Coming next is the review of their neighbor Tokyo Valentino..

Sometimes you just want A LOT of food. Fast. Late(ish). Hot. 

Thank you to the lovely Allison "not for long" P for toting me to Magnolia Cafe in the late hours. It wasn't her first choice, but it was what we needed! Despite the brief wait (WOW, on a Thursday night at 1030pm? Austin needs more late night diners!), we were seated quickly, equipped with the proper brown liquids (hot chocolate, Diet Coke, coffee), and orders whisked away to be prepped...

The #7 Queso Omelete with ham: a heavenly combo of avocado, cheese, onions, and queso slathered all up on it. Sides of black beans (only in TX, right?) and fresh fruit rounded out the plate. 

Friendly, fast service....no complaints. Not my favorite diner in the world, but it was my favorite last night. Queso love.

Stumbled upon this Ramen spot on the way home. Had their signature ramen, takoyaki, and karaage. 

The ramen has a good broth a bit on the salty side when you get near the bottom but overall pretty good. Noods was cooked to perfection the P. Belly was melt in your mouth good and the veggies were scrumptious. 

The Takoyaki was on point. Nothing too crazy about it. 

Tha Karaage was surprising. It didn't look much of an appeal but the flavors was definitely there! 

Overall this place was good. Everyone kept a distance there is service for dine in or outside. People who worked there was great! Definitely a good spot to come to on chilly nights!

I came in here on Labor Day for some breakfast to go with my boyfriend. We both got large iced coffees and bacon, egg and cheese sandwiches on bagels. I think it was about $20 for the four items which seems average. 

The decor was cute but the place was small, it was hard to find a place to wait while you were waiting for your food. 

My iced coffee was good. No complaints there. The egg sandwiches were below average though. I think they may be good if you paid for an extra egg on them but there was such little substance to the sandwiches it was like 90% bagel and 10% bacon, egg and cheese. The bagels weren't great, very bready. I would possibly try again and just order extra egg and extra cheese?

We decided to give this place a try for Valentines Day. The food was okay, nothing to write home about. The service was average, with long periods of no service, not to mention the loud music. But what really ruined this night, our V-Day together, was how I was called a "gentleman" by a waiter despite wearing a dress, heels, and makeup. Either this waiter was a certifiable moron or the least observant waiter I've ever had - either way, it needs to be addressed. Upon bringing this to the attention of our waiter, he told us that he would bring this problem to the attention of the management, which is the proper response.

I go here because I live within walking distance, can sit at the bar, and get a consistent burger. Watertown Center doesn't have a lot of restaurants or nightlife, so I'm glad its there. It's not a bad place, but it's a bit of a crap shoot. I always sit at the bar and try to go on the later side once the families with crying kids are gone. 

Some of the bartenders are super friendly and make you feel welcome to spend your money there. However, som\e are really standoffish and you could have your food put down in front of you, an empty beer glass, and they couldn't be bothered trying to sell you another beer. So now I see who is at the bar first and then decide if I'm going in.

The entrees are OK, but some of the salads are really overpriced. For example, last night I got a goat cheese salad with steak tips that was about $16 and it was really small with not much meat. My boyfriend got a fish entree that was a lot more substantial for about the same amount of money. I'm not really looking for the huge portion that some chain restaurant goers look for, and would prefer quality, but I didn't feel it was good value. Some of the other dinner salads are also kind of stingy for what you pay for.

I'm very familiar with Bongos as I used to go to the Miami location all the time, and I visited the Ft Lauderdale location a couple of times as well. Both of those are now closed, so I was excited when I saw there was one at Disney Springs. We chose this restaurant to celebrate our 1 year wedding anniversary this past weekend. The place was very lively with dancers and a live band. We were told there would be a 15-20 min wait so they took my phone # and said they'd text us when our table was ready. We waited outside but never received a text so we went inside to check and there was now a different hostess there who said she didn't have us down or our phone number. I pointed at the lady who took our names down but she just shrugged her shoulders. She was able to give us a table but we were seated in a back room with no other guests and we weren't able to see the performers, we just heard everyone having a good time. A friendly waiter came by and we placed our orders. I ordered the garlic shrimp with rice and sweet plantains, and my husband ordered the ropa vieja with rice and beans. The food came out in a reasonable time but it wasn't what I remembered from the other Bongos locations. It was just okay. I was very disappointed with my experience here, both food and service (other than our waiter).

This was our first time back to the H&B since the renovation, and we thought the outside looked great.  Inside had the same layout, but new facing.  Took down the half wall between the bar and dining tables, which I'm not sure if I would like if I wanted to go in there to eat at a table.  Nice big Flat screen TV's.  Bartender service was inconsistent as usual.  Not very friendly either.  Food was decent, about the same as it was before the renovation, but prices seem to have jumped significantly.  Would be nice to see a step up in food quality and selection for the price jump.

I came here with 8 other people for lunch on Saturday. We made a reservation for 1130am. The restaurant was not too busy when we walked in. The service was not bad. When I requested no sauce, they forgot and brought it with sauce. When I raised this issue, they brought it back to the kitchen and quickly re make and brought it back. Overall, the dining experience was not bad. The food was ok too. Although they were not able to split the bill for us, they accpeted credit card which was convenient.

I've only been there twice even though it's 1 block away from my house :P

the outside seatings are really nice since it's right next to a pond so you get somewhat of a view.  

there's always parking available.

weekend brunches were pretty good with average price.  dinner however, i ordered their special that night - kobe burger and was pretty disappointed.  it tasted like a regular cheese burger to me.  Crab and shrimp alfredo was pretty decent however but nothing too special.

Thus far, I recommend brunches only.  

If you have passport discount card, you could enjoy buy 1 get 1 free meal.  (except weekend brunches :(  )

Yellow Brick Pizza has a newer location on King Avenue. It's where a few cool restaurants were before. The pizza is as good as the original place. It also has a good bar. There's limited parking. 

It became the latest business to give this place a chance. Some came and went fast. This has changed many times over the years. It used to be Dragonfly, a hipster vegan restaurant that was overly expensive. This then became the hipster Till. It also was pretty expensive. This place is pretty good. It can still be expensive. They have a really good happy hour. I had a vodka and tonic. It's $2 at happy hour. They have specials for wells. I had a pizza with vegan cheese. It's about $12 for a small one. That's kind of much, but not unusual for fancy pizza. 

It doesn't take that long to make a pizza. It usually comes out fast. There's also salads.

Quality has dropped for me. In the beginning when they first opened they were more generous with their helpings. I just went in to get an avocabbo, she put 1/2 a scoop of chicken and 1/2 a scoop of bacon. There's ended up being a huge empty space in my salad, which she then ended up filling with THREE pieces of bread. Even when she closed the lid for the salad there was still still space between the salad and the lid (which wasn't the case when they first opened). For the $12.14 I paid for my salad I was pretty PO'd. My salad still tasted good and the service was still friendly and fast, but I definitely felt like I was ripped off.

I went there for lunch over the weekend with a couple of friends. The red bean and coconut smoothies were really tasty and authentic. I had the Vietnamese Sour Soup with fish. The shrimp and white fish were fresh & the unexpected ingredients like pineapple chunks livened up the dish. (As someone who likes really intense food, it could have been even more sour.)  Another friend had a  solid pad thai and the other had a chicken curry noodle soup that had a good amount of spice. The waitress came quickly, but the food was served at vastly different times, which wasn't difficult for us. We had somewhere else to go after lunch and the service slowed us down a bit.

We love Saigon's original location on Goldenrod, and this one being newer and closer to where we stayed at this time, we decided to visit here instead. This place is huge, a stand alone building with its own parking lot.  It looks like part of the restaurant can be used for banquets, with props and karaoke machine. 

Well, it's a different chef, and somehow the food isn't quite as good as the original.  The spring roll came out way too fast and was barely warm; it probably had been sitting out.  Some of the beef in our soup was also chewy and dry.

As for the service, it certainly wasn't rude, just plain weird... I appreciate the waiter trying to be friendly and helpful, but maybe tune it down a bit.  As we were sitting down, the waiter mumbled, "we have Vietnamese beer."  He put down the menu, "Saigon beer, from Vietnam."  Then he turned away and mumbled "two Saigon beer."  It took a moment for my brain to process what he was saying and yelled after him, "no I don't want beer!!"  Okay, I am not disputing that I am a beer lover, but I am not sure what body signal I gave for ordering a beer.  (I suppose fellow Yelper Derock H. got the same server we did, just that he "ordered" the chicken soup without saying a word.) 

Then, while we were eating, the waiter returned and said, no, you have to put the basil in.  We said, yes, we did.  And he insisted that we need to put in more.  And he stood there and waited for us to put more basil in.  No, you need more.  And kept watching till we threw in a few more leaves into our bowls.

We saw this diner featured on the Food Network and gave it a shot. 
The diner itself is not very clean. The men's bathroom had a trough-like urinal which was not very clean. My wife reports the woman's room and was clean. As I walked by the kitchen, I was was not impressed with the level of cleanliness. 
I ordered the day's special, a pulled pork eggs benny. The hollandaise sauce was not hot. The corn bread was also not warm and extremely dry. My wife loved her sockeye salmon with truffle potatoes albeit with hollandaise sauce that was not hot. 
The coffee was excellent. Hard to find great coffee at a diner. 
The service was quick and friendly. I don't like having to pay the bill in front of the Server... seems like undue pressure to tip. 
I thought the food tasted good despite the cold hollandaise sauce.

This is a 3 star review but I want to start out by saying I will still go to this place... I know not all 3 star reviews convey that.  

The good:
-We showed up at 7p on a Saturday with a group of 10 and they got us a seat inside immediately.  
-Staff was super nice about our large group (birthday) and even brought plates for us to use for the cake I brought (even though I brought plates)
-Initial drink order was prompt and correct

Note: I so appreciate a wait staff that is nice to large groups.  I know we are a pain in the ass sometimes, and they serisouly were SO SO nice to us.  Very accommodating.

The less good
-Then our waiter disappeared.  Took forever to get an order in because he was no where to be found.  When we finally got our food we were starving.  Then..... gone again.  We literally ended up staying an hour longer than we intended because we simply COULD NOT FIND THE GUY.  I think they may have had him serving outside, which is not his fault. But I think we saw the guy twice in 90 minutes.  We were going to order more drinks, but it took so long in between sightings we just decided to go.
-The pizza was very meh.  Seemed under done.  Too much cheese.  May have been a fluke.  
-The check was wrong for 3 people (mind you, I completely appreciated that he split it without asking, but then it took us 15 MORE minutes to try and sort out the check situation, when we would've been happy to split it and write out amounts ourselves if necessary.

This could all be a fluke but it was a little weird.  Hence, the mixed review.  The good news is that there is plenty of seating, the staff was very nice (when you got to interact with them), and good prices on food and drinks.  Just be prepared to wait for a while for food and check.  We will definitely return to see if our experience was abnormal, I'd love to provide a positive update!

Good seafood, good service, great location. Nothing amazing, and I think there are better deals for seafood in Boston---Summer Shack, etc. 

We had a reservation for 3. I arrived first, stood near the hostess station and was ignored by at least three people. Finally,  young server caught me eye, and I made the unversal sign of "WFT...!" He went and told the hostess I was there. So, one star gone. Restaurant owners, make sure your hostesses aren't snotty, as it makes old people mad, and we have plenty of disposable income as well as time to yelp.

Service was fast, thorough and gracious otherwise. We had tuna tartare, wellfleet oysters, goat cheese salad for apps. The smallish helping of tuna was ganged up on by the large amounts of avocado and the infinitesimal sprinkle of jalapenos to rescue it. Why are Boston chefs afraid of this mighty pepper? Oysters great, kinda can't go wrong, unless you're allergic, as my friend was. Ok, more for me. Goat cheese salad good too, with the right amount of dressing. The portion of salmon was large, with all items perfectly cooked. Lobster bisque meh----Legal is better. Crabcakes excellent but a dinner with two sides is $26 and includes guess how many crabcakes? That'd be 2.....
Good prices on our glasses of champagne and my cucumber martini rocked.  Check for 3 people, with two of us drinking one apiece: $160. Nice walk back to airbnb house and a lovely evening in all.

Most things are just ok here, but the lobster bisque is a definite stand out!  On Wednesday nights they have a dozen oysters for $7 and $4 house wines, so it's hard to turn that down.  But really wouldn't come here otherwise if it wasn't for the specials, there's just nothing that great about the food.  It's not bad, it's just not great.  I recently got grilled shrimp added to my salad, and there were 6 tiny little shrimp, I was not impressed!

Generally, I like the Final Cut steakhouse. The food us very good quality and I have never had a bad meal. My most recent visit, number five to be precise, is no exception. The service is spotty and the staff rotates frequently. This occasion I even asked for a different waiter and then the hostess didn't even come back to ask me why? The problem with the Final Cut is that the wait staff knows nothing of a wine list and feel that handing you an iPad with a listing of wines is adequate. No explanation of good pairings. My Final Cut on Final Cut...good steak, good wine selection, management and staff training needs to improve...a lot. Not the high end place is was when it opened. Too bad.

Decently priced for a theme park restaurant, suprisingly better than most places you could potentially go to here. For ~$15 you can get a shake, fries, and burger/chicken tenders/chicken sandwich/or bean burger.
Fries--well seasoned, excellent salt to fry ratio, possibly a hint of old bay seasoning?? But not in an overwhelming sense--get them, they're delicious! 
Chicken tenders--wow, full of real meat, and not heavily breaded! They're filling! 
Hamburger--well done, decent amount of meat. 
They have a spot for condiments: ketchup/mayo/mustard packets, napkins, and straws...however, the straws are UNWRAPPED, which I think is a health hazard, it's gross--everyone reaching and grabbing straws, who knows where their hands have been? 
Are they trying to pull an 'eco-friendly' move by having unwrapped straws? If so, kill the condiment packets and have condiment pumps everywhere.
Okay, now that that little rant is over, I will say it was nice that we were able to sit on the balcony, there was an excellent view of the hulk ride and other rides across the water, and you had pretty bushes and flowers by the balcony. 
Clean-ish tables and seating area, and clean bathrooms, and overpriced fast food at an amusement park...it is what it is. At least my cousin and I were full for about 6hours after lunch!

My husband and I went here for a quick lunch before a business meeting. It was convenient to Marriott and had been recommended by the concierge. The service was a bit slow, but the food was good. I had a salad with grilled chicken. The chicken was fresh and moist. My husband had a bowl of chowder. It was served in a huge pasta bowl, which did not seem appropriate for the portion size of the soup. The place was busy and a good vibe.

When I heard from a patron at another bar (DeeDee's) that the Six House was once Triple Os, Whitey Bulger's hangout, I was instanly intrigued. Thinking that we're going to a bar where some guy was "whacked" is cool in a Soprano's twisted sort of way.

This was the third stop on our Red Line Pub Crawl, and unfortunately for my curiosity's sake, the current bar didn't live up to stories about the bar it once was. Don't get me wrong, it is very nice -- and I should be happy that it's a very nice bar -- but I was expecting a bit more personality.

It's basically a long, spacious bar area with high tables along the left side of the room and windows overlooking Broadway, as well as huge flat-screen TVs above the shelves of alcohol. It looks new and spiffy (a little too spiffy for my taste in pubs), and they have a full stock of alcohol to choose from. I didn't check out the food menu, but I saw a waitress eating a yummy looking salad that I may come back to try when my goal is not to drink all day long.

Nice place, just not a whole lot of character to it. I'll still go there to watch a game if I'm in the area.

Stephen Mulrey, as the owner of Amrheins, I hope that you're interested in the feedback of your patrons, especially from one who was at your restaurant just four hours ago.

We were a party of 12 on the patio, and the food was great!!  The buffalo chicken dip was indeed fiery, and the clams casino special were tasty and substantial.  Each clams casino order had 2 clams and the shells were bigger than my palm and piled high with clams and stuffing.

Our party also ordered lobster mac and cheese - lots of lobster meat by volume, very rich and a full order can feed 2 people; sirloin tips - rare came out rare and medium rare came out medium rare, well flavored with good portioned side dishes; parmesan crusted haddock - the plate was cleaned off; lobster pie - tons of lobster by volume, very delicious.   Even the bread basket had ouch-it's-hot rolls that were light and slightly sweet with a great garlic/parmesan/olive oil dip on the side. 

What holds back Amrheins from being a top notch restaurant is the service.  Don't get me wrong, the waitstaff is polite and engaging (if you engage them first).  But they are not at all proactive in the service that they give.

Please don't tell me that you don't know about our surprise party reservation for 12 at five o clock, especially when the reservation was made 2 weeks ago and reconfirmed by us just yesterday.

Please give everyone a round of water right away.  And pay attention to refilling water glasses without being asked.

Please take our orders before my hair turns grey

Please check back at least ONCE to make sure that everything's ok

Please don't forget our dessert order for the one person who didn't have birthday cake (at least it didn't show up on the bill)

Maybe it was our waitress, Casey, was the exception, but I don't think so.  Mr. Mulvey, if you improve your staff's service level and attentiveness, Amrhein's will be top notch.

I could of sworn I took pictures inside Bo Bo Garden. Oh well. For lunch this place is a can't miss spot. Go! They have a combo that can't be beat for the price. Soup, entree, egg roll for less than $8. Perfect for coworker lunches because you are in and out. I had Mongolian beef. The vegetables were a nice size and everything was plated beautifully. 

The decor is festive. The staff seem to work well together. Everyone is polite and nice. I hear the dinners are even better. I'll have to come back. They also don't mind separate checks. Go! Enjoy!

It's not a good thing if I'm in a bad mood before I've even sat down. But not all service here is bad. Don't ask for directions to the parking garages they validate - you get an honest effort with a vague description and a condescending rebuttal when you look confused. However, our server was delightful, and the hostess graciously revived my dying cell phone at her station so I guess they evened out ok. 

Overall, the food itself was quite good though a bit overpriced. Not fantastic but just barely enough to override the incompetent directions - clearly the chef gives lucid directions...

My chicken was tasty, and the Vegetable Feuillate was impressive. I've never seen a French restaurant work with tofu, but it turns out they do "vegetarian meat" just as well. The soy-glazed tofu perched on flaky pastry with a mild but pleasantly-flavored vegetable ragout, and the basil vinaigrette completed the dish with pretty green ribbons of zest. 

Sandrine's is definitely not a bad idea, and I'm not sure how it compares to the myriad options Harvard Square offers, but in all Ve Ri Tas it's just not Gaslight or Aquitaine.

The one thing that keeps me coming back to the enormous room is how much I love the music. I usually end up weighing my desire to listen to the music against my willingness to deal with the lines and crowds. It's not even like an insane amount of people go there, the place is just too god damn small. It takes forever to get a drink from the teeny tiny bar and it takes for ever to wait in line for the teeny tiny bathroom.

Also, over the last year or two it seems as though the crowd is getting grope-ier and slimier. From what other people are saying, though, it sounds like I need to go during the week. I like the way the place is decorated (when I can see it amongst the crammed in people) and if the music is as good during the week as it is on the weekend, maybe it would get one more star for me.

I've stayed at better. Much better. But this hotel was actually ok if you plan to get out for the day and just come back to sleep. The beds are small but comfortable and the rooms are quiet. Rooms are clean for the most part but everything could use an update. The phone in my room didn't work, neither did the tv. The water pressure is low so it takes forever to wash your hair. Same with the elevators to the 15th floors. Food at the hotel is pretty bad, I would definitely skip it.

Soleil is a beautiful, Italian-Mediterranean restaurant located next to The Oasis.  My mother-in-law and I sat outside on the patio to enjoy the beautiful sunset on Lake Travis.  It is a fairly new restaurant, so I wasn't sure what to expect, but I was already impressed.

For starters, our server was great and I wish I could remember his name to give him the well deserved kudos.  It's hard to get good service these days.  All I remember is that he was from Boston because we talked about how my husband just happened to be in Boston on that day.  

He started by recommending a very nice Malbec.  Great recommendation!  For an appetizer, we ordered the calamari.  Although it was cooked to perfection, it lacked flavor.  This was very disappointing, but we weren't going to judge the restaurant on an appetizer.

I ordered the Fettuccine with Gulf crab, shrimp, and lobster cooked in a delicious lobster cream sauce.  It was excellent, and I wanted to eat it all!  It's a little pricey, but you definitely get a large portion, so it's worth it if you like leftovers.  

My MIL ordered the crabcakes and we both experienced a first with this plate!  She got one normal crabcake, and the other one was a crispy softshell crab.  We were laughing because we couldn't figure out if you were supposed to eat it as is, or not.  Our server assured us it was perfectly fine to eat it as is, shell and all!  It was the same batter used in the calamari, so again, it was a little bland.  But it was worth the laughs and good times!

Unfortunately, I only give Soleil three stars this time because only my plate was excellent that night, and the rest was just okay.  But, this is a new establishment and I would love to see it grow and succeed!  I would like to try it again to give it another shot because I think it's worth it.  The service, the beautiful scenery inside and outside the restaurant is worth visiting at least once.  Maybe you can decide for yourself!

My friend and I went her for their Tuesday Dollar oysters. I also had my 2 year old with me. Not the wisest choice but I wanted oysters! (I'm not a big drinker anyways). They are kid friendly :) If your child can handle the noise. Luckily, my child had a grand ol' time looking out the window.

We tried a couple of items from their Happy hour menu(?), regular menu and shared an entree. 

I don't remember the names.. 
-Squid and corn
-Roasted potatoes
-Popovers
-Pig ears!!
-Pork Belly with Clams

The oysters were fine. Raw oysters are kinda hard to mess up. 
The squid and corn was tasty.
The roasted potatoes could be cooked for a bit longer, they looked like they were boiled! I was expecting crispy goodness.
Popovers were very peppery. It wasn't bad, I just don't understand the obsession.

The PIG EARS WERE GLORIOUS!! Crispy where it should be, ooey gooey where it wasn't crispy. Just perfect. I wish there was more pig ears rather than a plate full of the shishito peppers.

The porkbelly. Sigh. I always have such high expectations for pork belly. It tasted like brisket to me. *shrugs* 

The service was wonderful. The place is very small, we got there early and was able to get seated right away. I believe there was a line by 6:30. Overall, average in my opinion. I gave it a try but most likely will not be back, unless it's for oysters. :)

N wanted Indian food downtown so I let her choose the spot. She's been a few times to Spicy 6, which is located upstairs over an eyewear store, Art Face Optical.
 
We dropped in on a Monday (around 5:30pm) and were the first customers of the night. It wasn't busy. The place oddly doesn't play any music. Service was friendly and they came by several times to refill waters. They ask you how spicy you want your dishes; we went with mild (N is a wimp when it comes to spicy food).

The two page menu consists of starters, non-vegetarian, vegetarian, tandoori creations and rice & naan. They also do a lunch buffet (11:30am to 2:30pm) on weekdays.

- Naan ($3.00) - standard fare. Soft and warm but not crispy.
- Chicken tikka masala ($16.00) - grilled chicken cooked in onion and tomato based sauce. Sauce was tasty but it's a small portion. Mostly onions with a couple sparse red and green peppers.
- Biriyani ($17.00) - basmati rice cooked with vegetables and we opted for lamb. Lamb was dry and needed the raita sauce. Biriyani itself was good but not worth the price point.

Prices are high at S6. Not a likely return visit for me when I want Indian food.

Got the Italian sub. It's nice, a little different than I expected, but a good sandwich. I know my sandwiches. The meat is very tasty, the bread is ok, not crusty enough. No lettuce/tomato as I would have expected.

But I almost fell down when they said it would be $14. I'm sorry, your fancy meats aren't worth it, and it's not that big of a sandwich. A nice sized Italian sub with some Boars Head salamis on there is $9, max. Cheapest sub on the menu here is $10.

I don't usually write reviews. But I respect the sandwich, and this is sandwich heresy.

As someone who grew up with pork roll, I am excited to try their breakfast sandwich, but it's 5.50. Pork roll is basically bologna, don't think you're gonna fancy it up and charge $5.50

Aesthetically pleasing and nice date type of place with either your SO or friends. The noise level is average, kinda small area, and super expensive. The wine was priced decent because it's wine, but we paid 18$ for three meatballs and three pieces of bread that was at most average. I would come for the wine and chill with friends but a no on the food. I know some places do quality of quantity, but there was nothing quality about these meatballs.

Great bar, awful food. I have eaten here 3 times. The first time was a salad. Pretty hard to screw that up. The second time I ordered chicken fingers with panko coating. Definitely not panko. And they were over cooked hard as a rock. The third time I ordered the spinach dip which was in a cardboard cup and was clearly microwaved. It was inedible. The staff has always been friendly and accommodating. I enjoy this as a place to go and have a drink. The bands are usually good. But now I eat somewhere else first.

Walking out of the scorching Texas August sun, into a dark hole in the wall, to a steaming bowl of..... CHILI...  that is exactly what we did last Saturday....

I wish I could give 3.5 stars. 

I had the Frito Pie with the black bean Chilli. It was satisfying, not delicious, not amazing, but not terrible. it was satisfying. My date had the chicken enchiladas with queso and seemed happy with the meal. 

The environment is casual, the decor is crowded, their drink specials were super cheap, however I was recovering from a cold so water it was for me (what no SWEET TEA - are we not in the south in Texas?).... The prices are perfectly reasonable.

The service however was amazing! Everyone was friendly, the service was prompt, every time we needed anything or so much as glanced up there was someone nearby to assess whether or not we needed something. Lately, in Austin especially in casual dinning I feel like the service leaves much to be desired... but at Texas Chili Parlor the service was fabulous!

We paid 20$ for parking. The restaurant was nice and quiet, but extremely dim. The food itself isn't anything special. It's very pricey for a regular Brazilian buffet. My family and I dined here for my 18th birthday. Our server, Jessica, was very nice. She was attentive and courteous. After telling her I was celebrating my 18th birthday she brought me a pudding with a candle on it which was very sweet of her considering I didn't ask. Creme brûlée wasn't too sweet, the flavoring was just right. Although the service was good, I won't be back due to high prices.

We made reservations for 7 people on a Saturday night on Saturday afternoon and were seated promptly. The place was packed and people were waiting. 
The service was great, the waiters were friendly and attentive, refilling our wine and water as needed, without having to be asked.
The appetizers were a mixed bag: the fried calamari was good, the antipasto was FANTASTIC, and the mussels were cold (some were cold, some were hot, were they microwaved? why?). 
The wine list seemed pricey for what the wines were, but they had a house wine that was reasonably priced. 
They  had a roaming accordion and violin player that gave some ambiance, but I wished it was just background music. An accordion can be pretty powerful when its right in your ear while you're trying to eat. 
Our entrees were also a mixed bag. My polenta with meatballs was good, but was boiling hot. The polenta itself was mild tasting, but the sauce and meatballs gave it a good kick. My husband's fruta di mare was poorly seasoned and was just frozen seafood. The tira misu for dessert was OUTSTANDING. I've never had better. 

Overall, a mixed bag but a pleasant experience. Seeing as though we've been going here for years, we will definitely be back.

The Field may very well be the result of a head-on collision between Central Square and TGI Fridays.  Its walls are cluttered with a hodgepodge of knicknacks, and the loud music, bright colors, and constant elbows make you feel like a plate of sizzling steak fajitas is about to get dumped on the pool table by a server sporting flair--though his mohawk will remind you that you're in Cambridge.  The bar offers a varied crowd and (here's the upside) decent prices for well-poured drinks.  While The Field is more a stop on a Central Square pub crawl than an actual destination, it's a great place to recover after a ritzy cocktail at the Enormous Room sends you into financial shock.

Last Saturday after my alcohol-induced buzz had reached levels that, while not epic, certainly diminished my orienteering skills, my friendly neighborhood DD shepherded our party of 4 to a bar I'd never in my life been in before, and for the life of me I had no idea where we were. It turns out we'd arrived at the Skybox Pub - a place I'd previously never heard of, and after setting foot inside, found to be somewhat out of place in the Sellwood/'moreland area.

The place is clearly a sports bar - the walls are festooned with jersey's, posters, and other garish bits of memorabilia and sports bric-a-brac. They even have a life-size mannequin in Jordan's #23 Bulls jersey, though we reached the conclusion that they must have used the lower half of a Charles Barkley dummy because I don't remember MJ's sticks being as thick as old growth redwoods.

They also have a good number of TVs, most (if not all) of the flat-panel variety, though many were only of middling size. I'd imagine the Skybox is a good place to just show up and watch whatever sporting event is on the tube, but the place is a bit small, and they don't have the best "stadium, big-screen" set-up, so I'm not sure if it's the best place to watch a really big game.

We didn't have any food, but I thought they had a pretty impressive beer selection for a somewhat random sports bar - not as good as the A&L or some other larger places, but way more than the standard Bridgeport IPA, Widmer Hefe, Black Butte Porter on tap - I enjoyed a pint or two of the DBA (Double Barrel Ale) from Firestone Walker, which was quite a nice West Coast take on a British Bitter.

The thing about this place though is that it's very bright - I mean, almost blindingly bright - inside! I don't always NEED dark/dank in my watering holes, but this was almost like walking into an operating theater the lights were so bright. Coupled with the visual commotion from the TVs and all the junk on the walls, and the Skybox is not what I'd describe as a "relaxing" atmosphere.

Ultimately if you're looking for a friendly little sports bar and live in the neighborhood then you should definitely give the Skybox a shot...but I wouldn't go out of my way to visit, and it certainly is a subpar destination for non-sports related drinking.

We came here for the restaurant week menu and the lunch prixfixe. When I reserved for the restaurant I noted that we would like to be seated by the view, but didn't get it initially when the host said that the table closer to the view (which was empty)was reserved. We said we would wait so after like 5 mins we were taken to another table by the view. 

From the restaurant week menu we got the soup(which was sweet and cinnamonny), the salmon which was decent(but a little fishy) and a chocolate cake. For 25 it was a good deal. From the lunch menu we got the New York strip steak, clam chowder she creme brûlée. At 42 it was also a good deal given the steak was shared between us. We were glad that the two prixfixe could be shared along 3 of us. And at the end we were all very full. Our server kindly asked us if we would like our food split so they were very accommodating. Even though the service was great I felt that not all the servers were knowledgeable when faced with more non-standard questions.

The creme brûlée was meh. The steak was decent. Food was really not that great.

Everyone should go to the Clermont at least once.  I was taken within my first month of living in Atlanta, and am a better Atlantan because of it.  Actually I think we all owe it to our of town guests to take them to the Clermont instead of the Varsity.  I mean, come on, would you rather experience one of the most unique dive bars in America or eat a greasy hotdog?  

The Clermont is divey, cash only, sometimes has a DJ, always great people watching, and just happens to have strippers (I use that term loosely).  My biggest gripe though:  for the past three times I've been here, Blondie has not been working.  I am assuming that Fridays and Saturdays are peak business hours, so where is this most illustrious beer crushing broad?  I repeat - three times, no Blondie, no bueno.  Has she retired and they just haven't told us?  Has Blondie moved to Miami Beach and become a Golden Girl?  Seriously though, what is going on?

Sure the Clermont is fun and games any time you go, but something is missing.  I only go when I have an out-of-towner to shock and entertain, and lately I feel as though I just haven't been properly delivering the full Clermont Lounge experience to my friends.  Sticking with my Varsity analogy, a night at the Clermont without Blondie is like a hotdog at the Varsity without a "What'll ya have?"  Until I see their most famed entertainer again, I'm sticking with my feelings of disenchantment chased with a PBR.

Pretty good. We're mostly vegan, so we're at a natural disadvantage at places like this. However, we had the Monk breakfast, and it was very good, but not outstanding. It's nice to see something as unique as this on a breakfast menu. The tea and coffee were fine, and we will definitely come back.

Update: Went in there yesterday morning with some friends right at 8AM when they opened. At about 8:45AM, after maybe 20 minutes with our food on the table, we were kindly asked if we could leave. What? I know there were people waiting to be seated, but I've never been asked to leave a restaurant after 45 minutes before! I thought that was a bit rude, and so I'm taking a star away!

This review is only for the food, as I didn't purchase a drink...

But basically it took them about an hour (maybe more) to make everything. I ordered the all day breakfast (2 eggs, 2 toasts, 2 sausages) + the brick toast with ice cream + curried fish ball. I understand that they're busy making drinks for other people, but priorities people!!! The male worker wasn't all that nice, but wasn't mean either. he did warn that the food would be a little longer, but not THAT much longer. 

The food was simple and you definitely get a deal for what you pay.

Probably won't come back for food!

Craving for Filipino cuisine and this one was recommended by some friends, we honestly chose to come here as most of my companions want to have the grilled pork intestines or isaw and  their boods menu. 
When we arrived we were lucky to be the first costumers they have that day as the place has an occupancy good for ten people as well as limit of four in each table, so we need to be separated, which is fine as they do indeed follow Co19 precautions. 
Originally we wanted to order the boods seafod or boods klasik however that order will take about two hours to wait, so probably next time call ahead or have it booked. 
For the food since its my first time I ordered the Chicken Inasal with Atsara which tasted  juicy and tender that goes well with the garlic rice. We were looking for some veggies as we think we lack some colour in our food which they only have okra and eggplant at the moment,we had the okra which comes with small shrimp dip or  bagoong alamang. The spring roll was delicious too, not oily and crispy. I haven't tasted the grilled pork intestine but my friend said that it was delectable when it was freshly served but after some minutes when it cooled down it became tough or chewy which they ended up not finishing it. 
Overall, the foods serve are your typical Filipino dish which is good when your in crave mode. The price is just right and the owners  are very accommodating.
Lastly, they don't have washroom inside and have limited street parking.

Before I get stacked for the 3 Stars, hear me out. We patiently waited to be seated for nearly 2 hours - which proves how excited we were to eat there. Our orders are listed below:

Fried okra- perfect! Great portion and the sauce was key. Perhaps providing 1-2 other sauces to change things up.

Fried chicken dinner- AMAZING! Batter was perfect along with the tenderness and moisture of the chicken. Seasoning was perfect. 

Chicken wings- this dish is what led me to dropping to a 3 Star review. First off, my first bite was a mouthful of salt! Being Filipino I love for salty dishes but this one went rogue! Then the smoked flavor of the wings caught me off guard. 

Cornbread- not worth buying. It was dry-enough said.

Mac N Cheese- was good, no wow factor. 
Baked Beans- a definite must! 

All in all, I'd go back just for the chicken breast dinner!

I was meeting up with my girlfriends at Medina Cafe and being the typical non-adventurous person that I am, I got the typical foods you would eat at Medina Cafe. Those being - the waffle, a flavoured coffee, paella and fricassee. 

The flavoured coffee I chose was the white chocolate pistachio rose mocha. I had the lavender last time, which was not bad but a little too strong on the lavender for me. This though, was surprisingly flavourful. I could taste the rose and I got bits of pistachio in my mocha. Unfortunately, exactly like what I was dreading, the white chocolate made it too sweet. But other than that I enjoyed it.

Rating: 7.5/10 

The paella was very spicy, maybe even a little bit TOO spicy. The chorizo and pepper made it very spicy and overwhelming that it masked the flavours of the base. The only flavours I could detect was sourness and spiciness, nothing else. I tried to use the avocado to tone it down, but it didn't help. Trust me, I love chorizo but unfortunately the balance of the spiciness of the chorizo was totally off in this dish. 

Rating: 6/10 

The fricassee was somewhat lacking flavour. It was more on the sweet side than the savoury side. When eaten with the leafy greens on top it was better balanced but nothing about this dish really stood out. The meat was pretty fall apart though which was a good thing. 

Rating: 6.5/10 

And finally of course, we had to finish with a waffle and salted caramel sauce. I've had the salted caramel sauce and it was pretty good so I had to order it again. The waffle though was somewhat disappointing. It was served warm which I thought was good, but the exterior lacked crunch which was disappointing. I remember last time I had it, it was crunchy so I guess it's just a consistency problem? 

Rating of waffle: 7/10     Rating of salted caramel sauce: 7.5/10 

Overall the impression that Medina Café gives me is that on weekends there are usually long lines out the door (luckily I went on a Tuesday at around 10 and we were seated within 5 minutes) and it's on the more expensive side. The service was pretty good. I think why a lot of people are attracted to this place is because of the hype and because there's snot much of this kind and style of brunch food that is open everyday. 

Rating: 7/10

Chung Wah Hong is perhaps the most consistent supermarket presence in Chinatown as I grew up. With the revolving door of Ming's (the original one burning to the ground when I was little), the 88's, the acquisitions of C-Mart, this little place keeps chugging along. It is owned by the same owners of Bao Bao Bakery around the corner. It has a very limited selection, but the pricing is reasonable. 

I come here to purchase very particularly... bok choy. They keep a very diverse selection of the vegetable always, from the more bulbous milky bok choy, the regular large ones, to the more elongated, almost endive-like baby Shanghai bok choy (though nowhere near as bitter) that does wonderfully when braised with a bit of ginger. The bok choy is stored in the open, rather than in the chilled refrigeration section. Sometimes, I get scallions and cilantro here when it looks fresh. The produce selection is a bit more limited than other places, but it isn't that large and they do compact the selection. I also acquire ground pork here for dumplings, Chinese steamed meatloaf, and stir-fries here, the grinder here a bit finer than at other places in the area.

I don't really purchase the produce outside often, but the tangerines I've picked up for sauces here have been alright.

Also, if you have a candy fix, this place seems to be the most consistent low pricing in Chinatown for Pocky, chocolate filled Koala cookies, and hard candies.

I ate there last night with low expectations.  I've been to their sister restaurant in west newton, hence the low expectations.  Last night exceeded my expectations.  I still think there is room for improvement and I hope they do.  The food was good and the beer selection was great, though they are changing the taps which is disappointing

First you MUST speed up the kitchen, it wasn't even crowded last night.  The was a problem at the original, so they need to bring in some outside help to show them how to get stuff moving through the kitchen.

Next do something about the decor, its nice, but it has no personality.

Overall good food, great vegetarian selections, and we had a nice bartender.

I'll start out by saying I haven't had much German food and I did not drink any of the beer.  I considered myself a bit of a foody living in multiple states and I have eaten at a lot of places.  I didn't find there food special at all.  First of all, when I spend $15 a plate I expect to leave full not hungry, portions are a bit small. My dish,  schnitzel and my wife's, lamb lacked spices to include salt and pepper.  The best part of the meal was the dinner rolls, nice crust with a slightly sour chewy center but you have to ask to get the free bread.  The rolls aren't enough for this guy to go back but if I did it would be to try the beer.

The store manager is a local white guy who never worked in the retail but worked as a librarian in Somerville, he once told me.  And, his lack of trained eyes are actually bothersome, sometimes. 

For example, this store sells the promotional fresh fruits in boxes.(fragrant Korean Melons, chamwoe, or Korean Pears $35 for 7 in one box). And, these are expensive, fragile, go bad fast and shouldn't be exposed to the room temperature, but be refrigerated. 

But, he let them sit on the store floor and then, let the latino staff to mob the floor with wet rags. soaking the boxes with the germ-filled mob water. And, he ignored my complaint. And, of course, these expensive fruits are all damaged, when I opened them at home. 

They also sold the "date-expired" Luna New Year gift set (Colorful Korean Traditional Rice puffs, Hangwa, Liquid Teas, or Royal Jelly, etc) at the discounted price. They do not disclose the date at the box outside (or erased). But, when I opened it, the snack was 2 months expired with the manufactured date in individual packages.
 
At other retail grocery stores, the items that are close to the expiry dates will still be sold. But, here, H-mart Cambridge sells 2-3 months already expired products, with the old date stamp on it. That is dishonesty.
