When I mention these issues to the same manager, on the phone, there was ZERO sincerity, or he explained No known store policy. He forgot to "apologize(expecting Korean Manners, and, isn't it Universal to apologize for such a letdown?)" for my inconvenience to travel to Cambridge and back home, and back next time to return. 

Although I said I lived 4 hours away from Boston, and, he still flatly said t bring in the receipt the next day to get the refund. Forget it. Instead, I complained to H-Mart NJ head office about him. But, Koreans in the head office didn't act like Customer services. Hopefully, you don't run into issues like I did at all costs.

Today,  I searched about H-Mart reviews on-line; others shared their nightmares, from CA locations actually H-Mart people change the expiry date, by erasing the inked date to a new one for the frozen seafood packages. 

*Blocked aisles : 
When there was a snack sampling, often the young female workers wander around to grab the sample snacks themselves into their vests. These sampling events are not for the shoppers, it just blocks the aisles. Other young male workers block the aisles, with step ladders and the card board boxes on the floor. The aisles  are too narrow and  impossible to get by if there is another cart or a wheeled basket.  3 customers in 1 aisles is too crowded.

*Shelving issues- poor categories
They stocked one frozen sea food next to Kimchi, but, dumplings are found opposite of the building, next to the ice cream! These store management really need to benchmark other major supermarkets. It all starts with Flower, Produce-Bakery/Deli- then long shelf life products, then, Meat-Dairy, Frozen, then, cashiers.

*Kimchi is not for the vegetarian! 
You should know there is NO Vegetarian Kimchi, as they use shrimp or fish fermented juice (rotting the raw fish with salt and the juice from their bodies produce-mixed with the beneficial bacteria, this will later be added to Salt-wilted Korean Vegetables to let them "fermented") So, although it is good, Kimchi is NOT vegetarian choice, Some of the Kimchi also have nuts. These should be mentioned for allergy alert.

*Poor Communication 
These Asian cashiers do NOT speak English. They are not from USA, unlike many Latino workers hired in Burlington (Most speak English and documented).
 
It is impossible to have any basic communication at the cashier's. The friendly part-time assistant manager has to come to each cashier area to translate English to Chinese. Well, how did H-Mart hire them to USA without understanding the basic? Other foreign workers who are hired in my town all speak English with the proper J-type document.

I suspect if this will entail other evasions. But, that is just my speculation. Burlington H-Mart, on the contrary, hires "local" people, except for the Koreans (LOL) who don't speak English and run away from the customers. And, IMO, they don't speak or comprehend Korean to Koreans, either :) The standard is low.

And, the reviewer below me, said about "paid" parking. This is  a CENTRAL "Public" Parking lot for all, before H-Mart opening. She should have known the sign of the public parking lot when she fed her parking meter. 

And, to other fellow yelpers, LOCAL tax payers & Voters,  
it is important to support the independent small business. A Large Big Box store can ruin the local community by taking over their business one by one. (Florist, Pharmacy, Deli, Corner Grocery stores, Cafe, Lunch places...) All Inner city business should be smaller-scaled not to "cripple" the community.

***I really want you to practice your own precaution, and demand for the better to H-Mart to support and be part  of the community.

A friend and I came here for brunch on a Sunday and the reviews had good things to say. They were pretty busy and I'm usually understanding about the circumstances but the service was pretty terrible. It took them 10+ minutes to bring us water (after we'd already received our meal), they never refilled my coffee or checked on us during our meal. They weren't kind or very personable and the waitress seemed to be having a hard day. 
That being said, the food was very good and was fairly redeeming for the circumstances. I try to keep an open mind when it comes to waitstaff but it could be improved.

I got a groupon from a friend. Foolishly, I waited to book, thinking I would not need more than a week or two in advance. As many have stated, they book groupon customers 2 months to 3 months in advance, and times are very limited. When I was looking there was nothing after 4pm so I had to go with a saturday.

Finding the place is not as hard as people make it out to be. I think the fact that I had it in my head that it was difficult made me look around more. It is really just up a set of stares in the plaza, and around the corner. Yes, they need better signs.

There is an older (married?) couple who works there and a younger man. The younger man did my mani and pedi and did a good job. The whole thing took like 2 hours, if I recall correctly....and that was with him working on my the whole time. So longer than I wanted, but it was quality work. I actually prefer going to a place where there is a language barrier, because the small talk here got out of hand. Everyone was chat chatting it up and I wanted to try to just relax. The older couple finished up their clients faster and had down time. They easily could have had more people in the salon, not sure why they don't book more people.

Lastly, I had a hard time picking out a color. There was not as much variety as I was hoping for.  All in all, it was fine for a groupon but I would not book again.

After a hike at the Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area (East Palisades trail), we used Yelp to find us some dinner food.

1) Tacos:
 * Asada (steak)
 * Pastor (marinated pork)
 * Chorizo (Mexican sausage)

I liked the Pastor taco a lot more than the other 2. The chorizo was quite spicy, but it was flavorful. These tacos came out plain style, so we had to go to the salsa bar to add the toppings (veggies and sauces) and we think the "mild" salsa may actually be spicier than mild for us. My bf liked the chorizo taco the most. There is a list of other meats and things you can fill your tacos with.

2) Flautas (chicken)
The toppings tasted really great and refreshing. The fried tortilla was crispy and good, but the inside chicken meat was too dried out. It was flake-like too, strange.

3) Tamale (chicken)
It is mildly spicy. Overall, my bf says he's had better and this did not win me over either. The wrap is made with corn husk.

4) Horchata drink
Since we're at a Mexican restaurant, we thought we get this for refreshment. Unfortunately, we did not enjoy this! It tasted like rice and cinnamon, but was just too too sweet.

Plenty of parking spaces. Clean bathrooms.

The food and atmosphere were not bad, but when they start to get busy plan on waiting a long time. We went the first time and waited 1 hour fifteen minutes for burgers and wings during a busy time.  Manager did his best to apologize but tough to defend. We wanted to give them another try a month later to see if anything had changed. Went 6 Friday night, crowded but still 5 or 6 empty tables.  Waited more than 40 minutes for burger, wings and kids hot dog party of 3.  If your hungry try another restaurant.

I'm a long time customer of Grand Central Bakery and Cafe. They have several locations in Portland and Seattle. It is run by a nice family and some good friends. They specialize in fresh daily, natural, local produce and ingredients from excellent soups, sandwiches, salads, artisan breads & mouth watering pastries (fresh baked each morning), fresh coffee and espresso and breakfast sandwiches.

I thought I'd try the new Panera Bread on Hwy 99 in Hazel Dell, Vancouver, WA.
Very average compared to Grand Central. Maybe since they are new they are still learning,  being trained, and don't have a high quality standard to compare to, but we tried a couple salads and sandwiches and they were just ok, but not the "A" grade that I know I will get at Grand Central on a regular basis.

I'm from Hawaii and absolutely love and know poke bowls. Flavor wise and quality is pretty good for Austin however, the service I've received the last two times I've gone there was mediocre. I asked for a variety of toppings including avocado which they barely provided for $1.50. I also asked for salmon instead of tuna which apparently is $3 extra and they still gave me tuna in the end. I also asked to have the bowl for here and then they still gave me my dish to go. So I think overall this place satisfies my poke craving and it's convenient since it's near to my place but, I think it's a bit pricey for what I ended up getting.

One Saturday night, we went out with friends and after drinking we decided to try out the Filipino food truck on W. 5th & Colorado. 

The food smells delicious! I ordered the pork fried rice with longganisa and egg. It was ok but I was expecting more flavor on the fried rice. The longganisa is not actually a real longganisa, it is more like a breakfast round sausage :(

My friends ordered a fried rice and adobo and the other ordered the tacos. 

We will have to try it again but for now, I will give it a 3-star for OK.

Since going back to BQE I needed to update my review 

BQE is still 5 stars up in my book! When it comes to FOOD...so I came here for the 12-5 day party on my birthday and enjoyed myself. The day party at BQE is every Saturday from 12-5. They serve brunch from 12-3 at affordable prices and from 3-5 they have a small affordable entree list you can select from. 

Drinks are very affordable, in fact it is much better  to get a party size depending on the number of people in your group. They have valet parking for $10 or $7 which is perfect because you don't want to struggle to look for parking or you can self park in lot, a block over for $5. 

After somewhat missing the brunch schedule, my party and I had to order off of the (after 3 side of the menu). Now, I am not a huge waffle fan, but I must say after tasting the red velvet waffles and tenders my cousin ordered, I can easily say I am impressed. I also ordered fried wings and fries which came back to be very well seasoned. Our waiter was very animated and helped us to enjoy our time there. 


Now on to my second experience...I decided to come back for my mom's birthday this past weekend. (The day party again) and our visit wasn't so great this time around. (Now pay attention to this next piece of what I'm about to say because it is very critical) We DID NOT make reservations because it would only be 3 of us. We were able to come right in and sit down. (Just as before) this time we were able to order on the  brunch menu and get mimosas. Now champagne bottles CAN NOT be shared by customers who did not pay to have mimosas. You must pay $22 per person if you and someone else wants to drink. Because both my mom and I wanted to drink I decided to pay the $22 per person.
A hour into drinking and eating. The waiter comes over and tells me my time is up. I start looking confused because I had no idea I was on a time limit. No one told me about this prior to sitting down. Well I spoke to a a manager and was told walks-in have 1 hour to eat and reservations have 2 and then you must leave. When I asked why this wasn't explained to me when I arrived, I got no answer. The best they could do was move me to the "standing bar area"'so I could finish my second bottle of champagne that I wouldn't have ordered, had I know I only had a hour to sit. To my surprise I was not the only customer treated this way as I saw more people, who was asked to leave their table, standing at the bar area with their champagne and wine. 

To say the least my bill was extremely high and I had to spend the rest of my visit standing up finishing a bottle of champagne. Because I wasn't informed of this. I won't be returning...the food is great, but the staff is sorry for failing to inform customers of this. That's poor customer service in my book and comes off as a dirty way to make money.

OK.. we ordered the sausage pizza and it was GREAT. Loved it as breakfast in the morning - always the best test, right ? So if you are someone who loves pizza and wants to try every place with good pizza - you must visit. 

So I give it OK because there was nothing spectacular about the place. The Pizzas I can believe will be good. The desserts - I did not order but tried all of them. Just about OK. Mango rice pudding - not impressive. The space is very hip but the seating was not so comfortable and so I could hang out for hours. I see myself going back of course and happily but not intentionally. The server was really nice too. We had a great conversation.

Great atmosphere.   Food - pretty good, but hit and miss.   Salad was over dressed.   Hostess tonight was having a bad night.  She definitely was stressed and it showed.   Bartenders upstairs were very nice, but not really properly trained.  The two bartenders were flustered when we wanted to pay cash and not leave a credit card or drivers license.  My buddy ordered a dinner at the bar and they insisted he had to leave a credit card or drivers license before they would enter the order.  He said no, so the compromise at this fine restaurant was that he pay cash in advance the second he put his order in.   Oh, he was supposed to tip too, before he got his food or any service.   It was perverse.   It really was a case of badly trained staff.   DF just doesn't offer a good consistent food value proposition.

We had some trouble getting reservations for weekend evenings, so I recommend calling more than a couple days in advance if you wanna go during a prime time. 

The complimentary corn bread was delicious and we were offered another serving later in the meal which was awesome! For starters we tried the fried oysters and mac and cheese fritters, which were a special that night. I thought the oysters were nicely breaded and very good, especially with the tangy aioli, and I enjoyed the accompanying pickled vegetables. The mac and cheese fritters were just average, and I probably wouldn't get it again. For my entree I got the fried chicken, which came in a generous portion. The mac and cheese here (not in fritter form) was great, but the collard greens were definitely on the sour side as noted in many other reviews. The chicken itself was very moist, including the breast meat, but the batter was a little too hard and crispy for me. 

Overall it's a nice restaurant with pretty big portions. I just think I've had better fried chicken elsewhere. It did seem like there was an extensive drinks menu relative to the food menu (almost everything on the "specials" menu was actually a drink), so that might be of interest to some people.

Went here due to the high rating on Yelp - 
What you should know?  Cash only and expensive - 
The pasta costs the same as their meat entrees - 

Not expecting this we ordered a nice Montepulciano at a very good price - 
Then we ordered and shared a Caesar Salad & a Rigatoni White Bean Pasta - Which we hate doing, but didn't have the cash for a real dinner with apps, wine & entrees. 

I guess I was expecting more, but my Rigatoni, Arugula, tomato, white bean pasta was $23 and tasted like something I could make at home.     

The place is charming and the service fine. We did share and they split the courses for us and the portions were perfect.  I would venture on to something different, unless you are looking for ok food at a really high price.

And yes (as mentioned previously)- at these prices, freshly grated parmesan should be a given.  Not something that has been from one table to another.

This is the second time I've visited Wal-Mart in 25 years.  The first visit was to shop for supplies for a family reunion at the coast in Lincoln City.  At the time, I knew nothing about it, and it did seem not unlike our chain of Fred Meyer stores.

This current visit was just a few days before Christmas to find an electric foot-massage bath at a very low price for Ron.  He is on his feet at work all day and wanted to get it because his feet do hurt at times.  Therefore, this review really only covers that area of the store where that item was located.

I thought parking was OK this close to Christmas.  Neither of us used the restrooms.  To be fair, this part of the store was in shambles due to probably frantic shoppers, but we were impressed by the employees we encountered.  They were uniformly cheerful and very helpful (I might have wanted to snarl were I in their shoes.). Once we had the foot bath in hand, checkout was quick and smooth.  

It isn't often I think I would feel the need to stop at Wal-Mart, but it turned out to be perfectly OK and largely made so by price and by the very enjoyable young employees.

OK so to all you Blue Star lovers,  and there must be many because there were a lot of people , no hate posts please. 
Personally I thought they were OK. Not life changing,  not orgasmic, not I don't care about my diet good and certainly NOT worth over $3. I bought the PB&J, Raspberry/rosemerry, Lemon/poppy, Mexican chocolate and Lemon  curd-$16. My favorite was the Lemmon poppy, the rest were meh and I didn't like the lemon curd it was way too tart/sour. The PB&J was interesting,  it was like eating PB but it was just the powder it was rolled in.They do have interesting flavors to try and that's half the fun but you pay for that fun.

I did not schedule this appointment with Blackmon. Otherwise, I probably wouldn't have based on the reviews.

We had to have them come out to clean our air conditioning vents that started to smell like mildew. 

I wasn't home but J said they were "nice enough" and although they attempted to clean up, it still took some sweeping from J and a full vacuum job from me to get up all the bits left behind. Only a slight irritation that they didn't put our child-proof electrical covers back on after using them. 

They also showed up late, but that was probably a miscommunication from the scheduler. 

Good news, no more funky smell!

They were very responsive but elusive about pricing- ( must be the corporate policy hook)  the tech showed up..he was great and unclogged the sink and went over pricing tho the fees were not broken down ( corporate policy too?)  the tech was awesome I do not fault him for anything. 

The pricing is very high for the service needed at least for me today and besides it Thanksgiving what options are there? ( another hook) 

Crafty company with good service and high fees. Gobble Gooble goes the $$ but an unclogged sink.

B

My friend and I went here at about 10:30 on a really cold Friday night in December. The bottom floor had some lingering diners and a decent bar crowd. Didn't spend too long here, but it seemed nice.

Second floor was pool tables and one small bar in the front. It was nicely crowded here as well. The third floor was closed for a private event, so it was hard to get a pool table. We had a couple drinks and chatted with people around the bar until a table opened up. It was expensive and I wouldn't come here just for a night of pool. But as a diversion between mingling and dancing upstairs, it's fine.

Around maybe 11:30 they opened the night club (with a $10 cover) on the fourth floor. Over the next hour, virtually everyone from downstairs went up there. It's a pretty small space, but the bar runs all the way along one side and practically the whole rest becomes a dance floor. I thought it was pretty good, actually. Nice and cozy. It is pretty loud though, so if you don't already have someone to dance with, it's going to be hard to talk to someone new. And this place didn't quite seem like the spot for the grind-your-way dance floor approach :-)

Went back downstairs around 1am and the other floors were practically empty. There were a couple pool players and a couple boozers on the bottom floor and not much else. It was freezing cold out that night, so possibly a little slower than other Fridays.

One other note: I think the entire staff is good-looking women. Maybe not in the back, but behind the bars and hostesses, that's all I saw.

EDIT: I went there for a friend's birthday on a Saturday night in january and had a blast. Great place to go with a group. It's too loud to really talk and meet new people (at least on the top floor) but fun to dance and hang out with a group. Also the weather was not as cold and there was a better crowd than the previous time. I would upgrade to 3.5 stars if that were possible.

We happened to be walking by one night, and decided to give it a try. Our overall experience there was nice - it was intimate and casual, which was exactly what we were in the mood for. The first dish we ordered was the baked endives wrapped with ham and served with a bubbling cheese sauce. It was delicious! The endive really cut through the richness of the ham & cheese. The lapin moutarde (rabbit with mustard sauce), however, was chewy and the Dijon overpowered all other flavours in the dish. The presentation & atmosphere was good, so I'd give it another chance.

Now... the menu is a hit & miss at this place.  While most of the items on the menu is Asian, the actual food item is actually American (turkey sandwich & etc).  

We came in at a slow night (there are only 2 other table than us)... 3 servers, 2 in hte kitchen & 1 serving, however, it took the waitress 5 minutes to come take our order, 10 minutes for the drinks to come out, another10 minutes for the sweet potato fries & popcorn chicken.  Bubble tea wise, it's ok but it is definitely the best in town so far.  Popcorn chicken-wise, it's flavorless, the Asian basil is more of a garnish than being part of the dish (being fried).  The owners supposed to be Taiwanese, however, the food items has a long way to go.  We will give it another chance in 6 month.

I've had better.  I ordered a miso based soup with meat and veggies.  It took a while to prepare and it came out with broth that wasn't very hot...temperature hot.  

The cashier wasn't all that warm and friendly, and the kitchen was backed up.  When I asked for hot broth (the most important part of a the ramen in my opinion), it was still lukewarm.  I don't usually give less than a three unless it's just absolutely disgusting.  It was passable.  Good luck with yours!

Went here tonight on a visit to Boulder. I did the tasting menu and the chef was attentive to my need to be gluten free. Food was good but not amazing. It also bothered me that I didn't get any beef in my tasting--fish, chicken and pork but I missed the satiety of beef. Bartender was very nice and attentive (I sat at the bar), but one server was a bit odd--kind of a close talker and didn't seem to know what she was talking about when she explained the dish. Also had to hear about some date she went on and the guy she kissed (I was overhearing--she didn't tell me the story). Overall, good experience. Worth $91 with a cocktail and tip? Not a chance. I should have ordered a $25 (beef) dish off the menu and I probably would have been happier.

We wanted to check out the history of Salem and their witches. We bought the three pack to see the history museum, dungeon, and the pirate. 

Ummmm....I do agree with the last review, that it really does depend on your tour guide. Our tour guide was pretty good. He didn't talk too fast and sound like he was simply repeating a script. You could tell he was passionate about the history. 

I also do agree with the comments about the museum being cheesy. Lol. It is pretty cheesy. But if you can get past that, the history and education is pretty interesting. So, I did enjoy the wealth of knowledge that was given to me. 

The only thing I was not a fan of, all three of the museums smelled the same. Which was dirty and dusty. They need to shut these museums down one day, once every three months, and one at a time and CLEAN. Wipe the dust off the figures and the objects. It would help with the presentation. If you are allergic to a lot of dust, these attractions may be difficult. Lol. 

But all in all, it was a decent tour.

Wow, I didn't think there was a place that could compete with Taco Bell's prices, and yet taste good.

Ordered the Carne Asada tacos for $1.75 each and a Lengua burrito.  The tacos were average size with good flavor, but the Lengua burrito??? AWESOME for $5.50.  Tongue meat was tender and flavorful and add a couple of jalapenos and homemade salsa  in containers on the outside of the food truck top it all off... tasty.

Overall Rating: 73%

Food: 4/5
Service: 3/5
Price: 4/5

Starbucks with a drive through - Amazing.

Speed of drive through at this Starbucks - Tortoise-tastic.

I order a very simple drink (Iced Quad Venti Latte, sometimes non-fat) pretty much every time.  I don't recall ever getting my order wrong, except when it was obvious they switched the order of the orders and I was handed the drink for the car behind me.  That has happened more than once, though not recently.  

 I did try sitting inside one day, hoping to make a phone call and kill some time.  Unfortunately the background music and AC were so loud there was no way I could make the call.

Overall, I recommend it only if you're driving by.

I don't care what anyone else says - this place is just fun. I've never attended any movies or special events here but I've had a few pleasant meals and had fun roaming the halls. Out of town guests stayed in the hotel and really enjoyed themselves. For the uninitiated, it's a nice introduction to the McMenamin's empire. 

Don't go here looking for gourmet dining. It's average pub grub, plain and simple.

I appreciate that McMenamins helps to preserve pieces of Northwest history like the Kennedy school. They get bonus points for hiring local artists to decorate the reclaimed hallways.

I live close to Rehanah's and walked by so many times without even noticing it. It looks like a deli store. Anyway I ordered food to take out a few times. The roti was always very tasty. However every time I ate there I got a migraine. Maybe coincidence but most likely the food has some MSG. I give only 3 stars as the store is closed most of the times (even when they supposed to be open according to the hours on the door). Payment is cash only.

This place is okay. I always go between 1am-5am so maybe the service and food is different at this time. Pretty standard pho. The one thing that I like about this place is that the chicken pho doesn't come with bone-on chicken which makes it easier for me to just eat it quickly. I don't think their service is consistent. They were good at the beginning when they started out, but it has been diminishing. Last week, I came in around 1:30am. I ordered a small chicken pho and there was less than average noodles in my bowl. I ended up finishing the noodles in 3 or 4 bites. The only reason I will visit this place again is if I am craving pho in the middle of the night and am hungry and I don't want to drive to the other 24 hour pho restaurant, I Luv Pho. I should try eating here during the daytime to see if it's any different.

Food is good, lots of unique options.  For an oyster bar I expected a slightly larger selection of oysters.  Service from the wait staff is decent but the wait time for food is horrendous!  It took more than 75 minutes for our entrees, and we didn't order anything exotic (fried egg, beans, bacon).  Easily 20 minutes between courses.  No acknowledgement of or apology for the long wait.  I mentioned the slow service to a woman who I believe was the assistant manager and was told that they'd "let the kitchen know (about the complaint)"..  If they could work on the kitchen speed, this would could be 4 stars, if not 5.

Three stars because this place is good, not great. 

I ordered take out. 12 inch pizza with three toppings and extra cheese. The toppings are sparse, and I had to pay $1.50 per extra topping (I got one free). The cheesiness is great! When you pull a slice away, you get that wonderful string of gooey cheese that you have to grab a hold of, love it! Like I said, the other toppings aren't really there. They definitely don't spread them like Donatos. (Not that I prefer Donatos lol) But they seem like fresh ingredients.

The crust is nothing special. It reminds me of the kind you get at the grocery store that says, "Just add water!" I actually didn't eat the crust for this reason. (After the first slice I tried, that is.) It's not greasy at all though, so that's a plus! 

There was only one person working, that I could see, and he was super nice and smiley. Gave me some coupons too. Pizza was ready when I got there.

Overall, I would eat it again. But I wouldn't say that I prefer it over all of the other pizza places near me.

Disclaimer: I LOVE Boston's casual and slightly-more-than-casual food scene, but I find the high-end restaurants underwhelming.  The value just doesn't justify the quality or quantity.  Bistro Du Midi is the perfect example.

I had the oysters to start with, which were okay, but nothing to write home about.  I sampled a few appetizers, none of which stand out in my mind.  For the main I had the coral-infused tagliatelle, which was disappointing: the calamari and mussels were chewy, and the pasta stuck together, and it was $26.  I sampled my friend's garganelli, which was much more delicious.  Also had the brussels sprouts appetizer, which was good, but there were only about ten sprouts, and it cost $7.  The desserts were actually quite good, and the only part of the meal that I really enjoyed.

I'd give Bistro Du Midi four stars if I had ordered the garganelli and the entrees were say, $7 less.  Or if I were rich.  I was here for a work event, otherwise I would have been more upset with the meal.

My wife targeted this business as a stop on our first visit to Portland, so we made it there about 10:30 am yesterday (2/20/17 - Monday) morning, not long after it opened at 10 am. We walked around and looked at all the different dealer booths and came away pretty impressed. We are visiting from Dallas, and the prices and quality of inventory from the dealers was better than any antique mall we frequent in Dallas, although one thing I will say is that there is a much higher demand in Dallas, so pieces are set accordingly (much higher than Portland) and most of the quality in Dallas is quickly picked through. It's all relative to location and supply/demand. However, there was some good stuff...we just didn't purchase anything with our limited luggage space to take home. Good space, good location.

My husband and I were actually on our way over to the Tradesman Cafe on a Saturday morning at 9 am when we walked past this place and saw the cute Mercato sign. We glanced over the brunch menu that was in the window and said, brunch? Why not? Unfortunately, once we were seated, we were handed breakfast menus and told brunch service doesn't start 'til 11am. Whomp whomp. Not their fault, we could have asked. 

The interior decor is well-thought out, with rustic touches throughout and the restaurant is connected to the Hyatt Centric hotel on the other side. We ordered espresso drinks, which are made from the coffee bar inside the hotel and brought to your table. 

I ordered the eggs benedict and my husband ordered the potato hash. There were maybe 2 other parties seated besides ourselves, so the place was rather empty. There was a couple who sat down after us who had ordered, received their food and finished their food before ours even came! We really don't mind sitting and chatting over coffee but we were at the point where we genuinely thought they might have forgot to place our order. My husband got up to see if our server knew if our food was coming but there was literally not a single person around. 

45 minutes after ordering, our food finally arrives. 

The eggs benedict was okay. The eggs were poached nicely with a perfect runny yolk, they were sitting on top of a bed of wilted spinach, lots of bacon and an english muffin that had been buttered and salty very generously. It was too salty, I actually had to remove some bacon and realized that it wasn't just the bacon but the english muffin had been loaded with salt. The hollandaise was nondescript, not creamy or tangy, just kind of bland. 

The potato hash looked delicious but the potatoes were only barely cooked through. They were charred nicely, which gave the appearance of doneness but the insides still had that almost slightly raw/crunchiness to them. 

It really seems like this place has potential but still is working out some pretty big kinks.

Food: 2.5/5
I ordered a hand pull noodle  and a lamb skewer for lunch. It's a hot day so I don't want noodle soup. However, the hand pull noodle is a disappointment. Even it looks very tasty but when I taste it, it's tasteless. And it has only noodle and chili oil. It looks spicy but it doesn't taste spicy. The lamb skewer is actually very good , I will order it again next time. I will be back for other thing like noodle soup since it's next to my workplace. 

Price: 5/5
It's cheap with most things in the menu less than $10 for the generous amount of food. 

Atmosphere & Services: 3.5/5
The restaurant is small and self serving, you take your number and wait. Then you get your food you will choose any table you want.

I wondered into this store for the first time while shopping on West Broadway the other day. The store is small but has a nice selection of flowers and the price wasn't too bad in my opinion. 

However, the saleswoman who arranged two bouquets for me, was rather aggressive and impatient. 
I must say that I'm not the quickest person when it comes to making decisions, but I felt quite rushed and flustered with her "hurry up and make up your mind" attitude. 
Looking frustrated, she even said something like "You know, I'm trying here so YOU need to tell me what you think!!". Um, I'm still thinking...Can I not have enough time to decide if I like these $60 bouquets? I even apologized to her in advance that I'm completely clueless with flower designing and that I feel bad for taking up her time. That was definitely not the kind of attitude I want from a salesperson. 

All in all, I am happy with my purchase but this place definitely needs to learn how to treat customers better if they want to keep their business.

We weren't real impressed. The food was good but not enough to go back and wait in the long line to pick it up. The price on menu for mine didn't match up when I paid. The whole time I was in the pickup line the music was too loud. It was some Jamaican Rap so after a few minutes it was just too much. You could,nor should,eat in. There are so many people standing around waiting on to go orders and so few tables you'll wish you'd gotten carry out. The food is good though.

I've been here a few times in the last year, because of the influx of Groupons (and Buywithme, et al), and because it's very close to my apartment. If I was to base this review on food alone, I'd probably give it at solid 4 stars. I've tried many things, and they've all been delicious. Top faves are the mussels fra diavlo, the chicken parm, and the Gorgonzola steak. The place is small, but cozy.   The waitstaff has always been friendly.  

However, like many others have noted, they do NOT know how to keep a reservation. They shouldn't accept so many reservations if they can't keep them. It's a small place, and tables aren't plentiful...they are presumably aware of this fact.  You shouldn't have to wait 40+ minutes to be seated if you have a reservation. To quote Jerry Seinfeld: "You know how to take the reservation...you just don't know how to HOLD the reservation. And that's really the most important part of the reservation....the holding." 

If you can get here in the afternoon when it's not crowded (late lunch or early dinner), it's a great meal, just don't go for dinner unless you are extremely patient or can make a reservation before 6PM.

cheap drinks woot woot!  Ok besides the fact that when you walk in the overwhelming smell of greasy fried double fried triple fried fries.  The crowd is quite eclectic.  I saw your standard toothless, dirty hot mess sitting at the bar playing some game, another table of hipsters, another table of mid-30's couples that were quite toasty and some singles that were all enjoying themselves. So besides the grease stink and as obvious that this place is a dive, everyone was a regular and they were drinking. Which is precisely what you do at dives.  This place is hardly about pretense. Just go for the cheap drinks and cheap eats without concern for what you are actually digesting.

Food
* Chocolate Croissant: Tasted alright. Texture was a little too soft and not crisp enough even though I had it heated up. It also had sprinkled sugar on top, and not enough chocolate filings inside. Might want to try other pastries instead if you're here.
* They also have infused water and regular iced water available for free


Atmosphere
* The place had good lighting and enough outdoor light comes into the space as well. The inside space is a little small, but enough bar seating for about 10 people. Love the marble tables that faces directly to the baking area and they have freshly baked stuff on display most of the time. 
* There's also plenty of outdoor space. This coffee shop is part of Urban Outfitter's Space 24 Twenty so the outdoor space is a shared area with other food trucks and restaurants in the vicinity. 
* Temperature in the indoor space is perfect, probably at around high 70 degrees
* Plenty of outlets available indoor and outdoor. The coffee shop's wi-fi didn't work when I went there, but there's also urban outfitters guest wi-fi that I can use, so its nice to have that available.
* Crowd: Mostly college students, as its a couple of feet away from UT. People generally buy stuff for to-go or just hang out there for a short period of time cause there's not very many seatings available. But, there are also plenty of students who are there to do work and are on their laptop for a longer period of time. 

* Service: All staff are nice and friendly. They also always have free samples of baked goods at the cashier.

Just came back from Auto-Glo and must admit the car looks great.

However, when I opened up the back of the Grand Cherokee to take a photo of the cargo area (we are about to sell the car) they had apparently not touched it and there was still a ton of debris and dog hair all over it.
They charge extra for vans, minivans, trucks and suv's so wtf?
Don't charge extra if you are not going to clean that area.
I just paid $45 including tip and I have to vacuum for 10 minutes when I get home?
HELLO.

Also, the guy behind the counter did not acknowledge anyone at any time and just stared at his Apple laptop the entire hour I was there.
When it came time to pay he was no where to be found and after 10 minutes of standing up at the desk I finally went outside and got one of the washers to check me out.
He was polite at least.

Probably will go back but will check my car thoroughly before leaving next time.

Had lunch here yesterday.  Ordered the quiche and it was actually pretty decent served with a small fruit cup and a not so great "salad".  Liked the bechemel sauce served on it though.  My dining companions both ordered one of the burgers and said it was great.  Huge and loaded on top with lots of stuff!!  Also tried one of their milkshakes which seemed to be their specialties.  You get to take home the plastic mason jar it comes in.  I was told it was the best milkshake ever.  Music not too loud (unlike most places in City Walk).  A little too theme oriented but it is a few steps from Universal Studios so what you would expect.  I would give it a second visit.

Just a heads up: this is a factory outlet store. This isn't your average BR. The benefits: cut price deals and a healthy selection of discounts. The negatives: not much attention paid to cleanliness and a drab looking store. I'm never inspired to step into this place, but I'll check every once and a while for a cheap shirt or item. You don't get the niceness of a real BR, but you also get much cheaper clothing. Life is all about compromise!

Let's face it...cheap accommodations are not easy to find in Boston. Especially at the last minute. I was supposed to leave the day Hurricane Florence made landfall, and I knew Logan and every other airport was going to be crazy. So I decided to stay in the city a few extra days. The problem was, the place I was staying didn't have any rooms available, but I was able to get a room at the Farrington Inn through booking.com. 

Because the stay was going to be more than just a couple of nights, they gave me a room with a private bath and a kitchenette. I can't speak to the rooms in the original house or the shared bathrooms. Given what others have said, I'd suggest trying to make sure you get a room in one of the other houses.

That said, it is a cheap inn, but it did what I needed it to do. I was able to sleep and have a warm shower--pretty much all I require when traveling. 

Andrew helped me with my bags and showed me the room. He was great, giving advice about laundromats and other places in the neighborhood. 

Yeah, the houses are old, and the rugs in the hallways are stained. I didn't notice any of the obnoxious odors others have complained about. There was a small cockroach in my room, but I've camped with bugs, so to tell the truth I didn't really care all that much. I know it would freak out some people, though, so just thought I'd give that warning.

The bed was probably the worst thing about the room. It was one of the old spring bed frames, except there wasn't any spring left in it. It sagged badly and my back really hurt in the morning. 

Other than that, it was fine. There was a small desk along with the kitchenette, the bathroom was pretty clean, and I was able to spend an extra couple days in the beautiful city of Boston without bankrupting myself.

If you want everything nice, then you probably need to spend two to four hundred dollars a night at a different place. If you just want a place to put yourself at night, then the Farrington Inn worked out for me.

This hotel has nice beds and a wonderful view of the city, but don't lose your receipt if you are on business the hotel will not give you another one. After talking to several people I found this to be disheartening that there was "Nothing they can do to email me another receipt".
I also found there to be mold in the bathroom, carpets not vacuumed well and my TV blacked out and I had to keep shutting it off, neither did the IHOME/IPOD/Clockradio work. The room was too hot for my liking even when the "air-conditioned" room temp was set on 60 degrees, you can only put the fan on, No actual air.  

Overall, if you can overlook these minor details. It is a convenient location to the arena district and the North Market all within walking distance. parking seems to be far away but with the skywalk, its just a few minute walk.

I don't shop here that often. Not for a lack of inventory or things that interest me, I am a sucker for all the journals and gifting section in addition to the books... but mainly because everything is so dang expensive. One book in particular I was was looking for today I had to google to find the name/author. In finding the name I saw I could get it at Target for $9 meanwhile the paperback copy I found in the store was twice that! That's just nuts. I was also drawn to the clearance Christmas stuff marked half off and fell in love with a cute wrapping paper, but it was still $5 even with 50% off. C'mon now. Ugh. 
I left with 5 books and some Christmas cards for next year, $100 poorer. At least I got one of the books half off. I really want to support the local stores and not always resort to buying on Amazon, but prices like that kinda force your hand...

I gave this hotel a 3 star rating because it is truly just A-OK. there's nothing too special about it. If you've never stayed at an Embassy Suites before you might be wowed by their nightly cocktail hour, or their daily made to order breakfast, both come free with your stay. But for those of us who travel a lot, you know this is standard. Not something to gain additional stars for.

The pros:
I checked in late and they held my reservation (I called ahead to let them know).
They gave me 2 bottles of water upon check in because of my Hilton Honors account.
My room was large - to be expected because it was a suite. The king bed was comfortable, one of the nicest I've stayed on in a while not counting mine at home.
Restaurant on site as well as room service.

The cons:
They held $100 additional for incidentals - seriously? This always annoys me because I never use credit cards, always just debit.
Parts of the room seemed to be from the 1970's - scratch that, parts of the hotel too. For example the coffee maker and microwave are in a closet with slat doors. Hmm??
My entire room smelled of disinfectant, which should me me happy but it wasn't homey at all. It actually gave me a headache.
The parking is free, so that's a pro for a hotel of this size. But the con is that there's not enough spots up front so you have to park all the way behind the hotel just to find a spot. Then drag your bags around the building just to check in.
The pool is right outside the elevators, so you have to look at nasty old dudes in the hot tub, or have them gawk at you every time you go up to your room.

I'm sure I'll stay here again, the rates were reasonable ($175ish an night), about the same as everything else in the area and with this I got to enjoy a suite. Like I said, all in all this hotel is A-OK.

Good sports bar with a number of beers on tap (plus pitchers at great prices), special cocktails for happy hour (M-F 3-6), and they will sub a veggie burger patty on any of their burgers. Service was pleasant and attentive, drinks were good and the food was decent. 

Besides the veggie burgers, there's not much more a vegetarian can eat other than a spendy mac and cheese plate with the caloric content to sustain a small nation for a week! It did look yummy but I'm certain it could do some serious damage to your waistline. 

They have a nice patio that's partially covered along with a large parking lot around the side and back of the building. Plenty of TVs to watch the sports game of your choice. They were playing some of my fav eighties music when we were there.

I remeber when I was growing up in Concord, there existed the eternal battle between Sorrento's and New London. IMO Sorrento's wins the pizza war, I prefer thin crust and they have a larger variety of specility pizzas here. The one thing you have to be wary of is that they tend to undercook the pizzas during their busy hours, but I like my crust on the crispier side. Also, the staff tends to be aloof or rude when the place is busy. If you are, however, in the mood for a sub I would suggest hoofing it across the street to New London, where they make delicious steak bombs and classic italians. 
Perhaps this is why the battle between the two venues rages on....

Only because I've been to the Winter Park location a number of times, will I give this a shot again. We just left a late Easter lunch at the Lake Nona location. (We had reservations no less)The restaurant was all but empty, other than a private  party of about 40. Our server greeted us by apologizing for slight delays, if any, that might be caused by that party. The delays were extensive. 

Needless to say, we clearly took a distant second seat to the party that he paid attention to. In the course of our meal we basically felt rushed to make our orders, as he kept looking back to where the other party was seated.  Additionally, once we ordered our drinks, appetizers and entrées we never saw our server after each arrived at the table. So if other things were missing, we needed refills or utensils we had to flag down other staff to assist us after a lengthy delays. They were accommodating, but we shouldn't have had to chase people down for help. We even had to flag down a manager in order to get us to get the check so we could finally get out of there. I certainly hope his VIPs took great care of him. That was very bad planning on the part of management and horrendous service by our designated server. Having worked as a server to put myself through college and law school, I would never leave no tip. However, I believe the gratuity fairly reconciled with the level of service provided. Worse yet, when I told the manager, he acted incredulous.  

By the way, the food was delicious. I'll try again and repost, if necessary.

Solid XLB and other home made dumplings. The XLB juices spilled into my mouth, as it should. The XLB stuffing was on point, but the skin is a little thicker and size bigger than I'd like. I believe they also make their own noodles for their noodle soups. Beef noodle soup - would prefer the soup to be more flavorful; the beef wasn't braised the way I usually like for TW beef noodle soup. Noodles were good though. Service was a little slow.

I am a sushi snob, so, put my review in the context of knowing that... Solid sushi but not top tier. Was also surprised at the lack of fresh wasabi when requested. Very loud place too. If you live and breath Sushi, visiting Miku is not a must. If you are dying for sushi without a need for a mind blowing experience, they will suffice. Given the incredible access to fresh pacific seafood and a massive Japanese presence in Vancouver, I would have expected better.

Everything about the Biergarten is ok. 

If you're looking for a quiet (quiet-ish) place, this is probably not the place for you. However, it is some great people watching (rich, hippie-esque sorority girls sprinkled with some actual hippies.. a great juxtaposition!). However, the beer is aplenty and one is able to get cozy with strangers when sitting on the long, wooden community tables. The next time I venture to Biergarten, I shall have to try some of their food... the schnitzels are calling mah name.

It looks like a lot of people have a lot of negative things to say about this Pizza Hut in Revere, but we stopped in here yesterday and had an average experience.

We ordered over the phone and they gave us a fifteen minute wait time. When we showed up fifteen minutes later, the pizza was done. The pizza was your typical Pizza Hut quality and the service was decent.

In the end, no real complaints here and we would totally grab pizza here again.

2.5 stars 
The FOOD isn't bad, it's just nothing special. 
DECOR? Nothing special. Did like the ceiling rafters and lighting. 
Service? Typical. Although, it wasn't busy. 
The place is pretty big. So are the menu and the portion sizes. I guess thats why it has 4.5 stars. 
It's more QUANTITY than QUALITY. I can't say the food was bad, I just can't say it was good, or that I would ever come back. I came with a party of 7. Not one person really cared for the food enough. 
to say it was anything but OK. 
Same for the drinks. Big drinks, just OK. 
I didn't have high expectations given the location, so I wasn't really disappointed. 
The prices... It's not cheap. Considering the quality level of the food, I'd expect each entree to be $2-3 less. 

FYI, I had the fish tacos. There were 3 and they were a good size, but a lot of sauce and nothing special at all. 

I suggest if you are in the area and want better Mexican, try Agave Azul

I've stayed at a number of Disney resorts and so far this has been my least favorite. Of course, this all comes down to personal preference but let me go over what I liked and what I didn't like about Old Key West.

Not a fan of...
...The size. This DVC resort is so big, it has mutiple bus stops, a lot of people which makes for very crowded buses. This also meant you could be very far from the main building which would mean being a bus ride away. We were in one of the closest buildings but we still had a bit of an outdoor walk to the main building. You need to allow extra time for the buses and prepare for them to be crowded.
...The design. I personally don't like staying at a villa and feeling like I'm staying at a value or moderate resort. Inconvenient elevators meant taking stairs most of the time. This wasn't great for my 65 year old mother and it was just tiring after a long day in the parks. I don't like having no indoor hallways or central entrance area for the building. This is all stuff I realized after staying here...I had to try the original DVC! :)
...Our studio villa had no couch!

A fan of...
...The staff! They were the usual great Disney cast members.
...We had a great view facing the water. I loved the little balconies.
...The Key West decor in the rooms and throughout the resort. Fun!
...I love sitting outside the restaurants and shops by the water and just relaxing. The feel of the main area of this resort is so nice and calm.

I didn't get a chance to try Olivia's and have heard great things so that's on my list to try still! For me personally, I prefer other DVC resorts to Old Key West and won't be staying here again.

Every time I walk past Uncle Willy's, it seems as if it is never open nor does it have any customers. One day, I decided to try it out with my brother at lunch and when I walked in, I was pleasantly surprised at the amount of customers they have during a weekday lunch, albeit mostly seniors, a good sign since it probably means the turnover rate of the food is probably quite frequent. Price for the lunch buffet is not too bad at $9.99/ adult and $9.29 for seniors. The food, especially the fried chicken and fish was more than decent considering this is a buffet. One negative point is that there wasn't any sweet and sour pork nor the taco station as one fellow yelper had mentioned in their previous review. I guess he went on a weekend when it had more variety due to more customers.  It was nice to know the service was friendly and they allow people to see what they are offering on their buffet table before letting them decide if they want to dine here or not.

This restaurant has Asian flare and lots of different options in the menu. 
We drove there by Uber from Americasmart and it took us less than five minutes. 
The area is up and coming... Perhaps a bit scary at night. 
The place is small and there are no waiters it's kind of a hole in the wall but food is very tasty.
They are not particularly nice or mean, just regular service. There was no line and food took about 5-10 minutes to be ready. 
We had chicken wings with BBQ sauce, they were very good. Then we had pho but the beef tasted like deli roast beef. It probably was. I wasn't impressed. 
Overall is good for the price but I wouldn't go there again.

I had a great time with the actual outing.  The instructor was awesome.  I'd have given them 5 stars except that there were problems after the fact.  My package was supposed to include a t-shirt and some pictures.  They forgot to give me the shirt or email the pictures.  They said they'd mail me the shirt but the instructor was away so they couldn't help with the pictures.  The shirt never arrived and they stopped responding to attempts to resolve the issue.  I've shared my experience, both the good and bad parts with friends but thought it was time to put this out there for people who are deciding if they want to do this.  It's a great experience.  Just be sure to get everything up front.

Ohhhh salt and straw, can't seem to get away from people raving about this place left and right. I've been myself several times and I'm not a huge fan. I think it's good, the flavors seem like someone tried waaaay too hard to think of the most obscure combinations possible to make the place seem "cool" when in reality most are just straight up gross. The line is usually about 45min- and hour wait no matter when you go. To me, I'd way rather spend my money at VooDoo doughnuts or somewhere equally as "famous", because frankly they're way better. Overall: the flavors are too wild, the line is too long, and it's frankly not worth it.

I ate lunch at Saba this week and it was my first visit.  The thing that actually inspired me to write a review wasn't the perfectly acceptable food but, rather, the practice of collecting a tip right at the register upon ordering.  I found the tip screen that popped up on the credit card terminal strange and rather off putting not least because I had to decide what to tip for service that I hadn't yet received while being watched by the cashier inches away from me at a restaurant that, with its counter ordering and self service beverage station, is clearly not full service.  Nevertheless, because the cashier could see exactly what percentage I chose, and I felt my food order might be at risk if I didn't opt for 20%, I opted for 20%.  This kind of implicit pressure to give a full service tip at a partial service (your food is brought to the table and the plates are cleared for you) restaurant is a practice that deserves a quick end.

Let me start by saying we love Cracker Barrel, or should I say the Cracker Barrels not around Orlando?

This particular one seemed under staffed. It wasn't that busy but we had to wait to be seated (that has never happened before at a CB, as they use greeter seaters.)

Our waitress was really nice and good, but she had too many tables. How do I know this? One of her colleagues started yelling at her 3 tables  away; drifting in and out of Spanglish about how one of the tables behind us was his.

The fellow tourists got to us as well; behind us was the family that gathered hands, stood up and started saying grace allowed as if no one else was there.  To our right and left were children running wild and screaming, parents couldn't care less.

The food was great, it always is at CB, hence the 3 instead of 1 star rating.

If you are looking for some amazing drinks and good food this is the place to check out.  My friend and I decided to check out the Agave Grill on a Saturday before a movie.  It was during happy hour and while drinks aren't half price, it's nice that they were a few bucks off.

I can tell you that the Agave Cosmo and the Margaritas were amazing!  They certainly don't skimp on the alcohol.  Since we decided to have a few drinks we thought a little food was necessary.  Some of their appitizers are also discounted for happy hour so we each got a quesadilla, I got chicken and she got shrmp.  Both were just ok.  Not bad...not great.  Good food that was certainly overpowered by the great drinks.

The wait staff was busy since the place was full but were more than happy to help each other out when we needed things and our waitress wasn't close by.

With all my hours spent watching the Cooking Channel, Travel Channel and The Food Network, the Lobster Roll is a sandwich that has always looked fantastic when described on any one of these shows.  With that marvelous site of abundant lobster meat busting out of a NE style hot dog bun, I've been craving the sandwich for a while.  Since I'm no where near the state of Maine, where the Lobster Roll originates, I began my pursuit to find the closest thing to the real deal here in Orlando.

It came down to CityFish, Winter Park Fish Co. and Boston's Fish House.  The reviews I read for the Lobster Roll at CityFish didn't look encouraging at all.  The Lobster Roll reviews I've come across for Winter Park Fish Co. were bi-polar.  Boston's Fish House looked the most promising since they actually have their Lobster's flown in weekly from Maine, have appetizing pictures of the roll on Yelp and from what I've seen, all great reviews.  So Boston's it was.

We arrived with a party of 8 and perused the menu, paid first and then were seated.  

Everyone got their own meals but we decided to get their Boston's Seafood Combo Platter.  Codfish, Sea Scallop, Shrimp, Onion Rings and Oyster all fried.  This was a mistake, as I preferred the platter broiled.  But I didn't have a choice in the matter.  Majority rule.  When the heaping pile of fried seafood hit our table, we all dug in.  To me, I couldn't differentiate flavors between the 4 different pieces of seafood on the platter because they were all fried.  They all tasted like fish fry.  I could have gone to Captain D's or Long John Silvers for this!

From this point forward, I'm convinced that it is a SIN to fry seafood.  Breading seafood, then deep frying it in oil zaps all the natural flavor and essence.  

Mahi Tacos, Mahi Sandwich, Salmon, Fish and Chips, Lobster Bisque and fried Catfish were also ordered in addition to my Lobster Roll.  Both the Mahi dishes were delicious with flavor since the Mahi was broiled.  The Salmon was also delicious.  The Fish and Chips, and Catfish were fried, so there's nothing to report there.  Again, think Captain D's.  The Lobster Bisque was a disappointment.  Although it had a couple of nice chunks of what looked like leg or claw meat, the soup overall was underwhelming.  We've certainly had better.   We should have gone with their Clam Chowder.  I've read and have been told it's a legitimate NE Clam Chowder in texture, ingredients and flavor.

Now the Lobster Roll!  Right away I can say I'm a fan of the sandwich.  I really wish I had 2 of them that night.  There was an abundance of Lobster that looked like it included tail, claw and leg meat.  It wasn't heavily mayonnaised, but just enough to hold all the meat chunks together on the NE style, butter toasted roll.  At the bottom of the roll and under the Lobster meat was a bed of fresh shredded lettuce.  Lobstery. creamy, crispy, buttery, toasty, fantastic.  

With that said, I do think it could have been approved upon in 3 different ways.  

1:  I expected the roll to be slightly bigger.  But for the price of $12.95, compared to the norm of $20.00 to $25.00 for a roll, the size met the price.  I wish there was an option to get 2 rolls or 1 big roll for $20.00.
2:  Instead of using lettuce, they could use bits of celery.  This way the sandwich gets more crunch and added texture.
3:  The top of the lobster meat could have been dusted with cayenne or paprika just to add a little zip and offset the tang of the mayo.

But again, as is, I personally enjoyed the Lobster Roll very much.

Overall, the experience was pleasant.  I'm rating my experience a 3 out of 5.  I badly want to give Boston's Fish House a 4 out of 5 but there are a couple of reasons for the 3 star rating.  The fried seafood ordered all around me tasted the SAME.  I realized I shouldn't take points off because everyone around me so happened to get fish fry, but at least add some FLAVOR to the fry.  Seasoning, a different batter.. something.  The Lobster Bisque was disappointing and even though the Mahi dishes and Salmon were tasty, they were nothing out of the ordinary. Lastly, most of the entrees and sandwiches come with 2 sides.  Unfortunately, none of the 14 different side options are healthy.  We thought getting a side of broccoli and green beans would be a nice alternative to french fries, or onion rings.  Wrong.  Their sides of veggies are mixed in with mayonnaise and candied bacon! So needless to say, it's difficult to be a discerning eater here.  

With all that said, I'd come back for the Lobster Roll and attentive service.  Not much else stood out enough that I couldn't get at CityFish or any other seafood faring restaurant closer to me.

With Namaskar sadly gone (although I have cautious hopes for the new spot opening in its place), I've been on the prowl lately for an at least solidly good Indian spot in the Medford-Somerville area. Guru certainly helps fill the void, but not so much for going out, so when my Indian food craving hit the other week, we were off to Masala for dinner. 

Overall the meal was, as Yelp puts it, "a-ok." The setting is typical and the service quite good--our waitress was friendly and quietly competent. The restaurant was rather quiet, but then again, this was around 8pm on a Monday, so that's not really surprising. If the windows are open, I would recommend asking to sit a bit away from them. It's certainly nice to get the breeze from outdoors, but the seats in the window feel a bit too close to the sidewalk. 

Unlike many Indian restaurants I've been to, Masala actually has a full bar, and they had a number of impressive deals to go along with it ($5 mojitos, anyone?). That being said, I have a hard time skipping my mango lassi, and Masala's rendition did not disappoint. It was a little less sweet and more tangy that others I've had--very tasty.

Masala offers two menus: a larger Indian one and a smaller Nepalese section. I was intrigued by some of the Nepalese options (not a cuisine I've had much), but I came in there with an Indian food craving and that was what I was ordering. The Indian side of the menu is fairly standard with the classics you'd expect.

After some nicely made pappadam we started out by splitting an order of the lamb samosas. They were my favorite thing on the night. Too hot to eat when they arrived, I couldn't help but try to eat them anyway thanks to their crispy exterior and well-spiced filling. Our entrees consisted of chicken vindaloo and malai kofta, with a side of aloo paratha. The vindaloo was okay, but certainly not the best I've ever eaten. The chicken pieces were a little bit strangely cut: the texture on them wasn't great, although the amount of chicken included in the sauce was generous. I also thought the dish could have definitely been spicier--I wouldn't be afraid to ask them to kick up the spice level a bit if you like your food hot. I also wasn't in love with the veggie dumpling part of the malai kofta. The texture wasn't great, and they were a bit dry inside. That being said, I greatly enjoyed the dish's sauce and would consider ordering them again just for it. The aloo paratha was solidly good--the bread had a nice texture.

Overall, Masala was no stand out, but certainly a decent choice with some definite highlights (lassi, bread, samosa, one of the sauces). I wouldn't recommend going out of your way to eat here, but if you're in the area, it's definitely a nice option to consider.

I'm not a huge fan of Boston Pizza but I think there is a time and place for it. This place is good if you have kids, Sundays are pretty cheap for them from what I've heard but it's not the reason I go.

For me it's a decent place to grab some pizza and beer and watch some sports or sit out on their lacklustre patio. I like going here instead of other sports bars as it's usually a little quieter and the food is better than most pub food.

Don't come here looking for some fantastic dining experience but if your expectations are set accordingly you shouldn't be disappointed.

The waitress we had was awesome, I wish I remembered her name.  The appetizers (Brie Fondue) and sides (Truffle Fries) were really good.  The ambiance and atmosphere were nice and they had a decent beer selection.

The burger I got was 17$ and not worth it at all.  It tasted like a frozen patty that had been overcooked.  It was really nothing special at all and I was a bit disappointed.

I'd go back for drinks and an app, but dinning there kind of dampened the experience.

Ordered curbside pick-up tonight. First time ordering from Ovation and I'm at the "Meh" stage. Nothing about my order was over the moon. 
The buffalo dip is good. Chips--meh. I'm going to swap those out for some I have at home. 
Chicken parm was over cooked. I'm not saying by a little bit either. Like it was well over cooked. Hockey puck over cooked. Tough and super dry. 
The brisket? Okay. Again, a little dry but it's brisket. It's hit or miss with that meat. I don't understand why it was shredded, but maybe it's the way they serve it here. 
Fries were mushy but it's because they were in a clamshell and I had to drive home. That's on me. 
Will I try this place again? Sure. I'll come in and sit down and eat. Not going to get the food to go though. 




However....

I'm not going to leave out the fact there was a hair in the brisket but that's what happens in food service. It happens. No one died though and no one ate it.

For Portland, the taste was good.

For places where ramen is a thing, taste was okay.

My biggest beef (I should say pork) was the portion size and the add-ons.

The ball of noodles were too small (and many of the individual noodles were surprisingly short, like they weren't cut right). Also, for $8 you you just get the basics. No meat, no egg, hardly anything. But, of course you can buy all that. To get what I would consider "ramen" you end up shelling out $10-$12 for a very small portion. When it comes to ramen, $12 should let you eat like a king.

Then again, in Portland people aren't going to know any better. It does taste fine, better than a lot of the ramen in the Portland area, though. So, if you have a skinny stomach and a fat wallet, be my guest.

was killing some time and wanted to buy some stamps to mail Christmas cards. Hey, this might be the ticket v. waiting in line at the U.S. Post Office.   After entering I browse to see if they had boxed cards - not overly worried, just curious to look.  There was one other customer and I got in line behind her.  I felt like I was in a small town, general store.  The customer was shipping packages, but the staff of two were re-packing one item for her.  It was kind of a cluster - with me witnessing this transaction.  At one point, the customer suggested they help me before they completed her transaction.  That was a great gesture and I would have gladly stepped in to buy my stamps with cash and leave.  But no, the clerk said "Oh no. This won't take long.........." It was long and the line behind me was growing.  I later was helped by another clerk and got my Santa stamps.  The original customer was still in there - Kind of poor behavior to show up, have the staff re-pack your item, and then later, fish for the mail address on your phone, while then later complaining about the price to ship items.  Ugh!  This isn't a negotiable process.  
1. Good manners for her though
2. Liked the hometown feel of the clerks and accommodating behavior to someone kind of needy.

In a strip mall, lots of parking.  Clean store, some cards, office supplies, a few trinkets, masks, wrapping/packing goods.

The neat thing about having a Madewell in town is that the pricing in-store for sale items is often much lower than online, even with free shipping. I've managed to get a dress more than half off the original price (online, it's still original price). (Although this might backfire for them -- now that I know this, my consumption of online purchases is going to decrease.) Compared to J. Crew Copley, the sale section is less appealing, but is often less picked through -- as a reviewer stated below, hit or miss. 

In general, Madewell folks are generally very good about welcoming you throughout the store, and are willing to take time to offer guidance on what styles to buy. That said, my most recent experiences here have been...meh. I was shopping with a friend, and she ended up needing to try a range of sizes for a particular item. It took about ten minutes to get one of the sizes, and the delay was so long that we ended up getting them ourselves. This is especially not cool if one of you has a pretty bad limp at the time. Second, I was told that the return period for the stuff I purchased last time was shorter than what it said on the website -- would be good to be more consistent on this information.

2 words:  not. memorable.

I came here on a Saturday night with a group of friends, with the intention of snacking / sharing food and getting drinks.  I got the "Day of the Dead" cocktail, which was tequila / lime based and was served with an inverted bottle of corona.  The drink was so cute and "insta-worthy" I must say, and the beer really helped mellow out the sweetness.  

Even though I really enjoyed the drinks here, the food itself was the part that was pretty forgettable.  We had the chicken karaage, fried shiitake mushrooms, beef tataki, a few rolls, ebi mayo, and creamy miso yaki udon.  The udon noodles did not taste like miso at all, and kind of reminded me of a tasteless cream sauce that you can get from a jar in the drug store.  

Don't get me wrong I love the modern esthetic / hip vibe of the place and its a cool place to grab drinks with friends if you plan to be on Davie street (you should make a reservation).  But if you're here with the intention of having more than a light bite, you might be disappointed.  There are plenty other Asian spots with more superior flavours!

Honestly, the food is average at best. I usually get an omelette and it's always perfectly fine, just a little over-cooked and nothing special. My friends usually go a different route. One really likes the waffle sandwiches, though she complained the last time we were there that they seemed to be smaller than they previously were, and another friend usually orders something sweet and is very pleased. It's really not the place to go if you're health conscious, so I guess I set myself up for that. I will say, though, that I have a lot of trouble resisting the sugar-coated biscuits and liquid chocolate they serve with breakfast dishes! Me-oh-my-oh! 

Come for the hot chocolate (dark is my favorite) in the adorable hug mugs. Stay for dessert. But don't bother with the savory stuff.

Also, service is always super friendly, but the food takes forever!

I enjoyed my experience here.
I came here on a Saturday night with my family. We sort of missed the evening rush since we got there around 9:00pm. So we only had to wait about 15 minutes before we were sat. They do take reservations so I would say get a reservation if you plan on coming during peak hours.

The food was filling. They are a scratch kitchen so it was nice to know that they made everything in house. Made me appreciate the bread even more knowing it was homemade.

I honestly forgot the name of what I ordered... but in layman's terms I had chicken with mushrooms drizzled on top and a side of sweet potato fries. Overall it tasted how it sounds. Great quality, clean and simple. I wasn't looking for anything too fancy so this did the trick. 

I would recommend this place to older families and maybe for a chill date spot since it had a very casual vibe.

El Arbol has good food.  That part is clear.  It's not interesting, or particularly inventive, but it's really good.  I particularly enjoyed my steak and the ceviche we started the meal with.  No one at our 4-top was disappointed with his or her meal.

The wine list and the sides and starters are all quality too.

Our server was attentive and knew his way around the menu.  He was a little stretched to begin with, but once some tables emptied and he focused more on us, he did a great job.

The space is incredibly huge for an outdoor spot.  They've got 3 levels of patios.  On a big Saturday night, they were maybe 1/3 full.  And I think that's what was disappointing about this meal.  There was no scene, no real vibe, and it didn't feel like as special a Saturday night meal is it should have for the cost.

I do quite like Kura but there are some drawbacks that I feel are worth discussing. First off, it is quite fun to come here as there haven't been many conveyer belt sushi places in Atlanta historically and most people around here haven't experienced it before. The salmon dishes are quite delicious and for me the highlight of the experience. On to the negative. Service is lacking which I think is unexpected given that the wait staff are not taking orders aside from drinks and are not serving dishes. Tea, when ordered in the past, has been just barely warm. You have to ask for wasabi and soy sauce, and what I especially don't like about the wasabi is that it is served to you in a communal container. As in, they don't swap the spoon, or the container, or the wasabi inside, or anything. This is different than a ketchup bottle- you don't have to personally reach inside the bottle to get the ketchup out, but you do with the wasabi. This is unsanitary to me. I get that it's traditional, but you're at the mercy of all of the customers before you who ever touched the wasabi when it comes to getting sick or not.  Speaking of unsanitary, Kura has received very poor food inspection scores in the past. Anyway, the line is also very long at times, but this is also the best time to come and eat because that is when the conveyer belt is stocked most. I have been during slower hours, and the conveyer belt was practically empty. There is also a very large portion of the menu that you must order off the iPad if you want to experience it, including some sushi selections. I get that the conveyer belt can only hold so many options, but it takes away from the convenient concept if you have to place an order and then wait for it to be delivered on the second belt. Finally, there are some foods that could use better quality control. For instance, on multiple occasions I've ordered takoyaki that were frozen in the middle. I get that it's unrealistic to expect fresh takoyaki to be made from scratch, but serving still-frozen food to customers is not acceptable. Also, a warning to those who are picky when it comes to sushi- Kura has a limited selection of rolls and mostly serves raw nigiri style sushi. I'm totally cool with it but others who like mostly cooked rolls will not be totally satisfied. Anyway, I'd recommend the salmon dishes and the crunchy rice dish from the iPad, it's good.

Three stars... I'd give 5 for the bartenders, but the rest is a 3.  Maybe a 3.5.

It's "A-ok."

I go for the burgers, but always end up getting an app first too.  The apps have been good, and I totally love the hummus.  Its a great sized portion with an awesome tomato pesto and pine nuts on top.  Bomb.  The bread is a crispy (fried) little bunch of wedges.  They hold up well.  Love it.

As I said, I always get a burger and I'm trying to work my way through the custom ones that they offer.  I just recently finished my last one off the list.  To be fair, the Tokyo is the best.  Wasabi on a burger?  Sprouts?  yeah, its pretty damn awesome.

Oh wait, the Paris is killer.  Truffle mayo?  The cheese selections?  yeah, get the Paris.

Hell, either is great.

Least favorite is the Mexico... its not really hot at all (to me at least, but I'm no weenie.)

The beer selection has a few nice rotating offerings as well, usually with at least one good hoppy choice.

Service at the bar, as i said, is great.  Friendly and inviting.

Why do I not give it a full 5 stars?  Well, the burgers are good, but thats mostly due to the great toppings.  The meat itself is kinda bland and dry.  I would never go for just a plain burger.  No way.

As far as the service goes, as i said, sit at the bar.  They have had some poor servers work there that have helped me in the past.  the bartenders should thank them, because this just encourages me to sit at the bar all the time.

Ever see the movie "waiting?"  You remember the really angry server girl from that film?  I think she works there.

Kudos to the bar and burger toppings (and hummus!).

IMPORTANT... My review is based only on sitting at the bar and having a beer.  This is not my kind if bar, not would I send my friends here.  So I can't give it a higher rating, based on my taste.
