It's very classy and is likely more known as a restaurant that has a bar.  Beautiful bar, my draft beer was $9.50.  hardly any TV's.  Just overall feels like a stuffy crowd.  Not for me.  Finishing my beer and head off to don't a better spot to hang out on vacation.

It's not my neighborhood, so I have to make a special trip there.  This was opening weekend, so I expected a few hiccups.  My first impressions are that the place is small, and prices are high-ish.  Was also surprised by the number of products that come in packaging, and not all packaging is environmentally friendly.  Thought I remembered that you would fill your own containers with milk?  Not yet.  Milk is sold in cartons, both cardboard and plastic. 

Aisles were narrow, I didn't really want to enter when there was even one other shopper there, as passing them could be a pain. I noticed others hesitating to enter aisles with shoppers, also.  

This is opening, so not all the stock has arrived yet.  There are empty bulk containers with names of products yet-to-come, others with signage inviting customers to suggest an appropriate product to go there.

Bottom line:  I made a bit of a trip, only found 1 item I needed, and it was in a plastic container.  Why did I bother measuring the tare weight of my mason jars?   Will only return IF I happen to be in the neighborhood, AND I have my containers with me.   Lightning may strike me twice before those both happen.

3.5 stars!

Jon-- 

I don't want to brag, but I grew up in LA and I've been eating at Chinese seafood restaurants since I was old enough to walk. Needless to say, I have some high expectations. Boston's gem falls short on some, but excels in others.

Wife and I had the ginger scallion lobster, fried taro nest with shrimp and scallops, and some sauteed pea stems. The pea stems were pretty good- a bit garlicky, but a good refreshing counterpoint to the other two dishes.

The fried taro nest was pretty nice, but we could barely taste the XO sauce. C'mon! I've had seafood baskets before, but never one made of taro. These guys could have scored a touchdown with this one, but the lack of the advertised XO sauce punch was like getting tackled on the 4th down at the one yard line.  

Ginger scallion lobster: take it away, wife!

Jenny--

So I was a little disappointed when we didn't get to pick our lobster (so we dropped them half a star), as our good friend had advertised. Perhaps we should have spoken up. The lobster meat was very sweet though. I thought the flavor was a little bland, but after a couple more tastes I was thinking that the chef probably doesn't want too overpower the natural sweetness of the fresh lobster. 

I didn't mind that I couldn't taste any XO sauce...I think the flavor of the nest contents (broccoli, mushroom, carrot, shrimp, squid, and other seafood) was pretty good. And the taro basket was so addictive! The husband and I devoured 3/4 of the hefty thing. Pea stems were good and we were given a huge mound of them.

The prices weren't too cheap or expensive, and I think the freshness of the lobster really trumps all the ginger scallion lobsters I've had in LA. 

Tip: Get the fried taro nest!

Came here for dinner with a friend. We ordered the chicken plate, a lamb and chicken souvlaki plate, a side order of fries, and a "what the fig?" cocktail, which came out to about $40 without tax. The food was decent, 3-4 out of 5. However, it became very clear that the food is not cooked fresh when the meals came out in about 4 minutes, and the chicken on the chicken plate was both overcooked to dryness and was cold. I asked if the chicken was supposed to be cold, and an employee said she would replace it with warm chicken, but when she returned she gave me a single souvlaki skewer, which was far less chicken than was on the chicken plate (approximately 50%). To their credit, the souvlaki was tender and warm (though mostly flavorless without the [meager amount of] tzatziki it comes with). The lemon potatoes were too sour for me but my friend enjoyed them. The Greek fries were tasty. The pita was surprisingly good. The atmosphere is casual and welcoming, the music downtempo and not too loud, and the service staff was very friendly. But the cold meal and the inadequate replacement dropped them a star.

We didn't try the chicken cause we are still from lunch-so just appetizers for a light dinner.
Because it is still too early in the season for Gulf Oysters, the oysters are from P.E.I. In Canada. We had some raw and some of the Lucha style wood fire grilled. They were ok-raw were better than cooked, but even the raw were not shucked very well, the tops on all of them were torn slightly.
We also had the daily special Jalapeño poppers w spicy cream cheese filling and avocado creama, I think that was the best thing we had, and the deep fried deviled eggs-we were really looking forward to these having read the menu the night before-the filling was made with the boiled egg yolks with some hot sauce added, I think it was Tabasco? this was not what we expected at all, nowhere on the menu or anywhere else did it mention that they were made w hot sauce? I don't see why they would do this Unless this is a Texas thing where "deviled" means devil like hot? They were kind of dry inside and just not very tasty, the hot sauce really took something away from the whole thing; for us any way.
Maybe I will come back for chicken since that is what they are known for, but this time we left disappointed

First, I'm from Lima where this all started.  I know the pizza and it's really good. We were excited to have it open in Easton. We went there Friday night. Arrived at 5:45 and was told it would be a 20 mins wait which was no problem. The wait area is nice and comfortable. It even has a wood burning fireplace. When it was our turn , we were taken around the entire restaurant only to be placed next to the bar at a high top with bar stools- uncomfortable. Strike 1. We were promptly met by the waiter to get our drink order to be told that we missed happy hour by 3 minutes, even though we were in the restaurant by 6 pm.  Strike 2

My friend had an Italian sandwich which is a standard sub. Not bad but nothing better than  average.  I had the Beer Barrel Bacon BBQ Burger. I attached a photo of how it was served.  First I was disappointed there was no cheddar cheese. The serve staff offered to take it back but I was hungry and declined the offer.  The menu states no cheese but it is a good opportunity to upsell for $1 more. The burger tasted a bit better than it looked. 

Overall, this place will compete with BJ Brewhouse. Tons of TV and atmosphere  However my money will go to BJs next time.

My brother was in town and he wanted to do some local beer tastings. 
Rogue is a pretty well known brewery so when it popped up on yelp he wanted to check it out. 
Sat at the table right by the bar. It took over ten minutes before anyone even noticed us. 
I ordered a flight with all their sours they had on tap plus one cider and he ordered a pint of one of the pumpkin beers. 
All very lack luster. I normally love sours, but I didn't enjoy any of them. They didn't have much flavor and to me, didn't even taste like a sour. 
It was a peach sour, Marionberry sour, lemon berliner weisse, and a fruit salad cider. 
My brother only drank half of his pumpkin beer because he said it was just alright. 
We kept waiting for someone to check on us and bring us the check but after 15 minutes I gave up and just went to the bar to track down a bartender so we could pay and leave. 
Overall, mediocre experience.

We usually go to the BWW in kissimmee but we wanted a different environment & atmosphere so we chose to go to the eye! 

We arrived and it was very empty, we ordered our usual drinks & we were very satisfied with how they came out. The bartenders were very friendly & made us feel welcomed. The food came out & my fiancés burger was not medium it was well done. Which a medium person would understand the difference. He still ate it though we didn't want to bother them. My wrap & fries were cold & the chicken in my wrap was kinda hard & chewy. 
I was a little upset cause I was looking forward to their Buffalo chicken wrap that I always order. 
I was very disappointed but I may give this location another shot some time in the future.

Re: snowshoeing @ Seymour

Great place to do some snowshoeing on the week-end.  Feel free to bring your dog as well.  People have let their dogs off-leash but there are park rangers that patrol the trails and you could be fined if they catch you!

Unfortunately, if you are just doing snowshoeing, you are only able to park on the hill and not in the parking lots.  Expect a 15-20 minute hike to the trails from your place on the hill.  The earlier you go the better as you get a closer parking spot.  After 10 am on the weekend you'll be hiking longer than that!

I got a very nice pair of boots here, but was disappointed with the service. The two women working here were pretty friendly when they spoke to me, but mostly spoke to each other. Since I went in on my own, I was hoping for an outside perspective, and they did not seem all that interested in giving one even when I asked. Nice selection, kind of pricey, not the best service from my experience. It could be that it was just an off day though. Who knows!

Not too shabby - Trudy's is definitely worth another look. I've been there before and the food was not good and not bad, just not memorable. 

First things first, I had the house margarita (frozen) and it was excellent - did not taste like the standard lots-of-sugar-to-cover-up-the-lack-of-flavor mix margarita. I'm no connoisseur, but it seems to be made with good stuff (for a house margarita). I'd say that it was on the same level as Baby Acapulco's.

For my meal, I had the Fajitas and Migas - which weren't too bad. The eggs were a little bit underdone for my taste - almost a creamy texture, but still tasty. The fajitas were not very impressive, just standard fajitas, but they were covered up by a huge pile of onion pieces and one or two slices of green pepper.

Overall, I would be more than happy to go back to Trudy's and keep trying stuff from their menu.

Came here for a little NYE dinner, had an 8:30 reservation through open table and was seated promptly. They placed us in far back end table for two on the bar side against the wall, quaint little spot but not that great considering it was the closest table to the restrooms, lots of foot traffic. 

Started off with the 4 course pre fixe menu, ordered the venison tartar -  roasted suckling pig -  grilled ribeye, and a desert that apparently i do not remember, that explains that besides the picture.

Waitress was emotionless, seriously.. I didn't know if she was happy or about to meltdown crying... No freaking idea... Everything was said with a straight face, no opinions or recommendations of the food when asked. This whole waitress issue ruined the experience overall... I felt like we were causing her physical and or emotional pain by just being there... I was scared.

The venison tartar was great, balanced texture with a truly raw taste going on, much enjoyed! Quail egg I believe, on top completed the dish. The roasted suckling pig, boy oh boy did you guys trick me! Even the guy next to me asked what my dish was because he had the same dish and didn't know if it's what he ordered (we both let out a good chuckle) This dish with undercooked pasta (yes, undercooked) I don't need no lesson on properly cooking a pasta dish...  was so disappointing, and the "pig" part, well good luck trying to find the quarter sized single piece under all the glorified cafeteria children's pasta, accompanied by a 1 inch streak of some type of BBQ sauce in the corner of the plate. The grilled ribeye, you were cooked amazingly rare, just how I ordered it. Sliced well, displayed well, you were delicious, and the best part of the meal. You saved my soul after experiencing the prior dish. The Desert was desert, some type of rice pudding banana treat I believe, nothing to remember. 

If the service was different and the pig dish didn't exist or I ordered a different 2nd course, but seriously... you read - roasted suckling pig - what the hell else would you order!?!  This is my second time here and wanted to give it the 2 time chance review but it let me down. It's a well deserving 3.5 if that helps. Hopefully if you check this spot out, you will get a waitress/waiter with life in their blood! Again, I was scared.

Located in a beautiful modern Marriott. Decor and atmosphere was lovely, the waitress was quite attentive. Food was decent. We had the century nuke cocktail which was a delicious blend of citrus juice that had the right mount of tartness to it. We shared appies and had our own entrees.  First off was the mushroom ravioli with crab and asparagus spears in a cream sauce- tasty but a tad cooler than I prefer. The hand cut fries had a good thickness to it, wasn't too hot to handle and had a lovely white truffle aioli sauce but we could have used a bit more.  Then came the entrees.  The west coast poke bowl was disappointing as the salmon and tuna pieces were slathered in a red spicy sauce, which didn't seem like the pineapple salsa to me. The menu also didn't say it was spicy.  The honey hot thin crust pizza was good- spicy capiocolla ham and jalapeño  peppers. The Mac and cheese was decent- had the right amount of cheese to it, and wasn't that rich, which is a good thing. 

Overall, I would still return for the cocktails, ambience and I would try other things on the menu. The hotel also would be a nice place to stay.

I'll preface this by saying that I was devastated when Privus closed - best drinks in the Boston area, in my opinion. So, when I heard that Bon Chon was opening with practically the same food menu, I was psyched to give it a try!

I got the spicy wings/drumsticks combo, and it was definitely yummy - my first impression was that it wasn't QUITE as good as Privus's, but I think that was because my time at Privus was my first experience with Korean fried chicken, and I was just super-impressed that there was this amazing food that existed that I had somehow never encountered before! I thought the spicy was just the right amount of spice - definitely had me going through more than a few glasses of water! I'd like to try the soy-garlic next time for comparison.

I was sad that the cool, loungey environment of Privus didn't quite carry over, and neither did the totally amazing, fresh fruit-infused drink menu, but at least I'll have a place to go if I have a craving for some seriously tasty fried chicken.

Note: Not a ton in the way of vegetarian options, so probably wouldn't suggest this for someone looking for a variety of meat-free options.

You may as well call this the internet dad joke cruise.  Really, I think it probably makes a big difference who is hosting the cruise, because the joke delivery is probably what is suppose to make the jokes funny.  As it was, I could barley hear our host, and what I could hear was truly lackluster.  There were a few reasonably good jokes.  "You've been an outstanding audience, now I need you to be out standing on that dock," and "If you've enjoyed this cruise, my name is _____, and this has been the Jungle cruise.  If you haven't, my name is Matthew and this has been the Hall of Presidents."  Generally, though, I don't think I'd get on this one again in a park so full of fun things to do.

I found this place walking around Harvard Common about 7 years ago. I liked the outdoor atmosphere & it had decent reviews. I celebrated an anniversary here. The hostess was curt when we requested a certain table. The service was a bit hostile. It reminded us of New York at the time. We ignored the high prices because the food was so good. 

Subsequent visits proved to be as tough as the first one. An empty dining area never guaranteed good service. 

I went there today. Stood at the hostess stand for a while. I tried to make myself known but was blown off. Once the hostess came she didn't come to me, she motioned for me to come inside. My companion was starting to become agitated because we had only 45 minutes. It was awkward for no real reason. 

The Red House has recently started offering a dozen oysters for $6. The best deal in town, as far as I know. They bring it to you on a plate w/o ice. The oysters are not cleaned. The cocktail sauce comes with plenty of horseradish considering there is only a half ounce. I used my water glass to clean off the sludge. The oysters are plump & tasty but the grit & lack of condiment is disappointing. The fact that the .50 oyster only applies to the first dozen, if you get 2 dozen you pay $1 an oyster ad nauseum. That doesn't sit well with me. 

They have recently installed an outside bar with draft beer. I was pleased that they had local brews. But when I asked for a recommendation our server asked if I liked IPAs. I said no. He said; you won't like them then. Why would a bar stock only one type of beer on draft? Well, one was a Porter but is that really a choice? Makes no sense to me. 

It's a great location. Smack dab in Harvard Square & on bus & T lines. A decent place to go if the beer garden at Charlie's Kitchen is full but I have a sneaking suspicion that that's not what the owners of Red House are looking for. 

I dunno, a place that can charge $33 for a Chicken Lobster gives you a wooden fork with your oysters, I don't care how frugal they are, isn't thinking big picture. 

There are better places.

At first, my friends and I were a bit leary of an eating establishment that encouraged tossing peanut shells on the floor.  We've now gotten used to the crunch under our shoes as we navigate to our tables.  I have ordered one thing off the menu here and that is the steak tips, with gravy, onions and mushrooms on mashed potatoes with a caesar salad.  Its my favorite and the only reason I come here.  TR has a full bar and pretty decent mixed drinks.  My husband really likes it when the staff head out to do a line dance (he usually joins them...).  My nephew is terrified of the Armadilla mascot that tours around to see the kids.  The waiters are always energetic and accomadating.

Typical Olive Garden, nothing really extraordinary about this location outside of being close to the Battery. 

The food has always been good here for me. I usually stick to lasagna or the tour of Italy. I wish the size of the ToI was like it was when it was first introduced.

My experience with the service here has definitely been better the times I set at the bar than when I was set at a table. This most recent time, we only saw our waitress about 4 times: She took our order, brought us water, brought us a margarita, then bought us our check. No refills on water and used plates stayed on the table until we got the check. The restaurant wasn't busy enough to have that lackluster level of performance. The table kiosk wasn't even usable, so we had to wait to pay our tabs. 

Overall, I wouldn't let one or two bad experiences keep me from recommending an establishment. This really is a decent location with average Olive Garden food, so if you're a fan, you should definitely give it a shot.

ok, so i actually give this spa 3.5 stars... i really like the spa and the services... I enjoyed the full couples package that comes with a body scrub, back massage and a rejuvenation soak.  the service was good, i loved the atmosphere... nothing much to complain about that.  the soak especially was delightful...
my complaint is about how the spa is connected to the gym and the pool.  i really hated that.  it just... totally takes it away from that luxurious feeling... a spa facility should be meant only for the spa guests... i really really hated the fact anyone using the pool and the gym can go in and out as they please.  even worse, the steam room was on the pool/gym side so i didnt even bother going.  I mean, i like sitting in the steam room wearing nothing but a towel and i did not feel comfortable passing by the pool area wher ther are old men and kids. even the showes and the lockerroom are shared with pool/gym users... what were they thinking??? totally not luxurious at all. 
so in conclusion.. service/atmosphere good, structure, horrible.

Have been eating Chi'Lantro for 7 or 8 years now, it used to be the absolute king of my quick go-to list. Previously I've rated it 5/5 on other platforms. 

I hate to be negative because I have so much love for the place, but the food isn't what it used to be. Not sure what changed, but in the last 2-3 years the consistency has declined greatly. Haven't had a 5/5 meal here in a while unfortunately. 

My go to has always been a ribeye burrito and queso, and while the quesos pretty much the same it seems like I regularly am noticing a poor showing/serving from one or more of the ingredients inside my burrito. The weak ingredients that prompted this review were the tough/chewy rice and sparse beef. The rice didn't taste good and the toughness made the burrito a chewing match. Felt the beef was way lacking quantity wise, I've had this so many times I had certain expectations but I'll freely admit that complaint is more subjective and less of an issue than the rice. 

My thinking is that I just got a batch that had been sitting a while, but I ordered at 8:30PM rather than right before close. Hopefully tonight was a Covid related issue somehow and not a snowballing of previous concerns I had 

Will absolutely continue to give them chances and hope to change this review, but my confidence is shaken

Uninspiring...just ok....really wasn't impressed by the food or the atmosphere.  My 19 year old son and I went, and rather than put us on the quieter side they made us wait for a table on the family side which looked a bit like a war zone this Thursday night.

Huge bun, smaller patty...hard to appreciate the flavor of the beef as its masked with all the toppings.  Fries were ok.  We didn't bother exercising the unlimited option.

So we went...probably won't feel the need to come back (so many better options).

I ordered the Boston Lemon Sole. I asked the waitress which she preferred the Chilean Sea Bass or the Sole and the said the Bass was spicy. She didn't really dive to in deep in that and she was kind of a meh waitress. I said I would probably want my fish sautéed but she said the Sole
Is best broiled. So I went with broiled. It came out with their whipped mashed potatoes and veggies that were still hard. Their mashed potatoes were awesome. I wanted Brussels sprouts but she said no substitutions (I think you can only add it to your meal but I didn't need three sides). The fish seemed undercooked and I had a hard time getting it on my fork. My friend ordered their chicken dish with rice and it was awesome. He was unable to finish it so he gave me half his chicken. I wish I would've tried the Chilean Sea Bass or had my fish cooked differently. It was broiled but it seemed not enough. The pineapple-Tini was awesome though. So the service wasn't that great, my seafood wasn't that great, drinks were good, and chicken was good.

This review is for Sunday brunch.

My wife and I have been to brunch at the Daily Cafe three times now over the past few months, and I'm afraid we most likely won't be going back.

We really wanted to like this place since it looks exactly like the type of place we like for brunch: interesting menu that changes week to week, and just a little pretentious to show that they take their food seriously.

Unfortunately, though, we haven't truly liked anything we've eaten here. Each time, the food has been merely ok, and especially when it comes to the muffins and scones -- they've always been quite bland. 

Overall, I'd suggest that you definitely give the Daily Cafe a try since the food seems to be high quality. We just haven't really liked it enough to keep going back.

My friend and I are visiting from CA and wanted to experience the boba scene in Boston. While we enjoyed Gong Cha down the street, we wanted to try something different. We looked on Yelp and the positive ratings for Tea Do convinced us that this would be our second boba stop. We visited on a Monday evening and found ourselves surrounded by customers. The establishment is bigger than Gong Cha and offers a handful of seating areas but we still found it difficult to move around. We waited approximately 10-15 minutes for our orders (Tiramisu Milk Tea, Zen's Awakening). I wasn't impressed with the drinks. On the plus side, you get cute Tea Do stickers if you like them on IG.

Great look, okay food.

What did I get
The BOMA experience! I could say, there is a large stretch of items to choose from. Meats, sounds, veggies, salads AND DESSERT! The theme here is Africa themed, they have mostly regular items and seasoning and just added a kick to it. My best find was the Oxtail soup! It was the best item on the list! Loaded with all kinds of beans and it has a kick to it. It was great and the best. The desserts were small which I like so I don't have regrets taking one of each! You get to taste it all.

Jungle Juice - This was great! But very sweet. I understand it is true juice and so but it was on the very sweet side of things.

Environment
Inside the Animal Kingdom Lodge hotel. Nicely themed. a Very opened space, there is ample seating available. The queue lines are not long for the buffet and also it is always clean and there is always someone there to greet you if you have any questions.

Niceness of the staff
We had Jeff and he is a gentleman! He was nice to put up with my requests.

Dollar
It was 59.00 for the buffet this excluded tax

Yes?
It was definitely not worth it for the money honestly.

#WendyWanders #WendyAnd

I go to Max Brenner practically every Tuesday after a weekly appointment. I sit at the bar and the bartenders have always been excellent. Except last week. A new guy behind the bar. The manager was also taking orders. My pasta arrived with meat in it when there was supposed to be no meat in the dish! I returned my dish (to the manager) and the bartender who took my order asked why I returned it. When I told him, there was no apology. The bartender's pour of the wine was terribly stingy. I ordered some hot chocolate to go and 15 minutes after the order, I still didn't get my hot chocolate. 

On my way out, I spoke with the manager, he tried to be apologetic. But in a halfhearted manner.

Next time I see the manager or the new bartender at the bar, I am walking straight out of the door.

Average average average.  

I won't repeat the endless reviews of this place, so here are my thoughts. 

If you come to Portland and you like donuts it's worth going for the "experience".  If you are someone who loves going to different donut spots, you will find this place overpriced and overrated like I did.  

If you want to spend 8 bucks for donut that looks like a blunt or a penis then I guess have at it.  I tried the grape ( too sweet), maple bacon ( bacon was old, look up Friendly's in Orange as a way to make it), and a lemon donut ( I actually liked it). If I come back here I would try the basic donuts only. 

I come up to the Northwest 1-2x a year and will try a different place next time ( I'm hearing about Blue Star), for now I will stick to the Donuttery for my donut fix.   Thanks!!

61/2016

On 3/15/17 Saturday night around 9:20 I decide to go for some chicken sandwiches at this place. there was a manager 2 cashier in the front . Two employees at the window. But there was like 5 customer in the line including my self . Well my turn comes  .
Cashier say my I help you ? And then I order the  kids meal for My daughter .first time ordering that for my baby at this place so I ask the cashier is that all my choices for the kids meal ? She move her head and try to say yes that way. Wow that was a big different comparing to the SERVICE AT THE BEN-WHITE LOCATION  SAY TO MY SELF . Then cashier say back to me WHY ? 
Well I said because there. cashier are given a warm welcome to the guess . They ask for your name . 
They repeat the order to you . They even offer to refill your drink at the table or ask if is there something that you need they can bring to your table . 
Then  the cashier say to me well today we are short on people is why we are all like that.  But I notice the manager JOSE was not really attending guess needs in the front he was more on RUSH  trying to close some of the register at the from not sure why .  I WAS ASKING FOR MY ORDER # since I don't GET ANY AND HE WAS NOT HELP FULL.'then I ASK THE CASHIER AND SHE GIVE ME ONE PLASTIC CONE FOR MY ORDER  I guess JOSE maybe WAS trying to take off early but. That was the crazy situation on my second time experience at this location  . 
Our Food COMES Ok. Like any other same CHAIN restaurant 



PLEASE EXCUSE MY BAD TYPING

Enh. The parking lot is not my favorite experience ever. The store is large, but at least when I went, it didn't have much that was of any use to me. I may have just hit it on a bad day for the things I was looking for, but it was a disappointment. I've liked the VV over in Tigard, so I don't know if it's the different location, or just bad timing of what-they-had versus what-I-wanted...but given it's a bit of a drive for me, I probably won't be back often.

I received pretty poor service, long wait lines and grumpy staff. However, I really love their sushi  bento options during lunchtime. I would go again for that. They also need to update their website. On the website they have a kid menu, however when I arrived in person I was told they didn't have any kid options. There was no way I was paying 11-15 dollars plus for a kid who barely eats anything anyways. Luckily we happened to show up that time during happy hour and I found options they liked.

Love the Italian Plaza and all that goes with it with one exception... And it's a big exception which is why I'm docking Stars here. The pizza at the very end of the Pavilion... Which should be some of the best pizza ever was probably one of .if not the worst pizza slices I have ever had in my life!  Epcot should be ashamed with this pizza as they are supposed to be representing Italy and this pizza couldnt even represent Little Caesars!  Actually this pizza is so bad it's an insult to Little Caesars! That's how bad it is!   I totally like Little Caesars compared to this garbage that they sell you at a ridiculous price. This is probably one of the biggest letdowns of the whole park. Whoever is in charge of makinf that pizza there... Should do everyone a favor and go to a local place and just buy pizza to resell because the pizza they're making isn't fit for a dog.

I was really excited to try The Independent, after hearing great things from various sources. I'm not a beer fan, but I was impressed by their beer menu, and the descriptions even made me want to order one (almost).  But if you're interested, they'll even bring you a small taster glass to try one of their many local brews.  As for food, I had a crab cake special and it was really "just alright".  The crab cakes were really deeply fried and lacked the large chunks of crab I would expect in a homemade crab cake.  The people at the table next to us ordered burgers, which looked like the right way to go.  However, their french fries were great, and the patio is a fun place on warm summer evenings. If you go, try the burgers (veggie!). 

Note: if you drive, they have a parking lot specifically for customers in the back.  Awesome!

I have occassionally do take-outs at this place.   The owner seems nice, always friendly, then again, isn't that expected of an owner operator of a food service establishment?     
The food is okay for the burbs, not as authentic as one would get.   But nevertheless, some of the dishes are tasty.
The problem with this restaurant is its identity crisis.   So is it a Chinese restaurant?   a Japanese restaurant?  or a Thai restaurant(they have Pad Thai on the menu)?    I'd suggest stay away if you want Japanese or Thai, but do come here for Chinese.

I have only been to Common Ground twice, both on Friday nights during their 90's night. I had a blast both times, and the crowd is always entertaining. This bar definitely attracts mostly college students, which is becoming less my scene, but I forgive them because of the good music/dancing. 


My one complaint about this bar is the TERRIBLE bar service. On a really busy Friday night, they have one bar with two bartenders. Both times I have gone here I have to wait 20 - 30 minutes to get a drink- Ridiculous! They need to hire an additional bar tender, or have an additional bar counter, something! It also gets backed up because everyone knows that there is a long wait for drinks so they order drinks for themselves and their 8 friends.

This is more of a value than quality hotel. It was the lowest price when we searched the Boston area but you definitely get what you pay for. The good: location - 12 min walk to the subway station and right next to Whole Foods and Trader Joe's. The ok - beds are comfortable but bathroom is very tight and has almost no space to put anything. You can hear every noise in the hallway. The bad: the shuttles are very unreliable - once we waited for over 40 min for what should have taken only 5-10. We called three times and finally they contacted  the shuttle driver.

I had high hopes for this new restaurant based on reviews of their other location.  I was very underwhelmed.   I ordered the Shrimp and Chicken Cashew dish.  I received 4 pieces of shrimp and the chicken was diced so finely it was hard to find with all the vegetables.  For the price I expected more meat and less filler.  The Crab Rangoon were good (the usual, not special).  I was also surprised that the kids menu only had 3 or 4 things on it. (Sweet and sour chicken, and BBQ ribs are the two I can remember). I felt it was not family friendly (which may be what they are going for). I might try it for sushi but I would not go back if I was looking for a more traditional entree.

After exercise in gym I suddenly want to have a burger. When I arrived the burger shop nobody is waiting. I ordered the the roots burger and my friend ordered jumbo burger. We also ordered spicy honey chicken wings. One thing to notice is that if you are too hungry or in a hurry, then don't choose here. We waited 30+ minutes. The burger is not bad, and actually one burger is enough for me. The wing is not bad as well, but spicy is more than sweet.

I mean, it's a decent place. It was fairly clean. But I think I just expected more. It's a fast, casual Italian restaurant. But I think everything is frozen and warmed up? Not really sure though. My wife and I came in and we ordered everything for In. Tables were clean and our meals were quickly brought out to our tables. Customer Service was fine. It was about 9pm on a Friday night and it was basically empty. 

Food was fairly tasteless. I ordered the chicken fettuccine pasta. My wife ordered the chicken Parmesan. She really enjoyed hers.  She said she grew up eating this restaurants food so she had high expectations. This was my first time, and it was OK. The breadsticks were salty but they were all right. Overall I give this place a three. It does have $5 lunch where you get a drink and a meal which is awesome. But I would steer clear from dinner we ordered two meals and a salad and pay $23.

Wanted to try out a new bar for late night and decided to come here for two reasons: 1) I'm always a sucker for darkly lit bars and 2) I heard about their mule variations.  So the bar space was pretty, except for the dead animal heads on the wall.  I didn't come here with expectations that they would cater to vegans, but eww on the decor.  Shared a pickle plate and fries.  Meh - I wasn't expecting anything spectacular so I don't really have any complaints.  I thought the service was ok but a little pretentious perhaps.  I actually didn't get a chance to try one of the mule variations so I'll probably be back, but only for that reason.

My silk tofu (A) was OK. Way too sweet for a dinner dish and with very little in the way of other flavors. I still love the purple rice, and the older woman I assume is the owner was perfectly sweet and helpful, but the food just doesn't speak to me.
 
I don't have much experience with Korean food, so maybe it's me, not Koriente. Then again, my dining companion didn't seem thrilled by anything in his bibimbap but the beef and sauce -- the colorful veggies were pretty, but not great eating, and mostly went untouched. Both of us finished about half our bowls of miso soup. It's a fine soup, but not so good that I kept sipping it after my entree arrived.

I've been on several boat trips through this organization.  The best one was on New Year's a few years ago.  Watching the fireworks from a boat is not an event I am likely to forget.  I've been on two whale watches, both times sighting many whales.  It amazes me that people who get sick on boats go on whale watches at all; since, they are - on a boat.  First, it is a 3 or 4 hour trip.  Second, the ride to the whales can be very bumpy.  The last trip I was on just about everyone puked, excluding myself and a few others who stood at the front.  The secret is to watch the horizon.  Oh, and remember warm clothes and your rain gear.  

I have been on trips to see the harbor islands.  Nice ride; however, my mother in law is in a wheelchair, and when we were to get off the boat this fact alluded the crew.  Everyone was told to go upstairs in order to get off the boat, we had to be taken to another dock.

I like going on boat rides.  The trips aren't expensive, and the city always looks pretty from the harbor.  It is my desire to next go on the Odyssey for a fancy dinner cruise!  Review to follow.

Came in for Sunday brunch and we grabbed a seat at the bar. Looked like they had a lot of tables open but they were reserved for reservations. 

Food: I got the steak and eggs, steak medium rare. My steak was cold and definitely more rare than medium, my eggs were also barely warm. Despite all that, the salsa on the steak was good and the home fries were good. Nothing to write home about for the toast or coffee. My boyfriend got the omelette plus chorizo and thought it was okay. 

I've been here before and had a better experience so I think it's a solid three stars. Nothing tasted bad but nothing tastes great.  In the sea of delicious brunch in the south end, I would say skip this and try a different restaurant.

You can't really go wrong with a bowl of beans and rice. For me, it's just about ordering it the right way - next time I visit I'll order my bowl without the trademark Tali Sauce - don't get me wrong, it is tasty, but the flavor just didn't seem to make sense with all the other ingredients (and they really pour a lot on). 

Aside from that, I just wish they that they didn't fill the bowl so high that the lid can't fit!

3-3.5 stars. Cute spot in the Downtown area to pick up coffee. However, they only had one cashier and person making the french press and drip coffee (there is another barista for the espresso based drinks), so the line can move slowly at times. We just got a standard French Press Coffee (Large, $3.10, http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=iwxFdSZwYwMI0R_5Er45KA&userid=76vIFZcC7owykCBjMfGVXg) which was good, but not the best coffee I've ever had. I think I would have had a better experience if we ordered an espresso based drink and/or breakfast taco, and/or were hanging out here since it's quite spacious inside and very modern. I would come back if in the area for more coffee, but would prefer to go to a boutique roastery. Parking in this area can be tough since there isn't a lot of street parking in the downtown area.

We made a reservation for 6:30, arrived on time and was told we would be sat in one minute. 
Then from there on, the two hosts and man in a business suit (manager?) who kept approaching the host stand ignored us completely and sat many others until 7:07pm. 
By this point, we were all very hungry and ate too much bread to enjoy dinner. My 6y old daughter was over it before we even got sat so she didn't even touch her food. 
All our dinners seemed to take longer to come out than others around us who ordered after even though we didn't order anything that took a long time to cook. My cocktail took exceptionally long to arrive. The server seemed to have 2-3 other tables and was very busy. 
Not once did a manager do a table touch to check in on us, even after taking so long to seat us. 
The actual food was good, but nothing I'd wait that long for. I could have gone to Tony Cs without a reservation or wait (we called and debated on leaving while being ignored). 
That being said, if I was to return it would not be during a busy time. This restaurant clearly needs to work on that.

I didn't even know this place existed as it's a bit tucked away, but am glad to have found it! 
Cute little coffee shop with free WiFi decent coffee and what looks like to be a decent menu. Prices are reasonable and the panini/sandwhiches others were ordering looked yummy. 
$3.40 for an iced americano with some flavoring seemed a bit much but not terrible. 
Liked that they had plenty of creamer/sweetners to mix into my drink and some decent seating. 
Staff seemed a bit cold and didn't talk much. No biggie really. I will certainly come back especially during warmer months to indulge in the patio seating and some yummy sandwhiches.

We stayed here during a conference being held at the Doubletree because it was half the price of the Doubletree. The room was great. Ours was clean, included a mini fridge and microwave (so we could buy groceries and save money), and housekeeping seemed to do a great job. The breakfast, however, left much to be desired and it was always a madhouse in the dining area. The bread and bagels tasted very cheap and were not filling. The sausage looked unappetizing, so I didn't try it. The scrambled eggs were okay. The coffee ran out my last morning there and I didn't have time to wait for them to bring more. The first morning, I was about to sit down and one of the staff members grabbed my chair practically out from under me and gave it to someone else. I stood there looking at her and then she said she would find me another chair. While some of the staff were very pleasant, some were quite rude (especially around the dining area). Also, they have an Orlando ticket booth set up in the dining area and I overheard the ticket agent tell someone, "Epcot is just learning about different cultures. There are no rides there. If you want your kids to have real fun, take them to Universal." I thought that was tacky and unprofessional. She should have given a description of each park and let the parent decide what would be "real fun" for her kids. Also, they were painting the walls in the hallway while we were there and I found the smell of the paint fumes to be nauseating. The location was walking distance from the Doubletree, so we were able to save on parking and they did let us leave our car there for a couple of hours after we checked out. I would recommend this location if you need an affordable place to stay, but would also recommend making other arrangements for breakfast. We ended up supplementing with granola bars and sometimes had to buy coffee somewhere else.

I've been to this location a few times and have always enjoyed the drinks. The taro milk tea is especially flavorful. I was pretty confused when I walked in today and found the menu reduced to about 5 choices?? (3 milk teas, 2 juice teas) I asked about the reduced menu and didn't get much explanation besides "Yes, this is the menu". They're also selling a big selection of imported Japanese chocolates in the store now which is cool, but I'd rather have the normal sized menu.

The map on the phone sent me into an apt complex. . Stopped in for Sunday lunch. Menu is small.  Small place about 8-9 tables, no high tops. You order your food and then take a seat. I got wings spicy tang and  garlic noodles.  Noodles are nice garlicly, enjoy that but the chicken was over cooked. I did tell the guy at the register but no response. The wings are jumbo style and very messy so be prepared for that, a lot of breading on them. Really enjoyed the garlic noodles, except for the chicken.

Market is definitely one of the restaurants worth trying for Dine Out Vancouver. Their Lunch dine out Vancouver menu is priced at $25 which is a pretty decent deal considering how much their usual menu prices are. But there wasn't a lot of selection for you to choose from for lunch dine out with additional added cost for other options. So I stuck with the stand dine out menu item and had the 
West Coast Seafood Rissott, Carmelized Celeriac Veloute, Market Cheesecake. The risotto was cooked just right and that's not an easy task and it was really filling being carb loaded! It also had a good amount of seafood in it too. The Veloute was my favourite - it was a creamy soup with so much flavour! There was so much food for lunch in that dine out menu and they were so rich that I could barely finish my meal and needed a nap right after! Overall a nice experience for dine out!

My girlfriend and I were relaxing the day before her wedding, trying to take her mind off the day of. We had finished all of the things on her to-do list and decided to get manis and pedis. We spent approximately 20 minutes on the phone calling places for an appointment and looking up reviews. We called Arboretum Nails and Spa and their prices were reasonable, and they said they only had a 10 minute wait. No problem. We told them we'd be right over and gave our names. Unfortunately, we should have realized that 10 minutes was a severe underestimation when we walked in. There were approximately 8 people in front of us. Since we'd already spent so much time looking up places, we decided to wait it out and choose our nail colors.

Forty-five minutes later, we were seated in the pedicure chairs.  Twenty minutes later, no one had even come over to us to begin, to inquire about what we wanted, or to talk to us.  Her rehearsal dinner was fast approaching and all brides feel the pressure of being on time, so we began debating whether or not we should leave. Typically, an hour is more than enough time for a pedicure and we'd already been there for over an hour by that time... but they hadn't even begun to work their magic yet.  The ladies overheard us talking and assured us that we'd be next, but we realized they would be skipping over another party to appease us.  A party, ironically, which was also trying to make it to their rehearsal dinner on time. It wasn't fair that they'd be skipped, so we got up and left.

There was NO way we should have been told a 10 minute wait.  I expect honesty and if my wait is going to be over an hour, you should tell me that when I call. You may notice that I still gave them three stars - I recently went back with my sister and we received great treatment. It was an off-day, not very busy, and we received great service. I do think when you actually receive service, they do a great job.

Boyfriend and I decided to try this place as we had an entertainment book coupon for it. I had made a reservation for 6, didn't get seated until 6:20ish and didn't get our order taken until 6:40. Our chef was actually cooking a meal for another party (prior to us going in, a party of 40 had come). Anyways, the staff were all overwhelmed with them so there was little or no attention for the new guests. After the party left, the service was a lot better and everyone was more attentive. Food was good too, but I found the portions to be a bit on the small side. Worst part: I had to pay $8 for parking since the 5 stalls they had were all occupied and I wasn't reimbursed for my parking :(.

Cobalt recently purchased the building I rent in and so far the experience has been mixed. I definitely think it's in part to the transition that comes with a change in ownership, but so far their communication has been subpar. We are thrilled to see improvements to our building, but less thrilled that these somewhat invasive improvements (tree trimming, removing and replacing our fence, HVAC work) have happened with little to no heads up. So far every time something has been happening in our building we have gotten a day off notification, which is problematic when repairs involve entering our home. 
There was also an instance where they sent a contractor to our home to do an estimate and did not notify us whatsoever. Management does not seem to understand why that would make us uncomfortable and has said they are not in control of that, but if they aren't, who is?

In our quest to try out all the neighborhood Mexican restaurants, my sweetie and I dropped in to pay Little Mexico a visit...

Its an eclectic little place, basically a house gutted and turned into a restaurant. Prices were very cheap, the service kind of average... you didn't get forgotten, but they didn't seem in a hurry for anything. We made our stop a little bit back, and the food was unexciting enough that I honestly can't tell you what I had. Seems we had the queso and found it... ok. I want to say I had a chipotle chicken, but it might have been a chile relleno. Whatever it was, I remember thinking it reminded me of a microwave dinner. 

I might have been really unhappy had I paid regular menu prices, but this was cheap enough that I didn't mind that it was cheap. If I was still a college student back in my partying days, I'd probably like this place a lot. Seeing as I'm not... I continue my quest.

Look I'm no expert on dive bars but when in Rome, do as the Romans, right?
I came here as a destination on a predetermined bar crawl and to my surprise I actually liked the place. Really! There was a kickass bartender pouring stiff drinks and not just the wells either, my Maker's Mark runneth over with a splash of soda that didn't knock the tint of color down even a notch. Nice.
I got a burger because this was my first chance to eat on the crawl and guess what, surprise! Best GD crinkle cut fries I've ever eaten in Portland, crispy brown and downtown baby! The burger was no slouch either, we're talking all kinds of fixin's stacked up high with a soft grill toasted bun. It was a professional burger without a doubt. I tasted someone else's Mac 'n Cheese and it was "nom nom" tasty and rib stickin' too.
They have a giant patio out back with a fire pit and it was very popular among the Neanderthal smoking crowd.
The Jukebox... I did not drop a single quarter but I loved every song that played out, plus they have a freakin' CSI pinball machine with William L. Petersen emblazoned on the back glass. Random weird.
It's hard to give a dive bar more than 3 stars because they are on every corner in every part of the city, but they are a solid 3 stars all day and night long.

Pricci is another upscale Italian restaurant in Buckhead Life's fleet.  Just like some of the other BL restaurants, as soon as you walk through the doors, you are hit with old-school style and elegance.  Pricci's interior reminds me of a cruise ship dining room with its combination of marble tile, carpet, wood, and white tablecloths.  We booked reservations on OpenTable for Friday and were seated immediately.  The restaurant was not very busy.  Most of those dining were your typical Buckhead Life crowd (middle-aged to blue hairs).

Pricci's dinner menu offers a simple variety of Italian appetizers, salads, pastas, and entrees.  They also serve pizzas Neapolitan-style.  I didn't really think of Pricci serving pizzas and I am intrigued about what they are like.  We didn't end up ordering any.  Instead, items off the menu I tried included:

Polpette - veal and parmesan meatballs with tomato basil sauce
Malfatti - ricotta gnocchi with braised Vidalia onions and sauce
Ossobuco - braised veal shank with Carnaroli risotto and lemon gremolada

The restaurant's meatballs are supposedly "famous" and they were hot, hearty, thick, and juicy.  I liked them.  The ricotta gnocchi was light, fluffy, and melted in my mouth.  The veal shank was served with the bone was cut open and there was a small silver fork inside which one can use to eat the marrow.  It was actually pretty good, especially when eaten with the meat itself.  The meat was savory.  I also tried a bite of the day's grilled fish.  I forget what type of fish it was, but it was served Asian-style, whole with bones, and had a crispy exterior.

The hostess and server were friendly.  The server was knowledgeable, but service was slow even though the restaurant was not busy.  Valet parking is available for $2.  Pricci was fine, but between the two Italian Buckhead Life restaurants, I am more of a Veni Vidi Vici fan.

I really wanted to love this place, I really did, especially after all the hype and then the monologue at my table by the "Chef" regarding the preparation of the savory ingredients going into my Monte Cristo.  I liked the whole idea, and ten dollars later was expecting a piece de resistance, however the end product was just, well....... okay. Where was this Mesquite Smoked Ham taste? And the Plum Apple Jelly taste that supposedly sets off this culinary masterpiece? I guess they had the day off. IMHO it tasted like a soggy deep fried grilled cheese sandwich.

All right, look. While this Stop and Shop often stocks sub-par produce and the "organic" section is so lacking that I feel it necessary to put quotations marks around the word, I've found this to be a pretty decent location overall. It's great for certain staples...but I'm not the kind of woman who does all her grocery shopping in one place. 

Stock up on your beans, rice, condiments, and other odds and ends here, but I recommend going elsewhere for the produce (and definitely for tofu) if you can. This place is Goya Heaven Jr. (Hi-Lo is Goya Heaven the elder), which is fantastic--I'm now addicted to those super sugary, ridiculously cheap sodas (note: try the Guava!).  

The staff here have always been pretty nice to to me. And while they are not always completely helpful on the vegan front, a little kindness goes a long way. For example, when I asked for ground flax seed and tamarind paste--which, apparently, classify as "crazy" ingredients--two staff members were more than willing to run all over this absurdly gigantic store with me, searching the aisles. It was a serious adventure. And the mission was 50% accomplished! 

Nothing to write home about (I mean, it's a grocery store), but it gets the job done.

This place is just A-ok, that's it. I am a bit biased with this place. We have a bittersweet relationship. I live out in Bedford, so when I come, I want to make sure I "stock up on my hair", so to speak. To me, this place has the best selections, as well as customer service. I had a bad experience with the two hair stores in Cambridge-bad service and wayyy too high prices. Well, this store sells a little above suggested retail value. Don't know much of the return policy, cause well I know what I'm getting before hand, I do hair. 

The prices, to me, I guess I'm just used to hair stores in the south where they have a huge vary of hair. And they have hair marked tremendously low on some, and then you pay, still a decent amount for the quality hair.

I would say go here, cause they really are nice, from my experience. Also, they do tend to have a lot of selections. Oh and Just an FYI the owner, the Asian lady behind the counter is NOT there for your assistance, she there to check you out and hand you a receipt, remember that!

How does one go about reviewing what is essentially a shipping service? BC Ferries' cargo is people, and their rates are fixed. They do try to make the journey comfortable, with a decent, albeit very overpriced, White Spot restaurant and snack bar.

I've traveled via BC Ferries on the Horseshoe Bay/Nanaimo run every weekend since July 2010, so have a lot of trips under my belt now, both as a walk-on passenger and as a vehicle driver, so here's some observations:

- if you can take the bus or bring a bicycle, do so. You'll save a ton of money. 
- pack a meal or a snack with you. There's a microwave in the café area for passenger use. The food on the ferry ain't cheap.
- a motorcycle is 2/3 of the cost of a car, so there's some savings, but you'll be proportionally ripped off considering the deck space a bike takes up vs a vehicle. You will, however, get priority boarding and don't need a reservation.
- you usually don't need to make reservations for a vehicle unless you're traveling during peak times (holidays, 3pm - 9pm)
- keep an eye on the weather; if there's any chance of high winds, your sailing may be delayed or even cancelled.
- if you're busing on the Nanaimo side, spend some time at the bctransit.ca site and plan your trip. Nanaimo's transit system is dismal when it comes to meeting sailings and even worse on Sundays and holidays. Note: there is no public bus service for Duke Point, so unless you're looking for a 10k walk to Nanaimo, take your car there or arrange a ride.
- if you're driving a car, please leave your car alarm off or you'll just get called down to the vehicle deck when it starts sounding due to the motion of the vessel.
- electrical outlets for your devices are on board, but you may have to go scrounging for them or share them with other passengers. Charge your devices at home first.
- the ferries have wifi, but I use that term generously. It's intermittent, and if there's a large number of passengers, you'll most likely not be able to connect (my personal theory is that the wifi is nothing more than a shared connection tethered to the Captain's cell phone).
- if you're bringing young kids on board, please don't park them around the business workstations. Most people on their laptops are trying to get some work done, and there's a kid's play area on every ferry.
- you can have a good chuckle over their tag-line "Experience the Difference!". I'm not sure what the difference is being compared to (swimming, perhaps?) as there are no other competing ferry services. If you're taking a car, then you may want to consider one of a handful of small airline companies that service Vancouver Island; it's almost as 'cheap' and will save you hours of travel time.
- weather permitting, get outside on the upper deck and take in the scenery. Regardless of which ferry route you take, you will be rewarded with BC's natural beauty every time!

Service was excellent - friendly, accommodating and efficient. 

The fish and chips were very good, light, crispy batter.  Good quality fish.  Fries were good.  Bottomless soft drinks/lemonade.

The restaurant doesn't have a view or much ambiance - but the good food and friendly service more than make up for this.

As a craft beer drinker - I would love to see a better selection of local craft. I mean Fuggles is nearby and an arrangement could be made with Britannia Brewing as well.  Four Winds is just in Delta - plenty of local craft to choose from if the establishment is interested.  They only served Granville Island draft (which is owned by a subsidiary of Molson/Coors).  There are much better m, locally owned craft beer options.  I can attest that a heffeweizen is a great accompaniment to fish and chips.  If they had a good selection of true craft beers and some rotating taps of seasonal brews, I would go more often.

Other than that .... a solid choice for fish and chips.

Btw - excellent kids menu options for the little ones.

It's a bit pricey, but they have many things Japan related that can be hard to find. My main gripe is that I asked for help buying some stuff and (I think it was the owner) person that helped me seemed consistently tried to get me to buy the most expensive items, even after I kept asking for something cheaper. I found that a bit tone-deaf and annoying. Your stuff is already expensive and please take a hint. It is a good place to find some things that are hard to find in Austin though.

We came in for a late lunch on New Years Eve.  We came here to eat their Shanghainese dumplings but unfortunately they were out of them by the time we came :(  We did get to try their crab dumplings which weren't the juicy kind but they were still pretty good.  Our waitress made the dipping sauce for us tableside.  We also got black bean sauce noodles which were totally different from what we've had before.  They hand pull their own noodles in the back.  Overall, the food was just okay.

This is the first time I've ever been to a Chinese restaurant where we were the only Asians in the restaurant, including the staff!  The staff was super friendly and the restaurant was pretty busy for 3PM.

Honestly, the three stars goes to their delicious wings and their Crave the New Black roll. We ordered the kimchi fried rice and it was not worth $15; it was bland and the portion size was ok. Service was good. The two stars goes to this "admin fee" that is added on to the bill. I've never seen this fee added before my numerous times here so I asked the server what's this fee about and she replies, "it's for processing credit card, but if it's paid with cash then you'd save 5%." I thought how weird that was and if it's a new thing now with restaurants in Boston charging this fee on top food tax, beverage tax, etc. The bill was about $110.00 including this "fee," and it was only my husband and I. I got home and being the auditor that I am, I really can't shake why this fee was added to the bill. I googled it and I can't seem to find the reason why. I spoke to my girlfriend about this and she says it's practically illegal. So please be aware of this fee and definitely question them about this, or maybe management will read this review and think twice about adding this fee to customers' bills or if it is a "legal" thing then I'd advise the management to train their staff to be upfront about this fee to their customers before they leave the bill on the table. 

I really wish I'd save this receipt before I left the restaurant. If management is reading this, do share your policy/law on this.

Parkway Cafe was a great help for those of us at the Marriott across the street.  It is a small cafe in an office building.  The prices are reasonable.  I had the eggs with biscuit and homestyle fries.  I wanted the breakfast burrito without the hash brown but he said it is all together and I could not have it separately.  As for my meal, the eggs were real eggs and tasted great, the biscuit was good but the fries were tasteless and dry.  Stay away from them.

I had been looking forward to trying Pinolo all summer. Having spent a decent amount of time in Italy, I've grown to love gelato and generally prefer gelato over ice cream, of which Portland has an abundance of popular shops. 

I'm also vegan, and was impressed by the non-fruit based, dairy-free flavors Pinolo lists on its website. In the shop, however, the only dairy-free flavors were fruit-based. When I asked the employee whether they had any of the flavors listed on their online menu, like caffe or almond, she seemed very confused and said it was "weird" that the online menu is so different. I was surprised that she had no idea about what the online menu listed. While I understand and appreciate that Pinolo may rotate its flavors seasonly, it is misleading to advertise so many non-fruit, dairy-free flavors and actually have none of them (in fact, the website lists 10 non-fruit, dairy-free flavors). Fruit sorbets are easy to find but other dairy-free flavors are less so. I was so looking forward to dairy-free caffe or bacio as the website had listed and as I love to enjoy in Italy!

I chose blueberry and yellow plum which were fine sorbettos, but not what I was hoping to eat. I recommend that Pinolo change its stated list of flavors on its website so no other dairy-free customers arrive expecting a wider variety of flavors. 

Meanwhile, my sister ordered the special flavor-- ricotta with apricot preserve-- and received a scoop with zero of the preserve.

My wife and I got our dog from PWP.  We love our dog (and obviously our affection for our pet has nothing to do with PWP).  As a result, I'm hesitant to give PWP a bad review because it's hard to fault them for working with so little.  That said, the house they use is kind of gross and smells like cat piss.  When we first got her, our dog was sick with bordatella (dog pneumonia) and run down.  However, after talking with the staff (mainly volunteers from OSU) you get the impression that the only reason PWP is run down is a lack of money (rather than a genuine desire to help animals find a loving home).  That said, get your pet from PWP because they need the money and donate to them because they really do care about getting their pets into a loving home.

I think this place is just okay. It can be high traffic at different points throughout the day, and because I was merely touristing throughout the different parts of Boston, I didn't have to experience North Station when it's probably very overwhelming.

Goodness gracious, they need to update this place. There's food scattered around the floor, pigeons everywhere, bathrooms that are either not functioning or doors that don't lock, and smells that make you look around.

Overall, it did the job, but this is a place where commuters come at the end of the day to unwind and relax. Updating the place would do everyone well, considering so many events take place in the building and near the track.

This place used to be really great. However, it seems like the owners are not as involved as they used to be and the customer service has declined as a result. I used to see the owners around all the time and now haven't seen them the last three times I've been here. This most recent visit, I was assisted by a young lady with quite an attitude. Their loyalty system has also gotten significantly less rewarding, going from a free entree to now only a $3.50 discount. I wish they would just go back to how they were when they first opened.

It was a late lunch on a Friday and the service was excellent. We started with the Shrimp & Brie Butter nut Squash Crostini - and wow it was really tasty! I could have eaten all 3. then we each had a cup of the Blue Crab and Corn Chowder - again really tasty. i then had the warm beet and bibb lettuce salad...the candied bacon was good, and in general it was good, but the beets were COLD. my Mom had  the Dungeness Crab Tower, which is pretty in presentation, and tasty, but "perfect for sharing" as the menu says...i don't think so! very small and more of an amuse bouche IMHO. perfect for my tiny Mom, but I would need 2 of them! My sister splurged on the $20 Lobster Cobb, which came presented as a "layered mold" and was pretty. However she was unamused by the overabundance of Blue cheese and the lack of lobster. I must say that the service was Super - and in reflection that is typical of this chain. Overall I think this chain has prices that are higher than they should be.

My mother is Japanese.  I grew up in a Japanese household.  This was not even close to authentic in any way.

The modern POS was awkward in that it had names and pictures, but no descriptions, so we had to keep stopping staff to ask what the ingredients were.

I don't know that I had the same experience with the service that others did.  I didn't find them pretentious or snooty.  They seemed hurried, and considering we ordered ourselves and all they did was bring it out, I don't know I expected much from them.

But, the food is all that matters and the food was not good.  All the dumplings were basically the same gyoza, prepared in different ways.  All pork, except the cashew something dumplings which were disgusting.  Why not a chicken or plain veggie option?  Why make the only non-pork option a mushy meat-substitute?  It was so inedible, we left half of them on the table.  I have made literally thousands of gyoza and I can do it better on my worst day.

The 'spicy' chicken bun was bland.  The spring rolls were bland.  I didn't eat the ramen, but...I could see the egg was overdone and dunked below the soup, which basically muddies it.  It felt like they just dumbed it down for people that didn't know better.

Expected so much more from Old Chinatown/new Downtown.  Seriously disappointed.

Left not so happy at a supposedly happy crepe place. 

I left really disappointed. Last time that I came here I had such a pleasant experience with my Pesto Chicken Crepe. I mean it was SOOO absolutely delicious and I wanted to go back for me. Everything just melted in my mouth. However, I didnt get that experience today with the Pesto Chicken Crepe. The chicken was so dry and it wasnt just my crepe. My friend got the Roasted Chicken and her chicken was try too. It was only tolerable because the Roasted Chicken has caramelized onions which made the chicken more moist. I found it hard to finish my meal because there was just not enough sauce, the chicken was dry, and the spinach was not cooked either. Did they get a new cook or something? Seriously, the last time I had the Pesto Chicen, it made my mouth water for more. This time, I had try it over and over again to make sure that I didn't like it. At some point, I couldn't stand eating it anymore. My friend said that they might have used chicken left over from yesterday as the reason for the dry chicken. I will have to try this place again sometime, when I finally feel like coming back. Maybe, I will just get the Pork Specialty because that was really good.

Sugar buns! We got a few at work for a breakfast and I must say these were very soft and light, not too sweet and the cream was oozing out of it. In fact, there was so much cream I had to squeeze most of it out so I can get the bun to cream ratio right. If you are a big fan of cream, then you should definitely try it.

I tried the regular sugar and matcha buns. Both were great, I'm just not a fan of an entire cup of cream filling with each bun.

This is the first time I've been to this location. I usually go to the one in Pearl which, in my opinion, is a lot better. 

We ordered two cheeseburgers and they both were pretty dry. They just didn't taste as juicy and good as the ones in the Pearl location. We also got fries and some of the fries had the truffle oil taste and some didn't. 

It wasn't like the service was bad, but the staff seemed lackadaisical. For example, there were plenty of open spots at the bar but they would place a finished order right in front of a customer at the bar, so the other customer had to reach in front of them to get their order. 

However, I did see one incident that they handled really well and I will give them props for that. There was a really rude customer that ate her whole burger and then complained that there wasn't any cheese in it. I mean, who does that?? You don't eat the WHOLE thing before you complain about missing an ingredient. Anyways, the staff handled it pretty well and just made her another burger, which was nice. 

I really like little big burger but the food just wasn't as good as I remembered it being compared to the Pearl location. I think next time I'm craving little big burger, I'm just going to get my fix there.

Visited Better Half yesterday thanks to recommendations from friends. First impressions were that I was very much out of place. There crowd there ranged from professionals to adults working and/or drinking. My roommate and I went purely to eat and got many stares from customers, maybe we were too young or individuals really don't order food. I was curious to try something at their coffee menu but my options were small and the prices were high. Defiantly more of a cocktails location than a coffee. Nonetheless the food we did order was good. The chips and queso was nice had a tiny bit of kick to it since the chips were seasoned. The hot chicken sandwich with the coleslaw on the side was VERY good but really overbearing. If you're big into spicy food skip this. My roommate and I commented on how the buns were superrrr different from anything we have had in Austin. The fries were good and crispy and she said her burger was well a burger. Overall enjoyed the experience and food for the night but most likely won't be returning for food. Cocktails maybe.

For anyone following my gardening saga ... this Home Depot has an excellent selection of outdoor plants, pots, soils, etc ... basically, they had all the cute pot styles that Art Knapp had, and more.  And, everything was 1/2 to 1/4 the price at Art Knapp.  I should have started- and finished- here.  

Yes, it's the giant crazy Home Depot experience and their staff know nothing, but at this time of year, the garden section is filled with suburbanites who are all too happy to talk tomatoes, so you can still get some good help.  

If you're doing a patio garden, it's worth the trip.

I was a bit hesitant to visit a violin shop near symphony hall since i'm a newbie, but the experience was not bad at all. The prices are pretty expensive but it is after all Boston. I knew going in after a few emails with Mr. Rutman, that if i got anything it would be their starter violin and I'd have to be approved for credit to afford that. he was happy to let me try out the violin. It sounded really nice, although i had tried out a similarly priced violin at Wood and string the other day which sounded just as nice, and there I could do a rent to own deal. I think this is a nice shop for students and musicians in the symphony hall area, and probably great for repairs, but for me I can do better closer to Cambridge. They are very attentive here though and happy to help.

This is one of those places you walked into and know it's going 1 of two ways; either really good or really bad.  It's a divey little diner that offers a salad bar and the price was very good.  It wasn't very busy for lunch time on a Saturday!

At the beginning our service was prompt and we received drink refills.  I ordered their mushroom swiss burger and added bacon, jalapeños, cheese and pickles.

The extra large glasses were a welcome sight but after our food arrived they weren't filled again.  We had to hunt down someone for a knife and for refills.  The server didn't stop back after we received our food and actually everyone completely disappeared. I noticed the other people in the restaurant looking around for someone too.

It's unfortunate because my burger was actually really good.  We paid our check at the hostess stand and headed out.

The cannolis here are really good. Better than Mike's, though fewer options. There's a regular shell, chocolate dipped shell, and chocolate shell. The fillings are regular ricotta, vanilla custard, and chocolate custard. I was planning on getting a chocolate one, but I said chocolate-dipped cannoli, and the lady was already off to the kitchen and got me a ricotta one. Which I didn't mind because it was really good, but still...
The reason it's only 3 stars is because the lady who runs it is pretty surly unless you are a regular, and half the things don't have prices which meant I was dumb and ordered marzipan fruits that were ridiculously overpriced.

Everyone knows about this place because you can't go to a single class without seeing someone wearing some partially-washed, wrinkled, (free!) Engineer's Bookstore t-shirt. The shirts are fugly. I'm not entirely sure, but I think they stopped giving these free shirts out. 

Anyways. These guys are the alternative to Barnes and Noble. You would think that they'd offer cheaper prices than B&N, but really, they don't. You would also think that they might offer you a better buy-back price compared with B&N, but they truly don't. I guess they're just counting on you and your morals - support a mega chain or the local neighborhood "deal"? At the end of the day it doesn't matter, cause in case you can't grab the book off of Amazon since the book is (of course) the exclusive "Georgia Institute of Technology Edition," you're still gonna be forced to drop a bundle of money.

Return policy is the same as at B&N - full refund only if returned by the end of the first week of classes.

I am such a fan of this atmosphere. But it has to be the owners first restaurant. 
No valet. Not a great idea in Midtown.
Rude about clearing out tables and turning paying customers away for an extra 10 minutes of kitchen closing.
Cocktails and wine are superb. 
Tar-tare could use a bit more acid as well as being more minced. 
I had the duck (I LOVE duck, could eat it everyday). Duck is so special. It needs to be properly seared well. If not the thick layer of duck fat will not be crispy, leaving a fatty piece of inedible meat on top of a succulent duck breast. The crispy skin makes it. Well mine was not crispy. Ruined my cheat meal of duck for me. 
The dessert was fantastic. Even though I can't exactly recall what it was. But I know it was awesome.
Also.... Can a girl get some bread? Like for real.. What fine dining restaurant doesn't serve bread?  
All in all The Lawrence was pleasant, I would revisit if they could eat a little humble pie.

Wait, did you guys know that there are a lot of clubs in Boston? Don't tell anyone, I don't want to let the cat out of the bag.

Oops!

Seriously though, every club/lounge has it's own draw, and the beauty of BOND is definitely unparalleled in these parts. 

On the flip side, there is a LOT of competition for greatness, and BOND doesn't blow me away by any means.

Came on Saturday night for drinks. No cover (yay), coat check (yay), nice entrance up the marble staircase (yay). Weird layout (boo), generally odd setup at the bar -- EVERYONE RUSH THE BARTENDER (boo), and no where to sit or stand except right in the main walkway (boo). 

Drinks are expensive, not anything to right home about. The bartender ran out of cranberry, so he told me I would have to wait. No biggie, I patiently waited and didn't make a big deal of it. After a few minutes, he says "it's going to be a little while".. I said, okay yah no problem. I thought they were just loading up the cranberry in the machine, so I was okay with waiting. Finally he says, "look, it won't be fixed for a while. What else do you want?" Kind of an asshole, if you ask me. Here I am being patient even though your bar is out of a staple mixer, and you're giving me an attitude? Come down off your high horse, bartender. 

I would come back with a small group (like three others or less), because it's just too weirdly setup to have a big group all together blocking the walking areas and there's no where else to be.

It pains me to give Chow Baby three stars, but this is mostly because this new-ish restaurant hasn't really gotten all of the kinks out of its system.  I've been three times, so I'm certainly a fan, but there is certainly room for improvement.

Heracles strengths: Something to please anyone!  Chow Baby is a 'mongolian grill' type restaurant, where patrons fill bowls that are then cooked on an open flat-top grill.  If you happen to be really into vegan-super-spicy-noodle-goodness, while your BFF is into beef-garlic-y-vegetable-rice-goodness, the odds are good that you both can find something.  The menu specifies what sauces and other items are vegan/gluten-free, as well as containing good descriptions of what each sauce tastes like.  Vegetable offerings change daily. 

Aphrodite factor:  A bit loud, but not necessarily a bad date spot.  You're more likely to see larger parties here, as well as smaller groups.
