Hermes rating: This is essentially the restaurant's Achilles Heel.  Chow Baby hasn't quite mastered the ebb and flow of traffic, and they don't always take reservations.  Sometimes there is no line to fill your bowl to get it cooked, and at other times there is a line that will take you 20 minutes to get through.  There doesn't seem to be good timing in terms of seating, so servers get swamped rather quickly.  Additionally, there are always TONS of large parties here for dinner.  I'd be interested to see what lunch is like with a business crowd.

Achilles heel: If you don't like your dish, you have no one to blame but yourself.  Go back and try again!  Also, the restaurant inexplicably has a DJ on weekends, so it can be quite loud.

Libations: Chow Baby has an awesome cocktail menu, but I wasn't impressed with my last trip.  I'm usually a huge fan of the Ginja Sour, because it had more of a syrupy-sweet taste than the awesome ginger note I was expecting.  I'm guessing it just depends on who is bartending.

Offering: Chow Baby is an all-you-can-eat restaurant and is priced accordingly.  Lunch is quite a bargain.

I doubt I'll be back here any time soon but their burgers were not bad. It gets packed for lunch during the week. You walk in, order your food, sit down and they'll call your name. We had to wait in line to order and then it took about 10 minutes to hear our names. I ordered a classic cheeseburger with LTO. It came back with ketchup and lettuce. Now, I LOVE onion so I was peeved but I wasn't about to go back in and ask for it since it was so packed. I was annoyed but wasn't going to fly off the handle about it either.

The prices are pretty good for the food. Around $5 for burger only. You can do a combo with fries and a drink for an extra couple bucks. We sat on the patio on High Street to eat so that was pretty cool.

A fine lunch just nothing to shake a stick at. They just opened so maybe there are some growing pains here. There are just other places I'd rather go for lunch near Gay Street.

Ever since they were featured on Diners, Drive-ins and Dives, I had to come here. During my December trip last year, I planned a day out to Salem and made sure I was able to eat here for dinner. Of course, I had to order the lobster claw martini (Lobsterini). It was anti-climactic only because I was so excited for the drink and don't get me wrong, it is interesting and delicious, but my claw was small in comparison to the others in my party who ordered it and it was served two fingers below the rim. When the claw was removed, the two finger space was lowered to almost half of the glass. Price aside, it was just upsetting and the drink seemed hardly worth it. 

Now, to eat I ordered the lobster roll New England-style with a side of tots and that was totally worth the money. The lobster claws, yes claws as there were many of them in my sandwich and falling out of it and into the basket, were not seasoned so you can just enjoy the natural flavor of the lobster. They were perfect with a squeeze of lemon and left me wanting more. I'd definitely come back for another roll!

Well, arrived Saturday night 9.30pm, stood second place in the line for 45 minutes with no-one (visibly) going in. Eventually met up with enough friends to make table service palatable (2 bottles/$600 minimum for Absolut) to find the place had lots of space...
Server was very pleasant but policy (?) is for them to take the bottle away and come back when there's an empty glass. Why?
Not a lot going on - Alibi much more fun.
btw - STRICT no sneakers policy.

Finally tried this Canadian chain.

I ordered the chipotle turkey panini, it was okay but had that cheap fast food taste. Accompanied the panini with a very delicious chili, it had mushrooms which was different but yummy. Finished the meal off with some timbits, oh yum!! And cheap!

This particular location, not that I've visited others,  boasts plenty of seats however for having free wifi there were no outlets in sight :/

Timbit flavors:
Sour Cream mmm
Coconut chocolate mmm
Honey glaZe, ehh
Raspberry filled powdered... Not the best very artificial from dough to filling
Cherry, good but only for one bite

3.5 stars

Wanting a fast, quick slice of pizza, this seemed like just the right place to go. I stood in line checking out the pizza options and decided on the gold ring and return of the wu however, I did not want 2 slices of pizza. I was very surprised to see that they offer CUTS; you can take any slice of pizza and have it cut in half and so you only pay half. I was happy that I got to try both slices without feeling the carb guilt.

This was a great spot to check out in Salem. This was the home of Jonathan Corwin who was a judge in the Salem witch trials. I was hoping to get a guided tour but they did not offer one. You walk through the home on your own. It's very small but there are many artifacts and plaques with information. I'm a big fan of the show Ghost Adventures and they did an episode here so I had to check it out. Very eerie and a cool place to visit!

Been back here more than once in the last week. Love their BBQed salmon belly... it's marinated in a sweet teriyaki sauce and served with a lime wedge that just takes it over the top. The maki is made with a bit too much rice, but overlooking that, it's a great value for what you get. They also only serve wild caught salmon from what I understand,  and thats a definite plus. Hubby didn't mind running in to grab some take out. They also do free delivery on $30 or more.. and it's pretty easy to hit that mark. Their 2 for $5.95 maki rolls are worth it and I am in love with their sweet potato /yam rolls.

Oh Ikea, why do I often feel you are the third sign of the apocolypse?

Everything you have in your store is so practical and cute...and how dare i not mention your low low prices.  Yet something within me is just not quite satisfied with my 800 pounds of rickety bookshelves i procured from you just a short while ago.  That's right, it may weigh a ton, but be hopeful a stiff wind doesn't come by and knock them over.

In all seriousness, the shelves are still holding together, though I highly doubt they would survive another move unscathed.  Another great example of the old addage:  you get what you pay for.

The food court on the other hand..delicious.  I find it hard to deny the $4 plate of meatballs on every trip to the store. That's right, no Ikea review is complete without mention of meatballs.  There you go, I did it.

My favorite Ikea sections however, as the crafty goddess that I am, is the fabrics.  Cheap, pretty decent quality stuff.  You're not getting prices like this at the shop down the street, and it really helps to supplement my stash with bright bold solids when I just can't afford to go out and get my beloved Kona cottons.  Sometimes, I even settle for solid colors of sheets from their bedding department.  What's a poor young diy junkie to do?

All in all I think I would deem Ikea to me as Kryptonite to Superman, yet I can not stay away.

Touche Ikea, Touche.

Acai bowls have taken Instagram by storm, and I've been craving one for months. I was ecstatic to find out Liquiteria had acai bowls. I ordered the Acai Parfait which was blended with nut butters, almond milk, honey, and fruits. Presentation-wise, it was in a regular paper cup and not quite as pretty as the acai bowls I had in mind. Taste-wise, the parfait was flavorful but a bit too dense, probably because it had both almond and peanut butter, and got monotonous and too watery towards the bottom of the cup. It did not quite live up to my expectations, but I'll keep looking elsewhere for a better acai bowl.

Service was fine, but they forgot to add berries to the top of my parfait until I reminded them. I have yet to try their smoothies and juices, but the prepackaged fruit and juices did not look too fresh or appealing. This place is definitely pricey at about $10 per item, and for the quality of the food, I would come back only occasionally.

Food was generally good.  Quite salty but I think this was intentional for the beef.  A little greasy.  Fries were tasty.  Onion rings were huge but again very greasy and salty.  This is not a place most people can afford on a weekly basis. ($85.00 for 5 people burgers fries and sundaes).  By the way the ice cream sundaes were some of the best I've ever had.  Smooth and thick. Overall good food but not anything that merits its high price.  You can do just as well at half the price.

We had a party of 13 go here for brunch on 8/2/15. It was a honeymoon sendoff gathering. The food was good but pricey. The service was slow and not attentive. The place was not very busy when we got there but the waiter seemed like he had never worked with a large party before. The food took quite some time to come out. The waiter just dropped off a large bill on the table without bothering to check if we wanted to do separate tabs. Maybe that's not custom in Portland but here the waiter/waitress always asks how the tab will be handled when its a large party before dropping it off. After i asked to have the tab split up, you would have thought i asked him to do a physics equation. It took quite a while for that to occur. Obviously, this place is more used to the local hipsters eating there that don't mind paying for the atmosphere. Myself, i just want a good breakfast with minimal attitude. Got the good food, just got too much attitude for me.

I took my godson here and he had a fun time. I used a groupon and paid  $23 which saved me $10 in admission. 

We came on a Saturday at 10:15 am right when they opened, I like to get things done early, and knowing this is a tourist area didn't want to be waiting around. The place is very small and it took us about 2 and a half hours to do the entire museum. The layout of it is really nice and the scavenger hunt kept my godson occupied, I just didn't expect it to be as small. If I am in the area I'll probably be back if I can get another groupon.

I have eaten there twice now. A lunch with friends and dinner with friends. I SO WANT TO LOVE THIS PLACE... But, I haven't found anything yet to get excited about. The service is rediculous. The food comes out for one person at a time with an annoying wait for all to be served. Unbelievable... I've shared about 7-8 dishes and I found them to be bland for the most part. But, seemingly well prepared and not greasy. I will try again and am hoping to find that fantastic dish that will be exceptional.

Today I picked up lunch for my workplace. It was my first time at Foodheads. The place is quaint; I'm all for the old house made into a restaurant thing. I got the Cesar Salad Sandwich. Even though I didn't get to eat it right away, it was still pretty good an hour later. The bread is perfect, not too soft where it gets mushy or not too hard that it cuts the roof of your mouth. The chicken was very flavorful. Its also pretty filling. I only ate half and saved the other half for later. Yay for 2 meals in one! Overall a very good sandwich. Even though I didn't eat there, I can see from other reviews that is can get pretty cramped. I have two complaints. One, parking is horrible. Unless they had a parking lot I was unaware of, its hard to find parking. The second complaint is how the smell of cooking sticks to you. I was only in there for 2 mins, but I smelt like Foodheads all day. I wouldn't mind giving this place another try to see what else they've got.

I honestly had to stop and try and remember if I went to Sound Bites or Ball Square Cafe yesterday... but it was definitely Sound Bites. They are literally right next door to each other, and apparently have the same menu, so we chose the one with the shortest wait. 

This place is pretty cute. Self Service coffee bar is pretty awesome. They have several different types of coffee and "add-ins". 

The home fries are like fried mashed potatoes with the perfect amount of garlic. You should definitely order some if your meal doesn't come with them.

Pancakes live up to the hype. They are the best I've had in Boston. I got the triple berry, and didn't even need syrup. 

Everything else I had was so-so. Eggs were a bit dry. Hollandaise sauce was a little powdery. Bacon was, well, bacon. 

The wait wasn't too bad for a Saturday morning. About eight different people helped us, so service is alright, but not incredibly consistent.

All in all, pretty good place to have breakfast.

Probably not saying anything that hasn't been said before, but here it goes anyway:)

went for RW and although the portions were tiny, the food was unique and inventive. great for a very light and expensive meal, perfect for something like an interview or business meeting when you are looking to impress.

what i enjoyed more than the food, however, was the lounge area. a great place to go and relax, as long as it does not get to crowded. as a bostonian who recently came back from nyc, it was a great mesh of the two; boston charm with nyc pretention. the lounge is a great place to meet a date or for a drink after dinner. i may not come back for the food, but the lounge is on the list.

We were excited to try this place out; I love good pizza. You order at the bar and they bring the food to you. I got a Scuola Nuova cocktail and my husband got the watermelon Paloma. Mine was good, but the name was confusing. It's an "Old Cuban" but the name translates to New School. Weird. Anyway, my husband's watermelon Paloma wasn't good. It basically just tasted like sweet cilantro. 

We ordered chicken bites. They were just okay; we didn't finish them. The pizza was average as well; I did like the flavor of the tomato sauce, but there was way too much of it. I'd choose Life of Pie, Oven & Shaker and Trifecta Annex over it 10/10 times. 

Overall, pretty disappointed.

Eh, not from Portland so of course like everyone else said... 'when in Rome'! I probably wouldn't be back, luckily it was raining out so the line wasn't too bad. The staff was. It friendly, however not rude, just didn't care and no smiles. We opted for just one donut, the maple bacon bar. It was good, nothing I haven't had before and certainly NOT worth $3.50!! 

I heard from a lot of the locals that Blue Star is better but we never made our way over to try it!

Anyways, cool little shop but not something to go to twice!

Pros:  The food is tasty. I like the soups.

Cons:
- they automatically add an optional 15% to your bill (they say basically that the kitchen staff doesn't make a fair living wage so they want to add this "optional" fee. There is a sign near the register where you pay at the counter, that many people miss, that says you can"opt out" -- so you have to tell the person at the register and they will deduct it.  But But otherwise they don't tell you about it. And you are certainly not going to see it if you call for a take-out order and pay on the phone. I stopped eating there for that reason. Felt slimy and deceptive.

- DO NOT TAKE OUT SOUPS. With take-out, the hot soups are put in very cheap plastic containers that get really soft due to the heat of the soup.  This will cause TOXIC LEACHING (of the plastic/chemical compounds, BPA etc.) into the soup.

Been 3 times and each time I'd give a different rating. 3 stars seems fair cumulatively. 

Go if you're feeling adventurous and flexible. The meal may be perfect, it may really, really not be. I value consistency over everything else, and this place doesn't have that going for it, but it's not bad...

Salads are good. The shrimp, beet combo with arugula was delish. Skip the trout bahn mi, Greek salad with falafel and anything pickled in house. 

The wait staff is eccentric but (and?) friendly

Ok...  So the manager is nice.  She knows the restaurant business.  From the sounds of it, she runs a tight ship.  

But, the food is surprisingly bland.  

I asked the bartender/assistant manager (???) what the Cuban spices are and was told they're cumin, oregano, and some garlic.  Sure enough...

We had a margarita, two appetizers (rellena and mofongo), an entree (Bistec de Pollo Empanizada (With Mango Salsa), and dessert (tres leches), reviews are as follows:
Margarita:  Was actually awful - and I've never had a margarita I didn't like;
Rellena: Is exactly as described, it reminded me of smashed tamales rolled around seasoned ground beef;
Mofongo: Similar to dry mashed potatoes;
Bistec de Pollo Empanizada: Scallopini chicken breast, very dry, slightly breaded;
Mango Salsa: Fantastic - very sweet and had a nice, slow heat
Tres Leches : Nice and moist - honestly, one of the best I've had

There were very few waitstaff and there appeared to be too many tables for them to cover; we even had to flag the waiter down to get water and the bill.

Will I go there again? Probably not.  
Would I recommend it?  Probably not.  
Would I decline to go if others wanted to? Probably not.

Well we had their breakfast and it was decent. It's location is pretty cool as it's in the industrial area under a bridge like what you would see in the movies in other cities. Our waitress was nice and quick with our orders & demands ha! I guess the highlight was when all the kids got their leftovers wrapped in a foil dragon, scorpion and palm tree, all of which provided entertainment for the young'uns in the car! I'll have to try this place again to give it a fair assessment especially since it features frog legs...say what!

The Good:
I ordered an avocado sandwich and that was tasty. I will end up giving this place another chance based on the sandwich alone as I was not impressed with anything else.

The Bad:
I ended up throwing away the crispy soy chorizo and potato tacos after two bites. When my order arrived it was already cold and the tacos were soggy. However, I will blame that on Grubhub being slow with the delivery. 

The Ugly:
Tacos were swimming in a pool of grease! With a name like Mr. Natural I was expecting something healthy not something so inundated with oil I needed to blot it with a napkin first. They should also consider separating the rice and beans from the tacos. Unless of course you don't mind picking up your tacos and getting refried beans all over your fingertips.

You usually can't go wrong with a Marriott and this place has most of the basics of a nice place.  Most but not all.  There were little things that were a little disappointing.  For instance you had to go get a coffee from the bar/restaurant instead of having a station to help yourself.  Also the drinks were very expensive and didn't leave an impression. No real complaints otherwise just nothing sticks out to make it a cut above.  Other places in town struck me as more aesthetically pleasing

I visited Moksa with a few friends in early May.  It was a Sunday evening and the back restaurant was jammed. We sat in the front bar area and shared 4 or 5 dishes. The Vietnamese spring rolls were outstanding, as was the Shao Bing. Blackened fish roti also a stand-out. Less thrilled with the dumplings. Wines by the glass list a bit thin.        I think Moksa is a work in progress; not where it could be but clearly not the disaster the Globe and other Yelpers depict. Great location, reasonably priced, welcoming service, interesting menu items...i'll give it another go-around in June.

I was at Kika tonight with a group of about 15 people.  I love Kika, I love the food and the Sangria, but the past two experiences I've had there have been less than stellar.  Tonight before we ordered one woman in our group was very politely asking the waiter about being able to split the bill by groups of 5 of us so that we would have 3 separate bills.  He very rudely cut her off several times and kept saying "don't worry about the bill, just enjoy the food."  At the end of the meal, he of course brought one bill for our entire table and told us he could only run 6 credit cards.  This would not have happened if he had let us finish our sentence in the very beginning. Don't cut off someone when they are politely asking you a question, don't assume that you know what is being asked.  Incredibly rude and then incredibly pushy about wanting us to order more food when everyone was satisfied with the amount they had ordered.   This was completely infuriating and rather sneaky and pushy.  I'm not sure I'll be going back anytime soon.

Overpriced. Which doesnt mean that the food isnt great, it just is over the price at which it should be. 

With an air of romanticism and modernity the decor seems to fall below its own standards. The restaurant was really neither, it was an attempt, and quite a feeble one as a place where you could take a date or your cool friends. 
Overall though, the place was clean and tidy, no item really stood out. The waiter was friendly enough and acknowledged that he had an idea about the menu. One dish out of the three entrees came out substantially later than the other two, that is a big problem, a huge mistake, the waiter should hold the other two plates in the kitchen, where it would be warmer than sitting in front of you. 
The venison stroganoff did not have the correct consistency in the sauce nor in the meat, but had good flavor regardless. The ragout and confit of the second dish was tasty, it lacked effort in design and visual aspects. The third entree on our table was the trout, it was fresh, well cooked, and had the sides of vegetables and mashed potatoes kind of thrown in really, no time was dedicated to its presentation. Oh, right, I really liked the bread and what appeared to be a hummus spread, it was the best done part of the meal. The water glasses were definitely too small, modernity should not lack comfortability or utility in restaurants, we go to eat and relax and have a good time, not drink shots of water with constant advisory to fill up all the glasses on the tables. The drinks were whatever, nothing special, the margaritas served in rocks glasses, the beer had a bit too much of head on it, which is fine really. 

The unmarked bathrooms are obnoxious, please, no one needs to have to ask where the restrooms are, its annoying and slightly uncomfortable. Out of the 8 tables in the house, 6 were occupied, and this was during normal dinner hours, its a good thing 4 more people werent eating there, or else we wouldnt have gotten a seat. I cant recall anything that stood out positively really, the lack of range on the menu really surprised me, and at that, it was limited in quantity and quality. 

all in all, it wasnt worth the money, but it was food in a centralized location, with warm tones that can welcome you in

We've come here multiple times and have ordered the eggplant bharta, the butter chicken, the palak paneer. The reason why I'm knocking some stars off is because of the chicken in the butter chicken. It's usually very dry and the sauce to chicken ratio end up not being right because you end up having to cut open and smother the chicken in sauce. So maybe they can make the chicken cubes smaller or add more sauce, or I don't know but in that regard they could definitely improve. Additionally the sauce that came with the lamb curry had oil separation and was rather oily so maybe use less oil or mix the oil and the other components of the sauce better ?
The flavours are good though ! And you can ask for everything at different levels of spiciness and they've always been pretty spot on in that regard.

The experience was just ok. There does not appear to be a full kitchen for the meals prepared. There was only one person behind the counter assembling food so the French toasts reached the table cold without the bacon which arrived cold five minutes later. The place is small and seating is at a premium as people hang out on the free wi-fi occupying seats. Oh. Last but not least, don't forget to ask the person preparing the food to get you the bathroom key as the bathroom door remains locked.

I had sausage and cabbage rolls combo. First of all, I had a confusion between the menu and picture because number of cabbage rolls didn't match. Correct answer was 4. A Sausage, 4 cabbage rolls, coleslaw and sour cream.
The owner told me I was the first person who asked and he didn't noticed the mistake even he ran the business few years. Really?? 

Sausage was alright. Nothing special. I loved their cabbage rolls. Brown rice with lots herbs and Tomato  sauce on top. I used to buy cabbage roll from Ukranian authodox church but this food truck one had more flavor. Delicious. And I'm glad they use brown rice for it.

It hurts me to have to rate Grezzo so low.  I'm a strong believer in the raw food diet, and while I don't follow it strictly, I am vegan and make it a point to eat as many raw foods as possible.  I found out about this lifestyle year or so ago from Alissa Cohen's (owner) website and became completely obsessed with the "Raw Food Talk" message boards (a great place to find out more about the raw food diet, if you're interested).  I was ecstatic when she opened her first restaurant so close to me, so when my dad expressed interest in raw foods, I jumped at the chance to finally try it.

The location is wonderful - a couple blocks off the main streets of the North End, I almost felt like I was back in Rome.  The atmosphere is dark and quite cozy, and shuffling the clunky chairs around to let others in/out of their seats can get kind of annoying, but that's the least of their problems.  It's obviously a small space, so it's inevitable the chairs and tables are going to be close together.

The problems come with how they handle the flow of people in their space and with their service in general.  A few minutes before 9pm, several groups of people arrived (they take reservations at 5, 7, and 9pm - it seems like they should stagger their times a little to avoid a sudden, disruptive influx of people like this), leaving at least 10 people crowded by the door/three surrounding tables, letting a freezing cold draft into the entire restaurant.  The group of six that had entered first was asking to be seated for their 7pm reservation.  All the tables were full at that point, but instead of being turned away, or asked to wait until others with reservations were seated, they were given room/seats at the bar to wait for the next open table.  The next group actually had a 9pm reservation, but because there was no room for them to wait inside, the waitress/acting-hostess suggested a cafe down the street to wait in until she called them.  The total downpour certainly did not help make this option any sunnier.  In this situation, it should have been the people on time who got first priority, and the group 2 hours late should have been asked to wait elsewhere.  The whole point of a reservation is that there will be a table available for you at a specific time.  Grezzo's lucky so many people are eager to try raw food, because at any other place, I know at least I would've just left.

That fiasco didn't have anything to do with me, except that the scene unfolded a few feet away from me, but the service was just as airheady for us.  Our waitress, while very smiley and friendly, constantly talked AT us and rattled off ingredients so quickly I couldn't even process what she was saying.  She also would come over and say something like "I'm so glad you're enjoying the food" without actually asking.  Just because I'm eating it, doesn't mean I love it.  She wasn't great about answering questions, especially when it came to explaining what ingredients are.  They should realize they're many of their customers have not encountered all of their ingredients before and should take the time to explain what things actually are in a way everyone can understand, particularly when asked.

The food itself was completely dynamic.  The flavors of fresh foods was so powerful, though at times overwhelming.  This is not the fault of Grezzo, and not something they should change.  For me, this really highlighted how limited and bland my own regular diet is.  I loved experiencing such a high level of food creativity.  I got the tasting menu and was glad I did.  It was a LOT of food.  The portions are not huge in the sense that you'll get 1 lb. of pasta on a serving platter all to yourself, but the dishes are very nutritionally-dense leaving me with a very full (but not too full) belly.  

The food at Grezzo renewed my enthusiasm for raw foods and I'm thrilled it's so close by.  However the service really needs to do some reevaluating in how they interact with customers and how they control the incoming flow of patrons, especially when it comes to reservations.  Also, it'd be great if they rethought the bulky acrylic menus.

9 Mile Station is definitely worth a visit for the views of the Atlanta skyline. If it weren't for the prime time location, though, I'm not so sure I would recommend it. We visited for brunch on a Saturday, and while our service was good, and the food wasn't particularly bad, nothing really stood out either. In our experience, the plates are all extremely overpriced for overcooked meats and under seasoned flavors. If you choose to visit, expect to be paying for the experience more than for good food. I'd say it's worth visiting once, but I don't think we loved it enough to come back any time soon.

We has a fun time on this tour.  Our guide was adorable and informative.   I called the day before to reserve a "handicap" tour due to having one person on a scooter and one with a walker.  I did not want to take up the limited "handicap" spots with able bodied people so we reserved 3 spots and figured the rest of us would do the walk down.  When we got the tickets,  they let all of us go on the "handicap" tour together otherwise we would have been separated.  They fail to inform you that the 8 flights of stairs are not descended consecutively.   Handicap parking is non-existent.  Plenty of shopping post tour and they even have a post office on site so you can purchase and send you post cards in one spot.

I have never been to Chili's before, fearing it was too spicy for me (the logo has a hot pepper on it after all). And this despite the fact there is a branch about 2 miles down the street I live on. I finally stopped into the Danvers branch today because a friend had a gift card and wanted to treat me to lunch.

All in all, I was impressed. The waitress was very pleasant and helpful. The food came quickly (perhaps too quickly...see below), and my meal was very nice. I started with a "house side salad" which was practically a meal in itself and very fresh. This was followed by a Margharita flatbread, which was delicious. Now obviously my choices were not "tex-mex" but they were very good.

My partner for lunch, however, was disappointed with her meal. She ordered the "smoked bone in wings" and a salad for lunch. The wings were on the menu as "Bone-in wings slow smoked in house over pecan wood. Served with Chili's classic BBQ sauce". The wings were not smoked, they were deep fat fried and had absolutely no seasoning on them at all, let alone the "smoked" seasoning promised. And the "classic BBQ sauce" was plain old ketchup with no BBQ taste whatsoever.  There were very few customers in the restaurant, so there was no real reason to take a shortcut and fry the wings.

So, a mixed review: my lunch was excellent, my companion's was not at all as advertised.

I decided to check out The Whip a few months ago for brunch and was not disappointed! Although I've been to better brunch spots, The Whip has a lot of offer on its own in terms of atmosphere, vibe, and taste. The restaurant itself has a cool, hipster vibe with neat decor inside. 

The food itself is just decent. Nothing amazing that wows your tastebuds. I ordered quite a bit. Eggs benny, poutine, parfait, a wrap, and French toast. I wish I had more to say about their food but it was really just mediocre. The French toast was amazing though. So out of all the dishes I ordered, only the toast left a lasting impression.

So let me start by saying that we went here for the burger, and to our surprise they now only offer 24 burgers per service. So when my husband ordered it the server was all like "uhh duhhh we only have 24 and we've been out for like at least 3 hours" Complete with EYE ROLL. Ok. So first there is no burger. Then there is a burger after 10. Then you can get the burger whenever you want. And now there are only 24 and you have to fight Hunger Games style and make 5pm reservations. So long story short if you want the burger go to Ponce City Market or a Braves game. I mean I've had it here before and it's a really good burger, but I don't get what the big deal is but whatever. 

Before the burger debacle we had a charcuterie plate which was above average. I ended up with flank steak and my husband got the half chicken. We also split the the sweet potatoes. We both really enjoyed our meals, buttttt it wasn't what we went there for. I get you don't want to be a burger joint, but it's confusing when the rules keep changing. Also the delivery of the "we only have 24" was full of attitude which is probably why I was irritated enough to write a review.

The baby-back ribs had so much potential, but they were pretty dry. I think my bf got the BBQ chicken, which was so succulent and awesome. I spent most of my time on his dish, haha. My mint julep and his whiskey shot were pleasantly served. When we were done eating, it took us 15-20 min for us to catch our waitress's attention (this was after we had both stood up and started to pack to leave). I would sympathize with the busy waitress, but she passed our table a few times and didn't think to check on us.

I would only come back for their happy hour.

I went to Eddie's V's to treat my friend.  The server was attentive and friendly! He was very helpful.  The three stars is for the food.  I ordered the yellowtail sashimi and the dish was warm.. I was a bit concerned.  The crab cake was dry and the flavor was underwhelming.  The crab fried rice was fried rice with crab meat on top.  I thought the crab meat would be cooked with the fried rice. I ordered the Chilean sea bass and it had potential to be more flavorful.  It sat at the bottom of a bowl in liquid.  I'm dairy free, so the dairy free options were very limited.  Flavors were mixed berry, passion fruit and mango, store bought flavors.  I really wanted to give Eddie V's 5 stars, however, the food was not 5 stars.  The service was :)

Two recent visits to No Mas were as different as night and day and consistency may be the biggest challenge facing the restaurant.  The most recent visit restored our faith in No Mas.

Previously, service was robotic and awkward and our server lacked the most basic social skills.  The owners were in desperate need of training for their service staff.  This time we had a delightful waitress who engaged in our playful banter and provided seamless, relaxed service and it definitely made for a more delightful meal.

On an earlier visit, the atmosphere was raucous, the restaurant filled with groups of 10, 12, 20 or more celebrating birthdays, a girls night out, prom dinner and any occasion where more's the merrier.  Our two top felt terribly out of place.  This time the restaurant was festive but filled with more traditional groups of three or four, although as the night wore on, tables were being pulled together for parties of 10 and 15.  And atmosphere is important here, with eye-popping décor making it unique and unlike anything else in Atlanta.  The owner's passion and love for all things Mexican is evident in the details used to carry out the theme.

Our table commented that on previous visits our food was decent, but not dazzling, and while we liked it fine, other Mexican restaurants had more flavorful food that satisfied us better.  This visit, though, provided the best food we've had yet.  We started with chips and salsa - light, crispy chips accompanied by a bowl of smoky chipotle salsa.  We added a guacamole appetizer, a bowl of creamy, slightly chunky avocado with a pile of diced tomatoes on the side plus a lemon wedge.  We mixed it all together and three baskets of chips later we testified that this was one terrific appetizer.

Two of us got the combination platter, where you put together your own mix of tacos, enchiladas and tamales with a choice of sauces.  I got the Playa del Carmen, a plate that comes with two shrimp enchiladas with a light cream sauce, plus a fried fish taco.  I kept the rice but subbed mixed veggies for the refried beans and they were superb.  All-in-all a lighter meal that was full of flavor.  Perhaps new hands in the kitchen are better equipped to deliver great Mexican food.

We used a $30 Groupon with no problem and since another one of our party bought the same Groupon, we'll be returning again and reporting on whether they've maintained the higher standard.

I have been going to this place for years. The food quality ebbs and flows, but is mostly good. They have a great veggie mezza platter, great labneh and kabobs. The staff seem to change frequently which effects the service which is often slow and somewhat poor, but the prices are reasonable. There is lack of consistency both in service and food which I think is the main issue, but if you have hankering for Lebanese  food this is good place to get your fix.

Beauty is in the eye of the beholder.  And the Orlando eye is no exception.  If you are a Florida native, you may find it a little cheesy with hazy vistas of other Florida theme parks and miniature downtown Orlando buildings.  Or if you are a tourist this would be just another trap that you'd be happy to get caught in.

The gf and I were able to take advantage of  the "First to Fly" weekend, so we can ride it before it opens to the general public.  You get a free pin to commemorate this day along with green screen photos that are reminiscent of those cruise vacations.  You start with a 4D movie of Florida landscapes which was actually pretty cool.  Gave me a little pride for my state!  Once that's over, you are escorted to one of the pods.  Ours fit about 10 people and they so graciously stopped it from moving in order to get a grandma and her walker on there safely.  Our pad also had an attendant that answered a bunch of questions regarding the structure of the Orlando Eye and any other points of interest that you can visibly see.  They say you can see Ft Lauderdale on a clear day.

Once the 20ish minute ride is over, like any other good amusement park/attraction, it takes you to the souvenir shop.  You can buy your green screen photos complete with a binder of more Florida facts.  Or you can buy pencils, teddy bears, mugs, etc at the shop.  I was upset that the frame that they were selling wouldn't fit the picture that we bought....fail.  After it was done, we went for ice cream at the nearby Ben & Jerry's and took in the remaining hours of daylight on the softest astroturf I've ever sat on.

So anyway, pretty cool.  I'm sure it's going to be one of those, one and done things that each Floridian will need to do sometime.  If i end up going again, i'll probably try and go at night when they light up the wheel.  I'll probably also wait until the new shops and restaurants open.

The best thing this place has going is the $10 burger and flight deal.  You can get a good burger with fries and a flight of five 6oz pours for ten bucks.  The tap list is usually pretty decent with plenty of stuff from Sam Adams, Long Trail and other New England breweries.  

I recommend John Brewer's for a good local place to watch the game.  They have about a million TVs and are well staffed with attentive waiters that never let your glass go empty.  They usually have the sound on for all the big games too.  The crowd is usually pretty fun with not too many bro-dudes.

Dazzling Café is a beautifully decorated restaurant that is perfect for bridal parties and special occasions because it is just such a photogenic restaurant.   We came without reservation and were able to get a table in about half an hour. The food is actually quite delicious as my friends and I ordered 4 different dishes to share.  We ordered 2 pastas and two pizzas to try.   We enjoyed all the dishes, but particularly enjoyed the truffle duck pizza.  We also ordered a dessert to share. The portions were quite small especially for the boys. But it was a decent amount for the girls. 

My only complaint would be that the service was a little irritating. I understand that they were busier as time went by, but trying to take our plates before we are finished eating is a little to much. Not once, not twice, but three times.  When we finally finished, we ordered the dessert and it took forever to come. So rushing us to finish our entrees was truly obsolete. 

With that being said, I would still go back hopefully things have settled down and service will have improved!

Really want to give more stars... They've done a ton of work in just a few years and the place looks great!  They're off the Beltline and there's a cute patio and juice/coffee bar.  But they're very laid back, verging on unprofessional. I've made several purchases here over the last six months. At check out, the associates are always talking to each other and not the customers (the only exception was when I started a conversation first).  Also, throughout all of my purchases, no one ever told me that there are only 24 hours to return (until I came in to return something).  Hopefully they will fix these issues, as I really do love the place and all the work they've put in.

This is definitely not the location you want to go to if you've never been to Kerbey Lane. Otherwise, you probably wouldn't understand why there's always a long wait here. With the other locations around Austin, in particular the old location that was across the highway, it's mostly justified due to the much better food and service. And being open 24/7 is nice. 

For some reason, this one has the same long wait as the other locations, but not very good service and just average food. It's not bad by any means. But they seem to be having some management issues at this particular location. They've mentioned that when there are long delays from the kitchen (for various reasons), they won't fill the building to capacity. So people will just wait despite empty tables. 

When we have managed to get seated in a reasonable amount of time, the food has been generally fairly good. Not great, just good. Although they've always had much better breakfast items than lunch/dinner. Which I always recommend. Once again, not your typical Kerbey Lane experience. 

So if you decide to stop by and notice empty tables and people waiting, I'd suggest going elsewhere unless you have a whole lot of time to kill. Otherwise, it's alright.

This place can be found in a very dark damp basement in Government Center. I've only gone here after work for some drinks and an app or two. I can highly recommend the macaroni cheese, but that is basically it. The drinks are on the cheaper side especially for the area. So if you are in the mood to get a quick drink or bite to eat and then split, here's your place. Don't make it a date place though. It's too dark and tiny and cramped. Also the service is not very impressive.

A great new place!  I don't know what a gastropub is, but I certainly love the Biltmore.  It gracefully replaces its crusty predecessor with a combination of casual hipness and tasty comfort foods.

Portions are generous and reasonably priced;  standouts include the cured meat appetizers, meatloaf, and the mussells.  Also, try the mixed drink concoctions such as the Bourbon Smash and Potomac Wave.

Only negative is that its slightly loud but I can overlook that given everything else.  Definitely worth a trip.

This is a good location for a little night club. There aren't any others really around that area. There was a line to wait in which caused some people to leave and cover charge. The people in the club were all very young. I would say 19-30ish but mostly early 20's, when I went.The club in small but looks cool. 
My drink was over priced and unusually small. There was no where to sit. The music was fun but a bit predictable. Those who where there seemed to be having a good time dancing. Mostly people in their early 20's. So if you only want to dance it's a good place for that.

I came here with three girls on a Sunday. This place I believe closes at 2 and we got here almost at 1 pm, so we figured we won't have much time to sit and chat, but this wasn't the case.

Just like many brunch places, this place usually has a long line on the weekends, but since we got here relatively late, there was only one couple ahead of us. However, we still got to wait for quite some time and weren't shown to our table for a while. 

This place is somewhat small and definitely looks cute. Even though we were there relatively late, it was mostly full. Once we got our menus, which did take a while, I realized that my picky-ness, lack of fondness towards brunch food, and the fact that I had brunch food the day before are enough for me to decide to order a few separate items from the "sides" menu. I ordered a plain bagel with cream cheese with tomato on it and a side of home fries. The bagel was ok, but I didnt get to really tell since it was toasted, it annoyed me a bit because I wasn't asked whether I wanted it toasted or not. The home fries were more like crispy potato wedges, they were ok but not much better than that.

It took the waitress a very long time to get our food to us, and a couple who ordered after us got their food before us. It also took her a while to give us our check as well. Although I did like the place, the service was really disappointing and the food that I did try was not impressive. I would however recommend trying their specials that are listed on the wall, they seem to be a win.

I got delivery here for the first time and delivery service was very fast the sushi was still cold while the udon stayed hot. The sushi itself was ok, I would go back for sushi for emergencies only! Emergency meaning I need a very quick sushi fix without leaving the comfort of my couch. It is very cheap here I got a sushi plate of 10-15 pieces for only $16. BUt again the quality is ok so you get what you pay for. 
The stir fried udon was not all that great it served its purpose but lacked flavor and the udon was slightly undercooked. 
Overall I would order here again but it will not be my go to place for sushi.

Here just for the weekend and was excited to find a Japanese place near the Airbnb. Needed a quick break from typical BBQ so decided to come check out Kemuri. We walked in (2 people) on a Friday night without reservations at 9pm and were seated within 15 minutes. In the meantime we grabbed some beers and really enjoyed the ambiance of the patio initially and the inside as well.

3 stars because the menu is quite limited. For a yakitori place I was pretty surprised by how there were about 10 skewer options on the menu. Thankfully they had staples such as beef tongue and chicken heart and things like that. The skewers we got: beef tongue, miso scallops, chicken + leek, head-on prawn, and chicken meatball. Our favorites were the first two. Skewers come on 1 stick so keep that in mind if you're sharing.

Other delicious things: the guaca-poke was really good. Fresh zesty guac, raw tuna + sesame oil, some pickled shallots and radish were a nice touch with crunchy pita-texture chips. We also shared their original ramen which was not bad - I liked the heavy helpings of green onions and thought the sweet egg was top notch - also points for creativity with adding a smoky piece of pork to flavor the soup.

We also got a hamachi sashimi special with a smoky chimichurri sauce which was interesting but the teeny-tiny portion was disappointing. Sashimi portion was like the size of my thumb.

I regret not getting the street corn because pictures look amazing. Good news is if the wait is long - there is an outdoor area where you can chill on some drinks.

We arrived before our reservations after the Bruins game on Saturday afternoon. It was very cold and windy out so we were glad they could seat us. That always gets stars in my book.
They gave us a great table in the corner next to the heater.

The food was very good. Our entrees were very good. It was hit and miss on the apps, though. The warm caprese salad was very good. However, the crab and asparagus was a miss..big miss. It just didn't taste right. 

The service was very good until the place got very busy and then we noticed gaps in the visits to our table. Gaps were you order another glass of wine  coffee, dessert etc. Because of these gaps we just grabbed the check and didn't have dessert.

I could give it a half star more if I had passed on the Crab-Asparagrus app. I could  give another half star if the service level remained at the level we had for 2/3 of our visit, but it was what it was.

I've been waiting for my chicken sandwich and Mac and cheese for 1 hour and 15mins now. The restaurant has been officially closed for 31 mins. The kitchen has been backed up. They were having a hard night. I realized that; even though I was hungry I still waited. I prayed with the waitress and manager plus left a decent tip. If we as consumers how a little patience and Courtesy every now and then, we may be able to see it from a different perspective. I'll go back, just not that late anymore

Lobster Mac and Cheese. Just so good. I don't know if someone can finish an entire bowl. The rich sauce and noodles made this mac and cheese a must.

The other foods at the fat cat were great to try. We ordered 4 dishes and split it among ourselves. 

All the other food is just as delicious.

Although, I wish the wraps were warm or toasted. They tasted a bit dry.

Try to make reservations, this place gets busy!

Try the fried pickles. It is yummy!

Happy Eating at the fat cat.

I'll say it- it was way better when they had the arcade.  The bowling lanes are very nice, don't get me wrong, probably some of the classiest bowling around....but, alas, its still bowling.  (The videos they show above the lanes can be a bit unnerving at times....)  Its still a fun place to come with a group, especially coworkers, as the billiards and bowling are a good focal point.  I always feel as if this place is empty when I come here though....perhaps because its so big?  

I did come here at night once and my friends and I found our way to an uninhabited balcony which was nice on a summer evening.  I don't think I could ever find it again though.

The soups are amazing! My favorite is the lobster bisque, it is very tasty with large chunks of lobster. 

That being said, their online ordering system may be easy, but my order has yet to be correct. I've ordered online a few times because I like to just go in and pick up, like Panera.

The last time I ordered online I ordered a sandwich add romaine and a cookie. I checked out online and paid before getting there. When I went in my order was ready. Great! In and out and back to work. I glanced in the bag and noticed there wasn't a cookie, I asked about the cookie and they said they forgot to make them today. Not sure why it is an option online and they gave me my order and said it was ready. They offered me a brownie instead and gave me a few extra punches on the punch card. Crisis averted, I got a brownie instead of a cookie I'm good to go.

I get back to the office and begin to eat my sandwich. I got the 3 cheese pesto add romaine. Well the cheese wasn't all the way melted and there was no romaine. Just my luck.

I will be back for the soup, but I will not order online ever again.

I was here with my dinner club. They offer valet parking at their circle drive, but many of us took the risk and parked at the shopping center next door. *shh* Don't tell. Luckily, we weren't booted or towed. There are some doors on that side of St. Cecelia, but don't try to enter that way. You can only enter/exit from the main doors at the circle drive. We had great seating at a long table with view of the kitchen since we were such a large group. That was nice. We started off with some focaccia bread. I wasn't a big fan as I like my bread more fluffy rather than dense. For my main dish, I got the good breed chicken with potatoe puree. I wasn't a fan. I ordered brussel sprouts as a side and these were fine though not great. Cannoli to wrap up the night. It had LOVELY presentation (wow!), but again was OK, but not great.

Normally I tend to shy away from reviewing food court restaurants because you tend to get what you expect. Cheap food, cheap taste, and a full stomach. I had high hopes here though given the mostly positive reviews. 

One of the first things I noticed was that they put lettuce, tomato, and mayo on their sandwiches. So it was odd to order a Cuban and have to ask for those things to be left off. The sandwich itself wasn't bad, but it was rather dry. It came with no mustard on it, and the bread was toasted to the point where it was a bit chalky. Again, it's a food court sandwich so it's not like I was expecting the world here, but I think it's fair to be objective about it. 

I'd most likely give it another shot someday, but I'd probably ask for a few things to be added to it (mustard, butter, etc) to make sure I get a more classic Cuban.

At the end of a long day exploring Epcot, we ended up at Nine Dragons (using the Disney app, we made reservations a few days prior that ultimately proved unnecessary as the restaurant was not busy at 5:45 PM on a February Thursday). We were seated quickly and the restaurant did fill up quickly around us. The menu is fairly limited, but standard Chinese favorites are accounted for. We had the pan fried dumplings and the pork belly bao to start. Dumplings were fantastic. The bao had too many toppings. There were the crunchy sesame sticks and red onions...when all it really needed was the delicious sauce and a bit of cabbage for crunch to be perfection. The buns were perfection.

For my main meal, I stuck with the tried and true honey chicken (which came with a small side of white rice and a little bowl of asparagus tips). I wished for more rice to go with the enormous portion of honey chicken (truly, it tasted just like a nugget dipped in sweet and sour sauce). Bae got the fried rice and said it was a decent fried rice (he ate it all, so no complaints, obviously). We skipped dessert in favor of finding something sweet in the park.

Service was excellent and our waiter was very pleasant and quick to refill our drinks. Ambiance was nice, pretty standard Chinese decor (a little flashier than back home - in a good way). We enjoyed the escape to the A/C and getting off our feet. It was certainly an enjoyable way to end our Epcot escapade.

Ate here with a friend two weekends ago. Overall experience was satisfactory. I ordered the chirashi bowl, we shared the brussels sprouts, and my friend had the Nature  Boy  Roll and Alaskan Roll. 

While food was decent, I was disappointed with the service. Our server was very difficult to understand and not clear about order changes, etc. My friend is gf, which I know can be difficult to handle at a restaurant, but at one point when she ordered a different roll our server just never brought it. Turns out it couldn't be made gluten-free. That's fine, but he never communicated that to us so we never knew until much later into our meal. 
My Chirashi bowl was decent - a bit on the smaller size for the price. Fish was good but the slices were very big for sashimi. 

I'd eat here again if someone really wanted to, but this will not be my go-to sushi place. Too bad, it's got a great name.

I work nearby so this sushi restaurant occasionally makes the lunch circuit. 

Proving that everything is relative, this place seems to do OK primarily because Kishapoppo is the only other establishment in the area that serves sushi. And I use the term sushi loosely to describe whatever it is Kishapoppo puts on your table.

I usually come here for lunch. My lunch crew walks here (takes about 7-8 minutes each way to walk), eats lunch and is back in the office within an hour. I haven't experienced the food being slow, but we do tend to leave for lunch @ 11:45 so we can get served before the lunch rush.

The Bento boxes are OK and they are priced appropriately. I do really like the Kamikaze specialty roll - it has great presentation and flavours.

It's clean and it has a pleasant atmosphere. Overall it's OK. If you are going to trek somewhere for sushi, don't go out of your way to come here. But if you're in the area and want sushi it's a decent (and really the only) option.

Ugh, I'm torn about this place. I like the general set up of the venue and it's pretty and has a bouncy floor BUT it's sooo hot in the summer due to no air conditioning and lack of ventilation and/or fans. Also hate that they separate the booze drinkers in their own tiny corner from everyone else. Also hate that during Friday night shows you'll be able to hear the Friday Night Video Dance Attack music bleeding into the show you PAID money for. BUT they get some GREAT acts. I guess I'll suck it up until a better venue opens up.

Lesson Number One:  Don't try and be cool by only asking for chopsticks to eat your to-go salad with.  Salads aren't meant to be eaten with chopsticks.  You will look like a fool.

Lesson learned, I certainly enjoyed my Thai Beef Salad much more that I was expecting to.  This salad looks rather petite in the box, but it is chock full of crispy beef, shelled edamame, cabbage and lettuce, cucumbers, and delicious rice sticks.  I asked for the dressing on the side, but ended up using both containers because it was so darn good.  Light but spicy, it added a nice tingle to my lunch.

The coworkers sometimes like to eat here, so I jumped at a gift card from Half Off Depot when they were posted a couple of months ago, which basically cut the cost of my $9 salad in half.

Doc Chey's also had the most delicious fortune cookie I have ever had.  Usually I don't eat these little guys, and just check out the fortune.  But Doc Chey's fortune cookie was perfect: buttery, crispy, and sweet.  And now I know that I "will be happy (my) husband/wife."  Uhh, good to know?

I was so excited to go try this place with my daughter and her boyfriend while I was visiting from Los Angeles.... the drinks were delicious and to our pleasant surprise, we landed at our table just as happy hour started!  Unfortunately, our waiter was not near as excited about us being there as we were.  He seemed like we were bothering him the few times he did come to the table.  
This place has good food, great atmosphere, and all that is overshadowed by crappy service.  
The nice guy that delivered each of our plates was all smiles... perhaps they should consider switching that arrogant,  crappy waiter with the perky and happy guy!

Fix your service!!! Love the burgers, but your counter staff has screwed up my orders on three separate visits this week (I caught two errors before I left and 1 that I didn't). Also, if I have to pay an extra dollar for Peter Luger's Steak Sauce please put enough in the to-go cup to cover my burger. I'm happy for the option, but please make it worth it. I know you guys have been open for only a week but I may have to make the drive to Winter Park again for awhile until things get on track...Love, one of your biggest fans :)

Pretty hip place and the prices aren't too bad. I do like that you can get a glass bottle Mexican coca cola here. 

I only give it 3 stars because I've had a lot of Cuban food over the years and unfortunately the good here is okay. Not bad but far from great. I've ordered multiple items from here as my co workers enjoy coming here for lunch  and everytime I'm a little disappointed. The bread for media noche is my very sweet. The Cuban sandwich lacks real flavor and the chicken quarters are a bit flat on flavor. 

What is great about this place is the atmosphere and the staff here are top notch. Honestly the reason I keep agreeing to come back is I like the vibe and the staff are super friendly. I also like that it's a local joint and I'd rather send my dollars here than to the local mediocre big chain sandwich or burger franchise.

I just had to look thru the other reviews to see if I was the only person who had to wait nearly an hour for a meal. Looks like I wasn't. Yep, I totally agree with the other reviews - pretty good food, a bit overpriced and be prepared to watch your waiter or waitress sleep walk around the cavernous space while your stomach grumbles. It was maddening watching my dessert sit on the chef's counter, ice cream melting, while the server tried to figure out how to use the water pitcher. 
However, to be fair, I must recommend the steak and fries and my group enjoyed the pasta with prawns and the salmon -  very good.
Question to mgmt: Why are you spending so much money on rent only to lose customers thru such sloowww service?

I was in Vancouver for a few days and setting up a large dinner, agreed that this place was probably a good bet. Better yet, it was "Taste of Yaletown" and the prix fixe was available.  After leaving the conference centre, we drove down and got parking just in front of the restaurant in this cute 'hood.  The enclosed, brick-walled courtyard was heated and was my pick for our 6pm reservation seating.  A few of the seats were sauna-hot, though, and after a few glasses of a lovely local red wine, my seat also started heating up.  The risotto appetizer was my pick, because I figured too much creamy rice might not be the healthiest. I followed this with the fish and panna cotta.  The dessert was the highlight for me! The light panna cotta with berries and a red sauce was a perfect end to this meal. I probably could have just had that and wine!  The fish was decent, but probably not as exciting as the non-prix fixe options.  I'd go again and the service was amazing, but order off the regular menu, regardless the cost.

I live near this cute little restaurant inside a refurbished train car. I wanted to try it, so I stopped by to pick up dinner for the family. I wanted to try a bit of everything 1/2 order of rotisserie chicken, some of the lamb and porchetta and some sides. The sides I got were the Roasted Carrots and Curry cauliflower. Also ordered Pear Almond Clafoutis. The lamb was very tender and had a great flavor. The chicken was good but nothing spectacular. Sides were flavorful. The dessert was OK. Overall the food was good but very expensive for the small portions that are given. I spent over $50 and food was not enough to feed family of 4 2 kids and 2 adults. Hopefully they work out the pricing or portion sizes.

A dedicated parking lot in the back of the building was very helpful, but their back entrance doesn't look particularly welcoming -just a plain door with an entrada sign, no other clues. We went in, up the steep stairs, and were pleasantly surprised by the interior. Ordered at the bar, got our numbers, and went to sit down. The food seemed a little expensive, but I figured it would be worth it. But then we waited, our appetizers no where in sight. We got our tacos first (I did really enjoy my carnitas taco) and then finally our order of cheesy rice and queso. The cheesy rice was not good - just rice with a heaping scoop of queso on top, which did not look appetizing. The queso was just bland and boring - definitely not worth the wait and it really should have come out before the rest of the meal. All in all it was fine, but I wouldn't go out of my way to return.

I realy want to give this place a 4 star but I am going with 3. Food was really good. I am from central California and I have at least a dozen mexican food restaurants and food trucks within a mile that serve "I just crossed the border and started cooking" mexican cuisine. 

When I saw them pressing out fresh tortillas I knew this place was at least trying to be authentic. The chips were obviously homemade and fresh. Nice thick crisp texture. The tortillas were thick and not the supermarket variety. 

The meat was decent. My fiance got a chicken plate with tortillas. I ordered the pork with queso and tortillas. Both were very good.

Overall a good experience. Not the most authentic mexican food experience but certainly above average.

We heard a commercial on the radio for this place & decided to try them out. We don't have Burgerville in Vegas & Elli needed some food! The restaurant was clean, the bathrooms were not. They do have a water dispenser and allowed us to refill our water bottles while we waited to order, which was cool! 

We ordered a chicken tenders kids meal, the Tillamook cheeseburgers and a double cheeseburger meal with an Oreo shake. Elli enjoyed the chicken tenders. Our burgers were well cooked. The fries were hot & not too salty. Eric loved his shake! 

The prices are a bit high. The food was good, but not great for the prices. I love visiting local burger places that we can't get back home. 
Most of the staff were very friendly, but the guy who served our food was not. He threw the baskets on the table and he didn't even respond when we said thank you, MULTIPLE times. There was a guy working who was singing the whole time we were there, which made me smile.

Hubby and I tried Cappa's this Sunday when I woke up starving after a late night out and didn't want to wait in line over at Blue Moon. Based on the reviews, I was worried that we'd still have a wait since we were going in at 9am on a Sunday, but there were plenty of tables when we arrive. 

The best words to describe Cappa's are fast, cheap, and O.K.

Service was good- friendly, attentive, and quick. 

Food is MAD CHEAP. our total bill was $20 and we got a ton of food. Hubby got the eggs benny and said it was "OK". Tasted good (average, not great) but was very sloppily made. I got the Two by Two with a substitution of pumpkin pancakes instead of regular. This is a ton of food. I got 2 eggs (good, it's hard to screw up eggs), Cinnamon toast (yum), homefries (bland and had this odd crunchy grill texture. Would not get them again) , and 2 pancakes. The pancakes were the highlight of the meal (thought I could only eat one of the 2). 

I'd go back to Cappa's if I were on a budget crunch or in a hurry to eat, but in the area I think there are definitely better options. Cappa's is very typical diner food.

With tickets to a show and 6:30 pm reservations I was concerned we would be rushed for time and the food & service would suffer. Fortunately that didn't happen and we had a delighful (if not a bit overpriced) meal. 

The four in our party shared dishes including small plates, an entree and salad, which included: sheimp lemongrass soup, lobster rangoon, crispy duck buns, brussell sprouts (my youngest exclaimed, upon trying these: "I've eaten for the first time"), clam cake, caesar salad and linguini with clams. It was a nice cross section of seafood with asian fused items and flavors.

Not everyone felt equally about the food save that everything was good & tasty. Nothing exceptional save the soup.

Our waiter was prompt, patient, attentive and ensured we were happy with our selections and prompt delivery.

One person in our party felt ths is more of a bar food place with their sized down menu and emphasis on cocktails of various sizes and kinds.

Our table (an open ended booth) was comfy, spacious and quiet (even though we were near the door / reception area).

LX exchange was a good place to try but with so many new spots in the area it'd just be one of many to sus out.

I've not purchased a vehicle at Kia Burlington but have been servicing my Kia there for years.

The service techs are great.  They know what they are doing and have on several occasions come out to explain the work done on the car, and to answer any questions.

As with any dealership, make sure you ask a lof of questions of the front staff regarding costs, how long the work will take, etc, so you don't have any surprises later.  It's your right to know, and it's your money and time.

Their 3.5 star rating is pretty much right on point. We had a fine dinner here, with some standouts, but the actual "fried" side of things was a little lackluster. 

We started with the burnt ends and cole slaw, followed by the chicken thigh sandwich, the fried chicken with mac and cheese, and burger with fries. The burnt ends, cole slaw, and French fries were fantastic. The main entrees were just okay. They were fine! But not outstanding. The fried chicken definitely could have been crispier, the burger was super greasy, the biscuit was very dense and a bit dry, and the mac and cheese wasn't very cheesy. 

We didn't try any of the tiki bar cocktails, which might have pushed this from a 3 to a 4. We also wanted to try some more of the BBQ items, since the burnt ends were so good. Maybe we'll return to give them another shot.

I've been going to Dr. Crook for about 6 years now. I have noticed that she can be a bit awkward in the chitchat phase of my annual exam, but that's not a big deal. I'm awkward too, after all she is about to give me a breast exam and discuss my digestive tract. Not to mention the ol' pap smear that we'll both have to endure in a few minutes.

So lets get to the meat of this review, but in vague, hazy terms so I don't share my medical problems with you people. That's my business! You just came here to hear about Dr. Crook.

I had a serious problem a few years back and instead of sending me to a specialist, Dr. Crook sent me to a surgeon. I'm not saying her decision was wrong, but I am saying that its a pattern of behavior.

This year, I had another serious problem (unrelated to problem #1). My symptoms at first were pretty nebulous, and could have been a lot of things. At my appointment, she didn't give me a physical exam. She diagnosed it as the most common option (again, not necessarily the wrong thing to do but neither was it thorough) BUT when i called a month later to say that there was no change and i was following her prescription and diet suggestions, she told me that I just needed to give it time. Another month went past. Finally I just thought, screw it. I made an appointment to see her. At this point I had done my research. I realized there were multiple tests she could have done to confirm her diagnosis. At this appointment, I showed her the list of changes I had made to accommodate her diagnosis, so she would realize that I was taking her seriously. I mentioned testing, I mentioned a referral to a specialist. She finally gave me a physical exam and immediately realized that it was probably something else totally unexpected. She sent me off to get more tests. I'm still okay with it at this point. Maybe not handled great, but we're getting stuff done. Its that when she called me with the results she said "Good news! You're not imagining things ...etc etc"

Seriously!? I knew i wasn't imagining things. That's why I ... waaaaaait... did you think I was just making it up?

Anyways, she sent me to another surgeon (still not the wrong thing to do). But now its three months after I noticed the problem and I have to get surgery. And the problem had only been getting worse for that two months that I was misdiagnosed, and the month spent with the whole surgery process.

Pros:
- She is not a bad doctor.
- She is capable.
- She will take care of you.
- She's gentle with your lady parts. Or man parts.
- Oh the jokes you can make with her name!
 
Cons:
- Diplomacy/tact not her strong point.
- Prefers surgery referrals to specialist referrals (at least in my experience).
- Needs firm responses and evidence to reconsider a diagnosis.

The location isn't that convenient for me so it's been a few years since i've been here.  I always thought it was pricey.  Fried foods are abundant but i was feeling "healthy" so i avoided them this time, but the Pappadeaux platter looked mighty good.  Started with a recommendation from the waiter who is a native of New Orleans.  He recommended the fried gator, fondue, boudin and one more i can't remember.  We got the fondue, cheesy but a little bland for me.  Dipping with french bread is a nice touch though.  Clam chowder was just ok.  I won't get it again.  My entree was a blackened catfish.  The cream sauce that they put on top was the best part.  One person got the etoufee.  It was very very good.  I think i will have one of those next time.  

overall, it was pricey and ok.  Not gonna make my starting rotation for places to take my friends who are visiting town though, but a nice change of pace.  Few cajun choices here in atlanta.  

3 adults who were hungry left full with take-home boxes for $115, no alcohol.  I was so full it hurt to sit, and then it hurt to stand.  Joey Chestnut, how do you do it???

Not a fan.  Calzone dough was just like a lazy piece of pizza dough folded over, soft and deflated, nothing like  the crispy full baked dough we were expecting.  Gluten free pizza dough was served to me almost warm and with no crispness to it.  We ate in and that's obviously not their thing... no plates and plastic cutlery.  The ingredients were fantastic however, so if you order a normal pizza and take it out i'm sure it will be great.   Dont think we'll go back.

We went about a month ago when the Barton Springs neighborhood was starting to cool down a bit.  We were looking for some dessert and came across Cannone Gelato.  The lady working the truck was super friendly, inviting and down to earth.  She would kindly explain the gelato and the unique flavors.  I ordered the coffee gelato and it didn't leave me wanting more or give me the wow factor.  Don't get me wrong though, it was good but so is a bucket of Haagen Daz or Ben & Jerry's ice cream.  For the cost of what you get, some would say there is more to be desired.

Holed up in a bargain strip mall, the only way this place was recognizable was because it says Korean, Japanese and Chinese food. The restaurant name is not visible, at least that I could tell. From the outside, this place looks sketch. Once inside, it's actually really nice. They've got a variety of table types, and a full bar (didn't expect that). I ordered a bibimbap (though it's not spelled that way on their menu), which comes with a variety of banchan (kimchi, tofu, broccoli, and I think radish). My bibimbap is a little skimpy on the beef, but overall flavoring is good. The rice was a bit too mushy for my taste (cooked with too much water), but at least it wasn't undercooked and hard. The runny egg on top is definitely a nice touch, and because the rice is still relatively hot, it cooks if you let it sit for a bit. 

To top it off, they've got local craft beers on tap. I wouldn't have guessed that, but hey why not. It seems like a lot of restaurants in the Portland area do that, as well as a full bar, which I personally think they have because getting liquor in this state is a hassle to do. 

If you're in the area, and don't want to eat the mall food, this is a good place to check out.

Sat at the bar last week with a friend. We planned to eat and stay for some drinks afterwards. Our food, burger special and fried chicken, we're both amazing. Our cocktails were on point as well. The only reason this is a 3 star review is we left after eating and only our second drink because of how surly and rude the bartender, I think her name was Alyssa, was to us. She was curt and abrasive to the point that we just wanted to leave. Bad vibes in what seems like a place that would be filled with good energy.

3.5 Stars.

-Entree was the filet, which I ordered rare.  it came out medium rare, so FYI order it a temperature cooler than what you want. the filet was about 3/4 inch thick, so not quite a steakhouse cut but the flavor was good and was very fresh nonetheless. a 7oz cut. it was drizzled in a balsamic-aujus reduction, which on its own was sour, but worked perfectly with the meat. comes with two sides. got the cubed fried potatoes which were cooked with garlic also. These were very crispy but still soft and potato-y inside.  2nd side: POLENTA! this was very creamy, and buttery. but lacked some of the grainy-ness that I prefer in polentas. not very italian a dish, but if you feel like protein, do it!

-the clam linguine was a well put together dish. the clams were smoky flavored and not at all fishy, this worked great with the little pancetta cubes, and yet was not like some crazed hickory pasta. came out a bit salty, but I would definitely suggest this dish.

-calamari appetizer: blech. not breaded (which would normally be fine).  the calamari tasted fishy and was at best, shallow-boiled in a weak salt/garlic base. came with uber-burned toast that tasted like ash.  the calamari came with a cream sauce that somehow magnified the fishiness. I shudder just thinking about this dish. *cries*

-cheese plate: tasty, consisted of a soft cow ripened cheese drizzled with honey. a sheep hard cheese and a goat bleu. also an interesting fig 'sausage' (not really sausage tasting but, still enjoyed it.

we were here for a birthday and the staff was incredibly friendly and helpful with the birthday cake and our dozens of photo ops (asian girls + 3-4 cameras = danger!!) + sunburns from all of the camera flashes

It was decent. I read the reviews but still decided to go since we were right there and I didn't want to drive else where since we're not from here. Service stinks :( I walked in signed in and then was bounced around a couple tables with the gel polish samples. Then finally a lady settled in. Apparently you have to pay $1 for the file/block file and then bring it back next time you come. I thought that was weird but I guess sanitary. She started to do the gel removal with the aluminum foil. Did not give enough time and started to take them off right after she put them on. In other words she was scraping the gel or my nails. Usually if you let the acetone sit, it flakes off.... Nope. But after that with the manicure it went well and did a great job cleaning all the cuticles off and applying the new gel and making sure it's nice. So by the end I was happy with the way they look.

Atmosphere and food are good. Service can be atrocious. 

I've dined here a couple times. The food is consistent and well-prepared; the restaurant itself has a good view and the table arrangement is very cleverly thought out so everyone gets to see the water. The bruschetta appetizer is not highly seasoned (i.e. there's not a lot of basil in it) but the tomatoes in the salad are very fresh and ripe, even in winter. They were willing to accomodate special requests on both visits. 

However - even with a reservation - even with calling ahead to confirm arrival time - they have "forgotten" to seat my party. Without more than a passing apology from the front of house staff, and then with a server who claimed to be focused on turning the evening around but couldn't even manage to bring us bread. Despite being asked three or four times. Over an hour. Or water. Pretty basic things that you shouldn't have to ask for half a dozen times, especially after you've been left waiting for so long before getting a table.

Food took literally 45 minutes to come out of the kitchen that night (which, after a 30 minute wait past reservation time to get seated, plus a 15 minute wait to see a server, started to really suck). Portions are perfectly sized - not too large or small. I would've actually split a dessert under normal conditions, but I just wanted to get out of there. To top it off, their validated parking didn't work once I got back to the garage.
