The other experience was better, but the last experience really turned me off - I expected at least to have a manager stop by  and see how things turned out, but apparently no one was interested in feedback. As a consequence, I haven't gone back since.

"Good Lunch"
We did not have reservations, as our lunch plans simply evolved from my release from Florida Hospital, following a diagnostic procedure, which required me to fast. We arrived in the not-so-crowded parking lot about 1:00 PM; and, self-parked. We had just a slight wait for a table; and, we were seated in the upper-tier. The place was very busy for lunch, which surprised me this late in the day.

My wife opted for iced tea; and, I chose hot tea (no refills), in lieu of the excellent wine list. To start, we asked for the foccacia bread with rosemary butter; it was light, tender, and tasty.

For mains, my wife opted for the crispy chicken sandwich; and, I chose the jumbo lump crab cakes... both were fine; but, nothing out of the ordinary.

Service was good; but not up to the normal Hillstone standards. Paying for a refill on hot tea was a bit disappointing, although the tea was excellent. At nearly $40 per-person (with tip,) this is a "treat" for lunch; and, not a regular stop.

We went for breakfast. Saturday around 11. It was pretty empty. 

We got mochas, meh, they were fairly expensive and too sweet. But caffeinated, so that was good.

Let me start by saying my kid had one of the worst in public meltdowns she has ever had, because a fly landed on her eggs. So, this isn't necessarily a completely neutral review. There was only one little fly, it's not their fault, but my daughter just lost it. I think she had too much sugar at school at the party on Friday. I digress. 

Hubby had a Denver omelet. He stated it was underseasoned.It had red and green bells in it, which he liked. But this is the man who usually complains about too much salt. He peppered it, seemed satisfied. Had toast and hashbrowns and water.The young server came and filled our water glasses without asking. I was impressed he braved my daughter's tears and still came to the table. Points for that. 

I had a Greek omelet. It had spinach, feta, onions, and tomatoes. The omelets here are very flat, not loaded with ingredients, but the eggs were tender and nice. I liked my omelet.A little more feta might have been good  but the spinach was tasty, the onions were soft and yummy, so it was ok.My wheat toast and hashbrowns were fine. 

Daughter had ordered an omelet special, ham and cheese, which was $4.99. Nice. Too bad she didn't eat it. Her first bites seemed happy enough. Until the whole fly thing. She wound up eating my toast and jam, which she liked. Hard to mess up toast ( although we have run into that before). 

The restaurant seems a little dated,the table wasn't completely clean, and the music was awful. But the server was nice, and the lady at the register was nice, and I might go back if I can get over the embarassment of my kid's tantrum. Maybe I will  leave her at home though.

P.S. the baklava at the register looked yummy.

You know, Red Robin is the typical formula for a chain restaurant.  

They have a good selection burgers, you can basically get one anyway you want it.  They will sub a veggie patty or boca burger on anyone at no extra charge. Fries are steak fries and bottomless.  If you sub a salad for the fries with your meal I have found that they don't completely skimp out on it, it is pretty decent, although not as big as a full size side salad.

You can also sub a veggie patty or boca burger on any of the entree salads that have meat.  I haven't really ventured out and tried any of the non-burger meals as I view RR to be a burger joint and only go there for that reason.

We were prepared to love the Feisty Lamb. Actually, everything was great--from the deliciousness of the food to the friendliness of the service to the restaurant atmosphere. The only downside was the portions were so small! I'm surprised no one is mentioning this in the reviews. My husband got the pancakes and I got the meatloaf. Both were very tasty, but we were starving still--and we aren't big people (in fact I'm a 110lb Asian girl). Our bill came to $40 and with tip it was nearly $50. After leaving, we stopped at Ken's Bakery and got a sandwich and a cookie to share. I wanted so much to give 5 stars...sorry Feisty Lamb.

Visited because of their great all day combo deals and toro sashimi for under 12$. The toro was a little bit fishy but the fatty flavour definitely shined. It was quite large in size and for the price, not bad at all! For the all day combo, we got the salmon donburi which had A LOT OF RICE and 3 slices of salmon sashimi. The fish was pretty good and tasted fresh. The spicy scallop nigiri was piled high with scallops in a mayo sauce BUT the rice underneath was packed and not flavoured all that well. The chicken yakisoba was the most disappointing as it was soaked in oil and had measly pieces of overfried chicken that were mostly skin. 

Overall, I understand the draw of this chinese run japanese restaurant (good prices, large portions) but I would definitely prefer eating at hyoga next-door.

I planned a dinner with a couple of my girlfriends and I wanted to try out a new restaurant in town. Price, cuisine and location were not of concern. 

We were seated promptly for a Friday night on the east side. Our waiter Ben, was adorable and very friendly. I might of developed a small crush and wanted to ask, out of friendly mockery, if he wore skinny jeans. 

I loved that the salsa had a kick but the chips on the table were a little thick for my linking. My two friends ordered the sangria, which came in a small pitcher, enough so that they could barely finish the entire drink. The sangria was sweet and flavorful, I approved. 

I ordered the lobster tacos which came with black bean and coconut rice. The tacos were petite but filling. Pieces of lobster were cooked in a spicy sauce, perfect amount of heat for my pallet. Atop the lobster were greens and avocado. I did have to add salsa to my tacos, but that's just because I like a wet taco. 

Now the rice was on a whole different playing field. I could taste the chicken broth and coconut throughout. Now this is what I would go back for. 

My overall experience was pleasant, well except that the place is poorly insulated and I was freezing the entire time. I think we even asked if they could turn the heat on, but no such luck. I am not dying to go back but, if someone was interested in trying it out, I might tag along.

Me and my husband come here all the time. Just about every Sunday after church. We continue to come here because of the quality of the food. However the old manager that is a guy is extremely rude!!! There is also a lady manager that is older and she's rude too! The portions here can be small but still pricey and they nickel and dime you for every extra item you get. We ordered extra sauce with one of our meals today and they charged us three dollars. Extra onions....two dollars. Again we like this place because of the food quality but the portions plus the management/customer service need some help.

I think just about every time I come in here, I see at least 2 people from high school.  I would never think a chain to be a towny place, but thats really what this place has turned into.  Maybe the townies think this is what fine dining is.  I can't really talk though because I haven't dined fine enough yet either.  I think there are better alternatives for chain restaurants though.  I prefer Fridays and Texas Roadhouse to Applebees.  

The waiters and waitresses are usually over nice or really big meanies.  I like how it looks inside though.  They have light wood all over and a nice bar in the center of the place.  There are also some TVs that you might be able to catch a peak of around the bar.  

The food is satisfying, but there isn't any WOAH! factor.  They have some good lunch deals that are pretty cheap.  It's anything you would expect from an Applebees.  The appetizers are good, but typical.  I guess the big thing now is the mini cheeseburgers.  There is a good selection of entrees, but I don't think I would get steak from here.  I would rather spend the money at a steak house.  The desserts are pretty good too.  Overall, I would say the food is average.  

If you do make a stop in here and aren't from the area, beware of  high school reunions going on around you.

Seriously, it's one of the worst cocktails that has been served to us in a decade. I don't want to sound unempathetic to the Covid pandemic, everyone is doing their best. If you visit this tavern (and you should) maybe stick to beer.  I don't recall their name of the drink, but it was a loose version of a spicy Moscow Mule. Everything was off... the pint glass it was served in, the jumbled flavor profile, the flat ginger beer, etc. it tasted like a 16 year old found stuff in their parents liquor cabinet, mixed it up, saw a jalapeño and said "this could work!"  We didn't complain.  We asked for the bill & told the bartender we had reservations elsewhere.  My wife barely finished her first sip, I took two drinks to see if maybe our tastebuds were just off. They weren't. We tipped 20% and left with full drinks on the table. I'm giving them "3 stars" because it would be unfair to trash the place when I didn't give them an opportunity to correct the issue, but it was an absolute "zero star" drink. Stick to beer.

My girlfriend and I have been here a few times.  The place is moderately nice, a traditional Italian looking place, and the help is quite friendly.  You can usually get a table pretty quickly, I think because it looks like they do a bit more business in takeout than they do in the dining area.  Anyways, the first time I ate here I got an Italian Sub and Flatbread pizza.  The sub was pretty good, nothing extraordinary but a pretty good version of Italian sub.  My only real complaint was it was a bit "bready" in a sense that it seemed like there was too much bread on the bun, but a minor complaint at that.  The flatbread pizza was incredibly good and a great portion size for one person.  My girlfriend enjoyed her meatball sub but she said it wasn't particularly great or bad, just average.

The last time we were here I got the spaghetti which was decent and my girlfriend got the chicken alfredo which was slightly overcooked and had rather bland sauce.  I think this place is a bit hit or miss but it's pretty value priced and not bad if you're just looking for a quick dinner.  Just realize that if you're looking for fine Italian dining you probably should look elsewhere.

I'd recommend the flatbread deluxe pizza, it was really the best item here from the two times we've eaten here.

I have now been to Sushi House Hayakawa four or five times so I can safely write this review.  The rave reviews about this place (even from well-trusted yelpers) made me believe that perhaps I was missing something...or that I had gone on bad nights.  I haven't written anything on this place up until now because I really wanted to like this place.  However, I'm just going to come out and say it now, that it has not lived up to all the hype. 

Let's talk about the good points first.  It can be a fun environment.  The sushi chefs will sometimes play games with the patrons and it is USUALLY a very welcoming environment.  (I'll get to the "usually" later)  Some of the food is pretty good as well.  They make a nice agadeshi tofu and some of their appetizer dishes are quite good.  Strangely enough, after at least four visits, I have concluded I prefer their appetizer dishes over their sushi.

Now onto the negatives:  I haven't ever been there when the the fish was that impressive or fresh.  Initially, I thought that I was going at the wrong time of the week before a fresh shipment, but I've been there on different nights of a week.  The waitstaff also seems a bit flustered when things get busy. While everyone seems genuinely very nice and usually very welcoming, it seems that the restaurant just doesn't stay cool under pressure.  Again, the people are nice, there just isn't a great system in place.  We've had our food delivered to the wrong table and our glasses almost always empty.

Would I recommend this place? It definitely does not make my top Atlanta sushi restaurant list.  However, if you are in the area and are looking for sushi, I wouldn't write it off either.

This is an honest review - I got my lashes done by Michelle yesterday in hopes that her work lived up to her reviews online. I'm new to Austin and wanted to find someone I could trust to do a good job considering lash extensions are on the pricey end...

I wish I could say that I'm satisfied but I'm not at all. I've had two previous eyelash technicians in the past whom I regularly went to and always did a phenomenal job. They're full set price points were 125 for volume lashes and I paid Michelle 150 for a set that looks quite honestly like a sub-par at home job done with one of those individual semi permanent lash sets you buy at CVS. I honestly wish I would have done that myself rather than paying 150 dollars for the same look. I am always willing to pay for good work and would have had no problem paying that if the results matched her rates. 

The lashes were not applied close enough to the root of my lashes (which are blonde) so you can literally see a gap of natural lash between my lid and lash extensions and it looks tacky! Not professional at all!! And since they are applied this way, they twist and flip and don't sit naturally. They are also falling out quite quickly - and yes, I haven't gotten them wet or picked them or slept on them.. they're falling out because of the way they were applied. 

Also, the room / office she works out of is not relaxing or professional feeling at all. It wreaked of strong perfume and it was quite cluttered. I felt dirty there. And I'm sorry, but if you charge 150 -200 dollars for a service... this includes a cleanly, relaxing and professional environment. Which is NOT what Michelle has as her set up. It's a tiny office in a professional business building downtown. The whole thing is weird and feels very out of place. I should have gone with my gut instinct and left when I saw her work space. 

I texted Michelle, kindly explaining my concerns asking if she could squeeze me in today to fix them and I haven't gotten a response in the four hours since then. So now, I'm writing this review as a very frustrated client. At this point I would rather remove them then go to a wedding with my lashes like this.. it's a shame. And only makes me realize how lucky I was to have such talented technicians in the past. 

Of course this could be one unfortunate instance, but first impressions are lasting impressions. I don't recommend and would not go again. I work hard for my money and it sucks when you pay for a service that is less than satisfactory. If I would have gotten a response from her, I would have loved to give her another chance and resolve this between the two of us. 

Perhaps I didn't explain well enough what I was looking for but I was just really surprised with what I ended up with and not in a good way. It seems like many of my lashes are without any extensions so the entire set was sparse and both eyes were uneven in the number of lashes on each side. It feels like as soon as they start falling out they will be gone quickly as there aren't many in the first place, which is nothing like my previous experiences having lashes. 

And let me add, I tried to call and Sam (her assistant? Idk who he is) answered and when I told him (very kindly) I'm not satisfied with my lashes he literally yelled "EXCUSE ME!? There is no one better in this town than Michelle." I said okay, I'm not trying to argue with you, I'm just telling you I paid 150 dollars + gratuity for something that I'm not happy with and I was wondering if she could fix them for me today. I'm not calling to complain, I'm just asking if there is anything she can do.. he was SO defensive and aggressive and told me he will have Michelle call me when she can... and that was it. So we will see if she calls, and I will update my review according to how this plays out.

UPDATE : Michelle contacted me in a timely manner and addressed my concerns and offered to get me in and have my lashes fixed as well as pay for my parking. She also informed me that the number I texted was a landline so that was my mistake I suppose.. She made it clear than she cares about my satisfaction and wanted to make it right. Which I really appreciate and have added two stars to this review for. Unfortunately I can't get in and have them fixed before I leave for my trip and after my experience with Sam on the phone I felt really uncomfortable returning there. I hate confrontation. So I'd rather just not return and just be refunded in some way, which probably won't happen... ugh. This experience just bums me out. I hate leaving negative reviews.. but sometimes constructive criticism is needed and can be improved upon.

Who's Got Soul was voted as one of the best soul food restaurants in metro Atlanta, according to a recent AJC article. I think for the most part, they live up to that standard. Favorite menu items include turkey wings, collard greens, yams, baked chicken, pork chops, and their corn bread. Pretty much everything I've had here has been good, and the quantity matches or exceeds the price. They even recently remodeled and slightly expanded the interior. I do like how most of the food is already made, so even if there is a long line, you still receive your food in a timely manner.

My wish is for the improvement on service. It can vary, and staff appear to have changed frequently over the years we have been here. And tonight when we dined, they close at 9 pm, but they were selling out of a lot of foods by 8 pm. However, when a customer tried to eat in the dining area around 8:15 pm, they said the lobby area was closed. When we were still eating, they were already cleaning up the dining area and putting up chairs. When we left at 8:30 pm, they closed the main gate in the front, making the restaurant appear closed altogether. I just think if you close at 9 pm, you should close at 9 pm. 

Parking can be tricky during busy hours (especially Sunday afternoons). They have a parking space, but it is very limited, so sometimes people park illegally on the street to the right. Overall, this place is close to home and they have pretty good soul food, so we will see them again.

I'm really quite undecided on this place and I think that's because my experiences at A Good Yarn have honestly been extremely inconsistent. The first time I went in (broke, jobless, but still loving to knit) I asked if they had any Lion Brand. I just happen to knit a lot with Lion Brand. The woman I spoke with with very rude. She said "What?!" in almost a "how-dare-you?" tone. When I said something to the effect of, "Or...well...anything with acrylic or synthetic fibers? I don't have a lot of money right now." She responded with raised eyebrows and said "No. We don't carry that." Okayyyy....So I basically avoided this place for a couple of years.

Second time I went in, staff was almost shyly friendly. Kind of smiling, kind of quiet, not overly helpful, but rang me up with a smile when I bought some merino on sale from their sale-bin. Cool.

The most recent time, everyone was VERY friendly. But it's really anyone's guess as to what kind of service you'll get on any given day. I haven't seen the service steadily improving, is what I'm trying to say.

I have to be honest. I also echo what a lot of reviewers have said about there often not being enough of a certain color or type of yarn to complete a large project. And their selection can be iffy. Great if you have a decent amount of money, but with knitting becoming so popular among younger groups you'd have thought they would carry some more inexpensive yarns. I do most of my shopping for yarn online. I can just find a wider selection at cheaper prices. But A Good Yarn has been my main source of buttons, books about knitting, and free or cheap patterns. Sometimes I'll find good deals for smaller projects in their sales bin and a few times I've caught an employee on a good day and managed to get some nice advice about types of cast-on's, techniques, and fibers to use for certain projects.

Wow....

This location is under construction, and very poorly managed in the process.  We arrived to a notice construction starts @ 9, then find no-one present at the front desk to assist.  After an enjoyable 5-10 minute wait, I was finally greeted by a manager and checked in.  

We arrived late in the evening, as we are on a work trip, and simply needed a place to grab a bite to eat, and sleep for the night.  After checking in we planned to grab some food, and noticed the lot looked quite full.  It was then that we were notified that if we leave, we are not guaranteed a parking spot...WTF?!?!?  Furthermore, no street parking, and no alternatives provided by the desk associate.  Didn't expect I'd need to walk a mile to get some food.  


Save yourself some hassle and go anywhere else, unless you don't plan on leaving the hotel.

EDIT:  Upon speaking with the manager at check-out, we received an apology, and were informed there is additional parking available.  The night staff did not have this information for some reason.  The renovations on the interior are complete, but exterior is not expected to be for awhile.  Excluding the parking issue, this is a nice hotel to stop at if you are looking for a clean/economical stop.

This was my 4th time coming here since it opened. Usually the food is decent, their beers good, and the service terrible. This trip the service was ok. I had a mojito and another drink. Both were good. We ordered a pizza for the two of us. It was cold. I mean so cold the little squares of cheese were not even slightly melted. Its curious they didn't notice that. The dough was raw. They took it back and heated it up and brought us another complete pizza and comped us the pizza. It did take a long time. I will say that something like this has happened every single time I've been but it usually has to do with bad service. There are a lot of other really great places nearby, try Crave or Elephant Bar. Both are always good.

We found The Pinewood pleasant enough but not quite a match for all the hype.

Grits tots were delicious, a hard act for hush puppies to follow. Tasty dipping sauce.
The brussels sprouts ($7) were quite al dente, and too salty for me but just right for others. Also, the stems were left on - why? We do these better at home.
All the above served in cute galvanized pails with wooden skewers to spear them.

The beet salad ($7) was overwhelmed by too much vinegar, balsamic or otherwise.

Entree portions were too small for the prices ($22 burrata cheese ravioli was about 5-6 small ravioli, little evidence of the "asparagus confetti"; $22 trout also skimpy). 

Can't speak to the libations except that the Jackie O was too sweet for my taste and the member of our party drinking old-fashioneds confirmed that they were indeed old-fashioneds.

Service desultory, on a slow Monday night. Long wait times between visits by server, no pleasantries. Server wanted to clear plates with food still on them but left empty plates throughout the meal. Party of five, we ran out of water twice (they leave it on the table, in old liquor bottles that don't hold much).

It certainly wasn't bad but it wasn't great either. Gave this Mexican joint two tries so far.  Love the chips. They are similar to Chili's. The atmosphere is cool, kinda had a throwback feel. Staff were friendly and knowledgeable about the menu and sauces. On my third visit our waiter Chris was so much fun. Love him!It's nice you can have any sauce you want for free. To be honest though I wasn't a fan of most of them. I liked the white one and the one you have pay for (bang bang?). Both queso are awesome and so is the guacamole. I've tried the beef taco and bang bang chicken enchiladas. Both were good! Just not great. My brother had this chicken that was fried-ish (sorry I can't remember the name) and that was pretty baller just very heavy. 
I have to say they have a great happy hour situation where you can go up to this old fashion car and get unlimited chips and such. It's great! 
My husband had the mojito and it was gross. Not saying I'll never go back but there are other Mexican joints in this price range I like better.

Convenient location from my workplace. I can stop by and pick up pastries and other yummy food. Prices are a little high but worth the convenience and few choices of places in Filipino food favorites in Oregon. Try the panders all and empanadas. They also do breakfast which I thought was great if your not up to cooking and in a hurry. Overall, I am just glad that more Filipino cuisine and bakery places are opening up slowly in this beautiful and weird City of Portland.

My first experience at coast was average at best. After waiting 25 minutes at a table with not even a hello from the wait staff I debated on walking out. Instead I asked for a manager. The manager apologized and made sure we were taken care of the rest of the night. The menu looked really good but I was disappointed when most of my food was waaayyyy too salty! Thank goodness I had the bread pudding at the end if the night to make me feel better. It was the best part of my experience. At the end of the day I will give them a second chance to redeem themselves.

wife and i went to this place the other night. we both enjoyed our meals. it's no Curras by any means but was decent. the remodel was done well, not really my cup of tee but i get what they were going for. pricing was a little como se dice high. truth be told that there are some hiccups but overall a good experience. wife says 3.5 or 3.75 stars. go check it out for yourself. need to keep a restaurant in this area.

Restaurant has gone down hill in the last year.  Last three times I've been, order hasn't been right and the food isn't as great.  I think they have gotten so busy they aren't putting out the quality of food they used to. The ladies bathroom always smells like a sewer!  I had to get someone to go find out the problem and was told it backs up a lot and they have to pour something in the drain. Too close to my food to want to go back.

I got the Spaghetti Aglio Olio delivered through Caviar. The pasta didn't feel handmade. I've had hand made pasta several times and it has been light and fluffy. It almost felt like mac and cheese. The pasta was too Al Dante. The cheese hadn't melted. The garlic and seasoning was good but I felt the butter had been overdone to compensate for the undercooked pasta. I couldn't finish the food and was left feeling oily and heavy. It almost felt like having a day old dry pasta. I really wanted to like this place after having heard so much. But I don't think I'll be ordering again.

NOT entirely sure what the fuss about this place is all about.
I did venture into this store during one of my stays in Austin  (I believe it was my second time).
Considering that, by American standards, anything 50years (25 for cars) or older is to be considered antiquity, there you  have the answer to the why this store may have all the success it does have.
Prices are a tiny too expensive for the items on display. Unlike other similar stores, this establishment does pride itself of keeping things organized.
However, nothing compared to true antique-shops back in Europe, where most of what is displayed here would be considered vintage and where antiques are at least 150-year-old.

The ramen here is excellent, but the attitude doesn't really work for me -- it's just too pretentious. Both times I've been, the staff are too cool to tell you how the line works, where you can sit, what you are and aren't allowed to order with what, yet there is a protocol for all those things. Unfortunately, I haven't gotten a good vibe on either of my visits. 

The tables are communal and space is TIGHT. You will be getting up close and personal with your neighbors. They don't do take out, and the line is usually out the door when I drive past, so be prepared for a wait. If none of the above bothers you, it's definitely worth it to try their offerings, but personally I prefer to grab Michi Ramen and eat it at home.

Ohana is definitely a family affair. One of the best views of the Seven Seas Lagoon/MK entrance there is. The service, like most Disney Resort restaurants, is impeccable. Everyone was very friendly and accommodating. 

Food here is all you care to have and literally everything is brought over to you. The salad was very tasty and fresh. The appetizers were standard Asian take out type fare but were very good, we ordered a couple of additional orders. The meats (entree course) is served in a fashion similar to a Brazilian steakhouse. They were all extremely over cooked, perhaps to avoid posting warnings about under cooked food. The steak was medium well and the shrimp was very firm and stringy. 

Bread pudding was amazing! I would come here again just for that, but will skip out on the meats. It is a tad on the expensive side for poor meat taste though.

I have a fondness for this place, because a close friend and I always go here to catch up, but I have to say, the last burger I had was not good--nor was the service from the way-too-cool-I-really-want-to-be-a-musician staff.  The buns on the burger got instantly soggy, due to a lack of quality bread and overly condiment-ized burger.  I was served a Guinness by the hostess, but the waiter found this reprehensible and I found myself involved in inner-employee feud.  Also, they had the misters going full-force even though it was a windy, cooler day, so it was like eating in a rain forest, with dripping sounds everywhere from all the moisture.  

I'll still go back--but I may be favoring the Opal's on 6th.  Seems like the experience and food is always better there.

+3 for the price and my first haircut there.
-2 for those other two haircuts. 

I've been here three times so far. I don't have very long hair, but I get tired of cutting it myself. Plus, like previously said, 30 bucks for a wash/cut/style including tip is great.

The first trip was in 2007. I tall guy with a tattoo on his neck did it then. I should have got his name, because he did an amazing job! And yelled at me for having bangs, because I don't have a big forehead. He was great to talk to and made me feel very comfortable.

The second trip was ok, I don't remember who did it, but I felt comfortable with them. The layers that were trimmed into my hair were ok. Nothing amazing. It grew out well though.

The third trip was this afternoon. I got an older woman, Roza was her name if I remember correctly, and she seated me as soon as I came in. There were no real pleasantries, no chit-chat, just trimming. I explained what I'd like to see and not to make it too short. It's kind of too short. She also styled it weird. mousse and that whole 80's fluffed up thing.... I had her at least part it before I left. When I got home, I soaked my hair a bit, rubbed out some product with a towel and went to blow drying it myself. And it's uneven!!! The layering/feathering that is going on on the right side of my head is not echoed on the left, at all. In fact I don't think she even did the same thing on both side..... And she trimmed my bangs weird. I hope it grows out well. 

I must also note that I am more or less blind without my glasses, so when I do get my hair cut, I can't watch what they are doing......

-edit-
Adding two more reviews for this place. I went back again on my 4th time and got Bridget. She did a really great job on my hair and listened to my gripes about the previous encounter with Roza and she sympathized with me about it. She also told me that I have hair that is difficult for some reason. BUT! She got the light layers in, evened everything out and made sure it looked right while it was dry. 

My 5th time was ok. It was a newer girl and she talked me into the special.... I paid 20 extra dollars for results that weren't great. This is my deciding factor on not going back again, unless I get Bridget.

I'm on the fence on how to rate my W Hotel experience... 

PARKING 

Valet only. $39 per night

CHECKING IN

Check in is at 3pm. We had booked 2 rooms for a 2 night stay. We arrived at the hotel by 4pm- only 1 of the 2 rooms were ready. I had to contact the front desk at 6pm to follow up with them about the second room. To their credit, they called me right back and shared that the 2nd room was finally ready. However, the fact of the matter was it was ready 3 hours past the advertised check in time and I had to follow up with them. Major points deducted. 

ROOM

Like other Yelpers, I'm feeling the trendy decor. However, for the cost and reputation of a W hotel I found the rooms to be lacking.  Our corner suite was just a queen bed. Why-- where's the king? The room layout was odd too. Like others mentioned, it advertises "space" but the strange layout appears to just be an attempt to have a room. Certain room amenities are also missing:

- drawer space
- a KING bed-- if you're sellin' sex and mayhem provide proper spaces!
- outlets near your bed (They should invest in the nightstands or lights that have outlets. Not the cheap Ikea nightstands. This is a huge pet peeve (can't you tell- lol) and provided that Austin boasts of being such a techie city I'm taken aback with the lack of outlets near the bed.). On a positive note, they do have a charging station with hook ups for older iPhones, iPhone 6 and Android phones.
- no coffee maker 

SERVICE

- 24 hour room service
- guests can text the front desk their needs
- concierge
- the staff was friendly

NIGHT LIFE

Not a local? Or are you a local 25-40 year old? The 4 linked louges provide a energetic night spot with a little bit of something for everyone. If you're staying a night, make sure to check it out. In town or a local weary of the same "6th Street" crowd- come here.  There are 4 different rooms providing a little bit for everyone at this venue.  

Happy Hour is also from 7pm to 10pm.

LOCATION

Within walking distance to the downtown mayhem.

I've only been here a few times for takeout, but I've really enjoyed everything I've had.  It's a little expensive, but since it is so close to where I work...the convenience is worth the extra few dollars.

I do recommend getting a lunch box if you like chicken/salmon/beef teriyaki.  For less than $20 you get a decent portion of protein, rice, a pretty big salad or soup, tempura vegetables and shrimp, and california rolls.  Though the food does not completely stand out, I still frequent Haru, but mostly for lunch.

I was so excited to learn that this kind of restaurant opened in the Boston area. I am used to be a fan of Minado. This one is a little different from Minado but very similar concept, except they're serve different Japanese dishes. 

First of all, I like their decoration, cozy, elegant and relaxing. 

I also like the fact, there are partial serve yourself and partial foods for made to order. The made to order gives the customers enjoy the foods to eat freshness. 

However, I was disappointed even after when I have been said, the sashimi aren't fresh and the oyster that been sitting on the buffet counter aren't fresh. That kind of throwing off my appetite. 

The waitress who served us aren't that friendly, no smile, quite rough on us. 

I'm not sure if I will coming back again. I might give this place another chance. The price is pretty reasonable for the area.

Not very authentic and so-so tasting in comparison to Thai restaurants in Los Angeles. Since it has good reviews on Yelp, my brother and I decided to give it a try. The Tom-Kha soup..what the hell!! First of all, Tom Kha is supposed to be WHITE and not orange. I didn't taste the lemongrass, lime leaf or lime at all. The soup was supposed to be sour, not too spicy and a bit salty. All we tasted was sweet and way too much coconut milk. The soup was not supposed to be thick. It tasted more like a red curry to us. The sea bass fillet with garlic, chilli and lime (pla ma-nao) was decent.  Papaya salad (som-tum) was not bad and it came with sticky rice (kao-niew) and 3 very thin slices of pork jerky. I told them a few times not to put ground peanuts in, but they still put 2 spoonful on it. Chicken with basil leaves (pad-kra pow) was okay. 

Anyway, service was pretty good. 

I know I shouldn't compare this place to those in Hollywood, but since I've lived in Los Angeles for 7+ years and spent many years in Thailand, I know what real, authetic Thai food tastes like. It's not too bad if you like the Americanized style, but it's just not for me.

Came here yesterday with my mom for Mother's Day.
Green Ginger has a very nice ambiance with low lights, dark clean decor, and a band playing in the background. What makes green ginger stand out is their decor, and their menu. They offer japanese, chinese, and thai dishes and they also have a build-your-own noodle bowl. 
For the food we ordered crab rangoon, two sushi rolls (green ginger & heaven roll) and a chicken curry dish with brown rice.

Green ginger roll - Fresh Fish, good rice but the roll was a little loose and kept falling apart. It  was rolled in your nontraditional soy paper so I won't hold that against them.

Heaven roll - My sister ordered this. It's not my kind of sushi roll but it was good. It consisted of cream cheese, a type or raw fish, and some fried cheese on top. 

Crab Rangoon - It was okay. Cream Cheese was very gooey.

Musseman Curry- Good sauce but dried chicken. 

Service- We actually had pretty good service. The food did take a while to come out but they were pretty packed when we came in. Our server was friendly and attentive. 

We also received a mother's day gift at the end of our meal. which was nice :)

Oh man, I so wanted to like this place more than I did. I read the rave reviews about their burgers and made a beeline for it. The girl working there was absolutely lovely and kind. I had a taste of their copper pennies and they didn't blow my mind, as I hoped they would given the reviews here. And the burger - I got the chevre bacon burger - was a disappointment. The meat was the problem. It was overcooked to the point of being charred, dry, and so did not melt in my mouth. Granted, I'm a burger snob. Favorite burgers in Portland are Gruner's, Castagna, White Owl Social Club and Yakuza. I don't get the fuss about Helvetia Tavern, Slow Bar's burger doesn't blow me away, so maybe I'm picky. I like the Kuza Burger they're turning out in the parking lot near The Colony, but it only seems to be open once in a blue moon, leaving us here in St. Johns desperate for a good steady consistent burger solution. If they just fattened up that burger a bit, improved the quality of the meat, went a bit more on the rare side, we'd be cooking with gas. I'll go back one more time, try a different burger in a different mood at a different time of day and hope to add another star onto this A-OK place.

First time to FBS was for a Thanksgiving eve party. I went with a group of friends. First impressions are the location is a bit strange and difficult to locate on our first attempt, we needed to drive around the block to find it. The Kendall neighborhood is supposedly up and coming with bars and more nightlife which could benefit this spot drastically.

The interior decor is spacey and modern with some elements of street grit to go  along with the tech design aspects. The elevated Dj stand is a cool touch... We wondered all night " how the hell did the Dj get up there?!"

The bar left something to be desired. Not a great selection. Not many flavored vodkas and they don't serve any energy drinks or Heineken. Also my drinks were taxed every time I ordered, seemed a bit strange to get a bill each time for 4.36$ for a 4$ beer. Seems like a pain in the ass for the bartenders...I haven't experienced that before.  On 1 trip to the bar I asked the bartender how much my beer was to quiz him and he charged me the $4 . Seems like he just didn't want to go through the hassle of collecting change.

All in all this place is cool, haven't tried the food, one friend reminded me that it looked like Toro in boston and that it's more of a bar/ grill so i have to try the food sometime. The open kitchen is a nice touch. Judging solely on the nightlife aspect it could use some work promoting but I liked the crowd that showed up and Cambridge is awesome so it has potential.

Because I enjoyed the last visit, I decided to try them again to see how some of their other items stacked up.  The breakfast burritos are very large, but honestly?  Eh.  The eggs tasted overdone, like when there is a lot of browning on scrambled eggs.  Maybe some folks like that but it really wasn't for me.  The tortilla was also rather toothsome like it had just been refrigerated and reheated. When you pulled it apart you could see how they browned the scrambled eggs.  I guess some folks prefer it that way?

We also ordered a quesadilla (my roommate isn't too adventurous) and wow, disappointed.  :(

Listen I get it's a quesadilla.  It's cheese in a tortilla.  But after trying it, I can honestly make better ones at home.  Chipotle of all places makes a better quesadilla.  This one was folded into thirds and large portions of tortilla had no cheese at all (which is probably why they rolled it into thirds).  But because of this, large amounts were just tortilla.  The tortilla was also cracker crispy at points and chewy in others, despite both lacking cheese on them. The whole thing was just bland overall.  Again I get it's cheese plus tortilla, but it wasn't very good despite being one of the simplest things one could order.

I think Victoricos does some dishes super well.  Their street tacos (lengua, so good) were amazing.  So I'm not bashing them, but I feel like quality is really inconsistent based on what you order/when you order it. Just a little disappointing.  I prefer Don Pedro's in Portland.  They can rock a breakfast burrito and also serve menudo.

I always refer to Southpark Meadows as the place where Austin's average restaurants end up. This is no different. 

Service was friendly. I have no issue with that. Prices were steep and on par with Pappadeaux. But the food wasn't as good. 

We tried the charbroiled oysters which were probably the best of the meal. In fact, I have grilled up something similar before. The raw oysters were small and unremarkable save for the fact that this was my first venture to eat raw oysters since I became ill from a selection at Pappadeaux back in 2009. I am happy to report no ill effects here and I am back on the oyster band wagon. Port A Cafe does have happy hour prices on shrimp and oysters which might be interesting one day.

My Crawfish po boy was edible even with the crawfish being cold. I expect it's fried up in a batch, reheated later and served. Fries were hot and tasty, but I only had a few bites of those. But the price of this was a ridiculous 13.95! Compare that to Cawfish Shack and Oyster Bar on Wells Branch where a similar yet superior offering is 6.95!

My wife had a salad with a bowl of clam chowder. She always likes chowder and had no complaints. 

Happy hour does look interesting with a selection of 3 for $5 sliders made from fish. That might get me back in. For a lunch or dinner destination it's unlikely I will return.

All hype in my opinion. 

One star for originality. The super hero theme is pretty nifty.
One star for quick turnover. We only waited ten minutes on a Sunday morning when there was a line.
One star for unique eats. We had the hulk sandwich made with a green waffle and the breakfast pizza. The sandwich had candied bacon in it and was drowned in syrup. Way too sweet. The breakfast pizza was good. We had to ask for forks and napkins. We also asked for hot sauce. The forks and napkins came five minutes later and the hot sauce never came. Our server asked if we would like another round of mimosas and we said we would. We got our check about ten minutes later, no drinks.

It was an interesting experience, but we won't be going back.

I debated between 3 and 4 stars for awhile and 3 stars won. I want to give it 3.5 stars... I can understand why people would not like this place, but I actually like it. Usually.

I've gone there a good number of evenings during the week with friends after working out, when I want food and some beer but don't really want to shower or care too much. On most weekday evenings, it's not too packed. The menu is HUGE (so you can always find what you're craving) and all the food is... good. Nothing I've found so far is too amazing, nothing is horrible. It's a bit pricey (aka not cheap) but the portions are huge so I'm mostly forgiving. They have an extensive beer/wine/cocktail list as well, and you can get pitchers of things like beer or sangria. And it's all tasty. Right after work and on weekends, it gets a bit more crowded, but not too bad.

They have about a million TVs, which is great when you just want to chill at the bar, or watch a random sports game (one time my friend wanted to watch the WVU game, so the bartender changed one of the TVs for him, which was awesome). However, when big sporting events are on, it gets super crowded and rowdy and the crowd quickly escalates into drunken douchedom. 

Last Sunday, we went for the all-you-can eat buffet for $16.99 for the first time. It was actually a pretty good deal. Drinks weren't included, and the service was spotty (our waiter gave us multiple death glares when we asked for things like iced tea or water). But they have a selection of standard breakfast items (pancakes, eggs benedict, scrambled eggs, french toast, hash browns, toast/bagels, etc.), some lunch items (which I didn't try, so can't comment on), a "make your own omelet" station, fruit and desserts. Some things were a bit dried out- I was excited for eggs benedict and pancakes and both disappointed me. But I ate about 20 pounds of bacon so that redeemed my meal for me. Overall, a fairly good deal.

I would just give two stars if this one did come with Fantasmic preferred seating.

The service was fine and served the purpose but the waitress was too busy to deal with too many tables. So we didn't really talk about anything other than she passed the pass to Fantasmic to me. 

The food was fine as an average buffet. The steak was not as good as Boma in Animal Kingdom lodge, nor the roasted chicken. Only one soup was provided. only one bowl of fruit was served to scoop from. The dessert section had limited options. 

I guess in the end, the kids are fed and we avoid getting to the show one hour earlier than the starting time. I will think twice before I book here again.

The food was...ok. I heard great things about this place and, hate to say, was a bit disappointed. Food was filling... seemed to expand after we ate, but my lamb shwarma was shredded... never had shredded shwarma before..and not seasoned much. (Maybe it is Iraqi style). Best part of the meal was the little cup of pea soup starter. The home-made hot sauce and flat bread were good too. The beet salad tasted like canned pickled beets mixed with sour cream.. not mind blowing as some diners have reported. It was filling, healthy food.

Fun atmosphere, good service, and good drinks.

The food was a little disappointing. Like usual, my friends and I came during happy hour and ordered almost everything on the appetizer menu. Most of the dishes were salty. The Thai chicken pizza, the calamari, the chicken lettuce wrap, the buffalo wings, and even the seared ahi sashimi - they were all salty. The crab cakes were pretty good. I've been to the location in Legacy Place and I think the food there is better.

Overall Yard House always makes a fun night, especially with those tall half yards. Next time, I will try some of the main dishes.

My sister and I went to this restaurant to try some Ramen on a rainy day. We walked in at 2 o'clock and we were informed that we had exactly 15 minutes to order lunch. We found the wait staff to be a little cold and unfriendly. We asked if it would be better to come back at another time and we were told it was not a problem. On the bright side the hazelnut Ramen was delicious. The Gyoza was good and would've been better had the sauce been more flavorful. Overall an OK spot but not the best Ramen spot that I've been to in Portland and a little pricey. If your looking for a Fancy spot to take a client it's certainly nice inside and not your usual IZAKAYA.

I was looking forward to trying Il Mulino at the Swan, but was underwhelmed with the experience.  The ambiance and staff were excellent! The food?  Well, it was ok, but I was expecting much more out of a place like this.  Unfortunately, in reading other people's  reviews, I would characterize my experience as being par for the course.

First, the service - my wine glass was never empty!  The staff was very attentive to the group I was dining with - there were about 15 of us in total.  The restaurant was well staffed, so there were several people tending to us.

The food?  Well, the pasta was just pasta.  Mine was a bit overcooked, and I honestly don't remember the sauce.  I also had the bone-in pork chop, which was nice - a generous cut, and nicely presented. The taste - well, I could have gotten something similar at a place like Outback.  This restaurant shouldn't be on par with Outback...

We finished with an assortment of deserts - flourless chocolate cake, tiramisu, and cheesecake.  All three were very good.  Possibly the best part of the meal.

Purveyor of fine rugs and kilims from Afghanistan, Iran, Turkey, Tibet, Nepal and Pakistan, warehouse style. A maze of stacked carpeting, two sizable rooms and a basement probably amounts to hundreds of herds of sheep And a mother load of mothballs, what an olfactory assault!

Imagine all the weaving hours that went into filling the place, people's whole lives. Which you can read about in pamphlets given by the salespeople, how Cambridge. They're aggressive too, so hold your own. I didn't buy, though I'm tempted. Makes me appreciate my father's collection as a 4'x6' costs over $700. I'll try Craig's List first.

this place is really just ok.  i don't understand why there are so many 'omg lebanese food its so revolutionary' or 'finally! greek food' - we've got phoenicia and that sarah's joint on burnet - and honestly i feel like there is some mcdonalized gyro place in barton creek mall.

its your standard mediterranean restaurant.  gyro, shwarma, falafel, dolmas etc etc.  everything tasted decent if not good and the portions were ginormous.

i dunno though, there's something slighty sketch there - like i feel like if they had to nuke yesterday's chicken they would do it.

the one last thing that seemed a little sketch was the lady working there pronounced the word gyro 'jai-wroe' instead of 'year-wroe'

Cold food, bland flavors.

I get that smoked barbecue doesn't necessarily have to be served hot. But when you wait 20 minutes after ordering for food that's been smoking for 4-6 hours, you don't expect to be served room temperature pulled pork and slightly warmer ribs. 

Speaking of the ribs, spare ribs? Why?!? For my money, I want baby backs. Plus - pro tip - you get charged $3 for the sides, regardless of whether you get a meal or not.

This is alright barbecue with below-average service. For that, it gets three stars. Anyone who rates it higher is giving them a star or two for the hype.

I'm not sure if I picked a bad night to go there, but the service we received was extremely slow. The place was mostly empty, so we saw no good reason for the slowness. It took us 20 minutes just to get a glass of water. And 35 minutes to get our appetizer after having waited 20 minutes to place the order for it. The sushi was good, but not great. The cocktails (lychee martini) were delicious. I much prefer Fugakyu (located across the street from this establishment).

After much deliberation, I decided that I would switch from Android to an iPhone, and this led me to visit Verizon Wireless.  I was moving from a Samsung Galaxy S4, a phone that I had used for 3 years.  The salesman let me know 5-6 times that I'm not the kind of customer they like, since I keep my device for several mobile phone generations.  I only need to hear "you're not the person who needs the latest phone" once.  Or if it'll help, I can say it myself, but please, it doesn't need to be repeated over and over.  Yes, I am older than your parents, and yes, I'm sure they upgrade every year.  There was no opportunity to back up my contacts to the cloud one last time before disabling my Galaxy.  I think the youthful salesman believed my ancient Galaxy S4 had cooties, and wanted to complete the transaction without stating its name or touching it.  We kept moving forward with the transaction, including the chance to buy add-on accessories.  While the VZW web site said my phone's trade-in value was $25, the salesman said it was of no value.  In the end, I walked out with a shiny new iPhone 7.

this place was featured on the food network and so we've always had this restaurant on our "to do list".

we went here a few weeks ago as a double date. this place is very hyped up, especially about their bacon popcorn and burgers. we didn't care for the popcorn, but we did come for their famous HF burgers. let's break down, shall we?

FOOD: like I said before, all 4 of us each ordered our own burgers. the burgers was your classic american cheeseburger. it came with 2 buns, 2 patties, and 1-2 slices of cheddar cheese. the ketchup and mustard is left on the side and they give you very little --  equivalent to one of those ketchup packets they give you at a fast food joint. other than the burger itself, the dish comes with fries. the fries are nothing special, just a touch of salt..no extra flavoring. I tried to burger by itself btw; i'll give 'em credit for the juicyness, but it still lacked flavor for me. I've been to enough burger places to compare. 


PRICING: for a double date (total of 4 ppl), with a burger per person and 2 drinks (from the bar)...our bill came out to around $70 for LUNCH! idk about you guys, but that's crazy expensive for a lunch bill. keep in mind that the burgers are real pricey at $12 each.

CONCLUSION: H&F didn't live up to all their hype. would I go back? maybe, but I won't be ordering their burgers though.

Let me just start off with saying that their queso and quesadillas are fantastic. The chips and salsa are also very good. The soft tacos are awesome! So why am I giving this place 3-stars instead of 4 or even 5? Simple, the service is absolutely not there.

Colibri has a ton of potential, and a lot of competition in the area. You think the service would be impeccable, due to the competition and amazing view of the lake. Wrong.

I've been to this establishment on several occasions and the company I work for frequently orders from this great restaurant. Nonetheless, I feel as if the service is just lack-luster, from when I've dined in and have taken food to-go.

I've stood at the front of the hostess area for 3 minutes while two employees are folding towels or something at the very front, and when I told them that I was picking up, they directed me to the bar. It would have been nice if you had told me 3 minutes ago...

It doesn't seem like anyone is happy to be there. It's just bland. Maybe it's just me being in a beautiful town like Baldwin Park, but I'd expect the restaurant to be a few steps above the Subway and Five Guys just a few blocks away in terms of service. It isn't. What a let down.

I picked up a carry-out order of some tacos that I was informed were part of the Taco Tuesday promotion, and was told by the manager that it's for dine-in only. This wasn't mentioned or listed anywhere on the website or on their menu. Nonetheless, the manager gave me the promotional discount, but let me know that it's for dine-in only. No problem and the gesture was greatly appreciated. The issue still stands: This exception wasn't mentioned anywhere, and it took me being vocally frustrated to the manager to get the promotion. The person who took my order over the phone did not let me know either, though. Regardless, the tacos I received (and a hearty bag of chips and salsa, which I've only received one out of the two times I've ordered carry-out, but a GREAT gesture nonetheless!) were excellent. I'm not sure if the chips and salsa are included with every to-go order or not, though...

If you would like solid food with an incredible view of Lake Baldwin, you won't be disappointed by Colibri. If you're expecting great service, you're going to have mixed feelings about this place like I do. As I mentioned before, the restaurant has a lot of opportunity to improve with their service. Having servers being more proactive, more relatable, more friendly, and more attentive would make this place easily up there as the best Baldwin Park establishment.

Just note that the Taco Tuesday special (and I assume every daily special) is dine-in only.

The bar area is probably the only reason I'd go back here.  The food and drinks are pretty inconsistent.  Sometimes the pasta dishes are great, but sometimes they are undercooked.  Sometimes you'll get a martini, but sometimes you'll get a dirty martini.  It would be unfair to say these were one time occurences, but I have been here a number of times.  I do like the ambiance.  It's loud and energetic.  As I said before, the bar area is cozy and great for HH.  In short, when Gaslight hits, it really hits.  When it misses, however, it misses badly.

We came in on a Thursday, probably around 5pm when nobody was in the restaurant, but a little after about three more tables had been sat. I found this place on Yelp actually, as one of the better places to have dessert in Coquitlam. 
I ordered a Peach Ice Tea, a Cotton Candy Frappe and a Brussels Melowna Waffle (Their liege waffle machine was broken so I had no choice). Their peach ice tea is amazing, it's not too sweet but not too plain, it definately tasted like peaches, it's actually comparable to 'Good Drink' if anyone's has that before (It's bomb, you gotta try them). My waffle had white chocolate, cantaloupe, melon and melona ice cream on it, the Brussels waffle wasn't too bad, it wasn't sweet at all, almost need a little bit of sugar actually. But it wasn't bad compared to other I've had. The fruit pieces were really sweet but didn't mix well with the waffle, luckily the melona ice cream did! Overall it was a good dessert dish just cause I could eat the fruit alone and eat the ice cream with the waffle and both were tasty, it could've used a little bit more white chocolate drizzle tho just because the little bit that was on there, pretty much froze up from the ice cream and I could barely taste it and it would've helped the plainness of the waffle. My boyfriend ordered the cotton candy frappe and it was sweet, he didn't finish it, but what do you expect from a cotton candy drink LOL 
Atmosphere: The decorations felt a little but rustic-hipstery, the store was really spacious because of the high ceilings and the huge hallway(?) in the middle that lead up to the counter. The place looked new and clean, but nothing amazing.
Service: The girl greeted, seated and brought us menus right as we entered, she took our order and brought our food but we had to pay at the counter, I always find that intresting and question whether you're supposed to tip or not, but there was a tip jar so I suppose it's a pooled tip. The employees always looked like they were doing something rather than just sitting around for customers, which seems to happen a lot at places that aren't that busy. I found it intresting that they had table menus but they also had a large board up with the food menus on them sort of like a quick service restaurant. 

Food: 4/5
Atmosphere: 3/5
Service:3/5

I'm rarely in this area, so I'm not sure if I'll be back, but that doesn't mean I wouldn't recommend it, for being near the mall and in Coquitlam, it's not a bad waffle place, maybe they should consider putting bubble tea on their menu to start competing with Ninja BBT cause Ninja BBT actually came up first under desserts in Coquitlam.

Not bad.  A lot of potential.  Personally, I always take off a star when considering a new Tex Mex or BBQ restaurant to visit because us Texans are so goofy on the cuisines we tend to over-rate them.  That said, I'll give this a solid 3 stars for my first visit.  A tad bit on the pricey side, but not completely out of whack.  The pork ribs were decent, could have spent more time on the smoker.  The jalepeno cheese link was pretty good.  It had more smokey flavor.  Beans were good, tasted like the bbq sauce was used in them to give flavor.  No onions or bacon/fatback was noticeable, too bad.  Half pound of pork ribs, 1 link, 1 small side of beans, and 1 sweet tea ran $14.38 with tax.  It would be good for them to create a combo plate to mitigate the cost of sides and tea.  Those items were almost $4 of my bill.

Beer+Bowling+Sports on the TV's = fun times had by all!

How can you argue with goofy two-tone rented shoes, an all-american past time and booze? I mean, don't expect steller service or a gourmet meal. Sometimes, there is not service at all!

However, there is the ever-present opportunity to transport yourself back to a time when you were 6 years old and your best friend's birthday party was held at a bowling alley...except this time you get to get drunk!

Don't you just love it when fond childhood memories are conjured up by equal parts atmosphere and alcohol??

Best thing about Cambridge, 1:  $18 Dogfish Head pitchers. That may not seem like a big deal to some, but I think it's a great deal, especially considering the sophisticated vibe of this place. Oh and they also have "pizza," but I wouldn't really call it that. It's more like flat bread with stuff on it. There's nothing that really resembles a sauce, and there's not a lot of cheese. The combinations are tasty and interesting, and the ingredients are fresh, but be prepared for something different. I enjoyed the potato pizza on one occasion, and the roasted onion pizza on another. However, I do feel that both pizzas were a little dry (hence why most pizza has sauce). An extra drizzle of EVOO might do the trick. Think about it.

Marriott's SpringHill Suites in Portland needs an upgrade from the '70's in decor and some help in service and upkeep, but it was an all right hotel stay.  I wouldn't stay here again due to the noise and some service issues.

I'm a Marriott rewards member, so I chose this hotel for the points after scouring many Yelp reviews for a hotel in Portland by the airport.  I stayed here for a couple of nights.  

Check-in was easy, with an odd request to fill out a separate piece of paper regarding the car I had, promising I wouldn't park anywhere I wasn't supposed to, yadda yadda.  Haven't seen that at a hotel before.

The hotel room came with a mini fridge, small microwave and sink area, along with a pull-out sofa, desk, flatscreen, and a full length mirror which I thought was a bonus.  The sink is separate from the shower and toilet.  The bed was comfortable, as well as the pillows. Loved the light canceling curtains.  Ironing board and iron in the closet along with a blow dryer. 

The only complimentary toiletries are Paul Mitchell brand shampoo, conditioner and lotion with bar soap.  Anything else, be prepared to purchase it in the mini convenience store next to the front desk.  Glad I packed Q-tips.  

No room service here.  They have a swimming pool and whirlpool, but I didn't use them.

Free breakfast from 4-10 am was nice. You can make your own waffle, and they had an assortment of fresh fruit along with scrambled eggs, sausage links, oatmeal, yogurt, cold cereal, breads, juices and milks.  The second night I was there, the serving area was packed and lucked out on finding somewhere to sit.  Other people were taking their food to their rooms to eat.

Went to watch TV one night and couldn't get the TV to turn on.  After fiddling around, figured out that it wasn't plugged in!  Then, after settling back into bed, the freaking remote required me to push each button 5-10 times before it would register.  Put some fresh batteries into the remote!  They don't offer a movie menu - that really stunk.  

Another night, I went downstairs at about 9 pm to buy something to drink from the mini store and no one was at the front desk.  Another guest came over and asked me for directions.  Not having my cell phone to help her out, we were both standing around for ten minutes before I gave up, put the drinks back and went back to my room. There was a sign on the desk that the one employee had stepped away for a minute.  That said, have your break later at night when clients aren't going to be needing assistance.

Be prepared to hear planes, trains and automobiles.  Also, you'll hear your neighbors showering, talking, banging suitcases, etc. as the walls are paper thin.

The elevator is slow, and hearing the door scrape, metal on metal, slowly every time it opened and closed killed the ears.  Get that fixed.

I went to get my hair cut at this salon in November, based on the Yelp reviews. I requested Summer and went early in the morning on a Saturday, so I guess I can't blame the place or the staff for being quiet. They were still drinking their morning coffees, after all.
The haircut was okay. Nothing too great, nothing bad about it. I have mid-length hair and went in for a trim. I also let Summer choose a semi-permanent colour for my hair, which turned out a little too fake-looking for my interest, but it was a nice change. Thank god it has washed out by now though.
Maybe my expectations were too high based on the other reviews posted on this site. What I got was a decent-priced , decent-looking haircut and nothing more. 
Usually when I find a reliable hair stylist I stick with them, rather than venture out to an unknown salon and risk a bad haircut. I don't think I'll go back to Salon Cu, not a keeper.

This is a review for take-out only.  I started out exceedingly skeptical because it's just so expensive for the amount of food that you get.  Also, their menus seem a bit messed up - their takeout menu is somewhat minimal compared to the regular menu, and when I called they said their takeout counter was actually closed and to order off the regular menu.  Well there are two versions of their regular menu on their site - the one that's written on the "menu" page that doesn't include the "combos" section (not sure why), and then the menu you get from the Download button that does, but lists the prices incorrectly compared to what they actually charge in the restaurant.  They've got a little housekeeping to do.  I was also pretty damn sad that there was no bbq sauce included with my takeout order.  Fix please!

The bottom line on the food:  The burnt ends are hands down the BEST burnt ends I've ever had in my life.  Ever ever ever.  Like, the crack version of meat.  Oh my god.

Everything else was underwhelming.  My bf said the brisket was good, but to me it looked like a slab of grey meat.  Their side game is pretty weak, both in terms of the choices and quality.  My boyfriend doesn't eat pork and doesn't like coleslaw, so really all I could get him was the cornbread and the seasonal side.  The cornbread is definitely good, but the seasonal side was sliced zucchini, essentially raw, with a sprinkle of cheese, a ton of cilantro, and really no dressing to speak of.  Super weird, and really not worth any $.  The beans were tasty but nothing to write home about, and the pimento mac + cheese is super gross cold.  Warmed up I actually really liked it, but acknowledge that it's an acquired taste and that I had the luxury of a microwave. It sounds like from other reviews that they serve it pretty cold in the restaurant.  I wish they had more sides, and that they were better.

So, the burnt ends themselves would get 10 stars - I will pay absolutely whatever they want to charge for a bulk order of that.  Everything else though, or eating in at the restaurant, isn't really worth it as of now.  Perhaps they'll improve as they get a bit older!

I love the decor. It looks very fresh and modern. I am always hesitant of restaurants that feature numerous styles of Asian cuisine, because I always wonder if they'll miss the mark and not quite master anything. 

I ordered the hot stone bimpibap, with tofu and edamame. While I typically love Korean food, this was just not good all. It's served in a hit stone pot, but there was no crunchy rice as is typical in this dish. The spicy sauce was served on the side (cold) which really didn't enhance anything, and the flavors were boring at very best. Honestly, the best part of my meal was the miso soup that came out first. 

The server was nice enough,  the location is great, and the ambience is nice. I just didn't think the food was good at all. In the future, I'll stick with Seoul in Beacon Hill.

With our building's washer out of order last weekend, we found ourselves in a bit of a pinch: too much dirty laundry to wait another week. Sarni was not only the closest laundromat, but also among the only ones open on Sunday afternoon (who knew, right?). The gentleman at the counter was friendly and helpful, but the setup at the place was a bit weird.

As others have noted, getting started at Sarni means buying a $5 card with a chip in it. You have to load the card with cash to use the machines, but the $5 is just a sunk cost; none of it is available for use to actually do laundry. This seemed a bit shocking (and expensive). From there, the machines were also a pretty steep price -- between $3.99 and $5.99 for a load of laundry (depending on the size of the machine) and additional money for a dryer. Sure, we could do multiple loads at once, but we ended up finding a few detergent stains on our clothes and the whole experience cost us ~$25 to wash and dry two loads of laundry. Here's hoping our washer is fixed sooner than later!

This is a clean hotel with upbeat, friendly customer service. I also dined in the lobby bar restaurant twice and it was quite good. Again, very friendly and cheery staff.

The rooms are decent but the bathrooms are quite narrow. I'm not a very large man but felt like one in the bathroom (see photo). Otherwise, the rooms are perfectly fine and offer some beautiful views of the water and downtown Portland. 

Another reviewer mentioned the "little things" here. I have to admit I noticed this as well. For example, there was a microwave and refrigerator stashed in the hallway right outside my door. It was there when I checked in early around 12:00 noon, and I simply assumed someone was finished with it and it was awaiting pick up. (see photos)

I was there at least 24 hours and I was a little surprised. Not only unsightly, but also opens it up for whoever wants to take it. Just unusual for a Marriott. 

But I guess the major disappointment came when I wanted to try out their highly-rated restaurant, Truss. It has great reviews so I set out about 7:00 pm to dine there, only to be met with a sign that said "Sorry We Missed You." They were closed, even though they were advertised to be open at that time. 

My loss, I'm sure. 

I went down to the lobby bar restaurant and had dinner. A steak salad that was very good. 

So all in all, a nice hotel and I'd stay again. Just hope to be able to try Truss.

The fries were good and the dipping sauces had very interesting names, like as someone mentioned earlier, the Vampire Slayer (which I had).  The dipping sauces were good too.  The service was pretty slow, considering we only ordered fries and they were moderately busy.  It seemed like some of the staff was new and learning how to use the equipment.  It took about 10-15 minutes to receive our order.  After having had Belgian frites on the streets of Belgium, it's close to the real thing, but still not as good.

I miss the salad they once served here that came with fried , they must've taken it off the menu since I've last been in here. Last night we came in and it was busy. People just sitting and waiting for tables but we got in right away as a party of 2.

The service was okay, it just took a long time to make sweet potato fries for my husband's order. We both ordered the Royal Red, which is super messy burger with meat, cheese, egg, tomato and lettuce. I would have to say for the money you can get the same thing at Steak n Shake for much less. Here you pay $10 for just that burger and the steak fries but at Steak n Shake you pay maybe $5 and it's not as messy or greasy.

They now have the easy pay system where you can swipe your credit card on the device at the table you sit at. Instead of waiting for the check. Most restaurants are doing this now. It's easy and effective. 

Now that they got rid of my favorite salad and the burger is over priced, I'm not sure I'll be back that often. I really have no reason to anyways since I don't reside in this part of town anymore.

I have to start by saying that the food is very good, and it would have earned a 4 stars, but the services were so so on my visit.  A friend who lives in the area recommended this place and swears that it is like food in Hong Kong.  She was dead right about that.  It is not a fancy place, small but lively.  Most of the servers or waitresses do not speak very good English. As a matter of fact, my dinner companion is the only 'Big Nose' - Caucasian.  Every one is Chinese speaking different dialect.  I was told by my friend to ask the serving staff for recommendation.  Everyone get a complimentary soup of the day, so I don't know why she recommended me to have fa Sliced Pork and Vegetable Hot Pot (which is a soup also) to me, we cannot finish half of the soup -- either of them.  I saw that there was the Yellow Eel Rice on the menu, she told me that I have to order it, which I found out later is not true.  The roast pigeon I ordered was nice. Crispy skin and tasty meat.  The Steak on Sizzling plate was ok, not a lots of beef, but plenty of onion.  The worse was the dishes comes out one at a time, I waited at least 20 minutes for each dishes, one by one.  It was no fun.  At the end we ate everything but the mixed vegetable dishes did not arrive. I asked to cancel it then, she kept saying that it will arrive in 3 minutes, if not, then we can cancel it.  10 minutes later, I asked to cancel it, no, at that point she brought out the dish, but the hot pot did not have tofu in it!! By that point we were so fed up, but the vegetable hot pot did taste good.  At the end she gave me a 10% discount, but it really did not compensate for my dinner experience.  I skipped complimentary dessert too, because I do not want to wait.

Great deal for all you can eat but Jeepers creepers your clothes will smell FOR DAYS. They're pretty big and will accommodate up to 8-10 people a party but it fills up quick on weekends! 
The food was good and service was lacking a tad but we just couldn't get over the pungent smell that fills the entire restaurant and follows you home. 
Don't get me wrong, it was great quality and we ate to our satisfaction but the lingering smell itself made us hesitant to come back. 

We didn't quite know how the ordering work and the workers weren't very helpful in navigating us but we managed to make it work! Some of our orders were missing but luckily we didn't order from the extra charge items so it was a clean split. 

Not sure if I'd be willing to come back considering the food and smell but I'd definitely recommend it if you want to try out a different hot pot place!

This location is very clean and newer than most of the locations I've seen in SoCal. I ordered the #1 Combination, #9 Sardine, and #4 Grilled Chicken Banh Mi ($4.49 each) along with a Thai Milk Tea ($3.49) and Vietnamese Coffee ($3.99). The wait time for my order was only 5-7 mins and there was plenty of parking in the private lot.

The banh mi were decent since the protein ingredients were flavorful. The sardine was soft and briny, but wasn't a sodium overdose. The grilled chicken had hints of charred flavor and tender. The combination jambon meat had a deli-like texture with a slight creamy spread of pate to add a meaty flavor.

For the price of $4.49 a banh mi, I felt the protein ingredients were very sparse in comparison to the large amounts of pickled daikon, carrots, cilantro, and jalapeno. The size of the banh mi was around 11 in length and 2.5 in width. 

The Thai Tea and Lee's Coffee were absolutely delicious and quenched my thirst immediately. The Thai Tea wasn't too sweet and had a creamy flavor from the splash of half and half. The coffee was sweet from the condensed milk, which complemented the shots of dark espresso very well.  I'd definitely come back for a Lee's coffee, which will keep me awake all day.

ok the food there is pretty good have to admit, chips and salsa delish! drinks not so strong, at all... and service they are nice.. but the service is terrible, you order a drink or anything for that matter they seem to ALWAYS forget, and takes them prob anywhere from half hour to an hour, so if they do come by to check be sure to order what u'll be needing in the next hour.. and i've been MANY times.. so im not complaining because i do go back, foods really good.. its mexican hard to go wrong. Takes forever for your food to come out!, and most of all WAY OVER PRICED FOR EVERYTHING! me an my friend went there for dinner the other night and i got the chimichangas, they got enchiladas ($14 each) 2 beers each $44 bill then + tip..

****************************3.5 stars**************************************

So on Cinco de mayo me and some buddies decided to celebrate this mexican holiday (and my bday) by going out and getting some food and drinks (hopefully on the cheap). So we were set up to go to no mas cantina at 7:30 (not a good idea). when we drove by it was packed to the brim everyone was waiting outside and it was a 2 hour wait for food and that was just an estimate (which is ridiculous). seeing our options dwindle we decided to head to mid-town and check out the prickly pear. 20 min later when we got there it was a cluster-f*ck. It was an apparent Cinco de Mayo 'block party' being thrown by two restaurants. Forget trying to put ure name a list of any sort it was complete mayhem and drunk guys to boot. Usually its not an issue but since the lady was in town this didn't bode over well with me. seeing an open table we sat down thinking it was part of the 'block party' but apparently Marlow's Tavern wasn't part of it. But seeing as we didn't want any part of any cluster-f*ck we decided to stay. menus were delivered promptly and the waiter came out to get our drink orders. 

Looking at the prices on the menu it didn't really jump out as expensive or pricey, pretty much on par with say 6 feet under or any other atl establishment. So off we went to order. Since i was hungry and wanted to drink i didn't wanna get anything too filling so the lady and i decided to just do appetizers. We ordered firecracker shrimp ($10), marlow's tavern sampler ($12) and some fried calamari ($11). And keeping with the theme we also got a margarita ($8) and a blueberry mojito ($8).
