So as we waited we just enjoyed the festivities and chatted up with some buddies. 15 min later as conversation was running dry and my buzz slowly slipping away i could wait no longer and jumped over next door to prickly pear to grab a drink. when i got back there were our drinks, oh well more for me. There was also an apparent mistake and two margaritas were delivered. So making quick work of the one in my hand, we continued to talk. Soon after, the food arrived and not a moment too soon. 

The food was nothing too special but well executed nonetheless. The sampler, which included shrimp and crab nachos, firecracker shrimp, and hummus was pretty good. Nachos were nice and cheesy and the filling was sufficient. Fire cracker shrimp were crisp and tender not over fried but seemed like it was just fancy Long John Silver's. the hummus tasted home made and earthy but had a layer of oil on the top so i didn't really know what to make out of it, but it was still good. The bigger order of firecracker shrimp was also well fried. The calamari was a little disappointing. Pieces stuck together and some of the tentacle pieces were a bit over cooked and dry. At least the cocktails were good. The lady really enjoyed her blueberry mojito (too bad she could order only 1 since they ran out of blueberry liquor). and the margarita i had could've been a bit stronger but its a cocktail so i wasn't expecting much liquor in it anyways. 

Overall Marlow's tavern was accommodating for a busy night. Their appetizers are good but nothing special. Their cocktails are better than their food but could be a bit stronger. and their prices are right on par with a restaurant of their caliber. I'd come back if i was in the area... dunno if i'd make the trek out here solely for the food since parking can be hectic... Decent food, Good drinks, good atmosphere, decent service.... Happy eating...

Sweet Hut used to have items that tasted of higher quality. Now the items taste like they came out of a package. You can just tell. I've been to this Midtown location several times but started going to Sweet Hut in KoreanTown-Atlanta (I.e. DULUTH/Lawrenceville) years ago. I know the items tasted better years ago. I have to say it's an average spot now at best. Sorry Sweet Hut! As a Korean I wanted to give it a higher rating but I can't lie to people.

Not bad. They came in around 1 hour and 10 minutes. I ordered Hanger DC-10 with AfterBurner and Garlic Parm & cajun waffle fries, fried chicken wrap AfterBurner & plain waffle fries, 2 XL AfterBurner sauces & a small cheese sauce. The cajun waffle fries and Garlic Parm chicken is SO GOOD. Paying for extra sauce is also awesome if you love sauce because you get A LOT of it. It's not as spicy as Wing-It's Suicide sauce-which I'm in love with- but still pretty good. The cheese sauce is like......Velveeta. The boneless chicken is nice & juicy. I love my food EXTRA spicy, so how you feel about "AfterBurner" would be a different experience from mine. It has a kick, but....meh.

For me, I'd order from here if I was craving their fries, boneless chicken & wanted to dip everything into sauces. I give them a strong 3 stars.

Clara was very accommodating and friendly, and had the dress that I wanted. When I was measured the women told me I had big hips for my size (I'm fairly petite), which I know already, but it was still an off-putting comment to make, especially when I am dropping close to $2,000 on a dress.
She did give me an excellent deal on my veil, and even offered to let me bring my dress back to be steamed right before my wedding. When I couldn't pick my dress up right on the day it came in, the employees were a bit catty about it, and Clara also didn't remember her offer to steam the wrinkles out of my dress before the wedding. 
An okay experience, but when it's your wedding dress, I'd expect better service, and more tact.

By the time I went into Adorn, I felt like I was in the movie Groundhog Day. The same shop, over and over and over again. It had some nice things, some well-made clothes in good fabrics. I do like a lot of the styles they carry - on the funky side. Some fun jewelry - I think they might have had a small piece or two for $12. 

It's bright, but somehow feels tighter than it should. There were quite a few folks milling around - and one very cute dog. Although I was warmly weclomed by the dog's person, I just didn't feel very comfortable walking to the back of the store. So I didn't. As I read though other reviews, I see maybe it's more that this is for young, hip, cool and thin people - of which I am maybe only .75 of one (cool, that is). So that doesn't feel too good. 

Nice things, sized out of my realm, priced out of my wheelhouse. But nothing I haven't seen before, maybe two doors down.

I absolutely love hibachi, so when I found a Paint Nite here at Kyoto I knew I had to check it out. My friend and I had hibachi dinner, and it was very good. Our cook was energetic and funny. The options were the same as most hibachi places. This time I ate the teriyaki chicken. The whole meal includes noodles too, I've noticed other hibachi places don't give you noodles. The servers were all very kind and helpful. Through the Paint Nite event, the bartender also was very attentive and recommend good drinks. Will definitely come by again whenever I'm around.

The Peddler is a really nice hyde park bike shop option, but not the only one. Can't say I'd recommend them for minor repairs over Clown Dog, but they're reasonably priced and they have an okay selection of bike accessories. The service is pretty nice, too. 

I've had pretty good experiences at the Peddler. I took my bike for a tune-up a while ago and they did a good job. Another time, at their old location on north loop, I randomly met another customer who, when he saw I was buying a new bike seat, offered instead to trade me a ladies Brooks saddle for my crappy 80's bike seat. Fantastic! More recently though, I got some plastic "strap-on" fenders (ok, that sounds dirty, but I don't know what else to call them) that really were horrible quality. They cost almost $50, and they were missing a part which I didn't realize until I got them home to install them. I returned them, and the Peddler gave me an almost-full refund without much hassle (couldn't give a full refund because they had been unpackaged). Still, I'm not sure if I'd buy parts from them any more. I'd return for minor repairs if I'm in the area.

I give 5 stars to laurelhurst market for their lunch sandwiches. 
I can't give near that for the dinner food - hence the lower rating overall.

All our dinner food was too salty and/or over flavored. No great ribeye needs to be brined in salt then covered in melting blue cheese. The seafood, stew and other items were all too harshly flavored. The smoked brisket was too salty and dry - so overcooked the surface was completely burned. I know my brisket and this doesn't come close. Please let good food shine thru on its own. Tone it down. 

I'll be back plenty for the creative and delicious sandwiches they make at the butcher counter. And there's no better place in town to purchase sausages and fine cuts of meat to cook yourself.

Whenever I'm strolling along the Drag, I can't help but stop into Wish. It's a really cute boutique with a variety of jewelry, purses, clothes, and shoes. I've never bought clothes there, because they're a bit pricey and I've never seen anything that especially stood out, but I've gotten a few bags (which were adorable but not the most durable) as well as inexpensive, fun earrings, and funky club shoes that have lasted a while. They actually had the hottest pair of heels there, in only one size, that tormented me for months. Every time I came in I was hopefuly that they would finally have my size. They never did . That and the less than great quality of the purses I bought are the reasons Wish only gets three stars from me.

I LOVE french food. So when my chance to go to Little Robbie's, I gladly accepted! Here was the biggest problem - We drove into the South End, because sadly I moved out of Back Bay into the suburbs - and I COULD NOT find a parking space to save my life. We drove around for 20 minutes... and in the heat, that does not go well in my book! We resorted to suing valet parking. Here was the worst part of this parking dilemma - the valet circled around - driving my car for 20 minutes and I saw my car pass me, sitting outside approximately 20 times. WHAT IS UP WITH THAT!? So DON'T valet park - the valet guy thinks its his car to cruise around the streets! 

Let me get to the better stuff - they sat us right away - the service staff were friendly and kept coming by frequently to refill water glasses and make sure we didn't need anything. 

We started with the trio of pate - it was good - didn't like the chicken liver part but it's an acquired taste so it doesn't hurt my impression of the restaurant. We also ordered escargot and it was Sooooo good! The bread was hot and toasty that we devoured it quickly with the pate and escargot. I had the Chicken coq au vin with buttered noodle. I was hesitant at first because of the buttered noodle but the waiter explained its not what I would think and he was right - I couldn't taste any butter. I probably won't have coq au vin only because I didn't like the red wine reduction as much as I thought but the food was still extremely tasty. My friend had the special - the rabbit leg - and as an act of bravery, I took a bite and it was extremely delicious! I should have ordered it!!! Better than chicken! My fiance ordered the rack of lamb and I didn't try that but had a bit of the potato that came with it and the sauce was delicious! 

We also had dessert - I had the profiterole with vanilla ice cream and fudge - it was sweet and I probably won't have it again but worth a try. My fiance had the Creme Brulee and they did it JUST RIGHT! YUMMY!! Our friend had the Frepe Suzette and that was good too. 

The experience was good only if I didn't see the valet driver driving my car up and down the street so many times during my stay at the restaurant.

Go find another breakfast/brunch place.  The food is typically very good but the service/staff and cleanliness was struggling.  The glasses/utensils weren't clean, water had particles floating in it.  We sat outside and never got checked on from the time the order was taken till food came out which was at least 30 min.  It came out, no apologies for the time.  The bathroom smelt like a zoo and wasn't clean.  I had gluten free French toast, it was very dry, like not soaked in a good egg mixture.

Keep in mind that this review is early on since they have been open less than a week. 

The location is one of the smaller layouts. The biggest issue with the location is that parking is severely limited. All of the parking on the end of the building belongs to ABC.   

I've been a couple of times so far and the food has been great both times. Top notch by Chipotle standards. I had quit going to the Semoran location as the food quality had gone down. I'm glad that this one is doing much better. 

The service has been friendly but slow. This isn't unexpected since most of the employees are new and they are still in the soft opening phase. 

Also be aware that online ordering is not yet available for this location. 

I'm sure they will improve over time. I'll be updating my review later.

Great service, good atmosphere, ridiculously overpriced drinks and food. Drinks are 15 dollars a pop, the appetizers were around 16 and the entrees averaged around 26. The gnudi was okay. Meh. The octopus salad was good, as were the scallops and black pasta. The pork tenderloin was a bit dry. On the bright side, the herb and olive bread was DELICIOUS. I wouldn't really eat here again. It wasn't spectacular for the amount of money you pay. I wouldn't mind the prices, if the food had at least been delicious. Most of it was, well, average. I would try something else in the Liberty.

Pretty decent. Not super amazing though. I had the pad see ewe and it was a little lacking on the sauce. The meat and vegetables tasted fresh, so I don't think the quality is bad. Food came out quickly. And service was prompt. Constantly checked our water levels. You know how you ask for more time to look at the menu and then no one comes back for a long time? Yeah, they actually come back. Good overall experience. Especially if you live in the area or need something near ACC.

On our first visit here we have mixed reviews.  First of all, we love the actual place.  Video poker in the back, pool table, and live music every night.  It was relaxed, a good temperature inside, and ultimately a great atmosphere.  

However, the food was not good.  We ordered flautas and mozzarella sticks (as we were just in for a small bite) and the flautas were literally 1. Clumped together 2. Just corn tortillas with completely dry chicken inside.  I don't honestly even think the chicken was seasoned.  It was literally like dry boiled chicken inside a corn tortilla.  The mozzarella sticks were average.  We had to ask for plates, though our server brought them promptly when asked.  

One of us ordered a Chardonnay and was brought the cheaper Chardonnay of the two options, did not like it at all and requested to exchange for the Kendall Jackson and the server exchanged it no problem and even charged only the cheaper price.  So that was really nice. 

Honestly, the menu looked like it had a lot of good options (breakfast all day!!) and the service was decent so we definitely WILL return to try other dishes.  I will update when we do so!

My take on this joint...

- It's different than the other bars and clubs around time. Instead of smashed against by a bunch of drunk horny people, you can sit at a table, drink your drink and sing along with the piano playing men...and laugh at those who go on stage and make a fool of themselves.

- The bar is full-service and there are a few very cute male bartenders there too. For those who love to take shots, they have a list of some fun, innovative ones to indulge in, but steer clear of the Gorilla Fart shot. It tastes and feels just as bad as it sounds. It's warm 151 and wild turkey...ick!

- The people are a nice blend of Central Florida residents/natives and tourists which makes for an interesting crowd. A lot of bachelorette and birthday parties happen here which can get kind of annoying.

- You can win a free happy hour party for you and up to 100 friends which means free and very cheap drinks, the place to yourself for 2 hours and some food. However, don't get too excited because the food usually consists of hot dogs, nachos with that fake, canned cheese and salsa.

- This place doesn't serve any kind of food aside from the happy hour parties, so eat beforehand. The good thing is that there a large number of restaurants surrounding it.

- For the most part, the servers are nice, but I've run into a few snobby and rude gals though.

-The women's bathroom attendant is by far my favorite part about this place. She is a loud, proud African American woman and she is always saying some off-the-wall but honest stuff. Love her!

Overall, it's okay. I don't make the long trip to I-drive often but I'll go for a special occasion every now and again.

El Sapo is located on the crowded Manor Rd where a bunch of other well known restaurants reside.  The location has been multiple establishments and the original building is a formatted auto shop.  The layout of the place gives outdoor seating to enjoy the sun or fully A/C indoor area with tables and a very large bar.  This places focuses really on two things.  Unique burgers and unique drinks all served in mason jars.  You can get burgers with jalapenos, black beans, fried egg, guacamole and other options.
I ordered an El Azul and my friend got the El Chilie.  The burgers are well sized and cooked about well done.  It is a flat wide patty cut burger.  Buns are toasted, toppings are very fresh.  As always a burger place gets judged by the beef.  It has an average flavor, no seasoning, and cooked well with decent texture.  My friend got the queso fries which are freshly cut fries topped with grilled onions and the queso sauce.  I felt the fries could have used some seasoning on them also.  The onion rings I got were thin cut, decent amount but very average breading.  Dude, whats up with no salt & pepper on the table.  I mean shouldn't that be a standard at a place serving burgers?  Drinks are served in the mason jars.  They also serve milk shakes and banana splits for dessert.  
Now this place would be great if you want to go just for drinks.  The alcohol drink menu seemed to have a good variety and you can sit up at the bar or lounge outside out on the bench seating.  This place is a good addition to the east side spots and I would go back.  I just felt the taste for a $10+ burger was a bit average.  Its a good cooked burger but it is not amazing and I would probably know several other burger spots I would pick besides El Sapo.

I was so excited to try this place! I liked the atmosphere, and the fact that you can bring in a huge group. The beer was OK. I only liked two out of the four in my flight. They have this terrible bud light style beer specifically for Americans. Oh gods! It was awful. 

The food was 50-50. I had potato soup. It tasted like it came from a can. Blah. The pretzels were ok. The potato pancakes were awful and greasy. I really liked the sour kraut balls. My husband had the schnitzel, and it was quite good.

I'd go back for the fun atmosphere and decent beer, but overall I was disappointed.

I hesitated to even review Gordon Biersch because I have only had beer here (no food).  I tried the bar out last summer.  It was a beastly hot ATL summer night and a friend and I wanted to wet our whistles and we were in the nieghborhood.  I mentioned I'd never been to one of these in ATL, so we stopped in for a pint.  

I have to say the beer was EXACTLY what I wanted.  It had body and character, was cold, but not to the point that I couldn't appreciate the fine brew.  But as I said, I sat a the bar and it wasn't busy, so the service was fine.  Can't comment about the food quality...maybe another time.

Pollo Campero is a decent joint.  I like the rice, and the fried chicken is sort of dry but the flavor is excellent.  There is a fixins bar too where you can go to town with the jalapenos, pico de gallo and other sauces.

I also like the water in here.  The fountain water is filtered so it does not have that Florida taste.  

I have not tried any other items here so I can't speak for them.  Also, the workers seem to have attitudes, when I was there the line was long and I guess the pressure was getting to them.

Have to say I was rather disappointed with my experience here. I made a reservation over a week in advance and when we initially came in we were seated at a lovely table with a great view. However, the very drunk group of 8 or 9 men behind us became a huge distraction. They were constantly yelling, swearing and talking offensively about women. My boyfriend, seeing how uncomfortable I was, asked our server to reseat us away from the drunk and out of control group.

What shocked me was that they 1) moved us to a worse table 2) lost our order 3) did not try and amend any part of the experience. With the price range and reputation of this restaurant I would have expected some gesture of trying to fix this problem. Instead we were rather ignored. 

Food: 5 stars
Service/conflict resolution: 1 star

Came for Father's Day Brunch. Had trouble with online booking so called, only to get put on hold and dropped several times. Front desk staff took my info (since I had tried many times and couldn't get through to restaurant). Never heard back so emailed but couldn't ever get indoor seating confirmation. Lovely employee (who was out of town but emailed me the day before) confirmed we were outside but suggested I talk to hostess when we arrive. Tried to but the hostess never really looked up from her ipad and mumbled no when we asked and didn't even try to work with us. Not quite the welcome one likes when they walk into a restaurant.  

Great atmosphere although patio very warm today and not totally shaded. Fans would have been helpful. Food was very good but wait staff seemed very indifferent which took away from the experience.

I ordered two tacos and a basket of chips. The taco meat tasted great but was super spicy and overwhelming with flavor. My forehead was seriously sweaty while attempting to eat it. I expected some onions and lettuce or cilantro or some sort of veggie on my tacos but they were just meat drowning in sauce on tortillas. The chips were a generous portion with a really nice crunch. I consumed the entire basket to try to calm my mouth down from the spiciness of the tacos.

I love Chipotle, this location was a little too busy though. 

The line wrapped around twice and took about 15 minutes to get through. Once we were up at the counter, you could see why it was taking so long. I think they had new employees or maybe a lot of lack of communication was going on, because every was a disarray of condiments and beans. 

The staff was short and obviously stressed with sweat dripping down their faces. 2 employees couldn't wrap my husbands burrito up correctly so someone else had to come over to do it. I got a quesadilla and right before handing it to me one of the employees snatched it back to show another one exactly how it should be folded up in the foil. The whole experience was rushed and awkward. I felt like only 1 or 2 people knew what was happening. They forgot our son's quesadilla and also forgot to give us salsa that we bought. 

Then when we sat down we saw how dirty the floors and tables were. This place was a disaster zone. The food is great, but my advise is to just take it to go.

First time I ever went and was mid lunch rush. I felt hurried along by the chipotle like pizza assembly line crew. First off when asked what sauce I asked in return "what are my options" and he looked back with a blank stare as if I should know this. "Reds fine I guess" I answered back. 

I wasn't clear exactly the price point so if you get 2 or more ingredients it's $8? Still not sure. 

Half my pizza was burnt black too a crisp on the bottom yet the crust was still flimsy when you pick it up and the toppings fell off. If I had dined in I would ask for a redo on the crust as I have a phobia of eating charred black food. The non burnt half was tasty and enjoyable but still not a fan of the hard but still flimsy crust texture. 

I did like the vast options you had and next time I'll go with a chefs choice from the menu and inspect my crust before I leave.

So I was a little prejudiced against this restaurant before my food came out: I walk in-- The hosts are hoity-toity & we-don't-need-you-because-we're-super-popular, the ambience is wanna-be-relevant (dark and loud), the bartenders ignore me until I ask for the menu (I was seated at the bar for dinner)...in fact the noise is so deafening that I can't hear myself think. Plus I'm missing the wiiiide variety of top notch *awesome* Italian in NYC (Been doing the Boston-NYC relationship until I caved and moved back to Boston). Truth be told, I'm tired and a bit grumpy that I've been ignored.

Then the bartender warms up to me a bit, cracks a couple of jokes, lets me know I can do half portions...and my 2-half pastas come out. And they are really solid. Very nicely seasoned, pasta is perfectly al dente, the cheese/ sausage sauce is hearty vs. the tomato sauce is tangy and dotted with sweet, tiny plump rock shrimp...

Ok, it's a great spot for good food. I live a block away, and I'm glad Cinquecento exists. I'll just dress up more next time so that I deserve you ;-)

The Rundown:
I would give Shanghai Fresh 3.5 stars if that was possible.  Authentic flavors and style, but misses the mark in terms of actual quality.  

Context:
Came here for dinner.  I am Shanghainese and have spent several years living in the city.

What I got:
Beef and Scallion Rolls (7.5/10)
I know this dish as Taiwanese (forgive me if I'm wrong on this), but one of my friends recommended it so we ended up getting it.  Surprisingly, this ended up being the best dish I had.  The flavors are quite simple - a scallion pancake wrapped around beef with some hoisin sauce for flavor.  The highlight is of course the beef - which was cooked and seasoned well.  The actual roll itself was a bit too doughy for my taste, but overall I was very satisfied with this dish.  Would likely order it again on a repeat visit.

Shanghai Soup Dumplings (7/10)
These were very nearly the best soup dumplings I've had in Boston - but unfortunately there's a critical flaw.  In terms of flavor and texture, they're spot on.  The thin skin was steamed well, the filling was the proper amount of savory, and as a whole it was quite satisfying.  So what's the issue? The soup.  There was nearly no soup in my soup dumplings, which is really a shame because the rest of the dumpling is quite good!  This problem is further exacerbated by how many of our XLB were stuck to the bottom of the basket, making it nearly impossible to eat without spilling some of the (already limited) soup. 

Traditional Style Sweet & Sour Pork (7/10)
I didn't expect the pork to be breaded, which was fine I guess. The actual flavor was traditional and certainly reminded me of home - this is what sweet and sour should taste like.  However, the stuff this sauce was covering was rather underwhelming - the pork hardly even tasted like meat for some reason and the breading added very little to the dish.

Rice Balls Simmered in Sweet Rice Wine (6/10)
A traditional Shanghainese dessert - not exactly done to its full potential here.  The rice balls were fine - although that's pretty hard to mess up.  The issue of course, is with the broth.  To put it simply, the "rice wine" part of the soup is vastly overpowered by the "sweet" part.  This dish is supposed to properly balance these two aspects and have a much more prominent rice wine flavor.  This is almost entirely absent and the end result is mostly just sweet.  Fine - but I wouldn't get it again.

3.5 Stars.

I have had the soft tacos here a few times and they are really good.  I usually order the spicy chicken and the spicy steak tacos with jalapenos & hot sauce.  Very filling and good value at $2.75 each.

Los Amigos is very small; no tables and only four seats along a window counter.

There is no private parking; only street parking on Centre Street.

I have not experienced any problems with the service.

I need to broaden my horizon at Los Amigos and try the burritos, quesadillas, and Mexican plates.

The drinks are unique, and have always been excellent. The food is constantly inconsistent. Service has always been nice. The lack of music - in the bar, or the private party room really makes Steel & Rye teeter over the edge of the waspy, south shore, most absolute usual experience. The decor is trendy, but the ambience when crowded is dismal. 

Sit at the bar, and pray that your buratta roulette yields the more tasty seasonal version of the often hit or miss cheese plate. How can cheese even be hit or miss? Bon appétit.

Ok, I'm big on sushi and have been to many places around the country and in Japan.  Almost all of my reviews are of sushi places.  I originally went to O-ya but they were booked up so they recommended that we go to Oishii.   

Here's my rating:
Decor ****
-The decor is very modern and hip
Service **
-The sushi took a long time to prepare.  I was very shocked with the price of one of the specials, i'll write more about this later. 
Sushi ***
-I had some traditional pieces, no rolls.  The fish freshness was average.  The Katsuo did not taste very good.  The fish wasn't bad, but it certainly wasn't very fresh. The maguro was not that fresh.    I'm also not a fan of seeing all the piles of sushi in the sushi bar cases all wrapped up in cellophane.  This tells me that the restaurant buys the fish in bulk and holds if for longer periods of time.  This may be a Boston thing.  I also find it strange that no one sits at the sushi bar.  Note that the price is for one piece.  I didn't read carefully so we had to wait another 30 min to get a second order.   We ordered 10 pieces for 2 guys.  I would think that the waiter would recognize that i misread the # of pieces per order.  Why would 2 guys order 5 pieces each, where every piece was different?

Overall my experience here was ok.  Here's what really bothered me.  I asked the waiter about the fois gras sushi on the menu which was $15.  I asked him to compare it to the "special" fois gras sushi that was not on the menu.  He highly recommended the special fois gras.   I expected it to be more expensive, perhaps $20 or $25.  But when i got the bill, it showed $50!!  I feel like the waiter should be obligated to mention the price if it's more than 3x the price of the similar one on the menu.  You can get a lot of good sushi for $50.  The special was good, but not $50 good.  I felt deceived.  This is why i gave the service **.  I certainly will not be coming back and will make reservations at O-ya in the future.

So let me first say that i like the food here; solid traditional carribbean fare but nothing out of the ordinary.  The food is consistent.   Although the oxtail and curried goat as well as roti are good eats,  my hats off to the spinach patties!  This is a unique eat and the owners should try to add  more unique eats to the menu.  My only pet peeve is having something on the menu that is only offerd aonce a week like Ackee & Saltfish.  This is only offered on Saturday mornings which is Jamaican tradition.  What is a dumb American to do?   The owners should add a  disclaimer to the menu to let the ignorant  know.

Starting our road trip from Boston through to Quebec City we stopped off here on the way to visit the Ulta store as the girls wanted to check out the cosmetic prices in the US. I visited Target to stock our car with water and snacks.

This has to be the biggest Target that I have ever seen. It has a full sized supermarket and Target in one and you can pretty much spend a full day there stocking up your car/house/living quarters.

Went here for father's day.     I don't really know what I was expecting, I guess the place kinda looks like a converted diner.

The chairs in the restaurant remind me of my first bachelor pad, cheap and old.   The service was rather slow too even though the restaurant wasn't busy at all.   We were also served lukewarm water to drink.  I ordered some alcoholic drink with ginger in it, and it didn't taste good at all.

I'm giving this place three stars because of the food.   The food was EXCELLENT.  I had the salmon and my wife had one of their bowls.

first time i went into fifty licks I really liked it and thought the service was on point. After going back recently i was a little less impressed and probably wouldn't end up going back again. The ice cream is good, but it seems as if it was annoying to try more than two flavors. There was no line and I wanted to try some i hadn't before.  The dude serving us just had a smug attitude like he didn't want to be helping me. It made me feel unwelcome and it actually kinda bummed me out after talking so highly of this place!

Masa is a nice restaurant in the South End area of Boston, but I have to say that their advertising is incredibly misleading -- they say that all their tapas are half off before 7pm on weekdays, but the catch is that you have to get 10 of them -- you can't pick and choose which ones you want. All 10 of them were really good, some better than others, but they should really advertise the "getting 10" part of the deal. 

Their habanero watermelon margarita was interesting -- sweet with a bit of a kick to it. It was a lot better than I expected. The regular menu doesn't seem that interesting to me, so I think I would stick with the tapas if I come here again.

Stayed here as part of a Costco and Disney package. Checked in well after midnight and the staff in duty was excellent. Day two we had no issues. Day three and beyond is when things started going down. The rooms are spacious, however, our bathroom had no counter space for toothpaste, etc... So we had to have it hanging of the sink. Some other rooms had space. Not sure why our room didn't. FYI RM182

The little things at day three and after is in part to housekeeping. It's the little things that did not get done which makes you wonder about the other things. Starters I left a glass 1/4 full and it wasn't emptied or replaced. I used the coffee maker and cups, sugar, creamer and coffee wasn't replaced. Towels were left in the bathroom on the floor. Sheets not being changed. Ice bucket not being cleaned and ice bag not being replaced. These things are minor but you would expect it to be taken care of. Not to mention housekeeping really has nothing to say to guest in passing in the halls. I've stayed at other hotels and staff is pleasant in passing. 

If housekeeping were like the front of house I'd be rating a four to five star. But housekeeping needs some work. Overall the place is nice. The pool, fitness room, kid zone, the little store. It's all nice. The American restaurant is a little pricey though. Maybe that's why it seemed empty most of our stay. If you find yourself here it's not as bad as some others say. But see for yourself!

We are expecting soon and have been visiting here quite a bit for checkups for mom and baby. So far our experience has been very good. I read in another review that walking into this hospital is like walking into a nice hotel and they are right, this place is very well decorated and has a nice vibe to it.

We have taken a tour of the hospital and I am probably the most impressed with how they have  places in the rooms for the fathers to sleep. I also like how they use electronic tracking (with bracelets) to make sure your baby doesnt get switched up with someone else's!!! Good Idea,LOL:)

On the few occasions that I have had to talk to anyone on the phone there at the hospital, they have been very nice although in some of my face-to-face interactions with billing, customer service,etc they sometimes come across as being a little short with you. So far I have just chalked this up to them probably having to deal with irate/irrational people all day long.

Our Doctor has been Dr. Stone and we love this guy. Super-smart doctor, excellent bedside manner and just an all-around nice person.

I am giving Northside 3-stars only because we havent had the baby yet, after the big day is finished, I will amend my review and probably be giving them 4-stars if what I have seen so far is any indication.

Stopped in late on a Friday night on our way to hotel after flight cancellation at ATL -- happy to find the kitchen still open somewhere other than Waffle House or McDonalds (is that even a kitchen?).  Place was pretty dead for a Friday night.  A couple of locals at the bar along with a business traveler hitting on the bartender.  One of the waitresses was essentially making out with her boyfriend at one of the tables but the management didn't seem to care.  
Sat at the bar and the bartender was very nice.  Good beer selection on draught and in bottles.  I had the shrimp and grits and it was good.  I was warned that it was spicy, but didn't really feel that much heat.  
Overall, a nice facility with a decent menu and bar, but the place was nearly empty on a Friday night.  The manager on duty clearly wanted to get out of there as he was telling the staff to start shutting things down well before the posted closing time, including telling the bartender to declare last call before she wanted to.  Seems like the place could use a jolt at the management level.  Otherwise, it was a ok place to stop for a drink and bite to eat.

We went back for Magical Dining month and I was not as impressed as I have been previously. I have visited this location back in April and have since visited the Tampa location and held the restaurant in high regard. I previously rated this restaurant 5 stars and have encouraged people who haven't visited to try it. This visit the grouper was not available, which was a bummer since we both wanted it and picked it out from the magical dining menu. They substituted swordfish which was at least good they provided another option instead of just saying it was not available. I had the sea bass and did not think it was worth the extra $10. I got this dish at the Tampa location and it was not as good as I remember. We also ordered the crab fried rice and again it was not as good as we remember from dining in Tampa. It was oily and bland. Even the bread pudding didn't seem as good as we remembered it from our visit a few months ago. It was a very busy night though and I wonder if it was so busy that the quality slipped. Overall after tip and paying $60 per person it didn't seem like the meal was anything special versus going to Bonefish. It was not extraordinary or worth the price.

I really like the concept, and the menu, and the food has been good. However, we came for Sunday brunch, and we are the ONLY table right now, and so far we've ordered our meals and it has taken an hour to bring our meals. And we've gotten 2 things. I took a picture to include with this review that illustrates the fact that we are the only table seated in the restaurant right now. How can service be so slow? The food really tastes good, but I had to send my cappuccino back twice because whoever is making them doesn't understand how to use the machine. The first cappuccino was fine. Very good, in fact. I suggested the coffee to my table-mates. But they couldn't get any because the restaurant doesn't serve decaf. So they brought my second cappuccino and it was just brewed coffee with a little spray of foam on top. The server said its because it was a "double." No, sorry. Not true. She brought out a third. It was still wrong. Same thing, brewed coffee with a little spray of  foam.  I told her that the first cappuccino had been perfect, so can't they just make another one like that? Finally, on the third try, they got me the right thing. It was perfect again! And the DJ.....I really like the music he plays. He does disco and 80's Pop and some 70's dance stuff. He apparently LOVES Michael Jackson. And who doesn't, honestly? But I think he played every single one of his albums. And the volume was way too loud. Like, WAY. Especially keeping in mind that we were the only table here. It's not like he needed to play over a bunch of talking. We were having a family brunch with some in-laws that we don't see very often because we are from out of town (moved away three years ago). We asked twice for him to turn the volume down. We wanted to be able to hear each other talk. He did reduce the volume once. But it's just really too loud for a Sunday brunch. Now, I have to tell you, the strawberry shortcake, praline pancakes, salad, frittatas, grilled salmon.....ALL EXCELLENT!!!!! Very very good food. I'm wishing we had one of these in Atlanta but they would definitely have to step up their service! I think we would try again based on the menu and food quality. But maybe not for a family brunch because we can't hear each other. And it takes a LONG time to get served. I would give 5 stars next time if these issues are fixed. The food is VERY VERY good!!!

I never dine in here, so this review is purely based on the food and take-out/delivery service. 

When my roommates and I moved to JP this was the first place we dined at and I'm pretty sure we didn't eat anywhere else for at least the first three days while we were getting unpacked/situated in the new place. The menu is massive to the point of being pretty overwhelming the first time you want to order something, but it's pretty fair to say that it has more hits than misses. Some of my favorites include their loaded skins, the Texan, the Columbian, and my roommates all swear by the Chicken Ranch as well as their pizza. Some disappointments I've had include their chicken fingers as well as their Top Shelf Italian. 

The staff are usually pretty friendly, but as I stated before, I usually just order take-out from this place. It's super convenient that you can call in to order or just do it on their website. Also, I once accidentally ordered take-out from their Roxbury location but went to pick it up at the JP spot and they were super friendly about it (even though I felt like an idiot) and made my sandwich for me fairly quickly. Also, on their website, I'm in love with the "preparing" icon of an animated knife cutting a tomato. 

All in all, it's a more than decent sandwich shop that is priced incredibly reasonably, particularly due to the fact that often one sandwich will feed me for two meals.

This theater could be a great theater if it hires the right people, not teenagers that call out making everyone suffer from their lack of responsibility. The theatre was my family's go to theater and everything was great except the concessions stands where sometimes it would be a long wait. I missed half of Moana because of the slow service of the concession stand. If you have kids like me, the kid packs were a good deal when they were $7.00 now they're up to I think $9.00, rip off. The theatre has reclining seats with stadium seating, best seats so far in a theatre that Ive been to. You can also reserve your seats when you purchase your tickets. We since moved to Central Florida where reclining seats in theatres are nonexistent and the $5.00 funnel cakes are missed.

PS. It is flocked with teens on some nights. It is good for late night movie dates as it has a bar, the s'mores martini is to die for!

First off, all the brunch entrees are $8 before noon, and that's a great deal, especially in Back Bay. That being said, few things disappoint me more when meat is overcooked. We ordered steak and eggs with the steak cooked medium rare, but what we received was definitely NOT medium rare. I'd rather pay full price and get what I ordered. 

Service was attentive although the restaurant was crowded. I may come back when the weather warms up for the patio, but I just wasn't impressed with the brunch happy hour.

This place is a flat out 3.5 stars for me based on their services, atmosphere and the food itself.
I've been here twice. Both at peak hours of the day and week. Luckily I was able to find seating for 2 and seating for 5. Its a pretty small place and parking is also limited. The people working behind the counter generally only speak Chinese with limited English. Like when you order in English, you should just tell them the number vs what it actually is cause they may not catch you properly. It doesn't look like they have a system on how their orders should be or how to serve people. So in other words, there may be a long wait for you or your order may be wrong. 

I also want to say, if you hate the smell of durian I suggest you to not stay here for long or even walk in. Once they make one durian dessert,  the whole place smells like durian. From what I remember, they have durian pancake and mochi. I also witness this one time that this customer ordered mango pancake, But cause you can't see the inside of the pancake, she got the durian one. Man, she spat it right out and was hardcore looking for water. It was such a funny scene. I totally understand how she felt when you were thinking it's mango in the middle but you got durian. 

The food itself is ok. No complaints nor is there one thing I love a lot that I have to go back for it. But I think in order to enjoy the dessert properly, I suggest you to take it to go. This place does make good mango desserts hence the name mango yummy. But personally I just don't like being in the store for too long. I would suggest people to come and try it out if you enjoy mango and don't mind the smell of durian.

I was excited to try Bistro 4 from all the lovely Yelps...

We went for dinner service which they started this past Jan 14.

The crab cake app was simply amazing and had plenty of crab and a nice spicy kick.

we ordered the short rib and shrimp etouffee  for our mains.

the short rib was done very well and shrimp etouffee was good but certainly did not stand out as something we would go back for.

We thought overall a nice place to eat but the crab cake was the highlight of the meal.

I want to go back and try their brunch which seems to be the star of the restaurant.

The dinner service still seems to be sorted out to be as good as the brunch...

I went here for the first time this afternoon.  It was good, but nothing special IMHO.  If you're in the area, then sure, make a trip, but it's not worth it to go out of your way to eat here.

I got a Cowboy style Killer Combo.  Overall the burger was tasty, and although no pink, it didn't seem overdone like another reviewer's comment that it's like the overcooked burgers at Five Guys.  The fries were good, but again, nothing special.  It was plenty of food, and a single patty filled me up.  The total bill came out to be around $9.

I do think I need to point out that people talk about how this is a place for "cheap eats", but I don't think it's that different in price compared to the competition?

The eating area seems to fill up quickly, but you can find seating elsewhere around the Sweet Auburn Market pretty easily.

Parking is free, as long as you get your ticket validated at the counter.

Its Kroger right? Welllll if you had ever gone into this location before the remodel, you would understand that this is NOT the same store. I graduated from OSU and lived on 8th for 2 years and avoided that old scary run down Kroger as much as possible. 

NOW....Since I was in the area, and there is not a Kroger very close to my current home I stopped in. This place is great. There is plenty of well lit parking, everything is well organized and neat on the shelves. 

I was not impressed with their selection of local produce from local farmers. It looked like it had not been watered, and needed to be restocked. Buying local is important to people these days. Having the display is a step in the right direction, but a "fail" based on what the produce looked like.

Also, I may have liked it better if someone had asked me if they could help me find anything. It still throws me off sometimes that the "Natural Foods" section is on the other side of the store as all the "other foods(?)" sections. I thought it was all edible food...but who am I?

A competetor store is closeset to my home location, but they cannot compete with Krogers prices. That is definately something that will keep me coming back, especially to this shiny new store.

There were plenty of cashiers waiting at the check out, and the bagger even helped me to unload my cart. Good stuff!

Upon leaving, the police officers in the parking lot made me take a second look. A Tuesday evening in a Kroger might be a dangerous place?...hmmm

Overall, a giant step in the right direction, but needs help keeping the momentum.

Some places are hyped up and can't live up to it, other places are praised and have stood the test of time for good reason; Mr. Bartley's is certainly that of the latter. Right in the middle-of-it-all on Mass. Ave in Harvard Square, this family run business has been serving up Boston's best burgers for almost fifty years, and they're not afraid to show it. Bombarded by "Best of" signs from any publication possible and Boston memorabilia scattered throughout, Bartley's has no shame in showing its the tops and that its all Boston all the time. But do they live up to it? Well, yes, mostly. Listing over thirty burgers on the big board, there's something for everyone, not to mention house made Raspberry Lime Rickey's (superb) and frappes (also superb). For around ten dollars you get a burger with fries or onion rings and a pickle. The burgers aren't huge, weighing in at 7 oz., but honestly, I can't say that I need much more then that these days anyway. One of us receives a very generous portion of onion rings while I seem to be lacking on the french fry end. The fries are good, solid, if unspectacular. The onion rings, however, are beyond awful. Limp, mealy and downright offensive, they have to be among the worst I've had in some time. The burgers, ground daily from choice beef, are nice, they come served on a delightful toasted sesame bun and my burger (the Tom Werner) comes with bacon and cheddar cheese. The first thing I notice is the cheese, as it oozes its way from all sides of the patty into melted cheese heaven, there is a perfect symphony of bread, meat and cheese in the first few bites. After that, however, I feel a little dryness, not in the burger itself, which is juicy, just not overly-so, but without condiments included in the sandwich, I feel the need to add some ketchup. (thankfully we're not at Louis Lunch) Ketchup could go either way for me, if I need it so be it, but its not a make or break situation, in this case I do need something, and I'm okay with that. My last few bites are all bread unfortunately, a big pet peeve of mine, and the meat was good, nice flavor, but not the best I've had. I will compliment them in that they are the first place to actually cook my burger properly. ( in this case a nice and red medium-rare) The waitress also offers a follow-up inquiry upon first bite to make sure it is cooked to my liking, so a huge compliment for that. Maybe its not the best burger we've had yet, but its up there, and there is something about this place you can't help but love. Maybe its the history, the fact that its still a family run establishment and all the sites, smells and sounds of a great burger place are all prevalent. Worth all the press and accolades? I'd say so, but still not burger perfection.

Porter Square Books is conveniently located close to where I live, so it's usually the first place I'll check if I'm looking for a book. Sometimes it's the only place I have to look, but often I have to check somewhere else. Maybe I'm looking for some pretty unpopular titles. 

More likely it's that PSB is-- relatively speaking-- a tiny store, a good portion of which is occupied by the cafe. That said, the selection is a pretty decent cross section but it's a tad dilettantish. While it's not Waldenbooks (are they still around?) or the South Station book stand, it still feels like any generic bookstore you might find at any other mall.

 I wonder if they might do better or worse by cutting back on the mass market stock and bulking up on more quirky and/or niche-market titles. With the space they're working with,  it seems like the only thing that is giving them any competitive edge over the good bookstore and great bookstore just a mile or so east on Mass Ave is the Cafe. 

It's a decent bookstore, and a conveniently local one (for me), but it could benefit from a little focus.

The food and service was excellent!  The steak was cooked perfectly and I didn't even need my knife.  Our waiter was attentive without being annoying.  The restaurant was completely booked and the food was still served in a very timely manner.  My only disaapointment on the menu is the lack of non seafood items as appetizers.

A couple things to consider though.  The restaurant is not easy to find.  I got completely turned around and had to call the restaurant twice.  My phone navigation and Mapquest were of no help because the restaurant is tucked behind the Ritz.  There is no one to greet you when you walk in so arriving by yourself can be awkward.  You have to walk around the bar to find the host stand.  If you are sensitive to smoke make sure you ask to sit away from the bar where is smoking is allowed.  The noise level was very high.  The music was good though.  This is not an ideal first date dinner place.  You would basically have to sit in your date's lap to have a normal conversation.  

While the food was excellent, I don't know that I would go back.  With so many other restaurants in the area something more convenient and not so noisy would better suit me.

Pros: 
Good food at a reasonable price
Quick

Cons:
Stuff is rude and in your face (this has happened to me twice)
They tend to be stingy about the sauce ($.25/thimble full)
Limited space

Overall:
I would go back for the food, but it is not worth it to be treated poorly.

*Note to staff* If you had forks and napkins at the table I wouldn't have to go get some. Sometimes, the holder is just missing-maybe it fell off the table maybe it was moved-but grabbing a plastic fork is no reason to yell at me and tell me to sit down.

My boyfriend took me here on a whim and it was great. But, unfortunately I can't give it 5 stars...it was lacking somewhere and neither him nor I could put our finger on it, but "something" was definitely missing. The taste of the food was great, but maybe it was the lack of any sides with the pricey main dishes? Cute little place, nice staff, but I don't see us returning. Especially with the abundance of places to choose from, that offer a bit more with a meal.

I don't know.. 

I want to love it, but I have a semi hard time paying this much for something that I can (easily) make at home . It was okay..I'm not mad that I tried it, and I might give Bareburger one more try before I decide if it's worth a few more stars. 

The burger was, again, just okay. The carrot slaw was probably one of the worst things I've ever eaten...I think anytime you are finely shredding a vegetable that you probably need to add salt and or pepper and not just "wasabi"--because, gross. 

The sweet fries would have probably been okay had they come with the sauce..plain fries are always just going to be...meh...to me.

We got yam fries, blueberry shaved ice, passion fruit slush, and a fruit sundae. 

Great texture for the fries but not yam-my enough. Pretty good price and portion for the shaved ice. I really liked the frozen blueberries. I would get it again ! 

Overall there's a huge variety of food to choose from which is great. Terrible service tho ! The server came like every 10 mins so we had to wait a while to order, and to get an extra spoon. Also she didn't speak or understand English very well. Also - very weird music

I was really craving a burger and found this place on Yelp as a must try. So the restaurant itself is very modern looking with a great looking bar and nice outdoor seating. Came here through an OpenTable reservation on a Friday night. We were sat immediately and served water. However, it took 15 mins after just to get a server to come by. There were about 4 tables in our section but for some reason did not get service off the bat. To the food now. Ordered Garlic Parmesan Fries for the appetizer which were amazing. The entrees were salmon and of course the B9 burger that I came for. The burger was cooked perfectly but was missing something on seasoning of the patty. Would recommend to order the pickled jalapeños and bacon on your burger. The salmon was tasty and the mushrooms were my favorite part of that dish. I rate this 3 stars due to the service and being a little underwhelmed on the burger. For a $20 burger I was expecting a lot more.

Pro's: Winnie the Pooh and friends for breakfast and Cinderella and friends for dinner. I was not aware the characters were going to be there so that was a nice surprise. They come right up to the table and talk with you so easy 1:1 time without having to wait in line and also nice photo taken before you go into the restaurant that is available for purchase. The Grand Floridian is also GORGEOUS so must see place while at Disney.

Con's: The food isn't great so if you do not care about meeting characters, do not go here. The food itself is definitely not worth the price. Also if you hate children (not judging but like if you hate kids unsure why you're at Disney anyways) then do not go here!! There are tons of super adorable little girls especially dressed up in princess costumes waiting to meet Cinderella.

Truthfully:  1 star in the Winter and 4 stars in the Summer.  

I know that averages 2 stars but as it is now Spring and there is no more rain, snow, sleet, "winter mix", and other painful things that fall from the merciless skies- I'll give it 3 stars.

I get to Charlestown Bridge at least 4 times a week, seeing as I live in the North End and my grocery store, my running route, some restaurants, lots of people I know, and church lies in Charlestown.  I know you are saying, why not use the locks in the winter?  It just adds so much more distance to my pedestrian commute.  :P  

In the winter, there is no place with more wind, rain, and anger being forced onto you as this bridge.  The street turns into massive puddles that become tsunamis when buses and bad Boston drivers splash through them.  I've seen the splashes go up to 15 feet high and have been splashed so many times my SADD seems more than justified.  

I know the gratings scare people, but I've learned that bridges were built to hold 5 times their maximum possible strain.  Still, it can be scary to look down through the grating during a storm and see the white caps and get reminded of scenes from Perfect Storm.

Anyways, it is Spring now, which means the bridge is beautiful again.  In no time, the bums will come back to live in the abandoned rotational tower and all will be well again.  At night, the bridge is beautifully lit up- more like a midway carnival booth and not in mood lighting like Zakim Bunker Hill Bridge or the TD Garden.  

Recommendation- walk on the left side of the road on the way to Charlestown to avoid the tourists and their silly picture taking.  It also allows you to descend to Paul Revere park easier.

We happened to stumble upon this restaurant in the battery area.

Ambience: has a 90s rustic feel with introducing decor and vibe (see pictures) with interesting furniture and wall decorations. 

Service: excellent! Our waiter was very helpful in explaining the menu and in our food choices. She was very responsive with our needs and even gave us extra bag of chips/salsa to go! 

Food: for the quality of the food, the cost did not match. Do not get me wrong though... the portion sizes were large but the food (especially the fluffy taco- which is basically an empty taco) was bland/not anything too new or interesting.

When you book this place, you should already have expectations that it isn't going to be a fancy stay. We were there in June. For the price of the room, it is very decent. It is a motel so flies/mosquitoes are likely to go into the room. However, the a/c is good so that can save you from mosquito bites. Bathroom is small, but everything works. It is very conveniently located near the light rail so you have easy access to downtown. It is also near some trendy eateries. If you like budget-friendly, this is your place.

Came back to Bar Louie for a happy hour visit. The atmosphere is laid back and kinda sport barish. The bartender was very helpful and the drinks were great. The bar louie cosmo was delicious--love the white cranberry juice & sugar cane blend. The bloody mary was spicy and tasty. Both only $5! 
1/2 off apps were a great deal! The calamari was pretty good, the pot stickers were yummy, and the schezwan wings were delicious! 
2 drinks + 3 apps for $25 before tip= Great deal! 

Over all a good happy hour experience! I will be back for sure!

La voile is a very cute and casual French restaurant hidden in the middle of Newbury Street. They are famous for their foie gras and of course, it did not disappoint me. If it is your first time here, you should try their combination foie gras - Les Deux - which contains both the pan-seared foie gras and foie gras terrine on toast (that's a lot of foie gras! share it with two or three people). For entree, I ordered "Le Filet De Boeuf" -  pan seared beef tenderloin with spinach. The entree did not impress me but it was not bad at all. It was just under my expectation, expecting it to be more juicy and soft. From what I've heard from my friends who came to La Voile before, they really loved their rissoto, so I'm gonna give it a try next time when I come here again for dinner! I personally didn't really like their dessert at all. I ordered a dessert called floating island that the waiter recommended - but it was basically a huge marshmallow floating above creamy juice. Try something else, don't order that!

Reading the reviews and hearing many people who have had Koi Fusion, my husband and I were desperate to try it. We looked for it for such a long time, and finally got the chance to try it. My husband got a bulgogi and chicken tacos. I ordered a bulgogi burrito. 
Maybe it was due to the high expectations... but I definitely have to say that it was not mind blowing, or addicting. It is hard to explain how it tastes, but it is korean food put into mexican context. Do not get me wrong, it is good, but not as mind blowing as it seemed to be for others. 
The meat is juicy and if you are going to get it, I would recommend getting it with kimchi.  The tacos seemed to be missing something, and the burrito was missing flavor. It is good, but to be honest, I'd rather have korean and mexican separate. I think that they just made it too non-extreme that, for me who loves authentic flavors, it seemed too bland. 
I might try it again, but if it was next to other carts, I might go somewhere else.

I was here for dinner recently.

Food 4/5: We ordered a variety of dishes to share amongst our group.  The skewers are fantastic -- nothing beats charcoal!  Get the quail egg wrapped in pork.  Other memorable dishes included the karaage and the soft shell crab fried rice.  Grilled rice balls were disappointing and way too salty.  I'd suggest not ordering the typical sushi and sashimi since there are so many other things on the menu to choose from.

Atmosphere 3/5: Small, busy restaurant.  Quite full on a weeknight.  Unless you're there early, you might want to get a reservation.  Tables in the backroom area where we were seated are pack WAY to tight.

Service 2/5: Hit and miss.  One of the male servers was friendly and attentive, but another female server was absolutely hopeless and borderline ignoring us.  Some dishes took quite some time to arrive and tea refills were few and far between.  They definitely need to work on this.

Value 3/5: Okay.  it's great to get away from the typical menu items found at other Japanese restaurants.  We spent about $25 each and left with full bellies.

Overall: 3/5.

I'm very on the fence about this place, I've had both good experiences and bad.

Bad stuff first: Only a couple things really bug me about Momo, but one is that they have a really awesome patio, but it's always overrun with smokers. I know that's not necessarily their fault, but it doesn't make the place any more appealing. On weekend nights, they also have someone at the door watching capacity, and the same guy has been very rude to me/my group on multiple occasions. It's really frustrating to be told there's a 20 minute wait when you can see plenty of standing room and three open booths right behind the guy. On top of that he's always kind of bratty and condescending about the whole situation.

Aside from that, the bar service is normally pretty solid with the exception of an off night here and there, but I think that's understandable for any given bar. They have a really great ambiance and pretty reasonable prices, and a good variety of beers.

End takeaways: Momo is great for happy hour, but one of that last places I'd try to go on a Friday or Saturday night.

Solidly 3 stars. 

The atmosphere is SUPER cool. I feel like this vibe is what Harvard used to be like in the 90s (Idk where I got that idea from.....). Anyways the place feels like an old moroccan cafe, with big wooden vaulted ceiling, old books and teapots everywhere, and like.... old church music? cathedral music? It adds to the atmosphere. The snacks are fine, the coffee is NOT good so don't come here expecting a fine brew. Maybe tea?

I think the prices are high for me to make this a regular study/work spot - an iced coffee and single cookie ran me $10 plus tip. But if you are looking for a quiet, chill spot, this just might be your place.

Had dinner here a week ago. The food was average but that's not really what this place is about. If you are looking for a decent beer list, the Brick House Tavern is not a bad choice. You got an ample list of good beers supported by typical fare. Fortunately, the food is reasonably priced so don't fret too much about the reviews trashing it. The beer can be served in a giant bong if you're thirsty, which is a nice diversion. I'd go here again for the beer list if nothing else.

I want to commend Zach, the Customer Service manger, for his persistence in calling me to follow up.

After our phone conversation, we scheduled time for Zach to come to our home. I had to reschedule and he was accomodating. 

When Zach came to our home, he listened to all of our concerns, adjusted the regulator valve to provide more water pressure in the house, and inspected the other work to make sure it was done appropriately. 

Most importantly,  he acknowledged where he felt the company had made mistakes and offered a reasonable solution. Zach has earned a five star rating for professionalism and service. 

OPINION: I believe Radiant wants to be a leader in the market for creating a great place to work and offering their employees great benefits.  However,  that translates into higher costs for services, and perhaps encouragement or reward for employees to 'find' problems to fix. They may be doing it for all the right reasons but the cost of service is probably the highest in the Austin market and other reviews share the same concerns.

That being said, a company's willingness to address concerns and find reasonable solutions is commendable.

Where I would go when I'm too lazy to walk to Starbuck or Dunkin. I mean no offense.
There are some very nice people here, but once or twice there would be someone wanting to bite my head off when asking what I want to drink. Such unpleasantly so early in the morning, ouch! My "have a nice day" was not well received, hic. 
So when I see those people at the counter, I just skip my coffee for the day and wait until nicer faces are ready to take my order.

But alas the ice chai is good. The ice tea is good when you dose it in unlimited liquid sugar. Some of their hot drinks though take a century to be made... There was like 2 people in line, making me late for class pooh. 

It's overall quite inconsistent but at least I know my ice chai and ice tea is delicious. I will only play it safe here, since on some occasion of being adventurous I was left with some funky tasting frap or late or something that made me quite depressed.

Food was good but a bit too pricey in my opinion. If the staff is allowed to wear jeans then it isn't as upscale as they make it to be. drinks are very expensive- they don't have basic grenadine or anything for people who don't like alcoholic beverages. My server was very knowledgeable and sweet, jacqueline i believe it was. Hostess, shaniq, was super kind when greeting me at the door. managers do not seem to know what they're doing, saw some gentlemen who seemed important yelling at them.. if you have to yell at your managers to do something, how do you think they treat the staff? might come back.

So cruising for a place for breakfast and noticed cultivate opened in the new development off of howell mill. Clicked on the post and instantly saw RUMCHATA FRENCH TOAST and I instantly said this is the place for me! I mean who wouldn't love Rumchata French's Toast, right!!?!!! 

A friend and I arrived to the restaurant and it looks really cool, great decor, Uber modern fun pop'ish art and inviting.  We were greeted by the host and sat down in the coffee bar area, the environment was terrific, and felt like it was almost out of a west elm catalog... (kudos to the decorator) 

Our server was friendly and attentive along with anyone we came into contact with during the course of our meal. At one point my friend made a comment there seems to be more workers than patrons in the restaurant and as I looked around he wasn't kidding... everyone looked happy and worked together in a unified team of people who really enjoyed where they were working...

Ok, now down to business... 
there was no doubt in my mind that I was gonna get those Rumchata French Toast... but after viewing the menu, I was instantly thrown in a conundrum of am I making the right decision. I questioned my need for what I really came here to experience because  EVERYTHING LOOKED D'LISH!!!! 

Holding on strong, I stuck to my gut and got the Rumchata French Toast and a cup of coffee, my friend got the Breakfast sandwich with and extra dalup of pimento cheese... because, you know, duh, why not (!!?!) and an ice tea.

To my dismay the coffee wasn't as yummy as I was hoping... Maybe it's was because it was just stronger than I expected? Maybe it's because of the acidity? Maybe it was just not a good batch? Maybe it wasn't the kind of coffee I was hoping? Maybe my taste buds were just off today? Maybe, maybe. I typically like a medium mild smooth coffee - so maybe it was just me. Maybe. The cream, yes- I like cream in my coffee curled the moment I poured it into my cup but it didn't smell bad so I thought well maybe it's just me being a brat.. it wasn't sour but also didn't look great in my morning cup of joe. 

Sigh, ok- I know you want to know my thoughts on this infamous Rumchata French Toast I've been going on and on about - it was super disappointing and I regretted every moment of this decision, especially when I looked around and saw everyone else's plate and, it ALLL LOOK AMAZING! 

Rumchata French Toast Review:
When my meal arrived it was a plate of toast with a side squirt of whip cream, a side of mixed berries and a small ramekin of a berry compote - question mark??? It also came with some very liquidity syrup.... I don't know about you but 'i think' syrup should have a more dense consistency? What do I know... 
 
But trying to be open minded I dug into my meal....
um......
WHERE WAS THE RUMCHATA!?!?! 
Again, 
WHERE WAS THE RUMCHATA!?!?! 

The French Toast was dry, (maybe not dipped in the batter long enough? ) with a hint of cinnamon. So, what does one do, add more drippy syrup and oh how about the compote... ok, lil'l better- thank goodness for the side of dry berries, it helped. 

So in conclusion - Rumchata  French Toast - not good. So Sorry. But you can't when them all right? 

On the other hand- the breakfast sandwich was fabulous! It was everything my friend could ever want in the world and he enjoyed every bite!! 

Looking around the avocado toast looked just as yummy ...

So, sorry for the long drawn out review...
Don't know if I'll be back... but glad I tried this place.

Nice museum area and exhibits with a lot of food options nearby. Air conditioning was a real treat after walking around in the Texas heat. Close to bus stops and lodging. Note special to researchers:  be warned if you're coming here for archival research. The heavyset, balding older guy with a mustache who was working the desk needed some serious customer service training. I saw him pretty much yelling at an undergrad (as loud as acceptable in an archive, anyhow), and being generally unhelpful to researchers. Get a grip. Rest of the staff were quite pleasant; just avoid that one.

Arrived there a bit before 11pm Friday night, not too big of a crowd. Music was great, and it finally started to pick up near midnight. Good atmosphere overall, and good-looking crowd too =). Bartenders and bouncers were pretty courteous as well.

Drinks were quite pricey ($11/Stolichnaya shot, 14$ for Red Bull-Grey Goose!) but relatively strong. Urinals and sinks were hard to tell apart sober, imagine when you've had a few drinks...

Overall though it was good night, just pre-gaming is recommended.

A lunch visit here recently showed up some of the themes of the reviews below. The service was spotty - I was undisturbed for quite a while after I was seated, for example - but not truly terrible.

As for the food, I ordered the fish tacos, and they needed some work. Mostly, they were underseasoned. The fried fish was quite plain, the guacamole had no garlic and not enough salt, and the salsa was more of a cooked tomato sauce - no cilantro in it, and very little heat. (There were a couple of cilantro sprigs on top of the three tacos, and they helped). The tortillas were flour, but had been run under a boiler or something, coming out rather hard and dry.

Well, as the waitress helpfully pointed out, I *had* ordered fish tacos in New England. Never mind that you can get better ones in Connecticut, and (presumably) better food here at LTK. . .

I've visited twice now, and while the food (or at least the one thing I ordered twice) is astounding, I don't think I'll be in a rush to return. Why not? Because they're clearly not in a rush to serve it.

That delicious dish that I ordered twice? Their poké bowl. It's fan-frickin-tastic. A healthy portion of ahi tuna served over a bed of rice and cabbage and god-knows-what else. It's perfectly portioned, hearty and healthy and really, just amazing.

So what's my problem? The wait. On my first visit, I waited 30 minutes for my meal. There was only one guy in the cart, and he apologized for the wait, saying that usually he has his wife there with him. It was frustrating, but he had a good excuse and the food was delicious, so I vowed to come back. I returned today, when the husband-wife team was both in action, and waited 40 minutes for the same dish. Again, delicious food. Again, apologies for the wait. I'd be much more likely to believe them if they were actually hustling to get stuff out, but they were moving around with what I saw as no sense of urgency. I get that you're serving island food, but I'm not on island time. I have meetings to attend and places to be, and waiting this long for food from a cart? Not ok.

At this point, the only way I'd return is if it were on a weekend and I was enjoying some beers in the pod, with nowhere else to be. One last time, the food is delicious. It just takes way, way too long to get out to you.

I attended my first-ever Celtics' home opener. Yes, the Celtics aren't the Red Sox (at least not this year), but my son and I love the NBA. Tickets were cheap and Miss Marry and I bussed down to meet Mark, who took the commuter rail up from Providence.

I love the walk from South Station over to TD Bank Garden. Knowing the prices for bad food and beer, we opted to eat beforehand.

There are all kinds of watering holes along Canal Street, near TDB Garden. Hurrican O'Reilly's is a favorite of the Celtics crowd, as we've been there before (probably before a Celtics game).

My wife and I went with the O'Reilly Burger, which was solid burger with sweet baby ray's" bbq sauce & aged cheddar cheese. It comes with fries for $9.00. You'd be hard-pressed to get a beer next door for that.

Rockin' place pre-game, and 98.5, The Sports Hub (w/ Felger & Mazz) were broadcasting live, sans Felger.

Hurricane O'Reilly's is a good place to drink and grab a bite before a game. Yes, it's crowded and noisy on game nights, but staff do a good job getting you in and out.

Serviceable and reasonably priced.

Had breakfast shortly after they opened.  It was a little strange that a place so big was so empty, but I'm sure this was mostly because of the poor weather the night before.  Service could have been better given how few people were in - it took a while for everyone to get their drinks.

I realize this place is all chocolate all the time, but it didn't really go with the omelet and egg dishes.  The rest of the food was average and could have used a little more flavor.

I'm in town for work and this place looked interesting. It was close to the hotel where I was staying, which met my criteria to choosing Barley's Brewing Company. The prices are good. The food is a basic bar menu with a few unique combo's of cheeses thrown in various dishes. I wasn't drinking so I can't comment on the craft brews, but it seemed like everyone in the place was enjoying their beers. The chili was good. All the vegetables were fresh and large (in a good way). The waiter and servers were efficient. The staff keep an eye on you, but were not overbearing. If I go again I'll focus more on the beer and less on everything else.

I've been going here for years because it's convenient and they take pride in their craft. But, this morning, per usual, the guy who wrote up my ticket tried to upsell me on several fronts. It's annoying, but he works on commission, I get it. When he asks if I wanted the yearly special for $28/month, I said no thank you and he yells at me while I'm walking away "see you next week for $37." What is that? Customer service? A tactic to close the deal? Meanwhile I'm ducking the guy who's leaning over my windshield, about to pressure me into fixing the small crack that is already filled in. It's all exhausting...all I wanted was a car wash.

Its a nice place to grab soup and and a sandwich if your on the north side of Boulder. The breads are excellent and the chicken noodle soup I had today was hearty, large pieces of vegetable and chicken. Its a self service lunch counter type setup with selections ranging from fresh breads, entrees, salads, soups and sweets. There is even a gelato counter. Its a little pricey for a daily lunch stop, the macaroni and cheese entree with soup and a baguette plus bottled water came to almost $15

I would categorize Boma as being a place to visit once, but I don't know if our next visit to Disney World will include this restaurant. 

Boma is a buffet style restaurant that does have a wide variety of vegetarian options with an African flare. Some of the dishes do have a different taste (but not horrible) 

Our waiter was nice guy from NY city and gave us a lot of space to enjoy one of our honeymoon dinners. 

The atmosphere was nice and clean and the girls at the front when we were waiting to be seated were very kind. 

Because it was our honeymoon, they gave us a special desert .

Matcha Ice-cream float with mochi $4.8 3/5
I wanted to order the matcha ice-cream with mochi but she suggested this instead.  1/3 of them was ice.  They were smaller pieces of ice so it was hard to dig them out.  The matcha tea was freshly made so it was warm.  I would rather have pre-made iced matcha tea.  The ice-cream was smaller and sweeter than expected consider it was in a Japanese restaurant.  I would say 1/3 of a McDonald's $1 ice-cream.  It only came with 4 pieces of mochi (2 pink, 1 white, and 1 green).  I wish there were more.  Not worth the extra $0.50.  It also took a while for her to make this simple ice-cream float.

Hmm....3.5 stars?

The four of us shared a calamari that was ok
I had the paella ($20) and my boyfriend had the steak tips ($16)
Our friends had the paella and salmon padthai.

My boyfriend loved the food. I thought it was pretty good.
I think for a restaurant at this price, it's a three star.
If the restaurant was charging under $15/ entree, it would be a four star.

On a side note, i thought the whole restaurant smelled like a mix of seafood and a moldy mop.
The restrooms had faucets a LOT higher than the sink so it splashes if ur not careful, and the toilet papers do not have covers.
