I really think if you're going to charge people that much, sanitation could be improved.

I'm not a big fan of fast food. I don't do drive throughs often and I try and stick to healthier food options. However, sometimes you just gotta bite the bullet. This McDonalds happened to be at the right place at the right time. I was hungry, in a hurry, and the only other option nearby was Tim Horton's across the street. Too bad it was raining, and I didn't want to get out of the car. 

I pulled up to order my food and was greeted right away by the attendant. It was a little hard to hear, maybe the speaker volume could be turned up, but within a minute I was pulling up to the first window, eager to pay for my breakfast. By the way, I ordered a hash brown and an egg and cheese sandwich. The gentlemen that took my money was friendly and fast. On to the second window... I hardly had time to push the break and the window was open and another gentleman was handing me my food. I pulled around and parked in a parking spot to scarf everything down. There were plenty of spaces available, it was clean, and I wasn't the only one sitting in a car eating my meal. 

My food was piping hot and was exactly what I ordered. Fast, cheap, and friendly. Honestly, I was surprised by this experience considering the other reviews, but glad I gave it a chance when I was borderline hangry. It did the trick.

This is a fairly decent Japanese restaurant in the Marpole area.  The space is clean and inviting.  If you care, the chefs aren't Japanese, but the food is still tasty.

I ordered several rolls and some sashimi to go and they were okay.  Not spectacular or that memorable but decent.  I wouldn't drive out of my way to return but if I had a craving for sushi and was in the area, it would definitely be on my radar to return here.

Everyone was very nice and caring.  Have many good things to say about them; including Dr. Sam. However.  There is a however.  $25,000.00 for complete uppers.  The plate came back not they way it should have from a clinic back east that does the bar that holds the teeth.  Not my fault but I had to pay and additional $3,00.00 to have it done over.  After several months and coming back and forth from outside the state I finally get what I asked for and paid twice for.  Within two weeks or so the the plate breaks in several places, dropping out of my mouth.  The reason I was told.  The plastic that held the teeth was "contaminated". So I got the original "wrong" set.  I made it known I was not happy and was told they had a new clinic that could do the job. I returned north expecting the contaminated set to be fixed only to be told that I was out of luck.  So, I felt like I not only had to over pay, I was jacked around.  As in The Godfather, nothing personal, strictly business.  They could have at least tried to do what they said they could do.  Perhaps without the contamination it may have worked.  After all, I paid for it.

This looks like it's going to be somewhat of an unpopular opinion... but I was not as impressed with Mediterranean Exploration Company as I would have liked to have been. But also, this review is for the happy hour only, so take from that what you will.

Food + Drinks:
- Octopus ($13): This is the thing that I saw on Yelp that made me go "Aha! I want to go there," because I love octopus-- especially grilled octopus. The presentation was of course, lovely, but to be perfectly honest, I did not think it was flavored as well as it could have been. I thought it was cooked well, with the right amount of chewiness, but the flavor was somewhat lacking. I have had better.

- Bacon wrapped date ($1 ea): This was alright. They replaced the pit of the date with an almond, which made for a nice crunch at the center. I feel like you can never go wrong with a good bacon wrapped date, but it wasn't anything wow-worthy. Pretty standard.

- Greek potatoes ($5): These Greek potatoes were a surprise hit with out table. We initially skipped out on ordering them, but we wanted more food, and I, being a big fan of anything potato, wanted to try them. The outsides were perfectly crispy and the seasoning was yummy.

- Hummus "Pitriyot" ($11): I loved the addition of mushrooms to this hummus. That made the hummus more unique and scrumptious. What I liked less was the price tag and the fact that the hummus came with a lone piece of pita. In order to eat all of that hummus with the one pita bread, I feel like you'd have to heap a small mountain of hummus onto each bite of pita. We ended up asking for another pita which unfortunately, took a rather long time to come out, so i resorted to just eating spoonfuls of hummus by itself. Which was not bad. But also not my ideal way of eating hummus. And yes, I know the pita is freshly baked, which may account for the long wait time for pita.

- Radicchio ($8): I am kind of obsessed with the radicchio salad at Pollo Bravo/Toro Bravo, so I really wanted to try the radicchio salad here. It was literally the first thing I decided to order. Did not like this version of the radicchio salad as much as the Pollo Bravo version, but this also wasn't bad. As one would expect, the MEC version has a way more mediterranean flair to it, though I did feel like the yogurt dressing got a bit overwhelming for me after a while.

- Turkish Coffee Stout ($3): I am a fan of coffee stouts, and this one did not disappoint.

Service: Eh, it was alright. Our server didn't seem particularly knowledgeable about the menu. We would ask him questions and he would always have to go back and check, before returning to give us an answer.

My overall impression of MEC was that it was a fine restaurant. Tapas style, so obviously everything is meant to be shared. And with tapas restaurants, unless you order a ton of food, you probably won't end up super full by the time you finish. 

tl;dr: My main reason for the three stars is that while the food was fine, it wasn't really wow-worthy for me, yet it was accompanied by a high price tag. Granted, this is my opinion of happy hour only. Given all the high praise that MEC is getting on Yelp, I wouldn't mind coming back to try a full dinner here.

If I were more of an outdoorsey type of person I would go totally nuts in here but be that as it may, sometimes they have just what I need in this store.  We got hubs this really nice light weight jacket here that is still going strong without any issues and recently I bought two pairs of cargo shorts at a buy one get one 50% off sale.

The shorts fit great and didn't cost too terribly much and I'm pretty positive they are going to last a good while.  The staff here is very helpful and it is so much fun to go back into their clearance section.  You never know what goodie you may find like the wool blazer I once found for a ridiculously low price.

And when all else fails you can buy one of their really cute "sporks"....I'm kidding but they do sell them here along with all sorts of outdoors things.  I cannot vouch for any equipment they sell here but the clothing?  A-OK!

It is located in the center of the city, so convenient if you want to grab a drink later in the evening.
I had the chicken sandwich here, the bread tasted very soft and had a distinct good flavor to it unlike the regular buns which made the sandwich tasty. The chicken stuffing was tasty with lots of onions and capsicum with some spices to it and there was very less cheese, perfect for me. The french fries that came with it was not great. It was a different taste for sure.
My husband had the lemon chicken with rice (9) where he felt the rice wasnt cooked well and chicken was decent. Their sauce that came with it was good one. 
Decent priced and open late night which awesome

This place was just sort of a necessary evil for me at first, but while thinking about to write I realized that they're pretty decent. The prices are good, the produce is typically good (with exceptions), they sell packets of frozen thinly sliced meats--including leg of lamb(!), they've had most of the Sichuan stuff I tried to find after reading some of Fuschia Dunlop's books, and there's a late middle-aged checkout lady who calls me "honey." Stop and Shop only has one of those things... well they're prices are OK too...

I guess at the end of the day if I wanted to drive to Russo's in Watertown* and then down to Quincy to finally check out C-Mart I could do that, but instead I can come here sometimes and kill two birds with one stone in my own neighborhood.

*Note I regularly do go to Russo's when I don't also need to restock on misc. Chinese and other Asian grocery items.

My pulled pork sandwich was tender and tasty, full of flavor.  Fries were delish.

The server was attentive and cool, definitely into the menu.

It was good, nice atmosphere, and good company...but I'm not sure I'd *run* back there.   A definite local gem. Partly because it does feel like a neighborhood joint, I felt a little out of place.   And menu items were maybe $2 more than I'd guess they should be.

But I'd go back and give it another try.  :-)   I hear the outdoor space is lovely in warmer weather.

Have been here twice now. Once just for coffee and dessert, and the other for lunch.

It's priced higher than average. The coffee is decent, but my cappuccino had way too much foam, which kinda tells me the baristas still don't know what they're doing. Good attentive service though; the servers came by many time to refill water when I was sitting there. 

The dessert/pastry is again higher priced, but does seem more refined. The ones I've had  are all excellent.

Now comes the bad part: their meal offering is tiny. I understand they're trying to keep their price points low, but it just doesn't really make sense when the sandwiches are this small (think appetizer size). I rather pay a few more dollars for a full size sandwich.

And it's not like the ingredients are particularly expensive. I had the char sandwich. Beside the piece of char (which is not very big), there were kelp and mayo, both of which should've been very cheap ingredients.

In the end though, I still would've given the place 4 star for its decor, service, availability of the bar, and pastries. However, this is Cambridge. There's Tatte 5 minutes away. There's Flour right down the street, not to mention Clover, which is pretty much right next door. It loses a star because all these places still manage to offer better deal for the dollar, for only (very) slightly less quality.

It's the closest park to me, and that's really the only part I enjoy. The summer park has a few lawn chairs that get peed on all day, and just shade from trees. The flat bit of the summer park is filled with holes and a definite hazard for running dogs. The winter park has a covered bit, but even for a sand park, it's filthy. Not to mention a lot of regulars don't pick up after their dogs at all. 

I've had multiple awful expertises with people that go there. One man hit my dog with an open hand, and another one threatened to kill her and sick his mastiff on my partner. My dog is a bit jumpy, so I totally understand when people get annoyed by that, but physical violence and threatening behavior is over the line.

Bed was great and so was the shower.  Location was good.  Didn't eat at the restaurant or order room service because it was too highly priced for what you get in my opinion.  The size of the room was small.  No fridge unless you pay for the mini bar/fridge package.  Coffee pot and ice bucket were in the bathroom.  No tub.  Parking was $29 granted it was valet but I felt I had no other choice.  Free wifi.

However I may stay there again because it was convenient and the bed was nice.  However it would be nicer to be closer to downtown activities.

I just had dinner at F2O.   I've been eating there since they opened and tonight was probably the most disappointing.  They have reduced the portion size without changing the menu price. Probably the most disturbing thing was how dirty the restaurant was. As we sat in the booth along the wall, there was a clear layer of dust that covered the entire wall. It doesn't look like it has been cleaned in months. I hope this is just a fluke. Many more experiences like this will force me to choose another dinner option.

I have been dying to go to this place since I heard about it on Vancity Buzz. I'm glad that a Facebook friend notified everyone in a status that you have to make a reservation before going or you will likely be turned away. So I made a reservation for today, about three weeks ago or so.

My best friend who loves cats as much as me came with me. It was a bit of a bitch to find the place, as it was in the International Village mall, but luckily we have excellent time management skills and got down there early enough to find it without being late. We checked into the cafe side of it. There you will find an assortment of pastries and drinks available to order, along with some cat paraphernalia available for purchase (shirts, books, travel mugs, etc).

We then went into the cat part of the Catfe and signed the waiver, read the rules about interacting with the cats. There were seven cats but we saw about 4 as a couple were sleeping. I felt a little bad for the cats; I mean, I'm glad that this business has helped with the adoption of the cats (they had to shut the place for a bit due to lack of cats) but most of them looked frightened or distressed. It makes sense, being surrounded by people all day.

And that was part of the problem I felt: so few cats and way too many people. The literal opposite of the type of place I want to be in. Everybody is crowding around the three cats available so getting time to interact with them is difficult. Or so many people gather that it scares them and they skitter away. 

The space they have to roam around is wonderful! Cubbies on the walls, tunnels, plenty of toys. It's great. The price to get in is 8 bucks or 5 bucks if you purchase a treat from the cafe side. The food is a bit pricey but I didn't really care. There is also more souvenirs available for purchase on the cat side: earrings, coin purses, pins. I got a cute little coin purse in the shape of a cat face/head.

So, seeing as I can't compare this place to anything else, as I have not been to anything like it, I'm giving it three stars. I wasn't wowed by it, but I'm glad I visited. You have an hour there and my friend and I left after 25 minutes. Plenty of time in my opinion. Something that stuck with me after is how I would rather volunteer at the SPCA as I feel I would get better/more interaction with the animals there than I did here. I don't know if I will return. I feel like I understand what this place is. It's a cool concept, and it's still new and working out the kinks. So maybe in time it will be better.

The salon is very clean and organized. There are a lot of colors to choose from. The staff was friendly during my visit. The reason for the 3 starts my gel mani wasn't that good. My technician prepped my nails really well but did not do the best job painting them. I showed her a picture of what I would like (very light color with a small design) she said she would be able to do it- unfortunately she could not. I would have chose a different color if she had originally told me she could not do what I wanted. There are a few dark strings stuck in my nails and one nail has a ripple down the center. From far away my nails look nice but up close they are pretty messy. My friends nails were done way better than mine. It seems like the type of salon that is a hit or miss depending on who does your nails.

The Century Plaza has a beautiful lobby, and so I was surprised to arrive at my room and find that the room was outdated and in need of a renovation. It seems like someone put a "fresh coat of paint" on the rooms where they really need new carpeting, beds, and woodwork. The bed was very uncomfortable, and the fitted sheet slipped off the corner two nights in a row, which is a sign of low quality sheets. The room was spacious, and I appreciated the kitchenette and large fridge. 
Bright spots: lobby, friendly staff, location, and view of the city on higher floors.

Food here is okay. Your typical bar food I guess. Of the 4 times I've been here, I only had one burger that was good - "El Guaco." Every other one I had made me feel gross and was super heavy. The tots are decent and are even better when you get their srirancha (sriracha-ranch). I don't get why this stuff isn't sold in more stores, it's SO good!

The main thing that is forcing me to give this place 3 stars instead of 4 is the service. While the waiters themselves are nice, the food takes SOOO long to come out. One time, I waited 25 minutes just to get the menu, only to have to wait another hour for my food to come out. The waiter didn't even seem to care that I waited so long for my food and even charged me for the srirancha I asked for even after all my trouble.

Maybe I just came in on "one of those days" so maybe I'll come back again after a while...

Weird. Weird. I just didn't get the vibe of this place. On the plus side: the person who I think was the owner was very jovial and friendly - waving hi and bye to people, and chatting up some customers at the outside tables. Also, there was this really cool string art thingy that I liked up on one of the walls. Oh, and the seating was kind of modern and pretty. BUT: there was just this weird sort of humid, old-air smell that hit you when you walked in the door. I admittedly have a sensitive nose, but I couldn't get past it.  Also, wine was good, pours were skimpy. Conversation with the server was limited to: "Do you know what you want?" followed by plunking things down on the table later on. The food: fine, in the way that something you could make at home is fine. The beet and bleu cheese salad was good, uncomplicated. The sun-dried tomato risotto tasted a little bit like Rice-A-Roni seasoning. I hate paying for bread and butter, but did it. The plates: tiny. $60+ for three glasses of wine and a few small plates and I left hungry. So many better places to go...

Went here last night for my mom's birthday.  It was alright. The entrees were a bit expensive and portions weren't great considering. I personally got a pizza which was delicious. Our waitress was not quite as attentive as I would expect from a good waitress and it wasn't even that busy. She came over and my glass was almost empty and she never even asked if I wanted another drink.  

I'd probably give it another shot but not in a rush to go back.

La Provence in a word is "okay". 
      Saturday morning I was hungry for a decent breakfast not too far from the home base so I yelped for something nearby. I think the other reviews I read were fairly accurate about this place. Food was decent, better than Shari's but not above mediocre. I had "LA Provence" omelet with potatoes and rye toast. It was okay but over-taxed with salt by the massive quantity of feta that covered it. The rye toast was the best part of the meal. 
     As for the service goes, I was lucky enough to get there "early" enough to beat the morning weekend crowd. Even though there were plenty of open tables I still had to wait 5 minutes to be seated (just one). The server took my order and I got my food in a respectable time but the cute young blonde girl seemed to be "out to lunch" and not so attentive. Long story short, The service is really under par. I think they could use better management. As I left I saw a good deal of people outside waiting to be seated (while there were plenty of open tables) and all I could think when I saw their faces was, "it's going to be a long time before you guys get through with this." Maybe the LO crowd enjoys long waits, I dunno.

I went to Clery's on a Saturday night and was warned that there might be a line to get in.  There wasn't, thank God, cos the place doesn't merit a line.

There's nothing inherently wrong with the bar.  The clientele is a bit frat-ish, but not as bad as other places I've been in Boston.  The drinks are normally priced ($5 - 7 for a beer).  We had no problem getting a table big enough to seat the seven people in our party.  We even ended up with a really friendly waitress, which was a surprise (not that she was nice but rather that she was able to help us in a timely manner on a busy night).

The only drawback is that if you want to dance, you're probably S.O.S.  Apparently the dance floor is super tiny, as evidenced by the line that snakes upstairs for your turn.  I never even got in line but a couple friends and I shook our rumps for about five minutes near the line before deciding we weren't THAT drunk.

But no cover, a satisfying if not wonderful beer selection, and a lively crowd that's not TOO loud makes for a fine night, if not particularly exciting.

I have mixed feelings about the soon-to-be Doubletree.

They were very accommodating for the room block I arranged for my wedding - we got a good rate and were able to fill it to the brim with guests.  However, a few of the members of my bridal party had a really rough time making reservations (miscommunications between the group sales desk and the reservations desk).  That got to be quite frustrating.

It was under construction when I made the arrangements in March, and I was told they would be done in September in time for the wedding.  They were not, which was fine, but added a certain odd-ness to the hotel.  There is a lot of unused space, which presumably will be used for events and conferences, but its a good 3-5 minute walk from the parking area to check-in.

The bar there is open until midnight, even on Sundays, which was a huge bonus - most of us went there for an after-party.

The first impression was a typical Portland hipster type hangout.  That part lived up to the impression.  A bit quirky, but not bad.  The music was really erratic....went from obnoxious trance, to pop, to thrash metal, back to trance.  The food was ok....that's it, just ok.  The scramble I had was something I could do at home easily.  The worst part was the wait....took a while for a simple order. All on all it was ok....nothing to write home about.  If you need breakfast and are 10 feet away....it's a good deal.

I give this group 3 stars instead of 1 because the medical procedures went well but the billing did not.

I'm experienced with medical procedures and dealing with insurance companies and providers.

We think the procedures were appropriate, completed competently and without complications. In that regard we recommend Dr. Gotvald.

On the other hand, what we were originally quoted for the procedures was grossly under what we were billed. Then it took 6 months to get things straightened out and once it was done I was not confident that it was correct in what they charged our insurance company or what they charged us. Their accounting procedures are so illogical that I wonder if they're ethical. I was willing to accept the result, even if we were slightly overcharged, so that we could be done with them after so many months of negotiations. I'm not sure the office staff is doing the right thing.

We wished we would have taken our second choice since they provided a written quote for the procedures and were rated/recommended equally. Gotvald initially was slightly cheaper until billing time. Without a quote there's no way to argue with them.

The wait here can be crazy long though with people pushing their way through, being impatient, and it was very hard to get the attention of anyone to get wait times or questions answered... 

I'm not sure the food is worth the crazy long wait, but I will say that once inside, the drink and soup combos they offer aren't too bad.  I've tried the fish based broth, spicy broth, and the laksa - all are pretty good - a nice light flavor, noodles and some meat - you can customize it all, which is kind of fun as well.

So the first time they came they sent a guy named Cory. According to them, he would get here and if i needed to purchase more time for him to finish he would say so. He came and he got started. I wasn't home, others were. In the time he was here, about 3-4 hours he cleaned the bathrooms and part of the kitchen. That's it. I called halfway through to ask what would happen since he was going really slow. They told me he had to leave but they would send out two cleaners to finish tomorrow. I came home and he had left dishes, clean, all over the kitchen table. He had put food and wine glasses on the floor. Dirty glasses and good food just on the floor. And they bathrooms were clean but for as much time as he spent you would think you could eat off them. The next team was much better. But i was told i can't rebook because he is the only person that works in my area so now i have to find a new service. So i would recommend, but not Cory.

Stopped in on a Wednesday night and found out that it was Restaurant week - place was packed! We found two spots at the bar and took them quickly. 
As always, I like the style of the place - yellow lit bar an overall modern and cool vibe. Ppl are all nicely dressed and the bar always seems to have a few bleached blonde ladies with their well-groomed man friends.
It's really crazy how we've had an almost identical experience every time we've come. Here's the summary: bar tender comes over, very friendly and cool. Gives advice and seems knowledgeable. We order our food, excited. There are always mistakes with the food. They apologize and fix it quickly. And a manager always comes to apologize, offering a discount for the mistake. We enjoy the food, then the bar tender forgets about us. Except this time he didn't forget about us.
Anyway, my fiancée got a petite syrah, which was nice - strong and full bodied,  but still fairly smooth. I got the Red Wedding, as it was featured in a magazine we were looking at (weird) and sounds SO good. I was disappointed. It had a pleasant mild flavor - but with all those great ingredients, I was expecting lots of flavor. This was bland and uninteresting. My fiancée thought it was fine - she doesn't like sweet drinks like I do.
We ordered the restaurant week deal (which was excellent, price-wise) and an additional meal.
Again, the place was packed, which explains why the food took forever, but it really took forever - like probably 15-20 minutes to get the appetizer. It was supposed to be a beet salad, but ended up being chowder. Which they took back after the bar tender seemed pretty dumbfounded. And didn't seem to care or apologize to us. The beet salad then took another 15 minutes. The salad itself was good - decent size and well flavored.
We then ordered the Norwegian salmon and stuffed chicken breast.
My fiancé liked the salmon - came in a butternut squash and apple puree. I thought the salmon wasn't strongly flavored (seasoning or fishy-wise), but the puree was really good and together they were great. She liked the salmon on it's own.
The stuffed chicken was pretty incredible. Stuffed with prosciutto and gouda, cooked really crispy. Really flavorful and pretty great. Mashed potatoes were also really flavorful and seasoned - really good. Also, the Brussels sprouts were well seasoned and nice and crispy. Entire meal was great. 
We ordered the blackcherry cheesecake for dessert. Turns out they were out of it, which they didn't realize until it was time to bring it out. They gave us some sort of chocolate ball stuffed with chocolate moose. It was quite good. 
Food was excellent, service was terrible. We waited so long for the food that my fiancée really wanted to leave. 
Manager came over, apologized, and gave us a discount. Very apologetic and nice. Too bad that things went wrong in order for that to happen. Again.

The Yard Milkshake Bar

Price: $16.24 For what you get, I'm not surprised by this price.

Pint sized coffeehouse cookies and cream ice cream, topped with whipped cream, chocolate drizzle and Oreo crumble with mini M&Ms. Glazed donut, vanilla almond milk

Taste: Never thought to combine coffee ice cream and Oreos, but I'm not mad at it. Definitely recommend this flavor. The donut wasn't the best because it was stale. Strong coffee taste that I liked a lot. 

Consistency: A bigger straw is needed to obtain the cookie chunks, there was less milk than ice cream so it dried out some and became hard to drink. 

Appearance: I would classify this as an extreme milkshake. I feel like the person who creates these milkshakes, has an eye for creativity. Everything was placed perfectly.

Quality of service: Both ladies were very nice. They answered my questions and were very patient while I made my selections. The domain location is in a nice area to sit outside while the inside portion is not a option at the time due to Covid. I will be returning to try more combinations.

Overall Rating: 3.5 Shakes

For more milkshake reviews and ratings follow me on Instagram @milkshakelogs

If you think Joe's is big, sheesh!

New store, and the first of this nationwide chain in Oregon, recently opened at Washington Square.  They have a massive selection of almost everything sports related in a huge space (formerly Mervyn's).

We found just what we were looking for (after the usual aggravation of trying to buy something at Foot Locker) and although they don't have a lot of clearance items or markdowns here, they have some coupons floating around.  

Kind of a cool mini-track near the athletic shoes for you to test them out.  They probably have the largest selection of Nike apparel outside of a Nike store.  

Couldn't get over how large the golf and camping sections were upstairs.  Staff was helpful and check-out was quick.  While I'd prefer to give my business to Joe's or another local store, it is another good option.

Quality of food here is just as good as it is at other locations. We had the Chicken Piccata and the Steak Diane - which were cooked exactly as we ordered and delicious. The cheesecakes we had for dessert were also pretty good - as expected.

Service on the other hand is much better at other locations like  Natick and Prudential in Boston. The hostess was quite depressed or something and didn't seem happy at all when we wanted to sit at a table other than the one she chose for us...Moreover, the food was a few minutes later than usual, which was weird because it was 4:30pm and the place was less than half full on a Friday.

Sofra's food is amazing (love the mezzes, the schwarma, the hummus with lamb) BUT I recently moved back to Boston and was extremely disappointed to learn that they no longer serve their warm, fluffy pita. It has been replaced by a cold, generic bread that is nowhere near as good as the pita (and honestly sort of ruins the mezzes, my favorite thing there!).

Sofra also has a major seating problem. It's a small restaurant, which is fine, but they should ask customers not to save seats before they have ordered (this is a pet peeve of mine, and one that Sofra patrons regularly violate -- often saving seats for 30+ minutes before ordering while waiting for people!!). All Sofra would need to do is put up a few signs asking people to order before they sit, which plenty of cafes do successfully. Also, the vast majority of the patrons seem to sit at their tables for hours after finishing their meals. Not sure there is much that Sofra can do about this, but it makes it challenging for people to find seating to eat (literally only need to sit for 15 minutes to eat my meal, but even that is a challenge, and nearly impossible if there are more than 2 in your party). 

I used to overlook the cramped / impossible seating and the challenging parking enough to go to Sofra with regularity, but without the pita, I am less likely to make the trip (and my husband has emphatically declared that he will not be returning until the pita is brought back!).

We used to brag about this place to everyone, especially because of their pork & mac. Lately it has been spotty on quality but decided to give it another try. Come to find out it isn't even offered anymore as a meal, have to piece it together on your own.

Service has never been great but have been able to look past that but since servers are different every time, I guess it's a management thing.

Owners: you had a great thing going but have succeeded in messing it up. Going to move on to your competitors unless you revert back to high quality!

For over a decade, Midori has been a staple on our list of usual neighborhood favorites, especially when we are in the mood for sushi.  It's a small place, and adorable atmosphere to be sure.  And, yes, the sushi is delicious.  Everyone loves the sushi.  Midori is an authentic Asian go-to.  But what about the other menu items?  All delicious, too, especially during lunch when everything is hot and fresh.  For dinner, however, skip the beef bulgogi, especially if you are a bulgogi purist.  

In 2010, another Yelper named Julie posted this pic of beef bulgogi: 
 https://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/midori-sushi-austin?select=FANdLnlLHVYa9bl0T7pgKA  

This is the beef bulgogi that I've enjoyed at Midori all these years.  What happened?  Maybe it was a fluke that tonight's version of beef bulgogi did not have the appearance or taste of grilled meat, and it was on a bed of somewhat steamed (or boiled?) vegetables with a LOT of broth.  Come to think of it, if you threw everything into a pot with some udon noodles, you would have one heck of a pho!  

Also, don't expect a lot of the traditional sides that usually come with bulgogi.  You'll get three little bowls of whatever along with a bowl of rice.  No sprouts, no kim chee, no watercress, etc.

Review for Tourists!
As a tourist to Texas myself,  I may have had a little too high expectations of this place since Texas is known for it's BBQ. With that being said, I ordered the pick 3 meats for 16.99, a glass of cold sweet tea, some of their "famous" home made bread, and the peach cobbler. The beef ribs,  pulled pork, and marbled pork were  juicy but bland and tasted like generic BBQ. As for the bread , it wasn't bad but wasn't really anything special... I have better at chains like Logan's or Outback. Actually we asked for their normal bread and liked it more, I think it's the honey butter that makes it.  However despite all the normal food...the view was absolutely beautiful! I think the view is the one saving grace that keeps this place in business.

For us cash-strapped college folks; eating out can really add up - especially when you don't have a kitchen. That's why I recommend the lunch specials here for $6.65. I had #22 (Homestyle eggplant with basil) and it's a vegetarian's dream (although I'm not one) with its ability to fill and fulfill. The eggplants were deceptively spicy and flavourful, with an almost meaty quality. However, it was a bit on the tangy side and I found it difficult to finish my rice with eggplant alone. Adding basil to this equation was an act of genius since it soaked up the tasty sauce while maintaining its own distinctive herby flavour. Lunch comes with rice and seaweed soup with eggdrop. Portions are large so be prepared for leftovers for another meal at home. Check it out if you're in the area for this cafe which specializes in "Taiwanese-style" eats.

I've been coming here for two or three years...it's in our 'hood.  I love the atmosphere.  We usually sit at the bar, which is why I'm writing.  Depends on the day of the week and time of day as to the service you can expect.  Recently, I joined my husband who was already here.  The bar was not slammed busy.  It took about five minutes for one of the THREE bartenders to see me.  I ordered a red wine and someone else brought me a white wine.  He asked me if it was separate checks?!?!

After about ten minutes, someone else finally asked us if we were ready to order food.  This was while two of the bartenders were chatting up two women across from us for a very long time, their backs to the other three sets of guests seated at the bar.  The food was brought out quickly by someone, who forgot silver service.  We got that ourselves.  I never was asked if I wanted a second glass of wine. By then, I decided to go home and open a bottle and serve myself because it was just easier.

Sometimes, the service is better.  Sometimes, it's worse.  meh.  It's a gorgeous spot and we love the food and atmosphere. The kitchen staff works hard.  We do wish whomever management was would have the bar staff step it up.  They clearly need supervision on a regular basis, and they need training on consistent delivery of outstanding service to everyone, regardless of status.  If this were to happen, I'd bump up my review...and visits.

Went here for Saturday lunch/brunch. The place was pretty busy, but based on the reviews here, it's often busy, so they should be used to it by now. But they weren't. Our waiter was stressed, rushed, and sweaty. He refused my husband's request to have his eggs scrambled instead of fried, saying that they were too busy for special requests. My chili burrito (veggie chili and avocado in a whole wheat wrap) was delicious but over-priced. I think people would be happier with this place if they included a side with the sandwiches.

You know the feeling when you leave the house and somethings not quite right? Then you spend all the time wondering what was actually wrong, oven on, water running, doors left wide open? Then it urns out to be nothing. 
Well it's been a month since we ate here, and the whole time I've had that feeling of something off. To be honest everything was fine. The service outstanding. Our guest thought her pepperoni pizza the best she's had, our salads and pizza and pasta all good as well. The interior trendy clean and structured. it all just left me feeling.... ambivalent at best. 
For us, it wasn't worth the trip.

The manicures&pedicures are good. People are nice. Do NOT not rely on them sticking to schedule. Does not matter if you make appointment or not-because they take walk ins they are often running late. Today we waited 45 min until started despite having appointments. I would come back only if I don't have to stick to a schedule. Mediocre attention re Covid practices-Even if not having to pay attention to schedule, I will likely not be back until we are in a safer times!

Got the chocolate chip pancakes and the serving was huge. Definitely enough food for two people. For the price, I felt like I was getting a steal. They weren't the best pancakes I've ever had, but they were satisfying. 
Also had the steak sandwich which was okay. It was served like a philly cheesesteak, but maybe a little on the dry side.
I do want to go back and try their egg sandwich. With their prices, it's a great place to go.

I haven't been here other than on the weekends. It seems like a good ol' boys bar. I think everyone here went to a Georgia college and have known each other since high school or earlier. Annoying for me since I'm from Cleveland, and I'm not really into the good ol' boys mentality anywhere.

I've heard the downstairs is pretty sweet but I think you might have to be a member or something to go down there. Also, I know bars with carpet is an English thing, but its gross. I don't like carpets in bars.

If you want to do shots with your frat brothers, while you wear something pastel-ee with khakis then this is your spot. Unfortunately, many of my friends fit this mold and that how I end up there so I take it in stride.

Very friendly staff. However I was disappointed with the food quality. I guess dineout week menu= lesser quality?

We love the clam spaghetti(w/surcharge), hanger steak,seasonal zuppa and panna cotta. They were flavorful and rich at the same time didn't taste too heavy nor salty. But in contrast, the kale Gemelli was so bland..I could have made a better pesto sauce pasta with Barilla pesto sauce. The chocolate cake with balsamic vinaigrette was a Nono. The Tuscan kale soup was not actually soup. It looked like some mashed beans and quinoa served on a plate. Tasted just ok. 

I felt that the taste and quality of food here weren't consistent. Some were good, some were straight out bland or strange. Staffs were extremely friendly.

We stopped in for Restaurant Week, and were pleasantly surprised to see that pretty much their entire menu was available for the $28 prix fixe. You could get any appetizer except the table-side guacamole, and any entree, though the crab cake appetizer was $3 extra and the steak entrees were $5 extra. You don't have a choice in dessert though, everyone gets the Tres Leches. 

We both ordered margaritas - mine had pomegranate juice in it, and my wife's had mango. Neither were particularly good, they were WAY too salty, and that was even before any of the salt on the rim fell in. Once I let the ice in mine melt to dilute it, it tasted a bit better. But overall, a $22 mistake. 

The appetizers were good. My wife got Queso Fundido and I got Empanadas de Hongos. The queso was way too much for one person, but with the empanadas you only get three small ones, so that's a bit more difficult to share. 

For entrees, she got the Enchiladas Mixtas and I got the Salmon Manchamanteles. From the description, she thought that she would be getting three enchiladas with one major listed ingredient (skirt steak, grilled chicken, chorizo) each, but what you get is two enchiladas with all three ingredients mixed together. The salmon wasn't wild-caught but it wasn't advertised as such on the menu either. It wasn't bad. I liked the mole manchamanteles that came with the salmon, and the plantains were good. 

After all that, we ended up getting the tres leches to go. Overall, I liked the meal and my wife just thought it was OK. Even with restaurant week, it seemed too expensive for what you got. We didn't regret coming but we probably won't be back.

What can I say about SilverCity Riverport?  It's kind of your average Cineplex - there's not much to differentiate one from the other these days.  This one has I think 19 theatres (!), but this means there are usually multiple showings per day of large commercial blockbusters - still no room for indie movies, although there is the occasionally Bollywood or classic film shown.  Hit up 5th Avenue Cinemas on Burrard if you want to see award-nominated films or things reviewed in the New Yorker. 

Some cool features of this Cineplex are: "serve yourself" beverage machines that allow you to customize your drink - for instance - you want a low/no calorie beverage? Click the button.  Want Coke Zero, Diet Coke, or Diet Sprite? Click the button.  Want Vanilla, Cherry, Strawberry, Lime or Orange Diet Coke? Click the button.  You see where I'm going with this.  World of Coke in Atlanta (Coke's world headquarters) has a tasting room with these exact same machines that is basically their main attraction, so having the machines handy at SilverCity Riverport is kinda nice.  They also have a full "Poptastic" popcorn centre, which is like Kernels, with lots of pre-popped flavoured popcorn on offer (this month's flavour? Maple Bacon.  UGH.)

I will say that I have had some good service interactions there.  On the last cheap Tuesday I went to, I bought my ticket at the automated kiosk ($7.50), while my friend went through the traditional line ($6.75).  I asked why there was a difference in price and a manager immediately came out to inquire as to how he could help, took note to call the programmers for his automated machines to change the price, and refunded me the difference.  You don't necessarily expect places like Cineplex to have great customer service but I was really pleased, anyway.

6.5/10.

I have been there probably 25 times, including this past weekend (April 2013). The food there is good and slightly better than what you'd probably expect from a pizza / entree joint on the affordable side.

Pasta dishes are one of their strong points, which appear to be made to order. The best ones I have tried are Chicken, Ziti, and Brocolli (Alfredo sauce); Chicken Marsala; and Chicken Piccata.

The pizza there is actually pretty good too. I have tried regular cheese; sicilian style; chicken alfredo pizza; and eggplant pizza. They also make paninis on homemade bread - I've tried almost all of those and they are great as well.

The downside - the service isn't that great. I've had orders missing items, super long wait times on the phone, and somewhat careless and off putting interactions with employees there. They seem to not want to be there, and it shows.

If you are in the area, I would definitely try this place out. I like it better than the close-by Giovanni's. But if you are looking for a truly great experience, you might not find it here.

I purchased my vehicle in 2018, it was a used vehicle and I was doing a trade in. I was ''offered'' 4K less than what my car was worth first off. Then I provided my Kelly Blue Book code which shows the true value of my vehicle... they took the code and revised my trade in amount, eventually resulting in a deal. But must do your own research or they will bite on the unknowledgeable person!

Second, my car purchase came with lifetime oil changes...A++. I recently went in for an oil change AND a wheel alignment. I brought my vehicle in at 4pm and it was miraculously complete at 4:59 which already was suspicious as they shut service down at 5pm.

Not to my surprise I was charged for a wheel alignment and the only service that was done was an oil change! They even printed out a before and after report of my wheel alignment. Pah!

I was baffled that a technician and management would really do this to a customer. Someone could of easily said ''we couldn't get to that today, would you mind coming back?'' Or something along those lines. That's good business and transparent to a buyer. That's what builds trust and a returning customer. I knew my car I knew an alignment was not done. So I called them to let them know this isn't right. They never apologized to me and I went back the next day. They quickly put me in the waiting area and ''re-did'' my wheel alignment.

Just know your car, your values and do your own research. 

The people in the customer service area however generally were polite to leave this on a positive note.

I used this dry cleaning service for two years because of convenience.  While I'll say it is certainly not high end dry cleaning, it gets the job done.

The shop is a little dingy and cluttered so don't expect to walk into a royal palace here.  

But the people are nice and greet you with a smile every time. There are also mints at the front... which I took advantage of on many occasions. 

Their turn around time is on average two days but if you want it faster you can (may be extra... not sure). 

The downside here is they have limited hours on Saturday and are closed Sunday... so plan accordingly.  

Finally, I must say I did have one incident where they stapled the dry clean tag right into my clothing... it didn't ruin the material but showed some carelessness.

Overall price is good, service is nice and turn around is quick... if you live in the Middle East part of Southie, give them a shot.

A nice place to go if you want to spend about 20 minutes in greenhouses.
They have a very small but, for the region good, selection of orchids and camellias.  And they have a wonderful old resident cat.

I went here for the annual herb sale, which offered many varieties of herbs and perennials all in great condition.  But, I was greatly disappointed, mainly because I had misunderstood that OLD varieties (i.e. from their historic greenhouses) had been propagated to raise funds for the estate and to share these plants with the public.  Many plants were supplied from commercial nurseries...  And these were not priced more favorably than Russo's.  That said the orchids for sale inside one of the greenhouses, on a regular basis, are fabulous and an excellent value!

This place may be 7 years older, but Winterthur or Fosters it is not.

This hotel is definitely not up to the regular Westin standards as some other yelpers have mentioned. 

We came in late for a weekend trip from Florida to Atlanta. The bad experience began from here -- the desk employee (Danny who apparently loves to travel) greeted us and asked us to hold on and he left for about five minutes with no reasoning or apologies. We were able to get checked in soon after he returned. 

When we opened our door, we saw that the room we booked (king bed) was two queens. Quickly, we called the front desk and the same employee gave a lame answer saying they had no other room available. We paid for a certain room, I would like a better answer than we ran out of those and sorry we can't do anything about it. 

Besides those issues, there were additional cleanliness issues within the room like leftover water on the bathroom floor and hair from a previous guest inside the bathroom. 

Definitely makes all other Westin hotels look bad.

Service was great! Didn't really care to have to sit outside when it was cold and windy, though. Requested inside, but they could not get us a table inside.  No sooner we sat down and ordered a cup of coffee to warm us up that we watched others being seated inside. The food was average. Loved the warm rolls and vegetables. The pot roast was good, but the steak and fish were below expectations. We would go back, again, as long as we could sit inside!

Review of the AYCE Sushi option.

We were dropping off my sister at the Orlando airport and it started to downpour. I mean you can't see one foot in front of you rain. Instead of driving through the rain to get back to Tampa, we decided to find someplace to eat dinner and wait out the rain. This means that I didn't have a chance to do the meticulous research I normally do before going somewhere. Instead I pulled up sushi restaurants in our general vicinity with a good rating and off we went. 

There are four options of ordering here. You can get AYCE Korean BBQ, AYCE Sushi/Sashimi, AYCE Korean BBQ/Sushi/Sashimi, or order off the menu. We went with the AYCE Sushi/Sashimi which was about $17 a person. 

I noticed that many of the rolls are either deep fried or include cream cheese. The AYCE option doesn't really include your healthier or more creative options. I actually ended up liking the spicy crab the best (it may be that it was good and I felt somewhat healthy eating it). We also tried the Golden California Roll, the Yummy Yummy Roll, the Las Vegas Roll, and the Volcano Roll. They were all perfectly fine, but nothing great. We also got Salmon and Escolar Sashimi. I found the Escolar to be a little fishy. The Salmon was ok. 

If you're looking to eat a ton for relatively cheap, then this is the place for you. Since I rather have quality over quantity I'm not a huge fan of this place. That being said, I will have to come back sometime to try the AYCE Korean BBQ.

Pretty good for a first try! 

I have been rather hesitant about trying this place, mostly because the Americanized version of Chinese food usually leaves me feeling like I've been greased to death. This place did not have that effect!

The food was fresh, fast, and very good! I've never had such tender shrimp, the hot and sour soup was well balanced and the menu offerings seemed to be more than your usual Chinese restaurant. Quite happy with the service, the prices, and the location.

The only things that I was not pleased with being the loud music with advertisements and the entryway waiting area layout. 

Overall it was a very pleasing dining experience. I would definitely go back. I would want to try all new things except for the house oil hot chili wontons. I need to eat those again someday soon.

This place is beautiful with an incredible sunset and golf view. The service is hit or miss but the servers are really nice. We ordered a couple of drinks and calamari. We had great service initially but then were ignored for about 45 minutes. We planned to get another round of drinks but ended up closing out once we decided to go inside and get a tab. The calamari was definitely pre-packaged as each piece was exactly the same and heavily breaded. I'd recommend for the view and a simple glass of wine but not the calamari. We ended up with stomach issues after the calamari - we eat pretty clean so it was probably loaded with preservatives.

Straight to my punch line: I would go for Tavola over this place any day.

Came minutes prior to opening hour on rainy Tuesday evening, we were promptly seated. I like the ambiance of the place - quaint, secluded, large windows with tree leaves covering outside view.

Pasta dishes were good, not special - we got "bored" halfway through the meal.

Ordered:
Fried cauliflower, chickpea, herbs & aoli - average 3/5
Pappardelle & duck ragu - average 3/5
Rigatoni alla bolognese - better 4/5

Service could be better, specifically they could be more friendly/chatty - the male server (curly black hair) came and take empty plate, light candle without saying anything, no eye contact or smile either. Female server service was ok. That said overall, didn't feel personal at all. We're not talking about busy restaurant here.

Again, my comparison is Tavola and simply put, Ask for Luigi fell short. Regret choosing this place for special event.

I don't normally eat dimsum. It's too far, and it's expensive. I like it though, and my favorite place to go was Royal China.

It's been a while since I went to Royal China for dimsum. It seems the quality has gone down. The shumai, fish balls, congee, and the other standard dimsum dishes were decent; but some of the other stuff was horrible.

One of our favorites, the sweet tofu tasted so bad we couldn't finish it. It used to be a a dish we scarfed down with no problem. We also had a hard time finishing the mango jelly. 

They also had some coconut sticky rice cakes which I didn't like. I'm not a big coconut fan. Overall, we left disappointed. With our unsatisfied meal, we paid nearly $50 for the two of us. Their service is stellar though. 

I would give it 1 or 2 stars, but because of all the good experiences I had with this place, I'll give it the benefit of the doubt and give it 3 stars for now. I just hope their food gets better next time I go.

Solid place to grab a beer but generally not impressed with the food. 

They have a wealth of beer options and the bartenders downstairs are knowledgeable. I asked for a recommendation and was very happy with it. 

When it comes to the food, I could take it or leave it. I could find something I like on the menu, but I wouldn't choose to come here. The grilled chicken sandwich was good and fit for a quick lunch, but honestly I'd recommend this as a place to grab drinks with friends after dinner elsewhere.

I moved from Blacklick Ohio to westerville and let's just say a move that could have taken 2 hours took 3! The movers were nice however the decisions they made were not the best! There was a scrap of the wall because they didn't want to take the legs off the couch. Scuff marks on the floor from sliding my dresser instead of picking it up or using a dolly, they broke a piece of my mirror. Ohio manager Christian was rude and showed no sympathy. I'll never use them again!!!

Tried it again and was hoping for a better experience.  The food wasn't bad, but it was overshadowed by the very slow service at lunchtime.  Parts of our order were sitting on the counter waiting at least 10 minutes for the server to come by, which was a little unnerving because it was right next to the order entry terminal and the staff generously leaned and worked over the waiting food.  yummy.  I ordered a Bento box and the sushi rice was better than last time and would have enjoyed the dumplings that came with it if they weren't buried in wasabi.  Actually it was gross and they were lazy just dumping it all in the same bento compartment.    Might try it again in a few years, but still there are so many better choices out there.

Not sure what the hype is all about. While there's nothing particularly wrong with this place, it's not the Mex saviour that it's been made out to be. 
I guess I am spoiled by the very high level of service which is common in Vancouver, but the service was average. The food is good but not mind blowingly so. We let the server pick their favourites for us to try so it should have been the good stuff. 
Maybe it was a case of elevated expectations . . . I will probably give it a second try as I lurrve Mexican food.

Great place to grab a bite while strolling Disney's Boardwalk.  You can grab a slice of either cheese or pepperoni, or you can grab a whole 15" pie.  If you get the whole pie, it's cut into 8 slices; but, if you grab a slice, the 15" is cut into 6 slices, so you get a pretty decent slice.  

The prices are pretty good for Disney.  You'll pay around $4 for a slice, and if memory serves me correctly, it's about $15 for a whole pie.  

Don't expect the best pizza you've ever had, but it is pretty good.  It's also very convenient if you are staying at the Boardwalk or one of the other nearby resorts, because you can grab however many you need for your family and take it back to your room.  It's also easy on the wallet if you're not wanting to spend a fortune on a sit-down meal at one of the restaurants.

Service is very friendly here.  Very clean.  They also even have paper plates for you.

We went here a few days ago after hearing a lot about it. We both ordered fried chicken and it was great. The hot sauce they serve is awesome! We also ordered drinks. The drinks and service were great as well. I gave the place 3 stars because the restaurant has a Old mildewy mop water smell. I thought it was the restroom but even after we moved to the bar to sit the smell was still there and VERY evident. Also the place was kind of raggedy inside. Some of the tables and chairs were wobbly and the entire place could really use a facelift. On the other hand though, besides the drinks and food being good, the music they were playing was also good. I would definitely go back though, it wouldn't be my absolute first choice but yea, they could very possibly get a second visit. Hopefully a few things will be better next time!

Ruth's Chris has always been my go-to steak place. When it's done correctly you won't find a more flavorful steak. A good steak doesn't need steak sauce but bearnaise sauce is the perfect compliment to the perfect steak at Ruth's. You can get a baked potato or mashed potatoes anywhere so do yourself a favor and get the au gratin potatoes. They're meant to be shared but if you're dining with me you'll need to get your own (yes, I eat them all). Ruth's creme brulee is consistently the best I've had anywhere. And I've had it at a lot of places supposedly known for their creme brulee. None have matched Ruth's. Nice and creamy with the perfect caramelized sugar crust on top.  

I only get to go to Ruth's once or twice a year so the anticipation of the deliciousness I know I will experience is high. On a recent visit before a show at Atlanta Symphony Hall we didn't have reservations so we sat in the bar. It was only 6:00pm but the service was slow. Took forever for someone to acknowledge us and take our order. The servers were friendly but we had two different ones who seemed a bit distracted and not really communicating with each other (both delivered the same check to us). The steak came undercooked (medium rare when I asked for medium), the plate was not sizzling hot, and it was drowning in butter. It took a bit to get their attention so I could send the steak back to be cooked more. When it came back the plate was sizzling (yay!) but the steak was once again drowning in butter (I literally soaked up the excess butter with bread). The perfect steak comes on Ruth's signature 500-degree plate with just enough butter you should hold your napkin up until the sizzle dies down a bit to prevent any splatter. If the temperature of the steak is undercooked just slightly you can cut it and place it briefly against the sizzling hot plate to finish it. On this particular visit the steak was too undercooked and the first plate not hot enough to be able to finish cooking.

Sometime in the last year Ruth's has begun charging $5 for a very small ramekin of bearnaise sauce. I understand an upcharge if you ask for your steak to have a peppercorn or blue cheese crust but it doesn't seem right to have Ruth's nickel and dime you for a sauce that used to be complimentary. Especially when they only give you a tablespoon or two--if that. For a couple bucks more you could have an entire vegetable side or dessert.

While ambiance is not why I go to Ruth's the ones connected to an Embassy Suites hotel are a bit lackluster and don't seem to be on par with what you expect from Ruth's. There were a lot of teens and pre-teens in the bar who were clearly just staying at the hotel which made the atmosphere very casual with a different kind of energy than you come to expect when dining at Ruth's. You wouldn't find that at a stand-alone location. I've had numerous four and five-star visits to Ruth's--I'm beginning to wonder if that's still possible?

It had been a few years since I'd last visited a Flatbread location, and I'd so enjoyed my last meal that I eagerly anticipated a visit to their Davis Square location. Oddly enough, the restaurant is co-located with a bowling alley, which detracts considerably from the experience simply due to the often-overwhelming noise level. This becomes a particularly acute problem during interactions with the staff.

Dropping in on a Sunday afternoon, I was pleasantly surprised that we were seated without delay. I though for sure that given the bowling alley, there would be a wait. Shortly after sitting, our waiter stopped by, and after providing the day's specials, he understandingly departed just as quickly since we hadn't yet had a chance to review the menu. Despite two excellent-sounding specials, I instead chose Flatbread's take on my favorite type of pizza: a sausage, sun-dried tomato, caramelized onion, and mushroom offering. I paired this with an Opa Opa Winter Warmer, though I received Opa Opa's Winter Strong Ale instead because the Warmer was no longer available; I'd have preferred that the waiter ask me for an alternate choice rather than making the decision for me, regardless of whether or not I would have ultimately ordered the Strong Ale.

Our pizzas arrived quickly, and noticing that it was sliced into rectangles, I grabbed my first sliver without hesitation. I was not disappointed by my choice in any way. The bold flavors of the maple fennel sausage and sun-dried tomatoes worked well together, while the mushrooms and caramelized onions added a noticeable and pleasing depth to the mix. The dough is thicker than I prefer, though far from a deep-dish style, and neither significantly enhances nor unduly detracts from the pizza. In almost no time at all, I finished three quarters of a large pizza, contradicting Flatbread's proposition that this size could comfortably feed two people.

I truly enjoyed my pizza, but the noise level, combined with the waiter choosing an alternative beer for me, marred my experience. As for the physical location itself, it is sparsely decorated save an expansive montage of images of Davis Square. The kitchen is open, allowing diners to watch as the staff deftly spins pizza dough in the air and carefully navigates the two large, wood-fired ovens. Despite their worn appearance, the chairs are also quite comfortable. The ambiance overall is very relaxed, making for a nice way to spend a Sunday afternoon or to unwind after a round of bowling.

On Boxing Day, we headed out to Steveston to avoid the crowds (before attempting to dive into them again later in the day).  Sure enough, the village was eerily quiet.  I felt like I was playing The Walking Dead, but that may have been because I was playing it everyday for the past few days.  (It's a really good game; download it now.) Of course, everything was closed, including Tapenade Bistro.  We walked around and ended up at Cimona Cafe for some brunch.

The special of the day sounded interesting -- steak omelette ($9.49).  At that price, I couldn't say no, but I was also a bit hesitant because of the price.  I wondered about the quiche-like dishes neighbouring tables were dining upon, only to realize that they were also actually omelettes.  I'm not picky on tradition and I do like quiches, so I didn't mind.  This was somewhat disappointing.  The steak was probably the worst part of the omelette, since the meat was quite tough and lacked flavour.  I also disliked the tomatoes, but that's just because of my distaste for them.

I also contemplated getting the country omelette ($8.49), filled with bacon, mushroom, and cheese -- which Doro ended up getting.  This was much better.  The bacon had flavour! And bacon and mushroom is always good.  The hashbrowns that came with all the dishes were just alright -- kind of dry, but lightly seasoned.  They reminded me of the ones from SFU Dining, which I'm also unenthusiastic about, unless they're slathered with gravy and egg.

Kem had the old favourite ($9.99), with choice of meat, eggs, hashbrowns, and pancakes.  The pancakes were somewhat fluffy, but they weren't that exciting.  It kind of felt like a fancier version of the breakfast at Bob's Subs, but I actually prefer Bob's way more.  Shredded hashbrowns are so much better.  And it's greasier and cheaper there.  Doro also ordered a french toast ($1) which was also just decent.  It seemed like it wanted to be a HK style french toast, but it also wanted to be a bit more traditional as well. Meh.

Cimona was okay.  I didn't really enjoy anything particularly, but it wasn't that bad at all (except for maybe the steak in my omelette).  Prices are fairly low, but if I wanted a cheap breakfast, I would just head to Bob's instead.

I've been on a rampage recently using the Hooked deals app and saw this thing come up. It's in a bustling food court area with some options (notably Gourdoughs right next door for dessert!). Prices are ok, perhaps a bit high for the college student but for a working guy, its about what I expect to pay at this point for a meal. Hooked deals make it a lot more manageable. 

I got a #1 - spicy, but I honestly didn't feel that much heat. The veggies are crisp and fresh and the bread grilled well. The meat was alright, not all that much of it, but enough to get explosive bites of flavor. One thing I notice is the beef/lamb mixture isn't as salty as other places I've been. The fries are pretty puffy, could be a bit crisper and a bit more quantity but they were alright.

Really nice staff. Could be faster on the food though.

So all in all, good place, not outstanding. Better places in town for similar food items, but for the price, location and hooked deal compatibility, they're a-ok.

Sky Sixty. A rooftop lounge? I was totally sold by that concept.

Unfortunately Sky Sixty was really not quite what I have imagined. I was really expecting a more swanky place. This club is rather small and very dead on a Thursday night. I was not a big fan of the music either. Not fault of them really. I just haven't done my homework. Techno isn't my thing. 

The half off drinks deal is great though and the people are friendly. I just can't dance to techno and house.

I have heard amazing things about Phnom Penh for years. However I've avoided coming here because one thing everyone tells me is that the wait to get a table are LONG. I finally went yesterday, and true to what everyone tells me ... the line was long. Even for 3pm on a Monday!! 

When we were finally seated, it was another wait before we were served. Ordering the chicken wings were an must. We were NOT disappointed with the wings, they were amazing! The outer coating was crisp and crunchy, piping hot, and full of flavour. It came with a delicious sweet and sour dip that complimented the wings perfectly. We also ordered the Butter Beef, another winner! Unfortunately I cannot say the same about the other dishes we ordered. I was very disappointed that the noodle soup I ordered lacked flavour and oomph and had a layer of fat floating on top. 

The restaurant is fairly neat and tidy. They are not wheel chair friendly. To use the bathroom facility, you have to go up a flight of stairs for women, and for men you have to go down a flight of stairs. 

Will I go again? For the wings? it's a definite YES

Third update: My nails have pretty much all popped off by now. It's not even the 2 week mark and I made an appointment for a fill when I was there last getting my nail fixed but now there's nothing to fill because they've all popped off at this point. I've been wearing acrylics for years and never had this issue. 80$ down the drain


Second update: Called and they were super nice and fixed the nail no charge. Definitely going to keep coming 

First update: Got my nails done for my birthday and literally 2 hours later one popped off ); gonna call and hope they fix it.

I live a few blocks away from this place on 23rd and have been to it several times. The food is decent but there are so many more worthwhile places in the neighborhood I never seem to want to seek out this place. There is also a large crowd of smokers that's a regular fixture to the outside of this bar. If you go here - get the steak bites on hh and if you don't mind the smoke on the way in then you'll have an okay meal. It won't be bad, but it more than likely won't be exceptional, or even remarkable for the price.

Stopped by Sushi Bang since I was in the area and was craving sushi. I decided to get the alaska roll since it said in the menu that it would be topped with a sauce and salmon maki. The alaska roll was just a california roll with salmon on top drizzled with teriyaki sauce, nothing special like the other places I've been to where alaska rolls were drizzled and topped with crazy different sauces. The crab filling in the roll was okay but lacked flavour. The salmon maki however was really delicious since it had the perfect rice to fish ratio and the piece of salmon was bigger than average. Restaurant was kept pretty clean and the washroom as well. It was quite crowded inside but the wait staff were still not as attentive as they should have been. Didn't get a refill of my tea until the very end of my meal when I asked the waitress for my bill and machine. Not sure if I would want to go back, I'm not against it but there are much better sushi places in the area that are better and better priced as well.

Popeye's Chicken...

Because every once in awhile, you just have to have a bucket of chicken. 

Whether its to feed an small army of Fried-Chicken Enthusiasts, or its to satisfy some insatiable, slightly alcohol-fueled need to eat 8-12 pieces of chicken all by yourself (perhaps while watching a late night "Robot Chicken" marathon). 

Or maybe its just that you have an insatiable need to put the empty bucket on your head, don a hockey mask and prance around playing air-guitar like Bucket head.

*One useful tidbit in my review today- they do have some slightly healthier choices available. These aren't noted on the outside drive-though window, but there is a small sign inside the restaurant that advertises slightly healthier, non batter, non breaded chicken wraps.

But why would you go to Popeye's and not get the tasty fried chicken?

Now if you'll excuse me, I've got to go put the bucket on my head and practice. We're getting the band together later.

Ate here in February 2016 and again in December 2016.  

They want to get you in and out as fast as possible.  I don't blame the waitstaff.  It's the highest ups who push this agenda so as to maximize volume. Other negatives: the room was freezing and the semipublic women's restrooms needed a clean. 

Having said all that, my food was pretty good.  I had the stuffed chicken entree and my wife had the salmon, which she reported as decent. The crab cake appetizer and beef carpaccio were very good too. 

The kids menu chicken breast was terrible: very unevenly cooked and essentially inedible.  To their credit they readily credited the item. 

Overall, good food but quite overpriced for the experience.

When I used to work in SE Portland, I would walk by Lardo's on a daily basis. It was always packed with customers spilling out and sitting in the permanent tent that they have setup next door to the restaurant. I then read the yelp reviews online and I got really excited to try Lardo's. I read so much great reviews about the dirty fries that I was convinced that I would love it. I tried the dirty fries and absolutely hated it. First the fries were really dry, then I hated the peperoncini's and the salty big chunks of pork mixed in.  I think that it is a terrible combination and I do not understand why other people like this dish.

I then tried the cold chicken sandwich with bacon which again sounded really good. I thought that it tasted really bland and was overall "meh". It would have been nice if the chicken was warmed, and if there was a zesty sauce added on top of the chicken. The best part was the bread roll that it came on. 

I am pretty sure that I just didn't order the right items. I am glad that I finally stopped in to see what Lardo's was all about.

I ordered through Bite Squad and got it delivered to the office. On that note, food hold up  ok (was just warm when delivered but the onion rings still had some crispyness to them) but the bread was inside the box so it wasn't a toast anymore but some wet piece of carbs. 

Onion rings were great! 

Mac and cheese left a lot to desire.... no flavor at all for an extra 3.95 .... never again.

Parmesan grits were good but they were my first grits ever so I am not sure how the taste is supposed to be. 

Pork was not pulled just chunks of it which I was super disappointed but the description never said pulled so I guess it was just an expectation. On the up side... it was cooked right, super tender.   

I had the pork dinner with the 2 sides and the extra mac and cheese. With tip and tax was 20 bucks ... Makes me feel I wasted half of it but I wouldn't mind more of those onion rings.

I wasn't expecting fine dining at this airport location, but the food came out somewhat cold. My daughter had boneless wings and fries and I had the French dip. The fries were lukewarm and the wings were down right cold. My daughter didn't seem to mind, as she is not picky. No time to send things back when you have to make your flight, so we ate it and ran to make our connection. In the plus side, we had a nice view of the runway which my daughter enjoyed !

I have a new groomer! yaaay!

I've been loyal to my neighborhood boutique dog store and groomers because it's an easy walk down the street, they offer great prices, and are friendly.  But I decided to "cheat" on them just to try something different for my dog's birthday, and I have to say... I think I'm about to enter a new relationship, lol :)

LOCATION: Off Cheshire Bridge road, right next to an Auto Body Shop (at the intersection of Woodland Avenue). It's suuuper easy to miss since it sits back from the road and isn't very noticeable. (It's close to Gail Fabrics)

PRICING: They have some general prices on the website, but you will have to call to get a quote as it will be based on the size, coat, etc. They are a bit more pricey than most groomers, but not by too much. For example, I usually pay between $42-$50 to get my toy dog groomed, but they charged me $60. 

DECOR/ATMOSPHERE: I must say, it's not as "pretty" as the boutique retail dog stores you may find nestled in Midtown or places near, but it is clean and neat. Its similar to most dog daycares/groomers with concrete floors instead of wood. I love that they have a lobby area where you can sit down-- a lot of places weirdly enough don't have that, lol. I also love that they have grooming station up front where they have your dog when you come in, they do a few last touches and voila your dog is ready to go!

CUSTOMER SERVICE: Pleasant. No issues thus far, let's hope it stays that way! Barry was also very friendly and nice-- which is important.

GROOMING: Fantastic!  I got the full groom and it took about 6 hours.  The cut was more precise, blended, and complimentary to my dog's body than ever before. My dog was also very happy and relaxed when I got there which made me feel like they took good care of him and were gentle with him. I've gone to some places and my dog seemed super anxious, like he couldn't wait to leave the place, lol! But this time he was happy, tongue out, tail wagging-- all the stuff a parent wants to see! Also the groomer owns dogs, including two poodles, which means he knows first hand how to take care of them and deal with their hair type. My only gripe is that I don't think they cleaned my dog's ears good enough, it was still a little hairy and waxy-- which is a no no for hairy breeds. 

SUMMARY: All in all this place gets an A in my book. It's a little pricier than other groomers, and takes a couple hours longer, but the groomer does a solid job. My little pooch will start to go here on a regular. I may go to my neighborhood spot sometimes since it's so close and they often can take my dog same day, but still at the very least my dog will certainly get all his cuts here.

***UPDATE***: While I love the clips given by Canine House of Style, the last time my dog received a cut he came back with TWO gnashes/knicks-- one large area on his foot, red and bleeding, and another on his private area, red, scabby, and long. It took 2 days for the bright redness to mellow down to a deep pink... this really is unacceptable. They should have ATLEAST acknowledged the clearly new wounds from the shave or cut they gave, but instead they just handed him to me like everything was okay. Very Disappointing. Also, his nails were uneven-- clip them, then file please... don't give a rush job. Lastly, while the girl upfront who wears glasses is always very nice, calm, and mellow the other one is sort of loud and aggressive-- basically she comes across too strong at times and talks really fast. I'd much prefer her to be a little more calm in her tone.  With all that said I have to change my 5 star review to 3 stars, well more like 2.5 but I'll round up to 3 for now. Hopefully they do better next time or else I'll have to change it to 1... I really hope they stop rushing and accidentally cutting my dog to the point that he draws blood.

I'd rate this new location at 3.5 stars.  Their menu is grammatically correct and properly laid out, which is already a good sign for Kissimmee.  We tried a few items, as their menu is extensive.  The traditional cheese pie was actually very good.  I'm not sure it would survive the cut in NY, but this is actually NY style pizza, as Avanti claims.  No sauces for the crusts, nothing stuffed into anything and one choice of crust thickness, just like pizza should be.

We also tried the Buffalo wings, which were quite good.  Other ancillary items - mozzarella sticks, onion rings, and fries were obviously frozen food service items and fine but nothing special.  Garlic knots were good, as is the case when pizza crust is authentic.  They could have used a garlic butter sauce rather than being served dry, but they did travel better.

This was a delivery order; oddly enough we live less than a half mile away but the order took an hour to reach us and as a result, the pizza could have been hotter.  They also need to learn how to prepare a Styrofoam box so that items inside aren't wilted by trapped steam.
