Avanti has been open at this location only a couple months, so there's time to smooth out the details.

All in all, we were pleased and welcome Avanti to the area as a new pizza location.  Prices are fair and I don't believe there's a delivery charge (though there is a $15 order minimum).  They also offer calzones, strombolis, hot and cold subs, gyros, empanadas, salads, all kinds of appetizers and desserts.  There's always a warning flag when one restaurant tries to trade in all manners of cuisine, but if you stick to the Italian specialties and pizza, Avanti is worth checking out.

3/17/16 - UPDATE (Critical)
I have to unfortunately remove two stars from this review.  After several tries, they just can't seem to work out delivery times.  That's probably because the entire operation takes up a corner of the counter in a Mobile gas station.  We found this out when we ordered 4 cannolis (we had a credit from a nearly 90 minute order delay previously.  The desserts, which are filled with sweetened ricotta cheese, were bad.  As in, rancid.

We called to make sure they stopped using it and planned to return the next day after it became clear that the service girl 1, refused to let us speak to a manager; 2, refused to give us or did not know the street address; and 3, instead of crediting the dessert back to us actually charged us again.

The next day we called the manager (or gas station owner) and he clearly did not understand the overcharge and neither of them had understood their food was bad so never pulled it from the shelf.  We went down in person and worked everything out.  To his credit, the gentleman was very courteous and tried to make everything right.  Unfortunately, this is a pizza made in a gas station, has had problematic health inspections twice since August, 2015, and customer service is lacking.  

The pizza is still good, but we cannot recommend this establishment for health safety concerns.

Went there for dinner tonight. My friend said that he got the "best Parmesan chicken" he's ever had there so on we went. The cashier suggested the Lemon Chicken so I went with that. It came beautifully presented, the skin had a nice crisp to it and the meat was tender and moist. But that's where it all ended. Yes it was decent food, yes the portion was sufficient (at $18 for 1/2 roasted chicken with lemon it had better be!) but I wasn't wowed. I tried my friend's Parmesan, it was good but again, didn't wow me. I don't expect every single restaurant meal to be a knockout, there are many decent places out there that I'll go to over and over. I guess my disappointment came from my friend overselling the place. It was decent food, I'll give it another try, just a different dish next time.

Had been to Kintaro Ramen many times over the years. However, it's been discouraging to see that it is declining in quality. It's still good, but not as good as before (would rate 4.5 stars before). My favourite is always Miso Ramen but had also had occasional Shio and Shoyu ramen. I would recommend ordering rich (better) or medium soup and fat BBQ pork if your arteries can handle them. 

Line always long, but servers are good and friendly. Give you a menu to read while you're waiting in line so they can get order started while you are almost top of the line. This contribute to the efficiency of this small place. (this is not a place for a nice sit down meal if you haven't figured out already..)

What contributed to the declining quality was the BBQ pork-- arguably the main ingredient of the ramen bowl! It was not fresh and was cold the past 2 times I had been there. The corn was also cold last time I was there. Cold items in a supposedly hot ramen bowl are complete turn-offs for me.

I was sure this place was gonna be divey... and whaddaya know... it is!
BUT... it's divey in all the right ways.

The food was delicious! I ordered the tom yum soup, the pork dumplings (which were more like crispy pork shumai) and drunken noodles. All were very good, solid options. 

Best around? No. But so incredibly convenient, and the guy at the front counter is both funny and helpful. It is a good, solid, regular, inexpsensive go-to shop for your Thai cravings.

PARKING: Big gravel lot.

ATMOSPHERE: Yikes. This isn't some pretty "industrial" rebuild in the pearl district, it's the real deal. Cold, spartan, almost spooky, like you could imagine a slasher flick being filmed here. It's cavernous, not intimate. Cold this time of year. Wear a warm jacket, maybe a hat. Big TV (projection, I think) with sports, but no sound. Music was unmemorable. What I do remember is the awful speakers, probably not helped by the acoustics of the place. Tables were basically slabs of wood on wheeled steel frames, presumably because this is a working brewery that's only open to the public on weekends. One of the crazy things about this place is the two-stool bar! 

SERVICE: Kinda lousy, but no big deal. Don't be timid and dainty, and you should be fine. This ain't Applebees, you won't have a perky polo-shirt-clad server.

BEER: Quite the barrel program here. I didn't realize. I had three, found them to be solid, with just one offputting flaw (or possibly deliberate; one never knows).  

FOOD: I hear there's a cart outside, but I didn't see it. 

PRESENTATION: Glassware is style-appropriate.

PRICE/VALUE: Printed taplist and chalkboard taplist is unpriced, but I know what beer goes for in this town, so I knew what to expect (except for that San Diego outfit...you know what I mean). But then I noticed off to the side of the taplist it says all beers are $5. Pour size varies from 4oz to a pint (16 I guess, they didn't look imperial). I think I saw a mention of $4 on Mondays, and there's a HH discount but I didn't see that mentioned anywhere (Shhh, don't tell them I told you).

RESTROOMS: Through an office and down a winding hallway, apparently shared with other tenants of the building, I would guess. Two, single occupancy. Funny, I was distracted by a bulletin board, and they both became occupied at the same, so I laughed at myself for being an idiot, and moved on. 

OVERALL:
I think this a love-it-or-hate-it place. I'm more on the hate side, but I do like the interesting approach to beer (weird one-off stuff). Maybe I'll try again when it's warm and the door is open.

I always come here with Jon whenever we're craving ice cream. It's usually really empty in here so we get our ice cream pretty fast. They have a lot of options for froyo and ice creams.

We usually get the vanilla golden froyo with the rainbow sorbet and gummy bears on top. I love the creaminess of the froyo, tartness of the sorbet, and the hardened gummy bears. Usually around $6 for a medium, and it satisfies our cravings. It's a really chill place to get our go-to ice cream!

The place was clean and the ambient was great.  But the long line wait to order and then you have to go pick up your own food was a big turn off for me.  

The chicken salad sandwich itself was nicely done, but the price they charge.  I would expected a bit more service then I was getting.  The presentation of the food was ok too.  But no one come and refill drink or if we are doing ok was kinda disappointing,  specially they have time to gather in a small group and talk among themselves. And ignore the customers completely.  I don't know maybe the concept need to go back and rethink about their customer service, a specially for price they are charging.

Local Hot Pot (All You Can Eat)

5/5 Service
3/5 Food

Extensive food selection. On the order sheet, instead of checking off your selections, you indicate how many pieces of food you want (number of slices of meat, for example).  They give you complimentary satay and soy sauces, but charge you for additional sauces and condiments (garlic, cilantro, sesame sauce, etc.).  The cost is minimal, but nitpicky. They offer several types of broths, however, you are charged for them. 

Food was average, but we really liked our server.  Very helpful, explaining how to order, clearing empty dishes, and making our dining experience enjoyable.

You take this establishment for what it is. It is not glamorous or pretentious. It's a neighborhood hangout that attracts some very unusual species. The bartenders are friendly. The clientele is not as much. It definitely has a cliquish atmosphere but not blatantly unfriendly. The patio can at times be a circus sideshow, that I personally find entertaining. It might turn some folks off. Not a big booze consumer but everything I have tried has been great. Stop by Sunday afternoons for a terrific free barbecue. If you come in with an open mind, you will be fine.

The fresh spring rolls here were excellent. Unfortunately, I ordered the shrimp ones for takeout that were supposed to come with avocado. There was no avocado in them. Boo. I loved the dipping sauces they came with, though!

I also had the mango cucumber salad, which was refreshing, but overpriced.

Finally, this irked me: I saw the bartender sipping on a Thai iced tea and got a craving, so I asked for one. The man behind the register (who I believe to be the manager) gave me a pseudo-confused look and asked, "Excuse me?" I repeated, "Could I get a Thai iced tea?" He sighed and said, "We don't have Thai iced tea here." I replied, "Oh, I thought I just saw him drinking one," and pointed at the bartender. The drink in question was beside him. The manager then changed his story and said, "Oh, well, we have the ingredients so the staff sometimes makes them for themselves. But we don't have that on the menu." "Oh...so I can't order one?" "No. But we are considering adding them to the menu." Umm...what? If you have the ingredients (which are most likely just condensed milk and either a powder or a syrup, I doubt the staff is brewing the stuff from scratch) then you can't just mix one up for me? Especially after I observed one of the staff members drinking one? Not exactly wonderful customer service.

It was a little expensive for Vietnamese food. I would get the spring rolls again but probably not a full meal.

Service was friendly, and the decor is cute.

I ordered the Crossroads taco and the Baja Shrimp taco. I liked the Crossroads better than the Baja. The Baja Shrimp had so much potential for what it is described as on the menu, but the breading of the shrimp overpowers the rest of the flavors of the taco. I thought it was just too heavy. Overall, the tacos were just ok. 

My friend and I shared the queso and guacamole. The queso was warm with just the right consistency and spice. We both enjoyed the queso far more than the guacamole. The guacamole was forgettable, needed some more flavor in every sense - more cilantro, more jalapeno, more lime juice, etc.

One of my Uber drivers during my Austin trip referred to Torchy's as the "white boy taco", with some American and modern twists on the classic taco, which is definitely true. I feel that this place is over-hyped for what it is. I've definitely had way better tacos.

I can't say that these cupcakes are reasonably priced, or that I have loved every single cupcake I have gotten from this place. That said, I have had some awesome cupcakes from Kickass. Really what I love is the fact that the frosting is homemade and super tasty. You don't get that slimy feeling in your mouth like you just ate a cupcake from the super market. Bottom line, these are too expensive, and I'll only get them on special occasions... but the quality has very good overall in my experience.

This review is based on food alone. I am excited to experiance the country bar atmosphere at some point. I enjoyed the fish and chips. Have gotten it twice.  The pork tacos were good, but the pork was shredded in such a way, you could tell it's not slow roasted/fresh. My main issue was the sliders. 2 sliders and coleslaw cost $7.75.  Not old did the the price put a bad taste in my mouth, but the meat was hard to swallow as well.  Will not order sliders again

Getting my nails done is a treat yo self type of thing that I'm willing to spend big bucks on. I love getting a fullest and will spend good money to get them done nicely. I read the great reviews for the salon and was super excited to go! And my visit did go very well! I got a mani-pedi and the pedicure was one of the best pedicures I have ever gotten in my life. They really massaged my feet and just overall I had a fantastic experience. I got a fullest with a power dip top coat. The technician I had, Amy, took her time and was in no hurry. My nails look fantastic and I was extremely happy. 
Until two days later and when putting away the dishes in my house, of my nails came off. My pedicure had chipped too and I was also slightly upset but it was the nail that really made triggered. I called the salon and made an appointment for the next day. I came in 15 minutes early to my appointment and told them that I had an appointment but they wouldn't take me. I waited 45 minutes, had three people come in and get helped before I finally spoke up quite annoyed and said I had an appointment for 30 minutes ago and that all I need was one replacement nail. When they finally helped me I was literally done in 7 minutes so I didn't understand why I had to wait 45 minutes for that little job. They did the replacement nail for free which was nice but also kinda a given because it fell off with no provocation two days after and I also waited a ton even though I had an appointment.
A week later two of my nails came off and by then I was just fed up. They treat you really nice and take their time but their services are just not durable. I spent a total of $96 and had three nails come off within a week an a half. I treat my nails well because I spend so much money on them and for the full set to just come apart a week later really annoyed me. I really liked the salon and the technicians but their services are just not worth the money. I was really bummed because I felt like a queen but I don't have the money to spend $96 on something that'll only last a week.

We were starving when we pulled in here, it was lunch time and people were really piling in. I thought for sure we'd have to wait forever, but it turns out, the place is ginormous and we got seated right away. The waitress was really on top of it. We started out with wings, which sort of threw me off, since they were going to rock it all fancy and just add lines of ranch of and buffalo sauce over the top. Like some fancy ice cream sundae. Applause for originality here, but boos for, where the hell is the sauce? I uploaded a picture of them and no I was not drunk when I snapped it, just appears that way.

They had an okay flavor, and then I added a Mozzarella salad for $2.95 and was surprised by the the size, the flavor was good. I was feeling pretty hopeful about my selection of shrimp tacos. My son had the cream of broccoli soup, which was pretty good, he gave me the last 1/2 cup of it or so. The small version was pretty large and he said it was getting really rich. 

Then they lost their other two yelp stars after that, the shrimp tacos were a major let down. Zip on the flavor and lots of stale chips on the side. Oh, they were pretty reds and blues, but tasted like they'd sat out all week. the shrimp tacos and chips came with two tiny cups of a sauce and salsa, not enough to dip chips, if you even were considering it and barely enough to add to the shrimp to bring em back to life. I asked for extra sauce, and the waitress didn't remember to bring it, and I was pretty much over it by that point. 

They are friendly enough, but if I had to do it again, I might have stuck with the lunch special for $5.95, in the picture it looks really small, but we saw them going by and it would have been plenty. My son had a lunch pizza and said it was really good and said the crust was really light.

Food spot on.  Side dish portions demonstrably different from in house dining or pre-pandemic.  Price is consistent but quantity way off in this new environment.  One side barely feeds one so order accordingly.  Asked for cheddar with the baked potato and received sour cream instead.  Had to ask for bread and butter which were always automatics.  Little sad as good will for past experience is what drove us to order pick up in these difficult times.  Pseudo costly experiment and results inconsistent.

Its hit or miss here. Sometimes Sue is in a great helpful mood and a joy to talk to about your project or yarn. Other times she is scowling in the corner and you really just want to avoid her and her shop. 
One of the employees (Collette maybe?) there talks non stop about her "knit" dragons. Its rather frustrating when you just want to be left alone to pet the yarn and dream about your next project and you are cornered and followed around the store while she puffs up her chest and tells you ALL about the stupid dragons. Its a turn off for sure.

I was a little nervous going to a corporate place but this ended so well for me and my hair! I went in with no appointment, totally prepared to be turned away, and Kristyn B. got me in. I did have to wait a few minutes longer than she said but it was so she could clean her station, her cut time was exactly what she quoted. 

When I tried to go back I asked for Kristyn and was informed that she was no longer there. I asked for someone who was good with curly hair and was informed by the manager that all the girls would be good. Um no. As manager of a salon you should know that people are particular about their hair. I reluctantly agreed and when I got there I found out they had raised the price by $10. I left immediately as I wasn't about to chance a horrible cut from someone who was good enough in the manager's eyes. When you ask for a Cadillac and the salesperson says "any car will be a Cadillac" do you buy a Ford Focus and call it good? No you don't.

This was our 4th year coming to Winebelly for Valentine's Day. It was good, but not as good as it usually is. The service and wine selection was great, of course. 

Although very rich, we loved the Brussel sprouts with the pork belly. Super flavorful. Cheese plate was good too. And my boyfriend liked the anchovies. 

Unfortunately, the foie gras special with the figs was a complete miss and not worth the $18 spent. It was way too sweet. The tomato bread, which i usually love, came out burnt on the top (should've sent it back). 

Menu doesn't change much. I'll probably be back for a few of the staple appetizers and cocktails, but I'd stay away from the specials... Seems very hit or miss with those.

I go to the place a lot and think they have a great selection for a reasonable price, but I'm torn because they sell a lot of expired food and they manually enter the prices for things and have made some mistakes before (purposefully or not I don't know) so I always have to be alert when I check out.  I've gotten sick from their natto which conveniently had the expiration date concealed somewhere.  Just because it's frozen doesn't mean it lasts forever!  I've also bought kimchee from here that had that carbonated taste.  It's hard to tell with kimchee b/c it's already got such a strong smell, but this was definitely past it's prime.  Also the imitation crab had some mold-like growths on the inside... 

But then again, they have all the sauces you'll ever need for Asian cooking, they have little household goods that you can't find at the American market and their frozen meats are good.  Bulgogi!  Yayuh!  

I recommend this place, but just be careful about the items that have a shelf life!

I found this place through yelp, and I was glad that I did. I came in looking for a skirt,and saw that they were having a sale. The workers here are pretty friendly, and try their best to help you out. They will also keep telling you about their specials. If you are looking for something in particular, make sure you show them a picture. When I asked the lady a question, she just said "don't worry no problem" without understanding what I was asking. It was fine to me,  but just want to let future customers know if you don't speak her language. 
Their skirts were on sale for $10-$20, and their scarves on sale for $4.99. Sale section had dresses up to 60% off, and they have tons of dresses to choose from, most if not all,  from India. This place also has alteration services available. The lady who did the alterations wasn't very friendly but she did a good job (very fast too).

Overall good service and good prices!

Decent food for a buffet. A certain kind of unspoken challenge arises at buffets to eat as much as you can. It's easy to do it here. Normal buffet food, though it seems as though they have more side dishes than entrees. The taco meat was horrible and greasy, but the pizza was great. A wide variety of desserts can satisfy any ones craving for sweets. Would like to see more vegetable options that aren't fried. Actually, I would like to see less fried food. Might go back if I get coupons in the mail again.

I went to Texas Roadhouse for a late lunch with my family last weekend. We were a party of 7. Since one member of our group was late to meet us we decided to wait on her before being seated. After we had been there a little while one of the hostesses pointed out that there was a table that could seat 7 open at the bar, and we should go ahead and grab that, since it could be awhile for another large table to open up. 

The table at the bar was an odd L-shaped booth, but we managed to fit. Our server, Tiffany, was really good. She was on top of things and was able to answer all of our questions.

For an appetizer I ordered the fried pickles. A couple people commented that they were too salty, but I thought they were pretty good. They were thin sliced dill pickles with a thin, crispy breading. And of course while we were waiting on the meals we all stuffed ourselves with the rolls and cinnamon butter. Those things are addictive, and our server kept bringing more.

Our meals were really good. The kids ribs portion was great, my daughter really liked that. The chicken critters are a huge pile of chicken tenders, and could easily be split between two people. Actually, most of the entrees were large enough to split. I had the chicken critter salad and had the tenders tossed in buffalo sauce, that was really good.

The only negative in our whole meal was that one of us had ordered chili, and it came out cold. And out of the whole meal that was the one time Tiffany wasn't around to check on us. After a few minutes of staring at the cold chili, one of us actually got up and walked it over to the kitchen. A fresh bowl of chili was brought out shortly, but really, that shouldn't have happened.

And I'll second the other reviewers, I don't like peanut shells on the floor. Why do restaurants keep doing that? There is a warning outside about peanut allergies, and that just makes the whole peanut shells everywhere thing seem even more pointless. Why do something that is messy and harmful to some people?

My boyfriend and I came for brunch on our one-year anniversary. We had a reservation so we were seated quickly. The decorations were a little lacking - not very elegant. Thin, green carpets and beige everywhere. 

Service was also, sadly, not up to par, especially for a really nice restaurant. We had to request water each time our glasses were empty. When our server brought our dessert, he just plunked it in front of us and walked away, greeting the table behind us cheerily. We may be just college students, but my boyfriend is notorious for 25%+ tips. Not this time. 

Food was A-OK. The appetizers of fruit kebabs were all right, but my boyfriend loved the dipping sauce. 
  My boyfriend ordered the fried chicken florentine and claimed the chicken was the best he ever had - he could cut it with the back of his knife. The wilted spinach was allright, but lacked flavor: some garlic would have been great. 
  I ordered the flight of french toast. The syrup was sooo good, but sadly, my french toast was in a pool of it, making it way too sweet. The french toast also had a thin layer of creamy white stuff - mascarpone perhaps? Overall pretty tasty, but hard to justify the $14.95 it cost. 
  The heavenly cheesecake was, in short, heavenly. It was light and fluffy, not at all like the heavy dense cheesecakes many places serve. The strawberries with the cracked pepper balsamic was delicious. 

Overall, the experience was all right. The view was great, the food was ok (not quite worth the price), and the service was lacking. We may come back during dinner just to catch the sunset, but afterwards, we probably won't come again. There are many restaurants that have phenomenal food that match the prices.

I've been to this location several times and recently 2 days ago. You go for the food, not really for the ambiance and service.  Hands down best eggs Benny and hollandaise sauce. Love it with the truffle hash browns or English muffin.  Have also had the French toast at another time and it was a delicious panko coating, but overall with the toppings too sweet for me. The not-so-great is the space is so small, very tight seating and ambiance. Waitstaff is average to inattentive. 2 days ago there was a line up just inside the door and after 5 minutes of staring there wondering who was going to come over to greet people waiting, I waved to a waitress to ask about seating. She gave me a glare and put her hand up to me and said, the hostess is just setting the tables. No apology and no smile. Not impressed. Go for the food, not the service and expect to wait.

Add Russian to the growing list of diverse Portland food cart cuisine that I've had. I'm not sure if this is the first Russian cart Portland's had, but still a rare find. The owners of this cart are from Moscow and want to give the people here a taste of what Russia has to offer. The menu here contains items like pelmeni, borscht, and piroshky.

Piroshky are usually baked buns that can be stuffed with a wide variety of fillings. Savory fillings can have meat or no meat, while sweet fillings are usually fruit-based.

I first tried the piroshky with lamb, potato, and onion ($2.49). A good, light blend of seasonings on the filling.  The potatoes were soft and the lamb retained some juiciness. The bun itself looked like a flat strudel-like item.

The "Very Berry" Piroshky ($2.49) at this cart is not a filled bun, but a flattened biscuit with berry jelly and a maraschino cherry on top. I do wish the jelly got injected into the bun here instead of having it spread on top. That way, I'm more likely to get the jelly in my mouth instead of having it end up in the container. It ended up being a bit messy.

All in all, two comforting food items. Nothing extremely memorable on this visit, though.

I'm not an expert on Russian food, so I can't speak to its authenticity. But hey, with very reasonable prices, this cart is worth a stop.

We love Keke's and have always had really great food and service. This location was new for us and thought the service level would be the same as all the other locations we have been to. We were wrong. Our server was nice enough but when I explained that I have had bariatric surgery and wondered if I could order a kids meal, she said no. I asked for a supervisor to explain the situation to. When a manager came over, he explained he could not let me as it is against company policy. We live in Orlando & have been to at least 6 other locations & we have never experienced this. I ended up not ordering a meal & just sharing anyway. Food is always good, but just wish the management had been kinder & more understanding. We will not be back to this location.

I'm a local and discovered this place a few months ago. I have a slew of allergies and found this place has the best gluten free vanilla frosting and vanilla cupcakes I've tasted. UNFORTUNATELY the young girl working behind the counter that looked like the girl from the Harry Potter movies couldn't have been more unfriendly. This is my second experience dealing with her and she seems miserable. When I inquired about the vanilla cake she looked happy to tell me that "it's been sold". The cupcake tasted a bit stale but I ate it anyways. Being friendly to customers is something that is important to me so I might have to make a big deal out of this one because it's unacceptable. You work at a bakery...eat a cookie or a cupcake and smile please.

I have to say this place was very nice, but there were some things that need to be worked on for a five star review. 

It has a nice atmosphere and the employees are super nice and helpful and try to do everything possible to make it a lovely time. I had scheduled an Adara head to toe which is a mani pedi and facial. The pedicure was nice, but I am a short girl and so the seats were a bit uncomfortable (I am sure that is me and not the seats). The pedicurist did offer me extra pillows to put behind me and tried extra hard to come closer to me not to have me move closer to the edge of the seat so I thank her for that. The manicure was lovely, lasted pretty well, the manicurist was nice and was very pleasant to talk to. She had some tips about how to make my nails stronger which really worked! 

Now I must admit I am a facial snob, and I have sensitive skin. Like others have said there is very little discussion about your skin. The environment was relaxing, instead of walking out of the room while you sit under the steam the facialist gives you a foot massage. The oil issue I have is that there was a lot of oil used, and the next day my face was not happy at all. 

The other issue I had, which they apologized for but it still should be mentioned. I was drying from my lovely manicure before my facial when a woman walked in for a facial... now this place is very time only one facial room so while I only needed about five more minutes and I had to sit and wait about 20 minutes for the facial room to open up and be cleaned. If they new a person was going to be coming in for a facial maybe they should have changed the order of my services.....

I've driven by this place for some time & I've never stopped. Mostly because there are other Asian restaurant's closer to my house in North Andover and I cant step foot into a Chinese restaurant without having a few Mia Tia's and who needs a dui.  One thing I've always noticed is the parking lot is always full.  I was out Friday night with a few friends that live in Middleton and we made this our last stop.   I was very surprise by how small this place is inside.  What was even more surprising was how full it was.   It reminded me more of a roadhouse/bar that a Chinese restaurant,. the bartender and the server were both non Chinese.  If fact the only Chinese persons I saw working here where through the kitchen window.   What was very clear is this is a townies hangout.   This place full of locals and they all knew each other.  I'd comment on the food but we never ate.  I did see a few people served some food & it looked fine.  The only thing that dragged us out was last call.   I'll go back again this time for the food & I'll update my review then.

I was sad to find out that this place opens 90 minutes before they start serving food.  90 minutes of drinking on empty stomach is never a good thing for Barney B or those that happen to be in his vicinity.

Bartender, forewarned, managed to grab me some charcuterie prior to the official start of service and I will admit it was some of the best meat/cheese board I have had in a while.

The space is big and open, the open kitchen is inviting, though the array of produce and bread at the most visible corner of the kitchen seemed very staged and didn't give me the impression it would actually make it into the night's meals. (my inner cynic, perhaps)

But I do look forward to a return - good food, friendly service, and an interesting, smallish menu are all good reasons imho

Well, it's big, it has A LOT of cardio machines and yeah... that's pretty much it. If you're into Olympic weight lifting, this gym is not for you. I joined because I had just started getting fit, but now I'm more interested in strong lifts, such as deadlifts, squats, bench press etc.

They have smith machines in leu of power racks, so this place is good for beginners who want to perfect their form. There's also no place to deadlift in this gym. Or would I be considered a "lunk" for wanting to deadlift? It's a shame.

If the free weight area is separate from the rest of the gym as to not "gymtimidate" anybody, I don't understand why Olympic weightlifting is still frowned upon. I wish they would replace half of their smith machines with power racks/cages. That way even the "lunks" are happy.

3 stars: A-OK

It's a steakhouse. 

They cook quality meats to the doneness of your preference. They usually get it right. 

Pros:
Seafood tower 

Cons:
Smells like moneyed old people

Chops is a good steakhouse. They are competent at executing the menu. If you are craving restaurant steak and want that seafood tower to accompany your beef, then this is where you are going to go. 

I like that they have multiple floors and multiple rooms. The exclusive club in the back is OK too, but smells like cigars, and to me, that ruins the dining experience. 

The staff here seems to know how to suss out the rich and those with expense accounts. If you feel poorly treated, it may be because your appearance or your order was not to their satisfaction. Shallow, yes. Unjust, yes. But there's not that much you can do about it. 

The steaks are good, so wear a power suit, and try to fit in.

I really wanted to love their spicy wings.. I really did. 
but they are slathered in sugar! ugh. and, they weren't crispy enough for my taste. double ugh. I don't like eating chicken wing skin that is still gooey and soft and.. triple ugh!
I did ask them to make them as crispy as possible.. and, while I enjoyed the chicken part, I don't like eating any kind of meat with sugar. 
It would be amazing if they offered them without sugar.. yum yum!!

I too have had mixed experiences with this Trader Joe's . They compromise there own core values. It's truly a managements task to reflect them in the customer experience. The staff that works there is in large a great group. That is the reason for the 3 stars. If they felt as is they were treated fairly, this store would be a better experience. The product and prices are great. Even with that in mind I won't go in there until there is change in how the current management treats the staff.

3 stars on yelp means A-ok, but my experience at pok pok was just, ok.  i had this lemon grass stuffed chicken.  it sounded good.  when i got it, it was just a plate of chicken pieces with none of the other things mentioned on the menu.  when i asked the waiter he said it was the stuffing and marinade and it was removed before serving.  meh.  he was ok too but not great.  my friend had this vegetable curry soup which was good.

what i'm saying is my experience did not match all the raves i heard about pok pok.  i walk by all the time and the place smells great but i didn't have the amazing experience i expected i would.

i really prefer appethaizing across the street.

I stayed here for a wedding for three nights. Overall I had a good experience, but there were a few things about the place that were just frustrating.

First, the good: the rooms were a decent size. Comfy beds. Sunlit with large windows that open and blackout shades. Located next to the T green line at the last stop Riverside. Good shower. Nice bar/restaurant with decent hotel food and a great post-wedding atmosphere. Cool pool area for evening lounging.

Now the less good...

1) service: I didn't feel the staff was that knowledgable or helpful.  In particular, We asked about areas to run and getting around without a car (best transportation options, are the surrounding streets walkable, etc). They didn't tell me anything beyond what I learned from basic google searching, and I am from out of state and unfamiliar with the area. 

2) Room amenities: no mini fridge, just one room temperature bottle of Fiji water. No ice or vending machines on our floor. Okay, it seems petty, but I had no way to keep anything (like a bottled water) cold! 

Then I am a heavy sleeper, but the door rattled all day and night from some sort of draft in the hall. The dead bolt didn't help, so we put our bag in front of it. If I were a light sleeper this would have been maddening.

The elevators were painfully slow, and during cleaning hours it seems they shut one down for the maids, so the one functioning elevator was always packed on a busy weekend. We wound up taking the steps each time to our 6 floor room, which wasn't bad because the lobby level is 2 and I actually prefer stairs. But if I had mobility problems, (again) the constant wait would have been maddening.

No room service printed menu, only a fuzzy one on the TV channels that is hard to read.

3) location in relation to Boston: if you stay here, rent a car. Being a NYer without a car, I saw it was next to public transit and thought it wouldn't be necessary. We were pretty stranded there and ordered delivery when we missed lunch. It also takes 45 mins to 55 mins to get into the city once on the train. It took us 45 mins each way to get to and from Fenway one weekend afternoon. Compared to NY or even DC, the T is just really, really slow. Plus a bunch of the ticket machines at the riverside station are in the sun and you can't really see the screen, so on BC'a alumni weekend, we waited in line to buy our T tickets because three of the machines aren't usable. If your main draw to the area is to see Boston, don't pick this place. But I could see it being a good location if you have a car or if you are going to be in the Boston College area. It was a $50 cab from Amtrak South Station. We had the wedding rate all weekend, so it was worth staying further out. But I notice the regular rates are very pricey, and I wouldn't have paid that much to be so far from the city otherwise.

We asked the hotel where we could walk to get food, and we were told to take the train several stops to Newton Center. Please see above commentary on the T.

Bottom line: yeah, it is a nice hotel. Some small issues could be bigger for other people. And it's location could be good or bad depending in your situation. Biggest negative was I wasn't overly impressed by the front desk.

I went to lunch with my rather persnickety know it all manfriends to take a trip on the sushi train. These guys couldn't get it together to meet at noon for the freshest round...so I reluctantly agreed to meet them there at 1. At 1:30 I walk in by myself...get a spot on the train route. Order water and sapporo.
I start with some stuffed mushrooms. Crabbish, with the same spicy sauce / 1000 island dressing found on the mussels on the half shell and several rolls. Spicy Tuna Roll, snarf. Salmon, snarf. Red Snapper, double snarf.
Oh hey guys...you made it! 1:40.
The guys join and get seated...order drinks...
By the time they got there, I realized that the items on the train had cooled considerably during their ride around the 10x20 foot room...So the shrimp balls were limp and cold by 2pm and the prime fatty tuna was gone. Bulgogi could have used a nuking. Not much tempura left of any sort which was probably just as well.
9 plates a piece or thereabouts...we ate till all there was left was salad and cheesecake...No major dent in anyone's wallet. Since the 1.50 special is over, I imagine it'll go to color coded plates from now on?
Note to self: get there early regardless.

Marco was very good, but ultimately didn't really alter my opinion that I can make Italian food just as good at home, and for a lot less money. The salads were tasty and fresh (really good tomato in the caprese), and the house-made pastas were delicious, but the appetizers were the standout and probably the only things I couldn't have replicated. I had the zucchini blossoms, which were deep-fried and stuffed with ricotta, and my fiance had the blue cheese-stuffed figs, which he liked very much but were not to my taste (the super-sweet figs and super-salty prosciutto didn't cancel each other out for me). It's a nice space, too, with the exception of some fake flowers... just, why??

Some negatives: they served our wine too warm, and our server, while very nice, didn't really seem to know what she was talking about -- she couldn't even pronounce the names of the pastas correctly.

So overall, a tasty meal, but I probably wouldn't go back, and thus my search for blow-your-mind Italian food (that isn't so fancy it can barely be called Italian anymore) continues.

this/viet cuisine,good location across  a mall,10%off every tuesday,free but limited parking by the rear plus street parking.small restaurant with diverse clientele.service is easy-calm-fast not excellent but not bad.good food.My relatives in Seattle everytime they visit Vancouver this is one of the place that is always at their bucket list,...aside from steambuns.......
I had the lemongrass chicken wit shredded pork and rice,plus i ordered fried spring roll,serving is not that generous by still to go half of my meal,just like before(been here often) yummy foods and im satisfied.Another resto that is Cash basis only......ill vist again soon....

A "specialist" did reach out to me, Brecken, "rhymes with wreckin," she said, and my initial concerns about the pop up transit fee were assuaged (compensated), and she was able to help with some other technical concerns. She provided a carfax link -- Carvana tours that they provide it, but I had to go through all of that to get it; it should be a link visible right under the car details, right up front. 
She acknowledged that my customer service experience had been problematic, and that the transit fee issue should be clearer. We'll see if Carvana makes adjustments to their software to inform customers of this fee earlier in the process. I found her to be helpful and professional. My advice to Carvana: release the Brecken earlier. 
The rest of the process using the website has continued to be kludgy, having to upload documents several times, delays in verification, delays in getting the contracts. About the contracts -- 23 pages! That you have to initial -- 20 times! Holy hell! I had to read carefully to make sure I wasn't promising my first born child. Seriously, reduce the legalese, please. 
I'm still not through the process, after many hours. This has not been easy, or seamless, by any stretch. It should be. That's what they promise. That's what we pay for. I hope they improve, because I love the concept.

Decent hotel option. I just had a couple of complaints that dragged it down to 3 stars over my Labor Day weekend:

*No soda machines on your floor for late night beverages.
*Pool was pretty small and always full of people
*I HATE when hotels, especially $200+ a night hotels, make you pay extra for WiFi
*Staff was ok, but not extremely welcoming. May have been overwhelmed with it being Labor Day
*Staff immediately came over to use when we came up with our half drank glasses of champagne and told us we had to ditch them by the pool. Note that our glasses were the plastic room cups, NOT glass, and I saw others there drinking out of tumblers. They cited a regulatory law, but I really think they just wanted us to buy their drinks at the bar.

Things I liked:
*Room service was quick and delicious
*Free water bottles
*Location was close to 6th, but far enough away that it was quiet
*Self Service parking for a cheaper $22/night was available. I hate Valet only places... I bought a room for myself, now I have to buy a place for my car too?
*Requested toothbrush was brought up quickly
*View from pool was pretty awesome
*Pretty cool looking lobby and elevators

All in all... decent option. Didn't walk away feeling great or like I got a good value, but didn't feel gypped either.

Let's set this straight, I didn't think I would ever review a department store like Macy's but here I am typing my life away. This Macy's been here (in downtown) since I can remember as a young child (actually it was Filene's but they moved across the street or under the tunnel to the current location). Majority of the clothes are in a neat pile and not like a tornado compare to other Macy's within a 100 mile radius. They offer more sales here than other Macy's and a bigger selection of a variety of sizes and styles from clothes to shoes and a decent home department. Bathroom is typically disgusting for the women on both basement and third floor. I can overlook it since it's not Nordstrom with higher standards for basically everything but what caught me off guard was when I lifted up pillows from their semi-decorated beds when shopping for furnitures and beds for my new home... there's mouse poop everywhere!!! I'm so disgusted by it. If anyone is interested, it's the "light gray" Monroe bed on the basement floor close to the ladies restroom and many other furnitures.  Despite having many childhood memories shopping with my girls after school or with my mom at this Macy's, I don't think I can ever shop here anymore.

Corporate, please give them more hours to clean or hire a cleaning company to help clean your big department store!!!

Review from an in-frequent gambler.
Seek table, odds, or dealer info from someone else. 
I was here for the concert entertainment.

I enjoy gambling on cruise ships. They are encouraged to have patience and help everyone play the games. Here, I felt the glances, head shakes and scowling of players and staff.

OK, I'll pick up my chips and go home.

This is no movie "James Bond casino atmosphere. This is sweatpants, and black NASCAR T-shirts kind of crowd.

I came here for an evening of entertainment. My group had different opinions. We sat in the O.H. restaurant and watched a show while dining. The "people watching" on the dance floor proved to be the entertainment. So now I can confirm that after dining at 2 restaurants, there is zero reason to come here for the food.

Here's what you should know about the FREE concerts promoted on their website. Baseball analogy~ The band plays on a respectable size stage with good audio and lighting. The stage is home plate. The O.H. Restaurant sits back from the 3rd base line. A limited seating bar with bar stools sits about 3rd base. VIP casino players sit in padded, roped off, elevated area at 2nd base. Casino tables and machines would occupy the outfield and 1st base line. A very large screen above the stage projects the entire stage show to the outfield, so you never have  to leave your gaming table. So where do you go to see the show? You stand! There is a large open area/dance floor in front of the stage for people to fill. It's from the very front of the stage to the VIP velvet ropes. Several viewers stood in the aisle behind the VIP seating. If you are lucky enough to catch a seat at the 3rd base bar or edge of the 3rd base line you can see most of the stage. They don't kick you out of the OHR if you finish your food and are watching the show, but they do keep asking "Will there be anything else".

I found out from a regular that minimum bets are increased on tables Friday and Saturday. Since the onslaught of people crowding the tables prevented me from playing comfortably, I bailed on that for machines. I had to ask someone where video poker games were. I found them back in a corner near the restrooms. Options to play for $.25, $.50, or $1 was a surprise. Bored after a short time, I walked the floor. I noticed only 4 servers moving around the floor with trays of drinks on a Friday night. I never saw a one come near the machines while I was seated.

Bathrooms were clean enough, and debris sitting on flat surfaces were not an issue.

XP

I'm kind of torn on how I should review the steak I had here last night... on one hand, I ordered my steak to be prepared medium rare and it ended up coming out medium... but then on the other hand, the steak was still pretty tasty. It would have been even more tasty had it come out medium rare like I would've liked it but the fact that they were able to prepare a steak medium and for it to have still been consumable, I have to commend them.

Was def let down by my experience. I was expecting a little more for the price and was let down. I felt like the food was okay and you were paying more for the name. We had the fondu appetizer and it was good but our entrees were just okay. I don't know that I would go again for the cost and def feel that it's more of a tourist trap. I'm glad we gave it a go and it was terrible it just didn't live up to my expectation.

After a haircut at Avenue Barbershop my Dad and I decided to grab some lunch at this Food court.  I was in the mood for more than just a hot dog or sliders so I tried out The Original New Orleans Po-Boy and Gumbo Shop.  I got a 6" blackened fish Po-Boy, french fries, and a drink.  The meal cost right under $10.  I thought it was a decent price for a lunch portion.  The fries order was a little small but were tasty and hit the spot after all.  The po-boy was good, but not great, fish could have used just a little more seasoning for my taste preference but overall had a good flavor to it.  The po-boy had all the fixings to go along with it; tomato, lettuce, mayo, and a dash of hot sauce.  The french bread was fresh and fluffy.  A decent po-boy in a grab it and go food trailer.

Not sure if it's because this place is extremely loud, but the servers always get our orders wrong. 

The bad experience(s) I had here as a group was when my colleague had asked for, oh I don't know a beer and she'd get a high ball, or when another colleague of mine asked for the bill 3 times and he'd get 3 drinks instead. Now, I don't know if this is their "tactic" to get the amount higher for the bills, but the servers don't even stick around for us to stop and tell them "no, this is not what I asked for" - drop and go, drop and go, really should be their motto. 

I do, however, love the space with games, sports tv and vibe for large groups. The food is good for a sports bar but again, what bar doesn't have good food? Its almost, always, fried goodies. 

No doubt I most likely would go back, only on the grounds that this place is good for large groups. 

The hosts/hostesses were super chill and nice though!!

Every time I've gone here to buy shoes I end up leaving with nothing. I keep hoping that I'll find a pair of shoes that will work for me. I'm a size 10 though, and W, and so ...it is tough to find comfortable shoes here. Last time there were only 2 choices that would work for what I was looking for and one of those was a size down...very tight. So I don't go here a whole lot, even though the prices are good, because the selection isn't great...I have a friend who absolutely loves this place.but  I never have had much luck.

I have never been a huge fan of CCF... Expect when I was 12 years old. My biggest problem is the size of their portions, it's simply insane. How the heck do they expect us to order a cheesecake after being on the verge of death after eating less than half of your meal. Also, the food has never blown my mind either. I've gotten nauseous from the 4 cheese pasta... However, it is a chain and the service tends to be decent whichever CCF I go to. If you're not a fan of the menu, give the almond crusted salmon salad, it's one of the best items I've had on the menu. (One of my friends lives by this place and so does my 8 year old brother so I've been dragged there over 20 times)

As far as Chinese food on the East Coast, this ranks as average.  I've had better and I've had a lot worse.  I would not go out of my way to come here, but if in the vicinity, I could possible try it again.  I'm not too picky when it comes to ordering Dim Sum from a cart or menu.  It's all the same quality to me.  This restaurant chooses the menu option.  No star deductions for that, but what really got me queasy was when I asked for water.  I noticed the waiter got it from the visible sink on the way to the bathroom.  I also noticed that this was the same sink that had a strainer for the waiters to dump plate contents in.  Knowing that, I didn't drink the water.

If you come here, I recommend the fried rice and pan fried noodles.

Okay, I'm going to do my best to give this place a fair review. After all, it seems unfair to compare the sushi from a shopping mall in New Westminster with the sushi that we had in Japan. So here goes... Woomi Sushi is located inside Royal Square Mall.

I wound up ordering their Special Bento Box E ($11.50) which included 2 pieces of tuna sashimi, 2 pieces of salmon sashimi, 2 pieces of yam tempura, chicken teriyaki, 4 pieces of California roll, salad and miso soup. I showed up just before noon on a weekday and it wasn't busy at all (not unexpected given how hidden this stall is).

The salad was crisp, the miso soup was hot, and the California roll was typical of sushi from a shopping mall... nothing outstanding here. Of everything, the yam tempura was probably the best as it had a light and crisp batter and seemed fresh. Meanwhile, the sashimi was the troubling part of this dish and you can kind of see it in how the sashimi appeared in the picture... it seemed to be still partially frozen. I even waited until the end of my meal to give the sashimi a chance to warm up a bit but I could still feel the slightly icy crunch from the inside of the flesh.

As for the chicken teriyaki, it tasted precooked and reheated and was served on a light bed of cabbage and limp broccoli. It's a shame because the people seemed nice and I really wanted to like this place more than I did.

all right I'm a make this short and sweet... The customer service is A-1...The prices aren't too bad compared to other specialty desserts shops such as this one.

they don't do any type of crazy flavors which is something I admire I do not like salt and straw so I decided to go here and I would say overall this is probably my second time going and I keep forgetting to write a review to myself to say "don't do it".

The ice cream is too darn sweet it almost taste like it was made with Splenda or some type of sweet and low...

Just my 2centz....

Ordered the lobster sliders that are 1/3 the size of the usual lobster roll so I could try more flavors. I had one Cajun and one Maine style both $5 each, served with a ton of chips. The Hawaiian roll was nicely buttered and fried on the outside but I felt the bread to lobster ratio was too high because the bread overwhelmed the lobster. Maybe this is just for the sliders and the normal sized roll would be better. The lobster meat itself was not flavored particularly well and makes me miss the lobster rolls I used to get in the Bay Area. It was buttered but somehow didn't have the rich flavor.

Pleasantly surprised to find this place near Disney.  Beware the Google directions, which put us in the shopping center across the street (where you'll find an unrelated Middle Eastern place that I'm glad we didn't mistake for Jerusalem Restaurant).  The service was pretty mediocre from our first waitress, but our group of 6 seemed to get handed off to a young man at some point near the end of our meal who was much friendlier and attentive.

Good, fresh, and proper Middle Eastern offerings, served with good presentation.

Let me say, I fully realize the implications of what I'm going to say during this post.  Pretty much everyone I've ever met in Austin talks about eating at the Salt Lick as an almost religious experience.  Well, this describes my experience: MEH.

First, the positives.  I LOVE the atmosphere.  It is the absolute perfect place to bring an out-of-town guest that wants a glossed over, stereotypically Texan experience without getting their hands too dirty at a more bare-bones, hot as hell BBQ joint (aka anything in what I view as a lil piece o' heaven, LOCKHART) You sit outside, drink beer or wine from the cooler (it's BYOB, for those that weren't aware) under huge, shady trees on long picnic tables.  On a beautiful, cool day, it is an absolutely sublime way to spend an afternoon with a group of close friends.  It's also perfect post-tubing in San Marcos.  If you haven't already noticed, there's a running theme here: booze.

In my humble opinion, though, the food is just alright.  I suppose it depends on your preference.  Salt Lick covers their meat in a bland sauce so you could be eating turkey, pork...whatever, and you'd never know, whereas, the more authentic places in places like Lockhart, view BBQ sauce as akin to blasphemy.  They passionately (and VERY rightfully) believe in the quality of their meat, and, thus, believe that it should speak for itself.  Some places will offer sauce (Black's), but it's definitely frowned upon.  Maybe if I'd never eaten at places like Smitty's or Black's, I would really dig Salt Lick, but, for me, the experience was pretty much ruined.  Don't get me wrong, I had a TON of fun.  But, after eating the insanely good, flavorful, delicious smokiness of the various briskets, homemade sausage and pork ribs lovingly cooked by the real Texas BBQ capital, nothing really stands a chance.  Also, the various owners are completely charming and the sense of history covering the walls of the restaurants is totally humbling.  Think, all the UT quarterbacks since forever ago thanking the owner of Black's, and personal letters of adoration from LBJ.  

So, this has completely snowballed into one long rant about how I kinda like Lockhart.  Just a little.  Bottom line, if you're looking for a place with ambience, then Salt Lick is a fun excursion to take friends from out of town and wind down after a raucous afternoon boozin it up on the river, but if you want the real deal, BBQ that brings you to tears of joy, Lockhart ALL THE WAY.

One of the reasons why it took me a while to get here even though this has been book marked on my list for two years was the cost. I also wanted to find someone special to go with. I came here with my girlfriend Peta.

When we came in it was quiet, therefore, we had a reasonable seat by the window to enjoy Gastown and the steam clock. It was raining but it was still nice to enjoy Vancouver none the less. 

I am not sure what the hype is about. Food is average, similar to what you can get at another pasta house just serverly overpriced. I am fine with $$ as a once in a while treat but the dishes weren't special. Black bean soup was okay, similar to what I had on commercial drive. The salmon was a few slices on a bed of greens with some cream cheese which was okay. It was appie size for $13!!!!

Our waiter was a little pushy with making us order more than we already did (bill was already high as is). I leave work to have a nice dinner into an environment of chill and relaxation, not to feel pushed. He tried a little too hard and making us order more, however, neither of us were that hungry. 

I was a little annoyed, therefore, I passively took out my frustration over the pushiness by drawing on the paper table cloth (see pic). 

They get 3 stars rather than 2 due to location and company and medium stars for food. 

You would expect the bathroom to be fancy, however, was disappointed that it looked like an upscale hole in the wall. 

I've had this on the list for 3 years but it was over hyped.

Like most of McMenamins historic locations, their Rock Creek Tavern is gorgeous, but this one was seriously lacking in the service department.

We seated ourselves upstairs, and waited for a server to notice us. He eventually did  and looked incredibly bored and mildly annoyed to be there. The food itself was ok, but it's nothing spectacular. The selections themselves are limited to salad, hotdogs, a few sandwiches and burgers. They had wings, but our waiter had no idea what they were like or how many were served. Between 2 people we ordered tots and a pork sandwich.  Nobody at the table requested that it be cut in half, but that's exactly how we received it. Two separate, sloppy plates with half a sandwich and a few fries thrown on. To make the sloppy plating worse, there were finger smudges of blue cheese on the plate and the dish did not contain any blue cheese.

After he cleared our sandwich plates, he came around again and asked if we wanted anything else. My husband still had some beer left, so he said not right now. The waiter took that as cue to bring us our check. We were considering ordering more drinks, but the check indicated to us that he wanted us to leave (and he did come around 1 or 2 more times to see if we paid the check yet). We eventually relieved him of his duties and went home completely dissatisfied with the service.

Not sure if we just got lucky with our waiter, but they really need to check their staff!

3 Stars for our dinning experience 5/28/11

Reasons for a 3 star rating:

1, The hostess and all of the staff were welcoming, smiling, very friendly and personable and we were about the third to be seated that evening in a fair placed spot in the middle of the restaurant. There was ample parking on Winsor Street although I suspect this was due to it being a holiday weekend.

2, We had what looked like an under pored portion servings of red wine. This became more apparent as the restaurants tables started to fill and other tables wine glass looked literally double the ounce size portion in comparison to ours. 

3, The appetizer was the Pear and Mache Salad which they split for us. Most other restaurants just plop the plate in the middle so the guests can eat from the same plate like Nubians. The presentation was above average and the flavor was as expected but nothing to throw a parade about.

4, Our entrees were the Hazelnut Agnolotti her and the Wild Striped Bass for myself. The Hazelnut Agnolotti was bland and not very hot and without much sauce, although the presentation was nice. The Wild Striped Bass presentation was beautiful and the flavor was bland. Both entrees could have used a heavier portion size given the cost. Both entrees were delivered in a timely manner.

5, A long wait for the check. I understand that by the time we completed out meal the restaurant was now full. However having one waitress for all those tables seemed excessive especially since there were multiple other staff available that could have dropped off the check. Another long wait for her to return with the charge card.

I'd say it would be highly unlikely that we'd return to Salts. Having eaten at many five star restaurants all over the world Salts falls short of a five star rating.

TLDR, the service here is fantastic! But stay away from the burgers and sandwiches on the lunch menu:/ Try coming for Sunday brunch or dinner though! There's a lot of good reviews on that! 

Decided to come here for lunch with my bf. They had complimentary valet on our way in and that was very nice. The ambiance was very refined, bright and beautiful! We were seated inside by the huge glass window/walls that displayed the river and garden they had going on outside. Everyone we encountered there, from the hostess to our waitress, was incredibly kind and welcoming. Our waitress was very knowledgeable about the menu and recommended us some nice dishes. We got the salmon appetizer to start, I got the angus burger, and my bf got a fish sandwich. 

We got some bread and butter to start. It was good, solid, nothing to write home about. Then the appetizer came out and was presented and plated fantastically! It tasted very fresh and delicious! The sauce was delightful! I was so eager to eat it that I forgot to take a photo!!! Sorry about that guys! 

Next, our entrees came out and unfortunately this is where Canoe lost 2 stars from me. The burger looked amazing. I had also read reviews and saw that a lot of people recommended the burgers here. But it was for the duck and beef burger, not the plain lunch angus burger. So maybe that's where I went wrong. Anywho, as soon as I bit into it, I realized that it was SO DRY and also BURNT on the bottom. I figured, ok, maybe I haven't gotten to the center where all the juices and flavors are. So I keep eating and eating (Bc I was also starving so i just put whatever into my mouth) and by the time I'm 3/4ths of the way finished, I realized wow...this burger is really just unseasoned, unflavorful, super dry, bitter, and hence was completely burnt on the bottom. I opened it up and yep. It was burnt and it looked like they tried to cover it up with sauces and stuff. 

That was probably one of the most disappointing and mediocre burgers I ever had in my life. I definitely would've enjoyed a shake shack burger more than this. My bfs sandwich was pretty good at least, but again, nothing spectacular and he even went as far as to make a joke that a McDonald's filet o fish would've been just as satisfying. At least the fries that came with our meals were delicious.

Overall, I can't rave enough about the amazing service and kindness of everyone, but I was incredibly blown by how meh the food was (except for the salmon appetizer, that was amazing!). I want to give them the benefit of the doubt and say that it's a great restaurant, but maybe only the dinner menu. The lunch menu is a hit or miss. Most of the great reviews on yelp are of the dinner or Sunday brunch menu. So I guess if I ever do come back (ehhh maybe??), I'll have to come back during those times:/

I frankly don't know what all the fuss is about. We were there in the afternoon when there was just a few customers about. The donuts are just doughnuts, priced quite a bit higher than what you will find elsewhere, with a few creative twists thrown in. We could tell that earlier there had been a massive crowd, rope line area lengthy and littered with paper coffee cups and napkins, pretty much a mess. If you need a doughnut and don't mind a little squaller, you can check it out and at least be able to say you've been there.

Good Peruvian food but I don't think it's a good value for your money. Yes it's a fine dining kind of place and slightly more expensive than your regular Portland restaurants but the food should also speak that well.

The complimentary bread and dips were really good ranging from mild to spicy..something for everyone. We didn't order the tapas because we were very hungry and so got the entrees. I wanted to get one tapas but $10 for half avocado with a little crab meat sounded too much to me.

We ordered Aji De Gallina (pulled chicken dish with peanut sauce, potatoes and garlic rice). It was good but a little in the sweeter side. Rice was very well seasoned and I could just eat rice on its own. We also ordered vegetarian Quinoa risotto. Really a lot could have been done with that dish but they seemed to not put any effort in it. Just some cooked quinoa with a couple of red pepper strips and one tiny blob of cheese and for $16!! Very expensive for those ingredients and preparation.

Red Sangria was very good. Like we've had in some South American countries.

Lots of outdoor seating which is fantastic, they have a new way to order which is tricky if you're not smart phone savvy but it keeps contact down between people. The menu is.... blah. We had a kid with us and she ordered the kid burger... they literally made a normal burger and cut it in half and served half a cheeseburger, where does the other half go? Seems wasteful, plus the photo shows a whole burger. I had the Ham and Swiss sandwich, it was again blah. Basically if you want beer and cider this is your place. No wine FYI.

Was all excited to try this place after all the great reviews. 

The store was Clean, sleek, the guy who greets and takes your order was as nice as everyone said. His name is Stephen. 
He explained it all and the emphasis was on all natural and healthy. 

Well, bottom line for us is we don't drink buba for our health. We drink it as a treat. 

We ordered our usual lychee and taro. Both had no taste. We would have returned them but already drove away. The bubba was included in the prices and were nice and soft. The drinks were bland.

It was so blah you couldn't tell what flavor it was suppose to be. 

Won't be returning but because the set up was comfortable, seating, free WiFi, free frequent buying club, plenty of parking and Stephen was so kind.... had to give them an extra star.

First time there, food was excellent all but me and my girlfriends porkchops 2 we share. Salads came out then porkchops and they were pink inside.. asked to get them more done 15 min later our sons food was done and he's ready to go.. I told her we didn't want them anymore she said I'll take them off your bill plus give them to you in a Togo container.. well the manager gave me my Togo 20 min later dinner.. there was one porkchops in the container I ordered two... oh my.. then the bill they were not taken off and then finallly the waitress removed it off my bill... our server was nice Erika is her name but that key manager Ashley needs to be retained on her job...Me or my family will not return

Maybe I'm a  "hard sell", but in the end, if a place doesn't have the whole package I will look elsewhere because in a town like this where there are at least a generous handful of pretty much every type of business, including hair salons with wonderful stylists. So why not support the place that has not just the mad skilled stylist but also an inviting, friendly, approachable, not snobby staff who have stellar customer service skills ???? This place is lacking. I called to make an appointment for a cut and color which I explained to the person setting the appointment would involve working with grown out platinum color on the ends of my hair. The woman said she knew exactly what was needed time wise, when I got there, sat in the chair, the stylist was so rude to me stating she'd only be able to do the cut and that the color needed way more time than was scheduled. It felt like she was shaming ME, not apologizing for the mistake made not offering go find another time that would work before my event, nothing! I left feeling like I had done something wrong. 

Luckily I walked down the street to Voodoo Hair Salon And was met by the warmest, kindest, most generous stylist and support staff. Like I said, shoot for the place that has it all. Enough with people making this town snobby. Boulder is a friendly place. 

Mean people suck!

We stayed at the Heathman Hotel for one night, quick getaway for my boyfriends 30th. It was O.K. The staff were very kind and changed our room from the 8th floor no view to the 10th floor decent view because our neighbor's pot was permeating the hallway and our room. There was a concert that night, Oktoberfest...and we could hear it from the room; it was actually kinda nice. In bed-listening to music. The room we had was extremely tiny. The bed takes up the majority of the room, which ended up being the best part of our stay, we slept like rocks. We ended up staying in for the night and it proved to be wayyyyy too small for a night in, I felt squished. We wanted to spend some time in the hot tub or sauna...but couldn't because they don't exist at the Heathman. That was my fault for not researching properly. The valet was overpriced at $42 per night, and hotel over $300 over priced.  Overall 3.5 for amazing staff, and location. I don't think I'd stay again mainly because of the price and size.

I was only in town for three days, and everyone was like "YOU HAVE TO GET VOODOO DOUGHNUT". Well, apparently everyone else's friends told them the same thing because the first time I went, the line was literally two blocks long. I would have felt like such a fat kid if I waited in a two-block line for a doughnut.

So then I tried to go after the bars, as I had heard Voodoo is 24 hours. It was closed. The universe did not want me to have these legendary doughnuts.

As I was leaving town I finally got one, but the selection was so overwhelming that I freaked out and just picked the first one that spun past me on that little rotating doughnut display, a Tang doughnut. It was unique, a little dry, nothing particularly special, but I'm glad I got to experience it, and wish I could go back to give it another try. I think it really does all just depend on what you get, so next time I'd spring for a dozen to sample a few more.

I love Pho and was really looking forward to trying this place out. They have a huge menu with so many choices. I ended up ordering a curry dish instead of Pho......I should have definitely stuck with my original choice. I also ordered crab Rangoon as an appetizer. They were delicious but very greasy. The oil was dripping out of them. The sweet and sour sauce was also very interesting and different. It was very sweet and not at all sour. My curry was delicious but more like a curry soup. It was very thin, but had tons of flavor. The staff was friendly, but it is kind of confusing whether or not you are supposed to order at the counter or just have a seat. The inside set up is very crowded and not set up very well. The tables were kind of sticky and not whiped down. I will most likely be back to try the pho, but will be getting my order to go.

So this was my first time at SeaWorld. The dolphin show and Shamu show was a blast. We went on a Thursday early and expected not too much of a crowd. We were wrong. Place was packed and after the show there were long lines for food. Also, the few rides they had were lined up for hours. Maybe it was just me and my non-liking of amusement parks, I dont know. Shows were nice though. I dont know if it was worth the $75 each.

I was intrigued by the idea of a Korean-style poutine so I decided to try this place.

My first foray was through UberEats (thank you pandemic) and I was instantly awestruck by the Korean counterpart to one of my favorite Canadian dishes. 

Important to know, if you order delivery there are a couple of sauces that come packaged separately from the main dish. One is hit chili sauce and the other is movie-theater-nacho-cheese-sauce. I only realized it after finishing my glorious mountain of spuds and bulgogi beef . 

My reprise was an in-person visit to make sure I experienced this spudtastic mashup in all its glory. Well, turns out the cheese-in-can sauce actually demotes the dish and takes away from the magic. I feel the cheese is there to balance the heat from the chili sauce but there's gotta be a better alternative than radioactive-yellow cheese sauce

(Dined 03/04/20 WE @ 12:00pm): This lad's arse was feeling pretty lard after eating this ginormous donut!

On the grounds of Universal Studios Resort Orlando (Universal Studios Florida to be exact), I had to drag my travel friend along to Lard Lad Donuts for a gigantic snack and its iconic Big Pink Donut from the animated series "The Simpsons" fame. I loved donuts - apple fritters to be exactly - but as a tourist I had to get this massive pastry. Did this donut have any merit or was it totally for show!?

PURCHASE
The Big Pink Donut ($7.49): This giant donut with sweet, creamy thick fluorescent pink frosting and rainbow sprinkles was a sight to behold, be held, and be eaten with all the childlike giddy tendencies you could muster. The pink frosting was layered on thick yet didn't crackle off which was a good thing while the actual breading was more dense than airy fluffy as I'd hoped, and I wished there were more rainbow sprinkles for complete coverage. A fun "meal" but could've been better https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=bWGb5pG-ZXX3cUN-0hbekg&userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw.

SERVICE
I was greeted by a middle-aged somewhat curmudgeon woman who wasn't in the mood for any pleasantries which I found odd. And when asked if they had the apple fritter, she vehemently retorted, "we have had those for over a week now!" Furthermore, unlike the Hollywood location where they had several donut types to choose from, these were the only options here. Anyway, I got my donut, paid up, and walked over to a nearby bench to grub down.

PARKING (Varied; N/A this instance)
General parking for the massive theme park started from $25.00, but my friend and I took a Lyft ride in and skirted parking altogether. Also, I believed if you stayed at any of the resorts in the area, shutter services were available.

ATMOSPHERE, DÉCOR, AMBIENCE
Truly a wooden shack the size of a large storage room with only a walk-up order/pick up window with barely enough room to fit two individuals inside let alone any available refreshments, you ventured nearby for a table to enjoy your purchase or walked with it. A very legible price menu was placed on a window where you ordered https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=X5O3iXgEh_6LOp-BDBpvBg&userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw. Plenty of natural lighting since you were outdoors while various electric light poles covered the rest. There were no TVs while the whirling sounds of conversations, rides, etc., filled the air. https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=xXV3yG5MFsznzsM8Tflg-g&userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw

ATTIRE
Totally casual, so I would normally be in a t-shirt, boardshorts, and flip-flops.

OVERALL
If you visited Universal Studios Resort Orlando (specifically the Universal Studios Florida park portion) and were a fan of "The Simpsons", then you definitely had to seek out Lard Lad Donuts for the experience of a giant donut to be eaten proudly while seen by others. Sure, this was 100% a marketing tool (my career has been in marketing for over 25 years!) because the donut wasn't amazing yet still fun to eat. But in my case, I was actually excited about the prospects of the apple fritter which they were out of. I'd go back again for merely shits-and-giggles and another cool photo op https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=B0x7IK4f4JP6QWD5Yta6Cg&userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw. I found good value based on the prices, service, and experience noted above (TOTAL paid experience was around $8.00 BEFORE any discounts and/or tip). And, they accepted my credit card of choice... AMEX! 3.0 STARS

Downtown Orlando needed a 24 hour diner and this place fills that niche when you're craving for breakfast , lunch or dinner.  I've been 2x now , once for lunch and once for dinner.  I do love the cool 50's theme with huge booths and fun sayings on the walls.   I see this being a popular choice with the weekend folks after a late night around Downtown. 

The menu has your usual diner fare - breakfast items, soups, salads, sandwiches and heartier entrees. On my first visit I had the Brioche grilled cheese and tomato soup. It was more than enough food for me and it came with waffle fries too! I loved the tomato soup and finished it off . Perfect comfort food. They also carry desserts by The Dessert Lady. We actually started off our meal with the Oh No Chocolate Cake which is the best way to start off every meal. 
Second visit was early evening. We had a larger party and I felt that the timing of when items came out took longer than it really should have. The restaurant was empty and most of us ordered breakfast items. The Belgian waffle is good and comes with butter and syrup. If you want to add fruit, chocolate chips or pecans- be prepared to fork up $1 EACH!   I also had the creamy mashed potatoes which are excellent and a highly recommended side item. They make them with red potatoes and they came out piping hot.

Service was a little so so on both visits. The first time , it took awhile for someone to approach our table to take our order.
