Luckily, once we flagged someone she was pretty attentive but took awhile to get our checks to us. The recent visit  was ok- our server wasn't as friendly and was sort of going through the motions?   Overall, service isn't consistent so you never know how your experience will be.   

I would probably check them out for dessert on a future visit or when I'm craving breakfast. It's a fun option for the Downtown crowd though and being open 24/7 will definitely work in its favor.

We tried this place based on the yelp reviews that looked pretty good. I would say that maybe the buffet would be worth a try but for a regular "off the menu" evening, it was a disappointment.  The mixed platter was dry, the shrimp was overcooked, the chicken had been sitting under the heat lamp too long. 
I will say the naan bread was great and the service was fantastic but that might have been because there weren't very many tables filled.  Anyway, consensus at a table of 5 was that we probably won't be coming back.

My colleague and I wanted to go to The Container coffee shop that was part of The Burrard Hotel, and found instead that its been replaced with Elysian Coffee recently.  I ordered the Flourless Chocolate Cookie with a Almond Chai Latte (cold).  My colleague got their Cheddar Scone (which looked really nice) and a coffee.  All the food displayed looked nice and it looks like they serve sandwiches for less than $8 too.  However, I just didn't like the taste of the food I got.  My cookie was reeallyy hard, when I was expecting a gooey, freshly baked cookie like I normally get at bakeries; but I guess they're not a bakery.  My Almond Chai Latte didn't taste like almond but there was another really strong taste to it I can't identify, but I wasn't fan.

The barista was nice, the location had a patio that overlooked Burrard Street, and it had a nice relaxing vibe.  I'll probably give them another chance - maybe I'll stick to more traditional coffee from them.

Decided to come here last night on a whim to get a Tex-mex fix. We've never been to this location but have been to Chuy's in Texas.

There's plenty of parking as the restaurant has its own parking lot. 

On a Friday night, the restaurant was probably only one third full, so there was no wait. The first thing I noticed upon walking in was the dirty floors (silverware, napkins, chips, etc). Lots of dirty tables too.. with minimal staff in sight.

Salsa is suuuuper fresh tasting and delicious. I didn't care for their jalapeño ranch sauce (honestly tastes like a dressing to me) or for the boom boom sauce which is highly reviewed. I will say my husband really likes the boom boom sauce. 

I ordered a skinny margarita which was OK - definitely tasted the sour mix. If I ever go back, I may try the sangria.

Got the Friday special for my meal- chicken enchiladas with green chili avocado sauce. The chicken was extremely tender. The enchiladas were decent. 

Everyone else in our party got the boom boom enchiladas. We all thought the enchiladas were extremely spicy. Much spicier than expected and we eat spicy food all the time!

Got the tres leches cake for dessert. It was decadent, rich, and delicious. Split between 4 people and we had trouble finishing it. The slice is HUGE.

Not sure if I will be back considering I was turned off by how dirty the restaurant felt, mediocre service, and OK food.

If I ever find myself here again, I will probably just fill up on chips and salsa... and dessert!

Overall, we enjoyed Chuy's in Texas more.

This is a cute little breakfast/lunch place in the SoDo area. They recently changed their menu as well to add healthier options as well. Whenever I come to this place there is always a long wait, but we seem to get seated in less time than suggested. My last experience was not so good though. There was a 25 minute wait so we decided to sit at the bar area. It was an immediate sit down and our order was taken quickly. This was all great until the actual food part. It took 26 minutes to get our food to us. I only know this because we could see our order on the screen with a time next to it lit up in red. I ordered an omelet (no meat) and my bf ordered scrambled eggs with potatoes. Both of these meals should have been made relatively quickly, but we saw that other meals came out before ours. We were both disappointed. The food wasn't bad but the service was not so great. :(

For such high prices, I was a little disappointed. 

We ordered:
Involtini di Melanzane: it tasted ok and had nice presentation, but it was quite small for a $10.50 appetizer. It was three very thin slices of eggplant wrapped around cheese, with marina sauce drizzled around and garnished with arugula. Tasted good, but nothing out of this world.

Polenta al forno: This was the best tasting dish of the night. The polenta was moist and delicate. I think it could have used more Gorgonzola for flavor. I felt like they skimped on it. 

Rigatoni al ragu: Pretty good, nice sauce. Worth $19.50, though? Probably more like $15. 

Trota alla grigla: Had some issues...the biggest being the fish did not taste very fresh. The menu said it was rainbow trout. Usually rainbow trout has a delicate, almost sweet flavor. This one had a fishy, unctuous flavor, and the texture was dense and kind of unpleasant. The sauce was OK, but why were there so many onions in the dish--sautéed with the side of asparagus in addition to diced raw on top of the fish? Seemed like onion overkill.

Overall, I thought the food was expensive and just average. 

A note about the bread: I've traveled through Italy, and the bread they serve is not authentic, my friend. Correct me if I'm wrong, but squishy soft bread is more of an American preference. Don't get me wrong, I devoured it. But it ain't Eye-talian. I might expect a crusty bread or maybe focaccia in a fine authentic Italian joint. 

For better food for the same or lower prices, try Olive and June or Enoteca. The ambience at those places is much more interesting as well.

Pizza is  Greek style. Order the Greek, the Arpeggio, or the White pizzas. The wonderful sons who help their father run this place - they will make a half and half pizza for you too. My favorites - the White and Greek. My husband loves the Arpeggio. Ask for extra sauce. Yum! Mediterranean food here is good too and so fresh! Hummus and gyros cannot be beat. Eat on the floor with pillows if you have  a craving to  do something different. I think pizza toppings have decreased somewhat from the last time I ordered.

I walked in during happy hour.  The menu was only limited to snacks and appetizers.  Meat charcuterie was bland even when eaten with the pickles and mustard.  Lumpia was lame and greasy.  Clyde burger was dry.  I should of just waited for the dinner menu.  Funny thing is...the dinner menu is served at 6pm and even at 5:45, they would not take a dinner menu order.  So it must be good.  Wrong.  We tried the pork belly as recommended by the waiter.  Was like a bland piece of bacon.  It did have good texture.  I was looking for this meld of flavors, but found none.  I wasn't even expecting exciting spice flavors.  Just disappointed.  We ordered the ginger ice cream cake...good, but not worth returning for.  I gave three stars for the ambience and nice waiter.  Not sure if the drinks were good since we didn't have any.

I went with a group of late 20-somethings on a Sunday evening.  Generally, it was a good experience.  First, there were a few vegetarian friendly items to choose from (fries of many kinds, hummus plate, flatbread pizzas, salads, pasta dishes).  Veg dishes are often overlooked at gastropubs.  Furthermore, there aren't many bars like it in the area.  We didn't have to wait, the food came out at the same time and quick, waitstaff was fairly attentive, but there were a few odd things:
1) We were the youngest people there.
2) The menu is upscale, supposedly, but I found it a bit over seasoned, like they were compensating for poor quality of base ingredients.
3) The beer is watery.  I had the apricot wheat ale, some friends got Bass, others got some kind of white ale.  All agreed the beer was a bit dilute.
4) The waitress whisked away our truffle fries even though we were still picking at them.  She didn't even inquire as to whether we were finished or not.  A big disappointment, as these were the highlight of the menu.

Other things sampled: chive and truffle mac n' cheese (okay,  a bit overseasoned and not baked in its serving dish, so there were no crunchy edges), kobe burgers (an overcooked disappointment, according to my carnivorous hubs), parmesean truffle fries (stonking great), homemade potato chips (crisp, fresh, good ranch dip), buffalo wings (the friend eating those was pleased with the amount of heat and juiciness), goat cheese salad (bigger portion than you'd expect and fresh).

I may be back on an off-night for drinks and dinner since it's convenient to where I live, but I wouldn't want to fight a crowd to come here.

I know everyone raves about the desserts here.  I don't like desserts so overloaded in sugar that you can't taste the flavors. It's a trendy thing here in the U.S. the sugar over-kill.  We've tried everything from the cinnamon rolls (or whatever they're called) and people rave about them. All I can say is "seriously"?   I did love the coconut cream pie, which is unusual. The chicken salad sandwich was the standout, AMAZING!  I did have a dessert that I had high hopes for but ended up going to return it at the counter (it's been a while so I can't remember) but it was one of those desserts that should have been light as air but instead was like a slab of cement. The counter person seemed shocked that I didn't like it but was super nice and exchanged it for something else. 

I still go there!  The staff is great, and as mentioned there are things that suit my taste that are fantastic.

I'd go to 3.5 stars if I could,  while I've never had a bad enough experience to post a negative review I certainly have had inconsistent experiences here.  From long delays likely kitchen related but poorly communicated by servers.  To cold food. And mixed up orders,  however their delicious margaritas,  and cold beer usually help forget that by the end of the meal. 

Also they are open breakfast lunch and dinner, and late dinner at that!
They can also accommodate crowds and parties.

Usually they are true to form,  loud music or a football game to watch as you eat/ drink. 

This is, in my opinion,  the best Mexican choice within the 2 mile radius it occupies (and there are many options)

We usually order heavy here,  and I've eaten most items on the menu, (often I'm in a party of 5) 

They are a consistent choice for an uncomplicated dining experience.

The service here was great waitor was very knowledgeable about the menu and even other restaurants in the area and the best places to try. The food on the other hand was not that impressive.  The chicken that I ordered was good but the donuts were not. Others at my table food was not good. The Cuban sandwich was really dry and didn't taste that good.
 The chicken and dumplings was okay as far as flavor but the chunks of chicken were huge and didn't really add much to the dish.

The waterfront atmosphere keeps this from being a 2 star.

Only in Boston can you claim to be a mexican restaurant and think a hot sauce selection of only tabasco is enough (actually if you press for it the kitchen can make you some custom hot sauce .. So push for it) 

I ate at the bar on a sunday evening at it was hopping. Didn't have dinner , just had some bar snacks which were dissapointing. The homemade guacamole seemed too shiny, like it had sour cream in it or mayo. The carnitas tacos were mushy. The good news is they have my two favorite tequilas:  Don Julio 1941 and Maestro Dobel. I recommend you get these neat as they over chill the shots and they come out too watered down.

The wait here is pretty brutal, and when we arrived at Marco's, I was almost delirious with hunger, and could have really used a cup of coffee while I waited, but there didn't appear to be any way to score any. 
Once we were (finally) seated, the food came quickly and was very tasty (especially with Secret Aardvark sauce added!). 
No complaints, but wow, don't go here if you're already hungry. 
Docking one star each for:
-not taking reservations
-not offering coffee while you wait for a table

This place is an amazing very well thought out concept! It truly is stunning first walking into the place. So many things to do here. We came here for a birthday party and the place was pretty dead. Unfortunately we had HORRIBLE service. No ones drinks were refilled almost the whole time. We had to  ask for things multiple times. Waitress only would come by once every 20 minutes, usually empty handed. One person's food didn't come out until everyone was already done eating. The waitress said her food would be comped but when the bill came it wasn't. The food itself was decent but not great. Portions were kind of small. Nothing had sauces on it. My chicken sandwich lacked the Alabama sauce and my wife's burger lacked the comeback sauce. Fries were pretty good. Overall I'd be willing to give them another shot.

I was drawn into this store by the moroccan-style lights they have in the window.  Not only are they really cool looking, but they are completely affordable.  Two thumbs up.  The rest of the store was nice, but I wasn't really feeling it.  My girlfriend was.  I glanced at a few nice Day of the Dead items that also seemed fairly priced.  I think I was burnt out on shopping at the point that we went here...we had been at it for a while and this was our last stop.  I will go back someday.

The Pour House has been our Friday lunch go to for as far as I can remember.  You can count on beer and pizza Friday's, no question on where the office was going to lunch.  But recently it seems that we cannot get our meal in a timely manner.  For the last three weeks it has taken a bit of time to get our food and it's nothing too complicated, pizza and salads.  It's sad to say that we may have to look for a new venue since we cannot risk going over our one hour lunch time.

Since all of the VS stores sell the same meh-quality merchandise, I'll do my best to write about this store's customer service instead. The girls that work here are friendly and helpful. All of the girls, all at the same time, all friendly, all helpful. Um, calm down, I just told you I knew what I wanted. I had four sales associates on my tail before I could even orient myself. When I told them I knew what I wanted, they didn't stop. They hovered like little perky boob-happy helicopters. I understand they're just doing their job, but seriously. That's more annoying than it is helpful and I ended up leaving and going to Macy's (where I got 3 bras for less than the price of one VS bra, and they'll probably last longer, too.)

I had a one-night business stay here. It's a decent choice in that area. 

Good things:
* Location - very close to Disney 
* Pool area - great resort feel with lots of fun things to do; beautiful to look at, too
* The pantry food area - way more offerings than the typical Marriott pantry (including some premade items in a refrigerated section)
* Breakfast buffet - lots of diversity on the buffet including a delicious cous cous salad, eggs benedict, tomato/mozzarella salad, etc. Very good service, too. Wilson was fabulous. 
* Room had a balcony (but a warning: there were a lot of wasps out there during the day)
* A full Starbucks in the lobby
* Elevators were pretty fast and available in spite of it being such a huge hotel 

Bad things:
* No M Club
* Stayed in a room that hadn't been renovated yet -- it was just OK and looked a little worn out. But renovated rooms are happening in waves there. 
* My room's AC was really struggling and wasn't cooling the room or taking the humidity out. If I had been staying there longer I would have had to move or get it fixed. 
* The parking options are self-park and valet, but the self park option is pricey ($24) and involves parking in a garage that is far enough away from the hotel that a shuttle runs you back and forth. You need to allow for time for the shuttle to get to you and then run you there and back. Valet is $35 a night. It's probably worth it just to valet. 
* Had to pay for the $30 a night resort fee even though I didn't use any of the pools or anything resort-like at all (as I was there for work). I did get "free" internet but I would have had that anyway with Titanium status 

If I stayed again in the area, I might stay here again if the price was right but I also would consider trying another Marriott property in the area.

I love Ramen... I really do! I was wicked excited when this place showed up to the scene. If I've said it on e I've saId it a 1,000 times, we don't get much way out here in the burbs, so when I heard ramen was coming so was all about it. 

I have to admit it's not in the nicest of strip malls so don't judge it when you drive by. They have painted the walls with some pretty dope art, it's pretty awesome. The food here is amazing, they keep it simple and let you pick and choose your broth and toppings etc.

FYI they dont serve booze so my first time here was a bit of a bummer, mama likes to pound grape with her dinner. Anyhow they allow BYOB, I would say bring a twist top wine or your own opener, the table next to us were in a bind without an opener. 

The service here is the only reason I went 3 stars, the 2 times I came here it was a complete meltdown on service. My waitress on my first visit got into with another worker, it was heated and she ended up crying in the corner so no water refills for us. The second visit they were struggling, they did say it was due to short staff but that was the case 2 weeks ago and clearly still an issue.

Tasty Ramen, BYOB for now but have some patience while the work out the kinks with their service.

The beer selection was excellent.  Had the Lobster roll.  Wasn't as good as I hoped.  The Lobster was a little on the rubbery side.  I was only visiting and I love lobster roll so I was a little disappointed.  So disappointed that the next day I tried the lobster roll at another restaurant, but there's was rubbery as well.   It could be that kind of year for lobster.  The service was excellent and beer was great, but I did go there for the food.

Really tried hard to love the food esp. after reading all the 4 and 5 star reviews from my favorite Yelpers - but couldn't. However the service was top notch, and I loved the ambiance. 

We had a party of 5, and shared 2 apps and 5 entrees - just the right amount of food. Everyone cleaned their plates :) Yes we did family-style dining at a restaurant where the food isn't designed for that - we just said we're going to share our food, and next thing you know, they brought all 5 entrees to the center of our table, and set 5 empty plates for each of us. Extra bonus points for portioning out some of the dishes, plus adding a few extra corn on the cob to equal 5 :) That's service! 

I so wanted to give 5 stars b/c of the great service but the food didn't live up to the hype. Part of me wonders if I should blame the ok food b/c we came on a Monday. Anthony Bourdain's "Kitchen Confidential" said Mondays aren't a good day to eat out at restaurants. 

COMPLIMENTARY CHIPS & SALSA
Love the blue chips and I liked that the salsa was spicy.

GUACAMOLE & CHIPS - $7 (full order)
Nothing special, and a full order is not really all that big ... good size for 5 people though.

GUAJILLO MUSSELS - $10.50
Mussels were small & fishy, and while the red chili citrus wine broth was tasty, I wish it were thicker. The flour tortilla seemed random ... I guess crusty bread wouldn't fit the southwestern theme. 

CHILI SEARED JUMBO DIVER SEA SCALLOPS - $19.50
Menu description set too high expectations :( Pan seared scallops in signature herb & chili rub, served w/ fire roasted tomato & serrano stone ground grits (salty) and honey cider collard greens (good & sweet). Just ok.

AGAVE FAMOUS CAYENNE FRIED CHICKEN - $15
Jumbo size boneless chicken breast but didn't get any cayenne flavor. Buttermilk marinated & fried (not crispy). Yukon Gold mashed potatoes were good, and grilled corn was too buttery for me and I couldn't taste the Poblano drizzle at all.

STUFFED MOUNTAIN TROUT TOMATILLO - $17.50
Just ok. Liked the stuffing more than the actual trout. Idaho trout was stuffed w/ crawfish, mushrooms, onions, and basil over Spanish rice w/ roasted tomatillo sauce and freshly cut cilantro (but I don't remember tasting any cilantro). 

SPICY TEQUILA ANEJO SHRIMP - $18.75
Biggest disappointment b/c this dish got the most positive reviews. Again menu description set very high expectations. Fresh gulf shrimp grilled & sauteed in fresh lime & tequila cream sauce (not spicy at all), and served a/ jalapeno & cheddar ground grits cake (good but mostly cheddar flavor and very salty), and grilled asparagus. The asparagus was probably my favorite item of the evening. 

TENDERLOIN MEDALLIONS - $23
Meat was pretty tender and one of the better dishes. Tenderloin pan seared over roasted tomato, garlic, and chile tequila puree, and served w/ Yukon Gold mashed potatoes (yum), fried cayenne onion rings (not spicy), and grilled zucchini. 

Overall, I thought the sides were better than the entrees. Also, couldn't taste all the flavors described in the menu. Other than the salsa, nothing was spicy. However like I said before, service was outstanding ... and maybe we just came on a bad day. I definitely want to try their drinks next time - almost every table around us had margaritas :)

FYI - complimentary valet parking is available but if you're lucky, you might be able to find nearby street parking on Carroll Street. Also join their VIP club to get 20% off your entire check Sun-Thur, or get $10 entrees if you come between 5-6pm any night of the week! Sign up now!

Mixed feelings about 49th.  The food here is average and a bit overpriced.  The coffee didn't taste that good and was expecting a better tasting cup of joe for all of the hype.  I will say they do have some creative donuts.  For $5 CAD you get a donut and a cup of coffee, which honestly isn't too bad, but then again the coffee wasn't that great.  

What we ordered:
The French Cruller was by far their best donut!  This donut was AMAZING!!!!!!  So crispy, fluffy and perfectly cooked.  Must must order!

The Old Fashioned Chocolate Peanut Butter donut was good, I wouldn't say it was my favorite but it was worth the try. 

The glazed donut was horrible.  Didn't taste good at all and it definitely was an old batch.  Don't order this one. 

The Doug was pretty good.  The eggs were bomb and were super tasty.  A bit over priced. $9 CAD 

Last but not least, the Avocado Toast.  This was terrible.  The avocado did not taste authentic.  I felt as if it were straight from a packet from the store.  

Over all nice place to visit and grab a quick bite, but be forewarned that not everything here is as good as the pictures make it out to be.

This evening a couple of my lady friends and I decided to play tourist in our own back yard.  So we went to TGIFridays to watch the bats while enjoying some beverages and snacks.  

My three star rating is an 'average' for the chain restaurant experience.  The food was up to standard and consistency of the well know brand.  I have no gripe there what so ever...   And to be honest,  I have to say that is hard to find decent chicken wings... TGIFridays never disappoints!  For maintaining their brand standards I give them a 4 star.

I give our server a 1.  After waiting SEVERAL minutes a server who clearly came over from another section asked us is we had been helped.  His name was Andrew and he was VERY friendly.   If we had been able to keep him as a server I think that our experience would have been ideal.  However, it was not his section and he was just being a team player.  Our server is nameless because he never introduced himself.  Of course they all wear name tags, and a name is usually on the guest check... however I was so unsettled from our bad experience that I had actually forgotten to put his name to memory.  Our server was constantly absent,  and it took him forever to bring items we may have requested.  We had to ask for water THREE times.  It took over five minutes to process our check.  

If you read my blog and my reviews here, you know that I am NOT accustomed to write about my negative experiences.  Therefor I guess that I just could not be bothered to put his name to memory.  Fitting I suspect, as he just could not be bothered to do his job!

The service was not up to standard for any establishment.   As a fellow server, I am embarrassed to have someone like this in my profession.  This kind of service gives the rest of us a bad rap, and he should be ashamed.

Inbound Pizza will be the death of me one day because I eat too much of it too often. Ah! Can I mention that I'm a born and bred New Yorker, and this pizza lives up to a New York slice? Yeah, for realz.

My roommate and I have come here many a time, whether it be for a quick slice, a full pie, or some food to satiate around drunk munchies. Most of the time they don't disappoint, and their pizza is pretty consistent. When it's good, it's good; when it's an off night, it can be really off. This doesn't happen often, but there have been nights when the pizza was just awful. I don't know if it was because someone else was cooking it or they were rushing, but it could be terrible on these types of unfortunate nights. Rare those nights are, though! They also take Level Up, which is awesome. I try to use it as often as I can, and I think I get the most mileage with that at Inbound.

If you're looking for a quick bite or a whole pie for a movie night in your apartment, I would bank on Inbound being the place to go!

Shake Shack just opened in this Winter Park location at the end of July 2014 and it's still pretty busy! We arrived on a Saturday for lunch, showing up around 11 am. We waited in line for quite a while just to order because there was only one cashier for the first fifteen minutes or so. After a while, they did move up to three cashiers and things moved much more quickly after that. There is an express line if you just want concretes, shakes, or other drinks. If you want food, though, you have to wait in the longer line.

Placing our order was easy. There's a limited menu, which makes it easier to figure out what you'll eat (less indecisiveness there!). We got two ShackBurgers and added pickles and onion for free--for whatever reason, they just come with lettuce and tomato unless you specify. We split one order of regular fries (they also offer cheese fries) and then each got a shake: peanut butter for me, caramel for my husband. I like that Shake Shack puts the calorie count next to their food items although it's just a range for things like shakes (it will say "Shakes, 640-930 calories," for example, instead of saying "Peanut butter shake, X # of calories" ... I'm pretty sure mine was the 930 calories one).

They give you a pager device and you wait for your food. Ketchup, mustard, mayo in packets, etc. is nearby. It took a while to get our food and in the short time that we waited, the place got PACKED. Like, no more tables inside packed; we had to go outside. It wasn't too hot yet but we did have to move our table out of the sun. Bonus: There is a pretty view of the lake. There's also a ping-pong table out there.

People kept having a hard time getting out to the patio and then back in to get their food because there's only one door that's unlocked so you can move in and out. There were supposed to be two but the second one kept getting re-locked. Some servers came over to prop it open finally but that lets out their air conditioning ...

Our food was good. I would say Burger Fi serves up a better all-around burger and Burger 21 does better shakes. But Shake Shack would be good for a quick bite if you're in the area. The burgers were pretty standard, tasty, on a soft bun and with "shack sauce," which appeared to be something like ketchup, mayo, and chopped pickles. Our shakes were disappointing. If I didn't know mine was peanut butter and his was caramel, I'd think we both got vanilla. Maybe the frozen custard base flavor is just overwhelming, but I didn't find the shakes to be worth the calories for me personally. Again, I'd rather have a Burger 21 shake, which is much more flavorful. The fries were good: They're crinkle-cut, which is a rarity at burger places, and they were hot and fluffy. Nothing out of this world, but they were good alongside the burger.

Our food was nearly $25. Would I go again? Probably not any time soon, but if I'm nearby and hungry, I'd definitely get a burger and fries again. I don't think I'll bother with another shake. Maybe I'll try one of their concretes instead--they have a rotating menu of daily flavors that they told me changes every month, and there were some good ones.

By the way, if you have dogs with you, you could sit on the porch and get them some dog biscuits or the Pooch-ini, which has dog biscuits, peanut butter sauce, and custard. Cute!

Oh yeah, there's only one bathroom for each gender as other reviews have said. If you're waiting for the bathroom, you have to stand in a small hallway where cooking staff often need to walk down, or you end up going into the dining area as overflow. Terrible idea to only have two bathrooms totals! Also, come here early if you want some food and to be able to get parking!

This place was mediocre.  It's a Mexican inspired restaurant, not authentic.  Not sure what the tikka tacos were about, they were odd.  My salad of shrimp and avocado was delicious.  A dining partner liked the fish tacos.  You can't order tacos ala carte, or at least, their menu doesn't offer this.  An order of tacos is exactly two tacos.  They don't serve Horchata, and our server said it's not customary in Boston.  The table side tomato salsa was good not great.  This visit made me miss the better authentic Mexican eateries in Chicago.  The service was friendly, the restroom was clean, the sunny second floor was lovely and the real estate is nice.

I joined a business associate at Little Bird for and after dinner cocktail and snack.  After being seated and looking at the menu, we decided to stay for dinner. 

Overall, I'd give the food kudos, however, I was not blown away.
Highlights were the fried beef tongue and the charcuterie plate. Low points were the coq au vin (sauce was inordinately smoky... from the lardons?), the too brown crepe with gruyere, and the overly burnt orange rind in my friend's cocktail.

But the biggest disappointments of the night were the desserts.  I was very excited to try some of Lauren Fortgang's creations, but both items were uninspired and inordinately sweet. We had the coconut cake and the hazelnut financier. The sorbet and ice cream quenelles that garnished our desserts were lovely, but the cakes themselves were awful.

The high point of the night was the service.  Attentive (although sometimes exceedingly so), friendly, and unpretentious. I'd go back just to chat with the bartender again and to enjoy the atmosphere.

I'll return, as perhaps it was an off night in the kitchen. Little Bird has the potential to be amazing!!

I have a hard time rating this place. I feel like they should do a better job communicating how the wait list works. Apparently, this place takes no reservation but can put you on the wait list which was suppose to help with the wait time. Not sure if it really did b/c this didn't go active until we got there for which they told us we had a wait time of 1hr and half. I felt like we got there at a reasonably early time but it took forever to find parking.  I would suggest dropping someone off if you can't find parking quickly so that you can at least check in and start your wait. 

This place is apparently known for its Bloody Mary's which I can't speak much about since I don't like bloody Mary's but what I can say is it was spicy.  The white sangria was good and sweet.  As for my entree I got the carrot cake French toast which was good but it can get overly sweet after a while. My friends seem to have enjoyed their food. I think the tacos had a spicy kick to them from the rice and beans that I tried.

This place does not have much waiting space which is a con b/c we had no where to move as people, waiter/waitresses were trying to pass by or leave. But I guess they don't expect people to wait around since they text you when your table will be ready.   But what if the weather wasn't great out.

The food and prices are very good! Convenient 24 hours, easily accessible from Portland. Brian was especially amazing. He is very customer friendly and business savvy. I can see him managing or hosting any restaurant with great success. 

The only 3 stars because the cook was arguing with Brian in earshot of the customers. Although Brian did give us our meal on the house, customers shouldn't be subjected to the "business".  Too much negative energy. Manager needs to give Brian more authority and boost morale. 

The food, prices, and location are all reasonable and no reason that place shouldn't be packed out every night!

I've been coming here for years. It's close to work, and it's cheap -- for $9, you get all the pizza and salad you can eat, and all the refills on soda or tea you can drink.

I used to call it "Dirty Daves" because, as with a lot of buffet places, the plate and utensil cleaning was spotty at best. I still get the occasional unidentifiable crusty thing on a fork or knife, but it is what it is -- a pizza buffet.

You know what you are getting at a place like this -- dodgy lettuce, miscellaneous veggies of questionable freshness, pepperoni rolls that range from all dough to a perfect ratio of dough to pepperoni. Greasy pizza and cheese sticks. Nothing surprising, nothing culinary adventurous. You can't knock a pizza buffet place for being a pizza buffet place.

For me, this is not a destination place other than an infrequent lunch spot when I feel the need to carbo-load. When I eat here and I walk out full, it isn't because I just had good pizza, it's because I wanted carbs.

You know Gatti's -- good salad bar, bad pizza. DD's is the opposite -- bad salad bar, adequate pizza. Not the best pizza, not the worst pizza. Again, it is what it is, nothing more, nothing less.

I almost made this a 2-star review but truth be told, I DO keep coming back, and barely-adequate lunchtime buffet pizza is still better than no pizza at all.

This newish sandwich place is alright.  The theme of 'fresh healthiness' that a place like Darwin's brings to the table is matched at All-Star...but replace fresh healthiness with 'greasy heaviness'...

...which isn't necessarily a bad thing.  You just need to be in the mood for it, which fortunately I was when I went.  My man and I stopped by for take out on a chilly weekend.  Service was quick and friendly.  Lots of choices-- we went with the "Gobbler", a huge concoction of turkey, stuffing, sausage and citrus relish, and the grilled cheese special, which was Monterey jack with guac on sourdough.  We split both sandwiches and they were really yummy, if a bit greasy, and very filling.  Prices are a bit high, but you get a whole lotta sandwich for your buck. 

I can't say I'll definitely be back, but the "Funky" sandwich special (yes, that's a category) on the day we were there was a grilled cream cheese and banana guava jam sandwich...which really really intrigued me....hmmmm....

I'ma check out your Box! 

I had the eggplant muffuleta with a side salad that I was upsold on. The staff were super friendly and I didn't have to wait very long to get my grub (which is nice considering you wait for half an hour or so before your food is up at some of the other food carts). Unfortunately I forgot to grab a fork and napkins before heading back to work so I had to make a detour.

The eggplant burger tasted pretty good, but it was a bit heavy for me. Not sure if this was due to the oil in the fryer (since the eggplant is deep-fried) or if its just my old age catching up with me. It's a good thing I opted for the side salad and not the fries in the end. The salad was great, it had cranberries, almonds and balsamic dressing, which happen to be my favourite things. 

$11.50 for lunch is a bit pricey, but I would still like to try their veggie burger and their poutine since its made with mushroom gravy and not meatyness, so I'll give this Box another go in the future.

Came here for Sunday brunch at noon and immediately loved the decor of the restaurant BUT it was empty (well a few tables were occupied).

The bloody Mary was excellent, good amount of horseradish but the food was disappointing. 
Blueberry muffin (best thing we had) was served whole, toasted sugar muffin top and butter on the side.  
Huevos Rancheros- Not bad, fried tortilla became very soggy under the mass of carnitas, could have used more egg (it is brunch).
Home fries- sweet tomato dipping sauce which was a nice surprise, fried crispy outside but lacked any flavor.  (maybe I'm expecting too much from a potato).
House smoked bacon- who doesn't like bacon?

Difficult to find a place where to eat when it's 10 pm, but in Nix's Mate it is possible! 
There is even a doorman to open you, the senior form! 
Beer, cocktails, screens, local food, everything is there. The bowl of (clams) chowder was the delicious good but with many of the other things that clams, and the steak of the burger was burned, of what to be a little left unsatisfied, but at the present time there we had no more too much the choice

My favorite reason for visiting Folks Kitchen is their affordable 3- course meals. 
Kids eat free on Tuesday, with the purchase of adult meal.
Folks Kitchen 3- course meal comes with a starter, entrée and dessert at a affordable price.
They have the best turkey and dressing and their fried catfish and chicken is out of this world.
The dinning room tables and floors could use a mop and bleach cloth every morning before they open and the women restroom as well.

My 1st visit at this one but i'm impressed and the food was great.I ordered the Turkey patty with cheese and egg on a onion bagel.She brought it out to me and was worried because it was well toasted that I would want another one,but that's how I cook them at home so no worry there sweetness. Place was clean and all you can smell are bagels.Staff is friendly and they seam to work well together,which is always a plus to me when I notice this in a place of business.When back in this part of Atlanta,I will stop by as you should too.

I'll start with the positives. I love the grand ballroom space with huge windows overlooking the water. The "check-in" counter upstairs with Italian stewardesses that guide you down to the main dining room themed to a retro airport terminal sets a promising start.

I also had great service. We were there at 5:30pm on weeknight, and there was more wait staff than actual guests so I know that helped, but after reading a few reviews of slow service that was definitely not the case. 

We ordered a glass of pinot grigio and the "summer" sangria that was the the lovechild of a sangria and a pina colada. Nice. Bread came, along with olive oil poured on the bread plates. Ok. The bread was a bit stale, but I'm not going to look gift dough in the mouth. 

Our first course was arancini, and it was great. Cripsy on the outside, moist on the inside. The pricing -- $14 for two golf ball-sized fried risotto balls -- seemed extreme, but on to the next course.

My wife ordered the spaghetti with meatballs. I went with chicken parm. Both were surprisingly ho-hum. The chicken parm comes with no accompaniments. I thought I had read that it came served with a side of penne, but I later discovered that I was eyeing the brunch menu online where it's served that way. I was surprised that the waiter didn't ask if I wanted a pasta side, since just eating chicken parm -- $29 chicken parm, at that -- by itself seems incomplete. My wife passed over some of the spaghetti -- thicker than usual noodles cooked al dente -- and it was fine, but both entrees were closer to Olive Garden quality than the high-end Italian joints that this place aspires to be. 

The brunch menu seems far more interesting/inviting, and maybe we'll check that out in the future. However, for an actual lunch or dinner meal there are at least six other places I'd rather go in Disney Springs, and if I'm craving Italian on property this is no Il Mulino.

I'm a first time customer with Bark Blowers and had about 2 cubic yards of aged hemlock blown in.  The price and quality was top notch but the customer service was sub-par.  

There is a narrow strip running around my yard that I chose to omit after speaking with the techs.  Mistake.  I called back the next day hoping that this could be fixed for a small fee but was told I would need to pay the minimum 0.5 yard price.  Understandable but disappointing nonetheless.

Make sure you get it right the first time.  You won't be given any favorable treatment once they're out the door.

Seeing Viet-Cajun instantly intrigued me. I wondered what kind of wild combinations I would find at this restaurant! I came during Portland Dining Month and was able to try one of everything that was listed on the menu. Overall, I was underwhelmed. 

The ambiance was cute but the food was nothing special. I think I liked the crawfish etouffee nachos the best, but how can you mess up nachos? 

The pork belly was tender but more on the salty side. The grits were rich and the steak was cooked perfectly.

Their Korean fried chicken is amazing! I didn't expect much when I first got it (esp since it's a poke restaurant), but I honestly think their chicken is better than their poke.

Their poke bows are just ok. I got spicy tuna thinking it would be just regular tuna with some spicy sauce but they used tuna paste which didn't taste good at all. It was also really spicy so make sure not to get that one if you can't eat spicy!

This is a great place to enjoy some delicious pho or for those of you who don't know, that means "Vietnamese noodle soup". It has a fairly large environment so lots of space and you can take out food quickly if you're interested.

The service and food quality is moderate and the environment is fairly peaceful and relaxed. I sat down with a friend and colleague for some carrot and beef noodle stew which was fairly tasty and they did bring us some extra veggies and lime to go with it. They were fairly quick at first but then forgot about us for about 30 minutes so I was a little disappointed with the service. They were very friendly however and accommodating and the food was very tasty and exceptional portions for the price.

I went here for the first time last night. It's a cozy little Irish pub and I would definitely come back (and try the food) but my friend and I had an interesting experience with the most apathetic bartender I've ever encountered. 

 First, this bartender was attentive throughout the night, that wasn't the issue. 

 But when we first ordered drinks, my friend got a black velvet and I got a jack d'or. 

 When the bartender brought them, she went to give us each the opposite drink, and we just laughed but corrected her and she apologized (not a big deal in any way, but relevant to the story). 

 So a little while later my friend has ordered another beer and then I order another beer. The bartender brings me a black velvet (what my friend ordered the first time) and I look over and realize that when she served my friend her second drink she'd given her a Jack D'or (my first drink). My friend likes both so hadn't said anything, but we (in visible sight of the waitress) switched drinks so we could each have the beer we actually wanted/ordered. 

 Finally it gets hilarious, because when we ordered a third round, the bartender just brought us two black velvets. What? At no time in the night did we order the same drink. It was like she'd forgotten whatever the other beer was we'd at some point ordered and so just brought two of the one she knew someone was drinking. 

 Anyway no harm done, it's St. Paddy's Day Weekend and we should all drink a little Guiness I suppose.

First off, the decor is not to my taste for a tea house. The stark, modern, all light color felt cold. Plus the blank, concrete walls echo people's voices all over the place. I was trying to have a private conversation and the two other couples in the shop were talking in normal volume, yet it was so loud in there you'd think it was packed. 
On to the tea. The menu is not very informative. Only the recommended tea lattes have ingredients listed. This meant my diabetic companion had to ask what was sugar free. The counter person didn't really know how to lead us through sugar free options. We had to ask about each item my friend was interested in. I know that many of the lattes here are premixed (something I do not care for) and therefore can't be made sugar free. At least the coconut milk and almond milk was unsweetened. I got the cardamom chia latte. It was nicely spiced but a too sweet for my taste. My companion got a London Fog latte with coconut milk. It tasted more of lavender than Earl Gray. He only finished half of it. 
At 6:30pm, the worker started putting everything away in preparation for closing. She even cleared away the water, napkins, pastries, and stir-ins well before 7pm, meaning the people who walked in about 20 minutes to closing weren't able to access these things. Ten minutes to closing she had brought in the outside sign, tables, and chairs. I've worked service management before, for years. I understand doing pre-closing but a half hour before closing to remove the water, stir-ins, and pastry case just tells your clientele "Get out" and "I'm not interested in serving you." 
Overall, it wasn't horrible but it wasn't great either. I have a meeting set there this weekend and I really wish Townshend's on Alberta was open from its remodel. I'd rather go there.

I had a great dinner at Sushi Lola. Friends have recommended it forever but I don't like sushi so I never went. My boo loves sushi so we decided to try it. I love Korean bool gogi so I decided to try it at sushi Lola's. Pretty dang good and a large portion! 

The restaurant was busy but we didn't have a wait. Almost every table was taken and they're quite close together so that's semi unpleasant to be sitting as close to the next table as if they were part of your own party. 

I don't recall what my boo thought of her sushi but she hasn't been requesting to return. I'd go back if she felt like going again.

I was going to give them 4 star, but I changed my mind to give a 3 instead. For two reasons- 1. I think their sushi is a little overpriced for its quantity. 2. My bill was being wrongly charged when the transaction was posted on my bank account. 

I had legend roll and uni (sea urchin) sushi. Legend roll was delicious, but only had 8 relatively small pieces. Sea urchin was $8 for two pieces. Friends had different orders from and they liked their orders. But same issue-quantity was on the low end. In terms of tastes, their sushi was low key good. They were delicious. However, I usually assess restaurants in a combination of factors, not just food tastes. Overall, the ambience was casual and service was decent. I was just very turned down by dishonest behaviors, though I am not sure whether it's the issue of the restaurant or the waiter/waitress.

OK, so they're GOOD donuts, but they're not the best I had in Portland, so what's the big deal?  Good decorating?

I got the Memphis Mafia and the Ain't That A Peach, both of which were fritters and HUGE.  And they were good!  But they weren't great.  I have had truly great donuts, and Voodoo donuts didn't live up to them.

The line thing - whatever.  I went as a tourist and considered it a Portland experience.  It was kind of fun.  I'm amused by sparkly things, so I had fun looking at the glitter-sprayed exterior brick wall, and also status-ing about the grump in back of me who was grumping to his girlfriend about waiting in line and it's stupid and blah blah blah.  It's a Portland thing, man!  Deal for your girlfriend!

Anyway, I also have to note that the prices are pretty high - I payed $4-ish each for two gigantic fritters; I'm not going to complain, but I did the Voodoo Doughnuts thing and I wouldn't go back again.

Wow.  Another tex-mex restaurant chain in Austin.  Hey, guess what!  They serve enchiladas, tacos and burritos with fresh tortillas and homemade salsa!  In fact, this is the first Texas expansion of a Colorado tex-mex chain.  COLORADO?  In Austin?  Come on people, can't we do this bit on our own?

It's not that Rio Grande is bad, or anything.  For those too young to know better, you might even be excited by the fact that it's housed in the warehouse that was used as the 'urban villa' housing that cast of crazies you loved the 'The Real World -- Austin.'  TRGMR is alright.  But that's all I can give it.

I loved how cozy and welcoming this small ramen shop was! We were warmly greeted by the server, immediately offered the menus, and were served delicious bowls of ramen very quickly. We tried the cold ramen (which was the summer special) and got a miso ramen. 

The server had offered to make the cold ramen a little softer, but I was scared that it would be too soft so I politely declined. However, I certainly will take that offer up next time to make it a little softer than the usual. 

The miso ramen noodles were perfectly cooked, but I wish there were a little more ingredients in the bowl as it only came with corn and bean sprouts (wish there were seaweed bits/bamboo/half an egg). I also read up on the advice of a few others and added the garlic paste to my ramen, which helped spice it up a little.

I enjoyed this ramen shop and loved how much more affordable it was in comparison to Jinya on the other side of metro! There was also a cool history behind this ramen shop as this is their third location to have opened up, and the first two locations are all in Japan! Certainly will come back if in the area again :)

Friendly staff, great free tasting. 

However, we feel mislead-- the implication was that all of the spirits were made in-house. After we purchased the $30+ bottle of Temperance Trader Bourbon, we flew home to realize that right there the back label states "Distilled in Tennessee & BOTTLED in Portland, OR."  It also doesn't state who distilled it-- how do we know that it's not just un-filtered Jack Daniels etc.?

The website says they are making an in-house distilled OR whiskey to be released in 2015, but there was no mention of that in person. 

Also disappointing; the flavor was significantly less smooth than what we had tasted. I  guess that's the risk with purchasing single-barrel whiskey.

3 stars for being a fun spot; just read the back label before purchasing!

The ladies here are really nice, and they were more than happy to make an appointment for me when I walked in.  

My only cons are that she did cut me on the whole length of my pinky cuticle with the drill bit file thing and it hurt, but I didn't want to make her feel too bad so I didn't say too much.  Now that I'm out of the salon and its scabbing over I can see it's kinda deep actually.  

My second con is that she didn't compare the nails on each hand to eachother to make sure they were filed the same way, every person that has done my nails before has done that.  She did a good job, except for my thumb nails are way different lengths and are glued on in way different spots down the nail. I may have to go get it fixed somewhere.

Overall nice ladies, clean, and a convenient location.

I wasn't that impressed with 33 during Restaurant Week 2008. The $14 cocktail was weak in proof and flavor as well, consisting mainly of soda water. It wasn't good enough to make me want another and it was just enough to make me sleepy. The salad was average, the $9 upgrade "Faux Tenderloin" itself was good but the sides were lukewarm to cold. The $4 upgrade desert tasted very out-of-box and the ice cream with it was grainy.

Others at the table had mixed reviews as well. One found the steak delightful with the addition of shaved black truffle at least. Another found the Oysters ($9 upgrade) absolutely inedible and in fact could not even swallow a mouthful. Seeing her turn green across the table was QUITE alarming. Yet another had a delightful cut of tasty salmon with a delicious  vanilla custard(?) type dessert.

Conclusion: 3 stars is not worth 5 $'s IMO. One would expect for that kind of money for there not to be burnt out bulbs and cracked mirrors in the place at least if not superb food. I'll pass on this place in the future.

After finally clarifying what exactly differentiated Hannah Montana from Miley Cyrus, my 6 year old cousin steered our post Thanksgiving Dinner conversation to Disney princesses:

"Which one do you like?" she asked. 

"Aurora from Sleeping Beauty" I replied. Easily my choice for as long as I can remember, heck my prom dress was the same sweet, soft, sleepy blue.  And although my cousin argued that the Little Mermaid was far superior, we agreed that in both cases their entourage and accessories definitely helped make them the characters they were.  

But of course this is the case with many young ladies.  So many stores push the little pieces that complete the look they are selling, and at Urban Outfitters it becomes an adventure to track them down.  Hidden around displays and near registers, sometimes it feels like you're cutting through a hipster forest to get to the little things that are actually worth picking up here. 

One such day found me standing in front of a table of fall scarves.  I was having one of those "Hmm... do I really want this?" moments, and my sister walked over:

"Which one do you like?" she asked.

I pointed out a pretty plaid merlot and after some deliberation decided that I could spring for it.  At $20, it was a little on the expensive side, but I'm a major sucker for winter accessories and this was exactly my kind of weakness. Though I almost left without it, as the challenge of finding someone from whom I could actually buy the thing proved a little much... Be wary of the folks who inhabit this place, sometime they are as sweet as fluttery fairies, pointing you in the right direction.  Other times very unresponsive, as if put under some sort of magical sleeping spell.   

Though generally speaking, there's a significantly lower percentage of witchy mistresses of evil that turn into fire breathing dragons.

So they've got that going for them.

This is definitely NOT a wonder-world, clean, organized, discount store, in the middle of downtown Waltham on Moody Street. This is more like the pits of Moody Street. 
That being said, if the deals weren't like they are, the location is great (right in the center of Waltham), and the staff are friendly and kind.
For the store, it wasn't clean, what-so-ever, yet had everything I needed and was a fine stop, with great prices and a good stock of everything you could need. Perfect for convenience, and they are most likely guaranteed to have what you need. Overall, it's ok. 3 stars.

Drive thru grabbed pork chili verde burrito and grande nachos for the wife. Burrito was very good but meat was very limited. The nachos were brutal and for 5.95 I expect more. When u pay that much you would expect toppings but 75% was chips the rest was sour cream and some meat olives and jalapeños. We are meat eaters and one of the perks about Mexican food is the meat. This place really is rationing the meat and not sure why. It would knock it out of the park if they would actually give us what we pay for. Love the salsa I got on the side I just wish when u order a burrito it was what it should be and nachos are actually nachos!

Ive had two haircuts here. The first i was extremely pleased. The second not so much. I ask for a master stylist i cant remember her name she was very quiet, anyways she did a good job. But my hair felt very heavy so she said they can texturize to lose the weight...so her teacher comes along to do the job. Beware its the older lady with short black hair. So she seemed to be in a crabby mood when i got there, was pretty rough and bumped my head a few times and did not appologise. Then she texturized she was very rough felt like she was hacking random chunks of hair off. While she was doing this she wasnt looking at my hair and talking to other people. So end result was stringy uneven and dissapointing. Dont let that lady touch your hair. Ive had my hair texturized before by a male teacher and he was gentle and took his time and made sure it was even and perfect. So i guess that one lady doesnt give a shit. Also my friend went in there said that same lady was in a pretty bitchy mood again. Ha.

It's all about the s'mores mocha! However, we we received the latte, there was no more latte art :( The toasted marshmallow was floating right in the center where the latte would be. The presentation just wasn't the same when you get it to go. Although this is a very different drink, I'm not sure that it justified the $8 price point. 

I also ordered an Americano with a single origin bean from Kenya, and it tasted a bit burnt. Not sure if the barista that day was new or inexperienced, since we did go during the holidays in the middle of a pandemic. I might give them another shot once they're serving more types of brews such as chemex, pour over, etc.

Great beer selection and atmosphere, hampered by the suckiest service.

FOOD
None, but you are welcome to bring your own. Falafels and Kibbeh from the Pita Hut next door is a great fav of mine. The beer selection is very good indeed.

SERVICE
Could not be worse if they tried. Stay away, stay far away. And it really pains me to say this because I live a 10 min walk away and really want nothing more than to come here often.

ATMOSPHERE
I love it - hip neighbourhood pub with a healthy mix of Ohio.

I'm kind of mixed on this place. 

Ordered a salad which was AWESOME and half a sandwich. I asked for no onion or sprouts on the sandwich & when it came out... you guessed it... had onions & sprouts. I sent it back and they quickly made me a new one. BUT after I took a bite and tasted onion, I lifted the bread and saw a few sprouts they forgot to "pick off" - yuck. They are lucky I just don't like onions & sprouts... what if I were allergic?!

Very similar to Starliner (LouiE's is run by two brothers from the same family that runs Starliner), but something in the Starliner magic was lost in the attempt to upscale the fare. The food isn't bad, but there's always something that it seems to be missing with the slightly higher prices. It's not a bad place, and if Starliner wasn't there I'd probably be over the moon for it, but I can't help but wonder if they'd be better if they were a bit farther away from their sister restaurant.

I came here because I had driven by their "It Could Always be Wurst" sign many times and decided to look it up. Once I found out they have specialty hot dogs, I absolutely had to give it a try. Unfortunately, the aesthetically pleasing decor and the good service were the highlights of this stop. The dog and the fries were just okay. I struggled with rating this 3 or 4 stars, but the 3 stars is listed as "a-ok" and that is exactly how I felt.

If you're looking for an easy after works spot to grab a drink before catching the train or T at South Station Trade is a great location. The inside is beautiful with lots of large windows and a good amount of space. 

The food is always solid but I found that the portions and menu have changed often over the years so I never know what they will have. It's also a little pricy for what the food is and the service was a bit slow.

I first came here when they just opened wasn't a fan but I gave it another shot since its 10 min walk from home and they've improved quite a bit so if your looking for a local spot to chill and listen to some Korean pop then this might be a place for you! 

Try the popcorn chicken! Spicy but goood! 

Drinks are ok though..........

I wish they would just do away with the cell phone area and make more space for the vivi customers but hey just a suggestion. 


Price, 
depends on what your getting since some can be a bit pricey. 

Parking, 
plenty of side streets and main street parking is avail without meters

It is really funny how when I asked for two donuts and proceeded to pay, the prompt on the screen asked how much gratuity I would like to add with the options of 15% and up. They do have an option for no tip FYI. Pretty sad that they ask for gratuity when the only customer service they provide is grab a donut from a shelve and box it, or pour coffee in a cup for ya. They don't serve tables or take your stuff to your tables. Aside from that, quality of donut is good. I would recommend if you're ok with spending $5 on a donuts plus another dollar for gratuity.

I had a business lunch at Madrid today (or, as I like to call it, "the old Wendy's").  The service was very attentive and good.  The atmosphere was also nice (not much changed from Barrio days).

I ordered the fish tacos.  While very tasty, it certainly was not enough to fill me up.  My one complaint (which I knew about going in) is that the "tacos" actually come on deep-fried won-tons (flat, not in a "U shape" taco form).  This factoid does not appear on the menu.  Madrid does offer shrimp tacos on soft shells . . . so, here's an idea - give me the option of ordering the soft shells on my fish tacos!

The "fish mixture" on top of the won-ton consisted of the fish, some jicama mint slaw, candied jalepenos and salsa.  Did I say fish?  Oh yeah, you kind of had to dig for it to find the protein (cut up in small pieces and not a lot of it).  My friend had the shrimp tacos and appeared to enjoy more protein than I did.

The prices aren't bad, but the taco portions are small.  Acceptable food for lunch in downtown Columbus, but nothing spectacular to draw me back repeatedly.  Larger portions and more fish on the fish tacos (two birds with one stone really) may have made me a repeat customer.

Came her a few weeks ago with a couple of colleagues at around 9 pm or so on a Friday. The place was extremely packed and so we had to pretty much stand around close to the bar area though not really at the bar while waiting for a seat. We were offered to put our names down on a waiting list so that we could be seated. 

They have a very wide range of drink selections particularly in their beers. I tried a spicy like beer that was pretty good but I wouldn't have been able to finish it all by myself as the flavor was too strong and a bit overpowering. We had to wait a while for  the bar tender to take our orders despite it being apparent that we a bunch of us were ready to order. 

Additionally, there was a table that was emptied out and we shimmied on over since no one had been seated and we were tired of standing with our drinks in hand. We were told that the table was being reserved and that was fine so we went back to our circle next ish to the bar. When I left a bit afterwards they still had not sat anyone down there which was a bit frustrating.

Either way, it's a pretty decent place to grab a drink but I wouldn't really recommend to a group unless you've made reservations or something beforehand - especially on peak times. Also when ordering at the bar just be patient.

Rating this on an "airport survival " curve it gets 3 stars. Outside of the airport it would get one star. I like P. F. Chamg's consistency of quality in locations from Sarasota to Salt Lake City. So what could possibly go wrong??
Maybe it is just an issue with what I ordered (pad Thai - a foolish choice in retrospect) , but it was highly spiced with Southern spices (peppery) and had only a passing resemblance in flavor to the real dish.  A few tiny peanuts (can't they come up with peanuts in Georgia!!) Large portion, but I had no interest in eating more than needed to survive the layover. 
Noisy and crowded, but I accept that for an airport eatery. Plates plunked down on table in flyby service - well, then why suggest tips ranging up to 22% on the checks?
Maybe I should have just gotten Starbucks and roughed it out till my final destination. ATL is not an airport with good options. Give me Legal Seafood in Boston, or Carrabas in Tampa, etc. Etc. Etc.

The 1927 S'mores Company is located where Chizu used to be, next to the Multnomah Whiskey Library. It's a small shop, decorated to make you feel like you're in a cozy cabin. There's only three stools at the counter, where you can stare outside and watch the people waiting around for MWL next door, but it's not really a place where you linger and savor your s'mores. You might need to eat standing up or walk out with it. 

I ordered the porter s'more. It was good - I liked the shortbread crackers around the house made marshmallow but I didn't really taste a difference between my order and my friend's. While the marshmallow was good, it wasn't really warmed up much - just toasted on the outside a little but the texture was still a firm marshmallow. The s'more was pretty good, but it didn't feel revelatory. It was still just a s'more at the end of the day and the novelty was gone after the first visit. It's a pricey place ($5-6) for a s'more and I'm not sure that it's that much better than a normal one, aside from the cracker. Maybe if they sold the shortbread crackers too, like in a bag to go, I might go back but otherwise I don't see a repeat visit in the future.

A little trip down memory lane:

Remember the original Mc & Schmick's? $2 happy hour, downtown PDX.?  Ahh, the food was fantastic, even for HH.   Dinners were top notch and it was a great Portland destination.  Ok, I am showing my age a bit as well as remembering via grandparents comments 20++ years back.

Well, M&S grill is an off-shoot of the original but don't be fooled pretty one's.............. it's not the same.  Nor is the original!!!  As soon as they became chain-ised (aka incorporated) their food quality took a big FAT dive.  Now, while it's less chain-like than those horrible other places in Bridgeport, it's still looking for a large file to escape it's prison.  I don't think there's any saving this place.  

Food: lunch is better than dinner and far more affordable.  Their menu is too large, so they can't possibly have 50 amazing dishes (this is a big obvious button for me).  Fish is fresh (just make sure you order "fresh").  
And the Brit likes the fish & chips gives it the "ok".  Plus lot of micro-brews on tap to wash it down.  Wine list is over-priced and I stick with cocktails here. 

Service can be patchy, but usually efficient and experienced.  I love seafood, but cookie cutter places are the norm-this one is just a cut above that.  For goodness sakes, we live 1 hour from the Pacific OCEAN!  I expect better.   Sorry you went corporate MS.

I checked this place out with some coworkers on a Tuesday night. 

No food yet, which was a bit of a disappointment since we were coming for happy hour and wanted some snacks to gnosh on. But they just opened so they're probably getting their food and kitchen in order! Or I wonder if the "Outdoor Kitchen" reference on their website means they'll only have food at certain events? 

No happy hour specials, despite the Yelp listing saying they have one. We ordered a few cocktails, which were normal prices for Austin (between $8-12 each). Cute renditions of popular cocktails, such as the Kitty Spritz (wine spritzer) and the Dr. Zhivago (similar to a moscow mule).

Cool mid-century modern decor. Flamingo wallpaper in the women's bathroom! There were some people wading in the pool while we were there, and they kept walking in and out of the bar area in suits and towels. A bit odd for a cocktail bar, but I guess Miami trashy is the vibe they're going for. Perhaps they'll open an outdoor bar soon, or on more crowded occasions?

I go to other BSC locations: usually Wellington and Woburn.  This review is for BSC South Station.

Let's do some Rating Math.  Starting at zero, they get:

(+ 2) Two stars for being right next door to my office and for friendly staff.  

(+ 3) Three stars for some pretty great instructors.  Love the Tuesday 1:15 and Wednesday 12:15 spin classes.  (I'm so bad with names. Sorry.)  But BSC spin instructors in general are good.  When I joined BSC, I'd been spinning for a couple of years at another gym.  I didn't realize how easy I'd had it.  My first few spin classes at a BSC were a wake-up call!  These guys know how to make you work AND they are very good at describing what your body should be feeling in terms of perceived exertion and what muscles should be working.  Makes for a great workout.  I've learned a lot and I'm in better shape.  

However: 

(-2) Minus two stars for a less-than-ideal spin studio.  It is small. Fine, ok -- it's downtown Boston, space is at a premium.  I can do small.  BUT.  The bikes are so often broken.  If you get to class early enough and can test the bikes, you're fine.  (But if you can get to class 10 minutes early in the middle of a work day or right after work, I want your job.)  If you can't, you might end up on a bike with a wonky pedal or worse. That gets in the way of a good workout.  

They typically do not overbook their classes.  That is: they seem to account for the broken bikes when letting (or not letting) people sign up.  But still.  I'm not giving back a point for that when they could just fix the bikes.

Many people first became familiar with 21 Nickels when Rob Courdry from the Jon Stewart Show did some interviews here. It's a great little pub, off the beaten path in Watertown. You probably wouldn't even know it was there unless you were a native or someone took you there.  Finally after living in the area for a couple of years we stopped in.

Part bar with a cool greenouse roof/part train car, this little pub has a lot of atmosphere and decent food. Good beer on tap and a large selection of bottled beer as well. A full bar compliments the tasty sandwiches and low-cost entrees. The honey mustard chicken sandwich is VERY good and messy. The mashed potatoes would have been excellent if they weren't cold, however. 

Will definitely be going back here more often to sample more and to soak up the atmosphere. Great place to hang with friends, I imagine or to watch a game on the many flat screen TVs.

Revolution donuts is a famous donut and coffee spot in Decatur. I love donuts but it feels a little overrated in my opinion. 

We had the chocolate cake, apple fritter, cinnamon sugar, and pistachio donut. The chocolate one was disappointing, I love chocolate donuts but this one did not make the cut. The apple fitter was delicious and sweet, you can't really mess up an apple fitter. Glad they didn't. The pistachio one also had orange flavor too. It was very sweet and the orange flavor over powered the pistachio. I liked the plain cinnamon sugar donut but wouldn't say anything special. The sprinkles and bacon one are famous but we don't eat meat so we didn't try it. 

Personally I like sublime donuts more and will be using my calories there. 

Revolution donuts is a welcoming cool shop with plenty of parking and people go crazy for this place. You can find me at Sublime donuts instead.

The ambience and atmosphere is VERY suave. Love the look and the vibe.. Those will probably be my only good points.. We got seated immediately for a party of 8. We were celebrating a a birthday dinner for my associate and it went completely downhill from there. The waiter was nice but did not seem to be up to par on his "duties".  The drinks were ordered however it took about 45 mins to get everyone situated and then he started to take the dinner order. The burgers came out separately than the fries (which were soggy but the Chef came out, apologized, offered fresh ones) and the service just got worse.  I have hope that this place will shape up but I don't think I will be revisiting this particular spot for a LONG time. "First impression is everything!"

I came here once before several years ago but I don't remember much of the visit. I got invited last night and decided to give it a go again. I left with mixed feelings.

The food was excellent! I absolutely have nothing negative to say about the food. Everything came out delicious and fresh. We got the calamari for an appetizer and it was great. The salad and cheese bread came out next and they were delicious as well! While waiting for our main courses, a manager came over with a sample of their ahi tuna nachos. I'm not much of a tuna fan, but I gave it a try and loved it. It was spicy and crunchy; the fish definitely tasted fresh.

I ordered the prime rib which was probably one of the best I've ever had. It was cooked perfectly and just melted in your mouth. The garlic whipped potatoes were delicious. I ended up ordering a side to go for my left overs (which I had a lot of!). I appreciated that the prime rib was anti-biotic and hormone free, it's one of the reasons I ordered it. Lastly, we finished off the meal with the chocolate grand marnier cake and it was out of this world. First off, the slice of cake was huge. Between three people we barely made a dent. The cake itself was rich and moist. The orange flavor really came through and mixed well with the chocolate.

The downfall was the service. Our server was friendly and pleasant; he was knowledgeable regarding the menu so all of that was good and well. It was just at times he was pretty nonexistent. Now I'm not a huge fan of an overly attentive server, I like my meal time peace!  But it took too long for refills, waiting for our check took over 30 minutes and when he was there he seemed rushed. We were seated at a booth tucked away all the way back of the restaurant and it seemed like he was serving the opposite side so maybe management just needs to better evaluate the flow of service. 

Like I said, the food was excellent and the place is beautiful. Our server was friendly, but it seemed like he had too much going on. I'd definitely return, but not anytime in the near future.

First time here. Been wanting to try out their breakfast for a while now. (Warning: pricing is different than what is listed on the website!)

Was seated right away. Great. Ordered a breakfast burrito and enchiladas. Server asked if we wanted red, green or Christmas chili. I asked which one was more spicy. Green was. Friend opted for red chili and I did the same, but asked for a side of green chili to taste. At the end of the bill we were charged $3 for a side of chili. First of all, we were NOT informed that there was additional charge for getting two chili. Since "Christmas" was offered, I figured there was no additional charge. Brought it up to my server's attention.

For those who are first timer- she suggested you say: I want CHRISTMAS, but have the green chili on the side. I did not know you have to say those "key words". Seriously? Would have been nice if you spent 30 seconds to explain to us our options, then we wouldn't have had this awkward conversation. Went on to explaining the chili is imported from New Mexico, spendy, that's why they charge extra, etc, etc., so specific lingo is important. Anyways, she took cared of charge for us. But another reason why they did not receive full stars on our books was that we were NOT informed they had a daily special nor unlimited mimosas on weekends. We only overhead this conversation through another server who sat a couple next to us (this happened AFTER we placed our order). Uhm.. what? THERE WAS A DAILY SPECIAL? What did I missed out? wow. just wow. Btw, my friend didn't even receive any water. He ordered horchata with his meal and that's all he got. Would have been nice to have a glass of water with his meal too. 

Anyways, food wise 5 stars!. We love both our food, was super delicious! Received one complimentary sopapilla (woohoo). I am hesitant to go back, would go back if I get a different server. SO go try it at your own risk of not having attentive/awesome service. ha. Good Luck!

This place isn't bad. The menu has a wide selection of food to choose from ranging from Salvadoran to Guatemalan. 

Portions are pretty generous for the price. 

FOOD (my sister and I ordered): 
- 1 Carne Asada Taco
- 1 Carne Asada Gordita 
- 2  Mixed Pupusas (beans/cheese/pork)  
- Charbroiled Chicken Breast Entree (comes with lettuce/tomatoes, beans, and veggie rice.)

All in all, good food. Nothing special about this place. The pupusas actually stood out because they tasted really good, but I wouldn't get that on a regular just because it's greasy and fried. 

Try this place out if you're ever on Buford Hwy! FREE Wi-Fi here.

Never been a fan of strip clubs (I prefer getting the real thing) so maybe I'm a bit biased.

I think I could do without the $8 beers and the below average women.  There is probably only one or two decent looking dancers here.  

The club itself is dark as hell, however, it's very clean and somewhat "classy".  The bathrooms are nice for a strip club.

I've gone a couple times, probably won't be back.  But if you enjoy throwing around dollar bills for boobs, this is the place to go!

Their falafel is 4 stars. If there is a way to get just the falafel, do that. 
It completely blew the low expectations I had. It is a larger size than most falafels and less leafy green based. It is perfectly fried so that it is not oily. It has the right amount of fluffy moistness on the inside and slight crunchiness outside.
However everything else is just mediocre. I paid a dollar extra for the hummus. I would skip this as you pay for a tiny one ounce scoop and it is watery. Most middle eastern restaurants have some hummus included in shawarma or bowls. The couscous is plain and has no hint of salt or seasoning. The toppings like the carrots, purple cabbage, and cucumber tomato salad are also just really bland. This place definitely needs to work on flavoring all of their food.

After reading the reviews on this place I was very intrigued.  I live only 5 minutes from this place so I tried it out. 
Interesting location inside a seniors home cafeteria.  Small menu but with options.  I tried a Genki bento box.  The place was busy for a Friday early lunch, I was seated closer to the " senior home lunch room " which was interesting, Im pretty sure they are use to having random strangers watch them have their lunch but I guess it works both ways.  Once you get over you're in a senior home's lunch room, the food wasn't bad.  My Genki box came with sashimi, rice, a potato croquette of some sort very tasty probably my favorite from the whole meal, and chicken.  Over all is ok value and taste but I don't know if Id come back.

Having been back to this place several times since- at first I admit somewhat kicking and screaming - I am convinced that the horrible experience I had was somewhat of a fluke. I am changing my rating because I have to say that since that ire-inspiring night I have had only positive interactions with every single person who works here. The service might not be spectacular, but the personalities are - so Twilight I apologize for my haste in judging you.

And your jello shots aren't bad at all.
