Zefferelli's is a decent place to grab Italian food on Robson without shelling out too much dough.

The atmosphere is nice with the pricing being the strong point amongst other higher priced restaurants in the area. Typically between $10-$20 a person.  The portions seem skewed towards being larger with the pasta dishes which is probably what I would suggest sticking with.

One part that was slightly disappointing was their desserts which I found were much better elsewhere, but that may be a matter of preference. I found the tiramisu overly dense and too sweet. Just a little over the top on every aspect, however if you like an uber rich dessert then it may serve you perfectly.

Wandered in here while looking for a Christmas gift for a friend. 
Great selection of loose leaf tea (I am talking any and all flavors under the sun!) and a really knowledgeable/friendly staff.  They have some great pre-made gift baskets that would be suitable for any tea lover. The store smells absolutely amazing and I was offered a delicious sample upon entry. 

They have rows and rows of different sized canisters filled with their more popular blends so you can grab and go. Another touch that I liked is that there is a good description of each product (with prices included) on the shelf with the teas. Call me anti-social, but I don't always like to ask a million questions to people in the store. I picked the decaf "Calm" blend, as something to help me wind down in the evenings; so far I quite like it. 

My one complaint is that they had a very limited selection of mugs and teapots. Only one mug that was available was a to-go type with the steeper basket kind of built in. Not exactly what I was hoping to find, but I will return in the future to try something new.

It's a good thing that the food and baked goods are delicious here, because THE SERVICE STINKS!!!  We waiting over 15 minutes for a bowl of soup to be brought to us.  When I politely acknowledged the long wait to the manager he asked me if I realized that it was lunch time and that they are busy during lunch.  WOW I didn't realize that just because I decided to come at lunch time I had to have bad service.  When the soup finally came we were given the wrong kind of soup.  After mix up was fixed, we finally got to try the soup.  It was wonderful and so was the bread!

Will I go back??  Yes....for the food and NOT during lunch time!

Dancing Goats is a nice, quaint, extremely busy/popular coffee shop in downtown Decatur.  However, I am not a big fan of their Batdorf & Bronson Coffee supplied by local Atlanta B&B Coffee Roasters. Their coffee if extremely bitter tasting and honestly, I can make better at home for a much more smooth, non-bitter taste. This is just from their regular drip coffee. Possibly a latte or cappuccino might provide for less bitter-tasting coffee with the extra milk added. 

Still, a nice vibe to this local coffee shop and the pastries in the glass counter where you order coffee always look extremely tempting!  Have only tried the mini donuts and while they are somewhat dry when eating them solo, they are rather yummy when dunked in coffee!

All in all, a nice place to try if you live or visit in the Decatur area.

I know everyone loves Harold, he seems really nice but don't use him during SXSW or any type of busy season, he will just forget. 

I have about 10 emails from 2 weeks before due date for a simple 500 copies 8.5x11 color prints. The first one took 2 days for him to respond to, I sent another email. I finally received an email saying they're ready and to come get them Friday, I ask if I can come on Monday so I can get payment. Monday okay. Arrive on Monday...the copies weren't ready. I waited 20 minutes to get them printed, which isn't bad but that's 20 minutes that were supposed to have already been done already. 

He's 'calm' which really just means he goes his own pace and his slower than a Kinkos. I want to support local businesses, but I'd rather use an outside printer if it means the things I need done get done on time. I almost went to him for ALL my oversized stuff like 18x24 posters and what not, those things take a lot of time to produce, usually 2 weeks would be sufficient but if it happened like my regular 8.5x11 prints I'd never have them in on time.

This was my second BBQ experience in Austin and I still haven't been blown away yet. I ordered the 2 meats and 2 sides plate. I picked shredded pork, house sausage, mashed sweet potatoes, and macaroni and cheese. Their BBQ sauce is decent, could be a tad spicer. The shredded pork was bland to me but I really liked the sausage. I wish they had put more of it on the plate. It wasn't even an entire link, it was half of one. 

The macaroni and cheese were the big shells, very Velveeta like, and more creamy than cheesy. It would be nice if they added a crunch element to it like a baked bread topping. The mashed sweet potatoes were good, I enjoyed the pecans on top, but it needed a little more sweet like brown sugar to balance out from the salt of the pecans. 

Overall, I would eat here again. I will stick to sausage only next time. I still want to try their fried okra and dessert. On the plus, we did get a free beer here tonight. A distributer was there and giving out full samples. I just felt that for the price, some of the food left us underwhelmed.

The curry here is awesome, the pad thai is perfect!

Why then am i giving it 3 stars? The service wasn't great. We ordered apps and watched everyone around us get theirs and then suddenly my curry came out then a few minutes later the pad thai we were sharing came out then even later my friends dish and finally the rice for the curry arrived. I asked for a second pair of chopsticks and where our app was and was told it was on the way and that the chopsticks would be right out. Well we never got the chopsticks and we canceled the app. Its too bad the service wasnt up to par. However the food is worth it.

I finally got the opportunity to get to Agave for dinner.  The atmosphere is lively and the restaurant got very loud.  It was a fun place to have dinner.  

I'll start by saying that the fried chicken breast did live up to all its hype.  It truly was delicious.  Seasoned nicely, moist, fabulous.  I'm a fan and it will probably be the one thing that gets me back to Agave.  Also, the drinks were superb.  I had the Peachtree Margarita and it was perfect. I also have to give it to them on the salsa that comes with the chips.  It was some of the best I've had.  I loved the blue chips too.  Loved the corn on the cob too. It was grilled and I tore it the hell up.  

On the flip side, the other items that I ate did not impress me.  The short ribs were very bland tasting, although very tender.  They failed to live up to what I was looking for and I was mad at them. Also, I had some spring rolls that were so incredibly spicy until I couldn't taste anything else.  It was obvious that too much of something was put in those.  The quesadillas were pretty good, but not anything special.  

I'm going to have to add that I felt that the entrees were overpriced. Just saying.  

The service was outstanding. Everything flowed like clockwork. A+ for service here.   

Parking here is plentiful with free valet.

The food earns at least two stars, and the restaurant itself earns one more, but the staff scores a goose egg.  When we entered on a Sunday afternoon, we waited at the hostess stand for a bit before the hostess sauntered over without making eye contact.  She stood, looking down at whatever important info was on the podium, and after about 10 seconds muttered "hi" without ever looking up.  Not sure if she was talking to us, we uttered "hi" feebly.

"Two?"  She finally looked up (so she could count how many pesky humanoids were filling her space).
We were escorted to a crappy table (the place was maybe 1/4 full), and we asked if we could have another table.  No answer, but more sauntering over to the desired table.

The perky waiter showed up after a bit, but acted shocked - SHOCKED!  that we didn't order wine.  Baaaad start!  We asked for a second plate so we could share a pizza, but that was too much information for him to process.  Instead of eating cold pizza, we improvised.

The food was delightful, as it has been the few times we've visited before, but the waitstaff needs to act like we're not interrupting their party with a loud expulsion of colonic gases.

Often times our best qualities, in their extreme, are our greatest weakness. And so it goes with Cameron's service model. Sat at the bar on date night recently, but decided against dinner because we couldn't carry on a cohesive conversation. With zero meaning being ignored and ten as perfectly attentive, the bartender was a 15. The tasty mushrooms and oysters Rockefeller appetizers were damn near perfect. Just wish we could've enjoyed them without the monologue on George Washington's proclivity for rum from Barbados and unsolicited interruptions.

Been here a few times and not much is new especially if you do the hibachi grill. 

Food always taste similar which is a good but bad thing. Good that it is always consistent. Bad that it all tastes the same. 

Now, we took our 3 year old here and he had a blast. It's a shame that you have to buy a $14 or so kid entree for a young children when they could easily share with you and mom. 

With that said, he did have so much fun. He enjoyed the flames, the fake train, the food tossing etc. 

Service was stellar, but when your tab is $125+ for 2 Adults and a young kids it's expected. 

Don't get me wrong, we had fun and the food was good, but that's expected; hence, the 3 stars.  

My boy is always wanting to come back again, but at the price point is an annul event at most. 

They surely did NOT disappoint. Just with it being so expensive, expectations are high.

I stopped into Gunshow over the weekend. For those that don't know, Gunshow is Kevin Gillespie's latest fine dining meets dim sum concept in Glenwood Park. The environment is extremely loud, cavernous and feels exactly like a pop-up, not a full-fledged restaurant. The food was good, service friendly and helpful, but in short, the only part of the equation that felt fine dining was the price.

Getting a reservation at Gunshow seemed difficult. They only had 9:30 slots open on Friday and Saturday. However, we were able to walk in at 8 PM and get a table for two with no problem.

Small plates - I love the concept. Getting to try many items that can show a kitchen's range and ability is always ideal. I'm not going to tell you how Gunshow operates (you can read that on every review of the place so far), but if you want to try the whole menu somewhere, Gunshow is a great place (so long as you brought your billfold). We ate a majority of the menu and really, that's not too difficult - the servings are small.

The reason for the dim sum/cart concept, as explained by Gillespie, is to keep things completely fresh from the kitchen. Nothing is supposedly precooked like many restaurants must do - parboiled rice for risotto was the example given in an early interview. I thought to myself, "OK that makes some sense." And I thought that until the first dish, Cuban chicken with black beans and rice, was delivered to our table - cold. 

Now, that Cuban chicken was mighty tasty. Well cooked, well seasoned and nice cumin flavored rice. However, there were no twists. It was a very straight-forward rendition of Cuban food. And the serving was a single chicken thigh over just enough rice and beans to provide a pedestal for a chicken thigh. Price - $14. This is about a $5 serving at any Cuban restaurant in the city and there just wasn't anything special about the dish that warranted the price. Even if you consider the fact that everything at Gunshow is local, you just can't hit that price point. And the chicken was cold.

Then came what Gunshow calls "Assorted Savory, Spicy, Crispy and Crunchy Snacks. This was delivered in two forms. 1. Some cubed melon with duck pastrami (smart combo) and 2. a Hopping John type of fritter. The Hopping John fritter was completely comforting and delicious. It was approximately the size of a golf ball. Price - $5. That's flat out criminal anyway you look at it. If there were three balls on the plate, maybe they should be able to charge $5. OK, I'll stop harping on the price now.

A "Closed on Sunday" chicken sandwich was a take on the Chick-fil-a sandwich. Again, delicious with a pillowy soft sweet roll bun (they called it a biscuit?), but extremely simple and straightforward.

There were three savory dishes that standout in my mind as excellent. A smoked lamb leg with field peas. The lamb was exceptionally tender, flavorful and the field pea ragout cut through the unctuous lamb with acidic precision. 

The country breakfast consisted of grits with chicken and bacon gravy, some pickled tomatoes and a poached egg on top. This combination is delicious but the yolk of the egg was gelatinized and overcooked, not runny. Again, not exactly fine dining execution.

Lastly, a wild mushroom tart was obnoxiously delicious. The entire top portion, which included figs and cheese, had a sweet and sour finishes that cut through the fatty cheese and butter crust much like the lamb dish.

If you didn't notice by now, vegetables are extremely underrepresented at Gunshow. The color green is often used as a garnish, not an accompaniment. Plan on a meat-centric meal. 

Dessert we had a peanut butter and chocolate dish that was simple and kind of a throwaway. The sticky toffee pudding, however was phenomenal. They used fig instead of dates to cut the fat again (seeing a theme yet?) and it was finished with some bacon and Morreli's Salted Caramel ice cream. I know that bacon and salted caramel are buzzwords and easy sells, but the dish would have probably been better with plain, ol' vanilla.

Did I like the food at Gunshow? Absolutely. Did I enjoy the experience? Yup. Am I being hyper critical? Yessir. But the bottom line is both the pricing and execution need serious tweaking. A $50 meal should not only be delicious and close to perfect, it should also be moderately filling. I applaud Gillespie's concept - local food prepared as freshly as possible and sold to you by cooks, not servers. I also love trying new items and the option of an ever-changing menu. Ultimately, Gunshow comes off as a pop-up, not a destination fine-dining restaurant.  I know the ingredients are expensive and the preparation is time consuming, but the overall experience at Gunshow doesn't equal the cost.

Atmosphere is excellent.  Seriously gorgeous. Friendly staff. Big selection on the menu.  Great ideas for fusion., but as we usually expect, that usually should be call "Asian Confusion".  It's a tough task to get right.  Even the Thai writing on the parking signs and on the menu were not correct.  Did they rely on Google translate?  The only sign that was correctly translated was the Exit sign.

We had Pad Thai, Shu Mai, Som Tam, Crab Fried Rice.  We are used to Traditional Thai food, having lived there and cook at home.  Flavored seem off.  Strange to find basil and mushy green beans in Pad Thai.  Papaya salad is not easy to perfect, which was the result here.  Shu Mai was great flavor.   Crab fried Rice was pretty good - a little sweet but decent.

This Target is kind of hidden and can be missed very easily coming from both sides of 50(colonial) but if you use your GPS you should have no problem getting here.

The store is not very huge about the size of a regular Target but has your normal things like appliances and clothe but they added food now and have a whole section with frozen and dairy products and even some meat plus your normal items like soups,chips and jelly's and also condiments. 

The staff was nice and the cashier was really nice and even explain to use what the Target card is that gets you a discount here. The parking was not so bad like other reviews have said  but the parking area is not so big like at other Targets.

The prices at Target are good when it comes to clothe and appliances but the food seemed expensive and the selection is limited. Not a bad store, I was in the area and stopped in here for some quick things and got some Yoplait Pumpking pie yogurt witch was delicious

I was so excited about this place when many many months back I got to sample some of their food while on a foodie bicycle tour. Everything was so delicious that when my friend suggested we go while on the East Austin Studio Tour, I said hell yeah!

First off, I absolutely love sweet potato fries. Theirs are really great. EXCEPT that they put some sort of sickly sweet sauce on it that is not mentioned in the menu. When I had sampled these before they were perfectly fried and dusted with a cinnamon spice mix that was a perfect balance. The sauce is too much and I would've 86'd it had I known about it.

I ordered the Willie Nelson burger because I love me some bacon, cheese, and fried onion rings. This burger was so huge, I almost couldn't get my mouth around it. And that's my biggest complaint. I love a good burger, but maybe my mouth is extra small (which is weird because I often am called a big-mouth). I just could barely eat this burger. Plus, it was MESSY! The cheese spilled out, the sauce ran everywhere and a lot of it ended up in the basket and not my mouth. Which is too bad because it was very tasty otherwise.

On the plus side, they have Mexican coke and some really great fried pickles and veggies. The staff is really hilarious and fun and it's very Austin. I'll try this place again, but will be real careful when I order. Wish they offered a smaller sized burger for those of us with tiny mouths.

Haven't been in a while due to the fact that Thai Spice was renovating. Ordered food for takeout, my usual chicken pad thai w/ vegetables. Since I wanted to add the veggies, didn't use their online order service.  I was charged to add vegetables to my order, however, was sadly disappointed to realize they were not in my food when I got home.  While Thai Spice had improved on the accuracy of their ability to have orders ready on time (we didn't have to wait beyond what was told), I'm disappointed with their lack of attention to detail with correctly making my order.
